title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: A Japanese national who acted as pimp for minor children without their knowledge by posting their pictures at the web site was arrested by National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) operatives during a raid at his residence in Davao City last week. NBI Director Magtanggol B. Gatdula identified the arrested suspect as: KAZUHISA AIZAWA, a resident of Tessa’s Place, 749 Gravahan,Matina, Davao City. ANGELICA BURGOS SINGH, live-in partner of Aizawa who was present during the raid was also invited for questioning. Aizawa was arrested by virtue of a search warrant issued by Davao City RTC Executive Judge Isaac Robillo Jr. for violation of RA 7610 (Child Abuse), RA 6955 (Matching Filipino Women for Marriage to Foreign Nationals), RA 9208 (Qualified Trafficking in Person) and Unjust Vexation. In an investigation report submitted by Acting Regional Director Atty. Max B. Salvador, of the Southeastern Mindanao Regional Office (SEMRO), it was disclosed that the search warrant was based on the complaint of two 15-year old minors who were victims. They alleged that Aizawa, an expert in computer, created a website, pinoymarry.com and posted the pictures of the complainants and other minors purportedly available for marriage to foreign nationals. The ads were without the knowledge and consent of the complainants. Complainants sought the help of the NBI in arresting the suspect. NBI- SEMRO operatives nabbed suspects at his residence in Matina. Found and confiscated were two (2) hard drives, one laptop computer and three (3) cellular phones used in the creation of website, publication and posting of pictures of the complainants and dissemination of the purpose of the website. Singh, who was with the suspect was also arrested. They are now detained at the NBI detention cell.

title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: Four impostors believed engaged in “hulidap” by using fake NBI IDs and selling the same for a fee were arrested by the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) in an entrapment in Cavite the other day. The subjects were identified as: VICTOR BROWN BORROMEO, 46, of No.722 Rest Heaven St., Cavite City; ROBERT JABINAL CONGE, 42, of Legaspi Wawa, Binakayan, Kawit, Cavite; DANTE BARLOS BRONDIAL, 40, of Bgy. De Ocampo, Trece Martires City, Cavite; and JULAN DE GUZMAN ELLOSO, 39, of Bgy. Gabino Maderan, Samaka Site, GMA, Cavite On September 14, 2012, a television network sent a letter-request to the NBI inquiring whether one Victor Borromeo is a regular NBI employee. Accordingly, together with Julan Elloso, they had been recruiting NBI confidential agents and selling fake NBI ID cards in Cavite. They charge amounts from P1,500-3,000 for each I.D. Surveillance operation by the NBI operatives of the Special Task Force confirmed the report that both “Victor Borromeo” and Julan Elloso do not appear in the roster of NBI employees. It was further learned that Borromeo’s group will conduct an “NBI operation” in Jollibee Restaurant in Bacoor, Cavite in the afternoon of September 18, 2012. This prompted the NBI to conduct an entrapment. At 1:30 P.M. of the aforementioned date, NBI agents proceeded to and positioned themselves at strategic points outside the above-said fast food in Bacoor, Cavite. Moments thereafter, Borromeo and his group arrived. It was noticed that subject Robert Conge was wearing a shirt marked “PULIS” and was seen to have a handgun tucked in his waist. On the other hand, Borromeo and Elloso were sporting t-shirts with big NBI markings. They were accompanied by Brondial and Conge. As the suspects were about to enter the establishments, NBI operatives approached Borromeo and demanded the latter’s authority and his cohorts in wearing said shirts with NBI and PULIS markings. Borromeo and Elloso showed NBI badges and NBI ID cards. The NBI team inspected and found that said credentials were fake. Both and the two other suspects were immediately arrested. Found and seized were a .38 caliber revolver with six (6) live ammunitions without proper documents. All suspects failed to show corresponding legal documents and permits authorizing possession of the gun and ammunitions. Also recovered from their possession were several fake NBI Confidential Agent identification cards. On February 14, 2012, the NBI Director released a memorandum on the revocation and recall of all NBI Consultants including confidential agents, IDs as well as those of the security volunteers issued by the past administration. This was announced in the media. The NBI is calling on those who might have been victimized by the group to come to the NBI or report the same so that appropriate charges can be filed against arrested subjects. Charges for violation of PD 1866 as amended by RA 8294 (otherwise known as the Law on Illegal Possession of Firearms), violation of Art. 177 of the Revised Penal Code, as amended (Usurpation of Authority); and violation of Art. 172 of the Revised Penal Code as amended (Falsification by Private Individual and use of Falsifed Documents) were filed against the suspects before the Imus Cavite Provincial Prosecutor’s Office.

title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today said operatives of NBI-Criminal Intelligence Division (NBI-CRID) have arrested an individual in an entrapment operation on January 11, 2018 in Manila for large scale illegal recruitment. Director Dante A. Gierran identified the Subject as RICO PAGUIO y GARCIA, former OFW who worked in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia and resident of Dagupan St., Tondo, Manila. The case stemmed from the complaint of six (6) individuals against the Subject who had been recruiting victims for work abroad, specifically in Saudi Arabia, under the pretext that he was connected to Sunergeous Mapower Services Corporation, when in fact he has resigned from the said corporation since February 2017. Subject had obtained from the Complainants a total of Php 98,200.00 allegedly as down payment for processing their overseas employment. As of press time, an estimated of more or less fifty (50) victims have been recruited by the Subject. Certification from Philippine Overseas Employment Administration (POEA) revealed that the Subject is not licensed nor authorized to recruit workers for overseas employment. With this information, an entrapment operation was conducted inside a mall in Manila resulting in the arrest of the Subject. Documents are now being readied gathered for filing of charges against Subject RICO PAGUIO for violation of R.A. 8042 (Large Scale Illegal Recruitment) and Estafa.

title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: On November 9, 2020, operatives of NBI-National Capital Region (NBI-NCR) seized 5 laptops, 70 OTP dangles, 8 cellular phones, 15 bank cards, and 1 POS machine in the premises of Huang Youmei. Items were seized by virtue of Search Warrants for alleged violation of RA 8484 (Access Devices Act of 1998) as amended by RA 11449. On November 17, 2020, operatives of NBI-Anti-Violence Against Women and Children (NBI-AVAWCD) arrested MARTINEZ, GABRIELA ADILYN y MARFURI, MARTINEZ, ROXANNE y MARFURI, and AGUILON ANNIKA y ROBILLOS for Human Trafficking. Subjects were arrested in an operation which stemmed from the information received that young girls including minors were allegedly being trafficked and exploited for sex in Zambales. On the aforementioned date, the rescue and entrapment operation was conducted resulting in the arrest of the Subjects and the rescue of 18 victims, 4 of whom are minors. Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the City Prosecutor’s Office, Olongapo City. On November 17, 2020, operatives of Iligan District Office (NBI-ILDO) arrested RANDY TIMBANGAN y CABASA for selling illegal drugs. Subject was arrested in a buy-bust operation conducted by NBI-ILDO at Bagong Silang, Iligan City. Bought from the Subject was 1 small size heat sealed rectangular transparent plastic sachet containing white crystalline substance suspected to be shabu weighing more or less 1 gram with an estimated value of Php 6,800.The said drug evidence was forwarded to Forensic Chemistry Division for quantitative and qualitative examination. Case for violation of RA 9165 (Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act) was being prepared for filing in court against the arrested Subject. On November 18, 2020, operatives of NBI-Rizal District Office (NBI-RIZDO) seized counterfeit Oxygen and Penshoppe products with an estimated value of Php 200,000. Items were seized in Brgy. San Jose, Hagonoy, Bulacan by virtue of Search Warrants for violation of RA 8293 (Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines) issued against SUSANA MALL PULL OUTS & MORE FB PAGE and/or ELEONOR SUNGA and/or occupants of its premises located at Brgy. San Jose, Hagonoy, Bulacan. On November 18, 2020, operatives of NBI-Puerto Princesa District Office (NBI-PUERDO) arrested ADONIS RAUSA by virtue of Warrant of Arrest for Rape by Sexual Assult. On November 19, 2020, operatives of NBI-Intellectual Property Rights Division (NBI-IPRD) seized 320 ampules of Azithromycin Dihydrate/Azitan (500mg), 1,600 ampules of Nitroglycerin/Nitrosan (1mg/1ml), 980 ampules of Norepinephrine Bitartrate/Sandine (4mg/4ml), and 560 ampules Bupivacaine/Bupican Heavy (5mg/5ml). Items were seized at Recytechphil Inc. located at Brgy. Tambubong, Bocaue, Bulacan by virtue of Search Warrants for violation of RA 8293 and RA 9711. On November 19, 2020, operatives of NBI-National Capital Region (NBI-NCR) arrested WILLIAM FRIEND by virtue of Warrant of Arrest for Robbery. Mr. Cabales requested for assistance in serving the Warrant of Arrest to the accused. WILLIAM FRIEND was then arrested in Meadowood Executive Vilage, Brgy. Panapan 8, Bacoor, Cavite. On November 19, 2020, operatives of NBI-Environmental Crime Division (NBI-EnCD) arrested spouses WOODY NUARIN y PERDIZ for Estafa. A complainant filed a complaint before the NBI against spouses WOODY NUARIN and ANTONETTE NUARIN. Complainant averred that she paid a total amount of Php 2 Million as full payment in exchange for a readily available condominium unit in Magnolia Place, Tandang Sora, Quezon City which was made to believe as owned and being held for sale at that time by spouses NUARIN. The spouses promised that she could immediately move-in after the full payment. However, after two months, no delivery of the condominium unit was made. The spouses asked for extension to comply with their obligation but after a few months, no delivery or transfer of ownership was made to the complainant. They offered another condominium unit in Tower I, Mezza II Residences Aurora Boulevard, Manila in exchange for the unit in Magnolia Place, Tandang Sora but with a higher selling price of Php 4.5 Million. Hoping that they will keep their promise, Complainant gave Php 200,000.00 to the spouses and another Php 63,000.00. However, after months of numerous demands for the delivery of the unit or the return of her payment with a total of amount of Php 2.263 Million, spouses still failed to comply. When the spouses offered another condominium in Capital Towers-Federal Land, E. Rodriguez Ave., Quezon City with an additional payment of Php 300,000.00, the entrapment operation was conducted resulting in the arrest of WOODY NUARIN. Subject was presented for inquest proceedings before the Quezon City Prosecutor’s Office for violation of Article 315 of the Revised Penal Code. On November 19, 2020, operatives of NBI-Environmental Crime Division (NBI-EnCD) arrested JOHN PATRICK REYES y AGUILAR, JHUN MORILLO y LOPEZ, FRANCIS PANGILINAN y BENJAMIN, JOHN MICHAEL MALIAS y SUPAL, EGILBERTO SAN PASCUAL y CAJES, RONALD LINSANGAN y MELO SANTOS, EDCEL RUIZ y NICDAO, VINCENT CANLAS y CUENCA, ALDRIN ANSON y GONZALES, JOMAR NAZAR y GUIRA, CHRISTOPHER MORENO y GUIRA, and JOEL ONG y POROL for illegal extraction and disposal of lahar materials. A report was received regarding an illegal quarrying in Brgy. Sapang Balen, Mabalacat city. Accordingly, the operation was undertaken without necessary permits required under the environmental law. Surveillance revealed the unrelenting extraction of lahar materials in the area. Verification from the DENR-MGB and PENRO shows that Guillermo Gamez Quarry is not a holder of a permit either from the MGB and Provincial Mining and Regulatory Board. Acting on the report, a joint team of NBI-EnCD and DENR-MGB conducted an operation resulting in the arrest of the above-mentioned Subjects who were caught in the act extracting and disposing lahar minerals without necessary permit required. Subjects were presented before the Department of Justice for Theft of Minerals under RA 7942. On November 23, 2020, operatives of NBI-Laoag District Office (NBI-LADO) arrested GIL B. PASCUAL for Estafa. Subject was arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from a complaint against the Subject. According to the complainant, Subject PASCUAL offered her a lot located in Brgy. Araniw, Laoag City with an agreed purchase price of Php 1.3 Million. Complainant paid the Subject an intial amount pg Php 100,000.00 and shall pay the additional amount of Php 200,000.00 as part of the agreed purchase price. While completing the amount of Php 200,000.00, complainant learned from certain Guillermo Agustin that the same lot was also offered for sale to him by the Subject. When Mr. Agustin discovered that there were several claimants/heirs over the said lot contrary to what Subject told him, he filed a complaint before the NBI-LADO. This prompted the complainant to also file a complaint before the NBI-LADO. On the above-mentioned date, the entrapment operation was conducted resulting in the arrest of the Subject. It was also found out that two other individuals were separately duped by the Subject using the same fraudulent scheme. Subject was presented for inquest proceedings before the City Prosecutor’s Office, Laoag City for violation of Article 315 of the Revised Penal Code. On November 24, 2020, operatives from NBI-Environmental Crime Division (NBI-EnCD) arrested 4 foreign nationals named STEPHEN FIELD (British), MARK HARRINGTON (British), MICHIELSEN DIRK JOSEF (Belgian), MARIA VICTORIA SCHAFER (Australian-Filipina), and 6 Filipino Subjects as MARY IRISH GUERRA, JOHNSON JACINAL, PATRICIA ANN VARGA, OSCAR DELOS SANTOS, ARTURO REVILLAME, and PAUL SAJISE. Subjects were arrested in an operation conducted by NBI-EnCD operatives against nine (9) establishments found to be encroaching forestland in Barangay Balabag, Boracay Island, Malay, Aklan per certification coming from DENR. All the establishments were never issued any tenurial instrument nor any other permits by the DENR. In the course of the operation, the 10 above-named individuals, who are identified as owners and care takers and presently in possession of the erring establishments, were arrested. SEA VIEW APARTMENT, ALOHA VILLA, LA DOLCE VITA/CASA MONTE, PRIVATE MOUNTAIN CASITAS BORACAY INN, COHIBA VILLAS, CAROLINA PARK VIEW, and BORACAY SUNSHINE SHUTTLE AND LIMOUSINE CORPORATION are the non-compliant establishments in the forestland areas and the 25+5 meter beach easement, as bared by the information and documents provided by BIARMG and CENR in Boracay Island. The aforesaid commercial establishments are big structures in Forestland Block E in Brgy Balabag, Boracay Island, Malay, Aklan. The fact that these structures were built in Forestland which is considered land of the Public Domain violates Section 20 in relation to Section 78 of Presidential Decree 705 otherwise known as the Revised Forestry Code of the Philippines, regarding the lack of permit, lease or any tenurial instrument from the government and unlawful occupation of Forestland. Other structures that violated the 25+5 meter beach easement no-build zone mandated under Malay, Aklan Municipal Ordinance are ARTISTA BEACH VILLAS and MONKEY HOUSE. The violation was committed since the structures or portion of it falls within the 25+5 meter beach easement no-build zone classified as Forest Land. Notwithstanding their violation of Municipal Ordinance and the issuance of a Notice to Self Demolition, ARTISTA BEACH VILLAS and MONKEY HOUSE have continuously defied the law. Their continued structural presence in 25+5 meter beach easement no-build zone which is part of the public forest is tantamount to occupation of forest land punishable under PD 705. Arrested Subjects were brought to the Prosecutor’s Office of Kalibo, Aklan for inquest proceedings for violation of PD 705 (Revised Forestry Code), PD 1067 (The Philippine Water Code), and the 25+5 meter beach easement ordinance of Malay, Aklan. On November 25, 2020, operatives of NBI-National Capital Region (NBI-NCR) seized counterfeit/fake aerosol spray cans bearing the trademarks of Butiki with an approximate value of Php 180,480.00. Items were seized by virtue of Search Warrants issued against ten (10) stores in Cabanatuan City, Nueva Ecija for violation of RA 8293 (Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines). On November 25, 2020, operatives of NBI-Eastern Visayas Regional Office (NBI-EVRO) arrested JAKE BERJA for Sextortion. Complainant received a message request from a Facebook account “Chris Abdon”. The message contained video of a woman taking a bath naked and the complainant recognized that it was her. Subject initially demanded nude photos of the complainant otherwise the said video would be posted in the social media and forwarded to her friends in Facebook. Complainant requested not to do it but Subject insisted until eventually, the demand was for the complainant to have sexual intercourse with him. This is when complainant sought the help of the NBI. With this, an entrapment operation was conducted resulting in the arrest of the Subject who was caught in the act of trying to remove complainant’s clothes while he was naked from the lower garment. Subject was detained at NBI-EVRO.

Subjects were arrested in an operation conducted by NBI-EnCD operatives against nine (9) establishments found to be encroaching forestland in Barangay Balabag, Boracay Island, Malay, Aklan per certification coming from DENR. All the establishments were never issued any tenurial instrument nor any other permits by the DENR. In the course of the operation, the 10 above-named individuals, who are identified as owners and care takers and presently in possession of the erring establishments, were arrested. SEA VIEW APARTMENT, ALOHA VILLA, LA DOLCE VITA/CASA MONTE, PRIVATE MOUNTAIN CASITAS BORACAY INN, COHIBA VILLAS, CAROLINA PARK VIEW, and BORACAY SUNSHINE SHUTTLE AND LIMOUSINE CORPORATION are the non-compliant establishments in the forestland areas and the 25+5 meter beach easement, as bared by the information and documents provided by BIARMG and CENR in Boracay Island. The violation was committed since the structures or portion of it falls within the 25+5 meter beach easement no-build zone classified as Forest Land. The message contained video of a woman taking a bath naked and the complainant recognized that it was her. Subject initially demanded nude photos of the complainant otherwise the said video would be posted in the social media and forwarded to her friends in Facebook. Complainant requested not to do it but Subject insisted until eventually, the demand was for the complainant to have sexual intercourse with him. This is when complainant sought the help of the NBI. body: PRESS STATEMENT July 09, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } Under the supervision of National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Director Judge Jaime B. Santiago (Ret.), the NBI – Batangas District Office (NBI- BatDO) arrested a certain “SHERWIN” at a restaurant along Laurel Highway, Balagtas, Batangas City for Estafa, as defined and penalized under Article 315 par. 2 of the Revised Penal Code. The operation stemmed from a complaint against the Subject for falsely pretending himself as someone who has power, connection and influence to process importation documents and tax returns with appropriate government agencies for a fee. Accordingly, Complainant met Subject SHERWIN in March 2025 at a restaurant in Lipa City, Batangas. During their conversation, Subject gave the impression that he has a lot of connections with the Bureau of Customs (BOC) and the Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR). As support, Subject showed proof of transactions and copies of documents he claimed to have been approved by the BOC and BIR making Complainant believe his falsehoods. Subject promised the Complainant that he has “right connection” and influence to process importation documents for a fee. Subject demanded One-Hundred Thousand pesos (Php 100,000.00) from the Complainant for processing fee. Subsequently, Complainant paid Twenty-Thousand Pesos (Php 20,000.00) as down payment to Subject SHERWIN. After the down payment, Complainant did not hear anymore from Subject SHERWIN. On June 30, 2025, Complainant informed this office that Subject SHERWIN contacted her to collect the balance on the processing fee amounting to Eighty-Thousand Pesos (Php 80,000). A certification issued by Office of District Collector – Bureau of Customs – Port of Batangas states that SHERWIN is not connected with the BOC in anyway. Moreover, he is not authorized, accredited or licensed to process, facilitate or issue customs-related transactions or documents. Thus, on July 02, 2025, the NBI-BatDO agents conducted an entrapment operation. After personally witnessing the tendering of the marked money to the Subject, NBI-BatDo agents gave the pre-arranged signal to the group. Thereafter, other NBI agents, who were positioned in the area immediately accosted Subject SHERWIN. The arrested Subject will be presented for Inquest Proceedings for violation of the aforementioned law before the Office of the City Prosecutor – Batangas City, Batangas.

body: PRESS STATEMENT August 12, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } PRESS RELEASE | NBI RESCUES 11 WOMEN, INCLUDING 6 MINORS, IN ANTI- HUMAN TRAFFICKING OPERATION The National Bureau of Investigation—Cordillera Administrative Region (NBI-CAR) successfully conducted an entrapment and rescue operation on August 3, 2026, at a hotel in Baguio City, resulting in the arrest of two alleged human traffickers and the rescue of eleven (11) female victims, six (6) of whom were found to be minors. The operation stemmed from verified intelligence information that a woman identified as “Rose” was allegedly offering and transporting female persons from Bulacan to Baguio City for sexual services in exchange for money. Through controlled communications, the subject allegedly agreed to bring several women to Baguio City and demanded that two private vans be provided for their transportation. On the day of the operation, the group traveled from Bulacan to Baguio City in two vehicles. Upon reaching the designated hotel, the female subject brought the eleven victims into the transaction room and presented them to undercover NBI personnel posing as customers. She thereafter received a white envelope containing the marked entrapment money and boodle money representing the agreed payment for bringing and delivering the victims for sexual services. After the subject accepted the payment, the pre-arranged signal was given, prompting the NBI-CAR arresting and rescue teams to enter the room, arrest the female subject, and secure the victims. Her male companion, identified as “Jivan,” was subsequently arrested at the hotel lobby after being positively identified as the person who allegedly assisted in organizing and transporting the victims. He was also reported to have escorted four of the victims into the second van and encouraged the women to perform well for their supposed customers so they could earn more. The rescued victims were immediately turned over to representatives of the Department of Social Welfare and Development for protective custody, assessment, counseling, and appropriate intervention. The arrested subjects were informed of the cause of their arrest and apprised of their constitutional rights. They were thereafter brought to the NBI-CAR Office for booking, medical examination, and custodial processing. Appropriate criminal charges for Qualified Trafficking in Persons in violation of Sec. 4 (a) and Sec. 6 (a) of Republic Act No. 9208, as amended, by Republic Act No. 10364 and Republic Act No. 11862, and Violation of Republic Act No. 7610 were filed against the arrested subjects. NBI Director Melvin Matibag reiterates the Bureau’s commitment to combating human trafficking and protecting women and children from sexual exploitation. He likewise encourages the public to report suspected trafficking activities to the nearest NBI office or appropriate law- enforcement authority. https://www.facebook.com/reel/1739527417368702

body: PRESS STATEMENT November 07, 2024 In line with the persistent battle of the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) against illegal drugs, the NBI-Dangerous Drugs Division (NBI-DDD) arrested an individual in Valenzuela City, for selling illegal drugs. The DDD received information that JJOANRO DAET CASTILLO alias JAY, company driver of Convalesce Inc., is engaged in selling and use of illegal drugs particularly shabu inside the company’s premises. The said company expressed concern over CASTILLO’s illegal activities that might compromise the safety and working conditions of its employees, and may lead to proliferation of illegal drugs within the company’s premises. Thus, on October 23, 2024, NBI-DDD operatives, in coordination with the PDEA, PNP, representatives from the National Prosecution Service-Department of Justice, proceeded to Convalesce Inc. at Brgy. Parada, Valenzuela City for the buy-bust operation. Subject CASTILLO was then arrested in flagrante delicto selling methamphetamine hydrochloride or shabu. JJOANRO DAET CASTILLO was presented for inquest proceedings for violation of Section 5 of RA 9165 otherwise known as the Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002.

body: A couple involved in child trafficking activities were nabbed by agents of the NBI – Anti Organized and Transnational Crime Division (AOTCD) during an entrapment operation at their residence in Pulang Lupa Uno, Las Pinas City recently. The suspects were identified by NBI Director Virgilio L. Mendez as: RESURRECCION A. FRANCO, Filipino and with address at Block 2, Lot-15 Pulang Lupa Uno, Las Pinas City; FLORENDO A. FRANCO, Filipino and with address at Block 2, Lot-15 Pulang Lupa Uno, Las Pinas City; and Dra. LAARNI L. DELENIANA, (at-large) Filipino and with business address at OB-GYNE Maternity & Lying-in Clinic, Block 2, Lot-15 Pulang Lupa Uno, Las Pinas City. NBI- Anti Organized and Transnational Crime Division (AOTCD) headed by HA Rommel Vallejo disclosed that they received an intelligence information last September 11, 2014, that a certain “REXY FRANCO”, a midwife, in Las Pinas City is engaged in the selling of newborn babies. A friend of the informant was allegedly approached by “REXY” and asked if he knew anyone who wanted to “adopt” newborn babies for a fee. To validate the information, undercover agents posed as the interested buyer of a baby. The undercover agent’s cellphone number was given to REXY who contacted her and initially offered her a new born baby. However, on September 12, 2014, REXY informed the undercover agent that the baby she initially offered to her for “adoption” was already sold by the mother of the child. Subject instead offered to sell another baby which according to her will be born sometime next week. At 1:00 pm of September 14, 2014 Subject informed the undercover agent that the mother was already on labor and would give birth sooner than expected. REXY instructed the undercover agent that she can pick-up the baby later in the afternoon in her residence and demanded the amount of Php 35, 000.00 as payment for the baby. On even date, an entrapment operation was immediately prepared and implemented by operatives of AOTCD wherein two (2) marked five hundred peso bills were mixed with other five hundred bills to be used as entrapment money . Two (2) undercover operatives posing as a couple buyers of the baby, together with a representative from the DSWD, Jelyn Bujatin, went to the house of Rexy at Block 2, Lot-15 Pulang Lupa Uno, Las Pinas City. Upon arrival at REXY’s residence, the undercover agents were ushered inside the house where they saw Florendo Franco, REXY’s husband. After few conversation REXY fetched the newborn baby at OB-GYNE MATERNITY and LYING IN CLINIC of Dr. Laarni L. Deleniana which is adjacent to the house and gave the same to the male undercover agent. Afterwhich, REXY and the couple discussed other details that involves documents and the baby’s name in which Florendo later joined them. At this point, REXY demanded the payment for the baby. The female undercover agent counted the money and gave the P35,000.00 to Rexy in the presence of Florendo. While Rexy was counting the money, the male undercover agent went out of the house, gave the prearranged signal to the AOTCD operatives who rushed inside the house, and placed the Subjects under arrest for violation of Child Trafficking under Section 7 of R.A. 7610. The new born baby was brought to Reception and Studies Center for Children of the Department of Social Welfare and Development at Misamis St. Bago Bantay, Quezon City. Charges for Violation of Section 7 (Child Trafficking) of Republic Act of 7610 (An Act Providing for Stronger Deterrence and Special Protection Against Child Abuse, Exploitation and Discrimination, and for Other Purposes were filed against the suspects at the Office of the State Prosecutor of the Department of Justice (DOJ).

title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: PRESS STATEMENT September 01, 2022 COURT FINDS ACCUSED GUILTY OF FALSIFICATION OF DOCUMENTS In its order dated August 3, 2022, Presiding Judge of RTC Branch 108, Pasay City rendered judgment finding accused NAMRAIDA KUNAIB y ZACARIA Guilty beyond reasonable doubt of Falsification of Public Document by a Private Individual (Article 172 in relation to Article 171 of the Revised Penal Code). KUNAIB was about to depart for Kuwait on July 21, 2021 but she was not allowed departure by the immigration officers of NAIA Terminal 1 for using dubious travel documents. She was then turned over to NBI-International Airport Investigation Division (NBI-IAID). As per standard procedure of NBI-IAID, KUNAIB was interviewed, photographed and her fingerprints were taken. In the NBI Fingerprint Identification Card she filled out, she stated that her date of birth is sometime in 1996, contrary to the date of birth appearing in her passport which was October 13, 1991. She admitted that she used her passport bearing the incorrect date of birth when she first travelled to Kuwait in 2016 to work. She renewed the said passport in 2020 and used the same in her attempt to depart for Kuwait. KUNAIB was placed under arrest for using a passport which was secured in any way by reason of any false statements. She was then presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor, Pasay City for violation of Section 19 (b)(2) of RA 8239 (Philippine Passport Act of 1996). During the court hearing, she pleaded guilty to the lesser offense of Falsification of Public Document by Private Individual.

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today announced the arrest of an individual in Roxas, Palawan for selling imported cigarettes without paying the proper taxes and duties. NBI Officer-in-Charge “(OIC)-Director Eric B. Distor identified the subject as WENZAR DASSAN y MAMAH (Filipino) a.k.a. WAWEN, who was arrested in an entrapment operation by Agents of the NBI-Puerto Princesa District Office (NBI-PUERDO) on May 15, 2021. OIC Director Distor said that the operation stemmed from intelligence report regarding the rampant selling and distribution of imported cigarettes particularly FORT, BRAVO, L.A., SORYA, GUDAM GARAM, R.S. (brand) and other imported cigarettes from Malaysia and Indonesia without paying the proper taxes and duties due to the Philippine government. To verify the veracity of the report, NBI-PUERDO conducted surveillance and test-buy operations in various public market in Palawan. NBI-PUERDO was able to purchase FORT, BRAVO, and NEW BERLIN cigarettes from Subject Dassan and a certain Abdul. Based on the packaging, the cigarettes were manufactured in Malaysia and Indonesia and does not have the proper seal and tax stamps of the Bureau of Internal Revenue, in violation of RA 1937 otherwise known as the Tariff and Customs Code. Given the authority, operatives of NBI-PUERDO, with prior coordination with other law enforcement agency, conducted an entrapment operation in the afternoon of May 15, 2021, which resulted in the arrest of Subject Wenzar Dassan as soon as he received the entrapment money in exchange for the smuggled cigarettes along the highway in Barangay Nicanor Zabala, Roxas, Palawan. The operation also resulted in the seizure of reams of New Berlin Cigarettes (Red), Fort Menthol Cigarettes (Green), Fort Full Flavour Cigarettes (Red), Fort Black menthol, cash, and entrapment money. Subject Dassan was presented for Inquest Proceedings before the Office of Provincial Prosecutor of Puerto Princesa City, Palawan for violation of R.A. 1937 otherwise known as the “Tariff and Customs Code” as amended by R.A. 10863.

Santiago lauded former NBI Head Agent and Chief of the Cybercrime Division, RONALD “JUN” PONCIO AGUTO, who has just been proclaimed as the duly elected Governor of the Province of Batanes. “Your NBI family is proud of you for winning the gubernatorial race in Batanes. Continue to emulate the core values of Nobility, Bravery, Integrity on your new journey as the father of the province,” Santiago said. Aguto won the election under the party of President Ferdinand R. Marcos, Jr’s Partido Federal ng Pilipinas (PFP). Aguto won a close match with Medardo Abad, Jr. by only 209 votes. Aguto belongs to Batch 36 (Class 1999) of the NBI Academy. He has attended many international trainings including the prestigious Royal Canadian Mounted Police, Criminal Investigation Bureau, National Police Agency of Taiwan, International Law Enforcement Academy (ILEA) Roswell, New Mexico, Asia Pacific Law Enforcement Academy, Hongkong Police College and FBI’s International Innocent Images Task Force in Calverton, Maryland, USA. He also attended and is a graduate of the Federal Bureau of Investigation National Academy (FBI NA). Aguto is a committed and dedicated public servant and a recipient of many commendations when he was still an NBI Agent. He has established a strong reputation for integrity and ethical behavior including his full support to the NBI Gender and Development (GAD) programs when he was the Chief of the Budget Division.

body: PRESS STATEMENT September 17, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } NBI EMPLOYEE ATTENDS MULTI-HAZARD TRAINING; SAVES FATHER FROM HEART ATTACK In a dramatic and urgent turn of events, an NBI employee found herself in a life-and-death situation when her father suddenly suffered a heart attack. Fortunately, she had received proper emergency-response training. Quickly recognizing the warning signs, she sprang into action and immediately began administering cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) on her father. Her firm and continuous chest compressions—totaling sixteen—were crucial in maintaining blood circulation. After her persistent efforts, her father finally began to breathe again, bringing hope and relief amid the crisis. After the incident, the employee took a moment to express her deepest gratitude to NBI Director Atty. Melvin A. Matibag, as well as to the NBI-Disaster and Victim Identification Division (NBI-DVI) and the NBI-Learning and Development Division (NBI-LDD), for their considerable effort in providing essential life-saving training programs for NBI employees. She specifically appreciated the comprehensive life-saving training she received through the Multi-Hazard Training for NSED Marshals, which covered a wide range of emergency response skills. This training not only equipped her with vital skills and knowledge but also boosted her confidence in handling emergencies. She acknowledged that without the insights and practical experience gained from this specialized training, her father’s faith in her could have been different. She emphasized the profound impact this training had on her ability to respond effectively in crises, underscoring its importance in her personal and professional development. Director Matibag praised the NBI employee for skillfully applying the valuable knowledge she gained during her specialized training, which played a crucial role in saving her father’s life. He also acknowledged the NBI-DVI and NBI-LDD for delivering comprehensive, targeted training sessions to NBI staff, emphasizing that these programs equip employees with vital skills they can use effectively during emergencies and difficult situations.

body: Five Taiwanese nationals allegedly engaged in international telephone fraud in the Philippines were arrested by agents of the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) in Marikina yesterday. The suspects were identified by NBI Director Magtanggol B. Gatdula as: CHANG HUNG-YI; CHEN CHUN-HSIEN; HSIEH FU-CHIN; CHEN HUNG-LUN and HO WEI-HUNG, all residing at of No. 2 Pres. Laurel St., Industrial Valley Complex, Marikina City. On April 8, 2011, the NBI received a letter request from the Taipei Economic and Cultural Office in the Philippines requested investigative assistance about a continuous operation of international telephone fraud in the Philippines. Most of the victims are Taiwanese and Chinese nationals. Immediately thereafter, the NBI-National Capital Region Office coordinated with the Ministry of Justice Investigation Bureau to obtain further information on the base of operation of the syndicate around Metro Manila and other parts of the country. A series of surveillance was conducted on the house located at No. 2 Pres. Laurel St., Industrial Valley Complex Marikina City. Reliable information disclosed that the house is discreetly engaging in a “telephone fraud operation” managed by Taiwanese nationals. During investigation of said area, a series of intertwined telephone/internet cables attached to the house was noticed. It was also observed that almost daily, only the Filipino driver employed in the house was the one who purchased food and basic needs of these Chinese-speaking people. Very seldom, did they leave the house. A search warrant was applied for the said premises occupied by a certain Song Ming Dong and companions. On August 1, 2011, Hon. Judge Zaldy B. Docena of the NCR-RTC Branch 170 Malabon City, issued a search warrant for violation of Sec. 9, RA 8484 (The Access Device Regulation Act of 1998) directing NBI operatives to search the premises of Song Ming Dong in the aforementioned place. On August 2, 2011, NBI-NCR operatives proceeded to the house of Dong and served said search warrant. In the premises were five (5) Taiwanese nationals simultaneously operating like call center agents. Moreover, the operatives noticed that said foreign nationals were reading some documents which accordingly, appeared to be a “script” used by suspects in perpetuating their unlawful activities. The searched place yielded the following: a Linksys wireless router, PLDT My DSL modem, two digital decoder, four Nokia 1616-2 cellular phones, a Nokia 1682 c cellular phones, five broadband USB, an HSDPA USB modem, four Aus laptop, and an Acer laptop. The suspects were brought to the NBI and were referred for inquest proceedings today before the Marikina City Prosecutor’s Office.

body: National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) agents nabbed two long wanted fugitives in estafa cases involving millions of pesos in two separate operations conducted in Quezon City last Wednesday. First to fall was VALERIE SANTIAGO VON SUCH alias Valerie Aquino y Such whose vehicle was intercepted by NBI operatives along 12th Avenue, Cubao, Quezon City. Von Such was served a Warrant of Arrest issued in May, 2008 by the Regional Trial Court Branch 85 of Quezon City for the crime of Estafa under Criminal Case No. Q-07-1493. Von Such was the subject of complaint by the general manager of Nissan Gallery of Libis, Quezon City for defrauding the firm of more than P19 million about an order and purchase by suspect of twelve (12) Nissan Sentra X-Trail Sports Utility Vehicle (SUV) and two (2) Nissan Sentra Patrol vehicles. Subject paid the said firm through a letter of credit and postdated checks which later proved spurious. In another operation, another long wanted fugitive, RICARDO MERCANO JR. was apprehended by the same team of NBI agents at his residence in Philip’s North Point Park Subdivision, San Bartolome, Quezon City by virtue of a Warrant of Arrest issued in August 2006 by the Regional Trial Court Branch 37, Calamba City for the crime of Estafa under Criminal Case No. 13027-05. Mercano and several others collected money from certain investors for a non-existing condominium project amounting to P3.5 million. The NBI is calling the general public who have been victimized by the said suspects to file their complaints at NBI main office, Taft Avenue, Manila. Both arrested suspects are currently detained at the NBI. The Bureau is checking on their records for more possible warrants of arrest issued against both subjects under different aliases.

body: Five ranking officers of a multi-level marketing firm who defrauded dozens of prospective investors of at least P10 Million pesos are facing charges recommended by the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) at the Department of Justice (DOJ) last Friday. The subjects are identified as: (1) EDMUNDO C. CACERES, JR., (2) MARLON C. CACERES; (3) CELIA E. ROMERO; (4) CELSO O. CABRERA; and (5) MONALIZA C. BRENDIA, all incorporators and trustees of ECC-LIVELIHOOD SOCIAL SERVICES, INC. with address at 2nd Level, Margarita Commercial Center, Dita, Sta. Rosa. Laguna. Caceres Jr. established Caceres Lending Investor Co. in 1999. In August 2011, Caceres adopted the concept of multi-level marketing and used the names Caceres Global Foundation, Inc. and Global Money Unlimited Incorporated (Global Money) in flyers and internet sites to recruit members. In March 2012 Caceres registered a new entity, ECC – Livelihood Social Services, Inc., with the Securities and Exchange Commission with subjects as incorporators. On March 26, 2012, the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) referred to the NBI for parallel investigation the activities of ECC-LIVELIHOOD SOCIAL SERVICES, INC. for possible estafa thru Ponzi and/or Illegal Pyramiding Scheme of the ECC Livelihood Social Services, Inc. as well as the Caceres Global Foundation Inc. and Global Money Unlimited Inc. or Global Money, earlier established by Edmundo C. Caceres. Two days, on March 28, 2012, after Kenie Martin and sixteen other complainants filed a complaint with the NBI and alleged that despite duly paying their membership fees and recruiting several members themselves, they were not able to avail of the promised incentives. Subject recruit members who are required to pay a fee of P1,000.00 each and recruit their own “down-lines” who pay the same fee, will be provided among others the following benefits: (1) Life Insurance – Accidental Death (P100,000.00), Total Permanent Disability (P100,000.00); (2) Hospitalization/Medical Assistance – P500.00 to P2,500.00; (3) GM Heart Fund – a certain amount given upon death of a member; (4) Money loan – P5,000.00 to P100,000.00; (5) Power Potential Income – P10,000 daily to P300,000 monthly; (6) Bonus Income – P20,000; (7) Loyalty Income – P50,000; and (8) Profit sharing – P50,000. Said benefits are given depending upon the member’s down-lines (recruits). On March 28, 2012, complainant Kenie Martin and 16 others filed a complaint alleging despite paying their membership fees and recruiting several members they were not able to avail of the promised incentives. Likewise, complainants Candida Panta and Wilfredo Pacatang diled a complaint and alleged that they were recruited as members and/or investors by subject Caceres and on 13 February 2012 they signed a memorandum of agreement whereby complainants, for a fee of P500,000.00 were authorized to open a branch office and complainants were entitled to 20% of the total “pay in inventory” in their branch, However, on 28 February 2012, subject Caceres alleged non-remittal of payments and took over their branch. The Insurance of the Philippine Islands Co., Inc. (IPI) said that while they agreed to insure the networkers of Global Money and released 10,000 insurance cards to them, the check payment for the premiums bounced leading to the cancellation of their memorandum of agreement with Caceres. On the other hand, the Insurance commission issued a certification that Edmundo Caceres Jr., Global Money Unlimited and ECC Social Livelihood Services, Inc. do not appear in the records of the Insurance Commission as having an existing license as insurance agents. Charges of Syndicated Estafa as defined and penalized under Art. 315, par. 2(a) of the Revised Penal Code as amended, in relation to Sec. 1 of P.D. 1689 were recommended before the Department of Justice on July 13, 2012.

title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: PRESS STATEMENT April 22, 2022 In line with the government’s drive against illegal recruitment, the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) announces the arrest of an individual by the NBI-International Airport Investigation Division (NBI-IAID) in NAIA, Pasay City for illegal recruitment. NBI Officer-In-Charge (OIC) Director Distor identified the subject as JONALYN BUENO y DACAYO. Director Distor said that on April 10, 2022, Subject Bueno was about to depart for Singapore via Cebu Pacific flight no. 5J803. However, immigration officers intercepted her after she was suspected of transporting with two (2) other passengers illegally recruited to work abroad. Subject Bueno was turned over to the NBI-IAID for further investigation. During the investigation, Subject Bueno said that she was travelling with her two (2) friends namely, Normina M. Sapad and Joy V. Agassid and claimed that she met Sapad through Facebook while Agassid was her friend from Nueva Vizcaya. On the other hand, Sapad claimed that she met Subject Bueno thru her cousin who was working in Dubai and Subject told her that she had sent a lot of people to Dubai for employment as she owns a travel agency named KABSAT Travel and Tours. Subject added that she will take care all her documents and they will first travel to Singapore as tourists while preparing for her visa and ticket for Dubai. Believing with the representations of Subject Bueno, Sapad deposited Php 63,200.00 in the BDO account of the Subject. Meanwhile, Agassid claimed that Subject Bueno offered her work in Dubai as a cleaner and was told that they will travel first to Singapore as tourists while preparing for her visa for Dubai. Verification with the Department of Migrant Workers revealed thru a certification that Subject Bueno is not licensed/authorized to recruit workers overseas employment. Thus, NBI-IAID placed Subject Bueno under arrest for Illegal Recruitment. Subject Bueno was presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor, Pasay City for violation of R.A. 8042 (Migrant Workers and Overseas Filipinos Act of 1995) as amended by R.A. 10022. Director Distor issued a stern warning against those who are into illegal recruitment that the NBI will be relentless in bringing them behind bars.

body: PRESS STATEMENT October 10, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } In line with the National Bureau of Investigation’s commitment to uphold justice and to protect the children from any form of violence, the NBI-Southeastern Mindanao Regional Office (NBI-SEMRO) arrested an individual for Qualified Rape, in violation of Republic Act No. 8353 (The Anti-Rape Law) as amended by R.A. No. 11648. The operation stemmed from a Warrant of Arrest issued by the Regional Trial Court, Branch 33, Davao City against the Subject for the aforementioned violation. According to the guardian of the minor victim, the Subject sexually assaulted his own minor daughter. The case was investigated by the Office of the City Prosecutor, Davao City, and this investigation was followed by the issuance of the Warrant of Arrest against the Subject. On October 7, 2025, agents of NBI-SEMRO, armed with the Warrant of Arrest, proceeded at Ecoland, Davao City where the Subject was selling banana-cue along the street. As a result, the Subject was arrested and brought to the NBI-SEMRO office for the standard booking procedure. NBI Director JUDGE JAIME B. SANTIAGO (Ret.) commended the agents of NBI-SEMRO for the arrest of the Subject and emphasized the importance of the mandate of the NBI in protecting children and supporting victims of sexual violence. Director added that the NBI will exhaust every lawful avenue to hold perpetrators of such heinous acts to account – because where a child is harmed, the full force of justice will follow.

The suspects were identified by NBI Director Nonnatus Caesar R. Rojas as BYRON E. FULE, manager of Grandeur Health Club, and a resident of No. 53 Torres Bugallon, Sangandaan, Caloocan City; GENEVA VEQUISO ROLLON, cashier, a resident of No. 8 Scout Ybardoloza St., Quezon City; JOSELYN FRANCO MEDINA, cashier, a resident of No. 36 Scout Torillo, Bgy. Sacred heart, Quezon City; and ANTONIO SAMSON NUEVO, a resident of 11 Madelaine St., Quezon City; and RICHARD VILLEGAO ORPANO, a resident of 190 Rd. 1, Pag-asa, Quezon City, are both roomboys. Bonoan revealed that on April 25, 2013, the NBI received a report that Grandeur Health Club, a massage parlor located in Timog Avenue, Quezon City employs minors in its human trafficking business. A composite team of NBI operatives and Department of Social Worker and Development (DSWD) personnel planned to rescue the victims. In the evening of May 3, 2013, NBI agents proceeded to the health club posing as customers while the rest were positioned in strategic places. body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today announced the arrest of an individual on March 12, 2021 by operatives of NBI-Special Action Unit (NBI-SAU) for illegal practice of medicine. NBI Officer-in-Charge (OIC) Director Eric B. Distor identified the Subject as GERLON SADSAD. OIC Director Distor said that Brigada GMA News and Public Affairs referred to NBI the complainant who averred that Subject performed on her a botched injection treatment which resulted in inflammation and discoloration on the injected area. Subject made a subsequent treatment to the complainant, supposedly to remove the inflammation and discoloration. However, no improvement was seen in complainant’s condition. Upon verification with the Professional Regulation Commission, it was found that Subject does not possess any license/authority to practice medicine. Hence, after the Subject set a follow up treatment on the inflammation and discoloration, an entrapment operation was hatched at Tivoli Garden Residences, Mandaluyong City resulting in the arrest of the Subject. Found in Subject’s possession were used and unused syringes, needles, topical anesthesia. 0.9% sodium chloride, wooden spatula, alcohol swabs, kitchen wrap, gauze pad, and underpants. Subject SADSAD was presented for inquest proceedings before the City Prosecutor of Mandaluyong for violation for RA 2382 otherwise known as The Medical Act of 1959) and Estafa under Article 315 of the Revised Penal Code.

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today announced the arrests of four (4) Nigerian nationals responsible for hacking several ATM and credit cards, then stole the funds therein. NBI Officer-in-Charge (OIC) Director Eric B. Distor identified the subjects as NKECHUKWU SUNDAY PROMISE EKEKWE, EMMANUEL OBI NWADKURE, DIVINE CHINECHEREM OBIOMA, and DOMIKE IZUCHUKOM OBIOMA. OIC Director Distor said that the operation stemmed from an investigation regarding a hacking incident involving the computer systems of a well-known general banking corporation. During the investigation, NBI-Cyber Crime Division (NBI-CCD) opetatives learned of the existence of one NKECHUKWU SUNDAY PROMISE EKEKWE, who is involved in the hacking of several ATM and credit cards. The operatives conducted undercover and surveillance operations and were convinced that probable cause exists to justify a search of his premises. On September 8, 2020, armed with Search Warrants, NBI-CCD proceeded to the two condominium units in Sucat Muntinlupa City. The operatives found and seized in the premises nine (9) smartphones, five (5) laptops, one (1) unit “ONE TIME PIN” (OTP), various debit cards, blank cards with POS device, one (1) wi-fi router, IDs, and documents, and others. The operatives also arrested Subject Ekekwe and his three companions. During the apprehension, Subject Ekekwe and Subject Nwadkure resisted arrest but were subdued by the operatives. Subjects were presented before the Office of the City Prosecutor of Muntinlupa for inquest proceedings for violation of Sec. 9(r) of R.A. 8484, otherwise known as the “Access Devices Regulation Act of 1998”, amended by R.A. 11449. In addition, Subject Ekekwe and Subject Nwadkure were also charged for Direct Assault punishable under Article 148 of the Revised Penal Code for resisting arrest.

body: PRESS STATEMENT September 23, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } In an effort to combat squatting syndicates and curb their activities, the National Bureau of Investigation – Organized and Transnational Crime Division (NBI-OTCD) arrested CRISTITA ASUNCION y BELARDO, NERIE ASUNCION y SARMIENTO, DOLORES CHAN y CABAEL, and LUZVIMINDA GOCHANGCO y CABAEL for Estafa through Falsification of Public Document; Falsification by Private Individual and Use of Falsified Documents as defined and penalized under Article 171 in relation to Article 172 of the Revised Penal Code; and violation of Section 27 of Republic Act No. 7279, otherwise known as “An Act to Provide for a Comprehensive and Continuing Urban Development and Housing Program, Establish the Mechanism for its Implementation, and for Other Purposes.” The case originated from a referral by the Department of Human Settlements and Urban Development – National Drive Against Professional Squatters and Squatting Syndicates (DHSUD-NDAPSSS), which concerned individuals involved in squatting syndicates and the illegal sale of properties. These individuals were using falsified land titles to defraud unsuspecting buyers and undermine the land registration system. On September 12, 2025, NBI-OTCD agents, DHSUD-NDAPSSS officers, and Chief of Inspection and Investigation Division of the Land Registration Authority (LRA), along with the private complainant, conducted an entrapment operation. They met with the Subjects at Farmers Plaza, Cubao, Quezon City. After the Subjects executed the Deed of Conditional Sale and received the payment, NBI-OTCD agents immediately arrested them and were informed of their constitutional rights. Subjects were then brought to the NBI-OTCD office for standard booking and documentation. They were presented for Inquest Proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor for Quezon City for the above-stated violations, and turned over to the NBI Detention Facility in New Bilibid Prison, Muntinlupa City, for custody and detention.

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today said a number of motor vehicles involved in the “Rent – Tangay/Rent – Sangla” Scheme would be released today to the legitimate and rightful car owners. The NBI said Department of Justice (DOJ) Secretary Vitaliano N. Aguirre II will personally turn-over the vehicles of different types to rightful car owners after the latter have complied with all the documentary requirements for claims set by the DOJ. The vehicles to be turned-over to the rightful car owners include Mitsubishi Montero Sport, Mitsubishi Mirage, Hyundai Tucson, Toyota Vios and Toyota Hi-Lux. These were earlier surrendered to the NBI – Cavite District Office (NBI-CAVIDO) in Tagaytay City after the Rent – Tangay/Rent – Sangla scheme news broke out in the open. On the basis of a directive by DOJ Secretary Aguirre, the NBI, specifically the NBI – National Capital Region (NBI-NCR) and Cavite District Office (NBI – CAVIDO) conducted investigations and case build-up against known personalities behind the Rent – Tangay (Rent – Sangla) Scheme, who have victimized more or less three (300) car owners. More than 250 motor vehicles have been recovered/surrendered to NBI – CAVIDO of which 138 vehicles have been released to rightful car owners (including the vehicles that would be released today). In addition, six (6) vehicles: 3 Toyota Hi-Ace; 2 Mitsubishi Montero sport; and a Toyota Fortuner were surrendered to the NBI – Olongapo District Office (NBI – OLDO) on March 2, 2017. Another vehicle was likewise surrendered to the NBI – Laguna District Office (NBI –LAGDO). Rent – Tangay (Rent – Sangla) Scheme is a modus where Subjects lured car owners to enter into a RENT – A – CAR agreement with a promise of large sums of cash ranging from P25,000.00 to P50,000.00 depending on the type of vehicle, only to discover later that the fees they were paid with, came from the mortgage of their vehicles. As of this date, more than 100 motor vehicles are still under the custody of the NBI awaiting claims by rightful and legitimate owners.

body: Two men introducing themselves as NBI agents and selling fake NBI identification cards were nabbed by agents of the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) in an entrapment in Zamboanga City last week. NBI Director Magtanggol B. Gatdula identified the suspects as: EDUARDO ROQUE BAUTISTA, a resident of No. 480, Tarcan, Baliuag, Bulacan; and JIMMY MASANGCAY ZABALA, of Putik Hi-way, Zamboanga City. Investigation by the Western Mindanao Regional Office (WEMRO) headed by Atty. Manuel A. Almendares disclosed that Federico Villar and Samuel S. Julio, both employees of the Zamboanga City Electric Cooperative (ZAMCELCO), a local provider of electricity in the said province, went to the NBI office in Zamboanga City to seek NBI investigative assistance regarding the two suspects, Zabala and Bautista. It was learned that Zabala and Bautista introduced themselves as NBI agents. Believing they were NBI agents, complainants detailed the suspects with their office to conduct investigation regarding pilferage and other internal concerns of the office. They were even provided furnished quarters during their stay with the company. When the suspects started selling fake identification cards, badges, permits to carry firearms and mission orders for P6,500.00 to unsuspecting employees of ZAMCELCO, complainants began to doubt the real identification of the two. On August 2, 2011, upon receipt of the complaint, NBI agents went to ZAMCELCO, Putik, Zamboanga City to validate the veracity of the report. Upon arrival, they saw Zabala in the act of performing the duties of an agent. They immediately arrested him while Zabala was nabbed at the Lavina Hotel, Gov. Alvarez Ave., Zamboanga City. Charges for violation of Art. 177 of the Revised Penal Code (Usurpation of authority, rank, title and improper use of names, uniforms and insignia) and Art. 315 in relation to Art. 172 of the Revised Penal Code, as amended (Estafa thru Falsification) were filed against the suspects before the Zamboanga City Prosecutor’s Office.

title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: A group of Koreans illegally operating an on-line casino were arrested by agents of the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) in Muntinlupa City on Monday The suspects were identified by NBI Director Nonnatus Caesar R. Rojas as: NARYUN KIM, YUNHEE HWANG, SEYOUNG CHUNG, WONSEOK YANG, and HOI CHERL YANG, Korean nationals, all of legal age, and residing at Ayala Alabang, Muntinlupa City According to investigative report of the NBI-National Capital Region (NCR) headed by Regional Director Elfren L. Meneses Jr. the NBI received a letter request from the Taiwan Economic and Cultural Office (TECO) concerning the continuous operation of international telephone fraud here in the Philippines, and sought investigation on the matter. On June 21, 2013, the NCR received a reliable information concerning several Taiwanese and Korean nationals engaged in fraudulent telephone operations in a place in Ayala, Alabang. The NCR immediately conducted investigation. A computer technician, who installed the expanded internet/telephone connections via VOIP at the said place was located and gave information. Accordingly, he was contacted by a Taiwanese national, Bao Shiao-Yu, the alleged syndicate leader. He personally saw the fully functional computer workstations manned by Chinese and Korean nationals as call center agents. He was also able to eavesdrop on the fraudulent calls inside a house. NBI operatives also noticed a series of intertwined telephone cables attached to the house. Subsequently, search warrants were applied for and issued by the Manila RTC, Br. 24. On July 8, 2013, by virtue of search warrants, NBI agents proceeded to the pinpointed place. Thereupon, they saw Kim, Naryun and Chung-Seyoung operating an on-line casino without the necessary permit. Suspects, Hwang-Yunhee, Yang-Wonseok and Yang-Hoi Cherl who were also present working as call center agents. They failed to produce their respective documents establishing their proper identities. Thereafter, the five suspects were brought to the NBI for booking and detention. Yesterday, charges for violation of PD 1602 as amended by RA 9287 (An Act Increasing the Penalties for Illegal Numbers Game, Amending Certain Provision of PD 1602 and for Other Purposes), and violation of RA 8484 “The Access Device Regulations Act of 1998” were recommended filed against the suspects before the Muntinlupa City Prosecutor’s Office.

body: The continuing effort of the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) against illegal drugs trade has led to the arrest of an individual last Sunday, May 3, 2020 in Intramuros, Manila. NBI Officer-In-Charge (OIC) Eric B. Distor said the drug pusher was identified as RAHIM ANDIL who was arrested in a buy-bust operation conducted by Agents of the NBI – Task Force Against Illegal Drugs (NBI-TFAID). OIC Distor also said that during the buy-bust operation, subject RAHIM ANDIL was found in possession of four (4) packs of suspected shabu and 1 heat sealed transparent plastic sachet also containing suspected shabu and several identification cards. Distor narrated that in the last week of April 2020 prior to the operation, a confidential informant reported to the NBI-TFAID regarding a certain RAHIM from Tondo, Manila, who offered to sell him high grade shabu. Based on the information, subject RAHIM is engaged in selling illegal drugs with the help of some Chinese nationals incarcerated in Manila City Jail. Distor added that on May 3, 2020, NBI-TFAID received information that subject RAHIM has with him about 200 grams of shabu amounting to P200,000.00, that he needs to sell within the week. Under strict orders, the TFAID devised a plan to conduct a buy-bust operation. On the same day, after coordinating with the PNP-MPD and PDEA, operatives of NBI-TFAID conducted a buy-bust operation in Anda Circle Intramuros, Manila that resulted in the arrest of subject RAHIM ANDIL. He was immediately brought to the NBI headquarters in Manila for booking procedures while the seized items were turned-over to the NBI-Forensic Chemistry Division for laboratory examination and safe keeping. OIC Distor added that subject RAHIM ANDIL was presented for inquest proceedings yesterday before the Office of the City Prosecutor of Manila for violation of R.A. 9165 otherwise known as the Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002.

body: PRESS STATEMENT June 03, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } PRESS RELEASE | NBI NABS TWO INDIVIDUALS IN CELEBRITY- LINKED MULTI-MILLION PESO BEAUTY CLINIC INVESTMENT SCAM IN QUEZON CITY The operatives from National Bureau of Investigation – International Operations Division (NBI-IOD) successfully apprehended two (2) individuals. The arrest was carried out at a beauty and wellness clinic located within a shopping mall in Fairview, Quezon City, following an extensive period of hiding that began when warrants were first issued in early 2025. The operation was initiated to serve multiple outstanding Warrants of Arrest issued by the Regional Trial Court, Branch 2 of Batangas City. The enforcement action aimed to penalize a multi-million-peso investment scheme orchestrated through a beauty and wellness enterprise that defrauded numerous investors by inducing them into fraudulent franchise partnerships and investment arrangements with false promises of substantial returns. This high-profile scam had gained significant public traction due to its links to celebrity co-accused individuals. To bring the Subjects to justice after they spent over a year evading the law, NBI-IOD utilized intelligence gathering, verification, and strategic physical surveillance to pinpoint their employment location, leading to their successful arrest and immediate processing. The individuals were discovered secretly employed at the clinic, serving as a Logistics and Procurement Officer and a Branch Manager, respectively. The two apprehended individuals face a litany of charges including multiple counts of Syndicated Estafa, Swindling, and violations of both the Securities Regulation Code and the Financial Products and Services Consumer Protection Act in relation to the Cybercrime Protection Act. Following their arrest, they were placed under temporary detention at the NBI Detention Facility at Building 14, New Bilibid Prison in Muntinlupa City. They currently await a formal commitment order from the court for their eventual transfer to the custody of the Bureau of Jail Management and Penology (BJMP) in Batangas City, where their criminal cases are pending.
