body: On May 2, 2019, operatives of NBI- Cybercrime Division (NBI-CCD) arrested ORISAKWE IFEANYI EMMANUEL, IKENNA DICKSON OKALLA, CHUKWUMA GEORGE ADIBLE, CHIBOY STANLEY AGBASY, DIM REMEDIOS, ABAS KASHMIR, and UBA LIVING for Catfishing/Love Scam. Subjects were arrested in an operation based on a Search Warrant issued by RTC Branch 21, Imus, Cavite against the occupants of Unit 315 Isabel Building, Urban Deca Homes Hampton, Brgy. Buhay na Tubig, Imus, Cavite. During the operation, the above-mentioned occupants tried to escape but were consequently apprehended. Subject ORISAKWE went wild and was able to break loose from being tied. He took a pistol into his hand and tried to shoot the responding operatives but he was eventually immobilized. However, when his pistol fell into the ground, he turned around and grab a hand grenade from a plastic drawer. Operatives fired at him causing the hand grenade to fall from his hand even before he was able to pull its pin off. When Subject ORISAKWE was already immobilized, operatives called up for an ambulance to bring ORISAKWE to the nearest hospital. Unfortunately, he was declared lifeless upon arrival of the responding CDRRMO personnel. On-site search resulted in the seizure of six (6) laptop units, eleven (11) mobile phones, one (1) skimming device, two (2) pieces one time password, one (1) hand grenade, one (1) 9mm pistol, eight (8) bundles of fake dollars, and various blank cards, security strips, sim cards, and credit cards. Results of the “Os Triage” confirmed the Catfishing/Love Scam operations being conducted live on the Subjects’ premises and details of which are reflected in the onsite forensic report by the NBI-Digital Forensic Lab (NBI-DFL). Charges for violations of PD 1866 as amended by RA 9516 (Law on Explosives), RA 10591 (Comprehensive Law on Firearms and Ammunition), and RA 8484 (Access Devices Regulation Act of 1998) in relation to RA 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012) will be filed against the arrested Subjects. On May 2, 2019, operatives of NBI-Bicol Regional Office (NBI-BRO) arrested ANTHONY B. CASTRO for violation of RA 9165 (Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002). Subject was arrested in an operation which stemmed from an information that Subject was dealing, selling, and disposing illegal drugs and was using his residence as his base of operation and stash house. After having verified the veracity of the information, a Search Warrant was applied for. On the aforementioned date, the Search Warrant was implemented. Seized were ten (10) heat-sealed transparent plastic containing 12.5054 grams of methamphetamine hydrochloride (shabu). Subject was presented for inquest proceedings for violation of RA 9165 (Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002). On May 2, 2019, operatives of NBI-Legazpi District Office (NBI-LEGDO) arrested ROSEMARIE DAYAP y MIRABEL for violation of RA 9165 (Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002). Subject was arrested by virtue of Search Warrant. The implementation of Search Warrant resulted in the seizure of sixteen (16) sachets of suspected shabu weighing more or less 20 grams. Subject ROSEMARIE DAYAP y MIRABEL was detained at NBI-Bicol Regional Office (NBI-BRO). On May 2, 2019, operatives of NBI-Laoag District Office (NBI-LADO) arrested ELMER GAGALA a.k.a. Balatong for human trafficking. Subject was arrested in an operation which stemmed from an information received regarding the alleged sex den fronting as beerhouse located in a secluded place in Brgy. Binsang, Pasuquin, Ilocos, Norte. Surveillance operations conducted confirmed that the girls working in the said beerhouse, including minors, were being offered for sex in exchange for money. During the operation, Subject ELMER GAGALA, the maintainer/owner of the beerhouse, tried to escape but was eventually subdued and placed under arrest. Four (4) victims, two (2) of whom are minors, were rescued. Subject was presented for inquest proceeding before the Provincia; Prosecutor’s Office, Laoag City for violation of RA 9208 (Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2003) as amended by RA 10364 (Expanded Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2012). On May 4, 2019, operatives of NBI-North Eastern Mindanao Regional Office (NBI-NEMRO) arrested ELMER D. GULTIANO, RAYKEN NICARIO, and BERBONS N. DADANG for Theft of Minerals. Subjects were arrested in an operation which stemmed from the letter request of Venray Construction Corporation to investigate their employees for theft of minerals of limestones. Investigation conducted revealed that employees of the said corporation were indeed engaged in accepting orders from any would-be buyers of complainant’s limestones without the latter’s knowledge and consent. Worst, the said employees use the complainant’s resources in conducting their illicit activities. With this, in coordination with the City Local Environment and Natural Resources Office (CLENRO) officials of Cagayan de Oro City, NBI-NEMRO operatives conducted the operation resulting in the arrest of the above-mentioned Subjects and the seizure of several quantities of limestones. Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings for Theft of Minerals in violation of RA 7942 (Philippine Mining Act). On May 8, 2019, operatives of NBI-National Capital Region (NBI-NCR) seized counterfeit Nike and Converse products with an estimated value of Php 47 Million. Items were seized in Pasay City by virtue of Search Warrants. Charges for violation of RA 8293 (Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines) were filed against the concerned individuals. On May 8, 2019, operatives of NBI-Central Visayas Regional Office (NBI-CEVRO) arrested MICHELLE TABANAO AGUILA for Estafa. Subject was arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from the complaint of Blesilda Gochoco who was enticed by the Subject to put up investment capital in the amount of Php 101,500.00 with the promise of earning Php 10,000.00 per week. Subject is a notorious swindler that had victimized a number of unknowing investors in Cebu City as well as in the nearby province of Negros Occidental thru her modus operandi of luring prospective investors to invest in her bogus business of crude oil supply. Several cases of Estafa had been filed against the Subject before the City Prosecutor’s Office of Cebu City. On May 12, 2019, operatives of NBI-Dagupan District Office (NBI-DADO) arrested BERNADIT U. BELTRAN, MANILYN SISON, DENVER BEJAR y CALUGAY, JOHN PAUL V. CRUZ, CONRADO HERMOSADO JR., CONRADO HERMOSADO SR., and ERNESTO DE GUZMAN for violation of the Omnibus Election Code. Subjects were arrested in an operation which stemmed from the complaint of Raul Sison y Palisoc regarding a vote buying incident at Brgy. Buer, Aguilar, Pangasinan. Acting on the complaint, NBI-DADO operatives immediately investigated the incident. Upon arrival at the area, operatives assessed the situation and interviewed the complainant as he formally turned over to the team the seized items and articles as well as the seven (7) above-mentioned Subjects whom he accosted by virtue of citizen’s arrest while they were committing acts that violate the provisions of the Omnibus Election Code. The case was filed the next day at the Provincial Prosecutor’s Office for preliminary investigation. On May 16, 2019, operatives of NBI-Bulacan District Office (NBI-BULDO) arrested eight (8) Chinese nationals namely: LUK CHUN GO, YING KUN CHU, TAN KIAO LOK, KENG TANG TIUQ, BIN CHUNG LAO, TUA YIN KIM, SHI LING SIM, and TIOK BU BHAN for Human Trafficking and Serious Illegal Detention. Subjects were arrested in an operation which stemmed from an information that a group of Chinese nationals are illegally operating business in the province of Bulacan. It was revealed that a certain Luzviminda Patrialba recruited group of persons most of whom came from Visayas and Mindanao regions. The recruited persons, some are minors, were allegedly transported to in a factory in Marilao, Bulacan and were working in a very inhumane condition and under restricted movement. Finding sufficient grounds to believe that the crime of human trafficking and serious illegal detention were being committed, a rescue operation was conducted. Upon arrival thereat, the warehouse was locked from the outside and nobody seemed to be inside. However, operatives heard shout of cry coming inside of the warehouse asking for help because they could hardly breath which prompted to force open the same. Upon entering, operatives were shocked when they witnessed the unhealthy working condition of the workers aside from being housed in very small rooms. The workers were randomly interviewed and they wanted to be rescued because they were under restricted movement. The arrested Chinese nationals were recommended for inquest prosecution before the Provincial Prosecutor’s Office, Malolos City for violation of RA 10364 (Human Trafficking) and Serious Illegal Detention. On May 22, 2019, operatives of NBI-Bicol Regional Office seized counterfeit cigarette products with an estimated amount of Php 178,500.00 in Brgy. Tagbong, Pili, Camarines Sur. Items were seized by virtue of Search Warrants that were implemented in the house of Subject RONNIE STA ANA. The operation was conducted based on the information received regarding the rampant proliferation of smuggled cigarettes in the various coastal On May 16, 2019, operatives of NBI-National Capital Region (NBI-NCR) arrested ARMANDO T. PADILLA for Esatafa. Subject was arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from the complaint of Mr. Oscar N. Hulinganga, former classmate of the Subject in a military training. According to the complainant, he met the Subject in one of their batch meetings in the military service sometime in May 2017. In the said meeting, Subject told the complainant that he is already a lawyer and an expert in handling civil cases. Upon learning that complainant is in need of a lawyer who will handle his civil cases for quieting of title, Subject offered his legal service to him. Believing that he is a legitimate lawyer, complainant accepted the offer for a fee. In total, Subject was able to collect an aggregate amount of more or less Php 270,000.00. Certification issued by the Office of the Bar Confidant stated that Subject PADILLA is not a member of the Philippine Bar. When Subject and complainant were scheduled to meet for the draft of the judicial-affidavit, the entrapment operation was hatched which resulted in the arrest of the Subject. Subject PADILLA was presented before the inquest prosecutor of Manila for consummated Swindling/Estafa.On May 17, 2019, operatives of National Bureau of Investigation-Special Task Force (NBI-STF) arrested JOVENAR PUNO for Robbery Extortion and Estafa. Subject was arrested in entrapment operation which stemmed from a complaint against Subjects JOHN CARLO CAYANGYANG and JOVENAR PUNO. Subjects mutually conspired in defrauding and extorting money from the complainant. Complainant, an online seller of cellphones and other merchandise, averred that Subject JOHN CARLO purchased seven (7) cellphone units from her amounting to Php 394,400.00. but complainant felt suspicious about the said Subject so he checked with PayPal the Subject’s credibility. However, PayPal told the complainant that it was too early to tell if Subject was a scammer. On May 6, 2019, Subject JOHN CARLO reported the complainant to PayPal that he already paid for the 7 cellphone units but complainant did not ship them. As a result, PayPal restricted complainant’s account and she was compelled to ship the cellphones through LBC. After receiving the cellphone units, Subjects JOHN CARLO made it appear that he received fake cellphone units and demanded Php 90,000.00 as settlement for the alleged fake units. Moreover, Subject JOVENAR texted the complainant that he will go to the barangay to file a complaint against the complainant. He told the complainant to meet him at Barangay 743, Malate, Manila for the Php 90,000.00. The complainant then sought the help of the NBI and filed a complaint against Subjects JOHN CARLO AND JOVENAR. Acting on the complaint, NBI-STF operatives conducted the entrapment operation resulting in the arrest of Subject JOVENAR. Subject JOVENAR PUNO was presented for inquest proceeding before the Office of the Prosecutor, Manila for Robbery Extortion and Estafa. Same charges were recommended to be filed against Subject JOHN CARLO CAYANGYANG who remains at large.On May 21, 2019, operatives of NBI-Environmental Crime Division (NBI-EnCD) arrested five (5) individuals at San Narciso, Zambales for violation of Forestry Code, Comprehensive Firearms and Ammunition Regulations Act, and Omnibus Election Code. Arrested Subjects are five (5) of the leaders of a land grabbing syndicate who occupied and started selling parts of 6.6 hectares of public forest land located at Brgy. La Paz, San Narciso, Zambales. Several unlicensed firearms were also recovered during the operation. Charges were filed against the Subjects before the Department of Justice (DOJ) inquest prosecutor.On May 22, 2019, operatives of NBI-Anti-Human Trafficking Division (NBI-AHTRAD) arrested EDRIL DELOS SANTOS DE VERA and JENNY LIBRADILLA CORAL in Makati City for human trafficking. Subjects were caught in-flagrante maintaining women for sexual exploitation for a fee, but undergone the guise of a legitimate business. Surveillance operation conducted at “Quija Spa” a.k.a “Native Palm Spa” revealed that there are indeed illegal activities on the said establishment. The spa offers a massage therapy for One Thousand Pesos (Php 1,000.00) and the “Extra Service” is around Three Thousand Pesos (Php 3,000.00). With this, an entrapment operation was conducted resulting in the arrest of the above-mentioned Subjects. The operation also resulted in the rescue of seventeen (17) victims – one (1) admitted to be a minor, while other three (3) had undergone dental ageing examination and the results are suggestive that they are also of minor age. Seized were boxes of condoms at the reception table. Subjects were presented before the Department of Justice, Manila City on inquest proceeding for violation of R.A. 9208, otherwise known as he Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2003, as amended by RA 10364 and violation of RA 7610 otherwise known as the “Special Protection Against Child Abuse, Exploitation, and Discrimination, and for Other Purposes”. On May 22, 2019, operatives of NBI-Special Action Unit (NBI-SAU) arrested ATTY. ROBERTO D. GEOTINA, a former Bureau of Customs employee, and his cohort NANCITA A. NUGUID for Estafa. Subjects were arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from the information coordinated by Director Jeoffrey C. On May 22, 2019, operatives of NBI-Bicol Regional Office seized counterfeit cigarette products with an estimated amount of Php 178,500.00 in Brgy. Tagbong, Pili, Camarines Sur. Items were seized by virtue of Search Warrants that were implemented in the house of Subject RONNIE STA ANA. The operation was conducted based on the information received regarding the rampant proliferation of smuggled cigarettes in the various coastal of Camarines Sur. Verification and confirmation from the neighbors of Subject revealed that he was peddling various items which includes not only Marlboro, Marvel, and Winston cigarettes but also other items with commercial value. On the above-mentioned date, the Search Warrants were implemented and resulted in the seizure of 51 reams of assorted cigarette brands with fake BIR strip stamps. Items were found in one the rooms of Subject RONNIE STA ANA’s house and in a single motorcycle loaded with a box. Verification from subject STA ANA revealed that the owner of the motorcycle is one RICKY AGOJO. Filing of cases against the two (2) Subjects shall follow upon completion of the necessary documentation. On May 23, operatives of NBI-Special Task Force (NBI-STF) arrested DONG DA SHUAI and YU QIAO, Chinese nationals, for Kidnapping and Serious Illegal Detention. The case stemmed from the complaint of Tian Weijing, also a Chinese national, against unidentified individuals for Serious Illegal Detention. The complainant narrated that the mother of her cousin YINGAO HUA told her that he was held by his employer for three (3) days in a room at their office in Alabang, Muntinlupa. Accordingly, victim HUA intended to resign from his work and go back to China but for some reasons, he was prevented from leaving, was locked up in a room and was beaten while being demanded that he needed to pay Php 218,000.00 in exchange for his release. Complainant tried to call YINGAO HUA but her calls were left unanswered. But after several attempts, YINGAO HUA were able to answer and informed the complainant about his situation. Complainant then sought the assistance of NBI. While complainant was filing her complaint, she was continuously receiving text message being sent from the phone of her cousin HUA demanding for the ransom money. With this, an entrapment operation was conducted resulting in the arrest of Subjects DONG DA SHUAI and YU QIAO and the rescue of two (2) victims Liu Shixin and Hua Yingao. Subjects were brought before the Office of the Prosecutor, Muntinlupa for inquest proceedings for Kidnapping and Serious Illegal Detention. On May 23, 2019, operatives of NBI-Dagupan District Office (NBI-DADO) arrested MARX LENEN S. DE DIOS for Corruption of Public Officials. Subject was arrested after he insisted in handling over Php 180,000.00 to Atty. Darwin Lising, NBI-DADO Executive Officer. Subject went to Atty. Lising’s office to ask for help regarding his case. Subject then showed the money to Atty. Lising and insisted to hand over the money in order to fix his case. Atty. Lising then called up the Chief of the command to inform of what was happening. He immediately went to the office and confronted the Subject. After which, Subject was arrested. He was presented for inquest proceedings before Dagupan City Prosecutors Office. Surveillance operation was conducted in coordination with the PNP Pangasinan and PDEA Pangasinan by the joint operatives of NBI-TFAID and NBI-LADO in the vicinity of Doña Trinidad Subdivision to interdict the subject vehicle. After two days of surveillance operation the subject vehicle was spotted and cornered by the operatives near Doña Trinidad Subdivision that led to the arrest of Subject Lu Jun and the seizure of 10 transparent ziplock bags allegedly containing shabu. On the evening of May 23, 2019, the operatives implemented eight (8) Search Warrants in four (4) target areas that resulted to the arrest of Subjects Lui Bin, Jack Lee, and Ye Ling. Subject Lui Bin was arrested in Doña Trinidad Subdivision and found illegal drugs inside the house. Subjects Jack Lee and Ye Ling were arrested in Calasiao and Mangaldan, Pangasinan respectively but yielded negative for illegal drugs. While on their way back to Manila the operatives spotted a vehicle supposedly owned by one of the target subjects and tailed it to Cubao Quezon City and arrested the driver identified as NORODIN GUIANI TASIL. The seized items were examined by the NBI-Forensic Chemistry Division (NBI-FCD) weighing 18.81 kilograms with an estimated total value of Php 124 Million. Subjects Lu Jun, Lui Bin, and Jack Lee will be presented for Inquest Proceedings before the Department of Justice in conspiracy for violation of RA 9165. In addition, Subject Lee will be charged for violation of Article 171 in relation to Article 172 of the RPC for using fake passport. Subject Ye Ling will be referred to the Bureau of Immigration for their appropriate action. Meanwhile, Subject Tasil was placed under investigation. On May 23, 2019, operatives of NBI-Dagupan District Office (NBI-DADO) filed charges for violation the Cybercrime Law (Sextortion) and Rape against JOHN KENNETH V. NASTOR. The case was filed based on the complaint of Carina F. De Vera who alleged that Subject was allegedly disseminating in social media their sex video scandal with her 15-year old daughter. She alleged that the Subject was asking sexual favor from her daughter to remove the video he sent online. When the entrapment operation was conducted, the subject did not show up. Nevertheless, aforementioned violations were directly filed against the Subject. In the last quarter of 2018, NBI-LADO received information regarding the presence of Chinese nationals in a rented apartment in Pagudpud, Ilocos, Norte. Acting on the information, LADO operatives monitored the activities of the said Chinese nationals but they lost track of them for about a month. In January 2019, a vehicle used by the group was seen and identified in Pagudpud, Ilocos Norte. Operatives tailed the said vehicle and it led to the identification of four (4) safehouses. The case was then referred to TFAID for more thorough and technical monitoring. After almost three (3) months of continuous surveillance alternately done by LADO and TFAID, one Subject, identified as SubjectLU JUN was intercepted. Searched inside his vehicle yielded 18.561 kilograms of shabu. Search Warrant was served on their safehouse in Urdaneta City resulted to the seizure of 250.9632 grams of shabu and several tools/equipment for dangerous drugs trafficking. Another cohort who tried to escape but was cornered was identified as Subject ZUO SHENG LI. During the service of Search Warrant at the safehouse in Calasiao, Pangasinan, LI YU was found and was charged with violation of RA 8239 in relation to Article 171 and 172 of the Revised Penal Code, for possession of fake passport. On May 24, 2019, operatives of NBI-Laguna District Office (NBI-LAGDO) arrested JUN MALOTO y ZOTOMAYOR alias Bunso, a fugitive who escaped from Laguna Provincial Jail on October 26, 2015. Banago, Nagcarlan, Laguna and that he was employed as company driver of a meat processing plant located in the said barangay using the name DOMINGO ALVAREZ SUPREMO to hide his identity. Banago, Nagcarlan, Laguna to arrest the Subject. They immediately swooped down the premises of the meat processing plant and found Subject MALOTO inside. Cruz, Laguna. Moreover, Subject MALOTO was also the suspect in the assassination attempt on Barangay Captain Luis Panisan of Brgy. Gatid, Sta. Cruz, Laguna. He was likewise charged for Qualified Theft in RTC, Sta. Cruz, Laguna. Subject was arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from the complaint of Junierose Morales y Manuzon who met the Subject through a mobile game chat and later led to a romantic relationship. Because the complainant trusted the Subject, she did sensitive acts in front of camera without knowing that Subject was recording such acts. When complainant broke up with the Subject, the latter won’t let her go and instead demanded that they would meet and be together. During their phone conversations, Subject implied that he has no money and that he needed it badly. Complainant objected to the demands of the Subject but the latter created dummy accounts and used it to send sensitive pictures and videos of complainant to people close to her. When complainant failed to meet the Subject’s demands, he sent the pictures and video to complainant’s close relatives and friends and threatened to spread complainant’s compromising pictures and videos unless she would comply with his demands. With this, an entrapment operation was conducted resulting in the arrest of the Subject. Subject was presented for inquest proceedings for the above-mentioned violations. On May 27, 2019, operatives of NBI-Bicol Regional Office (NBI-BRO) arrested ROSEMARIE DAYAP y MIRABEL for violation of RA 9165 (Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002). After having verified and validated the veracity of the information, a Search Warrant was applied for and granted. On the aforementioned date, the Search Warrant was implemented resulting in the arrest of the Subject and the seizure of sixteen (16) pieces heat sealed transparent plastic sachets which yielded positive result for the presence of methamphetamine hydrochloride (shabu) with a net weight of 14.5652 grams. Subject was brought for inquest proceedings before the City Prosecution Office, Legazpi City for the above-mentioned violation. On May 29, 2019, operatives of NBI-Cybercrime Division (NBI-CCD) arrested thirty-three (33) Chinese nationals for illegal online gambling. The Chinese nationals were arrested in an operation which stemmed from the information concerning a group of foreign nationals engaged in the illicit operation of online gambling and sports betting where members/players are required to register and submit their personal information and credit card data via membership gaming websites. The group was allegedly operating at Unit H, 19 th Floor, Burgundy Corporate Tower, Sen. Gil Puyat, Makati City. On the aforementioned date, the Search Warrants were implemented at the said unit and found thereat were the Chinese nationals engaged in their laptop computer systems. Computer application programs and online web pages connected with gambling operations were found live and running in the devices. Initial on-site search on the computers revealed that they were engaged in operating/administering/maintaining Illegal Online Casino/Gambling websites. Also seized were 113 cellphone units, 33 laptop units, 1 desktop computer, 4 wifi routers, various unused simcards, and various pertinent documents. Arrested Subjects were charged for violations of PD 1602 (Anti-Illegal Gambling Law) as amended, in relation to RA 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012) before the Office of the City Prosecutor, Makati City. Same charges were filed against LU ZHENDONG, the alleged manager of the operation, who is currently at large. On May 29, 2019, operatives of NBI-CARAGA seized three (3) units of 10 lbs. and two (2) units of 5 lbs. of Taurus Fire Extinguishers, three (3) pieces of Tri J&A Enterprises Inspection Tag, and one (1) booklet of Phiel Trading Sales Invoice. Items were seized by virtue of Search Warrants implemented at a store located at Flores St., Sikatuna, Butuan City. During the implementation of the Search Warrants, the store was tended by RODEL O. DUYAG. He claimed that the unnamed Subject offered the place for free provided that he will be the one to tend the store. Charges for violation of RA 8293 (Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines) and Estafa thru deceit were filed against the unnamed Subject before the City Prosecutor’s Office, Butuan City. On May 29, 2019, operatives of NBI-Dagupan District Office (NBI-DADO) arrested JANETTE ESTANISLAO, DANNY QUISORIA JR., and MARY ANN LARGUEZA for human trafficking. Subjects were arrested in entrapment operation conducted at Brgy. San Juan, San Carlos City, Pangasinan. The operation also resulted in the rescue of five (5) trafficked victims. Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings for violation of RA 9208 (Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2003). On May 31, 2019, operatives of NBI-Cybercrime Division (NBI-CCD) arrested JUNRONG JIA, XUEJIAN LI, and QUIJIN TIAN, Chinese nationals, for violation of Access Device Law. Subjects allegedly detained three (3) fellow Chinese nationals in a hotel in Paranaque City. The NBI received a report concerning a Chinese national allegedly detained against his will inside a hotel in Paranaque City. The illegal detention of the said Chinese national was brought about by certain Chinese syndicate, demanding for ransom from relatives and kin of the victim in Beijing, China. To verify the veracity of the information, NBI-CCD operatives proceeded to the hotel and coordinated with the building’s security department. They conducted inquiry therein to determine the individuals occupying the target room. They were able to identify the said Chinese national being held and five (5) other Chinese nationals were also found inside the premises. When asked for the reason of his stay in the said room, the Chinese national disclosed that he and his two (2) other colleagues were detained for ten (10) days against their will. With this, operatives arrested the above-mentioned Chinese nationals. They were apprised of the nature and case of their arrest as well as their constitutional rights in the language they fully understand. Search conducted in the premises resulted in the seizure of one (1) POS Terminal, two (2) skimming devices, various blank cards, several security strips, smartphones, USB, various holographic security sticker, and several identification cards. Balatong for human trafficking. On May 22, 2019, operatives of NBI-Bicol Regional Office seized counterfeit cigarette products with an estimated amount of Php 178,500.00 in Brgy. Tagbong, Pili, Camarines Sur. Items were seized by virtue of Search Warrants that were implemented in the house of Subject RONNIE STA ANA. The operation was conducted based on the information received regarding the rampant proliferation of smuggled cigarettes in the various coastal of Camarines Sur. Verification and confirmation from the neighbors of Subject revealed that he was peddling various items which includes not only Marlboro, Marvel, and Winston cigarettes but also other items with commercial value. On the above-mentioned date, the Search Warrants were implemented and resulted in the seizure of 51 reams of assorted cigarette brands with fake BIR strip stamps. Items were found in one the rooms of Subject RONNIE STA ANA’s house and in a single motorcycle loaded with a box. Verification from subject STA ANA revealed that the owner of the motorcycle is one RICKY AGOJO. Filing of cases against the two (2) Subjects shall follow upon completion of the necessary documentation. On May 23, operatives of NBI-Special Task Force (NBI-STF) arrested DONG DA SHUAI and YU QIAO, Chinese nationals, for Kidnapping and Serious Illegal Detention. The case stemmed from the complaint of Tian Weijing, also a Chinese national, against unidentified individuals for Serious Illegal Detention. The complainant narrated that the mother of her cousin YINGAO HUA told her that he was held by his employer for three (3) days in a room at their office in Alabang, Muntinlupa. Accordingly, victim HUA intended to resign from his work and go back to China but for some reasons, he was prevented from leaving, was locked up in a room and was beaten while being demanded that he needed to pay Php 218,000.00 in exchange for his release. Complainant tried to call YINGAO HUA but her calls were left unanswered. But after several attempts, YINGAO HUA were able to answer and informed the complainant about his situation. Complainant then sought the assistance of NBI. While complainant was filing her complaint, she was continuously receiving text message being sent from the phone of her cousin HUA demanding for the ransom money. With this, an entrapment operation was conducted resulting in the arrest of Subjects DONG DA SHUAI and YU QIAO and the rescue of two (2) victims Liu Shixin and Hua Yingao. Subjects were brought before the Office of the Prosecutor, Muntinlupa for inquest proceedings for Kidnapping and Serious Illegal Detention. On May 23, 2019, operatives of NBI-Dagupan District Office (NBI-DADO) arrested MARX LENEN S. DE DIOS for Corruption of Public Officials. Subject was arrested after he insisted in handling over Php 180,000.00 to Atty. Darwin Lising, NBI-DADO Executive Officer. Subject went to Atty. Lising’s office to ask for help regarding his case. Subject then showed the money to Atty. Lising and insisted to hand over the money in order to fix his case. Atty. Lising then called up the Chief of the command to inform of what was happening. He immediately went to the office and confronted the Subject. After which, Subject was arrested. He was presented for inquest proceedings before Dagupan City Prosecutors Office. On May 23, 2019, operatives of NBI-Task Force Against Illegal Drugs (NBI-TFAID) and NBI-Laoag District Office (NBI-LADO) in collaboration with NBI-Dagupan District Office (NBI-DAGDO), PNP Pangasinan and PDEA Pangasinan arrested LU JUN (A.K.A. ‘JEFF’, ‘LU JUN HAO’, ‘WU CHIN’, ‘HU TAO JIN’), ZUO, SHENG LI (A.K.A. ‘JUN HAO LU’, ‘TAO JIN HU’, ‘CHING’), LI YU (A.K.A ‘JACK LEE’, ‘HENRY SANTOS LEE’), and YE LING, all Chinese nationals for violation of RA 9165 (Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002). Surveillance operation was conducted in coordination with the PNP Pangasinan and PDEA Pangasinan by the joint operatives of NBI-TFAID and NBI-LADO in the vicinity of Doña Trinidad Subdivision to interdict the subject vehicle. After two days of surveillance operation the subject vehicle was spotted and cornered by the operatives near Doña Trinidad Subdivision that led to the arrest of Subject Lu Jun and the seizure of 10 transparent ziplock bags allegedly containing shabu. On the evening of May 23, 2019, the operatives implemented eight (8) Search Warrants in four (4) target areas that resulted to the arrest of Subjects Lui Bin, Jack Lee, and Ye Ling. Subject Lui Bin was arrested in Doña Trinidad Subdivision and found illegal drugs inside the house. Subjects Jack Lee and Ye Ling were arrested in Calasiao and Mangaldan, Pangasinan respectively but yielded negative for illegal drugs. While on their way back to Manila the operatives spotted a vehicle supposedly owned by one of the target subjects and tailed it to Cubao Quezon City and arrested the driver identified as NORODIN GUIANI TASIL. The seized items were examined by the NBI-Forensic Chemistry Division (NBI-FCD) weighing 18.81 kilograms with an estimated total value of Php 124 Million. Subjects Lu Jun, Lui Bin, and Jack Lee will be presented for Inquest Proceedings before the Department of Justice in conspiracy for violation of RA 9165. In addition, Subject Lee will be charged for violation of Article 171 in relation to Article 172 of the RPC for using fake passport. Subject Ye Ling will be referred to the Bureau of Immigration for their appropriate action. Meanwhile, Subject Tasil was placed under investigation. On May 23, 2019, operatives of NBI-Dagupan District Office (NBI-DADO) filed charges for violation the Cybercrime Law (Sextortion) and Rape against JOHN KENNETH V. NASTOR. The case was filed based on the complaint of Carina F. De Vera who alleged that Subject was allegedly disseminating in social media their sex video scandal with her 15-year old daughter. She alleged that the Subject was asking sexual favor from her daughter to remove the video he sent online. When the entrapment operation was conducted, the subject did not show up. Nevertheless, aforementioned violations were directly filed against the Subject. On May 23, 2019, operatives of NBI-Laoag District Office (NBI-LADO), NBI-Task Force Against Against Illegal Drugs (NBI-TFAID), and NBI-Dagupan District Office (NBI-DADO) seized 18.8119 kgs of shabu worth Php 124 Million. In the last quarter of 2018, NBI-LADO received information regarding the presence of Chinese nationals in a rented apartment in Pagudpud, Ilocos, Norte. Acting on the information, LADO operatives monitored the activities of the said Chinese nationals but they lost track of them for about a month. In January 2019, a vehicle used by the group was seen and identified in Pagudpud, Ilocos Norte. Operatives tailed the said vehicle and it led to the identification of four (4) safehouses. The case was then referred to TFAID for more thorough and technical monitoring. After almost three (3) months of continuous surveillance alternately done by LADO and TFAID, one Subject, identified as SubjectLU JUN was intercepted. Searched inside his vehicle yielded 18.561 kilograms of shabu. Search Warrant was served on their safehouse in Urdaneta City resulted to the seizure of 250.9632 grams of shabu and several tools/equipment for dangerous drugs trafficking. Another cohort who tried to escape but was cornered was identified as Subject ZUO SHENG LI. During the service of Search Warrant at the safehouse in Calasiao, Pangasinan, LI YU was found and was charged with violation of RA 8239 in relation to Article 171 and 172 of the Revised Penal Code, for possession of fake passport. Subjects LU JUN, HU TAO JIN, ZUO SHENG LI, and LI YU were charged for violation of RA 9165 (Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002). On May 24, 2019, operatives of NBI-Laguna District Office (NBI-LAGDO) arrested JUN MALOTO y ZOTOMAYOR alias Bunso, a fugitive who escaped from Laguna Provincial Jail on October 26, 2015. Subject was charged for violations of Sections 5, 11, and 12 of RA 9165 (Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002) and BP 881 (Omnibus Election Code) and allegedly fled to Minalin, Pampanga to elude arrest after escaping from Laguna Provincial Jail. On May 23, 2019, information was received that Subject JUN MALOTO was sighted at Brgy. Banago, Nagcarlan, Laguna and that he was employed as company driver of a meat processing plant located in the said barangay using the name DOMINGO ALVAREZ SUPREMO to hide his identity. With this information, on May 24, 2019, operatives of NBI-LAGDO, together with the elements of 22 nd MIC, 2 nd MIB of Philippine Army, and Laguna Provincial Jail, proceeded to Brgy. Banago, Nagcarlan, Laguna to arrest the Subject. They immediately swooped down the premises of the meat processing plant and found Subject MALOTO inside. Cruz, Laguna. Moreover, Subject MALOTO was also the suspect in the assassination attempt on Barangay Captain Luis Panisan of Brgy. Gatid, Sta. Cruz, Laguna. He was likewise charged for Qualified Theft in RTC, Sta. Cruz, Laguna. Subject was arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from the complaint of Junierose Morales y Manuzon who met the Subject through a mobile game chat and later led to a romantic relationship. Because the complainant trusted the Subject, she did sensitive acts in front of camera without knowing that Subject was recording such acts. When complainant broke up with the Subject, the latter won’t let her go and instead demanded that they would meet and be together. During their phone conversations, Subject implied that he has no money and that he needed it badly. Complainant objected to the demands of the Subject but the latter created dummy accounts and used it to send sensitive pictures and videos of complainant to people close to her. When complainant failed to meet the Subject’s demands, he sent the pictures and video to complainant’s close relatives and friends and threatened to spread complainant’s compromising pictures and videos unless she would comply with his demands. With this, an entrapment operation was conducted resulting in the arrest of the Subject. Subject was presented for inquest proceedings for the above-mentioned violations. On May 27, 2019, operatives of NBI-Bicol Regional Office (NBI-BRO) arrested ROSEMARIE DAYAP y MIRABEL for violation of RA 9165 (Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002). Subject was arrested in an operation which stemmed from the an information that Subject was dealing, selling, and disposing illegal drugs and uses her residence located at Brgy. 26, Dinagaan, Legazpi City as her base of operation and stash house. After having verified and validated the veracity of the information, a Search Warrant was applied for and granted. On the aforementioned date, the Search Warrant was implemented resulting in the arrest of the Subject and the seizure of sixteen (16) pieces heat sealed transparent plastic sachets which yielded positive result for the presence of methamphetamine hydrochloride (shabu) with a net weight of 14.5652 grams. Subject was brought for inquest proceedings before the City Prosecution Office, Legazpi City for the above-mentioned violation. On May 29, 2019, operatives of NBI-Cybercrime Division (NBI-CCD) arrested thirty-three (33) Chinese nationals for illegal online gambling. The Chinese nationals were arrested in an operation which stemmed from the information concerning a group of foreign nationals engaged in the illicit operation of online gambling and sports betting where members/players are required to register and submit their personal information and credit card data via membership gaming websites. The group was allegedly operating at Unit H, 19 th Floor, Burgundy Corporate Tower, Sen. Gil Puyat, Makati City. Through verification and surveillance, CCD operatives were able to collect sufficient information warranting the application of Search Warrants. On the aforementioned date, the Search Warrants were implemented at the said unit and found thereat were the Chinese nationals engaged in their laptop computer systems. Computer application programs and online web pages connected with gambling operations were found live and running in the devices. Initial on-site search on the computers revealed that they were engaged in operating/administering/maintaining Illegal Online Casino/Gambling websites. Also seized were 113 cellphone units, 33 laptop units, 1 desktop computer, 4 wifi routers, various unused simcards, and various pertinent documents. Arrested Subjects were charged for violations of PD 1602 (Anti-Illegal Gambling Law) as amended, in relation to RA 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012) before the Office of the City Prosecutor, Makati City. Same charges were filed against LU ZHENDONG, the alleged manager of the operation, who is currently at large. On May 29, 2019, operatives of NBI-CARAGA seized three (3) units of 10 lbs. and two (2) units of 5 lbs. of Taurus Fire Extinguishers, three (3) pieces of Tri J&A Enterprises Inspection Tag, and one (1) booklet of Phiel Trading Sales Invoice. Items were seized by virtue of Search Warrants implemented at a store located at Flores St., Sikatuna, Butuan City. During the implementation of the Search Warrants, the store was tended by RODEL O. DUYAG. He claimed that the unnamed Subject offered the place for free provided that he will be the one to tend the store. Charges for violation of RA 8293 (Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines) and Estafa thru deceit were filed against the unnamed Subject before the City Prosecutor’s Office, Butuan City. Subjects were arrested in entrapment operation conducted at Brgy. San Juan, San Carlos City, Pangasinan. The operation also resulted in the rescue of five (5) trafficked victims. Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings for violation of RA 9208 (Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2003). On May 31, 2019, operatives of NBI-Cybercrime Division (NBI-CCD) arrested JUNRONG JIA, XUEJIAN LI, and QUIJIN TIAN, Chinese nationals, for violation of Access Device Law. Subjects allegedly detained three (3) fellow Chinese nationals in a hotel in Paranaque City. The NBI received a report concerning a Chinese national allegedly detained against his will inside a hotel in Paranaque City. The illegal detention of the said Chinese national was brought about by certain Chinese syndicate, demanding for ransom from relatives and kin of the victim in Beijing, China. To verify the veracity of the information, NBI-CCD operatives proceeded to the hotel and coordinated with the building’s security department. They conducted inquiry therein to determine the individuals occupying the target room. They were able to identify the said Chinese national being held and five (5) other Chinese nationals were also found inside the premises. When asked for the reason of his stay in the said room, the Chinese national disclosed that he and his two (2) other colleagues were detained for ten (10) days against their will. With this, operatives arrested the above-mentioned Chinese nationals. They were apprised of the nature and case of their arrest as well as their constitutional rights in the language they fully understand. body: PRESS STATEMENT October 22, 2024 The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Iligan District Ofiice (NBI-ILDO) under the leadership of NBI Director JUDGE JAIME B. SANTIAGO (Ret.) rescued a Kidnap Victim in Tamparan, Lanao del Sur. Director Santiago said that NBI-ILDO received information regarding the Kidnapping incident occurred in Barangay Maliwanag, Tamparan, Lanao del Sur on September 26, 2024. It was revealed that the Victim, a 25 year old Arabic Teacher and a resident of the said Barangay was abducted by three (3) unidentified male individuals while he was walking home from the Mosque and was forcibly taken inside a red Toyota vehicle. The operatives of NBI-ILDO immediately proceeded to the area and coordinated with Tamparan Municipal Police Station, the Military, and the Anti-Kidnapping Group (AKG) of the PNP for assistance. Through the combined efforts of the NBI, PNP, Military, and local elders, the abductors were compelled to release the Victim. NBI-ILDO will file appropriate charges against the perpetrators. Director Santiago lauded the operatives of NBI-ILDO for the rescue of the Kidnap Victim.

body: PRESS STATEMENT June 24, 2024 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } The National Bureau of Investigation, on June 20, 2024, arrested an individual in Pasig City for possession of illegal drugs, falsification of documents, and computer-related fraud. Gardenia Bakeries Philippines filed a complaint before the NBI for Economic Sabotage, Illegal Access and Computer-Related Fraud against certain individuals, as allegedly, scrupulous individuals were able to access without authority their Shell Fleet Hub Account and created new users which resulted in illegal acquisition of diesel and gasoline products on different Shell Gasoline Stations amounting to Php 14,475,556.26. Review of the submitted IP logs indicated the confirmation of compromise as the report contained accesses that were made to the account other than their official IP. This illegal access led to malicious creation of several Shell Fleet Hub accounts under unauthorized names. Collected pieces of evidence, and statement from witnesses identified that the target personalities are MR. GURDEEP alias Gary and other occupants of #22 Ausmolo Cmpd., Ilaya St., Buting, Pasig City. On June 20, 2024, by virtue of Warrant to Search, Seize, and Examine Computer Data (WSSECD), operatives of NBI-Counter Intelligence Division (NBI-CID) and NBI-Cybercrime Division (NBI-CCD) proceeded to the target area. Thereat, operatives discovered several electronic devices. Three IDs that appeared spurious and apparently used in transactions, were also retrieved. Operatives likewise discovered drug paraphernalia inside Subject GURDEEPO PARMAR’s bedroom. Upon examination by the NBI-Forensic Chemistry Division (NBI-FCD), the improvised tooters found yielded positive result for the presence of methamphetamine. Subject PARMAR, GURDEEPO SINGH y EVORA was presented for inquest proceedings before the Pasig City Prosecutor’s Office for violation of Section 12 and 15 of RA 9165 (Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act) and Article 172 (Falsification by Private Individual and Use of Falsified Documents) of the Revised Penal Code. Results of examination shall be reflected in the final forensic report and shall be used as the primary evidence for the Direct Filing of Computer-Related Fraud Cases against the Subjects.

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today announced the arrest of an individual by operatives of NBI- Bulacan District Office (NBI-BULDO) in an operation in Sta. Maria, Bulacan for illegal possession of firearms and ammunitions. NBI Officer-In-Charge (OIC) Director Eric B. Distor identified the arrested subject as SAMSON GREFAL y ALBERTO following the issuance of a Search Warrant by the Regional Trial Court Branch 76 of Bulacan against Subject Grefal for unlawful possession of various firearms and ammunition. On 22 of June 2021, Agents of NBI-BULDO together with Barangay Kagawad Edgar Santos of Brgy. Camanyanan served the Search Warrant to Subject Grefal in his residence. As a result, NBI-BULDO found in the premises of the subject the following firearms and ammunitions: one ( 1 ) caliber .38 revolver; two ( 2 ) caliber .38 live ammos; four ( 4 ) caliber .40 live ammos; three ( 3 ) caliber .308 live ammos; one ( 1 ) caliber .50 live ammos; eight ( 8 ) caliber magnum .22 live ammos; one (1) Caliber Magnun .22 Frevolver; and one (1) sling bag. When asked for the license of the said firearms subject Grefal failed to show any. Thus, he was apprehended and the firearms and ammunitions were seized. Subject Grefal was charged before the Bulacan Provincial Prosecutor Office for violation of R.A. 10591, otherwise known as the “Comprehensive Firearms and Ammunition Regulations Act”.

body: PRESS STATEMENT June 02, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) and the PNP-Anti-Kidnapping Group (PNP-AKG) filed charges against individuals who conspired in kidnapping three foreign nationals in Nasugbu, Batangas. Santiago (Ret.) said that the case stemmed from intelligence reports and investigative efforts conducted collaboratively by the NBI-Organized and Transnational Crimes Division (OTCD) and the PNP-Anti-Kidnapping Group (PNP-AKG). body: PRESS STATEMENT August 15, 2025 .jusatified-text { text-align: justify; } In line with the directive from National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Director JUDGE JAIME B. SANTIAGO (Ret.) to intensify the operations against online sexual exploitation of children, the NBI-Violence Against Women and Children Division (NBI-VAWCD) arrested alias “TISAY” in Marilao, Bulacan. Subject was arrested for violations of Republic Act No. 9208 as amended by R.A. No. 11862 (Expanded Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2022), R.A. No. 11930 (Anti-Online Sexual Abuse or Exploitation of Children (OSAEC and Anti-Child Sexual Abuse or Exploitation Materials (CSAEM), and R.A. No. 7610 (Anti-Child Abuse Law). The operation stemmed from a referral by the Homeland Security Investigation (HSI) regarding Philippine phone numbers involved in Online Sexual Abuse and Exploitation of Children (OSAEC). According to the HSI, this referral was based on the arrest of a US citizen in Springfield, Massachusetts, by the US Federal authorities, for child exploitation crime. NBI-VAWCD’s investigation revealed the Subject’s involvement in offering sexually explicit content involving minors and sending CSAEMs to foreign pedophiles. Through surveillance, the Subject’s address was identified. Subsequently, NBI-VAWCD agents applied for a Warrant to Search, Seize, and Examine Computer Data (WSSECD), which was granted by the court. On August 13, 2025, NBI-VAWCD agents, with assistance from the HSI, NBI-Digital Forensic Laboratory Division (NBI-FLD), NBI-Evidential Multimedia Division (NBI-EMD), CyberTIP IACAT Intelligence Agents, and Social Workers from Marilao, Bulacan Municipal Social Welfare and Development Office (MSWDO), proceeded to the address of the Subject in Marilao, Bulacan, to implement the WSSECD. The operation resulted in the seizure of various gadgets used by the Subject in his online child sexual exploitation activities. Consequently, NBI agents arrested the Subject and rescued five (5) minor children, one of whom was the Subject’s niece. The arrested Subject was presented for inquest proceedings for the above-stated violations, while the rescued victims were turned-over to the custody and protection of MSWDO for appropriate intervention and aftercare services. Director Santiago commended the dedicated agents of the NBI-VAWCD for their hard work and determination, which culminated in the successful arrest of the Subject and the rescue of the minor victims.

body: PRESS STATEMENT August 19, 2025 .jusatified-text { text-align: justify; } On August 12, 2025, under the leadership of National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Director Judge Jaime B. Santiago (Ret.), the NBI-Dagupan District Office (NBI-DADO), together with representatives from the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD), rescued two (2) victims of human trafficking in Urdaneta City, Pangasinan. The case was endorsed to NBI-DADO by a non-profit organization that had received a request for assistance from the relatives of the victims. According to the relatives, Victims were allegedly under the custody of a syndicate engaged in human trafficking activities in Northern and Central Luzon. They added that they had received messages from the victims begging for help. Investigation revealed that the victims and 12 other females were recruited to work as waitresses at Mahogany KTV Bar in Agoo, La Union. Instead, they were coerced and exploited to work as female entertainers and were offered for sexual services to male customers. Victims and their companions were then transported and transferred to another KTV bar, 178 KTV Bar, in Urdaneta City, Pangasinan. They were also reportedly threatened with being shot if they attempted to escape. Agents of NBI-DADO, accompanied by DSWD personnel and relatives of the victims, went to the KTV Bar and successfully rescued two (2) of the victims. Both victims were turned over to DSWD for proper care. Victims affirmed the report received by NBI-DADO and added that they were recruited online with a promised of a monthly salary of Php 20,000.00. They also disclosed that they were forced to sign an agreement stating they had an acknowledged debt to the KTV Bar and would not leave until it was paid. However, they denied receiving any amount from the recruiters. Director Santiago commended the NBI-DADO agents. He assures the public that the Bureau will continue to locate and rescue the other female victims and will investigate on the recruiters and the KTV Bar owners and operators for the filing of appropriate charges against them.

body: PRESS STATEMENT October 17, 2024 The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI), under the leadership of NBI Director Judge Jaime B. Santiago (Ret.), arrested seventeen (17) Chinese nationals engaged in scamming activities. Director Santiago said that a Chinese national filed a complaint before the NBI- Cybercrime Division (NBI-CCD), alleging that his friend was illegally detained, tortured, and forced to render services involuntarily such as scamming and other money-making schemes. His passport was also hidden from him to control his mobility. Through intelligence gathering, the victim was spotted in La Casa Rabina, Tagaytay City. Thus, on October 15, 2024, NBI-CCD, together with the operatives from NBI-Special Task Force (NBI-STF) and NBI-Human Trafficking Division (NBI-HTRAD), hatched a joint rescue operation. Occupants of the premises were caught in flagrante delicto of engaging in scamming and money muling activities, social engineering schemes, and other nefarious activities, with numerous work stations surrounding the area. Mobile phones, sim cards, written scripts, and other customer ledgers painted with a vivid picture of organized deceit were also found. Santiago added that controlled viewing and examination on the desktop’s interface revealed several scripts, messaging applications with fictitious accounts, bank accounts, and fraudulent cryptocurrency investment platforms, suggesting massive fraudulent activities such as catfishing scams, credit card scams, cryptocurrency scams, and fake investment scams. The seventeen (17) Chinese nationals were placed under arrest for violation of Section 4(a) of RA 11862 (Expanded Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2022) and Social Engineering Schemes under Section 4(b)(1) and Economic Sabotage under Section 4(c)(1) of RA 12010 (Anti-Financial Account Scamming Act) in relation to RA 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012). Director Santiago commended the CCD, STF, and HTRAD operatives for successfully apprehending the Chinese nationals engaged in massive scamming activities. He stressed that the NBI continuous its tireless efforts to uncover cybercriminals in the country, regardless of nationality.

body: A known drug den was raided and six drug users were arrested by National Bureau of Investigation operatives during an operation in Biñan, Laguna over the week-end. NBI Director Nonnatus Caesar R. Rojas identified the suspects as: MARY ANN ALADA CARTA, aka Em-Em, married , and a resident of Tramo St., Bgy. Canlalay, Biñan, Laguna; ELMER ESPIRITU CARSOLA, married and a resident of #113 6th Street, Pacita Complex, San pedro, Laguna; PERCHILY VARGAS CAGAGAN, married, resident of B-5, L-9, Naga St., South City Homes, Biñan. Laguna; JENNY ALACANTARA IGNACIO, married, a resident of Tramo, Bgy. Canlalay, Biñan, Laguna; and EDWIN CINCO RECTIN, a resident of Tramo Gitna, Bgy. Canlalay, Biñan, Laguna. Investigation by the Reaction, Arrest and Interdiction Division (RAID) headed by Atty. Ross Jonathan V. Galicia disclosed that the NBI received information about rampant drug use by residents in Bgy. Canlalay, Binan, Laguna. It was reported that a house of a certain “Em-Em” along Tramo St., Bgy. Canlalay, Biñan, Laguna was being frequently used as a drug den. After a series of surveillance, the report was confirmed. A search warrant was applied for and issued by the Quezon City Regional Trial Court. In the afternoon of June 29, 2013, NBI agents launched an operation and proceeded to the pinpointed drug den. Upon arrival at the residence of Em-Em who was later identified as Mary Ann Carta, NBI operatives immediately swooped down, and surprised the suspects who were having a drug session. The operatives subsequently arrested the occupants identified as suspects Carta, Carsola, Cagagan, Ignacio and Rectin. Two of them, Carsola and Rectin attempted to escape but were subdued by alert NBI operatives. Found and seized were: several transparent plastic sachet containing crystalline substance (shabu), foils and other drug paraphernalia used by the suspects. Likewise, found were gambling machines for “Fruit Games”. Thereafter, suspects were brought to the NBI main office in Manila for booking and detention. Charges for violation of Sec. 6 (Maintenance of a den, dive or resort), Sec. 11 (Possession of Dangerous Drugs), Sec. 12 (Possession of equipment, instrument, apparatus and other paraphernalia for Dangerous Drugs during parties, social gatherings or meetings), Art. II of RA 9165; and PD 1602 as amended by RA 9287 were filed against the suspects before the Biñan City Prosecutor’s Office. No bail was recommended for Mary Anne A. Carta .

body: On July 27, 2020, the NBI-Death Investigation Division (NBI-DID) recommended for prosecution twelve (12) police officers of the Intelligence Section/City Drug Enforcement Unit of San Jose del Monte Police Office for the killing of six (6) individuals in fabricated anti-illegal drugs operations. Six (6) victims namely CHAMBERLAIN S. DOMINGO, CHADWIN D. SANTOS, ERWIN N. MERGAL, JIM JOSHUA CORDERO, EDMAR S. ASPRIN, and RICHARD C. SALGADO were forcibly taken without legal ground in Towerville, Brgy. Santo Cristo, CSJDM on February 13, 2020 and were brought to the CSJDM Police Office on board a white van. Blindfolded and hogtied, victims were placed in a room inside the Intel Office of the CSJDM Police Office instead of undergoing booking and documentation procedures. On separate occasions, victims were killed in fabricated buy-bust operations. Considering that the buy-bust operation was merely fabricated, it necessarily follows that the improvised shotguns, cartridges, and illegal drugs recovered at the scene were planted to set stage for the fabricated buy-bust operations. It is therefore difficult to comprehend how the victims could have acquired the said pieces of evidence when they were abducted on the evening of February 13, 2020, detained at the police station where they were blindfolded and hogtied until they were killed. Charges for Kidnapping/Serious Illegal Detention with Murder, violation of RA 9165 (Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002), and violation of RA 10591 (Comprehensive Firearms and Ammunition Regulation Act) were filed against PMAJ LEO COMMENDADOR DELA ROSA, PSSg BENJIE DE CASTRO ENCONADO, PSSg JAYSON MORALES LEGASPI, PSSg IRWIN JOY MORFE YUSON, PCpl JAY MARC MABASA LENCIO, PCpl HARVY CRUZ ALBINO, PCpl HERBERT LINOY HERNANDEZ, PCpl CONSTANTE RAMOS ESCALANTE JR., PCpl RAYMOND BABIDA BAYAN, PCpl PAUL JIMENEZ MALGAPO, Pat ERWIN OPLIMO SABIDO, and RUSCO VIRNAR ALCARAZ MADLA. On July 30, 2020, operatives of NBI-Central Luzon Regional Office (NBI-CELRO) arrested YANG SAN KIIO and LEE JARI, Chinese nationals, for selling Chinese food and health products that are unregistered with FDA. Subjects were arrested in an operation which stemmed from a report regarding a makeshift warehouse containing unregistered Chinese food and health products. Test buy operation conducted confirmed the said report as some of the products bought from the said establishment are verified by the FDA as unregistered. On the abovementioned date, operatives proceeded to the warehouse located in Malabanias, Angeles City to conduct the entrapment operation which resulted in the arrest of the Subjects who introduced themselves as the supervisors of the warehouse. Recovered during the operation were assorted Chinese food and health products worth Php 3,368. Additional unregistered Chinese food and health products being sold to the public were confiscated by the FDA and the warehouse was padlocked after the inspection. Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor, Angeles City for violation of RA 3720 (Food, Drug and Cosmetic Act) as amended by RA 9711 (FDA Act of 2009). On August 19, 2020, operatives of NBI-Intellectual Property Rights Division (NBI-IPRD) seized 2 bottles of Martell XO Cognac, 4 bottles of Martell Cordon Bleu Extra Old Cognac, and 10 bottles of Johnnie Walker Blue Label with an estimated value of Php 20,000.00. Items were seized in an entrapment operation conducted in Intramuros, Manila. Charges for violation of RA 8293 (Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines) were filed against RANNIEL ARVIN SANTIAGO y HERRERA aka JOAQIN GUZMAN. On August 19, 2020, operatives of NBI-Environmental Crime Division (NBI-EnCD) arrested SAIYAD MOHAMMAD DAWOOD JAMALUDIN for trading and possessing endangered forest product “agarwood”. Subject was arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from a report regarding a foreign national allegedly trading and in possession of agarwood. The trading or possession of the aforesaid forest product including its transportation without any documents required under the existing environmental laws is prohibited. Acting on the report, joint team of NBI-EnCD and DENR-NCR conducted an entrapment operation resulting in the arrest of the Subject in Pasay City. The operation also resulted in the seizure of 1.2 kilograms of high grade agarwood chips with an estimated market value of Php 196,078.00. The estimated environmental fee which represents the market value, forest charges and environmental damages of the forest products possessed and transported without permit is Php 1,960,788.00. Subject was presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor-Pasay City for violation of PD 705 as amended (Revised Forestry Code of the Philippines) and RA 9147 (Wildlife Resources Conservation and Protection Act). On August 17-19 of NBI-Cagayan Valley Regional Office (NBI-CAVRO), together with PDEA, RDEA PROCOR, RID PROCOR, Kalinga PPO, 1 st and 2 nd KPMFC, 1503 rd RMFB, 501 st and 503 rd RMFB, 501 st and 503 rd Brigade PA, Naval Force Northern Luzon, TOG 1& 2, CIDG-COR, discovered and destructed marijuana plantations in Tulgao, Tinglayan and Mt. Chumanchil, Loccong, Tinglayan. The marijuana plantations has an estimated land area of 22,370sqm.
