body: On August 2, 2018 , operatives of NBI-Rizal District Office (NBI-RIZDO) seized counterfeit Nike and Converse products with an estimated value of Php 27 Million were seized in Pasay City. Items were seized by virtue of Search Warrants issued by RTC Branch 24, Manila. Charges for violation of RA 8293 (Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines) were filed against Nina Ong and/or Jaimy Cruz Ong and the proprietors, officers, employees, occupants of Vansport Footwear Store located at various units at Harrison Wholesale Center, Cuneta Avenue cor. FB Harrison, Pasay City. On August 2, 2018 , operatives of NBI-Dagupan District Office arrested eight (8) STL cabos and three (3) individuals in entrapment operation for illegal gambling. These legitimate STL cabos were caught remitting their collections to illegal bookies operators while the three individuals were caught in possession of illegal gambling paraphernalia. Charges for violation PD 1602 (Illegal Gambling Law) were filed against the arrested Subjects. Charges for Qualified Theft were also filed against the STL cabos. On August 2, 2018 , operatives of NBI-Sarangani District Office (NBI-SARDO) arrested JUDELYN ALIPIN y DELGADO and ANABEL ALIPIN y DELGADO by virtue of Alias Warrant of Arrest for the crime of Qualified Theft as penalized by Article 310 of the Revised Penal Code as amended with No Bail recommended. On the said date, Subject was arrested while securing an NBI clearance at NBI-SARDO. A request for the issuance of Warrant of Arrest was made and immediately affected the arrest. Accused was temporarily detained at NBI-SARDO, waiting for the approved authority to travel to Manila to transfer the said accused to NBI Jail. On August 2, 2018 , operatives of NBI-Tagum District Office (NBI-TAGDO) arrested FELIX PAMILAR, MERLYN PAMILAR, and MYRNA B. SUMUNDA for human trafficking. The case stemmed from the information received that a Pamilar Store near Tagum City Public Market which operates as mini KTV Bar in the evening employs minors as their guest relations officers. The information was was validated that there was indeed three to seven minors working in the said KTV bar and that the minors could be taken out for a fee of Php2,500. Joint operatives of NBI-TAGDO, City Social Welfare and Development Office, and Tagum City Health Center then conducted an operation which resulted in the rescue of three (3) minors with ages ranging from 14-16 years old, and the arrest of the above-mentioned Subjects. The minor victims are now in the custody of CSWD. Charges for violation of RA 9208 (The Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2003) were filed against the Subjects. On August 3, 2018 , operatives of NBI-Central Luzon Regional Office (NBI-CELRO) arrested JEFFREY BECAYLAS y REMON, KIER ROME DE LEON y ALFONSO, and JUSTIN LUMANLAN y SANGALANG in entrapment operation for human trafficking. Eight (8) trafficked victims, one (1) of which is minor, were likewise rescued in the operation. Recovered from the Subjects was a total of Php 24,000. Charges for violation of RA 9208 (Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2003) as ameded by RA 10364 (Expanded Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2012) were filed against the Subjects. On August 7, 2018 , operatives of NBI-Western Visayas Regional Office (NBI-WEVRO) arrested RONALD G. BARNIZO for RA 10591 (Comprehensive Firearms and Ammunition Regulation Act), Article 177 (Usurpation of Authority) of the Revised Penal Code as amended. The case stemmed from a report that Subject and his cohorts are reported to have been possessing unlicensed firearms and posing as NBI agents, promising their supposed clients that they have the capacity to take care their concerns before the Department of Justice where NBI is an attached agency. Investigation and validation were conducted and it was found out that Subject and his cohorts are involved in extortion rackets posing as NBI agents. With this, an enforcement operation of Search Warrant was conducted in the Subject’s residence located at Brgy. Man It, Passi City, Iloilo. Various firearms and live ammunitions were seized in possession, control, and custody of the Subject. Subject is presently detained at the NBI-WEVRO pending the filing of charges against the Subject. On August 7, 2018 , operatives of NBI-International Operations Division (NBI-IOD) arrested MICHAEL ROSS CONROY and TERESITA MENDOZA-CONROY City for Estafa and violations of BP 22. Subjects enticed complainants to invest in their computer software company by making them a part owner and promising a hefty return of their investment. Complainants Dominico Lancian, Jr. and Jakerson Gargallo, disclosed that Subjects offered them to invest THREE HUNDRED THOUSAND PESOS (300,000.00) each with a promised return of FORTY-TWO MILLION PESOS (42,000,000.00) for every investment, as it will definitely make a return considering that election is near and the program that they are told to sell can be used for political campaigns. Records of the Bureau showed that Subjects have warrant of arrest issued by the Regional Trial Court Branch 134 Makati City and upon verification found out that the court has already issued a new warrant of arrest against the Subjects for service of sentence having already been convicted for the crime of Estafa. Derogatory records of the Subjects also revealed that they have other warrants of arrest issued by courts of Makati City, Marawi City and Cabadbaran City for the same crime/violations. With all the information and proper authority to serve the arrest warrant, operatives implemented the same and arrested the Subjects at the meeting place set by the Subjects at La Verti Residences North Tower. Subjects were brought to the office for standard operating procedures and was turned over to NBI-Jail. On August 8, 2018 , operatives of NBI-Isabela District Office (NBI-ISDO) arrested CHERRY MACATUNGGAL-SANTANDER for violation of PD 1602 (Illegal Gambling Law). Subject was arrested in entrapment operation which stemmed from a report that illegal jueteng operations were being conducted and proliferates in the municipality of Tumauni, Isabela. Acting on the operation, surveillance operations were conducted confirming the said information. During the operation, Subject was caught collecting bets under the guise of Sahara collectors. Seized and recovered from Subject’s possession were bills and coins as well as gambling paraphernalia. Subject underwent proper booking procedure after the arrest. On August 8, 2018 , the NBI-Counter Terrorism Division (NBI-CTD) recommended before the Department of Justice (DOJ) Anti-Terrorism Task Force the filing of Inciting to Sedition case against MOHAMMAD REZA KIRAM y LOHAMAN. Operatives of NBI-CTD regularly conduct internet surveillance of various social media and other websites to monitor, track, and if possible, interdict the persons responsible. It was discovered that there is a video wherein Subject was making seditious statements. It was clearly seen that Subject Kiram incited others to inflict acts of hate and violence by bombing, stabbing, and pouring gasoline on the homes, the persons and properties of public officers as well as other private individuals, non-Muslims and non-radical Muslims. Subject Kiram is one of the few Filipino citizens who are officially recorded to have gone over to Raqqa, Syria to join the ISIS. It is clear that Subject may be held criminally liable for the crime of Inciting to Sedition under Article 142 of the Revised Penal Code in relation to RA 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012). On August 8, 2018 , operatives of NBI-Anti-Human Trafficking Division (NBI-AHTRAD) arrested RONALD RAMOS y DELA CRUZ, JORDAN DUNCAN y BONGHAYON, ALDRIN PLACER y DE LOYAS, and JEREMY KIRK SANTOS y MUSNI for human trafficking in Antipolo, Rizal. Subjects were arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from a report that certain individuals are engaged in prostitution and child exploitation. Initial information disclosed that subjects are recruiting and offering minor victims whose ages are from 14-16 years old for sexual exploitation to their clients. Acting on the information, NBI-AHTRAD operatives conducted an entrapment operation which resulted in the arrest of the Subjects and the rescue of seventeen (17) victims twelve (12) of whom are minors. Victims were turned over to DSWD for custody. Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the State Prosecutor, Department of Justice for violation of RA 9208 (Trafficking in Persons Act of 2003) as amended by RA 10364 (Expanded Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2012) in relation to RA 7610 (Special Protection of Children against Abuse, Exploitation and Discrimination Act). On August 9, 2018 , operatives of NBI-Environmental Crime Division (EnCD) arrested PEDRITO FABRO JR. y BASA for violation of RA 9147 (Wildlife Resources Conservation and Protection Act). Subject was arrested in a follow-up operation in Nakar, Quezon in connection with the operations conducted on April 5, 2018 which resulted to the seizure of twenty-five (25) sacks of Bantigi plants. On the aforementioned date, a composite team composed of CENRO, Dingalan Aurora, CENRO, Real, Quezon, DENR-Biodiversity Management Bureau and the NBI-EnCD proceeded to the target area and chanced upon was Subject PEDRITO FABRO JR. in the act of piling, heaping, and layering trunks which according to DENR-BMB were Bantigi siit. A total of 34 socks of Bantigi siit which according to DENR-BMB has an estimated value of Php 250,000, were seized. Subject was arrested after he failed to present any permit. Subject was presented for inquest proceeding before the Office of the Prosecutor General, Department of Justice, Manila for violation of RA 9147 (Wildlife Resources Conservation and Protection Act of 2001) were filed against the Subject. On August 10, 2018 , operatives of NBI- International Airport Investigation Unit (NBI-IAIU) arrested SARAH JANE GUTIERREZ ESTEBAN for illegal recruitment. The operation was based from the information gathered from the offloaded passengers (victims), that they were recruited by a certain Sarah to work in Doha, Qatar as hotel staff. According to the victims they paid Subject Esteban TWENTY-FIVE THOUSAND PESOS (Php 25,000.00) each as processing fee which they sent through bank and/or money courier. Subject Esteban gave them tourist visa in Malaysia and from there they would be given working visa to work in Qatar. During investigation the victims disclosed that Subject Esteban will fetch them near NAIA area as the latter learned the offload incident. The operatives then proceeded to the location of Subject Esteban and arrested her for illegal recruitment. Per verification with the POEA, Subject Esteban is not licensed nor authorized to recruit Filipino workers for abroad. The Subject was brought before the Pasay Prosecutor’s Office for inquest proceedings. Violations of Republic Act 8042 otherwise known as the Migrant Workers and Overseas Act of 1995 as amended by R.A. 10022 and R.A. 9208 otherwise known as Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2003 were filed against the Subject. On August 13, 2018 , operatives of NBI-North Eastern Mindanao Regional Office (NBI-NEMRO) arrested ELMER DIASANA y QUINTANES and ROSENDO AGUANTA y LUMANDAS for violation of Article 168 (Illegal possession and use of false treasury or bank notes and other instruments of credit) of the Revised Penal Code. The case stemmed from a letter of Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas thru Nestor H. Arenas, Bank Officer II of Currency Issue and Integrity Office and Currency Investigation Division of the BSP, requesting for assistance for the planning of anti-counterfeit operation against certain individuals who are said to be violating Articles 166, 168, and 176 of the Revised Penal Code. Accordingly, these individuals proliferate counterfeit Philippine, US and other currency banknotes in Cagayan de Oro City and nearby provinces, cities and municipalities. In view thereof, operatives of NBI-NEMRO together with the agents of Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas conducted entrapment operation resulting in the arrest of the Subjects. On August 13, 2018 , JAY-R S. DANAO who has Warrant of Arrest for violation of RA 9262 (Anti-Violence Against Women and their Children Act of 2004), voluntarily surrendered to NBI-National Capital Region (NBI-NCR). Subject is a chief mechanic of Man Trucks & Bus Company and a Warrant of Arrest for the aforementioned violation was issued against him by the RTC Second Judicial, Branch 25, Bulanao, Tabuk, Kalinga. Subject was turned over to NBI Jail after the booking procedure. On August 14, 2018 , operatives of NBI-Anti-Organized and Transnational Crime Division arrested TWINKLE MAE ARCEO y DAVID, CITA ZAILON y CONTADO, SALVADOR GARCIA y CASTRO, and JOMER PERTIERRA y LAQUINDANUM for illegal gambling. Subjects were arrested in entrapment operation which stemmed from the letter of Chairman Abraham Kahlil B. Mitra of Games and Amusement Board (GAB) requesting apprehension and arrest on suspected illegal bookies operation. Recovered from the Subjects were peso bills and bet tickets. Subjects were presented for inquest proceeding before the Office of the City Prosecutor, Manila. On August 15, 2018 , operatives of NBI- Anti-Human Trafficking Division (NBI-AHTRAD) arrested EDWIN BAYONA y PRESINTACION, ALFREDO VALENZONA y DERECHO, RICHARD CAHUSAY y CASALJAY, AGUSTIN RAMIREZ y DIAZ, and CHARLIE QUIOBE y PRESINTACION in entrapment operation in Makati City for human trafficking. The operation stemmed from an information that certain individuals are engaged in prostitution sexual exploitation. Initial information disclosed that Subjects are recruiting and offering trafficked victims for sexual exploitation to their clients for a fee. The victims are also being offered in a house and their accommodation is just at the second floor of the said house. The Subjects operate in a “casa” style wherein a house is being used for their illegal activities. With this, in coordination with the PNP-Makati, DSWD-Makati, and Department of Justice Inter-Agency Council Against Human Trafficking Persons, the entrapment operation was conducted resulting in the arrest of the Subjects and the rescue of twenty-eight (28) women. The rescued victims were then turned over to the custody of Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD). Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings for violation of RA 9208 (Trafficking in Persons Act of 2003) as amended by RA 10364 (Expanded Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2012). On August 15, 2018 , operatives of NBI-National Capital Region (NBI-NCR) seized counterfeit Lacoste products with an estimated amount of Php 3,548,000.00. Items were seized in 168 Shopping Mall, Binondo, Manila by virtue of Search Warrants. Charges for violation of RA 8293 (Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines were filed against John/Jane Does. On August 16, 2018 , operatives of NBI- Environmental Crime Division (NBI-EnCD) arrested REX MESA for possession of coconut lumbers without necessary permits. Subject was the consignee of a large shipment of illegally cut and undocumented coconut lumbers that arrived in Pier 16, North Harbor on August 12, 2018. After confirming the information received about the alleged illegal shipment, EncD operatives coordinated with the Philippine Coconut Authority (PCA) for a possible joint operation to apprehend the Subject. PCA requested the Bureau of Customs to hold the release of twenty-one (21) container vans under the name of the Subject. On August 16, 2018, Subject appeared at the PCA office and presented transshipment clearances that are expired or recycled. Subject was then invited by the PCA and NBI to accompany them at Port Area Manila where the said container vans are located. Seized during the inspection were 21,261 board feet coconut lumbers bound for Manila, 19,000 board feet of coconut lumbers bound for Cebu, 84,000 board feet of coconut lumbers bound for Manila and 14,000 board feet of coconut lumbers bound for Cebu, totaling to 138,261 board feet. All shipments have expired transshipment clearance and is not covered by a new or a valid transport permit. Certification issued by the PCA also confirmed that Subject is not a registered coconut lumber trader and has not secured a consolidation permit for the transport of coconut lumbers as required under the Implementing Rules and Regulation of Republic Act 8048, as amended. Operatives then arrested the Subject and on August 17, 2018, Subject was presented to the Office of the Prosecutor General, Department of Justice for inquest proceeding for violation of RA 8048, as amended by RA 10593 in relation to Section 37 (a) and (e) of PCA Administrative Order No. 03 Series of 2018. On August 16, 2018 , operatives of NBI-Environmental Crime Division (NBI-EnCD) arrested REX MESA in Port Area, Manila for possession of coconut lumbers without necessary permits.NBI-ENCD, in coordination with the Philippine Coconut Authority (PCA) for a joint operation to apprehend the Subject. PCA requested the Bureau of Customs to hold the release of twenty one (21) container vans under the name of the Subject. On the aforementioned date, Subject appeared at the PCA office and presented expired or recycled transshipment clearances. Subject was then invited by the PCA and NBI to accompany them at Port Area, Manila where the said container vans are located. Seized during the inspection were 138, 261 board feet of coconut lumbers. All shipments have expired transshipment clearance and is not covered by new or a new valid transport permit. Certification issued by the PCA also confirmed that Subject is not a registered coconut lumber trader and has not secured a consolidation permit for the transport of coconut lumbers. Subject was then arrested and presented for inquest proceeding before the Office of the Prosecutor General, Department of Justice for violation of RA 8048 (Coconut Preservation Act of 1995) as amended by RA 10593 in relation to Section 37 (a) and € of PCA Administrative Order No. 3 Series 2018. On August 18, 2018 , operatives of NBI-International Operations Division (NBI-IOD) arrested REGINA BONEZA SENSON at Ninoy Aquino International Airport by virtue of Warrant of Arrest for Qualified Theft. Prior to the operation, a request for issuance of Red Notice to Subject was made by the NBI-IOD from the Philippine Center for Transnational Crime (PCTC) with the information that Subject had already been issued a Warrant of Arrest and her passport had been cancelled. With the Red Notice already available, request for assistance for the deportation of the Subject was submitted to the Ambassador of the Embassy of United Arab Emirates. Surprisingly, NBI-IOD received a message from Interpol Abu Dahbi-UAE thru the PCTC concerning the deportation and turning over custody of Subject Senson that led to the arrest of the Subject. Subject is currently detained at the NBI Detention Cell. On August 18, 2018 , operatives of NBI- International Operations Division (NBI-IOD arrested REGINA BONEZA SENSON at Ninoy Aquino International Airport (NAIA) by virtue of Warrant of Arrest issued by RTC of Navotas City, Branch 212 for Qualified Theft. Prior to the operation, a request for issuance of Red Notice to Subject Senson was made by the NBI-IOD from the Philippine Center for Transnational Crime (PCTC) with the information that Subject Senson had already been issued a Warrant of Arrest and her passport had been cancelled. With the Red Notice already available, request for assistance for the deportation of the subject was submitted to the Ambassador of the Embassy of United Arab Emirates. Surprisingly, NBI-IOD received a message from Interpol Abu Dahbi – UAE thru the PCTC concerning the deportation and turning over of custody of Subject Senson that led to the arrest of the Subject. Subject REGINA BONEZA SENSON was, thereafter, brought to the NBI where she underwent standard booking procedure. Atty. Kim Villanueva, representative of the complainant, positively identified Subject Senson. Subject is currently detained at the NBI Detention Cell. On August 20, 2018 , operatives of NBI- Environmental Crime Division (NBI-EnCD) arrested GLENN ALBERT BINOYA y AGUINALDO, who is allegedly responsible for shipping undocumented corals to the United States of America. The case stemmed from a letter from Special Agent of the United States Department of Interior, U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (USFWS) requesting assistance for an investigation and possible case build up against smuggle rs of undocumented corals from the Philippines to the United States of America. After proper coordination and surveillance activities, a search warrant was issued by RTC Bacoor Cavite for search and seizure of hard and soft corals, tools and other paraphernalia. Recovered from the Subject were numerous live hard and soft corals. Also recovered in “plain view” three (3) giant clams known as “taklobo.” Almost one thousand eight hundred (1,800) pieces of corals and other species were seized during the implementation of Search Warrant. These marine species have a commercial value of Fifty-Four Thousand US dollars ($54,000.00) or equivalent to Two Million Seven Hundred Thousand pesos (Php 2,700,000.00). The National Fisheries Research Development Institute disclosed that the corals submitted for analysis and identification are classified as Live Hard/Stony Corals, order Scleractinia. The report also identified the clams as Tridacna spp, which is included in the Appendix II list in the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (CITES) and is categorized as Endangered. Subject was presented for inquest proceeding before the Department of Justice for violation of Section 96 and 102 of R.A. 8550 as Amended by R.A. 10654. On August 24, 2018 , the NBI-Anti-Organized and Transnational Crime Division (NBI-AOTCD) filed Estafa charges against sixteen (16) officers and employees of WAHANA Credit and Loan Corporation for being involved in an investment scam. The Subjects are identified as MA. LYSA SOLER, SALVE ANAHAW, NICOLE BARRERA, RHIZA ANAHAW, MHARINA PELAGIO, ROSE ANN TOLENTINO, NORA BARTOLATA, ZAIDE MENDOZA, ROCHELLE REYES, JEMMAR BARTOLATA, ENGELYN VIDENA, RAYMOND OFALLA, GEM SOLIS, JUDITH ZAFRA, MICO BARRERA, and MARECRISTELLA MERIDA MARCELO. The case stemmed from reports sometime in February 2018 that a multi-million investment scam is being committed by WAHANA Credit and Loan Corporation (WCLC), and in March 2018, more complaints were received against WCLC. Complainants alleged that WCLC is involved in gathering investments from the public with the promise that they will earn 7-12% interest weekly from the companies’ Casino Financing Scheme. In addition, Subjects also promised investors that they can earn from their referrals the amount of Php 20,000 per referral, and that their investment and interest may be withdrawn upon demand. Contrary to the promises made by Subjects, the return of investments never materialized since WCLC, Wahana Multi-Purpose Band, and Barrera Management Consultancy stopped returning their investments despite complainants’ demands. It was also discovered that those companies are not registered with the Security and Exchange Commission (SEC), hence not authorized to publicly offer or sell securities and to solicit investments from the public. Subjects were recommended to be charged for Estafa in relation to PD 1689 (An Act Increasing the Penalty for Certain Forms of Estafa). Therefore charges were filed before the Task Force on Securities and Business Scam of the Department of Justice (DOJ). The second and third batches of complaints were likewise forwarded for review, and is expected to be filed before the DOJ. On August 24, 2018 , operatives of NBI-Cabanatuan District Office (NBI-CABDO) arrested JOEL CALACSAN y DIVINA in a buy-bust operation for selling shabu. Subject’s urine/drug test showed positive results for the presence of marijuana and shabu as per NEPCLO certification. Subject was presented for inquest proceedings for violation of RA 9165 (Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002). On August 25, 2018 , operatives of NBI-Central Luzon Regional Office (NBI-CELRO) arrested WILSON BUREROS PLARISAN and JUDITH MILCA DOINOG WILSON for human trafficking. Subjects were arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from the complaint of Lidelma Cardeno Capila regarding the Arcadia Night Bar that was engaged in prostitution. Surveillance operations confirmed the said information so the entrapment operation was conducted which resulted in the arrest of the Subjects. Seventy six (76) trafficked victims were likewise rescued and turned over to DSWD. Charges for violation of RA10364 (Expanded Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2012) were filed against the Subjects. On August 28, 2018 , operatives of NBI-Environmental Crime Division (EnCD) arrested MICHAEL PAMINTUAN for illegally selling endangered wildlife species. Subject was arrested in a buy-bust operation which stemmed from the information received by the NBI regarding Subject’s illegal activity. After positively conducting the buy-bust operation, Subject voluntarily surrendered to the NBI operatives. Recovered from Subject were 28 live mynas and 11 live sugar glyders. The seized wildlife species were turned over to DENR-BMB for custody. Charges for violation of RA 9147 (Wildlife Resources Conservation and Protection Act) were filed against the Subject. On August 29, 2018 , the NBI recommended the filing of Murder charges against SPO2 RODANTE SICAT LALIMARMO, PO3 ARTHUR YASONIA LUCY and PO1 JOSE LUNAR MERCADO and seven (7) John Does and Jane Doe (8 individuals) for the killing of Deputy City Prosecutor Rogelio A. Velasco on May 11, 2018 in Quezon City. After conducting a thorough and exhaustive investigation for almost three (3) months, the NBI-Death Investigation Division (NBI-DID) found probable cause to collectively charge the three (3) policemen and eight (8) others for the crime of Murder. On August 30, 2018 , operatives of NBI-Anti-Human Trafficking Division arrested ANSARY JAMIL y CALI aka CHERRYANN CHERRY, MAOLINE PAULITE aka MAOLYN PAULITE AND EDEN TIMON AGUILAR aka MITCH in entrapment operation in Antipolo City. The case stemmed from the information relayed by an internationally recognized Christian non-profit organization, Destiny Rescue Philippines, that an alleged human trafficking activities are taking place in the areas of Cainta and Antipolo, Rizal. Information revealed that Subjects Cherryann and Maolyn are maintaining prostitutes that offer sexual intercourse with clients preferably foreigners thru online media. Acting on the information, the entrapment operation was conducted resulting in the arrest of the Subjects and the rescue of ten (10) women, two (2) of whom were confirmed of minor age. Subjects were presented before the City Prosecutor of Antipolo for inquest proceedings for violation of R.A. No. 9208 otherwise known as the “Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2003,” as amended by R.A. No. 10364 and violation of R.A. 7610 otherwise known as the “Special Protection Against Child Abuse, Exploitation and Discrimination Act,” as amended. On August 31, 2018 , operatives of NBI-Central Mindanao Regional Office (NBI-CEMRO) arrested JESSA CANJA PENACERADA, MARIA JEMMA PENACERADA ZARATE, GUILLERMA PENACERADA ZARATE, and PO3 RETCHIE BOY SILOT BUCA for human trafficking. Subjects were arrested in an operation which stemmed from a report an alleged cybersex operation in multiple areas of Polomolok, South Cotabato involving minor recruits. Surveillance operations were conducted confirming the information, and on the above-mentioned date, Search Warrants were implemented and the Subjects were caught in flagrante doing the illegal activities. Charges for violations of RA 10364 (Expanded Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2012), RA 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012) and RA 10591 (Illegal Possession of Firearms) were filed against the Subjects before the Office of the Provincial Inquest Prosecutor of South Cotabato. On August 31, 2018 , operatives of NBI- Anti-Organized and Transnational Crime Division arrested LANA DELA CRUZ in Las Piñas City for Estafa. Subject presented herself as an employee of Senator Cynthia Villar and was authorized to facilitate the selling of condominium units at Royal Palm Villa, Las Piñas City allegedly owned by the Villar family which Senator Villar donated to her staff. According to the complainant, Subject offered her and her grandfather a unit located at 8 th floor of Royal Palm Villa for Php 350,000. Convinced, complainant decided to buy the said unit. Later on, Subject again offered another condominium unit for the same amount and the same was also allegedly Se. Villar’s donation to her staff. Complainant and her sister then began to doubt. They compared Sen.Villar’s signature they found on the internet to the one on the purported authorization letter, and noticed that there is something unusual in them. They also discovered that Subject’s ID was issued by OHANA Place which is not owned by the Villar Family. Complainant then went to the office of Sen. Cynthia Villar and was informed by one of the staff that Subject is not an employee of Sen. Villar and that she is not donating any condominium units to her staff. Moreover, Royal Palm Villa is not owned by the Villar family and the signature of Sen. Villar appearing in the authorization letter given to the complainant is not the signature of Sen. Villar. Thus, complainant decided to file a complaint against the Subject. Acting on the complaint, an entrapment operation was conducted on August 31, 2018 resulting in the arrest of the Subject. Certification from the Office of Sen. Cynthia Villar showed that Subject is not connected at all any time in their office and certification from PRC stated that Subject does not appear in the database of Real State Brokers. Subject was brought for inquest proceeding before the Office of the City Prosecutor, Las Piñas City for Estafa in relation to RA 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012) and violation of RA 9646 (Real Estate Service Act of the Philippines). In three (3) successful operations, the NBI-Intellectual Property Rights Division (NBI-IPRD) seized various counterfeit products with an aggregate amount of Php 1,090,000.00 by virtue of Search Warrants. On August 15, 2018 , Php 500,000 worth of counterfeit Harris welding and cutting equipment were seized in Paranaque City. Charges for violation of RA 8293 (Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines) were filed against Tiger Enzo Enterprises and the proprietor/owner/manager/custodian/operator of the store and storage facility/warehouse located at Unit F time Square Building, Brgy. San Dionisio, Paranaque City. On August 24, 2018 , more or less Php 60,000 worth of empty sacks of rice were seized in Tondo, Manila and Dasmarinas, Cavite. Charges for violation of RA 8293 (Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines) were filed against John/Jane Does, owners and operators of various warehouses located in the said areas. On August 28, 2018 , Php 30,000 worth of medical books were seized in Cebu City. C&E Publishing, Inc. filed a complaint against Cebu Navs Books and Supplies for selling pirated medical books and reviewers, distribution of which is exclusively licensed by McGraw-Hill and Elsevier to C&E Publishing. An entrapment operation was then conducted which resulted in the arrest of MR. WILLIAM ALMACIN JR and the seizure of the said pirated books. Charges for violation of Copyright or Economic Rights of RA 8293 (Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines) were filed against the Subject.

Charges for violation of RA 9208 (Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2003) as ameded by RA 10364 (Expanded Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2012) were filed against the Subjects. On August 7, 2018 , operatives of NBI-Western Visayas Regional Office (NBI-WEVRO) arrested RONALD G. BARNIZO for RA 10591 (Comprehensive Firearms and Ammunition Regulation Act), Article 177 (Usurpation of Authority) of the Revised Penal Code as amended. The case stemmed from a report that Subject and his cohorts are reported to have been possessing unlicensed firearms and posing as NBI agents, promising their supposed clients that they have the capacity to take care their concerns before the Department of Justice where NBI is an attached agency. Investigation and validation were conducted and it was found out that Subject and his cohorts are involved in extortion rackets posing as NBI agents. With this, an enforcement operation of Search Warrant was conducted in the Subject’s residence located at Brgy. Man It, Passi City, Iloilo. Various firearms and live ammunitions were seized in possession, control, and custody of the Subject. Subject is presently detained at the NBI-WEVRO pending the filing of charges against the Subject. On August 7, 2018 , operatives of NBI-International Operations Division (NBI-IOD) arrested MICHAEL ROSS CONROY and TERESITA MENDOZA-CONROY City for Estafa and violations of BP 22. Subjects enticed complainants to invest in their computer software company by making them a part owner and promising a hefty return of their investment. Complainants Dominico Lancian, Jr. and Jakerson Gargallo, disclosed that Subjects offered them to invest THREE HUNDRED THOUSAND PESOS (300,000.00) each with a promised return of FORTY-TWO MILLION PESOS (42,000,000.00) for every investment, as it will definitely make a return considering that election is near and the program that they are told to sell can be used for political campaigns. Records of the Bureau showed that Subjects have warrant of arrest issued by the Regional Trial Court Branch 134 Makati City and upon verification found out that the court has already issued a new warrant of arrest against the Subjects for service of sentence having already been convicted for the crime of Estafa. Derogatory records of the Subjects also revealed that they have other warrants of arrest issued by courts of Makati City, Marawi City and Cabadbaran City for the same crime/violations. With all the information and proper authority to serve the arrest warrant, operatives implemented the same and arrested the Subjects at the meeting place set by the Subjects at La Verti Residences North Tower. Subjects were brought to the office for standard operating procedures and was turned over to NBI-Jail. Subject was arrested in entrapment operation which stemmed from a report that illegal jueteng operations were being conducted and proliferates in the municipality of Tumauni, Isabela. Acting on the operation, surveillance operations were conducted confirming the said information. During the operation, Subject was caught collecting bets under the guise of Sahara collectors. Seized and recovered from Subject’s possession were bills and coins as well as gambling paraphernalia. Subject underwent proper booking procedure after the arrest. Operatives of NBI-CTD regularly conduct internet surveillance of various social media and other websites to monitor, track, and if possible, interdict the persons responsible. body: PRESS STATEMENT October 13, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } The National Bureau of Investigation-International Airport Investigation Division (NBI-IAID), under the leadership of NBI Director Judge Jaime B. Santiago (Ret.), arrested an individual in Pasay City for illegal recruitment and human trafficking. On October 11, 2025, Subject ABDULLAH TAHER ASNAWI, together with a 20-year old woman, was intercepted at NAIA Terminal I by Immigration Officers. They were bound for Saudi Arabia but were intercepted as their names were included in the active OFL (Offloading) record, with the instruction to refer them to IPROBES for strict assessment. Investigation disclosed that Subject ASNAWI recruited the 20-year old woman despite the latter being not allowed to work in Saudi Arabia due to age requirement. Subject ASNAWI then suggested they use an Umrah Visa. They were initially cleared for departure by Immigration Officer JOHN REY FADROGANI, but were later flagged down. Verification with the Licensing and Regulations Bureau of the Department of Migrant Workers (DMW) revealed that ABDULLAH TAHER ASNAWI is not licensed nor authorized to recruit workers for overseas employment. Accordingly, Subject ASNAWI committed the crime of trafficking by recruiting, transporting, and facilitating travel by means of fraud or deception, and took advantage of the victim’s financial vulnerability for the purpose of labor exploitation. Consequently, ABDULLAH TAHER ASNAWI was placed under arrest. He was apprised of his constitutional rights and underwent the standard operating procedure. He was presented for inquest proceedings before the Inquest Prosecutor of Pasay City for violation of R.A. No. 9208 (Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2003) as amended, R.A. No. 8042 (Migrant Workers and Overseas Filipinos Act of 1995) as amended by R.A. No. 10022. He was thereafter turned over to the NBI Detention Center in Muntinlupa. On the other hand, Immigration Officer JOHN REY FADROGANI, who is currently at large, was recommended for prosecution for violation of Section 5(e) of R.A. No. 9208, as amended, for allowing, clearing, and facilitating the exit from the country of the victim without valid working permits or documents or complying governmental requirements for the purpose of subjecting them her for labor exploitation.

body: PRESS STATEMENT October 21, 2024 The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI), under the leadership of NBI Director Judge Jaime B. Santiago (Ret.), arrested two (2) foreign nationals for violation of RA 9208 (Anti Trafficking in Persons Act of 2003). On 07 October 2024, CRID received a complaint from a certain JINWEN YANG (YANG) alleging that his friend SIAW PING LIM (LIM) a.k.a. SHOWSHOW, a Malaysian National, is being held against her will and is trafficked by her Chinese employer/boss MA SHANG LAI (LAI). Per the complainant, the company operates an online scamming enterprise inside a residential house in Greenwoods Village, Taytay, Rizal. There are other call center employees, all foreigners, who are similarly situated with that of the victim. They are all housed in the residential building and are not allowed to go out of the premises at will. The employer refuses to give back her passport, thus, deterring her plans to leave or escape from her employer’s place. With dispatch, CRID conducted a series of surveillance operations on the suspected place where LAl holds office. After ascertaining the alleged location and considering the urgency of the situation, CRID hatched a plan to conduct a rescue operation. Thus, at around 11:55 P.M. of 16 October 2024, CRID operatives, after completing all the operational procedures, rescued the victim inside the subject’s establishment in Meadowood Street, Greenwoods Executive Village, Taytay, Rizal. In sum, four (4) individuals were rescued while two (2) Chinese nationals were arrested. They were later all brought to the office of CRID for proper booking and identification procedures. The arrested individuals, namely; WANG KUN and LIU XIAO XIAO were duly afforded of their Constitutional Rights. Meanwhile, LAI was not present during the operation and remains at large but was not spared from a criminal complaint considering his participation as LIM’s employer. On 18 October 2024, respondents, WANG KUN and LIU XIAO XIAO were presented for Inquest Proceedings before the Provincial Prosecutor’s Office of Rizal. Aside from LIM, LIN DONG BAI, LI TAN and GAN LIN LONG, all Chinese nationals, also joined as complainants in a criminal complaint for violation of Section 4 of Republic Act No.9208 (Anti Trafficking in Persons Act of 2003) as amended.

body: A former employee of a closed rural bank who kept without authority dozens of land titles and demanded money for their redemption was apprehended by agents of the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) during an entrapment in Bukidnon last week. The suspects were identified by NBI Director Nonnatus Caesar R. Rojas as: ALFREDO ALEJO CABARDO JR., a resident of Puro 17-A, Valencia City, Bukidnon. Investigation conducted by the NBI Anti-Fraud and Action Division (AFAD) headed by HA Cesar Bacani in coordination with the Northeastern Mindanao Regional Office (NEMRO), disclosed that on June 4, 2013, complainants Cerilo D. Espelita and Mary Ann C. Crisostomo, an official of the Philippine Deposit Insurance Corporation (PDIC) filed a complaint against suspect Cabardo. In 2000, Espelita obtained a loan of P303,500 for a reconditioned truck from Southeast Asia Motors Corp. (SAMC) in Valencia City, Bukidnon. As security for the loan, Espelita and his wife executed a blank real estate mortgage over a property covered by Original Certificate of Title (OCT) No. AO-1554 registered under the complainant’s deceased father, Jose C. Espelita in favor of Philippine Farmers Bank (PFB). The PFB was ordered closed by Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas on 17 September 2009 and was under the receivership of the Philippine Deposit Insurance Corporation (PDIC). Thereafter, complainant learned from PDIC that he has still outstanding loan balance which he needs to pay in order that the Official Receipt (OR) and Certificate of Registration (CR) of this truck will be given to him. However, he was also informed that OCT No. AO-1554 was marked “missing on file” and was not included in the inventory of titles which were turned-over to the PDIC. On May 26, 2013, Cabardo visited Espelita in his residence in Kalilangan, Bukidnon and informed him that OCT No. A-1554 is in their possession. Cabardo then asked the complainant to redeem it for P6,000, the amount allegedly he still owed from the PFB including the so-called “SOP” amount of P3,000. Due to suspicion of irregularity, Espelita sought the advice of the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP) who endorsed the case to the NBI-AFAD because Cabardo has no authority to possess, transact nor convey the said OCT since all assets including collateral titles of borrowers of PFBI are deemed in custodia legis and should be turned over to the PDIC as statutory receiver. On June 4, 2013, Cabardo called Espelita to meet him in Valencia City, Bukidnon the next day if he is really keen in getting back the OCT. With this information, an entrapment was planned. title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: In line with the relentless campaign of the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) against human trafficking, the NBI today said operatives of NBI-International Airport Investigation Unit (NBI-IAIU) have arrested three (3) human traffickers and rescued one hundred thirty seven (137) female victims in Pasay City last Saturday. NBI Director Dante A. Gierran identified the Subjects as PATRICIA LAMBINO a.k.a. “Mommy”, ROSIE LOPEZ and MARILYN FILOMENO. The three subjects were arrested in a rescue operation based on an information received by the NBI from a minor who was turned over by DSWD on May 4, 2018. The said 16-year old minor was intercepted by Immigration Officers for attempting to travel to Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. Investigation revealed that the minor was recruited in her home province of Maguindanao. She was able to get a passport through the help of one Pamiya Muhammad and who made it appear therein that she was twenty three (23) years old. She said that she stayed in an apartment at Tolentino St., Pasay City that was provided by Global Connect Manpower Resources, the recruitment agency facilitating her deployment abroad. Certificates on TESDA training and pre-departure seminar were given to her by the said recruitment agency even though she did not attend the training and seminar. According to her, she has a friend, also a minor, and others who are still in the apartment and are due for deployment abroad. Acting on the information under strict instructions from Director Gierran, the NBI-IAIU operatives, together with representatives from the Inter-Agency Council Against Trafficking (IACAT) and DSWD, proceeded to Pasay City to rescue the female victims. Found and rescued in the apartment are a total of 137 female-victims. Out of thirty nine (39) rescued who appear young and had undergone examination, twenty nine (29) were found to be minors who came from the provinces of Maguindanao, Sultan Kudarat, Lanao Del Sur, and Cotabato. The three (3) arrested Subjects were likewise identified by the minor-victims as the ones who were in charge while they were staying in the apartment and who instructed them in going to Pasay City from their provinces. All the Subjects were brought before the Department of Justice, Manila for Inquest proceedings for violations of RA 9208 (Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2003) as amended by RA 10364 (Expanded Anti-Human Trafficking in Persons Act of 2012) and RA 8042 (Migrant Workers and Overseas Filipinos Act of 1995).

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) has recommended before the Department of Justice the filing of criminal charges against seven (7) officials and staff of Tricity Medical Center for fraudulent claims from Philippine Health Insurance Corporation (PhilHealth). NBI-Officer-In-Charge (OIC) Director Eric B. Distor identified the Subjects as ENRICO C. CRUZ, M.D., Hospital Administrator and a Member of the Board of Directors of Tricity Medical Center, Dr. GJAY LALU ORDINAL, Dr. FROILAN ANTONIO DE LEON and Dr. LOURDES RHODA REYES PADILLA, all of whom are doctors of Tricity Medical Center, CHERRY CATALAN FLORES, R.N. of the hospital, ARLENE JOY G. SEBUC, Philhealth Staff of Tricity Medical Center, and SVEND AGODILOS RANCES, hospital clerk. Director Distor said that the investigation stemmed from an intelligence information received by the NBI-Anti Graft Division (NBI-AGD) on January 8, 2020, alleging that Tricity Medical Center, Inc. situated in Pasig City has been fraudulently facilitating or claiming reimbursement from PhilHealth for its supposed hemodialysis patients which turned out to be non-existent or deceased already at the time of the supposed hemodialysis treatment. Under the direct authority of the Director, the NBI-AGD conducted an investigation to determine the veracity of the information and to arrest those who are responsible for the fraudulent claims. Thorough investigation conducted by the NBI-AGD, which took more than a year revealed that there was at least 318 Fraudulent Claims with a total amount of Php 824,200.00 filed by Tricity Medical Center based on recorded dates of Hemodialysis Treatment after the death of patients. NBI-AGD also emphasized that its thorough investigation showed a strong possibility that the fraudulent claims could be higher is highly probable based on the 2016 to 2019 Philhealth Database which showed a total of Php 4,308,000.00 involving the above-mentioned patients. Thus, on September 20, the NBI-AGD recommended the filing of charges against the seven (7) Subjects before the Department of Justice (DOJ) for Estafa defined and penalized under Article 315 (2) of the Revised Penal Code (RPC, as amended; and violation of Section 44 of R.A. 7875, otherwise known as the “National Health Insurance Act of 2013, as amended by Republic No. 9241 and R.A. 10606.

body: PRESS STATEMENT December 03, 2024 On December 2, 2024, operatives of the National Bureau of Investigation – Criminal Intelligence Division (CRID), Counter Terrorism Division (CTD), Counter Intelligence Division (CID) and Intelligence Research and Analysis Division (IRAD), under the guidance of NBI Director JUDGE JAIME B. SANTIAGO (Ret.), served an alias warrant of arrest issued by the Regional Trial Court (RTC) – Caloocan against ANWAR ROMUROS y ABEDIN aka ANOUAR ABEDIN ROMUROS ABDULRAUF for murder and attempted murder. Director Santiago said that Subject Romuros is an incumbent Vice Mayor of the City of Marawi and is now using the name Anouar A. Abdulrauf to evade arrest. The Subject was arrested at the Hall of Justice in Marawi City after the flag-raising ceremony at Marawi City Hall. The arrest was made possible with the help of the Philippine Army of the 103rd Infantry Army, Task Force Marawi of Marawi City, and Task Force Oro of Cagayan De Oro City. The cases for murder and attempted murder were filed by the wife of the slain victim, Latip Sultan. The witness in the case Abdulraof Alim Dimaporo positively identified the incumbent vice mayor of Marawi City as the same person Anouar Abedin Romuros Abdulrauf, one of the accused in the aforementioned cases. The killing of the victim happened during a legitimate service of a Search Warrant for violation of RA 9165 (Dangerous Drugs Act) by NBI CID-IS in Tala, Caloocan City in 2013. The NBI operatives were already implementing the Search Warrant when a group of armed individuals led by the Subject opened fire at the operatives killing the victim and wounding others. Other co-accused in the said cases are still at large and a continued manhunt operation is being conducted. Director Santiago commended the NBI operating units as well as the Philippine Army of the 103rd Infantry Army, Task Force Marawi of Marawi City, and Task Force Oro of Cagayan De Oro City for the implementation of the warrant of arrest.

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today said it has seized a total of Php 143 Million worth of counterfeit items in series of successive operations. The NBI said the operations were conducted by operatives of the Intellectual Property Rights Division (NBI-IPRD) and Anti-Fraud Division (NBI-AFD) on various stalls in shopping centers located in Dau, Mabalacat Pampanga, Quezon City, Manila, Greenhills, San Juan and a warehouse in Binan, Laguna. The IPRD operations were conducted on the strength of the Search Warrants issued by the Manila Regional Trial Court (RTC) Branch 46 and Pasig Regional Trial Court Branch 159 that resulted in the seizure of fake GIBSON shoes worth about P418,500.00 and Personal Computers loaded with unlicensed Autocad software with an estimated value of P6.6 Million, respectively. The case stemmed from a complaint by Mr. Antonio Andres Jr. that certain establishments in Dau and Mabalacat Pampanga were engaged in sale and distribution of shoes/boots, bearing the trademark “GIBSON”. Shoes being sold in the said establishments are allegedly from China, and imitating products of GIBSON’S, a company located in Marikina City which provides uniform footwear for the Armed Forces of the Philippines and the Philippine National Police. Acting on the complaint, a discreet surveillance was conducted on the suspected establishments particularly Ria & Edsel Store and Tess Galang Store located in Dau Shopping Center, Dau, Pampanga. After confirming the items as counterfeit by a product exprert and the corresponding Search Warrants were secured, an operation was conducted resulting in the seizure of the counterfeit products. Another operation conducted by the IPRD group on January 27, 2016, led to the seizure of Personal Computers loaded with unlicensed Autocad Software owned by URE-SHII TECHNOLOGIES and/or TOCHIGI-KEN TECHNOLOGIES INTERNATIONAL, INC located in Mile Business Park Brgy. Maduya, Carmona, Cavite. The case stemmed from a complaint of Autodesk Corporation, represented by Quisumbing Torres Law Office, against URE-SHII TECHNOLOGIES and/or TOCHIGI-KEN TECHNOLOGIES INTERNATIONAL, INC. Operatives of the Anti-Fraud Division, on the other hand, seized on January 27 and 28, 2016) seized 4,130 pieces of counterfeit Burberry, Bvlgari and Chanel products with an approximate amount of Php136.17 Million in various stalls at different shopping centers located in Manila and Greenhills, San Juan on the strength of Search Warrant issued by Manila Regional Trial Court (RTC) Branch 46 Presiding Judge Rainelda H. Estacio-Montesa. The AFD said the case stemmed from a complaint of See Hock Heng aka J See. Charges for Violation of Copyright Infringement under Section 177 in relation to 217 of R.A. 8293 otherwise known as the Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines are now being prepared against the Subjects in the series of operations.

body: On October 11, 2020, operatives of NBI-Southeastern Mindanao Regional Office (NBI-SEMRO) arrested eleven (11) individuals involved in the maintenance and operation of illegal cockfight at Sitio Malagamot, Brgy. Panacan, Davao City. Subject were presented for inquest proceedings for violation of PD 449 (Cockfighting Law of the Philippines) and PD 1602 (A Decree for Stiffer Illegal Gambling Penalties). They are temporarily detained at NBI-SEMRO for custody and safekeeping. On October 12, 2020, operatives of NBI-Samar District Office (NBI-SAMDO) arrested GRACHEL FLORES DANTE and LEMUEL PAROLI RESCO for Human Trafficking. Subjects were arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from an information that Wacky’s Pension House in Catbalogan City, Samar is offering women, including minors, to its guests. Surveillance operation conducted by NBI-SAMDO operatives confirmed the said illegal activity wherein poseur-customers were offered by Subject GRACHEL with two (2) girls with sex service fee of Php 1,000.00 each. Upon confirming the illegal and exploitative acts committed against the victims, NBI-SAMDO operatives conducted an operation on the above-mentioned date to apprehend the pimps engaged in human trafficking. Subject LEMUEL showed pictures of women to the poseur-customers. The price of each girl is Php 3,000.00 for single sex service. After completing the transaction, operatives effected the arrest of the Subjects. Charges for violation of RA 9208 (Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act) as amended by RA 10364 (Expanded Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act) and RA 7610 (Special Protection of Children Against Child Abuse, Exploitation and Discrimination Act) were filed against the arrested Subjects. On October 13, 2020, operatives of NBI-Central Visayas Regional Office (NBI-CEVRO) arrested ARMANDO UGSANG y DOBLE, LEONEL RIVERA y DEMECILLO, JUNREY ROSALES y CONSEJA, WELFREDO JORDAN JR. y GELLIDO, SERAFEN ABEAR y LLENYADO, BELMAR LABARDOR y LLENYADO, and LORETO MAPAIT y MANTOS in a buy-bust operation conducted at Sitio Back Blessed, Brgy. Tejero, Cebu City which also includes neutralization of two (2) drug dens. Subjects BERMAR was caught in flagrante delicto handling three (3) small sachets of shabu while Subjects ARMANDO and SERAFEN were the maintainer of the said drug dens. The rest were arrested for visiting the drug den and using the dangerous drug. Charges for violation of RA 9165 (Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act) were filed against the arrested Subjects. On October 13, 2020, operatives of NBI-Anti-Organized and Transnational Crime Division (NBI-AOTCD) arrested MALBERT MARCOS for duping people by introducing himself as the son of the late President Ferdinand Marcos. Subject misrepresented himself as the son of former president Ferdinand E. Marcos and duped people by presenting fake gold bullion certificates and getting donations in return of trillion of dollars he is going to give back once he allegedly gets the Marcos wealth deposited in Switzerland, London and New York, USA. Record check on Subject MALBERT MARCOS revealed that he has an outstanding Warrant of Arrest for Carnapping issued by RTC Branch 88, Quezon City dated May 3, 2019. On the above-mentioned date, Subject MALBERT MARCOS was arrested by virtue of Warrant of Arrest at No.5 Royal Avenue, Vermont Executive Village, Marcos Highway, Mayamot, Antipolo City, Rizal. Subject is currently detained at the NBI Jail. Further investigation is being conducted to ascertain the true name and identity of MALBERT ALBERTO MARCOS. On October 15, 2020, operatives of NBI-Saranggani District Office (NBI-SARDO) arrested ALDY “JOJO” PLAERA and ROGEN LOPEZ for illegal selling of petroleum products. An owner of a legitimate petroleum dealer and a client of Sea Oil Depot Petroleum Products at Sta. body: On May 30, 2018, the 12-year old minor victim, accompanied by her guardian, filed a case against her father for Rape. Included in the complaint were the victim’s grandmother and aunt. The victim narrated the incestuous act of her father who destroyed her purity and trust by repeatedly raping and making her his sex slave from January 1, 2017 until March 14, 2018. The beastly act of her father left her in quandary as to where and who to run to every time she is being sexually used and abused. With her mother in Oman, Jordan working as OFW, she decided to suffer in silence and painstakingly lived each day being devoured by the incestuous lust of her father. On May 20, 2018, she finally mustered enough courage to tell her mother who was then on a short vacation, her grandmother, and her aunt, that she is being repeatedly raped by her father. Before leaving for Oman, victim’s mother entrusted her to a guardian and requested the latter to do whatever necessary legal action to bring the father to justice. Victim’s grandmother and aunt brought her to the hospital for genital check-up where it was confirmed that the minor victim is no longer a virgin. However, much to the victim’s surprise, instead of standing up to defend her honor, the grandmother convinced her to point to somebody else as the one who raped her, and her aunt also suggested not to disclose the result of her check-up to her mother. Worse, in an attempt to cover-up the crime committed, the grandmother tried to convince the doctor to change the result of the examination and to make it appear that the victim is still a virgin. This fact was attested by the doctor who also executed a statement. Record check on the Subjects disclosed that the father has a bench warrant of arrest for Reckless Imprudence Resulting in Damage to Property issued on April 18, 2005. Arrested Subjects are presently detained at the NBI Detention Cell.

body: PRESS STATEMENT August 20, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } PRESS RELEASE | NBI ARRESTS HIGH-END PIMP IN MAKATI CITY; RESCUES 1 BEAUTY QUEEN, 5 RUSSIAN NATIONALS FROM SEXUAL TRAFFICKING Pasay City, Philippines – To intensify the campaign against human trafficking, the National Bureau of Investigation-International Operations Division (NBI-IOD) arrested an individual in Makati City for violating Republic Act No. 10364 (Expanded Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2012). NBI Director Melvin Matibag praised the dedicated agents of NBI-IOD for their diligent efforts, which significantly contributed to the operation’s success. He reiterated the NBI’s unwavering commitment to its core mandate of combating human trafficking, emphasizing the agency’s relentless efforts to identify, rescue, and support victims who have been exploited and manipulated by traffickers. The operation stemmed from reliable information alleging that a certain individual is engaged in the sexual exploitation of women for commercial sex. Allegedly, the victims include pageant titleholders, artists, and models, including foreign nationals, who are allegedly being maintained and offered for commercial sexual exploitation at various hourly or overnight rates. The services offered include companionship travel, both local and international. The undercover agent established contact with the Subject and arranged a booking for women offered for sexual services. The Subject agreed to provide women at a discounted rate of Php25,000.00 each, plus commission. They agreed to meet on August 12, 2026, at a condominium in Makati to deliver the women. On the aforementioned date, the agents of NBI-IOD proceeded to the agreed meeting place and positioned themselves discreetly. Upon handing over the marked money to the Subject, the agents immediately arrested him. During the entrapment operation, the agents rescued six (6) trafficked victims, including a beauty queen and five (5) Russian nationals. The rescued victims were turned over to the Makati City Social Welfare and Development Officer for appropriate aftercare services, assessment, and other necessary interventions. https://www.facebook.com/reel/1240016074910653

body: The relentless crackdown against international drug syndicates scored anew following the arrest of a Malaysian drug courier or human mule, and the confiscation of P15 million worth of shabu during an operation by operatives of the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) in Pasay City over the week-end. The suspect was identified by NBI Officer-In-Charge Atty. Nonnatus Caesar R. Rojas as: BING SYE POH , 37, Malaysian national, and a resident of 347 Jalan Bk 2/7 Bandar Kurara, Puchong, Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia. SInvestigation conducted by the Reaction, Arrest and Interdiction Division (RAID) headed by Atty. Ross Jonathan V. Galicia led to the discovery of the WADS cell which utilizes Vietnamese, Malaysian and Filipino drug couriers to smuggle methamphetamine hydrochloride or shabu from Africa to the Philippines. The syndicate uses different nationalities to deliver or pick up the drugs to mislead authorities of their modus operandi. Earlier, an information was received by the NBI that a West African Drug Syndicate (WADS) based in Africa shipped into the country an undetermined quantity of cocaine and shabu on March 23, 2012. A courier by the name of Bing Sye Poh was sent by the group to the Philippines via Air Asia Flight No. AK 1438, Clark Terminal, Pampanga to pick up the luggage/suitcase and transport it to its final destination. Poh was billeted at Crosswinds Asian Hotel in Parañaque area. NBI operatives continued to check his whereabouts. At 12:00 noon of March 23, 2012, Poh was spotted en route to the said hotel. He checked-in using the name Bing Sye Poh “David.” Minutes after checking-in, NBI operatives saw him leaving the hotel and boarded a taxi without any luggage. NBI agents discreetly trailed him. Poh alighted along Buendia corner Harrison St., Pasay City and was seen entering a private compound. Minutes later, Poh came out carrying a brown leather luggage/suitcase and boarded a taxi not knowing that the driver is an NBI agent. Poh instructed him to proceed to the hotel. However, while traversing along Taft Avenue before reaching the intersection of EDSA , Rotonda, Pasay City, Poh alighted from the taxi. He placed his luggage at the sidewalk and started running in the middle of the road towards EDSA prompting the NBI operatives and gave chase. He was eventually caught inside a supermarket along EDSA, Pasay City. When questioned, Poh disowned the luggage and allegedly was only requested by his friend “Pepe”, also a Malaysian national to come to the Philippines and pick up a luggage from a certain person with codename “666” and bring it to Malaysia in consideration of US$1,500. Charges for violation of Section 5 (Transportation of Dangerous Drugs) Art. II of RA 9165 (The Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2001) were filed against the suspect before the Pasay City Prosecutor’s Office.

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today said operatives of NBI-Special Action Unit (NBI-SAU) arrested an individual in Quezon City on July 23, 2021 for posing as NBI Agent and extorting money. NBI Officer-In-Charge (OIC) Director Eric B. Distor identified the Subject as CHARLESTONE MESA CAÑALES. OIC Director Distor said the case stemmed from a complaint filed against the Subject for alleged Usurpation of Authority, Extortion, and violation of the Anti-Red Tape Act of 2007. According to the complainant, they were having a legal problem with the seller of their purchased dump truck, wherein despite having received the down payment failed to deliver the same as agreed. As such, they asked for somebody who could help them initiate legal action against the seller. A complainant’s friend then introduced them to CAÑALES who introduced himself as an NBI Agent. CAÑALES allegedly assured the complainant that they could help them solve their problem. However, complainant was surprised when CAÑALES demanded Php 200,000 as mobilization fee. Sensing that CAÑALES is not a real NBI Agent, they reported the matter before the NBI-SAU. Acting on the complaint, an entrapment operation was hatched. NBI-SAU operatives instructed the complainant to contact CAÑALES and ask the latter to lower the amount being demanded. CAÑALES agreed to receive an initial amount of Php 100,00 on the condition that the remaining balance later on. On July 23, 2021, NBI-SAU operatives proceeded at the parking lot of a bank in Brgy. Lourdes, Quezon City and strategically positioned themselves in the area. Minutes after, CAÑALES arrived at the area on board a taxi wearing NBI jacket. Thereafter, complainant, approached CAÑALES and handed over the marked money to which the latter received. Upon seeing that Subject received the marked money, NBI-SAU operatives approached CAÑALES, introduced themselves as NBI operatives, apprised CAÑALES of his constitutional rights, and placed the latter under arrest. Seized from the Subject are the marked money, NBI badge, smart phone, jacket with NBI logo, voter’s ID under the name CAÑALES, CHARLESTON MESA, a black holster, and facemask with NBI logo. CAÑALES was brought to the NBI for the standard booking procedures. NBI Personnel Division issued a certification that the name CHARLESTONE MESA CAÑALES does not appear in the roster of NBI employees. CHARLESTONE MESA CAÑALES was presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor, Quezon City for Robbery/Extortion, Usurpation of Authority/Official Functions and violation of RA 9485 otherwise known as the Anti-Red Tape Act of 2007.

As such, they asked for somebody who could help them initiate legal action against the seller. A complainant’s friend then introduced them to CAÑALES who introduced himself as an NBI Agent. NBI-SAU operatives instructed the complainant to contact CAÑALES and ask the latter to lower the amount being demanded. Lourdes, Quezon City and strategically positioned themselves in the area. Minutes after, CAÑALES arrived at the area on board a taxi wearing NBI jacket. body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today said operatives of NBI-Counter Terrorism Division (NBI-CTD) have arrested a couple selling fake NBI IDs and other documents in Quezon City yesterday. Subject SOLOMON VILORIA y LEGASPI, an employee of the Office of the Civil Defense under the Department of National Defense, is a subject of an intelligence report engaged in illegally scanning, manufacturing and printing the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) documents and other items, and sells these through recruitment into an alleged NBI Civilian Agent Group which he supposedly leads himself. The arrested Subject claims to be an organic or active NBI Agent or NBI Intelligence Agent assigned to the Counter Terrorism Division (CTD, and Special Investigator (SI) assigned at the Counter Intelligence Division, which he blatantly professed interchangeably. After a series of undercover operations, CTD operatives were able to meet the Subject in a restaurant in Quezon City where he misrepresented himself as an Intelligence Agent of the CTD before the undercover operatives presently assigned at CTD. There, Subject SOLOMON VILORIA y LEGASPI presented the firearm he was selling together with the NBI identification cards, Mission Order and Permit to Possess and Carry Firearms. body: In line with the relentless drive of the government against illegal drugs, government agents from National Bureau of Investigation-International Airport Investigation Division (NBI-IAID), PDEA, BOC, and PNP Aviation Security Group, arrested an individual who claimed a package from Malaysia containing illegal drugs. NBI Officer-In-Charge (OIC) Director Eric B. Distor identified the Subject as 34-year old KRISTOPHER CARLOS SEGUMBANG y SABALZA. Subject was arrested in a controlled delivery operation participated by operatives of NBI-IAID as member of the NAIA-Inter-Agency Drug Interdiction Task Group (IADITG). Distor said that the operation stemmed from the discovery of an inbound parcel from Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia, shipped by one Simon via FedEx and consigned to a certain NICK DIMAGIBA of Bagbaguin, Caloocan City. The package, which was declared snacks containing fifteen (15) pieces of sealed Kopiko L.A., contained a total of 622 grams of dangerous drugs Ketamine. Distor stressed the same was previously intercepted by the Bureau of Customs (BOC) at NAIA. The drugs have an estimated value of Php 3,110,000.00. The NAIA-IADITG was alerted of the said package and a controlled delivery operation was then put in place for the arrest of the named consignee and his possible cohorts. In the morning of May 17, 2021, operatives positioned themselves around the premises of Bagbaguin, Talipapa Wet and Dry Market, Caloocan City. At about noon, subject SEGUMBANG, a resident of Kaingin St., Barangay Parada, Valenzuela City, claimed the package. At this juncture, he was arrested and informed of his rights under the law. He was presented for In inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor, Caloocan City for violation of RA 9165 (Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002).

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today announced the arrest of three (3) individuals by the NBI-Task Force Against Illegal Drugs (NBI-TFAID) in Quezon City on June 30, 2021 for selling COVID-19 vaccines. NBI Officer-In-Charge (OIC) Director Eric B. Distor identified the subjects as HARJIT KOUR GONZALES SINGH, ALEXIS FRANCO DE GUZMAN, and CALVIN MAXIMILLIAN YEUNG ROCA. OIC Director Distor said that the operation stemmed from an information that a certain Harjit is selling COVID-19 vaccines, specifically, Sinovac vaccines. Acting on the said information, NBI-TFAID operatives conducted a series surveillance operations, undercover work, and interviews. Sometime after, the informant again forwarded an information that Subject Harjit has in her possession 300 doses of Sinovac vaccines available for P840,000.00 and that she needs to sell it within the week. NBI-TFAID then communicated with the subject to order and subsequently planned an entrapment operation. The NBI-TFAID operatives were able to place an order from the subject and agreed to meet in Amoranto Sr. St. in Quezon City. Thus, on June 30, 2021, NBI-TFAID operatives proceeded to the target meeting area to hand over the money in exchange for the 300 doses of Sinovac. One of the operatives who acted as poseur-buyer together with the informants met with Subject Harjit and her group inside their SUV vehicle parked along Amoranto Sr. St. and handed over the marked money to Subject Harjit while her two (2) male companions wait near the said SUV. After hand over of money, Subject Harjit took the vaccines contained in a styrophore and transferred it to the operative’s vehicle. After the consummation of the transaction, the undercover agent gave a pre-arranged signal to the other operatives and immediately rushed into the area where they apprehended Subject Harjit and her two (2) companions identified as De Guzman and Roca. The operation also resulted in the seizure of 300 doses of Sinovac, boodle money, cellphones, vehicle, and identification cards. The operatives were able to identify Subject ALEXIS DE GUZMAN as a government employee of the City of Manila assigned at Gat Andres Bonifacio Memorial Medical Center as Nurse. The Subjects were brought to the NBI office for the standard booking procedure. They were presented for Inquest proceedings before the Departmemt of Justice on July 2, 2021 for violation of R.A. 9711 otherwise known as The Food nd Drug Administration Act.

title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: Consistent with National Bureau of Investigation’s drive against all kinds of crimes, NBI-Isabela District Office (NBI-ISDO) have arrested two individuals and filed charges against several others for using DITO Telecom Corporation (DITO) in fraudulent acts. NBI Officer-in-Charge (OIC) Director Eric B. Distor identified the main Subjects as FELIDO C. BAUTISTA, JULIET BAUTISTA, RYAN BAUTISTA, and FLORENCIO PADERNAL SR. Also included are the employees of B. BAUTISTA QUALITY CONSTRUCTION BUILDERS, INC. who claims to be connected with DITO. Distor said that the case stemmed from information received by NBI-ISDO regarding an alleged telecommunication fraud syndicate victimizing landowners in the province of Isabela and some parts of Region 2. According to the informant, a certain ENGR. FELIDO “BOBOT” C. BAUTISTA of B. BAUTISTA QUALITY CONSTRUCTION BUILDERS, INC. located in Santiago City, is claiming to be the lead contractor of DITO. The said scammer and fake civil engineer has defrauded individuals in Isabela province with his scheme. The modus operandi of Subject BAUTISTA is to make representations as having the authority and capacity to identify and approve certain land areas in Region 2 for the construction of DITO towers. Allegedly, the respective areas will be leased by DITO on a lump sum offer of P3 Million to P3.5 Million for ten years subject to renewal. Those who will qualify with the specifications of the desired land area are required to present and submit photocopies of documents needed such as land title, tax declaration, and valid ID. Thereafter, qualified landowners are being compelled to pay an amount ranging from P60,000 to P65,000 for relocation, back fill and vicinity map. However, since 2020, the promised construction of DITO towers did not materialize. Certification from the Professional Regulation Commission (PRC) in Tuguegarao City, Cagayan revealed that the name FELIDO C. BAUTISTA does not appear in the database of all Engineering professions who are authorized to practice Engineering in the Philippines. On the other hand, verification with DITO revealed that FELIDO BAUTISTA is not an authorized agent, contractor, or sub-contractor of DITO. With these, on July 6, 2021, poseur- landowner applicant inquired in B. Bautista’s office where RYAN BAUTISTA, son of FELIDO BAUTISTA, discussed the corresponding requirements. On July 9, 2021, a follow-up transaction transpired in the same office where the poseur-landowner applicant was entertained by a staff identified as JULIET “JHET” BAUTISTA, wife of FELIDO BAUTISTA, who discussed some processes and the corresponding payment. After confirming the Subjects’ operation of fraud, Search Warrants were applied for and RTC Second Judicial Region, Santiago City issued the corresponding Search Warrants against FELIDO B. BAUTISTA and all employees of B. BAUTISTA QUALITY CONSTRUCTION BUILDERS, INC. On July 30, 2021, operatives NBI-ISDO implemented the Search Warrants resulting in the seizure of various documents, DITO Tower Perspective View, Table of Organization (DITO Telecommunication Project), list of DITO Tower Cost, Special Power of Attorney/ Authorization as well as computers and other office equipment. Operatives were about to arrest the Subjects when FELIDO BAUTISTA suddenly collapsed prompting the operatives to rush him to the hospital. Due to the commotion in the area of operation, JULIET “JHET” BAUTISTA and some employees managed to flee and elude arrest. RYAN BAUTISTA and FLORENCIO PADERNAL SR., however, were immediately taken into custody, apprised of their rights, and were brought to NBI-ISDO for booking procedures. Subjects were presented for Inquest proceedings before the City Prosecutor’s Office of Santiago City, Isabela for Syndicated Estafa and violation of R.A.544, as amended (Civil Engineering Law).

body: PRESS STATEMENT October 03, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } The National Bureau of Investigation – National Capital Region (NBI-NCR), in an effort to combat the rampant selling of unregistered vape products, arrested a Chinese national identified as KE LIANG and his cohort CHRISTIAN E. CALONSAG in Pasay City for violation of Republic Act No. 11900 (Vaporized Nicotine and Non-nicotine Products Regulation Act). The operation stemmed from information that a certain “Paolo” was illegally selling and distributing unregistered vape/vapor products in Metro Manila. The informant specified that “Paolo” is a Chinese national who sells prohibited products in bulk to interested buyers, with negotiations conducted via cell phone and internet. Acting on the informant’s endorsement, “Paolo” communicated with the poseur-buyer, offering the vape products for Php 1,050.00 each. The poseur-buyer agreed to purchase Php 1,125,000.00 worth of unregistered vape products, and they agreed to meet on September 29, 2025, in Manila. The NBI-NCR agents sought the assistance of the Department of Trade and Industry – Office for the Special Mandate on Vaporized Nicotine and Non-nicotine Products (DTI-OSMV), to carry out the entrapment operation. Operatives then proceeded to the designated meeting location in Manila. While waiting, the poseur-buyer was approached by a male individual who calimed to be sent by his boss “’Paolo’) for “Paolo,” to collect payment before delivering the vape products. The poseur-buyer handed over the entrapment money to this individual and was instructed by “Paolo” to proceed to an establishment in Pasay City for the delivery of the vape products. Upon arrival at the establishment, the male individual delivered the entrapment money to Calonsag, who then passed it on to “Paolo,” later identified as Ke Liang. At that moment, NBI-NCR agents approached and announced the arrest of the two individuals. Subjects Ke Liang and Christian Calonsag were subsequently taken to the NBI-Forensic Chemistry Division (NBI-FCD) for an ultraviolet light examination, which revealed yellow fluorescent specks and smudges on their hands. The arrested individuals were presented for inquest proceedings for violating Republic Act No. 11900. NBI Director Judge Jaime B. Santiago (Ret.) commended the NBI-NCR agents for their successful operation. He likewise expressed gratitude to the officers of DTI-OMV for their invaluable support during the operation.

body: PRESS STATEMENT November 20, 2024 Director Judge Jaime B. Santiago welcomes back graduates of the NBI Academy during the 2024 “Balik Akademya” organized by the NBI Investigators Mutual Benefit Association, Inc. (NBI-IMBAI). The Balik Akademya is celebrated yearly to foster camaraderie and rekindle friendship among all NBI Agents, including retired NBI Agents. Among the notable retired agents include retired Regional Director Crisostomo F. Balancio (Batch 12-Class 1966), former Deputy Director Filomeno S. Bautista (Batch 15-Class 1968) and Ex Judge Domingo Maristela (Batch 19-Class 1972). In his inspirational message, Santiago mentioned to be proactive in investigation and never put the organization in bad light. “Tumaas na ang kredibilidad at tiwala ng taong bayan sa NBI, ituloy tuloy lang natin ang magandang serbisyo para sa bayan,” Santiago said. Meanwhile, as part of the anniversary celebration, the IMBAI came up with the NBI Director’s Cup 2024 (Level II shooting competition) on November 16&17, 2024 at the Iron Sight Shooting Range in Silang, Cavite. The shooting competition has a widest participation from agents and operatives from Luzon, Visayas and Mindanao with a total of 421 shooters. The 2-day event concluded very well with no untoward incident noted. Magmula ngayon weekly na ang shooting natin at libre ang bala, Santiago said during the Monday Directorial Staff Meeting.
