Subjects were arrested in entrapment operation which stemmed from a letter from Cybertower Development Corporation requesting for investigation and possible prosecution against persons who were allegedly selling to the public the real property of the corporation. After proper investigation, the entrapment operation against the officers of SHALOM MOUNTAIN PRIME LANDS CORPORATION was conducted resulting in the arrest of the aforementioned Subjects who received a reservation fee of Php 20,000.00 in relation to the sale of a lot inside a subdivision under the name of Cybertower Development Corporation. Subjects are awaiting for the schedule of inquest proceeding at the City Prosecutor’s Office, Cebu City. Subject was arrested in a buy-bust operation which stemmed from an information regarding the selling of shabu allegedly conducted by a certain alias PRAN-PRAN later identified as FRANZ CHRIS MUTYA y CLAVANO in the area of Brgy. Poblacion, Iligan City. Surveillance operation was conducted confirming that Subject was indeed engaged in selling shabu. On the above-mentioned date, the buy-bust operation was conducted resulting in the arrest of Subject MUTYA. Seized from the Subject were three (3) pieces large size heat sealed rectangular transparent plastic sachets containing white crystalline substance suspected to be shabu, one (1) digital weighing scale, and the marked money. Subject was brought to NBI office for the standard booking procedure. Examination conducted by the Forensic Chemist gave positive results for methamphetamine hydrochloride or shabu. Charges for violation of RA 9165 were filed against the arrested Subject before the Office of the Prosecutor, Iligan City. BERONIO in Brgy. Barra, Opol, Misamis Oriental for selling illegal drugs in violation of RA 9165. Subject was arrested in a joint buy-bust operation conducted by NBI-ILDO and Iligan City Police Station 1 in Famous Pension House located at Brgy. San Miguel, Iligan City. Bought from the Subject was one (1) piece medium size heat sealed rectangular transparent plastic sachet containing white crystalline substance suspected to be shabu weighing more or less 1 gram with an estimated value of Php 6,800.00. The confiscated drug evidence was forwarded to Forensic Chemistry Division for examination. Case for violation of RA 9165 was being prepared for filing in court against the arrested Subject. On August 18, 2020, operatives of NBI-Environmental Crime Division (NBI-EnCD) arrested JOSEPH MAYO y FERNANDEZ, PEDRO DEL SOCORRO y ABARQUEZ, ROBERTO DEL SOCORRO y DABUETE, DANTE DEL SOCORRO y ABAIGAR, and GARY DEL SOCORRO y ABAIGAR for illegal occupation of land in Sitio Anawangin, Brgy. Pundakit, San Antonio, Zambales. Information was received that a group of unidentified individuals were engaged in illegal occupation of parcel of land in the said area without any permit or authority under existing laws and regulation. Surveillance confirmed the presence of multiple individuals in the target area and illegally constructed structures such as concrete buildings and wooden nipa huts were observed. DENR-CENRO verified that the parcel of land in the said area is an accretion area/unclassified public land. It was also verified that no foreshore land application was filed with their office for the parcel of land in question. On the aforementioned date, NBI-ENCD operatives, together with DENR-CENRO conducted an operation to stop the illegal occupation and resulted in the arrest of the above-named Subjects. Subjects failed to show documents and permits allowing them to build constructs and occupy the accretion area/unclassified public land. Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the Provincial Prosecutor, Iba, Zambales for violation of PD 705 (Revised Forestry Code of the Philippines).

body: PRESS STATEMENT May 15, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } PRESS RELEASE | TWO SUBJECTS ARRESTED BY THE NBI, CONVICTED BY THE COURT FOR MONEY LAUNDERING AND OTHER VIOLATIONS On April 23, 2026, the Regional Trial Court of Zamboanga City found the officers of Silverlion Livestock Trading, guilty for violation of Section 4(b) of Republic Act No. 9160 (Anti Money Laundering Act of 2001), Section 8 (Requirement of Registration of Securities), Section 26 (Fraudulent Transactions), and Section 28 (registration of Brokers, Dealers, Salesmen, and Associated Persons) of the Securities Regulations Code. The NBI-Western Mindanao Regional Office (NBI-WEMRO) investigated the case following a formal request for assistance from the SEC-Zamboanga regarding the activities of Silverlion Livestock Trading Corp. (Silverlion) and its officers. The investigation confirmed that Silverlion was operating a “Ponzi” scheme, soliciting unauthorized investments by promising a 35% return within 15 days. These returns were falsely presented as profits from legitimate livestock trading, even though the entity lacked the necessary license to sell securities or investment contracts. On November 26, 2022, two (2) search warrants were executed against the corporation, resulting in the seizure of various paraphernalia used in the commission of the fraud and the immediate arrest of the corporation’s officers. Subsequently, the NBI-WEMRO filed charges against the officers with the Prosecutor’s Office. In response, the DOJ filed an information with the RTC of Zamboanga against the subjects. The evidence secured during the operation served as the essential predicate for a secondary financial investigation conducted by the Anti-Money Laundering Council (AMLC), which helped secure the conviction of the individuals involved. NBI Director Atty. Melvin A. Matibag commended the dedicated NBI-WEMRO agents for their meticulous work, which led to the thorough identification of the subjects involved, the proper documentation of evidence, and the subsequent filing of cases against them. Their diligent work exemplifies a strong commitment to justice, effective law enforcement, and the pursuit of justice, culminating in the conviction of the persons involved.

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today announced the voluntary surrender of an individual to the NBI Special Action Unit (NBI-SAU) due to the relentless and persistent hot-pursuit operations of its Agents. NBI Officer-In-Charge (OIC) Director Eric B. Distor identified the subject as JOHN ALLEN DANCEL y OBRIGO a.k.a. ELONG. Director Distor said that the operation stemmed from the complaint filed by actor GERALD ANDERSON against three (3) unidentified individuals who were involved in the robbery of his personal belongings worth P830,000.00.According to the complaint, on January 30, 2022, while Anderson was playing basketball with his friends inside his gym located in Quezon City, an individual forced open and broke the window of the complainant’s vehicle parked outside the said gym, and took two (2) bags containing the stolen items. A day later, a certain individual hacked the coins.ph account of Anderson using a certain mobile number. Verification made revealed that the mobile number used in the hacking of the Anderson’s coins.ph account belongs to BENJAMIN CARREON JR, a resident of Tindalo St. Brgy. 254, Tondo, Manila. Investigation conducted by the NBI-SAU revealed that the perpetrators behind the robbery is a Tondo-Manila group, notorious for “basag kotse”. The perpetrators used a black Honda Click motorcycle and a mint green MIO I 125 motorcycle in the robbery of the complainant’s belongings. Thus, NBI-SAU dispatched a tracking team to hunt down the perpetrators behind the crime. On February 3, 2022, NBI-SAU operatives proceeded to the address of Carreon but he, together with alias Elong, were able to evade the operatives. CCTV footages recovered by the operatives showed that the two (2) subjects were able to escape through a window on the 2nd Floor of the house. During the course of the hot-pursuit, NBI-SAU operatives were able to recover from the adjacent house the personal belongings of the complainant. Further investigation revealed that the 2nd Floor of the target house is occupied by one of the perpetrators identified Subject Dancel. On February 7, 2022, due to the relentless and persistent hot-pursuit operations by the NBI-SAU, one of the subjects identified as Subject Dancel voluntarily surrendered before the office of NBI-SAU and gave his statement admitting the crime. Subject Dancel surrendered one (1) luxury bag belonging to the complainant and stated that he handed over to a certain LIANNY “YHANG” CARLOS two (2) valuable watches belonging to the complainant, which were eventually sold for Php 150,000.00. Subject Dancel was presented for inquest proceedings before the Quezon City Prosecutors Office for violation of Article 293 (Robbery with force upon things) of the Revised Penal Code. Also included in the charge are his cohorts namely JOHN LOUIE ROSARIO a.k.a MARK LOUIE and ISAGANI DELA CRUZ a.k.a GANI, who are still at-large.

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today announced the seizure of various ukay-ukay products by the NBI-Cebu District Office (NBI-CEBDO) in Lapu-Lapu City. NBI Officer-In-Charge (OIC) Director Eric B. Distor said that on February 18, 2022, NBI-CEBDO assisted by the NBI-Central Visayas Regional Office (NBI-CEVRO); and in coordination with the Bureau of Customs Intelligence and Investigation Services (CIIS) and Enforcement Security Group (ESS-Custom’s Police) implemented a Search Warrant issued by Lapu-Lapu City RTC against the premises of MINJ ABATAYO, owner of MINJ UKAY UKAY Clothing. The Search Warrant was issued against the Subject’s premises for violation of R.A. 4653 (Illegal commercial importation of used clothing/rugs) in relation to Section 6. Of R.A. 10175 (Anti-Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012) for selling assorted used clothes “ukay-ukay” believed to be from Korea and Japan through online. The caretakers of the premises failed to present any document or business permit authorizing the sale of the said imported products. Thus, the joint operatives seized 300 bundles/bales of assorted VIP used clothes with an estimated value of Php 2 Million. Further investigation revealed that the place Subject of the Search Warrant is actually owned by a certain CRESSIA CABALES-ANTONIO, a Manila-based trader from the certification obtained from CAMELLA Homeowners’ Association and the counselled statements from her employees who were at the place operating and maintaining the business for and in behalf of their employer CRESSIA ABALES-ANTONIO.

body: PRESS STATEMENT February 12, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } Ang mga human traffickers ay nagnanakaw ng kinabukasan at buhay. We fight to take them back. NBI Arrests Suspects for Illegal Recruitment , Qualified Trafficking and Use of Falsified Document PASAY, Philippines — The National Bureau of Investigation International Airport Investigation Division (NBI-IAID) has successfully arrested three (3) individuals suspected of large-scale illegal recruitment and human trafficking operations targeting Filipinos for fraudulent work in Cambodia. On February 5, 2026, the NAIA Task Force Against Human Trafficking endorsed eight repatriated passengers from Cambodia to the NBI-IAID, four of whom positively identified fellow travelers as the recruiters responsible for their exploitation. Investigation revealed that the victims were lured via social media with promises of high-paying jobs as customer service representatives. Upon the victims’ arrival in Cambodia, their passports were immediately seized to prevent escape, and their movement was strictly restricted as they were confined to a compound and denied the freedom to leave. The victims detailed the experience characterized by strict control and systemic deception, reporting that they were subjected to forced labor where they were ordered to scam foreign nationals under constant threat of harm. These abusive conditions persisted until the victims successfully sought sanctuary and assistance from the Philippine Embassy in Cambodia, which ultimately facilitated their repatriation. Following the identification by victims, authorities discovered that the Subjects possessed no license to recruit workers for overseas employment. Furthermore, a counterfeit immigration stamp was found within the suspect’s own passport. The NBI-IAID has formally filed charges against the Subjects for Large-Scale Illegal Recruitment in violation of R.A. No. 8042 (Migrant Workers and Overseas Filipinos Act of 1995), as amended, and Qualified Trafficking in Persons (Large Scale) under R.A. No. 9208 (Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2003), as amended by R.A. No. 11862. Additionally, the individual faces charges for the Use of Falsified Documents as defined under Article 172 of the Revised Penal Code. NBI Acting Director Atty. ANGELITO DLP. MAGNO stated that “The NBI remains relentless in its mission to dismantle predatory recruitment networks and hold exploiters accountable to the fullest extent of the law. However, we remind the public that vigilance is your best defense: if a job offer seems too good to be true, it is likely a trap. Do not trade your safety for a promise that isn’t real.” #NBIServes Media Contact: HA Palmer U. Mallari NBI Spokesperson [email protected]

Santiago (Ret.), arrested PHAM TIEN THANH, a Vietnamese national, in Makati City for selling illegal drugs. The NBI-OTCD received an information that a Vietnamese national identified as alias “LIU” and his unidentified cohorts are engaged in online peddling of illegal drugs, specifically ketamine and ecstasy, posted through the Telegram platform. OTCD Agents conducted a series of verification and surveillance operations in a condominium at Barangay San Antonio, Makati City, and confirmed Subject’s illicit activities. Thus, on January 21, 2025, an entrapment operation was hatched which resulted in the arrest of PHAM TIEN THANH, who was caught in flagrante delicto selling ketamine and ecstasy. PHAM TIEN THANH was informed of his constitutional rights under the circumstances in a language known to him and was made aware of the use of an alternative recording device. The illegal drugs were turned over to the NBI-Forensic Chemistry Division for laboratory examination, which yielded positive results for the presence of ketamine with a total net weight of 51.4596 grams, and methylenedioxymethamphetamine commonly known as ecstasy with a total net weight 13.3755 grams, both classified as dangerous drugs under R.A. 9165 otherwise known as “The Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002”. PHAM TIEN THANH was presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor of Makati for violation of Article II, Sections 5 & 11 of R.A. 9165 in relation to R.A. 10175 or the “Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012”.

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) arrested seven (7) operators and managers of an entertainment club that fronts as prostitution den and rescued 60 women, 19 of whom were minors during a raid along Roxas Blvd., in Paranaque City the other week. In a report submitted to NBI Officer-In-Charge Atty. Nonnatus Caesar R. Rojas by the Anti-Human Trafficking Division (AHTRAD) chief Atty. Dante B. Bonoan, the suspects are all floor managers of AREA 51 KTV Entertainment Club along Roxas Blvd., Parañaque City. On May 3, 2012, NBI received an information from the International Justice Mission (IJM), a non-government organization accredited by the IACAT that the said entertainment club is engaged in the trafficking of minors. It confirmed the presence of GROs who appeared to be minors who not only dance in full nudity but were also offered to the customers and can be taken to the club’s VIP rooms, and render sex services for a fee. After confirming the illegal and exploitative acts by the management against the victims, a rescue operation was planned. On May 5, 2012, at 10:00 pm, an NBI operative, posed as customer while other NBI agents were posted nearby. A total of 60 women were rescued and 19 of them were confirmed minors who were turned over to DSWD. Suspects were brought to the NBI. Charges for violation of RA 9208 and RA 7610 were filed against the victims before the Department of Justice.

body: PRESS STATEMENT February 25, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI), under the leadership of NBI Director Judge Jaime B. Santiago (Ret.), arrested five (5) individuals on February 20, 2025, for violation of the Espionage Act. After the arrest of several Chinese nationals and some Filipinos last month for the same offense, an intel packet from the intelligence service of the Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) revealed numerous vehicles equipped with unauthorized International Mobile Subscriber Identity (IMSI) catchers conducting signal intelligence. On February 14, 2025, the NBI-Cybercrime Division (CCD) and NBI-Special Task Force (STF) were alerted on suspicious vehicles purportedly utilizing IMSI catchers, frequenting military and police camps, other essential systems, facilities, and national government assets within Metro Manila. CCD and STF Agents validated the information and identified actionable intelligence via network monitoring, interference detection, and signal analysis tools. Systems were employed to locate and analyze rogue or unlicensed BTS, unauthorized transmissions, and interference sources which yielded positive results. A Rogue BTS is an unauthorized or malicious base station that impersonates a legitimate cellular tower to intercept, manipulate, or disrupt mobile network communications. It is often used for unauthorized surveillance, eavesdropping, data theft, and network disruption. Given the significant implication of the powerful tools with regard to national security and people’s right to privacy, simultaneous interdiction operations were hatched on February 20, 2025. The interdiction operations resulted in the arrest of OMAR KHAN KASHIM JOVERES, LEO LARAYA PANTI, and MARK ANGELO BOHOLST BINZA. They said that they were commissioned by NI QINHUI, Chinese national residing in a condominium in Malate, Manila. They further alleged that they were instructed to drive through key areas, including Villamor Airbase, Camp Aguinaldo, Malacañang, Camp Crame, and the U.S. Embassy, among others, for a fee of 2,500,00 to 3,000.00 a month. Thus, NBI Agents proceeded to QINHUI’s residence, and through coordinated efforts, he was eventually arrested together with his cohort ZHENG WEI. QINHUI’s wife admitted that QINHUI had several ICT equipment (IMSI catchers) in their condominium unit, and he did employ Omar, Leo, and Mark to run and operate the same ICT equipment within Metro Manila. To prove that she has nothing to do with it, Melody voluntarily surrendered multiple sets of said equipment (IMSI catchers, among others), to the NBI operatives. Arrested Subjects underwent inquest proceedings before the Office of the State Prosecutor, Department of Justice, for violations of R.A. 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012) and Commonwealth Act No. 616 (Espionage).

body: The National Bureau of Investigation today said operatives of NBI-Anti-Organized and Transnational Crime Division (NBI-AOTCD) have arrested an individual for Estafa on June 7, 2017 in Pasay City. NBI Director Dante A. Gierran identified the Subject as ENCAR CORDOVA y FUENZALIDA a.k.a. MARK ANTHONY PANGILINAN who was arrested inside the Casino of City of Dreams by virtue of three (3) Warrants of Arrest for Estafa and one (1) for Violation of Batas Pambansa 22 (An Act Penalizing the Making or Drawing and Issuance of a Check Without Sufficient Funds or Credit and for Other Purposes) issued by Judge Noemi J. Balitaan of Parañaque RTC Branch 258 and Judge Harold Cesar C. Huliganga of Parañaque Metropolitan Trial Court Branch 90 respectively. Investigation disclosed that Subject ENCAR F. CORDOVA used to be the owner/president of an investment company named I-Top International Trading Corportation. In May 2015, Subject enticed the Complainant and three (3) other relatives to invest Php 6.1 Million in the said company, with huge return of investment. However, after several months, the company closed and Subject was nowhere to be found, leaving hundreds of investors behind. In 2016, Subject and his friends established another investment company named Innov8 Beauty and Wellness Inc. in Puerto Princesa City, Palawan. They enticed locals thereat to invest with huge returns on investment but after two (2) months, the company suddenly closed and the owners were nowhere to be found. Upon learning of the Subject’s arrest, NBI-Puerto Princesa forwarded to NBI-AOTCD five (5) Warrants of Arrest issued by Judge Angelo R. Arizala of Puerto Princesa RTC Branch 52 with No Bail recommended, while Judge Leah E. Delos Reyes of Puerto Princesa RTC Branch 48 likewise issued one (1) Warrant of Arrest with No Bail recommended. Judge Mona Lisa V. Tiongson-Tabora of Baguio City RTC Branch 7 also issued a Warrant of Arrest against the Subject for Estafa with Bail recommended at Php 150,000.00. To date, thirty (30) Warrants of Arrest were in the hands of NBI-Puerto Princesa for transmission to NBI-AOTCD. Subject’s cohorts MARK LEVONNE GERONIMO CORTADO a.k.a. PHILIP NEMESIS TABING and KENNETH L. GRONES a.k.a. ANDREW CRUZ are still at large while BRYLLE DELA CRUZ a.k.a. JEROME DELA CRUZ was arrested by PNP Palawan.

title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today announced the arrest of two (2) individuals by the NBI-Special Action Unit (SAU) in Quezon City for conducting Unauthorized Swab Testing, Estafa and Falsification. NBI Officer-In-Charge (OIC) Director Eric B. Distor identified the subject as BERNADETTE UBANTE LAGAT and PAULO AREVALO ONATE. OIC Director Eric B. Distor said that the case stemmed from a complaint that a certain Facebook page “Swab Test Pilipinas” is offering a home service swab test for Php 3,500.00 per test. According to the complainant, a certain Berna Lagat entertained her and subsequently communicated with her thru Subject Lagat’s cellphone number. The actual swab test was performed by Subject Lagat herself on the complainant’s brother and nephew on April 11, 2021 at their residence in Sampaloc, Manila. The complainant demanded from the subject the issuance of official receipt but the subject refused and informed them that they will not issue onsite. A day after, complainant received the result of her nephew with a negative RT-PCR result carried out by Hero Laboratories. When complainant verified the same to the laboratory, she was informed that Hero Laboratories did not perform a RT-PCR test to her nephew. NBI-SAU operatives validated the complaint and communicated with the Facebook page Swab Test Pilipinas. They claimed that their laboratory is affiliated with DOH’s accredited laboratory Marilao Medical Diagnostic Center, hence, authorized to perform home service swab testing. Upon verification with the Health Facilities and Services Regulatory Bureau of DOH, the operatives of NBI-SAU found out that there is no existing licensed facility as COVID-19 Testing Laboratory by the name of “SWAB TEST PILIPINAS”. On the other hand, upon the verification with Hero Laboratories as to the RT-PCR of her brother and nephew, where their specimens were brought for laboratory testing, it was certified that their respective results did not exist nor match on their records and did not undergo RT-PCR test from Hero Laboratories. On April 19, 2021, NBI-SAU conducted entrapment operation at Don Pepe, Sto. Domingo, QC. Inside the residence where swab testing collection was performed, it was observed that the specimen was just placed in an ordinary container stuffed with other used materials where contamination is higher contrary to the issued guidelines of DOH for conducting remote specimen collection where the specimen shall be stored in a refrigerator or in a transport box with temperature maintained at 2°C to 8°C at all times while awaiting to be transported to the COVID-19 testing laboratory. Moreover, when the subjects were asked to provide any documents to prove their authority to conduct swab test, they failed to produce DOH License and when asked if they are trained by the RITM to perform swabbing, both subjects answered in the negative. Thus, subjects were placed under arrest and presented for electronic inquest proceedings before the City Prosecutor of Quezon City for four (4) counts of Estafa under Article 315 (2)(a) of the RPC as amended and two (2) counts of Falsification under Article 172 of the RPC in relation to the Cybercrime Law.

body: PRESS STATEMENT September 11, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } In line with the campaign to stop the proliferation of counterfeit products, the National Bureau of Investigation – National Capital Region (NBI-NCR) enforced Search Warrants at nineteen (19) stores and five (5) warehouses in the cities of Pasay, Manila, Valenzuela, Malabon, and Quezon City for violation of Republic Act No. 8293 or the “Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines.” On September 03 and 04, 2025, NBI-NCR implemented search warrants in thirteen (13) stores in Baclaran, Pasay City; three (3) warehouses and one (1) store in Sta. Cruz, and one (1) store in Binondo, Manila; two (2) stores in Malinta and two (2) warehouses in Dalandanan, Valenzuela City; one (1) store in Tinajeros, Malabon City; and one (1) store in North Fairview, Quezon City. The case stemmed from a complaint filed on behalf of VICTORIA’S SECRET and BATH & BODY WORKS. Director Santiago lauded the NBI-NCR for successfully implementing the search warrants and for their law enforcement actions to stop the proliferation and distribution of counterfeit products.

body: PRESS STATEMENT April 23, 2024 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } The National Bureau of Investigation – Violence Against Women and Children Division (NBI-VAWCD) arrested an individual in an entrapment operation in Norzagaray for violation of R.A. 8353 (Anti-Rape Law of 1997) and R.A. 9262 (Anti-Violence Against Women and Their Children Act of 2004). The operation stemmed from a complaint filed by the mother of the minor Victim, alleging that Subject has carnal knowledge with the Victim, his biological daughter. The complainant revealed that she bore Victim out of her romantic relationship with Subject. However, Subject abandoned them when the Victim was barely three (3) months old. Subject never gave support. There was also no communication from him until the Complainant discovered that Subject had contacted the Victim at around first week of September 2023. From then on, Complainant allowed Victim to temporarily live with Subject together with his live-in partner in many instances from October 15, 2023 to March 14, 2024. Thru the information given by the live-in partner of the Subject, Complainant discovered the sexual relationship of the Victim and Subject and that Subject will be renting an apartment so he could live with the Victim. The allegations were evidenced by recorded phone calls and admission of Subject to his live-in partner. Subject and Victim were set to meet on April 18, 2024 in Cubao and will eventually travel to Bulacan to live together. Thus, on April 18, 2024, NBI-VAWCD operatives proceeded to the meeting place and discretely followed the two (2), who checked-in at a motel in Norzagaraay, Bulacan. NBI-VAWCD operatives immediately arrested the Subject as they were getting out of the motel. Victim revealed to the operatives that she and her father has a sexual relationship which began around last week of 2024. Subject was presented for inquest proceeding for the above-mentioned violations.

body: A member of a swindling syndicate who enticed prospective buyers of supposedly auctioned goods at the Customs bureau was arrested by operatives of the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) in an entrapment operation in Intramuros, Manila last Wednesday. Atty. Nonnatus Caesar R. Rojas, Officer-in-Charge of the National Bureau of Investigation, identified the arrested suspect as MARIO REYES OCAMPO, 59, and residing at of No. 362 Madrid St., Tondo, Manila. The case arose from a complaint of Oliver Fabio and Louie Ongpauco who were victimized by a group of swindlers who misrepresented themselves as employees of the Bureau of Customs. They were induced to buy supposed goods being auctioned at the Bureau of Customs at much lower prices than the prevailing costs in the market. Convinced of the very affordable prices that was offered, the complainants agreed to buy the items. Romy Bon Huy Lim verified from the Bureau of Customs the authenticity of the employment of Ocampo. Certification from said office revealed that he is not connected thereat. On May 30, 2012, during an entrapment Ocampo was arrested by NBI agents after receiving marked money from the complainants inside a fastfood parlor in Intramuros, Manila. The suspect was presented for Inquest Proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor of Manila and was recommended to be prosecuted for Attempted Estafa and Falsification of Public Documents. He is presently detained at the NBI jail. The public is warned from entertaining calls or text messages offering for sale of items allegedly to be an auctioned at the Bureau of Customs.

body: Despite continuous warning of the government against those who take advantage of the COVID-19 pandemic, some still continue with their illegal activities. Thus, the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today announced the arrest of an individual in Cebu City for selling COVID-19 Rapid Test Kits. NBI Officer-In-Charge Eric B. Distor identified the subject as JEMUEN CENON y MIER who uses a Facebook Account under the name of JEMSKIE CENN to sell COVID-19 Rapid Test Kits. OIC Distor said that information received from an official of 3012nd Air Intelligence and Security Squadron of the Philippine Air Force (PAF) revealed that certain individuals are taking advantage of the pandemic by selling COVID-19 Rapid Test Kits through Facebook which is prohibited under existing laws. Acting immediately on this information, on June 22, 2020, joint operatives of NBI-Central Visayas Regional Office (NBI-CEVRO) based in Cebu City headed by its Regional Director Tomas Enrile and Food and Drugs Administration (FDA) in coordination with the Philippine National Police (PNP) set up an entrapment operation. NBI-CEVRO established communication with the subject online and ordered 134 boxes of COVID-19 Rapid Test Kits. At the agreed meeting place, upon handing over the marked money by the poseur-buyer to the subject, operatives effected the arrest of Subject Cenon who was caught in flagrante. Seized from the subject are 134 boxes of COVID-19 Rapid Test Kits with an estimated value of Php 3,484,000.00. OIC Distor said that under R.A. 9711 or the Food and Drug Administration Act of 2009 as amended, in relation to FDA Advisory No.2020-497, 2020-498, and FDA Circular No.2020-016, it states that Anti-body COVID-19 test Kits are strictly for medical professional use and not intended for personal use. In addition, Rapid Test Kits must be strictly distributed to appropriate establishments or institutions and the product must be acquired through prescription from a licensed physician from a licensed hospital or drugstore. Subject Cenon was presented for inquest proceedings thru Teleconference before the Inquest Prosecutor of Cebu City.

body: Fifty five (55) container vans loaded with lumber estimated at P30 million of pesos were seized by the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) at Pier 16 North Harbor Manila today. On June 27, 2012, the NBI received a request for the confiscation of the load from Davao City allegedly declared as cement, but in truth it is lumber. Said load allegedly was shipped by NMC thru vessels NMC Gen. Geronimo and Lorenzo and scheduled to arrive in Manila by June 28, 2012. The following day, an NBI team proceeded to North Harbor and were informed and the vessels would surely docked at Pier 16, North harbor. Verification with the Philippine Port Authority (PPA) at Pier 16 revealed no vessels from Davao bound for Manila is set to arrive that day at 3 a.m. A certification regarding of the none scheduled arrival of the vessels were secured from the PPA main office. The NBI was informed that a vessel from Davao arrived at around 3 a.m. of June 26, 2012. A copy of the Cargo Manifest was requested. Upon examination of said cargo manifest, the NBI discovered that 55 container vans coming from Davao City were declared as cement. Subsequently, a written request for the holding and opening of said container vans was done with the customs collector of North Harbor, Office of the DENR, and the PPA North Harbor. Thereafter, in the early morning of June 29, 2012, NBI operatives proceeded to Pier 16. In the presence of DENR, PPA and representatives of other government agencies the container vans were opened revealing fully loaded to the brim with “hot lumber”.

title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today announced the arrest of a Chinese national, KE LIANGPENG, in Lapu-Lapu City for illegal practice of medicine and selling of pharmaceutical products without registration or authority from the Food and Drug Administration (FDA). NBI Officer-In-Charge Eric B. Distor said the joint operation was conducted on July 24, 2020 by combined Agents of the NBI assigned at the Office of the Deputy Director for Regional Operations Service (ODDROS), NBI-Central Visayas Regional Office – 7 (CEVRO-7) and Food and Drug Administration (FDA) Visayas Cluster Office in full coordination with the Lapu-Lapu City Police and the Criminal Investigation and Detection Group (CIDG) and Lapu-Lapu City Police Field Office. OIC Distor stressed that a Certification issued by Director Jesusa Joyce Cunanan, Chief for Drug Regulation and Research of FDA based in Manila states that the establishment/premises nor its proprietors have no authority or license to sell and dispense pharmaceutical products and neither its product sold to the public at large. For his part, Deputy Director for Regional Operations, Atty. Antonio Pagatpat, said that on this basis, a buy-bust operation was conducted in Teakwood Subdivision, Barangay Soong, Lapu-Lapu City resulting in the seizure of several boxes of unregistered, mislabelled and unbranded pharmaceutical products mostly labelled with Chinese character labels valued by the FDA at Ten Million Pesos (P10,000,000.00). Pagatpat added that the operation also resulted in the arrest of KE LIANGPENG, who was caught “en flagrante delicto” receiving the marked money in exchange for the antibiotic drug he prescribed to an NBI poseur-buyer, the prescribed drug of which was previously labelled as unregistered by the FDA. OIC Distor emphasized that the operation also led to the discovery of several hospital beds catering to ill patients, mostly Chinese, seeking treatment, cure and medications from KE and his cohorts. As a matter of fact, Distor added, a female Chinese, a resident of Sunberry Subdivision, Soong, Lapu-Lapu City, was found lying in one of the hospital beds with intravenous device linked to her arm. Subject KE claimed that he is a Medical Doctor in China but could not produce authorization nor special permit for him to legally practice medicine in the Philippines. He could not also present any documents to show the FDA registration of the pharmaceutical products found at his premises. Deputy Director Pagatpat said subject KE has been presented for Inquest proceedings before the Lapu-Lapu City Prosecutor’s Office for violation of Food, Drugs and Cosmetics Act under R.A. 3720 as amended by R.A. 9711 defined under Section 10 and penalized under Section 11 for Selling Unregistered Pharmaceutical Products and violation of Philippine Pharmacy Act under R.A. 5921 as amended by R.A. 10918 for operating the establishment as retail outlet of pharmaceutical products to the public without authority from FDA. Another case for violation of the Medical Act under R.A. 2382, as amended by R.A. 4224 will be filed against subject KE once a Certification from the Professional Regulations Commission shall have been obtained confirming that subject KE HAS NO LICENSE TO PRACTICE, Pagatpat added.

body: PRESS STATEMENT January 21, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } NBI THROWBACK | A Case That Shocked the World In 2015, the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI), led one of the most complex and harrowing international cybercrime operations in history—the apprehension of Peter Gerard Scully, an Australian national behind a massive online child exploitation network. After fleeing to the Philippines in an attempt to evade fraud charges in his home country, Scully continued his criminal activities by operating an international child abuse ring through the dark web. Through meticulous intelligence gathering, digital forensics, and close coordination with international law enforcement agencies, the NBI successfully tracked, located, and arrested Scully in February 2015. The Supreme Court of the Philippines later affirmed Scully’s conviction, sentencing him to life imprisonment without parole for qualified trafficking, with additional prison sentences totaling 129 years for crimes including rape, child abuse, and child pornography. The ruling reinforced the government’s firm stand that crimes against children will be met with the strongest penalties under the law. This case stands as a powerful reminder of the NBI’s unwavering commitment to justice, child protection, and international cooperation in the fight against cyber-enabled crimes. #NBIServes

title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today said operatives of NBI-Death Investigation Division (NBI-DID) have dismantled a multi-million investment company scam in Quezon City on October 1, 2021 by virtue of an entrapment operation. NBI Officer-in-Charge (OIC) Director Eric B. Distor said that based on investigation, AUREA ORGANICA milked millions of pesos from unsuspecting victims who were lured to invest their money in exchange for thirty percent (30%) return after thirty (30) days. The company uses beauty essentials such as whitening soap, oils, skin toner, and perfume as the face of their business. Upon verification, AUREA ORGANICA is not registered with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) nor does it possess a secondary license to operate as an investment company. Arrested during the entrapment operation is the company secretary LOTTA LOVE REYES who received the entrapment money. Subject was properly charged before the Quezon City Prosecutor’s Office for violation of RA 8799 otherwise known as the Securities Regulation Code. Charges for violation of RA 8799 and Syndicated Estafa were also filed against BEATRIZ PIA ESPINA WHITE a.k.a. PIA ESPINA, JOSE NARCISO D. TERRADO II a.k.a. JOHN TERRADO II. Distor cautions the public in entering into these kinds of investment scam or Ponzi schemes. According to SEC, the public can notice a Ponzi scheme with its guaranteed high investment returns, unlicensed or unregistered sellers, and overly consistent returns. The NBI further advises the public to be vigilant and to report these kinds of illegal activities to the Bureau.

body: Three minors were rescued and three pimps who engaged in their immoral activity through internet were arrested by agents of the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) in an entrapment last week. The suspects were identified as: MARIO BENITO VALERA, alias “Mike Garcia”, 56, and a resident of No. 21-A Fourth St., Ignacio Village, Quezon City; MAUREEN TOLENTINO ESCALANTE, alias “Mao”, 21, a resident of No. 1983 Kahilom II, Pandacan, Manila; and MATTHEW CONCEPCION PARAS, 17, a resident of 2324 F. Balagtas St., Pandacan, Manila. Rescued were “Lorna”, 16; “Aida’. 16; and “Fe,” 17, (not their real names). Investigation by the NBI-Anti-Human Trafficking Division (AHTRAD) disclosed that on March 7, 2013, the NBI received a reliable report that an internet website is actively engaged in human trafficking activities. It was learned that the said website is an internet forum or online community not accessible to any user. To validate the information, a covert account was registered to gain access to the website. It was confirmed that through its forum, various pimps and other independent sex workers post their advertisements, profiles and so-called “rules of engagement.” Mobile phones are also listed after every ad to be contacted for further details. Website’s sub-forum solicits prospective clients for sexual services for an agreed price. Moreover, it was found out that suspect Valera is the owner of the online profile promoting a group of managed escort service providers. Escalante, meanwhile, is the “handler” of the trafficked victims, while Paras acted as “guide and escort” of the said victims. Acting on this information, an entrapment was planned. Meanwhile, continuous exchange of communication either by emails and text messages ensued between Valera and an NBI agent who posed as customer. He was being offered young ladies for P5,500 each. Finally, it was decided that Valera would deliver young ladies to the poseur-buyer. Pictures of said ladies were attached thru emails to be viewed prior to the actual meeting. They were initially introduced as “Gold 18Y”, “Unica,” “Zarra 6K” and “Kelli.” In consideration, suspect demanded and charged P5,500, of which P3,00 goes to each lady. A room was booked and reserved at the Cherry Hotel & Restaurant in Bocobo Ext., Ermita, Manila where it will be used for the meeting. Surveillance camera was set up inside Room 509 situated at the 5th Floor of the hotel. At about 2:30 PM of April 3, 2013, NBI agents proceeded to said room of the hotel. Meanwhile, other agents positioned themselves nearby. During exchanges of messages “Mike Garcia” texted that his errand girl “Mao” would instead accompany the young ladies and that he preferred to wait downstairs. At around 4:00 PM, Escalante arrived, together with the three young ladies/victims. The poseur/customers gave the money to Escalante. While in the act of counting marked money, NBI operatives swiftly approached, announced their authority, and placed Escalante under arrest. She pinpointed suspect Mike Garcia as the one who sent her and disclosed his exact whereabouts. Valera was arrested during a follow-up operation, together with Paras who accompanied victims to their supposed paying customers. They are presently detained at the NBI detention cell. Charges for violation of RA No. 9208 (Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2003), Syndicated and Large Scale, Qualified Human Trafficking, as amended by RA No. 10364 (Expanded Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2012), and RA 7610 (Special Protection of Children Against Abuse, Exploitation and Discrimination Act) were filed against the suspects before the Department of Justice.

NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION

Three minors were rescued and three pimps who engaged in their immoral activity through internet were arrested by agents of the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) in an entrapment last week. The suspects were identified as: MARIO BENITO VALERA, alias “Mike Garcia”, 56, and a resident of No. 21-A Fourth St., Ignacio Village, Quezon City; MAUREEN TOLENTINO ESCALANTE, alias “Mao”, 21, a resident of No. 1983 Kahilom II, Pandacan, Manila; and MATTHEW CONCEPCION PARAS, 17, a resident of 2324 F. Balagtas St., Pandacan, Manila. Rescued were “Lorna”, 16; “Aida’. 16; and “Fe,” 17, (not their real names). Investigation by the NBI-Anti-Human Trafficking Division (AHTRAD) disclosed that on March 7, 2013, the NBI received a reliable report that an internet website is actively engaged in human trafficking activities. It was learned that the said website is an internet forum or online community not accessible to any user. To validate the information, a covert account was registered to gain access to the website. It was confirmed that through its forum, various pimps and other independent sex workers post their advertisements, profiles and so-called “rules of engagement.” Mobile phones are also listed after every ad to be contacted for further details. Website’s sub-forum solicits prospective clients for sexual services for an agreed price. Moreover, it was found out that suspect Valera is the owner of the online profile promoting a group of managed escort service providers. Escalante, meanwhile, is the “handler” of the trafficked victims, while Paras acted as “guide and escort” of the said victims. Acting on this information, an entrapment was planned. Meanwhile, continuous exchange of communication either by emails and text messages ensued between Valera and an NBI agent who posed as customer. He was being offered young ladies for P5,500 each. Finally, it was decided that Valera would deliver young ladies to the poseur-buyer. Pictures of said ladies were attached thru emails to be viewed prior to the actual meeting. They were initially introduced as “Gold 18Y”, “Unica,” “Zarra 6K” and “Kelli.” In consideration, suspect demanded and charged P5,500, of which P3,00 goes to each lady. A room was booked and reserved at the Cherry Hotel & Restaurant in Bocobo Ext., Ermita, Manila where it will be used for the meeting. Surveillance camera was set up inside Room 509 situated at the 5th Floor of the hotel. At about 2:30 PM of April 3, 2013, NBI agents proceeded to said room of the hotel. Meanwhile, other agents positioned themselves nearby. During exchanges of messages “Mike Garcia” texted that his errand girl “Mao” would instead accompany the young ladies and that he preferred to wait downstairs. At around 4:00 PM, Escalante arrived, together with the three young ladies/victims. The poseur/customers gave the money to Escalante. While in the act of counting marked money, NBI operatives swiftly approached, announced their authority, and placed Escalante under arrest. She pinpointed suspect Mike Garcia as the one who sent her and disclosed his exact whereabouts. Valera was arrested during a follow-up operation, together with Paras who accompanied victims to their supposed paying customers. They are presently detained at the NBI detention cell. Charges for violation of RA No. 9208 (Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2003), Syndicated and Large Scale, Qualified Human Trafficking, as amended by RA No. 10364 (Expanded Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2012), and RA 7610 (Special Protection of Children Against Abuse, Exploitation and Discrimination Act) were filed against the suspects before the Department of Justice.

title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: In line with the relentless drive of the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) against all forms of crimes, operatives of NBI-Special Action Unit (NBI-SAU) arrested an individual in Quezon City for using the name of Congressman Michael Romero to illegally solicit money. NBI Officer-in-Charge (OIC) Director Eric B. Distor identified the Subject as CHRISTINE JOY LAGRISOLA. Distor said that the case stemmed from a request for investigation of Congressman Michael Romero, Representative of 1PACMAN Party-list, and a complaint against Subject CHRISTINE JOY LAGRISOLA. Based on investigation, Subject was fraudulently representing herself as a member of Cong. Romero’s staff and was soliciting money on the latter’s behalf to be invested in his alleged financing business. According to the Subject, the supposed investor of which will be a sub-junket operator. Through Subject’s false pretense, complainant was moved to invest and gave Subject a total of Php 2,500,000.00. Complainant averred that Subject promised a 27% interest in 6 days. However, the former did not receive any return of investment despite several demands. Rather, Subject has issued a check to complainant but when the latter presented it to the bank for deposit, it was dishonored due to closure of account. Complainant personally verified with Cong. Romero’s office if Subject is indeed his staff and has the authority to solicit investment money on his behalf. Cong. Romero disproved the representations of Subject. Upon learning of Subject’s scam, Cong. Romero and complainant filed a complaint before the NBI. Through a letter addressed to Distor, Cong. Romero stated that he is not acquainted with the Subject nor a member of his staff. Further, Cong. Romero said he has never been in financing business as an investor or financer in any casino business in the country. Complainant called the Subject and demanded the outstanding interests. However, the latter insisted the she would issue another check to replace the dishonored check. Further, Subject informed complainant that the casino rolling investment was still open for investors thus the latter told the Subject that her cousin was willing to put money into business. A meeting was then set between Subject and complainant together with the supposed new investor at complainant’s residence in a condominium in New Manila, Quezon City. With these, on July 16, 2021, an entrapment operation was hatched for the payment of the initial investment of Php 1 Million by the new investor. Poseur-investor, together with the complainant, met the Subject in the lobby of the condominium. Subject, wearing an ID lanyard with emblem logo of House Representatives, flawlessly explained the mechanics of the investment to the poseur-investor and demanded Php 1 Million afterwards to which the Subject received and issued an acknowledgement receipt. At this juncture, NBI-SAU operatives immediately approached the Subject, introduced themselves, and explained the purpose of the entrapment. Items found in the possession of the Subject were inventoried as witnessed by Atty. Von De Castro, Chief of Staff of the Office of Cong. Romero and the security officer of the condominium. Subject CHRISTINE JOY LAGRISOLA was presented for inquest proceedings before the Quezon City Prosecutor’s Office for Swindling/Estafa as defined and penalized under Article 315 of the Revised Penal Code.

title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) announced today the arrest of two (2) individuals in Parañaque City for selling COVID-19 test kits which is prohibited under the law. NBI Officer-In-Charge (OIC) Eric B. Distor identified the subjects as SHANON APRIL MEJIA ALEGRE and ESSELINE RAISA SY ONG , who were arrested by operatives of the NBI-Anti Organized and Transnational Crimes Division (NBI-AOTCD) in an entrapment operation on May 14, 2020. OIC Distor said that the case stemmed from information received by the NBI-AOTCD that there are individuals engaged in the online selling of COVID-19 test kits despite the issuance of Food and Drugs Administration (FDA) Advisory Nos. 2020-497 and 498 in April 2020 reiterating to all license importer/distributors that COVID-19 test kits are strictly for medical professional use and not intended for personal use and that said product should be acquired by the general public through a prescription from a licensed physician, hospitals or drugstores and pharmacies. The FDA Circular No. 2020-016 also stated that online selling of FDA certified COVID-19 antibody test kits is strictly prohibited. On May 13, 2020, NBI-AOTCD was able to identify an online seller of test kits. AOTCD operatives immediately established communication to the online seller of test kits for cash on delivery (COD) within Metro Manila. At the same time, the NBI coordinated with the FDA. An undercover poseur-customer ordered 200 boxes at P12,000.00 per box of test kits worth Php 2,400,000.00 through the contact number of the seller. The seller then instructed the poseur-customer to pick up the test kits in a house in BF Homes Parañaque City. On May 14, 2020, NBI-AOTCD operatives together with the FDA representatives conducted an entrapment operation. They were greeted by Subject Alegre who invited the poseur-customer inside the garage and presented 200 boxes of test kits which bear the markings “Wondfo SARS-COV-2 Antibody Test (Lateral Flow Method).” They were then invited inside the house for the payment and as soon as Subject Ong received the entrapment money, AOTCD operatives swoop down inside the house, declared their authority and placed Subjects Alegre and Ong under arrest. Subjects Ong and Alegre failed to show any License-to-Operate when asked by the FDA representatives. The operation also resulted in the seizure of 200 boxes worth Php 2.4 Million. OIC Distor stressed that a Certification issued by the FDA states that online sellers do not have a License-to-Operate or Special Certification in the selling or distribution of the said test kits. Criminal charges are now being readied against the subjects and will be filed before the Prosecutor’s Office.

title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today said operatives of NBI-Special Action Unit (NBI-SAU) arrested two individuals in Tondo, Manila for selling Covid-19 vaccination slots. NBI Officer-in-Charge (OIC) Director Eric B. Distor identified the Subjects as BENJIE LAGASCA MONTAOS and ARTURO FLORES MAGTALAS. Distor said that the case stemmed from a report regarding an alleged illegal sale of vaccination slots to POGO employees by certain “BENJIE”. According to the information received, BENJIE offered to personally assist the individuals who wish to avail the vaccination in Manila. BENJIE further explained that in order for these individuals to get vaccinated, they should each possess a stub or ticket in the vaccination site. The stubs of tickets would be given personally by BENJIE on the day of the vaccination for the consideration of Php 6,000 per vaccination slot. Under the instruction and supervision of NBI-SAU, the informant responded to BENJIE that ten (10) POGO employees would avail of the vaccination slots he offered for a total of Php 60,000. BENJIE further instructed the informant to register the details of the POGO employees online through www.manilacovid19vaccine.ph and to use the address 1248 Juan Luna St., Tondo, Manila, Brgy. 56, Zone 5, District 1, Tondo 1 in the said registration and had all the copies thereof sent to his Viber account. On July 23, 2021, BENJIE contacted the informant and told him that the ten slots for vaccination would be available the following day in General Vicente Lim Elementary School, Tondo, Manila. With this, an entrapment operation was hatched. On July 24, 2021, NBI-SAU proceeded to the said vaccination site and strategically positioned themselves around the area. Poseur-clients and the informant were personally met by BENJIE and male companion identified as Brgy. Kagawad ARTURO MAGTALAS. BENJIE and MAGTALAS assisted the team in the parking and guided them to the reserved seats in the waiting area of the vaccination site. BENJIE asked for the hard copies of the waivers and vaccination ID QR code. When the team asked for the stubs/tickets for the vaccination slots, BENJIE instructed them to discreetly board a black Hyundai Starex with plate number WLI 182 parked nearby. Inside the said vehicle, BENJIE handed to the poseur-client ten stubs with numbers 222-231. BENJIE then demanded for the Php 60,000 which the poseur-client handed to BENJIE. At this juncture, NBI operatives approached BENJIE and KGWD. MAGTALAS, introduced themselves as law enforcement officers, identified their authority and explained the purpose of the entrapment. Subjects were then placed under arrest and were apprised of their constitutional rights. BENJIE was identified as BENJIE MESA MONTAOS through the identification cards found in his possession. Subjects were brought to NBI Office for the standard booking procedures. Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor, Manila for violations of RA 11032 or the Anti-Red Tape Act of 2007 and RA 3019 or the Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act. Additional charges for violation of R 6713 (Code of Conduct and Ethical Standards for Public Officials and Employees) were filed against ARTURO F. MAGTALAS

title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today announced the arrest of an Abu Sayyaf member by the operatives of NBI- Counter Terrorism Division (NBI-CTD) in an operation in Culiat, Quezon City for Kidnapping and Serious Illegal Detention. NBI Officer-In-Charge (OIC) Director Eric B. Distor identified the arrested subject as ALBAZIR ABDULLA y HAMSI a.k.a ABU SAIF. Based on the information received by the NBI-CTD, a certain ABU SAIF, who was involved in the 2001 Golden Harvest Plantation Kidnapping was sighted in NCR. A victim-witness identified ABU SAIF in a CTD photo line-up as one of the abductors and a member of the ASG. A series of casing and surveillance operations was conducted by the NBI-CTD in coordination with counterparts from the Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP), to gather more information which revealed the actual residence of ABU SAIF. Thus, on September 10, 2021, NBI-CTD proceeded to the target area in Salam Compound, Brgy. Culiat, Quezon City and apprehended Abu Saif who was later identified as Subject Abdulla. The arrested ASG member was then brought to NBI Detention Facility. Director Distor added that due to continued monitoring, the NBI-CTD was able to track down and apprehend a number of ASG members who blended in the society. He stressed that Subject ABU SAIF is the 2nd member of the terrorist group, ASG, to be arrested this year. On May 7, 2021, Wahab S. Jamal a.k.a. Ustadz Halipa was arrested at Maharlika Village in Taguig. & Albazir H. Abdulla @Abu Saif, Arrested 10 sept at Salam compound, Distor emphasized that back in 2001, the terrorist group, Abu Sayyaf Group (ASG) headed by their late leader Isnilon Hapilon and other senior ASG leaders raided the Golden Harvest Plantation in Brgy. Tairan, Lantawan, Basilan Province. The terrorist group seized the supplies from sari-sari stores and houses; livestock, firearms and ammunition from the plantation security. The ASG burned the chapel and detained 14 plantation workers, two (2) of whom were beheaded by the terrorist group. After four (4) months of captivity, the victims were able to escape on separate ocassions from their captors during the rescue operations by the government security forces. After the incident, the ASG stayed in the mountains and some of its members assimilated back to society as “sleepers” or “spies”.

body: PRESS STATEMENT August 09, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } In line with the directive from National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Director JUDGE JAIME B. SANTIAGO (Ret.) to intensify the operations against human trafficking, the NBI-Organized and Transnational Crime Division (NBI-OTCD) arrested JERWIN CANTUBA LAILA in Pasay City. Subject was arrested for violation of Republic Act No. 9208 (Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2003), as amended by R.A. No. 10364, and further amended by R.A. No. 11862. The operation stemmed from information received by NBI-OTCD agents regarding the alleged operation of a prostitution den by foreign nationals at a particular hotel in Malibay, Pasay City. According to the informant, the operators offered Japanese, Korean, Chinese, and Vietnamese women to Chinese nationals for sexual services through online booking platforms. The NBI-OTCD agents conducted a series of surveillance operations, and through a confidential informant, they were able to secure two (2) bookings from a Telegram account. On August 2, 2025, NBI-OTCD agents set up an entrapment operation and proceeded to the agreed upon pick-up area. Two (2) Chinese informants posed as clients and were picked up by a man driving a grey car. After the poseur-clients entered the hotel, NBI-OTCD agents tailed same grey car observing it pick up three (3) female foreign nationals. Once the unlawful transaction was completed, NBI-OTCD agents immediately arrested the driver of the grey car, identified as Subject Laila. During the operation, the NBI-OTCD agents rescued a female Vietnamese national and two (2) female Chinese nationals. The rescued foreign nationals executed sworn statements, which revealed that a certain TAO YUAN was the one who offered them for sexual services via online booking and that Subject Laila regularly fetched them when they had clients. On August 4, 2025, Subject Laila was presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor of Pasay City for the aforementioned violations. In addition, a person with the alias TAO YUAN was also charged with violation of R.A. No. 9208, as amended by R.A. No. 10364, as further amended by R.A. No. 11862. Director Santiago commended the dedicated agents of the NBI-OTCD for their diligent efforts and perseverance, which culminated in the successful arrest of Subject Laila.

body: SURRENDER YOUR REVOKED NBI CA ID’S or FACE THE PENALTY OF THE LAW. This is the stern warning issued by the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) to those persons who persist on keeping their revoked NBI Consultant (Confidential Agent) identification cards. body: A kidnapped Overseas Filipino Worker (OFW) was rescued while one of the abductors arrested, and another killed during an operation conducted by the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) agents in Talisay City, Cebu on Monday. The suspect was identified by NBI Director Nonnatus Caesar R. Rojas as: RONELO MARTEL ROBLE, 47, married, of Kalinaw 2, San Rafael, Talisay, Cebu; At-large are: PO3 Lee Colina, of PNP Cebu City, a John Doe and a Peter Doe. Killed during the operation was Wane B. Tiano, a member of the kidnapping group. Investigation by the NBI-Central Visayas Regional Office (CEVRO) headed by Regional Director Antonio M. Pagatpat revealed that in the morning of June 17, 2013, a certain Minerva B. Laborada requested for assistance for the rescue of Reneboy Agraviador, an OFW and her common-law husband. According to complainant Laborada, the victim was forcibly taken by five (5) unidentified men at about 9:00 AM of the same date at the junction of Rabaya St., Talisay City, Cebu and Highway of Cebu South Road Properties (SRP). Later, the kidnappers called up Laborada and demanded P50,000 ransom for Agraviador’s release. Acting with dispatch, a rescue operation was planned. The complainant and the kidnappers agreed to meet at noon of the same day, June 17, 2013, near the Evergreen Cemetery located at SRP, Talisay City, Cebu. On the appointed time and place, NBI agents discreetly accompanied complainant Laborada. While the pay-off was in progress, NBI agents immediately moved in and rescued Agraviador. A shoot-out between the kidnappers and NBI operatives ensued injuring one of the NBI’s assets. One of the kidnappers, Tiano, was shot dead while Roble was arrested. However, the three other suspects, escaped prompting the NBI to launch a nationwide manhunt operation. Meanwhile, the victim identified PO3 Colina as having participated in the kidnapping and identified by NBI agents during the shoot out. Recovered from the suspects were the ransom money amounting to P50,000; a cell phone recovered from the body of Tiano used in communication during the negotiation; two motorcycles, one owned by the victim, Agraviador; .45 caliber; wallet with assorted cards; and other personal belongings. Charges for Kidnapping for Ransom and Carnapping were filed today against the suspect before the Talisay City, Cebu Prosecutor’s Office.

body: The National Bureau of Investigation today said operatives of NBI-Laguna District Office (NBI-LAGDO) arrested BIENVENIDO RAMIREZ y GASILO last May 29, 2017 in San Pablo City, Laguna for Murder and Illegal Possession of Firearms and Ammunitions. In 2013, a Complainant, widow of the Subject’s victim, filed a complaint against the Subject and his cohort. Victim, identified as GRACIANO GERARD ISLETA GALANG, was shot to death by gunmen on board a motorcycle on October 18, 2013. According to a witness who positively identified Subject BIENVENIDO RAMIREZ, a speedy motorcycle passed by the victim then gunshot was heard. After which, victim was seen laying on the street being shot successively by the assailant. On May 28, 2017, NBI-LAGDO received an information that Subject BIENVENIDO RAMIREZ, who has a standing Warrant of Arrest issued by the RTC Branch 29, San Pablo City, Laguna for the crime of Murder, was serving as a barangay tanod at Barangay 1-B, San Pablo City, Laguna. With this information, after proper coordination with the authorities, LAGDO operatives proceeded to the barangay hall where the Subject was rendering his regular duty. After confirming Subject’s presence thereat, operatives swooped down the area, approached the Subject and effected the arrest. Recovered from Subject’s possession were one (1) unit Norinco .45 caliber pistol, one (1) 8 rounder magazine .45 caliber, one (1) 8 rounder chip Mc Cormick .45 caliber magazine, one (1) 8 rounder Novaks .45 caliber magazine, and seventeen (17) live rounds of .45 caliber ammunition. Verification with the Firearms and Explosives Division (FED) of the Philippine National Police (PNP), Subject is not a registered owner/holder of any kind of firearm. Aside from the Subject’s standing Warrant of Arrest for Murder, charges for violation of R.A. 10591 otherwise known as the Comprehensive Firearms and Ammunition Regulation Act were filed against the Subject.

body: The alleged Commander-in-Chief of USAFFE (an ultra-rightist group who claims to be the “Defenders of the Filipino People”) involved in the foiled bomb attack at the NAIA 3 and who has outstanding warrants of arrest issued by MTC of Quezon City was arrested by agents of the Anti-Organized and Transnational Crime Division (AOTCD) at NAIA Terminal 2. ELLY PAMATONG The arrest of lawyer ELLY PAMATONG was not made for his involvement in last Monday’s foiled attacks at the NAIA 3, but on the basis of an outstanding warrant issued against him for inciting to sedition that stemmed from the threats he made against the government after he lost in the 2004 presidential elections and for malicious mischief issued by the MTC Caloocan City. On September 3, 2014, information was received that lawyer ELLY PAMATONG was scheduled to arrive in Manila from Cagayan de Oro. Acting on said information, AOTCD operatives proceeded to the NAIA Terminal 2 to effect his arrest. Upon disembarking, PAMATONG was arrested by operatives of AOTCD at around 6:00 p.m. PAMATONG was brought to the NBI main office in Manila for booking and detention.

title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: In a series of operations conducted on July 17, 20, and 21, 2020, three (3) Abu Sayyaf Group (ASG) members were arrested by the NBI Counter-Terrorism Division (NBI-CTD) in coordination with the Special Action Force-Rapid Deployment Battalion of the Philippine National Police and counterparts from the Armed Forces of the Philippines. NBI Officer-In-Charge (OIC) Eric B. Distor said that the successful operations were based on the intelligence reports from the NBI-CTD in connection with sightings of alleged ASG members in Metro Manila who were involved in the kidnapping of 6 members of a Christian religious sect in Patikul, Sulu on August 20, 2002. OIC Distor added that all three (3) subjects are included in the Order of Arrest docketed under Criminal Case No. 128923-H A to E for 6 counts of Kidnapping and Serious Illegal Detention with Ransom currently pending before the Regional Trial Court Branch 271, Taguig City. These positice developments are results of relentless efforts of NBI Intelligence operatives as far as tailing subjects from Jolo and identifying the subjects, their residences in Metro Manila and monitoring their activities that led to their arrest. Given the authority to investigate by OIC Distor, operatives from NBI-CTD and AFP Counterparts initiated the case build-up and conducted series of surveillance operations to identify the subjects, their residences, workplaces and other relevant information. On 13 July 2020, a witness under the DOJ-Witness Protection Program was able to identify one photo from a CTD photo line-up as ERIE. Subject ERIE, who was initially identified as Ben Saudi was likewise identified to have used the alias ERIE (It is common for ASG members to use several aliases or “kunya”). The witness in the abovementioned case executed the corresponding Sworn Statement identifying ERIE as one of the ASG members who held the victims in captivity. At around 2:00 PM, of 17 July 2020, subject ERIE was arrested by the group composed of NBI-CTD, PNP SAF-Rapid Deployment Battalion and AFP Counterparts at Sultan Kudarat Street, Maharlika, Taguig City. He was then informed of his rights and was processed for booking as per standard procedure and is now in the NBI Detention Facility. The same witness also identified during the photo line-up the subject known as JABER and thereafter executed a Sworn Statement identifying JABER as one of the ASG’s perimeter guard at the time they were held captive. In the afternoon of 20 July 2020, JABER was arrested by a team comprised of NBI-CTD, PNP SAF-RD and AFP Counterparts at Craig St., Sampaloc Manila. Subject JABER was informed of all his rights and was processed for booking as per standard procedure and is now in the NBI Detention Facility. JABER gave his official name as AJVIER KUHUTAN y SABTULA. Another individual also identified by the same witness in the photo line-up is subject OSEIN or ABDURAYA. A Sworn Statement was executed on 13 July 2020 by the same witness identifying the subject as an ASG member who guarded the kidnap victims. On 21 July 2020, the following day after the arrest of subject JABER, his relatives arrived at the NBI-CTD office to verify the nature/cause of his arrest and claim his personal belongings. One of the relatives is ADZMI KUHUTAN y SABTULA, who claimed to be AJVIER’s older brother. According to the intelligence report received earlier, it was revealed that one OSEIN/ABDURAYA who was also involved in the said kidnapping case and is listed in the Order of Arrest thereof is the brother of JABER. ADMZI was then requested to present identification (Barangay ID) and was asked to temporarily remove his face mask to verify if he is the same person in the ID he presented. Upon removing his mask, the Agents of the CTD recognized him as the same person identified by the witness on 13 July 2020 as OSEIN/ABDURAYA. ADZMI was shown a copy of the witness/complainant’s Sinumpaang Salaysay and did not deny that the photograph of the person identified as OSEIN/ABDURAYA therein is him. The CTD, as augmented by operatives from NBI TFAID, TID and CRID agents arrested ADZMI also known as OSEIN/ABDURAYA. He was informed of his rights, processed for booking and is currently detained in the NBI Detention Facility. OIC Distor stressed that the arrested ASG members who are now under the custody of the NBI are awaiting transfer to the Special Intensive Care Area (SICA), BJMP in Taguig City. Distor likewise emphasized that the NBI thru its Counter-Terrorism Division headed by HA Raoul Manguerra, in full coordination with the PNP and counterparts from the AFP, will continue in its relentless efforts against terrorists and other lawless elements. With R.A. 11479 or the Anti-Terrorism ﹰAct of 2020, the fight against terrorism has given the government a stronger law as basis in running against terrorists, Distor added.
