body: On March 3, 2021, operatives of NBI-Special Action Unit (NBI-SAU), with the assistance of Makati Police Station, Palanan Substation, by virtue of Search Warrant issued by RTC of Makati City, entered the premises of WANG LIANGGUI alias WANG and/or occupants of 3813 Cuenca St., Palanan, Makati City. The search, which was conducted in the presence of a Brgy. Kagawad, resulted in the discovery of illegal items and articles such as 4 pistols, 1 hand grenade, 2 jungle bolos, handcuff, sight and scope for firearm improvement, suspected illegal drugs and paraphernalia. A Chinese national was also found inside the subject house as a victim of kidnapping by one of the Chinese occupants. He was then rescued. Several Chinese nationals were invited to the NBI for identification and verification in order to determine probable cause to believe that they were involved in the commission of the illegal acts. Charges involved are violations of RA 9165 (Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002), RA 10591 (Comprehensive Firearms and Ammunition Regulation Act), and Kidnapping. On March 3, 2021, operatives of NBI-Cavite District Office (NBI-CAVIDO) seized 25 pcs laptop, 20 pcs OTP dangles, 2 pcs internet routers, 32 pcs mobile phones, 30 pcs various access devices, 1 pc uninterrupted power supply, 1 pc digital video recorder, and 1 pc printer. Items were seized at FRC Mall, E. Aguinaldo H-way, Palico III, Imus, Cavite by virtue of Search Warrant issued by RTC Branch 109, Cavite against JIANDONG LI, SHANYONG LI, et.al for violation of RA 8484. On March 3 and 4, 2021, operatives of NBI-Intellectual Property Division (NBI-IPRD) seized counterfeit electrical wires bearing the mark “Powerflex” with an estimated value of Php 7,500.00. Items were seized by virtue of Search Warrants for violation of RA 8293 issued against thirteen (13) hardwares located in Manila, Malabon, Tarlac, and Pampanga. On March 4, 2021, operatives of NBI-Western Visayas Regional Office (NBI-WEMRO) arrested JUNELYN O. GREGORIO, ARNEL B. GEMOTO, JESSIE M. BARRIATOS, PIO D. CASTILLANES and GRACE INCHON for Syndicated Estafa. Subject was arrested in an entrapment operation conducted at West Avenue, Molo, Iloilo City. Subject was caught in flagrante delicto after receiving marked money representing the supposed new investment on her “25 Day Double Your Money Investment Scheme”. Despite having no secondary license obtained from SEC or permits from any government agency to engage in investment taking business from the public yet, Subjects continue to carry out the scheme and even promoted a new scheme wherein payout is released allegedly on daily basis. Charges for Syndicated Estafa Committed on Large Scale in relation to Cybercrime Law will be charged against Subjects before the Iloilo Prosecutors Office. On March 4, 2021, operatives of NBI-CALABARZON arrested EDUARDO PARAS y MANALASTAS, AMALIA VILLALON y GUADALUPE, MYRNA MIQUE y OBNIAL, and MYLENE HIZOLA y VILLANUEVA in an entrapment operation conducted in Cabuyao, Laguna, for Syndicated Estafa. Subjects are now under detention while documents and the pieces of evidence necessary for their inquest proceedings at the City Prosecutor of Cabuyao City are being prepared for violation of 315 of the Revised Penal Code in relation to PD 1689 and RA 9829 (Pre-Need Code of the Philippines). On March 4, 2021, operatives of NBI-Naga District Office (NBI-NADO) arrested GEORGIO SOLON SANCHEZ, ROMEL CAMACHO AMPO, ARNIEL AUZA BELICARIO, JUNREY DONCILLO CODENIERA, JONATHAN CABILAO PEREZ, JERON ESPRA ABESIA, ROEL ARANAS TOLENTIN, MARLON DELIMA LARITA, ANNEX LABRADOR LOSENTES, JENNIFER GABUTAN CUI, DENNIS SANCHEZ OPURA, and CARLO JOHN LAKANDULA for violation of RA 9165 (Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002). Subjects were arrested in buy-bust operation conducted after confirming the illegal drug trade activity thru test-buy and the maintenance of drug dens by the main target, GEORGIO SOLON SANCHEZ also known as “POLOY” or “POLONG”. Subjects are temporarily detained at NBI-CEVRO Detention Cell while charges for violation of RA 9165 to be made thru inquest proceedings are being prepared. On March 4, 2021, operatives of NBI-Southeastern Mindanao Regional Office (NBI-SEMRO) rescued a minor victim, an alleged kidnap victim. Victim was rescued at Purok 1 Bayanihan Padada, Davao del Sur. The said operation was coordinated with the MSSDO and PNP, Kiblawan, Davao del Sur. On March 5, 2021, operatives of NBI-Dagupan District Office (NBI-DADO) rescued eleven (11) trafficked workers. On the aforesaid date, joint personnel of Department Labor and Employment (DOLE), Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD), local police of Brgy. Baquioen, Sual, Pangasinan, and NBI-DADO conducted an operation to rescue individuals who were working as bangus feeders. During the operation, it was observed that employees were working in hazardous environment and unsafe condition. The said employees disclosed that they were lured to work there for promised of good benefits but in fact, they were exploited, defrauded, and threatened by the use of law or legal processes when they tried to leave. The fish farm is registered corporation named as Unicorp Agri-Aqua Ventures, Inc. owned and operated by certain AH GONG, who was not around during the operation. Three (3) Chinese nationals were invited for verification. Upon verification, it was learned that the two (2) of the Chinese nationals have working visas and with regard to the other Chinese national, operatives were advised to turn over his person to the custody of Bureau of Immigration. Request letter for the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) for the incorporators of Unicorp was prepared being for filing of appropriate charges. Rescued individuals are now under the custody and disposition of DSWD. On March 5, 2021, operatives of NBI-Laoag District Office (NBI-LADO) arrested CRISTINA LORETO ACDAL and CRISTINA RAMOS for illegal retailing of petroleum products. An information was received regarding the alleged illegal retailing of gasoline being perpetrated with impunity by sari-sari store owners in Poblacion, Pagudpod, Ilocos Norte. Thereafter, surveillance and test buy from the two individuals mentioned in the report. Verification with the Department of Energy (DOE) reveals that the said individuals named LORETO ACDAL and CRISTINA RAMOS in the database system of Liquid Fuels Retail Outlets’ Owner/Operator/Company with valid Certificate of Compliance from the Department of Energy. With these, an Inspection Order was secured from the Bureau of Protection (BFP) LADO operatives, together with BFP personnel, conducted a buy-bust operation resulting in the seizure of several bottles of petroleum product, plastic containers containing gasoline for retail and plastic hose used to siphon gasoline into bottles. Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the Provincial Prosecutor’s Office, Laoag City and separately charged for violation of BP 33, as amended by PD 1865 and violation of DOE Department Circular 2003-11-010. On March 9, 2021, operatives of NBI-Anti-Violence Against Women and Children (NBI-AVAWCD) arrested MARVIN INCIONG y RUIZO by virtue of Warrant of Arrest. An information was received by AVAWCD regarding the Subject, a fugitive from justice, whose whereabouts had been established in the province of Batangas. He was involved in the recent infamous jailbreak at the Galas Police Station that occurred on January 7, 2021. Acting on the information and after proper coordination with the local police and NBI Batangas, NBI-AVAWCD proceeded to Lipa City, Batangas. Thereat, the informant disclosed that the fugitive can be found inside San Vicente Church, Banay-Banay, Lipa City. After confirming the fugitive’s presence inside the church, operatives effected the arrest. MARVIN INCIONG did not resist arrest and yielded to the operatives. On March 10, 2021, operatives of NBI-Special Operations Group (NBI-SOG) arrested JOHN CARLOS PEDRAGOSA GARCIA for misrepresenting himself as connected to Senator Christopher Lawrence “Bong” Go (Senator Go) and extorted money from unsuspecting prominent businessmen and private individuals. One of the victims alleged that a certain John Carlos Garcia introduced himself to be connected to Senator Go and was able to dupe prominent businessmen and private individuals from Albay, Laguna, Quezon and Rizal in various amounts totaling P6 M. One of the victims narrated that he was duped by Subject Garcia for P50,000.00. He also relayed to the operatives the names of the other individuals who were victimized by subject Garcia. Another victim in San Pablo, Laguna stated in her affidavit that her friend offered her a project for the construction of a facility to be used for operation of a Philippine Offshore Gaming Corporation in Buhatan, Sto. Domingo, Albay. The victim accepted the offer and was introduced to Subject John Garcia. Subject Garcia then told her that the secretary of Senator Go named Geraldyne Riano (Riano) is his friend. Subject Garcia demanded from the victim a total amount of Php 1 Million as advance payment for the project in Albay and Malunay, Quezon. Subject Garcia promised the victim that he will arrange a meeting between her and Senator Go but the meeting did not happen. The victim went to the office of Senator Go and was surprised to learn that Riano and Garcia are not employees of Senator Go. Another victim revealed that Subject Garcia bought from her a Suzuki Ertiga car and issued a check amounting to Php 250,000.00 as initial payment but was not honored by the bank. A record check on subject Garcia showed that he has a Warrant of Arrest issued by the RTC Mandaluyong City for Estafa (2 counts). NBI-SOG continued the surveillance operation and was able to track the whereabouts of the subject. On March 10, 2021, Subject Garcia was sighted in a resort in Bolinao, Pangasinan using the car he purchased from one of his victims. Thus, armed with a Warrant of Arrest, NBI-SOG proceeded to the target resort and immediately apprehended Subject Garcia. Subject Garcia was brought to NBI office where he had undergone standard booking procedures. On March 11, 2021, operatives of NBI-Environmental Crime Division (NBI-EnCD) arrested Brgy. Balanac Chairman DENNIS OLIPANO, MICHAEL ABAD y MARTINEZ, RANDY DELOS REYES y MARTINEZ, DANILO NORIEL y SATERA, and ABNER DAVAC y CABREGA for disposing and extracting boulders and minerals from Balanac River without permits from the DENR-MGB or the PMRB-Laguna. Subjects were arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from a report regarding an alleged illegal quarry operation in Brgy. Balanac, Municipality of Magdalena, Province of Laguna. Series of surveillance operation confirmed the veracity of the information and they were able to confirm the ongoing quarry operation at the said area. They were also able to transact with the seller, the Chairman of Brgy. Balanac, DENNIS OLIPANO, who agreed to sell four (4) truck loads of boulders for a price of Php 17,000 per truck. On March 11, 2021, a joint team of NBI-EnCD, DENR-Environmental Protection and Enforcement Task Force (EPETF), DENR-Mines and Geosciences Bureau (MGB) and Philippine Army 1 st Infantry Battalion conducted the operation resulting in the arrest of the aforementioned Subjects. Seized from the operation are four (4) trucks with a total estimated value of Php 6 Million and 30 cubic meters of boulders and fabricated screens with an estimated value of Php 43,000. Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the Prosecutor, Department of Justice, Manila for violation of Section 103 of RA 7942 (Philippine Mining Act of 1995) and Section 3 (e) of RA 3019 (Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act). On March 13, 2021, operatives of NBI-Northeastern Mindanao Regional Office (NBI-NEMRO), together with PDEA RO-X Camiguin, arrested HASMINE “BIBI” ALIB SAID and MACMAC MAUNTOL COMADUG for selling illegal drugs in violation of RA 9165 (Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act). Subject was arrested in a buy-bust operation which stemmed from an information that a certain BIBI is selling shabu in Iligan City, Cagayan de Oro City, Marawi City and neighboring municipalities of Misamis Oriental, Lanao del Norte and Lanao del Sur. The operation also yielded 983.9871 grams of shabu with an estimated street value of Php 6,800.00. On March 16, operatives of NBI-Dagupan District Office (NBI-DADO) arrested JACQUELYN DE GUZMAN (manager), MARJORIE DE GUZMAN CASTILLEJOS (owner), and MARK IAN DE GUZMAN (employee/pimp) for Human Trafficking. Subjects were arrested in an entrapment/rescue operation conducted at Marjorie Resto Bar in Urdaneta City, Pangasinan. The operation also resulted in the rescue of six (6) victims. Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the City Prosecutor’s Office, Urdaneta City for violation of RA 9208 (Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act). On March 18, 2021, operatives of NBI-Central Visayas Regional Office (NBI-CEVRO) arrested ROGELIO SUMALINOG NEBRES and RAKIM SULTAN BUSARA for falsifying RT-PCR Test Result. On March 17, 2021, the incumbent Mayor of San Miguel, Bohol and Bohol and former NBI Director Atty. Virgilio Mendez gave the information that there is a widespread selling of falsified RT-PCR Test Result at Cebu City ports. These negative RT-PCR Test results are being offered to passengers bound for Bohol, particularly for Tagbilaran and Tubigon, in the amount of Php 1,500.00. After surveillance and verification, NBI-CEVRO was able to confirm the peddling of falsified RT-PCR Test results. The Regional Office immediately coordinated with Cebu Port Authority conveying theillegal activity at the ports area. Consequently, an entrapment operation was made on the aforementioned date which resulted in the arrest of ROGELIO SUMALINOG NEBRES at the vicinity of Pier 1, Port of Cebu and RAKIM SULTAN BUSARA at his shop located across Oriente Bldg. in Colon St, Cebu City. Subjects were caught in conspiracy with one another in creating falsified negative RT-PCR Test result using an editing computer software and demanding Php 1,500. Thus, it has been recommended that Subjects ROGELIO SUMALINOG NEBRES and RAKIM SULTAN BUSARA be prosecuted for Estafa through Falsification of Public Document penalized under Article 315 in relation to Article 171 and Article 8 of the Revised Penal Code in relation to RA 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012). On March 19, 2021, operatives of NBI-Intellectual Property Division (NBI-IPRD) seized 631 pieces of counterfeit Louis Vuitton products with an estimated value of Php 86, 798,321.35. Items were seized by virtue of Search Warrants issued against PAULITO BALLANO and/or occupants of No. 94 K7 St., Barangay East Kamias, Cubao Quezon City for violation of RA 8293. On March 21, 2021, operatives of NBI-Criminal Intelligence Division (NBI-CRID) arrested ROGER CRISTOBAL JR y ROXAS aka JAY-AR CRISTOBAL for Grave Coercion in relation to RA 10175 and RA 9995. Subject was arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from the complaint of Subject’s victim. According to the complainant, she met the Subject thru a mobile game “Mobile Legends”. Therefrom, they started their friendship and exchange messages thru Facebook Messenger. Subject then took advantage of their indecent/immoral conversation and threatened the complainant that he will pass said conversation to her live-in partner, who is working in Malaysia, if she will not give her nude picture. Because of fear, complainant submitted to Subject’s request. Thereafter, Subject threatened her that he will share her nude picture in social media if she will not follow him. From then on, Subject asked her to take pictures of her nude body and send to him thru Messenger. Complainant reported the matter to the NBI and said that Subject will see her in Baclaran, Pasay City. With this, the entrapment operation was hatched in the motel where Subject and complainant agreed to meet. The operation then resulted in the arrest of Subject ROGER CRISTOBAL JR y ROXAS aka JAY-AR CRISTOBAL. Charges for Grave Coercion in relation to RA 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012) and RA 9995 (Anti-Photo and Video Voyeurism Act of 2009) were filed against the Subject. On March 23, 2021, operatives of NBI-Environmental Crime Division (NBI-EnCD) arrested EDWARD DOBLADO y ESTEBAN, RONNEL ISIP y SUNGA, MARK PAUL RUNAS y MERCADO, and ANTHONY DAVID y FEXEL for illegal selling and occupation of land in San Mateo and Antipolo, Rizal. The operation stemmed from the letter sent by DENR-PENRO requesting for assistance in addressing the illegal selling and illegal occupation of land within the Upper Marikina River Basin Protected Landscape (UMRBPL) in San Mateo, Rizal. DENR-PENRO added that upon their on-site monitoring they discovered three (3) illegal development and construction built within the UMRBPL Antipolo, Rizal. NBI-EnCD operatives together with DENR representatives conducted a surveillance operation within the target areas. The joint team discovered permanent structures were built within UMPRBPL and they were able to verify the existence of five (5) structures. With these, NBI-EnCD and DENR-PENRO conducted an operation and proceeded to the target areas on March 23, 2021. The joint operatives were able to arrest the owners/occupants Subject Isip and Subject Doblado in San Mateo Rizal, while Subjects Runas and David were arrested in Antipolo, Rizal. The owner of the fifth improvement in Antipolo which at the time of the operation is still under construction was nowhere to be found. The four Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the Provincial Prosecutor of Rizal for violation of R.A. 7586 (National Integrated Protected Areas System Act of 1992) as amended by R.A. 11038 and violation of P.D. 705 (Revised Forestry Code of the Philippines) as amended. In addition, the owner of the fifth structure identified as JAIME GONZALES (at-large) was included in the charge. On March 23, 2021, operatives of NBI-Cagayan Valley District Office (NBI-CAVRO) arrested ARDELYN U. ABAD for having in control, possession, management and sale of imported used clothes. Subject was arrested in Brgy. Ugac Sur, Tuguegarao City, Cagayan, by virtue of Search Warrant for violation of RA 4653 (An Act to Safeguard the Health of the People and Maintain the Dignity of the Nation by Declaring it a National Policy to Prohibit the Commercial Importation of Textile Articles Commonly Known as Used Clothing and Rags). Subject was duly apprised of her rights and was brought to NBI-CAVRO for proper booking procedures. On March 24, 2021, operatives of NBI-MIMAROPA arrested JOELIFER ANN ENRIQUEZ y COMIA and ROMEL MAGTIBAY y CABESA in a videoke bar located at Sitio Curva, Pinagsabangan, Naujan, Oriental Mindoro, for violation of RA 9208. Nine (9) women were likewise rescued in the operation. Documentation is on-going for inquest proceeding before the Provincial Prosecutor’s Office. On March 24, 2021, operatives of NBI-Cagayan Valley District Office (NBI-CAVRO) arrested BILLY IBARRA SISTOZA et.al. for Syndicated Estafa. Subjects were arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from the complaint of Subjects’ victim. According to the complainant, Subjects are posing as legitimate registered land owners of parcels of land situated in the municipality of Santa Ana, Cagayan. Believing that one of the arrested Subjects is the registered owner of parcels of land, complainant entered into a contract of sale with the Subjects. Complainant paid an initial payment in the amount of Php 1,500,000.00 as part of the total consideration for the parcels of land. In the interim, complainant learned that the real owner of the parcels of land offered for sale had long been deceased. Feeling aggrieved and since Subjects were still asking money as part of the total consideration for the parcels of land, complainant went to NBI-CAVRO. Acting on the complaint, operatives conducted an entrapment operation which resulted in the arrest of BILLY IBARRA SISTOZA et.al. for violation of Article 315 of the Revised Penal Code in relation to PD 1689 (Syndicated Estafa). Subjects were duly apprised of their rights and were brought to NBI-CAVRO for proper booking procedures. On March 24, 2021, operatives of NBI-Ilocos Regional Office (NBI-IRO) arrested JOHN LLYOD VILLANUEVA in an entrapment operation conducted in San Fernando City, La Union for violation of RA 10364 (Expanded Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act). On March 25, 2021, operatives of NBI-Dagupan District Office (NBI-DADO) arrested ROSED M. KITAMURA, ROLEN N. CATALUNA, and VIRGILIO S. ORDOQUEJO JR. in Rosales Pangasinan for Attempted Estafa in relation to Cybercrime Law. Subjects were arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from a complaint of Subjects’ victim. According to the complainant, Subjects represented themselves as having the capacity to supply gold scanner based on the latter’s Facebook account. The complainant ordered the product and gave Php 300,000.00 as partial payment. Subjects promised to deliver the item after 10 days but they failed to deliver the product and even blocked the complainant’s call after the latter demanded the delivery and return of his money. The Subject demanded again from the other client half the price of the gold scanner worth Php 450,000. With this, complainant sought the assistance of the NBI. Acting on the complaint, an entrapment operation was conducted resulting in the arrest of Subjects ROSED M. KITAMURA, ROLEN N. CATALUNA, and VIRGILIO S. ORDOQUEJO JR. Subjects were brought to NBI-DADO for the proper booking procedures and temporary detention. They were presented for inquest proceedings before the Provincial Prosecutor’s Office for Attempted Estafa in relation to Cybercrime Law. On March 26, 2021, operatives of NBI-Bacolod District Office (NBI-BACDO) arrested RANDYL SATUR y ARCENIO for selling illegal drugs. Subject was arrested in a buy-bust operation conducted at Purok Talaba, Sitio Magsungay, Brgy. Singcang, Bacolod City, Negros Occidental. Seized during the operation are two (2) heat-sealed transparent medium sachets and one (1) heat-sealed small sachet, all containing white crystalline substance suspected to be shabu with an estimated street value of more or less Php 30,000.00. The seized drug items were submitted/turned over to PNP Negros Occidental Provincial Crime Laboratory for examination and safekeeping. Charges for violation of RA 9165 (Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002) were being readied against the Subject who will undergo inquest proceedings before the Inquest Prosecutor, Bacolod City. The NBI-Death Investigation Division (NBI-DID) filed several criminal charges against eleven (11) individuals who were involved in the untimely death of Christine Angelica F. Dacera. Included in the charge is a Police Official who first conducted the autopsy on the cadaver of Victim Dacera. The charged individuals were MARK ANTHONY ROSALES, ROMEL GALIDO Y DALURO, JOHN PASCUAL DELA SERNA III Y REYES, DARWIN JOSEPH MACALLA Y DE LEON, GREGORIO ANGELO RAFAEL DE GUZMAN Y DELA FUENTE, JEZREEL RAPINAN Y PAMISA, ALAIN CHEN Y DAYANAN, REYMAR ENGLIS Y MABINI, ATTY. NEPTALI G. MAROTO, LOUIE DELIMA Y SUNGA, and P/MAJ MICHAEL NICK W. SARMIENTO, M.D. Upon directive of Department of Justice (DOJ) Secretary Menardo Guevarra and the letter of Sharon Rose Dacera (victim’s mother) requesting a parallel investigation on her daughter’s death, NBI conducted an investigation on the death of Dacera. Testimonies of the witnesses and persons involved revealed that on December 27, 2020, Dacera together with her friends Subjects GALIDO, ENGLIS, DELIMA, DELA SERNA, and RAPINAN booked an overnight stay in City Garden Hotel in Makati City starting from December 31, 2020 to January 1. 2020. According to the Duty Manager of the hotel he was a friend of Dacera’s companion and asked by Dacera’s group to facilitate their booking and accommodated the booking. Dacera’s group was first designated to Room 2309 but later transferred to Room 2209 due to the Air-Conditioning malfunction. In the evening of December 31, 2020, Victim Dacera together with her friends partied in their hotel room while drinking several liquors. Coincidentally, while waiting for the New Year countdown, ED (one of the companions of Victim Dacera in Room 2209) brought them to Room 2207 where his friend identified as DHEEJ is also checked-in. CCTV footages revealed that the victim and her friends were seen go back and forth in Rooms 2207 and 2209. Results of the autopsy report conducted by the NBI- Medico Legal Division Chief revealed that in contrast to the autopsy report of P/Maj. Sarmiento, M.D., Victim’s urinary bladder was full of urine and in fact the NBI Forensic Team was able to extract 130 ml of urine and no abrasion was found in her labia majora. According to the testimonies of the witnesses who checked-in at Room 2207, around 03:00 a.m. in the morning, Victim Dacera told them that she did not want to be at Room 2209 because her companions because they were high for taking party drugs in contrast to the sworn statements of the victim’s friends and companions at Room 2209. Thus, based on the forensic evidences and testimonies of the witnesses, NBI-DID filed before the Department of Justice (DOJ): Violation of Sec. 3 (a) of the R.A. 9165 (Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002) against Subject ROSALES for introducing the party drugs to his companions; Violation of Section 3 (k) of R.A. 9165 against Subjects ROSALES and GALIDO for delivering and giving away the party drugs; Perjury against Subjects GALIDO, DELA SERNA, and MACALLA for providing false testimonies; Obstruction of Justice against Subjects ROSALES, GALIDO, DELA SERNA, DE GUZMAN, RAPINAN, CHEN, ENGLIS, MACALLA, and ATTY. MAROTO for giving false or fabricated information to mislead or prevent the law enforcement agencies form apprehending the offenders; Reckless Imprudence Resulting in Homicide against Subjects DELA SERNA, RAPINAN, CHEN, and DELIMA for recklessly neglect the condition of Victim Dacera which led on to her untimely death; Article 171 par. 4 of the RPC (Falsification of Official Document by Public Officer) against POLICE MAJOR SARMIENTO, M.D. for declaring untruthful findings on his autopsy report. The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) filed charges against LORETA MORALES y VELASCO, Barangay Chairman of Barangay 143 of Pasay City over an alleged irregularities in the implementation of DSWD Social Amelioration Program (SAP). The case stemmed from a report received by the NBI-Anti-Graft Division (NBI-AGD) alleging the irregularities in the implementation of the DSWD SAP in the said barangay. Complainant appeared before the NBI complaining against their barangay chairman. Investigation conducted revealed that Subject, being the barangay chairman, distributed SAP form to residents of Pasay City not qualified to receive the same based on the existing guidelines. Among the persons not qualified to receive the SAP were the daughter of the barangay chairman, common-law wife of the barangay treasurer, and seventeen (17) individuals who are no longer residents of Barangay 143 as they are already residing at Trece Martires, Cavite. After thorough investigation, there was sufficient evidence found to warrant the filing of charges against Subject LORETA MORALES y VELASCO. The distribution of SAC forms to unqualified individuals constitutes giving unwarranted benefits, advantage or preference in the discharge of the official administrative function which was committed through manifest partiality, evident bad faith or gross inexcusable negligence. In addition, the distribution of SAP funds to families other than what was provided for by the law constitutes Technical Malversation. Subject, being the Barangay Chairman, was held accountable through her participation in the implementation of SAP. Finally, the unjustified distribution of SAP to residents of another LGU who are claimed to be election supporters and to that of Subject’s daughter, is inconsistent with the mandates of the Code of the Conduct and Ethical Standards for Public Officials and Employees. Charges were filed against Subject LORETA MORALES y VELASCO before the Ombudsman for violation of Section 9 in relation to Section 3(e) of RA 3019 (Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act), Illegal Use of Public Funds (Technical Malversation) under Article 220 of the Revised Penal Code, and violation of Section 11 in relation to Section 4(a) and 4(d) of RA 6713 (Code of Conduct and Ethical Standards for Public Officials and Employees). The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) announces the promulgation of Sta. Cruz, Laguna Family Court Branch 6, convicting Subjects MARY JANE MENDOZA y PARAISO and MAGDELANA VIRAY y MASALONGA, who were arrested by the elements of NBI-Anti-Violence Against Women and Children Division (NBI-AVAWCD) on September 26, 2019 and charged for Human Trafficking. The court hearings were attended by the victims and witnesses who gave their testimonies which solidified the fact that Subjects Mendoza and Viray indeed committed the crime of Qualified Trafficking. On March 04, 2021, a judgment was promulgated finding accused MARY JANE MENDOZA y PARAISO and MAGDALENA VIRAY y MASALOGA guilty beyond reasonable doubt for five (5) counts of Qualified Trafficking in Persons as defined and penalized under R.A. 9208 as further amended by RA 10364. The court ordered the two (2) accused to suffer Life Imprisonment for each count and also ordered them to pay a fine of Php 2 Million without eligibility for parole and to pay each private complainants the amount Php 200,000.00 as moral damages and Php 100,000.00 as exemplary damages. The court, however, ordered the acquittal of WARREN MASACAYAN Y REYES for failure of the prosecution to prove the guilt of the latter. The NBI-Intellectual Property Division (NBI-IPRD) seized 29 machines under the label Pay&Go. Machines were confiscated after the implementation of Search Warrants issued on March 22, 2021, by the Pasig Regional Trial Court (RTC) Branch 159 for the protection intellectual property rights of complainant, MANILA EXPRESS PAYMENT SYSTEM (MEPS), the owner of “Touchpay” machine, a duly patented and registered Utility Model before the Intellectual Property Office of the Philippines. The Search Warrants were implemented in different parts of Metro Manila – Quezon City, Makati, Taguig and Muntinlupa and they and resulted in the confiscation of the 29 machines under the label Pay&Go as these machines created confusion and false beliefs to users that they are MEPS’ APM (Automatic Payment Machines) resulting in infringement to the intellectual property rights of MEPS. this was discovered due to complaints received by MEPS from their customers about defective machines but upon checking it was not their machine but a machine owned by ELECTRONIC TRANSFER AND ADVANCE PROCESSING, INC. (e-TAP) distributed by BTI Payments Philippines. Criminal complaints for violation of Section 168 (Unfair Competition) of R.A. 8293 otherwise known as the “Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines will be filed before the Prosecutors Office against PERSEVERANDO HERNANDEZ, MARLON PORTUGAL, ANTONIO LASALA, REYNALDO ISIDRO, RACHEL MERCADO (Officers of e-TAP), DAVID SCOTT GLEN, PETER, ALEXANDER BLACKET, DANILO IBARRA, and ALINA SISON (Officers of BTI Payment Phils, Inc.).

NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION

On March 3, 2021, operatives of NBI-Special Action Unit (NBI-SAU), with the assistance of Makati Police Station, Palanan Substation, by virtue of Search Warrant issued by RTC of Makati City, entered the premises of WANG LIANGGUI alias WANG and/or occupants of 3813 Cuenca St., Palanan, Makati City. The search, which was conducted in the presence of a Brgy. Kagawad, resulted in the discovery of illegal items and articles such as 4 pistols, 1 hand grenade, 2 jungle bolos, handcuff, sight and scope for firearm improvement, suspected illegal drugs and paraphernalia. A Chinese national was also found inside the subject house as a victim of kidnapping by one of the Chinese occupants. He was then rescued. Several Chinese nationals were invited to the NBI for identification and verification in order to determine probable cause to believe that they were involved in the commission of the illegal acts. Charges involved are violations of RA 9165 (Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002), RA 10591 (Comprehensive Firearms and Ammunition Regulation Act), and Kidnapping. On March 3, 2021, operatives of NBI-Cavite District Office (NBI-CAVIDO) seized 25 pcs laptop, 20 pcs OTP dangles, 2 pcs internet routers, 32 pcs mobile phones, 30 pcs various access devices, 1 pc uninterrupted power supply, 1 pc digital video recorder, and 1 pc printer. Items were seized at FRC Mall, E. Aguinaldo H-way, Palico III, Imus, Cavite by virtue of Search Warrant issued by RTC Branch 109, Cavite against JIANDONG LI, SHANYONG LI, et.al for violation of RA 8484. On March 3 and 4, 2021, operatives of NBI-Intellectual Property Division (NBI-IPRD) seized counterfeit electrical wires bearing the mark “Powerflex” with an estimated value of Php 7,500.00. Items were seized by virtue of Search Warrants for violation of RA 8293 issued against thirteen (13) hardwares located in Manila, Malabon, Tarlac, and Pampanga. On March 4, 2021, operatives of NBI-Western Visayas Regional Office (NBI-WEMRO) arrested JUNELYN O. GREGORIO, ARNEL B. GEMOTO, JESSIE M. BARRIATOS, PIO D. CASTILLANES and GRACE INCHON for Syndicated Estafa. Subject was arrested in an entrapment operation conducted at West Avenue, Molo, Iloilo City. Subject was caught in flagrante delicto after receiving marked money representing the supposed new investment on her “25 Day Double Your Money Investment Scheme”. Despite having no secondary license obtained from SEC or permits from any government agency to engage in investment taking business from the public yet, Subjects continue to carry out the scheme and even promoted a new scheme wherein payout is released allegedly on daily basis. Charges for Syndicated Estafa Committed on Large Scale in relation to Cybercrime Law will be charged against Subjects before the Iloilo Prosecutors Office. On March 4, 2021, operatives of NBI-CALABARZON arrested EDUARDO PARAS y MANALASTAS, AMALIA VILLALON y GUADALUPE, MYRNA MIQUE y OBNIAL, and MYLENE HIZOLA y VILLANUEVA in an entrapment operation conducted in Cabuyao, Laguna, for Syndicated Estafa. Subjects are now under detention while documents and the pieces of evidence necessary for their inquest proceedings at the City Prosecutor of Cabuyao City are being prepared for violation of 315 of the Revised Penal Code in relation to PD 1689 and RA 9829 (Pre-Need Code of the Philippines). On March 4, 2021, operatives of NBI-Naga District Office (NBI-NADO) arrested GEORGIO SOLON SANCHEZ, ROMEL CAMACHO AMPO, ARNIEL AUZA BELICARIO, JUNREY DONCILLO CODENIERA, JONATHAN CABILAO PEREZ, JERON ESPRA ABESIA, ROEL ARANAS TOLENTIN, MARLON DELIMA LARITA, ANNEX LABRADOR LOSENTES, JENNIFER GABUTAN CUI, DENNIS SANCHEZ OPURA, and CARLO JOHN LAKANDULA for violation of RA 9165 (Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002). Subjects were arrested in buy-bust operation conducted after confirming the illegal drug trade activity thru test-buy and the maintenance of drug dens by the main target, GEORGIO SOLON SANCHEZ also known as “POLOY” or “POLONG”. Subjects are temporarily detained at NBI-CEVRO Detention Cell while charges for violation of RA 9165 to be made thru inquest proceedings are being prepared. On March 4, 2021, operatives of NBI-Southeastern Mindanao Regional Office (NBI-SEMRO) rescued a minor victim, an alleged kidnap victim. Victim was rescued at Purok 1 Bayanihan Padada, Davao del Sur. The said operation was coordinated with the MSSDO and PNP, Kiblawan, Davao del Sur. On March 5, 2021, operatives of NBI-Dagupan District Office (NBI-DADO) rescued eleven (11) trafficked workers. On the aforesaid date, joint personnel of Department Labor and Employment (DOLE), Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD), local police of Brgy. Baquioen, Sual, Pangasinan, and NBI-DADO conducted an operation to rescue individuals who were working as bangus feeders. During the operation, it was observed that employees were working in hazardous environment and unsafe condition. The said employees disclosed that they were lured to work there for promised of good benefits but in fact, they were exploited, defrauded, and threatened by the use of law or legal processes when they tried to leave. The fish farm is registered corporation named as Unicorp Agri-Aqua Ventures, Inc. owned and operated by certain AH GONG, who was not around during the operation. Three (3) Chinese nationals were invited for verification. Upon verification, it was learned that the two (2) of the Chinese nationals have working visas and with regard to the other Chinese national, operatives were advised to turn over his person to the custody of Bureau of Immigration. Request letter for the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) for the incorporators of Unicorp was prepared being for filing of appropriate charges. Rescued individuals are now under the custody and disposition of DSWD. On March 5, 2021, operatives of NBI-Laoag District Office (NBI-LADO) arrested CRISTINA LORETO ACDAL and CRISTINA RAMOS for illegal retailing of petroleum products. An information was received regarding the alleged illegal retailing of gasoline being perpetrated with impunity by sari-sari store owners in Poblacion, Pagudpod, Ilocos Norte. Thereafter, surveillance and test buy from the two individuals mentioned in the report. Verification with the Department of Energy (DOE) reveals that the said individuals named LORETO ACDAL and CRISTINA RAMOS in the database system of Liquid Fuels Retail Outlets’ Owner/Operator/Company with valid Certificate of Compliance from the Department of Energy. With these, an Inspection Order was secured from the Bureau of Protection (BFP) LADO operatives, together with BFP personnel, conducted a buy-bust operation resulting in the seizure of several bottles of petroleum product, plastic containers containing gasoline for retail and plastic hose used to siphon gasoline into bottles. Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the Provincial Prosecutor’s Office, Laoag City and separately charged for violation of BP 33, as amended by PD 1865 and violation of DOE Department Circular 2003-11-010. On March 9, 2021, operatives of NBI-Anti-Violence Against Women and Children (NBI-AVAWCD) arrested MARVIN INCIONG y RUIZO by virtue of Warrant of Arrest. An information was received by AVAWCD regarding the Subject, a fugitive from justice, whose whereabouts had been established in the province of Batangas. He was involved in the recent infamous jailbreak at the Galas Police Station that occurred on January 7, 2021. Acting on the information and after proper coordination with the local police and NBI Batangas, NBI-AVAWCD proceeded to Lipa City, Batangas. Thereat, the informant disclosed that the fugitive can be found inside San Vicente Church, Banay-Banay, Lipa City. After confirming the fugitive’s presence inside the church, operatives effected the arrest. MARVIN INCIONG did not resist arrest and yielded to the operatives. On March 10, 2021, operatives of NBI-Special Operations Group (NBI-SOG) arrested JOHN CARLOS PEDRAGOSA GARCIA for misrepresenting himself as connected to Senator Christopher Lawrence “Bong” Go (Senator Go) and extorted money from unsuspecting prominent businessmen and private individuals. One of the victims alleged that a certain John Carlos Garcia introduced himself to be connected to Senator Go and was able to dupe prominent businessmen and private individuals from Albay, Laguna, Quezon and Rizal in various amounts totaling P6 M. One of the victims narrated that he was duped by Subject Garcia for P50,000.00. He also relayed to the operatives the names of the other individuals who were victimized by subject Garcia. Another victim in San Pablo, Laguna stated in her affidavit that her friend offered her a project for the construction of a facility to be used for operation of a Philippine Offshore Gaming Corporation in Buhatan, Sto. Domingo, Albay. The victim accepted the offer and was introduced to Subject John Garcia. Subject Garcia then told her that the secretary of Senator Go named Geraldyne Riano (Riano) is his friend. Subject Garcia demanded from the victim a total amount of Php 1 Million as advance payment for the project in Albay and Malunay, Quezon. Subject Garcia promised the victim that he will arrange a meeting between her and Senator Go but the meeting did not happen. The victim went to the office of Senator Go and was surprised to learn that Riano and Garcia are not employees of Senator Go. Another victim revealed that Subject Garcia bought from her a Suzuki Ertiga car and issued a check amounting to Php 250,000.00 as initial payment but was not honored by the bank. A record check on subject Garcia showed that he has a Warrant of Arrest issued by the RTC Mandaluyong City for Estafa (2 counts). NBI-SOG continued the surveillance operation and was able to track the whereabouts of the subject. On March 10, 2021, Subject Garcia was sighted in a resort in Bolinao, Pangasinan using the car he purchased from one of his victims. Thus, armed with a Warrant of Arrest, NBI-SOG proceeded to the target resort and immediately apprehended Subject Garcia. Subject Garcia was brought to NBI office where he had undergone standard booking procedures. On March 11, 2021, operatives of NBI-Environmental Crime Division (NBI-EnCD) arrested Brgy. Balanac Chairman DENNIS OLIPANO, MICHAEL ABAD y MARTINEZ, RANDY DELOS REYES y MARTINEZ, DANILO NORIEL y SATERA, and ABNER DAVAC y CABREGA for disposing and extracting boulders and minerals from Balanac River without permits from the DENR-MGB or the PMRB-Laguna. Subjects were arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from a report regarding an alleged illegal quarry operation in Brgy. Balanac, Municipality of Magdalena, Province of Laguna. Series of surveillance operation confirmed the veracity of the information and they were able to confirm the ongoing quarry operation at the said area. They were also able to transact with the seller, the Chairman of Brgy. Balanac, DENNIS OLIPANO, who agreed to sell four (4) truck loads of boulders for a price of Php 17,000 per truck. On March 11, 2021, a joint team of NBI-EnCD, DENR-Environmental Protection and Enforcement Task Force (EPETF), DENR-Mines and Geosciences Bureau (MGB) and Philippine Army 1 st Infantry Battalion conducted the operation resulting in the arrest of the aforementioned Subjects. Seized from the operation are four (4) trucks with a total estimated value of Php 6 Million and 30 cubic meters of boulders and fabricated screens with an estimated value of Php 43,000. Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the Prosecutor, Department of Justice, Manila for violation of Section 103 of RA 7942 (Philippine Mining Act of 1995) and Section 3 (e) of RA 3019 (Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act). On March 13, 2021, operatives of NBI-Northeastern Mindanao Regional Office (NBI-NEMRO), together with PDEA RO-X Camiguin, arrested HASMINE “BIBI” ALIB SAID and MACMAC MAUNTOL COMADUG for selling illegal drugs in violation of RA 9165 (Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act). Subject was arrested in a buy-bust operation which stemmed from an information that a certain BIBI is selling shabu in Iligan City, Cagayan de Oro City, Marawi City and neighboring municipalities of Misamis Oriental, Lanao del Norte and Lanao del Sur. The operation also yielded 983.9871 grams of shabu with an estimated street value of Php 6,800.00. On March 16, operatives of NBI-Dagupan District Office (NBI-DADO) arrested JACQUELYN DE GUZMAN (manager), MARJORIE DE GUZMAN CASTILLEJOS (owner), and MARK IAN DE GUZMAN (employee/pimp) for Human Trafficking. Subjects were arrested in an entrapment/rescue operation conducted at Marjorie Resto Bar in Urdaneta City, Pangasinan. The operation also resulted in the rescue of six (6) victims. Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the City Prosecutor’s Office, Urdaneta City for violation of RA 9208 (Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act). On March 18, 2021, operatives of NBI-Central Visayas Regional Office (NBI-CEVRO) arrested ROGELIO SUMALINOG NEBRES and RAKIM SULTAN BUSARA for falsifying RT-PCR Test Result. On March 17, 2021, the incumbent Mayor of San Miguel, Bohol and Bohol and former NBI Director Atty. Virgilio Mendez gave the information that there is a widespread selling of falsified RT-PCR Test Result at Cebu City ports. These negative RT-PCR Test results are being offered to passengers bound for Bohol, particularly for Tagbilaran and Tubigon, in the amount of Php 1,500.00. After surveillance and verification, NBI-CEVRO was able to confirm the peddling of falsified RT-PCR Test results. The Regional Office immediately coordinated with Cebu Port Authority conveying theillegal activity at the ports area. Consequently, an entrapment operation was made on the aforementioned date which resulted in the arrest of ROGELIO SUMALINOG NEBRES at the vicinity of Pier 1, Port of Cebu and RAKIM SULTAN BUSARA at his shop located across Oriente Bldg. in Colon St, Cebu City. Subjects were caught in conspiracy with one another in creating falsified negative RT-PCR Test result using an editing computer software and demanding Php 1,500. Thus, it has been recommended that Subjects ROGELIO SUMALINOG NEBRES and RAKIM SULTAN BUSARA be prosecuted for Estafa through Falsification of Public Document penalized under Article 315 in relation to Article 171 and Article 8 of the Revised Penal Code in relation to RA 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012). On March 19, 2021, operatives of NBI-Intellectual Property Division (NBI-IPRD) seized 631 pieces of counterfeit Louis Vuitton products with an estimated value of Php 86, 798,321.35. Items were seized by virtue of Search Warrants issued against PAULITO BALLANO and/or occupants of No. 94 K7 St., Barangay East Kamias, Cubao Quezon City for violation of RA 8293. On March 21, 2021, operatives of NBI-Criminal Intelligence Division (NBI-CRID) arrested ROGER CRISTOBAL JR y ROXAS aka JAY-AR CRISTOBAL for Grave Coercion in relation to RA 10175 and RA 9995. Subject was arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from the complaint of Subject’s victim. According to the complainant, she met the Subject thru a mobile game “Mobile Legends”. Therefrom, they started their friendship and exchange messages thru Facebook Messenger. Subject then took advantage of their indecent/immoral conversation and threatened the complainant that he will pass said conversation to her live-in partner, who is working in Malaysia, if she will not give her nude picture. Because of fear, complainant submitted to Subject’s request. Thereafter, Subject threatened her that he will share her nude picture in social media if she will not follow him. From then on, Subject asked her to take pictures of her nude body and send to him thru Messenger. Complainant reported the matter to the NBI and said that Subject will see her in Baclaran, Pasay City. With this, the entrapment operation was hatched in the motel where Subject and complainant agreed to meet. The operation then resulted in the arrest of Subject ROGER CRISTOBAL JR y ROXAS aka JAY-AR CRISTOBAL. Charges for Grave Coercion in relation to RA 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012) and RA 9995 (Anti-Photo and Video Voyeurism Act of 2009) were filed against the Subject. On March 23, 2021, operatives of NBI-Environmental Crime Division (NBI-EnCD) arrested EDWARD DOBLADO y ESTEBAN, RONNEL ISIP y SUNGA, MARK PAUL RUNAS y MERCADO, and ANTHONY DAVID y FEXEL for illegal selling and occupation of land in San Mateo and Antipolo, Rizal. The operation stemmed from the letter sent by DENR-PENRO requesting for assistance in addressing the illegal selling and illegal occupation of land within the Upper Marikina River Basin Protected Landscape (UMRBPL) in San Mateo, Rizal. DENR-PENRO added that upon their on-site monitoring they discovered three (3) illegal development and construction built within the UMRBPL Antipolo, Rizal. NBI-EnCD operatives together with DENR representatives conducted a surveillance operation within the target areas. The joint team discovered permanent structures were built within UMPRBPL and they were able to verify the existence of five (5) structures. With these, NBI-EnCD and DENR-PENRO conducted an operation and proceeded to the target areas on March 23, 2021. The joint operatives were able to arrest the owners/occupants Subject Isip and Subject Doblado in San Mateo Rizal, while Subjects Runas and David were arrested in Antipolo, Rizal. The owner of the fifth improvement in Antipolo which at the time of the operation is still under construction was nowhere to be found. The four Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the Provincial Prosecutor of Rizal for violation of R.A. 7586 (National Integrated Protected Areas System Act of 1992) as amended by R.A. 11038 and violation of P.D. 705 (Revised Forestry Code of the Philippines) as amended. In addition, the owner of the fifth structure identified as JAIME GONZALES (at-large) was included in the charge. On March 23, 2021, operatives of NBI-Cagayan Valley District Office (NBI-CAVRO) arrested ARDELYN U. ABAD for having in control, possession, management and sale of imported used clothes. Subject was arrested in Brgy. Ugac Sur, Tuguegarao City, Cagayan, by virtue of Search Warrant for violation of RA 4653 (An Act to Safeguard the Health of the People and Maintain the Dignity of the Nation by Declaring it a National Policy to Prohibit the Commercial Importation of Textile Articles Commonly Known as Used Clothing and Rags). Subject was duly apprised of her rights and was brought to NBI-CAVRO for proper booking procedures. On March 24, 2021, operatives of NBI-MIMAROPA arrested JOELIFER ANN ENRIQUEZ y COMIA and ROMEL MAGTIBAY y CABESA in a videoke bar located at Sitio Curva, Pinagsabangan, Naujan, Oriental Mindoro, for violation of RA 9208. Nine (9) women were likewise rescued in the operation. Documentation is on-going for inquest proceeding before the Provincial Prosecutor’s Office. On March 24, 2021, operatives of NBI-Cagayan Valley District Office (NBI-CAVRO) arrested BILLY IBARRA SISTOZA et.al. for Syndicated Estafa. Subjects were arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from the complaint of Subjects’ victim. According to the complainant, Subjects are posing as legitimate registered land owners of parcels of land situated in the municipality of Santa Ana, Cagayan. Believing that one of the arrested Subjects is the registered owner of parcels of land, complainant entered into a contract of sale with the Subjects. Complainant paid an initial payment in the amount of Php 1,500,000.00 as part of the total consideration for the parcels of land. In the interim, complainant learned that the real owner of the parcels of land offered for sale had long been deceased. Feeling aggrieved and since Subjects were still asking money as part of the total consideration for the parcels of land, complainant went to NBI-CAVRO. Acting on the complaint, operatives conducted an entrapment operation which resulted in the arrest of BILLY IBARRA SISTOZA et.al. for violation of Article 315 of the Revised Penal Code in relation to PD 1689 (Syndicated Estafa). Subjects were duly apprised of their rights and were brought to NBI-CAVRO for proper booking procedures. On March 24, 2021, operatives of NBI-Ilocos Regional Office (NBI-IRO) arrested JOHN LLYOD VILLANUEVA in an entrapment operation conducted in San Fernando City, La Union for violation of RA 10364 (Expanded Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act). On March 25, 2021, operatives of NBI-Dagupan District Office (NBI-DADO) arrested ROSED M. KITAMURA, ROLEN N. CATALUNA, and VIRGILIO S. ORDOQUEJO JR. in Rosales Pangasinan for Attempted Estafa in relation to Cybercrime Law. Subjects were arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from a complaint of Subjects’ victim. According to the complainant, Subjects represented themselves as having the capacity to supply gold scanner based on the latter’s Facebook account. The complainant ordered the product and gave Php 300,000.00 as partial payment. Subjects promised to deliver the item after 10 days but they failed to deliver the product and even blocked the complainant’s call after the latter demanded the delivery and return of his money. The Subject demanded again from the other client half the price of the gold scanner worth Php 450,000. With this, complainant sought the assistance of the NBI. Acting on the complaint, an entrapment operation was conducted resulting in the arrest of Subjects ROSED M. KITAMURA, ROLEN N. CATALUNA, and VIRGILIO S. ORDOQUEJO JR. Subjects were brought to NBI-DADO for the proper booking procedures and temporary detention. They were presented for inquest proceedings before the Provincial Prosecutor’s Office for Attempted Estafa in relation to Cybercrime Law. On March 26, 2021, operatives of NBI-Bacolod District Office (NBI-BACDO) arrested RANDYL SATUR y ARCENIO for selling illegal drugs. Subject was arrested in a buy-bust operation conducted at Purok Talaba, Sitio Magsungay, Brgy. Singcang, Bacolod City, Negros Occidental. Seized during the operation are two (2) heat-sealed transparent medium sachets and one (1) heat-sealed small sachet, all containing white crystalline substance suspected to be shabu with an estimated street value of more or less Php 30,000.00. The seized drug items were submitted/turned over to PNP Negros Occidental Provincial Crime Laboratory for examination and safekeeping. Charges for violation of RA 9165 (Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002) were being readied against the Subject who will undergo inquest proceedings before the Inquest Prosecutor, Bacolod City. The NBI-Death Investigation Division (NBI-DID) filed several criminal charges against eleven (11) individuals who were involved in the untimely death of Christine Angelica F. Dacera. Included in the charge is a Police Official who first conducted the autopsy on the cadaver of Victim Dacera. The charged individuals were MARK ANTHONY ROSALES, ROMEL GALIDO Y DALURO, JOHN PASCUAL DELA SERNA III Y REYES, DARWIN JOSEPH MACALLA Y DE LEON, GREGORIO ANGELO RAFAEL DE GUZMAN Y DELA FUENTE, JEZREEL RAPINAN Y PAMISA, ALAIN CHEN Y DAYANAN, REYMAR ENGLIS Y MABINI, ATTY. NEPTALI G. MAROTO, LOUIE DELIMA Y SUNGA, and P/MAJ MICHAEL NICK W. SARMIENTO, M.D. Upon directive of Department of Justice (DOJ) Secretary Menardo Guevarra and the letter of Sharon Rose Dacera (victim’s mother) requesting a parallel investigation on her daughter’s death, NBI conducted an investigation on the death of Dacera. Testimonies of the witnesses and persons involved revealed that on December 27, 2020, Dacera together with her friends Subjects GALIDO, ENGLIS, DELIMA, DELA SERNA, and RAPINAN booked an overnight stay in City Garden Hotel in Makati City starting from December 31, 2020 to January 1. 2020. According to the Duty Manager of the hotel he was a friend of Dacera’s companion and asked by Dacera’s group to facilitate their booking and accommodated the booking. Dacera’s group was first designated to Room 2309 but later transferred to Room 2209 due to the Air-Conditioning malfunction. In the evening of December 31, 2020, Victim Dacera together with her friends partied in their hotel room while drinking several liquors. Coincidentally, while waiting for the New Year countdown, ED (one of the companions of Victim Dacera in Room 2209) brought them to Room 2207 where his friend identified as DHEEJ is also checked-in. CCTV footages revealed that the victim and her friends were seen go back and forth in Rooms 2207 and 2209. Results of the autopsy report conducted by the NBI- Medico Legal Division Chief revealed that in contrast to the autopsy report of P/Maj. Sarmiento, M.D., Victim’s urinary bladder was full of urine and in fact the NBI Forensic Team was able to extract 130 ml of urine and no abrasion was found in her labia majora. According to the testimonies of the witnesses who checked-in at Room 2207, around 03:00 a.m. in the morning, Victim Dacera told them that she did not want to be at Room 2209 because her companions because they were high for taking party drugs in contrast to the sworn statements of the victim’s friends and companions at Room 2209. Thus, based on the forensic evidences and testimonies of the witnesses, NBI-DID filed before the Department of Justice (DOJ): Violation of Sec. 3 (a) of the R.A. 9165 (Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002) against Subject ROSALES for introducing the party drugs to his companions; Violation of Section 3 (k) of R.A. 9165 against Subjects ROSALES and GALIDO for delivering and giving away the party drugs; Perjury against Subjects GALIDO, DELA SERNA, and MACALLA for providing false testimonies; Obstruction of Justice against Subjects ROSALES, GALIDO, DELA SERNA, DE GUZMAN, RAPINAN, CHEN, ENGLIS, MACALLA, and ATTY. MAROTO for giving false or fabricated information to mislead or prevent the law enforcement agencies form apprehending the offenders; Reckless Imprudence Resulting in Homicide against Subjects DELA SERNA, RAPINAN, CHEN, and DELIMA for recklessly neglect the condition of Victim Dacera which led on to her untimely death; Article 171 par. 4 of the RPC (Falsification of Official Document by Public Officer) against POLICE MAJOR SARMIENTO, M.D. for declaring untruthful findings on his autopsy report. The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) filed charges against LORETA MORALES y VELASCO, Barangay Chairman of Barangay 143 of Pasay City over an alleged irregularities in the implementation of DSWD Social Amelioration Program (SAP). The case stemmed from a report received by the NBI-Anti-Graft Division (NBI-AGD) alleging the irregularities in the implementation of the DSWD SAP in the said barangay. Complainant appeared before the NBI complaining against their barangay chairman. Investigation conducted revealed that Subject, being the barangay chairman, distributed SAP form to residents of Pasay City not qualified to receive the same based on the existing guidelines. Among the persons not qualified to receive the SAP were the daughter of the barangay chairman, common-law wife of the barangay treasurer, and seventeen (17) individuals who are no longer residents of Barangay 143 as they are already residing at Trece Martires, Cavite. After thorough investigation, there was sufficient evidence found to warrant the filing of charges against Subject LORETA MORALES y VELASCO. The distribution of SAC forms to unqualified individuals constitutes giving unwarranted benefits, advantage or preference in the discharge of the official administrative function which was committed through manifest partiality, evident bad faith or gross inexcusable negligence. In addition, the distribution of SAP funds to families other than what was provided for by the law constitutes Technical Malversation. Subject, being the Barangay Chairman, was held accountable through her participation in the implementation of SAP. Finally, the unjustified distribution of SAP to residents of another LGU who are claimed to be election supporters and to that of Subject’s daughter, is inconsistent with the mandates of the Code of the Conduct and Ethical Standards for Public Officials and Employees. Charges were filed against Subject LORETA MORALES y VELASCO before the Ombudsman for violation of Section 9 in relation to Section 3(e) of RA 3019 (Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act), Illegal Use of Public Funds (Technical Malversation) under Article 220 of the Revised Penal Code, and violation of Section 11 in relation to Section 4(a) and 4(d) of RA 6713 (Code of Conduct and Ethical Standards for Public Officials and Employees). The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) announces the promulgation of Sta. Cruz, Laguna Family Court Branch 6, convicting Subjects MARY JANE MENDOZA y PARAISO and MAGDELANA VIRAY y MASALONGA, who were arrested by the elements of NBI-Anti-Violence Against Women and Children Division (NBI-AVAWCD) on September 26, 2019 and charged for Human Trafficking. The court hearings were attended by the victims and witnesses who gave their testimonies which solidified the fact that Subjects Mendoza and Viray indeed committed the crime of Qualified Trafficking. On March 04, 2021, a judgment was promulgated finding accused MARY JANE MENDOZA y PARAISO and MAGDALENA VIRAY y MASALOGA guilty beyond reasonable doubt for five (5) counts of Qualified Trafficking in Persons as defined and penalized under R.A. 9208 as further amended by RA 10364. The court ordered the two (2) accused to suffer Life Imprisonment for each count and also ordered them to pay a fine of Php 2 Million without eligibility for parole and to pay each private complainants the amount Php 200,000.00 as moral damages and Php 100,000.00 as exemplary damages. The court, however, ordered the acquittal of WARREN MASACAYAN Y REYES for failure of the prosecution to prove the guilt of the latter. The NBI-Intellectual Property Division (NBI-IPRD) seized 29 machines under the label Pay&Go. Machines were confiscated after the implementation of Search Warrants issued on March 22, 2021, by the Pasig Regional Trial Court (RTC) Branch 159 for the protection intellectual property rights of complainant, MANILA EXPRESS PAYMENT SYSTEM (MEPS), the owner of “Touchpay” machine, a duly patented and registered Utility Model before the Intellectual Property Office of the Philippines. The Search Warrants were implemented in different parts of Metro Manila – Quezon City, Makati, Taguig and Muntinlupa and they and resulted in the confiscation of the 29 machines under the label Pay&Go as these machines created confusion and false beliefs to users that they are MEPS’ APM (Automatic Payment Machines) resulting in infringement to the intellectual property rights of MEPS. this was discovered due to complaints received by MEPS from their customers about defective machines but upon checking it was not their machine but a machine owned by ELECTRONIC TRANSFER AND ADVANCE PROCESSING, INC. (e-TAP) distributed by BTI Payments Philippines. Criminal complaints for violation of Section 168 (Unfair Competition) of R.A. 8293 otherwise known as the “Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines will be filed before the Prosecutors Office against PERSEVERANDO HERNANDEZ, MARLON PORTUGAL, ANTONIO LASALA, REYNALDO ISIDRO, RACHEL MERCADO (Officers of e-TAP), DAVID SCOTT GLEN, PETER, ALEXANDER BLACKET, DANILO IBARRA, and ALINA SISON (Officers of BTI Payment Phils, Inc.).

body: PRESS STATEMENT June 23, 2022 DISTOR PROMOTES 9 TO HEAD AGENT(HA) NBI Director ERIC B. DISTOR has promoted nine (9) NBI personnel to Head Agent positions. Promoted to Head Agent (HA) are Virgilio C. Reganit (Agent-in-Charge, BAYDO), Normando B. Anire (Chief of Staff, ODDROS), Gregorio S. Zuñiga Jr. (Acting Chief,CTD), Alexander G. Bautista (Acting Chief, AGD), Christopher Lyndon N. Godinez (Executive Officer, OD), Atty. Giselle O. Garcia-Dumlao (COS, OAD for Legal), Joey B. Moran (Chief, IOD), Paul Alain M. Moises (Executive Officer for Operations, CAR), and Heli B. Tiu (Agent-in-Charge, LAGDO). body: PRESS STATEMENT July 12, 2022 NBI ARRESTS ONE FOR ESTAFA The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today announced the arrest of a certain JOHN D. BOMBITA by operatives of NBI – Bulacan District Office (NBI-BULDO) in an entrapment operation in Parañaque for Estafa. The operation stemmed from the complaint filed before the office of NBI-BULDO by the victim of Subject Bombita. According to the complaint, the victim/complainant met Subject Bombita sometime in March 2020 and offered him an investment opportunity (Poultry Project). Subject Bombita was able to convince the complainant to visit the poultry site located at Talugtug, Nueva Ecija. The complainant was introduced to a certain Ramil Bautista, the alleged Project Manager of the Poultry project and told complainant the same earnings as what Subject Bombita has told him. Thus, enticing the complainant to invest in the said project because of the huge Return of Investment (ROI). In the same month, the complainant visited again the poultry and was lured to invest on three (3) slots worth Php1.5 Million. The complainant handed over Php750,000.00 to Subjects Bombita and Bautista for the half of what was agreed for the three (3) slots but no receipt was issued for the payment. After sometime, the two (2) subjects called the complainant and instructed him to pay the remaining balance of Php750,000.00 or else he will lose his two (2) slots. The subjects compelled the complainant to pay the remaining balance and the latter complied and was told that the construction of the poultry will start after six (6) months. Seven months later, Subject Bombita called an emergency meeting with the investors and introduced a certain Ulysses F. Barcial as the new person in charge of the project because Ramil Bautista took away the money intended for the Poultry project and assured the investors that the Poultry project will move forward. body: PRESS STATEMENT January 22, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } The National Bureau of Investigation – National Capital Region (NBI-NCR) under the leadership of NBI Director JUDGE JAIME B. SANTIAGO (Ret.), and direct supervision of Regional Director Ferdinand M. Lavin, arrested ten (10) foreign nationals in Paranaque City for violation of R.A. No. 12010 (Anti-Financial Account Scamming Act). The operatives of NBI-NCR were able to arrest seven (7) Vietnamese nationals identified as PHAN VIET NGAN, DO ANH TUAN, NGUYEN DUC ANH, PHAN KIM SANG, VO HONG SY, NGUYEN VAN KHANH, and DOAN VAN DUNG and three (3) Chinese nationals identified as ZHANG MING YI, XIN YAO HUANG, and HIMEN CHEN. The operation stemmed from an intelligence report that groups of foreign nationals are engaged in Investment Fraud, Crypto Asset or Crypto Currency Scam, Artificial Intelligence scam and High Yield Investment Program (HYIP), Romance scam and identity theft through the use of social engineering scheme and digital communication systems. In response, operatives of NBI-NCR conducted surveillance operations, which confirmed the veracity of the information. Thus, on January 14, 2025, NBI-NCR applied for a Warrant to Search, Seize, and Examine Computer Data (WSSECD), which was granted by the court. On January 15, 2025, after proper coordination with concerned government agencies, the operatives of NBI-NCR implemented the WSSECD against the subject address located in Multinational Village, Paranaque City. The service of the warrant resulted in the arrest of the above-stated Subjects and seizure of computer units and Transcripts with Chinese characters. Based on the seized translated transcripts, Subjects are indeed engaged in phishing and scamming activities. In addition, OS Triage conducted on the seized computer units revealed the illegal activities of the Subjects like romance scam, fictitious messaging accounts, fraudulent cryptocurrency schemes and fake investment solicitations. Director Santiago commended the operatives of NBI-NCR for the successful arrest of the foreign nationals and stressed the NBI’s unwavering commitment in protecting the public against unscrupulous individuals.

body: A man who misrepresented himself as an architect and allegedly involved in a multi-million peso project was arrested by agents of the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) during an entrapment in Baguio City recently. The suspect was identified by NBI Director Nonnatus Caesar R. Rojas as: ROWELL VALDEZ, 21, single, a resident of #49 Sampaguita, Bgy. San Luis, Baguio City. Investigation by the NBI-Violence against Women and Children Division (VAWCD) headed by Head Agent Auralyn L. Pascual disclosed that a Bangladeshi businessman, Anwar Hossain, sought NBI assistance regarding two compatriots, suspects Swapan and Wasim, who kept on harassing and threatening him with death. Investigation by the NBI-Cordillera Administrative Region (CAR) headed by Regional Director Jose A. Limmayog, Jr., disclosed that Valdez, introduced himself to complainant, Rodelio Sotalbo, as a licensed architect. He allegedly won in a project bidding at the GoshenLand Corporation for the construction of a three-storey condominium building worth P281 million. located at #18 Eagle Crest Bakakeng Norte, Baguio City. To prove that he is indeed an architect, he showed him his alleged Professional Identification Card issued by the Professional Regulations Commission (PRC), Transcript of Records and diploma from the University of the Cordilleras and the GoshenLand Service contract agreement. Valdez said he needed money to acquire a bank certificate as one of the requirements needed by GoshenLand. He then approached and convinced Sotalbo to open for him a savings and checking accounts at the PNB, Session Road Branch, Baguio City. Valdez also said that once a bank certificate is issued to him, he would immediately return the complainant’s money. If complainant will help him in his financial need, he will be the one to sub-contract the project. Eventually, Sotalbo deposited P362,000 in the name of the suspect Valdez on June 3 and 4, 2013, respectively. But unknown to the former, Valdez immediately started withdrawing money from his account on June 5, 2013. On the other hand, complainant Sotalbo later became suspicious when he could not contact the suspect for several days. Thereafter, he found out that Valdez’s PRC Professional Identification Card, Transcript of Records and diploma from the University of the Cordilleras were all fake. Likewise, the GosheLand project he allegedly won in the bidding is non-existing. This prompted him to seek NBI investigative assistance. Later that day, suspect was again asking money from the complainant for another project. Sotalbo learned that Valdez was about to withdraw again from suspect’s own account at the said bank on June 10, 2013. An entrapment operation was planned. The complainant, together with NBI operatives proceeded to the PNB Branch in Session Road. All along, Valdez was tailed by NBI agents and the complainant. After withdrawing money from the PNB, Valdez was arrested by NBI agents who were posted nearby. He was brought to the NBI Record check with NBI files on suspect revealed that he has three outstanding warrants of arrest for Large Scale Illegal Recruitment issued by RTC Branches 3, 7 and 60, Baguio City. He allegedly recruited overseas workers for non-existing jobs in Japan. On June 13, 2013, charges for Estafa Thru Falsification were recommended filed against the suspect before the Baguio City Prosecutor’s Office.

title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: The National Bureau of Investigation announced the arrest of an individual by operatives of the Anti-Fraud Division (NBI-AFD) in Marilao, Bulacan for Estafa and Usurpation of Authority. NBI-Officer-In-Charge (OIC) Director Eric B. Distor identified the arrested Subject as RUBY ANN DIZON y DELA CRUZ a.k.a. “FRANCHESCA DELA CRUZ”. Director Distor said that the operation stemmed from a complaint filed by the victim of Subject Dizon for defrauding her on the sale of a real estate property. According to the complaint, the victim inquired about a house and lot being sold by its supposed owner Franchesca Dela Cruz in Marilao, Bulacan for Php 2.6 Million. During their meeting, Franchesca presented documents of the property. Subject Dizon also claimed to be a Civil Engineer and presented a PRC Identification Card. Believing in Subject’s representations, complainant made an initial payment of Php 500,000.00 at Subject Dizon’s residence in Marilao, Bulacan. The complainant and the Subject agreed that the remaining balance will be paid in installment from August to September 2020 which the victim fully paid within their agreed date. Subject Dizon then gave to the complainant a Special Power of Attorney (SPA) to transact with the developer. A few months later, the complainant discovered that Subject Dizon has arrears from June 2020 to August 2020. The complainant also discovered from PRC that Subject Dizon is not a Civil Engineer. The complainant immediately informed the Subject but despite demands, Subject ignored her calls. The complainant then filed a complaint in Barangay Sta. Rosa Dos. Despite the barangay mediation proceedings, Subject Dizon threatened the complainant and her family that charges will be filed against them; and that Subject would send a letter to the developer for the foreclosure of the property. Subject Dizon demanded Php 40,000.00 from the complainant for her not to proceed with the said threats, which the complainant complied and paid an initial of Php 27,000.00 because for fear that Subject might make true her threats. On September 14, 2021, while filing a complaint before the NBI-AFD, Subject Dizon called the complainant demanding Php 13,000.00, which they agreed to be handed over on the same day in a restaurant in Marilao, Bulacan. Thus, the NBI-AFD operatives together with the complainant proceeded to the meeting place and positioned themselves strategically near the premises. Upon handing over of the marked money by the complainant to Subject Dizon, NBI-AFD operatives immediately approached the Subject and placed her under arrest. Subject Dizon was brought to the NBI-AFD office for standard booking procedure and the examination conducted by the NBI-Forensic Chemistry Division revealed that Subject Dizon’s hand is positive for fluorescent specks and smudges. Also, a certification issued by the PRC revealed that Ruby Ann Dizon is not a registered Civil Engineer. Subject Dizon was presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the Provincial Prosecutor of the City of Malolos, Bulacan for violation of Article 315 (Estafa) in relation to Article 172 (Falsification of Public Documents) of the Revised Penal Code (RPC), as amended; and violation of Article 177 (Usurpation of Authority) also defined and punished under the RPC.

title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: The National Bureau of Investigation today said operatives of NBI-Cyber Crime Division (NBI-CCD) have arrested a Nigerian national for alleged online scam in a mall in Manila yesterday. The Subject, who was arrested in an entrapment operation, was identified as JOSEPH KAMANO a.k.a. SAYID BARKAT a.k.a. HENRY SOMA. According to the Complainant, Subject offered her a business proposal thru social media. Subject informed the Complainant that they will send the latter a package full of money as capital in their business. Complainant was also instructed to open a new email address so they can monitor the package. A photo of the package was likewise sent to prove that it is real. Moreover, Subject told the Complainant that she will receive the package after paying the processing fees of the documents for the package such as certification of ownership, payment of taxes for three (3) years, signing of documents, and for the delivery of the package at the Complainant’s house. Convinced of the scheme presented by the Subject, the Complainant, therefore, paid the Subject a total of Nine Hundred Forty Nine Thousand Ten Pesos (Php 949, 610.00) through bank and money transfer. Complainant, however, did not receive the package. Subject KAMANO even called the Complainant and asked her to pay another Two Hundred Forty Thousand Pesos (Php 240,000.00) for the delivery charge. When Complainant discerned about the modus operandi of the Subject, she sought the assistance of the NBI. Under strict orders from NBI Director Dante A. Gierran to promptly act on the matter, NBI-CCD operatives, on the aforementioned date, together with the Complainant, conducted the entrapment operation resulting in the arrest of Subject KAMANO. Subject will be presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the Prosecutor of Manila for violation of R.A. 315 otherwise known as Estafa.

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today announced the arrest of an employee of the Bureau of Internal Revenue Office –RDO 91 by the NBI- Dipolog District Office (NBI-DIPDO) in Dipolog City for robbery extortion. NBI Officer-In-Charge (OIC) Director Eric B. Distor identified the subject as RENAN HECHANOVA y ALFORQUE. Director Distor said that the operation stemmed from the complaint by the victim of Subject Hechanova. The complainant alleged that sometime in November 2021, a Letter of Authority that was served to him by the BIR-RDO 19, stating that he has a tax deficiency of Php 4.5 Million. The complainant added that sometime in December, personnel from the BIR, Dipolog City, called him and asked for Php 400,000.00 as settlement of his tax deficiencies. The complainant added that he was threatened that if he will not comply with the demand, his case will be forwarded to their Regional Office in Zamboanga City and he will be forced to pay Php 4.5 Million. On the third week of December 2021, the complainant went to the BIR office where he met two (2) BIR examiners namely Renan Hechanova and Benjie Sumalpong. The subject begged to the two BIR examiners to give him time to produce the demanded Php 400,000.00 which was granted by the two (2). Thus, an entrapment operation was planned and on January 18, 2022, the NBI-DIPDO operatives together with the complainant proceeded to the BIR-Office in Dipolog City but upon arrival at the target area in the morning of the same date, the complainant was instructed to return at 4:30 in the afternoon. As instructed, Agents and Complainant returned in the afternoon. The operatives positioned themselves strategically in the vicinity of the BIR office and upon receiving of the pre-arranged signal, signifying the perfection of the transaction, the operatives immediately swooped in and apprehended Subject Hechanova in flagrante. Recovered from the subject were the marked money he received from the complainant. Subject Hechanova will be charged for violation of Article 294 (Robbery with violence against or intimidation of persons) under the Revised Penal Code, as amended; violation of R.A. 3019 (Anti-Graft and Practices Act); and violation of R.A. 6713 (Code of Conduct and Ethical Standards for Public Officials and Employees).

As instructed, Agents and Complainant returned in the afternoon. The operatives positioned themselves strategically in the vicinity of the BIR office and upon receiving of the pre-arranged signal, signifying the perfection of the transaction, the operatives immediately swooped in and apprehended Subject Hechanova in flagrante. Recovered from the subject were the marked money he received from the complainant. Subject Hechanova will be charged for violation of Article 294 (Robbery with violence against or intimidation of persons) under the Revised Penal Code, as amended; violation of R.A. 3019 (Anti-Graft and Practices Act); and violation of R.A. 6713 (Code of Conduct and Ethical Standards for Public Officials and Employees).
