body: On June 04, 2020, National Bureau of Investigation-Central Luzon Regional Office (NBI-CELRO) operatives, headed by Atty. Rustico Vigilia, Regional Director, NBI-CELRO conducted an entrapment operation and arrested three Chinese Nationals at a warehouse in Clarkhills, Clark Freeport Zone, Mabalacat City, Pampanga. The Chinese nationals were identified as ZIDONG GUO , 53 years old, who represented himself as a doctor to his Chinese customers, CHEN WEIMING , 31 years old and HONG QIAO LING , 28 years old. Gabuna, Officer-In-Charge, North Luzon Cluster exercised their visitation and inspection power thereby inventoried and confiscated Chinese medicines, food and cosmetic products that were being sold to Chinese customers. body: PRESS STATEMENT July 30, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } In accordance with the order of National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Director JUDGE JAIME B. SANTIAGO (Ret.) aimed at enhancing operations against the illegal practice of medicine, the NBI-National Capital Region (NBI-NCR) arrested a Chinese national identified as CHEN HONG RU in Binondo, Manila. The arrest was made for violations of Republic Act No. 2382 (The Medical Act of 1959) and R.A. No. 9711 (Food and Drug Administration Act of 2009). On July 7, 2025, confidential informants reported to the NBI-NCR that a certain CHEN HONG RU (CHEN) was allegedly engaged in illegal practice of medicine for representing himself as a physician, conducting medical procedures in a makeshift clinic, and dispensing Chinese medicines without proper authorization from the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and other relevant government regulatory agencies. On July 8, 2025, NBI-NCR agents, along with Filipino-Chinese informants, conducted an immediate test-buy operation in Binondo, Manila to verify the accuracy of the information. The NBI informant, pretending to suffer from a severe headache and stomach pain, was examined by the subject. After the consultation, Subject Chen sold to Informant one (1) box of Betaloc AstraZeneca (labeled in Chinese) and several Chinese medicines contained in four (4) self-sealing plastic sachets. In return, Informant paid Subject Chen Php1,500.00 for the check-up and medicine. Thus, confirming the accuracy of the information. On July 14, 2025, NBI-NCR agents proceeded to the clinic of Subject Chen and conducted an entrapment operation, which resulted in his arrest, in the act of dispensing medicines and examining the informant who was with an undercover agent. Subject Chen was presented for inquest proceedings before the Manila Prosecutor’s Office for the abovementioned violations. Director Santiago commended the dedicated agents of the NBI-NCR for their exceptional teamwork and determination during a successful operation, which culminated in the arrest of a Chinese national. Santiago highlighted that the operation demonstrated the NBI’s commitment to enforcing the law and ensuring public safety.

body: On March 6, 7, and 8, 2020, operatives of NBI-Western Mindanao Regional Office (NBI-WEMRO), together with the Bureau of Customs (BOC) Port of Zamboanga, Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR)-Zamboanga, Provincial Intelligence Unit Zamboanga Del Sur Provincial Police Office, Dinas Municipal Police Station, and Labangan Municipal Police Station conducted a joint operation against ALEX CHUA et.al. Documents gathered from the local government of Dinas Municipality revealed that ALEX CHUA y TIU, BENJAMIN M. ISRAEL, and STEVEN CU are the registered owners of the warehouse where cigarette making machines, raw materials and spurious documentary stamp tax were seized. VITAN, and YOLLIE TAN GO are the registered owners of the apprehended trucks containing cigarette making machines and counterfeit cigarettes. Verification from the Bureau of Immigration is yet to be received while verification with other agencies was held in abeyance due to Covid-19 pandemic. On May 26, 2020, operatives of NBI-Northeastern Mindanao Regional Office (NBI-NEMRO) arrested two (2) Subjects in separate operations for selling shabu in violation of RA 9165 (Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act). Subjects were arrested in a buy-bust operations which stemmed from the information that they were selling shabu in Cagayan de Oro City. Subject “AGAW/TIKOY” was arrested around 11am and the poseur-customer bought from him was around 3 grams of shabu. On the other hand, Subject “JUNIEL” was apprehended around 5:30pm and bought from him was around 5 grams of shabu. On May 29, 2020, operatives of NBI-International Operations Division (NBI-IOD) arrested ABEGAIL SIWA and her mother GLORINA JULIAN CARANDANG for unauthorized sale of rapid test kits and Estafa. Subjects were arrested in entrapment operation which stemmed from the complaint filed on May 12, 2020. In the complaint, SIWA allegedly required the complainant for a down payment of Php 4.6 Million for a promise to deliver 10,000 sacks of rice amounting to Php 16.6 Million in Cebu City. After complainant settled in cash the down payment, subject failed to comply with her promise and despite exhaustive efforts to reach her, Subject Siwa evaded to communicate with the complainant. With this, the entrapment operation was conducted resulting in the arrest of the above-mentioned Subjects. Subjects were recommended for prosecution before the Office of Prosecutor, Manila for violations of RA 9711 (FDA Act) in relation to RA 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act), and Estafa. On May 29, 2020, operatives of NBI-Task Force Against Illegal Drugs (NBI-TFAID) arrested LIANG JUNSHUAI, PINGQIANG LONG, YANYUN JIANG, and TANG HONG SHAN, Chinese nationals for illegal practice of medicine and operating makeshift hospital inside the Multinational Village in Paranaque City without License to Operate or Certificate of Accreditation issued by the Bureau of Medical Services of the Department of Health (DOH). Moreover, the group prescribes and sells Chinese drugs not approved and registered to the Food and Drug Administration. On the above-mentioned date, TFAID operatives proceeded to Multinational Village in Paranaque City for the entrapment operation. While inside the premises, operatives noticed in plain view a makeshift hospital with a large volume of assorted medicines in Chinese characters and several types of hospital equipment and paraphernalia placed inside a room adjacent to the garage of the said house primarily devoted for the operation of the facility for the diagnosis, treatment, and care of individuals suffering from illness, disease, injury, or in need of other medical and nursing care. NBI-ISDO, together with BIR Revenue Officers proceeded to Lucky J 888 Rice Mill Corporation allegedly owned by one PETER HOU. Thereat, BIR personnel were still on the process of retrieving their seized items, secured by the Naguilian Police Station. STEVEN TAN, CHEN QUN, GONG WU JIA, and WU YAO MEI were the ones present inside the warehouse. Subjects failed to present any proof of their respective identities. They were placed under arrest for violations of the provisions of the National Internal Revenue Code as amended particularly Sec. 260 (Unlawful Possession of Cigarette Paper in Bobbins or Rolls) and Sec. 265 (Possession of Counterfeit Stamps). Poseur-customer was able to contact and transact with a pimp/operator identified as DONGTAI YE together with his business partner YUNMAN LI. The Subjects offered the poseur-customer a minimum sex service of 3 hours for Php8,000, additional hours would cost Php12,000 and overnight sex service for Php18,000. On June 3, 2020, the entrapment operation was conducted resulting in the arrest of the aforementioned Subjects. Six (6) Mongolian nationals and two (2) Chinese nationals who were trafficked victims, were likewise rescued. Charges for above-mentioned violations were filed against the Subjects. On June 4, 2020, operatives of NBI-Central Luzon Regional Office (NBI-CELRO) arrested ZIDONG GUO, CHEN WEIMING, and HONG QIAO LING, Chinese nationals, at a warehouse in Clarkhills, Clark Freeport Zone, Mabalacat City, Pampanga. Subjects were arrested in an entrapment operation following a positive test-buy conducted by the undercover agents. The Food and Drug Administration (FDA) likewise exercised their visitation and inspection power thereby inventoried and confiscated Chinese medicines, food, and cosmetic products that were being sold to Chinese customers. It was further disclosed that the said warehouse was the supplier and source of the makeshift medical facilities that were raided by the authorities at Brgy. Anunas, Angeles City and Fontana, Clark, Mabalacat City. According to the FDA, seized items have an estimated amount of more or less Php 20Million. Permits of the said stores were still being validated from the FDA and the local government of Mabalacat City. The establishments were closed and locked afterwards. Subjects are detained at NBI-CELRO detention facility and will be presented for inquest proceedings for violations of RA 2383 (The Medical Act of 1959) and RA 3720 as amended by RA 9711 (FDA Act of 2009) before the Office of the City Prosecutor, Mabalacat City. On June 4, 2020, operatives of NBI-Central Luzon Regional Office (NBI-CELRO) arrested HONG QIAULING, GOU ZIDONG, and CHEN WEIMING, Chinese nationals, for selling and distributing unregistered Chinese medicines. On the basis of a report and test-buy that were conducted on June 2, 2020, an entrapment operation was conducted against an alleged Chinese doctor and his cohorts for illegal practice of medicine, selling and distributing unregistered Chinese medicines without authority and license from the government in violations of RA 2382 (The Medical Act of 1959), RA 3720 as amended by RA 9711 (Food and Drug Administration Act of 2009), and The Pharmacy Law under RA 5291 as amended by RA 10918. Subject HONG QIAULING was arrested in a warehouse located at Clarkhills, Clark Freeport Zone, Mabalacat City, Pampanga. Recovered during the entrapment operation were assorted Chinese medicines worth Php100,000.00. The products were submitted for verification/laboratory examination The FDA likewise seized huge Chinese medical supplies, medicines, and other paraphernalia. Follow up operations on two (2) other locations, (restaurant and grocery store) were conducted and through FDA visitation and inspection power, additional unregistered Chinese medicines that were also sold to the public without authority from the government were confiscated by the FDA. The alleged Chinese doctor/pharmacist GOU ZIDONG and his cohort CHEN WEIMING were also arrested for illegal practice of medicine and illegally selling and distributing Chinese medicines. Subjects were presented for inquest before the Mabalacat City Prosecutors Office, Pampanga for the aforementioned violations. The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) lauds the conviction of DAVID TIMOTHY DEAKIN, an American national, who was sentenced for life imprisonment by a Court in Angeles, Pampanga for Human Trafficking. The case against David Timothy Deakin took more than two (2) years, following his arrest on February 27, 2017 by the operatives of NBI-Anti-Human Trafficking Division (NBI-AHTRAD) in Sta. Maria 1, Balibago, Angeles City. Records of the case showed that for a period of time, Deakin took advantage of the vulnerability of the victims, and unlawfully and knowingly recruited, offered and maintained them to and for foreign customers for the purpose of pornography through the use of computers. On May 26, 2020, the Court found Deakin guilty beyond reasonable doubt of the crime of Qualified Trafficking in Persons and was sentenced to life imprisonment and fine of Php 2 Million. He was also ordered to pay damages to his three (3) victims amounting to Php 500,000 each for moral damages and Php 100,000 each for exemplary damages.

Subjects were arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from a report that several foreign individuals in Binan, Laguna particularly of Chinese descent are allegedly maintaining, operating and are continuously hiring foreign nationals to engage in prostitution acts for a fee. Poseur-customer was able to contact and transact with a pimp/operator identified as DONGTAI YE together with his business partner YUNMAN LI. The Subjects offered the poseur-customer a minimum sex service of 3 hours for Php8,000, additional hours would cost Php12,000 and overnight sex service for Php18,000. On June 3, 2020, the entrapment operation was conducted resulting in the arrest of the aforementioned Subjects. Six (6) Mongolian nationals and two (2) Chinese nationals who were trafficked victims, were likewise rescued. Charges for above-mentioned violations were filed against the Subjects. Subjects were arrested in an entrapment operation following a positive test-buy conducted by the undercover agents. The Food and Drug Administration (FDA) likewise exercised their visitation and inspection power thereby inventoried and confiscated Chinese medicines, food, and cosmetic products that were being sold to Chinese customers. It was further disclosed that the said warehouse was the supplier and source of the makeshift medical facilities that were raided by the authorities at Brgy. Anunas, Angeles City and Fontana, Clark, Mabalacat City. According to the FDA, seized items have an estimated amount of more or less Php 20Million. Permits of the said stores were still being validated from the FDA and the local government of Mabalacat City. The establishments were closed and locked afterwards. Subjects are detained at NBI-CELRO detention facility and will be presented for inquest proceedings for violations of RA 2383 (The Medical Act of 1959) and RA 3720 as amended by RA 9711 (FDA Act of 2009) before the Office of the City Prosecutor, Mabalacat City. On June 4, 2020, operatives of NBI-Central Luzon Regional Office (NBI-CELRO) arrested HONG QIAULING, GOU ZIDONG, and CHEN WEIMING, Chinese nationals, for selling and distributing unregistered Chinese medicines. On the basis of a report and test-buy that were conducted on June 2, 2020, an entrapment operation was conducted against an alleged Chinese doctor and his cohorts for illegal practice of medicine, selling and distributing unregistered Chinese medicines without authority and license from the government in violations of RA 2382 (The Medical Act of 1959), RA 3720 as amended by RA 9711 (Food and Drug Administration Act of 2009), and The Pharmacy Law under RA 5291 as amended by RA 10918. Subject HONG QIAULING was arrested in a warehouse located at Clarkhills, Clark Freeport Zone, Mabalacat City, Pampanga. Recovered during the entrapment operation were assorted Chinese medicines worth Php100,000.00. The products were submitted for verification/laboratory examination The FDA likewise seized huge Chinese medical supplies, medicines, and other paraphernalia. Follow up operations on two (2) other locations, (restaurant and grocery store) were conducted and through FDA visitation and inspection power, additional unregistered Chinese medicines that were also sold to the public without authority from the government were confiscated by the FDA. The alleged Chinese doctor/pharmacist GOU ZIDONG and his cohort CHEN WEIMING were also arrested for illegal practice of medicine and illegally selling and distributing Chinese medicines. Subjects were presented for inquest before the Mabalacat City Prosecutors Office, Pampanga for the aforementioned violations. The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) lauds the conviction of DAVID TIMOTHY DEAKIN, an American national, who was sentenced for life imprisonment by a Court in Angeles, Pampanga for Human Trafficking. The case against David Timothy Deakin took more than two (2) years, following his arrest on February 27, 2017 by the operatives of NBI-Anti-Human Trafficking Division (NBI-AHTRAD) in Sta. Maria 1, Balibago, Angeles City. Records of the case showed that for a period of time, Deakin took advantage of the vulnerability of the victims, and unlawfully and knowingly recruited, offered and maintained them to and for foreign customers for the purpose of pornography through the use of computers. On May 26, 2020, the Court found Deakin guilty beyond reasonable doubt of the crime of Qualified Trafficking in Persons and was sentenced to life imprisonment and fine of Php 2 Million. He was also ordered to pay damages to his three (3) victims amounting to Php 500,000 each for moral damages and Php 100,000 each for exemplary damages.

body: In line with the efforts of the government to combat illegal activities relative to the pandemic, operatives of National Bureau of Investigation – Anti-Graft Division (NBI-AGD) arrested three individuals in Pasay City for unauthorized selling of medicines used to treat Covid-19. NBI Officer-In-Charge (OIC) Director Eric B. Distor identified the Subjects as KAREN AMERO y BOMBASE, RONALDO CERIOLA y DELOS SANTOS, and ERICKSON SORIANO y LAUREL. Distor said Dr. Arnold G. Alindada, Director II, South Luzon Cluster-Field Regulatory Operations Office, Food and Drug Administration (FDA), thru a letter, requested for investigation and possible entrapment operation on the alleged unauthorized selling of medicines used in the treatment of Covid-19 such as Remdesivir, Tocilizumab, Baricitinib among others. The medicines are allegedly being sold thru online platforms such as Facebook, Shopee, and Lazada. Per FDA Advisory No. 2021-0759, Remdesivir is not approved by FDA for treatment of Covid-19 and has not been granted yet with Certificate of Product Registration (CPR). Thus, said medicine cannot be marketed commercially. In addition, use of Remdesivir for a limited amount and for a particular patient may only be allowed in hospitals or physicians who are granted with a Compassionate Special Permit (CSP). Test-buy was conducted by FDA personnel on September 14, 2021 confirmed the unauthorized selling of Remdesivir. After proper coordination with the concerned authorities, NBI-AGD operatives conducted the buy-bust operation on September 28, 2021 at the premises of Crestly Building located at Perla St., Pasay City resulting in the arrest of the Subjects. Subject KAREN AMERO, who introduced herself as Office Manager of LMCSL Trading, resisted the arrest claiming that they have necessary license from FDA relative to the product they sell. Subject AMERO even proceeded to her unit located at the ground floor of Crestly Building to show her alleged license. During the conduct of inspection by FDA personnel assisted by NBI-AGD operatives, several medicines were found in the area together with two other individuals later identified as Subjects RONALDO CERIOLA y DELOS SANTOS and ERICKSON SORIANO y LAUREL who introduced themselves as delivery riders of LMCSL Trading. Verification by FDA personnel revealed that it is the LMCSL Trading located at Caroyroyan, Pili, Camarines Sur has the existing License to Operate and not the one located at Crestly Building, Pasay City where the buy-bust operation took place. Found and recovered from the possession of the Subjects are various types of medicines including Ivirem-Remdesivir. On September 29, 2021, charges for violation of Section 11(a), (j), and (k) of RA 3720 as amended by RA 9711 otherwise known as the Food and Drug Administration Act of 2009 and violation of Section 45(a) and (p) of RA 10918 otherwise known as the Philippine Pharmacy Act were filed against the arrested Subjects before the Office of the City Prosecutor, Pasay City. Subjects are currently under the custody of NBI Detention Facility, Taft Avenue, Manila.

body: In line with the directive of NBI- Officer-In-Charge (OIC) Director Eric B. Distor to conduct investigation on all online cyber related fraud including the proliferating online investment schemes, the National Bureau of Investigation announces the arrest of two (2) individuals by operatives of NBI-Special Task Force (NBI-STF) in an entrapment operation in Lipa, Batangas. Director Distor identified the subjects as YRON RECODO y QUIMPO and KATRINA OLOTEO y CABALCE, both of HACIENDA NIRVANA (Nirvana) operated by ARCADIA PRIME DEVELOPMENT CORPORATION (Arcadia). Director Distor said that Nirvana is one among the many subjects of the monitoring and cyber surveillance efforts of the NBI-STF. Through continuous monitoring, the operatives were able to discover that Nirvana is a project owned and operated by Arcadia with office located at RDC Plaza, Ayala Highway, Barangay Balintawak, Lipa, Batangas. NBI-STF agents were able to set a meeting with Subject Recodo and an entrapment operation was hatched. On March 31, 2022, NBI-STF operatives together with the poseur-clients proceeded to the office of Arcadia and positioned themselves strategically outside the office of Arcadia. After the orientation and ascertaining that Arcadia is offering investment, the undercover agents agreed to invest and handed over four checks in the amount of Php 300,000.00 and Php 500,000.00 under the name of ARCADIA PRIME DEVELOPMENT CORP. Thus, the undercover agents gave the pre-arranged signal indicating that the transaction has been completed. NBI-STF operatives immediately entered the office of Arcadia and arrested Subject Recodo and the Administrative Officer of Arcadia identified as Subject Oloteo, who was in possession of the checks issued by the operatives. The arrested subjects were brought to the NBI office for standard booking procedures and were presented for inquest proceedings before the Lipa Prosecutor’s Office, Batangas for violation of R.A. 8799 (Securities Regulation Code).

body: PRESS STATEMENT January 16, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } NBI AND OTHER LAW ENFORCEMENT AGENCIES ARREST THREE INDIVIDUALS IN PASAY CITY, SUBSTANTIAL VOLUME OF ILLEGAL DRUGS SEIZED MANILA, Philippines — The NAIA-IADITG, comprising the National Bureau of Investigation – International Airport Investigation Division (NBI-IAID), PDEA RO NCR, the Bureau of Customs – Customs Anti-Illegal Drugs Task Force (BOC- CAIDTF), the PNP Aviation Security Group (AVSEG), the Airport Police Department (APD), the PNP Drug Enforcement Group (DEG), the Bureau of Immigration, and the Office for Transportation Security (OTS) conducted a joint interdiction operation at the PAIR-PAGS Center, NAIA Complex, Pasay City. The operation resulted in the arrest of three (3) Subjects for violating Section 4 of Republic Act No. 9165 (Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002). The operation resulted in the seizure of several boxes, each wrapped in packaging tape marked with an “X.” Each box contained plastic bags filled with a white crystalline substance concealed inside green figurines. The total weight of the seized illegal drugs amounted to 16,848 grams, with an estimated standard value of PHP. 114,566,400.00 and a street value of PHP. 25,272,000.00. Director Magno emphasized that the successful operation underscores the government’s unwavering commitment to combating the illegal drug trade in the country. He further stressed that effective coordination and seamless cooperation among law enforcement agencies remain vital to the success of all anti-illegal drug operations. “By working together, law enforcement agencies play a crucial role in the success of operations to dismantle drug networks, protecting our communities from the harmful impact of illegal drugs. Together, we can create a safer and healthier environment for everyone.” — ATTY. ANGELITO DLP. MAGNO Acting Director, National Bureau of Investigation #NBIServes Media Contact: HA Palmer U. Mallari, NBI Spokesperson 09691033406 [email protected]

body: PRESS STATEMENT May 23, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } PRESS RELEASE | NBI ARRESTS INDIVIDUAL, INLCUDING ONE MINOR FOR SELLING ILLEGAL DRUGS In line with the directive from NBI Director Atty. Melvin A. Matibag to intensify the NBI’s campaign against illegal drugs, the NBI-Dangerous Drugs Division (NBI-DDD) conducted a buy-bust operation in the City of Manila, resulting in the arrest of two (2) individuals for violating Republic Act No. 9165, the Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002 and rescue of one (1) minor. The operation was carried out after agents of NBI-DDD, utilizing cyber-patrolling techniques, discovered a Facebook account involved in the sale and distribution of illegal substances such as “Marijuana,” “Tuklaw,” and “Carts.” Following this discovery, the agents undertook online surveillance of the Facebook account and identified its connection to a specific Instagram account. A test-buy operation was then initiated, during which undercover agents purchased one piece of Kush weighing 0.5 grams for Php350.00 and one unit of Carts for Php1,900.00. The purchased illegal drugs were promptly sent to the NBI-Forensic Chemistry Division (NBI-FCD) for laboratory examination. The forensic analysis confirmed that the items contained 0.4986 grams of marijuana and 1 ml of tetrahydrocannabinol, thereby establishing that the individuals managing the Facebook account were engaged in the illegal sale of illegal drugs. On May 20, 2026, NBI-DDD agents conducted an entrapment/buy-bust operation in the City of Manila to apprehend the individuals behind the Facebook account. After the sale was completed, the agents approached the subjects, but the subjects attempted to evade arrest and fled the scene. A brief hot pursuit ensued, ultimately resulting in the arrest of the Subjects. Subsequently, the rescued thirteen (13)-year-old minor was turned over to a government-operated social welfare facility in Manila for proper custody and intervention, while the sixteen (16)-year-old minor subject, having been assessed by a social worker to have acted with discernment, was presented for inquest proceedings together with the twenty (20)-year-old subject. for the above-mentioned violation. NBI Director Matibag commended the NBI-DDD agents for the successful operation, which highlighted the NBI’s commitment to upholding the law. He emphasized that the arrest marked a significant step in their ongoing crackdown on illegal drug activities facilitated through online platforms.

body: PRESS STATEMENT March 16, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } NBI FACILITATES SAFE SURRENDER OF BIFF, DI LINKED INDIVIDUALS IN MAGUINDANAO DEL SUR; HIGH-POWERED FIREARMS TURNED OVER The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) successfully facilitated the safe surrender and extraction of three individuals linked to the Bangsamoro Islamic Freedom Fighters (BIFF) and Dawlah Islamiyah (DI) during an operation conducted on 14 March 2026 in Mamasapano, Maguindanao del Sur. The operation was carried out by NBI-Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (NBI-BARMM) personnel in coordination with the NBI Central Mindanao Regional Office (NBI-CEMRO), NBI- Sarangani District Office (NBI-SARDO), NBI Counter Terrorism Division (NBI-CTD), and partner security units following intelligence information indicating that certain individuals affiliated with extremist groups operating in the area had expressed their intention to disengage from armed activities and surrender to government authorities. According to intelligence sources, the individuals sought a secure and neutral channel for surrender due to fears of possible retaliation from remaining BIFF and DI elements in the area. Acting on the information, authorities conducted a protective extraction operation to ensure the safety of both the surrendering individuals and the operational team. The subjects who voluntarily surrendered were reportedly members of the BIFF/DI Karialan faction operating in Mamasapano. During the surrender, the subjects turned over several high-powered firearms and weapons, including: • One (1) Barrett Rifle (.50 caliber) • One (1) M79 Grenade Launcher • One (1) M203 Grenade Launcher Tube • One (1) Mosin Rifle with magazine • Two (2) rounds of 7.62mm live ammunition Following the successful extraction, the individuals were safely transported to a secure facility for documentation, initial debriefing, and security processing. Authorities reported that the operation concluded without any untoward incident NBI Director Atty. Melvin D. Matibag commended the operating units for the successful and peaceful outcome of the operation. “This successful surrender demonstrates that even those who have once taken the path of armed extremism can still choose peace. The National Bureau of Investigation remains committed to supporting government efforts that provide safe and lawful avenues for individuals who wish to abandon violence and reintegrate into society. Through cooperation with our partner security agencies and the community, we will continue to work toward lasting peace and stability in the Bangsamoro region,” the NBI Director said.

body: On June 2, 2020, operatives of NBI-Environmental Crime Division (NBI-EnCD) arrested SANTIAGO RENE y YUMUL, ACUÑA, JOSEPH y NIVERA, IBASCO, NORMAN y POSADA, MOJELLO, JEOVY y REVILLA, LAXAMANA, RAUL y DIZON, TORRES, ERNESTO y DAVID, BALAJADIA, REYNALDO y CABRERA, and SANTOS, RYAN y TIQUI illegal quarrying in Tarlac City. Subjects were arrested in an operation which stemmed from an information that a quarry operation and processing of minerals in Brgy. Telabanca, Concepcion, Tarlac is operating without the necessary permit from the Provincial Mining Regulatory Board of the Province of Tarlac and the Department of Environment and Natural Resources – Mines and Geosciences Bureau Region III (DENR-MGB Region III). Surveillance operation conducted confirmed the said illegal activity. Based on the updated List of Quarry Permits as of January 28, 2020 provided by the Office of the Governor, Province of Tarlac, there is no issued quarry permits in Brgy. Telabanca, Concepcion, Tarlac. In another certification of MGB-Region III, there are only two (2) mining tenements (Industrial Sand and Gravel Permit) issued in the province of Tarlac. On the above-mentioned date, NBI-EnCD operatives together with personnel from the DENR-MGB Region III conducted the operation against the illegal quarry operation at J2KAT Vibro Sand Trading in Brgy. Telabanca, Concepcion, Tarlac resulting in the arrest of the Subjects. They failed to show a quarry permit or any permits issued by the Provincial Mining and Regulatory Board of the Province of Batangas or the DENR-MGB Region III. Seizure receipt of heavy equipment and minerals found at the quarry site was made and the total value of the seized items id Php 3,942,000.00. Charges for violation of Section 3 of RA 7942 (Philippine Mining Act of 1995) were filed before the Office of the Prosecutor General, Department of Justice (DOJ) against the arrested Subjects and MARK JOHN M. GOPEZ, who is currently at large. On June 5, 2020, operatives of NBI-Technical Intelligence Division (NBI-TID) arrested ATTY. CAMILO L. SABIO, former Chairman of the Presidential Commission on Good Government. The arrest of Sabio was based on a Bench Warrant of Arrest issued by the Fourth Division of the Sandiganbayan in relation to the execution of judgment in one of the criminal cases pending before the court. Sabio, who chaired the PCGG in 2005-2010, has a number of graft charges pending before the Sandiganbayan for violation of Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act allegedly committed during his stint at the PCGG. After the usual booking procedures, Sabio was brought to the Sandiganbayan, however, was temporarily closed due to the sanitation of the area because of Covid-19. Sabio was then returned to the NBI detention detention center. He will be presented before the Sandiganbayan on Monday. On June 5, 2020, operatives of NBI-Tagum District Office (NBI-TAGDO) arrested GEMMA ANTONIO ATOS for violation of RA 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act) or Cyber Libel. Subject was arrested in the Municipality of Gov. Generoso, Davao Oriental by virtue of Warrant of Arrest. Other accused, EDRALYN ATOS, remains at large. body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today announced the arrest of a Chinese national by the NBI Anti-Fraud Division (NBI-AFD) in an entrapment operation in Parañaque City for Human Trafficking. NBI-Officer-In-Charge (OIC) Director Eric B. Distor identified the Chinese national as ZHANG YANG MING a.k.a. “MIKE”. Distor said that the operation stemmed from information alleging that a local recruitment company named “INTERPRETACOMMUNICATION SERVICES (Interpretation) located in Parañaque City is engaged in human trafficking where Filipina women who seek local employment as receptionists for Chinese-owned KTVs and restaurants end up being offered by Chinese bosses as Personal Assistants to Chinese clients. To verify the veracity of the information, agents of NBI-AFD conducted surveillance operation against the target recruitment company. A Chinese poseur-customer went to the office of Interpretation. Two (2) Chinese nationals identified as Ming, assistant manager and CI KE, manager of Interpretation, showed the poseur-customer photos of Filipino women who, according to them can be hired on a short or long term basis as personal assistant doing all the things that a girlfriend or a wife should be doing with their partners, including unlimited sex. Upon confirming that the target recruitment company is in to human trafficking, an entrapment operation was planned. Thus, On March 17, 2022, operatives of NBI-AFD proceeded to the office of Interpretation. An Agent and a Chinese asset acted as poseur-customers and were welcomed by Subject Ming who then invited the two undercovers inside his office and told them that they can have the women of their choice for 30 days for a fee of P100,000.00. Subject Ming then showed them a sample of the service contract, which stated the reciprocal duties/obligations/penalties of the client and the woman that the former paid for. The contract also stated that if the client and the girl had misunderstanding within 1st to 3rd day of their liaison, the girl could only get one-fourth of the Php 100,000.00 monthly fee and if it happened on the 4th up to the 15th day, the girl gets the half of the fee. Subject Ming then brought three (3) women inside his office and in return, the undercover agents handed over the marked money to Subject Ming as payment to the girls. At this juncture, the undercovers gave the pre-arranged signal to the other operatives who immediately rushed inside the office, resulting in the arrest of Subject Ming in the act of receiving the marked money. NBI-AFD operatives were able to recover from the Subject marked money and various documents pertaining to business permit of said company. According to the sworn statements of the three (3) girls offered by Subject Ming to the undercovers, it stated that they thought that Subject Ming was introducing them to Chinese clients and/or owners of KTV restaurants as applicants for receptionist and that they have no idea that they were being offered as potential wives for them. Ultraviolet examination conducted by the NBI-Forensic Chemistry Division (NBI-FCD) revealed that Subject Ming is positive for the presence of orange fluorescent specks and smudges. Subject Ming was charged before the Prosecutor General of the Department of Justice (DOJ) Manila for violation of Section 4 (e) of R.A. 9208 otherwise known as the Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2003 as amended by R.A. 10364 otherwise known as the Expanded Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2012 in relation to R.A. 10175 or the Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012. Likewise, a Chinese national identified as CI KE (at-large) and MELANIE REYES MANCENIDO (at-large) were also charged for the same crime.

body: PRESS STATEMENT October 02, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } On September 11, 2025, NBI-PUERDO agents arrested one individual who voluntarily surrendered in connection with large scale illegal recruitment charges. On January 22, 2025, NBI-PUERDO agents, working in close coordination with Barangay Officials of Bangcalaan and the Municipal Police Station of Balabac, successfully rescued six (6) victims of illegal recruitment. This operation was prompted by intelligence reports concerning the illegal recruitment activities. body: In line with the relentless campaign of the government against all forms of criminalities, operatives of NBI-Anti-Organized and Transnational Crime Division (NBI-AOTCD) arrested two (2) individuals for Swindling/Estafa. NBI Officer-in-Charge (OIC) Director Eric B. Distor identified the Subjects as SHAGOPTHA BASHIR KHAN PUNZALAN and ROSENDA MOHAMMAD JIMENEZ aka RADZHATA MOHAMMAD SAMPANG. Subjects were arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from complaints against the subjects. According to the complaints, Subject SHA induced them to invest in her Cash Energy (Payday Loans) Services with a promise of high interest returns in merely weeks. Complainants invested a total amount of Php 2,870,000.00 with pertinent documents acknowledged by SHA. Upon issuance of the investment money, complainants were issued bank checks as assurance of the returns. Most of the checks bounced for reason that they were drawn against a closed account. Complainants then realized that they were deceived by SHA and therefore demanded refund on their investment. However, SHA was not able to deliver nor refund the amounts owed to complainants. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) issued a certification to the NBI showing that there is no registration granted to Cash Energy (Payday Loans) Services as a corporation or as a partnership. Further, this entity has not been given secondary license as a Lending Company, Broker, or Dealer of Securities, Dealer in Government Securities, Investment Adviser of an Investment Company, Investment House and Transfer Agent. Records also stated that SHAGOPTHA BASHIR KHAN PUNZALAN has not been issued a Certificate of Registration as registered Associate Person, Compliance Officer, Salesman, and Certified Investment Solicitor of a Broker Dealer in Securities Investment, Investment House, Underwriter of Securities, Investment Company Adviser, and Mutual Fund Distributor. Another complainant was contacted by SHA through a common friend and was invited to invest this time using Philippine Offshore Gaming Operations (POGO). She offered the same high interest returns and gave her bank account to the complainant. Being prudent, complainant checked SHA on the internet and discovered that many were scammed by subject SHA. He did not pursue the investment but SHA was persistent in calling and chatting him. With this, complainant sought the assistance of NBI and acting on the information, AOTCD operatives hatched a plan for an entrapment operation. On August 14, 2020, an entrapment operation was conducted when complainant and subject SHA agreed to meet in front of a coffee shop along United Nations Avenue, corner Bocobo Street in Manila. As soon as subject SHA received the entrapment money from the complainant, NBI-AOTCD operatives arrested subjects SHAGOPTHA BASHIR KHAN PUNZALAN and her companion, ROSENDA MOHAMMAD JIMENEZ aka RADZHATA MOHAMMAD SAMPANG. Found and seized from the Subjects were the boodle money, documents on business contracts, loan agreements, Cash Energy Payday Loans, investment agreements, bank checkbooks and passbooks, and several demand letters from other possible victims. Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor, Manila for violation of Article 315 (Swindling/Estafa) of the Revised Penal Code in relation to RA 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012).

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today said a suspect in an Illegal Drugs and Firearms cases currently detained at the NBI Detemtion center was rushed to the Philippine General Hospital (PGH) yesterday afternoon. NBI Officer-In-Charge (OIC) Eric B. Distor identified the subject as PHILIP JACOB NOCOM, a 47-year old inmate who is facing charges for Illegal Drugs and Illegal Possession of Frearms. OIC Distor said Subject Nocom was arrested by operatives of the NBI-International Operations Division (NBI-IOD) and NBI-Task Force Against Illegal Drugs (NBI-TFAID) on June 25, 2020 in a condominium unit in Marikina City. When he was found by the NBI operatives together with security officers of the condominium tower and barangay officials, subject Nocom, a.k.a Alex Benson Vergara y Maragondon, a.k.a. John Robert Bautista y Chua, and a.k.a. Joseph Francis Lee y Camacho, was lying on his bed almost unconscious and weak. Various firearms and ammunitions and 2 kilos of illegal drugs (shabu) worth P13 Million were also found in his condo unit. Various identification cards bearing his aliases and different addresses were also found in his unit. He was brought to the NBI and was presented thru e-inquest before the Office of the Prosecutor of Marikina City on June 26, 2020 after which he was turned over to the NBI detention center on the same day. On July 2, 2020, PNP officers from San Juan Police Station arrived at the NBI and served subject Nocom a Warrant of Arrest issued by the RTC of Pasig City. At about 2pm yesterday, OIC Distor said, subject Nocom was found slumped in his cell by his fellow inmates and was immediately rushed by NBI security officers to the Philippine General Hospital (PGH) but was declared Dead On Arrival. OIC Distor said that they are still awaiting the report from the doctors as to the cause of his death. According to the doctors, however, an autopsy may only be conducted with the consent of subject Nocom’s relatives. According to the security officers at the NBI detention center, subject Nocom was always on the wheel chair and cannot stand alone and did not eat anything the whole time he was inside the detention cell. A day before he was rushed to PGH, subject Nocom took a Rapid Test for COVID-19 administered by the Medical Staff of the City Government of Manila and was tested negative. Operatives of the NBI are now trying to locate any relative of subject Nocom in the addresses indicated in his identification cards to get their consent for the autopsy to determine the cause of death.

SANTIAGO (Ret.), NBI Dagupan District Office (NBI-DADO) arrested SHAWN ABNER GOLDEN a.k.a. CHOT, in San Antonio, Zambales, for Murder and Frustrated Murder. NBI-DADO agents met the Subject along the seashore of Pundaquit. At that time, the NBI-DADO agents explained their presence and properly informed the SUBJECT GOLDEN of his constitutional rights. He then voluntarily surrendered to the agents and boarded their vehicle. Subject GOLDEN was brought to NBI Dagupan District Office, Dagupan City, where he was properly booked and processed. Following standard operating procedure, he was also submitted for medical examination, and mug-shots were taken for record purposes.

body: PRESS STATEMENT February 28, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } In the NBI’s continuing efforts to support the President’s campaign against rice hoarders and agricultural smugglers, NBI Director Judge Jaime B. Santiago (Ret.) met with representatives of the Philippine Rice Industry Stakeholders Movement (PRISM) of Bocaue, Bulacan on February 27, 2025 at the NBI Main Office in Pasay City. Orly Manuntag, co-founder of the PRISM, manifested that the recent operations conducted by the NBI and other law enforcement agencies against rice hoarders raised concerns among legitimate rice millers and importers in their area in Bulacan. This prompted them to directly seek the guidance of the NBI. In response, Director Santiago assured the dealers/millers that the NBI gives utmost importance to the observance of the rule of law and due process in all its operations. The Director maintained that the NBI’s operatives shall in no way exert undue pressure or harassment on legitimate businesses. In particular, Director Santiago directed that no operation relating to rice and agricultural smuggling shall proceed without the strict review and approval of the Assistant Director for Intelligence Service, Assistant Director for Investigation Service and the Director himself. After a brief discussion on the price, the rice millers of Bulacan agreed to sell rice at Php35.00 per kilo, as their way of expressing support to the government’s efforts towards rice stability and sustainability. At the request of Director Santiago, the PRISM members also committed to report to the NBI any rice smuggling or illegal rice activities within their area.

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today said operatives of NBI-Bulacan District Office (NBI-BULDO) arrested an individual for violation of RA 9995 (Anti Photo and Voyeurism Act), RA 9262 (Anti -Violence Against Women and Children Act) in relation to RA 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act), and RA 8353 (Anti Rape Law) NBI Officer-In-Charge (OIC) Director Eric Distor identified the Subject as ERICK HERNANDEZ y PONCE. Subject was arrested in an operation which stemmed from the complaint of the victim, Subject’s girlfriend. According to the complainant, she and Subject had developed a romantic relationship since May 19, 2020 and in several instances had sexual encounters, mostly in the house of the Subject. In one of their sexual bouts, Subject surreptitiously took video of her in nudity. When she noticed it, she immediately took his cellular phone and deleted it. While still harboring question on his sincerity, complainant discovered that Subject also has relationship with a gay. Because of this, they often had heated argument and she started to veer away from the Subject. Complainant was later informed that Subject drank a bleaching liquid to end his life, but was averted when he was brought to the hospital. Complainant learned that the reason of his attempt on his life was her break up with him. Subject also sent her a photo of him with a rope wrapped around his neck. body: PRESS STATEMENT December 06, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI), through its Western Mindanao Regional Office (NBI-WEMRO), successfully seized 350 master cases of smuggled imported cigarettes in Zamboanga City, with an estimated street value of Php 14,974,750.00, as part of its intensified anti-smuggling campaign. The operation also led to the arrest of four individuals identified as MARLON PULAON y SALLIH, JAMAR SALLIH y MOHAMMAD, ABNER JUBAIL y SALLIH, and ALFAIK SAMMY u LADJA. The operation was initiated following intelligence information received from the Philippine Navy-Western Mindanao Naval Command concerning a motorized watercraft, a “Jungkong” named “NURSHAIMA,” which was intercepted during a maritime patrol off the coast of Zamboanga City. NBI-WEMRO agents promptly conducted a confirmatory investigation, establishing the veracity of the report. The arrested individuals were identified as the crew manning the vessel. Upon inspection, they failed to present any requisite transport documents or import clearances from the proper regulatory agencies. The subjects were subsequently arrested, and the vessel and its cargo were seized. Criminal charges have been filed against the individuals for violating Section 7(a) and Section 7(g) of Republic Act No. 12022 (which penalizes the unauthorized importation and transportation of regulated products). Acting Director Atty. Angelito DLP Magno firmly emphasized the Bureau’s commitment, stating: The NBI remains relentless in its commitment to dismantling smuggling syndicates nationwide. These illegal activities severely undermine the local economies by distorting market prices. It cripples and reduces revenue of the government and fosters a climate and corruption. Hence, the Bureau will continue to priorities the suppression of these kind of illegal activities.

body: A member of the notorious Dominguez carnapping group who was involved in the abduction of car dealer Venson Evangelista was arrested by operatives of the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) in Las Piñas City this morning. The suspect was identified as Joel Jacinto y Celestino with aliases Eduardo Fernandez and Joel, 42, a native of Cabanatuan City and residing in Greenfiled, CAA, Las Piñas City. He was arrested by virtue of a warrant of arrest for carnapping with homicide issued by Hon. Ma. Luisa C. Quijano-Padilla of the Quezon City RTC Branch 215. Jacinto alias Joel is a member of the notorious Dominguez Group involved in several carnapping incidents in Metro Manila and nearby provinces. Joel was reportedly one of the abductors of car dealer Venson Evangelista whose burned cadaver was found in Cabanatuan City, Nueva Ecija on January 14, 2011. Evangelista was kidnapped during a test drive of a Toyota Land Cruiser he was selling. The victim’s father and complainant, Arsenio “Boy” Evangelista who is Task Force Director Volunteer Against Carnappers, with the assistance of media informants requested the service of warrant. Jacinto alias Joel is presently detained at the NBI.

body: In line with the continuing anti-illegal drug campaign of the government, the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today said operatives of NBI-Task Force Against Illegal Drugs (TFAID), in partnership with the NBI-Western Mindanao Regional Office (NBI-WEMRO), Philippine National Police (PNP), Philippine Drug Enforcement Agency (PDEA), and the Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) arrested one of the most wanted fugitives in the country, yesterday morning in Zamboanga City. NBI Director Dante A. Gierran identified the Subject as JUN NO, a Korean-American businessman who is wanted for drug trafficking involving the sale of a party drug ecstasy after he escaped from the hospital following his surgery for appendectomy last April 15, 2017. Subject also has a pending case of illegal possession of dangerous drugs and a Warrant of Arrest for drug trafficking. Acting on the Immigration look out bulletin order issued by the Department of Justice (DOJ) against Subject JUN NO a.k.a. “Jazz”, and under strict orders from NBI Director Gierran, the NBI-TFAID, headed by Atty. Ross Jonathan V. Galicia, mobilized its operatives to track down the Subject. Investigation conducted disclosed that from April 18 to April 22, 2017, Subject hid in different condo units and motels in Manila, Parañaque and Makati City to avoid the authorities, then he decided to go to Cebu via Philippines Airlines. Subject stayed in Cebu City from April 29 to May 26, 2017 wherein he was hopping from one hotel to another to avoid detection. While residing in the area, he spent most of his time with drug junkies and escort girls whom he used to hang out with. The NBI-TFAID chased the Subject in Cebu but managed to elude arrest on several occasions. Nevertheless, some of his personal belongings were recovered from his hotel in Cebu City, which provided an indication of the Subject’s plan to leave the country using the back door going to Malaysia. Knowing that the authorities are closing in on him, Subject JUN NO left Cebu City and managed to enter Zamboanga City using fake identification card and passport bearing the name CHOI MINSOO. On May 31, 2017, TFAID operatives proceeded to Zamboanga City to track down the Subject. The following day, TFAID operatives were able to caught the Subject in a computer shop in Barangay Tetuan, Zamboanga City while checking the money coming from his family. Subject JUN NO then did not resist arrest. Criminal case for violation of Article 172 in relation to Article 171 of the Revised Penal Code as well as violation of the Anti-Alias Law and R.A. 8239 (Passport Law) will be filed against the Subject.

body: PRESS STATEMENT July 29, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } In line with the directive from National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Director Judge JAIME B. SANTIAGO (Ret.), the agents of NBI-National Capital Region (NBI-NCR) intensified their operations against individuals practicing optometry without a license. Their effort resulted in the arrest of ENRICO MABALAY ABESAMES in the City of Manila for violation of Section 32 (b), (f), and (g) of Republic Act No. 8050 (Revised Optometry Law of 1995) and Article 172 (Falsification by Private Individuals and Use of Falsified Documents) of the Revised Penal Code (RPC), as amended. On June 29, 2025, NBI-NCR received a complaint regarding the alleged illegal practice of optometry profession by Subject Abesames. The agents of NBI-NCR immediately conducted a surveillance operation and proceeded to EYEZONE OPTICAL CENTRE (Eyezone), which was reportedly operated by Subject Abesames. During the surveillance, the agents of NBI-NCR availed the services of Subject Abesames at the said establishment, posing as a registered Optometrist. Thus, confirming the veracity of the information. On July 17, 2025, an entrapment operation was hatched by NBI-NCR at Eyezone. One of the agents of NBI-NCR who acted as a patient was attended by Subject Abesames, who examined the undercover agent’s eyes using an Auto Refractometer and a trial case set with an LCD monitor, which contains different sizes of letters to measure the grade of the undercover agent’s eyes. Upon handing over the marked money to Subject Abesames, the NBI agents immediately placed him under arrest. Subject was presented for inquest proceedings for the aforementioned violations. Director Santiago commended the dedicated agents of the NBI-NCR, highlighting their relentless efforts and meticulous investigative work that culminated in the successful arrest of Subject Abesames.

body: PRESS STATEMENT August 04, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI), led by Director Judge Jaime B. Santiago (Ret.), arrested an individual in Tacloban City for unauthorized reproduction and distribution of copyrighted review materials. The case stemmed from a letter received by the NBI-Cybercrime Division (NBI-CCD) from Jurists Bar Review Center (Jurists) requesting to take appropriate actions on the alleged unlawful reproduction and distribution of video lectures and review materials owned by or registered to Jurists as its intellectual property, without the latter’s authority, in violation of R.A. No. 8293 also known as the “Intellectual Property Code”, R.A. No. 8792 or the “Electronic Commerce Act of 2000”, and R.A. No. 10175 otherwise known as the “Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012”. Investigation revealed that Subject, identified as BOANERGES TY HIDALGO (Subject HIDALGO), was blatantly and rampantly distributing the video lectures and review materials thru a Facebook group “Philippine Law Student Help Group” in exchange for money, without the consent of or authority from Jurists to the latter’s damage and prejudice. Acting promptly, NBI-CCD agents conducted a test-buy operation. Subject HIDALGO agreed to provide copies of the video lectures and review materials and have them saved in an external drive. Subject HIDALGO then agreed to meet with the poseur-client in Tacloban City. On July 31, 2025, the NBI-CCD, with the assistance of NBI-Eastern Visayas Regional Office (NBI-EVRO), conducted an entrapment operation at Trece Martirez St., Brgy 1 & 4, Tacloban City, which resulted in the arrest of Subject HIDALGO. Subject HIDALGO will be presented for inquest proceedings for violation of the following: Cybercrime through Misuse of Devices under Section 4 par. (5)(i)(aa) in relation to par. (5)(ii) of Republic Act No. 10175, also known as the “Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012”; Piracy under Section 33(b) of R.A. No. 8792, also known as the “Electronic Commerce Act of 2000” in relation to Section 6 of R.A. No. 10175; and Copyright Infringement under Section 217.1 of R.A. No. 8293, also known as the “Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines”in relation to Section 6 of R.A. No. 10175. Pursuant to DOJ Department Circular No. 20 s.2023 (Policy on Pro-Active Involvement of Prosecutors in Case Build Up), coordination with the Office of the Prosecutor, Tacloban City was made. Documents are being prepared for inquest proceedings against Subject HIDALGO for the above-stated violations. Director Santiago commended the NBI-CCD and NBI-EVRO agents whose vigilance and assistance were instrumental in the operation. He stressed that the arrest of Subject HIDALGO underscores the NBI’s commitment to uphold intellectual property and to protect authors and publishers from piracy and other forms of copyright infringement, especially nowadays that ill-minded individuals create opportunities to exploit and act with impunity.

title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: Twenty-one Chinese and Taiwanese nationals allegedly involved in telephone fraud victimizing their compatriots were arrested by agents of the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) during a raid of a resident in Angeles City last week-end. Investigation report disclosed that the suspects are: Huang Li Sin; Huang Shih-Ting; Teng Ya-Huei; Chang Shu-Chu; Lai Chao-Ming; Wu Shu-Lun; Lin Jen Chien; Cheng Chih-Lung; You Jiafu; Huang Cheng Hui; Chan Chih Hsien; Yang Yen Chun; and Wang Pai Lu; Lin Shia Hao; all Taiwanese nationals. Xiang Hong; Hong Xia Juan; Zhang Dongmei; Feng Jianbin; Li Wu Xiu; Luo Jia Xin; and Luo Shi You, all Chinese nationals. Mr. Shih Liang Shia alias Mr. Chen, the alleged leader of the syndicate, remains at-large. On July 5, 2012, the NBI received a letter-request from Mr. Beny Chen, Senior Assistant, Taipei Economic and Cultural Office (TECO) requesting for an investigative intervention relative to the intelligence report of the Ministry of Justice Investigation Bureau (MJIB) regarding the telephone fraud activities of some Taiwanese nationals suspected as syndicate members. They are believed to be operating in the National Capital Region and Luzon. The said fraud syndicate are using high-technology equipment in their operations and have successfully defrauded millions of New Taiwan Dollar (NT$) from Taiwanese and Chinese nationals. The NBI immediately conducted an investigation. An informant who is a computer technician, said that he was contacted by a certain Shih-Liang Shia alias Mr. Chen, a Taiwanese, the leader of the syndicate, to install expanded internet connections of his premises located at Nos. 16-10 and 16-12 Grande St., Riverside Subdivision, Bgy. Anunas, Friendship, Angeles City, Pampanga. During the installation, he observed the fully functional workstations manned by Taiwanese and Chinese nationals as call center agents. Surveillance operations were conducted resulting to the discovery of strategically installed and concealed CCTV cameras at electric posts between houses located at the said address and intertwined telephone and internet cables attached to the same. Further, chants of Chinese speaking people can be heard by adjacent neighbors. A Chinese was always seen in the area acting as a runner. On July 20, 2012, the NBI applied for and was issued a search warrant by Manila RTC Br. 22 Exec. Judge Marino M. Dela Cruz, Jr. By virtue of said warrant, operatives conducted a search on the premises of Mr. Chen. Seized were laptops, telephones, routers, modems, and other apparatus. These are being used as access devices which are unauthorized to obtain money to initiate transfer of funds other than the use of paper instruments. Charges for violation of RA 8484 (the Access Device Regulation Act of 1998) were filed against the suspects before the Angeles City Prosecutor’s Office. In the inquest proceedings, the prosecutor found that the respondents were caught en flagrante delicto. Later, they were brought to Manila where they are detained at the NBI.

body: PRESS STATEMENT May 12, 2022 NBI FILES CRIMINAL CHARGES AGAINST TWO EMPLOYEES OF MAKATI CITY BEFORE OMBUDSMAN In line with the government’s drive against corruption, the National Bureau Investigation (NBI) announces the filing of charges before the Office of the Ombudsman against two (2) employees of Makati City Government for alleged Carnapping and Obstruction of Justice. NBI-Officer-In-Charge (OIC) Director ERIC B. DISTOR identified the subjects as ANSELMO ATIENZA y MORENO, former Officer-In-Charge (OIC) of Impounding Unit and currently assigned at Makati City – Public Safety Department (PSD) and REYNALDO C. PONCE, assigned at the Makati City – General Services Department. Director DISTOR said that the case stemmed from a complaint filed by the owner of a Honda big bike, which was unlawfully taken by the above-named Subjects. According to the complaint, sometime in 2018, the subject motorcycle was confiscated and brought to the Impounding Unit of Makati City-PSD located at Urban St., Brgy. Pio Del Pilar, Makati City. The motorcycle was apprehended during a checkpoint conducted by the elements of the PNP Makati for City Ordinance violation. However, before the Complainant had a chance to redeem the impounded motorcycle, he found out that his motorcycle was missing at the Impounding Unit. The complainant tried to locate his motorcycle but to no avail. After sometime, the Complainant received information regarding with the whereabouts of his motorcycle. Thus, the complainant informed the operatives of NBI-AGD regarding with the information received by the complainant. NBI-AGD operatives immediately conducted a surveillance operation and confirmed the information regarding with the whereabouts of the motorcycle. Thus, the operatives applied for a Search Warrant, which was obtained from RTC Branch 5, Lemery, Batangas against the premises of Subject ATIENZA located at Bauan-San Luis Road, Barangay Taliba, San Luis, Batangas. NBI-AGD operatives implemented the Search Warrant, which resulted in the recovery of the subject motorcycle. Macro-etching examination conducted by NBI-Forensic Chemistry Division revealed that the motorcycle recovered by the NBI-AGD is the same motorcycle of the complainant. In his defense, Subject Atienza claimed that the motorcycle seized by the NBI was gifted by him to the occupant of the premises where the motorcycle was seized. Subject Atienza added that he allegedly bought the motorcycle in scrap or junk condition in Makati City from junkshop McJO Trading (McJO) – the supposed winning bidder, after said motorcycle was allegedly disposed through a public auction by the City Government of Makati. Subject Atienza presented a Delivery Receipt in support of his claim. However, investigation by the NBI-AGD revealed that the motorcycle of the complainant was not included in any public auction by the City Government of Makati. Further, the supposed “Delivery Receipt” pertaining to the said motorcycle was fraudulently obtained and falsified. Thus, on May 5, 2022, NBI-AGD filed charges against Subject Atienza before the Ombudsman for Malversation under Article 217 of the Revised Penal Code; Violation of Sections 3 and 4 of R.A. 10883, otherwise known as the “New Anti-Carnapping Act of 2016”; Use of Falsified Documents under Article 172, paragraph 3 of the Revised Penal Code (RPC); Violation of Section 4(A)(a) and (b), in relation to Section 11 of R.A. 6713, otherwise known as “Code of Conduct and Ethical Standards for Public Officials and Employees”; and Serious Dishonesty and Grave Misconduct under Section 50 of Paragraph A(1) and A(3) of the 2017 Rules on Administrative Cases in Civil Service pursuant to Administrative Code of 1987. In addition, Subject Ponce was included in the charge for Obstruction of Justice, who knowingly and willfully obstructs, impedes, frustrates or delays the apprehension of suspects and the investigation of a crime. Subject Ponce induced McJO to produce a Delivery Receipt in order to make it appear, and support the defense of Subject Atienza that the subject motorcycle was bought from McJO.

title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: PRESS STATEMENT January 20, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI), under the leadership of NBI Director Judge Jaime B. Santiago (Ret.), arrested a Chinese national and two Filipinos for conducting illegal surveillance and spying activities in the vicinities of the Philippines. Sometime in December 2024, the NBI-Special Task Force (STF) and NBI-Cybercrime Division (CCD) received an intelligence report from the AFP-Naval Operatives, that a group of Chinese nationals, in the guise of developing autonomous vehicle, is allegedly engaged in surveillance operations, unlawfully obtaining and disclosing information affecting national defense, utilizing advanced technologies. Acting on the report, the NBI operatives conducted a validation process and identified six (6) members of the group, namely: DENG, YUANQING (a software engineer a.k.a. DENG); two (2) unnamed Hardware Engineers (currently in China); a female financier a.k.a. WANG, (currently in China); and two Filipino cohorts, RONEL JOJO BALUNDO BESA and JAYSON AMADO FERNANDE. Investigation further revealed that DENG is affiliated with PLA University Science and Technology (PLAUST), under automation and engineering discipline, with top specialties in Control Engineering. PLAUST is a prestigious research-oriented university located in Nanjing, Jiangsu, China, operated by the People’s Liberation Army (PLA). As the group’s financier, WANG orchestrated the acquisition of a white vehicle, and ensured the installation of ICT equipment for the planned ISR operations. From December 13, 2024 to January 16, 2025, subject vehicle was monitored traversing to and fro the National Capital Region and the general divisions of Luzon, conducting detailed scouting, collating comprehensive image of the terrains and structures and the over-all topography of the potential targets, without consent and authority from the Philippine Government. Obtaining this critical information affecting national defense without proper authority or necessary permits from any concerned government agencies are flagrant violations of the provisions of Commonwealth Act No. 616 (An Act to Punish Espionage and Other Offenses Against National Security). Thus, operatives hatched an enforcement action on January 17, 2025. NBI operatives spotted the subject vehicle within the vicinity of Palm Tower, Makati City. The vehicle was occupied by DENG YUANQING, Chinese national, who was working on the ICT equipment mounted at the rear compartment, and two Filipinos identified as RONEL JOJO BALUNDO BESA and JAYSON AMADO FERNANDEZ, the driver and companion of DENG. When questioned about his identity, permit, and any authorization, DENG attempted to hide the storage device and flee, prompting the NBI operatives to arrest him as well as the other two. Controlled viewing and onsite search were conducted on the subject ICT equipment, and the same disclosed sensitive data/information comprising topographic footage, mapping the critical infrastructures of the Philippines, among others. A clear violation of Section 1(a) of Commonwealth Act No. 616. Further analysis on the ICT equipment revealed active programs designed to allow users to access and control devices remotely over the internet. Surprisingly, during the onsite search, the forensic examiner found a Chinese character user account with device ID 918 452 619, currently controlling the computer system inside the subject vehicle, specifically the portable keyboard, files, and cameras. This is tantamount to unlawful disclosure of information affecting national defense under Section 2(a) of Commonwealth Act No. 616. Subjects were informed of their constitutional rights and were brought to the NBI main office for the standard booking procedures. They were presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the State Prosecutor, Department of Justice for violation of Section 1 (a) and (b) of Commonwealth Act No. 616 in relation to R.A. 10175 or the “Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012”.

body: PRESS STATEMENT July 03, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } The NBI-Cavite North District Office (CAVIDO-North), under the supervision of NBI Director Judge Jaime B. Santiago (Ret.), arrested Subjects ACE DELA CRUZ GARCIA and REGINALD VENTURA LLANTO in Parañaque City for violation of Sections 4 (d), 12 (j) and 18 of RA 11900 otherwise known as “Vaporized Nicotine and Non-Nicotine Products Regulation Act”. The case stemmed from information received by the NBI-CAVIDO North on the alleged sale and distribution of vaporized nicotine and non-nicotine products that are non-compliant with the registration requirements prescribed by RA 11900. A certification was issued by Department of Trade and Industry – Office for the Special Mandate on Vaporized Nicotine and Non-Nicotine Products (DTI-OSMV) which revealed that the vape products submitted were considered unregulated and substandard. Thus, an entrapment operation was set together with DTI personnel to capture and arrest the Subjects in flagrante delicto of committing the offense. On July 02, 2025, after several hours of transaction and waiting, the entrapment was finally consummated. Subjects were arrested and several boxes of vape products were recovered from them. Seized during the operation were 49 master cases which contain 8,200 pieces of vape pod and 1,600 pieces of vape device among others. Inventory conducted by the agents of NBI-CAVIDO-North and DTI Personnel yielded an estimated value of Php 3,920,000.00. Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the Parañaque City Prosecutor’s Office.

body: PRESS STATEMENT April 30, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } In line with the directive of the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Director Judge Jaime B. Santiago (Ret.) to intensify the campaign against Trafficking in Persons, the NBI – Bataan District Office (BATADO) arrested eight (8) individuals in Meycauayan, Bulacan, for violation of Section 4(a) in relation to Section 6(c) of Republic Act No. 9208 as amended by Republic Act No. 10364 as further amended by Republic Act No. 11862 otherwise known as the “Expanded Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2022.” On 15 April 2025, the NBI-BATADO received a letter from DESTINY RESCUE PILIPINAS INCORPORATED regarding a case of sexual trafficking involving female victims, many of whom are minors, from Region 3 and the National Capital Region. The trafficking operations were reportedly being conducted within an establishment known as “L.A. RESTO BAR” in Brgy. Iba, Meycauayan, Bulacan. Subsequent surveillance operation validated the said information. Thus, on 24 April 2025, in coordination with the Meycauayan City Police Office, NBI-BATADO Agents with social workers from the Department of Social Welfare and Development – Field Office III (DSWD-FO3) proceeded to the location. One Subject, a floor manager of L.A. RESTO BAR, assisted the NBI agents who posed as poseur-customers to order food and drinks. Thereafter, Subject “JORDAN” facilitated a “show-up” of the girls, wherein the girls line up in front of paying customers who are then given a chance to choose among the girls whose service they would avail. Subject JORDAN informed the poseur customers that they can take any of the girls to the VIP rooms and avail of sexual services for Two Thousand Pesos (Php 2,000.00) per “VIP.” Conversation with the entertainers/waitresses disclosed that the operator/manager of the bar offered them to a VIP with the customers in exchange for Two Thousand Pesos (Php 2,000.00), where Seven Hundred Pesos (Php 700.00) is allocated to the operator/manager and the remaining amount is given to the entertainer/waitress. After handing over the marked money, establishing that the transaction for the VIP had been made and completed, the poseur customer agents signaled for the remaining NBI Agents waiting within the vicinity to proceed to the bar. Subjects were caught in flagrante delicto offering and maintaining minor victims for sexual exploitation for a fee and were immediately placed under arrest, and duly apprised of their rights. Subjects were brought to the NBI Bataan District Office. Eight (8) Subjects, including the owner/operator, the “Mamasang”/floor manager and those who engaged the services of the trafficked victims for prostitution, were all recommended to be charged for Qualified Trafficking in Persons under Section 4(a) in relation to Sec. 6(c) of the Expanded Trafficking in Persons Act of 2022, and Sec. 10 of RA 7610. Seventeen (17) individuals, twelve (12) of whom are minors, nine (9) female “trafficked victims” and three (3) male “children-at-risk,” were rescued from the area. The rescued victims were placed under the custody of the social workers from DSWD-Field Office 3 for eventual turnover to their temporary shelters.

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today announced the arrest of an individual by NBI-Special Operations Group (NBI-SOG) for misrepresenting himself as connected to Senator Christopher Lawrence “Bong” Go (Senator Go) and extorted money from unsuspecting prominent businessmen and private individuals. NBI Officer-in-Charge (OIC) Director Eric B. Distor identified the subject as JOHN CARLOS PEDRAGOSA GARCIA. OIC Director Distor said that the operation stemmed from a complaint filed by one of the victims alleging that a certain John Carlos Garcia introduced himself to be connected to Senator Go and was able to dupe prominent businessmen and private individuals from Albay, Laguna, Quezon and Rizal in various amounts totaling P6 M. On February 24, 2021, NBI-SOG operatives interviewed one of the victims who narrated that he was duped by Subject Garcia for P50,000.00. He also relayed to the operatives the names of the other individuals who were victimized by subject Garcia. The following day, NBI operatives proceeded to San Pablo Laguna and met with another victim who stated in her affidavit that her friend offered her a project for the construction of a facility to be used for operation of a Philippine Offshore Gaming Corporation in Buhatan, Sto. Domingo, Albay. The victim accepted the offer and was introduced to Subject John Garcia. Subject Garcia then told her that the secretary of Senator Go named Geraldyne Riano (Riano) is his friend. Subject Garcia demanded from the victim a total amount of Php 1 Million as advance payment for the project in Albay and Malunay, Quezon. Subject Garcia promised the victim that he will arrange a meeting between her and Senator Go but the meeting did not happen. The victim went to the office of Senator Go and was surprised to learn that Riano and Garcia are not employees of Senator Go. Another victim revealed that Subject Garcia bought from her a Suzuki Ertiga car and issued a check amounting to Php 250,000.00 as initial payment but was not honored by the bank. A record check on subject Garcia showed that he has a Warrant of Arrest issued by the RTC Mandaluyong City for Estafa (2 counts). NBI-SOG continued the surveillance operation and was able to track the whereabouts of the subject. On March 10, 2021, Subject Garcia was sighted in a resort in Bolinao, Pangasinan using the car he purchased from one of his victims. Thus, armed with a Warrant of Arrest, NBI-SOG proceeded to the target resort and immediately apprehended Subject Garcia. Subject Garcia was brought to NBI office where he had undergone standard booking procedures.

body: PRESS STATEMENT June 11, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } PRESS RELEASE | NBI RESCUES 15 VICTIMS, ARRESTS 3 IN ILLEGAL SURROGACY OPERATION IN PAMPANGA The National Bureau of Investigation–Human Trafficking Division (NBI-HTRAD) arrested three (3) individuals and rescued fifteen (15) victims in an operation conducted against an alleged illegal surrogacy agency in Porac, Pampanga. The operation stemmed from a complaint filed by a former surrogate mother against House of Surrogacy PH (HOS PH). The complainant alleged that HOS PH recruits financially disadvantaged women to bear children for intended parents (IPs) under deceptive agreements, for the purpose of exploitation. According to the complaint, these women were paid to carry pregnancies and surrender custody upon birth to prospective adoptive parents. After which the Subjects facilitate the falsification of children’s details on the birth certificates. Acting on the complaint, NBI-HTRAD conducted verification with the Department of Health, which confirmed that HOS PH is is neither licensed nor accredited as a healthcare facility. Coordination was likewise made with the NBI-Central Luzon Regional Office (NBI-CELRO) and the Municipal Social Welfare and Development Office (MSWDO) of Porac, Pampanga. Subsequent surveillance and an undercover operation led NBI-HTRAD operatives to identify the individuals involved and uncover the alleged exploitation of surrogate mothers. Operatives also discovered a second facility in Porac, Pampanga housing additional pregnant women victims. Upon confirming the presence of both the Subjects and victims in the two locations, NBI-HTRAD, together with representatives from the MSWDO and Project Rescue Children, conducted a simultaneous raid, which resulted in the arrest of the three (3) Subjects and the rescue of fifteen (15) victims. The arrested individuals were apprised of the violations they committed and their constitutional rights, and were subsequently brought to NBI-HTRAD to undergo the booking procedure. Documents are currently being prepared for the conduct of inquest proceedings against the subjects for violations of pertinent laws. NBI Director Atty. Melvin A. Matibag emphasized that the Bureau remains steadfast in its mission to combat human trafficking and all forms of exploitation. “No individual should be treated as a commodity or be exploited because of their circumstances. The NBI will relentlessly pursue those who prey on the vulnerable and will continue working closely with partner agencies to uphold the law, protect victims, and ensure that justice prevails,” Director Matibag added.

body: PRESS STATEMENT July 31, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } PRESS RELEASE | NBI, Inaresto ang Isang Indibidwal sa Paggamit ng Nakaw na Pagkakakilanlan Inaresto ng National Bureau of Investigation – Human Trafficking Division (NBI-HTRAD) ang isang indibidwal dahil sa pag-oorganisa ng online fraudulent scheme sa pamamagitan ng paglikha at pagpapatakbo ng mga pekeng online persona sa iba’t ibang social media at messaging platforms. Ang scam ay nagresulta sa pagkalugi ng biktima ng humigit-kumulang Php470,000.00. Bukod dito, ginamit ng Subject ang pagkakakilanlan at mga larawan ng isang taong nang walang pahintulot upang lumikha at magpatakbo ng isa sa mga pekeng online persona. Base sa imbestigasyon na ang mga pekeng Viber, Facebook, at Instagram account ay nauugnay sa isang email address at mobile number na nakarehistro sa ilalim ng pangalan ng Subject. Dahil dito, noong Hulyo 24, 2026, nagsagawa ang NBI-HTRAD ng entrapment operation at nagpatupad ng Warrant to Search, Seize, and Examine Computer Data (WSSECD) sa tirahan ng Subject sa Santa Maria, Bulacan. Kinumpirma ng pagsusuri ng NBI Digital Forensics Laboratory na ang mga kaugnay na Instagram, Facebook, at Viber account ay naka-log in sa mga nasamsam na kagamitan ng Subject. Sa komprontasyon, mariing itinanggi ng complainant (na ilegal na ginamit ang pagkakakilanlan) na siya ay may kaugnayan sa Subject, at itinanggi na pinahintulutan niya ang paggamit ng kanyang pangalan, mga larawan, at personal na impormasyon. Inaresto ng NBI-HTRAD ang Subject para sa kasong Estafa sa ilalim ng Artikulo 315 ng Revised Penal Code kaugnay ng Republic Act No. 10175 o ang Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012, at Cyber-related Identity Theft sa ilalim ng Seksyon 4(b)(3) ng R.A. No. 10175. https://www.facebook.com/reel/2087601382140906
