body: PRESS STATEMENT August 09, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } Acting under the direction and guidance of National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Director Judge Jaime B. Santiago (Ret.), the NBI International Operations Division (NBI-IOD), along with the Bureau of Immigration – Fugitive Search Unit (BI-FSU), and representatives from the Supreme Prosecutors’ Office of the Republic of Korea, successfully arrested Korean national JANG, SEJONG, who was the subject of an active Interpol Red Notice for multiple fraud charges. The successful joint law enforcement operation was carried out on August 8, 2025 at Bayshore 1 Resorts Condominium Cluster 2. Barangay Tambo, Parañaque City, where the Subject was residing. After coordinating with the building administration and security personnel, the arresting team proceeded to Unit 12A and served the Interpol Red Notice, JANG, SEJONG was informed of the charges and his constitutional rights. Subject was brought to the NBI for booking procedures, including fingerprinting. photographing, documentation, and a medical examination. He was then turned over to the Bureau of Immigration for custody and deportation proceedings. Director Santiago commended the team, stating that the operation highlights strong cooperation between Philippine and Korean authorities in upholding international justice and the country’s continued commitment in apprehending fugitives hiding within its borders.

body: Vowing to protect consumers from profiteers who take advantage of the crisis brought about by COVID-19, the NBI raided a number of stores of medical supplies in Manila and Rizal yesterday for overpricing. NBI Director Eric Distor who himself led the operation in Sta. Cruz along Rizal avenue Manila, together with operatives of NBI-Special Action Unit (NBI-SAU), said the operation resulted in the seizure of 1,360 pcs of thermal scanners and 7, 680 pieces of face masks worth more than P10 Million. Director Distor said the operation stemmed from an information that the store was selling thermal scanners for P8,000.00 per piece which is 8 times higher than its normal price of P1,000. Distor added that the store had a signage at its front door “OUT OF STOCK THERMAL SCANNER” and “OUT OF STOCK ANY KIND OF MASK”. Distor said during the operation yesterday, several boxes containing 1,360 thermal scanners and boxes with 7,680 pieces of face masks were found in the storage room of the store. Arrested were the Assiatant Manager, cashier and their salesladies who will be charged for violation of RA 7581 otherwise known as the Price Act of the Philippines. Mr. Rudy Miranda, owner of the store who was not in the area during the operation, will likewise be charged for the same offense. In the second operation also yesterday, the NBI-Rizal District Office headed by Atty. Igmidio Congzon, Jr. raided the Professional Skin Care Formula by Dr. Alvin in Taytay Rizal for overpricing of Isopropyl alcohol. Director Distor said the operation was prompted after a poseur customer was able buy 2 gallons of alcohol at P750.00 each which is very much higher than the price dictated by the DTI in pursuance of the price freeze on medical supplies and basic necessities due to the COVID-19. The operation yielded 8 gallons of 70% Isopropyl alcohol that are also being sold in refill by small bottles. A request for Certification for product registration and/ or notification has been made with the FDA. Charges are being readied against its owner/proprietress, LYNDY MAROLLANO of Cainta Rizal and her staff, ANNABELE TIRADOS MENDOZA, for violation of R.A. 7581 otherwise known as the Price Act of the Philippines as amended by R.A. 10623 on Automatic Price Control and for possible violation of R.A. 3720 as amended by R.A. 9711, otherwise known as the Food and Drug Administration Act of 2009. Director Distor assured the public that the NBI will be relentless in its campaign against profiteers and overpricing to protect consumers especially during this crisis. http://nbi.gov.ph/uploads/2020/03/video-1584785592.mp4 http://nbi.gov.ph/uploads/2020/03/video-1584785675.mp4

body: The National Bureau of Investigation today said operatives of the NBI- Special Action Unit (NBI – SAU) have arrested a Subject for alleged large scale illegal recruitment, yesterday in Pasay City. NBI Director Dante A. Gierran identified the Subject as ANALYN DUCUSIN, who was arrested by NBI – SAU operatives yesterday afternoon in an entrapment operation, in a mall in Pasay City after victimizing about ninety five complainants who trooped to the office of the NBI after learning of the arrest of the Subject. The victims have filed their complaints against Subjects MARIA THERESA BUMATAY BARUELO alias “MARIA TERESITA BARUELO, MARIA TERESA BUMATAY BURUELO, MA. body: On July 2, 2021, operatives of NBI-Rizal District Office (NBI-RIZDO) seized counterfeit Nike and Converse products with an estimated value of Php 15 Million. Items were seized in Quezon City and province of Pampanga by virtue of Search Warrants issued against SHIWEN LIM, JASMINE GUILLERMO, and proprietors/employees/occupants of SABRINACIO FOOTWEAR and XIAOO CLOTHING for violation of RA 8293 (Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines). Charges for violation of RA 8293 will be filed against the said Subjects. On July 3, 2021, operatives of NBI–Iligan District Office (NBI-ILDO) arrested JESTY ESTEFANIO y ALBERT for selling illegal drugs in Iligan City. Subject was arrested in a buy-bust operation conducted by NBI-ILDO on July 3, 2021 at Purok 24A, Zone 10, Brgy. Maria Cristina, Iligan City. Bought from the Subject was one piece large size heat-sealed white rectangular transparent plastic sachet containing white crystalline substance suspected to be shabu weighing more or less 7 grams with an estimated market value of Php 47,600. Confiscated from the possession of Subject ESTEFANIO were one (1) genuine 500 peso bill, thirteen (13) pieces 1,000 peso bill boodle money, one (1) identification card, one (1) improvised pipe, one (1) keypad cellphone and one (1) black and white surgical mask. Subject ESTEFANIO was brought to NBI-ILDO office where he was booked, fingerprinted, photographed, and temporarily detained. The confiscated drug evidences were forwarded to NBI Regional Office 10, Forensic Chemistry Division for quantitative and qualitative examination. Case for violation of RA 9165 (Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act) was being prepared for filing in court against the Subject. On July 7, 2021, operatives of NBI-Rizal District Office (NBI-RIZDO) arrested ANGELICA OLLAGUE y FUTOL in Taytay, Rizal for human trafficking. Subject was arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from an information that alleged human trafficking activities are taking place in the nearby towns of Rizal. According to the information, several pimps at the said area are maintaining prostitutes who appear to be minors and are offering them to possible clients for a quick sexual intercourse in nearby hotels and resorts in exchange for monetary considerations. Surveillance conducted revealed that a certain “Geca”, is maintaining, harboring, offering, and delivering girls who appear to be minors for sexual intercourse and other sexual favors. On the above-mentioned date, the entrapment operation was conducted resulting in the arrest of ANGELICA OLLAGUE y FUTOL. Nine (9) trafficked victims, five (5) of whom are minors, were likewise rescued in the operation. Subject ANGELICA “GECA” OLLAGUE y FUTOL was presented for inquest proceedings before Rizal Provincial Prosecutor’s Office for violation of RA 9208 (AntiTrafficking in Persons Act of 2003) as amended by RA 10364 (Expanded Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2012) and violation of RA 7610 (Special Protection Against Child Abuse, Exploitation and Discrimination Act). On July 8, 2021, operatives of NBI-National Capital Region (NBI-NCR) JULIETA V. SANTOS and RENATO FRANCISCO for Syndicated Estafa, Perjury and Falsification of Public Documents. Subjects were arrested in an operation which stemmed from the complaint against Santos, Francisco and a certain Emerlita Santo Domingo, regarding an 8,632 sqm. parcel of land, which the complainant purchased in 2005 from Antonio Altiveros and Amelita Altiveros (previous owners) as evidenced by a notarized Deed of Absolute Sale. Sometime in July 2015, complainant visited the property and was surprised to see a structure erected in her property. Complainant lodged a complaint before the Barangay where the property is situated. The Barangay Chairman invited the offending party for a meeting. At the meeting, Subjects Santos and Francisco together with the current possessor of the property Teodora Cremat, all 3 of them claimed the property was sold to Cremat by Antonio and Amelita Altiveros as evidenced by a Deed of Absolute Sale dated October 3, 2005. However, a discrepancy was later discovered in the purported Deed of Absolute Sale. Antonio Altiveros (previous owner) died on March 24, 2005, seven months prior to the Deed of Absolute Sale to Cremat where subjects Santos and Francisco signed as witnesses despite knowing that Antonio Altiveros is already dead. Complainant also verified the authenticity of the notary of the Deed and it was found that the subject Deed of Sale was not registered to the Notarial Registry. The complainant also found that the subjects unlawfully represented themselves as the owners of the 8,632 sq.m. property and even sold multiple small portions to various parties. To stop further illegal acts of sale and subsequent illegal structures on the property, complainant deployed security guards in May 2021. Complainant also discovered that the subjects falsified a Real Estate Mortgage (REM) Agreement by the subjects with the intention of foreclosing the property. While conducting the investigation, it was discovered that Santos and Francisco were trying to sell 3 other parcels of land owned by the complainant. NBI operatives, acting as poseurbuyers of the parcel of lots, under the guise of being interested buyers, were given photocopies of titles of the 3 parcels of lots. On July 8, 2021, NBI-NCR operatives conducted an entrapment operation in a resort in Tanza, Cavite. As soon as P1Million marked- money was handed over a downpayment for the property and subsequent signing of Acknowledgement Receipt, subjects were immediately apprehended. Subjects JULIETA SANTOS and RENATO FRANCISCO were presented for inquest proceedings before the Provincial Prosecutor of the Province of Cavite in the City of Imus for violations of Article 315 (Estafa), Articles 171 and 172 (Falsification of Public Documents/Use Falsified Documents) and Article 183 (Perjury) all under the Revised Penal Code as amended. Tambo, Lipa City, Batangas by virtue of Warrant of Arrest issued by RTC Branch 21, Imus, Cavite for six counts of Cyber Libel and by Family Court Branch 4, Imus, Cavite for violation of RA 7610 9231 (Special Protection of Children Against Abuse, Exploitation and Discrimination Act). The operation was upon receipt of letter from Julita Belmonte requesting assistance in serving the said Warrants of Arrest. Maria, Bulacan by virtue of Search Warrant issued against NORWEIGIE PAUL PRIETO CACANINDIN and/or REACHGOLD CONSUMER GOODS TRADING for violation of RA 3720 as amended by RA 9711 (Food and Drug Administration Act of 2009). On July 14, 2021, operatives of NBI-Environmental Crime Division (NBI-EnCD), together with DENR-Environmental Law Enforcement and Protection Service, Local Government Unit of Minalin and Sto. Tomas, Pampanga, conducted an inspection and validation of the alleged illegal discharge of poultry farm waste in the Municipality of Minalin and Sto. Tomas, Pampanga. During the inspection, more than 30 poultry farms and a total of 213 poultry buildings/pens covering an estimated area of 30 hectares were documented directly discharging its waste to a water body deemed as a swamp area without proper segregation and sanitary equipment. The discharge of waste leads directly to Ilug Balen and Masaloso River, Pampanga which drains into th Manila Bay. Further, a poultry farm was discovered operating with minors as employees. On July 16, 2021, operatives of NBI-Puerto Princesa District Office (NBI-PUERDO) arrested JUENIES BAYBADO y BANDAJANDONG for violation of RA 10883 (Carnapping) and Robbery. The case stemmed from the complaint of Gregorio Echague III, the authorized representative of Conrado N. Mancao who executed a Special Power of Attorney (SPA) authorizing Echague to file, appear, transact process or any other legal action in relation to the recovery of his vehicles under his business name THE PROMISE MARKETING. According to the complaint affidavit of Echague, NELSON V. DORIA, LOLI CABINGABANG, ENGR. EDDIE C. NALICA, ANDRE C. VIDUYA, JUENIES BAYBADO y BANDAJANDONG carnapped and took the battery, starter, ignition coil of the vehicles owned by Conrado Mancao. Certification issued by LTO revealed that the vehicles are registered in the name of Conrado N. Mancao and The Promise Marketing. On July 15, 2021, NBI-PUERDO received a report that the vehicles and heavy equipment were sighted in Purok Centro 1, Brgy. Sta. Lourdes, Puerto Princesa City. Thus, on July 16, 2021, NBI operatives conducted an operation resulting un the arrest of JUENIES BAYBADO y BANDAJANDONG who claimed to be the owner of the premises where Dong Fe dump truck registered in the name of The Promise Marketing was found. Arrested Subject was presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor, Puerto Princesa City for the abovementioned violation. On July 21, 2021, operatives of NBI-Anti-Fraud Division (NBI-AFD) arrested BERNIE LIMPIADA y REVADENERA a.k.a. BRIX, MARVIN OJEDA y JAUREZ, a.k.a. MARVIN JUAREZ OJEDA, GLORY ANN PILLORA y ID, ROGELIO LAVERINTO FAMBUENA JR., and SISON INOCENCIO y NICOLAS for illegal investment activities. The case stemmed from the report of a walk-in informant regarding an alleged investment scam perpetrated by AGRI-WEALTH FARM VENTURES INC. owned and operated by Subjects BERNIE LIMPIADA y REVADENERA and MARVIN OJEDA y JUAREZ. Informant and his associate, accompanied by the officials of Anti-Red Tape Authority (ARTA), reported to NBI-AFD the illegal investment activities of Subject LIMPIADA and his cohorts. According to the informant, AGRI-WEALTH is offering investment to the public with the promise of 160% return of investment within the period of 100 days. Subjects promised investors a daily profit ranging from 1.6% to 2.5% of the invested amount. For each direct referral or recruit that one brings to the company, he gets an additional 5% of the invested amount of his referral and additional 2% for the second level recruits and 1% for the succeeding levels of recruit until the 10th level. Verification with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) revealed that AGRI-WEALTH is neither registered as corporation nor was it issued a secondary license as a Lending Company, Broker, or Dealer of Securities, Dealer in Government Securities, Investment Adviser of an Investment Company, Investment House and Transfer Agent. Moreover, AGRI-WEALTH has not filed nor has any pending application for a secondary license with SEC. With these, entrapment operations were hatched at a restaurant in a mall in Quezon City for the scheduled submission of the collected investment money to Subject LIMPIADA, and at AGRI-WEALTH’s office in New Manila, Quezon City. The entrapment operations resulted in the arrest of the abovementioned Subjects. When asked to present their SEC registration papers, business permits, and other pertinent documents relating to the operation of their business, Subjects failed to present any. Arrested Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor, Quezon City for violation of Sections 8 and 26 of RA 8799 otherwise known as The Securities Regulation Code. Items were seized in Binondo, Manila by virtue of Search Warrants issued against John/Jane Does of various stalls located in 168 Shopping Mall, Binondo, Manila for violation of RA 8293 (Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines). Appropriate charges will be filed against the said establishments. On July 23, 2021, operatives of NBI-Special Action Unit (NBI-SAU) arrested BENJIE LAGASCA MONTAOS and ARTURO FLORES MAGTALAS in Tondo, Manila for selling Covid-19 vaccination slots. The case stemmed from a report regarding an alleged illegal sale of vaccination slots to POGO employees by certain “BENJIE”. According to the information received, BENJIE offered to personally assist the individuals who wish to avail the vaccination in Manila. BENJIE further explained that in order for these individuals to get vaccinated, they should each possess a stub or ticket in the vaccination site. The stubs of tickets would be given personally by BENJIE on the day of the vaccination for the consideration of Php 6,000 per vaccination slot. Acting on the complaint, an entrapment operation was hatched on July 24, 2021. NBI-SAU proceeded to the said vaccination site and strategically positioned themselves around the area. Poseur-clients and the informant were personally met by BENJIE and male companion identified as Brgy. Kagawad ARTURO MAGTALAS. BENJIE and MAGTALAS assisted the team in the parking and guided them to the reserved seats in the waiting area of the vaccination site. BENJIE asked for the hard copies of the waivers and vaccination ID QR code. When the team asked for the stubs/tickets for the vaccination slots, BENJIE instructed them to discreetly board a black Hyundai Starex with plate number WLI 182 parked nearby. Inside the said vehicle, BENJIE handed to the poseur-client ten stubs with numbers 222-231. BENJIE then demanded for the Php 60,000 which the poseur-client handed to BENJIE. At this juncture, NBI operatives approached BENJIE and KGWD. MAGTALAS, introduced themselves as law enforcement officers, identified their authority and explained the purpose of the entrapment. Subjects were then placed under arrest and were apprised of their constitutional rights. BENJIE was identified as BENJIE MESA MONTAOS through the identification cards found in his possession. Subjects were brought to NBI Office for the standard booking procedures. Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor, Manila for violations of RA 11032 or the Anti-Red Tape Act of 2007 and RA 3019 or the Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act. Additional charges for violation of RA 6713 (Code of Conduct and Ethical Standards for Public Officials and Employees) were filed against ARTURO F. MAGTALAS. The case stemmed from a complaint filed against the Subject for alleged Usurpation of Authority, Extortion, and violation of the Anti-Red Tape Act of 2007. According to the complainant, they were having a legal problem with the seller of their purchased dump truck, wherein despite having received the down payment failed to deliver the same as agreed. As such, they asked for somebody who could help them initiate legal action against the seller. A complainant’s friend then introduced them to CAÑALES who introduced himself as an NBI Agent. CAÑALES allegedly assured the complainant that they could help them solve their problem. However, complainant was surprised when CAÑALES demanded Php 200,000 as mobilization fee. Sensing that CAÑALES is not a real NBI Agent, they reported the matter before the NBI-SAU. Acting on the complaint, an entrapment operation was hatched resulting in the arrest of the Subject after receiving the marked money. Seized from the Subject are the marked money, NBI badge, smart phone, jacket with NBI logo, voter’s ID under the name CAÑALES, CHARLESTON MESA, a black holster, and facemask with NBI logo. CAÑALES was brought to the NBI for the standard booking procedures. NBI Personnel Division issued a certification that the name CHARLESTONE MESA CAÑALES does not appear in the roster of NBI employees. CHARLESTONE MESA CAÑALES was presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor, Quezon City for Robbery/Extortion, Usurpation of Authority/Official Functions and violation of RA 9485 otherwise known as the Anti-Red Tape Act of 2007 On July 26, 2021, operatives of NBI-Anti-Organized and Transnational Crime Division assisted the Bureau of Customs (BOC) in recovering stolen vehicles supposedly under the possession and custody of BOC-CISS. On March 27, 2019, LOA was issued by the Commissioner of Customs. Armed with Mission Order which was subsequently issued by the District Collector, Customs personnel proceeded to FEIDATONG WAREHOUSE located at Phase 2, Blk. 2 Lot 14, Brgy. Tabing Ilog, Marilao, Bulacan and implemented the LOA. As a result thereof, several merchandise were seized by BOC personnel. On February 4, 2020, a certain Jerry Ang requested clearance to remove from FEIDATONG warehouse five motor vehicles purportedly owned by him. Said vehicles were parked inside the warehouse when the LOA was served. The Commissioner denied the request. After some time, the vehicles went missing. Acting on reliable information, on July 26, 2021, NBI-AOTCD and BOC-CISS proceeded to Silver Gate, St. John Industrial Estate, Brgy. Duhat, Bocaue, Bulacan where they found several vehicles parked along the street. Considering that nobody is claiming ownership of the vehicles, administrator of the Industrial Estate and Security Detachment Commander found opposition in towing away said vehicles. Considering that the matter is within the jurisdiction of the BOC, the vehicles were turned over to BOC-CISS as witnessed by the Executive Officer of Brgy. Patubig, Marilao, Bulacan. The vehicles were brought to BOC impounding area at Port Area, Manila. On July 28, 2021, operatives of National Bureau of Investigation-National Capital Region (NBI-NCR) arrested JOREN MARI TAMAYO BECHAYDA for selling illegal drugs. The case stemmed from a report regarding a certain alias Corine and his cohorts who were allegedly engaged in the sale, trading, administration, dispensation, delivery, distribution, and transportation of dangerous drugs in the cities of Paranaque and Pasay, in violation of RA 9165 otherwise known as the Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002. body: PRESS STATEMENT July 19, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } The National Bureau of Investigation has taken note of Senator Alan Peter Cayetano’s remarks referring to NBI Director Melvin A. Matibag as a “minion.” No one in the Bureau will take offense at the label, nor will it be answered in kind. The Bureau’s work rests on evidence, on documents, and on the law — and none of these is moved by name-calling. The Director answers to no one’s interest but the public’s. The inquiry into the conduct and financing of the 2019 Southeast Asian Games was opened for a single reason: billions in public funds appear to have been disbursed outside the ordinary safeguards of competitive bidding and government audit, and the Filipino people are entitled to know how their money was spent. That question stands regardless of who asks it or who is discomfited by it. It bears noting that the loudest objections to an audit seldom come from those with nothing to account for. When a position cannot be defended with facts, it is often defended with insults. The Bureau reads the Senator’s choice of words in exactly that light – and proceeds undeterred. The NBI’s inquiry is impartial, evidence-based, and grounded squarely in its mandate under the law. It presumes no one guilty and exempts no one from scrutiny. We invite anyone with knowledge of the matter — the Senator included — to bring their evidence to the Bureau, and not to a livestream. Director Matibag will continue to do the work the Filipino people expect of him. He may be called many things. Beholden will never be one of them. Office of the Director, National Bureau of Investigation

body: PRESS STATEMENT September 11, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } In line with the directive from National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Director JUDGE JAIME B. SANTIAGO (Ret.), the NBI-Iligan District Office (NBI-ILDO) has intensified operations against individuals falsely portraying themselves as NBI agents. As a result, BRENNETH RYAN BUOT y SOLIDUM has been charged with violation of Article 177 (Usurpation of Authority) of the Revised Penal Code (RPC), as amended, before the Office of the City Prosecutor of Iligan City on September 3, 2025. The case stemmed from a complaint alleging that Subject BUOT falsely claimed to be an agent of the NBI and encouraged individuals to invest in FU DALU Agricultural Products Trading. Investigation conducted by NBI-ILDO agents revealed that Subject BUOT consistently displayed a fake NBI badge and identification, carried firearms, and introduced himself as an NBI agent at both private and public gatherings. On one occasion, he even picked up the complainants from the airport, escorted by armed individuals dressed in police and military uniforms, thereby creating the misleading impression that he possessed official government authority. Several witnesses informed the investigating agents that they personally saw Subject BUOT displaying his NBI badge, ID, and firearms, while openly boasting about his alleged affiliation with the NBI. Verification with the NBI-Human Resource Management Division (NBI-HRMD) disclosed that Subject BUOT is not a member or employee of the NBI. Director Santiago commended the agents of NBI-ILDO for the successful filing of a case against the fake NBI agent. He stressed that he will not tolerate any illegal activities that could harm the reputation of the NBI. Additionally, he warned that the agency will be relentless in pursuing individuals who misrepresent themselves as NBI agents.

In this case, the failure of the above-named officers resulted in the death of the four (4) Philippine Army members. body: PRESS STATEMENT February 10, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) formally conducted a turnover ceremony marking the leadership change at its International Operations Division (IOD), highlighting the Bureau’s continued commitment to global cooperation against transnational crime. Representatives from international law enforcement and diplomatic partners attended the event, including the Federal Bureau of Investigation, Australian Federal Police, Homeland Security Investigations, National Crime Agency, Chinese Police, and officials from the Embassies of Thailand, the Netherlands, Germany, and the United States. In her farewell message, outgoing IOD Chief Filipinas Astrero expressed gratitude to NBI leadership, personnel, and international partners for their trust and support. Assuming leadership is Atty. Christopher Hernandez, who thanked Acting NBI Director Angelito DLP Magno for his confidence and pledged to strengthen international partnerships while upholding the Bureau’s core values. Director Magno emphasized continuity in service, noting that while new leadership steps in, the outgoing chief will take on another vital role within the Bureau. The ceremony reaffirmed the NBI’s strong collaboration with global partners in addressing international criminal threats through cooperation and professionalism. #NBIServes

body: PRESS STATEMENT March 04, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } The National Bureau of Investigation-Cavite North District Office (CAVIDO North), under the supervision of NBI Director Judge Jaime B. Santiago (Ret.), arrested two individuals for Illegal Recruitment and Estafa. The case stemmed from the complaint of seven individuals against Subjects GIRISH FUEGO and GLENMORE BANAGAN. In his sworn statement, one of the complainants stated that he received a call from Subject FUEGO who introduced herself as a Recruitment Agent of CPL Masters Recruitment INC. and that she is recruiting skilled workers for deployment to Austria. FUEGO added that qualified recruits would receive around Php100,000.00 monthly salary. Complainant, finding the offer of work and salary quite alluring, manifested his desire to apply for the position of mason. He had paid FUEGO a total of Php 166,600.00 allegedly for medical, processing fee, working visa, travel insurance, placement fee, and plane tickets. However, FUEGO told the complainant that the employer in Austria refused to issue work permit and for this reason he will instead be deployed to Croatia as factory assistant for which the complainant acceded. Complainant, together with other applicants stayed in the house of FUEGO in Nueva Estancia Subdivision, Gen. Trias Cavite. Thereat, they met Subject BANAGAN who latter introduced himself as a representative of a foreign recruitment agency and the one responsible for finding employers for the Filipino recruits. Subject BANAGAN then took the passport of all the applicants purportedly for the purpose of Visa application and issuance of Overseas Employment Certificate (OEC). Applicants/Victims stayed in the house of FUEGO for several weeks while waiting for the promised Overseas Employment Certificate, Working Visa and eventual deployment abroad but to no avail. After more than a year of waiting, applicants/victims sought the assistance of the Department of Migrant Workers (DMW). Through DMW’s certifications, they found out that FUEGO and BANAGAN are not licensed nor authorized by DMW to recruit workers for overseas employment. Further, Subjects have no record of employment with Placewell International Services Corporation and CPL Masters Recruitment Agency Inc. Since Subjects were still communicating with the complainant, CAVIDO North Agents hatched an entrapment operation on February 27, 2025, which resulted in the arrest of Subjects FUEGO and BANAGAN. Subject BANAGAN admitted that he was also prosecuted and arrested for large scale illegal Recruitment in the provinces of Batangas and Marinduque. Subjects GIRISH FUEGO and GLENMORE BANAGAN were presented for inquest proceedings for violation of Section 5 of R.A. 8042 as amended by R.A. 10022 otherwise known as the Migrant Workers and Overseas Filipinos Act of 1995, and for Estafa under Article 315 paragraph 2(a) of the Revised Penal Code, as amended.

SANTIAGO (Ret.), to crackdown the illegal drug trade in the country, the NBI-Dangerous Drugs Division (NBI-DDD) arrested ISABELO MARI FELICIANO in Quezon City for violation of Republic Act No. 9165 (Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002). The arrested subject was presented for inquest proceedings for the said violation. Director Santiago commended the agents of NBI-DDD for the successful arret of the subject.

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today said operatives of NBI-Anti-Fraud Division (NBI-AFD) arrested an individual on January 30, 2018 in Malate, Manila for Large Scale Illegal Recruitment. Director Dante A. Gierran identified the Subject as MALKAH BILLONES DOLOR. The case stemmed from the complaints against the Subject and three (3) others for alleged Estafa and illegal recruitment. According to the Complainants, Subject MALKAH recruited them as house keepers and room attendants for Corinthia Hotel in London with a three-year contract and with monthly salary of Two Thousand Five Hundred Pounds (GBP 2,500). They were required by the subject to pay Php 9,500 for the employment processing fee. Enticed by the Subject’s representation, Complainants paid the aforesaid processing fee. Payments were made through bank deposits under the name of FERDINAND DUMOL DOLOR and money remittances received by MARY JOY CAPE and BON KRISTOFFER GABAY. However, Complainants grew suspicious about the contractual agreement and the alleged Schengen visa to be provided by the Subject. They personally inquired the matter before the Philippine Overseas Employment Administration (POEA) where they discovered that Subject MALKAH and her cohorts are not authorized to recruit workers for overseas employment. They were then advised to report the matter to NBI. Subject MALKAH continuously demanded additional processing fees from the Complainants. With this, an entrapment operation in Malate, Manila where one of the Complainants agreed to meet with the Subject. The operation resulted in the arrest of Subject MALKAH after he received the marked money. Subject MALKAH was presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the Prosecutor General, Department of justice (DOJ) for Large Scale Illegal Recruitment and EStafa, and is presently detained at the NBI Detention Center.

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today announced the arrest of a Bureau of Jail Management and Penology (BJMP) officer by operatives of NBI-Task Force Against Illegal Drugs (NBI-TFAID) on January 16, 2021, for alleged Rape. NBI Officer-In-Charge (OIC) Eric B. Distor identified the Subject as BJMP SR. INSP. RAMON CAROLINO y PADOLINA. OIC Distor said that the victim, a 26 year old lesbian, accompanied by her partner filed a complaint for Rape against his landlord, Subject BJMP SR. INSP. RAMON CAROLINO y PADOLINA. Victim was crying, weak and appeared traumatized when she reported the alleged crime. According to the victim, at around 5:30AM of January 16, 2021, after a drinking session in their boarding house at Pasay City, Subject, thru threat and intimidation, had carnal knowledge of her. Medico-Genitalia examination was conducted on the victim and preliminary report by NBI-Medico Legal Division (NBI-MLD) found lacerations/injuries on victim’s genital. Acting on these information, NBI operatives conducted hot pursuit of the Subject. At around 3:00PM of the same day, NBI-TFAID operatives, together with the complainant and NBI-Forensic Chemistry Division (NBI-FCD) officers, proceeded to 1957 Leveriza, Pasay City. Subject was present in the area and was informed of the nature of the complaint against him as well as his constitutional rights. He was then placed under arrest. Witnessed by Brgy. Kagawad Romeo Crisostomo Casanova, NBI-FCD recovered boxer shorts, bed sheet of Subject, pillow case, blanket and bed sheet of the victim containing blood stains and body fluids. Items seized in the crime scene were subjected to chemical analysis by the NBI-FCD. Subject RAMON CAROLINO y PADOLINA was presented for inquest proceedings before the Pasay City Prosecutors Office and was charged with Rape under Article 266 of the Revised Penal Code as amended by RA 8353.

body: PRESS STATEMENT March 30, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } NBI SEIZES COUNTERFEIT BEAUTY PRODUCTS IN RIZAL RAID PASAY CITY, Philippines – The National Bureau of Investigation – Rizal District Office (NBI-RIZDO) has successfully shut down a major illegal manufacturing and distribution network specializing in unregistered and hazardous cosmetic products. The operation led to the arrest of the individual behind the “Dimple Soaps” social media accounts, which marketed high-risk products including hair treatments and specialized soaps. The operation was initiated after three victims approached NBI-RIZDO reporting physical injuries and adverse side effects after using products purchased from the Subject. Following these reports, NBI-RIZDO conducted cyber surveillance operation targeting the social media platforms of the Subject. Investigation revealed that the unauthorized manufacturing facility was located in San Jose, Antipolo. The Subject utilized online storefronts to market a variety of products, most notably unregistered feminine hygiene bars and soaps marketed with unsubstantiated health claims. On March 25, 2026, a joint enforcement team composed of the NBI-RIZDO, the Food and Drug Administration (FDA), and the Antipolo Business Permit and Licensing Office (BPLO) executed the raid, resulting in the on-site arrest of the owner and operator of the targeted social media accounts. During the operation, authorities seized various illicit products, including hair rebonding treatments and various soaps, such as the “HIKARI” brand feminine bars and novelty-molded soaps. Furthermore, an inspection by the Antipolo BPLO confirmed that the manufacturing facility, operating under the names “DIMPLE SOAP,” “Dimple Sabon”, and “D Organics Soap”, lacked a valid License to Operate (LTO) and the necessary business permits to function legally. The Subject was presented for inquest proceedings for violations of Republic Act No. 9711 (Food and Drug Administration Act of 2009) and Republic Act No. 7394 (Consumer Act of the Philippines), both in relation to Section 6 of the Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012. The NBI and FDA emphasize that these unregistered products have not undergone mandatory quality and safety testing. Because cosmetics are classified as health products, using unauthorized substances poses a significant risk of chemical burns, infections, and long-term health complications. #NBIServes

body: PRESS STATEMENT October 24, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } In an effort to eradicate the proliferation of individuals engaged in the unauthorized practice of medicine, the National Bureau of Investigation – National Capital Region (NBI-NCR) intensified its campaign against individuals involved in the said unlawful activities. This resulted in the arrest of MARIA GERIELYN BARIS SERRANO, MARIAM ELIAS SINALIMBO, ISMAYRA SOLAYMAN INDAO, ZURIKA TEGEL PASANDALAN, PRINCESS DILANGALIN INDAI, JOHN LLOYD SAN JUAN ROMERO, and MARCIAN DILANGALIN INDAO for violation of Section 10 of R.A. No. 2382 (The Medical Act of 1959) and Section 11(a) of R.A. No. 9711 (The Food and Drug Administration Act of 2009). The operation commenced after a Complainant reported receiving a botched “Thread Lift Procedure” at the “Lavender Clinic”, which she found through social media. She developed a soft tissue infection after procedure, which was conducted under unsanitary conditions. The Complainant discovered after the procedure that the practitioners who conducted the procedure were not licensed medical professionals and only had minimal training from a foreign employer. In response to the complaint, Agents from the NBI-NCR carried out a series of surveillance operations which revealed that the clinic was offering medical procedures to potential clients. During the surveillance, the clinic staff were questioned about the qualifications of the individuals performing these procedures. They claimed that the practitioners were “aesthetic nurses,” but they refused to provide any names or professional licenses. Moreover, the Agents were able to identify the medical products being offered and used by the clinic for their medical procedures. Further surveillance showed that the clinic is owned by Gabriel Honario Jr., who was found to be an unlicensed physician, according to verification from the Philippine Regulatory Commission (PRC). Additionally, verification with the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) disclosed that the products used by the clinic are unregistered. On October 16, 2025, after obtaining an appointment for a medical procedure at the target clinic, NBI-NCR Agents conducted an entrapment operation in Makati, which resulted in the arrest of seven (7) individuals who were caught in the act of performing medical procedures without proper licenses. Verification made with the PRC revealed that aside from Subject Serrano, who is a registered nurse, all of the arrested individuals are not licensed healthcare professionals. All the arrested Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the Prosecutor, Makati City for the aforementioned violations. NBI Director JUDGE JAIME B. SANTIAGO (Ret.) commended the NBI-NCR agents for their successful operation, resulting in the arrest of the subjects.

body: The National Bureau of Investigation- Dumaguete District Office (NBI-DUMDO) has seized various antibiotics and other pharmaceutical drugs sold without any prescription in Mabinay, Negros Oriental. NBI OIC-Director Eric B. Distor said a report was received by NBI-DUMDO regarding a group of unscrupulous individuals engaged in selling antibiotics and other pharmaceutical drugs without any prescription. Acting on the said report, NBI-DUMDO operatives proceeded to the area on January 23, 2022 and observed thereat that medical drugs including prescription drugs were sold in an open market just like ordinary goods. Operatives asked the saleslady identified as GINA TOMANDOC whether or not she has authority from Food and Drug Administration (FDA) to sell or if she is a licensed pharmacist. TOMANDOC failed to show any proof thereof. Subsequently, the medical drugs, with an estimated value of Php 25,000.00, were confiscated and properly inventoried. GINA TOMANDOC was brought to NBI office for further questioning. Cases for violation of RA 7394 (Consumers Act of 1991), RA 5921 (Pharmacy Law), and RA 2883 (Philippine Medical Act) will be filed after completion of the documentary and testimonial evidences.

body: A Filipino doctor who defrauded the US government of millions of dollars and fled to the Philippines was arrested by the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) during the weekend. The suspect was identified by NBI Officer-In-Charge Nonnatus Caesar R. Rojas as: ERIC UY CHAN, aka Eric Uy Garchitorena, 48, with last known address is No. 684 T. Mapua St., Manila, and a medical doctor. He is connected with the Armed Forces of the Philippines in Camp Aguinaldo, Quezon City as a Medical Corps Reservist with the rank of Lieutenant Colonel under the name Eric Chan Garchitorena. Chan is wanted to stand trial in the Superior Court of the State of California, county for Felony Complaint No. BA189685 and for Sentencing in the Superior Court for the County of Los Angeles, State of California for Information/Case No. YAO36536, both for Conspiracy to Commit a Crime, Grand Theft and Health Care Fraud or Presenting False Medical Claims by collecting/receiving payments from the California Medi-Cal Program amounting to more than US$3 million. Investigation conducted by the Foreign Liaison Division (FLD) headed by Atty. Claro C. De Castro Jr. disclosed that the case started sometime in 1996, suspect Chan and his co-conspirators Diadema and Chan Annielie Arcangel Ferrer operated Green Cross Medical Clinic located at Carson St., Carson, California although they did not possess any medical license in California and has no group provider number. In order for Medi-Cal to pay the cost of any service, bills must be submitted through a provider number issued to a licensed physician. Thus, they hired Dr. Hyun Hong Kim, a licensed physician to work with them and without her knowledge applied and received in her name a provider number. They then submitted claims for services that were not actually provided by using Dr. Kim’s provider number. A total of US$516,656.48 was paid by Medi-Cal to the bank account of Chan and company. After Dr. Kim discovered the unauthorized billing in her name, she left the medical clinic and notified the authorities to have her provider number deactivated. In March, 1997, suspects hired Dr. Saifuddin Saifee to work at their new Evergreene Medical Clinic also located at Carson, California using the same modus operandi and were able to obtain Medi-Cal provider number (00A452161) in the name of Dr. Saifee and were able to open a joint bank account in the name of Dr. Saifee and Ferrer. They purchased copies of Medi-Cal beneficiary identification cards, manufacture patient charts to make it appear that service had been provided and submit fraudulent claims to Medi-Cal without Dr. Saifee’s knowledge. Medi-Cal records showed that payments totaling US$1,695,252.10 were paid to Dr. Saifee’s provider number. In April, 1998, a Search Warrant was executed at Evergreene Medical Clinic and at Chan’s residence. Chan and his co-conspirators were arrested but posted bail afterwards. After being released from custody on bail, Chan continued his illegal activities and opened up again West Coast Intermed Management and hired again a licensed physician named Dr. Herman De Bardlabon and used his name again to obtain Medi-Cal provider number. Chan and his group persuaded Dr. De Bardlabon to order unnecessary medical diagnostic tests on patient who had been brought to the clinic to submit medical testing and to sign off on fabricated patient charts and the copied test results to make it appear he ordered the tests and analyzed the results. Ferrer, on the other hand, hired several medical assistant and directed them to fabricate patient charts for Medi-Cal beneficiaries who had never been treated. In December, 1999, a Search Warrant was served at the clinic and the residence of Chan. In January, 2000 a Search warrant was issued again against Chan but he was not apprehended and never appeared in Court while his co-accused Ferrer plead no contest to all the charges and was sentenced to five (5) years to state prison. Also in January, 2000 Judge Kathleen Kennedy-Powell of the Superior Court of Los Angeles, California issued a Warrant for the arrest of Chan. In February, 2003, Judge Jacqueline A. Connor of the Los Angeles Superior Court, California issued a No Bail Bench warrant against Chan for his failure to appear for sentencing in Felony complaint No. YAO036536. Both warrants remain valid and outstanding. The United States government requested the Philippines Department of Justice (DOJ) for the extradition of subject. The DOJ filed with RTC of Manila Branch 1 the Petition for Extradition with Case No. 0114185 against suspect Chan. On August 28, 2006 said Court issued a (No Bail) Warrant of Arrest and ordered the NBI-Foreign Liaison Division (FLD) to serve said warrant. After a series of investigation, he was traced to the Philippines. On February 11, 2012, FLD agents arrested him at the AFP after he attended a Saturday conference at Camp Crame.

title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: Four (4) illegal labor recruiters who promised to several women jobs as entertainers overseas were arrested by agents of the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) in Bulacan last week. The NBI identified the suspects as: MARCIAL RONQUILLO BERNARDO, of legal age, a resident of 126 Bgy. San Pablo, Hagonoy, Bulacan; MASAKAZI HIRATSUKA, in his 50s; NOBUHARU KOBATAKE, 67; and TEROO TSUDA, 48, all friends of Bernardo and from Tokyo, Japan. The complainants are Lovely Sanchez, of Sto. Nino, Marikina City, Diane V. Berna, of Vista Verde, Caloocan City, and nine (9) other young women mostly from Hagonoy and Malolos, Bulacan, as well as from Valenzuela City and Pampanga. According to investigation by the NBI-Anti-Human Trafficking Division (AHTRAD), on July 29, 2013, it received a complaint from Diane V. Bernal and companion that suspect Bernardo has been recruiting models and other entertainers bound for Malaysia and Japan. When they went to Bernardo’s residence in Hagonoy, Bulacan on July 25, 2012, to audition, they were asked to come back on July 30, 2013. He said his Japanese friends who would want to see them and choose who would be sent to Japan for employment hasn’t arrived. There other women who were apparently being recruited for the same job. The complainants doubted Bernardo’s capability to send them abroad as he has no office to show and just holds audition for talents at his house in Hagonoy, Bulacan. Verification made with the Philippine Overseas Employment Administration (POEA) disclosed that Bernardo is not licensed to recruit nor deploy workers/talents abroad. This prompted the victims to seek NBI assistance. Upon receipt of the complaint on July 29, 2013, an entrapment was planned the following day. In the afternoon of the same date, NBI – AHTRAD operatives went to Bernardo’s residence in Hagonoy, Bulacan. The complainants went ahead of the arresting team to see Bernardo. At around 5 P.M., one of the complainants texted the team leader of the NBI – AHTRAD informing of their presence in Bernardo’s residence. When the NBI agents arrived, they confronted Bernardo, who was at that time interviewing some of the women applicants. He was informed that he was illegally recruiting overseas workers having no license to do so. Subsequently, he was placed under arrest together with the three (3) Japanese nationals who were with him. They were brought to the NBI office for booking and detention. There were at least ten (10) other women who were being recruited by Bernardo and the said three (3) Japanese nationals at the time of the raid. During the cursory search conducted, pictures of applicants, employment contract, passports and schedule of payments to Bernardo were found. On July 31, 2013, charges for violation of Section 6 of R.A. 8042 otherwise known as the Migrant Workers and Overseas Filipinos Act of 1995, as amended were filed before Inquest Prosecutor of the Department of Justice.

title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: PRESS STATEMENT August 16, 2022 NBI ARRESTS ONE FOR FRAUD The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today announced the arrest of a certain ALDRIN OLETA y BALDOVINO by operatives of NBI – Anti-Fraud Division (NBI-AFD) in an entrapment operation in Ermita, Manila for Swindling (Estafa) and violation of R.A. 8799 or the “Securities Regulation Code.” The operation stemmed from a complaint filed by the victim of Subject Oleta, who averred that he was enticed to invest in the latter’s supposed piggery business for an initial investment of P72,000.00 as pay-in for ten (10) heads of pigs, and with earnings of P28,000.00 after three (3) months. However, before the supposed meet-up with Subject Oleta, complainant discovered that the said piggery investment business was a fraud because Subject Oleta has consistently failed to release the supposed profits to other investors and that the piggery business is non-existent. Despite this, Subject Oleta has been constantly demanding payment of investment from target investors that prompted complainant to report to NBI. Further investigation by the NBI-AFD revealed that Subject Oleta was also the Subject of the same investment scheme which defrauded other victims of more than P11Million. On August 11, 2022, Subject Oleta was arrested by NBI-AFD operatives in an entrapment operation and was presented for Inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor of Manila.

Tovera, Chief of the AOTCD-AIDU, cited that the conduct of the operation on August 29, 2015, was based on the service of a Search Warrant in Barangay Inchican, Silang, Cavite. Tovera said when the AOTCD-AIDU operatives swooped down on the target area, the Korean nationals were caught in the act of committing violations of R.A 10175 (Cyber Crime Act of 2012) in relation to PD 1602 (Anti-illegal Gambling Act). body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today announced the arrest of a local businessman on April 30, 2020 in Paranaque City. NBI Officer-In-Charge Eric B. Distor identified the subject as ROLANDO RAPISURA, JR., y CASTOR, who was arrested in an entrapment operation by Agents of the NBI-International Airport Investigation Division (NBI-IAID) for violations of R.A. 11469 or the Bayanihan to Heal as One Act and R.A. 7394 otherwise known as the Consumer Act of the Philippines. OIC Distor said the case stemmed when operatives of NBI-IAID purchased 2-one liter bottle of Family Care rubbing alcohol from a store in Paranaque City, which purports to be 75% Isopropyl alcohol. Distor said that on this basis, the NBI forwarded a sample to the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) with a request for determination of its isopropyl content. Distor said the NBI-IAID then hatched an entrapment operation that resulted in the arrest of the subject on April 30, 2020, right inside the store while in the act of receiving the P75,000.00 marked money in exchange for ordered bottles of alcohol. Subject ROLANDO RAPISURA was presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor of Paranaque City.

title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today announced the arrest of three (3) individuals for Robbery Extortion in Calinog, Iloilo by operatives of NBI-Western Visayas Regional Office (NBI-WEVRO). NBI Officer-In-Charge (OIC) Director Eric B. Distor identified the subjects as OLIVER ESTROPE Y HINGCO, MIKE ESTROPE Y HINGCO, and NIÑO DIOMAR MIRANDA y BARRIOS. OIC Director Distor said that the operation stemmed from a complaint filed before the NBI-WEVRO by an owner/operator of a quarrying operation in Barangay Lonoy, Calinog, Iloilo, which was granted permit by the Office of the Governor of Iloilo. The complainant alleged that sometime in March 2021, subjects put up barricades of woods, planks, and branches on the roads where complainant’s dump trucks and heavy equipment would pass. The three (3) subjects claimed that they are the legal owners of the bed and bank of the river where the dump trucks and heavy equipment passed-by and demanded Php 1,000.00 as fee for the “right of way” for each truck to gain entry and Php 300.00 for every truckload of extracted material they will remove and carry from their quarry site. The subjects also threatened the complainant and his workers with physical violence and will create damage to complainant’s quarry business should they refuse to give the demanded amount. Out of fear for their personal safety and not to hamper their operations, complainant caved-in to the demand of the subjects on several ocassions from March 28 to April 26, 2021. Aggrieved, the complainant was compelled to file a complaint before the NBI-WEVRO. An NBI-WEVRO informant proceeded to the area of operation of the complainant to validate the complaint where he saw firsthand the extortion activities of the subjects. Subject Oliver Estope sent text messages to the complainant and demanded P150,000.00 as full payment for the fee of truck load of extracted materials which he asserted that the complainant failed to pay since March 25, 2021. Thus, on May 10, 2021, NBI-WEVRO operatives hatched an entrapment operation and strategically positioned near the area where the demanded money will be handed over by the complainant. Subject Oliver Estrope arrived with four (4) persons. Upon handing over the marked-money, NBI-WEVRO Agents immediately arrested Subject Oliver Estrope and his 4 companions. Two of his companions were later identified as senior citizens and gave statement that they were just invited by subject Oliver Estrope because he has something to arrange with the complainant. They were allowed to stay with a promise that they will cooperate in the investigation. The NBI-WEVRO said that the claims of the subjects that they owned the far side of the river, the bed and the river bank is misplaced and has no sufficient basis in fact and in law. The 3 other subjects were brought to the NBI-WEVRO and booked per standard operating procedure. The next day, Subjects were presented for Inquest Proceedings before the Iloilo Provincial Prosecutor’s Office for Robbery Extortion punishable under Article 294 of the Revised Penal Code, as amended in relation to Cybercrime Law.

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) issued today a stern warning to motorists who continue to display the NBI 75th anniversary commemorative plates in their vehicles which have expired in April this year. In a statement released, the NBI said that the Department of Transportation and Communication (DOTC) in a letter dated June 8, 2012 disapproved a previous request to extend the validity period of the two (2) plates issued by the NBI on the occasion of its 75th anniversary in November last year. The two (2) plates are: 1. “NBI @75” issued in November 2010 and expired on April 12, 2012. 2. “NBI (with 75th anniversary logo)” plate which expired on April. The NBI strongly advises all motorists whose vehicle still sport said plates to immediately remove them from their cars to avoid getting entangled with authorities. Vehicle owners who refuse to dismantle these expired commemorative plates face criminal liability.

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today said operatives of NBI-Eastern Visayas Regional Office (NBI-EVRO) have arrested two (2) individuals in Tacloban City on January 17, 2022 for transporting banned species of illegally cut lumber known as “iron wood”. NBI Officer-In-Charge (OIC) Director Eric B. Distor identified the subjects as CLYDE REY BALAAN and ELWARD LOMONGCAN. Director Distor said that the operation stemmed from an information received by NBI-EVRO regarding a possible violation of PD 705 otherwise known as the Forestry Reform Code of the Philippines. According to the information received by the NBI, one CLYDE REY BALAAN, a Barangay Councilor and resident of Lianga, Surigao del Sur, is transporting banned species of illegally cut lumber “iron wood” or “magkuno”. The logs are allegedly coming from the island of Mindanao on board a twenty-footer wing van/truck using the Port of San Ricardo as the point of entry. Logs are allegedly distributed in the municipality of Bato, Leyte and Maasin City, Southern Leyte. An NBI-EVRO operative, using an alias, was able to talk with the Subject and gathered additional information such as the sizes of the logs, its corresponding prices as well as names of previous customers and locations of the delivery. After which, NBI-EVRO operatives, together with DENR Region VIII, conducted an entrapment operation and successfully arrested Subject CLYDE REY BALAAN and the truck driver ELWARD LOMONGCAN. Seized from the Subjects were Php 900,000.00 marked money, one (1) unit wing van, twelve (12) wheeler truck and thirteen (13) pieces “magkuno/iron wood” lumbers. The wing van and the thirteen (13) pieces “magkuno/iron wood” lumbers were turned over to DENR-PENRO, Palo, Leyte pending necessary documentation. Subjects CLYDE REY BALAAN and ELWARD LOMONGCAN were presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor, Tacloban City for violation of PD 705 (Forestry Reform Code of the Philippines).

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today said operatives of Death Investigation Division (NBI-DID) arrested JOHN JOMEL SIASON y MALIWAT on January 11, 2017 in Balintawak, Quezon City, for the crime of Rape. Atty. Jose Justo S. Yap, NBI Deputy Director for Investigative Service, disclosed that the aforesaid case arose from the complaint of a sister-in-law of the Subject JOHN JOMEL SIASON for having carnal knowledge with her against her will by means of force and intimidation, on January 15, 2011 in Caloocan City. He is presently detained at the NBI Jail pending order from the court of jurisdiction for his transfer to the regular jail.

title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: A returning overseas Filipino worker from the United Arab Emirate and her brother-inlaw were arrested for allegedly kidnapping the 5-year-old daughter of her lover, by operatives of the National Bureau of Investigation in Valenzuela City last week. The suspects were identified as: MYRA SUBA-MAGALANG y MACASPAC, 28, married, a caregiver in the UAE and a resident of Bible St., Simeon Doon Compound, Karuhatan, Valenzuela City; and ANGELITO CEDENO MAGALANG, her brother-in-law and residing at the same address. Investigation conducted disclosed that Myra and the complainant, Kerwin M. Escanilla became sweethearts through the internet Facebook. On January 10, 2013, suspect Myra arrived from the UAE. The next day, Myra and Kerwin met, and on January 13, Kerwin introduced Myra to his two kids and parents. Myra invited and took Kerwin’s 5-year-old daughter to spend the night at her house in Valenzuela City. He consented out of trust. The following morning, Kerwin and Myra had a misunderstanding regarding the latter’s relationship with an ex-boyfriend. Kerwin demanded that Myra return his daughter but she refused unless the former pay her back P3,000 as payment for expenses incurred in treating him and his family for foods and drinks. Thereafter, she threatened Kerwin to pay her or he will not see his daughter again. She scheduled a meeting with him on January 15, 2013 at the public market of Karuhatan, Valenzuela City. This prompted Kerwin to seek NBI assistance. An entrapment was planned. On the appointed date and time Kerwin, accompanied by NBI agents proceeded to the designated meeting place. NBI operatives were posted nearby. After an hour, Myra arrived on board a motorcycle driven by Angelito with Kerwin’s daughter. Kerwin gave the demanded amount to Myra. After giving the signal, NBI agents approached, introduced themselves and arrested suspects. Charges for Kidnapping and Failure to Return a Minor under Art. 270 of the Revised Penal Code were filed before the Valenzuela City Prosecutor’s Office against the suspects who are presently detained at the NBI.

The suspects were identified as: MYRA SUBA-MAGALANG y MACASPAC, 28, married, a caregiver in the UAE and a resident of Bible St., Simeon Doon Compound, Karuhatan, Valenzuela City; and ANGELITO CEDENO MAGALANG, her brother-in-law and residing at the same address. Investigation conducted disclosed that Myra and the complainant, Kerwin M. Escanilla became sweethearts through the internet Facebook. On January 10, 2013, suspect Myra arrived from the UAE. The next day, Myra and Kerwin met, and on January 13, Kerwin introduced Myra to his two kids and parents. Myra invited and took Kerwin’s 5-year-old daughter to spend the night at her house in Valenzuela City. He consented out of trust. The following morning, Kerwin and Myra had a misunderstanding regarding the latter’s relationship with an ex-boyfriend. Kerwin demanded that Myra return his daughter but she refused unless the former pay her back P3,000 as payment for expenses incurred in treating him and his family for foods and drinks. Thereafter, she threatened Kerwin to pay her or he will not see his daughter again. She scheduled a meeting with him on January 15, 2013 at the public market of Karuhatan, Valenzuela City. This prompted Kerwin to seek NBI assistance. An entrapment was planned. On the appointed date and time Kerwin, accompanied by NBI agents proceeded to the designated meeting place. NBI operatives were posted nearby. After an hour, Myra arrived on board a motorcycle driven by Angelito with Kerwin’s daughter. Kerwin gave the demanded amount to Myra. After giving the signal, NBI agents approached, introduced themselves and arrested suspects. Charges for Kidnapping and Failure to Return a Minor under Art. 270 of the Revised Penal Code were filed before the Valenzuela City Prosecutor’s Office against the suspects who are presently detained at the NBI.

body: PRESS STATEMENT October 14, 2022 NBI ARRESTS FIVE FOR CHILD SEXUAL EXPLOITATION, RESCUES SEVEN MINORS In line with the relentless efforts of the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) against child sexual exploitation, operatives of NBI-Anti Violence Against Women and Children Division (NBI-AVAWCD) arrested five individuals engaged in selling child sexual exploitation materials. Subjects were arrested in an operation which stemmed from an information received regarding a certain individual who had been offering and selling child sexual abuse or exploitation materials (CSAEM) to foreign individuals. According to the information received, an American citizen named CHARLES WHEAT was arrested in the U.S. for possession, production, and distribution of CSAEM. He admitted that he was receiving CSAEM from SYRRA who was allegedly abusing prepubescent children in the Philippines. Investigation conducted by NBI-AVAWCD confirmed that Subject indeed offers CSAEM to foreign individuals in exchange for a fee. With these, AVAWCD operatives hatched an entrapment and rescue operation. The poseur-client was able to communicate with Subject thru Facebook Messenger where Subject sent CSAEM to the former. She even agreed to have a video call with the poseur-client to show the minor victims for sexual exploitation. On October 6, 2022, armed with a Warrant to Search, Seize and Examine Computer Data (WSSECD) and in cooperation with the Inter-Agency Council Against Trafficking in Persons (IACAT), HSI Transnational Crime Investigative Unit (HSI-TCIU), and City Social Welfare and Development (CSWD) of Pampanga, NBI-AVAWCD operatives, together with NBI-Digital Forensic Laboratory (NBI-DFL) agents, proceeded to the residence of the Subject in Pampanga. As agreed upon, Subject called the poseur-client via Messenger video call showing that she was with the two (2) minor victims. Upon confirmation that Subject was with minor victims, operatives immediately proceeded to Subject’s house resulting in the arrest of five (5) individuals. The operation also resulted in the rescue of seven (7) minor victims, the youngest of whom is eight (8) months old. Based on the on-site examination of the DFL, it was confirmed that SYRRA is indeed engaged in distribution of CSAEM. Arrested Subjects were charged with violations of RA 11930 or the (Anti-Online Sexual Abuse or Exploitation of Children (OSAEC) and Anti-Child Sexual Abuse or Exploitation Materials (CSAEM) Act; RA 9208 or the Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2003, as amended by RA 11862 or the Expanded Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2022; and RA 7610 or the Special Protection of Children Against Abuse, Exploitation and Discrimination Act, all of which are in relation to Section 6 of RA 10175 or the Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012. Notably, this case was initially worked on during the Advanced Investigative Workshop (AIW), a training and casework event led by the International Justice Mission (IJM) held throughout the month of September 2022. The workshop was attended by different law enforcement officers in the country who work with other professionals from foreign law enforcement organizations specializing in OSAEC work. The training focuses on the application of skills learned from the training to real cases in collaborative casework environment. The first session was hosted by IJM, the Australian Federal Police, and the National Police of the Netherlands. The second session, during which the case was worked on, was hosted by the United States Homeland Security Investigations (HIS) and IJM.

body: PRESS STATEMENT March 30, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } NBI ARRESTS TWO IN PASAY FOR P200K PASSPORT RANSOM EXTORTION PASAY CITY, Philippines – On March 26, 2026, the National Bureau of Investigation-Special Action Unit (NBI-SAU) arrested two individuals in an entrapment operation following reports of extortion and grave coercion involving a foreign national’s travel documents. The operation was launched after a complainant alleged that the Subjects were unlawfully withholding his Indian passport as collateral for a loan. According to the Complainant, the Subjects demanded Php 200,000 for the return of his passport. The Complainant reported a pattern of harassment characterized by continuous threats sent via digital platforms. The Subjects allegedly intimidated the Complainant by threatening to destroy his passport and further pressured him by claiming they would report his expired visa status to immigration authorities to compel the payment of the demanded amount. Upon validating the complaint, NBI-SAU operatives hatched an entrapment operation at a designated meeting point in a mall in Pasay City. Undercover agents observed the transaction and moved in to effect the arrest immediately after the marked money was handed over. The Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor – Pasay City, facing charges for violation of Article 286 (Grave Coercion) of the Revised Penal Code, in relation to Section 6 of Republic Act No. 10175, otherwise known as the Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012. This successful operation is a clear indication of the NBI’s proactive and intensified efforts to combat all forms of criminality across the nation,” NBI Director Atty. Melvin A. Matibag stated. “We reassure the public of our unwavering commitment to safeguarding the community from unscrupulous individuals. Our mission remains to foster a safer environment for all citizens and foreign nationals alike. #NBIServes

Upon handing over of the marked money, Subject Lagman in return, gave the Court Order containing the dismissal of the case in favor of the defendant. At this juncture, NBI-CCD operatives immediately entered the court staff room and arrested Subject Lagman.

body: PRESS STATEMENT January 03, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI), under the leadership of its Director, Judge Jaime B. Santiago (Ret.), arrested DIAHN SANCHEZ DAGOHOY (DIANE), BOLKISAH BALT DATADACULA, ALEJANDRO BARCENA LORINO JR., RONALD, JOESPH CATUNAO, LEOMER ABON and TITA NATIVIDAD for Syndicated Estafa and violation of Article 177 (Usarpation of Authority or Official Functions) of the RPC. Santiago said that on January 02, 2025, a complaint was filed before the office of the Special Task Force (STF) and Cybercrime Division (CCD), alleging that on December 29, 2024, a certain Diane contacted the complainant and offered him a seat as a member of the Bangsamoro (BARRM) Parliament. Accordingly, the position was offered for an amount of eight million pesos (Php 8,000,000.00). Complainant played along to make it appear that he was interested. After a series of conversation, Complainant and Subject Diane came to an agreement for the appointment of the former’s son and nephew in the BARMM parliament with a corresponding fee of Fifteen Million Pesos (P 15,000,000.00). Subject Diane assured the Complainant of two positions (seat) that will be reserved for and will be arranged by no less than the First Lady. Subject further claimed that successful appointees will be taking their oath of office by January 3, 2025. A meeting was set between the Complainant and the group on January 2, 2025 at the Manila Hotel. Acting on the information, STF and CCD immediately hatched a joint entrapment operation. Subjects were arrested after they received the marked money and misrepresented themselves as employees of the Office of the President. Certification issued by the Office of the President (OP) confirmed that the above mentioned Subjects are not their employees nor in any way connected with the Palace. Director Santiago commended the operatives of STF and CCD for their swift action on the matter and emphasized that no way that the government positions are for sale.

body: PRESS STATEMENT July 28, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } The National Bureau of Investigation-Technical Intelligence Division (NBI-TID), under the supervision of NBI Director Judge Jaime B. Santiago (Ret.), arrested the individual who, in a road rage incident, claimed to belong to the NBI. The operation stemmed from a report pertaining to a road rage incident, where a motorcycle driver sought the assistance of the program “Raffy Tulfo in Action”. Complainant appeared in Senator Tulfo’s program, complaining about one “PAUL JOHN C. JIMENEZ”. The CCTV footage showed that Paul John Jimenez was the driver of a black SUV, while complainant was riding a motorcycle. In the video, the black SUV later turned on its emergency flashers, trying to avoid the motorcycle rider. Jimenez’s SUV then rammed the motorcycle and its rider and tried to escape the scene. According to the complainant, Jimenez showed an NBI Badge on several occasions. He claimed to be a member of the NBI and allegedly threatened Complainant’s life. Per verification of NBI records, PAUL JOHN JIMENEZ is not in any way connected with the NBI, either as employee, job order worker or consultant. This fact was also mentioned by Senator Tulfo in his program. A confidential informant, who personally knows the Subject, said that the real name of JIMENEZ is JAY AR CABANA and is currently residing in a condominium in Quezon City. Record check on the Subject disclosed that Subject has a standing Warrant of Arrest for Syndicated Estafa with No Bail Recommended issued by the RTC Branch 55, Lucena, Quezon. Thus, on July 24, 2025, NBI-TID agents proceeded to the known residence of CABANA where they served the Warrant of Arrest. During the conduct of the arrest, several IDs were found in the immediate vicinity of Subject, all bearing the name PAUL JOHN JIMENEZ and JAY AR CABANA with photographs of CABANA including a fake NBI ID and NBI Wallet Badge. Subject CABANA was informed of his rights, and his counsel was informed of his arrest through telephone call. He likewise underwent the Bureau’s standard booking procedure. Subject CABANA was thereafter transferred to the NBI Detention Facility in the Bureau of Corrections in Muntinlupa. Return of the warrant was made with the issuing court. Also, for representing himself to belong to the NBI and carrying fake NBI ID and badge, CABANA is recommended to be prosecuted for violation of Art.177 of the Revised Penal Code (Usurpation of Authority), Art. 179 of the Revised Penal Code (Illegal Use of Insignia) and Sec. 3 of CA 142 (Anti-alias Law). Director Santiago commended the agents of NBI-TID for the successful arrest of JIMENEZ aka CABANA, and warns individuals who are misrepresenting themselves as NBI Personnel that they shall be dealt with accordingly. He further emphasized that the NBI does not practice any form of harassment, maltreatment or abuse of power towards the public.

body: PRESS STATEMENT April 18, 2022 NBI NEUTRALIZES LEADER IN AMBUSH-KILLING OF 7 PDEA AGENTS Agents of the National Bureau of Investigation have neutralized the leader in the ambush-killing of seven (7) Philippine Drug Enforcement Agency (PDEA) Agents in Barangay Malna, Kapai, Lanao Del Sur last October 2018. NBI OIC-Director ERIC B. DISTOR identified the subject as WILLIAM GANDAWALI COMAYOG, incumbent Barangay Chairman of Inudaran, Tagoloan II, also former Municipal Mayor of Tagolan II, Lanao Del Sur. At about 3 o’clock in the afternoon on April 13, 2022, joint operatives of the NBI-Iligan District Office (NBI-ILDO) led by Atty. Abdul Jamal Dimaporo, and government forces from PDEU/SOG LDSPPO and Special Action Force (SAF) implemented the service of Warrant of Arrest against subject WILLIAM GANDAWALI COMAYOG in Pilintangan, Wao, Lanao Del Sur. However, while the government Agents were approaching the residence of the subject, they were fired upon using an M79 Grenade Launcher and M16 Rifle. An armed confrontation ensued that resulted in the neutralization of said subject and the wounding of Patrolman RASUL ASILUM on the side of the operating team during the firefight, which lasted for more than an hour. The subject was immediately rushed to Wao District Hospital for medical intervention but was declared dead on arrival by the attending Physician. Patrolman RASUL ASILUM was given medical assistance and was declared out of danger. The Operating Team was able to recover a cache of high powered firearms and ammunitions. DISTOR stressed that subject COMAYOG has an Outstanding Warrant of Arrest for Violation of Section 28 (a) of R.A. 10591 issued by the RTC Branch 10 of Marawi City on February 2019. Moreover, subject COMAYOG was the leader of the GANDAWALI Group which was involved in the illegal drug activities and the Mastermind in the ambush-killing of 7 Agents of PDEA in October 2018. He was the brother of MACAPAGAL COMAYOG who was on the Government’s drug watch list and who was killed in a buy-bust operation in Marawi City. OIC-Director DISTOR has directed his Agents to conduct follow-up operations to apprehend the cohorts of subject COMAYOG who are involved in the ambush-killing of 7 PDEA Agents as he emphasized that the NBI will not stop until they are brought to justice to answer for their crimes.

body: The Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP) has extended its appreciation to the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) for the latter’s assistance it has extended relative to the BSP’s request to investigate complaints coming from BSP-Supervised Financial Institutions regarding rampant cyber-attacks, particularly phishing activities, perpetuated by cybercriminals during the Enhanced Community Quarantine. Benjamin E. Diokno, Governor of BSP, commended the NBI particularly the Bureau’s Cybercrime Division (CCD) for the fervent and unwavering effort to stamp out online bank frauds. The commendation came after the arrest of Jayson N. Dela Cruz and Kevin L. Marmolejo on April 14, 2020 in Novaliches, Quezon Cityby operatives of NBI-CCD for alleged text-messaging scams, phishing activities, and online bank fraud with the use of illegally procured access devices (Automated Teller Machine cards) belonging to third persons. The two were charged with violation of RA 8484 (Access Devices Regulation Act of 1998). On April 22, 2020, operatives of NBI-CCD arrested Justin B. Claveria in Lemery, Batangas. Justin is allegedly a top-level computer hacker involved in cybercriminal activities for the last two (2) years. He is suspected to be the mastermind of the cybercriminal activities and is responsible for developing or purchasing computer applications, software, and tools to be used for stealing depositors’ bank account information. The NBI charged him with violation of RA 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012) and RA 11469 (Bayanihan to Heal as One Act of 2020). According to Mr. Diokno, the recent arrest of the said cybercriminals delivered a big blow to the proliferation of online bank fraud in the country, especially during this Covid-19 crisis. As many more cybercriminals are out there preying on suspecting public, Mr. Diokno is requesting the NBI to continually intensify its operations and investigation against suspected computer hackers who specialize in online bank fraud and victimize the depositing public of their hard-earned money. The BSP on its part, is committed to collaborate with the NBI as it continue to fight against cybercriminals.
