body: In line with the government’s campaign against overpricing of medical supplies in this time of crisis, the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) arrested five (5) Subjects including a Chinese national in Caloocan and Quezon Cities on April 01 and 02, 2020, respectively. NBI Director Eric B. Distor identified the Subjects as JOHN DERICK DELA ROSA y TAPISPISAN, JOMEL TAPISPISAN Y MENDOZA, SARAH GRACE TAPISPISAN y SO, NATHANIEL PALINGKOD y PIEDAD and CHEN, TIAN MAN , a Chinese national, who are all involved in selling overpriced ethyl alcohol and non-contact thermal scanners. Director Distor said the first operation stemmed from an intelligence report received by NBI-Criminal Investigation Division (NBI-CRID) that a businessman from Valenzuela City is selling 100% alcohol in bulk or in drum amounting to Php37,500.00 the amount of which is more than the allowed selling price set by the DTI that is pegged at P25,000.00 per drum. After evaluating said report, Distor added, an entrapment operation was hatched by CRID operatives for the purchase of two (2) drums of 100% ethyl alcohol. Upon arrival of operatives at the meeting place at Mercury Drugstore Caloocan near the rotunda, transaction ensued that resulted in the arrest of the first 4 subjects. They were presented for inquest proceedings before the Caloocan City Prosecutor’s Office for violation of Sec. 5(2) of RA 7581 in relation to RA 10623 otherwise known as the “The Price Act of the Philippines” as penalized under Sec. 15 in relation to DTI Memorandum Circular No. 20-07 dated March 19, 2020 and violation of Article 52(b) of RA 7394 or the Consumer Act as penalized under Article 60 in relation to Article 14(7) of the Revised Penal Code. In the second operation, NBI Director said operatives of NBI-Environmental Crime Division (NBI-EnCD) arrested CHEN, TIAN MAN, a Chinese national, for alleged hoarding, profiteering, and price manipulation of medical supplies in Quezon City on April 2, 2020. Subject Chen was arrested for selling overpriced non-contact thermal scanners at Php4,400.00 per unit as against the DTI allowed price range of P599.00 – P3,400.00 per unit. The operation also resulted in the seizure of 1,000 pcs of thermal scanners with an estimated value of Php4.4 Million. Subject Chen was presented for inquest proceedings before the Quezon City Prosecutor’s Office for violations of Article 50(j) in relation to Article 60 of R.A. 7349, otherwise known as the “Consumer Act of the Philippines”, Section 5(2) of R.A. 7581 or “The Price Act of the Philippines”, and Section 6(c) of R.A. 11469 or the “Bayanihan to Heal as One Act.”

body: PRESS STATEMENT June 27, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI), under the leadership of NBI Director Judge Jaime B. Santiago (Ret.), arrested three (3) Filipinos identified as TEOTIMA G. BATUTAY, ROSE L. TORION, and MICHAEL D. CASTULO, and six (6) Indian nationals identified as SAJJAN SARKAR, SAI CHARAN, KULVATNH THATI, GAYATRI SARMA, RAY ANAND, and NITHIN KAMEPALLI in an entrapment operation in Paranaque City. The Subjects were arrested for Carnapping and Syndicated Estafa. The operation stemmed from a complaint filed against the Subjects for the recovery of Complainant’s vehicle, which was sold by the Subjects without his consent. Complainant disclosed that he failed to pay the monthly amortization of the subject vehicle to PSBank and offered it for “assume balance” (pasalo). The said vehicle was assumed by MCars, and passed it to Subject Batutay who allegedly sold the vehicle to Castulo. Castulo together with Sarkar, mortgaged it to Anand for Php120,000.00. PSBank ran after the Complainant after the amortizations fell due, but Complainant was not able to return the vehicle. Complainant was able to talk to Subject Castulo for the recovery of the vehicle, but he demanded Php450,000.00 from Complainant for its return; otherwise, Subject Castulo threatened Complainant that the car would be parted out (chop chop). Thus, Complainant was compelled to file a complaint before the NBI-NCR. Thereafter, an entrapment operation was hatched. Subject Castulo told Complainant to meet him at a casino hotel in Paranaque City on June 24, 2025 for the Php450,000 demand. During the meet-up, the money was reduced to Php250,000.00. NBI-NCR agents were able to apprehend the above-stated Subjects who are members of a syndicate involved in the “assume balance-talon” scheme. The operation also resulted in the recovery of Complainant’s vehicle. The arrested Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings for the above-mentioned violations. Director Santiago commended the agents of NBI-NCR for the successful operation, which resulted in the arrest of the Subjects and the recovery of the Complainant’s vehicle. Director Santiago likewise advises the public to be more cautious in their financial transactions to avoid falling prey to this scheme of unscrupulous individuals.

body: PRESS STATEMENT May 21, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } PRESS RELEASE | NBI NABS ONE FOR THEFT IN RIZAL The National Bureau of Investigation – Rizal District Office (NBI-RIZDO) on May 12, 2026, arrested a female individual for Qualified Theft in Tanay Rizal. The case stemmed from a complaint filed against the Subject by the President of the Crowne Pacer Development Corp. (CPDC). According to the complaint, Subject was hired as liaison officer for BIR, particularly in preparing their BIR submissions and paying their tax obligations, regularly. From August 2023 to March 2026, Subject billed them more than the amount to be paid, and worse there were some unpaid taxes and no-account document submissions. In March 2026, Subject again informed Complainant of their current tax obligation and informed her further that she had already advanced the tax payment to avoid penalties for late payment. She billed the Complainant Php289,391.01 and is constantly following up for the refund of the amount she purportedly advanced. Investigation disclosed that Subject made no payments for CPDC for that particular billing (Php289,391.01) for the month of March and or April 2026, as certified by the Bureau of Internal Revenue RDO46. Subject again contacted the Complainant and demanded for the payment of the amount she purportedly advanced as tax payments. NBI-RIZDO operatives immediately planned and implemented an entrapment operation at the office of the CPDC. Subject was arrested in-flagrante-de-licto after receiving the marked money and signing the voucher for the payment of the refund she was demanding. Subject was presented for inquest proceedings before the Provincial Prosecutors Office of Rizal for violation Article 310 (Qualified Theft) and Estafa under the Revised Penal Code.

body: PRESS STATEMENT March 31, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } The National Bureau of Investigation – Lucena District Office (NBI-LUCDO) under the guidance of NBI Director Judge JAIME B. SANTIAGO (Ret) successfully apprehended VICTORINO DIEZMO BORLONGAN, JR. on March 27, 2025, for allegedly committing repeated acts of Estafa (Swindling) under Article 315 of the Revised Penal Code. Subject Borlongan and his accomplice (live-in partner) misrepresented three parcels of land as unencumbered despite them being previously encumbered and sold to Prime Global Finance Corporation in December 2022 and June 2024. Subjects mortgaged the properties for Php10,000,000.00. When Subjects demanded an additional Php30,000.00 from Complainant, an entrapment operation was hatched. Subject Borlongan was arrested inside Complainant’s residence in Pagbilao, Quezon after Subject accepted the marked money. Subject’s live-in partner and co-accused in the complaint, was not present during the arrest. Both individuals are alleged to have concealed material facts about the land’s ownership to facilitate the fraudulent transaction. NBI-LUCDO is preparing the necessary documents for the filing of formal charges against the Subject before the Quezon Provincial Prosecutor’s Office. The case will be pursued under Article 315 of the Revised Penal Code (Estafa) and other pertinent laws. Director Santiago reiterates its commitment to combating fraud and upholding justice, he also urges the public to report similar crimes to its offices nationwide.

body: PRESS STATEMENT December 18, 2024 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } In line with the relentless efforts of the National Bureau of Investigation to prosecute subjects of human trafficking, four accused were recently convicted by Regional Trial Court Branch 86, Quezon City of Qualified Trafficking in Persons under Section 4 (k) in relation to Section 6 (a) of RA 9208 as amended by RA 10364. In March 2022, a plea from parents for the return of their then eight-month old baby trended online. Accordingly, the mother of the baby decided to sell her child to a person she met on Facebook through a group called “Bahay Ampunar’ because of online sabong debts. On March 3, 2022, the mother agreed to meet the person, later on found to be just a middleman, in a fast food chain in Quezon City and exchanged the baby for P45,000.00. An entrapment and rescue operations were conducted by operatives of Human Trafficking Division (HTRAD) which resulted to the rescue of the baby and the arrest of one Filipina and one Nigerian national in Sta. Cruz, Laguna. Likewise, the mother of the baby and the middleman were apprehended by virtue of a warrant of arrest in May 2022. Cases of Kidnapping under the Revised Penal Code, violation of RA 7610 or the Special Protection Against Children Abuse, Exploitation and Discrimination and violation of RA 9208 or the Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2003 were filed against Subjects. On 18 October 2024, Acting Presiding Judge of Regional Trial Court Branch 86 Quezon City found all accused GUILTY beyond reasonable doubt of Qualified Trafficking in Persons under Section 4 (k) in relation to Section 6 (a) of RA 9208 as amended by RA 10364 and sentenced them with LIFE IMPRISONMENT and fine of P2,000,000.00 each. In connection to this, last 29 November 2024, Hon. Mayor VICTOR MA REGIS N. SOTTO of Pasig City and City Social Welfare and Development Office-Pasig City headed by CSWDO Head MA. TERESA O. BRIONES awarded the key individuals responsible for the conviction of this case. Among them are the four NBI agents who were the arresting officers of this case for their commitment in ensuring the well-being and welfare of a Pasigueño child who was a victim of trafficking. Their consistent and truthful testimony was invaluable in securing justice not for the said child but also for victims of human trafficking everywhere. Said recognition happened during the 2024 Children’s Congress and State of the Children Address of Pasig City. Director JUDGE JAIME B. SANTIAGO (Ret.) said that the judgment rendered by the Regional Trial Court Branch 86 in Quezon City against all accused is a living testament of the resolute effort of the NBI to eradicate human trafficking in the country. Director SANTIAGO also said that the decision serves as a strong warning to those who are engaged in human trafficking, sexual exploitation and other crimes against women and children. He added that the decision inspires the Bureau’s operatives, particularly HTRAD agents who played a crucial role in the prosecution of the case.

Cruz, Laguna. Likewise, the mother of the baby and the middleman were apprehended by virtue of a warrant of arrest in May 2022. Cases of Kidnapping under the Revised Penal Code, violation of RA 7610 or the Special Protection Against Children Abuse, Exploitation and Discrimination and violation of RA 9208 or the Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2003 were filed against Subjects. On 18 October 2024, Acting Presiding Judge of Regional Trial Court Branch 86 Quezon City found all accused GUILTY beyond reasonable doubt of Qualified Trafficking in Persons under Section 4 (k) in relation to Section 6 (a) of RA 9208 as amended by RA 10364 and sentenced them with LIFE IMPRISONMENT and fine of P2,000,000.00 each. In connection to this, last 29 November 2024, Hon. Mayor VICTOR MA REGIS N. SOTTO of Pasig City and City Social Welfare and Development Office-Pasig City headed by CSWDO Head MA. TERESA O. BRIONES awarded the key individuals responsible for the conviction of this case. Among them are the four NBI agents who were the arresting officers of this case for their commitment in ensuring the well-being and welfare of a Pasigueño child who was a victim of trafficking. Their consistent and truthful testimony was invaluable in securing justice not for the said child but also for victims of human trafficking everywhere. Said recognition happened during the 2024 Children’s Congress and State of the Children Address of Pasig City. Director JUDGE JAIME B. SANTIAGO (Ret.) said that the judgment rendered by the Regional Trial Court Branch 86 in Quezon City against all accused is a living testament of the resolute effort of the NBI to eradicate human trafficking in the country. Director SANTIAGO also said that the decision serves as a strong warning to those who are engaged in human trafficking, sexual exploitation and other crimes against women and children. He added that the decision inspires the Bureau’s operatives, particularly HTRAD agents who played a crucial role in the prosecution of the case.

body: On August 2, 2021, operatives of NBI-Iligan District Office (NBI-ILDO) arrested OMAR DIMAPORO y ACA-AC and DAN JOHNSON PARTOS y PLANTO for selling illegal drugs in Marawi City. NBI-ILDO together with the Marawi City Police Office, conducted an antiillegal drug operation at Barangay East Basak, Marawi City which resulted to the immediate apprehension of Subject Dimaporo and his cohort Subject Partos. Confiscated items from Subject Dimaporo were one (1) Large Size Heat-sealed white rectangular transparent plastic sachet containing white crystalline substance suspected to be “shabu” weighing more or less 5 grams with an estimated street value of Php 34,000.00, one (1) Small Size Heat-sealed white rectangular transparent plastic sachet containing white crystalline substance suspected to be “shabu”, one (1) Large Size Heat-sealed white rectangular transparent plastic sachet containing shabu residue, Barangay ID, Disposable Lighter with Improvised Burner, Glass Totter, Disposable Lighters, Scissors, and Plastic Case containing empty small sachets. While, confiscated from Subject Partos were Thirty One (31) Size Heat-sealed white rectangular transparent plastic sachet containing white crystalline substance suspected to be “shabu” weighing more or less 6 grams with an estimated street value of Php 40,800.00, Voter’s ID, Glass Totter, Assorted Disposable Lighters, Assorted Empty Plastic Sachets, Assorted Rolled Foil, Small Plastic Box and Disposable Lighter with Improvised Burner. The subjects will be charged for violation of R.A. 9165, otherwise known as the “Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002”. On August 2, 2021, operatives of NBI-Cordillera Administrative Region (NBI-CAR) arrested MARIA JULIE ANN USON ESPILOY for selling falsified BIR TIN cards. Subejct was arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from the letter of Hon. Douglas A. Rufino, Regional Director, Bureau of Internal Revenue-CAR, Baguio City, seeking the assistance of the Bureau for the arrest of an online seller named JEN NE SIS, who is openly distributing BIR Tax Identification Numbers cards and offering services for Php 200 without any authority, as evidenced by a certification issued by the BIR. Acting on the said request and to verify the alleged illicit activity, NBI-CAR operatives, acting as poseur-client transacted with the Subject and ordered BIR TIN cards. The transaction was ten consummated. Hence, the poseur-client again ordered eleven (11) BIR TIN cards from the Subject in the amount of Php 2,200.00. An entrapment operation was then hatched resulting in arrest of the Subject. Subject was later on identified as MARIA JULIE ANN USON ESPILOY, who, according to BIR-CAR is not a registered taxpayer and has never been an employee of the BIR. The BIR TIN card recovered from the Subject bearing her name is likewise spurious. Subject is now detained at NBI-CAR detention cell, pending the inquest proceedings for violations of RA 9485 as amended by RA 11032 (Anti-Red Tape Act of 2007), NIRC Regulations, Usurpation of Authority, and Falsification of Public Documents. On August 3, 2021, operatives of NBI-Bohol District Office (NBI-BOHDO) Spouses CASIANO ORO y SEPADA and ANABEL ORO y VALENTOS for selling petroleum products without permit from the government. Subjects were arrested in an operation which stemmed from a report received by NBI-BOHDO that subject spouses are engaged in the illicit trade of Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG). Series of surveillance operations and confirmed that subject spouses are operating an unlicensed refilling and retailing of LPG, particularly Butane. The Department of Energy-Visayas Field Office has issued a Certification stating that subject spouses are not registered with them for the issuance of Standard Compliance Certificate for the refilling, retailing, distribution, and hauling of LPG. With these, the buy-bust operation was conducted resulting in the arrest of the Subjects. Subjects were presented for Inquest proceedings before the Provincial Prosecutor’s Office of Tagbilaran City for illegal trading of petroleum and/or petroleum products, prohibited and penalized under Sec 2(a) of P.D. 1865. On August 4, 2021, operatives of NBI-Olongapo District Office (NBI-OLDO) arrested JACKYLOU LASTIMADO, RAMIL ENTERNO, MONICA LABANDELO, and JESTHONY TELAN y GOMEZ for Human Trafficking in Olongapo City. Subjects were arrested two simultaneous operations which stemmed from an intelligence report provided by Destiny Rescue Filipinas regarding the human trafficking activities of a certain JACKYLOU LASTIMADO a.k.a. “JACKY” and MONICA CORUM a.k.a. “MONIC” in the City of Olongapo and nearby municipalities. According to the report both Subjects Lastimado and Corum acted as pimps to prospective clients by procuring, offering, promoting, facilitating or inducing minors specifically high school students and out of school youths by taking advantage of their vulnerability to engage in prostitution and other sexual activities in exchange for monetary consideration. After validating the report, 2 operations in different venues/hotels were planned by NBI-OLDO. Thus on the above-mentioned date, the simultaneous operations were conducted at the agreed meeting place in Subic Freeport Zone, Olongapo City resulting in the arrest of the Subjects. Subjects were presented for Inquest proceedings before the City Prosecutor’s Office of Olongapo City on August 5, 2021 for 5 counts of Human Trafficking under R.A. 9208 otherwise known as the AntiTrafficking in Persons Act of 2003 and 5 counts for violation of R.A. 7610 or the Special Protection of Children Against Abuse, Exploitation and Discrimination Act. On August 4, 2021, operatives of NBI-Environmental Crime Division (NBI-EnCD), together with NBI-Agusan Del Sur District Office (NBI-ADSDO), DENR-CARAGA, Local PNP, and AFP troops implemented the Search Warrants against subject shops which resulted in the seizure of Mangkono and Dipterocarps lumber and flitches, furniture souvenir, and novelty items worth Php 2,440,156.40. The operation stemmed from the letter from the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR) CARAGA Region XIII requesting assistance in the conduct of investigation regarding with the alleged illegal trading of Mangkono (Xanthostemon werdugonianus) finished items. Surveillance operation in twelve (12) open souvenir/furniture shops in San Agustin, Surgao Del Sur verified that the owners of the said shops are in possession and control of Mangkono lumber and flitches. Thus, on August 4, 2021, the operation was conducted resulting in the seizure of the aforementioned items. The NBI-EnCD is now preparing charges for violation of R.A. 9147 otherwise known as the Wildlife Resources Conservation and Protection Act. On August 4, 2021, operatives of NBI-Bayombong District Office (NBI-BAYDO) arrested KNIGHT BALISI CO and JOHNLERY PATRICIO ALLAREY for illegal selling of chainsaws and other cutting equipment in Bambang, Nueva Vizcaya. the case stemmed from an information received by NBI-BAYDO regarding several establishments in Bambang, Nueva Vizcaya that are involved in the sale and distribution of chainsaws and other cutting implements through electric and internal combustion engine without necessary permit. According to the information received, among the establishments involved are ALLMIGHTY INDUSTRIAL and KHAMI ENTERPRISES. NBI-BAYDO then validated the information and it was found out that the said establishments are indeed offering chainsaws and other cutting equipment for sale to the general public with price ranging from Php 7,000 to Php 60,000. Through a Certification issued by the Community Environment and Natural Resources Office (CENRO), ALLMIGHTY INDUSTRIAL and KHAMI ENTERPRISES were not issued authority or permit to sell and distribute the aforesaid cutting implements. With this, simultaneous entrapment operations were conducted on August 4, 2021 at ALLMIGHTY INDUSTRIAL located along the national highway of Bambang, Nueva Vizcaya and at KHAMI ENTERPRISES located at Almaguer North, Bambang Nueva Vizcaya resulting in the arrest of Subjects KNIGHT BALISI CO, sales representative of ALLMIGHTY INDUSTRIAL and JOHNLERY PATRICIO ALLAREY, sales representative/mechanic of KHAMI ENTERPRISES. The owner of the ALLMIGHTY INDUSTRIAL was identified as JETHRO CYRUS GAMBITO through his sales representative and through the DTI and business permit posted at the establishment. On the other hand, the proprietor of KHAMI ENTERPRISES is ANNALIZA DONATO, as disclosed by Subject ALLAREY. Seized were 2 sets of chainsaw worth P47,000.00. Charges for violation of RA 9175 (Chainsaw Act of 2002) were filed before the Office of the Provincial Prosecutor, Bayombong, Nueva Vizcaya against arrested Subjects KNIGHT BALISI CO and JOHNLERY PATRICIO ALLAREY as well as at-large business owners JETHRO CYRUS GAMBITO and ANNALIZA DONATO. On August 7, 2021, operatives of NBI-MIMAROPA seized 36 pieces of good lumber in Naujan, Oriental Mindoro. Unfortunately, Subjects were able to escape onboard a jeep. On August 9, 2021, operatives of NBI-Cagayan Valley Regional Office (NBI-CAVRO) arrested TESSIE PASCUA MANGABAT a.k.a. MINDA PLANTA VILLA and REBECCA MANDING ALLAYBAN for alleged Estafa and Falsification of Public Documents. the case stemmed from a complaint against the Subjects for alleged Estafa and Falsification of Documents. According to the complainant, Subjects duped him on entering a mortgage contract on two parcels of land under the name of a certain Dionisio Planta. Accordingly, Subject Mangabat represented herself as MINDA PLANTA VILLA, sister of Dionisio Planta. The latter was able to persuade the complainant to give a total amount of Php 460,000 for the mortgage. Later on, Subject offered for the sale of the said lots for a total amount of Php 800,000. Complainant accpeted the offer but even before he could give the remaining balance of Php 340,000, he received an information that Subject Minda is a fraudster which prompted him to file a complaint before NBI-CAVRO. When Subject demanded for the remaining amount, the entrapment operation was conducted resulting in the arrest of Subject Minda whose real identity is TESSIE PASCUA MANGABAT. The latter just pretended to be a sister of Dionisio, the registered owner of the lots. Mr. Dionisio Planta averred that the documents of his properties went missing from his filing cabinet after he accommodated Subject Tessie Mangabat to stay in his house for nine days. Arrested Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the City Prosecution Office and were temporarily detained at NBI-CAVRO Detention Facility. On August 11, 2021, operatives of NBI-Isabela District Office (NBI-ISDO) arrested NINA CARLOTA BAQUIRAN-MANSIBANG for Human Trafficking. Subject was arrested in an operation which stemmed from an intelligence report that Subject Nina is engaged in the illicit sex trade, offering young women for sexual services in exchange for a fee. Surveillance operation confirmed the information. Thus, on the above-mentioned date, NBI-ISDO operatives, together with the poseur-client, proceeded to Barangay Alibagu, Ilagan City to conduct the operation. Subject Nina arrived together with the 2 young ladies. One of the poseur-clients brought the ladies into their car and went back to Subject Nina to handover the entrapment money. As soon as the marked money was received by the subject, the rest of the operatives immediately approached the subject and placed her under arrest. The 2 young ladies rescued were turned-over to the Provincial Social Welfare and Development of Isabela. Subject was presented for inquest proceedings before the City Prosecutor of Ilagan City, Isabela for violation of R.A. 9208 as amended by R.A. 10364, otherwise known as “The Expanded Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act”. On August 12, 2021, operatives of NBI- International Airport Investigation Division (NBIIAID), together with NAIA- Inter- Agency Drug Interdiction Task Group (NAIA-IADITG), Philippine Drug Enforcement Agency (PDEA), PNP Aviation Security and Drug Enforcement Group, and Bureau of Customs (BOC), seized P3.031 Million worth of illegal drugs in Baguio City. The operation stemmed from the interception of a parcel by the Bureau of Customs at NAIA. Said parcel was declared as bed sheets and shoes but upon inspection the parcel in fact contains 1, 783 tablets of Ecstasy or Party Drugs with an estimated street value of more than P1,300,000.00 which was shipped by Fostina Obobo of Neuss, Germany and consigned to Joyce Annsan Antono of Rm. 101 Brisle Ridge Residences, Pacdal Rd., Baguio City. Thus, the NAIA-IADITG members proceeded to Baguio City for a controlled delivery operation. On August 11, 2021, consignee was expected to claim the subject parcel from Baguio Post Office, the NAIA-IADITG members positioned themselves near the area to arrest the claimant. Unfortunately, the consignee did not claim the parcel and gave information that she will claim the said parcel at her residence in Bristle Ridge Residences. The next day, the joint operatives proceeded and positioned themselves in front of Bristle Ridge Condominium. A few moments later, a woman who was later identified as Subject Millare went outside to claim the subject parcel. At this juncture, the joint operatives immediately approached Subject Millare and placed her under arrest. Mayor Benjamin Magalong of Baguio City went to see the arrested Subject and express appreciation to the joint operatives for the arrest of the Subject. Subject Millare was presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the Prosecutor, Baguio City for violation of Section 4 (Importation of Dangerous Drugs) of R.A. 9165. In addition, the consignee, JOYCE ANNSAN ANTONO a.k.a. JOYCE ANN SAN ANTONIO (at-large) was also included in the charge. On August 16, 2021, operatives of NBI- Special Task Force (NBI-STF) arrested JOHN PAUL GINETE ALINDOGAN with aliases “GLYBER ANTHONY ESPARTINEZ SIOSON”, “SY GUISSEPE ARMSTRONG CLAINGACION”, “RANDY PALACIO CRUZ”, and GUILLER RAYMOND ASIS REYES” in an entrapment operation in Antipolo City for violation of the Cybercrime Law. A complaint was filed by the victim of Subject Alindogan. According to the complainant, she met the Subject through Tinder. Subject Alindogan introduced himself as Guiller Raymond Asis Reyes, 37 years old, single, and a resident of Ayala Alabang and currently works at Germany as an oil rig manager. The complainant averred that the subject was very persistent and was always asking her to go out until the complainant gave in and met with him. The complainant added that they became lovers since May 2021, and claimed that the Subject enticed her to create an email account for her to organize and link all her credit cards and personal email account into one. The complainant agreed and the subject created an email account where he linked all the complainant’s credit cards and personal email account. During the duration of their relationship the complainant had no idea that Subject Alindogan was already stealing and syphoning her money from her credit card accounts and BDO bank account. To cover his illegal activities Subject Alindogan showered the complainant with false promises like to build a diagnostic center for her to run. Subject Alindogan was able to use the credit cards which he used in his unauthorized purchases and withdrawals amounting to Php 169,186.07. In addition to the unauthorized purchases and withdrawals by Subject Alindogan, the complainant also claimed that the Subject enticed her to invest in stocks and gave to the subject a total of Php 984,886.00 for the said investment in five different dates. Subject Alindogan and the complainant was supposed to meet but the subject never appeared. A day later, a certain Major Bernie texted the complainant informing her that Subject Alindogan was missing. The subject allegedly claimed that he was kidnapped but because of the inconsistencies to his claims the complainant did not believe his alibis and started to suspect the subject. The complainant checked her credit card and bank account and found the unauthorized transactions made by the subject. Thus, the complainant appeared before the NBI to file a complaint against the subject. The complainant also found that her jewelries amounting to Php 900,000.00 were also missing and only the subject knows where she was keeping the said jewelries. Subject Alindogan texted the complainant incessantly forcing her to fixed their relationship. The NBI-STF conducted cyber patrolling and verification against the subject and found that the subject is wanted for qualified theft. On August 16, 2021, the NBI-STF received a message from the complainant informing them that the subject suddenly appeared in the clinic where she works and forcing her to meet with him and believe his alibi that he was kidnapped. Operatives immediately proceeded to the clinic in Antipolo City to arrest the subject. Subject introduced himself to the operatives as GUILLER RAYMOND ASIS REYES. The operatives notice the resemblance of Reyes to the picture of the wanted individual named ALINDOGAN. The operatives asked for his identification card as proof and the subject presented his driver’s license under the name of ALINDOGAN JOHN PAUL GENETE. Thus, the NBI-STF operatives immediately placed the subject under arrest for using another name to conceal his true name. Subject Alindogan was presented before the Antipolo City Prosecutor’s Office for violation of Section 4(a)(1) of R.A. 10175 otherwise known as the “Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012; Article 172 in relation to Article 171 of the RPC (Falsification); Article 310 (Qualified Theft); Article 315 (Estafa); violation of C.A. 142, otherwise known as the “Anti-Alisa Law”; violation of R.A. 9262, otherwise known as the “Anti-Violence Against Women and Their Children Act of 2004”; and violation of R.A. 8484, otherwise known as “The Access Device Regulation Act”. On August 18, 2021, operatives of NBI- Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (NBI-BARMM) arrested BAI SOFIA S. TUAS for Human Trafficking. The case stemmed from an information received by the NBI-BARMM regarding the alleged proliferation of human trafficking activities in Cotabato City. Subsequently, NBI-BARMM conducted a verification and validation which revealed that alias “BEA” or alias “PIA” as one of the perpetrators. After two weeks, the NBI-BARMM was able to establish communication with alias PIA and come to an agreement that the subject will provide nine (9) female sex workers under the Subject’s ward for Php 5,000.00 each. When the poseurcustomer and the Subject agreed to meet, the entrapment operation was conducted together with representatives from the Ministry of Social Welfare and Development. The operation resulted in the arrest of Subject TUAS and the rescue of nine (9) trafficked victims. Subject Tuas was presented for Inquest proceedings before the City Prosecutor’s Office of Cotabato City for violation of R.A. 9208 as amended by R.A. 10364. On August 20, 2021, operatives of NBI-Task Force Against illegal Drugs (NBI-TFAID) seized repacked imported Chinese cigarettes with an estimated value of P1.35 Billion in Subic Bay Gateway Park (SBGP) in Subic Bay Freeport Zone (SBGP) in Olongapo, City, Zambales. The operation also resulted in the arrest two (2) Malaysian nationals namely TAN AH SENG and TAN YAN TENG. The case stemmed from information relayed to NBI-TFAID about a warehouse of BUMI JAYA owned by TAN AH SENG and his group who are allegedly involved in the illegal repacking of imported cigarettes from China and diverting it to domestic market. Investigation revealed that BUMI JAYA was incorporated on January 9, 2002. On November 18, 2015, Mr. Vincent Sauvalere, Head of Tobacco and Counterfeit Goods Unit of European Anti-Fraud Office requested the Bureau of Customs (BOC) to conduct investigation on BUMI JAYA in relation to smuggling of tobacco products into the European Union. BUMI JAYA became a licensed transshipper engaged in transshipping tobacco products to different countries on January 4, 2017. On August 17, 2021, informant submitted to NBI-TFAID the video footages and photos showing the repacking and placing of tax stamps on each pack of Chinese cigarettes inside BUMI JAYA warehouse, and further attests that the finished repacked cigarettes were transferred and stored to the second warehouse of BUMI JAYA also in SBFZ. The said acts by BUMI JAYA are in violation of Section 1423 (Removing or Repacking Goods in Warehouse) of RA 10863 (Customs Modernization and Tariff Act). With these, Search Warrants were issued by RTC Branch 97, Olongapo City, directing the TFAID to immediately search the premises of BUMI JAYA. On August 20, 2021, TFAID operatives implemented the Search Warrants which resulted in the seizure of repacked Chinese cigarettes, equipment used in repacking, repacking materials, and several BIR tax stamps. NBI-TFAID also seized 45,000 master boxes of assorted Chinese cigarettes with estimated value of Php 1,350,000,000. Workers of BUMI JAYA were also caught in flagrante repacking Chunghwa cigarettes. TAN AH SENG and TAN YAN TENG were then placed under arrest and were informed of their rights. Subjects TAN AH SENG and TAN YAN TENG were presented for inquest proceedings on August 23, 2021 before the Office of the City Prosecutor, Olongapo City for violation of Section 1423 of RA 10863. Incorporators of BUMI JAYA INTERNATIONAL CORP. namely: GINA TSAI, TAN LIAN HONG, ADELIA C. TAN, and CHI JUNG HSIAO aka CHI YIN HSIAO, all at large, were also charged with violation of Section 1423 of RA 10863 even though they are not present during the implementation of Search Warrants. Pursuing its investigation, NBI-TFAID will request the BIR to certify whether or not the seized tax stamps are counterfeit, in preparation for filing of additional charges against the incorporators/officers of BUMI JAYA for violation of National Internal Revenue Code. On August 25, 2021, operatives of NBI- Environmental Crime Division (NBI-EnCD) arrested RICHIE CINCOFLORES y GIMONGALA, ALLAN SEDUCO y ROSALES, and ROLLY OLAYAVAL y SELOS for violation of environmental laws. Based on the information received by the NBI, the above-named Subjects are occupying, dwelling, constructing, maintaining permanent structures within the Upper Marikina River Basin Protected Landscape covered under the National Integrated Protective Area System without the necessary permits. Surveillance operations conducted by the NBI- Environmental Crime Division (NBI-EnCD) confirmed such information. The criminal offenses by the Subjects were committed and is continually being committed in open view of the public. Thus, on August 25, 2021, NBIEnCD operatives conducted an operation that led to the arrest of the subjects and were presented for inquest proceedings before the Antipolo Prosecutor’s Office in Rizal for violation of Section 20 ( n) and (o) of R.A. 7686, otherwise known as the “National Integrated Protected Areas System (NIPAS) Act of 1992”, as amended by 11038 and Section 81 (formerly Section 71) of Presidential Decree No. 705, otherwise known as “The Revised Forestry Code of the Philippines”, as amended. Rufino, Regional Director, Bureau of Internal Revenue-CAR, Baguio City, seeking the assistance of the Bureau for the arrest of an online seller named JEN NE SIS, who is openly distributing BIR Tax Identification Numbers cards and offering services for Php 200 without any authority, as evidenced by a certification issued by the BIR. An entrapment operation was then hatched resulting in arrest of the Subject. Subject was later on identified as MARIA JULIE ANN USON ESPILOY, who, according to BIR-CAR is not a registered taxpayer and has never been an employee of the BIR. body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) lauds the conviction of an American national who was sentenced for life imprisonment by a Court in Angeles, Pampanga, for human trafficking. NBI Officer-In-Charge Eric B. Distor said that the judgment rendered by the Regional Trial Court – Branch 58 in Angeles City, Pampanga, against American national DAVID TIMOTHY DEAKIN is a living testament of the resolute effort of the NBI to eradicate human trafficking in the country. OIC Distor also said that the decision serves as a strong warning to those who are engaged in human trafficking, sexual exploitation and other crimes against children. He added that the decision inspires the Bureau’s operatives, particularly the Anti-Human Trafficking Division (AHTRAD) Agents who played a crucial role in the prosecution of the case. The case against David Timothy Deakin took more than two (2) years, following his arrest on February 27, 2017 by the operatives of the NBI-AHTRAD, at his two-storey residence in Sta. Maria I, Balibago, Angeles City. Two (2) minor victims were rescued in the operation. On March 26, 2018, Deakin was charged before the RTC of Angeles City for Qualified Trafficking in Persons under R.A. No. 9208, as amended by R.A. No. 10364, otherwise known as the Expanded Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2012. Subsequent to the arrest of Deakin, other human trafficking victims, including two (2) minors, likewise filed complaints against him. Three (3) other victims testified before the Court about their harrowing experience under Deakin’s hands. Records of the case showed that for a period of time, including January 2016 to September 2016, Deakin took advantage of the vulnerability of the victims, and unlawfully and knowingly recruited, offered and maintained them to and for foreign customers, for the purpose of pornography through the use of computers, and information and communication technology. Deakin required the victims to perform sexually explicit acts, such as naked shows, in front of web cameras. On May 26, 2020, the Court found Deakin guilty beyond reasonable doubt of the crime of Qualified Trafficking in Persons and was sentenced to life imprisonment and a fine of Two Million Pesos (P2,000,000.00). Deakin was also ordered to pay damages to his three (3) victims, amounting to P500,000.00 each for moral damages, and P100,000.00 each for exemplary damages.

The operation stemmed from a reliable informant regarding the alleged sale and distribution of “Tirzepatide,” a drug believed to be unregistered with the Food and Drug Administration (FDA), within the Manila area. The said product is being marketed and offered to individuals with weight-related conditions. Acting on the information, NBI-DDD agents conducted online surveillance, which revealed several social media pages offering the drug. A certificate issued by the FDA, at the request of the NBI, confirmed that the drug is unregistered. In response, a buy-bust operation was planned and conducted, resulting in the arrest of the subjects in the act of selling unregistered drugs. The operation also resulted in the seizure of Tirzepatide worth Php 310,000.00. No. 7394 (Consumer Act of the Philippines). NBI Director Atty. Melvin A. Matibag commended the NBI-DDD agents for their recent successful operation, which resulted in the apprehension of the subjects. He underscored the importance of exercising caution and vigilance when purchasing unregistered drugs, highlighting the potential health hazards and serious safety risks that such substances can cause. Furthermore, he reiterated the NBI’s unwavering commitment to intensifying its efforts in combating the proliferation of unregistered products, emphasizing the agency’s dedication to safeguarding public health and maintaining safety within the community.

body: PRESS STATEMENT November 27, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } The National Bureau of Investigation-Cybercrime Division (NBI-CCD) successfully dismantled a cyber-scamming operation in Parañaque City, leading to the arrest of Chinese national Li Zhenjie. Li was arrested for violating Section 4(b)(1) (Social Engineering Schemes) of Republic Act No. 12010, the “Anti-Financial Account Scamming Act,” in relation to Republic Act No. 10175, “The Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012.” The arrest was initiated following a report from a confidential informant concerning a sophisticated scam operating from a condominium unit in Parañaque City. The perpetrators were reportedly using spoofed contact numbers, impersonating agents of the New Haven Police Department in Connecticut, USA, and the FBI in Washington. They would demand victims in the United States transfer cryptocurrency, typically ranging from $3,000 to $5,000, to an account under the alias “GENERAL” in exchange for not issuing a fictitious nationwide online arrest warrant. NBI-CCD agents immediately sought a Warrant to Search, Seize, and Examine Computer Data (WSSECD) for the target condominium unit. The warrant was promptly granted by the Regional Trial Court (RTC) of Makati on November 20, 2025. On November 21, 2025, NBI-CCD agents, assisted by condominium security personnel, executed the warrant. The operation resulted in the seizure of devices containing critical social engineering scripts and the arrest of Subject Li. This successful execution marks a significant step in disrupting transnational cybercrime infrastructure and highlights the NBI’s effectiveness against sophisticated fraud schemes. OIC Director Atty. Angelito DLP Magno emphasized that this operation clearly demonstrates the NBI’s effective and unwavering commitment to combating cybercrime. He assured the public that the NBI remains relentless in pursuing these perpetrators and issued a strong warning: “The NBI will always be one step ahead of those who seek to exploit the public through cybercrime, reaffirming the agency’s dedication to public safety and cybercrime prevention.”

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today said operatives of the Anti-Human Trafficking Division (NBI-AHTRAD) have rescued 3 minors in an entrapment operation in Caloocan City and the arrest of three (3) individuals for human trafficking. In a Post Operation Report, the AHTRAD said the operation was hatched after their agents have confirmed the information that human trafficking of minors is taking place in Caloocan City. Surveillance information received from AHTRAD and Inter-Agency Council Against Trafficking (IACAT) operatives yielded positive results after they were able to initially transact with one a.k.a. YOLLY who was later identified as YOLANDA VILLAGOMEZ y SERRANO. Subject VILLAGOMEZ offered young ladies, who appear to be minors, to have sexual intercourse for a fee ranging from one thousand five hundred pesos (P1,500.00) to two thousand five hundred pesos (P2,500.00) for each girl depending on the quality of the minors. Subject VILLAGOMEZ even offered minors who are virgins for ten thousand pesos (P10,000.00) up to twenty thousand pesos (P20,000.00). In the operation that led to the rescue of 3 minors and arrest of Subject VILLAGOMEZ, IACAT and AHTRAD operatives acted as poseur customers who were made to select young girls inside a restaurant, the operatives ended up choosing minor-victims. After handing the marked money to Subject VILLAGOMEZ as payment for the sexual services, they were directed to proceed to a hotel in Caloocan City. In the course of operation, the 3 trafficked victims, who were rescued inside the hotel, admitted that the nature of their work is to give sexual favors to customers being brought to them by Subjects. In their Sworn Statement, the victims admitted that they are sex workers that Manahan and Dela Pena were responsible for offering them to pimps like VILLAGOMEZ, who in turn, looked for clients. Of the money received from clients, Subject VILLAGOMEZ receives P500.00 per client while Manahan and Dela Pena receives P100.00 per client. body: PRESS STATEMENT July 07, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } On July 03, 2025, the National Bureau of Investigation-National Capital Region (NBI-NCR), under the leadership of Director Judge Jaime B. Santiago (Ret.), arrested VINCENT G. SULIMA, CHRISTIAN F. LAO, JOHN REY E. PETALLAR, RENZ JOEL R. PENSON and MERCY T. VILLON in an entrapment operation in Sta. Cruz, Manila. The case stemmed from an intelligence report received by NBI-NCR regarding illegal distribution and online sale of vape products by a certain VINCENT SULIMA, operating from 1753 Felix Huertas Road, Sta. Cruz, Manila. The suspect was reportedly using social media platforms, including facebook.com/port2pasok, to market unregistered vape products in violation of Republic Act No. 11900 (Vaporized Nicotine and Non-Nicotine Products Regulation Act). The NCR Team conducted surveillance at the subject’s location. During the surveillance, agents successfully conducted a test-buy and purchased three vape products, which were later verified by the Department of Trade and Industry (DTI) to be unregistered. The team also documented the premises and formally sought the DTI’s assistance through a letter sent on the same date. On June 27, 2025, Agent on Case also conducted a separate online test-buy through the suspect’s Facebook account, acquiring additional products labeled “Haze”, “Astra”, and “Black Market”. On July 03, 2025, in coordination with the Department of Trade and Industry-Office for the Special Mandate on Vaporized Nicotine and Non-Nicotine Products, their Devices and Novel Tobacco Products (DTI-OSMV), the NBI Team and DTI representatives conducted a joint briefing. Later that evening, the NBI and DTI team made a joint entrapment operation at the suspect’s address, apprehending in flagrante delicto Subject SULIMA along with his four (4) cohorts. The operation resulted in the seizure and confiscation of 25,653 pieces of vape products, with an estimated market value of PhP8,164,570,00. Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the Manila City Prosecutor’s Office for Violation of Section 4 (a) (i) & (ii) and (d); Sections 4 & 5 in relation to Section 23 (d); Section 18 of Republic Act No. 11900 (Vaporized Nicotine and Non-Nicotine Regulations Act), in relation to Section 6 of R. A. No. 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act 2012); and Violation of Section 40 (j) and (k) of Republic Act No. 7394 (Consumer Act of the Philippines) also in relation to Section 6 of R.A. No. 10175. They were and are currently detained under the custody of the NBI- Security Management Division (SMD). This successful operation underscores the Bureau’s commitment to safeguarding public health and enforcing laws against the unlawful trade of regulated products in collaboration with government agencies.

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today announced the arrest of two (2) Chinese nationals in Parañaque City for selling unauthorized Chinese medicines. NBI Officer-In-Charge Eric B. Distor identified the subjects as CHUI BAO CAI and WANG JIN QI, both Chinese nationals engaged in selling Chinese medicines without proper permits and authority. The operation stemmed from the report of a confidential informant received by NBI-Task Force Against Illegal Drugs (NBI-TFAID) that a certain CHUI BAO CAI is operating a warehouse with built-in online pharmacy/ drug outlet without a Certificate of Registration (COR) and Professional Identification Card (PIC) duly issued by the Professional Regulation Commission (PRC), and License to Operate (LTO) issued by the Food and Drugs Administration (FDA). Surveillance operation was conducted which revealed that Subjects Cai and Qi have created underground online pharmacy/ drug outlet in Airport Village, Parañaque City, being sold only to Chinese nationals, without COR, PIC, and LTO issued by various government agencies. Further investigation revealed that Subject Cai is one of the biggest suppliers of Chinese medicines to other underground hospitals and pharmacies operated by Chinese nationals in the National Capital Region (NCR) and nearby provinces. Subject Cai also engages in the illegal practice of dispensing medical drugs to Chinese nationals without prescription from a licensed physician. On June 24, 2020, NBI-TFAID proceeded to the target warehouse in Parañaque to conduct an entrapment operation against the subjects. One of the operatives and the informant posed as buyers and were able to buy unregistered Chinese medicines using the marked money prepared earlier. Subjects Cai and Qi failed to present to the raiding team necessary permits and documents such as COR, PIC, PRC, and LTO. Thus, operatives of NBI-TFAID arrested Subject Cai and Qi for unauthorized selling of Chinese Medicines. Seized form the subjects were 380 boxes of assorted unregistered Chinese medicines amounting to multi-million pesos. Subjects Cai and Qi were presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor of Parañaque City for violations of R.A. 9711 (Food and Drug Administration Act of 2009), R.A. 7394 (The Consumer Act of the Philippines), and R.A. 10918 (Philippine Pharmacy Act).

body: In line with the government’s campaign against criminality, the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) announces the arrest of two individuals for selling/trading illegal drugs in Cavite City. NBI Director Dante A. Gierran identified the Subjects as REYNALDO MORAL CORDERO and IRENE ILAYA BIAZON, both residents of Maricaban, Pasay City. Subjects CORDERO and BIAZON were on board a colored red 2001 Mitsubishi Lancer with plate number WTY 942 along Panapaan 4, Bacoor City, when they were apprehended by the NBI. Director Gierran said that on January 27, 2020, an Intelligence Report was received by NBI-MIMAROPA together with NBI-NCR relative to a certain “KIM’s” group regarding the alleged drug trafficker who is operating within Metro Manila and nearby provinces. Gierran added that based on said information, “KIM’s group will be transporting a huge volume of shabu somewhere in Bacoor and Imus Cavite. Under strict orders of Director Gierran and Deputy Director for Regional Operations Antonio Pagatpat, at around 6:30 in the evening of the same date, operatives of NBI-MIMAROPA and NBI-NCR positioned themselves in Brgy. Lotus Bukid, Panapaan 4, Bacoor City where “KIM’s” group is believed will traverse. After waiting a few minutes, a red Mitsubishi Lancer appeared as described by the informant and was immediately blocked by the NBI operatives. The Subjects where then apprehended and were properly appraised of their constitutional rights. Seized in the possession of Subjects was a sack inside the vehicle’s spare tire compartment with ten (10) plastic bags of white crystalline substance, placed inside a Chinese Tea Pack, believed to be methamphetamine hydrochloride or “Shabu”, with a volume of more than 10 kilograms. The illegal drugs (shabu) have an estimated value of P68 Million. The vehicle used by the Subjects to transport illegal drugs was likewise seized. Subjects were later turned-over to the NBI- Forensic Chemistry Division (FCD) for drug testing and post-processing procedures at NBI-NCR for properly booking, photographed and medical examination. The seized illegal drugs were likewise turned-over to the FCD for forensic examination. Subjects were also charged for Violation of RA 9165 (Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002) as amended.

body: PRESS STATEMENT October 28, 2024 In two separate operations, the Inter-Agency Task Force Against Illegal Drugs composed of the National Bureau of Investigation – Pampanga District Office (NBI-PAMDO), Philippine Drug Enforcement Agency (PDEA), Bureau of Customs (BOC), and Philippine National Police (PNP), conducted a Drug Interdiction at FEDEX Warehouse, Mabalacat City, Pampanga. On October 14, 2024, operatives opened two (2) parcels in the said warehouse. The first parcel, declared to be containing men’s track suit, contains 486 grams of dried leaves and fruiting tops suspected as High-Grade Marijuana (Kush) with an estimated street value of Php 729,000.00. The second parcel which was declared Runmax adjustable weighted vest contains two (2) black plastic packs with four (4) transparent sachets, the contents of which were suspected to be High-Grade Marijuana (Kush), weighing 2056 grams with an estimated value of Php2,084,000.00. On October 21, 2024, the same Inter-Agency Task force opened a parcel, containing two sealed packs, that was wrapped in sports clothing. Inside the packs, 262 grams and 264 grams of suspected KUSH were discovered, with an estimated market value of ₱789,000.00. The consignee was identified as to be a resident of Valenzuela City, and the shipment originated from KY Wholesale in Sacramento, USA. The seized items were turned over to PDEA for further testing. No controlled delivery has been planned at this time, pending advice from PDEA’s Director General.

NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION

PRESS STATEMENT October 28, 2024 In two separate operations, the Inter-Agency Task Force Against Illegal Drugs composed of the National Bureau of Investigation – Pampanga District Office (NBI-PAMDO), Philippine Drug Enforcement Agency (PDEA), Bureau of Customs (BOC), and Philippine National Police (PNP), conducted a Drug Interdiction at FEDEX Warehouse, Mabalacat City, Pampanga. On October 14, 2024, operatives opened two (2) parcels in the said warehouse. The first parcel, declared to be containing men’s track suit, contains 486 grams of dried leaves and fruiting tops suspected as High-Grade Marijuana (Kush) with an estimated street value of Php 729,000.00. The second parcel which was declared Runmax adjustable weighted vest contains two (2) black plastic packs with four (4) transparent sachets, the contents of which were suspected to be High-Grade Marijuana (Kush), weighing 2056 grams with an estimated value of Php2,084,000.00. On October 21, 2024, the same Inter-Agency Task force opened a parcel, containing two sealed packs, that was wrapped in sports clothing. Inside the packs, 262 grams and 264 grams of suspected KUSH were discovered, with an estimated market value of ₱789,000.00. The consignee was identified as to be a resident of Valenzuela City, and the shipment originated from KY Wholesale in Sacramento, USA. The seized items were turned over to PDEA for further testing. No controlled delivery has been planned at this time, pending advice from PDEA’s Director General.

body: PRESS STATEMENT December 19, 2024 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } In line with the instruction of National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Director JUDGE JAIME B. SANTIAGO (Ret.) to clamp down the human trafficking activities in the country, the NBI – International Airport Investigation Division (NBI-IAID) arrested CHRISTIAN SORIO UBAS and CHELSEA YSALEIGH FENIX in NAIA Terminal 1 for violation of Section 6 of R.A. No. 8042 (Migrant Workers and Overseas Filipinos Act of 1995) as amended by R.A. No. 10022 and Section 4 of R.A. No. 9208 (Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2003) as amended. Director Santiago said that on December 11, 2024, the above-stated Subjects together with four (4) passengers (Trafficked Victims) were bound to Singapore as tourists and were intercepted by the Bureau of Immigration (BI) Officers for inconsistencies in their travel purpose. The intercepted passengers were turned-over to the NBI-IAID for investigation. Immediately, the operatives of NBI-IAID conducted investigation, which revealed that the intercepted passengers were pretending to be tourists bound for Singapore and their true purpose of their travel is to work in a Pogo Hub in Cambodia via Singapore. In their sworn statement, the offloaded passengers revealed that they were recruited as Customer Service Representatives in a Pogo hub in Cambodia and were accompanied by the Subjects in their flight to Singapore and eventually to Cambodia. Thus, the NBI-IAID operatives placed the Subjects under arrest. The arrested Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor of Pasay City for the above-stated violations. Director Santiago commended the operatives of NBI-IAID for their swift action resulting in the arrest of the Subjects and warned the public against illegal recruiters.

body: Swift response to a call from an advocacy group led to the rescue of six minors, and the arrest of two prostitution den maintainers during an entrapment by agents of the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) in Angeles City, Pampanga recently. The suspects were identified as ESMERALDO “Jay” TEJERO AMURAO, Jr. and MARLYN “Lyn” DIZON VALENCIA, pimps, residents of Balibago, Angeles City, Pampanga. Investigation report of the NBI-Central Luzon Regional Office (CELRO) revealed that it received a request from the International Justice Mission (IJM), a non-government organization involved in Anti-Human Trafficking projects. It reported the unabated pimping activities of a certain “Jay” at or around Natalia Hotel, Fields Avenue, Balibago, Angeles City, Pampanga. On February 19, 2013, acting with dispatch, the NBI-CELRO operatives verified and confirmed the IJM report, and a rescue operation was planned at the Natalia Hotel in the evening of the next day. On the appointed date and time, an NBI team proceeded to said hotel and a poseur-customer met “Jay”. As previously arranged, he came with six (6) girls. The poseur gave the marked money of P8,000.00 to Jay, who handed a portion of the money to the girls, and to Lyn, his companion. A pre-arranged signal was given to the NBI agents who posted themselves inside the hotel. At that instance, the operatives approached Jay and Lyn, and placed them under arrest. The six girls whose ages range from 9 to 17 years old were whisked to safe distance nearby. Thereafter, the two suspects were brought to the NBI-CELRO office for booking and detention. Meanwhile, the six (6) minor girls were immediately referred to the Department of Social Welfare Development (DSWD) Office in the city, which took them under their custody. On February 21, 2013, the NBI-CELRO recommended the filing of a case against suspects Amurao and Valencia for violation of RA 9208 (Qualified Human Trafficking) and Violation of Sec. 5 of RA 9610 before the prosecutor’s office in Angeles City.

body: PRESS STATEMENT May 30, 2024 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } Operatives of National Bureau of Investigation-Cybercrime Division (NBI-CCD), on May 28, 2024, arrested the officers and employees of a recruitment agency for violations of Section 5 of R.A. No. 10022 (Migrant Workers and Overseas Filipinos Act of 1995, as amended); Section 4 of R.A. No. 10364 (Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2003); Estafa under Article 315 of the Revised Penal Code; and Serious Illegal Detention under Article 267 of the Revised Penal Code, all in relation to Section 6 of R.A. No. 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012). The case stemmed from the complaint of one of the victims’ relatives who averred that applicants were being detained by Maanyag International Manpower Corp. in their office and accommodation in Paranaque City. Further, victims’ passports and other travel documents were being withheld in the fear that they will be reported to the police if they run away, and will be blacklisted in all recruitment agencies. Thus, NBI-CCD operatives conducted a rescue operation on the above-mentioned date wherein they rescued a total of fifteen (15) victims. The rescued victims confirmed the report and added that they have to reimburse all the processing fees they spent so their documents will be released, and they have to secure their plane tickets going back to their respective provinces. In addition, they were ordered to do household chores, including manually washing the clothes of the staff and their families. The victims stayed in the accommodation for five months at most, while hundreds of victims still want to be rescued. Having confirmed that laws were violated in flagrante delicto, NBI-CCD operatives arrested the officers and employees involved in the above-stated violation of laws.

body: PRESS STATEMENT September 19, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } In its commitment to safeguarding children from the harm of abuse and exploitation, the National Bureau of Investigation – Human Trafficking Division (NBI-HTRAD) rescued a minor victim of online sexual exploitation on September 16, 2025, in Bacoor City, Cavite. The case was referred by the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) through the Philippine Internet Crimes Against Children Center (PICACC). An investigation was launched into a foreign national who is allegedly engaged in online sexual abuse and exploitation of children, as well as the possession, manufacture, and distribution of child sexual abuse and exploitation materials. These acts are in violation of Republic Act No. 11930, also known as the “Anti-Online Sexual Abuse or Exploitation of Children (OSAEC) and Anti-Child Sexual Abuse or Exploitation Materials (CSAEM) Act,” in relation to R.A. No. 10175, the “Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012.” According to the report, the foreign national had been grooming the victim for sexual exploitation. Investigation revealed that the victim, who is located in Cavite, Philippines, was sexually exploited online repeatedly. NBI-HTRAD, in coordination with the NBI-Cavite North District Office (CAVIDO-North), conducted surveillance to confirm the victim’s physical location and identity. Upon validating the intelligence, NBI-HTRAD initiated inter-agency coordination with the Department of Justice – Inter-Agency Council Against Trafficking (DOJ-IACAT), the DOJ National Coordination Center against Online Sexual Abuse or Exploitation of Children and Child Sexual Abuse or Exploitation Materials (NCC-OSAEC-CSAEM), the City Social Welfare and Development (CSWD)-Cavite, and the Local Police Office. Thereafter, agents, along with social workers from the CSWD, successfully rescued the victim and placed them under the protective custody of the CSWD Office. Charges will be filed against the perpetrators for violations of: • R.A. No. 11930 in relation to Sec. 4(c)(2) of R.A. No. 10175 • R.A. No. 9208, also known as the “Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2003” as amended by R.A. No. 10364 (the “Expanded Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2012”), and further amended by R.A. No. 11862 (the “Expanded Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2022”) • Republic Act No. 7610, also known as the “Special Protection of Children Against Abuse, Exploitation and Discrimination Act.” This operation underscores the firm resolve of NBI Director JUDGE JAIME B. SANTIAGO in the Bureau’s commitment to protecting Filipino children from online exploitation. His uncompromising stance against OSAEC continues to drive the Bureau’s aggressive pursuit of perpetrators, both domestic and foreign. NBI-HTRAD vows to hunt down perpetrators of OSAEC and ensure they are relentlessly pursued and brought to justice.

body: PRESS STATEMENT December 13, 2024 In line with the order of National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Director Judge Jaime B. Santiago (Ret.) to remain steadfast in protecting individuals from threats and acts of violence, particularly women, the NBI-Bataan District Office (NBI-BATADO) arrested JOEL BERINGUELA y RIVERA on December 5, 2024 for violations of Article 294 (Robbery with Violence Against or Intimidation of Persons) of the Revised Penal Code, RA No. 9262 (Anti-Violence Against Women and Their Children Act of 2004), and RA No. 9995 (Anti-Photo and Video Voyeurism Act of 2009). The case stemmed from a complaint filed against Subject BERINGUELA. According to the complainant, when she learned that Subject’s marriage is not tumultuous as he claimed, and that his relationship with his wife is going fair and well, she decided to end her relationship with him. After which, Subject BERINGUELA escalated his tactics, sent slanderous messages to complainant’s colleagues, and threatened to ruin her career by releasing intimate videos of her unless she pays him Php 300,000. Feeling that Subject was just doing it for her to reunite with him, complainant sought the assistance of the NBI. Acting on the complaint, an entrapment operation was hatched. Complainant agreed to meet with Subject BERINGUELA in a restaurant in Subic Bay Freeport Zone on December 5, 2024. During the meeting, complainant handed over the marked money to Subject BERINGUELA but he confronted the complainant about the insufficiency of the amount and demanded that she either give the full Php 300,000 or engage in sexual acts. Complainant then signaled the NBI operatives who swiftly moved in, arresting BERINGUELA at the scene. The marked money was recovered from Subject’s possession during the arrest. Subject was presented before the Office of the City Prosecutor of Olongapo for inquest proceedings for the above-stated violations of law. Director Santiago commended the BATADO operatives for their swift action and dedication to upholding the Bureau’s commitment in protecting the public from violence and exploitation. With this rapid response, justice is being served, and the agency remains vigilant in addressing similar cases to ensure the safety and well-being of individuals, especially women.

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today announced the arrest of an individual by operatives of NBI-Special Action Unit (NBI-SAU) inside the NBI Headquarters in Manila who extorted money from an NBI clearance applicant. NBI Officer-in-Charge (OIC)- Director Eric B. Distor identified the subject as MARK ENDAYA CABAL. OIC Distor said that the operation stemmed from a complaint filed by the victim of Subject Cabal. According to the victim, he met the subject outside the NBI Clearance building, who was then wearing an NBI polo shirt, which made him think that the subject was an NBI employee and asked for information on where to get an NBI clearance. Subject Cabal then offered to help the complainant regarding the NBI clearance. After a while, Subject Cabal told the victim that upon checking his records, the victim has a pending drug case with a Warrant of Arrest. The subject threatened the victim that he will be arrested if he will not give Php 100,000.00. The victim then returned the following day to hand over Php 40,000.00 to the subject. Not satisfied with Php 40,000.00, Subject Cabal continued to threaten the victim that he might not only suffer imprisonment but might be killed for his involvement in drugs. The victim then asked the subject to give him a week to produce the additional Php 60,000.00. The victim, upon the advice of his friends and appeared before the office of NBI-SAU to file a complaint against the subject. Upon discovery of the scheme of Subject Cabal, NBI-SAU agents immediately hatched an entrapment operation. Subject Cabal and the victim agreed to meet inside the NBI Headquarters parking lot.Thus on February 3, 2020, the operatives strategically positioned themselves in the area and upon handing over the entrapment money the operatives immediately approached Subject Cabal and announced his arrest. Recovered from the possession of the subject were three (3) heat-sealed plastic sachets with white crystalline substance suspected to be shabu. Based on the certification issued by the NBI-Forensic Chemistry Division (NBI-FCD), one of the sachets tested positive for Ephedrine with a net weight of 0.2718 and the two (2) other sachets tested positive for Methamphetamine hydrochloride with a combine weight of 12.2653. Upon verification, NBI-SAU also found that Subject Cabal has several complaints against him for Robbery/Extortion and Estafa. Subject Cabal was presented for Inquest proceeding before the Office of the Prosecutor of Manila.

title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: In its continuing support to the government’s campaign against illegal drugs, the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today said operatives of NBI-Task force Against Illegal Drugs (NBI-TFAID) have arrested three (3) individuals in a buy-bust operation in Mandaluyong City on May 10, 2017. The arrested Subjects were identified as DORIAN ALAN PEÑA, Filipino-American professional basketball player, known as the “Junkyard Dog” who played for San Miguel Beer, Barangay Ginebra, Barako Bull and Global Port Batang Pier; JOSE PAOLO AMPESO a.k.a “JP”, son of Jose Arthur Ampeso, former Chief Consul General for Vancouver, Canada; and LEDY MEA MESIA VILCHEZ a.k.a. “Mae”, escort girl and live-in partner of Ampeso. NBI Director Dante A. Gierran said “the NBI-TFAID operatives, in pursuit of fugitive JUN NO, a Korean-American national who is wanted for drug trafficking, involving the trafficking of a party drug ecstasy, stumbled upon an information that Subject “Mae” was the last known companion of JUN NO after the latter escaped from the hospital after undergoing a surgery for appendectomy.” Gierran also said that intelligence network brought in the information that “Mae” is an escort girl who delivers drugs for Korean clients. The NBI said that with the help of an informant, a drug deal was set up at Merryland Village in Mandaluyong City between “Mae” and an undercover operative. The 3 Subjects were having a pot session before they were arrested, after the exchange of the marked money and methamphetamine hydrochloride or shabu. Subjects resisted arrest and manifested signs of being under the influence of illegal drugs. Subjects later on likewise tested positive for drug use. Several pieces of drug paraphernalia and weighing scale were seized during the operation. The 3 Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the Department of Justice (DOJ) for violations of Sections 5, 6, 11, 12, 15 and 26 of R.A. 9165 (Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002) with respect to Subjects JOSE PAOLO AMPESO and LEDY MEA MESIA VILCHEZ and violations of Sections 7 and 15 of R.A. 9165 for Subject DORIAN PEÑA. Director Gierran stressed, “With the arrest of the 3 Subjects involving a Filipino-American professional basketball player and a son of a former Diplomat of the Philippine Government, the NBI sends the clear message that there is no untouchable in the war against drugs under the present Administration.”

title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: PRESS STATEMENT April 01, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } PRESS RELEASE | NBI ARRESTS CHINESE NATIONAL FOR UNLAWFUL SALE OF SIMCARDS PASAY CITY, Philippines – The National Bureau of Investigation – International Operations Division (NBI-IOD) confirms the successful arrest of a Chinese national involved in the unlawful distribution and sale of pre-registered SIM cards. The operation took place on March 30, 2026 in Tondo, Manila. It was the culmination of an investigation into reports that the Subject was utilizing the encrypted messaging platform Telegram to market pre-registered SIM cards. Investigation revealed that the SIM cards were being sold to clandestine POGOs, individuals, and syndicates engaged in various online scamming activities. During the entrapment operation, an undercover NBI-IOD agent tested a Smart SIM card provided by the suspect. Upon accessing the official registration portal, a system notification confirmed the number was already registered, verifying the illegal nature of the sale. The Subject was arrested in flagrante delicto upon receiving the marked money from the undercover operative. During the operation, the NBI-IOD recovered and seized forty-nine (49) pieces of pre-registered Smart SIM cards and one (1) mobile phone used for the illegal transactions. The Subject was presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor of Manila for violation of Section 7 of Republic Act No. 11934 (SIM Card Registration Act), in relation to Section 6 of Republic Act No. 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012). The NBI remains steadfast in its commitment to dismantling networks that facilitate cybercrime. By enforcing the SIM Card Registration Act, the Bureau aims to strip online scammers and illegal offshore operators of the anonymity they require to exploit the public. #NBIServes

body: PRESS STATEMENT September 29, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } NBI Conducts Multi-Hazard Training in Batangas City The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) – Disaster Victim Identification Division (DVID) conducted Multi-Hazard Training on September 21-25 in Batangas City. The training aimed to enhance the knowledge, skills, and preparedness of NBI participants and marshals to respond to various types of hazards and emergencies. It also gave participants the opportunity to understand the risks associated with natural and human-induced hazards and to strengthen their capacity to respond effectively during emergencies. The training, which consisted of lectures, interactive discussions, demonstrations, and practical exercises, covered important topics related to hazard identification, risk assessment, emergency preparedness, response procedures, safety protocols, and coordination among responding agencies. Participants learned appropriate strategies for managing various hazards, including earthquakes, floods, landslides, fires, severe weather events, and other emergencies. The training was intended to help participants share their learnings with family, colleagues, friends, and others

title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: PRESS STATEMENT October 06, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } In line with the government’s drive against the proliferation of fake products, the National Bureau of Investigation-Intellectual Property Rights Division (NBI-IPRD) seized 13,412 canisters of counterfeit Bao Li Lai aerosol insecticides and 3,042 canisters of counterfeit Big Bie Lai aerosol insecticides worth Php1,972,320.00. The operation stemmed from a complaint filed by the registered owners of the trademarks regarding the rampant selling of their products in the market. In response, the NBI-IPRD agents conducted surveillance and test-buy operations on multiple occasions against the EveryJuan Shop in Valenzuela City and associated warehouses in Tondo, Manila. These operations successfully confirmed the illegal activities o the involved establishments. On October 1, 2025, NBI-IPRD agents implemented Search Warrants granted by the Regional Trial Court of Manila, Branch 46, against the subject establishments and warehouses, which resulted in the seizure of fake insecticides. Charges will be filed against the owner of the establishment for violation of Section 155 in relation to Section 170 (Trademark Infringement) of Republic Act No. 8293 (Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines. Director Santiago commended the agents of NBI-IPRD for the successful operation and warned the public to refrain from patronizing fake products.

body: PRESS STATEMENT September 23, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } In two separate operations, the NBI-Cybercrime Division (NBI-CCD) arrested two subjects in General Trias City, Cavite for violation of Section 4(a)(1) (Illegal Access) of Republic Act No. 10172 (Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012). In a second operation, the NBI agents arrested one in Naguilian, La Union, for violations of Section 4(a)(1) of R.A. No. 10175, Section 4(a)(3) (Misuse of Devices and System Interference) of R.A. No. 10175, and Unauthorized Distribution of Network Services in relation to Estafa under the Revised Penal Code (RPC) and R.A. No. 8484 (Access Devices Regulation Act of 1998). On June 4, 2025, a representative from an internet service provider company filed a complaint with the NBI-CCD against individuals who were allegedly offering internet services to the public through a Facebook account named “RECON VERGECON”. Investigation revealed that the said account offered various services, including reactivation of disconnected internet services, bandwidth enhancement for current subscribers, modem support, connection of new subscribers, and speed boosting for existing customer connections at a lower price, all without the authority of the internet service provider. Acting on the complaint, NBI-CCD agents conducted technical tracing and physical tracing of Complainant’s proprietary Network Access Point. The NBI agents confirmed that the illegal activities were being carried out at a residence in General Trias City, Cavite. Subsequently, the agents applied for a Warrant to Search, Seize, and Examine Computer Data (WSSECD), which was granted by the Regional Trial Court Branch 130, Trece Martirez. On August 28, 2025, NBI-CCD agents arrived at the residence of the Subjects in General Trias City, Cavite, to execute the WSSECD. Upon entering the property, agents found one subject at an operational computer on the ground floor. They also found the other subject using a computer on the second floor. The NBI Digital Forensics team conducted an on-site search and examination of the computers, which revealed that four (4) of the MAC addresses identified by the internet service provider as the devices used for illegal access were indeed present in the computer systems. At that point, NBI-CCD agents arrested the Subjects and seized the computer devices for evidence. On September 16, 2025, NBI-CCD agents implemented a WSSECD against a three-storey house in Cabaritan Sur, Naguilian, La Union. The operation resulted in the seizure of various computer devices used by the Subject to illegally distribute internet connections to several houses within the vicinity without authority from the internet service provider. Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings for the aforementioned violations. NBI Director Santiago commended the agents of the NBI-CCD for their successful operation, leading to the apprehension of the subjects.
