body: PRESS STATEMENT February 19, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } NBI-CCD Nabs Individual in Pasay City for Cyber-Related Estafa and Multi-Million Peso Investment Scheme PASAY CITY, Philippines – The National Bureau of Investigation-Cybercrime Division (NBI-CCD) has successfully arrested an individual involved in an investment scam targeting aspiring Overseas Filipino Workers (OFWs). The operation took place on February 10, 2026 that led to the arrest of the Subject during an entrapment at a local mall. The investigation began following a complaint from a victim who was lured into a fraudulent foreign exchange trading scheme. The Subject allegedly utilized the messaging app Telegram to manage an investment group, enticing members with the promise of “faster income” and guaranteed returns on investment (ROI). Driven by the prospect of financial security before working abroad, the Complainant transferred a total of Php 957,700.00 across several transactions. This included a final “third ride” payment of Php 60,000.00, which the Subject claimed would double in value. When the promised returns failed to materialize despite repeated demands, the Subject attempted to solicit an additional Php 4,000,000.00 from the victim. Realizing the fraudulent nature of the business, the Complainant coordinated with the NBI-CCD. An entrapment operation was conducted at a restaurant inside a Pasay City mall, where a meeting had been scheduled for the delivery of the additional investment. The Subject was subsequently arrested by NBI-CCD operatives while in the process of accepting the marked currency.” The Subject was presented for inquest proceedings and now faces formal charges for Estafa under Article 315, paragraph 2(a) of the Revised Penal Code in relation to Section 6 of Republic Act No. 10175, also known as the Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012. NBI Acting Director Atty. Angelito DLP Magno lauded the swift action of the Cybercrime Division and issued a sharp rebuke to those preying on the hard-earned savings of Filipinos. “This is a stern warning to criminals: stop your illegal activities or face justice behind bars,” said Acting Director Magno. “The NBI remains dedicated to upholding justice and protecting our citizens from digital predators.” The NBI advises the public to be cautious of investment opportunities shared through private messaging apps that promise “guaranteed” or “unusually high” returns. ATTY. ANGELITO DLP. MAGNO Acting Director, NBI #NBIServes Media Contact: HA Palmer U. Mallari NBI Spokesperson [email protected]

title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: PRESS STATEMENT October 24, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } The National Bureau of Investigation – Cavite District Office North (NBI-CAVIDO North) arrested HUBERI LIWANAG (“GENERAL”) and JUALINIO ABUTIN (“CONG WALLY”) for violation of Article 315 par. 2(a)(c) of the Revised Penal Code. In December 2024, Complainants met with “CONG WALLY”, a candidate for Congress from Cavite’s 7th District, who offered to sell them 700,000 disposable vape juice cartridges. Although the price initially surprised the Complainants, they were assured the products would be released once they paid an initial reservation fee of Php20 million. On December 29, 2024, “CONG WALLY” proposed a meeting with a government official. The official allegedly assured them the transaction would go through, stating she would only need to speak with the Commissioner of Customs about the release of the vape products. Despite paying a total of Php 45.5 million to different individuals, as advised by “CONG WALLY” for “processing” at the Bureau of Customs and other connections, the release of the aforementioned vape products never occurred. When complainants demanded their money back, “Cong Wally” only offered excuses and false pretenses. Instead, he offered one of the Complainants a new brand of vape products purportedly coming from a certain “General.” Sensing that this was another attempt to cover his previous obligation, the Complainant decided to seek the assistance of NBI-CAVIDO North. The Subjects were subsequently apprehended during an entrapment operation. Thereafter, Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor of Bacoor City, Cavite for the above-mentioned violations.

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today announced the arrest of an individual in San Francisco, Agusan Del Sur for illegal practice of dentistry. NBI Officer-In-Charge (OIC) Director Eric B. Distor identified the subject as ANALIZA M. CONSTANCIO who was arrested in an entrapment operation by operatives of the NBI-AGUSAN Del Sur District Office (NBI-ADSDO) on May 11, 2021. body: PRESS STATEMENT March 18, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } On February 27, 2025, joint teams from the National Bureau of Investigation – Pampanga District Office (NBI-PAMDO) and the military intelligence of the Philippine Air Force (PAF), under the guidance and supervision of NBI Director Judge Jaime B. Santiago (Ret.), implemented a Warrant to Search, Seize, and Examine Computer Data (WSSECD) at a condominium in Brgy. Sta. Cruz, Porac, Pampanga. The case stemmed from the information that the aforementioned premises operate as an illegal online gambling hub without a license from Philippine Amusement and Gaming Corporation (PAGCOR). Acting on the said information, WSSECD for Illegal Online Gambling under Presidential Decree No. 1602 in relation to Republic Act No. 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012) was applied for and granted by the Presiding Judge of Regional Trial Court (RTC) Branch 81, Malolos City, Bulacan. The operation led to the arrest of four Korean nationals: KIM MINHA, KIM HAESU, KIM MINSUU, and JANG JIN. During the operation, authorities seized computer devices and online gambling paraphernalia. The arrested individuals were subsequently indicted for illegal online gambling under Presidential Decree No. 1602 in relation to Republic Act No. 10175. As part of the investigation, the NBI-PAMDO agents, in collaboration with INTERPOL, the Korean Embassy, and the Korean National Police Agency, discovered that Kim Minha and Kim Haesu were Korean fugitives wanted for prosecution by the Korean government. Both individuals have been issued an Interpol Red Notice. Based on records, KIM MINHA and KIM HAESU are members of a Korean voice phishing syndicate operating in the Philippines since 2017. They defrauded their victims by posing as bankers, amassing approximately USD 840,000.00 from their scams. The Chuncheon District Court of the Republic of Korea has issued an arrest warrant for fraud (Criminal Act 347-(1)) against the two (2). The case is scheduled for trial at RTC Branch 115 in Angeles City. Subjects Kim Minha and Kim Haesu are currently detained at the NBI-PAMDO. Director SANTIAGO lauded NBI-PAMDO and PAF intelligence for the successful law enforcement operation and for establishing international collaboration with counterparts to arrest fugitives hiding in the country.

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today said it has seized counterfeit products of signature brands with an estimated value of P200 million in five (5) shopping malls in Manila. The suspect were identified by NBI Officer-In-Charge Atty. Nonnatus Caesar R. Rojas as: BARTOLOME S. ATIENZA , 52, team leader, MERMAR G. MERCADO , 35, traffic enforcer; JOSEPH A. DILAY , 42, traffic enforcer, all of the Land Transportation Office in Batangas City. assigned in the area; and REDENTOR M. SILVA ; and FELIX A. CONDUCTO JR., both civilian operatives. Vigilia, disclosed that the case arose from a complaint of NBI Agent Adeodato Logroño that the suspects after having extorted from his truck helper, Bonnie Magulod, P5,000 and demanded P2,000 monthly protection money. This is to insure the passage of the delivery truck in Batangas City area without being apprehended. Magulod also received repeated text messages from them demanding the monthly protection money. An entrapment operation was planned with the assistance of NBI Cavite District Office (CAVIDO) agents. On April 18, 2012, the operation pushed through leading to the arrest of the suspects who were brought to the NBI Batangas office. Charges for Robbery/Extortion and violation of the Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act were filed against the suspects before the Inquest Prosecutor of Batangas City.

body: PRESS STATEMENT July 17, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } Alinsunod sa utos ni NBI Director Atty. Melvin A. Matibag, pinaigting ng NBI-Human Trafficking Division (NBI-HTRAD) ang kampanya nito laban sa human trafficking, na nagresulta sa pagkaaresto ng isang indibidwal sa Lungsod ng Maynila dahil sa paglabag sa Republic Act No. 8042 (Migrant Workers and Overseas Filipinos Act of 1995) at Estafa sa ilalim ng Artikulo 315 ng Revised Penal Code. Nagsimula ang operasyon mula sa isang reklamong inihain laban sa Subject, na inakusahan ng illegal recruitment sa mga nagrereklamo upang magtrabaho sa South Korea. Bilang tugon sa alegasyon, mabilis na nagplano ng isang entrapment operation ang mga ahente ng NBI-HTRAD upang mahuli sa akto ang Subject. Noong Hulyo 14, 2026, nagtungo ang mga ahente ng NBI-HTRAD, kasama ang isang nagpanggap na aplikante (poseur applicant), sa isang itinalagang klinika sa Maynila para sa isang medikal na pagsusuri bilang bahagi ng diumano’y pagpapadala sa aplikante sa South Korea. Sa loob ng klinika, ipinaalam ng Subject sa aplikante na kailangan ng bayad na Php 12,000.00 para sa medikal na pagsusuri.Matapos nito, tinanong ng aplikante kung may lisensya o awtorisasyon ang suspek na mag recruit ng mga manggagawa para sa trabaho sa ibang bansa. Bilang sagot, sinabi ng suspek na wala siyang koneksyon sa alinmang lisensyadong recruitment agency at ipinaliwanag na ang pagpapadala ay ipoproseso na lamang sa pamamagitan ng LGU-to-LGU (local government unit) na kasunduan. Matapos iabot ang marked money sa Subject bilang bayad sa medikal na pagsusuri, agad na lumapit ang mga ahente ng NBI-HTRAD at inihayag ang kanyang pagkaaresto. Pinuri ni Director Matibag ang mga ahente ng NBI-HTRAD para sa kanilang natatanging pagsisikap sa nagdaang operasyon na naghantong sa pagkaaresto ng indibidwal na kasangkot sa illegal recruitment. Ang matagumpay na pagsugpong ito ay sumasalamin sa commitment ng NBI na labanan ang human trafficking at protektahan ang mga mahihirap na indibidwal laban sa exploitation. Binigyang-diin ni Director Matibag na ang mahalagang tagumpay na ito ay nagpapakita ng kahalagahan ng kanilang trabaho upang matiyak ang mas ligtas na kapaligiran para sa mga naghahanap ng trabaho. https://www.facebook.com/reel/1056713437040885

body: PRESS STATEMENT September 17, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI), demonstrating its commitment to environmental protection, has launched a simultaneous operation against illegal mining activities in two sites located in Purok Lanipga and Purok Mandaupan, both in Barangay Bahi, Marasugan, Davao de Oro. The operation was a collaborative effort between the NBI-Southeastern Mindanao Regional Office (NBI-SEMRO) and the Mines and Geosciences Bureau (MGB) Region XI, with support from the Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP)and the Philippine National Police (PNP). Acting on reports of illegal mining, the team investigated the sites and discovered abandoned mining operations equipped with bunkers and tunnels, indicating recent activity. The operation successfully dismantled both illegal mining sites and resulted in the seizure of various mining equipment along with numerous sacks of copper and mineral ores. NBI Director Santiago praised the efforts of the NBI-SEMRO agents and expressed appreciation for the collaboration with the MGB, which was crucial for the successful seizure of the mineral ores and mining equipment. He also extended his gratitude to the PNP and AFP for their valuable support during the operation.

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today announced the arrest of three (3) Korean fugitives by Agents of NBI-Special Action Unit (NBI-SAU) Senta Tower, Legazpi Village, Makati City. NBI Officer-In-Charge (OIC) Director Eric B. Distor identified the subjects as CHANGJOO CHO, DAWON BEOM, and CHANGWOO HONG. OIC Director Distor said that the operation stemmed from information received by the NBI-SAU regarding said Korean nationals Park Joo Hwan, Dawon Beom, Changwoo Hong and Changjoo Cho who are allegedly engaged in Kidnap-for-Ransom operating in Manila and Makati City. The Syndicate is reportedly in possession of unlicensed high-powered firearms, which they use in their illegal activities. NBI-SAU verified the records of the subject Korean nationals with the Bureau of Immigration (BI) and it was revealed that CHANGJOO CHO, DAWON BEOM, and CHANGWOO HONG are fugitives from South Korea wanted for prosecution with outstanding Warrants for their arrest. Records showed that the three (3) subjects were charged for violations of Article 26 of the Korean National Sports Promotion Act with maximum penalties up to seven (7) years. While PARK JOO HWAN has a derogatory record for alleged Kidnap-for-Ransom activities. On June 15, 2021, joint operatives of NBI-SAU and BI-Fugitive Search Unit, proceeded to a unit in Senta Tower in Legazpi Village Makati City where the subject Koreans are residing. Upon entering the premises the joint operatives found the four (4) Korean subjects. Major Sungsoo Chang, Police Liaison Officer of Korean Embassy followed shortly after at the target unit and he positively identified CHANGJOO CHO, DAWON BEOM, andG HONG CHANG WOO as Korean fugitives. The operation was conducted with the presence of building security and lessor/owner of the unit. SOOHWAN PARK who was also found in the company of the three (3) fugitives was cleared of any derogatory record but was invited to the SAU office for proper identification and documentation. The three (3) arrested Korean fugitives were later turned-over to BI-Fugitive Search Unit.

body: PRESS STATEMENT June 10, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } Under the leadership of National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Director JUDGE JAIME B. SANTIAGO (Ret.), the NBI-Cabanatuan District Office (NBI-CABDO) arrested an individual in Dau, Mabalacat City, Pampanga for Grave Coercion in relation to Republic Act No. 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012), violation of R.A. No. 9262 (VAWC Law), and R.A. No. 9995 (Anti-Photo and Video Voyeurism Act). The operation stemmed from a complaint filed with the NBI-CABDO. Complainant revealed that she met Subject through a mobile gaming application called “Mobile Legends,” and they eventually became romantically involved. However, Complainant later discovered that Subject was also in a relationship with another woman he had met through the same application. As a result, Complainant decided to end their relationship. After some time, Subject began sending through Facebook images of their past sexual encounters to Complainant’s new boyfriend. He also sent Complainant photographs and videos of their sexual encounters. Subject demanded that Complainant meet him and have sexual intercourse with him. He threatened the Complainant that he would post their photographs online if she declined to comply with his demand. The Subject instructed the Complainant to meet him at the bus terminal in Dau where he will pick her up. On June 2, 2025, agents of NBI-CABDO, in collaboration with agents of NBI-CELRO, proceeded to the bus terminal in Dau, Mabalacat City, Pampanga. The joint team strategically positioned themselves and witnessed the meeting of the Subject and the Complainant. The joint team discreetly followed the two into a nearby motel where the Subject planned to take the Complainant. While entering the hotel, the apprehending team immediately approached the Subject and announced his arrest. Subject was presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor of Mabalacat City, Pampanga. Director Santiago commended the agents of NBI-CABDO and NBI-CELRO for the successful operation, which led to the arrest of the Subject.

body: PRESS STATEMENT April 19, 2022 NBI FILES CHARGES AGAINST PHILHEALTH OFFICIALS FOR IRREGULARITIES IN HCP ACCREDITATION The National Bureau of Investigation-Anti-Graft Division (NBI-AGD) has filed charges before the Office of the Ombudsman against officers of PhilHealth Regional Office – National Capital Region (PRO-NCR) Accreditation Committee in relation to Health Care Provider (HCP) accreditation renewal. NBI Officer-In-Charge (OIC) Eric B. Distor identified the PRO-NCR officials and personnel as DR. NENITA EPIFANIA F. BALBUENA, DR. IMELDA TRINIDAD DE VERA-PE, JANICE GEM P. PERLAS, MD, ROFIEN H. ISON, MD, DIODE G. LANTORA, ATTY. YASSER ISMAIL A. ABBAS, ALLAN M. DE VILLA, ALEJANDRINO T. PEREZ, MD, JEFFREY Y. PE, DENNIS S. MAS, and DR. CELSTINA MA. JUDE P. DELA SERNA. OIC Director Distor said that in October 2016, the complainant received a letter from DENNIS S. MAS, Vice President of PRO-NCR informing her that her application for reaccreditation was denied by PRO-NCR Accreditation Sub-Committee from July 1, 2016 to June 4, 2019 due to practice inconsistent with the acceptable quality of care. In May 2017, complainant, through Atty. Paulo S. Selva, requested the NBI to conduct an investigation on the alleged injustice committed by PRO-NCR officials on the HCP reaccreditation. But in July 2017, complainant withdrew her complaint as she received verbal advice from DR. CELSTINA MA. JUDE P. DELA SERNA, former Interim/Officer-In-Charge, President and CEO PHIC that she will be accredited as HCP if she withdrew her complaint in NBI. However, in September 2020, complainant requested for revival of the case as the reaccreditation did not push through. The notice of denial was dated October 13, 2016 but the Accreditation Sub-Committee denial order was ante-dated from July 1 2016 to June 4, 2019. Minutes of Accreditation Sub-Committee Meeting PRO-NCR dated October 10, 2016 was deliberated, approved, and signed by the Sub-Committee NCR Members DR. NENITA EPIFANIA F. BALBUENA (Chairperson), DR. IMELDA TRINIDAD DE VERA-PE, JANICE GEM P. PERLAS, MD, ROFIEN H. ISON, MD, DIODE G. LANTORA, ATTY. YASSER ISMAIL A. ABBAS, ALLAN M. DE VILLA, ALEJANDRINO T. PEREZ, MD, and JEFFREY Y. PE. It shows that the denial was August 3, 2016. According to PHIC, the denial is due to the administrative case filed against the complainant with the Prosecution Department of PHIC. Complainant, however claimed that she was denied of due process guaranteed under National Health Insurance Act of 1995, the grounds used for the denial was not explained well and there were no specifics given. She was not also informed or notified of any inquiry or validations made by the PHIC. Further, PHIC was not able to resolve the allegations against her after serving the suspension from July 2016 to June 2019. Looking at the circumstances on how the renewal of accreditation was denied, it appears that the Accreditation Sub-Committee agreed to reopen the deliberation on the application for accreditation and unanimously voted to recommend the denial of application for accreditation. Also, at the time the denial was made, there was no pending case filed against the complainant. Further investigation conducted reveals that the basis of denying the application for accreditation was not sufficiently established by PhilHealth. PhilHealth’s authority to deny accreditation of complainant requires that the applicant be first convicted to fraudulent acts. From the records, it appears that complainant was denied of her accreditation even before the case was heard by the Arbitration Office and without a formal complaint and an effort to conduct a fact-finding investigation as mandated by NHI Law. While it is within the PhilHealth’s power to suspend, revoke, or refuse Accreditation, it must be emphasized that the power to suspend or revoke is exercised based on the existence of grounds and must be compliant with law governing the same. The PhilHealth must observe due process in that it must afford the applicant notice and opportunity to be heard. DENNIS S. MAS, and DR. CELSTINA MA. JUDE P. DELA SERNA, as Vice President of PRO-NCR and PCEO of PhilHealth respectively, they are presumed to know all existing policies, guidelines, and procedures in carrying out the agency’s mandate. DELA SERNA also acted in bad faith when she promised to reaccredit complainant if she withdrew her complaint at NBI. NBI-AGD then recommended that above-mentioned Subjects be prosecuted for violation of Section 3(e) of RA 3019 (Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act). Subjects were also recommended to be administratively charged for violation of RA 6713 (Code of Conduct and Ethical Standards for Public Officials and Employees).

title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today said operatives of the NBI-Special Task Force (NBI-STF) have arrested a Subject in Caloocan City yesterday for illegal practice of Dentistry. NBI Director Dante A. Gierran identified the Subject as RONALYN J. CRUZ-TAN who maintained a dental clinic in Caloocan City. He added that the illegal practice of Dentistry of Subject RONALYN J. CRUZ-TAN is in violation of Republic Act No. 9484 otherwise known as the Philippine Dental Act of 2007. The case stemmed from a January 17, 2018 complaint filed before the NBI by Dr. Ariel Go, Chairman of the Anti-Illegal Practice Committee of the Philippine Dental Association (PDA), stating that as early as December 2017, Subject RONALYN J. CRUZ-TAN is engaged in dental practice without the necessary license and certificate required under the law. After conducting proper verification and surveillance operation by the NBI-STF wherein Subject RONALYN J. CRUZ-TAN performed a dental procedure on an undercover operative, an entrapment operation was hatched resulting in the arrest of Subject RONALYN J. CRUZ-TAN, who will be charged for violation of R.A. 9484 otherwise known as The Philippine Dental Act of 2007.

title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: In line with the relentless campaign of the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) against environmental crimes, operatives of NBI-Environmental Crime Division (NBI-EnCD) arrested nine (9) individuals dumping hazardous wastes in Cabangan, province of Zambales. NBI Director Dante A. Gierran identified the Subjects as HUIZU HUA (Master of the vessel), WANG AIMIN (Chief Mate), DANNY BAÑES y PLARISAN (LCT Yellow River Captain), CLIEFORD CALINGACION y BUSIO (LCT Second Mate), ALBERTO RENDON y MAGNAYE, EDGARDO AQUINO y BONDOC, EDDIE SINGUELO SR y GONZALES, and the Filipino Brokers, BENJAMIN BAUTISTA y MAAMBONG, and JESSE ROMANO SUNGA y NATIVIDAD. On November 15, 2019, an information was received by the NBI regarding an alleged shipment of hazardous substance or waste called phosphogypsum in the province of Zambales. The next day, NBI-EnCD operatives proceeded to the target area and conducted surveillance of the shipment of phosphogypsum. Upon arrival in the area, operatives observed a large vessel anchored more or less 1.5 kilometers from the shoreline of Brgy. Sto. Nino, Cabangan, Zambales. Moreover, there were Landing Craft Tanks (LCT) docked in a private jetty port. The vessel was identified as MV Dayang Century and the LCT were identified as Yellow River and CTH181. Director Gierran said the NBI operatives observed that the LCT CTH181 was docked in the private jetty port containing what appears to be soil type substance. The cargos of CTH181was being unloaded by a backhoe which are then transferred to a dump truck. When the dump truck was filled, it would leave the area and return after several minutes just to be filled again. NBI-EnCD operatives, thereafter, proceeded to a road entering the private jetty port and had observed that a truck was dumping soil-type substance just across the river of Brgy. Sto. Nino, Cabangan, Zambales. Investigation revealed that M/V Dayang Century, a Liberian-registered Flag Vessel, is transporting 53,000 metric tons of toxic waste known as phosphogypsum from Gwangyang, South Korea to Cabangan, Zambales. Certification from the DENR-Environmental Management Bureau (DENR-EMB) cited that the importation of phosphogypsum is prohibited and not included in the allowed recyclable materials to be imported here in the Philippines. The DENR-EMB also certified that the phosphogypsum is a waste and by-product from fertilizer production and is radioactive due to the presence of naturally occurring radioactive elements. Furthermore, Yori Yori Trading, consignee of the shipment, has not secured any importation clearance and has no import registry from the DENR-EMB. Thus, while in the act of still unloading the phosphogypsum, joint elements of Philippine coast Guard (PCG) and NBI-EnCD boarded M/V Dayang Century and LCT Yellow River that eventually led to the arrest of the above-mentioned Subjects while the custody of the M/V Dayang Century and LCT Yellow River are within the PCG. Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the Department of Justice (DOJ) Manila for violation of RA 6969 (Toxic Substances and Hazardous and Nuclear Wastes Control Act of 1999) and RA 9003 (Ecological Solid Waste Management Act of 2000.

body: In line with the government’s drive against individuals taking advantage of the situation over the COVID-19 outbreak, the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) announces the arrest of three (3) individuals by operatives of NBI- Environmental Crime Division (NBI-EnCD) on March 29, 2020, in the City of Manila for selling overpriced disposable masks and non-contact thermal scanners. NBI Director Eric B. Distor identified the subjects as CHIRSTIAN E. CALONSAG, MARIE AGNES S. LAURENCIO, and CELINA B. STA. ANA. The operation was based from the alleged hoarding, profiteering and price manipulation of medical supplies particularly disposable facemasks and non-contact thermal scanner of certain individuals. Thus, on March 29, 2020, operatives of NBI-EnCD conducted an entrapment operation that led to the arrest of Subjects Calonsag, Laurenciano, and Sta.Ana in the City of Manila. the operation also resulted in the seizure of 25,800 pieces of disposable facemasks sold for Php 1.2 Million. Subjects were presented for inquest proceeding before the Office of the City Prosecutor, City of Manila for violation of Article 50(j) in relation to Article 60 of R.A. 7349, otherwise known as “The Consumer Act of the Philippines” , Section 5(2) of R.A. 7581, otherwise known as the “Price Act” and Section 6(c) of R.A.11469, otherwise known as the “Bayanihan to Heal as One Act.”

title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: An employee of a telecom company and his companion who sold modems without authority through internet were arrested by agents of the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) in an entrapment in Cabanatuan City last Tuesday. NBI Director Nonnatus Caesar R. Rojas identified the suspects as: RAMON CHRISTOPHER MARQUEZ ROSALES, 27, married, a resident of Bgy. Cojuangco, Sta. Rosa, Nuieva Ecija; and a part-time employee of Globe Telecom; and ANDREW DOMINGO DELA CRUZ, 27, married, and a resident of Bgy. La Fuente, Sta. Rosa Nueva Ecija. Investigation by the Cabanatuan District Office (CABDO) headed by SA Rizaldy F. Jaymalin revealed that a security investigator of Globe Telecom sought investigative assistance regarding the unlawful sale and distribution of Globe Wimax modem through the internet committed by a certain Jay-Ar. To validate the complaint, he was able to transact with Jay-Ar for the sale of Globe Wimax modems. With this development, an entrapment was planned on June 25, 2013. At noon of the appointed date, CABDO operatives, together with security investigators of Globe Telecom proceeded to Bgy. Rizal, Sta. Rosa, Nueva Ecija, the place designated by the suspect as their place of transaction. An NBI agent and the complainant who acted as poseur-buyers met with the suspects and were able to forge a deal for the purchase of three (3) pieces of Globe Broadband Wimax modems for only P2,000. During the deal, the payment (marked money) was handed to Jay-Ar and later handling it over to Dela Cruz who counted the bills. Thereafter, the suspects handed the three pieces of Globe Broadband modems to the poseur-buyers. It was at this juncture that the NBI agent nearby approached and announced his authority and arrested suspects. The marked money was recovered from the suspects possession. Rosales and Dela Cruz were brought to the NBI Cabanatuan District Office for booking and detention. Suspects were found positive for fluorescent powder. Certification from the Globe Telecom Company stated that suspects Rosales and Dela Cruz are not their employees. Moreover, the three pieces Globe Telecom Broadband modems have a value of P18,000 owned by Globe Telecom. Charges for violation of Section 09 of RA 8484 otherwise known as “An act of regulating the issuance and use of access devices prohibiting fraudulent acts committed relative thereto, providing penalties and for other purposes” were filed against the suspect before the Cabanatuan City Prosecutor’s Office.

body: On February 3, 2019 , combined elements of NBI-Counter Terrorism Division (NBI-CTD), NBI-Western Mindanao Regional Office (NBI-WEMRO), Philippine National Police-Special Action Force (PNP-SAF) and Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) arrested HARUB JALJALIS a.k.a. INDAL and PINKY ANI HADJINULLA, members of Abu Sayyaf Group (ASG). The two (2) ASG members were arrested by virtue of standing Warrants of Arrest for multiple counts of Kidnapping and Serious Illegal Detention issued by the RTC of Basilan. These Warrants of Arrest were issued in connection with the Golden Harvest Kidnapping incident in 2001. Both are believed to be members of the ASG-Urban Terrorist Group cell based in Zamboanga City. HARUB JALJALIS a.k.a. INDAL was arrested in a canteen at Lustre corner Evangelista St., Brgy. Sta. Catalina, Zamboanga City while PINKY ANI HADJINULLA was arrested at Southway Mall also in Zambonga City. After their arrest, both are identified by victims of Golden Harvest Kidnapping. INDAL is the brother of arrested Abu Sayyaf member Isjanir Saccam Aminudin a.k.a. Abu Fatima. Allegedly, they have two (2) other brothers who are active members of the ASG and are said to be working closely with PINKY ANI HADJINULLA in doing reconnaissance work in Zamboanga Peninsula. Any plan as to whether they are planning to conduct bombing operation in the Western Mindanao Region is yet to be verified by the NBI investigators. Nevertheless, their capture is considered a significant victory in the Philippine’s fight against terrorism. On February 4, 2019 , operatives of NBI-Anti-Organized and Transnational Crime Division (NBI-AOTCD) arrested KENNETH DONG in Muntinlupa City by virtue of alias Warrant of Arrest. KENNETH DONG had been hiding after an Arrest Warrant was issued by the court against him. DONG YI SHEN a.k.a. KENNETH DONG is the alleged mediator/facilitator of the 602.297 kilograms of methamphethamine hydrochloride commonly known as shabu with an estimated value of Php 6.4 Billion raided by the NBI-AOTCD and Bureau of Customs (BOC) on May 26, 2017 at Hong Fei Logistics warehouse located in Valenzuela City. The arrest was effected by virtue of alias Warrant of Arrest issued by RTC Branch 46. Manila dated February 12, 2018. Other personalities who are related to the case namely CHEN JU LONG a.k.a. RICHARD TAN, LI GUANG FENG a.k.a. MANNY LI, TEE JAY MARCELLANA, CHEN I-MIN, JHU MING JHUN, and CHEN RONG JUAN are still being hunted. They are included in the criminal charges filed by the Department of Justice (DOJ) before the Regional Trial Court of Manila on January 25, 2018 for Violation of R.A. 9165 otherwise known as the Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002. On February 4, 2019 , the NBI-Western Visayas Regional Office (NBI-WEVRO) recommended the charging and prosecution of CATHERINE BERIOSO-CABUGA, SHIRLEY I. BERIOSO, CASELYN BERIOSO-ORTIZ, ATTY. JOSE MAX ORTIZ, P/SSUPT. FRANCISCO EBREO, P/SUPT. RICHIE YATAR, P/SINSP. JAMES ADRIAN ALBAYTAR, SPO2 JOSHUA T. BARILE, PO3 RONALD T. ORTIZ, DOLLY YASA, and JOHN/JANE DOEs. Subjects were charged in relation to the ambush incident that transpired at the junction Murder of Atty. Efren R. Palamares Jr. and injuries of Atty. Erfe C. Del Castillo. Subjects were charged based on the investigation and sworn statements of Atty. Del Castillo and two (2) witnesses. Subjects were recommended for prosecution before the City Prosecutor of Talisay City for the crime of Murder and Frustrated Murder. In two separate operations dated February 6 and 12, 2019 , operatives of NBI-Rizal District Office (NBI-RIZDO) seized counterfeit Mighty and Marvel cigarettes as well as Bvlagari, Hermes, and Chanel perfumes with an estimated aggregate amount of Php 4.5 Million. Items were seized in Valenzuela City and Makati City by virtue of Search Warrants. Charges for violation of RA 8293 (Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines) were filed against Jhun-Jhun Paraguirre, GVL Supermarket/Legarda Grocery, Lilia Legarda (for the counterfeit Mighty and Marvel cigarettes), Ken Albert La Rosa/Kan La General Merchandise/Scent Phil (for counterfeit Bvlagari, Hermes, and Chanel perfumes). On February 7, 2019 , operatives of NBI-Environmental Crime Division (NBI-EnCD) arrested nineteen (19) Subjects for illegal quarrying in the province of Pampanga in two (2) separate operations. The two (2) operations were conducted after the NBI received reports about the illegal quarrying activities in the areas of Dolores, Bacolor, Calsadang Bayu, and Manibaug Pasig, province of Pampanga. Surveillance operations were conducted in the said areas and it was confirmed that at least two (2) mining/quarrying firms namely SAMMI VIBRO and BM MARIMLA PLANT were conducting extraction of Lahar-based minerals in the area near the Mega Dikes River. Surveillance also confirmed the presence of stockpiles of minerals as well as mineral-processing equipment used in the processing plants. Verification with the Mines and Geosciences Bureau (MGB) revealed that both firms are not listed as having been issued valid Industrial Sand and Gravel Permits (ISAG Permit). After confirming the alleged illegal quarrying and mining activities occurring within Brgy. Dolores, Bacolor and Brgy. Calsadang Bayu, Porac, Pampanga, NBI operatives secured all the necessary documents/permits, and conducted the enforcement operations. In Brgy. Dolores, Bacolor, Pamapanga, caught in-flagrante in the actual operation were the laborers of SAMMI VIBRO firm. Arrested Subjects were GI MAN LEE, JEONG SUNMI (Korean nationals and operators of SAMMI VIBRO Firm), JOHN PAUL SUMAT y LAGRIMAS, JORY SABACAN y FELIZARDO, ALBERTO LINGAD y SABADO, JOSEPH DE LEON y LACSAMANA, SANDY VOSOTROS y MORALLOS, ALEX BASILIO y ESO, FERNANDO TOMAS y DUPITAS, TYRON MANALO y BAUTISTA, MARK GLEN REYES y SUNGA, RUDY LIBUNAO y MATIAS, JOEY MADRONA y BAITE, MARCELINO BUNDOC y ISON, and LAMIX ABOGAN y EJERCITO. In the operation conducted in Brgy. Calsadang Bayu, Porac, Pampanga, laborers of MARIMLA firm namely ALFER NUEVA, RODOLFO PINEDA y DELA CRUZ, HIGINIO JAVATE y MATEO, and ENER DELA CRUZ y EVANGELISTA were arrested after being caught in-flagrante conducting the illegal quarrying in the said area. Subjects in both operations failed to present valid documents or permits that will justify their mining operations. Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the Prosecutor General, Task Force Environmental Laws, Department of Justice, Manila for violation of Section 103 (Theft of Minerals) of RA 7942 otherwise known as The Philippine Mining Act of 1995. On February 7, 2019 , operatives of NBI-Cordillera Administrative Region (NBI-CAR) arrested SALVADOR G. COMUYOG for Estafa and Robbery/Extortion. Subject was arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from a complaint against the Subject who demanded Php 50,000 in exchange for the manipulation of the case in favor of the complainant who has Estafa case. The complainant was aware of her two (2) Estafa cases pending before the MTCC Branch 1, Baguio City. When complainant failed to comply with what the Subject wanted, he threatened the complainant that he will ask the judge to convict her in her pending case. Complainant personally met Judge Roberto R. Mabalot who denied all the representations of Subject Comuyog. Complainant then filed a complaint before the NBI. With this, entrapment operation was conducted resulting in the arrest of Subject. Subject Comuyog was brought for inquest and after finding probable cause, the Inquest Prosecutor ordered the filing of information against the Subject and his detention at the Baguio City Jail. On February 7, 2019 , operatives of NBI-Bicol Regional Office (NBI-BRO) arrested KAYE AHNE MARIE PAGAO y METRE for offering PhilHealth Membership Registration and Member Data Record (MDR) with PhilHealth ID for a fee of Php 600.00. Subject was arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from the complaint of Ireneo A. Dacillo, CSIO-LHIO Chief of Philippine Health Insurance Corporation , Camarines Norte Local Health Insurance Office against the Subject. Acting on the complaint, an entrapment operation was conducted resulting in the arrest of the Subject who was caught en flagrante delicto facilitating the speedy completion of transactions for monetary gain or any other advantage or consideration. Philippine Health Insurance Corporation , Camarines Norte issued a certification that the recovered PhilHealth ID is authentic. Case for violation of RA 9485 (Anti-Red Tape Act of 2007) were filed against the Subject before the Office of the Provincial Prosecutors Office of Camarines Norte. In two (3) separate operations conducted on February 7 and 8, 2019 , operatives of NBI-Dagupan District Office (NBI-DADO) arrested a total of twenty-five (25) individuals for illegal gambling. Subjects were arrested in entrapment operations conducted in Burgos, Mangaldan, and Calasio, Pangasinan. All the arrested Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings for violation of PD 1602 as amended by RA 9287 (Increasing Penalty for Illegal Numbers Games). On February 8, 2019 , operatives of NBI-Task Force Against Illegal Drugs (NBI-TFAID) arrested EDITHA VILLACILLO, EDGAR HERNANDEZ EUGENIO, and WILLIAM EUGENIO ILAGAN for maintaining a drug den, possession and use of illegal drugs. Subjects were arrested in an operation which stemmed from the information that Subject EDITHA was using her unit in Sampaloc, Manila as den where shabu is used and sold in retail to some drivers and conductors of Farinas Bus Company. Subjects were arrested by virtue of Search Warrants implemented at #1358 and #1340 Barangay 486, Vicente Cruz Street, Sampaloc, Manila. Two (2) transparent plastic sachets containing crystalline substance, two (2) digital weighing scales, aluminum foils, and several drug paraphernalia used for dangerous drug were seized in the areas. Specimens tested positive for methamphetamine hydrocholoride known as shabu and urine of the arrested Subjects showed reactions indicative for the presence of methamphetamine. Charges for violation of RA 9165 (Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002). On February 8, 2019 , operatives of the NBI-International Operations Division (NBI-IOD) arrested SITTIE AISAH DIAMLA y MANGOTARA, JUSTIN EUSEBIO y SANTOS, CAMILLE KEITH SEÑO y PELAGO, and JR RONDA y PARADO for selling an infant online. Subjects were arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from the information that a group of individuals is using a Facebook page “Legal Adoption in the Philippines” to entice childless couples and frustrated parents to adopt newborn babies. During investigation, it was found out that Subject AISAH, the moderator of the Facebook page, is a pregnant fifteen year old minor, out of school youth and unemployed. Her companion is Subject JUSTIN, eighteen years old, works as a porter and the father of AISAH’s unborn child. Subject CAMILLE is the biological mother of the six-day old child while Subject JR is the biological father. The rescued infant was turned over to the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD). Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the City Prosecutor of Las Piñas for violation of RA 7610 (Special Protection of Children Against Child Abuse, Exploitation and Discrimination) in relation to RA 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act). Subject AISAH, the minor, was turned over to DSWD for custody. On February 9, 2019 , operatives of NBI-Bacolod District Office (NBI-BACDO) arrested AIZA ALINGASA y LEGANAD, JONAH MANGUBAT y CERVANTES, and WARLITO RIVERA y HALEGADO for human trafficking. Subjects were arrested in entrapment operation where they were caught en flagrante engaging in human trafficking. The two (2) other Subjects, HAN SUAN CHANG and MAYRAME ALINGASA CHANG, alleged owners of the establishment LITTLE DARLINGZ BAR were not present at the time of the operation. Aforementioned Subjects were immediately brought to NBI-BACDO for the booking procedures. Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the office of the Bacolod City Prosecutor for violation of RA 9208 (Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2003). On February 12, 2019 , operatives of NBI-Environmental Crime Division (NBI-EnCD) arrested NELSON SANTOS y NICOLAS for Estafa. Subject was arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from the complaint of Lilian Canaleta who alleged that Subject defrauded her by selling high-end vehicles such as Camarro, bullet-proof Land Cruisers, Raptor Pick-Up and Lexus. Subject said he has connection to officials of Bureau of Customs at the Port of Batangas and offered the sale of said vehicles. Complainant was deceived thru Subject’s fraudulent means and was able to amass a total of Php 455,500.00 from the complainant. Acting on the complaint, an entrapment operation was conducted resulting in the arrest of Subject NELSON SANTOS. Subject was presented for inquest proceeding before the Office of the Provincial Prosecutor, Province of Rizal for violation Article 315 (Estafa) and Article 151 (Resisting Arrest) of the Revised Penal Code. On February 13, 2019 , operatives of NBI-Cybercrime Division (NBI-CCD) arrested MARIA ANGELITA RESSA, Chief Executive Officer of online news website Rappler, for cyber-libel. RESSA was arrested by virtue of Warrant of Arrest issued by Manila RTC Branch 46 for violation of Section 4(C) (4) of RA 10175 (Cyber Libel). The case stemmed from the complaint filed by Department of Justice (DOJ) that involves a Rappler article published in May 2012. After proper documentation and coordination, operatives proceeded to Rappler office at Unit B, 3 rd floor, North Wing Estancia Office, Capital Commons Center, Pasig City. Operatives introduced themselves and informed the staff of Ressa about the service of warrant. The staff asked for an ample time for their lawyers to arrive who will accompany Ressa to the NBI. Subject was apprised of the nature and cause of her arrest and Constitutional Rights upon the arrival of her lawyers. Subject was brought before the office of the NBI-CCD where she was properly booked, medically examined, photographed and fingerprinted. A certificate of detention was issued upon the request of her counsels. On February 14, 2019 , operatives of NBI-Dagupan District Office (NBI-DADO) arrested ROSEANN ARAZA y DOLLENTE and JOYCE TORCELINO y MAGLAQUI in an entrapment operation for human trafficking. The operation also resulted in the rescue of JESSICA A CANETE, female employee of JOJO’s Bar and Restaurant. Charges for violation of RA 9208 (Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2003) were filed against the arrested Subjects. Despite the absence of the restaurant owner, ORLANDO FARINAS DOMINGO, he will also be charged for the aforementioned case. On February 15, 2019 , operatives of NBI-Anti-Organized and Transnational Crime Division (NBI-AOTCD) arrested KAIKAI WANG a.k.a. JACKSON ONG, Chinese national, and JUNEROSE TAGUBA for Large Scale Illegal Recruitment. Subjects were arrested in entrapment operation which stemmed from the information that Subject KAIKAI WANG and his assistant JUNEROSE TAGUBA are recruiting Filipina job applicants for China as housekeeper, caregiver and the like. An applicant was scheduled to apply on the above-mentioned date, thus, an entrapment operation was conducted resulting in the arrest of the Subjects. Two (2) recruits were likewise rescued. Certification from the POEA revealed that Subjects are not authorized to recruit workers for overseas employment. Charges for violation of RA 8042 (Migrant Workers Filipinos Act of 1995) as amended by RA 10022 and violation of RA 9208 (Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act) and RA 10364 (Expanded Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act) were filed against the Subjects. On February 18, 2019 , operatives of NBI-Isabela District Office (NBI-ISDO) arrested ARLENE AGUILAR-MARAYAG for Illegal Recruitment and Estafa in an entrapment operation. The case stemmed from a complaint against the Subject who was recruiting workers for overseas employment. Complainant was enticed with the assertions and representation of the Subject, so she immediately inquired for an available work in which she can apply. Subject demanded Php 100,000.00 as processing fee inclusive of visa and plane tickets, complainant then requested the Subject to have a considerable mode of payment. Complainant prepared an acknowledgement receipt to be signed by the subject after she paid Php 30,000 to the Subject but the latter refused to sign it. Sensing that there’s something wrong with the Subject’s manner of recruiting, complainant made some background check and discovered that Subject allegedly defrauded some of her clients. With this, complainant sought the assistance of NBI. Verification was then made and Philippine Overseas Employment Administration (POEA) disclosed through a certification that Subject is not licensed to recruit workers for overseas employment. An entrapment operation was conducted resulting in the arrest of the Subject. Subject ARLENE was brought to NBI-ISDO for booking procedures and temporary detention awaiting for Inquest Proceedings. On February 19, 2019 , operatives of NBI-International Airport Investigation Division (NBI-IAID) arrested MYRLA OLOR and ALI MOH KHALIL TARRISH, a Jordanian national, for Large Scale Illegal Recruitment. The case stemmed from the complaints against the Subjects who illegally recruited them. Complainants were about to travel abroad when they found out that their travel and flight documents are all fake. Subjects were at NAIA Terminal 4 at that time for their flight to Davao to elude the complainants. The latter then sought the assistance of the PNP Aviation Security Group at NAIA to stop the Subjects from travelling to Davao. After which, the Subjects and complainants were referred to the NAIA Inter-Agency Council Against Trafficking in Persons which in turn referred the Subjects to the NBI-IAID. Subjects recruited complainants for overseas employment upon the referrals of Conchita Paculba who is currently detained at NBI headquarters, Virginia Adling and Mel Madera who are both at large. Php 25,000 to Php 32,000 placement and processing fees were demanded from the Complainants and they have been scheduled several times for their departure but they repeatedly failed to deploy complainants. Verification with the POEA revealed that Subjects are not licensed/authorized to recruit workers for overseas employment, thus, placing them under arrest. Record check on Subjects likewise revealed that Subject Tarrish has a standing Warrant of Arrest for Estafa. Subjects OLOR and TARRISH were presented for inquest proceedings before the Prosecutor of Pasay City for violation of RA 8042 (Migrant Workers Filipinos Act of 1995) and violation of Article 315 of the Revised Penal Code. Subjects The other three (3) Subjects Conchita Paculba, Virginia Adling, and Mel Madera were likewise charged for the same offense. On February 19, 2019 , operatives of NBI-Dumaguete District Office (NBI-DUMDO) arrested JOEL SIANGCO JUMALON for violation of RA 10175 (Anti-Photo and Video Voyeurism) and RA 9262 (Anti-Violence against Women and their Children Act of 2004) by virtue of warrant of arrest. The case stemmed from the complaint of Monette Claire Alpuerto y BALANAY who was in an amorous relationship with the Subject. Subject had set up a spy cam in her own residence and purposely to capture the victim naked but had a fight and broke up with him. Subject threatened the victim that he will publish her intimate photos via social media unless she agreed to resume their relationship. Subject then sought the assistance of NBI-DUMDO. Subject later on was arrested at the target area at Robinson’s Place. Subject was transferred to the Negros Oriental Provincial Jail. On February 21, 2019 , operatives of the NBI-Special Task Force (NBI-STF) arrested JOSE A. VILLAFUERTE for posing as Secretary Salvador S. Panelo in Facebook. in an entrapment operation which stemmed from the letter from the Office of the Chief Presidential Legal Counsel (OCPLC) seeking for investigation of individuals who are behind the Facebook account bearing the name, photos, and other circumstances under the identity of Secretary Salvador S. Panelo. In the said Facebook account, all the legal updates and announcements from the legitimate Facebook account of the OCPLC were copied and posted. Results of investigation and statements of the victims revealed that the Facebook account was made to appear as owned and manned by the OCPLC under the leadership of the Secretary with all the faces of the Secretary posted on the account’s wall. Most of the victims added the Facebook account for the purpose of asking favors or questions that only the Secretary has the authority to answer. As they start the conversation and ask for some help, victims were demanded to send money which will be used allegedly as donations to some project or for the good cause that the Secretary is still working, while in fact, there is none. One NBI-AOTCD operative was able to chat with the fake Facebook account using the name HENRY TAN. The fake Secretary Panelo then started to demand money which according to him will be used in his rehabilitation project for typhoon victims in Naga City, and if the amount will be paid, Henry Tan will receive lucrative contracts from the Department of Health (DOH). With this, an entrapment operation was hatched resulting in the arrest of the Subject. Charges for Computer-related Identity Theft, Obstruction of Justice, Unlawful Use of Alias, Use of Falsified Documents, Falsification of Public Documents, Usurpation of Authority or Official Functions, and Use of Fictitious Name Concealing True Name were filed against the Subject. On February 22, 2019 , operatives of NBI-Anti-Fraud Division (NBI-AFD), with the assistance of NBI-CARAGA Regional Office and the 30th Infantry Battalion of the Philippine Army arrested ROGELIO SUMANDO for Murder by virtue of warrant of arrest issued by RTC Branch 29, Surigao City. Subject Sumando was reported to have introduced himself several times as an NBI Agent of NBI CARAGA while accompanying a local politician in some local events. Subject was booked and fingerprinted at the NBI-CARAGA office and was turned-over to Butuan City PNP detention facility. On February 25, 2019 , operatives of NBI-Special Task Force (NBI-STF) arrested VINCENT CAPINIG et al., for murder by virtue of warrant of arrest issued by RTC Branch 158, Pasig City. Seized from the subject was a Baretta Firearm Cal. 25 with eight (8) live ammunition (0.25 cal). Subject was brought to NBI Manila for filling of Illegal Possession of Firearm in relation to COMELEC gun ban. Subject was brought to NBI Manila for the return of Warrant of Arrest as well as filing of Illegal Possession of Firearm. On February 26, 2019 , operatives of NBI-Environmental Crime Division (NBI-EnCD) arrested the top officials of Multifarms Agro Industrial Development Corporation (MAIDC) for aquatic pollution and violation of the Clean Water Act. The MAIDC officials were identified as SANTIAGO CHUA III, ROSALIO ARINGO AGUANTA, JAYSON FRITZ BOLO AGUANTA and JERAMIL SABALA. The case stemmed from the information received that the said corporation was discharging inadequately treated wastewater from their piggery farm into the sea water of Sitio Baho, Brgy. Sangat, San Fernando, Cebu. EnCD operatives conducted surveillance to verify the illegal discharge of wastewater, upon arrival at the area, they noticed the foul odor of animal waste coming from a piggery farm. They personally saw and observed the continuous flowing of sewage/pollutants coming from the compound of MAIDC that goes through treatment facility. Clearances secured from DENR-EMB Region 7 confirmed that MAIDC has no valid permits and clearances pursuant to the environmental rules and procedures. Acting on this, joint operation by the NBI-EnCD, NBI-Central Visayas Regional Office (NBI-CEVRO) with the Bureau of Fisheries and Aquatic Resources (BFAR), Philippine Coastguard and Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) Region 7 implemented the Search Warrants. Arrested Subjects were brought to the inquest prosecutor for violation of RA 8550 as amended by RA 10654 (Philippine Fisheries Codes of 1998) and RA 9275 (Philippine Clean Water Act of 2004). On February 26, 2019 , operatives of NBI-Anti-Organized and Transnational Crime Division (NBI-AOTCD) arrested CARIDAD DOGUILES and MICHAEL E. TORILLO for violation of PD 1602 (Illegal Gambling) in an entrapment operation. The case stemmed from an intelligence report that several persons in the area of Lakandula St. Tondo, Manila, were engaged in the operation of “Bookies” or Horse Race Bettings without license or permit from Games and Amusements Board (GAB). Seized from the Subjects were pieces of materials used for Horse Race Bettings. Certification from GAB confirmed they did not issue any permit/license authorizing the taking of horse racing bets by the Subject DOGUILES. Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor of Manila for above-mentioned violation. On February 27, 2019 , operatives of NBI-Anti-Human Trafficking Division (NBI-AHTRAD) arrested HAN WANG aka LOGAN WANG and FENGPI G YUE aka AMBER YUE, both Chinese national and two Filipinos identified as RICHELLE ATHENA MAXINE LANDICHO y ONELLA and RC CORDERO y JAVIER for human trafficking. Sixteen (16) females, eleven (11) of whom are minors were likewise rescued in the operation. The case stemmed from the report of the Philippine Air Force (PAF) that a minor victim sought their assistance after she was recruited by a certain MAXINE to work for a Chinese national named LOGAN who offer minor girls to his clients for prostitution. After getting the information of the new condo unit where Maxine and Logan were harboring and maintaining the minor girls, NBI operatives proceeded to the area. Seized from the target area were box full of sexy lingerie and costumes, several boxes of condoms and lubricants and believed to be used by the girls during their sexual engagements. Cellphones of the four subjects were also seized as part of evidence. Subjects were brought to NBI for booking requirements and presented for inquest proceedings at Department of Justice. On February 27, 2019 , operatives of NBI-MIMAROPA arrested YOUSEF NOURYOUSEFI in an entrapment operation for Robbery/Extortion. The case stemmed from the complaint of the victim who alleged that she was married to Subject but had been estranged for several years after she could no longer stand the physical and emotional pain she suffered from the Subject. The latter threatened the victim complainant that he will spread photos of their sexual act if she failed to give him Php 350,000.00. Subject demanded money in exchange of not spreading or sharing their sex videos and photos in the internet. Acting on the complaint, an entrapment operation was conducted resulting in the arrest of the Subject. Subject was presented for inquest proceeding before the Calapan City Prosecutor’s Office for Robbery/Extortion and violation of RA 9262 (Violence Against Women and Their Children) and RA 9995 (The Anti-Photo and Video Voyeurism). On February 28, 2019 , operatives of NBI-Special Action Unit (NBI-SAU) arrested Police Officer 1 NONITO BINAYUG for torturing an inmate. Subject BINAYUG, had gone into hiding after being impleaded for violation of RA 9745 otherwise known as the Anti-Torture Act of 2009. Subject NONITO BINAYUG is the younger brother of the police official who was caught on a video torturing an inmate by pulling a string attached to the genital organ of the latter. After the NBI received an information that Subject was seen in the areas of Manila, proper coordination with the local police was conducted and on the aforementioned date, operatives of the NBI-SAU proceeded to the target area in Tondo, Manila. The operation led to the arrest of the Subject by virtue of Warrant of Arrest issued by RTC Branch 1, Manila. Subject NONITO BINAYUG did not resist arrest and submitted himself peacefully to the operatives. On February 28, 2019 , operatives of the NBI-Special Operations Group (NBI-SOG) arrested RODRIGO SABENECIO a.k.a EARL JOHN CRUZ for Robbery with Intimidation. Subject was arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from the complaint received by the NBI regarding the alleged blackmailing committed by the Subject. According to the complainant, she received messages through Facebook Messenger from a certain EARL JOHN CRUZ, which contains a screenshot of album with nude pictures and videos of her. Thereafter, EARL JOHN CRUZ asked the complainant Php 5,000.00 in exchange of not sharing the nude pictures and videos, through Palawan Express under the name of EAL JOHN CRUZ. On February 28, 2019, out of fear complainant sent money to “EARL JOHN CRUZ” through Palawan Express. However, the complainant cannot produce the amount of Php 5,000.00, she was only able to send Php 2,000.00. EARL JOHN CRUZ demanded that the complainant shall send the remaining Php 3,000.00 the following day and assured that he will not share the nude pictures and videos upon receiving the balance. Complainant then sought the assistance of the NBI. Acting on the complaint, NBI-SOG operatives planned and conducted an entrapment operation which led to the arrest of the Subject. Subject was presented for inquest proceeding before the Office of the City Prosecutors of Manila for violation of Article. 294 (Robbery with Intimidation) of Revised Penal Code, in relation to RA 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012). On February 28, 2019 , operatives of NBI-Iligan District Office (NBI-ILDO) arrested ANTONIO RELACION and BELLA RELACION in an entrapment operation for violation of RA 9484 (The Philippine Dental Act of 2007). Subjects are engaged into invasive and non-invasive dental procedures such as impression taking, denture construction, and tooth preparation at their Dental Laboratory without the supervision of a Licensed Dentist. Seized from the target area were seven (7) impression tray, two (2) impression material, two (2) mouth mirror, assorted empty sachets of Alginate Impression Material “Replica Brand”, assorted sachets of Alginate Impression Material “Replica Brand”, one (1) denture teeth. Charges were filed against the Subjects and they were detained at NBI Iligan District Office. On February 28, 2019 operatives of NBI-Cavite District Office (NBI CAVIDO) arrested KEVIN SALGADO by virtue of Warrant of Arrest for Rape. NBI received a request from complainant-victim Keith Madelleine De Guzman for the service of the said Warrant of Arrest. After a reliable information that Subject was working as a helper in a makeshift canteen in Kawit, Cavite, NBI operatives proceeded to the area and Subject was arrested thereat. Subject was brought before the NBI CAVIDO for proper processing. On February 28, 2019 , operatives of NBI-Cagayan Valley Regional Office (NBI-CAVRO) arrested ANDRES BABARAN SAQUING for Attempted Rape in relation to RA 7610 (Special Protection of. Children Against child Abuse, Exploitation and Discrimination Act) and violation of RA 9995 (Anti-Photo and Video Voyeurism Act of 2009). The case stemmed from the complaint of a minor, MARY JANETAGUINOD, who was allegedly being sexually molested by the Subject. After receiving an information that Subject brought the victim at Sunshine Traveller’s Inn located at Tuguerro City, NBI CAVRO operatives immediately proceeded thereat and found the minor victim who was shouting and struggling while the Subject was caught in the act on top of the minor victim. Furthermore, operatives found the Subject’s cellphone on the table that was video recording the happening inside the room before and during the rescue. Charges were filed against the Subject.
