NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION

On February 3, 2019 , combined elements of NBI-Counter Terrorism Division (NBI-CTD), NBI-Western Mindanao Regional Office (NBI-WEMRO), Philippine National Police-Special Action Force (PNP-SAF) and Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) arrested HARUB JALJALIS a.k.a. INDAL and PINKY ANI HADJINULLA, members of Abu Sayyaf Group (ASG). The two (2) ASG members were arrested by virtue of standing Warrants of Arrest for multiple counts of Kidnapping and Serious Illegal Detention issued by the RTC of Basilan. These Warrants of Arrest were issued in connection with the Golden Harvest Kidnapping incident in 2001. Both are believed to be members of the ASG-Urban Terrorist Group cell based in Zamboanga City. HARUB JALJALIS a.k.a. INDAL was arrested in a canteen at Lustre corner Evangelista St., Brgy. Sta. Catalina, Zamboanga City while PINKY ANI HADJINULLA was arrested at Southway Mall also in Zambonga City. After their arrest, both are identified by victims of Golden Harvest Kidnapping. INDAL is the brother of arrested Abu Sayyaf member Isjanir Saccam Aminudin a.k.a. Abu Fatima. Allegedly, they have two (2) other brothers who are active members of the ASG and are said to be working closely with PINKY ANI HADJINULLA in doing reconnaissance work in Zamboanga Peninsula. Any plan as to whether they are planning to conduct bombing operation in the Western Mindanao Region is yet to be verified by the NBI investigators. Nevertheless, their capture is considered a significant victory in the Philippine’s fight against terrorism. On February 4, 2019 , operatives of NBI-Anti-Organized and Transnational Crime Division (NBI-AOTCD) arrested KENNETH DONG in Muntinlupa City by virtue of alias Warrant of Arrest. KENNETH DONG had been hiding after an Arrest Warrant was issued by the court against him. DONG YI SHEN a.k.a. KENNETH DONG is the alleged mediator/facilitator of the 602.297 kilograms of methamphethamine hydrochloride commonly known as shabu with an estimated value of Php 6.4 Billion raided by the NBI-AOTCD and Bureau of Customs (BOC) on May 26, 2017 at Hong Fei Logistics warehouse located in Valenzuela City. The arrest was effected by virtue of alias Warrant of Arrest issued by RTC Branch 46. Manila dated February 12, 2018. Other personalities who are related to the case namely CHEN JU LONG a.k.a. RICHARD TAN, LI GUANG FENG a.k.a. MANNY LI, TEE JAY MARCELLANA, CHEN I-MIN, JHU MING JHUN, and CHEN RONG JUAN are still being hunted. They are included in the criminal charges filed by the Department of Justice (DOJ) before the Regional Trial Court of Manila on January 25, 2018 for Violation of R.A. 9165 otherwise known as the Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002. On February 4, 2019 , the NBI-Western Visayas Regional Office (NBI-WEVRO) recommended the charging and prosecution of CATHERINE BERIOSO-CABUGA, SHIRLEY I. BERIOSO, CASELYN BERIOSO-ORTIZ, ATTY. JOSE MAX ORTIZ, P/SSUPT. FRANCISCO EBREO, P/SUPT. RICHIE YATAR, P/SINSP. JAMES ADRIAN ALBAYTAR, SPO2 JOSHUA T. BARILE, PO3 RONALD T. ORTIZ, DOLLY YASA, and JOHN/JANE DOEs. Subjects were charged in relation to the ambush incident that transpired at the junction Murder of Atty. Efren R. Palamares Jr. and injuries of Atty. Erfe C. Del Castillo. Subjects were charged based on the investigation and sworn statements of Atty. Del Castillo and two (2) witnesses. Subjects were recommended for prosecution before the City Prosecutor of Talisay City for the crime of Murder and Frustrated Murder. In two separate operations dated February 6 and 12, 2019 , operatives of NBI-Rizal District Office (NBI-RIZDO) seized counterfeit Mighty and Marvel cigarettes as well as Bvlagari, Hermes, and Chanel perfumes with an estimated aggregate amount of Php 4.5 Million. Items were seized in Valenzuela City and Makati City by virtue of Search Warrants. Charges for violation of RA 8293 (Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines) were filed against Jhun-Jhun Paraguirre, GVL Supermarket/Legarda Grocery, Lilia Legarda (for the counterfeit Mighty and Marvel cigarettes), Ken Albert La Rosa/Kan La General Merchandise/Scent Phil (for counterfeit Bvlagari, Hermes, and Chanel perfumes). On February 7, 2019 , operatives of NBI-Environmental Crime Division (NBI-EnCD) arrested nineteen (19) Subjects for illegal quarrying in the province of Pampanga in two (2) separate operations. The two (2) operations were conducted after the NBI received reports about the illegal quarrying activities in the areas of Dolores, Bacolor, Calsadang Bayu, and Manibaug Pasig, province of Pampanga. Surveillance operations were conducted in the said areas and it was confirmed that at least two (2) mining/quarrying firms namely SAMMI VIBRO and BM MARIMLA PLANT were conducting extraction of Lahar-based minerals in the area near the Mega Dikes River. Surveillance also confirmed the presence of stockpiles of minerals as well as mineral-processing equipment used in the processing plants. Verification with the Mines and Geosciences Bureau (MGB) revealed that both firms are not listed as having been issued valid Industrial Sand and Gravel Permits (ISAG Permit). After confirming the alleged illegal quarrying and mining activities occurring within Brgy. Dolores, Bacolor and Brgy. Calsadang Bayu, Porac, Pampanga, NBI operatives secured all the necessary documents/permits, and conducted the enforcement operations. In Brgy. Dolores, Bacolor, Pamapanga, caught in-flagrante in the actual operation were the laborers of SAMMI VIBRO firm. Arrested Subjects were GI MAN LEE, JEONG SUNMI (Korean nationals and operators of SAMMI VIBRO Firm), JOHN PAUL SUMAT y LAGRIMAS, JORY SABACAN y FELIZARDO, ALBERTO LINGAD y SABADO, JOSEPH DE LEON y LACSAMANA, SANDY VOSOTROS y MORALLOS, ALEX BASILIO y ESO, FERNANDO TOMAS y DUPITAS, TYRON MANALO y BAUTISTA, MARK GLEN REYES y SUNGA, RUDY LIBUNAO y MATIAS, JOEY MADRONA y BAITE, MARCELINO BUNDOC y ISON, and LAMIX ABOGAN y EJERCITO. In the operation conducted in Brgy. Calsadang Bayu, Porac, Pampanga, laborers of MARIMLA firm namely ALFER NUEVA, RODOLFO PINEDA y DELA CRUZ, HIGINIO JAVATE y MATEO, and ENER DELA CRUZ y EVANGELISTA were arrested after being caught in-flagrante conducting the illegal quarrying in the said area. Subjects in both operations failed to present valid documents or permits that will justify their mining operations. Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the Prosecutor General, Task Force Environmental Laws, Department of Justice, Manila for violation of Section 103 (Theft of Minerals) of RA 7942 otherwise known as The Philippine Mining Act of 1995. On February 7, 2019 , operatives of NBI-Cordillera Administrative Region (NBI-CAR) arrested SALVADOR G. COMUYOG for Estafa and Robbery/Extortion. Subject was arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from a complaint against the Subject who demanded Php 50,000 in exchange for the manipulation of the case in favor of the complainant who has Estafa case. The complainant was aware of her two (2) Estafa cases pending before the MTCC Branch 1, Baguio City. When complainant failed to comply with what the Subject wanted, he threatened the complainant that he will ask the judge to convict her in her pending case. Complainant personally met Judge Roberto R. Mabalot who denied all the representations of Subject Comuyog. Complainant then filed a complaint before the NBI. With this, entrapment operation was conducted resulting in the arrest of Subject. Subject Comuyog was brought for inquest and after finding probable cause, the Inquest Prosecutor ordered the filing of information against the Subject and his detention at the Baguio City Jail. On February 7, 2019 , operatives of NBI-Bicol Regional Office (NBI-BRO) arrested KAYE AHNE MARIE PAGAO y METRE for offering PhilHealth Membership Registration and Member Data Record (MDR) with PhilHealth ID for a fee of Php 600.00. Subject was arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from the complaint of Ireneo A. Dacillo, CSIO-LHIO Chief of Philippine Health Insurance Corporation , Camarines Norte Local Health Insurance Office against the Subject. Acting on the complaint, an entrapment operation was conducted resulting in the arrest of the Subject who was caught en flagrante delicto facilitating the speedy completion of transactions for monetary gain or any other advantage or consideration. Philippine Health Insurance Corporation , Camarines Norte issued a certification that the recovered PhilHealth ID is authentic. Case for violation of RA 9485 (Anti-Red Tape Act of 2007) were filed against the Subject before the Office of the Provincial Prosecutors Office of Camarines Norte. In two (3) separate operations conducted on February 7 and 8, 2019 , operatives of NBI-Dagupan District Office (NBI-DADO) arrested a total of twenty-five (25) individuals for illegal gambling. Subjects were arrested in entrapment operations conducted in Burgos, Mangaldan, and Calasio, Pangasinan. All the arrested Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings for violation of PD 1602 as amended by RA 9287 (Increasing Penalty for Illegal Numbers Games). On February 8, 2019 , operatives of NBI-Task Force Against Illegal Drugs (NBI-TFAID) arrested EDITHA VILLACILLO, EDGAR HERNANDEZ EUGENIO, and WILLIAM EUGENIO ILAGAN for maintaining a drug den, possession and use of illegal drugs. Subjects were arrested in an operation which stemmed from the information that Subject EDITHA was using her unit in Sampaloc, Manila as den where shabu is used and sold in retail to some drivers and conductors of Farinas Bus Company. Subjects were arrested by virtue of Search Warrants implemented at #1358 and #1340 Barangay 486, Vicente Cruz Street, Sampaloc, Manila. Two (2) transparent plastic sachets containing crystalline substance, two (2) digital weighing scales, aluminum foils, and several drug paraphernalia used for dangerous drug were seized in the areas. Specimens tested positive for methamphetamine hydrocholoride known as shabu and urine of the arrested Subjects showed reactions indicative for the presence of methamphetamine. Charges for violation of RA 9165 (Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002). On February 8, 2019 , operatives of the NBI-International Operations Division (NBI-IOD) arrested SITTIE AISAH DIAMLA y MANGOTARA, JUSTIN EUSEBIO y SANTOS, CAMILLE KEITH SEÑO y PELAGO, and JR RONDA y PARADO for selling an infant online. Subjects were arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from the information that a group of individuals is using a Facebook page “Legal Adoption in the Philippines” to entice childless couples and frustrated parents to adopt newborn babies. During investigation, it was found out that Subject AISAH, the moderator of the Facebook page, is a pregnant fifteen year old minor, out of school youth and unemployed. Her companion is Subject JUSTIN, eighteen years old, works as a porter and the father of AISAH’s unborn child. Subject CAMILLE is the biological mother of the six-day old child while Subject JR is the biological father. The rescued infant was turned over to the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD). Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the City Prosecutor of Las Piñas for violation of RA 7610 (Special Protection of Children Against Child Abuse, Exploitation and Discrimination) in relation to RA 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act). Subject AISAH, the minor, was turned over to DSWD for custody. On February 9, 2019 , operatives of NBI-Bacolod District Office (NBI-BACDO) arrested AIZA ALINGASA y LEGANAD, JONAH MANGUBAT y CERVANTES, and WARLITO RIVERA y HALEGADO for human trafficking. Subjects were arrested in entrapment operation where they were caught en flagrante engaging in human trafficking. The two (2) other Subjects, HAN SUAN CHANG and MAYRAME ALINGASA CHANG, alleged owners of the establishment LITTLE DARLINGZ BAR were not present at the time of the operation. Aforementioned Subjects were immediately brought to NBI-BACDO for the booking procedures. Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the office of the Bacolod City Prosecutor for violation of RA 9208 (Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2003). On February 12, 2019 , operatives of NBI-Environmental Crime Division (NBI-EnCD) arrested NELSON SANTOS y NICOLAS for Estafa. Subject was arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from the complaint of Lilian Canaleta who alleged that Subject defrauded her by selling high-end vehicles such as Camarro, bullet-proof Land Cruisers, Raptor Pick-Up and Lexus. Subject said he has connection to officials of Bureau of Customs at the Port of Batangas and offered the sale of said vehicles. Complainant was deceived thru Subject’s fraudulent means and was able to amass a total of Php 455,500.00 from the complainant. Acting on the complaint, an entrapment operation was conducted resulting in the arrest of Subject NELSON SANTOS. Subject was presented for inquest proceeding before the Office of the Provincial Prosecutor, Province of Rizal for violation Article 315 (Estafa) and Article 151 (Resisting Arrest) of the Revised Penal Code. On February 13, 2019 , operatives of NBI-Cybercrime Division (NBI-CCD) arrested MARIA ANGELITA RESSA, Chief Executive Officer of online news website Rappler, for cyber-libel. RESSA was arrested by virtue of Warrant of Arrest issued by Manila RTC Branch 46 for violation of Section 4(C) (4) of RA 10175 (Cyber Libel). The case stemmed from the complaint filed by Department of Justice (DOJ) that involves a Rappler article published in May 2012. After proper documentation and coordination, operatives proceeded to Rappler office at Unit B, 3 rd floor, North Wing Estancia Office, Capital Commons Center, Pasig City. Operatives introduced themselves and informed the staff of Ressa about the service of warrant. The staff asked for an ample time for their lawyers to arrive who will accompany Ressa to the NBI. Subject was apprised of the nature and cause of her arrest and Constitutional Rights upon the arrival of her lawyers. Subject was brought before the office of the NBI-CCD where she was properly booked, medically examined, photographed and fingerprinted. A certificate of detention was issued upon the request of her counsels. On February 14, 2019 , operatives of NBI-Dagupan District Office (NBI-DADO) arrested ROSEANN ARAZA y DOLLENTE and JOYCE TORCELINO y MAGLAQUI in an entrapment operation for human trafficking. The operation also resulted in the rescue of JESSICA A CANETE, female employee of JOJO’s Bar and Restaurant. Charges for violation of RA 9208 (Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2003) were filed against the arrested Subjects. Despite the absence of the restaurant owner, ORLANDO FARINAS DOMINGO, he will also be charged for the aforementioned case. On February 15, 2019 , operatives of NBI-Anti-Organized and Transnational Crime Division (NBI-AOTCD) arrested KAIKAI WANG a.k.a. JACKSON ONG, Chinese national, and JUNEROSE TAGUBA for Large Scale Illegal Recruitment. Subjects were arrested in entrapment operation which stemmed from the information that Subject KAIKAI WANG and his assistant JUNEROSE TAGUBA are recruiting Filipina job applicants for China as housekeeper, caregiver and the like. An applicant was scheduled to apply on the above-mentioned date, thus, an entrapment operation was conducted resulting in the arrest of the Subjects. Two (2) recruits were likewise rescued. Certification from the POEA revealed that Subjects are not authorized to recruit workers for overseas employment. Charges for violation of RA 8042 (Migrant Workers Filipinos Act of 1995) as amended by RA 10022 and violation of RA 9208 (Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act) and RA 10364 (Expanded Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act) were filed against the Subjects. On February 18, 2019 , operatives of NBI-Isabela District Office (NBI-ISDO) arrested ARLENE AGUILAR-MARAYAG for Illegal Recruitment and Estafa in an entrapment operation. The case stemmed from a complaint against the Subject who was recruiting workers for overseas employment. Complainant was enticed with the assertions and representation of the Subject, so she immediately inquired for an available work in which she can apply. Subject demanded Php 100,000.00 as processing fee inclusive of visa and plane tickets, complainant then requested the Subject to have a considerable mode of payment. Complainant prepared an acknowledgement receipt to be signed by the subject after she paid Php 30,000 to the Subject but the latter refused to sign it. Sensing that there’s something wrong with the Subject’s manner of recruiting, complainant made some background check and discovered that Subject allegedly defrauded some of her clients. With this, complainant sought the assistance of NBI. Verification was then made and Philippine Overseas Employment Administration (POEA) disclosed through a certification that Subject is not licensed to recruit workers for overseas employment. An entrapment operation was conducted resulting in the arrest of the Subject. Subject ARLENE was brought to NBI-ISDO for booking procedures and temporary detention awaiting for Inquest Proceedings. On February 19, 2019 , operatives of NBI-International Airport Investigation Division (NBI-IAID) arrested MYRLA OLOR and ALI MOH KHALIL TARRISH, a Jordanian national, for Large Scale Illegal Recruitment. The case stemmed from the complaints against the Subjects who illegally recruited them. Complainants were about to travel abroad when they found out that their travel and flight documents are all fake. Subjects were at NAIA Terminal 4 at that time for their flight to Davao to elude the complainants. The latter then sought the assistance of the PNP Aviation Security Group at NAIA to stop the Subjects from travelling to Davao. After which, the Subjects and complainants were referred to the NAIA Inter-Agency Council Against Trafficking in Persons which in turn referred the Subjects to the NBI-IAID. Subjects recruited complainants for overseas employment upon the referrals of Conchita Paculba who is currently detained at NBI headquarters, Virginia Adling and Mel Madera who are both at large. Php 25,000 to Php 32,000 placement and processing fees were demanded from the Complainants and they have been scheduled several times for their departure but they repeatedly failed to deploy complainants. Verification with the POEA revealed that Subjects are not licensed/authorized to recruit workers for overseas employment, thus, placing them under arrest. Record check on Subjects likewise revealed that Subject Tarrish has a standing Warrant of Arrest for Estafa. Subjects OLOR and TARRISH were presented for inquest proceedings before the Prosecutor of Pasay City for violation of RA 8042 (Migrant Workers Filipinos Act of 1995) and violation of Article 315 of the Revised Penal Code. Subjects The other three (3) Subjects Conchita Paculba, Virginia Adling, and Mel Madera were likewise charged for the same offense. On February 19, 2019 , operatives of NBI-Dumaguete District Office (NBI-DUMDO) arrested JOEL SIANGCO JUMALON for violation of RA 10175 (Anti-Photo and Video Voyeurism) and RA 9262 (Anti-Violence against Women and their Children Act of 2004) by virtue of warrant of arrest. The case stemmed from the complaint of Monette Claire Alpuerto y BALANAY who was in an amorous relationship with the Subject. Subject had set up a spy cam in her own residence and purposely to capture the victim naked but had a fight and broke up with him. Subject threatened the victim that he will publish her intimate photos via social media unless she agreed to resume their relationship. Subject then sought the assistance of NBI-DUMDO. Subject later on was arrested at the target area at Robinson’s Place. Subject was transferred to the Negros Oriental Provincial Jail. On February 21, 2019 , operatives of the NBI-Special Task Force (NBI-STF) arrested JOSE A. VILLAFUERTE for posing as Secretary Salvador S. Panelo in Facebook. in an entrapment operation which stemmed from the letter from the Office of the Chief Presidential Legal Counsel (OCPLC) seeking for investigation of individuals who are behind the Facebook account bearing the name, photos, and other circumstances under the identity of Secretary Salvador S. Panelo. In the said Facebook account, all the legal updates and announcements from the legitimate Facebook account of the OCPLC were copied and posted. Results of investigation and statements of the victims revealed that the Facebook account was made to appear as owned and manned by the OCPLC under the leadership of the Secretary with all the faces of the Secretary posted on the account’s wall. Most of the victims added the Facebook account for the purpose of asking favors or questions that only the Secretary has the authority to answer. As they start the conversation and ask for some help, victims were demanded to send money which will be used allegedly as donations to some project or for the good cause that the Secretary is still working, while in fact, there is none. One NBI-AOTCD operative was able to chat with the fake Facebook account using the name HENRY TAN. The fake Secretary Panelo then started to demand money which according to him will be used in his rehabilitation project for typhoon victims in Naga City, and if the amount will be paid, Henry Tan will receive lucrative contracts from the Department of Health (DOH). With this, an entrapment operation was hatched resulting in the arrest of the Subject. Charges for Computer-related Identity Theft, Obstruction of Justice, Unlawful Use of Alias, Use of Falsified Documents, Falsification of Public Documents, Usurpation of Authority or Official Functions, and Use of Fictitious Name Concealing True Name were filed against the Subject. On February 22, 2019 , operatives of NBI-Anti-Fraud Division (NBI-AFD), with the assistance of NBI-CARAGA Regional Office and the 30th Infantry Battalion of the Philippine Army arrested ROGELIO SUMANDO for Murder by virtue of warrant of arrest issued by RTC Branch 29, Surigao City. Subject Sumando was reported to have introduced himself several times as an NBI Agent of NBI CARAGA while accompanying a local politician in some local events. Subject was booked and fingerprinted at the NBI-CARAGA office and was turned-over to Butuan City PNP detention facility. On February 25, 2019 , operatives of NBI-Special Task Force (NBI-STF) arrested VINCENT CAPINIG et al., for murder by virtue of warrant of arrest issued by RTC Branch 158, Pasig City. Seized from the subject was a Baretta Firearm Cal. 25 with eight (8) live ammunition (0.25 cal). Subject was brought to NBI Manila for filling of Illegal Possession of Firearm in relation to COMELEC gun ban. Subject was brought to NBI Manila for the return of Warrant of Arrest as well as filing of Illegal Possession of Firearm. On February 26, 2019 , operatives of NBI-Environmental Crime Division (NBI-EnCD) arrested the top officials of Multifarms Agro Industrial Development Corporation (MAIDC) for aquatic pollution and violation of the Clean Water Act. The MAIDC officials were identified as SANTIAGO CHUA III, ROSALIO ARINGO AGUANTA, JAYSON FRITZ BOLO AGUANTA and JERAMIL SABALA. The case stemmed from the information received that the said corporation was discharging inadequately treated wastewater from their piggery farm into the sea water of Sitio Baho, Brgy. Sangat, San Fernando, Cebu. EnCD operatives conducted surveillance to verify the illegal discharge of wastewater, upon arrival at the area, they noticed the foul odor of animal waste coming from a piggery farm. They personally saw and observed the continuous flowing of sewage/pollutants coming from the compound of MAIDC that goes through treatment facility. Clearances secured from DENR-EMB Region 7 confirmed that MAIDC has no valid permits and clearances pursuant to the environmental rules and procedures. Acting on this, joint operation by the NBI-EnCD, NBI-Central Visayas Regional Office (NBI-CEVRO) with the Bureau of Fisheries and Aquatic Resources (BFAR), Philippine Coastguard and Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) Region 7 implemented the Search Warrants. Arrested Subjects were brought to the inquest prosecutor for violation of RA 8550 as amended by RA 10654 (Philippine Fisheries Codes of 1998) and RA 9275 (Philippine Clean Water Act of 2004). On February 26, 2019 , operatives of NBI-Anti-Organized and Transnational Crime Division (NBI-AOTCD) arrested CARIDAD DOGUILES and MICHAEL E. TORILLO for violation of PD 1602 (Illegal Gambling) in an entrapment operation. The case stemmed from an intelligence report that several persons in the area of Lakandula St. Tondo, Manila, were engaged in the operation of “Bookies” or Horse Race Bettings without license or permit from Games and Amusements Board (GAB). Seized from the Subjects were pieces of materials used for Horse Race Bettings. Certification from GAB confirmed they did not issue any permit/license authorizing the taking of horse racing bets by the Subject DOGUILES. Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor of Manila for above-mentioned violation. On February 27, 2019 , operatives of NBI-Anti-Human Trafficking Division (NBI-AHTRAD) arrested HAN WANG aka LOGAN WANG and FENGPI G YUE aka AMBER YUE, both Chinese national and two Filipinos identified as RICHELLE ATHENA MAXINE LANDICHO y ONELLA and RC CORDERO y JAVIER for human trafficking. Sixteen (16) females, eleven (11) of whom are minors were likewise rescued in the operation. The case stemmed from the report of the Philippine Air Force (PAF) that a minor victim sought their assistance after she was recruited by a certain MAXINE to work for a Chinese national named LOGAN who offer minor girls to his clients for prostitution. After getting the information of the new condo unit where Maxine and Logan were harboring and maintaining the minor girls, NBI operatives proceeded to the area. Seized from the target area were box full of sexy lingerie and costumes, several boxes of condoms and lubricants and believed to be used by the girls during their sexual engagements. Cellphones of the four subjects were also seized as part of evidence. Subjects were brought to NBI for booking requirements and presented for inquest proceedings at Department of Justice. On February 27, 2019 , operatives of NBI-MIMAROPA arrested YOUSEF NOURYOUSEFI in an entrapment operation for Robbery/Extortion. The case stemmed from the complaint of the victim who alleged that she was married to Subject but had been estranged for several years after she could no longer stand the physical and emotional pain she suffered from the Subject. The latter threatened the victim complainant that he will spread photos of their sexual act if she failed to give him Php 350,000.00. Subject demanded money in exchange of not spreading or sharing their sex videos and photos in the internet. Acting on the complaint, an entrapment operation was conducted resulting in the arrest of the Subject. Subject was presented for inquest proceeding before the Calapan City Prosecutor’s Office for Robbery/Extortion and violation of RA 9262 (Violence Against Women and Their Children) and RA 9995 (The Anti-Photo and Video Voyeurism). On February 28, 2019 , operatives of NBI-Special Action Unit (NBI-SAU) arrested Police Officer 1 NONITO BINAYUG for torturing an inmate. Subject BINAYUG, had gone into hiding after being impleaded for violation of RA 9745 otherwise known as the Anti-Torture Act of 2009. Subject NONITO BINAYUG is the younger brother of the police official who was caught on a video torturing an inmate by pulling a string attached to the genital organ of the latter. After the NBI received an information that Subject was seen in the areas of Manila, proper coordination with the local police was conducted and on the aforementioned date, operatives of the NBI-SAU proceeded to the target area in Tondo, Manila. The operation led to the arrest of the Subject by virtue of Warrant of Arrest issued by RTC Branch 1, Manila. Subject NONITO BINAYUG did not resist arrest and submitted himself peacefully to the operatives. On February 28, 2019 , operatives of the NBI-Special Operations Group (NBI-SOG) arrested RODRIGO SABENECIO a.k.a EARL JOHN CRUZ for Robbery with Intimidation. Subject was arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from the complaint received by the NBI regarding the alleged blackmailing committed by the Subject. According to the complainant, she received messages through Facebook Messenger from a certain EARL JOHN CRUZ, which contains a screenshot of album with nude pictures and videos of her. Thereafter, EARL JOHN CRUZ asked the complainant Php 5,000.00 in exchange of not sharing the nude pictures and videos, through Palawan Express under the name of EAL JOHN CRUZ. On February 28, 2019, out of fear complainant sent money to “EARL JOHN CRUZ” through Palawan Express. However, the complainant cannot produce the amount of Php 5,000.00, she was only able to send Php 2,000.00. EARL JOHN CRUZ demanded that the complainant shall send the remaining Php 3,000.00 the following day and assured that he will not share the nude pictures and videos upon receiving the balance. Complainant then sought the assistance of the NBI. Acting on the complaint, NBI-SOG operatives planned and conducted an entrapment operation which led to the arrest of the Subject. Subject was presented for inquest proceeding before the Office of the City Prosecutors of Manila for violation of Article. 294 (Robbery with Intimidation) of Revised Penal Code, in relation to RA 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012). On February 28, 2019 , operatives of NBI-Iligan District Office (NBI-ILDO) arrested ANTONIO RELACION and BELLA RELACION in an entrapment operation for violation of RA 9484 (The Philippine Dental Act of 2007). Subjects are engaged into invasive and non-invasive dental procedures such as impression taking, denture construction, and tooth preparation at their Dental Laboratory without the supervision of a Licensed Dentist. Seized from the target area were seven (7) impression tray, two (2) impression material, two (2) mouth mirror, assorted empty sachets of Alginate Impression Material “Replica Brand”, assorted sachets of Alginate Impression Material “Replica Brand”, one (1) denture teeth. Charges were filed against the Subjects and they were detained at NBI Iligan District Office. On February 28, 2019 operatives of NBI-Cavite District Office (NBI CAVIDO) arrested KEVIN SALGADO by virtue of Warrant of Arrest for Rape. NBI received a request from complainant-victim Keith Madelleine De Guzman for the service of the said Warrant of Arrest. After a reliable information that Subject was working as a helper in a makeshift canteen in Kawit, Cavite, NBI operatives proceeded to the area and Subject was arrested thereat. Subject was brought before the NBI CAVIDO for proper processing. On February 28, 2019 , operatives of NBI-Cagayan Valley Regional Office (NBI-CAVRO) arrested ANDRES BABARAN SAQUING for Attempted Rape in relation to RA 7610 (Special Protection of. Children Against child Abuse, Exploitation and Discrimination Act) and violation of RA 9995 (Anti-Photo and Video Voyeurism Act of 2009). The case stemmed from the complaint of a minor, MARY JANETAGUINOD, who was allegedly being sexually molested by the Subject. After receiving an information that Subject brought the victim at Sunshine Traveller’s Inn located at Tuguerro City, NBI CAVRO operatives immediately proceeded thereat and found the minor victim who was shouting and struggling while the Subject was caught in the act on top of the minor victim. Furthermore, operatives found the Subject’s cellphone on the table that was video recording the happening inside the room before and during the rescue. Charges were filed against the Subject. title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: PRESS STATEMENT March 26, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI), led by Director Judge Jaime B. Santiago (Ret.), arrested six Chinese nationals and one Filipino for violations of Commonwealth Act No. 616 (Espionage Law), Articles 172 (Falsification by Private Individuals and Use of Falsified Documents) and 178 (Using Fictitious Name and Concealing True Name) of the Revised Penal Code, R.A. No. 10591 (Comprehensive Firearms and Ammunition Regulation Act), and the COMELEC Gun Ban. On March 17, 2025, the NBI, through the Cybercrime Division (CCD), received a letter from the AFP’s Military Intelligence Unit regarding foreign nationals suspected of carrying out covert intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance operations on critical infrastructures within Region III. Apparently, Central Luzon’s proximity to contested areas in the West Philippine Sea, combined with its flourishing economy, creates a favorable environment for the Chinese Communist Party-United Front Work (CPP-UFW) to carry out a variety of covert and overt operations aligned with their geopolitical objectives in the region and the whole nation. Notably, Grande Island, located within Subic Bay approximately 56 kilometers North of Manila Bay, has attracted attention as foreign nationals have reportedly been conducting surveillance activities there. Intelligence report from the AFP revealed that six individuals on the island were closely monitored for engaging in deemed suspicious activities, involving a collection of sensitive data related to “Critical Infrastructure” or data affecting national defense within the area. They were identified as HE PENG a.k.a. NAN KE, XU XINING, YE TIANWU a.k.a QUI FENG/QUING FENG, YE XIAOCAN, DICK ANG, and SU ANLONG. Counter-intelligence efforts disclosed that these individuals were occupying the island under the guise of recreational fishers, frequently lingering at the wharves until the wee hours. However, multiple witnesses reported that the group was utilizing hi-tech drones in the guise of transporting fishing bait – conducting surveillance on naval assets, including those from local forces and allied nations, passing through Grande Island. Due to its contiguity and strategic location, the island allows the group to monitor naval assets entering and exiting Subic Bay during maritime patrols or joint naval exercises in the West Philippine Sea. Verification conducted on the foregoing personalities revealed that YE TIANWU a.k.a QUI FENG/QUING FENG has an outstanding Warrant of Arrest for violation of R.A. No. 8799 or the Securities Regulation Code by the RTC Branch 63, Tarlac City. On March 18, 2025, an eyewitness saw the same group of QUI FENG operating a drone, in the guise of a fishing game, conducting their usual ISR operations towards the Subic Bay. On March 19, 2025, NBI Agents, led by Director Santiago himself, together with the AFP Intelligence Units and SBMA law enforcers, arrived at the target location to implement the said Warrant of Arrest and carry out a hot pursuit operation. The operation yielded in the arrest of the above-named Subjects. Photographs and documents of Philippine and US Naval Assets were found inside the Subjects’ units. Electronic gadgets containing surveillance photos and videos were also seized together with fake documents (BIR) and identification cards. The Filipino bodyguard, MELVIN AGUILLON, was also arrested for possession of an unregistered firearm. On March 21, 2025, Subjects were presented for inquest proceeding before the Office of the Provincial Prosecutor, Bataan for the above-stated violations of law. The arrest follows a series of similar incidents earlier this year wherein foreign nationals were caught attempting to gather intelligence or engage in covert operations. Director Santiago said that the NBI, as well as its law enforcement counterparts, remains steadfast in strengthening efforts to detect, prevent, and respond to espionage activities in order to safeguard national security.

title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: The continuing effort of the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) against illegal activities related to coronavirus or COVID-19 pandemic has resulted in the arrest of a Chinese national in Manila on April 22, 2020, for selling and distributing capsules purportedly as a cure or treatment for COVID-19. NBI Officer-In-Charge (OIC) Eric Distor identified the Chinese national as SHI JIANCHUAN who was arrested by operatives of the NBI-Anti Organized and Transnational Crime Division (NBI-AOTCD) in Binondo, Manila following an entrapment operation. Prior to the arrest, Distor stressed, the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) had issued a statement that there is no registered drugs or vaccines that are licensed specifically for use in COVID-19 treatment or prevention. OIC Distor said that on April 20, 2020, the NBI received an information that there are groups of Chinese nationals who are selling and distributing capsules purportedly as a cure or treatment for COVID-19, which may be ordered via the social media app “WeChat”. Acting on said information, a plan was made for possible entrapment operation by Agents from NBI-AOTCD who were tasked as undercover agents, ordered six (6) boxes of said medicine for a total of P240,000.00 on April 22, 2020, thru the “WeChat” app. A box contains 400 packs, which in turn, contains 24 capsules per pack. Coordination was likewise made with the FDA by the NBI-AOTCD. In the afternoon of the same day, NBI operatives together with a team from the FDA proceeded to the target area for the entrapment operation prior to the 2pm meet with the subject in San Nicolas Manila. When subject arrived in a car, subject informed undercover agents to follow him. Along Madrid street in Binondo, Manila, subject unloaded 2 boxes of the purported medicine. Undercover agents then asked for the other 4 boxes and placed and additional order of 4 boxes then handed P400,000.00 payment to subject. Subject then led the undercover agents to a nearby truck and unloaded the remaining boxes ordered. At this point, subject was informed of his violations and was placed under arrest. OIC Distor stressed that items found and seized from the subject were the P400,000.00 payment including the marked money, 34 boxes of capsules with an estimated value of P1,360,000.00. The packages of the medicine bear Chinese character markings and the English characters “LINHUA QINGWEN JIAONANG”. Distor emphasized that a Certification issued by the FDA states that SHI JIANCHUAN does not have a License-To-Operate and that the capsule is unregistered in their office. Subject was presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor of Manila on April 23, 2020, for violations of Section 11 (k) of R.A. 3720 otherwise known as the Food, Drug and Cosmetic Act as amended by R.A. 9711 or the Food and Drug Administration Act of 2009, and Section 6 (c) of R.A. 11469 otherwise known as the Bayanihan to Heal as One Act.

title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: PRESS STATEMENT November 14, 2024 Director Judge Jaime B. Santiago (Ret.) attended the 92nd Session of the INTERPOL General Assembly on November 4-7, 2024 in Glasgow, United Kingdom. The annual assembly comprises of delegates appointed by the governments of its countries who make major decisions affecting general policy, needed resources for international cooperation and working methods. The meeting covers topics on global partnerships, governance and data processing in addition to general policing capabilities. On separate occasions, the Director signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) between the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) and Norwegian Police Service, and another Memorandum of Understanding Service between the NBI and The Netherlands Police. The said MOU between the NBI and The Norwegian Police Service covers mutual cooperation to combat sexual crimes and abuse of children, while the MOU with the Netherlands Police calls for the protection of children and youth against sexual abuse. These MOUs between the mentioned counterparts will further strengthen its commitment thru information sharing and investigative cooperation and collaboration. The multi-lateral support of other countries has helped our country in attaining another new record and milestone of being the first ASEAN country to have maintained its Tier 1 ranking for the ninth straight year as we continue pursue serious and sustained efforts to combat human trafficking through OSAEC. Director Santiago said that the MOU with the Norwegian Police Service and the Netherlands Police is very timely to fight the rapid and accelerating global problem of high incidence of exploitation of women and children.

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today announced the arrest of an individual in Manila by operatives of NBI-Special Operations Group (NBI-SOG) for Serious Illegal Detention. NBI Officer-In-Charge (OIC) Director Eric B. Distor identified the arrested Subject as NOEMI MAGPUSAO y FRANCISCO a.k.a. NAOMI MAGPUSAO. On August 26, 2021, after almost two (2) years in hiding, Subject NOEMI MAGPUSAO y FRANCISCO a.k.a. NAOMI MAGPUSAO was finally arrested by NBI-SOG operatives in Sta. Ana Manila.

body: A joint team of National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) and Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP) operatives raided a retail store printing and selling fake peso bills and arrested its owner in C.M. Recto Avenue, Manila yesterday. The subject was identified as AERIES S. VILLARUEL with aliases Irish and Aires, 29, of Henry Yang Complex, G/F, 1871 C.M. Rector Ave., Sampaloc, Manila. On June 7, 2012, the BSP received reliable information that suspect Villaruel is allegedly involved in the manufacture/printing of counterfeit Philippine and US currency notes at his rented store in CM Recto Ave., Manila. Operatives went to the store and saw the fake P1000 and P500 peso bills on top of a table and various printing paraphernalia. A test-buy was immediately made. An operative bought from Villaruel a counterfeit one-piece 1000-piso note at the price of P150.00 and one piece 500-piso note at the price of P100.00 On June 18, 2012, a search warrant was applied for and issued by Manila RTC Branch I Presiding Judge Tita Bughao Alisuag. In the afternoon of July 4, 2012, BSP and NBI agents raided the said store, served the warrants and arrested Villaruel. Found and seized were fifteen (15) pieces counterfeit P1000 bills, and other printing paraphernalia. Charges for violation of Art. 166 (Forging Treasury or Bank Notes or Other Documents), and Art. 168 (Illegal Possession and Use of False Treasury or Bank Notes and Other Instruments of Credit) of the Revised Penal Code were filed against the suspect before the Manila City Prosecutor’s Office.

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today announced the arrest of an individual by the NBI-Special Action Unit (NBI-SAU) in Quezon City for illegal practice of Medicine. NBI Officer-In-Charge (OIC) Director Eric B. Distor identified the subject as HAZEL G. PABLO a.k.a. “HAZEL PABLO LANIOG”. OIC Director Distor said that the operation stemmed from a complaint against Subject Pablo alleging that the latter introduces herself as a Doctor of Aesthetic Medicine. The complainant who is a licensed Medical practitioner also added that Subject Pablo had been using her name, signature and physician license number in prescribing post-procedure medicines to her clients in the her clinic named ZSS MEDICARE INC./ZELAH SKINCARE STATION (CLINIC) located in San Antonio 1, Quezon City. Witnesses also stated that there had already been complaints by some clients of Subject Pablo of some botched medical procedures performed to them by the subject. The complaint was supported by three (3) former employees of Subject Pablo. Thus, on August 2, 2021, an entrapment operation was hatched to catch Subject Pablo in the act of practicing medicine. An NBI agent accompanied the poseur-client proceeded to the CLINIC to undergo medical procedure while the other operatives strategically positioned themselves near the area. Inside the clinic, Subject Pablo explained to the poseur-client together with the undercover agent the procedures before the syringe containing fat eliminator substance will be administered. The subject also told the poseur-client and the undercover agent that the cost of the entire treatment is Php 50,000.00. After the preparatory procedures, Subject Pablo informed the poseur-client that she will be injected with a syringe containing the fat eliminator substance. When Subject Pablo was about to inject the syringe, the undercover agent gave the pre-arranged signal to the other operatives. The NBI-SAU operatives immediately swooped in and caught Subject Pablo in the act, holding the syringe. title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: The National Bureau of Investigation today said operatives of NBI-Anti-Graft Division (NBI-AGD) have arrested individuals engaged in fraudulent activities by posing as personalities connected to the present administration. On June 2, 2016, NBI-AGD operatives conducted an entrapment operation pursuant to the request of a local bank against a syndicate asking for donations pretending to have links or connections with then incoming Duterte administration. An unidentified caller falsely represented himself as PETER LAVIÑA, campaign spokesperson of then President-elect Duterte, and asked from the bank One Million Pesos (Php 1,000,000.00) monetary assistance to be used allegedly at a victory party. The said entrapment operation resulted in the arrest of a group of individuals led by a certain JERICO JAY SAUCO. The group was caught in the act of withdrawing the money in San Pedro City. Apprehended Subjects asserted that they were only instructed by MANUEL FUNA JR. and a certain “JAYVEE” to withdraw the money. Correspondingly, they expressed their intention to cooperate with the NBI to determine the identities of the orchestrators of the crime committed against the local bank. Further investigation conducted by the NBI resulted in the identification of “JAYVEE” as one VIMBI FLORES AVILLA. Based on NBI records, in 2012, AVILLA had been previously arrested by the operatives of the INTERPOL Division for allegedly posing as former Vice President Jejomar Binay in order to extort money from a business tycoon. Furthermore, AVILLA had an outstanding Warrant of Arrest for the crime of Attempted Murder, issued in RTC Branch 34, City of Manila, on January 15, 2016. After several weeks of verifications, surveillance, and casing operations, Subject AVILLA was arrested at a restaurant in San Pedro City on March 1, 2017. A cellular phone which was recovered from the Subject during the arrest, was submitted to forensic examination. Based on the conversations or messages found in AVILLA’s phone, the NBI found out that he had committed another fraud by posing as Secretary Arthur Tugade of DOTR, where he was able to extort Php 950,000.00 from a businessman. In view of the alarming circumstances and by reason of the possible magnitude of the crimes committed against innocent victims by this syndicate, the NBI-AGD recommends in-depth investigation in order to determine persons involved in this organized crime as well as to determine if there are other persons defrauded. It is further recommended that the general public be informed with this modus operandi to prevent it from happening again.

body: On April 24, 2020, operatives of NBI-Southeastern Mindanao Regional Office (NBI-SEMRO) arrested RYAN RESMA in entrapment operation for violation of RA 3720 as amended by RA 9711 (Food and Drug Administration Act), RA 11469 (Bayanihan to Heal as One Act), and RA 7581 (Price Act) all in relation to RA 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act). On April 27, 2020, operatives of NBI-Southeastern Mindanao Regional Office (NBI-SEMRO) arrested ELVIE Q. SABALANDE in an entrapment operation for selling overpriced Kn95 facemasks which is in violation of RA 3720 as amended by RA 9711 (Food and Drug Administration Act), RA 11469 (Bayanihan to Heal as One Act), and RA 7581 (Price Act) all in relation to RA 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act). Subject, however, was released on the account of the failure of online inquest currently implemented by the City Prosecutor’s Office. Case will be filed thru regular filing. On April 29, 2020, operatives of NBI-Mimaropa seized 7 boxes of Ginebra San Miguel and 24 bottles of San Miguel Beer Apple Flavor. Items were seized in an operation which stemmed from a report that a certain Marlon Malapitan allegedly smuggle large volume of liquors possibly from Batangas City and sells liquors from his place of residence overpriced more than the suggested SRP. Surveillance and test buy conducted by the operatives yielded positive. On the aforementioned date, the entrapment operation was conducted resulting in the seizure of the above-mentioned items which were bought from the minor son Marlon Malapitan. Items were brought to the NBI for evidence safe keeping and for regular filing of violation of City Ordinance 58-2020 in the City of Calapan, Oriental Mindoro. On April 29, 2020, operatives of NBI-Lucena District Office (NBI-LUCDO) arrested JERECO CRUZ NATAN, GLADYS ALBUNAN PASCUA, MARJORIE RAGO MALABUNGA, and MELODY PRADO MONICIT for selling overpriced ethyl alcohol. Subjects were arrested in an operation which stemmed from the letter of Julieta L. Tadiosa, Provincial Director of Department of Trade and Industry-Quezon regarding Famacia Ni Dok , a drug store in Sariaya Quezon that was allegedly refilling ethyl alcohol at an exorbitant price of Php 130.00 per 500ml. Surveillance was conducted on the aforementioned establishment and it was discovered that JMAN Pharmaceutical and Medical Trading, a business entity owned by Jereco Cruz Natan, who is a franchise of Farmacia Ni Dok has been seling or offering for sale refilled and unbranded ethyl alcohol at prices grossly in excess of those set by the DOH. Test buy was also conducted and after obtaining proof of violations, the entrapment operation was conducted resulting in the arrest of the above-mentioned Subjects. Subjects were presented for inquest before the Inquest Prosecutor, Quezon Provincial Prosecutor’s Office for violation of RA 7581 (Price Act) as amended by RA 10623 in relation to DOH Circular No.2020-0186. On April 30, 2020, operatives of NBI-Southeastern Mindanao Regional Office (NBI-SEMRO) arrested MICHAEL S. JAVIER, owner/proprietor of Success Formula Enterprises for selling illegally manufactured hand sanitizers and disinfectants. Subject was arrested in a follow-up operation conducted after a certain Rey Epis y Mamites was apprehended while delivering illegally manufactured hand sanitizers and disinfectants in Ecoland, Davao City. According to Rey Epis, the source of the items was Subject Michael Javier. In the follow-up operation, the said laboratory was inspected which resulted in the discovery of 509 gallons of antibacterial hand sanitizers and other illegal products with an estimated value of Php106,080.00. Subject Michael S. Javier is presently detained at NBI-SEMRO. On April 30, 2020, operatives of NBI-International Airport Investigation Division (NBI-IAID) arrested ROLANDO RAPISURA JR. y CASTOR for selling unregistered rubbing alcohol. Subject openly sold and distributed Family Care Rubbing Alcohol which it purports to be 75% isopropyl alcohol. NBI-IAID operatives bought 2 plastic bottles of Family Care Rubbing Alcohol at Php230 per liter from the said store. NBI-IAID forwarded the sample to the FDA for examination and the FDA Test Report shows that the sample contain only 44.7% isopropyl alcohol contrary to its representation to be 75%. Upon visit at the store, it was still selling huge volumes of the said alcohol. With this, the entrapment operation was conducted resulting in the arrest of Subject Rolando Rapisura who was caught in the act of receiving the marked money in exchange for 250 pcs (200ml and 500ml) Family Care Rubbing Alcohol at a total selling price of Php 75,000. The FDA discovered that the Family Care Rubbing Alcohol is not registered in their office and therefore not allowed to be sold and distributed in the Philippines. Further, Subject was not issued a license or permit to sell pharmaceuticals in the Philippine market. Charges for violation of RA 11469 (Bayanihan to Heal as One Act) and RA 7394 (Consumer Act of the Philippines) were filed against the Subject. On May 1, 2020, operatives of NBI-Special Action Unit (NBI-SAU), together with CIIS-BOC and Philippine Coast Guard, seized 372 boxes of Linhua Qingwen Jiaonang medicines with an estimated amount of more or less Php 90,000,000.00. Items were seized in an operation which stemmed from an information relayed from a confidential source that some unidentified Chinese nationals are strong smuggled Covid-19 medicines in a warehouse located in Malate, Manila. After verification, on May 1, 2020, the joint operation was conducted resulting in the seizure of the aforementioned items after failure to present the necessary permits and documents of the goods. Seized samples of Linhua Qingwen Jiaonang medicines will be submitted to Food and Drug Administration for examination. On the other hand, coordination with the BOC is already being made relative to the documents pertaining to the illegal entry of the said medicines in our country to support the filing of possible criminal charges for violation of Tariff and Customs Code and Falsification of Public Documents against the owners and operators of the warehouse. On May 3, 2020, operatives of NBI-Task Force Against Illegal Drugs (NBI-TFAID) arrested RAHIM ANDIL for selling illegal drugs. Subject was arrested in a buy-bust operation which stemmed from an information regarding a certain Rahim from Tondo, Manila, who was engaged in selling illegal drugs with the help of some Chinese nationals incarcerated in Manila City Jail. On the aforementioned date, an information from a confidential informant was received that Subject Rahim has with him about 200 grams of shabu amounting to Php 200,000.00 which he needed to sell within a week. With this, the buy-bust operation was conducted resulting in the arrest of Subject Rahim. Found in Subject’s possession of four (4) packs of suspected shabu and 1 heat-sealed transparent plastic sachet also containing suspected shabu. Subject was presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor of Manila for violation of RA 9165 (Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002). On May 5, 2020, operatives of NBI-Southeastern Mindanao Regional Office (NBI-SEMRO) arrested JANET T. PASTOR and GUINILITO B. DUYAN JR. in entrapment operation for violation of RA 7581 (Price Act) and RA 11469 (Bayanihan to Heal as One Act). On May 5, 2020, operatives of NBI-Anti-Human Trafficking Division (NBI-AHTRAD) arrested MARICOLE RAMOS y MENDOZA and ALEXANDER PERALTA y ABAD for Human Trafficking. Subjects were arrested in entrapment operation which stemmed from the report that a certain individual has been recruiting and offering minor girls for sexual exploitation to clients for a fee in Quezon City. Report disclosed that Subject has a Facebook Account with the name Maricole Ramos II. Subject Ramos allegedly offers young girls with ages 14-21 years old to have sexual intercourse with customers in exchange for a fee amounting to Php3,000. Subject was using Trivago, AirBnB and similar platforms to book accommodations (hotel, condominium, penthouse, apartelle) where supposed child trafficking may take place. On the above-mentioned date, NBI-AHTRAD operatives, together with DOJ-IACAT and Social Services Development Department, Quezon City, conducted the entrapment operation which resulted in the arrest of Subjects MARICOLE RAMOS and ALEXANDER PERALTA and the rescue of two trafficked victims. Both Subjects do not also have Quarantine Pass amid the ECQ being implemented in the NCR and Subject Peralta does not also have driver’s license. Charges for violations of RA 9208 as amended by RA 10364 (Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act) and RA 11469 (Bayanihan to Heal as One Act) were charged against the Subjects. On May 6, 2020, operatives of NBI-Dipolog District Office (NBI-DIPDO) arrested RAQUEL LABADLABAD BERNARDO GONZALES was arrested for selling overpriced alcohol. Subject was arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from the information that one of the online sellers in Dipolog City is selling/trading overpriced medical supplies amid Covid-19. Surveillance operations were conducted confirming the said information. The online seller, identified as Subject Raquel, was contacted and she offered to sell several gallons of ethyl alcohol for Php840 per gallon. 12 gallons in the amount of Php 9,000 were ordered and on the aforementioned date, the entrapment operation was conducted resulting in the arrest of the Subject. Seized from the Subject were 3 boxes containing 4 gallons of Nur & Ryvi Ethyl Alcohol. Charges for violations of RA 11469 in relation to RA 10175 and RA 7581 as amended by RA 10623 were filed against the Subject. On May 7, 2020, operatives of NBI-Iligan District Office (NBI-ILDO), in coordination with together with Iligan City Police Station 5 and PDEA 10, arrested RAPCY ONG y SOLON in buy-bust operation at Brgy Saray, Iligan City. Bought and confiscated from the Subject during the operation were 1 pc small size heat sealed transparent plastic sachet containing white crystalline substance believed to be shabu, Php500 buy bust money, 3 pcs small size heat sealed transparent plastic sachet containing white crystalline substance believed to be shabu, 1 pc medium size heat sealed transparent plastic sachet containing white crystalline substance believed to be shabu with an estimated weight of 3grams and estimated market value of Php18,000.00, 1 pc large size heat sealed transparent plastic sachet containing dried leaves substance believed to be marijuana with estimated market value of Php500, 1 pc .45 Caliber Colt, 2 pcs .45 Caliber magazine, 20 pcs .45 Caliber live ammunitions and 1 pc .22 Caliber Black Widow, and 5 pcs 0.22 LR Magnum Live Ammunitions. On May 7, 2020, operatives of NBI-CALABARZON arrested ALEX DAYAO a.k.a. Kamote for violation of RA 9165 (Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act). The implementation of Search Warrant issued by RTC Branch 12, Lipa City resulted in the seizure of several plastic sachets containing white crystalline substance suspected to be shabu and other drug paraphernalia and the arrest of the Subject. Documents and other pieces of evidence necessary for the inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor of Lipa City are being prepared for the filing of appropriate chanrges against the apprehended individual.

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today said it has foiled an escape-attempt of 3 prisoners from the NBI Detention Center led by Rolan “Kerwin” Espinosa. NBI OIC-Director Eric B. Distor said that the swift and timely action of his Agents prevented the escape of Espinosa and 2 other prisoners. Distor added that he commends his new Chief and his Executive Officer (ExO) of the Security Management Section (SMS) for acting with dispatch that resulted in thwarting the plan of Kerwin Espinosa from escaping from the NBI jail. “As soon as they received the info, they immediately acted on it without delay”. He said that on January 13, 2022, the Chief of the NBI-SMS and his ExO received an info that Rolan “Kerwin” Espinosa and 2 other detainees are planning to escape our detention facility thru the hole of the exhaust fan at the ceiling. On the same night, they immediately conducted an inspection of the jail. In one of the cells of the jail, the raiding team of Agents observed a deformed exhaust fan, which when emoved, exposed a hole fit for a detainee to escape. “In view of this incident, security measures at the jail has since been tightened with regular inspection of all jail facilities”, Distor emphasized.

body: PRESS STATEMENT June 27, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } On June 25,2025, joint forces of the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) and the Bureau of Immigration (BI) arrested nine (9) Korean nationals in Paranaque City, for online fraud schemes. Acting pursuant to a Mission Order, operatives of NBI-Organized and Transnational Crimes Division (NBI-OTCD) and Bureau of Immigration-Fugitive Search Unit (BI-FSU) conducted a law enforcement operation in a condominium in Parañaque City, which led to the discovery of nine (9) Korean nationals inside a unit thereat. The Korean nationals were found operating computer workstations that run multiple applications displaying foreign-language scripts and exhibiting user interface windows typically associated with financial transactions and online communication platforms. The configuration and real-time display of these systems raised reasonable suspicion of involvement in online loan fraud schemes. The Korean nationals were identified as HAN JAESEONG, LEE HYUNWOO, KWON YEON JI, PARK KWANGJUN, KIM HEEJUN, JEONG SEONGAE, BAE SEHWAN, RYU JUHSANG, and KIM YOUNGSEOP. The Subjects were taken into custody by the BI-FSU and are currently under temporary detention at the NBI-OTCD office. They will be turned over to the Bureau of Immigration Warden Facility (BIWF) for safekeeping upon completion of the standard booking and documentation procedures. Thereafter, Subjects undergone inquest proceedings conducted by the Bureau of Immigration (BI) for violations of the Philippine Immigration Act (PIA) of 1940, as amended.

body: A man who claims can facilitate the release of a gun ban exemption certificate from the Commission on Election for a fee was arrested by agents of the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) during an entrapment at a shopping mall yesterday. The suspect was identified as RICARDO III VIAJEDOR VILLAFLOR, 42, jobless, and a resident of No. 663 Villa Beatriz, Old Balara, Quezon City. Investigation conducted by the Anti-Organized Crime Division (AOCD), disclosed that complainant, Carlito Edano Jr. who works as a security consultant, was introduced to a certain alias “Ricardo” later identified as suspect Ricardo III V. Villaflor, who can allegedly facilitate release of COMELEC gun ban exemption. Villaflor guaranteed that Edano will be given said exemption for a fee of P5,500 allegedly as payment of the COMELEC gun ban exemptions. Suspect also alleged that this is possible thru the assistance of his acquaintance who is currently working at the COMELEC. With the assurance, the complainant and his other colleagues, agreed to have their exemptions processed by the suspect where they gave their Permits To Carry (PTC) and firearms licenses. Villaflor demanded an additional P9,000 supposedly for the person who would facilitate their papers. Complainants and his companions were instructed to deposit the amount of P45,000 to a Western Union Bank in San Fernando, Pampanga in the name of “Rico Pandi.” After a week of constant follow-ups, a “Certificate of Authority” was handed allegedly representing the COMELEC Gun Ban Exemptions allegedly issued by the Committee on the Ban Firearms and Security Personnel of the COMELEC duly signed by Commissioner Elias R. Yusoph, P/C Supt. Miguel C. Antonio Jr. and BGen. Rodelio V. Santos. However, before the original certificate of gun ban exemptions will be released, Villaflor demanded an additional amount of P10,000 representing “for the boys” of his group at the COMELEC. Complainants gave the amount asked by the suspect. After receiving the said exemptions, they felt uneasy. So they went to the COMELEC to verify the authenticity of the documents. Upon verification, indeed, the documents given to them were spurious. Complainants immediately went to the NBI to file their complaints. While at the NBI, complainant Edano received a call from the suspect demanding an additional P2,000 allegedly for the release of the official receipts. Operatives of the NBI-AOCD arranged an operation for the suspect’s arrest. In the afternoon of February 25, 2013, complainant and suspect meet at SM Manila. NBI operatives who accompanied Edano strategically positioned themselves nearby. Edano handed the marked money to Villaflor. Moments after, NBI agents moved in and apprehended suspect Villaflor. He was subsequently brought to the NBI. At the Bureau, suspect gave his name as Major Ricardo V. Villaflor of the Armed Forces of the Philippines. However, upon verification, it was learned that he is not a member of the AFP. Upon a thorough search, he was found to be in possession of several identification cards indicating that he is a member of the Philippine National Police (PNP)_ and the Philippine Marines. Charges for violation of Articles 172 (1) (Falsification by private individual), 177 (Usuraption of Authority), and 315 Swindling (Estafa) of the Revised Penal Code were filed against the suspect before the Manila City Prosecutor’s Office.

body: PRESS STATEMENT April 08, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } PRESS RELEASE | NBI ARRESTS 5 CHINESE NATIONALS FOR ALLEGED ILLEGAL DETENTION; RESCUES A CHINESE VICTIM Pasay City, Philippines – On March 31, 2026, the NBI-National Capital Region (NBI-NCR) agents arrested five (5) Chinese nationals for alleged violation of Article 267 (Illegal Detention) of the Revise Penal Code (RPC). The operation was initiated based on a complaint filed by a friend of a Chinese national who was being detained. Allegedly, the victim has been held against his will by a certain Chinese national in a residential house in Parañaque City since March 29, 2026. Furthermore, the victim was forced to participate in an online love scam activity by an individual known as “Boss Aping.” He was reportedly beaten and threatened with death by the subjects if he attempted to escape. A surveillance and validation operation was conducted by NBI-NCR agents, which confirmed the accuracy of the information received. Consequently, a rescue operation was planned, and the agents proceeded to the target residence in Paranaque City, leading to the successful rescue of the victim. The operation also resulted in the arrest of the subjects, who were positively identified by the victim as his abductors and tormentors. The arrested individuals were then presented for inquest proceedings at the Paranaque City Prosecutors’ Office for the aforementioned violations. NBI Director Atty. Melvin A. Matibag commended the dedicated agents of the NBI National Capital Region for their outstanding performance during a recent law enforcement operation. In his remarks, he reaffirmed the agency’s steadfast commitment to its mandate, emphasizing that the NBI remains vigilant and proactive in its efforts to uphold the law and ensure the safety and security of all communities. Director Matibag assured the public that the NBI will continue to enhance its operations to effectively combat crime and maintain public trust. #NBIServes

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today said the agency will file ill-gotten wealth charges against former PNP Deputy Director General Marcelo P. Garbo, Jr. and his spouse, Atty. Rosalinda S. Garbo before the Office of the Ombudsman. NBI Director Dante A. Gierran said the NBI-Anti Graft Division (NBI-AGD), which spearheaded the investigation will file today the charges against the former PNP official and his spouse for amassing assets way beyond their legitimate income and for non-declaration of said assets in his statement of assets, liabilities and networth (SALN), which by law is required for all public officials and employees. Director Gierran added that in the course of their investigation, the NBI discovered assets such as various vehicles and shares of stocks of retired General Garbo and his spouse, that were not declared in his SALN. Gierran said among the charges that the NBI will file against retired General Garbo include Falsification of Public Documents as defined and penalized under Article 171 of the Revised Penal Code for making untruthful statements in a narration of facts in his SALN for the properties he failed to disclose in his SALN as established by the investigation, Violation of Section 8 in relation to Section 11 of the Code of Conduct and Ethical Standards for Public Officials and Employees or R.A. 6713, Violation of Section 7 of the Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act or R.A. 3019. For both retired General Garbo and his spouse, charges for violation R.A. 1379 or An Act Declaring Forfeiture in Favor of the Government of Unlawfully Acquired Property, pertaining to the properties presumed to have been unlawfully acquired for being manifestly out of proportion to the lawful income of General Garbo and his spouse, Atty. Garbo. The NBI likewise recommended that a corresponding request through the Mutual Legal Assistance Treaty or MLAT be made with the US Government to determine if indeed Atty. Rosalinda S. Garbo or any member of the family owns a real property in the US and for their eventual forfeiture in favor of the Philippine Government in accordance with law.

body: In line with the continuing effort of the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) against all illegal activities, operatives of NBI-Anti-Human Trafficking Division (NBI-AHTRAD) arrested three (3) individuals for impersonating a Notary Public to clients for a fee. NBI Officer-In-Charge (OIC) Eric B. Distor identified the Subjects as PILLAR TABUCBOC PAROAN, CHERRIE ACOB BARABAD, and ANGELICA ACOB BARABAD. Subjects were arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from a complaint that a certain individual has been using his notarial services/license without his consent. According to the complainant, he was commissioned as a Notary Public in Quezon City for the year 2019-2020. On February 6, 2020, a man went to their office requesting for a certification of a certain notarial document. Verification with his records show that the same was not entered in his notarial books. Complainant asked the said person where he got the notarized document which the latter said he notarized the document near the LTO at Biak na Bato, Quezon City. As part of the scheme, Subject, not a member of the Philippine Bar, has been notarizing affidavits and other documents under the name of the complainant. Acting on the said complaint and information, NBI-AHTRAD operatives conducted the entrapment operation on July 3, 2020. The said notarial services was located at Banawe St., corner Florentino St., Quezon City. The target area was tagged with Notary Public and TPL Insurance. The operation resulted in the arrest of the above-mentioned Subjects after they were caught in flagrante impersonating a Notary Public to clients for a fee. The poseur customer asked Subject Pilar if they have notarial services for Affidavit of Loss as poseur-customer’s driver’s license was lost. The latter answered in affirmative and handed over the Affidavit of Loss to Subject CHERRIE who affixed the signature of the complainant in the presence of Subject ANGELICA. The poseur-customer then handed over the payment of Php 200.00 to Subject Pillar. Operatives then declared their authorities and accosted the Subjects. According to Subject Pillar, her boss is MARIA LUISA SANTOS CRUZ, was the one who has been ordering and instructing them to do the notarial services under the complainant’s name. It was further revealed that Subject Cruz is a paralegal of Viron Transit. Arrested Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor, Quezon City for Usurpation of Authority, Falsification of Public Documents, violation of Notarial Practice Law, Counterfeited Insigna, or Notarial Seal, and Estafa.

body: NBI ARRESTS BIR EMPLOYEE FOR EXTORTION In line with the relentless campaign of the government against erring government employees and officials, operatives of NBI-Western Mindanao Regional Office (NBI-WEMRO) arrested an employee of Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR)-District 93A Zamboanga City for extorting money from a businesswoman. NBI Officer-In-Charge (OIC) Director ERIC B. DISTOR identified the Subject as FLORA SARAU ALBAO, Revenue Officer IV (A) of BIR District 93A Zamboanga City. The case stemmed from the complaint of a businesswoman who owns a bakery and a grocery store. According to the complainant, a Notice of Discrepancy dated April 20, 2022 was served to her stating that she has internal tax liabilities for the taxable year January 1, 2020 to December 31, 2020 amounting to Php 30,716,845.24 and was given five (5) days to present and explain her side on the discrepancies noted by the investigating Revenue Officers. On May 13, 2022, complainant went to the office of Subject ALBAO to clarify her internal tax liabilities and submitted her Purchase Receipts to substantiate her purchases or cost of sales amounting to P90,584,782.83. body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today said operatives of NBI-Special Action Unit (NBI-SAU) arrested two individuals in an entrapment operation in Malate, Manila on Wednesday, for Swindling/Estafa. Director Dante A. Gierran identified the Subjects as ABRAHAM VICTOR alias “George” and HARRY SHOUM TEENESSEE alias “Harry” (Liberian nationals). Subjects allegedly swindled the complainant with Ten Thousand US Dollars (USD 10,000.00) when he gave them the money as initial payment after he was made to believe, through false pretenses, that he was investing in the purchase of chemicals that would purportedly convert special paper money into genuine US Dollars. Director Gierran said the Subjects gave the complainant securely wrapped package supposedly with a machine that allegedly combines a special chemical with paper which turns the paper into US Dollars. However, to complainant’s surprise, the package did not contain a machine but instead contained nothing more than an improvised vault with worthless green colored paper cut in the size of money bills. When the Subjects asked another USD 90,000.00 alleged balance, complainant reported the matter before the NBI. Under strict orders from Director Gierran, the SAU operatives conducted an entrapment operation resulting in the arrest of the aforementioned Subjects. Subjects VICTOR and TEENESSEE were presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor of Manila.

body: The National Bureau of Investigation today said operatives of the NBI-International Operations Division (NBI-IOD) and NBI-Intellectual Property Rights Division (NBI-IPRD) have arrested RODOLFO “BOY” GAMUYAO for the crime of Murder. The NBI said the Subject, RODOLFO “BOY” GAMUYAO, 64 years old, a former Philippine Constabulary officer and a retired Police Officer 3 (PO3) had gone into hiding and has remained at large in order to evade arrest and prosecution, right after the Regional Trial Court, Branch 54, Bacolod City issued on July 1, 1992 a (No Bail) Warrant of Arrest against him for the crime of Murder. Intelligence information disclosed that Subject and his group are engaged in illegal activities such as gun running of high-powered firearms and drug distribution in Region VI. After a series of discreet investigation, NBI operatives were able to confirm from informants that the Subject used to hang out with former PC officers in some areas in Ilo-Ilo, Bacolod and Guimaras. A joint operation of NBI-IOD Interpol and NBI-IPRD was then formed to apprehend the Subject. On April 19, 2017 at around one o’clock in the afternoon, Subject was spotted in the food court of Terra Plaza, Bacolod City taking his lunch with some friends. Immediately thereafter, operatives approached the Subject, introduced themselves and arrested him. After the apprehension, Subject was brought to NBI-Bacolod District Office where he was booked, photographed and fingerprinted for record purposes. In the evening of the same day, Subject was brought to NBI Manila where he again underwent the Bureau’s standard booking procedures. A return of Warrant of Arrest was made with the court in compliance with the Court’s order. Subject RODOLFO “BOY” GAMUYAO is temporarily detained in NBI detention cell, awaiting for the Court’s commitment order.

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today announced the arrest of twelve (12) individuals by the NBI-Environmental Crime Division (NBI-EnCD) in Rodriguez, Rizal for illegal quarrying activities. NBI Officer-in-Charge (OIC)-Director Eric B. Distor identified the arrested subjects as ERICSON CINCO y MAYO, RAUL GARCIA y LOBETANA, WINDEL BUENO y TALAGA, PABLO RIMORIN y GAPASIN, NICO YUNAPA, ROLDAN BONIFE y HONOR, DEXTER COLAS y COCOY, JOJIE MANZANILLO y DE GUZMAN, ALBERT ESTO y COCOY, FERNANDO LOPEZ y CRISTY, RANDY CAGANAN y LORING, and DANIEBOY ALEJANDRO y SALEM. Director Distor said that the operation stemmed from the information received by the NBI-EnCD on August 26, 2021, regarding with the alleged rampant illegal mining/quarrying activities being conducted by certain individuals in Barangay San Isidro, Rodriguez, Rizal. The information also revealed that this group of individuals were extracting and disposing minerals without the necessary permit from the Provincial Mining Regulatory Board of the Province of Rizal and the Department of Environment and Natural Resources – Mines and Geosciences Bureau Region IV (DENR-MGB Region IV). Thereafter, NBI-EnCD operatives immediately conducted a series of surveillance operations in the said area which confirmed the existence of ongoing quarrying operation. A certification issued by DENR-MGB on October 12, 2021 states that there was no valid and existing Mineral Production Sharing Agreement or Industrial Sand and Gravel Permit that was issued for the extraction of materials in relation to the sanitary landfill project in the Municipality Rodriguez, Rizal. The certification also provides that based on the data provided by the Provincial Mining Regulator Board of Rizal, as of 2nd Quarter of 2021, no valid and existing Quarry Permit, Industrial Sand and Gravel, Small Scale Mining Contract or Special Permit to Transport and Dispose was issued in relation to the sanitary landfill project in the said municipality. Thus, on October 18, 2021, joint operatives led by the NBI-EnCD together with the personnel from the DENR-MGB Region IV-A proceeded to Barangay San Isidro, Rodriguez, Rizal which resulted in the arrest of the subjects. The operation also resulted in the seizure of 13 unit backhoe, 3 unit bulldozer, 1 unit drill rig, 6 unit dump truck, 6 unit conveyor belts, 40 M3 S1 manufactured sand and 9,000 M3 extracted / liberated aggregates with a total estimated value of Php 36,465,000.00 . On October 19, 2021, the twelve (12) arrested subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of Provincial Prosecutor of Rizal for violation of Section 103 (Theft of Minerals) under R.A. 7942, otherwise known as the “Philippine Mining Act of 1995”. In Addition, JOSE ALLAN CRUZ y ABARRA (at-large), was also included in the charged for the same violation of the law.
