body: PRESS STATEMENT August 12, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } PRESS RELEASE | NBI RESCUES VICTIMS OF COMMERCIAL SEXUAL EXPLOITATION IN QC The National Bureau of Investigation-Organized and Transnational Crime Division (NBI-OTCD) successfully rescued nine (9) female victims of commercial sexual exploitation in Quezon City. The case stemmed from intelligence information regarding the alleged operation of SPA KYOTO (also known as SPAKYOTO SPA) located in Sta. Mesa Heights, Quezon City. The establishment was reportedly operating as a massage spa while offering female therapists to clients for commercial sexual services through its Telegram account. Surveillance, online investigation, and verification confirmed that the establishment was operating and using Telegram to advertise female therapists and offer “All-In” or “All the Way” packages that included commercial sexual services for a fee. These circumstances established reasonable grounds to believe that the establishment was engaged in Trafficking in Persons using Information and Communications Technology (ICT). On August 05, 2026, an entrapment and rescue operation was conducted by NBI-OTCD in coordination with the Department of Justice Inter-Agency Council Against Trafficking (DOJ-IACAT), Social Services Development Department (SSDD) of Quezon City, NBI Human Trafficking Division (HTRAD). During the operation, undercover agents successfully booked three (3) female therapists under the establishment’s “All-In” package. The subjects verified the booking, demanded and received the agreed-upon down payment, while one Subject assisted in facilitating the transaction. After a pre-arranged signal, the Subjects were immediately arrested, and the nine (9) victims were rescued. Based on the victims’ sworn statements, they disclosed that they were recruited, maintained, and offered to clients for commercial sexual services, and that they accepted or remained in such work due to financial necessity and other vulnerable circumstances. The rescued victims were referred to the SSDD of Quezon City for appropriate intervention. Cases for Qualified Trafficking in Person (Large Scale) under Section 4(a), in relation to Section 6 (c), of Republic Act No. 9208, otherwise known as the (Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2003) as amended by Republic Act No. 10364, in relation to Section 6 of Republic Act No. 10175 were filed against the subjects. NBI Director Melvin A. Matibag reaffirms the bureau’s commitment to dismantling human trafficking operations in the Philippines through coordinated intelligence gathering, sting operations, and enforcement of anti-trafficking laws. https://www.facebook.com/reel/1761876294822848

body: In line with the continuing effort of the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) against environmental crimes, operatives of NBI-Environmental Crime Division (NBI-EnCD) arrested eight (8) individuals for illegal quarrying in Tarlac City. NBI Officer-In-Charge (OIC) Eric B. Distor identified the Subjects as SANTIAGO RENE y YUMUL, ACUÑA, JOSEPH y NIVERA, IBASCO, NORMAN y POSADA, MOJELLO, JEOVY y REVILLA, LAXAMANA, RAUL y DIZON, TORRES, ERNESTO y DAVID, BALAJADIA, REYNALDO y CABRERA, and SANTOS, RYAN y TIQUI. Subjects were arrested in an operation which stemmed from an information that a quarry operation and processing of minerals in Brgy. Telabanca, Concepcion, Tarlac is operating without the necessary permit from the Provincial Mining Regulatory Board of the Province of Tarlac and the Department of Environment and Natural Resources – Mines and Geosciences Bureau Region III (DENR-MGB Region III). Surveillance operation was conducted at the quarry area and vibro plant, and thereat, operatives observed several trucks coming in and out of the quarry site. Trucks coming in the quarry site were going out loaded with minerals. Also seen in the area were equipment being used in the extraction, disposition and processing of minerals. Operatives also witnessed several stockpiles of sand and mineral products (vibro sand) present in the quarry site which clearly manifests that there was an ongoing mining operation. Based on the updated List of Quarry Permits as of January 28, 2020 provided by the Office of the Governor, Province of Tarlac, there is no issued quarry permits in Brgy. Telabanca, Concepcion, Tarlac. In another certification of MGB-Region III, there are only two (2) mining tenements (Industrial Sand and Gravel Permit) issued in the province of Tarlac. On June 2, 2020, NBI-EnCD operatives, together with personnel from the DENR-MGB Region III, conducted the operation against the illegal quarry operation at J2KAT Vibro Sand Trading in Brgy. Telabanca, Concepcion, Tarlac. Upon arriving at the area, operatives immediately noticed a vibro plant currently operating and backhoe equipment extracting minerals from the area. Not far from the area was a truck unloading a mineral waste coming from the vibro plant. Operatives managed to control the driver identified as SANTIAGO RENE y YUMUL as well as the three (3) vibro plant operators and one (1) vibro electrician identified as ACUÑA, JOSEPH y NIVERA, IBASCO, NORMAN y POSADA, MOJELLO, JEOVY y REVILLA, LAXAMANA, RAUL y DIZON, respectively. The site/plant manager and the owner of the lot where the vibro plant and stock pile is located identified as TORRES, ERNESTO y DAVID and BALAJADIA, REYNALDO y CABRERA, respectively. Recovered from possession of Ernesto was booklet of delivery receipt of J2KAT Vibro Sand Trading which is a clear manifestation that they were selling the vibro sand. Indicated in the delivery receipt is the owner/operation manager of J2KAT Trading names MARK JOHN M. GOPEZ. Also apprehended is ANTOS, RYAN y TIQUI, the backhoe driver currently operating at the time of operation. Operatives required them to show a quarry permit or any permits issued by the Provincial Mining and Regulatory Board of the Province of Batangas or the DENR-MGB Region III but they could not produce any. Seizure receipt of heavy equipment and minerals found at the quarry site was made and the total value of the seized items is Php 3,942,000.00. Charges for violation of Section 3 of R.A. No. 7942 (Philippine Mining Act of 1995) were filed before the Office of the Prosecutor General, Department of Justice (DOJ), against the arrested Subjects and MARK JOHN M. GOPEZ, who is currently at large.

Distor identified the Subjects as SANTIAGO RENE y YUMUL, ACUÑA, JOSEPH y NIVERA, IBASCO, NORMAN y POSADA, MOJELLO, JEOVY y REVILLA, LAXAMANA, RAUL y DIZON, TORRES, ERNESTO y DAVID, BALAJADIA, REYNALDO y CABRERA, and SANTOS, RYAN y TIQUI. Subjects were arrested in an operation which stemmed from an information that a quarry operation and processing of minerals in Brgy. Telabanca, Concepcion, Tarlac is operating without the necessary permit from the Provincial Mining Regulatory Board of the Province of Tarlac and the Department of Environment and Natural Resources – Mines and Geosciences Bureau Region III (DENR-MGB Region III). Surveillance operation was conducted at the quarry area and vibro plant, and thereat, operatives observed several trucks coming in and out of the quarry site. Trucks coming in the quarry site were going out loaded with minerals. Also seen in the area were equipment being used in the extraction, disposition and processing of minerals. Operatives also witnessed several stockpiles of sand and mineral products (vibro sand) present in the quarry site which clearly manifests that there was an ongoing mining operation. Based on the updated List of Quarry Permits as of January 28, 2020 provided by the Office of the Governor, Province of Tarlac, there is no issued quarry permits in Brgy. Telabanca, Concepcion, Tarlac. In another certification of MGB-Region III, there are only two (2) mining tenements (Industrial Sand and Gravel Permit) issued in the province of Tarlac. On June 2, 2020, NBI-EnCD operatives, together with personnel from the DENR-MGB Region III, conducted the operation against the illegal quarry operation at J2KAT Vibro Sand Trading in Brgy. Telabanca, Concepcion, Tarlac. Upon arriving at the area, operatives immediately noticed a vibro plant currently operating and backhoe equipment extracting minerals from the area. Not far from the area was a truck unloading a mineral waste coming from the vibro plant. Operatives managed to control the driver identified as SANTIAGO RENE y YUMUL as well as the three (3) vibro plant operators and one (1) vibro electrician identified as ACUÑA, JOSEPH y NIVERA, IBASCO, NORMAN y POSADA, MOJELLO, JEOVY y REVILLA, LAXAMANA, RAUL y DIZON, respectively. The site/plant manager and the owner of the lot where the vibro plant and stock pile is located identified as TORRES, ERNESTO y DAVID and BALAJADIA, REYNALDO y CABRERA, respectively. Recovered from possession of Ernesto was booklet of delivery receipt of J2KAT Vibro Sand Trading which is a clear manifestation that they were selling the vibro sand. Indicated in the delivery receipt is the owner/operation manager of J2KAT Trading names MARK JOHN M. GOPEZ. Also apprehended is ANTOS, RYAN y TIQUI, the backhoe driver currently operating at the time of operation. Operatives required them to show a quarry permit or any permits issued by the Provincial Mining and Regulatory Board of the Province of Batangas or the DENR-MGB Region III but they could not produce any. Seizure receipt of heavy equipment and minerals found at the quarry site was made and the total value of the seized items is Php 3,942,000.00. Charges for violation of Section 3 of R.A. No. 7942 (Philippine Mining Act of 1995) were filed before the Office of the Prosecutor General, Department of Justice (DOJ), against the arrested Subjects and MARK JOHN M. GOPEZ, who is currently at large.

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today announced the arrest of three (3) individuals by the NBI- Western Mindanao Regional Office (NBI-WEMRO) in Zamboanga City for Large Scale Estafa. body: PRESS STATEMENT March 12, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } NBI-NCR NABS CONVENIENCE STORE PERSONNEL FOR SALE OF ILLICIT, UNREGISTERED CIGARETTES PASAY CITY, Philippines – On March 09, 2026, the National Bureau of Investigation – National Capital Region (NBI-NCR) arrested an individual in an entrapment operation for alleged illegal sale of unregistered cigarettes. The operation was launched following an intelligence report identifying a convenience store in a condominium along Roxas Boulevard, Parañaque City for the illegal sale of cigarettes lacking both the required Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR) tax stamps and mandated graphic health warnings. A test-buy conducted by NBI-NCR operatives on March 5 confirmed the allegations. The purchased items featured Chinese characters and lacked the Graphic Health Warnings required by law. Subsequent verification with the BIR indicated that the products were not duly registered and were non-compliant with Philippine tax laws. On March 9, 2026, NBI agents executed the entrapment operation, resulting in the immediate arrest of the store’s cashier. The Subject was presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor of Parañaque for alleged violations of the Tax Reform Act of 1997 (R.A. No. 8424) and the Graphic Health Warnings Law (R.A. No. 10643) NBI Director Atty. Melvin A. Matibag emphasized that these operations are vital for both public safety and fiscal integrity. “The sale of illicit tobacco products undermines our health regulations and deprives the government of essential tax revenues,” said Director Matibag. “We are intensifying our crackdown on these illegal distributions and urge the public to report any establishments selling unregistered tobacco to help protect Filipino consumers.” #NBIServes

body: PRESS STATEMENT November 06, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } In line with the mandate of the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) under Republic Act No. 10867 Section 5, the NBI – Human Trafficking Division (NBI-HTRAD) rescued five (5) minors in an operation conducted in Palo, Leyte, in relation to Republic Act No. 11930, or the “Anti-Online Sexual Abuse or Exploitation of Children (OSAEC) and Anti-Child Sexual Abuse or Exploitation Materials (CSAEM) Act.” The NBI-HTRAD received a case referral from the Criminal Intelligence Service of Austria, indicating that during the service of a search warrant at the residence of an Austrian national for child sexual exploitation, upon review of their seized mobile device, members of the Austrian Police identified communication with a Filipina WhatsApp user (Subject). Forensic analysis revealed that the Subject (mother of the minors) had been receiving financial support from the Austrian national. Chat logs and digital evidence indicated that the suspect had engaged in sexual activities with the Subject’s minor children. Moreover, child sexual abuse and exploitation materials depicting her children were recovered from the suspect’s mobile device. The Austrian national had cultivated a relationship with the Filipina Subject by presenting himself as a father figure to her children. While the mother was away, he exploited their vulnerability and innocence, committing heinous acts under the guise of care and support. On October 28, 2025, HTRAD agents launched a coordinated rescue operation following extensive surveillance efforts to locate the Subject and the minor victims. The operation yielded positive results, culminating in the successful rescue of five (5) children: a 6-year-old female, a 9-year-old male, a 10-year-old female, a 13-year-old female, and a 16-year-old male. The operation was conducted in collaboration with local police, NBI-Eastern Visayas Regional Office (NBI-EVRO), Non-governmental organization partners Exodus Philippines and International Justice Mission, the DSWD-Region VIII, and the MSWDO-Leyte. The rescue of the victims marks a significant outcome in the ongoing efforts of the NBI to protect vulnerable individuals and uphold child welfare. NBI warns families across the country: Do not readily entrust your children’s safety to individuals offering money, help, or affection. Predators often disguise themselves as generous supporters or parental figures, only to exploit the very trust they cultivate. Vigilance, discernment, and community awareness are essential in protecting the most vulnerable members of society.

body: PRESS STATEMENT September 29, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } In an anti- human trafficking operation conducted by the NBI-Cybercrime Division (NBI-CCD), a Chinese national identified as WANG GANG alias Kelvin Lee was arrested by the NBI Agents in a hotel in Parañaque City for violation of Republic Act No. 9208 (Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2003), as amended by R.A. No. 10364, and further amended by R.A. No. 11862, in relation to R.A. No. 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012). The operation stemmed from an intelligence report regarding a certain “Kelvin Lee,” who was engaged in human trafficking activities, particularly the sexual exploitation of women. Lee was reportedly offering women to foreigners for sexual favors for Php20,000.00 per night. Acting on this, NBI-CCD agents, together with the informant, contacted the account of Kelvin Lee through social media. During the engagement, it was confirmed that Kelvin Lee was indeed offering women for sexual services at prices ranging from PHP 25,000 to PHP 70,000. Lee and the poseur customers agreed to meet in a hotel in Parañaque City, where Lee would deliver two (2) Vietnamese women for Php35,000.00 each. Lee demanded a downpayment of Php5,000.00 to confirm the transaction. On September 25, 2025, NBI-CCD agents proceeded to the agreed meeting place in Parañaque City and strategically positioned themselves in the vicinity. Upon arrival at the hotel the poseur-customers were met by a Chinese national later identified as Subject Wang. Along with him were two (2) Vietnamese women. Subject Wang escorted them to a certain unit of the hotel, and after receiving the entrapment money, the agents of NBI-CCD immediately placed him under arrest. The operation also resulted in the rescue of two (2) Vietnamese trafficked victims. Subject was presented for inquest proceedings for the aforementioned violations. NBI Director Santiago commended the agents of the NBI-CCD for their successful operation, leading to the apprehension of the Chinese national.

body: PRESS STATEMENT November 07, 2024 On October 30, 2024, the National Bureau of Investigation – National Capital Region (NBI-NCR) together with NBI-Intellectual Property Rights Division (IPRD) implemented Search Warrants for violation of Sec. 155 in relation to Sec. 170 of RA 8293 (Trademark Infringement) against five (5) premises in Bulacan and Valenzuela. The operation, based on a complaint by Lee Bumgarner Inc. on behalf of Victoria’s Secret, resulted in the seizure of counterfeit Victoria’s Secret products valued at approximately PHP 72,319,500. Confiscated items included empty and filled bottles bearing Victoria’s Secret trademark, perfume solutions, sprayers, and collars. The search was conducted peacefully in the presence of representatives and witnesses, who signed the inventory. Director Judge Jaime B. Santiago (Ret.) commended the NBI-NCR and NBI-IPRD for the enforcement action taken to stop the proliferation and distribution of counterfeit products.

body: On December 5, 2018 , operatives of NBI-Special Action Unit (NBI-SAU) arrested ROWENA URNOS QUIRAY for human trafficking. The case stemmed from the complaint of four (4) individuals against the Subject QUIRAY and certain ERNESTO PAAT who were allegedly recruiting Filipinos to work as tutors domestic helpers in China. Accordingly, after the applicants submit their video tape recorder (VTR), they would just have to wait in the accommodation provided by QUIRAY and PAAT at Balagtas Street, Pasay City until they would be provided with tickets going to Vietnam passing through the immigration line as tourists. Subjects asked two (2) complainants a total of Php 330,000 to hasten their application and payment to immigration officers, plane fare, and fees for their escorts but the promise of employment did not happen. She did not have an employer and worst, she was arrested by the police from their accommodation in China and was imprisoned for two (2) months for illegal entry. Verification with the Philippine Overseas Employment Administration (POEA) revealed that QUIRAY and PAAT are not licensed or authorized to recruit workers for overseas employment. With this, an entrapment operation was conducted resulting in the arrest of Subject QUIRAY. Subject was presented for inquest for Large Scale Illegal Recruitment as penalized under RA 10022 amending RA 8042 (Migrant Workers and Overseas Filipinos Act of 1995) and violation of RA 10634 (Expanded Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2012). On December 7, 2018 , operatives of NBI-Anti-Organized and Transnational Crime Division (NBI-AOTCD) arrested MALONE MORALES y DE LEON for Robbery/Extortion. . The case stemmed from the complaint against the Subject who demanded Php 20,000.00 in exchange for the Certificate of Proficiency in navigation. Complainant was told that he has “pending certificate” because he lacks sea service experience. He was also asked to surrender his Regulation II/4 certificate as it was obtained without the required sea service experience. Further, the matter was referred to the Legal Division of MARINA (Maritime Industry Authority) for further investigation. Subject offered help to the complainant for a fee of Php 20,000.00. When the complainant went to MARINA Legal Division to follow up his clearance, he informed one Atty. Boco about the Subject’s demand. Complainant was then advised to report the matter to the NBI. An entrapment operation was then conducted resulting in the arrest of the Subject. Subject MALONE MORALES y DE LEON was brought before the Office of the Prosecutor, Manila for inquest proceeding for Robbery/Extortion. On December 7, 2018 , operatives of NBI-Special Task Force (NBI-STF) arrested MARY CHRIST PALMA for violation of Article 172 in relation to Article 171 of the Revised Penal Code, violation of Article 315 (Estafa) of the Revised Penal Code and violation of RA 8239 (Philippine Passport Act of 1996). The case stemmed from the complaint of a victim named Chester after he received a call from the manager of the Bank of Commerce informing him that he need to pay a penalty for issuing numerous checks. Victim was dumbfounded with the information received because he never issued checks to several individuals he never had transaction with. He later discovered that his checkbook was stolen by Subject Palma, whom he had cigarette business with. Subject Palma is the one who issued checks to several individuals. Victim also learned that there are other persons defrauded by the Subject either by issuing bouncing checks or by enticing them to make business investments which never materialized. There are also Warrants of Arrest issued against the Subject in connection to Estafa cases. Victim Chester then sought the assistance of the NBI. It was revealed that Subject Palma uses several identification cards with different names such as CIARA FRANCESCA DOMINGO, MARY CHRISTINE LEVISTE PALMA, MA. THERESA DOMINGO, CIARA FRANCHESKA DOMINGO, and MARY CHRISTINE PALMA. Record checks on the Subject verified that there are Warrants of Arrest issued against the Subject by RTC Branch 33, Nueva Ecija for Estafa. Subject Palma was then arrested by virtue of the said Warrants of Arrest and for using falsified IDs and passport. She was then presented for inquest proceedings before the City Prosecutor of Manila for the above-mentioned violations. g On December 10, 2018 , operatives of NBI-Special Task Force (NBI-STF) arrested RICARDO LINSANGAN PERALTA a notorious leader of a gun-for-hire group. From the information that a gun-for-hire group led by Subject Peralta was operating in Central and Northern Luzon and was frequently seen in the province of Bataan, a coordination with the NBI Intelligence and Regional Operations Services was made by NBI-STF operatives for the continuous monitoring and verification of the whereabouts of Subject Peralta. Subject was then monitored in the municipality of Mariveles, Bataan transferring from one place to another to evade law enforcers. In the early morning of December 10, 2018, an information that Subject Peralta was at a farm resort in Upper Biyaan, Barangay Balon Anito, Mariveles, Bataan was received by NBI-STF operatives. Acting on the information received, NBI-STF operatives proceeded to the target area and Subject Peralta was successfully arrested. also has standing Warrants of Arrest issued by RTC Branch 8, Manila, RTC Branch 88, Sto. Domingo, Nueva Ecija, and RTC Branch 83, Malolos, Bulacan for the crime of Murder. There are also published reports that Subject PERALTA has several Arrest Warrants for Multiple Murder, Kidnap for Ransom, Carnapping, and Attempted Homicide. Subject was immediately brought to the NBI main office for the proper booking procedures. On December 11, 2018 , operatives of the NBI-Anti Human Trafficking Division (NBI – AHTRAD) rescued two (2) female minors and arrested one Subject in an entrapment and rescue operation in Market Market, Taguig City. Subject is a relative of the victims, who was offering two (2) minor victims for sexual exploitation and for possession of child pornographic videos and images. The case stemmed from the information received by AHTRAD of the illegal activities of the Subject in connection with the case referred to the Philippine National Police (PNP) by the Dutch Police of Netherlands for human trafficking in 2016. After about three months of case build up in the third quarter of this year and with strong coordination with the local PNP, Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD), City Social Welfare and Development (CSWD), Inter-Agency Council Against Trafficking of the Department of Justice (DOJ-IACAT), and International Justice Mission (IJM) the operation was conducted that led to the arrest of the Subject and rescue of two (2) children ages eight (8) and eleven (11). The minor victims were being offered by Subject to have intercourse with their customers. Victims were taken into custody by the DSWD social workers for after care procedures. Subject was presented for inquest proceedings before the Department of Justice for violations of R.A. 9208 as amended and R.A. 9775 (Child Pornography Law). On December 11, 2018 , operatives of NBI- NBI-Cybercrime Division (NBI-CCD) arrested CHEN YA TING, CHEN CHENGANG, SUN QIAO YAN, WEI BING, LEI SHI FENG, GAO CHENG FENG, LIN JIN, WANG HAI TAO, WU CHENG PIN, RUAN CHENG HUI, GAO FEI and CHEN LONG XI , all Chinese nationals, for operating/maintaining illegal online casino or gambling websites. The NBI received an intelligence report concerning illegal online gambling activities managed by Chinese looking nationals conducting various illegal number game and online casino without a license from pertinent government agency. body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today announced the arrest of three (3) individuals by operatives of NBI-Central Visayas Regional Office (NBI-CEVRO) in an entrapment operation in Talisay City, Cebu for pilferage of electricity. NBI Officer-in-Charge (OIC)-Director Eric B. Distor identified the subjects as MAXIMO BAGUIO MARIOT JR., DOROTEO VALMORIA AUXTERO JR., and BRYAN BURLAOS SACMAR. According to Director Distor, the operation stemmed from the information given by the President COO of Visayan Electric Company (VECO), which revealed that certain individuals are taking advantage of the recent calamity (Typhoon Odette) to extort money from consumers who were affected by the said typhoon in exchange for priority electricity repairs and immediate energization. The NBI-CEVRO immediately conducted a surveillance operation to verify the veracity of the information and was able to confirm that Subject Mariot is demanding money from the consumers of VECO in exchange for immediate restoration of electricity. The operatives were also able to discover that Subject Mariot disregarded safety protocol and would merely connect electricity from any available source. Thus, on January 25, 2022, NBI-CEVRO proceeded to Talisay City, Cebu for the entrapment operation. Upon handing over to Subject Mariot the entrapment money, the NBI-CEVRO operatives immediately approached the subject and effected his arrest. During the entrapment operation, the operatives were also able to arrest the cohorts of Subject Mariot who were identified as Subject Auxtero and Subject Sacmar, who were VELCO accredited linemen. The operatives were able to recover from the subjects the marked money, VECO ID and assorted IDs of Subject Mariot, cash bills, three smart phones, one (1) VECO jacket, and one (1) bundle of VECO billing statements. The arrested subjects will be charged for violation of R.A. 7832 (Anti-Electricity and Electric Transmission Lines/ Materials Pilferage Act of 1994).

body: PRESS STATEMENT March 16, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } NBI AND TASK GROUP SEIZE OVER ₱43 MILLION IN ILLEGAL DRUGS AT NAIA OPERATIONS PASAY CITY, Philippines – The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI), as part of the NAIA Inter-Agency Drug Interdiction Task Group (NAIA-IADITG), successfully intercepted a massive haul of illegal drugs valued at ₱43,149,400.00 during back-to-back operations at the Customs Bonded Warehouses in Parañaque City. On March 2, 2026, the NBI’s International Airport Investigation Division (NBI-IAID) and its partner agencies conducted targeted interdictions at the DHL Express Philippines facility. The operations uncovered high-grade stimulants and party drugs concealed within seemingly ordinary shipments. The task group first identified and seized three abandoned parcels. The sophisticated concealment methods included a shipment from Lusaka, Zambia, bound for Dasmarinas, Cavite, was found to contain 3,596 grams of suspected Shabu (Methamphetamine Hydrochloride) with an estimated street value of ₱24,452,800.00. Two parcels arriving from Berlin, Germany, addressed to a family in Pasig City, yielded 4,046 grams of suspected Ecstasy, valued at approximately ₱5,259,800.00. In a subsequent sweep, authorities flagged an inbound parcel declared as a “Steel Roller,” also originating from Zambia and destined for General Trias, Cavite. Upon inspection and testing with a drug analyzer, the “roller” was found to be a vessel for Shabu. The seizure accounted for ₱13,436,800.00 in illegal drugs. “The successful execution of this operation reflects the agency’s strategic efforts and collaborative approach in combating the illegal drug trade,” said NBI Director Atty. Melvin A. Matibag. “The NBI remains unwavering in its dedication to enhancing the government’s comprehensive anti-drug campaign.” #NBIServes

body: The continuing crackdown of the government against profiteering and overpricing has resulted in the arrest of 2 individuals in 2 separate operations in Manila and Quezon City by operatives of the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) for overpricing medical supply worth P1.422 Million. NBI Director Eric Distor identified the subjects as RICHARD SUAY BELOY who was arrested in Manila on Monday and DR. CEDRIC JOHN SARMIENTO DE CASTRO who was arrested in Quezon City yesterday both in an entrapment operation by Agents of the NBI-Special Action Unit (NBI-SAU) in line with the relentless campaign of the government in the midst of the pandemic COVID-19 now afflicting the country. Director Distor said in the first operation, the NBI-SAU received an intelligence report on Monday relative to the rampant selling of overpriced gun-typed thermal scanners by Jasrich Medical Supply and Hospital Equipment store along Quiricada street, Sta. Cruz Manila. On the same date, the store was placed under close monitoring. Distor added that validation made by NBI-SAU revealed that the gun-type thermal scanner is being sold by said store at P7,500.00 per unit as against its actual cost of around P500.00 to P1035.00 in the local market. Due, however, to extreme demand caused by the recent viral infection, thermal scanners have gone scarce, Distor stressed. Under strict orders, an entrapment operation was hatched on the same day with marked money dated, pre-marked and inserted at the bills comprising of P127,500.00 for the purchase of thermal scanners. At about 1:30 in the afternoon of the same day, after coordinating with the local PNP, NBI-SAU operatives proceeded to the said store. A poseur-customer asked to purchase 17 units of thermal scanner for P7,500.00 each or a total of P127,500.00. After handing over the amount, the NBI operatives declared their authority and placed subject RICHARD SUAY BELOY under arrest. In the second operation, Director Distor said NBI-SAU received a report relative to the alleged sale through social media of overpriced gun-type thermal scanner by a certain DR. CEDRIC SARMIENTO DE CASTRO, in violation of R.A. No. 7581 (The Price Act) as amended and R.A. 7394 (The Consumer Act). An Agent of the NBI acted as poseur-customer and initiated communication with the subject, and had to use an account that is a member in the restricted Facebook group, “N95 mask surgical mask supplier”. The poseur-customer was able to receive a reply which reads: “9,300 per unit. The communication continued and ended with an arrangement for the sale of 150 pieces of thermal scanners for P9,300.00 each or a total of P1,395,000.00, which can be picked up in the subject’s address at 95, 13 th street, Mariana, Quezon City. Interestingly, subject introduced herself as a Doctor who said that the thermal scanners she is selling are excess of those she donated to hospitals. Accordingly, Distor said, an entrapment operation was hatched. After coordination with the local police, SAU operatives proceeded to the area and as soon as the poseur-customer handed over the entrapment money to the subject, declared their authority and placed the subject under arrest. The subject was identified as Dr. CEDRIC JOHN SARMIENTO DE CASTRO, a registered Physician with the Professional Regulations Commission (PRC). She claimed that she is involved in fund-raising efforts that aims to help those in need The arrested subjects in the 2 operations have been charged for violation of Section 5 (2) (Profiteering) of R.A. 7581 in relation to R.A. 10623 otherwise known as the Price Act of the Philippines as penalized under Section 15 in relation to DTI Memorandum Circular No. 20-07 dated March 19, 2020; and violation of Art. 52 (b) of R.A. 7394 otherwise known as the Consumer Act of the Philippines as penalized under Art. 60 in relation to Art. 14 (7) of the Revised Penal Code will be filed against the subject. Director Distor stressed “it is deeply saddening and at the same time disturbing that there are people who would be involved in such a heartless act of profiteering at a critical time such as now.” Distor emphasized “This is the time when people should be displaying acts of kindness in order to help each other to alleviate the struggle we have to face in fighting the dreaded disease, COVID-19, which have claimed thousands of lives throughout the globe.”

body: PRESS STATEMENT May 07, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } PRESS RELEASE | NBI RECEIVES SWORN STATEMENTS OF PDAF STATE WITNESSES CONTRADICTING CLAIMS OF ATTY. LEVITO BALIGOD Pasay City, Philippines — The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) confirmed that it received sworn statements from Marina C. Sula and Mary Arlene B. Baltazar, both state witnesses under the Witness Protection Program (WPP) of the Department of Justice (DOJ) in connection with the Priority Development Assistance Fund (PDAF) or “Napoles PDAF” plunder cases. The sworn statements were formally transmitted to the Office of the NBI Director through counsel following recent public statements allegedly made by Atty. Levito Baligod claiming that he supposedly resigned as counsel for whistleblower Benhur Luy in 2014 due to disagreements with the administration’s alleged “selective prosecution” of politicians involved in the PDAF scam. In their affidavits, Sula and Baltazar disputed these claims and asserted that they did not witness any disagreement between the DOJ and the NBI regarding the prosecution of personalities implicated in the PDAF cases. The two witnesses further claimed that Atty. Baligod’s services as counsel for Benhur Luy and Merlina Suñas were allegedly terminated, contrary to public claims that he voluntarily resigned over issues involving “selective justice.” The affidavits also contained allegations that Atty. Baligod allegedly exercised influence in identifying which lawmakers would supposedly be included in succeeding investigations related to the PDAF scam. According to the witnesses, they are executing the sworn statements to correct what they described as misleading claims and to remove any aspersions cast against government agencies involved in the investigation. The NBI emphasized that the sworn statements now form part of official records received by the Bureau and will be evaluated in accordance with existing laws, rules, and procedures. “The Bureau remains committed to the impartial investigation of cases based solely on evidence, sworn testimony, and due process,” NBI Director Atty. Melvin Matibag said.

body: PRESS STATEMENT January 31, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } The National Bureau of Investigation – Cebu District Office (NBI-CEBDO), under the guidance of NBI Director JUDGE JAIME B. SANTIAGO (Ret.) arrested BRIAN ANTHONY SAVELLON for violations of R.A. No. 10883 (New Anti-Carnapping Act of 2016), Article 315 (Estafa) of the Revised Penal Code (RPC), Article 172 (Falsification) of the RPC. The case stemmed from a complaint filed against Subject SA VELLON and a certain Richard Cupin regarding the six (6) vehicles owned by the Complainant, which were entrusted to the Subjects for his car rental business. However, the said vehicles were either sold and mortgaged by Subjects SAVELLON and CUPIN to interested buyers without the knowledge of the Complainant. Investigation conducted by the Agents of NBI-CEBDO revealed that the buyers of the subject vehicles transported the same in their respective provinces in Cotabato City, Zamboanga City, Talisay City and the Province of Bohol. Subsequently, Subject SAVELLON submitted himself voluntarily for investigation before the NBI and executed an Extra-Judicial Confession admitting his participation to the crime. Thus, a follow-up investigation was conducted by the Agents of NBI-CEBDO, which resulted in the recovery of one (1) Mitsubishi Montero Sports vehicle found in Talisay Cebu that was mortgaged by Subject SA VELLON. Meanwhile, the Complainant informed the Agents that one (1) of the carnapped vehicle, a Toyota Grandia Van, was brought to the Province of Bohol, which was monitored by the Complainant through a tracking device installed to the vehicle. On January 15, 2025, the Agents of the NBI-CEBDO together with the Complainant proceeded to the Province of Bohol and with the assistance from the Agents of NBI-BOHDO, the said vehicle was recovered at the town of Carmen, Bohol. The buyer of the recovered Toyota Grandia Van, appeared before the office of NBI-BOHDO and voluntarily submitted the falsified documents pertaining to the sale of the vehicle and informed the Agents his intention to file a case against the seller Subject SAVELLON. Director Santiago lauded the Agents of NBI-CEBDO and NBI-BOHDO for the successful operation, which resulted in the arrest of the Subject and recovery of the carnapped vehicles.

The suspect is identified by NBI Director Virgilio L. Mendez as: ROBERTO TUPAS GALON, 22 years old and a resident of No. 290 Joseph Street, Annex 41, Barangay Sun Valley, Paranaque City. According to the investigation report by the Criminal Intelligence Division headed by HA Romy Bon Huy Lim disclosed that an intelligence information from an undercover agent revealed that a Mercedez Benz Sedan is offered to him for a cheaper price. Knowing that such car is an expensive one, he made verifications with LTO and found out that the owner of the said car is one AMITH CHANDARAMANI, of Corinthian Gardens, Quezon City and the car is carnapped. On July 9, 2014, a joint operation by agents of Criminal Intelligence Division and Anti-Organized and Transnational Crime-Anti-Illegal Drug Unit is planned and materialized. Subject ROBERTO GALON was arrested by operatives of CRID-AOTCD-AIDU operatives along Espiritu Street, Parkview Homes, Sun Valley, Paranaque City while in the act of selling a carnapped color black Mercedez Benz Sedan to an undercover NBI Agent, who acted as the poseur-buyer. Investigation disclosed that on on June 15, 2014 at around 2:30 a.m., a color black Mercedez Benz Sedan (with Plate Nos. AAA 06) was forcibly taken by two (2) males at gun point from two (2) female print and commercial models along Aguirre Avenue, BF Homes, Paranaque City. The victims went to the NBI Office and identified subject ROBERTO GALON as one of the suspects in the said carnapping incident. Victim positively Subject because he wore the same polo shirt when they carnapped the vehicle. One of the victim is the fiancée of the owner of the car. Subject ROBERTO GALON is recommended to be charged with violation of R.A. 6539, otherwise known as the Anti-Carnapping Act before the Office of the City Prosecutor of Paranaque. Presently subject is detained at the NBI Jail and faces a possible imprisonment of 30 years if convicted.

title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: PRESS STATEMENT February 18, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } NBI Joins Presidential Task Force on Media Security; Formalizes Partnership in Ceremonial MOA Signing PASAY CITY, Philippines – In a significant move to strengthen the protection of press freedom, the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) officially formalized its membership in the Presidential Task Force on Media Security (PTFoMS) through a ceremonial Memorandum of Agreement (MOA) signing held today at the NBI Headquarters. The event marks a reinforced government front against violence and threats directed at the press. Following the ceremony, the NBI hosted the 1st Inter-Agency Meeting of the year, convening various stakeholders to align strategies for the protection of media practitioners. The MOA establishes a robust framework designed to enhance the protection of media practitioners through several key initiatives. It prioritizes seamless information exchange to facilitate the sharing of critical data relevant to media-related cases, while simultaneously strengthening joint investigation efforts to ensure that violations against journalists are handled with speed, impartiality, and comprehensive oversight. Furthermore, the agreement focuses on resource integration by leveraging the NBI’s specialized investigative expertise to fully support and advance the Task Force’s mandate. NBI Acting Director Atty. Angelito DLP. Magno has designated its Investigation Service (OADINVS), Homicide Division (NBI-HD), and Public Relations and Information Division (NBI-PRID) to lead the charge. A dedicated Focal Person has also been appointed to oversee case monitoring and liaison efforts with other PTFoMS member agencies. With the Bureau’s inclusion in the PTFoMS, the NBI remains proactive, firm, and committed in its mandate to protect press freedom and uphold justice for members of the media,” said NBI Acting Director Atty. Angelito Magno. He further emphasized that under Republic Act No. 10867 (The NBI Reorganization and Modernization Act), the Bureau maintains specific jurisdiction over the investigation of media-related killings, ensuring that such crimes are met with the full force of the law. The inclusion of the NBI—the country’s premier investigative body—is seen as a critical step in addressing the culture of impunity. By integrating the Bureau’s forensic and investigative capabilities with the PTFoMS’s oversight, the government aims to fast-track the resolution of high-profile cases involving media workers. #NBIServes

body: PRESS STATEMENT March 14, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } In line with the directive from National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Director Judge Jaime B. Santiago to intensify the campaign against sexual exploitation of children, the NBI – National Capital Region (NBI-NCR) has arrested an individual in Botolan, Zambales for violating several laws. These include paragraphs (a), (c), (g), and (e) of R.A. No. 11930 (Anti-Online Abuse and Exploitation of Children); Qualified Human Trafficking under Republic Act No. 9208 (Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2003), as amended by R.A. No. 10364; Republic Act No. 7610 (Child Abuse Law); and Section 12 (Possession of Equipment, Instrument, Apparatus, and Other Paraphernalia for Dangerous Drugs) and Section 15 (Use of Dangerous Drugs) under Republic Act No. 9165 (Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002). The operation was based on an intelligence report about a specific social media account on Telegram that promoted a live show featuring a minor as young as four years old, with fees ranging from $50.00 to $150.00. Verification revealed that a similar case is currently under investigation by the Philippine Internet Crimes Against Children Center (PICACC), which was referred by the National Crime Agency of the United Kingdom. Agents from the NBI-NCR successfully obtained the Telegram account used by the subject in the online sexual exploitation of children. The NBI-NCR agents communicated with the Subject via Telegram and received two videos. In the first video, two (2) children are being forced to give oral sex to an adult male, while the second video showed a child around 5 years old lying on a bed with a male standing over him while masturbating and ejaculates on the child’s face and body. The Telegram user even encourages the NBI asset the idea of a live show involving his own daughter. The agents from the NBI-NCR confirmed the identity of a Telegram user through online surveillance and conversations. The NBI undercover agent agreed to send a package to the Telegram user, who in turn provided his address. To prove he was not a scammer, the user even sent a photo of his driver’s license. After establishing the identity of the Subject and identification of his residential address, the agents of NBI-NCR applied for a Warrant to Search Seize and Examine Computer Data (WSSECD), which was granted by the RTC Branch 70, Iba Zambales. On March 11, 2025, agents of the NBI-NCR conducted a WSSECD operation at the premises of the subject, leading to his arrest and the rescue of six victims. Among those rescued were the subject’s wife, their two minor children, and three of the wife’s siblings, two of whom are also minors. An onsite preview was conducted by the NBI agents on the phone of the Subject, which revealed that the phone’s number was the same number used by the Subject’s Telegram account. Also found in the cellular phone were several videos showing foreigner minors who are being abused by male adults. The NBI agents recovered several items from the subject, including suspected marijuana leaves and drug paraphernalia. They also found cellular phones, a GCash Visa card, an X-Pay Quadx Visa card, a Komo Visa card, a Go Rewards debit card from Union Bank, a green card, one Paymaya Visa card, and a driver’s license. The arrested individual was brought before the Department of Justice in Manila for inquest proceedings regarding the aforementioned violations. Director Santiago commended the agents of NBI-NCR for the successful rescue of the victims and arrest of the Subject.

title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: The NBI today said its operatives have arrested Atty. CAMILO L. SABIO, former Chairman of the Presidential Commission on Good Government, at his residence in Quezon City last Friday, June 5, 2020. The arrest of Sabio by Agents of the NBI-Technical Intelligence Division (NBI-TID) was based on a Bench Warrant of Arrest issued by the Fourth Division of the Sandiganbayan in relation to the execution of judgment in one of the criminal cases pending before the court. The Warrant orders the law enforcement agency to “Arrest the person of Camilo L. Sabio who may be found at 48-B Biak na Bato street, Sta. Mesa Heights, Quezon City and bring him before this Court to be dealt with as the law and Rules of Court direct”. After the usual booking proedures at the NBI head office, Sabio was brought to the Sandiganbayan in the afternoon of the same day. The Sandiganbayan, however, was temporarily closed due to the sanitation of the area because of COVID-19. Sabio was then returned to the NBI detention center. He will be presented before the Sandiganbayan on Monday. The 83-year old Sabio, who chaired the PCGG in 2005 up to 2010, has a number of graft charges pending before the Sandiganbayan for Violation of the Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act allegedly committed during his stint at the PCGG.

title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today announces the arrest of two (2) individuals in Teachers Village in Quezon City in an operation that resulted in the seizure of various illegal drugs. NBI OIC-Director Eric B. Distor identified the Subjects as RAMON LOARCA and WILSON DE LARA APALISOC. Loarca is an American citizen but re-acquired his Filipino citizenship while Apalisoc is a Filipino citizen. OIC-Director Distor said that based on intelligence information received by the NBI, a house in Teachers Village was allegedly used as haven for drug users by its owner, a retired serviceman of the U.S. Air Force. Distor stressed that discreet monitoring was immediately conducted by operatives of the NBI-Task Force Against Illegal Drugs (NBI-TFAID) under the Intelligence Service of the Bureau that resulted in the discovery of drug den and eventual application before the Regional Trial Court of Quezon City for the issuance of a Search Warrant on the Subject’s premises. On November 19, 2021, operatives of the NBI-TFAID implemented the Search Warrant and swooped down on the residence in Teachers Village. During the conduct of the search, operatives found and seized a staggering quantities of ecstasy totalling 27, 334 tablets, shabu, cocaine, kush, marijuana sticks, chemicals, laboratory equipment and drug paraphernalia with an estimated value of P65 Million. Also seized during the operation include a 9MM Uzi sub-machine gun, Remington shotgun, Glock pistol, .22 Automatic rifle, 800 pieces of ammunitions for different calibers, and a high explosive munition. Distor emphasized that the Subjects are believed to be concocting an undetermined kind of dangerous drugs by mixing pulverized ecstasy with methamphetamine and cocaine to produce a new party drug for their clientele. Subjects were presented for Inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor of Quezon City for violation of the R.A. 9165 otherwise known as the Comprehensive Drugs Act of 2002.

title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: PRESS STATEMENT April 22, 2022 NBI ARRESTS 13 CHINESE NATIONALS FOR PHISHING In line with the directive of National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Officer-In-Charge (OIC) Director Eric B. Distor to eradicate cyber related crimes, NBI-Special Task Force (NBI-STF) operatives arrested thirteen (13) Chinese nationals who are into phishing activities victimizing foreign nationals. Director Distor identified the subject Chinese nationals as CHEN QI JUN; OU ZHONG QI; CHEN BINGGUI; CHEN BEI XIN; WU XINGZE; YIN PENG; ZHENG ZHI FA; XU SHAO PENG; WEI CHEN; LI CHUANGIN; YU ZOU WU; CHEN HUA SHENG; and ZHENG SHUN JIN. The operation stemmed from information received by the NBI-STF from the employee of 2G Company (2G) alleging that she was taught by the subject company to participate in their elaborate scheme of scheming several foreign victims using allures of cryptocurrency. Informant added that since her first day she was taught of the means of how to chat with prospective victims until she will lure and entice them to open a Binance and Metamask accounts. They were provided with a script that they must master in chatting with their foreign victims. Informant and her co-employees are given a list of possible target victims who they will chat using a fake account or they are directed to scour dating sites like Tinder using fake account and look for victims who must be employed and earning at least USD 3,000.00 or whose professions are automotive engineers, computer programmers, or machine operators. They will start chatting with these individuals using Tinder and will convince them to continue their conversation using Whatsapp using fake accounts. The informant added that they will make friends with the foreigner and sometimes make the foreigner fall in love with their fake representations. Once the foreigner takes the bait, they will gradually introduce cryptocurrency trading and make it appear that there is really good money in their established scheme. Once the victim downloaded and opened an account on Binance or Metamask, they will send a phishing link where 2G has created a backdoor and the details such as the username and password of the victim will be sent to their controlled site or email. Thus, NBI-STF applied for a Warrant for Search, Seizure, and Examination of Computer Data (WSSECD) and on April 13, 2022, NBI-STF operatives proceeded to the office address of 2G to implement the said Warrant. Operatives of NBI-Digital Forensic Laboratory conducted on-site forensic examination (OS Triage) on the computer desktops and other devices being used by the subjects. Through OS Triage, the operatives were able to discover that the computer devices used by the Subjects were indeed running fraudulent computer software applications, and thru the use of photographs, links, websites and other deceptive computer system and data, are performing computer-related fraud. At this juncture, the above named Chinese nationals were placed under arrest by the agents of NBI-STF. Also, computer devices used by the Subjects were seized and inventoried for further off-site examination. On April 19, 2022, the arrested Chinese nationals were presented for inquest proceedings before the City Prosecutor of Parañaque for violation of R.A. 10175 otherwise known as the Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012.

title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: A Chinese national who is an international organized crime figure wanted for felony in the United States was arrested by agents of the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) at the Ninoy Aquino International Airport (NAIA) during the week-end. The suspect was identified by NBI Officer-In-Charge Nonnatus Caesar R. Rojas as SOON AH KOW, in his 70’s, born in Malaysia, a holder of a Chinese passport, a Hong Kong resident/businessman. Kow stands charged with fourteen (14) counts of felony violations before a federal grand jury in the District of New Jersey. He is an international organized crime figure who arranges and brokers large scale smuggling of drugs and counterfeit goods from different Southeast Asian countries. Further, information revealed that Kow is known to have travelled using fraudulent and/or inaccurate documentation. It was also revealed that Kow has previously used multiple passports from different countries. By his own admission to undercover US agents, he has “business associates” in China. Secretary of Justice Leila M. De Lima, issued a Memorandum dated Feb. 2, 2012 to NBI Officer-In-Charge Atty. Nonnatus Caesar R. Rojas forwarding the letter-request of the United States Department of Justice Attache regarding Soon Ah Kow. She directed the National Bureau of Investigation thru Atty. Claro C. De Castro Jr., Chief of Foreign Liaison Division (FLD) to arrest Soon Ah Kow who will be arriving at the Ninoy Aquino International Airport Terminal 1 from Hong Kong via Dragon Air flight No. KA931 on February 25, 2012. On February 10, 2012, the NBI Foreign Liaison Division (FLD) filed an Urgent Ex-Parte Application For Provisional Arrest against KOW before the Manila Regional Trial Court and was raffled to Branch XIV. Presiding Judge Buenaventura Albert J. Tenorio, Jr., issued an order of Provisional Arrest granting the application and serves as the authority for the immediate apprehension of SOON AH KOW. It was upon arrival of Kow’s flight at the NAIA in the evening of February 25, 2012 when waiting NBI-Foreign Liaison Division (FLD)/Interpol and NAIAID agents immediately apprehended and brought him to the NBI for booking and detention.

body: Four members of a kidnap-for-ransom group were arrested while the victim rescued during a shootout between agents of the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) and the suspects in Manila this morning. The arrested suspects were identified as: GERALD V. DOMINGO, 45, a former Overseas Filipino Worker, a resident of Hizon St., Sta. Cruz, Manila MARY JANE SAN MARTIN, 29, a resident of NPC Village, Bgy. Pasong Tamo, Quezon City. EMMANUEL YANCE DE JESUS. Another suspect, EDWIN S. DE CASTRO, alias Orlando S. Sanchez alias Bong, was rushed to Jose Reyes Memorial Hospital due to gunshot wounds and is in critical condition. The other suspects, one alias Benjie and one alias Randy eluded arrest. The case stemmed from an intelligence report that a kidnap-for- ransom group headed by a certain “Gerald” is planning to kidnap Flor Ty, a casino financier at the Manila Pavillion-Casino located in United Nations Avenue, Ermita, Manila. Said group will demand P20 million ransom. A surveillance operation was conducted on the group’s movements. It was found out that Gerald’s group will abduct victim Ty, between 2:00 AM – 3:00 AM of April 15, 2013 on her way home in Sta. Cruz, Manila. Acting on this information, Anti-Organized Crime Division (AOCD) agents immediately coordinated with the Manila Police District (MPD), proceeded to the vicinity of Avenida Rizal near the corner of Fugoso St., Sta. Cruz, Manila. At around 3:00 A.M. this morning, the PAGCOR black Ford Chrysler carrying the victim was suddenly blocked by a red Ford Lynx Sedan with Plate Number XSV-574 while traversing said road. Three men armed with pistols jumped out of the vehicle and pointed their guns at the PAGCOR driver and ordered him to open the door as one of the gunman boarded the car. Meanwhile, “Gerald,” with Mary Jane on board a Mitsubishi Lancer with Plate Number VIE-999, were tailing the PAGCOR car. At this juncture, NBI agents who were strategically positioned in the area shouted at the suspects introducing themselves. However, the gunman who was pointing his gun at the driver, instead fired his gun at the NBI operatives starting a gunfight. The suspects boarded their vehicle and sped off but NBI agents gave chase. A hot pursuit ensued that resulted in the arrest of another suspect Emmanuel De Jesus and the recovery of the Ford Lynx which was used in the aborted kidnapping. Another suspect, Edwin Castro was brought to Jose Reyes Memorial Hospital for medical treatment after sustaining a gunshot wound. Found beside him was a caliber.45 pistol with five live ammunitions. Meanwhile, Gerald and Mary Jane San Martin were likewise arrested and brought to the NBI for questioning. Charges for Attempted Kidnapping, Frustrated Homicide, Illegal Possession of Firearms and violation of Comelec Gun Ban are readied against the suspects before the Manila City Prosecutor’s Office.

body: PRESS STATEMENT February 16, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } NBI-NCR IMPLEMENTS SEARCH WARRANT AT MUNTINLUPA SCAMMING HUB; SEIZES DIGITAL EVIDENCE PASAY, Philippines — The National Bureau of Investigation – National Capital Region (NBI-NCR) has successfully dismantled the technical operations of a scamming hub located within an exclusive village in Muntinlupa City. The operation focused on the legal seizure and forensic examination of computer data used by an organized criminal syndicate. This follow-up operation stems from a prior NBI-NCR operation on February 5, 2025, which led to the arrest of two Chinese nationals for illegal detention and the rescue of a Chinese victim. The victim had been held against his will and forced to work as an encoder for the syndicate. Following the initial rescue, NBI agents identified a significant array of electronic devices at the site. This discovery prompted the Bureau to apply for a Warrant to Search, Seize, and Examine Computer Data (WSSECD), which was subsequently granted by the court. On 13 February 2026, agents from the NBI-NCR returned to the target villa to implement the WSSECD. The operation resulted in the orderly seizure of multiple laptops, smartphones, and other pieces of electronic hardware allegedly used by the syndicate to facilitate online scams and digital communication. All confiscated items have since been turned over to the NBI-Digital Forensic Laboratory (NBI-DFL) for a comprehensive, off-site forensic analysis aimed at uncovering the full scale and network of the criminal group’s activities. NBI Acting Director Atty. Angelito DLP Magno commended the NBI-NCR agents for their systematic approach to dismantling the group’s infrastructure: “The successful implementation of this search warrant is a critical step in our fight against cyber-enabled crimes. By securing this digital evidence, our forensic experts can now trace the network behind these operations. We remain committed to ensuring that those who exploit individuals and technology for criminal gain are held accountable.” ATTY. ANGELITO DLP. MAGNO Acting Director, NBI #NBIServes Media Contact: HA Palmer U. Mallari NBI Spokesperson [email protected]

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today said operatives of the Bureau’s Ant-Fraud Division (AFD) have arrested an employee of a prestigious bank following an entrapment operation on July 18, 2017 in Makati City. NBI Director Dante A. Gierran identified the Subject as MA. VICTORIA “Marivic” S. Lopez, Head of the bank’s Corporate Service Management who was arrested for alleged qualified theft, falsification and violation of the General Banking Law. Director Gierran said that the entrapment operation was made upon request by the bank after an official of the bank filed a complaint before the NBI against Subject Lopez on July 13, 2017. The official alleged that he noticed several irregularities in the letter request concerning a loan transaction of a client being facilitated by Subject Lopez. The official added that upon verification with the client, the client confirmed that they were not aware of the letter request and even the account from which the Manager’s Check was supposed to be debited. Gierran stated that further investigation by the bank revealed that the bank supposedly issued a loan in favor of the client covered by a promissory note, which is fictitious. It also revealed that Subject Lopez uses the account to facilitate fictitious loans. Upon strict orders by Director Gierran, operatives of the NBI-Anti Fraud Division set up the entrapment operation on July 17, 2017 in the bank’s premises. On July 17, 2017, as soon as Subject Lopez gave instructions to debit the amount of P2,250,000.00 from the client’s saving’s account, the bank issued a debit memo to Subject Lopez, as evidence of the processing of transaction. Thereafter, right after an official of the bank got confirmation that client is not aware of the loan transaction, Subject Lopez was arrested. Subject was presented for inquest proceedings at the Makati City Prosecutor’s Office on July 18, 2017.

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today said operatives of NBI-Technical Intelligence Division (NBI-TID) arrested a person long wanted for Syndicated Estafa, evening of January 19, 2018 in Cabanatuan City. Director Dante A. Gierran identified the Subject as RANDY RUBIO , one of the co-accused of Rosario Baladjay, a celebrated investment and pyramiding scam queen who was arrested and convicted for syndicated estafa on December 3, 2012. Said decision was affirmed by the Supreme Court on July 26, 2017. Subject RUBIO was arrested in Cabanatuan City by virtue of Warrant of Arrest with No Bail Recommended after the NBI received a reliable intelligence information about the whereabouts of the Subject. Relative thereto, the NBI hatched COPLAN PYRAMID to take immediate action on possible apprehension of Subject RANDY RUBIO. In the course of technical surveillance operations, an information was secured that Subject Rubio will be attending as speaker in a religious gathering in Cabanatuan City on January 19, 2018. Under strict orders from Director Gierran, operatives of NBI-TID, in coordination with NBI-Cabanatuan District Office (NBI-CABDO), conducted an operation to apprehend the Subject. After confirming that Subject was at the said gathering, the NBI operatives decided to wait until after the gathering was finished because it is prohibited by law to interrupt any religious worship or prevent or disturb the ceremonies or manifestations of any religion. When the car Subject Rubio was in exited the gate of the compound, operatives tailed them, plugged down the car and presented the Warrant of Arrest to the Subject in a professional manner. Subject RUBIO was then placed under arrest, after which was brought to NBI-CABDO and to the office of NBI-TID office in Manila where he underwent the proper booking procedures. After the proceeding, Subject was turned over to the NBI Jail for appropriate action.

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today announced the arrest of an individual in Pasay City for Qualified Trafficking by the operatives of NBI-Anti-Human Trafficking Division (NBI-AHTRAD) in an entrapment operation. NBI Officer-In-Charge (OIC) Director Eric B. Distor identified the subject as CYRUS RAMOS y RAFAEL. Director Distor said that the operation stemmed from intelligence report received by NBI regarding a certain individual who is engaged in the illicit activity of offering minor girls for sexual exploitation to paying customers thru Facebook and Facebook Messenger under the name of “ARNIE RESGONIO DOLINDO”. The informant also revealed that the subject in the illicit activity is also known as “CYRUS” and that he has already offered several minor girls and is continuously offering minor girls for sexual purposes to paying customers. The informant relayed to the operatives that Subject Ramos offered to meet in the afternoon of March 3, 2022 outside a hotel in Buendia, Pasay City, that Subject Ramos will bring young women for customers to choose from, and that the rate would be Php 2,000.00. Thus, on March 3, 2022, NBI-AHTRAD with the assistance of Pasay Department of Social Welfare and Development Department (PSWDD), and Department of Justice – Inter-Agency Council Against Trafficking (DOJ-IACAT) proceeded to the agreed meeting area outside SOGO Hotel in Pasay City. Three (3) members of the joint operatives acted as poseur-client and met with Subject Ramos, who has brought six (6) girls. The undercover agents chose four (4) out of the six (6) girls brought by Subject Ramos. Upon handing over of the marked money to the subject, NBI-AHTRAD operatives immediately approached the subject and announced his arrest. The operation also resulted in the rescue of 6 trafficked victims, four (4) of whom are minors. Subject Ramos was presented for inquest proceedings before the Pasay City Prosecutor’s Office for violation of R.A. 9208 (Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2003) as amended by R.A. 10364 in relations to Section 6 Paragraph (a) for Qualified Trafficking; R.A. 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012); and R.A. 7610 (Special Protection of Children Against Abuse, Exploitation and Discrimination Act).

body: PRESS STATEMENT May 31, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } PRESS RELEASE | NBI NABS FOUR INDIVIDUALS FOR SELLING UNREGISTERED HOUSEHOLD HAZARDOUS PRODUCTS The NBI – BATAAN DISTRICT OFFICE (BATADO) arrested One (1) Chinese National, and Three (3) Filipinos in two (2) separate establishments in the Province of Bataan for Violation of R.A. 9711 (Food and Drug Administration Act of 2009). The case stemmed from intelligence report relayed by a confidential informant, that certain establishments from the Province of Bataan are into selling and distributing unregistered Household Aerosol Insecticide, considered as Household/Urban Hazardous Substance. Acting on the information, a test-buy was conducted by NBI-BATADO Agents. Thereafter, said products were submitted to Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for product verification. Through Certification, the FDA confirmed that the subject product of test-buy were indeed unregistered. In this connection, on May 26, 2026, a joint Entrapment and Inspection Operations were conducted by NBI-BATADO and the Food-Drug Regulation Officers from FDA Regulatory Enforcement Unit – North Luzon Cluster, Region III, against two (2) separate establishments in Orani and Abucay, Bataan. The entrapment (buy-bust) operation resulted to the arrest of Four (4) individuals and seizure of various Unregistered Household/Urban Hazardous Products, with an estimated value of more or less Php 120,000.00. Following the operation, arrested individuals were presented before the Office of Provincial Prosecutor – Bataan, for inquest proceedings for Violations under Republic Act 3720 otherwise known as “The Food, Drug and Cosmetic Act”, as amended by Republic Act 9711 known as “The Food and Drug Administration Act of 2009”

Santiago (Ret.), seized a substantial quantity of imported brands of cigarettes in Nueva Ecija. body: PRESS STATEMENT August 14, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } The National Bureau of Investigation – Cybercrime Division (NBI-CCD) under the leadership of Director Judge Jaime B. Santiago (Ret.), arrested three (3) Chinese nationals for Kidnapping and Serious Illegal Detention on August 08, 2025, in Paranaque City. The case stemmed from the complaint received by NBI-CCD alleging that the victim was being unlawfully detained and coerced into working by Subjects ZOU TAO, JIN CAI, and JUNYING LYU. The complainant, a friend of the victim, reported that the victim was also being threatened with death if he attempted to escape. Thus, NBI-CCD agents conducted a rescue operation. After proper coordination with the PNP, the City Prosecutor’s Office, the Barangay, and condominuim’s Security Management, the NBI-CCD agents and the complainant proceeded to the reported location. Inside the unit, they found the three (3) Subjects and the victim sitting on his bed. Victim positively identified the three (3) individuals as those responsible for his unlawful detention. The three (3) Subjects were arrested and apprised of their constitutional rights. A pair of handcuffs used to restrain the victim was also recovered from the premises. Additionally, live computers were discovered. An initial inspection of the desktop interfaces, however, revealed no indication of cryptocurrency-related or investment scam activities. A Warrant to Search and Examine Computer Data will be applied for to subject these computers to digital forensics. Subjects were brought to the NBI-CCD office and undergone standard booking.

body: In line with the relentless drive of the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) against human trafficking and child exploitations, operatives of NBI-MIMAROPA have rescued three minor girls in Puerto Galera and apprehended a Dutch national who was with them. NBI Officer-In-Charge (OIC) Director Eric B. Distor said the NBI received an information regarding an alleged child exploitation transpiring in White Beach, Brgy. San Isidro, Puerto Galera, Oriental Mindoro. The illegal activity was said to be perpetrated by 57 -year old Dutch national identified as JAN ANTHONIE VAN HIERDEN. Distor said that NBI operatives immediately conducted verification where it was discovered that a reservation was made by subject JAN ANTHONIE VAN HIERDEN for a stay at Casa Marco Suites, White Beach, San Isidro, Puerto Galera, Oriental Mindoro from June 19 to June 22, 2021. Together with VAN HIERDEN were three (3) minor children aged 10, 13 and 14 years old wherein they occupied Room at Casa Marco Suite. Informants further said that they have observed that VAN HIERDEN had been acting strangely and suspiciously thereby branding him to be suspected as pedophile. NBI MIMAROPA then coordinated with Barangay Women’s Desk/Local MSWD and Barangay Officials of Brgy. San Isidro, Puerto Galera, Oriental Mindoro, who manifested support to protect the tourism business in the locality. About 6:20pm on June 21, 2021, one of the three minors descended from Casa Marco Suite Room 305 and went to the establishment’s cashier. After seeing that she was leading back to the room , NBI operatives and barangay officials cordially approached the open doors of the room occupied by VAN HIERDEN. Initial inquiries were conducted on VAN HIERDEN with the three minors. VAN HIERDEN asserted that the three minors are his nieces with her girlfriend identified only as ROMINA TICONG and that the biological parents of the minors are both in Malaysia. Operatives also questioned why the minors were at Puerto Galera with VAN HIERDEN despite the strict prohibitions that minors must be at home or in case of such travel, must be with their parents or guardians. Despite the efforts of the barangay officials to let VAN HIERDEN realize his violations, he asserted that he is the guardian or ward of the three minors. NBI-MIMAROPA and the barangay officials then learned that the biological parents of the minors are presently in Malaysia and are not aware that VAN HIERDEN brought with him the children. At around 8:00 of the same evening, NBI-MIMAROPA appraised VAN HIERDEN of his violation of law and invited him to come with them. VAN HIERDEN agreed to come with the operatives while the minors were turned over to the Provincial Social Welfare Office where proper case assessment and study case report, necessary in the investigation of the case, will be conducted. It is believed that VAN HIERDEN violated Section 6 in relation to Section 5 (Attempt to Commit Child Prostitution) of RA 7610 (Special Protection of Children Against Abuse, Exploitation, and Discrimination Act) since the biological parents of the minor children are unaware that VAN HIERDEN brought them to Casa Marco Suite in Puerto Galera. VAN HIERDEN could be liable of the provision of law during this pandemic wherein the minors were exposed and endangered. On June 23, subject JAN ANTHONIE VAN HIERDEN as well as BRENDA BEJEN TICONG (at-large) biological mother of the minors, and FRANCIS JONATHAN MARIADASS (at-large) Malaysian national and the biological father of the minors were presented for Inquest proceedings before the Provincial Prosecutor’s Office of Calapan City, Oriental Mindoro. At the same time, A letter addressed to the Netherlands Embassy was sent informing the Embassy of VAN HIERDEN’s case as well as the rescue of the three minor children. As per standard operating procedure, VAN HIERDEN was submitted to booking, fingerprint, and photograph. He remains under the custody of NBI MIMAROPA.

body: PRESS STATEMENT November 27, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } As part of the intensified efforts of the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) against child abuse, the NBI–Human Trafficking Division (NBI-HTRAD) arrested a male individual in Hagonoy, Bulacan, for violation of Republic Act No. 11930, otherwise known as the “Anti-Online Sexual Exploitation of Children (OSAEC)”. A minor female complainant, accompanied by her mother, appeared before the NBI-HTRAD office to report that an unidentified individual had been threatening her to produce and send Child Sexual Exploitation and Abuse Materials (CSAEM). In response, the agents of NBI-HTRAD immediately launched an investigation, which led to the identification of the individual responsible for the threats, who turned out to be a relative of Complainant. Subsequently, the NBI-HTRAD agents applied for a Warrant to Search, Seize, and Examine Computer Data (WSSECD) for the Subject’s premises, which the court later granted. On November 25, 2025, agents from the NBI-HTRAD, supported by the NBI-Digital Forensic Laboratory (NBI-DFL), the Inter-Agency Council Against Trafficking, the MSWDO of Hagonoy City, and a non-governmental organization, conducted an entrapment operation to apprehend the Subject and enforce the WSSECD. This operation led to the seizure of three mobile phones belonging to the Subject, which were examined on-site by forensic experts. During this examination, the NBI discovered the suspect’s Facebook account, which was positively identified by the victim. Additionally, they found incriminating chat messages, twelve pieces of Child Sexual Exploitation Materials, evidence of sextortion, and indications of group activities related to pedophilia. OIC Director Magno emphasized that the NBI remains unwavering in its commitment to fulfilling its mandate to safeguard the public’s interests, with a particular focus on protecting minors. This dedication involves actively working to prevent the exploitation of young individuals by those who may seek to take advantage of their vulnerabilities. “End the exploitation of minors immediately, or be prepared to face the full consequences of the law” Atty. Angelito DLP. Magno Officer-in-Charge, NBI

body: PRESS STATEMENT May 03, 2022 NBI TURNS OVER P11 BILLION WORTH OF ILLEGAL DRUGS TO PDEA The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) has turned over P11 Billion worth of illegal drugs to the Philippine Drug Enforcement Agency (PDEA). NBI OIC-Director ERIC B. DISTOR said the turn-over of the illegal drugs to PDEA was in compliance with the Orders of the Regional Trial Court under the Fourth Judicial Region of Infanta, Quezon. In compliance with said Order, the NBI thru its Forensic Chemistry Division (FCD) that has custody of the illegal drugs, turned over to PDEA on April 11 and 26, 2022, a total weight of 1,855.0 kilograms. DISTOR said that on March 15, 2022, joint operatives of the NBI led by the Task Force Against Illegal Drugs (NBI-TFAID) seized more than one (1) ton of suspected illegal drugs worth P11 Billion in Barangay Comon, Infanta, Quezon. DISTOR stressed that aside from operatives of TFAID, the dawn operation involved the Agents of NBI-Research and Analysis Division (RAD) and Lucena District Office (LUCDO), in coordination with PNP Infanta, Quezon and PDEA Lucena. The operation likewise resulted in the arrest of ten (10) malefactors while in the act of transporting the suspected illegal drugs on board three (3) commuter vans. DISTOR stressed that following the seizure of the illegal drugs, the 10 arrested Subjects were presented for Inquest proceedings before the Office of the Prosecutor of Infanta, Quezon for Violation of RA 9165 otherwise known as the Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002. On April 11, 25 and 26, 2022, Team of Prosecutors, PAO lawyers for Defense of suspects, Court staff of Infanta Quezon went to NBI Head Office in Quezon City to witness the taking of representative sample of the seized illegal drugs and weighing of the same for the turn-over to the PDEA and its eventual destruction as ordered by the Court. The RTC Judge of Infanta Quezon was also present (virtual). DISTOR emphasized that the war against illegal drugs will continue and will be relentlessly pursued for as long as there are unscrupulous individuals who ply illegal drugs to the detriment of our society. Unprecedented and historic considering the volume and amount, as of date, this is the biggest drug haul in Philippine history, DISTOR added.
