body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today said operatives of NBI-Bayombong District Office (NBI-BAYDO) arrested two individuals for illegal selling of chainsaws and other cutting equipment in Bambang, Nueva Vizcaya. NBI Officer-in-Charge (OIC) Director Eric B. Distor identified the Subjects as KNIGHT BALISI CO and JOHNLERY PATRICIO ALLAREY. Distor said that the case stemmed from an information received by NBI-BAYDO regarding several establishments in Bambang, Nueva Vizcaya that are involved in the sale and distribution of chainsaws and other cutting implements through electric and internal combustion engine without necessary permit from the concerned government agency particularly the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR), in violation of RA 9175 otherwise known as the Chainsaw Act of 2002. According to the information received, among the establishments involved are ALLMIGHTY INDUSTRIAL and KHAMI ENTERPRISES. NBI-BAYDO then validated the information and it was found out that the said establishments are indeed offering chainsaws and other cutting equipment for sale to the general public with price ranging from Php 7,000 to Php 60,000. Through a Certification issued by the Community Environment and Natural Resources Office (CENRO), ALLMIGHTY INDUSTRIAL and KHAMI ENTERPRISES were not issued authority or permit to sell and distribute the aforesaid cutting implements. With this, simultaneous entrapment operations were conducted at ALLMIGHTY INDUSTRIAL located along the national highway of Bambang, Nueva Vizcaya and at KHAMI ENTERPRISES located at Almaguer North, Bambang Nueva Vizcaya. The operations resulted in the arrest of Subjects KNIGHT BALISI CO, sales representative of ALLMIGHTY INDUSTRIAL and JOHNLERY PATRICIO ALLAREY, sales representative/mechanic of KHAMI ENTERPRISES. Subject CO sold a chainsaw worth Php 7,500 while Subject ALLAREY sold heavy duty chainsaw for Php 55,000. Both were arrested after receiving the marked money. The owner of the ALLMIGHTY INDUSTRIAL was identified as JETHRO CYRUS GAMBITO through his sales representative and through the DTI and business permit posted at the establishment. On the other hand, the proprietor of KHAMI ENTERPRISES is ANNALIZA DONATO, as disclosed by Subject ALLAREY. Seized were 2 sets og chainsaw worth P47,000.00 Charges for violation of RA 9175 (Chainsaw Act of 2002) were filed before the Office of the Provincial Prosecutor, Bayombong, Nueva Vizcaya against arrested Subjects KNIGHT BALISI CO and JOHNLERY PATRICIO ALLAREY as well as at-large business owners JETHRO CYRUS GAMBITO and ANNALIZA DONATO.

body: Eighty-nine (89) young girls, including minors, were rescued and twenty-three (23) maintainers key personnel of an entertainment network arrested during a raid by National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) operatives in Parañaque City during the week-end. The suspects were identified as ISAGANI BORDAMONTE, Officer-In-Charge of Asian Entertainmnet Network with business address at Jafttra Enterprises Inc., and Asian Entertainment Network, 701 Roxas Blvd., Baclaran, Parañaque City; SHIELA O. VARGA, MARIBEL Y. CUSTODIO, DANILO V. TAN, HELEN R. MENDOZA, JULIE B. CHAVEZ, OFELIA B. YUPANO, JOSE V. TAN, JOSEPHINE C. DULU, SHERYL BELTRAN, ERLINDA G. ROXAS, MIGUEL VILLAR, MARICEL P. BERMOY, NERIE M. ANGELES, FELICIDAD A. ROXAS, CHRISTOPHER G. GODINEZ, LEAH P. DE LEON, EMERITA J. PARGAS, MERCY R. REBLANDO, ROWENA B. SANTOS, JOSIE M. MENDEZ, ELLA F. MARQUEZ, and LOLITA L. SANCHEZ, all personnel of the aforementioned club. Delfin Lim and a certain alias “Kenji”, the owners of Asian Entertainment Network are at-large. Investigation conducted by the NBI Anti-Human Trafficking Division (AHTRAD) under Head Agent Dante B. Bonoan revealed that on July 25, 2013, the NBI received information from the International Justice Mission (IJM) regarding the alleged human trafficking activities perpetrated at the Asian Entertainment Network along Roxas Blvd., Baclaran, Parañaque City. Accordingly, several female entertainers including suspected minors are being offered for prostitution, and female dancers are asked to perform nude shows inside the establishment. A series of surveillance was conducted by the NBI-AHTRAD which confirmed the information. It was found out that Guest Relations Officers (GROs), some of who are obviously minors employed, and offered for sexual services with customers at the VIP rooms. Some are being made to perform live nude shows. Based on this validated information, an entrapment and rescue operation was planned by the NBI in coordination with the complainant entity and other government agencies. body: The crime-fighting capability of the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) is greatly enhanced with the assurance of complete additional technical support to its Automated Fingerprint Identification System (AFIS) by a US agency during a visit of its officials in Manila yesterday. During a meeting between NBI officials led by Director Nonnatus Caesar R. Rojas and Rear Admiral James E. Rendon and his party representing the Joint Inter-Agency Task Force West (JIATF), the visitors were shown the in-placed infrastructure to house the facility’s mainframe. With this development, the package assistance by the donor agency for the AFIS of the NBI will find completion. The JIATF is the US agency that provides much of the funding for training and initiatives in the Philippines. It is also the primary funding source for the ongoing Automated Fingerprint Identification System (AFIS) that is being installed at the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI). The AFIS is an advanced state-of-the-art equipment which functions provides immense advantage to law enforcement in combating crime and lawlessness. AFIS aids law enforcement in expeditious identification of a person-subject in a crime through the use of high-speed and computerized matching of fingerprints. Most law-enforcement agencies globally now avail of the AFIS. Adm. Rendon expressed gladness of their partnership with the NBI in furtherance of their mutual goals. For his part, Director Rojas thanked Adm. Rendon and his party for the donation and assured of the Bureau’s cooperation in the common quest to fight crime.

body: PRESS STATEMENT March 14, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } In accordance with the directive from National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Director JUDGE JAIME B. SANTIAGO (Ret.), to enhance efforts in the fight against the twin evil of human trafficking and illegal recruitment, the NBI – International Airport Investigation Division (NBI-IAID) arrested ANAMAE CRISTINA YNOT LIGA and DANICA ANN ALEJO BERNARDO at NAIA Terminal 1. They were charged with violations of R.A. No. 8042 (the Migrant Workers and Overseas Filipinos Act of 1995), as amended by R.A. No. 10022 in large-scale and violation of R.A. No. 9208 (the Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2003), as amended. On March 5, 2025, the NBI-IAID received an endorsement from the NAIA Taskforce Against Trafficking – Inter-Agency Council Against Trafficking (NAIATFAT-IACAT) regarding six passengers who were denied departure by the Bureau of Immigration. An investigation conducted by NBI-IAID agents revealed that the passengers were originally bound for Singapore on a company incentive tour. However, during their Immigration Inspection departure procedures, the four passengers revealed that the true purpose of their travel was to seek employment as performers. They also indicated that their companions, subjects Liga and Bernado, were acting as their escorts. Further investigation revealed that the four passengers were previously Overseas Filipinos who had worked as performing artists in Singapore, Japan, and Dubai. The passengers reported that their recruiter, referred to as “Sir M,” invited them to meet at a restaurant in Malate, Manila, which is co-owned by Subjects Liga and Bernardo. During the meeting, Sir M assured them that he would cover all travel expenses and that there would be no issues with the Immigration Inspection departure procedures regarding their documents. On March 3, 2025, the recruits met with Sir M in Muntinlupa City for the second time, where they were informed that they would be leaving for Singapore on March 4, 2025. Verification with the Department of Migrant Workers (DMW) confirmed that Liga and Bernardo are neither licensed nor authorized to recruit workers for overseas employment. On March 6, 2025, the arrested Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor in Pasay City for the above violations. Director Santiago commended the agents of NBI-IAID for the arrest of the Subjects and warned the public to be cautious especially with offers of overseas employment.

body: The National Bureau of Investigation today said operatives of NBI- Anti-Graft Division (NBI-AGD) have filed charges against 2 BOC employees and 3 others for violation of Section 3 (a) and (e) of R.A. 3019 otherwise known as the “Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act” and R.A. 6713 otherwise known as “Code of Conduct and Ethical Standards for Public Officials and Employees.” NBI Director Eric B. Distor identified the BOC employees as LOMONTOD MACABANDO, Customs Operations Officer V and GAMALODEN MUSOR, Customs Security Guard 2, and three (3) others, namely: BANGSA-AN A. MIMBALAWAG, ABRAHAN A. MIMBALAWAG, and one (1) unidentified subject. Records show that subjects Macabando and Musor were arrested on May 5, 2018 by officers of the Bureau of Customs assigned in NAIA Terminal 3 for allegedly smuggling assorted pieces of jewelry from Dubai. An officer of BOC saw somebody handed a clutch bag to Macabando who was with Musor in the restricted area of the airport. BOC officers blocked Subject Macabando and requested him to turn over the clutch bag but he refused and escaped by running. Subject Macabando was later subdued and they talked to the passengers, later identified as Subject Abraham Mimbalawag and Bangsa-an Mimbalawag, who claimed ownership of the clutch bag. When the spouses were asked by the Customs officials to open the bag, it turned out to contain 24 pieces of gold rings, 1029 pairs of gold earrings, 155 pieces of gold pendants, 5 pieces of gold earrings and pendants, 19 pieces of gold bangles, 295 pieces of gold chains, and 101 pieces of gold bracelets, without a receipt. NBI-AGD subpoenaed the subjects but only Subjects Mimbalawag spouses submitted their counter-affidavit. Spouses Mimbalawag disclosed to the NBI-AGD operatives that they were carrying pieces of jewelry from Dubai. That they contacted Subject Macabando, a distant relative to help them get a fair and lawful assessment even in the absence of a receipt because they cannot find it. Careful viewing of the CCTV cameras showed that Subject Musor was seen talking to an unidentified person who handed the clutch bag to Subject Macabando. Based on the evidences gathered by the NBI-AGD the requirements of Section 3 (a) and (e) of Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act (R.A. 3019) are sufficiently established. Thus, graft charges were filed before the before the Office of the Ombudsman.

body: PRESS STATEMENT October 22, 2024 The National Bureau of Investigation-Dangerous Drugs Division (NBI-DDD), under the leadership of NBI Director Judge Jaime B. Santiago (Ret.), arrested an individual in San Miguel, Manila for violation of RA 9165 or the Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002. NBI-DDD received an information regarding a certain FRANCISCO SORIANO JR. a.k.a. JUNTOT and alias “FACE” who are engaged in selling dangerous drugs particularly methamphetamine hydrochloride or shabu, and maintaining a drug den inside the Malacañang Complex. Director Santiago said that with the assistance of the Presidential Security Group (PSG) and after a series of test buy which confirmed the illicit activity, an operation was hatched by DDD operatives. On October 16, 2024, in coordination with the Philippine Drug Enforcement Agency (PDEA) and the local police, DDD and PSG operatives implemented the Search Warrant issued by RTC Branch 37, Manila in the premises of Francisco Soriano Jr and alias “Face” located at 946 Nicanor Padilla St., San Miguel, Manila. Found and seized during the operation were nine (9) heat sealed transparent plastic sachets containing white crystalline substance suspected to be illegal drugs, and other drug paraphernalia. EDGAR VENTURA alias FACE was arrested and duly apprised of his constitutional rights. He was brought to NBI-DDD for the standard booking and arrest procedures. The seized drug items were submitted to the NBI-Forensic Chemistry Division for examination. The fifteen (15) individuals present inside the premises during the operation were also invited to DDD office for drug test. EDGAR VENTURA a.ka. FACE will be presented for inquest proceedings for violation of RA 9165 (Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002). At-large Subject FRANCISCO SORIANO JR a.ka. JUNTOT as well as other individuals who will be found positive for use of shabu will also be charged with the same violation of law. Director Santiago commended the DDD, PDEA, and PSG operatives for the success of the operation.

body: PRESS STATEMENT May 15, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } The NBI International Airport Investigation Division (NBI-IAID) arrested two (2) passengers – MARIA ZENAIDA CALLOS OTANI and TAKAYUKI TOMITA, a Japanese National, for violation of RA 8042 (Illegal Recruitment) as amended by RA 10022 and RA 9208 (Anti-Trafficking in Persons) as amended by RA 11862 (Expanded Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2022). Subjects together with 13 other passengers bound for Nagoya, Japan who were believed to be victims of Trafficking in Persons/illegal recruitment were turned over to NBI-IAID by the NAIA-IACAT for investigation. body: PRESS STATEMENT October 02, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } In connection with the Alice Guo case, the NBI-Bulacan South District Office (NBI BUSDO) has filed two separate cases against dismissed Bamban Mayor Alice Leal Guo, also known as Guo Hua Ping, and her family for establishing businesses and purchasing real property in Marilao, Bulacan. During a Senate inquiry in aid of legislation, it was revealed that the real name of Alice Guo is Guo Hua Ping, a Chinese national. It was also disclosed that Shiela Leal Guo, also known as Mier Zhang, is a Chinese national. Investigation conducted by the NBI found that Alice Guo and other family members are incorporators of several companies, including QJJ Group of Companies Inc., QSeed Genetics Inc., QJJ Meat Shop Inc., QJJ Slaughter House Inc., QJJ Smelting Plant Inc., and QJJ Embroidery Center Inc. All of these companies share a principal address on Maligaya Street, Barangay Patubig, Marilao, Bulacan. The property was purchased by Alice Guo on October 5, 2010, for Php 2,000,000.00 and covers an area of 4,636 square meters, as detailed in the Absolute Deed of Sale and accompanying documents obtained from the Registry of Deeds of Meycauayan City and the Tax Declarations of Marilao. Further investigation by NBI-BUSDO revealed that Alice, Shiela, and Siemen declared themselves as Filipinos in the Articles of Incorporation of the aforementioned companies, holding the majority of the shares. Moreover, GUO JIAN ZHONG and LIN WEN YI were co-incorporators in the companies mentioned above. Based on the investigation and documentary evidence gathered, charges were filed against GUO HUA PING (a.k.a. Alice Leal Guo), MIER ZHANG (a.k.a. Shiela Leal Guo and Mi er Zhang), SEIMEN/SIEMEN GUO, and LIN WEN YI. The charges include: Thirty (30) counts of Falsification of Public Documents (under Article 172 in relation to Article 171 (4) of the Revised Penal Code) for falsifying the Articles of Incorporation, Secretary’s Certificate, and 2021 General Information Sheet (GIS) of the corporations. Thirty (30) counts of Simulation of Minimum Capital Stock (under Section 2 of Commonwealth Act No. 108, or the Anti-Dummy Law). Four (4) counts of Falsification of Public Documents for falsifying applications for Business, Occupancy, and Building Permits. Furthermore, GUO HUA PING was charged with an additional six (6) counts of Falsification of Public Documents, under Article 172 in relation to Article 171 (4) of the RPC for falsifying the Deed of Sale and Documentary Stamp related to the ownership of real property. Director Santiago praised the NBI-BUSDO agents for their comprehensive investigation, which led to additional charges being filed against GUO HUA PING and her family.

body: Department of Justice Secretary Menardo I. Guevarra will be the Guest of Honor and Speaker on the 83rd Founding Anniversary of the National Bureau of Investigation tomorrow, November 13, 2019, with the theme “NBI @83: Exemplary Public Service, Our Identity, Our Legacy”. To be held at the Diamond Hotel along Roxas Blvd. Manila, the whole-day anniversary celebration will begin with a Thanksgiving Mass at 8:00 a.m. The formal program begins at 9:00 a.m. that will include the awarding of Plaque of Recognition to Outstanding Agents, Special Investigators and operating units and Service Awards to NBI employess who have been in the Bureau for 40 years. Highlight of the celebration us the Anniversary message of the Secretary of Justice. In the afternoon of the same day, there will be a Balik- Akademya, considered the Annual Alumni Homecoming of Agents and Special Investigators who graduated from the NBI Academy in Baguio City. Gierran and Assistant Director Medardo G. de Lemos led the Wreath Laying at the Wall of Honor to remember the NBI Agents and Special Investigators who have died in the line of duty.

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today said the agency will look into reports alleging the involvement of three (3) NBI agents in the kidnapping of a South Korean national in Angeles Pampanga on Friday, November 24, 2017. Upon being informed of the incident, NBI Director Dante A. Gierran said he has already formed a team that will investigate and verify the veracity of statements issued by the PNP Chief in a press briefing that implicated NBI agents in the kidnapping incident. Gierran said he has already received the report from the NBI Regional Director and Acting Assistant Regional Director of the NBI-Central Luzon Regional Office (CELRO), which has jurisdiction over Angeles Pampanga, showing that all NBI Agents assigned in Pampanga are all accounted for. The report, likewise, stated that there was no NBI operation conducted in the area in Angeles Pampanga, that was participated in by any of NBI Agents or personnel of CELRO or in any of the District Offices, which operation involved a Korean citizen being apprehended or being forcibly taken into custody and detention, on the date of the incident where the victim, Lee Jung Dae, was kidnapped. Gierran emphasized that the leadership of the NBI including all its Agents adhere to a high standards of ethics with stringent policies and procedures in the conduct of operations, expressing his deep concern over the statement of the PNP Chief relative to the involvement of NBI Agents, which are all unverified reports by the PNP-Anti Kidnapping Group (AKG). In view of this, the NBI is now studying the filing of charges against the PNP for issuing statements to the media based on unverified reports the statements of which destroy the high credibility of the NBI. It may be recalled that in previous kidnapping incident of another Korean national, the PNP also implicated 3 NBI officials in the kidnapping of Jee Ick Joo who was later killed right inside Camp Crame. The 3 NBI officials were later exonerated by the panel of prosecutors of the Department of Justice.

body: PRESS STATEMENT October 03, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } The National Bureau of Investigation-National Capital Region (NBI-NCR), under the leadership of Director Judge Jaime B. Santiago (Ret.),7, arrested two (2) foreign nationals in Pasay City on September 15, 2025, for illegal detention. The operation stemmed from a complaint received by the NBI-NCR against “alias BOSS YONG” and others for alleged illegal detention. Complainant sought assistance to immediately rescue a certain Mr. Yi, who was being unlawfully deprived of his liberty in a condominium hotel in Pasay City. Complainant executed his sworn statement and submitted screenshots of distress messages, pictures, and victim’s location. According to the complainant, the victim applied for an IT analyst position in August 2025 via Telegram and was accepted. However, after some time, the victim discovered that the Subjects’ activity was illegal. When he attempted to resign and leave, both the boss and manager refused, threatening the victim with death if he attempted to escape or leave the workplace. On September 15, 2025, the victim was traced on the 3rd floor of a building located at Cuneta Ave., Pasay City. After coordinating with the local police and the Office of the Prosecutor General of the Department of Justice (DOJ), NBI-NCR agents proceeded to the target location. Upon arrival, the team coordinated with the Building Administrator before proceeding to Room 311, where the victim was reportedly being held against his will. The operatives identified themselves, announced the purpose of their presence, and asserted their authority. The victim was recognized immediately from the photograph provided earlier. He approached the NCR Agents and identified the Subjects. Subjects were identified by the victim as DO YANG ZHE and HU YONG. They were then placed under arrest and were apprised of their constitutional rights. It was discovered that Subject DO YANG ZHE and OUYANG ZHE are the same person after he presented a picture of his passport. Subjects were brought to the NBI-NCR office where they underwent the standard operating procedures. They were presented for inquest proceedings before the City Prosecution Office, Department of Justice for Illegal Detention under Article 267 of the Revised Penal Code. Director Santiago lauded the NBI-NCR for their swift action and coordination that led to the safe recovery of the victim and the apprehension of the Subjects.

body: PRESS STATEMENT March 17, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } NBI ARRESTS FAKE CHINESE DOCTOR IN ENTRAPMENT OPERATION PASAY CITY, Philippines – On March 12, 2026, the National Bureau of Investigation – National Capital Region (NBI-NCR) arrested a Chinese national in Manila City for illegal practice of medicine. The investigation was initiated following an intelligence report regarding a foreign national engaged in medical practice without the necessary credentials. To verify the report, NBI-NCR operatives conducted a surveillance mission where the Subject was observed performing physical examinations and making clinical diagnoses. Investigation revealed that the Subject was caught in the act of illegally practicing medicine, specifically diagnosing and performing physical examinations on an undercover NBI agent posing as a patient. Formal verification with the Professional Regulation Commission (PRC) confirmed that the Subject is not a licensed physician, as records show he has not held an approved board certification or a Commission Resolution granting a special permit to practice in the Philippines since 1997. The Subject was presented for inquest proceedings before the Manila City Prosecutor’s Office for violation of Republic Act No. 2382 (Medical Act of 1959). NBI Director Atty. Melvin A. Matibag reiterated the Bureau’s hardline stance against fraudulent practitioners who endanger public health. “The National Bureau of Investigation, steadfast in its mission to protect citizens, will diligently and relentlessly pursue those individuals who engage in these illegal practices,” Director Matibag stated. “We are committed to ensuring that such violators are brought to justice.” Director Matibag further urged the public to exercise due diligence and verify the credentials of medical professionals through official PRC channels before seeking treatment. #NBIServes

body: PRESS STATEMENT July 30, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } Under the directive of the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Director JUDGE JAIME B. SANTIAGO (Ret.) to enhance efforts in the fight against the twin evil of human trafficking and illegal recruitment, the NBI – International Airport Investigation Division (IAID) arrested PAOLO NICANDRO CUNETA for “Qualified Trafficking in Person” under R.A. No. 9208 (Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2003), as amended by R.A. 11862, and “Large-Scale Illegal Recruitment” under R.A. No. 8042 (Migrant Workers and Overseas Filipinos Act of 1995), as amended by R.A. 10022. NBI-IAID received a referral from the Migrant Workers Protection Bureau – Department of Migrant Workers (MWPB-DMW) involving eight (8 ) departing passengers for Vietnam on 14 July 2025 at the NAIA Terminal 3. Investigation established that the said passengers were promised employment as Housekeepers and Customer Service Representatives (CSRs) for a company allegedly owned and operated by Chinese nationals based in Cambodia. Recruitment took place through social media platforms in June and July 2025. According to the victims, they were offered a basic monthly salary of USD 1,000, exclusive of performance bonuses and other incentives. All travel-related expenses to Cambodia were to be shouldered by the employer. The group was instructed to first exit the country as tourists to Vietnam before being transported to Cambodia. On the day of their scheduled flight, they were promised an allowance of Four Thousand Pesos (Php 4,000.00) and travel documents to support their cover as tourists. They were required by their employer to send via Telegram their passport biographical data pages, whole body pictures, medical certificate, and typing proficiencies. Each applicant was interviewed via Telegram and informed that they had passed the employer’s selection process. On 13 July 2025, they were notified through their Telegram group chat of their flight to Vietnam the next day, July 14, 2025. On the day of departure, the passengers proceeded to NAIA Terminal 3 in Pasay City. There, they met a certain “HR Dylan,” another individual from their Telegram group who claimed to be connected with the employer. This person personally handed them the Php 4,000 allowance. Thereafter, they proceeded to the airline and travel tax counters. A second contact met them at the terminal – later identified as PAOLO NICANDRO CUNETA – who introduced himself as an Immigration Assistant. CUNETA allegedly works for the same online gaming operation previously operated by the Chinese recruiter. He provided and facilitated the passengers with documents to be presented to the Bureau of Immigration during departure, and coached them on how to go through pre-departure immigration checks, even pointing them to a specific counter and officer. However, before they could proceed to immigration screening, they were invited by the DMW employees at their office pertaining to their flights. They were told that they were reported to the Department of Migrant Workers as potential victims of human trafficking for being illegally recruited and leaving the country to work in Cambodia without the necessary requirements and documents from the Department. body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today said it has arrested a Belgian national engaged in Trafficking In Persons by receiving and maintaining minor Filipina girls for the purpose of sexual exploitation. The NBI said the Belgian national, PROSPER SLACHMUYLDERS, was arrested in his house located at Purok 2, Soom, Trinidad, Bohol in the evening of June 26, 2015, on the basis of illegal possession of child pornographic materials and for being caught inflagrante while about to engage in a sexual act with a minor, both of which are violations of R.A. 9775 (Anti-Child Pornography At of 2009) and R.A. 9208 (Anti-Trafficking In Persons Act of 2003 as Amended), respectively. In a Post-Operation Report to the Deputy Director for Special Investigation Service (DDSIS) on July 02, 2015, the NBI-Anti-Human Trafficking Division (NBI-AHTRAD) said the arrest of Subject SLACHMUYLDERS is a result of a week-long surveillance conducted by the NBI operatives on the area of the Belgian national in Bohol. The AHTRAD report stated that the case stemmed from a referral of an information on June 18, 2015 by the Citizen Crime Watch, a non-governmental organization that monitors the crime situation in the country. Initial information provided by the group to the NBI showed that a Belgian national is engaged in human trafficking of minor Filipina girls and in particular had repeatedly sexually exploited several Filipina minors inside his own house in Bohol. That Subject SLACHMUYLDERS has been taking and keeping nude pictures and videos of Filipina minors in his residence for a fee. After confirming the initial information, AHTRAD applied for a Search Warrant on June 25, 2015, which was granted on the same day by Judge Irma Zita V. Masamayor of Regional Trial Court Branch 52 of Talibon, Bohol. As directed by the Court, the items to be seized in the premises of Subject SLACHMUYLDERS include the following: “personal computer sets and laptops; hard drives; and/or flash drives (USB); internet memory stick/broad band; internet servers; pornographic films and other pornographic materials; sex toys; we cameras, digital cameras; DSLR cameras; video cameras; cell phones; and other tools and materials used or intended to be used in the commission of the crime.” On June 26, 2015, at about 11:30 p.m. NBI-AHTRAD operatives headed by its Chief, Atty. Czar Eric M. Nuque, conducted the operation resulting in the arrest of the Subject Belgian national. Seized during the operation are computer set, flash drives and camera, which contains files of naked Filipina-looking girls, some of whom appear to be minors. Also recovered during the search was the “SAMURAI” used by Subject SLACHMUYLDERS to threaten his victims, and a small white crystalline substance suspected to be methamphetamine hydrochloride or shabu. The following day, June 27, Subject SLACHMUYLDERS was brought before the Office of the Provincial Prosecutor of Bohol in Tagbilaran City for violation of R.A. 9208, R.A. 7610 (Child Abuse Law) and R.A. 9775 (otherwise known as the Anti-Child Pornography Ct of 2009). The Subject is temporary detained at Bohol Provincial Jail. Efforts to identify and locate about twenty five (25) other victims are still on-going pending the result of forensic examination of the harddrive, memory card and flash drives that were seized from Subject SLACHMUYLDERS. Three (30) other victims have already surfaced and gave their Sworn Statement during the preparation of documents for inquest proceedings.

body: An Iranian national who was indicted in the United States for conspiracy to defraud the US government was arrested by the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) agents at the Ninoy Aquino International Airport (NAIA) last week. In a report submitted to NBI Officer-In-Charge Atty. Nonnatus Caesar R. Rojas by the Foreign Liaison Division (FLD) headed by Atty. Claro De Castro, the subject was identified as: PARVIZ KHAKI alias Martin, 43, and an Iranian businessman. Investigation report disclosed that Khaki and his companions have conspired to defraud the United States of America by submitting false documents to smuggle hi-tech materials, including twenty (20) tons of specialized steel from the US in order to deliver the items to Iran. Many of these materials have nuclear applications, including the 20 tons of specialized steel, which is particularly suited for gas centrifuges used in uranium enrichment. Khaki and others were indicted by the District Court of Columbia for six (6) counts of conspiracy to defraud the United States of America, one of which was by interfering with and obstructing a lawful government function by deceit, craft, trickery and dishonest means in violation of Title 18, United States Code, Section 371; and to export and cause the exportation from the United States to Iran in violation of Title 50, United States Code, Section 1705 and Title 31, Code of Federal Regulations, Section 560.230 and 560.204; Some of the other counts pertain to fraudulent export from the United States, merchandise, articles and objects, namely — twister lathes in violation of Title 18 United States Code, Sections 2 and 554; wilfull violation of the United States laws regarding the embargo against Iran by exporting/causing to export from the US to Iran, namely nickel alloy 120 in violation of Title 18 United States Code, Sections 2 and 554. Khaki and others were also indicted in District of Columbia for smuggling, in violation of United States Code, Section 554; violating the International Emergency Economic Powers Act in violation of title 50 of the United States Code, Section 1705 and conspiracy to commit money laundering in violation of Title 18 of the United States Code, Section 1956. On May 23, 2012, the Department of Justice transmitted to the NBI Director thru the Chief, FLD, a letter request dated March 22, 2012, of the United States Department of Justice with the enclosed copy of “indictment” and “warrant of arrest” issued by the United States District of Columbia. On the same day, NBI FLD agents applied for an Urgent Ex-Parte Application for Provisional Arrest of Khaki. Thereafter, it was served to Parvis Khaki as prelude to a formal request of his extradition to the US issued by the Manila RTC Branch 31. The Order was served to Khaki before his departure at the Ninoy Aquino International Airport Terminal I to Qatar via Qatar Airways Flight QR 649. Khaki was immediately brought to the NBI where he is presently detained. The Department of Justice and the Embassy of the Islamic Republic of Iran were informed accordingly.

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today announced the arrest of one (1) individual in Antipolo City by the NBI- Special Task Force (NBI-STF) for violation of the Cybercrime Law. NBI Officer-in-Charge (OIC)-Director Eric B. Distor identified the Subject as JOHN PAUL GINETE ALINDOGAN with aliases “GLYBER ANTHONY ESPARTINEZ SIOSON”, “SY GUISSEPE ARMSTRONG CLAINGACION”, “RANDY PALACIO CRUZ”, and GUILLER RAYMOND ASIS REYES”. OIC Director Distor said that the operation stemmed from a complaint filed by the victim of Subject Alindogan. According to the complainant, she met the subject through an online dating application “Tinder”. Subject Alindogan introduced himself as Guiller Raymond Asis Reyes, 37 years old, single, and a resident of Ayala Alabang and currently works in Germany as an oil rig manager. The complainant averred that the Subject was very persistent and was always asking her to go out until complainant gave in and met with the Subject. The complainant added that they became lovers since May 2021, and claimed that Subject enticed her to create an email account for her to organize and link all her credit cards and personal email account into one, to which she agreed. In the course of their relationship, the complainant had no idea that Subject Alindogan was already stealing and syphoning her money from her credit card accounts and BDO bank account. Subject Alindogan showered the complainant with false promises like to build a diagnostic center for her to run. The subject even accompanied her to buy and negotiate for several diagnostic equipment to gain her full trust and confidence. Subject Alindogan was able to use the credit cards which he used in his unauthorized purchases and withdrawals amounting to Php 169,186.00. In addition, complainant also claimed that the Subject enticed her to invest in stocks and gave the Subject a total of Php 984,886.00 for the said investment. Unfortunately, it was too late for the complainant to know that Subject Alindogan did not invest the money and misappropriated it for himself. Days after, Subject Alindogan and the complainant was supposed to meet but the Subject never appeared. A day later, a certain Major Bernie texted the complainant informing her that Subject Alindogan was missing. The Subject allegedly claimed that he was kidnapped but because of the inconsistencies in his claims,the complainant did not believe his alibis and started to suspect the Subject. The complainant checked her credit card and bank account and found the unauthorized transactions made by the Subject. Thus, the complainant appeared before the NBI to file a complaint against the Subject. The complainant also found that her jewelries amounting to Php 900,000.00 were also missing and only the Subject knows where she was keeping them. The Subject even threatened the complainant that he might do something she will regret if she continues to avoid him. NBI-STF conducted verification against the Subject and found that Subject is wanted for Qualified Theft. On August 16, 2021, the NBI-STF received a message from the complainant informing them that Subject suddenly appeared in the clinic where she works and forcing her to meet with him and believe his alibi that he was kidnapped. The NBI-STF operatives immediately proceed to the clinic in Antipolo City. When complainant informed the operatives that Subject was on his way out of the clinic, the NBI-STF operatives approached the Subject and asked his name. The Subject introduced himself to as GUILLER RAYMOND ASIS REYES. The operatives noticed the resemblance of Reyes to the picture of the wanted individual named ALINDOGAN. The operatives asked for his ID as proof and the Subject presented his driver’s license under the name of ALINDOGAN JOHN PAUL GENETE. Thus, the NBI-STF operatives immediately placed the Subject under arrest for using another name to conceal his true identity. Subject Alindogan was presented before the Antipolo City Prosecutor’s Office for violation of Section 4(a)(1) of R.A. 10175 otherwise known as the “Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012; Article 172 in relation to Article 171 of the RPC (Falsification); Article 310 (Qualified Theft); Article 315 (Estafa); violation of R.A. 9262, otherwise known as the “Anti-Violence Against Women and Their Children Act of 2004”; and violation of R.A. 8484 otherwise known as “The Access Device Regulation Act”.

body: PRESS STATEMENT February 16, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } NBI FILES CYBER LIBEL CHARGES AGAINST FORMER NEWSMAN AND YOUTUBER OVER FAKE PRESIDENTIAL MEDICAL REPORTS PASAY, Philippines — The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) has filed criminal charges before the Department of Justice (DOJ) against a former newsman and a prominent YouTuber for the alleged dissemination of false medical information concerning President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. The charges follow a targeted cyber-surveillance operation conducted by the NBI-Cybercrime Division (NBI-CCD) in January 2026, which identified two primary sources of the misinformation. These include Jose Yumang Sonza, also known as Jay Sonza, for posts made via his Meta-verified Facebook account, and Jeffrey Luces Celiz, also known as Ka Eric Celiz, for content broadcasted via his YouTube channel, which commands nearly 10 million total views. On January 28 and 29, 2026, NBI agents documented online posts featuring a CT-scan report alongside images of the President. The posts called for transparency regarding the President’s “fitness for duty” and alleged a “deterioration” in his medical condition. Although the original Facebook posts were eventually deleted or restricted, the NBI successfully secured the evidence using digital forensic screenshots and by tracking the content as it continued to spread via reposts and citations. Simultaneously, surveillance of the “Ka Eric Celiz” YouTube channel uncovered videos that further amplified these claims, questioning the President’s ability to lead based on the unverified medical documents. The NBI has recommended that both Subjects be prosecuted for Cyber Libel under Section 4(c)(4) of R.A. 10175, also known as the Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012. Additionally, they face charges for the Unlawful Use of Means of Publication under Article 154 of the Revised Penal Code, in relation to Section 6 of the Cybercrime Prevention Act. “In an era where information can rapidly influence public perception, we remind all stakeholders that freedom of expression carries with it the responsibility to ensure accuracy and accountability,” said NBI Director Atty. Angelito DLP. Magno. Director Magno emphasized that the Bureau remains committed to policing the digital space to prevent the spread of malicious misinformation. He noted that while the NBI respects the fundamental right to free speech, it emphasizes that this right is not absolute and does not grant a license to infringe upon the rights of others. As a matter of law and public responsibility, one’s freedom of expression ends where the rights of another are violated. #NBIServes Media Contact: HA Palmer U. Mallari NBI Spokesperson [email protected]

Additionally, they face charges for the Unlawful Use of Means of Publication under Article 154 of the Revised Penal Code, in relation to Section 6 of the Cybercrime Prevention Act. “In an era where information can rapidly influence public perception, we remind all stakeholders that freedom of expression carries with it the responsibility to ensure accuracy and accountability,” said NBI Director Atty. Angelito DLP. Magno. Director Magno emphasized that the Bureau remains committed to policing the digital space to prevent the spread of malicious misinformation. He noted that while the NBI respects the fundamental right to free speech, it emphasizes that this right is not absolute and does not grant a license to infringe upon the rights of others. As a matter of law and public responsibility, one’s freedom of expression ends where the rights of another are violated. #NBIServes Media Contact: HA Palmer U. body: PRESS STATEMENT February 19, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } NBI ARRESTS ONLINE SCAM SUSPECT; ₱25 MILLION IN APPLE PRODUCTS INVOLVED PASAY CITY, Philippines – The National Bureau of Investigation – Cybercrime Division (NBI-CCD) arrested an individual for his alleged involvement in an online scam that has reportedly caused an estimated ₱25 million worth of losses in Apple products from various distributors and resellers. The case stemmed from a complaint filed by a reseller of Apple products and other technology devices who reported being defrauded through an online transaction. Investigation revealed that the Subject falsely represented himself as an authorized representative of a legitimate company, without the knowledge or authority of said company, in order to gain the trust of distributors and resellers. Using this fraudulent representation, the Subject was able to transact and acquire high-value Apple products through deceit. The scheme involved the issuance of a falsified check as payment to complete the transaction. Following a strategic investigation, NBI-CCD operatives launched an entrapment operation. The Subject was caught in flagrante delicto (in the act) as he attempted to finalize a transaction using a falsified check. The Subject is currently in custody and faces multiple criminal charges, including Estafa in relation to Section 6 of Republic Act No. 10175, also known as the Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012, Use of Falsified Documents, and the Use of Fictitious Names. This operation serves as a stern reminder that the NBI remains vigilant in the face of evolving scams. We urge business owners to exercise the highest level of due diligence: verify every identity, scrutinize every transaction, and ensure you are dealing only with authorized representatives to protect your interests from those who hide behind false titles. ATTY. ANGELITO DLP. MAGNO Acting Director, NBI #NBIServes Media Contact: HA Palmer U. Mallari NBI Spokesperson [email protected]

body: In line with the relentless efforts of the NBI against those who take advantage of the pandemic, operatives of NBI-Anti-Fraud Division (NBI-AFD) arrested a Chinese national in Manila for selling Covid-19 vaccination slot. NBI Officer-In-Charge (OIC) Director Eric B. Distor identified the Subject as XIAO SHI a.k.a. FENG WANG QUN. OIC Director Distor said that the operation stemmed from a complainant who averred that she was lured by Subject XIAO SHI to part P18,000.00 in exchange for Covid-19 vaccination slot in Manila. Subject represented himself as a member of the Manila Covid-19 vaccination team and that he could secure a vaccination slot and inoculation for the complainant since he had the right connections with the Officials of Barangay 239 Binondo, Manila. Believing Subject’s representation, complainant paid Subject P18,000.00 as pconsideration for her first dose of Covid 19 vaccine. However, after payment, Subject became elusive and kept telling the complainant to just wait. This led complainant to conduct her own verifications and contrary to Subject’s representation, the latter is not an employee nor connected with Manila Covax Team. Complainant likewise discovered that Covid vaccination slot in Manila is free. Realizing she was scammed, complainant reported the matter to NBI-AFD. During the probe, complainant averred that she was made to believe Subject’s representation as Subject showed proof of Chinese clients who got vaccinated through his assistance. On September 9, 2021, while at NBI-AFD, Subject called asking her if she was still interested to avail of Covid shot for an additional fee of Php 5,000. She agreed for a meet up at a mall Manila at around 4:00pm of the same day. After coordination with local police, NBI-AFD hatched an entrapment operation against Subject. Operatives proceeded to a mall in Binondo, Manila and strategically positioned themselves within the vicinity. Subject and complainant then met and went inside the Barangay Hall of Brgy. 239. While coming out of the hall, operatives approached the Subject. The latter, becoming aware of the presence of the operatives, attempted to fight back. Subject attempted to disarm one of the operatives causing a scuffle and commotion in the area. Subject was eventually pinned down, pacified, and placed under arrest. Recovered from Subject’s possession were the marked money handed to him by the complainant, a Covid vaccination ID of Subject bearing the name QUN F. WANG and two more Covid 19 vaccination ID bearing the names CUIYIN LIN and WENJUAN YANG and a sheet of paper bearing Chinese characters and listed amounts of money. Subject was brought to NBI-AFD office where he underwent standard booking procedures. Online verification conducted on the Covid Vaccination cards recovered from Subject SHI’s possession showed that the QR Codes of the vaccination IDs are either tampered or non-existent with the exception of WENJUAN YANG showing that the latter is fully vaccinated. In order to determine if Subject is indeed connected with the Manila Covax Team or has contacts with the barangay or the local health office, a follow up investigation/verification is on-going. Charges for Estafa under Article 315, Direct Assault under Article 148 and Disobedience of Lawful Orders of Persons in Authority under Article 151, all of the Revised Penal Code, were filed against Subject XIAO SHI a.k.a. FENG WANG QUN before the Office of the City Prosecutor, Manila.

body: PRESS STATEMENT November 8, 2022 NBI ARRESTS SEVEN AND RESCUES 36 FEMALE VICTIMS IN TWO ANTI-HUMAN TRAFFICKING OPERATIONS The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) conducted two (2) Anti-Human Trafficking operations against a massage parlor and a resto bar in Bocaue, Bulacan, which led to the arrest of JOMAR PAGADORA y MANAHON, RISA CARDOVA y LOMASAY, LORD M. RODRIGUEZ, GLENDA A. LISING, EDNA E. OSCARES, BELEN O. FLORIN, and KIT APRIL ROSE J. MORALES. The 2 operations stemmed from intelligence report received by NBI-Bulacan District Office (NBI-BULDO) on the alleged Human Trafficking activity perpetrated by several individuals in the area of Bocaue, Bulacan. Acting on the said information, NBI-BULDO conducted a surveillance operation to verify the veracity of the operation and subsequently planned an entrapment operation to apprehend the persons behind this unlawful activity. On the first operation,2 NBI-BULDO together with Provincial Social Welfare and Development Office proceeded to PISCES HEALTH SPA MASSAGE and were able to arrest Subjects Pagadora and Cardova. The operatives were able to rescue eleven (11) trafficked victims. Subsequently, NBI-BULDO proceeded to the second target, DUMAGAT GRILL RESTO BAR, and were able to arrest Subjects Rodriguez, Lising, Oscares, Florin, and Morales, who are the pimp, floor managers, and cashier, respectively of the said bar. The operation also resulted in the rescue of twenty-five (25) trafficked victims. On October 8, 2022, the arrested subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the Provincial Prosecutor of Bulacan for violation of R.A. 9208, otherwise known as the Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2003, as amended. RA 11862 is the most recent Expanded Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act.

body: PRESS STATEMENT June 10, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } In line with the relentless campaign of the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) against human trafficking, the NBI-Human Trafficking Division (HTRAD), together with NBI-South Eastern Mindanao Regional Office (SEMRO), and NBI-Digital Forensic Laboratory (DFL), under the supervision of NBI Director Judge Jaime B. Santiago (Ret.), arrested three individuals in Davao Oriental for child sexual exploitation. The case stemmed from the case referral of the Belgian Police involving a Filipina who was suspected of producing and distributing Child Sexual Abuse and Exploitation Materials (CSAEM) in exchange for monetary compensation. According to the Referral Letter, a Belgian national was lawfully apprehended in his home jurisdiction and agreed to cooperate with authorities. During the case investigation by -the Belgian Police, he disclosed the identities of CSAEM providers he had transacted with, including the Subject. Acting swiftly, the NBI-HTRAD Agents conducted surveillance operations at the Subject’s residence in Lupon, Davao Oriental, which yielded positive identification of the Subject, victims, and the location where the CSAEMs were being taken. Thus, an entrapment operation was hatched. A Warrant to Search, Seize, and Examine Computer Data (WSSECD) issued by Branch 32, Regional Trial Court of Lupon, Davao City was likewise secured. On June 3, 2025, in coordination with the local police, joint elements from NBI-HTRAD, NBI-SEMRO, and NBI-DFL, together with the Destiny Rescue Pilipinas, conducted the entrapment operation, with the assistance of DOJ IACAT, NCC-OSAEC CSAEM, Cybertip Monitoring Center, Destiny Rescue Pilipinas, Exodus Road Philippines and International Justice Mission. Upon arrival, five adult males were found outside the premises and were immediately subjected to frisking and control measures. The Subject was found inside a room with her three minor children (one daughter and two sons). Subject’s two minor nieces (children of her brother-in-law) were also present, one of whom has been seen in some of the CSAEM materials. Following a positive result of the entrapment operation, operatives served the WSSECD against the Subject, witnessed by her relatives and Barangay Officials. With assistance from the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) Region 11 and the Municipal Social Welfare and Development Office (MSWD) Lupon, Davao Oriental, all five minor children were rescued and transferred to DSWD custody for interview and formal statement-taking. Preliminary interviews also confirmed the presence of the father of the two nieces (Subject’s brother-in-law) during the operation. A detailed search of the residence resulted in the seizure of multiple mobile phones, a tablet, and a computer with a webcam setup. Various sex toys of different forms and sizes were also recovered. Onsite forensic examination yielded positive for CSAEM materials and chat logs evidencing transactions between the Subject and her clients. Subject, her husband, and brother-in-law were informed of their constitutional rights and were immediately placed under arrest for violation of Section 4(r), R.A. No. 11930 (Anti-Online Sexual Abuse or Exploitation of Children and Anti-Child Sexual Abuse Materials Act of 2022) in relation to Section 6 of R.A. No. 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012). On June 4, 2025, Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of City Prosecutor, Mati City for the aforesaid violations of law.

body: PRESS STATEMENT December 17, 2024 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI), under the leadership of its Director, Judge Jaime B. Santiago (Ret.), rescued a trafficked victim, unveiled a scamming operation, and arrested seven (7) Chinese nationals. Santiago said that the case stemmed from the complaint received by the NBI- Cybercime Division (CCD) on December 11, 2024. According to the complainant, his friend was being illegally detained and was forced to render service involuntarily and against her will. Acting on the complaint, CCD hatched an operation for the rescue of the trafficked victim, who, based on information provided by complainan, could be found at #16B Jhon Paul St., Multinational Village, Moonwalk, Paranaque City. Consequently, the NBI operatives were able to rescue the trafficked victim. Surprisingly, during the rescue operation, while the trafficked victim was identifying the perpetrators responsible for his plight, the NBI operatives witnessed and were astonished by the operational set-up found in one of the rooms of the residence, which clearly indicated that the individuals inside were engaged in scamming activities. The presence of multiple desktop computers, mobile phones, SIM cards, written scripts, and customer ledgers strongly implies an organized deceit. Santiago added that by way of controlled viewing and upon examination in plain view of the desktops used by the individuals at the area, several scripts, messaging applications with fictitious accounts, bank accounts and fraudulent cryptocurrency investment platforms were readily determined on the desktop’s interface, which strongly suggested that the individuals using these devices are engaged in fraudulent activities. Accordingly, these scripts and tools are used in scamming activities such as catfishing scams, credit cards scams, cryptocurrency scams and fake investment scams among others. There being a crime committed in the presence of the NBI operatives, seven (7) Chinese nationals were arrested in flagrante delicto for violation of (1) Section 4(a) of RA 11862 or the Expanded Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2022; Computer-related Forgery under Section 4(b) (1) of RA 10175 otherwise known as the Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012; Social Engineering Schemes under Section 4(b)(1)) of R.A 12010 otherwise known as the Anti-Financial Account Scamming Act (AFASA) in relation to RA 10175 and (4) Republic Act 10361 otherwise known as the “Domestic Workers Act” or “Batas Kasambahay”. Director Santiago commended the NBI-CCD for successfully rescuing the trafficked victim, and acting sensibly during the operation, thereby discovering the scamming activities and arresting the Chinese nationals.

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today announced the arrest of an individual in Mapandan, Pangasinan by operatives of NBI-Dagupan District Office (NBI-DADO) for selling dog meat products. NBI Officer-In-Charge (OIC) Eric Distor identified the Subject as REAH ELLASUS y SALINAS. On September 16, 2021, NBI-DADO received a report that REAH’S CANTEEN located in Mapandan, Pangasinan is engaged in selling and distribution of dog meat products to different personalities in the province. Operatives coordinated the information to Department of Agriculture Region 1, National Meat Inspection Service for validation and surveillance. On October 13, 2021, after the information was validated and securing authority to operate, NBI-DADO operatives proceeded to the target area to conduct entrapment operation. On the same day, operatives bought Php 500 worth of dog and cooked meats from Subject REAH, owner of REAH’S CANTEEN. Subject was arrested in possession and selling two (2) dog heads, eight ( 8 ) meat legs, and cooked dog meat. It is presumed that Subject had slaughtered the dogs whose meats were being sold. Subject was apprised of her constitutional rights and was brought to NBI-DADO for standard booking procedures and temporary detention. Subject REAH ELLASUS y SALINAS was presented for inquest proceedings before the Provincial Prosecution Office, Dagupan City, Pangasinan for violation of The Animal Welfare Act of 1998 as amended by RA 10631. To reiterate, the Department of Agriculture, National Meat Inspection Service issued a certification that killing of any animal other than cattle, pigs, goats, sheep, poultry, rabbits, carabaos, and horses, are declared unlawful and violation of The Animal Welfare Act.

title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: PRESS STATEMENT May 8, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } Under the leadership of Director Judge Jaime B. Santiago, the DNA Division was able to identify the missing OFW who were among the casualties of the earthquake that hit Myanmar on March 28, 2025. Director Santiago on April 4, 2025, immediately dispatched the NBI Forensic Team composed of doctors, dentist, forensic chemist, DNA Analysts, photographer, and other support staff to assist in the identification of fatalities. Thereat, the embassy officials turned over biological samples (hair and two (2) teeth from each body) of two (2) Filipinos previously retrieved from the collapsed Sky Villa Condominium in Mandalay. On April 5, 2025, the group travelled from Yangon to Mandalay. Two (2) other Filipino casualties were recovered by local authorities and later identified by the NBI Forensic Experts with the assistance of the relatives of the deceased, through secondary parameters (tattoos, personal belongings, identification documents, and similarity on the comparison of dental profile with the photographs of the teeth on the recovered remains). The dental profile picture was provided by relatives and friends of the victims. On April 9, 2025, another dead body of a Filipino was retrieved from the condominium and was properly identified and documented with the guide of dental photographs and profile. In the DNA Report dated May 02, 2025, it was concluded that the DNA profile obtained from the specimen samples obtained from the earthquake fatalities i.e. hair strands, two (2) pieces teeth in comparison, from the reference samples-Buccal swab and blood taken from the immediate member of the family matches that of the four (4) casualties. The NBI Director congratulates the brave men and women of the forensic team for their hardship, sacrifices, and commitment to public service in performing their respective tasks.

She mustered enough courage to tell her mother who was then on a short vacation, her grandmother, and her aunt, that she is being repeatedly raped by her father. Before leaving for Oman, victim’s mother entrusted her to a guardian and requested the latter to do whatever necessary legal action to bring the father to justice. It was confirmed by the medical check-up that the victim is no longer a virgin. However, instead of standing up to defend her honor, the grandmother convinced her to point to somebody else as the one who raped her, and her aunt also suggested not to disclose the result of her check-up to her mother. Worse, in an attempt to cover-up the crime committed, the grandmother tried to convince the doctor to change the result of the examination and to make it appear that the victim is still a virgin. This fact was attested by the doctor who also executed a statement. Record check on the Subjects disclosed that the father has a bench warrant of arrest for Reckless Imprudence Resulting in Damage to Property issued on April 18, 2005. On the other hand, an alias arrest warrant was issued on June 29, 2007 against the grandmother for Estafa. After confirming that the arrest warrants were still out and standing, operatives of NBI-Special Action Unit (NBI-SAU) arrested the victim’s father and grandmother in their residence in Dasmarinas, Cavite. Subject was subjected for inquest proceedings for the aforementioned violations. Cyber surveillance was then conducted confirming that the Subject was engaged in online selling of endangered species. Subsequently, an entrapment operation was hatched resulting in the arrest of the Subject. The case stemmed from the information of Mr. Jose Ferdinand Tuason regarding the Subject who was allegedly using the Presidential Management Staff Office in order to entice people to join the group of Moral Recovery Program with a promised monetary benefits to the members for a consideration of Php 500 membership fee. Acting on the information, an operation was conducted confirming the illegal activity. Verification from Presidential Management Staff Office revealed that the Subject is not authorized to conduct such activity and they confirmed that they have no existing programs/projects/activities with the Baptist Bishop of the Philippines. With this, Subject was formally arrested and was presented for inquest proceedings for the above-mentioned crimes. On June 16, 2018 , operatives of NBI-National Capital Region arrested DANILO DE LEON CHAN in an entrapment for Robbery/Usurpation of Authority. The case stemmed from the complaint of Rizalea B. Magramo against some personalities who were collecting money from her. It was gathered that Subject CHAN collects aggregate amount of Php 65,000 a week from more than ten (10) clubs/bars in Angeles City which he remits to a certain Reniel who represented himself as an NBI employee and currently being investigated. Acting on the complaint, NBI-NCR operatives conducted an entrapment operation resulting in the arrest of the Subject. Subject was presented for inquest proceeding before the City Prosecutor, Angeles City, Pampanga for the above-mentioned crimes. On June 16, 2018 , operatives of NBI-CARAGA arrested ELGIN FREDRIC ANDERSON, An American national, for violation of RA 9775 ( Anti‐Child Pornography. Act of 2009) in relation to RA 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012). Subject was arrested by virtue of Search Warrant issued by RTC Branch 2, Butuan City. The case stemmed from an information that a foreign national is in possession and maintenance of child pornographic materials with the aid of a computer at his rented house at Brgy. 2 Lawang, Buenavista, Agusan Del Norte. Recovered from the subject were soft copies of nude pictures of minors, some were doing lascivious sexual acts. The operation was duly coordinated with the US Embassy in Manila and the Bureau of Immigration through the Office of the Cybercrime, Department of Justice, Manila. Subject was presented for inquest proceedings before the CARAGA Prosecutor’s Office for the aforementioned violations. On June 19, 2018, operatives of NBI-Cybercrime Division (NBI-CCD) arrested MICHELLE CLAVECILLAS by virtue of Warrant of Arrest for Theft. Subject was a subject of investigation by the command. Coincidentally, Subject has an outstanding Warrant of Arrest for three (3) counts of Theft. Hence, NBI-CCD operatives apprehended the Subject in her residence at Gen.Trias, ImusCavite. Subject underwent proper booking procedures and was detained at the NBI detention cell. On June 21, 2018 , operatives of NBI-Special Task Force (NBI-STF) arrested ARTURO D. BUNIOL, GARY V. ATANACIO and EDGARDO Y. JAVIER, Special Investigators at the BIR – Regional Investigation Division (BIR – RID) for violations of RA 3019 (Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act), RA 6713 (Code of Conduct and Ethical Standards for Public Officials and Employees) and Article 210 (Bribery) of the Revised Penal Code. The case stemmed from a complaint affidavit filed by Commissioner GRECO BELGICA of the Presidential Anti-Corruption Commission (PACC) before the NBI-Special Task Force against the three (3) employees of the BIR-RID. Based on the complaint affidavit, Commissioner Belgica received an information from an employee of a Chinese Restaurant that employees of the BIR-RID were conducting surveillance/investigation on the operation of their restaurant despite the fact that said restaurant has only been operating for one year. The complaint also stated that the BIR-RID has already conducted the investigation and has assessed the restaurant’s tax liability amounting to P1,200,000.00. The above-named Subjects later on informed the employee of the restaurant that they need to pay 50% (P600,000.00) of the assessed tax liability and to secure the services of an accountant. Based on this information, PACC Commissioner Belgica thereafter acted as a lady accountant using the name KATH LEGASPI thru text messages to determine the purpose of the P600,000.00 that the Subjects were asking for. Thru exchange of messages, Comm. Belgica (acting as KATH LEGASPI) discovered that the Subjects were asking for P75,000.00 from the P600,000.00 for restaurant’s alleged tax liability and the balance will be given to the “other side”, which the Subjects were referring. On the basis of the complaint-affidavit operatives of the NBI-STF conducted an entrapment operation in Greenhills San Juan which resulted in the arrest of the Subjects. On June 21, 2018 , operatives of NBI-Cybercrime Division (NBI-CCD) arrested ALEX ENDOSO SANCHEZ in entrapment operation for violations of RA 9262 (Anti-Violence Against Women and Their Children Act of 2004), RA 9995 (Anti-Photo and Video Voyeurism Act of 2009) in relation to RA 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012). The case stemmed from the complaint of Jobelyn S. Badol who alleged that Subject threatened to spread out her pictures and sex video should she failed to comply with his demands. Subject was apprehended in flagrante delicto by the NBI-CCD operatives. He was presented for inquest proceedings for the aforementioned violations. On June 22, 2018 , operatives of NBI-Intellectual Property Rights Division (NBI-IPRD) seized counterfeit Hyundai items with an estimated amount of Php 15 Million , in Las Pinas, Manila and Paranaque by virtue of Search Warrants. The case stemmed from the complaint filed by Hyundai Motor Company before the NBI, seeking assistance against an erring business establishments that are engaged in the sale, marketing, manufacturing, distribution and commercial use of the Hyundai registered trademarks without the consent and authority of the true owner, Hyundai Motor. Charges for violation of RA 8293 (Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines) will be filed against the appropriate individuals. On June 22, 2018 , operatives of NBI-International Airport Investigation Unit (NBI-IAIU) rescued (17) female human trafficking victims in a rescue operation in Indang Cavite. The operation also resulted in the arrest SIMPLICIO RIGAT PUNZALAN, driver of the recruitment agency ADVANCE STEP INTERNATIONAL MANPOWER SERVICES. The operation was based on information gathered from a victim, a passenger bound for Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, who was denied departure by Bureau of Immigration at NAIA Terminal 1 for appearing to be a minor. Investigation conducted by the NBI-IAIU disclosed that said victim was indeed a minor and told the NBI-IAIU that she was recruited by a certain HAIRIA UGAN of ADVANCE STEP INTERNTIONAL MANPOWER SERVICES in General Santos City and stayed in an accommodation house of the agency in Ermita, Manila and Cubao, Quezon City, together with several applicants for abroad who she believed to be minors. The victim also told the NBI-IAIU that she learned through her messenger account that all the young applicants of the agency are to be transported to Indang, Cavite accommodation house as the agency was alarmed of her departure denial. It was confirmed that the house in Indang, Cavite where the minor applicants were moved is owned by Subject PUNZALAN. The Subject was brought before the Pasay City Prosecutors Office for inquest proceedings. Also recommended for prosecution are the officers of ADVANCE STEP INTERNATIONAL MANPOWER SERVICES, INC. for violation of Republic Act 9208 in relation to R.A. 7610, and Republic Act 8042, namely: RUEL F. LUCAS, President; GLENDA S. SHAMMARY, Corporate Treasurer; GLADYS SACUEZA, Director/General Manager; JOANN OLIVEROS, Director; and GLERICA SACUEZA, Corporate Secretary/Liaison Officer. In two separate operations dated June 6 and June 20, 2018 , operatives of NBI-Laguna District Office (NBI-LAGDO) arrested three (3) individuals for illegal gambling. The Subjects are identified as DARWIN NOLASCO GONZAL, CRISENCIO BAGO MULLET, and RAFAEL MOLDEZ GUAPEZA. Subjects were arrested in anti-gambling operations for acting as bet collectors in the areas of Muntinlupa City, and Las Pinas City. Seized from the Subjects’ possession are betting list, jueteng paraphernalia, and bet money. Charges for violation of PD 1602 in relation to RA 9287 (Illegal Gambling Law) were filed against the Subjects before the City Prosecutor of Muntinlupa City.

ATANACIO and EDGARDO Y. JAVIER, Special Investigators at the BIR – Regional Investigation Division (BIR – RID) for violations of RA 3019 (Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act), RA 6713 (Code of Conduct and Ethical Standards for Public Officials and Employees) and Article 210 (Bribery) of the Revised Penal Code. body: PRESS STATEMENT October 28, 2024 In accordance with the marching order of National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Director JUDGE JAIME B. SANTIAGO (Ret.) to eradicate the crime of online child sexual exploitation and abuse, the NBI- Human Trafficking Division (NBI-HTRAD) arrested a Filipina Facilitator in an entrapment operation and implementation of Warrant to Search and Examine Computer Data (WSSECD) in Taguig City. The operation stemmed from an information received by the NBI-HTRAD that an alleged facilitator in the Philippines is transmitting sexually exploitative images and videos of minors into the United States (US). Acting on the information, NBI-HTRAD operatives conducted a series of surveillance operations, which resulted in the discovery of the whereabouts of the Subject and the victims. The NBI-HTRAD then applied for a WSSECD against the Subject, which was granted by the Regional Trial Court, Branch 15, Family Court of Taguig City. On October 21, 2024, information provided to the NBI-HTRAD disclosed that Subject continues to offer live shows of her two (2) minor daughters in exchange for money. Subject informed the undercover agent that the live show will commence at exactly 01:00 in the afternoon on the same day. Thus, on even date, the operatives of NBI-HTRAD conducted an entrapment operation and implemented the WSSECD against the premises of the Subject. The operation resulted in the arrest of the Subject in the act of offering her children to perform sexually explicit shows and the rescue of four (4) minor victims. The operatives also confiscated computer devices, various sex toys, and money remittances in the Subject’s premises. Director Santiago commended the NBI-HTRAD for their action in the NBI’s campaign against online sexual abuse of children and appealed to the public to report to the NBI any information that may lead to the arrest of persons involved in this nefarious activity.

body: PRESS STATEMENT May 26, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } In line with the campaign to stop the proliferation of counterfeit products, the National Bureau of Investigation Intellectual Property Rights Division (NBI-IPRD), under the leadership of Director JUDGE JAIME B. SANTIAGO (Ret.), implemented multiple search warrants in various locations in Manila City, Navotas City, Quezon City, and Bacoor, Cavite on May 15 and 19, 2025 for violation of Section 155 (Trademark Infringement) and Section 168 (Unfair Competition) in relation to Section 170 of Republic Act 8293 or the Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines. The cases stemmed from the complaint filed by LEE BUMGARNER INC. (LBI) on behalf of their clients, VICTORIA’S SECRET, BATH & BODY WORKS, and PROCTER & GAMBLE (P&G). On May 15 and 19, IPRD agents implemented search warrants against seventeen (17) stalls in Binondo, Manila, one (1) store in Tondo, Manila, one (1) store/facility in Navotas City, one (1) store in Quezon City, and one (1) store in Bacoor, Cavite. Enforcement of these search warrants resulted in the seizure of a voluminous quantity of counterfeit/fake products. Seized items include Five Thousand Five Hundred and Ninety-One (5,591) pieces of assorted products bearing the “Victoria’s Secret trademark, Two Thousand One Hundred and Seven (2,107) pieces of assorted products bearing the “Bath & Body Works” trademark, and Five Thousand One Hundred and Twenty-Eight (5,128) products bearing the “Procter & Gamble” trademark, with a total estimated value of Seven Million Two Hundred Fourteen Thousand One Hundred and Fifty-Five Pesos (Php 7,214,155.00). The searches were conducted in a peaceful and orderly manner in the presence of the Respondent’s witnesses, Building Representative, and Barangay Representative. Director Santiago lauded the NBI-IPRD for successfully implementing said warrants and their enforcement actions to stop the proliferation and distribution of counterfeit/fake products. NBI reminds the public to refrain from patronizing pirated products to give protection to the intellectual property rights owners and enhance our economic growth.

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today announced the arrest of four (4) individuals by the operatives of NBI- Olongapo District Office (NBI-OLDO) for Human Trafficking in Olongapo City. NBI Officer-In-Charge (OIC) Director Eric B. Distor identified the subjects as JACKYLOU LASTIMADO, RAMIL ENTERNO, MONICA LABANDELO, and JESTHONY TELAN y GOMEZ. OIC Director Distor said that the operation stemmed from an intelligence report provided by Destiny Rescue Filipinas regarding the human trafficking activities of a certain JACKYLOU LASTIMADO a.k.a. “JACKY” and MONICA CORUM a.k.a. “MONIC” in the City of Olongapo and nearby municipalities. According to the report both Subjects Lastimado and Corum acted as pimps to prospective clients by procuring, offering, promoting, facilitating or inducing minors specifically high school students and out of school youths by taking advantage of their vulnerability to engage in prostitution and other sexual activities in exchange for monetary consideration. After validating the report, 2 operations in different venues/hotels were planned by NBI-OLDO. Thus on August 4, 2021, NBI-OLDO conducted 2 simultaneous operations at the agreed meeting place of the poseur-client and subjects in Subic Freeport Zone, Olongapo City, which led to the arrest of the 4 subjects. The operations also led to the rescue of ten (10) trafficked victims, six (6) of whom are minors. The minors were turned- over to the City’s Social Welfare and Drvelopment Office. The arrested subjects were presented for Inquest proceedings before the City Prosecutor’s Office of Olongapo City on August 5, 2021 for 5 counts of Human Trafficking under R.A. 9208 otherwise known as the Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2003 and 5 counts for violation of R.A. 7610 or the Special Protection of Children Against Abuse, Exploitation and Discrimination Act.

body: PRESS STATEMENT May 19, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } PRESS RELEASE | NBI-SAU DISMANTLES ONLINE LOVE SCAMMING AND CRYPTO FRAUD OPERATION IN PARAÑAQUE CITY; 17 ARRESTED The National Bureau of Investigation – Special Action Unit (NBI-SAU) successfully conducted an operation against an alleged organized online scamming syndicate engaged in “Love Scamming Activities,” “Pig Butchering,” and “Cryptocurrency Investment Fraud” in Parañaque City. On May 15, 2026, NBI-SAU operatives proceeded to No. 9 Patmos Street, Multinational Village, Parañaque City to serve the Warrant to Search, Seize, and Examine Computer Data (WSSECD) issued by the Regional Trial Court of Parañaque. Upon serving the warrant, SAU operatives discovered that the alleged illegal activities were being conducted on the third floor of the premises, where they found a call center-like setup consisting of multiple computer workstations, mobile phones, internet routers, and other digital devices allegedly used in online scamming operations. Operatives also discovered a separate room allegedly intended for “models,” where a computer installed with the “AI SWAP 2” application, reportedly capable of AI-based face replacement or deepfake technology, was recovered. Seventeen (17) individuals were arrested during the operation, including fourteen (14) Filipino nationals and three (3) foreign nationals, who were allegedly caught actively operating computer systems and communication devices at the time of the raid. Initial forensic examination conducted by the NBI-Digital Forensic Laboratory revealed that the alleged operation systematically targeted foreign nationals, particularly individuals in the United States, Bangkok, and several European countries, through online dating applications and messaging platforms such as WhatsApp, Telegram, Grindr, and similar services. Investigators discovered alleged fake online identities, deceptive romantic approaches, and pre-written scripts designed to build trust, establish emotional relationships, obtain personal and financial information, and eventually persuade victims to send money. Operatives further uncovered alleged schemes involving fabricated financial emergencies, investment opportunities, and urgent personal situations, with victims reportedly instructed to transfer funds through cryptocurrency wallets linked to a suspected bogus cryptocurrency website identified as “cexonline.uk.” Investigators believe the use of cryptocurrency was intended to conceal the traceability of transactions and facilitate the movement of illegally obtained funds. All digital evidence and equipment covered by the warrant were seized, inventoried, and documented in accordance with established procedures. The arrested individuals were subsequently brought to NBI-SAU office for proper booking and documentation. On May 16, 2026, Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the State of Prosecutors of the Department of Justice for violation of Section 4 (b)(2) of R.A. No. 10175, or the Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012. NBI Director Atty. Melvin A. Matibag said that the successful dismantling of the alleged online fraud operation demonstrates the Bureau’s firm commitment to protecting the public from cyber-enabled crimes and holding accountable those who exploit technology to deceive and victimize others. “As cybercriminals continue to evolve and adopt more sophisticated methods, the NBI continues to work closely with our partner agencies to pursue individuals and groups engaged in illegal online activities and ensure that justice is served,” he added.
