body: A well- known member of the Abu Sayaff Group (ASG) was arrested by the National Bureau of Investigation – Counter Terrorism Division (NBI- CTD) during an operation in Zamboanga City. The suspect is identified by NBI Director Virgilio L. Mendez as: ABDULLA SATTAR, of legal age and a resident of Barangay Tumalutab Island, Zamboanga City. In an investigation report, it was disclosed that Sattar, also known as Satar or Abu Satar was the acting ASG financier in a Kidnap for Ransom activities which was under the leadership of Ustadz Ibrahim Ali y Kalim. On June 22, 2014 the NBI- CTD law enforcement together with the Presidential Anti- Organized Crime Commission (PAOCC), Naval Special Operation Group and Task Force Zamboanga led an operation upon receiving a warrant of arrest for Kidnapping and Serious Illegal Detention with Ransom, issued by RTC branch 266 of Pasig City. The said warrant was under Criminal Case No. 128923- H A to E (6 counts). An affidavit of identification of a victim/ witness was also subscribed before a State Prosecutor of the Department of Justice raided the house of Sattar situated at Barangay Tumalutab Island, Zamboanga City. Sattar’s location was pinpointed by the Armed Forces of the Philippines through their intelligence operative. During the operation, the suspect was arrested and was informed of his constitutional rights and reason of arrest. Abdulla Sattar was brought to Manila at the headquarters of the National Bureau of Investigation where he was booked, fingerprinted and photographed, right after the NBI- CTD operatives went to the Police Regional office 9 for the initial tactical questioning.

body: ⦁ On July 22, 2020, operatives of NBI- Environmental Crimes Division (NBI-EnCD) arrested NARCISO PEJI y DIONIDO, MARY JANE MAALA y ILAGAN, RYAN NAPARAM y ROCERO, ALVIN AQUINO y CORNEJO, JOSE REMY COPONES y LOVITE, EMMANUEL MANAO y SACE, ROBERT DELOS SANTOS y AQUINO, JOEBERT AGUISANDA y ANBANO, and ROGER BETONIO y SALAZAR in Ternate, Cavite for illegal mining. Subjects were arrested in entrapment operation which stemmed from the request of DENR-MGB IV-A to implement a Cease and Desist Order for illegal mining. Subjects were seen in the area supervising, hauling, and transporting minerals without necessary permits or documents issued by the DENR. The operation also led to the seizure of multiple mining equipment and minerals valued at around Php 10.1 Million and Php 6,500, respectively. Subjects were presented for online inquest proceedings before the Office of the Provincial Prosecutor-Imus, Cavite for violation of Section 103 (theft of Minerals) of RA 7942 otherwise known as the Philippine Mining Act of 1995. ⦁ On August 4, 2020, operatives of NBI-International Airport Investigation Division (NBI-IAID) recommended for prosecution Immigration Officers (IO) as PERRY MICHAEL Q. PANCHO, IO at Mactan Cebu International Airport (MCIA) and MARCUS S. NICODEMUS, IO at NAIA Terminal 1, Pasay City for falsifying travel records of an Austrian national with criminal records. On June 25, 2020, reports came out that Austrian national JAN MARSALEK, the subject in the US 2.2 Billion Dollar Wirecard fraud in Germany had entered the Philippines on June 23, 2020 in order to evade authorities in Europe. As this information circulated in the airports, operatives of NBI-IAID conducted investigation. Investigation conducted shows that MARSALEK’s most recent travel records to the country include spurious ones, to wit: Arrival on June 23, 2020 at NAIA 1 processed by a certain IO Ilagan but with a “cancelled by user” remark, and a Departure on June 24, 2020 at Mactan Cebu International Airport processed by IO Perry Michael Pancho. body: PRESS STATEMENT June 30, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } PRESS RELEASE | NBI ARRESTS A BOGUS ALECO PERSONNEL IN ILLEGAL ELECTRICITY PILFERAGE The National Bureau of Investigation-Bicol Regional Office (NBI-BRO) arrested an individual in an operation against violation of Republic Act 7832 (Anti-Electricity Pilferage Act of 1994), Estafa and Grave Coercion. The operation emanated from a complaint filed by a consumer and a request of Albay Electric Cooperative, Inc. (ALECO) against unidentified male individuals allegedly representing themselves as ALECO employees conducting inspection and related activities. During a visit said individuals inquired about consumer’s electric bill and thereafter offered to reduce her monthly billing in exchange for money. Relying on the representation that they were legitimate ALECO personnel, the consumer agreed and paid Php1,000.00. Thereafter, the individuals allegedly tampered with the electric meter, assured her that her electric bill would decrease and provided a Facebook account for further communication. After more than one month, a male person claiming to be an ALECO inspector checked her electric meter and allegedly found a bypass wire (jumper). He proceeded to make a Metering Facilities Inspection Report and then informed this consumer that she could face criminal charges and fine should his report be submitted to ALECO. He further stated that he would receive incentives ranging from Php14, 000.00 to Php 16, 000.00 upon filing the report. The inspector then allegedly offered to withhold said report in exchange for money equivalent to his incentive. The amount was eventually reduced to Php10, 000.00. Fearing legal action and penalties, she gave an initial Php1,500.00 with the remaining Php8, 500.00 to be collected later. Based on these circumstances, consumer believed that the individuals were acting in concert and were using deception, intimidation, and false representation as ALECO personnel to extort money from her. This prompted her to seek the assistance of the NBI. Verification with ALECO revealed that there was no work order, mission order, service order, authority or similar directive for the conduct of meter inspection, anti-pilferage operation or any other related field activity at the premises of the said consumer on said dates. On the basis of the foregoing information, an entrapment operation was planned. Subsequent surveillance was conducted, sworn statements were taken and marked money was readied. On June 18, 2026, NBI-BRO Agents strategically positioned themselves in the vicinity of the consumer’s residence. At around 8:40 AM, the alleged ALECO Inspector arrived. After conversing with consumer, he opened the electric meter and removed the bypass wire (jumper). Immediately thereafter he collected and received the marked money from consumer. Upon receipt of the marked money, NBI-BRO agents approached, introduced themselves as NBI agents and arrested said individual. He was caught in flagrante delicto tampering with the electric meter without the consent or authority from ALECO and at the same time was caught red handed in possession of the marked money. Subsequently, NBI-BRO Agent informed him of his constitutional rights. After securing the Subject, the Team together with the Subject proceeded to the Office of the NBI-BRO where Subject was properly booked, fingerprinted, photographed as per standard operating procedure. Medical Examination was then conducted by NBI-Medico-Legal Doctor. After preparing the necessary documents for inquest proceedings, criminal complaints for Republic Act 7832 (Anti-Electricity Pilferage Act of 1994), Estafa, and Grave Coercion were filed before the City Prosecutor’s Office of Legazpi City, Albay. Thereafter, on June 22, 2026, NBI-BRO received an Inquest Resolution from the Office of the City Prosecutor of Legazpi City finding prima facie evidence with reasonable certainty of conviction.

body: PRESS STATEMENT November 08, 2024 The National Bureau of Investigation-Cebu District Office (NBI-CEBDO), under the supervision of NBI Director Judge Jaime B. Santiago (Ret.), conducted follow-up operations as regards the POGO Hub in Lapu-Lapu City, Cebu. The follow-up operations were an offshoot of the joint operation conducted on August 31, 2024 at the POGO Hub located at the compound of the Tourist Garden Hotel at Brgy. Agus, Lapu-Lapu City, Cebu by composite teams from NBI-Central Visayas Regional Office (NBI-CEVRO), NBI-Cebu District Office (NBI-CEBDO), Presidential Anti-Organized Crime Commission (PAOCC), Military Intelligence Group (MIG-7), Philippine Transnational Crime Commission, Inter-Agency Council Against Trafficking (IACAT-7) and the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD-7), where more or less one hundred sixty nine (169) foreign nationals, mostly Chinese and Indonesians, were rescued and sixteen (16) Chinese and Burmese nationals were indicted for violation of RA 9208 or the Trafficking in Persons Act of 2002. As follow up to the said operation, Search Warrants were applied for and duly granted by RTC Branch 67, Lapu-Lapu City, to search the two (2) buildings inside the compound of the Tourist Garden Hotel where the online illegal activities of the foreign nationals are concentrated. Implementation of said Search Warrants resulted in the seizure of voluminous computer units and electronic gadgets as well as several vaults. On October 22, 2024, an application for another Search Warrant was initiated for the conduct of a search on Building No. 8 occupied as offices and bedroom of the POGO Operator, MR. ZHAO, SHOU QI. On October 23, 2024, said Search Warrant was duly implemented at the subject building wherein bundles of documents indicating the active engagement on POGO operation by Subject ZHAO SHOU QI were seized. Also, found inside the offices of MR. ZHAO, SHOU QI were several computer units and seven (7) steel vaults which were then preserved and stored at the said office of ZHAO, SHOU QI. As granted by the court, the seven (7) steel vaults were opened and resulted in the seizure of documents which will be used to solidify the cases filed against Subject ZHAO, SHOU QI et. al. for violation of RA 9208. Aside from the documents, cash in the total amount of Php 440,620.00 was likewise recovered and seized. The same will be turned over to the issuing court. Director Santiago lauded the NBI-CEBDO and law enforcement counterparts for pursuing the case. He stressed that NBI is dedicated to upholding the law and will never tolerate the harm that these POGO Hubs cause to individuals and society as a whole.

body: In line with the relentless campaign of the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) against environmental crimes, operatives of NBI-Environmental Crime Division (NBI-EnCD) arrested five individuals for disposing and extracting boulders and minerals from Balanac River, Laguna without necessary permits. NBI Officer-in-Charge (OIC) Director Eric B. Distor identified the Subjects as Brgy. Balanac Chairman DENNIS OLIPANO, MICHAEL ABAD y MARTINEZ, RANDY DELOS REYES y MARTINEZ, DANILO NORIEL y SATERA, and ABNER DAVAC y CABREGA. OIC Director Distor said that the operation stemmed from a report regarding an alleged illegal quarry operation in Brgy. Balanac, Municipality of Magdalena, Province of Laguna. Operatives conducted series of surveillance operation to verify the veracity of the information and they were able to confirm the ongoing quarry operation at the said area. They were also able to transact with the seller, the Chairman of Brgy. Balanac, DENNIS OLIPANO, who agreed to sell four (4) truck loads of boulders for a price of Php 17,000 per truck. On March 11, 2021, a joint team of NBI-EnCD, DENR-Environmental Protection and Enforcement Task Force (EPETF), DENR-Mines and Geosciences Bureau (MGB) and Philippine Army 1st Infantry Battalion was formed to conduct the operation. At around 2pm of that day, above-mentioned Subjects were arrested for disposing and extracting boulders and minerals from Balanac River, Laguna without necessary permits from DENR-MGB or the PMRB-Laguna. Seized from the operation are four (4) trucks with a total estimated value of Php 6 Million and 30 cubic meters of boulders and fabricated screens with an estimated value of Php 43,000. Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the Prosecutor, Department of Justice, Manila for violation of Section 103 of RA 7942 (Philippine Mining Act of 1995) and Section 3 (e) of RA 3019 (Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act).

body: PRESS STATEMENT August 2, 2022 NBI ARRESTS FUGITIVE FOR SEVERAL YEARS The National Bureau of Investigation- Task Force Against Illegal Drugs (NBI-TFAID) arrested FRANK CHUA, a fugitive from justice for several years. It was on August 10, 1989 when FRANK CHUA and several others were arrested for shabu smuggling. A criminal complaint for violation of Section 14 of RA 6425 otherwise known as the Dangerous Drugs Act of 1972 was filed on August 18, 1989 against CHUA et.al. before Candon, Ilocos Sur RTC for importation of 58 kilograms of shabu in Ilocos Sur. CHUA and other accused were transferred to Vigan Provincial Jail pending their trial. However, on March 22, 1990, all the accused escaped from Vigan Provincial Jail. Trial in absentia ensued and on October 7, 1994, the court found CHUA and all other accused guilty of the charge against them and sentenced them to suffer the penalty of Reclusion Perpetua. CHUA hid in several places in the Philippines but settled inside the Subic Bay Freeport Zone in 1997 and even put up Ding Ho Restaurant and Zone Swan International Inc. with PHILLIP CHUA and ANTON ANG, as front companies in their drug trafficking activities. FRANK CHUA was arrested by operatives of NBI-Anti-Illegal Drug Task Force on July 4, 2003 at Ding Ho Restaurant, Subic Bay Freeport Zone and was committed to New Bilibid Prison (NBP). When the NBI Anti-Illegal Drugs Task Force operatives went to the NBP to get information from FRANK CHUA about the shabu smuggling incident, they failed to see him as NBP officials claimed that he did not want to talk to anyone, even to his own lawyer. This led to suspicion that FRANK CHUA may no longer be inside the NBP and the action of some NBP officials was just a cover-up to hide the true whereabouts of FRANK CHUA. Unknown to the NBI and other law enforcement authorities, FRANK CHUA, while serving his time at the NBP, was confined at the Metropolitan Hospital in Binondo, Manila but escaped therefrom on February 28, 2004. No Alert Notice or Request for Manhunt of the escaped convict FRANK CHUA was sent to the Department of Justice (DOJ), Bureau of Immigration (BI), NBI, and other law enforcement authorities. On July 28, 2022, after over 18 years of freedom, FRANK CHUA was arrested by NBI-TFAID in Sampaloc, Manila. FRANK CHUA admitted that he was the same person arrested for drug offense several times.

NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION

PRESS STATEMENT August 2, 2022 NBI ARRESTS FUGITIVE FOR SEVERAL YEARS The National Bureau of Investigation- Task Force Against Illegal Drugs (NBI-TFAID) arrested FRANK CHUA, a fugitive from justice for several years. It was on August 10, 1989 when FRANK CHUA and several others were arrested for shabu smuggling. A criminal complaint for violation of Section 14 of RA 6425 otherwise known as the Dangerous Drugs Act of 1972 was filed on August 18, 1989 against CHUA et.al. before Candon, Ilocos Sur RTC for importation of 58 kilograms of shabu in Ilocos Sur. CHUA and other accused were transferred to Vigan Provincial Jail pending their trial. However, on March 22, 1990, all the accused escaped from Vigan Provincial Jail. Trial in absentia ensued and on October 7, 1994, the court found CHUA and all other accused guilty of the charge against them and sentenced them to suffer the penalty of Reclusion Perpetua. CHUA hid in several places in the Philippines but settled inside the Subic Bay Freeport Zone in 1997 and even put up Ding Ho Restaurant and Zone Swan International Inc. with PHILLIP CHUA and ANTON ANG, as front companies in their drug trafficking activities. FRANK CHUA was arrested by operatives of NBI-Anti-Illegal Drug Task Force on July 4, 2003 at Ding Ho Restaurant, Subic Bay Freeport Zone and was committed to New Bilibid Prison (NBP). When the NBI Anti-Illegal Drugs Task Force operatives went to the NBP to get information from FRANK CHUA about the shabu smuggling incident, they failed to see him as NBP officials claimed that he did not want to talk to anyone, even to his own lawyer. This led to suspicion that FRANK CHUA may no longer be inside the NBP and the action of some NBP officials was just a cover-up to hide the true whereabouts of FRANK CHUA. Unknown to the NBI and other law enforcement authorities, FRANK CHUA, while serving his time at the NBP, was confined at the Metropolitan Hospital in Binondo, Manila but escaped therefrom on February 28, 2004. No Alert Notice or Request for Manhunt of the escaped convict FRANK CHUA was sent to the Department of Justice (DOJ), Bureau of Immigration (BI), NBI, and other law enforcement authorities. On July 28, 2022, after over 18 years of freedom, FRANK CHUA was arrested by NBI-TFAID in Sampaloc, Manila. FRANK CHUA admitted that he was the same person arrested for drug offense several times.

body: PRESS STATEMENT October 12, 2022 NBI ARRESTS ONE FOR ILLEGAL PRACTICE OF OPTOMETRY The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today announced the arrest of JOSEPHINE NAZARREA y BALANG for illegal practice of Optometry in Brgy. San Francisco, Iriga City. NBI received a complaint from the Integrated Philippine Association of Optometrists, Inc. (IPAO)-Camarines Sur regarding the alleged illegal practice of Optometry they monitored in N. Balang Sagara Optical Clinic at the New Iriga City Public Market. Thus, agents of the NBI Naga District Office conducted a surveillance on the said establishment and confirmed the information. NBI-NAGA requested a certification on Philippine Regulation Commission (PRC) to validate the licensed of the Subject. PRC issued a document stating that LORENZO NAZARREA, JOSEPHINE BALANG NAZARREA, NANCY BALANG SAGARA, and HILDA BALANG do not appear on their database of registered or licensed Optometrist. On September 29, 2022, agents of the NBI-NAGA strategically positioned themselves on the area. Subject Josephine Nazarrea conducted an eye examination on one agent who acted as a poseur-client. Subject instructed the poseur client and thereafter prescribed for the use of a complete eyeglass worth Php 3,500.00. When Subject agreed and received the initial payment of Php 1,000.00 marked money, agents of the NBI-NAGA latter announced their authority and placed her under arrest. Seized items were; One (1) set Trial Case with incomplete lenses (10) Diopter), One (1) piece Trial Frame, One (1) piece Reading Chart, One (1) piece Php 1,000.00 peso bill used as marked money, One (1) piece Prescription Paper, One (1) piece of Nike Brand Plastic frame and One (1) piece Snellen Chart. Subject Josephine Nazarrea y Balang was presented for inquest proceedings before the City Prosecutor’s Office of Iriga City for violation of Section 32(f) in relation to Section 5 of RA 8050, which is penalized under Section 33 of RA (Revised Optometry Law).

body: PRESS STATEMENT May 31, 2022 The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today said operatives of NBI-Anti-Human Trafficking Division (NBI-AHTRAD) arrested two individuals in Makati City for Large Scale Illegal Recruitment and Estafa. NBI Officer-In-Charge (OIC) Director ERIC B. DISTOR identified the Subjects as SAMUEL GIL PAEZ and MARY ROSE MAGAT. The case stemmed from the complaint filed against SAMUEL GIL PAEZ, MARIA LUISA FERNANDEZ, and MARIE MICHELLE DELGADO who, according to the complainants were conducting recruitment activities and making promises to the complainants that they can work abroad once processing fees and other fees were paid. According to the complainants, they went to Wallstreet Overseas Manpower in Makati City in March 2022 and inquired about employment abroad. Inside the office, complainants met Subjects PAEZ, FERNANDEZ, and DELGADO and introduced themselves as authorized representatives of Wallstreet. On March 14, 2022, one of the complainants went to Wallstreet as walk-in job applicant along with other work seekers. Complainant transacted with Subject PAEZ and inquired about employment abroad. He was offered to work in Dubai as cleaner with supposed monthly salary amounting to 1,500AED. Subject PAEZ demanded P32,000.00 as processing fee and P12,500.00 as training fee. On March 22, 2022, complainant again went to Wallstreet and gave the money to Subject PAEZ together with Subjects FERNANDEZ and DELGADO. According to the complainant, Subjects FERNANDEZ and DELGADO were “Superior” or “Boss” of Subject PAEZ. They were the ones giving instructions to Subject PAEZ as to recruitment of workers, processing application and receiving fees from job applicants. Several dates of supposed departure were given by Subjects to complainants but the former still failed to deploy the complainants. Felt being duped by Subjects, complainants decided to file their complaints with the NBI-AHTRAD. During investigation, it revealed that Subjects SAMUEL GIL PAEZ, MARIA LUISA FERNANDEZ and MARIE MICHELLE DELGADO are not in the list of officers and staff submitted by the Wallstreet Overseas Manpower with the POEA. Neither were they authorized by Wallstreet to recruit in their behalf. Further, proprietress of Wallstreet stated that PAEZ, MAGAT, FERNANDEZ, MARI MICHELLE DELGADO and MICHAEL DELGADO are not employees of Wallstreet. When complainants reported to the operatives that they will be meeting with the Subjects, an entrapment operation was immediately hatched. On May 24, 2022, NBI-AHTRAD operatives proceeded to the Wallstreet office and strategically positioned themselves. The operation resulted in the arrest of Subjects MARY ROSE MAGAT, who introduced herself as the Secretary of Wallstreet, and SAMUEL GIL PAEZ, who received the Php 12,500.00 entrapment money allegedly for training fee. PAEZ and MAGAT were caught inflagrante delicto for falsely pretending to be the authorized representatives of Wallstreet. They were likewise processing applications of workers for overseas employment without license/authority from Wallstreet and POEA. Subjects PAEZ and MAGAT were presented before the Office of the Senior State Prosecutor, Department of Justice, for Inquest proceeding for Large Scale Illegal Recruitment and Estafa.

body: PRESS STATEMENT May 09, 2024 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } On May 02, 2024, the National Bureau of Investigation – Violence Against Women and Children Division (NBI-VAWCD) conducted a rescue operation in Mandaluyong City which resulted in the rescue of a minor female victim of Online Sexual Abuse or Exploitation of Children (OSAEC). The operation stemmed from a case referred by the Royal Canadian Mounted Police (RCMP). According to the RCMP, they received an information from the Ontario Provincial Police (OPP) that one of their victim identification investigators located posts on a certain image hosting website showing Child Sexual Abuse or Exploitation Materials (CSAEM). The posts were of a young female victim believed to be located in the Philippines. In response to the information, agents of the NBI-VAWCD conducted further investigation and surveillance, which revealed the Victim’s real name and address. Thus, the NBI-VAWCD together with CSWDO social worker successfully rescued the minor female victim in her residence.

body: PRESS STATEMENT April 24, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } PRESS RELEASE | NBI RESCUES 54 WOMEN IN ORTIGAS TRAFFICKING BUST; ESTABLISHMENT LINKED TO FAMILY OF FORMER LAWMAKER PASAY CITY, Philippines- The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI), through various operating divisions led by the NBI Special Task Group (NBI-STG), successfully conducted an entrapment and rescue operation against a suspected trafficking-in-persons network operating within a nightclub and hotel establishments identified as Chicago Nightclub and Bleu Hotel in Ortigas, Pasig City. The operation was launched following information received from a confidential informant regarding the alleged recruitment and exploitation of women for sexual services. Surveillance and case build-up operations confirmed that the establishments were facilitating a systematic scheme of sexual exploitation. Investigators established that customers were initially entertained inside Chicago Nightclub, where women were presented through a “line-up” system. Once a customer made a selection, the parties were then brought to rooms at Bleu Hotel, where the sexual services were allegedly consummated. Evidence gathered during the operation indicates that transactions ranged from approximately ₱10,000.00 to ₱20,000.00 per sexual services, with portions of the payment allegedly distributed among facilitators, managers, and other individuals involved in the operation. On April 21, 2026, NBI operatives, in coordination with the Department of Justice – Inter-Agency Council Against Trafficking (DOJ-IACAT), the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD), and other partner agencies, executed the operation, resulting in the rescue of fifty-four (54) women victims and the apprehension of fifteen (15) individuals, including managers, officers, facilitators, and customers who were found to have engaged the services of the trafficked women. The said customers are likewise being subjected to appropriate charges for their participation in the unlawful activities, in accordance with existing laws penalizing the exploitation of trafficked persons. Those arrested are now facing charges for violations of: * Republic Act No. 9208, as amended (Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act), and * Republic Act No. 9165 (Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002) Recovered during the operation were marked money, suspected illegal drugs, drug paraphernalia, and documentary evidence relevant to the unlawful activities. The rescued victims have been turned over to the appropriate social welfare authorities for proper care, protection, and assistance. Corporate records obtained in the course of the investigation indicate that the registered owners of the establishment are the wife and son of former Congressman Mike Defensor. The NBI emphasizes that this information is part of the ongoing investigation and does not, by itself, establish criminal liability. All persons concerned are presumed innocent unless proven guilty in a court of law. The NBI reaffirms its unwavering commitment to dismantle human trafficking networks, safeguard vulnerable individuals, and ensure that all those responsible are held accountable in accordance with the law. https://www.facebook.com/reel/1686562102517029

body: PRESS STATEMENT October 15, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } In an effort to combat child prostitution, the National Bureau of Investigation-Ilocos Regional Office (NBI-IRO), under the leadership of NBI Director JUDGE JAIME B. SANTIAGO (Ret.), arrested ROBERT ZHIEN CU a.k.a. “WARREN or WARREN CRUZ” and VANESSA BALLIENTOS BERNALDO a.k.a. “VHANZ” in La Union for violation of Section (a) of Republic Act No. 9208 (Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2003), as amended by R.A. No. 10364; and Section 10 (a) of R.A. No. 7610 (Child Abuse Law), in relation to R.A. No. 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012). The operation was conducted based on information provided by a non-governmental organization (NGO) that advocates against child trafficking. It was reported that trafficking activities in San Fernando City, La Union, were being facilitated by an individual using the alias “Warren,” later identified as ROBERT ZHIEN CU. Subject Cu, through social media, was offering minor females and males for sexual services in exchange for a fee. Transactions were either made in person or online, for a sum of Php3,000.00 to Php4,000.00 per victim. Online surveillance conducted by the Agents of the NBI-IRO confirmed that Subject Cu is indeed involved in the prostitution of minors. As a result, they contacted Warren through social media and arranged a meeting. Subject Cu and the poseur-clients then met in San Fernando City, La Union, where the former introduced two female companions who will provide sexual services to the latter. The next day, the poseur-clients and Subject Cu met again. This time, the Subject introduced his friend, alias “VHANZ,” who was later identified as VANESSA BALLINETOS BERNALRDO, to facilitate male minors to the poseur-clients ‘supposed foreign friends. They agreed to meet again on October 9, 2025, and had Subject choose a resort for the delivery of the minor victims. On October 9, 2025, NBI-IRO Agents, together with NGO personnel and local social workers, proceeded to the agreed meeting place in Bauang, La Union, and positioned themselves strategically. Warren arrived together with the minor female victims and a male adult. Sensing that it was an entrapment operation, Subject Cu was able to flee. Thus, a hot-pursuit operation ensued. Meanwhile, Subject Bernaldo was attempting to escape but was immediately neutralized by the NBI-IRO agents. Subject Bernaldo admitted her participation in prostitution and revealed that she was transacting with a certain “Jepot”, who recruited the male minor victims in Baseco, Tondo, Manila. Meanwhile, a vehicle boarded by four male minor victims arrived. The driver was interviewed and disclosed that he was hired only to carpool the minors to the instructed area. The hot-pursuit operation resulted in the arrest of Subject Cu, who was apprehended in a motel in San Fernando, La Union. On the other hand, the driver who brought the minor children called the driver of another vehicle where “Jepot” is boarding. He informed the other driver that the payment for their carpooling service will be paid by Subject Cu or Subject Bernaldo and instructed him to bring “Jepot” to the NBI-IRO office. Upon arrival, “Jepot” was immediately apprehended by the agents and was positively identified by the minor victims as the one who recruited them. “Jepot” who is a minor was turned over to Social Welfare (CSWD). During the operation, 18 female victims, 4 female minor victims, 1 male victim, and 3 male minor victims were rescued. The Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings for the aforementioned violations. Director Santiago commended the agents of NBI-IRO for the successful operation, which resulted in the arrest of three individuals and the rescue of 26 trafficked victims.

body: On September 24, 2020, operatives of NBI-Cabanatuan District Office (NBI-CABDO) arrested MARY ROSE D. CALUB in an entrapment operation for Estafa. Subject asked money in exchange for a document from the Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA) particularly a Form 5 or the cenomar, using the position of her lived-in partner, Engr. Rolando Occasion, Municipal Civil Registrar of Municipality of Guimba, Nueva Ecija as a stunning play to gain money. Complainant gave Php 44,000 for the transaction with the Subject but the same became futile which prompted the complainant to demand for the return of her money but to no avail despite massive attempts. When Subject again demanded additional money for the continuance of the transaction, the entrapment operation was conducted resulting in the arrest of the Subject. Documents are now being prepared for inquest proceedings before Cabanatuan City Prosecutor’s Office, Nueva Ecija for Estafa under Article 315 of the Revised Penal Code. On September 24, 2020, operatives of NBI-Cabanatuan District Office (NBI-CABDO) arrested MARY ROSE y DIAZ for Estafa. Charges were filed against the Subject before the Cabanatuan City Prosecutor’s Office. On September 29, 2020, operatives of NBI-Northeastern Mindanao Regional Office (NBI-NEMRO) arrested JEFFREY “Ilonggo” MENDEZ for Human Trafficking. Subject was arrested in an operation which stemmed from a complaint filed by a minor victim assisted by her custodian social worker against a certain JEFFREY “Ilonggo” MENDEZ for violation of RA 7610 (Special Protection of Children Against Child Abuse, Exploitation and Discrimination Act) and RA 9208 (Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act). The minor victim made a sworn statement in the presence of the social worker. Accordingly, NBI-NEMRO operatives, together with DSWD Region 10 and CSWD of Cagayan de Oro City conducted anti-human trafficking operation against the Subject and rescue the remaining minor victims allegedly still in the custody of the Subject. Found inside the apartment located at Gmelina St., Carmen, Cagayan de Oro City were three (3) female individuals all believed to be minors. Documents are now being prepared for filing criminal case against the Subject before the City Prosecutor’s Office for violation of RA 7610 and RA 9208. On September 30, 2020, operatives of NBI-Bulacan District Office (NBI-BULDO) arrested ERICK HERNANDEZ y PONCE for violation of RA 9995 (Anti-Photo and Video Voyeurism Act), RA 9262 (Anti-Violence against Women and their Children Act) in relation to RA 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act), and RA 8353 (Anti-Rape Law). Subject was arrested in an operation which stemmed from the complaint of Subject’s girlfriend. According to the complainant, she broke up with the Subject but the latter was persistent and threated to end his life. Complainant gave him another chance for fear that Subject might make good of his threat to kill himself. She even acceded to his plea for a sex video call but she was not aware that Subject took photo of her in complete nudity while they were in a video call. Having realized she had been used, complainant went on silent mode but this silence made Subject to resort to the same threat mode of exposing her nude photos to her family and friends. On the abovementioned date, complainant called the NBI for help as Subject took her to Capitol Inn in Malolos, City. Operatives immediately proceeded to the said area and arrested the Subject. He was brought to NBI-BULDO for proper booking procedures. Charges for the abovementioned violations were filed against the Subject before the Office of the City Prosecutor, Malolos City, Bulacan. body: On April 30, 2020, operatives of NBI-Southeastern Mindanao Regional Office (NBI-SEMRO) arrested DEXSIE BUHIAN y MANAGQUIL for violations of RA 3720 as amended by RA 9711 (Food and Drug Administration Act), RA 11469 (Bayanihan to Heal as One Act) and RA 7581 (The Price Act) all in relation to RA 10175. Subject was arrested in an operation which stemmed from the complaint for online selling of overpriced KN95 face mask at Php195 filed in the NBI. Pursuant thereto, an entrapment operation was conducted resulting in the arrest of the Subject after he received the marked money from the poseur-buyer. The case, however, was filed through direct filing for failure of the online inquest currently implemented by the City Prosecutor’s Office and the needed certification from FDA. The FDA requested for a conduct of investigation relative to the online selling of Rapid Covid Test Kits which is prohibited under the prevailing Circular and Advisories of the said agency at the height of Covid-19 pandemic. After surveillance and monitoring, a sale transaction involving the said product was closed. Consequently, an entrapment operation was conducted resulting in the arrest of the Subject. On May 8, 2020, operatives of NBI-Special Action Unit (NBI-SAU) arrested KIM TAE YOUNG, a Korean national fugitive. On May 6, 2020, NBI-SAU operatives, together with the Bureau of Customs (BOC) and Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) implemented Letter of Authority of the BOC against certain warehouse in HK Sun Plaza, Diosdado Macapagal Boulevard, Pasay, Metro Manila. In the course of the implementation, the team was able to talk to KIM TAE YOUNG, one of the alleged owners of the illegal goods. As a matter of procedure for foreign nationals who are subjects for investigation, personal circumstances of the said person was verified with the BI and with the Embassy of Republic of Korea. The said verification showed that KIM TAE YOUNG has derogatory record and charged as an undesirable alien and has two (2) Warrants of Arrest issued in Seoul, Korea for committing Special Extortion, Punishment of Violence, Etc. Act. The said extortion made by KIM TAE YOUNG involved an amount of KRW 500,000,000.00 of Php20,500,000.00 more or less. On May 8, 2020, NBI-SAU operatives apprehended KIM TAE YOUNG at HK Sun Plaza, Pasay City. Subject was detained at the NBI facility for the mean time and will be properly turned over to BI-FSU once its jail facility opens. On May 8, 2020, operatives of NBI-Special Action Unit (NBI-SAU) arrested CHERRYGIL DEL ROSARIO ARRIOLA for large-scale selling of adulterated alcohol. Subject was arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from a report relative to large-scale selling of adulterated alcohol by the Subject in her shop, CreativeLab Cosmetic Products located at Sampaloc, Manila. According to the report, Subject, herself, is mixing ethyl alcohol and methanol to increase volume. By Methanol, by its nature, is highly corrosive and a toxic substance not suitable for human consumption. Acting on the said report, NBI operatives conducted a test buy operation and the alleged ethyl alcohol and disinfectant were submitted to Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for laboratory examination. Test result issued by FDA states that the alleged ethyl alcohol contains 96.1% Methanol and 4.9% Ethanol. With this, the entrapment operation was immediately conducted and resulted in the arrest of Subject CHERRYGIL DEL ROSARIO ARRIOLA. Subject failed to present authority to sell the products and could not also present chemical analysis of the alleged 99.9% ethyl alcohol that she was selling. Subject CHERRYGIL DEL ROSARIO ARRIOLA was recommended to be prosecuted for violation of RA 11469 (Bayanihan to Heal as One Act), RA 7394 (Consumer Act of the Philippines), and RA 9711 (Food and Drug Administration Act of 2009). On May 10, 2020, operatives of NBI-Cordillera Administrative Office (NBI-CAR) arrested BRENDA GUILLERMO a.k.a JESSICA YAGO for selling overpriced isopropyl alcohol. Acting on the validation report received, NBI-CAR operatives proceeded to Jessica’s Yago’s residence located at 88A 1 st Road, Quezon Hill Proper, Baguio City to conduct the buy-bust operation against the latter for probable violation of RA 7581, RA 7394, RA 11469, in relation to RA 10175 and DOH Department Order No.2020-0131. Subject was arrested after being caught in flagrante delicto of delivering/selling three (3) gallons of isopropyl alcohol solution for Php 780 per gallon which was way beyond the maximum ceiling price. Subject was brought for inquest proceedings for violation of RA 7581, RA 7394, RA 11469, in relation to RA 10175 and DOH Department Order No.2020-0131. On May 11, 2020, operatives of NBI-Dagupan District Office (NBI-DADO) arrested RONNEL MAS, a public high school teacher who posted in his Twitter account an offer to give Php50 Million reward to anyone who can kill President Duterte. Subject posted on his Twitter account, “I will give Php50 Million reward kung sino makakapatay kay Duterte.” Upon receipt of the information given, NBI-OIC Eric Distor ordered NBI-DADO to track down Subject MAS and placed him under arrest. Subject was located at Brgy. Poblacion North in Sta. Cruz, Zambales. In coordination with the barangay officials, Subject was arrested. Subject was presented for inquest proceedings before the Department of Justice for Inciting Sedition in relation to RA 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act) and violation of RA 6713 (Code of Conduct and Ethical Standards for Public Officials). On May 11, 2020, the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) filed charges against Barangay Kagawad DANILO FLORES, Brgy. Executive Assistant RICHARD “BOY” BAUTISTA and Barangay Chairman JASON G. MENDOZA, all officials of Barangay San Agustin, Hagonoy, Bulacan. Graft and corruption cases were filed against the three (3) barangay officials in relation to anomalies in the distribution of Social Amelioration Program (SAP) funds. Two (2) private individuals namely, LEVI COSAY, former barangay kagawad, and REGINE BAUTISTA, wife of Subject Bautista were likewise included in the charges filed before the Department of Justice. Three (3) complainants from Barangay San Agustin alleged that SAP beneficiaries who received Php6,500 from DSWD were demanded Php4,000, a portion of the SAP subsidy, by certain Michael Perez. Subject Flores allegedly claimed that Php3,500 shall be given to Hagonoy Municipal Mayor Raulito Manlapaz Sr. and the Php500 will be given to the frontliners of the Municipality of Hagonoy. Further investigation revealed that Subject Flores threatened the complainants that if they refuse to give Php4,000, they will be blacklisted and eventually delisted as beneficiaries of all subsequent relief or amelioration grants of the government. Witnesses stated that a total of Php117,000.00 collected by Subject Flores was turned over to Subject Bautista and his wife Regine Bautista. Barangay Kagawad Danilo Flores, conspiring and confederating with one another, acted pursuant to the agreement with the Barangay Chair’s confidant, Richard Bautista, to collect the money and disposed of it. Such act, taken together, implies conspiracy. On May 12, 2020, operatives of NBI-Saranggani District Office (NBI-SARDO) arrested PEARLYN GUILLERMO TUANZON for selling overpriced alcohol-based sanitizers in violation of RA 7581 as amended by RA 10623 (Price Act) in relation to DTI Memorandum Circular No.20-01. Subject was arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from the information that one online seller using Love Love Chow account was monitored selling overpriced alcohol-based sanitizers which cost Php1,300 per gallon and 70% Ethyl Alcohol at Php1,100 per gallon. Said products have marking/branding Green Solutions liquid hand sanitizers with disinfectant manufactured by Universal Solutions Industries allegedly FDA approved but according to FDA Region XII, said manufacturer is not on their list of approved manufacturer of hand sanitizers and alcohols. On the aforementioned date, the entrapment operation was conducted resulting in the arrest of the Subject. Items recovered as evidence in the possession of Subject were 19 gallons Green Solutions alcohol-based hand sanitizer. Subject was brought to NBI-SARDO for booking procedures and proper disposition. On May 11, 2020, operatives of NBI-Pagadian District Office (NBI-PAGDO) arrested DIAN SABANAL FALAMINIANO for violation of RA 7581 (Price Act) and RA 11469 (Bayanihan to Heal as One Act). Subject was arrested in a buy-bust operation wherein she sold 500ml of Green Cross Isopropyl Alcohol at Php150. Incident to a lawful arrest, a search was conducted that resulted in the seizure of two (2) 500ml Green Cross Isopropyl Alcohol, one (1) 500ml Casino Ethyl Alcohol, one (1) 150ml Green Cross Isopropyl Alcohol, and two (2) 60ml Alcoplus Isopropryl Alcohol. Total value of the seized items amounts to Php367. Subject was brought to NBI-PAGDO’s office for temporary detention. She will be presented for inquest proceedings after all documents are collated. On May 12, 2020, operatives of NBI-Cybercrime Division (NBI-CCD) arrested PHOEBE BONIFACIO y BATIANCILA for creating fake Facebook account and posting a collage photo with a caption cursing and threatening President Rodrigo Roa Duterte. The case stemmed from the complaint of Alfred P. Rioflorido who alleged that on May 9, 2020, he was informed that a Facebook account named after him posted a collage photo of him and President Duterte with the caption cursing and threatening the President due to the complainant’s alleged dismay because of ABS-CBN network shutdown. Complainant vehemently denied his involvement to the post and claimed that he has a different Facebook account username. He initially thought of Subject Phoebe’s involvement in creating the fake Facebook account due to Subject’s threats of making his life miserable after their recent argument. Subject also made threats against the life of complainant and his siblings. Complainant was informed that Subject and her family created the fake Facebook account and that the Subject manages the account and the one responsible for posting the viral post that made the complainant became a subject of public scrutiny and threats. On May 12, 2020, after being informed of complainant’s meeting with the Subject, operatives of NBI-Cybercrime Division (NBI-CCD) conducted surveillance and entrapment operation. Subject was placed under arrest after confirming that the log in details of fake account “Alfred P. Rioflorido” is the one appearing on the cellular phone of the Subject. Charges for violations of RA 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012) and Grave Threats under Article 282 of the Revised Penal Code in relation to RA 10175 were filed against the Subject. On May 12, 2020, operatives of NBI-Southeastern Mindanao Regional Office (NBI-SEMRO) and PDEA RO XI conducted buy-bust operations at Sta. Lucia Brgy. Centro, Agdao, Davao City that resulted in the arrest of BRYAN DUERO alias BRYAN, JOEMAR TAYLARAN, JUSTIN ALEGADO, SANNERSON SERNA, JAYMERSON TACSON, and FITZ GERALD ROLLON. The operations also resulted in the dismantling of suspected drug den which was also considered as PDEA’s High Impact Operation and the seizure of drugs and non-drugs items. The seized suspected shabu weighs 12,8 grams with an estimated market value of more or less Php192,000. On May 13, 2020, operatives of NBI-Southeastern Mindanao Regional Office (NBI-SEMRO), together with PDEA RO XI, conducted illegal drugs buy bust operation that led to the arrest of GILBERT GIPTE alias JEFREY, JULIUS TAMAYO JOSON, JASPER TAGNIPIS, JAIME ARAT, ERNESTO AVELINO, and RODNEY QUINTO, all high value targets of PDEA. The said anti-illegal drug operation also resulted in the dismantling of suspected drug den and the seizure of suspected shabu weighing more or less 36 grams with an estimated value of Php540,400 along with other drug paraphernalia. Cases for violation of RA 9165 (Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act) have been prepared against the arrested Subjects before the Office of City Prosecutor, Davao City. On May 14, 2020, operatives of NBI-Cavite District Office (NBI-CAVIDO) arrested RUSSEL CAMPANA y DONES by virtue of Warrant of Arrest for Syndicated Estafa. Atty. Noel G. Morales, Ex-O, NBI-CAR requested to locate the whereabouts and possibly arrest RUSSEL CAMPANA y DONES who was issued a Warrant of Arrest by RTC Branch 20, Imus, Cavite for Syndicated Estafa. NBI-CAVIDO operatives immediately proceeded to the area where Subject was positively located. Subject was then arrested at 24 Brgy. Tanzang Luma, Imus, Cavite. Subject is currently detained at the NBI-CAVIDO detention cell. Return of Warrant of Arrest is being prepared in compliance in the Rules of Court. On May 14, 2020, operatives of NBI-Anti-Human Trafficking Division (NBI-AHTRAD) arrested a 34-year old woman in entrapment operation in Angeles City, Pampanga for human trafficking. The case stemmed from a report regarding the Subject’s exploitation of her minor daughters into online child pornography in exchange for a fee. The NBI conducted validation of the report using a dummy account and confirmed the said illegal activity. On the aforementioned date, NBI-AHTRAD operatives, together with PNP-WCPC and NBI-Central Luzon Regional Office (NBI-CELRO), proceeded to Angeles City, Pampanga resulting in the arrest of the Subject and the rescue of three (3) victims with ages 6, 11, 14 years old. Two (2) of the victims were later on identified as Subject’s daughters and on1) as her step daughter. Victims were taken into custody by the Angeles City CSWD social worker. Subject will be subjected for inquest proceedings for violation of RA 9208 (Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act) as amended, RA 7610 (Special Protection of Children Against Abuse, Exploitation, and Discrimination Act), and RA 9775 (Anti-Child Pornography Act).

On May 14, 2020, operatives of NBI-Cavite District Office (NBI-CAVIDO) arrested RUSSEL CAMPANA y DONES by virtue of Warrant of Arrest for Syndicated Estafa. Atty. Noel G. Morales, Ex-O, NBI-CAR requested to locate the whereabouts and possibly arrest RUSSEL CAMPANA y DONES who was issued a Warrant of Arrest by RTC Branch 20, Imus, Cavite for Syndicated Estafa. NBI-CAVIDO operatives immediately proceeded to the area where Subject was positively located. Subject was then arrested at 24 Brgy. Tanzang Luma, Imus, Cavite. Subject is currently detained at the NBI-CAVIDO detention cell. Return of Warrant of Arrest is being prepared in compliance in the Rules of Court. On May 14, 2020, operatives of NBI-Anti-Human Trafficking Division (NBI-AHTRAD) arrested a 34-year old woman in entrapment operation in Angeles City, Pampanga for human trafficking. The case stemmed from a report regarding the Subject’s exploitation of her minor daughters into online child pornography in exchange for a fee. The NBI conducted validation of the report using a dummy account and confirmed the said illegal activity. On the aforementioned date, NBI-AHTRAD operatives, together with PNP-WCPC and NBI-Central Luzon Regional Office (NBI-CELRO), proceeded to Angeles City, Pampanga resulting in the arrest of the Subject and the rescue of three (3) victims with ages 6, 11, 14 years old. Two (2) of the victims were later on identified as Subject’s daughters and on1) as her step daughter. Victims were taken into custody by the Angeles City CSWD social worker. Subject will be subjected for inquest proceedings for violation of RA 9208 (Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act) as amended, RA 7610 (Special Protection of Children Against Abuse, Exploitation, and Discrimination Act), and RA 9775 (Anti-Child Pornography Act).

body: PRESS STATEMENT January 31, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } In line with the directive of National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Director Judge Jaime B. Santiago (Ret.) to intensify the campaign against the proliferation of smuggled cigarettes in the country, the NBI Batangas District Office (NBI- BatDO) arrested ANGELO AZUR y BACARISAS and ARGIE GARCIA y CUELLO in Santo Tomas City, Batangas for violation of Republic Act 12022, otherwise known as the “Anti-Agricultural Economic Sabotage Act”. The operation stemmed from an information that unknown individuals are engaged in the transportation and selling of smuggled manufactured tobaccos or cigarettes in the province of Batangas. Acting on the said information and there being continuous transaction to the transportation and selling of the illicit items and after the said individuals declared that the cigarettes are smuggled and sold at a low price, an entrapment operation was planned and conducted. In an undercover capacity, Subjects agreed to deliver 20 master cases of smuggled cigarettes in the amount of 1.2Million in Santo Tomas City, Batangas. On January 23, 2025, Subjects arrived at the agreed place where the items will be unloaded and paid. After inspecting the declared smuggled cigarettes and after they received the pre-marked entrapment money, Agents declared their authority under the law and arrested the Subjects. The entrapment operation also resulted in the seizure of twenty (20) master cases of smuggled cigarettes containing ten thousand (10,000) packs in total. The proliferation and eventual sale to the market without obtaining the processes and requirements set forth by law deprives the government from lawful revenues. On January 24, 2025, Subjects were presented for Inquest Proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor – Santo Tomas City, Batangas

title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: PRESS STATEMENT October 08, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } On October 7, 2025, the National Bureau of Investigation – Cybercrime Division (NBI-CCD) arrested Michael P. Romero a.k.a. “Mike Romero” in Pagadian City for Inciting to Sedition under Article 142 of the Revised Penal Code (RPC) in relation to Republic Act No. 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012). The arrest stemmed from a malicious Facebook post by a user identified as Mike Romero. The post gained attention on social media due to its caption, “Headshot,” alongside an image of President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr., which was overlaid with a red arrow. In response, NBI-CCD agents immediately launched an investigation. Through cyber patrolling, they were able to identify the individual responsible for the post. On October 6, 2025, NBI-CCD agents proceeded to Pagadian City to apprehend Subject Romero on a hot pursuit operation. In a joint operation with NBI-Pagadian District Office (NBI-PAGDO) agents, they conducted surveillance operations that successfully identified the Subject’s residence. On October 7, 2025, Subject Romero when confronted, admitted that he is the owner of the Facebook account “Mike Romero.”Following this admission, NBI agents placed him under arrest and informed him of his constitutional rights. Subject Romero was then transported to the NBI-CCD office in Pasay City, where he underwent standard booking procedures. Director Santiago commended the agents of NBI-CCD and NBI-PAGDO for the successful operation. He urged the public to use social media responsibly and avoid posting malicious content.

body: On September 2, 2019, joint efforts of NBI-Tagum District Office (NBI-TAGDO), Naval Intelligence Service Group Eastern Mindanao (NISG-EM), and PNP Regional Intelligence Division-PRO 11, arrested JULIVER CABATING y SORIANO, alias “JERRY”, and alias “RAMIL” for the murder of Judge Reymar L. Lacaya of RTC Zamboanga. Subject JULIVER was arrested by virtue of Warrant of Arrest for the Murder of Judge Reymar L. Lacaya, Acting Presiding Judge of RTC Branch 28, Liloy, Zamboanga del Norte. The victim was shot inside the premises of RTC Branch 28 on May 9, 2019. Aside from Subject Juliver, two (2) other individuals, identified as “JERRY” and “RAMIL” who conspired in the shooting incident, were also identified. All circumstances, supported by pieces of evidences paint a picture that Juliver, Jerry, and Ramil conspired in killing Judge Lacaya. The three were then recommended to be charged in court after conducting the prerequisite preliminary investigation for violation of Article 248 of the Revised Penal Code (Murder). On September 2, 2019, operatives of NBI-Special Action Unit (NBI-SAU) arrested GERRY BUNDALIAN alias “Jerry” in Harrison Plaza, Malate, Manila for Robbery Extortion. The NBI received a report from Intelligence Group – Bureau of Customs (IG-BOC) and Counter Intelligence-Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) that a certain Jerry is involved in extortion racket among customs broker in exchange for customs facilitation. “Jerry” floated himself that he is well connected with customs officials and has the capacity to lift alert of incoming shipments. Relative to the report, customs brokerage firm, Moriel’s Trading Brokerage, represented by the owner Jay Gutierrez, filed an extortion complaint against alias Jerry. On the aforementioned date, the entrapment operation was conducted by NBI-SAU operatives, together with IG-BOC and PCG personnel proceeded to Harrison Plaza, Malate, Manila and Subject BUNDALIAN was arrested. Subject was presented for inquest proceeding before the Office of the City Prosecutor, Manila the next day. On September 2, 2019, operatives of NBI-Anti-Organized and Transnational Crime Divion (NBI-AOTCD) arrested ENRICO MORILLO y NATIVIDAD for Extortion. Complainant Matthew William V. Ng alleged that on August 21, 2019, Subject ordered chicken feet in Kowloon House in Diliman, Quezon City and complained to the management that his chicken feet has a cockroach. Subject threatened the complainant and Marion Theodore Guayco that if Kowloon will not pay him Php 175,000.00, Subject will upload a video taken by him that there is a cockroach in the chicken feet. Subject instructed Guayco to meet with him in the Office of the City Planning and Development Office (CPDO), Quezon City Hall and bring with him Php 175,000.00. With this, the entrapment operation was conducted resulting in the arrest of the Subject. Subject was presented for inquest proceeding before the Office of the Prosecutor, Quezon City. He is currently detained at the NBI detention facility awaiting the resolution of the case. On September 2, 2019, operatives of NBI-Anti-Fraud Division (NBI-AFD) seized 113 units of counterfeit sewing machines bearing the trademarks of SINGER Company Ltd. with market value of Php 450,000.00. The case stemmed from the letter of Baranda & Associates requesting for assistance in the investigation of certain establishments in Manila that were allegedly engaged in the selling of counterfeit products bearing the trademarks of SINGER Company Ltd. On the aforementioned date, Search Warrant was implemented resulting in the seizure of said items. In the afternoon of September 3, 2019, operatives of NBI-Anti-Fraud Division (NBI-AFD) received information was received that a wanted person, JOEL AVIZO, was located and reportedly staying at different phases of San Lorenzo Village, Binan, Laguna. Prior to the report, Atty. Emmanuel Joseph Menez requested for the service of Warrant of Arrest against JOEL AVIZO. Atty. Menez’s request contained documents identifying the accused. He also disclosed that the Subject was a counsilor at Brgy. Binan, Laguna and was related to different political personalities. Upon receipt of the Subject’s location, NBI-AFD operatives verified all phases of San Lorenzo Village until he was located at Phase V. The service of Warrant of Service was conducted in a peaceful manner. JOEL AVIZO is currently detained at the NBI Detention Center. On September 4, 2019, operatives of NBI-International Airport Investigation Division (NBI-IAID) arrested JENNIFER ERIN TALBOT for carrying an infant boy inside a sling bag. TALBOT was about to depart for the United States (US) via Delta Air Lines when she was intercepted at the Boarding Gate of NAIA Terminal 3 by Delta Air Lines personnel. She was found carrying the baby inside a sling bag which was tucked at her side without proper travel documents. TALBOT was able to pass thru the immigration counter without declaring the baby. TALBOT failed to present Travel Clearance issued by the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) or written consent from the baby’s parents. Per the documents shown by TALBOT, the baby’s name is ANDREW DULAP, born on 29 August 2019 at Southern Philippines Medical Center, Davao City. TALBOT presented an Affidavit of Consent and Support allegedly executed by MARICRIS DULAP, the mother of the baby which was notarized in Davao City, alleging that MARICRIS gave her consent for her son to travel to US with her. However, the same was not signed by MARICRIS DULAP. Verification with DSWD revealed that no travel clearance was issued to ANDREW DULAP. TALBOT was placed under arrest for violation of R.A. No. 9208 (The Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act) as amended by R.A. No. 10364 (Expanded Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2012), R.A. No. 7610 (Special Protection of Children Against Child Abuse, Exploitation and Discrimination Act), and Art. 267 of the Revised Penal Code (Kidnapping and Serious Illegal Detention). On September 5, 2019, operatives of NBI-Iligan District Office (NBI-ILDO) arrested OMIESA JAY PASANDALAN y FERNANDEZ and SHEILA UNGAB y CANTINA in two separate operations for Estafa thru Falsification of Public Documents. Subjects were arrested in entrapment operations which stemmed from complaints against the Subjects who were introduced to complainants in separate occasions. Subject PASANDALAN offered to pawn properties with a total area of 240 sq.meters allegedly owned by the Subject’s parents for a total of Php 130,000.00 only while Subject CANTINA offered to pawn a property lot with total 336 sq.meters allegedly owned by her husband for Php 200,000.00. Thru sweet and convincing words, Subjects were able to convince the complainants to pawn the parcels of land when in fact, the documents presented to the complainants were bogus and spurious. When complainants went to the Office of BIR-Iligan City for the Documentary Stamps Declaration/Return for the annotation of the TCT, the head of office of Registry of Deeds informed them that all the documents they have are fake. Complainants then filed a complaint against the Subject and on the September 5, 2019, the entrapment operations were conducted resulting in the arrest of the Subject. Subjects are temporarily detained at NBI-ILDO for booking and documentation and case for violation of Article 315 of the Revised Penal Code was filed against the Subject. On September 6, 2019, operatives of NBI-Rizal District Office (NBI-RIZDO) seized 1,446 pieces of rash guard bearing the North Face trademarks and logos with an estimated market value of Php 5.7 Million. Items were seized in Binondo, Manila by virtue of Search Warrants. Charges for violation of RA 8293 (Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines) were filed against FAAB GENERAL MERCHANDISE and/or FAYE ANJANETTE ABANO BALMES, MR. XU, and/or other proprietors/employees/occupants of the retail store located at 999 Shopping Mall, Binondo, Manila. On September 10, 2019, operatives of NBI- Anti-Violence Against Women and Children Division (NBI-AVAWCD) arrested JENNYFER PESTANO y CHUA aka “JENNYLYN” and JOHN MIGUEL MORAL y ORAA aka “JHANNA” for Human Trafficking. The operation was based on the information from a confidential informant that certain individuals were engaged in Online Human Trafficking, offering minor girls to perform sexual services in exchange for a fee. The confidential informant also revealed that the photos of women offered as sexual workers were posted in a social media platform. Upon proper coordination, the operatives, assisted by DSWD personnel, an entrapment operation was conducted wherein the Subjects offered minor girls who will perform sexual services for a fee. Subjects were then placed under arrest and twelve (12) minor girls were rescued. The victims were turned over to the DSWD personnel for proper disposition. Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the DOJ, Manila, for Human Trafficking in relation to R.A. 7610. On September 10, 2019, operatives of NBI-Anti-Organized and Transnational Crime Divion (NBI-AOTCD) arrested AL PIERRE RAVIZ y LEGADA for spreading nude photos of the minor complainant and using the same in threatening the minor to have sex with him. Minor complainant and Subject RAVIZ met on Facebook and later entered into a relationship. After several demands of the Subject to have sex with him, the minor victim heeded to such demand. Unknown to the victim, Subject captured all their activities using his camera. Minor complainant later discovered such fact after Subject sent her nude photos to her sister after Subject and complainant had an argument. Subject would always accuse the complainant of having relationship with another person and from then on, Subject would always threaten the complainant that he will spread her nude photos if she will not have sex with him. Out of fear and possible humiliation in her community, complainant was forced to stop going to school. Sometime in August 2019, Subject told the complainant that he will delete the photos and videos if she will have sex with him. Complainant agreed but Subject did not delete the photos and videos and continued to demand complainant to have sex with him in exchange of not sending nude photos to other people. At this point, complainant, represented by her mother, requested the assistance of the NBI to apprehend the Subject. Thus, on the above-mentioned date, an entrapment operation was conducted resulting in the arrest of the Subject. Subject was brought to NBI Manila for the booking procedures and was, thereafter presented for inquest proceedings. On September 11, 2019, operatives of NBI-South Eastern Mindanao Regional Office (NBI-SEMRO) arrested MICHAEL ROY COLONIA and ANGELO VALENTIN for Human Trafficking. Subjects, both are gay pimps, were arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from the information regarding the high level of prostitution in the area of Dacudao particularly at Del Pilar St. where a portion of the area is heavily covered with darkness and used as meeting place of individuals involved in “flesh trade”. Further information disclosed that those involved are minors aged 12-13 years old. Information received was confirmed, thus, on the aforementioned date, the entrapment operation was conducted resulting in the arrest of the Subjects who offered and presented minor girls for sexual activity. Subjects are presently detained at the NBI detention facility. On September 11, 2019, operatives of NBI-Iligan District Office (NBI-ILDO), in coordination with the PDEA ARMM, conducted buy-bust operation at Brgy. Raya, Mulondo, Lanao del Sur that resulted in the arrest of COUNCILOR MACAPANTON M. COSAIN, PANGANONUN RAKIM y SUMANGAN, and ALIMATAR MANGOTARA y MAMA. Bought from the Subjects is one (1) piece knot-tied transparent plastic sachet containing white crystalline substance believed to be shabu weighing more or less 55 grams with a market value of Php 200,000.00. Subjects were brought to NBI office for the booking procedures and temporarily detained thereat. On September 11, 2019, operatives of NBI-Special Action Unit (NBI-SAU) arrested LAURO AALA y ATAJAR and LOWELL POTENCIADO y PLATOLON for illegally selling giant clams/pearls known as “Taklobo”. Subjects were arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from the information that a group of individuals from Calatagan, Batangas were engaged in selling giant pearls produced by giant clam. Through an informant, communication with the Subjects was established and the latter straightaway offered to sell giant pearls. With this, the entrapment operation was hatched resulting in the arrest of the above-mentioned Subjects. Found in the control and possession of the Subjects were the alleged giant pearls and entrapment money. Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the Prosecutor General, Department of Justice for violations of RA 8550 (The Philippine Fisheries Code of 1998) as amended by RA 10654 (An Act to Prevent, Deter and Eliminate Illegal, Unreported and Unregulated Fishing) and RA 10066 (National Cultural Heritage Act). On September 12, 2019, operatives of NBI-Anti-Fraud Division (NBI-AFD) arrested NAGAISVARAN RAMASAY for violation of RA 9262 and Direct Assault. A certain Carolyn Aquinde requested assistance for the service of Warrant of Arrest against her ex-husband NAGAISVARAN RAMASAY. A Warrant of Arrest for violation of RA 9262 (Violence Against Women and Their Children Act) was issued against NAGAISVARAN RAMASAY by the RTC Branch 49, Urdaneta City Pangasinan. Operatives then proceeded to Ram and Ram Poultry Farm, Brgy. Balligi, Laoac, Pangasinan to serve the said Warrant of Arrest. Instead of submitting himself to the authorities, RAMASAY forcibly pushed an NBI operative and attempted to run to his vehicle. Operatives tried to stop him but he still resisted and punched one of the operatives causing the latter’s tooth to dislocate and suffered scratches on his arms. RAMASAY was eventually neutralized. He was then brought to NBI main headquarters for the booking procedures and was thereafter inquested for Direct Assault and Resisting Arrest. On September 13, 2019, operatives of NBI- Anti-Fraud Division (NBI-AFD) arrested LEONORA DEMESA HERNANDEZ for using fictitious/fabricated land title to scam her victims. The operation was based on the complaint filed by the victim against Subject Hernandez who lured the complainants to invest on a property in Valenzuela City, containing more or less an area of 14.5 hectares under the name of Wilfredo Torres. She convinced the victims to invest Php 5 Million for the titling and transfer of the said property, promising them with a return of investment of Php 65 Million upon sale of the property. Subject Hernandez gave them the title of the property proving that it was transferred into her name and asked from the victims additional funding for the uploading of the titles and taxes. The complainant started to doubt the subject and verified the title of the property involved bearing TCT number V-28779. Upon verification with the Land registration Authority and Registry of Deeds of Valenzuela, it was revealed that the property bearing TCT number V-28779 is actually registered to Dina A. Bondoc and was already transferred to Spouses Rizal Laderio and Consuelo I. Laderio under TCT number V-47881. An entrapment operation was then conducted and resulted in the arrest of the Subject. Subject was brought before the Pasay Prosecutors Office for inquest proceedings for violations of Article 315 of the PRC (Estafa) and Article 172 in relation to Article 171 of the RPC (Falsification of Public Documents). On September 16, 2019, operatives of NBI-Bacolod District Office (NBI-BACDO) arrested EDMER GULMATICO for Estafa and Usurpation of Authority. Subject was arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from the complaint of Princess Mae Ahunin. Subject represented himself as a private law practitioner and offered his legal service to the complainant for a fee of Php 150,000.00. Subject was brought to the NBI-BACDO office for the booking procedures and was thereafter presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor, Bacolod City for Estafa and Usurpation of Authority. On September 17, 2019, operatives of NBI- Cybercrime Division (NBI-CCD) arrested OKOROIKE HARRISON CHIBUIKE , a Nigerian national and his Filipino companion EDUARD PARCEDES GODOLESON for online scamming. Subjects were arrested in an operation which stemmed from an information regarding the illegal activities of certain individuals operating in Cavite City. According to the informant, occupants of the target address were conducting various online scams targeting Filipinos. Upon securing Search Warrants, operatives proceeded to the target address where Subject Eduard introduced himself as a member of the Philippine Army and told the operatives to back out for there was an ongoing operation by their unit. Subject Okoroike then appeared on board a motorcycle heading towards Subject Eduard as if going for a ride. Sensing that Subject Eduard was trying to deceive the operatives and came out to Subject Okoroike’s rescue, operatives immediately apprehended the Subjects. Subject Okoroike became violent posing great threat on the lives and limbs of NBI operatives. Compelled to protect themselves, operatives shot Subject Okoroike. He was rushed to the nearest hospital but was pronounced Dead On Arrival (DOA). Investigation disclosed that the blank cards were being sold by Subject Eduard to a group of Nigerian individuals for their access device fraud activities. Upon controlled viewing of Subject Okoroike’s cellphone, there are text messages revealing that Subject Eduard was indeed in cahoots with Subject Okoroike. Subject EDUARD PARCEDES GODOLESON was presented for inquest proceedings before the City Prosecutor for Direct Assault, Usurpation of Authority, Obstruction of Justice, and violations of RA 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act) and RA 10175 (Access Devices Regulation Act). On September 17, 2019, operatives of NBI-National Capital Region (NBI-NCR) seized Php 101,500.00 worth of counterfeit products with JUUL trademark. Items were seized in Malate, Manila by virtue of Search Warrants. Charges for violation of RA 8293 (Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines) were filed against the Cube Store and/or any of its proprietors, stockholders, incorporators, managers, employees, and/or occupants of the premises located in Unit 8B, Ground Floor, One Archers Place, Malate, Manila. On September 17, 2019, operatives of NBI-Environmental Crime Division (NBI-EnCD) arrested MARK LESTER ALAFRIZ MARAINGAN for illegally trading wildlife animals. Subject was arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from an information regarding an alleged illegal selling of yellow-spotted river turtle and other wildlife species inside a pet shop in Brgy. Manggahan, Rodriguez, Rizal. Verification with the DENR-Biodiversity Management Bureau (DENR-BMB) disclosed that the trading and/or possession of yellow-spotted river turtle is prohibited and the latter is considered as endangered species. The operation also resulted in the seizure of wildlife animals in the store including two (2) Ball Python, one (1) Leopard Gecko, one (1) Pig-nosed Turtle, one (1) yellow-spotted turtle, three (3) Red-eared Slider, one (1) Alligator Snapping Turtle, one (1) Soft-shelled Turtle, and one (1) Bearded Dragon. Subject was presented for inquest proceedings before the Department of Justice for violation of RA 9147 (Wildlife Conservation and Protection Act). On September 18, 2019, operatives of NBI-Intellectual Property Rights Division (NBI-IPRD) seized 25 boxes of counterfeit Powerflex cables with an estimated value of Php 62,500.00. Items were seized in the province of Laguna by virtue of Search Warrants. Charges for violation of RA 7393 (Consumer Act of the Philippines) were filed against John/Jane Does of Golden Bay Merchandising in Calamba, Laguna, Johnson Uy Chua, John/Jane Does/owners/operators of Fortune Nine Trading in Los Banos, Laguna, John/Jane Does/owners/operators of Zero One Merchandising Center in Cabuyao, Laguna, Bobby G. Coronado, John/Jane Does/owners/ operators of New Hign Max Hardware in Calamba, Laguna, Andy S. Ang, John/Jane Does/owners/ operators of Southern Sky Construction Supply in Cabuyao, Laguna. On September 18, 2019, operatives of NBI-Anti-Human Trafficking Division (NBI-AHTRAD) arrested ALVIN BALDOMAR y NICOLAS a.k.a. Maja Nicolas and JHUNEMAR MORALINA y ROXAS. Subjects were arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from the report that Subject “Maja” was offering young girls for sexual intercourse in exchange for a fee of Php 3,000 – Php 5,000. Six (6) victims, five (5) of whom are minors, were likewise rescued in the operation. They were turned over to DSWD-Pasig Social Welfare Department for proper custody. Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor General of the Department of Justice for violation of A. No. 9208 (Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act) as amended by R.A. No. 10364 (Expanded Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2012) and R.A. No. 7610 (Special Protection of Children Against Child Abuse, Exploitation and Discrimination Act). On September 18, 2019, operatives of NBI-Southeastern Mindanao Regional Office (NBI-SEMRO) proceeded to the compound of Muews Radio Station where Board Member Jun Blanco had operated and managed KAPA Community Ministry International Inc. Poseur investors paid a marked money in the amount of Php 10,000.00 was duly received by his staff. Thereafter, operatives swooped down the area and recovered from their possession the marked money, bill counter, and shot gun with four (4) live ammunitions without pertinent documents and other pieces of evidence relative to their operation. A case for violation of PD 1689 in relation to Art. 315 of the RPC, violation of RA 8799 (Securities Regulation code, and violation of RA 10591 (Comprehensive Firearms and Ammunition Regulation Act). On September 18, 2019, operatives of NBI-Rizal Distict Office (NBI-RIZDO) arrested CAMILLE CANDELARIO y LICUDAN for Human Trafficking. Subject was arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from the information of Destiny Rescue Phils. Regarding the human trafficking activities particularly sexual exploitation of minor victims committed by pimps in the areas of Marikina City and nearby cities. Verification and surveillance operations confirmed that Subject Camille was maintaining, harboring, offering, and delivering girls for a quick sexual intercourse. With this, the entrapment operation was hatched in Rosalinda Garden Resort, Brgy. Sta. Cruz, Antipolo City, resulting in the arrest of the Subject who offered female prostitutes with an agreed price of Php 1,500 for sexual intercourse with the selected female and Php 1,000 as commission for the pimp. The operation likewise resulted in the rescue of thirteen (13) victims, eleven (11) of whom are minors. Subject Camille Candelario was presented for inquest proceedings before the City Prosecutors Office, Antipolo City for violations of RA 9208 (The Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act) as amended by R.A. No. 10364 (Expanded Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2012), R.A.
