NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION

On September 2, 2019, joint efforts of NBI-Tagum District Office (NBI-TAGDO), Naval Intelligence Service Group Eastern Mindanao (NISG-EM), and PNP Regional Intelligence Division-PRO 11, arrested JULIVER CABATING y SORIANO, alias “JERRY”, and alias “RAMIL” for the murder of Judge Reymar L. Lacaya of RTC Zamboanga. Subject JULIVER was arrested by virtue of Warrant of Arrest for the Murder of Judge Reymar L. Lacaya, Acting Presiding Judge of RTC Branch 28, Liloy, Zamboanga del Norte. The victim was shot inside the premises of RTC Branch 28 on May 9, 2019. Aside from Subject Juliver, two (2) other individuals, identified as “JERRY” and “RAMIL” who conspired in the shooting incident, were also identified. All circumstances, supported by pieces of evidences paint a picture that Juliver, Jerry, and Ramil conspired in killing Judge Lacaya. The three were then recommended to be charged in court after conducting the prerequisite preliminary investigation for violation of Article 248 of the Revised Penal Code (Murder). On September 2, 2019, operatives of NBI-Special Action Unit (NBI-SAU) arrested GERRY BUNDALIAN alias “Jerry” in Harrison Plaza, Malate, Manila for Robbery Extortion. The NBI received a report from Intelligence Group – Bureau of Customs (IG-BOC) and Counter Intelligence-Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) that a certain Jerry is involved in extortion racket among customs broker in exchange for customs facilitation. “Jerry” floated himself that he is well connected with customs officials and has the capacity to lift alert of incoming shipments. Relative to the report, customs brokerage firm, Moriel’s Trading Brokerage, represented by the owner Jay Gutierrez, filed an extortion complaint against alias Jerry. On the aforementioned date, the entrapment operation was conducted by NBI-SAU operatives, together with IG-BOC and PCG personnel proceeded to Harrison Plaza, Malate, Manila and Subject BUNDALIAN was arrested. Subject was presented for inquest proceeding before the Office of the City Prosecutor, Manila the next day. On September 2, 2019, operatives of NBI-Anti-Organized and Transnational Crime Divion (NBI-AOTCD) arrested ENRICO MORILLO y NATIVIDAD for Extortion. Complainant Matthew William V. Ng alleged that on August 21, 2019, Subject ordered chicken feet in Kowloon House in Diliman, Quezon City and complained to the management that his chicken feet has a cockroach. Subject threatened the complainant and Marion Theodore Guayco that if Kowloon will not pay him Php 175,000.00, Subject will upload a video taken by him that there is a cockroach in the chicken feet. Subject instructed Guayco to meet with him in the Office of the City Planning and Development Office (CPDO), Quezon City Hall and bring with him Php 175,000.00. With this, the entrapment operation was conducted resulting in the arrest of the Subject. Subject was presented for inquest proceeding before the Office of the Prosecutor, Quezon City. He is currently detained at the NBI detention facility awaiting the resolution of the case. On September 2, 2019, operatives of NBI-Anti-Fraud Division (NBI-AFD) seized 113 units of counterfeit sewing machines bearing the trademarks of SINGER Company Ltd. with market value of Php 450,000.00. The case stemmed from the letter of Baranda & Associates requesting for assistance in the investigation of certain establishments in Manila that were allegedly engaged in the selling of counterfeit products bearing the trademarks of SINGER Company Ltd. On the aforementioned date, Search Warrant was implemented resulting in the seizure of said items. Prior to the report, Atty. Emmanuel Joseph Menez requested for the service of Warrant of Arrest against JOEL AVIZO. Atty. Menez’s request contained documents identifying the accused. He also disclosed that the Subject was a counsilor at Brgy. Binan, Laguna and was related to different political personalities. Upon receipt of the Subject’s location, NBI-AFD operatives verified all phases of San Lorenzo Village until he was located at Phase V. The service of Warrant of Service was conducted in a peaceful manner. JOEL AVIZO is currently detained at the NBI Detention Center. TALBOT was about to depart for the United States (US) via Delta Air Lines when she was intercepted at the Boarding Gate of NAIA Terminal 3 by Delta Air Lines personnel. She was found carrying the baby inside a sling bag which was tucked at her side without proper travel documents. TALBOT was able to pass thru the immigration counter without declaring the baby. TALBOT failed to present Travel Clearance issued by the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) or written consent from the baby’s parents. Complainants then filed a complaint against the Subject and on the September 5, 2019, the entrapment operations were conducted resulting in the arrest of the Subject. title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today announced the arrest of a 25-year old public high school teacher who posted in his Twitter account an offer to give P50 Million reward to anyone who can kill President Duterte. body: A call center trainee who presented a fake NBI clearance and wanted for a string of cases was finally caught by agents of the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) in Quezon City yesterday. The subject was identified as RUBIO, MICHAEL PAUL CHRIS JR y ALCANTARA. 24. A resident of 438 Sct. Delgado, Brgy. Laging Handa, Quezon City. Prior to his apprehension, a multi-national call center company under which he is presently on-the-job training requested the NBI to authenticate his clearance certificate. The NBI through its clearance verification process found said clearance certificate to be fake. Further, NBI record check made on subject Rubio disclosed that he has numerous standing warrant of arrest under the name Michael Paul Chris A. Rubio in the following: 1. Criminal Case No. Q-07-148343 for Robbery by Quezon City RTC Branch 219 in 2007; 2. Criminal Case No. Q-07-148344 for Attempted Murder issued by Quezon City RTC Branch 220 in 2007; 3. Criminal Case No. Q-07-148344 for Attempted Murder issued by Quezon City RTC Branch 220 in 2008; and 4. Criminal Case No. Q-07-148345 for Anti-Carnapping Law issued by Quezon City RTC Branch 221 in 2007. At 1:00 a.m. yesterday, NBI agents proceeded to Rubio’s workplace, a call-center in Cubao, Quezon City. By virtue of said warrants of arrest, NBI agents arrested Rubio Appropriate charges will be filed against subject Rubio and deeper probe will also be conducted to identify the cohorts behind the fake NBI clearance certificate. He is now detained at the NBI jail. In the wake of this and similar incidents in the past, the NBI is issuing a stern warning to unscrupulous persons to avoid dealing with fixers in securing NBI clearance. Individuals found presenting or in possession of fake NBI clearance will be dealt with the full force of the law.

title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: The Information Division is pleased to submit herewith the significant cases of the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) for the following aforementioned period as follows: On June 18, 2020, operatives of NBI-Laoag District Office (NBI-LADO) arrested ERNESTO MACALIPIS, a fugitive from justice for 36 years and one of the accused in the abduction and rape of two (2) women in November 1984. MACALIPIS’ arrest came 2 days after his co-accused ALBERTO BUMANGLAG was arrested by NBI-LADO in another barangay. MACALIPIS went into hiding after the commission of the crime and was never arrested and remained at large since then and the case against him was ordered “archived” by the court. On June 18, 2020, operatives of NBI-Environmental Crime Division (NBI-EnCD) arrested NINO PAULO A. MANALO in Amadeo, Cavite for illegal possession of wood specie. Subject was arrested in an operation which stemmed from a report regarding an individual allegedly in possession of undetermined number of lumber and flitches of different wood specie without appropriate documents as required under the existing environmental laws. Operatives of NBI-EnCD, DENR-PENRO CAVITE, and elements of Philippine Army and Philippine Air Force implemented the Search Warrant. Recovered and seized from the possession of Subject are a total of 43,103.91 board feet of various premium wood specie with an estimated value of Php 3,499,183.91 and 237 pieces of assorted furniture made from said lumber and flitches with a market value of Php 323,000.00. Subject was brought before the Office of Provincial Prosecutor – Cavite for inquest proceeding for violation of PD 705 as amended (Revised Forestry Code of the Philippines). On June 19, 2020, operatives of NBI-Ilagan District Office (NBI-ILDO) arrested RAJIV CALI y SARIP alias ADAM for Falsification of Public Documents. Subject was arrested in an entrapment operation conducted in Brgy. Bangon, Marawi City where fake COMELEC ID was being made whose main source is Subject RAJIV. Transacted from the Subject is one (1) COMELEC ID in the amount of Php 600. Recovered from the Subject were the entrapment money, computer set and printing equipment. Subject was brought to NBI-ILDO for booking procedures and was temporarily detained thereat. On June 19, 2020, operatives of NBI-Ilagan District Office (NBI-ILDO) arrested SITTIE AINAH M. HADJI NASSER for Falsification of Public Documents. Subject was engaged in selling fake COMELEC IDs online. Payments are made either thru meet up or money remittances. Subject was arrested in an entrapment operation wherein a COMELEC ID in the amount of Php 1,500 was transacted with the Subject. Recovered from the possession of the Subject were COMELEC IDs of her clients. Subject was brought to NBI-ILDO for booking procedures and was temporarily detained thereat. On June 20, 2020, operatives of NBI-CALABARZON, with the assistance of NBI-Cavite District Office (NBI-CAVIDO), NBI-Laguna District Office (NBI-LAGDO), NBI-Lucena District Office (NBI-LUCDO), Batangas City PNP, and CIDG Batangas, arrested a total of 47 individuals for illegal cockfights and gambling sessions. The operation was conducted in compliance with the Search Warrant against FERNAN BAYLOSIS of Berberabe Subdivision, Pallocan West, Batangas City for alleged violation of PD 1602 as amended by RA 9287 (Anti-Illegal Gambling Law). On June 22, 2020, operatives of NBI-Central Visayas Regional Office (NBI-CEVRO) arrested JEMUEN M. CENON for illegal selling of Covid-19 Rapid Test Kits. Subject was caight red handed by joint operatives of NBI-CEVRO and FDA as he received the marked money for online sale transaction consisting of 134 boxes of Covid-19 Rapid Test Kits for a total value of Php 3,484,000. Under RA 9711 (FDA Act of 2009), Antibody Covid 19 Test Kits are strictly for medical professional use and not intended for personal use and it must be strictly distributed to appropriate establishments or institutions. The product must be acquired through prescription from a licensed physician from a licensed hospital or drugstore and it is therefore strictly prohibited to be sold online. Subject JEMUEN M. CENON was presented for inquest proceedings for violation of RA 9711 in relation to RA 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012). On June 22, 2020, operatives of NBI-Northeastern Mindanao Regional Office (NBI-NEMRO) arrested MOHAMMAD NAWAF Y. CAAYAMAN and NICE B. YLURAN for illegal selling of Rapid Test Kit. Subjects were arrested in entrapment operation after they received marked money from the poseur-buyer as payment for 15 boxes of Innovita One Step Rapid Test Kit. Subjects, however, were released from custody after an interview made by FDA operatives who informed the NBI that certification coming from their main office could not be produced within the period prescribed by law. On June 23, 2020, operatives of NBI-Northeastern Mindanao Regional Office (NBI-NEMRO) arrested a certain alias ROY in a buy-bust operation. NBI-NEMRO received information that “ROY” was selling shabu in Balingasag, Misamis, Oriental. The buy-bust operation was then conducted resulting in the arrest of the Subject who was found out to be a current Kagawad of Brgy. 4. On June 24, 2020, operatives of NBI-Environmental Crime Division (NBI-EnCD) arrested ERWIN FELICIANO y GUECO, EUGENE MADOLID y CALLOS, ROLLY VERDEFLOR y LAPIG, ALEX GATO y FIL, RENOEL PAULINO y LABORDO, RODEL DE JESUS y RAMIRO, RICO DURON OBIN, and GILBERT CUBELO y YAGAO for illegal quarrying. Subjects were arrested in an operation which stemmed from an information regarding an illegal quarry operation in Brgy. Sta. Lucia, Capas, Tarlac. Surveillance operations ascertained that along the banks of Bangut River, Brgy. Sta. Lucia, Capas, Tarlac, a group of heavy equipment were observed extracting lahar minerals from the river and directly loading the same in the queuing trucks. Upon inquiry within the vicinity, the quarry operation was being held and conducted by “A SAND QUARRY”. A SAND QUARRY sells the minerals extracted from Bangut River for Php 5,000-6,000 per dump truck. Operatives were informed by the Office of the Governor, Province of Tarlac that no quarry permits were issued for the whole province of Tarlac by the Provincial Mining Regulatory Board-Tarlac. Documents show that A SAND QUARRY had no existing mining and quarry permit from the Mines and Geosciences Bureau of Region 3 and is not authorized nor listed as one of the permittee by the DENR. Thus, operatives proceeded to the said barangay and upon arrival thereat, three (3) dump trucks were coming from the Bangut River and loaded with lahar sand and transporting its way to the National Road. The dump trucks were halted by the operatives and recovered from the dump trucks operators EUGENE MADOLID y CALLOS, ROLLY VERDEFLOR y LAPIG and ALEX GATO y FIL were Sand and Gravel Delivery Receipts from the office of the Treasurer, Province of Tarlac. Operatives proceeded to the cashier/checker’s place wherein ERWIN FELICIANO y GUECO was preparing receipts of payment for dump truck loaded with lahar sand and recovered from his possession is a booklet of Sand and Gravel Delivery. At the quarry site, RENOEL PAULINO y LABORDO was found in flagrante delicto operating a pay loader and loading lahar sand to the dump trucks. Dump truck driver RICO DURON y OBINA was likewise on his way to the cashier’s office for payment after his dump truck was loaded with lahar sand. The other dump truck drivers were RODEL DE JESUS y RAMIRO, RICO DURON OBINA, and GILBERT CUBELO y YAGAO. Operatives asked for the necessary documents required but Subjects failed to produce any. DENR-MGB seized the equipment used in the quarry and the value of the seized items is more or less Php 10,860,000.00. Above-mentioned Subjects were then placed under arrest for Theft of Minerals. Charges for violation of RA 7942 (Philippine Mining Act of 1995) were filed against the Subjects. On June 24, 2020, operatives of NBI-Task Force Against Illegal Drugs (NBI-TFAID) arrested CHUI BAO CAI and JIN QI WANG, Chinese nationals for operating built in online pharmacy/drug outlet without Certificate of Registration, Professional Identification Card duly issued by the Professional Regulation Commission and License to Operate issued by the Food and Drugs Administration. Subjects were arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from an information that a certain CHUI BAO CAI is operating a warehouse with built in online pharmacy/drug outlet pertinent permits and documents. Surveillance operations confirmed the said information and Subject CHUI BAO CAI was operating with his cohort JIN QI WANG at Brgy. Vitalez, Airport Village, Paranaque City, vending only to Chinese nationals. Subject CAI is one of the biggest suppliers of Chinese drug medicine to other underground hospitals and pharmacies operated by Chinese nationals in NCR. He also engages in the illegal practice of dispensing medicinal drugs to Chinese nationals without prescription froma licensed physician. On the aforementioned date, the entrapment operation was conducted resulting in the arrest of the Subjects after failing to present necessary documents. Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of City Prosecutor, Paranaque City for violation of RA 9711 (FDA Act of 2009), RA 7394 (Consumer Act of the Philippines), and RA 10918 (Philippine Pharmacy Act). On June 25, 2020, operatives of NBI-Cybercrime Division (NBI-CCD) arrested JOHN RAVEN AQUINO, the founder and leader of Global Security Hacker Group. Subject was arrested after a thorough investigation conducted relative to the complaint filed by representatives of San Beda University regarding the alleged hacking and defacement of the SBU’s online School Management System Portal. Notre Dame of Dadiangas University (NDDU) in Genral Santos City was also hacked with similar defacement page and script to SBU web portal. Cyber-surveillance conducted revealed that the Subject created a github.com account under username @yougotpwn and dumped the extracted SBU’s log in database. Audit report from SBU showed logs of high risk malwares penetrated their system and Subject installed a backdoor web shell solus.php. Investigation with Justin Claveria, allegedly a top-level computer hacker involved in cybercriminal activities and allegedly a top-level computer hacker involved in cybercriminal activities who was arrested in April 2020 in Lemery, Batangas, revealed that @solus is one of the cohorts of Claveria in hacking, phishing, and scamming activities. Information gathered disclosed and supported that @solus is John Raven Aquino. On the basis of Search Warrants, operatives proceeded to JOHN RAVEN AQUINO’s house in Novaliches, Quezon City. Operatives found JOHN RAVEN inside his house with an ongoing operation and seized from the possession of Subject were various Paymaya cards, blank cards, skimming devices, and computer sets. Subject was brought to NBI Main Headquarters for the booking procedures and was turned over to NBI detention cell as per standard operating procedure.

title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) has recommended to the Ombudsman the filing of graft charges against the former Mayor of Municipality of Siayan Zamboanga Del Norte and two (2) municipal employees who conspired with each other in commiting illegal acts. Also recommended to be charged is the incumbent Mayor of the Siayan for Obstruction of Justice. NBI Officer-in-Charge (OIC)-Director Eric B. Distor identified the subjects as former MAYOR FLORA LAGRINA VILLAROSA, the 2 employees, ANA DOTAR MARCO and JENNIFER SALDON PUMICPIC, and incumbent Mayor, ATTY. JOSECOR GEPOLONGCA. OIC Director Distor said that the recommendation was arrived at after months of exhaustive investigation conducted by the NBI-Anti Graft Division (NBI-AGD). Distor said an anonymous letter of request for investigation was filed with the NBI alleging that former Mayor Villarosa has acquired numerous businesses, real estate properties, vehicles and money which are manifestly disproportionate to her salary and other sources of lawful income during her incumbency as Municipal Mayor of Siayan, Zamboanga Del Norte from 2010 to 2019. It is also alleged in the letter that Villarosa hid all her assets through dummy accounts, which used the names of other persons as owners and sole proprietors of various properties and businesses which she actually owns. A complaint was also received from Subject Marco, one of the employees of Siayan Municipality, who alleged in her Affidavit that she and former Mayor Villarosa used to be friends and because of this, she agreed to Villarosa to use her name as dummy to the former Mayor’s businesses identified as MIDWAY GAS STATION and MIDWAY ENTERPRISES located in Saiyan. Subject Marco also revealed that Villarosa used her name and other persons’ name in most of her businesses in order to engage contracts with the Municipality of Saiyan, during her incumbency as Mayor. Subject Marco also added that another employee, subject Pumicpic, was introduced to her as the secretary of Villarosa. According to the statements of witnesses who, during Villarosa’s incumbency as Mayor, were employees of the Municipal Government of Saiyan and a Barangay Official testified that the owner of MIDWAY GAS STATION and MIDWAY ENTERPRISES is actually former Mayor Villarosa. body: PRESS STATEMENT November 06, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } The National Bureau of Investigation-Organized and Transnational Crime Division (NBI OTCD) arrested a Chinese national identified as XIANG LONGYIYU for violations of Section 37(a)(7) (Overstaying) and Section 37(a)(2) (Undesirability) of Commonwealth Act No. 613 (Philippine Immigration Act of 1940). The operation is a response to a referral from the Cybercrime Investigation and Coordinating Center (CICC) regarding a Chinese national named Xiang Longyiyu, who is allegedly involved in scam-related activities in Metro Manila. The Subject has transitioned to a decentralized, work-from-home setup after previously being affiliated with a known scam hub that operated in Makati. Information from the CICC indicates that the subject also uses the alias “Sam Lee” and currently resides in a condominium in Makati City. Verification made with the Bureau of Immigration (BI) revealed that the Subject has overstayed in the country. The NBI agents also detected scam operations in the digital activities of the Subject, including the use of anonymized communication platforms. remote access tools, and potential coordination with external accomplices. Additionally, no records of any legitimate business registration or lawful employment were found linked to the Subject’s current activities. NBI-OTCD agents, together with the investigators from CICC, immediately initiated surveillance operations, which confirmed the Subject’s presence in the target condominium unit. On November 4, 2025, a joint team from the NBI-OTCD, the BI Fugitive Search Unit (BI-FSU), and the CICC conducted an operation at a targeted condominium. This action was carried out under a Mission Order issued by the BI Commissioner, which authorized the verification and investigation of the individual known as Xiang. The operation was successful, resulting in the apprehension of the subject. During the operation, the Subject was found in possession of several electronic devices that showed signs of use in online scamming and illegal gambling activities. NBI OIC Director ANGELITO DLP MAGNO said that the agents of NBI-OTCD will apply for a Warrant to Search, Seize, and Examine Computer Data (WSSECD) for these electronic devices. Their ongoing efforts include thorough investigations and collaborative operations aimed at protecting victims from various fraudulent schemes. Through these actions, the NBI strives to ensure a safer environment for the public and to hold accountable those who engage in deceptive practices. OIC Magno added that the NBI has consistently demonstrated its commitment to end criminal activities perpetrated by foreign nationals in the country by actively targeting and dismantling scamming operations that prey on innocent individuals.

body: A fake lawyer and long wanted by the law for carnapping was finally caught by agents of the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) in Quezon City last week. The subject was identified as RICHARD GITALADA ALPAPARA, 58, a resident of Blk. 17 Lot 22 Simeon St., North Olympus Subd., Bgy. Kaligayahan, Novaliches, Quezon City. Last month, the NBI received a complaint from Ma. Cristina P. Bernardo, a Quezon City resident that a man later identified as Alpapara whom she hired as her legal counsel, is not a member of the Bar. Bernardo met “Atty. Sarte” at the Quezon City Hall of Justice when she looked for a lawyer to help her in her real estate problem. It pertains to a property she bought in Novalicehs, Quezon City. Sarte demanded for P30,000 as acceptance fee which she paid. Further, he also demanded P3,000 as appearance fee for every hearing. After the preparation of the initial documents, she came to know form a reliable source that Sarte is a not a lawyer. She demanded for the repayment of the fees she paid him as well as the return of her documents. Despite repeated demands he refused to return the money. A certification obtained from the Office of the Bar Confidant, Supreme Court proved that Sarte is not really a lawyer. Record check with NBI files disclosed that he has a standing warrant of arrest under the name Richard Gitalada Alpapara in Criminal Case No. 117802 for Carnapping by Makati RTC Branch 139 in 1985 and Criminal Case No.Q-08-153981 for Estafa issued by Quezon City RTC Branch 85 in 2008 in the name of Sarte. It is believed that Alpapara who used the name Richard A. Sarte have victimized other clients in Quezon City and in the Bulacan areas. Alpapara was arrested by NBI agents on June 28, 2012 at his residence in Novaliches, Quezon City. Charges of Falsification, Usurpation of Authority and Estafa are being recommended against Alpapara. He is now detained at the NBI jail.

body: • On January 4, 2022, operatives of NBI-Anti-Violence Against Women and Children Division (NBI-AVAWCD) arrested RODEL FRANCISCO DEL ROSARIO in Tanay, Rizal for the killing of a 12-year old boy and critically wounding of others. on January 3, 2022 a gruesome incident happened inside the Claret residence in Colinas Verdes Residential Estates and Country Club, City of San Jose Del Monte (CSJDM), Bulacan. According to the residents nearby they heard loud screaming coming from the above said residence desperately begging for help described as “tulungan nyo kami, pinapatay kami!”. One of the neighbors saw a bloodied man rushing outside the said residence and entered a parked car outside, drove it and sped away. Another neighbor noticed that his service gate was open thereby concluding that an attempted trespass to dwelling occurred and he noticed that one of his stay-in employees had been missing for hours. The said neighbor then reported the incident to NBI-AVAWCD. Investigation made by the Bulacan PNP revealed that the incident led to the death of a 12-year old boy and critically wounding of other members of the subject residential house. On January 4, 2022, NBI-AVAWCD agents received a call from the employer of Subject Del Rosario informing the NBI that his employee (Subject Del Rosario) confessed to him that he is the perpetrator of the gruesome incident. Subject Del Rosario told his employer that he will only surrender to the NBI in the presence of a respected senior church leader. Thus, on even date, NBI-AVAWCD operatives proceeded Tanay, Rizal where the subject is said to be staying. While cruising the Marikina-Infanta Highway in Barangay Cuyambay, the operatives spotted the subject. Upon seeing the NBI-AVAWCD operatives, Subject Del Rosario voluntarily surrendered himself. Subject was brought to the NBI Headquarters, V-tech tower, G. Araneta Avenue corner Maria Clara St., Sto Domingo, Quezon City. On January 5, 2022, elements of the PNP CSJDM arrived at the NBI, Taft Avenue, Manila to take the custody of the subject to present him before the Office of the City Prosecutor, CSJDM Bulacan for inquest proceedings. • On January 11, 2022, operatives of NBI-Dagupan District Office (NBI-DADO) acted on the complaint of Michael Soriano and letter request from MSWDO, Sta. Barbara, Pangasinan to assist in rescuing complainant’s children at Quirino Hill, Baguio City where the children are believed to be being kept by their aunt Alpha Balong. Acting on the request, NBI-DADO operatives, together with the complainant and Social Welfare Officers, proceeded to Baguio City and sought for amicable meeting. A confrontation was held at the Brgy. Hall of Ucab at the Office of the Barangay Council for the Protection of Children and it was agreed that the three (3) older children aged 9, 12, and 13 will be left temporarily at their aunt while the youngest child aged 4 will return back with his father to Pangasinan. Thus, complainant requested to close the case. • On January 13, 2022, the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) foiled an escape-attempt of 3 prisoners from the NBI Detention Center led by Rolan “Kerwin” Espinosa. The swift and timely action of Agents prevented the escape of Espinosa and 2 other prisoners. The new Chief and Executive Officer (ExO) of the Security Management Section (SMS) acted with dispatch which resulted in thwarting the plan of Kerwin Espinosa from escaping from the NBI jail. As soon as the info was received NBI-SMS personnel immediately acted on it without delay. On January 13, 2022, the Chief of the NBI-SMS and its ExO received an info that Rolan “Kerwin” Espinosa and 2 other detainees are planning to escape our detention facility thru the hole of the exhaust fan at the ceiling. On the same night, they immediately conducted an inspection of the jail. In one of the cells of the jail, the raiding team of Agents observed a deformed exhaust fan, which when removed, exposed a hole fit for a detainee to escape. OIC Distor said that in view of this incident, security measures at the jail has since been tightened with regular inspection of all jail facilities. • On January 17, 2022, operatives of NBI-Eastern Visayas Regional Office (NBI-EVRO) arrested CLYDE REY BALAAN and ELWARD LOMONGCAN in Tacloban City for transporting banned species of illegally cut lumber known as “iron wood”. The operation stemmed from an information received by NBI-EVRO regarding a possible violation of PD 705 otherwise known as the Forestry Reform Code of the Philippines. According to the information received by the NBI, one CLYDE REY BALAAN, a Barangay Councilor and resident of Lianga, Surigao del Sur, is transporting banned species of illegally cut lumber “iron wood” or “magkuno”. The logs are allegedly coming from the island of Mindanao on board a twenty-footer wing van/truck using the Port of San Ricardo as the point of entry. Logs are allegedly distributed in the municipality of Bato, Leyte and Maasin City, Southern Leyte. An NBI-EVRO operative, using an alias, was able to talk with the Subject and gathered additional information such as the sizes of the logs, its corresponding prices as well as names of previous customers and locations of the delivery. After which, NBI-EVRO operatives, together with DENR Region VIII, conducted an entrapment operation and successfully arrested Subject CLYDE REY BALAAN and the truck driver ELWARD LOMONGCAN. Seized from the Subjects were Php 900,000.00 marked money, one (1) unit wing van, twelve (12) wheeler truck and thirteen (13) pieces “magkuno/iron wood” lumbers. The wing van and the thirteen (13) pieces “magkuno/iron wood” lumbers were turned over to DENR-PENRO, Palo, Leyte pending necessary documentation. Subjects CLYDE REY BALAAN and ELWARD LOMONGCAN were presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor, Tacloban City for violation of PD 705 (Forestry Reform Code of the Philippines). • On January 18, 2022, operatives of NBI- Dipolog District Office (NBI-DIPDO) arrested RENAN HECHANOVA y ALFORQUE in Dipolog City for Robbery Extortion. the operation stemmed from the complaint by the victim of Subject Hechanova. The complainant alleged that sometime in November 2021, a Letter of Authority that was served to him by the BIR-RDO 19, stating that he has a tax deficiency of Php 4.5 Million. The complainant added that sometime in December, personnel from the BIR, Dipolog City, called him and asked for Php 400,000.00 as settlement of his tax deficiencies. The complainant added that he was threatened that if he will not comply with the demand, his case will be forwarded to their Regional Office in Zamboanga City and he will be forced to pay Php 4.5 Million. On the third week of December 2021, the complainant went to the BIR office where he met two (2) BIR examiners namely Renan Hechanova and Benjie Sumalpong. The subject begged to the two BIR examiners to give him time to produce the demanded Php 400,000.00 which was granted by the two (2). Thus, the entrapment operation was conducted resulting in the arrest of the Subject Hechanova. Subject was charged for violation of Article 294 (Robbery with violence against or intimidation of persons) under the Revised Penal Code, as amended; violation of R.A. 3019 (Anti-Graft and Practices Act); and violation of R.A. 6713 (Code of Conduct and Ethical Standards for Public Officials and Employees). • On January 18, 2022, operatives of NBI-Cybercrime Division (NBI-CCD) arrested five individuals, two of whom are Nigerian nationals, for their involvement in the “Mark Nagoyo Heist Group”, a group responsible for hacking BDO affecting more than 700 customers. Nigerian nationals IFESINACHI FOUNTAIN ANAEKWE a.k.a. DADDY CHAMP and CHUKWUEMEKA PETER NWADI were arrested in an entrapment operation conducted by operatives of NBI-Cybercrime Division (NBI-CCD) in Mabalacat, Pampanga on January 18, 2022. The operation stemmed from an information provided by the informant who had transactions with the Subjects. The informant voluntarily appeared before the NBI-CCD to give information regarding several individuals believed to be leaders, members, or affiliates of MARK NAGOYO GROUP. According to the informant, Subjects were engaged in the business of providing access devices to anyone looking for options to cash out funds fraudulently obtained. These access devices range from bank accounts, crypto wallets, or even point-of-sale terminals of otherwise legitimate merchants. Further, when a certain MARK FROILAN called the informant about money cash outs, the latter contacted DADDY CHAMP who then said that he will provide the informant three (3) different accounts so she can be transferring in it Php 10 Million each, apparently referring to the funds from BDO alluded to by MARK FROILAN. With these, the entrapment operation was hatched resulting in the arrest of Subjects IFESINACHI FOUNTAIN ANAEKWE a.k.a. DADDY CHAMP and his companion CHUKWUEMEKA PETER NWADI after they were caught in flagrante delicto offering accounts for sale. Meanwhile, Subject JHEROM ANTHONY TAUPA y DIAWAN was arrested by operatives of NBI-CCD in a buy-bust operation also on January 18 in Floridablanca, Pampanga for selling “scampage” or phishing website. Another informant disclosed that JHEROM TAUPA is one of the masterminds behind the MARK NAGOYO HEIST. According to the informant, Subject TAUPA is currently offering for sale scampage, particularly an imitation of Gcash Webpage. Accordingly, TAUPA modified the code in order to gather the log in details of unwitting victims who would access the scampage in the mistaken belief that they were opening Gcash’s official portal. The owner of the scampage would thus be able to get into the victim’s Gcash accounts to steal their hard-earned funds. To prove his averments, informant showed the operatives his conversation with TAUPA showing their past transactions involving scampages. The buy- bust operation was then conducted wherein informant and Subject TAUPA agreed on the price of Php 2,000.00 to be paid in cash direct as consideration for the scampage. The operation resulted in the arrest of Subject TAUPA after receiving the marked money. TAUPA admitted that he was selling Gcash scampages which he stored in his computer. Further investigation revealed that Subject JHEROM TAUPA is involved in a group heist, being the one sending the emailing list containing personal details of various bank customers to a group of individuals responsible for sending email to the former. The said email contains a link which when clicked, will be used for the hacking process of the heist group. Also arrested in a separate operation by NBI-CCD were Subjects RONELYN PANALIGAN, and CLAY S. REVILLOSA. Both Subjects are likewise involved in the BDO hacking as web developer and downloader. Subjects IFESINACHI FOUNTAIN ANAEKWE a.k.a. DADDY CHAMP and CHUKWUEMEKA PETER NWADI were presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the Prosecutor General, Department of Justice, Manila for Trafficking in Unauthorized Access Devices under Section 9 of RA 8484 otherwise known as the Access Devices Regulation Act of 1998. Subject JHEROM ANTHONY TAUPA y DIAWAN was presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the Prosecutor General, Department of Justice, Manila for Misuse of Devices under Section 4(a)(5)(i)(aa) of RA 10175 otherwise known as the Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012. • On January 19, 2022, operatives of NBI- Special Action Unit (NBI-SAU) arrested JOEYLYN CASTRO, VIRGILIO YALUNG, ZENIA ANDRES, and MARILYN LUCERO in Angeles City for illegal possession and use of false treasury or bank notes and other instruments of credit. The operation stemmed from the information that a group of individuals were about to proceed to a money changer in Angeles City to exchange the counterfeit US Dollars into Philippine Pesos. NBI-SAU coordinated with the Payments and Currency Investigation Group, Office of the Assistant Governor, Payments and Currency Development Sub-Sector, Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (PCIG-PCDSS, BSP), and the local authorities. The operatives were able to arrange a meeting through an informant, where two (2) of the subjects would bring and use the counterfeit bills. The NBI-SAU proceeded to Angeles City and closely monitored the movements of the two (2) subjects later identified as Castro and Yalung. Subjects Castro and Yalung then proceeded to a money changer where they tried to exchange the US Dollars but the money changer refused because the US Dollars were counterfeit. At this juncture, NBI-SAU approached the subjects and effected their arrest. Seized from the subjects were seventy-eight (78) pieces of counterfeit One Hundred US Dollar bills with various serial numbers. Subjects Castro and Yalung revealed to the operatives their source of the counterfeit bills, which resulted in a follow-up operation. The arrested subjects led the operatives to the house of their source in Anopol, Bamban, Tarlac where the two (2) undercover agents were met by two (2) elderly women later identified as ZENIA ANDRES and MARILYN LUCERO. Upon asking the undercover agents about the counterfeit bills, the operatives immediately apprehended them. The operatives were able to seize seventy-eight counterfeit US Dollar bills and two (2) bundles of counterfeit One Thousand Peso bills from Subjects Andres and Lucero. The seized items were presented to the Bank Officer of PCIG-PCDSS, BSP, who confirmed that the seized bills were counterfeit. The four arrested subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the Prosecutor – Department of Justice, Manila for violation of Article 168 (Illegal possession and use of false treasury or bank notes and other instruments of credit) in relation to Article 166 (Forging treasury or bank notes on other documents payable to bearer) both under the Revised Penal Code, as amended. • On January 19, 2022, operatives of NBI-Iligan District Office (NBI-ILDO) arrested ABU MOHAIMIN ISMAEL y DUMADU alias DADDY for selling illegal drugs. Subject was arrested in a buy-bust operation conducted by NBI-ILDO operatives at Milestone St., Famous Pension House, Brgy. San Miguel, Iligan City. Bought from the Subject were one (1) heat- sealed large size white rectangular plastic sachet containing white crystalline substance suspected to be shabu weighing more or less 5 grams. Apprehended Subject was brought to NBI-ILDO Office for the standard booking procedure and temporary detention. The confiscated drug evidence was forwarded to NBI Regional Office 10, Forensic Chemistry Division for quantitative and qualitative examination. Case for violation of RA 9165 was filed in court against the arrested Subject. • On January 19, 2022, operatives of NBI-Cebu District Office (NBI-CEBDO) arrested LERIO GULMAYO y LOZADA, NARYL MAE TUNACAO y BAUTISTA, JONA RIZALYN ABRIGANA y LOVITOS, GENALYN YGOT y BERNASIBO, MARY MAE GESTOPA, and ROSSAN AGUAS y MANINANG for illegal gambling in violation of RA 9287 in relation to RA 10175. Subjects were arrested in a bet-bust operation conducted upon the request of PCSO GM Royina M. Garma and PCSO Cebu Glenn Jesus M. Rada. • On January 21, 2022, operatives of NBI-Anti-Organized and Transnational Crime Division (NBI-AOTCD) arrested JENNIFER E. AVENES et.al for violation of Article 294 and Article 315 of the Revised Penal Code. A complaint against Subjects was filed before the NBI for Extortion in the amount of Php 38,000.00. Acting on the complaint, NBI-AOTCD conducted an entrapment operation resulting in the arrest of Jennifer E. Avenes et.al. Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the Prosecutor’s Office. • On January 21, 2022, combined elements of the NBI-Special Action Unit (NBI-SAU), Bureau of Customs (BOC), Philippine Coast Guard (PCG), and Manila Police District (MPD) seized several rapid antigen test kits in the City of Manila. The operation stemmed from the Mission Order issued by the BOC, requesting assistance for the service of BOC LOA against a warehouse in the City of Manila for alleged violation of Customs Modernization and Tariff Act (CMTA). On the above-mentioned date, operatives proceeded to the target unit used as a warehouse located at HMT Building 555 Carlos Palanca St., San Miguel, Manila to implement the said LOA issued by the BOC. The joint operatives were able to seized two (2) large box Clungene Rapid Test Kit (Covid-19 Antigen Test Kits-Saliva) containing seventy-four (74) small boxes which has twenty (20) test cassettes per box; ten (10) pcs. Clungene Rapid Test Kit cassettes, and ten (10) parcels of J&T Express containing antigen kits. The seized items were valuated at around Php 250,000.00. Upon arrival of the joint operatives to the target unit warehouse they spotted a certain CHI ZHI CHAO inside the premises. However, Mr. Chao insisted that he is only a visitor and not the lessee of the said unit, this was corroborated by the building administrator maintaining that Mr. Chao has no involvement in the prohibited online selling of the seized antigen kits. Further investigation revealed that the target unit is being occupied by a certain MARICEL BACCAY y LUSTRE. Unfortunately, the said occupant was neither at the office or anywhere in the building premises. Violation of R.A. 9711 (Food and Drug Administration Act of 2009) in relation to FDA Advisory No. 2021-3523 will be filed against the operators behind the importation, moreover, sale/ distribution of unregistered antigen kits. • On January 23, 2022, operatives of NBI–Dumaguete District Office (NBI-DUMDO) seized various antibiotics and other pharmaceutical drugs sold without any prescription in Mabinay, Negros Oriental. A report was received by NBI-DUMDO regarding a group of unscrupulous individuals are engaged in selling antibiotics and other pharmaceutical drugs without any prescription. Acting on the said report, NBI-DUMDO operatives proceeded to the area on January 23, 2022 and observed thereat that medical drugs including prescription drugs were sold in an open market just like ordinary goods. Operatives asked the saleslady identified as GINA TOMANDOC whether or not she has the authority from Food and Drug Administration (FDA) to sell or if she is a licensed pharmacist. TOMANDOC failed to show any proof thereof. Subsequently, the medical drugs were confiscated and properly inventoried. GINA TOMANDOC was brought to NBI office for further questioning. Cases for violation of RA 7394 (Consumers Act of 1991), RA 5921 (Pharmacy Law), and RA 2883 (Philippine Medical Act) will be filed after completion of the documentary and testimonial evidences. • On January 24, 2022, operatives of NBI-Special Action Unit (NBI-SAU) arrested MARICHU MILITAR, DAISY BUCCAT, NENITA PELECIA, and MARY ANN APURA for Qualified Theft and Robbery/Extortion. On Septempber 16, 2021, a complainant filed a complaint against MARY ANN APURA, MARICHU MILITAR, TEOFILO T. DE BELEN II, and ROBERTO DIONCO for alleged Qualified Falsification and Qualified Theft. Complainant averred that she entrusted the processing of her land titles to APURA but the latter stole the same and sold some of it without her knowledge and consent. Complainant pleaded for the return of her land titles but to no avail. On January 24, 2022, complainant was informed by the Real State Agent that MILITAR agreed to release the land titles only to a buyer but demanded Php 4 Million in exchange. Complainant immediately reported the matter to the NBI. Hence, the entrapment operation. The operation was conducted inside a bank in Las Pinas City and resulted in the arrest of Subjects MILITAR, BUCCAT, and PELECIA. In a follow-up operation, Subject APURA was also arrested inside her residence in Pilar Village, Las Pinas City. Police Corporal Magan D. Alvarez, Baby Boy V. Catilo, John Fritz Benigay, Helen Rose O. Pagonaling, and George G. Ayon-ayon were also invited for identification and investigation to determine their participation. All Subjects are presently under the custody of NBI-SAU while appropriate charges are being prepared against them. • On January 24, 2022, operatives of NBI-Task Force Against Illegal Drugs (NBI-TFAID) arrested ASRAP KAMAD KASAN, TATO DALUNDONG, and JERKLIE ABDULKARIM, a nominee of the Party List Peoples Volunteer Against Illegal Drugs (PVAID). The operation stemmed from an information regarding a certain “DATU” later identified as Jerklie Abdulkarim who was selling high grade shabu. Informant relayed that DATU has with him a fair amount of shabu amounting to Php 900,000.00 and needed to be sold within a week. Acting on the information received, NBI-TFAID immediately hatched a buy-bust operation. On January 24, 2022, “DATU” instructed the informant to fetch him together with a companion identified as ASRAP KAMAD KASAN somewhere along Roxas Boulevard, Pasay City for them to proceed to Paliparan III Dasmarinas, Cavite where the alleged contact of DATU will hand over the Php 900,000.00 worth of shabu. After proper coordination with the Philippine Disrug Enforcement Agency (PDEA) and PNP Cavite Provincial Office, the remaining operatives proceeded ahead at the said area and positioned themselves strategically for the buy- bust operation. At the location, the contact of DATU identified as TATO DALUNDONG handed to ASRAP a small box. After confirming that the box contains illegal drugs, undercover operative handed over to ASRAP the bag with buy-bust money. At this juncture, operatives announced their authority and arrested the Subjects. Seized from the Subjects were six (6) heat-sealed transparent plastic sachets containing white crystalline substance, which upon examination by NBI-Forensic Chemistry Division (NBI-FCD), tested positive for shabu with a net weight of 293.5185 grams. After the booking procedure, it was found out that DATU is a nominee of the Party List Peoples Volunteer Against Illegal Drugs (PVAID). On the other hand, TATO alleged that he is a 17-year-old minor. However, he acted with discernment knowing that he was in possession of shabu. Arrested Subjects were charged for violations of Sections 5 and 11 of RA 9165 (Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002). • On January 25, 2022, operatives of NBI-Central Visayas Regional Office (NBI-CEVRO) arrested MAXIMO BAGUIO MARIOT JR., DOROTEO VALMORIA AUXTERO JR., and BRYAN BURLAOS SACMAR in Talisay City, Cebu for pilferage of electricity. Subjects were arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from the information given by the President COO of Visayan Electric Company (VECO) that certain individuals are taking advantage of the recent calamity (Typhoon Odette) to extort money from consumers who were affected by the said typhoon in exchange for priority electricity repairs and immediate energization. NBI-CEVRO immediately conducted a surveillance operation and was able to confirm that Subject Mariot is demanding money from the consumers of VECO in exchange for immediate restoration of electricity. The operatives were also able to discover that Subject Mariot disregarded safety protocol and would merely connect electricity from any available source. With these, NBI-CEVRO operatives proceeded to Talisay, Cebu and conducted the entrapment operation which resulted in the arrest of the above-mentioned Subjects. Arrested Subjects were charged for violation of R.A. 7832 (Anti-Electricity and Electric Transmission Lines/ Materials Pilferage Act of 1994). • On January 25, 2022, operatives of NBI-Cebu District Office (NBI-CEBDO) arrested CHRISTINELINE DEPAUDHON, MARIA JULIET DUMADAG y LONOP, MYKEL CERIOLA TAN and JESSEL FAITH CATARINEN y BERCEDE for illegal selling of Covid-19 Rapid Test Kits in Mandaue and Cebu City. NBI join hands with the Food and Drugs Administration (FDA) Cebu Field Regional Office and conducted relentless buy bust operations in several establishments, against group of unscrupulous individuals who take advantage of situation. As a result thereof, above-mentioned Subjects were caught red handed on separate occasions by the joint elements of NBI-CEBDO and FDA operatives after receiving marked money for the online sale transaction of 200 boxes of Clungene and Joinstar Covid- 19 Rapid Test Kits with an estimated value of Php 1,000,000.00. Both products have expired and the importer/distributor failed to secure product registration (CPR) which constitutes to violation of Section 11(a) of RA 9711 otherwise known as the Food and Drug Administration Act of 2009 as amended. Further, the arrested Subjects do not have License to Operate violating the provision of the same law under Section 11(k). Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the Inquest Prosecutors of Cebu and Mandaue City. • On January 26, 2022, operatives of NBI-Intellectual Property Rights Division (NBI-IPRD) seized 30 boxes containing 100 pieces of counterfeit Bioflu tablets. Items, with an estimated amount of Php 27,000.00, were seized in an entrapment operation conducted in Marikina City. Charges for violation of RA 8293 (Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines) were filed against JOMAR J. MALLARI. • On January 26, 2022, operatives of NBI-Special Task Force (NBI-STF) arrested TAREK SIAM, a Jordanian national, in Makati City for illegal possession of firearm and violent acts inside a hotel premises. The NBI received a letter complaint from Congressman Anthony Rolando T. Golez, Attorney-in-Fact of Makati Hotel and Residences Condominium Corporation, requesting law enforcement assistance regarding MR. TAREK SIAM who had been violently harassing the employees of a hotel in Makati City and even threatened several security guards of the said establishment with a gun violating election gun ban and the Comprehensive Firearms and Ammunition Regulation Act of 2012. On January 25, 2022, NBI operatives received a phone call from the management of the hotel requesting immediate law enforcement assistance to avert the violent acts being committed by TAREK SIAM inside the hotel premises. As relayed, TAREK SIAM was in possession of a hand gun as he was destroying and breaking the hallway lights of the 22nd floor of the hotel. NBI operatives immediately responded but upon arrival, TAREK SIAM went back inside his room. Meantime, operatives were shown CCTV footages showing that TAREK SIAM was indeed in possession of a firearm and while outside his residence, he loaded his gun. According to the management of the hotel, TAREK SIAM had been brandishing and drawing his gun against any hotel personnel. NBI-STF checked the database of criminal records and found out that there is a Warrant of Arrest issued by the Manila Regional Trial Court Branch 005 against TAREK SIAM for violation of RA 7610 otherwise known as Special Protection of Children Against Abuse, Exploitation, and Discrimination Act. With the Warrant of Arrest at hand, operatives patiently waited for someone from TAREK SIAM’s room to come out, taking into consideration the safety of the hotel residents as TAREK SIAM may react violently using his gun. On January 26, 2022, when a female individual came out of the room, operatives took the opportunity to sneak inside. NBI-STF operatives declared their presence and informed TAREK SIAM of his Warrant of Arrest and placed the Subject under arrest after being apprised of his statutory and constitutional rights. Charges for violation of RA 10591 otherwise known as the Comprehensive Firearms and Ammunition Regulation Act and violation of The Omnibus Election Code were filed against TAREK SIAM before the City Prosecutor, Makati City. • On January 27, 2022, operatives of NBI-Bicol Regional Office (NBI-BRO) arrested CHERRYLAINE BONACUA NUYDA for selling counterfeit Bioflu tablets in violation of RA 8203 (Special Law on Counterfeit Drugs). Subject was arrested in a buy-bust operation conducted at Purok 3, Brgy. 3 EM’s Barrio East, Old Albay, Legazpi City. Seized from the Subject were 100 fake Bioflu tablets and Php1,000 bill marked money. Seized drugs were sent to FDA for product verification. • On January 27, 2022, operatives of NBI-Ilocos Regional Office (NBI-IRO) arrested ADRIAN “RYAN” TUGARINO y TEJADA in Rosales, Pangasinan for illegally selling hybrid seeds. Subject TUGARINO was apprehended in an entrapment operation conducted at the parking lot of a mall in Carmen, Rosales, Pangasinan. He was arrested after receiving the marked money from the poseur-buyer of hybrid seeds that were exclusively researched and produced by complainant Syngenta Philippines, Inc. Syngenta is a leading agricultural company working to provide premium seeds and crop protection innovation to enhance the prosperity of farmers. Seized from Subject TUGARINO were two (2) bags with a total weight of twenty (20) kilos of hybrid seeds. Inquest transmittal was received by the Assistant Prosecutor of Rosales, Pangasinan charging the Subject for violation of RA 8293 (Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines) in relation to Section 6 of RA 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012). Subject is currently detained at NBI-IRO Jail awaiting case resolution. • On January 28, 2022, operatives of NBI-Bohol District Office (NBI-BOHDO) arrested FELIX PANIMDIM y AMONSOT a.k.a. EYET AMONSOT at Purok 6, Bool Dist., Tagbilaran City for illegal gambling in violation of PD 1602 (Anti-Illegal Gambling Law) in relation to Sec. 3(a) of RA 9287 (An Act Increasing the Penalties for Illegal Numbers Game).

NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION

• On January 4, 2022, operatives of NBI-Anti-Violence Against Women and Children Division (NBI-AVAWCD) arrested RODEL FRANCISCO DEL ROSARIO in Tanay, Rizal for the killing of a 12-year old boy and critically wounding of others. on January 3, 2022 a gruesome incident happened inside the Claret residence in Colinas Verdes Residential Estates and Country Club, City of San Jose Del Monte (CSJDM), Bulacan. According to the residents nearby they heard loud screaming coming from the above said residence desperately begging for help described as “tulungan nyo kami, pinapatay kami!”. One of the neighbors saw a bloodied man rushing outside the said residence and entered a parked car outside, drove it and sped away. Another neighbor noticed that his service gate was open thereby concluding that an attempted trespass to dwelling occurred and he noticed that one of his stay-in employees had been missing for hours. The said neighbor then reported the incident to NBI-AVAWCD. Investigation made by the Bulacan PNP revealed that the incident led to the death of a 12-year old boy and critically wounding of other members of the subject residential house. On January 4, 2022, NBI-AVAWCD agents received a call from the employer of Subject Del Rosario informing the NBI that his employee (Subject Del Rosario) confessed to him that he is the perpetrator of the gruesome incident. Subject Del Rosario told his employer that he will only surrender to the NBI in the presence of a respected senior church leader. Thus, on even date, NBI-AVAWCD operatives proceeded Tanay, Rizal where the subject is said to be staying. While cruising the Marikina-Infanta Highway in Barangay Cuyambay, the operatives spotted the subject. Upon seeing the NBI-AVAWCD operatives, Subject Del Rosario voluntarily surrendered himself. Subject was brought to the NBI Headquarters, V-tech tower, G. Araneta Avenue corner Maria Clara St., Sto Domingo, Quezon City. On January 5, 2022, elements of the PNP CSJDM arrived at the NBI, Taft Avenue, Manila to take the custody of the subject to present him before the Office of the City Prosecutor, CSJDM Bulacan for inquest proceedings. • On January 11, 2022, operatives of NBI-Dagupan District Office (NBI-DADO) acted on the complaint of Michael Soriano and letter request from MSWDO, Sta. Barbara, Pangasinan to assist in rescuing complainant’s children at Quirino Hill, Baguio City where the children are believed to be being kept by their aunt Alpha Balong. Acting on the request, NBI-DADO operatives, together with the complainant and Social Welfare Officers, proceeded to Baguio City and sought for amicable meeting. A confrontation was held at the Brgy. Hall of Ucab at the Office of the Barangay Council for the Protection of Children and it was agreed that the three (3) older children aged 9, 12, and 13 will be left temporarily at their aunt while the youngest child aged 4 will return back with his father to Pangasinan. Thus, complainant requested to close the case. • On January 13, 2022, the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) foiled an escape-attempt of 3 prisoners from the NBI Detention Center led by Rolan “Kerwin” Espinosa. The swift and timely action of Agents prevented the escape of Espinosa and 2 other prisoners. The new Chief and Executive Officer (ExO) of the Security Management Section (SMS) acted with dispatch which resulted in thwarting the plan of Kerwin Espinosa from escaping from the NBI jail. As soon as the info was received NBI-SMS personnel immediately acted on it without delay. On January 13, 2022, the Chief of the NBI-SMS and its ExO received an info that Rolan “Kerwin” Espinosa and 2 other detainees are planning to escape our detention facility thru the hole of the exhaust fan at the ceiling. On the same night, they immediately conducted an inspection of the jail. In one of the cells of the jail, the raiding team of Agents observed a deformed exhaust fan, which when removed, exposed a hole fit for a detainee to escape. OIC Distor said that in view of this incident, security measures at the jail has since been tightened with regular inspection of all jail facilities. • On January 17, 2022, operatives of NBI-Eastern Visayas Regional Office (NBI-EVRO) arrested CLYDE REY BALAAN and ELWARD LOMONGCAN in Tacloban City for transporting banned species of illegally cut lumber known as “iron wood”. The operation stemmed from an information received by NBI-EVRO regarding a possible violation of PD 705 otherwise known as the Forestry Reform Code of the Philippines. According to the information received by the NBI, one CLYDE REY BALAAN, a Barangay Councilor and resident of Lianga, Surigao del Sur, is transporting banned species of illegally cut lumber “iron wood” or “magkuno”. The logs are allegedly coming from the island of Mindanao on board a twenty-footer wing van/truck using the Port of San Ricardo as the point of entry. Logs are allegedly distributed in the municipality of Bato, Leyte and Maasin City, Southern Leyte. An NBI-EVRO operative, using an alias, was able to talk with the Subject and gathered additional information such as the sizes of the logs, its corresponding prices as well as names of previous customers and locations of the delivery. After which, NBI-EVRO operatives, together with DENR Region VIII, conducted an entrapment operation and successfully arrested Subject CLYDE REY BALAAN and the truck driver ELWARD LOMONGCAN. Seized from the Subjects were Php 900,000.00 marked money, one (1) unit wing van, twelve (12) wheeler truck and thirteen (13) pieces “magkuno/iron wood” lumbers. The wing van and the thirteen (13) pieces “magkuno/iron wood” lumbers were turned over to DENR-PENRO, Palo, Leyte pending necessary documentation. Subjects CLYDE REY BALAAN and ELWARD LOMONGCAN were presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor, Tacloban City for violation of PD 705 (Forestry Reform Code of the Philippines). • On January 18, 2022, operatives of NBI- Dipolog District Office (NBI-DIPDO) arrested RENAN HECHANOVA y ALFORQUE in Dipolog City for Robbery Extortion. the operation stemmed from the complaint by the victim of Subject Hechanova. The complainant alleged that sometime in November 2021, a Letter of Authority that was served to him by the BIR-RDO 19, stating that he has a tax deficiency of Php 4.5 Million. The complainant added that sometime in December, personnel from the BIR, Dipolog City, called him and asked for Php 400,000.00 as settlement of his tax deficiencies. The complainant added that he was threatened that if he will not comply with the demand, his case will be forwarded to their Regional Office in Zamboanga City and he will be forced to pay Php 4.5 Million. On the third week of December 2021, the complainant went to the BIR office where he met two (2) BIR examiners namely Renan Hechanova and Benjie Sumalpong. The subject begged to the two BIR examiners to give him time to produce the demanded Php 400,000.00 which was granted by the two (2). Thus, the entrapment operation was conducted resulting in the arrest of the Subject Hechanova. Subject was charged for violation of Article 294 (Robbery with violence against or intimidation of persons) under the Revised Penal Code, as amended; violation of R.A. 3019 (Anti-Graft and Practices Act); and violation of R.A. 6713 (Code of Conduct and Ethical Standards for Public Officials and Employees). • On January 18, 2022, operatives of NBI-Cybercrime Division (NBI-CCD) arrested five individuals, two of whom are Nigerian nationals, for their involvement in the “Mark Nagoyo Heist Group”, a group responsible for hacking BDO affecting more than 700 customers. Nigerian nationals IFESINACHI FOUNTAIN ANAEKWE a.k.a. DADDY CHAMP and CHUKWUEMEKA PETER NWADI were arrested in an entrapment operation conducted by operatives of NBI-Cybercrime Division (NBI-CCD) in Mabalacat, Pampanga on January 18, 2022. The operation stemmed from an information provided by the informant who had transactions with the Subjects. The informant voluntarily appeared before the NBI-CCD to give information regarding several individuals believed to be leaders, members, or affiliates of MARK NAGOYO GROUP. According to the informant, Subjects were engaged in the business of providing access devices to anyone looking for options to cash out funds fraudulently obtained. These access devices range from bank accounts, crypto wallets, or even point-of-sale terminals of otherwise legitimate merchants. Further, when a certain MARK FROILAN called the informant about money cash outs, the latter contacted DADDY CHAMP who then said that he will provide the informant three (3) different accounts so she can be transferring in it Php 10 Million each, apparently referring to the funds from BDO alluded to by MARK FROILAN. With these, the entrapment operation was hatched resulting in the arrest of Subjects IFESINACHI FOUNTAIN ANAEKWE a.k.a. DADDY CHAMP and his companion CHUKWUEMEKA PETER NWADI after they were caught in flagrante delicto offering accounts for sale. Meanwhile, Subject JHEROM ANTHONY TAUPA y DIAWAN was arrested by operatives of NBI-CCD in a buy-bust operation also on January 18 in Floridablanca, Pampanga for selling “scampage” or phishing website. Another informant disclosed that JHEROM TAUPA is one of the masterminds behind the MARK NAGOYO HEIST. According to the informant, Subject TAUPA is currently offering for sale scampage, particularly an imitation of Gcash Webpage. Accordingly, TAUPA modified the code in order to gather the log in details of unwitting victims who would access the scampage in the mistaken belief that they were opening Gcash’s official portal. The owner of the scampage would thus be able to get into the victim’s Gcash accounts to steal their hard-earned funds. To prove his averments, informant showed the operatives his conversation with TAUPA showing their past transactions involving scampages. The buy- bust operation was then conducted wherein informant and Subject TAUPA agreed on the price of Php 2,000.00 to be paid in cash direct as consideration for the scampage. The operation resulted in the arrest of Subject TAUPA after receiving the marked money. TAUPA admitted that he was selling Gcash scampages which he stored in his computer. Further investigation revealed that Subject JHEROM TAUPA is involved in a group heist, being the one sending the emailing list containing personal details of various bank customers to a group of individuals responsible for sending email to the former. The said email contains a link which when clicked, will be used for the hacking process of the heist group. Also arrested in a separate operation by NBI-CCD were Subjects RONELYN PANALIGAN, and CLAY S. REVILLOSA. Both Subjects are likewise involved in the BDO hacking as web developer and downloader. Subjects IFESINACHI FOUNTAIN ANAEKWE a.k.a. DADDY CHAMP and CHUKWUEMEKA PETER NWADI were presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the Prosecutor General, Department of Justice, Manila for Trafficking in Unauthorized Access Devices under Section 9 of RA 8484 otherwise known as the Access Devices Regulation Act of 1998. Subject JHEROM ANTHONY TAUPA y DIAWAN was presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the Prosecutor General, Department of Justice, Manila for Misuse of Devices under Section 4(a)(5)(i)(aa) of RA 10175 otherwise known as the Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012. • On January 19, 2022, operatives of NBI- Special Action Unit (NBI-SAU) arrested JOEYLYN CASTRO, VIRGILIO YALUNG, ZENIA ANDRES, and MARILYN LUCERO in Angeles City for illegal possession and use of false treasury or bank notes and other instruments of credit. The operation stemmed from the information that a group of individuals were about to proceed to a money changer in Angeles City to exchange the counterfeit US Dollars into Philippine Pesos. NBI-SAU coordinated with the Payments and Currency Investigation Group, Office of the Assistant Governor, Payments and Currency Development Sub-Sector, Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (PCIG-PCDSS, BSP), and the local authorities. The operatives were able to arrange a meeting through an informant, where two (2) of the subjects would bring and use the counterfeit bills. The NBI-SAU proceeded to Angeles City and closely monitored the movements of the two (2) subjects later identified as Castro and Yalung. Subjects Castro and Yalung then proceeded to a money changer where they tried to exchange the US Dollars but the money changer refused because the US Dollars were counterfeit. At this juncture, NBI-SAU approached the subjects and effected their arrest. Seized from the subjects were seventy-eight (78) pieces of counterfeit One Hundred US Dollar bills with various serial numbers. Subjects Castro and Yalung revealed to the operatives their source of the counterfeit bills, which resulted in a follow-up operation. The arrested subjects led the operatives to the house of their source in Anopol, Bamban, Tarlac where the two (2) undercover agents were met by two (2) elderly women later identified as ZENIA ANDRES and MARILYN LUCERO. Upon asking the undercover agents about the counterfeit bills, the operatives immediately apprehended them. The operatives were able to seize seventy-eight counterfeit US Dollar bills and two (2) bundles of counterfeit One Thousand Peso bills from Subjects Andres and Lucero. The seized items were presented to the Bank Officer of PCIG-PCDSS, BSP, who confirmed that the seized bills were counterfeit. The four arrested subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the Prosecutor – Department of Justice, Manila for violation of Article 168 (Illegal possession and use of false treasury or bank notes and other instruments of credit) in relation to Article 166 (Forging treasury or bank notes on other documents payable to bearer) both under the Revised Penal Code, as amended. • On January 19, 2022, operatives of NBI-Iligan District Office (NBI-ILDO) arrested ABU MOHAIMIN ISMAEL y DUMADU alias DADDY for selling illegal drugs. Subject was arrested in a buy-bust operation conducted by NBI-ILDO operatives at Milestone St., Famous Pension House, Brgy. San Miguel, Iligan City. Bought from the Subject were one (1) heat- sealed large size white rectangular plastic sachet containing white crystalline substance suspected to be shabu weighing more or less 5 grams. Apprehended Subject was brought to NBI-ILDO Office for the standard booking procedure and temporary detention. The confiscated drug evidence was forwarded to NBI Regional Office 10, Forensic Chemistry Division for quantitative and qualitative examination. Case for violation of RA 9165 was filed in court against the arrested Subject. • On January 19, 2022, operatives of NBI-Cebu District Office (NBI-CEBDO) arrested LERIO GULMAYO y LOZADA, NARYL MAE TUNACAO y BAUTISTA, JONA RIZALYN ABRIGANA y LOVITOS, GENALYN YGOT y BERNASIBO, MARY MAE GESTOPA, and ROSSAN AGUAS y MANINANG for illegal gambling in violation of RA 9287 in relation to RA 10175. Subjects were arrested in a bet-bust operation conducted upon the request of PCSO GM Royina M. Garma and PCSO Cebu Glenn Jesus M. Rada. • On January 21, 2022, operatives of NBI-Anti-Organized and Transnational Crime Division (NBI-AOTCD) arrested JENNIFER E. AVENES et.al for violation of Article 294 and Article 315 of the Revised Penal Code. A complaint against Subjects was filed before the NBI for Extortion in the amount of Php 38,000.00. Acting on the complaint, NBI-AOTCD conducted an entrapment operation resulting in the arrest of Jennifer E. Avenes et.al. Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the Prosecutor’s Office. • On January 21, 2022, combined elements of the NBI-Special Action Unit (NBI-SAU), Bureau of Customs (BOC), Philippine Coast Guard (PCG), and Manila Police District (MPD) seized several rapid antigen test kits in the City of Manila. The operation stemmed from the Mission Order issued by the BOC, requesting assistance for the service of BOC LOA against a warehouse in the City of Manila for alleged violation of Customs Modernization and Tariff Act (CMTA). On the above-mentioned date, operatives proceeded to the target unit used as a warehouse located at HMT Building 555 Carlos Palanca St., San Miguel, Manila to implement the said LOA issued by the BOC. The joint operatives were able to seized two (2) large box Clungene Rapid Test Kit (Covid-19 Antigen Test Kits-Saliva) containing seventy-four (74) small boxes which has twenty (20) test cassettes per box; ten (10) pcs. Clungene Rapid Test Kit cassettes, and ten (10) parcels of J&T Express containing antigen kits. The seized items were valuated at around Php 250,000.00. Upon arrival of the joint operatives to the target unit warehouse they spotted a certain CHI ZHI CHAO inside the premises. However, Mr. Chao insisted that he is only a visitor and not the lessee of the said unit, this was corroborated by the building administrator maintaining that Mr. Chao has no involvement in the prohibited online selling of the seized antigen kits. Further investigation revealed that the target unit is being occupied by a certain MARICEL BACCAY y LUSTRE. Unfortunately, the said occupant was neither at the office or anywhere in the building premises. Violation of R.A. 9711 (Food and Drug Administration Act of 2009) in relation to FDA Advisory No. 2021-3523 will be filed against the operators behind the importation, moreover, sale/ distribution of unregistered antigen kits. • On January 23, 2022, operatives of NBI–Dumaguete District Office (NBI-DUMDO) seized various antibiotics and other pharmaceutical drugs sold without any prescription in Mabinay, Negros Oriental. A report was received by NBI-DUMDO regarding a group of unscrupulous individuals are engaged in selling antibiotics and other pharmaceutical drugs without any prescription. Acting on the said report, NBI-DUMDO operatives proceeded to the area on January 23, 2022 and observed thereat that medical drugs including prescription drugs were sold in an open market just like ordinary goods. Operatives asked the saleslady identified as GINA TOMANDOC whether or not she has the authority from Food and Drug Administration (FDA) to sell or if she is a licensed pharmacist. TOMANDOC failed to show any proof thereof. Subsequently, the medical drugs were confiscated and properly inventoried. GINA TOMANDOC was brought to NBI office for further questioning. Cases for violation of RA 7394 (Consumers Act of 1991), RA 5921 (Pharmacy Law), and RA 2883 (Philippine Medical Act) will be filed after completion of the documentary and testimonial evidences. • On January 24, 2022, operatives of NBI-Special Action Unit (NBI-SAU) arrested MARICHU MILITAR, DAISY BUCCAT, NENITA PELECIA, and MARY ANN APURA for Qualified Theft and Robbery/Extortion. On Septempber 16, 2021, a complainant filed a complaint against MARY ANN APURA, MARICHU MILITAR, TEOFILO T. DE BELEN II, and ROBERTO DIONCO for alleged Qualified Falsification and Qualified Theft. Complainant averred that she entrusted the processing of her land titles to APURA but the latter stole the same and sold some of it without her knowledge and consent. Complainant pleaded for the return of her land titles but to no avail. On January 24, 2022, complainant was informed by the Real State Agent that MILITAR agreed to release the land titles only to a buyer but demanded Php 4 Million in exchange. Complainant immediately reported the matter to the NBI. Hence, the entrapment operation. The operation was conducted inside a bank in Las Pinas City and resulted in the arrest of Subjects MILITAR, BUCCAT, and PELECIA. In a follow-up operation, Subject APURA was also arrested inside her residence in Pilar Village, Las Pinas City. Police Corporal Magan D. Alvarez, Baby Boy V. Catilo, John Fritz Benigay, Helen Rose O. Pagonaling, and George G. Ayon-ayon were also invited for identification and investigation to determine their participation. All Subjects are presently under the custody of NBI-SAU while appropriate charges are being prepared against them. • On January 24, 2022, operatives of NBI-Task Force Against Illegal Drugs (NBI-TFAID) arrested ASRAP KAMAD KASAN, TATO DALUNDONG, and JERKLIE ABDULKARIM, a nominee of the Party List Peoples Volunteer Against Illegal Drugs (PVAID). The operation stemmed from an information regarding a certain “DATU” later identified as Jerklie Abdulkarim who was selling high grade shabu. Informant relayed that DATU has with him a fair amount of shabu amounting to Php 900,000.00 and needed to be sold within a week. Acting on the information received, NBI-TFAID immediately hatched a buy-bust operation. On January 24, 2022, “DATU” instructed the informant to fetch him together with a companion identified as ASRAP KAMAD KASAN somewhere along Roxas Boulevard, Pasay City for them to proceed to Paliparan III Dasmarinas, Cavite where the alleged contact of DATU will hand over the Php 900,000.00 worth of shabu. After confirming that the box contains illegal drugs, undercover operative handed over to ASRAP the bag with buy-bust money. At this juncture, operatives announced their authority and arrested the Subjects. Seized from the Subjects were six (6) heat-sealed transparent plastic sachets containing white crystalline substance, which upon examination by NBI-Forensic Chemistry Division (NBI-FCD), tested positive for shabu with a net weight of 293.5185 grams. After the booking procedure, it was found out that DATU is a nominee of the Party List Peoples Volunteer Against Illegal Drugs (PVAID). On the other hand, TATO alleged that he is a 17-year-old minor. However, he acted with discernment knowing that he was in possession of shabu. Arrested Subjects were charged for violations of Sections 5 and 11 of RA 9165 (Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002). • On January 25, 2022, operatives of NBI-Central Visayas Regional Office (NBI-CEVRO) arrested MAXIMO BAGUIO MARIOT JR., DOROTEO VALMORIA AUXTERO JR., and BRYAN BURLAOS SACMAR in Talisay City, Cebu for pilferage of electricity. Subjects were arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from the information given by the President COO of Visayan Electric Company (VECO) that certain individuals are taking advantage of the recent calamity (Typhoon Odette) to extort money from consumers who were affected by the said typhoon in exchange for priority electricity repairs and immediate energization. NBI-CEVRO immediately conducted a surveillance operation and was able to confirm that Subject Mariot is demanding money from the consumers of VECO in exchange for immediate restoration of electricity. The operatives were also able to discover that Subject Mariot disregarded safety protocol and would merely connect electricity from any available source. With these, NBI-CEVRO operatives proceeded to Talisay, Cebu and conducted the entrapment operation which resulted in the arrest of the above-mentioned Subjects. Arrested Subjects were charged for violation of R.A. 7832 (Anti-Electricity and Electric Transmission Lines/ Materials Pilferage Act of 1994). • On January 25, 2022, operatives of NBI-Cebu District Office (NBI-CEBDO) arrested CHRISTINELINE DEPAUDHON, MARIA JULIET DUMADAG y LONOP, MYKEL CERIOLA TAN and JESSEL FAITH CATARINEN y BERCEDE for illegal selling of Covid-19 Rapid Test Kits in Mandaue and Cebu City. NBI join hands with the Food and Drugs Administration (FDA) Cebu Field Regional Office and conducted relentless buy bust operations in several establishments, against group of unscrupulous individuals who take advantage of situation. As a result thereof, above-mentioned Subjects were caught red handed on separate occasions by the joint elements of NBI-CEBDO and FDA operatives after receiving marked money for the online sale transaction of 200 boxes of Clungene and Joinstar Covid- 19 Rapid Test Kits with an estimated value of Php 1,000,000.00.
