Further, the arrested Subjects do not have License to Operate violating the provision of the same law under Section 11(k). Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the Inquest Prosecutors of Cebu and Mandaue City. • On January 26, 2022, operatives of NBI-Intellectual Property Rights Division (NBI-IPRD) seized 30 boxes containing 100 pieces of counterfeit Bioflu tablets. Items, with an estimated amount of Php 27,000.00, were seized in an entrapment operation conducted in Marikina City. Charges for violation of RA 8293 (Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines) were filed against JOMAR J. MALLARI. • On January 26, 2022, operatives of NBI-Special Task Force (NBI-STF) arrested TAREK SIAM, a Jordanian national, in Makati City for illegal possession of firearm and violent acts inside a hotel premises. The NBI received a letter complaint from Congressman Anthony Rolando T. Golez, Attorney-in-Fact of Makati Hotel and Residences Condominium Corporation, requesting law enforcement assistance regarding MR. TAREK SIAM who had been violently harassing the employees of a hotel in Makati City and even threatened several security guards of the said establishment with a gun violating election gun ban and the Comprehensive Firearms and Ammunition Regulation Act of 2012. On January 25, 2022, NBI operatives received a phone call from the management of the hotel requesting immediate law enforcement assistance to avert the violent acts being committed by TAREK SIAM inside the hotel premises. As relayed, TAREK SIAM was in possession of a hand gun as he was destroying and breaking the hallway lights of the 22nd floor of the hotel. NBI operatives immediately responded but upon arrival, TAREK SIAM went back inside his room. Meantime, operatives were shown CCTV footages showing that TAREK SIAM was indeed in possession of a firearm and while outside his residence, he loaded his gun. According to the management of the hotel, TAREK SIAM had been brandishing and drawing his gun against any hotel personnel. NBI-STF checked the database of criminal records and found out that there is a Warrant of Arrest issued by the Manila Regional Trial Court Branch 005 against TAREK SIAM for violation of RA 7610 otherwise known as Special Protection of Children Against Abuse, Exploitation, and Discrimination Act. With the Warrant of Arrest at hand, operatives patiently waited for someone from TAREK SIAM’s room to come out, taking into consideration the safety of the hotel residents as TAREK SIAM may react violently using his gun. On January 26, 2022, when a female individual came out of the room, operatives took the opportunity to sneak inside. NBI-STF operatives declared their presence and informed TAREK SIAM of his Warrant of Arrest and placed the Subject under arrest after being apprised of his statutory and constitutional rights. Charges for violation of RA 10591 otherwise known as the Comprehensive Firearms and Ammunition Regulation Act and violation of The Omnibus Election Code were filed against TAREK SIAM before the City Prosecutor, Makati City. • On January 27, 2022, operatives of NBI-Bicol Regional Office (NBI-BRO) arrested CHERRYLAINE BONACUA NUYDA for selling counterfeit Bioflu tablets in violation of RA 8203 (Special Law on Counterfeit Drugs). Subject was arrested in a buy-bust operation conducted at Purok 3, Brgy. 3 EM’s Barrio East, Old Albay, Legazpi City. Seized from the Subject were 100 fake Bioflu tablets and Php1,000 bill marked money. Seized drugs were sent to FDA for product verification. • On January 27, 2022, operatives of NBI-Ilocos Regional Office (NBI-IRO) arrested ADRIAN “RYAN” TUGARINO y TEJADA in Rosales, Pangasinan for illegally selling hybrid seeds. Subject TUGARINO was apprehended in an entrapment operation conducted at the parking lot of a mall in Carmen, Rosales, Pangasinan. He was arrested after receiving the marked money from the poseur-buyer of hybrid seeds that were exclusively researched and produced by complainant Syngenta Philippines, Inc. Syngenta is a leading agricultural company working to provide premium seeds and crop protection innovation to enhance the prosperity of farmers. Seized from Subject TUGARINO were two (2) bags with a total weight of twenty (20) kilos of hybrid seeds. Inquest transmittal was received by the Assistant Prosecutor of Rosales, Pangasinan charging the Subject for violation of RA 8293 (Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines) in relation to Section 6 of RA 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012). Subject is currently detained at NBI-IRO Jail awaiting case resolution. • On January 28, 2022, operatives of NBI-Bohol District Office (NBI-BOHDO) arrested FELIX PANIMDIM y AMONSOT a.k.a. EYET AMONSOT at Purok 6, Bool Dist., Tagbilaran City for illegal gambling in violation of PD 1602 (Anti-Illegal Gambling Law) in relation to Sec. 3(a) of RA 9287 (An Act Increasing the Penalties for Illegal Numbers Game).

body: A con artist posing as a lawyer for a long time finally fell into the hands of the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) during an operation in Mandaluyong City early this week. The NBI identified the suspect as, SENEN JOSE C. DUADICO, 50 years old, a resident of Cordillera St. Mandaluyong City. Investigation disclosed that complainant Rosalind A. Geolagon met suspect Duadico sometime in March 2012 while she was looking for a notary public who could prepare a complaint affidavit. She was considering filing charges against the management of a Mandaluyong City based mall where she owns a stall at its “tiagge section”. Duadico volunteered to represent Geolagon and charged P1,800.00 as filing and notarial fees. However, the lawyer-client relationship turns sour when Duadico failed to produce receipts for the filing fees he collected from complainant despite the latter’s persistence in asking for it. Geolagon became suspicious prompting her to verify with the Supreme Court if Duadico is indeed a lawyer. It turned out that suspect is not a member of the Philippine Bar as certified by the Office of the Bar Confidant of the Supreme Court of the Philippines. Record check conducted revealed that Duadico had been issued warrants of arrest by various courts, and upon verification, it was learned that the same remained standing as suspect have not yet been arrested. The warrants include, 1. Pasig RTC, Br.69 for Indirect Contempt; 2. Quezon City RTC, Br.224 for Direct Contempt; 3. Makati MTC, Br.64 for Estafa and Usurpation of Authority. Subsequently, on June 11, 2012 NBI operatives proceeded to suspect’s office in Mandaluyong City and served the arrest warrant issued by the Pasig City Court. Duadico was brought to the NBI main office where he was booked. He is presently detained at the NBI detention cell. Charges for estafa under Art. 315 of the Revised Penal Code and usurpation of authority under Art.177 of the RPC are readied against Duadico before the Mandaluyong City Prosecutor’s Office.

body: PRESS STATEMENT July 29, 2022 NBI ARRESTS SEVEN FOR ILLEGAL QUARRYING The National Bureau of Investigation-Environmental Crime Division (NBI-EnCD) conducted an entrapment operation in Brgy. Mascap, Rodriguez, Rizal, which resulted in the arrest of BANDO, ALEXANDER y MAGUINDA; AUSTRAL, ROCHELO y PARUCHEL; NAVARRO, RAUL y ROMANO; EPANTO, ALBER y SANDICO; CORNELIA, KENNETH y BICLAR; DEL ROSARIO, BERNY y GARIN; and MALIGAYA, MENARDO y ANDAL. The operation stemmed from information received by NBI-EnCD regarding the alleged rampant illegal mining/quarrying activities in Barangay Mascap, Rodriguez, Rizal. The information revealed that a group of individuals are extracting and disposing minerals without the necessary permit from the Provincial Mining Regulatory Board (PMRB) of the Province of Rizal and the Department of Environment and Natural Resources – Mines and Geosciences Bureau Region IV-A (DENR-MGB Region IV-A). A series of surveillance operations conducted by operatives of NBI-EnCD revealed that there was indeed an ongoing quarrying activity in the target area. Verification made with the DENR-MGB Region IV-A regarding the ongoing quarrying activity disclosed through a Certification that Amiterra Aggregates Corporation (Amiterra) was granted permit to conduct quarrying operation within the area of Barangay Mascap of the same municipality. In addition, an updated list of Quarry Permit Holders and Transport and Hauling Permit Holders in the Province of Rizal provided PMRB-Rizal revealed that Amiterra and their contractor (San Rafael Far Eastern Resources Inc.) were not included on the said list. Thus, on July 26, 2022, NBI-EnCD operatives together with the personnel of DENR-MGB Region IV-A devised a law enforcement operation against the group of individuals behind the illegal quarrying operation in Barangay Mascap, which resulted in the arrest of the above named subjects. The arrested subjects were presented for inquest proceeding before the Office of the Provincial Prosecutor, San Mateo, Rizal for violation of Section 103 of Republic Act No. 7942, otherwise known as the “Philippine Mining Act of 1995.”

body: Agents of the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) rescued eleven (11) victims from an American septuagenarian who recruited them for sexual exploitation and pornography during an entrapment in Tacloban City last week. The suspect was identified as DONALD JACOB NAGEL, 72, a US citizen and a resident of Bgy. 61, Real St., Tacloban City. Investigation conducted by the Eastern Visayas Regional Office (EVRO) in Tacloban City disclosed that the NBI received information that suspect Nagel is keeping several minors at his residence. He reportedly recruited said minors and pimps them for financial gain. The NBI-EVRO conducted surveillance that confirm his activities. In the morning of February 17, 2013, in coordination with the City Social Welfare and Development (CSWD), being members of the Task Force on Trafficking in Persons, the team raided suspect’s residence. The said operation proved fruitful, as ten young boys, five male of whom are minors, five teenagers and a female youngster were found inside the premises. Consequently, Nagel was placed under arrest. It was further learned that the victims were being exploited for sexual and pornographic purposes. Also found inside the suspect’s residence are pornographic materials, computers, cameras and other electronic devices used in the commission of the crime. Nagel presently detained at the NBI-EVRO detention cell. Charges for violation of Article VI, Section 10 paragraph (b), Republic Act No. 7610, otherwise known as the “Special Protection of Children Against Child Abuse, Exploitation and Discrimination Act” and Section 6 paragraph (a) of Republic Act no. 9208 (Qualified Trafficking) were filed against the suspect before the Tacloban City Prosecutor’s Office, the following day February 18, 2013.

body: On July 1, 2020, operatives of NBI-Anti-Organized and Transnational Crime Division (NBI-AOTCD) arrested JINKY B. CANDELARIA, Filipino, and three (3) African nationals namely CHUBUH NGEIBUH FESTUS, LYONGA L. ETIMBE LUMA, and ALEX TONY for Estafa. Subjects were arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from a complaint against them for Black Dollar Scam/Swindling/Estafa. Complainant alleged that the group enticed him to invest money in the production of Black Dollar. The group showed the complainant the process of making US Dollar out of “white paper money”. Subjects took complainant’s investment money purportedly to buy chemicals worth $40,000 equivalent to Php 2 Million but it was never returned. The processed Black Dollar remained unfinished because Subjects did not buy the chemicals. Complainant researched about the Black Dollar in the internet and he realized that the group is a scammer. So when the group called the complainant asking him to invest another Php 3 Million, he reported it to the NBI. Acting on the complaint, the entrapment operation was conducted in Makati City resulting in the arrest of the aforementioned Subjects. Charges for violation of Article 315 of the Revised Penal Code (Estafa) were filed against the Subjects. On July 2, 2020, operatives of NBI-Northeastern Mindanao Regional Office (NBI-NEMRO) arrested RONILO “BABYZEN” SILVERIO ENAL for selling shabu. Subject was arrested in a buy-bust operation in Brgy. Bugo, Cagayan de Oro City which stemmed from an information that Subject is selling shabu in Cagayan de Oro City. Poseur-buyer bought three (3) grams of shabu from the Subject. The City Prosecutor’s Office of Cagayan de Oro charged the Subject with violation of RA 9165 (Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002). On July 2, 2020, operatives of NBI-Environmental Crime Division (NBI-EnCD) arrested DANILO CAPUNO MONTES, GILBERT LAROYA RAMISO, and JOHNEDEL IMPERIAL BONDAD for illegal occupation of forest land in San Felipe, Zambales. NBI-EnCD received a report regarding a group of individuals who were engaged in illegal occupation of parcel land classified as Public Forest Land in Brgy. San Rafael, San Felipe, Zambales. Surveillance conducted yielded positive and operatives were able to verify the existence of the continuing and ongoing unlawful occupation of forest land. Upon verification from DENR-Community Environment and Natural Resources Office (CENRO)-Olongapo, it was found out that the groups of individuals are illegal occupants and have no issued permits or any tenurial instrument from CENRO-Olongapo. On the aforementioned date, the entrapment operation was conducted resulting in the arrest of the above-mentioned Subjects for violation of PD 705 (Revised Forestry Code of the Philippines). Operatives also recovered one (1) Cal.45, Colt in the forest land occupied by Subject DANILO MONTES, in violation of RA 10591 (Comprehensive Firearms and Ammunitions Regulation Act). Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the Provincial Prosecutor’s Office of Zambales. On July 3, 2020, operatives of NBI-Anti-Human Trafficking Division (NBI-AHTRAD) arrested PILLAR TABUCBOC PAROAN, CHERRIE ACOB BARABAD, and ANGELICA ACOB BARABAD for impersonating a Notary Public. Subjects were arrested in entrapment operation which stemmed from a complaint of an individual that someone has been using his notarial services/license without his consent. According to the complainant, he was commissioned as a Notary Public in Quezon City for the year 2019-2020. On February 6, 2020, a man went to their office requesting for a certification of a certain notarial document. Verification with his records show that the same was not entered in his notarial books. Complainant asked the said person where he got the notarized document which the latter said he notarized the document at Biak na Bato, Quezon City. As part of the scheme, Subject, not a member of the Philippine Bar, has been notarizing affidavits and other documents under the name of the complainant. Acting on the said complaint and information, NBI-AHTRAD operatives conducted the entrapment operation resulting in the arrest of the Subjects. The poseur customer asked Subject Pilar if they have notarial services for Affidavit of Loss as poseur-customer’s driver’s license was lost. The latter answered in affirmative and handed over the Affidavit of Loss to Subject CHERRIE who affixed the signature of the complainant in the presence of Subject ANGELICA. The poseur-customer then handed over the payment of Php 200.00 to Subject Pillar. Operatives then declared their authorities and accosted the Subjects. According to Subject Pillar, her boss is MARIA LUISA SANTOS CRUZ, was the one who has been ordering and instructing them to do the notarial services under the complainant’s name. It was further revealed that Subject Cruz is a paralegal of Viron Transit. Arrested Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor, Quezon City for Usurpation of Authority, Falsification of Public Documents, violation of Notarial Practice Law, Counterfeited Insigna, or Notarial Seal, and Estafa. On July 3, 2020, operatives of NBI-Isabela District Office arrested GERRY BUMANGLAG y GALAM for violation of RA 9484. Subject was arrested in entrapment operation conducted at Subject’s dental clinic at Brgy. San Roque, Delfin Albano, Isabela. Subject was brought to NBI-ISDO together with the confiscated pieces of evidence for the standard operating procedures. On July 6, 2020, operatives of NBI-Northeastern Mindanao Regional Office (NBI-NEMRO) arrested RUDY JAMES S. LLAGAS for selling shabu in violation of RA 9165 (Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002). Subject was arrested in a buy-bust operation which stemmed from an information that Subject is selling shabu in Cagayan de Oro City. Poseur-buyer bought five (5) grams of shabu from the Subject and 300 grams of shabu was seized from his possession along with drug paraphernalia. On July 8, 2020, operatives of NBI-Intellectual Property Rights Division (NBI-IPRD) seized two (2) desktop computers and one (1) laptop containing NX Seimens Software with an estimated value of Php 4 Million. Items were seized in Sta. Rosa, Laguna by virtue of Search Warrants. body: PRESS STATEMENT January 07, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } The NBI-National Capital Region (NBI-NCR), under the leadership of NBI Director Judge Jaime B. Santiago (Ret.), filed charges against several individuals for Piracy punished under Article 122 of the Revised Penal Code, as amended by Republic Act No. 7659. Director Santiago said that Hongkong River Engineering Co., Ltd., through its authorized representative, sought the assistance of the NBI to recover their vessel, M/Tug “ASL PROSPER” and to arrest those who illegally seized the said vessel. Sometime in November 2024, PENCON8 Salvage Corporation, a local salvage company, caused the publication of an article in the People’s Journal maliciously claiming that M/Tug “ASL PROPSER” is abandoned and a hazard to navigation. Hongkong River Engineering Co., Ltd. sent a letter to the District Commander of Philippine Coast Gard (PCG) North-Western Luzon, informing him that M/Tug “ASL PROSPER is not abandoned and to be wary of unscrupulous individuals mentioning PENCON8, a local salvage company. Despite such letter, the Sual Pangasinan Station Commander issued an Emergency Salvage Permit in favor of PENCON8. On December 17, 2024, a certain RHINA I FOLLERO, together with ALBERTO C. PLATINO and a certain MARGIE, boarded M/Tug “ASL PROSPER” and threatened the vessel’s watchmen that cases will be filed against them should they refuse to leave the said vessel. Out of fear, the watchmen disembarked from the vessel. On January 3, 2025, an information was received that M/TUG ASL PROSPER was sighted at the Navotas Fishport Complex Pier 4. Inquiry made with the Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) Substation Commander disclosed that M/T MAGILAS, arrived at their port coming from Sual, Pangasinan, has in tow M/T ASL PROSPER. The crew named therein are DANIEL LUSTE and RICARDO PADUA, JR. It was later found that DANIEL LUSTE is connected with Sealoader Shipping Corporation and not from PENCON8. In the midnight of January 4, 2024, the operatives sighted M/TUG ASL PROSPER surreptitiously hidden or covered by a large vessel named SUPER SHUTTLE RORO 12. Noticeable and found onboard M/TUG ASL PROSPER are three (3) individuals later identified as DANIEL JR., LUSTRE y RAGANAS, ELDRINE CHRISTOPHER LASANAS y MAGA and RENE MATADOS y DUPO. When LUSTRE, LASANAS and MATADOS were asked of their legal personalities, they identified their names and mentioned that they were connected with SEALOADER SHIPPING CORPORATION owned by a certain RICARDO T. VELOSO. When asked for any documents to prove their authority to board or to possess M/TUG ASL PROSPER, they could not present any. Since LUSTE, LASANAS and MATADOS are in flagrante delicto committing the crime of Piracy having been in possession of M/TUG ASL PROSPER which vessel was taken against the will of the registered owner thereof and was transferred from Sual, Pangasinan to Navotas Fishport Complex, they were placed under arrest. They were informed of the nature and cause of their arrest for Piracy punishable under Article 122 of the Revised Penal Code, as amended by Rep. Act No. 7659, as well as their constitutional and statutory rights. Considering that M/Tug “ASL PROSPER” was seized against the will or without the consent of the registered owner; the persons who attacked or seized the vessel at the berthing place in PPA Sual Pangasinan are not members of its complement; and the persons who boarded the vessel from Sual Pangasinan to Navotas Fishport are not even connected to PENCON8 but a third-party corporation which is SEALOADER Shipping Corporation, the NBI recommended that the above-mentioned persons, together with several others, including the officers and directors of PENCON8 Salvage Corporation, be charged with and prosecuted for the crime of Piracy punished under Article 122 of the Revised Penal Code, as amended by Republic Act No. 7659.

body: On July 9, 2020, operatives of NBI-Environmental Crime Division (NBI-EnCD0 arrested EUMIR ROMMEL RAGANIT y NOLA and BRUCE KENNETH TAN y ONG for ____. Subjects were arrested in entrapment operation which stemmed from information regarding an alleged illegal trader and possessor of various endangered species such as Hamilton’s Turtle. On the aforementioned date, at Limay St., Tondo, Manila, Subjects were arrested for trading various turtles and tortoise without the necessary permits from the DENR. Recovered from the Subjects’ possession were five (5) Hamilton’s Turtles, marked money and two (2) cellphones, thirty seven (37) pieces consisting of six (6) Diamond-Backed Turtles, three (3) Sulcata, six (6) Hamilton’s Turtles and twenty-two (22) Red –Footed Tortoise. Subjects were presented for violation of RA 9147 (Wildlife Resources Conservation and Protection Act) in relation to RA 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012). On July 9, 2020, operatives of NBI-Eastern Visayas Regional Office (NBI-EVRO) arrested JOSE ESPINOSA JR., for selling unlicensed firearms. Subjects were arrested in a buy-bust operation which stemmed from an information that a certain Jose Espinosa Jr. et. al. were engaged in selling unlicensed firearms. Information has it that Subject already sold firearms to different buyers in the region for several occasions, most of the transactions were said to have been made during elections previously held. A transaction was made with the Subject and poseur-customer bought two (2) .45 caliber pistols. Subject was then placed under arrest after the entrapment money was handed to him. Recovered from the Subject were 2 units .45 caliber pistol, 2 pcs .45 caliber magazine clip, 6 pcs .45 caliber live ammunition, 7 pcs .45 caliber live ammunition, 1 bundle boodle money, and red bag with Nike markings. Charges for violation of RA 10591 (Comprehensive Firearms and Ammunition Regulation Act) were filed against the Subject. On July 10, 2020, operatives of NBI-Cabanatuan District Office (NBI-CABDO) arrested VENUS VILLASIS y PADILLA in an entrapment operation at Del Pilar St., Cabanatuan City, Nueva Ecija. Subject is now detained at the NBI Detention Cell, Cabanatuan City and documents are being prepared for inquest proceedings for violation of RA 9208 (Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2003). On July 14, 2020, operatives of NBI-Cordillera Administrative Region (NBI-CAR), together with PDEA-CAR and PNP CIDG, arrested FEDERICO B. OLIVEROS for selling and using shabu. Subject was arrested in a joint operation which stemmed from a report that a certain FEDERICO B. OLIVEROS a.k.a. FREDERIC a.k.a. ERIC with residential address at San Carlos Heights, Irisan, Baguio City. Allegedly, the latter is engaged in the sale and use of shabu. Upon verification, Subject was inveterate to be a notorious high value target of the PDEA and included in their drug list. Further, Subject was allegedly armed and dangerous, considering that he was possession of several firearms and ammunitions with diverse calibers. Subject’s parents are presently incarcerated at the National Bilibid Prison, Muntinlupa City, for the same offense. After confirming the illicit transaction of the Subject in his house, operatives proceeded to the area and served the Search Warrant. Seized inside the Subject’s house were 50 grams of suspected shabu, 7ml of suspected liquid shabu, one (1) .25 caliber pistol, 29 pieces of .25 caliber ammunitions, and assorted drug paraphernalia. Subject was arrested and presented for inquest procedure. Subject is presently detained at Baguio City Jail. On July 14, 2020, operatives of NBI-Special Action Unit (NBI-SAU) arrested PAUL MICHAEL PADUA IGNACIO, Philippine Sports Commission (PSC) employee, for falsifying the payroll register of the athletes and coaches and credited their allowances into his own bank account. The case stemmed from a letter sent by the PSC seeking assistance for the investigation of suspected fraud committed by a PSC employee. The letter likewise stated that the Landbank of the Philippines sent a letter to the OIC of PSC regarding an unusual payroll transactions credited to the account of Subject Ignacio. Subject Ignacio is the one tasked to prepare the payroll for the monthly allowance of qualified coaches and athletes and forward the same to LBP. Subject Ignacio then includes the names of unqualified coaches and athletes in the payroll and puts his own payroll account number for them. Based on initial verification, Subject has already embezzled Php 14,448,254.35 from August 2015 to May 2020. On the above-mentioned date, NBI-SAU operatives proceeded to the PSC office to conduct investigation. It was discovered that for the month of June 2020, Subject Ignacio included in the payroll three (3) unqualified coaches and three (3) unqualified athletes with a total amount of Php 450,150 to be credited into Subject’s payroll account. With sufficient evidence on hand, Subject Ignacio was placed under arrest. Subject’s laptop and desktop units issued by the PSC were seized for forensic examination. Subject was presented for inquest proceedings for violation of RA 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012) and Article 310 in relation to Article 309 (Qualified Theft) through violation of Article 172 in relation to Article 171 (Falsification of Public Documents) all under the Revised Penal Code. On July 16, 2020, operatives of NBI-Intellectual Property Rights Division (NBI-IPRD) seized counterfeit Vans and Under Armour Shoes with a total estimated amount of Php 51,570,500.00. Items were seized by virtue of Search Warrants issued against John/Jane Does/owners/occupants/proprietors of warehouses located at One Shopping Centre, Pasay City and Harrison Shoe Plaza, Pasay City.

body: PRESS STATEMENT June 19, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } In line with the campaign to stop the proliferation of counterfeit products, the National Bureau of Investigation – National Capital Region (NBI-NCR), under the leadership of Director JUDGE JAIME B. SANTIAGO (Ret.), enforced multiple Search Warrants at various locations in Caloocan, Valenzuela, and Pasay City, for violation of Section 155 (Trademark Infringement), in relation to Section 170 of Republic Act 8293 or the “Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines.” The case stemmed from the complaint filed by LEE BUMGARNER INC. (LBI) on behalf of their client CROCS. On 09 June 2025, the NBI-NCR agents implemented search warrants against seven (7) stores in Pasay City, one (1) warehouse in Valenzuela City, and one (1) warehouse in Caloocan City, resulting in the lawful seizure of Twenty-Six Thousand and Fifty-Seven (26,057) pieces of Assorted counterfeit/fake Products bearing the “Crocs” Trademark, with an estimated value of Seventy-Three Million Eight Hundred Eighty-Eight Thousand Two Hundred and Fifty Pesos (Php 73,888,250.00). The searches were conducted in a peaceful and orderly manner in the presence of the Respondent’s witnesses, Building Representative, and Barangay Representative. Director Santiago lauded the NBI-NCR for successfully implementing said search warrants and their law enforcement actions to stop the proliferation and distribution of counterfeit/fake products. NBI reminds the public to refrain from patronizing pirated products to give protection to the intellectual property rights owners and enhance our economic growth.

body: PRESS STATEMENT May 31, 2022 NBI ARRESTS SUBJECT FOR POSING AS ZCDRRMO OFFICIAL The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today said operatives of NBI-Western Mindanao Regional Office (NBI-WEMRO) arrested an individual for posing as a high-ranking official of Zamboanga City Disaster Risk and Management Office (ZCDRRMO) and recruiting aspiring officers for a fee. NBI Officer-In-Charge (OIC) Director ERIC B. DISTOR identified the Subject as JENNIFER QUEBITE y MOLINA. OIC-Director Distor said the Subject was arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from the complaint of thirteen (13) individuals who alleged that they were victims of fraud by the Subject. In their sworn statements, complainants alleged that they were recruited by the Subject to undergo intensive training to become an officer of ZCDRRMO, on different occasions beginning January to March 2022 in Brgy. Ayala, Zamboanga City. In the recruitment process, Subject invited the complainants to her barracks located at the above-mentioned area where she introduced herself as high-ranking official of ZCDRMMO. Subject also stated that she is the one authorized as “Leader Supervisor” to recruit applicants and supervise them as trainees for three (3) months of intensive training to become a full pledge member of ZCDRMMO. Allegedly, the whole duration of training covers the period of February 2022 to April 2022, which includes physical exercises likened to a military of PNP basic training course where complainants were required to do jogging, push up, squat, and water survival with the main objective of preparing complainants for rescue operation in calamity and disaster. After finishing the said training, they are said to become a member of ZCDRMMO titled as “Medical Officer or Medic” with a promising salary of Php 25,000 to Php 30,000 per month plus weekly allowance of Php 2,000 while on training. This prompted the operatives to conduct the entrapment operation on May 23, 2022, which resulted in the arrest of the Subject. On May 24, 2022, Subject was presented before the Office of the City Prosecutor, Zamboanga City for Inquest proceedings for violation of Article 315 of the Revised Penal Code as amended, committed in a large scale.

NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION

PRESS STATEMENT May 31, 2022 NBI ARRESTS SUBJECT FOR POSING AS ZCDRRMO OFFICIAL The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today said operatives of NBI-Western Mindanao Regional Office (NBI-WEMRO) arrested an individual for posing as a high-ranking official of Zamboanga City Disaster Risk and Management Office (ZCDRRMO) and recruiting aspiring officers for a fee. NBI Officer-In-Charge (OIC) Director ERIC B. DISTOR identified the Subject as JENNIFER QUEBITE y MOLINA. OIC-Director Distor said the Subject was arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from the complaint of thirteen (13) individuals who alleged that they were victims of fraud by the Subject. In their sworn statements, complainants alleged that they were recruited by the Subject to undergo intensive training to become an officer of ZCDRRMO, on different occasions beginning January to March 2022 in Brgy. Ayala, Zamboanga City. In the recruitment process, Subject invited the complainants to her barracks located at the above-mentioned area where she introduced herself as high-ranking official of ZCDRMMO. Subject also stated that she is the one authorized as “Leader Supervisor” to recruit applicants and supervise them as trainees for three (3) months of intensive training to become a full pledge member of ZCDRMMO. To convince the applicants, Subject shows a photo of her with Elmer E. Apolinario, Department Head of ZCDRMMO. Allegedly, the whole duration of training covers the period of February 2022 to April 2022, which includes physical exercises likened to a military of PNP basic training course where complainants were required to do jogging, push up, squat, and water survival with the main objective of preparing complainants for rescue operation in calamity and disaster. After finishing the said training, they are said to become a member of ZCDRMMO titled as “Medical Officer or Medic” with a promising salary of Php 25,000 to Php 30,000 per month plus weekly allowance of Php 2,000 while on training. However, prior to the start of the training, complainants were made to pay a total of Php 10,400 each for uniform, medical kit, personal things. In their desire for a decent job, complainants produced the said amount and gave the same to Subject QUEBITE. Unfortunately, complainants were not given any receipt instead their names were merely listed in the ZCDRMMO attendance sheet. Those who paid early started their training on the last week of January 2022 while others in the month of February and March 2022. On the third week of April 2022, after almost three months of training, complainants began to question the legalities of their training because they observed some irregularities. They confronted the Subject but the latter was evasive until such time that she could no longer reach out causing damage and so much to their anguish. Because of these, complainants decided to have the matter be investigated by NBI-WEMRO. Upon taking cognizance of the complaint, verification was made to ZCDRMMO whether or not Subject is their employee, official, or authorize in any capacity to recruit. In their response, ZCDRMMO issued certification stating that JENNIFER QUEBITE y MOLINA is not connected nor authorized in any capacity to recruit applicants under the Office of the City Disaster Risk Reduction and Management or any Department in the City Government of Zamboanga. This prompted the operatives to conduct the entrapment operation on May 23, 2022, which resulted in the arrest of the Subject. On May 24, 2022, Subject was presented before the Office of the City Prosecutor, Zamboanga City for Inquest proceedings for violation of Article 315 of the Revised Penal Code as amended, committed in a large scale.

title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: The Information Division is pleased to submit herewith the significant cases of the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) for the following aforementioned period as follows: • On August 1, 2017, operatives of NBI-Tagum District Office (NBI-TAGDO) arrested EFREN LIGAN RABINA, ARNAE VALDERAMA LARA, and RICARDO GODIN UY by virtue of Search Warrants. The operation was conducted based on the information received from a reliable source about the Subjects. During the operation, Subjects were caught having a pot session of shabu. Seized from their possession were two (2) heat-sealed transparent plastic sachet containing white crystalline substance believed to be shabu, and other drug paraphernalia. Charges for violation of R.A. 9165 (Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002) were filed against the Subjects. • On August 2, 2017, operatives of NBI-Bohol District Office (NBI-BOHDO) arrested JEFIE MALNEGRO y BARBARONA alias TOKLOY in a buy-bust operation in Tagbilaran City, Bohol. Seized from the Subject were two (2) pieces heat-sealed transparent strip containing white crystalline substance believed to be shabu, used aluminum foil with shabu residue, and other dug paraphernalia. Charges for violation of R.A. 9165 (Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002) were filed against the Subject. • On August 4, 2017, operatives of NBI-Environmental Crime Division arrested JIMMY GONZALES y AQUINO, JESTONI AQUINO y ZAMORA, FRANCIS ALCUISAR y ESQUIVEL, BENEDICT AQUINO y PARUNGAO, ROMMEL GONZALES y AQUINO, JUANITO SANTIAGO y AQUINO, and JOEL ALQUIZAR y ANGELES in a buy bust operation for illegally selling various wildlife species specifically hanging parrots or Colasisi in Quiapo, Manila. Recovered from the Subjects’ possession were various endangered parrots, dove, munia, and sparrows. Certification issued by the DENR-Bidiversity Management Bureau showed that the aforesaid vendors had not been issued a permit to collect, possess, transport and trade wildlife species. Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the Assistant City Prosecutor, Office of the city Prosecutor, Manila for violation of R.A. 9147 otherwise known as Wildlife Resources Conservation and Protection Act of 2001. • On August 7, 2017, NBI-National Capital Region (NBI-NCR) filed charges against ISAIAS PURA y MACAPAGAL for firing a gun at a dog owned by the complainant, Mary Khristine Kate Caasi y Tebigar. According to the complainant, her dog was walking outside their house when the Subject called the complainant and asked if the dog was hers and simultaneously fired shot towards the dog causing its instantaneous death. Subject’s wife screamed to the dog owners that her husband was traumatized with dogs due to previous experience of being bitten. However, the complainant said their dog not have any history of biting or rage to any person. Complainant reported the incident to their Barangay and sought the assistance of the local police but their complaint was rejected since the victim was a dog. She then filed a complaint before the NBI. Subpoena was issued against the Subject but the latter failed to appear on the scheduled hearing and did not cooperate with the investigation. Verification with the PNP-Firearms and Explosives Office disclosed that Subject is a registered gun owner of Armscor Pistol Caliber .45. However, ballistics examination and cross-matching of the bullet taken from the dog’s cadaver and of the said Armscor Pistol Caliber .45 yielded negative results, Thus, it was deduced that Subject used an unlicensed or loose firearm in shooting the dog. Charges for violation of R.A. 8485 (The Animal Welfare Act of 1998) as well as R.A. 10591 (Comprehensive Firearms and Ammunition Regulation Act) were filed against Subject ISAIAS PURA. • On August 8, 2017, operatives of the NBI- Special Task Force (NBI-STF) arrested EDNA BUSAYSAY, ANTHONY APON, and SUSANA VILLACUATRO in an entrapment operation for illegal practice of dentistry, in violation of R.A. 9484 otherwise known as the Dental Act of 2007. The case stemmed from the complaint filed before the NBI-STF by Dr. Mark Villalobos, President of the Philippine Dental Association (PDA). According to Dr. Villalobos, there are two (2) dental laboratories in Commonwealth, Quezon City that are engaged in dental practice. Accordingly, dental practice are limited only to those who have passed the necessary government licensure exam and are given authority to operate by the government. NBI-STF operatives then conducted a surveillance operation to verify the veracity of the allegations and to plan counter actions against the Subjects. Simultaneous entrapment operation on the two (2) reported laboratories, both located in Commonwealth, Quezon City were also conducted resulting in the arrest of the aforementioned Subjects after they performed oral denture impression on the poseur-customers. Charges for violation of R.A. 9484 (Dental Act of 2007) as well as Article 215 (Swindling and Estafa) of the Revised Penal Code were filed against the arrested Subjects. • On August 8, 2017, operatives of NBI-National Capital Region (NBI-NCR) arrested LEONARDO DE LEON JR. for the alleged rape of his step-daughter. Victim’s biological mother sought the assistance of the NBI after she discovered the incident. The minor daughter of the complainant was allegedly molested and rape by the Subject when she was not around because of her day job. When interviewed, victim recounted the rape committed by her step-father. NBI-NCR immediately conducted counter-actions on the matter and proceeded to the victim and complainant’s residence in Olongapo City. During the operation, operatives noticed a .38 caliber 5-shooter revolver with several bullets within the immediate possession of the Subject. When asked about the loose firearm, Subject admitted that it was his but failed to present any license appertaining to the same. Charges for Rape under Article 266-A of the Revised Penal Code in relation to R.A. 7610 (Child Abuse Law) as well as violation of R.A. 10591 (Comprehensive Firearms and Ammunitions Act) were filed against the Subject. • On August 9, 2017, operatives of NBI-Environmental Crime Division (NBI-EnCD) arrested JUN ESATAN y AMANIA, RONULFO PEREZ y SIGUIN, ERVIN TREMOTCHA y ENOC, FLORO DELA FUENTE y CLARITO, ROLLY BELING y PIJAN, TIRSO BELING y PIJAN, LEOMAR JUGARAN y ARAGON, ROLANDO RUSIANA y FREJONES and RICHE LANGIT y BAZAR for illegal fishing. The operation stemmed from an information that several individuals were engaged in unauthorized fishing activities using DANISH SEINE/Modified Danish Seine also locally known as “HULBOT” within the municipal waters of Navotas City. After validating the said information, EnCD operatives proceeded to the area and conducted the operation resulting in the arrest of the aforementioned Subjects. Charges for violation of Republic Act No. 8550 or the Philippine Fisheries Code of 1998 as amended by Republic Act NO. 10654, (An Act to Prevent, Deter and Eliminate Illegal or Unauthorized, Unreported and Unregulated Fishing) were filed against the Subjects. • On August 9, 2017, operatives of NBI-National Capital Region (NBI-NCR) arrested NORBERTO VITANGCOL y ABELLA in Paranaque City by virtue of Warrant of Arrest issued by RTC Branch 45, Manila for Estafa thru Falsification of Public Documents. The arrest of the Subject is based on the letter request of Manuel Bocaling to serve the aforementioned Warrant of Arrest. • On August 13, 2017, operatives of NBI-Dumaguete District Office (NBI-DUMDO) arrested EDUARDO VILLACES DEQUITO and JAMSA ABDURASID BASARA for human trafficking. The case stemmed from the complaint of Edgardo Torres, father of a minor who was enticed by the Subjects for several occasions to engage herself in sexual services for fee ranging from Php 2,000 to Php 3,000 for every customer she will engage into. There were also other minors who were allegedly enticed by the Subjects to do the same. Acting on the complaint, surveillance operations were conducted and on the aforementioned date, the Subjects were arrested in an entrapment operation while negotiating with the victim for the sexual services. Charges for violation of R.A. 9208 ( ) as amended by R.A. 10364 (Qualified Trafficking in Persons) were filed against the arrested Subjects. • On August 14, 2017, operatives of Anti-Fraud Division arrested ENGR. DESIDERIO T. ESTINOZO and NESTOR O. LEHETEMAS for allegedly duping Php 6 Million worth of foreign donations for the victims of super typhoon Yolanda. The case stemmed from a complaint filed by Glenn Bais and Intared Foundation, a Spanish NGO. An agreement that InteRed Foundation (Fundacion InteRed) will provide funding support worth 100,000 Euros (Php 6,000,000.00) to PhilDHRRA project for the repair and rehabilitation of damaged schools, day care and health centers and capacity building interventions in three (3) island barangays in Guiuan, Eastern Samar. Two weeks after the Memorandum of Agreement between the InteRed and PhilDHRRA was signed, no fund transfer was received through the designated bank account of PhilDHRRA. When Mr. Bais sent a message to Ms. Barrueta about the status of the fund transfer, the former was informed that she already made the transfer to the new bank account three (3) days after she received the revised MOA. Mr. Bais, however, told her that he did not send a revised MOA with a new bank account and he did not authorize anybody or other company to receive the fund transfer in their behalf. The email hacker communicated with Ms. Barrueta for an amendment in MOA on the fund transfer agreement from the original bank account of PhilDHRRA in Davao City to Banco de Oro account of DTE Construction and Development Corporation in Cebu City. Investigation was then conducted and a case of Estafa was filed against DTE Corporation, its President, Subject ENGR. ESTINOZO et.al. A Warrant of Arrest was likewise issued by RTC Branch 17, Davao City. Complainants then requested the NBI to serve the Warrant of Arrest. After several months of surveillance, AOTCD operatives arrested the Subjects ENGR. DESIDERIO T. ESTINOZO and NESTOR O. LEHETEMAS, in Malate, Manila. Subjects were brought to the NBI headquarters for the booking procedures. • On August 14, 2017, operatives of NBI-Laguna District Office (NBI-LAGDO) arrested ARTEMIO LOPENA y GUENOBAN, MERLINDA ARGANA y VALENCIA, and TERESITA ASNE for conducting illegal jueteng operations in Muntinlupa City. The operation stemmed from the complaint of Happy Cool Games and Amusement Corporation, the Authorized Agent Corporation (AAC) to operate Small Town Lottery (STL) in Southern District of the National Capital Region, that illegal gambling activities continue to proliferate in the area. Seized from the Subjects during the operation were several pieces of betting list and bet money worth Php 1,961.00. Charges for violation of R.A. 9287 (An Act Increasing the Penalties for Illegal Numbers Games, Amending Certain provisions of P.D. 1602 and for Other Purposes) were filed against the Subjects. • On August 14, 2017, operatives of NBI-Counter Terrorism Division (NBI-CTD) arrested GLENN LAGRITO y MAGBANUA, CHRISTOPHER HERNANDEZ y ESTRELLA, IRENEO GONZALES JR. y GALANG, REYNALDO MATEO y ALBERTO, REY PETALCORIN y GONZALES, ROMEO DOMINGO JR. y SAN PEDRO, and JAIME DEL ROSARIO y PEREZ for illegally selling high-powered firearms. Subjects were arrested in a buy-bust operation conducted in Metro Manila. Seized from the Subjects were different kinds of high-powered firearms. Charges for violation of R.A. 10591 (Comprehensive Firearms and Ammunition Regulation Act) were filed against the Subjects. • On August 14, 2017, operatives of NBI-Central Visayas Regional Office (NBI-CEVRO) arrested LENIELOU DARDOL CALUNOD for Robbery Extortion. The case stemmed from the letter of Atty. Braulio C. Padilla, representing his client Douglas S. Tan, requesting for investigation against the Subject who was allegedly extorting and threatening Mr. Tan. The latter and the Subject knew each other years ago and Mr. Tan supported the Subject financially out of compassion and pity since he found out that Subject’s livelihood is engaging into intimate activities to various men for a fee. Subject got pregnant at the age of 18 and left her parents. When she got pregnant again, she claimed that Mr. Tan is the father of the child. She then demanded huge amount of money from Mr. Tan and the latter refused to give, she resorted to threatening messages and calls. Subject’s demand even went up to Php 20 Million or otherwise, she will go to Complainant’s wife and will ruin his family. The demand and intimidation was constant and persistent, thus an entrapment operation was conducted resulting in the arrest of the Subject. Charges for violation of Article 293 (Robbery Extortion) of the Revised Penal Code in relation to Sec. 6 of R.A. 10175 (Cyber Crime Prevention Act) were filed against the Subject. • On August 17, 2017, operatives of NBI-Special Task Force (NBI-STF) arrested NICKOLE FERNANDEZ AND CHARLENE JOY GONZALES for illegal practice of dentistry. The case stemmed from the complaint of Dr. Jessie Albeus, an officer of the Philippine Dental Association (PDA), who alleged that the two (2) Subjects were engaged in the installation of dental braces without the proper licensed under the law. Accordingly, dental practice is only limited to those who passed the necessary government licensure exam and are given authority by the government. Acting on the complaint, NBI-STF operatives conducted a surveillance operation confirming the veracity of the allegations. An entrapment operation was then conducted resulting in the arrest of the Subjects. Charges for violation of R.A. 9484 (Dental Act of 2007) as well as Swindling and Estafa were filed against the Subjects. • On August 17, 2017, operatives of NBI-Western Mindanao Regional Office (NBI-WEMRO) arrested REYNER R. SIOKO and NICKO A. ATILANO for Robbery and violation of R.A. 9995 (Anti-Photo and Video Voyeurism Act of 2009), R.A. 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012) and R.A. 7610 (Special Protection of Children Against Abuse, Exploitation and Discrimination Act). The case stemmed from the complaint of GLADYS F. SUMAGASAY, mother of JAENNINE F. SUMAGASAY, a minor whose phone was stolen while she was on board a motorcycle. JAENNINE’s friends later on received her nude photos sent via her Facebook account. JAENNINE was then threatened that if they will not give money, all the saved nude photos and videos in her cellphone will be published. Acting on the complaint, an entrapment operation was set resulting in the arrest of the Subjects. Charges for violation of R.A. 9287 (An Act Increasing the Penalties for Illegal Numbers Games, Amending Certain provisions of P.D. 1602 and for Other Purposes) were filed against the Subjects. • On August 18, 2017, operatives of NBI-Environmental Crime Division arrested JEFFERSON CO for violation of R.A. 9147 otherwise known as Wildlife Resources Conservation and Protection Act of 2001. Charges for the above-mentioned violation were filed against the arrested Subject. • On August 18, 2017, operatives of NBI-National Capital Region (NBI-NCR) arrested TEOH WILLIAM, a Malaysian national, for Robbery Extortion, Estafa, Direct Assault, and Resisting Arrest. The complainant asked for the Subject’s passport for assurance, but Subject had also convinced the complainant to give his passport. When complainant was asking for the return of his passport, Subject said that he could only get his passport if he would give an additional Php 200,000.00. Acting on the complaint, the NBI set an entrapment operation. While the Subject was being arrested, he resisted and with force pushed an operative on the face and kicked the latter’s leg. The counterfeit UNILAB products, which has an estimated amount of Php 250,000, were seized on the strength Warrant. NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION

The Information Division is pleased to submit herewith the significant cases of the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) for the following aforementioned period as follows: • On August 1, 2017, operatives of NBI-Tagum District Office (NBI-TAGDO) arrested EFREN LIGAN RABINA, ARNAE VALDERAMA LARA, and RICARDO GODIN UY by virtue of Search Warrants. The operation was conducted based on the information received from a reliable source about the Subjects. During the operation, Subjects were caught having a pot session of shabu. Seized from their possession were two (2) heat-sealed transparent plastic sachet containing white crystalline substance believed to be shabu, and other drug paraphernalia. Charges for violation of R.A. 9165 (Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002) were filed against the Subjects. • On August 2, 2017, operatives of NBI-Bohol District Office (NBI-BOHDO) arrested JEFIE MALNEGRO y BARBARONA alias TOKLOY in a buy-bust operation in Tagbilaran City, Bohol. Seized from the Subject were two (2) pieces heat-sealed transparent strip containing white crystalline substance believed to be shabu, used aluminum foil with shabu residue, and other dug paraphernalia. Charges for violation of R.A. 9165 (Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002) were filed against the Subject. • On August 4, 2017, operatives of NBI-Environmental Crime Division arrested JIMMY GONZALES y AQUINO, JESTONI AQUINO y ZAMORA, FRANCIS ALCUISAR y ESQUIVEL, BENEDICT AQUINO y PARUNGAO, ROMMEL GONZALES y AQUINO, JUANITO SANTIAGO y AQUINO, and JOEL ALQUIZAR y ANGELES in a buy bust operation for illegally selling various wildlife species specifically hanging parrots or Colasisi in Quiapo, Manila. Recovered from the Subjects’ possession were various endangered parrots, dove, munia, and sparrows. Certification issued by the DENR-Bidiversity Management Bureau showed that the aforesaid vendors had not been issued a permit to collect, possess, transport and trade wildlife species. Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the Assistant City Prosecutor, Office of the city Prosecutor, Manila for violation of R.A. 9147 otherwise known as Wildlife Resources Conservation and Protection Act of 2001. • On August 7, 2017, NBI-National Capital Region (NBI-NCR) filed charges against ISAIAS PURA y MACAPAGAL for firing a gun at a dog owned by the complainant, Mary Khristine Kate Caasi y Tebigar. According to the complainant, her dog was walking outside their house when the Subject called the complainant and asked if the dog was hers and simultaneously fired shot towards the dog causing its instantaneous death. Subject’s wife screamed to the dog owners that her husband was traumatized with dogs due to previous experience of being bitten. However, the complainant said their dog not have any history of biting or rage to any person. Complainant reported the incident to their Barangay and sought the assistance of the local police but their complaint was rejected since the victim was a dog. She then filed a complaint before the NBI. Subpoena was issued against the Subject but the latter failed to appear on the scheduled hearing and did not cooperate with the investigation. Verification with the PNP-Firearms and Explosives Office disclosed that Subject is a registered gun owner of Armscor Pistol Caliber .45. However, ballistics examination and cross-matching of the bullet taken from the dog’s cadaver and of the said Armscor Pistol Caliber .45 yielded negative results, Thus, it was deduced that Subject used an unlicensed or loose firearm in shooting the dog. Charges for violation of R.A. 8485 (The Animal Welfare Act of 1998) as well as R.A. 10591 (Comprehensive Firearms and Ammunition Regulation Act) were filed against Subject ISAIAS PURA. • On August 8, 2017, operatives of the NBI- Special Task Force (NBI-STF) arrested EDNA BUSAYSAY, ANTHONY APON, and SUSANA VILLACUATRO in an entrapment operation for illegal practice of dentistry, in violation of R.A. 9484 otherwise known as the Dental Act of 2007. The case stemmed from the complaint filed before the NBI-STF by Dr. Mark Villalobos, President of the Philippine Dental Association (PDA). According to Dr. Villalobos, there are two (2) dental laboratories in Commonwealth, Quezon City that are engaged in dental practice. Accordingly, dental practice are limited only to those who have passed the necessary government licensure exam and are given authority to operate by the government. NBI-STF operatives then conducted a surveillance operation to verify the veracity of the allegations and to plan counter actions against the Subjects. Simultaneous entrapment operation on the two (2) reported laboratories, both located in Commonwealth, Quezon City were also conducted resulting in the arrest of the aforementioned Subjects after they performed oral denture impression on the poseur-customers. Charges for violation of R.A. 9484 (Dental Act of 2007) as well as Article 215 (Swindling and Estafa) of the Revised Penal Code were filed against the arrested Subjects. • On August 8, 2017, operatives of NBI-National Capital Region (NBI-NCR) arrested LEONARDO DE LEON JR. for the alleged rape of his step-daughter. Victim’s biological mother sought the assistance of the NBI after she discovered the incident. The minor daughter of the complainant was allegedly molested and rape by the Subject when she was not around because of her day job. When interviewed, victim recounted the rape committed by her step-father. NBI-NCR immediately conducted counter-actions on the matter and proceeded to the victim and complainant’s residence in Olongapo City. During the operation, operatives noticed a .38 caliber 5-shooter revolver with several bullets within the immediate possession of the Subject. When asked about the loose firearm, Subject admitted that it was his but failed to present any license appertaining to the same. Charges for Rape under Article 266-A of the Revised Penal Code in relation to R.A. 7610 (Child Abuse Law) as well as violation of R.A. 10591 (Comprehensive Firearms and Ammunitions Act) were filed against the Subject. • On August 9, 2017, operatives of NBI-Environmental Crime Division (NBI-EnCD) arrested JUN ESATAN y AMANIA, RONULFO PEREZ y SIGUIN, ERVIN TREMOTCHA y ENOC, FLORO DELA FUENTE y CLARITO, ROLLY BELING y PIJAN, TIRSO BELING y PIJAN, LEOMAR JUGARAN y ARAGON, ROLANDO RUSIANA y FREJONES and RICHE LANGIT y BAZAR for illegal fishing. The operation stemmed from an information that several individuals were engaged in unauthorized fishing activities using DANISH SEINE/Modified Danish Seine also locally known as “HULBOT” within the municipal waters of Navotas City. After validating the said information, EnCD operatives proceeded to the area and conducted the operation resulting in the arrest of the aforementioned Subjects. Charges for violation of Republic Act No. 8550 or the Philippine Fisheries Code of 1998 as amended by Republic Act NO. 10654, (An Act to Prevent, Deter and Eliminate Illegal or Unauthorized, Unreported and Unregulated Fishing) were filed against the Subjects. • On August 9, 2017, operatives of NBI-National Capital Region (NBI-NCR) arrested NORBERTO VITANGCOL y ABELLA in Paranaque City by virtue of Warrant of Arrest issued by RTC Branch 45, Manila for Estafa thru Falsification of Public Documents. The arrest of the Subject is based on the letter request of Manuel Bocaling to serve the aforementioned Warrant of Arrest. • On August 13, 2017, operatives of NBI-Dumaguete District Office (NBI-DUMDO) arrested EDUARDO VILLACES DEQUITO and JAMSA ABDURASID BASARA for human trafficking. The case stemmed from the complaint of Edgardo Torres, father of a minor who was enticed by the Subjects for several occasions to engage herself in sexual services for fee ranging from Php 2,000 to Php 3,000 for every customer she will engage into. There were also other minors who were allegedly enticed by the Subjects to do the same. Acting on the complaint, surveillance operations were conducted and on the aforementioned date, the Subjects were arrested in an entrapment operation while negotiating with the victim for the sexual services. Charges for violation of R.A. 9208 ( ) as amended by R.A. 10364 (Qualified Trafficking in Persons) were filed against the arrested Subjects. • On August 14, 2017, operatives of Anti-Fraud Division arrested ENGR. DESIDERIO T. ESTINOZO and NESTOR O. LEHETEMAS for allegedly duping Php 6 Million worth of foreign donations for the victims of super typhoon Yolanda. The case stemmed from a complaint filed by Glenn Bais and Intared Foundation, a Spanish NGO. An agreement that InteRed Foundation (Fundacion InteRed) will provide funding support worth 100,000 Euros (Php 6,000,000.00) to PhilDHRRA project for the repair and rehabilitation of damaged schools, day care and health centers and capacity building interventions in three (3) island barangays in Guiuan, Eastern Samar. Two weeks after the Memorandum of Agreement between the InteRed and PhilDHRRA was signed, no fund transfer was received through the designated bank account of PhilDHRRA. When Mr. Bais sent a message to Ms. Barrueta about the status of the fund transfer, the former was informed that she already made the transfer to the new bank account three (3) days after she received the revised MOA. Mr. Bais, however, told her that he did not send a revised MOA with a new bank account and he did not authorize anybody or other company to receive the fund transfer in their behalf. The email hacker communicated with Ms. Barrueta for an amendment in MOA on the fund transfer agreement from the original bank account of PhilDHRRA in Davao City to Banco de Oro account of DTE Construction and Development Corporation in Cebu City. Investigation was then conducted and a case of Estafa was filed against DTE Corporation, its President, Subject ENGR. ESTINOZO et.al. A Warrant of Arrest was likewise issued by RTC Branch 17, Davao City. Complainants then requested the NBI to serve the Warrant of Arrest. After several months of surveillance, AOTCD operatives arrested the Subjects ENGR. DESIDERIO T. ESTINOZO and NESTOR O. LEHETEMAS, in Malate, Manila. Subjects were brought to the NBI headquarters for the booking procedures. • On August 14, 2017, operatives of NBI-Laguna District Office (NBI-LAGDO) arrested ARTEMIO LOPENA y GUENOBAN, MERLINDA ARGANA y VALENCIA, and TERESITA ASNE for conducting illegal jueteng operations in Muntinlupa City. The operation stemmed from the complaint of Happy Cool Games and Amusement Corporation, the Authorized Agent Corporation (AAC) to operate Small Town Lottery (STL) in Southern District of the National Capital Region, that illegal gambling activities continue to proliferate in the area. Seized from the Subjects during the operation were several pieces of betting list and bet money worth Php 1,961.00. Charges for violation of R.A. 9287 (An Act Increasing the Penalties for Illegal Numbers Games, Amending Certain provisions of P.D. 1602 and for Other Purposes) were filed against the Subjects. • On August 14, 2017, operatives of NBI-Counter Terrorism Division (NBI-CTD) arrested GLENN LAGRITO y MAGBANUA, CHRISTOPHER HERNANDEZ y ESTRELLA, IRENEO GONZALES JR. y GALANG, REYNALDO MATEO y ALBERTO, REY PETALCORIN y GONZALES, ROMEO DOMINGO JR. y SAN PEDRO, and JAIME DEL ROSARIO y PEREZ for illegally selling high-powered firearms. Subjects were arrested in a buy-bust operation conducted in Metro Manila. Seized from the Subjects were different kinds of high-powered firearms. Charges for violation of R.A. 10591 (Comprehensive Firearms and Ammunition Regulation Act) were filed against the Subjects. • On August 14, 2017, operatives of NBI-Central Visayas Regional Office (NBI-CEVRO) arrested LENIELOU DARDOL CALUNOD for Robbery Extortion. The case stemmed from the letter of Atty. Braulio C. Padilla, representing his client Douglas S. Tan, requesting for investigation against the Subject who was allegedly extorting and threatening Mr. Tan. The latter and the Subject knew each other years ago and Mr. Tan supported the Subject financially out of compassion and pity since he found out that Subject’s livelihood is engaging into intimate activities to various men for a fee. Subject got pregnant at the age of 18 and left her parents. When she got pregnant again, she claimed that Mr. Tan is the father of the child. She then demanded huge amount of money from Mr. Tan and the latter refused to give, she resorted to threatening messages and calls. Subject’s demand even went up to Php 20 Million or otherwise, she will go to Complainant’s wife and will ruin his family. The demand and intimidation was constant and persistent, thus an entrapment operation was conducted resulting in the arrest of the Subject. Charges for violation of Article 293 (Robbery Extortion) of the Revised Penal Code in relation to Sec. 6 of R.A. 10175 (Cyber Crime Prevention Act) were filed against the Subject. • On August 17, 2017, operatives of NBI-Special Task Force (NBI-STF) arrested NICKOLE FERNANDEZ AND CHARLENE JOY GONZALES for illegal practice of dentistry. The case stemmed from the complaint of Dr. Jessie Albeus, an officer of the Philippine Dental Association (PDA), who alleged that the two (2) Subjects were engaged in the installation of dental braces without the proper licensed under the law. Accordingly, dental practice is only limited to those who passed the necessary government licensure exam and are given authority by the government. Acting on the complaint, NBI-STF operatives conducted a surveillance operation confirming the veracity of the allegations. An entrapment operation was then conducted resulting in the arrest of the Subjects. Charges for violation of R.A. 9484 (Dental Act of 2007) as well as Swindling and Estafa were filed against the Subjects. • On August 17, 2017, operatives of NBI-Western Mindanao Regional Office (NBI-WEMRO) arrested REYNER R. SIOKO and NICKO A. ATILANO for Robbery and violation of R.A. 9995 (Anti-Photo and Video Voyeurism Act of 2009), R.A. 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012) and R.A. 7610 (Special Protection of Children Against Abuse, Exploitation and Discrimination Act). The case stemmed from the complaint of GLADYS F. SUMAGASAY, mother of JAENNINE F. SUMAGASAY, a minor whose phone was stolen while she was on board a motorcycle. JAENNINE’s friends later on received her nude photos sent via her Facebook account. JAENNINE was then threatened that if they will not give money, all the saved nude photos and videos in her cellphone will be published. Acting on the complaint, an entrapment operation was set resulting in the arrest of the Subjects. Aside from the stolen cellphone, one (1) transparent sachet containing white crystalline substance suspected to be shabu and drug paraphernalia were found inside Subject REYNER’s room. Charges for the above-mentioned violations were filed against the Subjects before the City Prosecutor of Zamboanga. • On August 17, 2017, operatives of NBI-Laguna District Office (NBI-LAGDO) arrested RUEL MENDOZA y RODRIGUEZ, AGUINALDO PASAY y VEDAÑO, ARJAY TOLEDO y OCAMPO, JEFF SOLOMON y VIDAL, JELLY ABUEDO y GUERRERO, JUANITO ALVISON y LIBOON and BENJAMIN ESPLAGO y CAMDO for conducting illegal jueteng operations in Muntinlupa City. The operation was conducted based on the complaint of Hon. Jose Jorge C. Corpuz of Philippine Charity Sweepstake Office (PCSO). Seized from the Subjects were several pieces of betting list, jueteng paraphernalia and bet money. Charges for violation of R.A. 9287 (An Act Increasing the Penalties for Illegal Numbers Games, Amending Certain provisions of P.D. 1602 and for Other Purposes) were filed against the Subjects. • On August 18, 2017, operatives of NBI-Environmental Crime Division arrested JEFFERSON CO for violation of R.A. 9147 otherwise known as Wildlife Resources Conservation and Protection Act of 2001. On the aforementioned date, ENCD operatives, together with the personnel from Department of Environment and Natural Resources-Biodiversity Management Bureau (DENR-BMB) Enforcement Division, implemented the Search Warrant issued by the RTC Branch 40, Dagupan City, Pangasinan, resulting in the seizure of endangered species including a pair of albino Burmese phyton, one (1) aldabra tortoise, one (1) black emys tortoise, two (2) sulcate tortoise, and four (4) red foot tortoise. Charges for the above-mentioned violation were filed against the arrested Subject. • On August 18, 2017, operatives of NBI-National Capital Region (NBI-NCR) arrested TEOH WILLIAM, a Malaysian national, for Robbery Extortion, Estafa, Direct Assault, and Resisting Arrest. The case stemmed from the complaint of Ingeol Lim, a Korean national, who alleged that Subject made him believe that a fund transfer of 100,000 USD was made by the Subject from Malaysia to the Philippines. Complainant was convinced by the Subject so when they met, he gave the Subject Php 1.3 Million as partial compliance to the total amount of Php 5 Million. The complainant asked for the Subject’s passport for assurance, but Subject had also convinced the complainant to give his passport. When complainant was asking for the return of his passport, Subject said that he could only get his passport if he would give an additional Php 200,000.00. Acting on the complaint, the NBI set an entrapment operation. While the Subject was being arrested, he resisted and with force pushed an operative on the face and kicked the latter’s leg. It took some time to bring the Subject to the car because he kept on resisting. The operatives were left with no choice but to drag him forcefully to the car to be bought to the NBI-NCR. Subject was thereafter presented for inquest before the Office of the City Prosecutor, Pasay City. • On August 18, 2017, operatives of NBI-Intellectual Property Rights Division (NBI-IPRD) seized 198 pairs of counterfeit Lacoste slippers with an estimated amount of Php 396,000. in Malabon and Pasay City. The fake items were seized on the strength of Search Warrants issued by RTC Branch 24, Manila. Charges for violation of R.A. 8293 (Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines) were filed against the owners/tenants/occupants of certain warehouses and shopping centers in Malabon and Pasay City. • On August 23, 2017, operatives of NBI-Laguna District Office (NBI-LAGDO) arrested OSCAR SENOBIO y PAJARES, RONALD GRAFE y BRAZIL, CYRIL SEXIONA y DAVID, REYNALDO CREBILLO y AGNILA, DANILO ROBEDILLO y LORETO, and JOSEPH CAMPOS y DOLOURES for conducting illegal jueteng operations. Subjects were arrested in an entrapment operation in Paranaque City. Seized from their possession are several pieces of betting list, jueteng paraphernalia, and bet money. Charges for violation of R.A. 9287 (An Act Increasing the Penalties for Illegal Numbers Games, Amending Certain provisions of P.D. 1602 and for Other Purposes) were filed against the Subjects before the City Prosecutor of Paranaque. • On August 24, 2017, operatives of Central Mindanao Regional Office (CEMRO) arrested ROY DEIMOY y LOPEZ a.k.a. BALONG DELA PEÑA for violation of R.A. 9165 (Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002) and violation of R.A. 7610 (An Act Providing for Stronger Deterrence and Special Protection against Child Abuse, Exploitation and Discrimination, providing penalties for its violation and for other purposes). Based on the information received by the NBI from a reliable source, Subject was engaged in rampant sale of dangerous drugs, marijuana. Furthermore, he uses his children in selling marijuana, targeting students as their clients. Subject’s children were also ordered to pack the marijuana for sale. Subject was arrested on the strength of Search Warrant issued by RTC Branch 35, City of General Santos. Seized from the Subject were Marijuana, motorcycle used in transporting the illegal drug, and more or less Php 200,000 cash. Meanwhile, two (2) minors namely RIZLLYOD O. ABOJADO and BERNARD B. MANSUARA who served as witness against the Subject were turned over to DSWD. • On August 24, 2017, operatives of NBI-National Capital Region (NBI-NCR) arrested CHARLIE F. GERCAN, VENUS CEPEDA, KATHERINE V. LAROGA, ARLOU FALCON GERCAN, ETHELINDA CASTILLO, and ALONA ESPERA DOTON in an entrapment operation for defrauding several applicants for employment in Dubai. Subjects, through false pretenses and without valid license or authority required by law to enable them to engage in the recruitment and placement of workers, falsely pretended to possess power and ability to recruit victims for overseas employment for a fee. Charges for Syndicated and Large Scale Illegal Recruitment/Estafa were filed against the Subjects. • On August 25, 2017, operatives of NBI-Laguna District Office (NBI-LAGDO) arrested EDGARDO VILLANUEVA y CAGUBAT, LUZVIMINDA PACETE y MEDINA, LEONILA PUMAREJOS SR. y NIDOY, SUSANA VITOCRUZ y NUÑEZ, and JONAS DANOSO y TRAIN for conducting illegal jueteng operations in Las Piñas City. The operation stemmed from the request of PCSO Chairman, Jose Jorge C. Corpuz, to Secretary of Justice to curb illegal gambling and the complaint of Happy Cool Games and Amusement Corporation, the Authorized Agent Corporation (AAC) that operates Small Town Lottery in Southern District of National Capital Region, that illegal number game (jueteng) still proliferates and remained unabated in Las Piñas City. Charges for violation of R.A. 9287 (An Act Increasing the Penalties for Illegal Numbers Games, Amending Certain provisions of P.D. 1602 and for Other Purposes) were filed against the Subjects. • On August 29, 2017, operatives of NBI-Anti-Organized and Transnational Crime Division (NBI-AOTCD) arrested GIAN DENVER COLORADO y POBLETE, by virtue of Warrant of Arrest issued by the RTC Branch 26, Manila for two (2) counts of Qualified Theft with No Bail recommended. Subject was a former liaison officer/messenger of a brokerage firm in Intramuros, Manila managed by the Complainant Jennifer Ann M. Reyes. Subject is presently detained at the NBI detention cell. • In five (5) successive operations, operatives of NBI-National Capital Region (NBI-NCR) seized several counterfeit products with an aggregate amount of Php 49,189,000.00. On August 1, 2017, operatives of NBI-National Capital Region seized 6,742 pieces of counterfeit The North Face bags with an estimated amount of Php 20 Million in Pasay City. The case stemmed from the complaint of The North Face Apparel Corp. represented by Betita Cabilao Casuela Sarmiento Law Firm. The counterfeit items were seized on the strength of Search Warrants. Charges for violation of R.A. 8293 (Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines) were filed against E.S. Ebolin General Merchandise et.al. On August 8, 2017, operatives of NBI-National Capital Region seized counterfeit VANS products with an estimated amount of Php 1,939,000.00 in Pasay City and Binondo, Manila. The counterfeit items were seized on the strength of Search Warrants issued by RTC Branch 46, Manila. The operation stemmed from the letter complaint of Lee Bumgarner Inc. (LBI) requesting, on behalf of their client VANS, investigation and enforcement actions to stop the proliferation and distribution of fake VANS products in Metro Manila. Charges for violation of R.A. 8293 (Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines) were filed against the owners/managers/operators/occupants/lessees of various stalls/stores in different shopping malls in Binondo, Manila and Baclaran, Pasay City. On August 14, 2017, operatives of NBI-National Capital Region (NBI-NCR) seized counterfeit Safeguard and Silka soaps in Binondo, Manila and Pasay City. The fake items were seized on the strength of Search Warrants issued by RTC Branch 24, Manila. The case stemmed from the complaint of Lee Bumgarner Inc. (LBI) requesting in behalf of their client, Procter and Gamble “P&G” and Cosmetique Asia Corp, investigation and enforcement actions to stop the proliferation and distribution of fake Safeguard and Silka products in Metro Manila. Charges for violation of R.A. 8293 (Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines) were filed against the owners/managers/operators/occupants/lessees of various stores and stalls of different shopping malls in Binondo, Manila and Pasay City. On August 15, 2017, operatives of NBI-National Capital Region (NBI-NCR) seized 849 pieces of counterfeit tablets/capsules of drug products bearing without authority the registered marks and the same containers or a dominant feature thereof owned by UNILAB INC. The counterfeit UNILAB products, which has an estimated amount of Php 250,000, were seized on the strength Warrant. Charges for violation of R.A. 8293 (Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines) were filed against CATHERINE S. TOLENTINO/NEW HARVEST DRUG/NEW HARVEST DRUG AND MERCHANDISE. On August 25, 2017, operatives of NBI- National Capital Region (NBI-NCR) seized a total of Php 27 Million worth of counterfeit Nike footwear in an operation in Teresa, Rizal Province. The operation, which stemmed from the complaint of I-Data Consolidators that represented Nike, resulted in the seizure of twenty-two thousand six hundred eighty nine (22,689) pieces of assorted counterfeit footwear apparels bearing replicas and unauthorized representations/reproductions of Nike design trademark and logo. Charges for Violation of R.A. 8293 (Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines) were filed against CESAR MIRANDA ONG and others.

body: PRESS STATEMENT August 07, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } PRESS RELEASE | APAT NA MENOR DE EDAD INILIGTAS NG NBI SA VALENZUELA Pasay City, Pilipinas – Noong Hulyo 28, 2026, nailigtas ng National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Cybercrime Division ang apat na menor de edad sa Valenzuela City matapos ang pagbabanta, gamit ang isang pekeng social media account, na papatayin ang kanilang guro at ang anak nito. Nagsimula ang operasyon mula sa reklamo ng isang guro, na nagsabing nakatanggap siya ng banta ng kamatayan sa kanyang social media account. Ayon sa reklamo, ang sender, gamit ang isang pekeng account, ay nagsabing saksakin at babarilin siya sa ulo, sasaktan ang kanyang anak, at ilalagay ang kanyang hiniwang katawan sa isang drum. Agad na nagsagawa ang mga operatiba ng NBI-CCD ng cyber investigation na matukoy ang mga nasa likod ng pekeng account. Natuklasan ng mga ahente na ang pekeng account ay nilikha at pinapangasiwaan ng apat na menor de edad. Dahil dito, nakipag-ugnayan ang mga ahente ng NBI-CCD sa Valenzuela Social Welfare Development Office (CSWDO). Noong Hulyo 28, 2026, nagsagawa ang NBI-CCD, kasama ang Valenzuela CSWDO at sa tulong ng NBI-HTRAD at mga Digital Forensic Officers, ng operasyon na nagresulta sa pagliligtas sa 4 na menor de edad. Sa panayam, naibunyag ng mga menor de edad na ang pagbabanta ay nag-ugat sa matinding pagkamuhi sa kanilang guro. Ibinunyag din ng pinuno ng apat na menor de edad na may koneksyon siya sa isang lokal na gang. Nadiskubre rin na ang isa sa mga nakababatang kapatid ay miyembro ng nasabing gang, at madalas siyang makipag-ugnayan dito sa isang popular na online game para sa mga bata na tinatawag na Roblox. Ipinasok ang kustodiya ng apat na menor de edad sa Valenzuela City Child Protection Center para sa mas malalim na panayam at angkop na intervensyon. Ipinahayag ni NBI Direktor Melvin Matibag ang kanyang pagkabahala sa tumataas na bilang ng mga krimeng kinasasangkutan ang mga menor de edad. Binigyang-diin niya na ang NBI ay hindi titigil sa kanilang mandato na iligtas ang mga menor de edad sa pang-aabuso o nasasangkot sa ilegal na gawain. https://www.facebook.com/reel/1018623147875704
