body: The Information Division is pleased to submit herewith the significant cases of the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) for the following afore-mentioned period as follows: On July 7, 2017 , operatives of the NBI- Special Task Force (NBI – STF) arrested ROSALIE ANN SAYSON for Estafa and Illegal Recruitment, in Cainta, Rizal. The operation stemmed from a complaint of two (2) individuals who appeared before the NBI. Upon record check with the NBI-Identification and Records Division (NBI-IRD) on Subject SAYSON, it was disclosed that Subject SAYSON has several Warrants of Arrest issued by the RTC of Manila for Estafa and Illegal Recruitment. Upon verification with the RTC of Manila, the said Warrants of Arrest are outstanding and a certification to that effect was issued by the court. On the above-mentioned date, after receiving an information that the Subject was seen at her residence in Cainta, Rizal, NBI-STF operatives immediately proceeded to the area confirming the presence of the Subject. Coordination with Barangay officials was made and the Warrants of Arrest were served to the Subject. Subject SAYSON was then brought to the NBI-STF for booking procedures and was turned over to the NBI Detention Center. On July 8, 2017 , operatives of NBI-National Capital Region (NBI-NCR) arrested JARMAIDA PULALON, JEZTHER FLOYD DE GUZMAN y LUNOD, AARON ARVIN ESCASENAS y FAUSTINO, RUDOLF VALENTINO ABELLO y BLAS, RHEA GERONIMO, and ALVIN M. YTABLE for Qualified Theft. The case stemmed from the letter of Atty. Marissa T. Academia, Vice President, Legal Affairs, MELCO RESORTS LEISURE CORPORATION, requesting investigation of Subject PULALON, who is one of their dealers assigned at the City of Dreams Casino, Paranaque City, was illegally conniving with her above-named co-conspirators. Investigation conducted revealed that Subject PULALON was deliberately overpaying, on several occasions, her co-conspirators DE GUZMAN, ESCASENAS, ABELLO, and GERONIMO and placing bets on the gaming table after the winning cards in games of Baccarat had been revealed, to make it appear that her co-conspirators had placed winning bets at the beginning of the game. Surveillance operations conducted revealed the Subjects’ fraudulent activities which caused losses in the company in the total amount of Php 220,000.00. After confirming that Subjects were engaged in the illegal activity in the casino, they were immediately apprehended and brought to the NBI for the booking procedures. Confiscated from Subject ABELLO were four (4) Php 10,000.00 COD chips, six (6) Php 1,000.00 chips, seven (7) Php 100.00 chips, and two (2) Php 25.00 chips. On the other hand, confiscated from Subject ESCASENAS were eight (8) Php 1,000.00 chips and seized from Subject GERONIMO was Php 71,000.00 cash. Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the Prosecutor Office, Paranaque City. On July 11, 2017 , operatives of NBI-Special Task Force (NBI-STF) arrested BENJIE SUMIDO y BRANZUELA for Estafa and Illegal Recruitment. The case stemmed from the complaint of Dennis V. Diaz against Subjects BENJIE SUMIDO y BRANZUELA, LEAH IRENE HARASAWA, RONALD A. MARTIN, GARY O. ANTONIO, and LUCY ANTONIO MARTIN. According to the Complainant, Subjects conspired with one another in making him believe that he can have a stable employment in Japan with a monthly salary of Php 175,000.00, exclusive of overtime pay. Subjects demanded several payments from Complainant that amounted to a total of Php 172,500.00, but despite repeated promises, Complainant was not sent abroad. Complainant then decided to file a complaint to NBI-STF. Verification with the Philippine Overseas Employment Administration (POEA) revealed that no one among the Subjects was issued a license or authority to recruit for employment abroad. Certification from the POEA was issued certifying the absence of any issued license of the Subjects. Subsequently, an entrapment operation was conducted in Las Piñas City resulting in the arrest of Subject BENJIE SUMIDO. Subject SUMIDO’s cohorts, LEAH IRENE HARASAWA, RONALD A. MARTIN, GARY O. ANTONIO, and LUCY ANTONIO MARTIN remain at large as they were able to evade arrest. Subject SUMIDO was brought to NBI-STF for the booking procedures and was brought to the National Prosecution Office Services of the Department of Justice (DOJ) for inquest proceedings. Charges for violation of R.A. 8042 (Migrant Workers Act of 1995) and violation of Article 315 (Estafa) of the Revised Penal Code were filed against the at large Subjects. On July 12, 2017 , NBI-Cybercrime Division (NBI-CCD) filed charges against DANIEL ANGELO NOBLEZA SALASALAN for falsely claiming that he had been credited with more than Php 12 Billion which was allegedly reduced to Php 8 Million after BPI experienced from electronic data processing glitch or error. Subject SALASALAN posted on his Facebook account a “cropped out” picture of a BPI Express Online page showing that he has an alleged balance of Php 12,435,323,567.04 and a similarly cropped BPI ATM terminal showing an alleged balance of Php 8,121,791.59. Subject was interviewed by several media outlets wherein he claimed that his account balance ballooned to Php 12,435,323,567.04. Subsequently, Norman Simon M. Tiongco, Assistant Manager of BPI, claimed that based on the investigation conducted by the Cyber Security Operations Center (CSOC) the pictures shared by the Subject were not his own BPI account but were merely fabricated. Thereafter, Subject was subpoenaed to give his side of the complaint. He appeared and submitted his hand written letter addressed to the BPI Executive Vice President Ramon Jocson and President Consing wherein he admitted that his claims were all false and he asked for forgiveness for making such false claims. He also promised to cooperate with the probe and to submit his affidavit. With this, Subject was held liable for online libel and falsification. Criminal complaints for Falsification by Private Individuals and Use of Falsified Documents under paragraph 1 of Article 172 of the Revised Penal Code in relation to paragraph 6 of Article 171 of the same code, as well as Cyber-Libel of R.A. 10175 in relation to Article 355 of the Revised Penal Code were filed against Subject DANIEL ANGELO NOBLEZA SALASALAN. On July 12, 2017 , operatives of NBI-Northeastern Mindanao Reginal Office (NBI-NEMRO) apprehended BENJAMIN “NONONG” SALUSAD , a long wanted notorious fugitive. Subject SALUSAD, a former Kumander of the New People’s Army (NPA) based in San Fernando, Bukidnon, voluntarily surrendered to the Philippine Army sometime in November 2011. Subject’s son, ALDE “BUTSOY” SALUSAD, a commander of an armed group not affiliated with NPA, maintained close ties with his father and together they gained notoriety when they enjoyed the protection of the Philippine Army to the extent that they perpetrated a series of murder in their area without fear of being apprehended because they presumed they were backed up by the military. Until on July 12, 2017, a civilian informant disclosed that Subject BENJAMIN SALUSAD was wounded as he and his comrades were ambushed by CPP/NPA in Barangay Dau, San Fernando, Bukidnon. After coordination with the Philippine National Police (PNP), Subject was confirmed to have been confined at Valencia Sanitarium Hospital/Adventist Medical Center located in Brgy. Poblacion, Valencia City. All the Warrant of Arrest were then duly served upon the Subject inside the hospital. It was found out that Subject BENJAMIN SALUSAD used the alias name “RONALD VALLERO” to hide his real identity and to evade the law enforcement authorities. Proper documentation and booking was made upon the Subject. A heightened security in the hospital premises was implemented due to the serious threats that Subject will be rescued by the armed men led by his son ALDE “BUTSOY” SALUSAD. On July 13, 2017 , operatives of NBI-Naga District Office (NBI-NADO, together with the elements of DENR-V conducted forest protection activity at Brgy. San Isidro Norte, Lagonoy, Camarines Sur resulting in the seizure of illegal logs, lumbers, and flitches of Narra, PMG, and other premium tree species, along with semi-furnished furniture items with a total volume of 2,534.93 board feet inside the unregistered furniture shop of certain ELADIO OLIVER now being operated by his son, DANISIE OLIVER y ASIDO. Subject was placed under further investigation of DENR for proper disposition and filing of necessary case in violation of Section 77 of PD 7095, as amended. On July 14, 2017 , operatives of NBI-Environmental Crime Division (NBI-ENCD) arrested JHEUSUL PARAS and ALPIE JUN JUGUILON for violation of R.A. 9147 (Wildlife Resources Conservation and Protection Act of 2001). The case stemmed from the request of Biodiversity Management Bureau based on the information received from United States Fisheries and Wildlife Service (USFWS), to investigate the rampant illegal shipment of reptiles from the Philippines to the United States using the different services of different courier company like FEDEX. Sometime in December 2016, a package containing six (6) pieces of monitor lizards concealed in a Xenon brand speakers, was confiscated by the Bureau of Customs (BOC). It was shipped by a certain HARVEY SALVADOR from Cebu City to CARIDAD CEMEDO of Massachusetts, USA. Based on the investigation and information received, a certain ALPIE JUN JUGUILON and JHEUSUL PARAS were the ones responsible for shipping reptiles to the United States. Surveillance was conducted and Subjects’ location was located. By virtue of Search Warrants issued by Judge Gernerosa G. Labra of RTC Branch 23, Cebu City, threatened and non-threatened wildlife species were seized and Subjects JUGUILON and PARAS were arrested. They were presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor, Cebu City. On July 16, 2017 , operatives of NBI-Special Action Unit (NBI-SAU) arrested ANALYN DUCUSIN for large scale illegal recruitment. The case stemmed from about ninety-five (95) complainants who filed their complaints before the NBI. The victims filed their complaints against Subject DUCUSIN, MARIA THERESA BUMATAY BARUELO alias “MARIA TERESITA BARUELO, MARIA TERESA BUMATAY BURUELO, MA. THERESA BORUELO, MARITES FORES FRIO alias “TESS”, YOLANDA CABINTOY, and unidentified cohorts. According to the complainants, aforementioned Subjects recruited them for overseas employment with them paying Php 31,000 and Php 38,000 respectively for the process of their visa applications as well as other documents for work abroad. However, after several months, Subjects failed to deliver their promises and despite repeated demands, Subjects refused to return the complainants’ money, prompting the victims to file their complaints before the NBI. When the NBI received a call that Subject DUCUSIN had asked to meet with the complainants for another payment of Php 40,000, an entrapment operation was conducted resulting in the arrest of Subject DUCUSIN. Subjects ANALYN DUCUSIN, as well as the other subjects MARIA THERESA BUMATAY BARUELO alias “MARIA TERESITA BARUELO, MARIA TERESA BUMATAY BURUELO and MA. THERESA BORUELO, MARITES FORES FRIO alias “TESS”, YOLANDA CABINTOY , and JOHN and JANE DOES shall be prosecuted for Illegal Recruitment as Committed by a Syndicate and In Large Scale/Involving Economic Sabotage, as defined and penalized under R.A. 8042 (Migrant Workers and Overseas Filipinos Act of 1995), as amended by R.A. 10022 as well as Estafa, as defined and penalized under Article 315 (2) (a) of the Revised Penal Code, as amended. On July 18, 2017 , operatives of NBI-Anti-Fraud Division (NBI-AFD) arrested VICTORIA “Marivic” S. LOPEZ, Head of Metrobank’s Corporate Service Management Division, for alleged qualified theft. The operation stemmed from a complaint of Jose L. Ballesteros, Head of the Department of Internal Affairs-Investigation Section and authorized representative of Metrobank against the Subject for alleged qualified theft, falsification and violation of the General Banking Law. The official said that he noticed several irregularities in the letter request concerning a loan transaction of a client being facilitated by the Subject. Verification with the client disclosed that they were not aware of the letter request and even the account from which the Manager’s Check was supposed to be debited. Further investigation revealed that bank supposedly issued a loan in favor of the client covered by a fictitious promissory note. It is also revealed that Subject LOPEZ uses the account to facilitate fictitious loans. Acting on the said information, an entrapment operation was set up. As soon as Subject LOPEZ gave instructions to debit the amount of Php 2,250,000.00 from the client’s savings account, the bank issued a debit memo to the Subject as evidence of the processing of transaction. Thereafter, right after an official of the bank got confirmation that client is not aware of the loan transaction, Subject LOPEZ was arrested. She was then presented for inquest proceedings at the Makati City Prosecutor’s Office on July 18, 2017. On July 21, 2017 , operatives of NBI-Special Task Force (NBI-STF) arrested LEONARDO NICOLAS , Sr. Graft Investigator in the Office of the Ombudsman, and his cousin ISAGANI NICOLAS , Labor Arbiter in the National Labor Relations Commission, for extortion activities in Lingayen, Pangasinan. The case stemmed from a complaint filed by Amado T. Espino Jr. against Subject LEONARDO NICOLAS for violations of Article 210 of the Revised Penal Code (Direct Bribery), violation of Article 293 of the Revised Penal Code (Robbery Extortion) and violation of Section 7(d) in relation to Section 11 of R.A. 6713 otherwise known as “The Code of Conduct and Ethical Standards for Public Officials and Employees. Sometime in May, Subject Nicolas had been calling the Provincial Legal Officer and Provincial Accountant of Pangasinan demanding sums of money for the dismissal of cases filed against Congressman Espino and his son, Jumel Espino (Bugallon, Pangasinan Municipal Mayor) in the Office of the Ombudsman. When Mayor Jumel Espino and Atty. Geraldine Baniqued met with Subject Nicolas, the latter demanded that the case may be settled if the Mayor will pay at least Php1,350,000.00 which he firmly rejected. On the other hand, Subject NICOLAS demanded Php 3,000,000.00 for the three (3) pending cases against Congressman Espino Jr. in exchange for the resolution of the cases from the Office of the Ombudsman. When Mr. Soriano received a call from Subject NICOLAS reiterating his threat that the complaint against Mayor Jumel Espino and Congressman Amado Espino Jr. will be docketed and that Mayor Espino will be suspended, they sought the assistance of the NBI. Thereafter, in coordination with the Office of the Ombudsman, an entrapment operation was conducted resulting in the arrest of the two Subjects. On July 21, 2017 , operatives of NBI-Task Force Against Illegal Drugs (NBI-TFAID) seized more than ten (10) kilos of illegal drugs with an estimated street value of Php 60 Million . The operation stemmed from a letter from the Bureau of Corrections requesting the assistance of NBI in the arrest of a group that is allegedly involved in large scale selling of drugs in South of Metro Manila. After coordination with the BuCor officials, NBI-TFAID implemented counter action against the said group. During the operation, operatives only found an abandoned vehicle parked along the sidewalk in Ermita, Manila. Found inside the vehicle is one (1) bag containing crystalline substances which tested positive for the presence of Dimethoxy Methylphenethylamine. On July 27, 2017 , operatives of NBI-Anti-Human Trafficking Division (NBI-AHTRAD) arrested GLADY DULOT y EUGENIO and CHERRY ANN LASCANO y BATITIS for human trafficking. Subjects were arrested in an operation in Caloocan City which stemmed from information that a group composed of several pimps (bugaw) were offering young girls for sexual services. NBI-AHTRAD operatives immediately arranged a meet up with the pimps to verify the information which was later confirmed. The pimps were asking for Php 6,000 for every girl that would be chosen while those who are not chosen would be given consolation of Php 1,000. On the above-mentioned date, an entrapment operation was conducted resulting in the arrest of Subjects DULOT and LASCANO. Subjects brought seventeen (17) minor girls to a private resort in Caloocan City, the eldest of which is seventeen (17) years old and the youngest is thirteen (13). Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the Department of Justice (DOJ) for violations of R.A. 9208 (Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act, as amended) and R.A. 7610 (Anti-Child Abuse Law). Follow up investigation will be conducted to identify and possibly apprehend/charge other members of the group. In five (5) successive operations, operatives of NBI-National Capital Region (NBI-NCR) seized several counterfeit products with an aggregate amount of Php 114,878,002 . On July 5, 2017 , operatives seized counterfeit Under Armour products with an estimated amount of Php 14,988,850.00. The operation stemmed from the complaint of LEE BUMGARNER INC., in behalf of their clients, requesting investigation and enforcement actions to stop the proliferation and distribution of fake Under Armour products in Metro Manila. The fake items were seized in various stores in Baclaran Terminal Mall, Taft Avenue Extension, Pasay City, on the strength of Search Warrants issued by Judge Rainelda H. Estacio-Montesa of RTC Branch 46, Manila. Charges for violation of R.A. 8293 (Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines) were filed against John/Jane Doe and owners/managers/occupants/lessees of various stores in Baclaran Terminal Mall. On July 7, 2017 , 22,223 pairs of counterfeit Nike and Converse footwear with an estimated market value of Php 66,700,000.00 were seized by IPRD operatives. The operation stemmed from the letter –complaint of Mr. Jaime S. Dela Cruz of I-Data Consolidators Inc., requesting the Bureau’s assistance in stopping the rampant illegal importation, distribution, and sale of counterfeit Nike and Converse products. Counterfeit items were seized on the strength of Search Warrants issued by Judge Maria Victoria A. Soriano-Villadolid of RTC Branch 24, Manila. Charges for violation of R.A. 8293 were filed against Subjects JOAN CO a.k.a. XU BI LIAN, CELINE GO, JASON XU, NIKKI XU, owners/managers/occupants/lessees of several units in F.B.Harrison Street, Pasay City. On July 11, 2017 , 64,667 pieces of counterfeit Safeguard and Silka soaps in plastic sachets with an estimated total amount of Php 1,239,152.00 were seized in Sta. Cruz and Binondo, Manila. The case stemmed from a letter complaint filed by Lee Bumgarner Inc. (LBI), on behalf of their clients, Procter and Gamble (P&G) and Cosmetique Asia Corp., requesting for investigation and enforcement actions to stop the proliferation and distribution of fake Safeguard and Silka products in Metro Manila. The counterfeit items were seized on the strength of Search Warrants issued by Judge Maria Victoria Soriano-Villadolid of RTC Branch 24, Manila. Charges for violation of R.A. 8293 were filed against John/Jane Does, owners/managers/occupants/lessees of various stalls located in Sta. Cruz and Binondo, Manila. On July 14, 2017 , counterfeit Vans products with an estimated value of Php 11,600,000.00 were seized in Pasay City and Binondo, Manila. The case stemmed from the letter complaint of Lee Bumgarner Inc. (LBI) requesting on behalf of their client, VANS, for investigation and enforcement actions to stop the proliferation and distribution of fake VANS products in Metro Manila. The counterfeit VANS items were seized on the strength of Search Warrants issued by Judge Maria Victoria A. Soriano-Villadolid of RTC Brach 24, Manila. Charges for violation of R.A. 8293 were filed against John/Jane Does, owners/managers/operators/agents/occupants/lessees of various stores/stalls in 999 Shopping Mall, Binondo, Manila and One Shopping Center, Pasay City. On July 19, 2017 , counterfeit Lacoste products with an estimated value of Php 20,350,000.00 were seized by NCR operatives in Pasay City and Binondo, Manila. The case stemmed from the letter complaint filed by MARKSPRO Law Firm on behalf of their client Lacoste, requesting investigation and enforcement actions to stop the distribution of fake Lacoste products in Metro Manila. The counterfeit items were seized on the strength of Search Warrants issued by Judge Rainelda H. Estacio-Montesa of RTC Branch 46, Manila. Charges for violation of R.A. 8293 were filed against the owners/managers/operators/occupants/lessees of various stores in 999 Shopping Mall, 168 Shopping Mall, both located in Binondo, Manila and Baclaran Terminal Plaza, Pasay City. In four (4) successive operations, NBI-Intellectual Property Rights Division (NBI-IPRD) seized various fake products with an aggregate amount of Php 23,610,000.00. On July 3, 2017 , 178,100 pieces of Snowbear candies with an estimated amount of Php 200,000.00 were seized in the province of Leyte. Items were seized on the strength of Search Warrants issued by Judge Elam M. Rafallo-Lingan of Branch 159, City of Pasig. The operation stemmed from the complaint of Mr. Mitchell Vy Chua of Snowbear. After proper coordination with the Philippine National Police (PNP), the Search Warrants were implemented resulting in the seizure of the fake Snowbear candies. Charges for violation of R.A. 8293 (Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines) were filed against John/Jane Does, owners and operators of ARG General Merchandise in Kalderon St., Bato, Southern Leyte, a warehouse in Tacloban City, and a house in Brgy. Tinagoy, Southern Leyte. On July 18 and 26, 2017, operatives seized 2,317 bottles of Jo Malone and Lacoste perfumes with an estimated cost of Php 20,610,000.00. Items were seized on the strength of Search Warrants issued by Judge Rainelda H. Estacio-Montesa of Branch 46, Manila. The case stemmed from the complaint of Mr. Maximo Ocampo and Atty. Michael Untalan of BNU Law Offices. Charges for violation of R.A. 8293 (Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines) were filed against World Wanted Perfume/Wadoodun Corporation, John/Jane Does, owners/operators/managers/employees of several stalls in 999 Shopping Mall and 168 Shopping Mall both located in Binondo, Manila. On July 19, 2017 , 182 rolls and several loose TAIYO welding cables with an estimated amount of Php 3 Million were seized in Manila, Caloocan, and Quezon City. The operation stemmed from the complaint of Mr. Wilbert Wong and the counterfeit items were seized on the strength of Search Warrants issued by Judge Rainelda H. Estacio-Montesa of Branch 46, Manila. Charges for violation of R.A. 8293 were filed against John/Jane Does, owners/operators of JACOB INDUSTRIAL & MILL SUPPLY, JENTROUS MARKETING, AIRTECH INDUSTRIAL CORPORATION, all located in Caloocan City as well as GOOD TRADE MARKETING, UNITED POWER HARDWARE & CONSTRUCTION CO., INC., NEW CIRCULATED ELECTRICAL SUPPLY, all located in Sta. Cruz, Manila, and warehouses located in Sto. Domingo Avenue, Quezon City.

Proper documentation and booking was made upon the Subject. A heightened security in the hospital premises was implemented due to the serious threats that Subject will be rescued by the armed men led by his son ALDE “BUTSOY” SALUSAD. On July 13, 2017 , operatives of NBI-Naga District Office (NBI-NADO, together with the elements of DENR-V conducted forest protection activity at Brgy. San Isidro Norte, Lagonoy, Camarines Sur resulting in the seizure of illegal logs, lumbers, and flitches of Narra, PMG, and other premium tree species, along with semi-furnished furniture items with a total volume of 2,534.93 board feet inside the unregistered furniture shop of certain ELADIO OLIVER now being operated by his son, DANISIE OLIVER y ASIDO. Subject was placed under further investigation of DENR for proper disposition and filing of necessary case in violation of Section 77 of PD 7095, as amended. On July 14, 2017 , operatives of NBI-Environmental Crime Division (NBI-ENCD) arrested JHEUSUL PARAS and ALPIE JUN JUGUILON for violation of R.A. 9147 (Wildlife Resources Conservation and Protection Act of 2001). The case stemmed from the request of Biodiversity Management Bureau based on the information received from United States Fisheries and Wildlife Service (USFWS), to investigate the rampant illegal shipment of reptiles from the Philippines to the United States using the different services of different courier company like FEDEX. It was shipped by a certain HARVEY SALVADOR from Cebu City to CARIDAD CEMEDO of Massachusetts, USA. Based on the investigation and information received, a certain ALPIE JUN JUGUILON and JHEUSUL PARAS were the ones responsible for shipping reptiles to the United States. Surveillance was conducted and Subjects’ location was located. By virtue of Search Warrants issued by Judge Gernerosa G. Labra of RTC Branch 23, Cebu City, threatened and non-threatened wildlife species were seized and Subjects JUGUILON and PARAS were arrested. They were presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor, Cebu City. On July 16, 2017 , operatives of NBI-Special Action Unit (NBI-SAU) arrested ANALYN DUCUSIN for large scale illegal recruitment. The case stemmed from about ninety-five (95) complainants who filed their complaints before the NBI. The victims filed their complaints against Subject DUCUSIN, MARIA THERESA BUMATAY BARUELO alias “MARIA TERESITA BARUELO, MARIA TERESA BUMATAY BURUELO, MA. THERESA BORUELO, MARITES FORES FRIO alias “TESS”, YOLANDA CABINTOY, and unidentified cohorts. According to the complainants, aforementioned Subjects recruited them for overseas employment with them paying Php 31,000 and Php 38,000 respectively for the process of their visa applications as well as other documents for work abroad. However, after several months, Subjects failed to deliver their promises and despite repeated demands, Subjects refused to return the complainants’ money, prompting the victims to file their complaints before the NBI. When the NBI received a call that Subject DUCUSIN had asked to meet with the complainants for another payment of Php 40,000, an entrapment operation was conducted resulting in the arrest of Subject DUCUSIN. Subjects ANALYN DUCUSIN, as well as the other subjects MARIA THERESA BUMATAY BARUELO alias “MARIA TERESITA BARUELO, MARIA TERESA BUMATAY BURUELO and MA. THERESA BORUELO, MARITES FORES FRIO alias “TESS”, YOLANDA CABINTOY , and JOHN and JANE DOES shall be prosecuted for Illegal Recruitment as Committed by a Syndicate and In Large Scale/Involving Economic Sabotage, as defined and penalized under R.A. 8042 (Migrant Workers and Overseas Filipinos Act of 1995), as amended by R.A. 10022 as well as Estafa, as defined and penalized under Article 315 (2) (a) of the Revised Penal Code, as amended. Ballesteros, Head of the Department of Internal Affairs-Investigation Section and authorized representative of Metrobank against the Subject for alleged qualified theft, falsification and violation of the General Banking Law. The official said that he noticed several irregularities in the letter request concerning a loan transaction of a client being facilitated by the Subject. Verification with the client disclosed that they were not aware of the letter request and even the account from which the Manager’s Check was supposed to be debited. Further investigation revealed that bank supposedly issued a loan in favor of the client covered by a fictitious promissory note. It is also revealed that Subject LOPEZ uses the account to facilitate fictitious loans. Acting on the said information, an entrapment operation was set up. As soon as Subject LOPEZ gave instructions to debit the amount of Php 2,250,000.00 from the client’s savings account, the bank issued a debit memo to the Subject as evidence of the processing of transaction. Thereafter, right after an official of the bank got confirmation that client is not aware of the loan transaction, Subject LOPEZ was arrested. She was then presented for inquest proceedings at the Makati City Prosecutor’s Office on July 18, 2017. Espino Jr. against Subject LEONARDO NICOLAS for violations of Article 210 of the Revised Penal Code (Direct Bribery), violation of Article 293 of the Revised Penal Code (Robbery Extortion) and violation of Section 7(d) in relation to Section 11 of R.A. 6713 otherwise known as “The Code of Conduct and Ethical Standards for Public Officials and Employees. body: A luxury car owned by Manuel K. Amalilio, head of the Aman Futures Trading was found abandoned in the basement of a condominium in Mandaluyong City by agents of the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) recently. In a report submitted to NBI Director Nonnatus Caesar R. Rojas by the Technical Investigation Division, Intelligence Services, the said luxury car, a Lamborghini Gallardo 560 Coupe Regolare was imported from Italy based on the import entry number C 23754 , was found parked at BSA Twin Tower Condotel, BSA Twin Towers Bank Drive cor. J. Vargas St., Ortigas Center, Bgy. Wack Wack, Mandaluyong City. It was disclosed that a certain Mr. Shaffic Risaib Shah parked the vehicle at BSA Tower Condominium because the parking area at BSA Condotel was full. Mr. Shah then leased the parking slot for one month leaving a calling card for reference. The parking lot was already sold out and the owner wanted the parked vehicle removed. But Mr. Shah did not respond though contacted through letter, phone, text and e-mail. The abandoned vehicle was also reported to the police and was recorded or “blottered.” Consequently, they have decided to turn over the custody of the vehicle to NBI. Per verification, the car was registered to Manuel K. Amalilio, accused in the Aman Futures who is now in Malaysia.

body: The National Bureau Investigation (NBI) today announced the arrest of two individuals by the operatives of NBI-Bohol District Office (NBI-BOHDO) in Sagbayan, Bohol for selling petroleum products without permit from the government. NBI Officer-In-Charge (OIC) Director Eric B. Distor identified the subjects as Spouses CASIANO ORO y SEPADA and ANABEL ORO y VALENTOS. OIC Distor said that the operation stemmed from a report received by NBI-BOHDO that subject spouses are engaged in the illicit trade of Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG). NBI-BOHDO conducted a series of surveillance operations and confirmed that subject spouses are operating an unlicensed refilling and retailing of LPG, particularly Butane. The Department of Energy-Visayas Field Office has issued a Certification stating that subject spouses are not registered with them for the issuance of Standard Compliance Certificate for the refilling, retailing, distribution, and hauling of LPG. Under strict instructions from Director Distor, NBI-BOHDO planned a buy-bust operation against the subject spouses. An undercover agent/ poseur-buyer ordered 300 pieces of Butane. Thus, on August 3, 2021, NBI-BOHDO strategically positioned near the target area in Sagbayan, Bohol. Upon arrival of subject spouses, they showed the poseur-buyer 300 cans of Butane and loaded it into the poseur-buyer’s vehicle, then handed over the marked money to subject spouses giving the pre-arranged signal that the transaction has been consummated. The undercover agent together with the rest of the NBI-BOHDO operatives immediately apprehended the subject spouses. Subjects were presented for Inquest proceedings before the Provincial Prosecutor’s Office of Tagbilaran City for illegal trading of petroleum and/or petroleum products, prohibited and penalized under Sec 2(a) of P.D. 1865.

body: In line with the directive of Secretary of Justice Menardo I. Guevarra, the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today announced the creation of TASK FORCE-PHILHEALTH that will conduct an investigation of Philippine Health Insurance Corporation (Philhealth). NBI Officer-In-Charge (OIC) Director Eric B. Distor said that he has issued a Memorandum Order creating TASK FORCE-PHILHEALTH that will conduct an investigation on the various allegations of corruption and anomalies in Philhealth. OIC Director Distor added the investigation of TASK FORCE – PHILHEALTH will include the audit of the Philhealth finances and the conduct of lifestyle checks on its officials and employees. OIC Director Distor stressed “considering that the NBI is still conducting investigation on alleged Philhealth anomalies, the creation of a task force on this matter will certainly help intensify and hasten the investigation”. He added that TASK FORCE PHILHEALTH will be composed of Agents and Investigators from the Bureau’s Anti-Graft Division (AGD), Anti-Fraud Division (AFD), Special Action Unit (SAU), Computer Crimes Division (CCD), Special Operations Group (SOG) and Digital Forensic Laboratory (DFL). The Task Force shall be headed by NBI-NCR Regional Director Cesar Bacani and shall be under the supervision of Deputy Director for Regional Operations Service (DDROS) Antonio Pagatpat to be assisted by Deputy Director for Investigation Service (DDInvS) Vicente De Guzman III. TASK FORCE-PHILHEALTH will also coordinate with the Department of Justice (DOJ) on the progress of the investigation, Distor emphasized. In 2019, the NBI conducted an investigation on Philhealth regarding the ghost dialysis fees involving WellMed Dialysis and Laboratory Center Corporation (WellMed) and Philhealth. The investigation revealed that WellMed charges Philhealth for dialysis claims of patient-members who are already dead. body: PRESS STATEMENT December 09, 2024 Under the leadership of NBI Director Judge Jaime B. Santiago (Ret.), the Operatives of the NBI conducted a nationwide operation on the alleged illicit trade of depleted Uranium, in violation of R.A. No. 5207, as amended, otherwise known as the “Atomic Energy Regulatory and Liability Act of 1968, which resulted in the unprecedented seizure of about 100 kilos of radioactive materials and the arrest of the responsible individuals. The case stemmed when the Representatives of the Philippine Nuclear Research Institute (PNRI) met with Director Santiago, and sought for assistance in investigating the aforesaid illegal trade of depleted Uranium. According to the PNRI, depleted Uranium poses a serious threat to national security because such can be used as source material for nuclear weapons. Terror organizations are after depleted Uranium to improve their weaponry. Additionally, due to its radioactivity and toxicity, it can expose the people in close contact with it to health threats. Upon the order of the Director, a Team of Operatives was immediately dispatched to investigate, to recover the dangerous materials, and to arrest the Subjects. Investigation disclosed that the group of ROY CABESAS VISTAL offered for sale the said radioactive materials to the public by misrepresenting that the same are precious metals. Consequently, the Operatives of NBI-OD, HD, NCR, and STF, led an entrapment operation in Pasay City on October 18, 2024 that resulted in the arrest of MAE VERGEL ZAGALA a.k.a. “Madame Mae”, ROY VISTAL’s partner, and ARNEL GIMPAYA SANTIAGO, VISTAL’s agent, and the recovery of 20 kilograms of metal bars and 3 kilograms of black powder, all positive for Uranium-235 and Uranium-238. VISTAL, however, remained at-large at time time. On even date, the NBI and the PNRI Technical Team, also implemented Search Warrant against ROY VISTAL, et. al., at his residence in Pasay City. The search led to the seizure of about 3 kilograms of black powder, rock material, small metal materials, and other contaminated items that all tested positive for Uranium235 and Uranium-238. Moreover, the PNRI discovered that VISTAL’s residence in Pasay City is heavily contaminated with an undeterminable quantity of depleted Uranium powder. As part of PNRI’s safety protocols, the area is currently undergoing decontamination procedure before its release to the owners. As a result of the manhunt operation of this Bureau, VISTAL was eventually arrested on October 28, 2024 in Cagayan de Oro City. On October 28, 2024, Operatives of NBI-OD, HD, NCR, NEMRO, and the PNRI Technical Team, assisted by the CBRNC, PA, 4ID and PAF, AFP, also implemented Search Warrant at VISTAL’s residence in Cagayan de Oro City. The operation resulted in the seizure of several radioactive and contaminated materials, including a black pot, weighing three (3) to five (5) kilograms that tested positive for Uranium 238 and Uranium-235. The Team also detected severe surface contamination with Uranium-238 and Uranium-235 in the various areas of the subject residence, including the family vehicle. Further investigation disclosed that VISTAL’s group allegedly sourced the depleted Uranium from Cebu. On November 8 and 9, 2024, Operatives from NBI-OD, HD, STF, CEVRO, and CEBDO, PNRI, and the troops of the AFP Cebu Joint Task Force, conducted another search and seizure operation in Mandaue City that paved the recovery of about 60 kilograms of block metals, which tested positive for Uranium-238 and Uranium235. The arrested Subjects were presented for Inquest Proceedings before the Department of Justice, Padre Faura. Subsequently, a criminal case for Violation of Section 6, in relation to Section 16, of Republic Act No. 5207, as amended, was filed before the Courts in Pasay City and CDO. Director Santiago commended the Teams for their dedication and bravery to seize the radioactive materials, in spite of its intrinsic hazards. He said that the successful operations would not have been made possible absent the collaborative and relentless efforts of the men and women of the NBI, PNRI, intelligence community, AFP, local government units, and private institutions.

body: PRESS STATEMENT January 12, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } In line with the instruction of National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Director JUDGE JAIME B. SANTIAGO (Ret.) to beef up the campaign against illegal practice of medicine, the NBI – Organized and Transnational Crime Division (OTCD) arrested a Vietnamese national identified as TRINH THI KIEU NGUYEN a.k.a. “DR. ROSA” in Mandaluyong City for violation of Section 10 in relation to Section 28 of R.A. No. 2382 (Illegal Practice of Medicine). Director Santiago said that the operation stemmed from an information from a confidential informant regarding the illegal practice of medicine being perpetrated by a female Vietnamese national at a beauty clinic in Mandaluyong City. In response, agents of NBI-OTCD conducted surveillance operation, which confirmed the veracity of the information. It was revealed that a female Vietnamese national is offering medical procedures such as eyelid surgery, vaginal tightening, Botox and other cosmetic procedures for a fee at JK Beauty Clinic (JK) located at the ground floor of Jovan Condominium Building in Mandaluyong City. The confidential informant who also acted as poseur customer was able to secure an appointment with JK for a Botox procedure. On January 8, 2025, the operatives of NBI-OTCD proceeded to JK and the poseur customer accompanied by one of the undercover agent entered the clinic for the scheduled Botox procedure and nano filler on the chin priced at Php8,000.00 each. Upon paying Php16,000.00 for both procedures and when the procedure is about to start, the undercover agent gave the pre-arranged signal to the operatives, which resulted in the arrest of Subject Nguyen in the act of violating R.A. No. 2382. The operatives were able to recover from the Subject the marked money and various medical paraphernalia. On January 9, 2025, the arrested Subject Nguyen was presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor of Mandaluyong for the above-stated violations. Director Santiago said that an ongoing verification as to the status of the stay of the said Subject is being made with the Bureau of Immigration. He commended the operatives of NBI-OTCD for the successful operation and further emphasized that the NBI will be committed in apprehending individuals who are engaged in the illegal practice of medicine.

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today said operatives of the Bureau’s Environmental Crime Division (NBI-EnCD) arrested nine (9) individuals in Navotas City yesterday for illegal fishing. NBI Director Dante A. Gierran identified the 9 subjects as JUN ESATAN y AMANIA (Boat Captain), RONULFO PEREZ y SIGUN (Segunda Maestro), ERVIN TREMOTCHA y ENOC (Makinista), FLORO DELA JENTE y CLARITO (Segunda Maestro), ROLLY BELING y PIJAN (Makinista), TIRSO BELING y PIJAN (Boat Captain), LEOMAR JUGARAN y ARAGON (Boat Captain), ROLANDO RUSIANA y FREJONES (Boat Segunda Maestro) and RICHE LANGIT y BAZAR. Director Gierran said the NBI received information that several individuals were engaged in unauthorized fishing activities using DANISH SEINE/Modified Danish Seine also locally known as “HULBOT” within the municipal waters of Navotas City. After validating the said information and under strict orders from Director Gierran, operatives of the NBI-EnCD led by its Chief, Atty. Czar Nuqui, proceeded to the area and conducted an operation using 2 motorized bancas. After the Boat Captains of the “HULBOTs” with marking ‘F/V PATRICIA-E, “PATRICIA AARON” and F/V CARLOS failed to produce any valid fishing permit, Subject individuals were placed under arrest for violation of Republic Act No. 8550 or the Philippine Fisheries Code of 1998 as amended by Republic Act NO. 10654, entitled “An Act to Prevent, Deter and Eliminate Illegal or Unauthorized, Unreported and Unregulated Fishing,” such as Operating a Commercial vessel with NO LICENCE, and Possession of a fishing gear or operating a fishing vessel in a fishing area with NO LICENSE, among others. Aside from the above-cited violations, it is noteworthy to state that under Fisheries Administrative Order (FAO) No. 246, series of 2014, the use and operation of Danish Seine and modified Danish Seine (commonly known as HULBOT) are already banned in Philippine waters. Thus, aside from the arrest of the 9 Subjects, the NBI and Bureau of Fisheries and Aquatic Resources (BFAR) personnel seized the HULBOTs and other fishing paraphernalia. Corresponding charges will be filed against the subjects before the Department of Justice Task Force-Environmental Crimes.

body: PRESS STATEMENT February 18, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } On February 17, 2025, the National Bureau of Investigation – Pampanga District Office (NBI-PAMDO), in collaboration with the Technical Intelligence Division (TID), Ilocos Regional Office (IRO), Cordillera Administrative Region (CAR) and Dagupan District Office (DADO), under the guidance of NBI Director JUDGE JAIME B. SANTIAGO (Ret.), arrested JOHN MICHAEL SERRANO GARCIA at Purok Wakas, Barangay Mambog, Malolos City, Bulacan after months of collaborative and relentless efforts to capture him. GARCIA, who is the accused in the killing of LUKE MARANEG, son of NBI Agent, has an outstanding Warrant of Arrest for Murder and Attempted Murder issued by RTC Branch 78, Baguio City. Investigation disclosed that on November 24, 2024 at around 1:30 A.M., GARCIA shot LUKE MARANEG at Happy Homes, Barangay Ferdinand, Baguio City. However, witnesses disclosed that GARCIA’s target was actually GINO MANOLO CASTILLO BANTA because of the latter’s past relationship with GARCIA’S girlfriend, who earlier had sexual trysts with BΑΝΤΑ. Since then, GARCIA went into hiding and has been moving to different places within Baguio City, Pangasinan and La Union based on technical surveillance. Task Force GARCIA was then organized by this Bureau composed of Agents from PAMDO, TID, IRO, CAR and DADO. Relentless efforts and intelligence gathering of the members of the Task Force continuously tracked GARCIA’s location. However, GARCIA has been mobile for months and has been moving to different places. Finally, on February 14, 2025, technical surveillance conducted by TID tracked the Subject’s location within Barangay Mambog, Malolos City, Bulacan. Thereafter, physical surveillance conducted by NBI-PAMDO Agents confirmed the Subject’s exact location inside his auntie’s apartment at Purok Wakas, Barangay Mambog, Malolos City, Bulacan where he was eventually captured. Subject is currently detained at NBI-PAMDO pending the issuance of a Commitment Order by the Honorable Court. Director SANTIAGO lauded the collaborative and relentless efforts of PAMDO, TID, IRO, CAR and DADO in order to bring the fugitive into the arms of law.

body: PRESS STATEMENT March 23, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } NBI–NCR PROBES ALLEGED ILLEGAL TRANSFER OF CLOA LANDS IN BATAAN TO POGO-LINKED FIRM The National Bureau of Investigation – National Capital Region (NBI–NCR) is currently conducting an investigation into a complaint involving the alleged illegal transfer of agrarian lands in Bataan. At present, around fifteen (15) to twenty (20) farmer-complainants are at the NBI–NCR office to formally execute their sworn statements and provide supporting documents relative to the case. The complaint alleges that parcels of land covered by Certificates of Land Ownership Award (CLOAs) were transferred to a private corporation reportedly engaged in Philippine Offshore Gaming Operations (POGO) and linked to personalities, including former Presidential Spokesperson Harry Roque, without the required clearance from the Department of Agrarian Reform (DAR). Preliminary information further indicates possible falsification of documents in the processing and transfer of the land titles, raising serious concerns over the legality and validity of the transactions. The NBI–NCR is presently undertaking a thorough case build-up to determine the existence of probable cause and identify all individuals who may be held criminally liable. The Bureau assures the public that the investigation will be conducted impartially and in accordance with existing laws, particularly those protecting agrarian reform beneficiaries. #NBIServes

body: Finding a strong ally from the passage of a Bill in the Senate against online sexual exploitation, the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) welcomed the Senate’s approval of Senate Bill 2209 otherwise known as the Special Protection Against Online Sexual Abuse and Exploitation of Children (OSAEC). NBI OIC-Director Eric B. Distor said that with the passage SB 2209, the gov’t has given the NBI and other law enforcement agencies more teeth to run after those who commit the dastardly crimes against our children. On May 27, 2021, the Senate unanimously approved on third and final reading the said bill, with 23-0-0 voting. Senate Bill 2209 defines and penalizes OSAEC as a specific crime. The said bill advocates the provision of special protections to children from all forms of sexual violence, abuse and exploitation, especially those committed with the use of information and communication technology (ICT). Under the bill, production or creation of any form of child sexual materials, participation in the production, or facilitating in the creation of such materials is punishable by law. Individuals or adults who engage in the grooming of children for the purpose of facilitating the commission of sexual exploitation activity, as well as accessing, subscribing, or streaming any form of child sexual abuse and exploitation materials will also be penalized. The bill obliges internet service providers and social media intermediaries to block or remove the existence of child sexual abuse or exploitation material or the streaming/live-streaming of a child sexually abused or exploited, within twenty four (24) hours from receipt of notice containing sufficient information to identify the content and its source. They are also required to develop and adopt a set of systems and procedures for preventing, blocking, detecting, and reporting of OSAEC committed within their platforms, and to establish high privacy setting as default safety and privacy settings for children, and where necessary, adopt age-verification controls and protocols to restrict access to such materials. “The NBI supports the approval of the bill as one of the Bureau’s Anti-Human Trafficking Division’s objectives is to combat online abuse and sexual exploitation of children and strengthen their protection. With SB 2209, the NBI upholds its mandate to reinforce investigation, prosecution and adjudication of OSAEC cases”, Distor emphasized.

body: PRESS STATEMENT November 13, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) commemorated its 89th Founding Anniversary on November 13, 2025, marking nearly nine decades of steadfast public service and excellence in law enforcement. The commemoration of this year’s anniversary carries the theme, “NBI @89: Huwaran ng Kahusayan, Tapat na Lingkod-Bayan,” which underscores the Bureau’s unwavering commitment to excellence, integrity, and dedicated public service to the Filipino People. The festivities commenced with a Thanksgiving Mass held at the Grand Ballroom of the Rizal Park Hotel, a historic venue in Manila known for its cultural significance. The program proper followed, highlighting Usec. Fredderick A. Vida, Officer-in-Charge of the Department of Justice, who delivered his congratulatory anniversary message as the Guest of Honor. In the afternoon, the Service Awards Ceremony took place to recognize and honor the outstanding contributions and unwavering loyalty of NBI personnel who have demonstrated consistent excellence in the performance of their duties. This recognition highlights their dedication to upholding the Bureau’s mission and values through exemplary service to the Filipino people. On November 14, 2025, OIC Director Angelito DLP Magno, together with the Directorial Staff, will preside over the Command Conference-an annual event dedicated to reviewing the Bureau’s accomplishments over the past year and setting strategic priorities for the year ahead. NBI officials from regional and district offices will convene to discuss initiatives aimed at strengthening public service delivery and aligning efforts with the Bureau’s long-term goals and directives. The anniversary celebration will culminate with “Balik Akademya,” a gathering of NBI Academy alumni. This homecoming event aims to rekindle camaraderie, celebrate shared experiences, and strengthen professional and personal ties among graduates of the Academy. OIC Director Magno extends his heartfelt congratulations to all awardees and commends the men and women of the NBI for their 89 years of dedicated, loyal, and selfless service to the Bureau and the nation.

body: PRESS STATEMENT January 14, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } NBI ARRESTS AN INDIVIDUAL FOR ILLEGAL POSSESSION OF FIREARMS The National Bureau of Investigation, through the Dangerous Drugs Division (DDD) and Organized and Transnational Crime Division (OTCD), arrested an individual in Makati City for illegal possession of firearms. The subject, identified as DAVID SARMIENTO SIA a.k.a. DAVID RHO, was arrested in a buy-bust operation that stemmed from the information received regarding a group of Chinese and Taiwanese nationals allegedly engaged in the sale of firearms and illegal drugs, purportedly led by the subject. On the evening of December 29, 2025, joint-operatives of the DDD and OTCD conducted the buy-bust operation, resulting in the arrest of the subject and the seizure of the following items: one (1) M3 submachine gun, a caliber.45 with no serial number; one (1) empty magazine; and the marked money. Further search of the subject’s vehicle yielded the following items: One (1) Pistol STI GP6 with serial number GO14059 with magazine loaded with 16 ammos; One (1) Pistol Ruger EC9 with Serial Number 455-32319 with magazine loaded with 7 ammos.; One (1) magazine box containing approximately 200 pcs of 9mm ammos.; Eight empty 9mm magazines; Four (4) boxes of .9mm ammos (50 per box); One (1) empty 5.56 magazine; One (1) magazine loaded with 21 pcs of M855 Green Tip ammos.; One (1) plastic box containing 100 pcs of reload 9mm ammos.; One (1) suppressor/silencer.; One (1) IMI Defense Pistol Conversion Kit. Upon verification, the subject was able to present a valid license to possess the Pistol Ruger EC9s with Serial No. 455-32319, but failed to present a license for the Pistol STI GP6 with Serial No. GO14059. The subject was duly informed of the cause of his arrest and of his constitutional rights, after which he was brought to the to the NBI Office for standard booking procedures and ultraviolet (UV) light examination. The forensic examination conducted on the dorsal and palmar surfaces of both hands yielded positive results, indicating the presence of yellow fluorescent specks and smudges. The subject claims to be a Filipino citizen born in the Philippines. However, observations indicate that he speaks broken or limited Tagalog and experiences difficulty writing in both English and Tagalog. In view of these circumstances, further verification of his identity and nationality is deemed necessary. Additionally, coordination with the PNP Firearms and Explosives Division will be undertaken to verify the authenticity of the firearm license presented by the subject. Subject is now presently under the custody of NBI-DDD and will be presented for inquest proceedings before the office of the City Prosecutor of Makati City for violation of R.A. 10591 otherwise known as the Comprehensive Firearms and Ammunition Regulation Act. Acting Director Atty. Angelito DLP Magno stated that the successful operation highlights the Bureau’s resolve to enforce the law with integrity and vigilance, and encouraged the public to remain engaged and assist the Bureau in addressing crimes, as collective effort is vital to ensuring community safety. #NBIServes

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today announced the arrest of an individual by the NBI-Ilocos Regional Office (NBI-IRO) for Robbery/Extortion and Usurpation of Authority in San Fernando City, La Union. NBI Officer-in-Charge (OIC)- Director Eric B. Distor identified the arrested subject as VICENTE FAILON MARTINEZ. OIC Director Distor said that the operation stemmed from a complaint filed by the victim before the NBI-IRO regarding the crime committed against him by the subject. According to the victim-complainant, Subject Martinez was able to dupe him a total amount of Php 486,000.00. After sometime, the swindling elevated to extortion when Subject Martinez concocted a spurious Intelligence Report (IR) allegedly from NBI-IRO and NBI Manila. Using the same IR, Subject Martinez demanded P1 Million from victim-complainant and forcing him and forced him to surrender his motor vehicle and was coerced to execute a blank Deed of Absolute Sale of a Motor Vehicle with a current Market Value of Php 500,000.00. Also, subject Martinez subsequently demanded an additional P500,000.00 to complete the P1Million by way of threat and coercion, threatening victim-complainant hewill be arrested by NBI-IRO and NBI Manila if he fails to produce the said amount at St. Jude Church, Poro, City of San Fernando, La Union. Thus, On May 4, 2021, an entrapment operation was hatched by operatives of NBI-IRO, resulting in the arrest of Subject Martinez who was caught red-handed in the act of receiving the entrapment money from the victim-complainant. Subject Martinez was then brought to the NBI-IRO Office and had undergone standard booking procedures. Documents are being prepared for the filing of Robbery/Extortion and Usurpation of Authority against the subject.

body: PRESS STATEMENT October 10, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } Under the leadership of National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Director JUDGE JAIME B. SANTIAGO (Ret.), the NBI-Southern Mindanao Regional Office (NBI-SEMRO) conducted an entrapment operation at HEAVEN PERSONAL MASSAGE SPA, Jacinto St., Davao City, on October 07, 2025, resulting in the arrest of RAMELYN CEMENE SUMODONG a.k.a. “MADAM RAM” for violation of Republic Act No. 10364, otherwise known as the “Expanded Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2012,” in relation to R.A. No. 7610, or the “Special Protection of Children Against Abuse, Exploitation, and Discrimination Act.” The victim’s mother and grandmother sought help after the victim traveled to Davao City to work at Heaven Personal Massage SPA and they discovered that minors were being used as sex workers. An undercover SEMRO agent posed as a customer and negotiated with the establishment’s operator, known as “Madam Ram.” When the minors were presented, and the price of Php3,500.00 for the illicit service was confirmed, agents moved in. Madam Ram was immediately taken into custody and brought to NBI-SEMRO, where she underwent standard booking procedures. Evidence gathered at the scene and during the operation has been secured for investigation and prosecution. The rescued minors were promptly turned over to the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) for debriefing, medical examination, psychosocial intervention, and temporary protective custody. NBI-SEMRO coordinated closely with complaints, DSWD, child protection units, and local authorities to ensure the victims receive comprehensive care. NBI’s operation sends a clear message: traffickers will be chased from the shadows into the light until every child is safe.

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today announced the arrest of a medical student by NBI- Special Action Unit (NBI-SAU) in a buy-bust operation in Quezon City for selling illegal drugs. NBI-Officer-In-Charge (OIC)Director Eric B. Distor identified the subject as ROSE VILL MALDO a.k.a “ARVIE MALDO”. Distor said that the operation stemmed from information received by NBI-SAU, a medical practitioner is selling Cannabis oil online as medicine for cancer, epilepsy, pain relief and other diseases and as an additive to e-cigarette/vape juice. The operatives was able to confirm such illicit activities and immediately planned an entrapment operation. Thus, on March 9, 2022, NBI-SAU hatched a buy-bust operation, which resulted in the apprehension of Subject Maldo in a coffee shop in Barangay Doña Imelda, Quezon City. The operatives were able to confiscate a total of 27 ml of Cannabis oil with an estimated value of Php 26,000.00, a 9mm Taurus G3 pistol and several pieces of ammunition. The seized illegal drugs were submitted before Forensic Chemistry Division (NBI-FCD) for laboratory examination and analysis, which yielded positive results for the presence of TETRAHYDROCANNABINOL, a dangerous drug with total net weight of 27 ml. Verification with the PNP Firearms and Explosives Office revealed that Subject Maldo has a License to Own and Possess Firearm with expiry date on March 4, 2023 and registered under Subject’s name, a 9mm Taurus Pistol. However, Subject Maldo failed to present a Certificate of Exemption from Gun Ban. Upon further investigation, Subject revealed that he is a medical student/intern and during the conduct of tactical interrogation, he admitted that he is not a licensed physician. On March 10, 2022, Subject Maldo was subjected to e-inquest before the Office of the City Prosecutor-Quezon City for violation of Section 5 of R.A. 9165 otherwise known as “The Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002, Comelec Resolution No. 10728 in relation to Omnibus Election Code, and Article 172 in relation to Article 171(Falsification by Private Individual and Use of Falsified Document) of the Revised Penal Code, as amended.

body: PRESS STATEMENT May 08, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } PRESS RELEASE | NBI ARRESTS FIVE INDIVIDUALS FOR UNFAIR COMPETITION AND MISUSE OF GRAPES BRAND IN LA UNION On May 05, 2026, the National Bureau of Investigation – Ilocos Regional Office (NBI-IRO) in an entrapment operation at Barangay Urayong, Bauang, La Union arrested five (5) individuals who were engaged in unlawful acts constituting Unfair Competition, penalized under Section 168 in relation to Section 170 of Republic Act No. 8293, otherwise known as the Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines. The case arose from a verified complaint filed by a proprietor of Gapuz Grapes Farm, who alleged that certain individuals have been deliberately and fraudulently misrepresenting themselves as authorized or accredited tour guides of the said establishment. Investigation disclosed that these individuals were using the business name “GAPUZ GRAPES PICKING” without authority, with the intent to deceive the public and divert customers to a vineyard other than that owned and operated by the complainant, thereby causing undue injury, financial loss and damage the goodwill and integrity of the business. Acting upon said complaint, NBI-IRO operatives conducted surveillance and case build-up, which confirmed the illegal scheme employed by the subjects. Consequently, an entrapment operation was planned and executed, during which the suspects were caught in flagrante delicto while transacting with poseur-buyers using materials bearing the complainant’s registered business name acts that are fraudulently or deceptively, misleading the public into believing goods come from the complainants’ farm. Immediately upon their arrest, the subjects were informed of the nature of their arrest and were duly apprised of their constitutional rights. The operation likewise resulted in the confiscation of several incriminating items and pieces of evidence, including tarpaulins/signboards marked “GAPUZ GRAPE PICKING,” marked entrapment money, and handwritten receipts evidencing the unlawful transactions. Subjects were presented for inquest before the Office of the Provincial Prosecutor Bauang La Union.

body: PRESS STATEMENT January 30, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } NBI Nabs Married Man for Leaking Ex-Partner’s Intimate Videos and Demanding Sexual Favors PASAY, Philippines – On January 20, 2026, the National Bureau of Investigation, through its Cybercrime Division (NBI-CCD), apprehended a male Subject in an entrapment operation in Antipolo City, Rizal for the alleged distribution of intimate materials and using the same in coercing his former partner to engage in sexual intercourse. Official report shows that the complainant and the Subject were in a romantic relationship since June 2024 which the former later ended upon discovering the Subject’s repeated infidelity and the fact of his marriage. In December 2025, the complainant was alerted by friends and colleagues that her intimate photos and videos were being circulated online via multiple “fake” social media accounts. When confronted, the Subject denied involvement but later admitted distributing the said sexually explicit content. The Subject persisted in his malevolent scheme by allegedly threatening to send the explicit materials to the complainant’s parents. He reportedly used these images as leverage in forcing the complainant to have sexual intercourse with the him in exchange for not releasing the said content. Driven by these threats, the complainant sought the assistance of the NBI-CCD, leading to the Subject’s arrest during the entrapment operation. Subject was brought for inquest proceeding before the Office of the Prosecutor of Antipolo City and will be facing numerous charges of the following crimes, all in relation to R.A. No. 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012), to wit: 1.Republic Act No. 9262 (Anti-Violence Against Women and their Children Act of 2004); 2. Section 4(a) of R.A. No. 9995 (the Anti-Photo and Video Voyeurism Act of 2009) and; 3. Articles 286 (Grave Coercion); and 282 (Grave Threat) both under the Revised Penal Code (RPC). NBI Acting Director Atty. Angelito DLP Magno emphasized the Bureau’s zero-tolerance policy toward gender-based violence and digital harassment. “The National Bureau of Investigation takes violence and abuse against women seriously and will employ its full resources and expertise to ensure that individuals who perpetrate violence, discrimination, or any form of abuse against women will face justice,” said Director Magno. “We remain unwavering in our commitment to safeguarding women’s rights and holding digital offenders accountable.” The NBI encourages victims of similar “sextortion” or cyber-harassment schemes to come forward and report these crimes to the Cybercrime Division for immediate action. ATTY. ANGELITO DLP. MAGNO Acting Director, NBI Media Contact: HA Palmer U. Mallari NBI Spokesperson [email protected] #NBIServes

body: PRESS STATEMENT May 17, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } PRESS RELEASE | NBI APPREHENDS INDIVIDUAL WANTED FOR RAPE; EVADES ARREST FOR 15 YEARS The National Bureau of Investigation -Iligan District Office successfully served and implemented a Warrant of Arrest against accused Ricardo Mabulay y Frias on May 14, 2026, at the Office of the NBI-lligan District Office, Iligan City. The accused who personally appeared at NBI-ILDO for his NBI clearance application. During the conduct of the standard quality control, verification, and evaluation procedures of his application records, an attached derogatory record for the crime of Rape with an “ACTION TAKEN: WANTED” remark was discovered. Further verification disclosed that the derogatory record reflected the same name, criminal case number, offense charged, court of origin, and address appearing in the Warrant of Arrest issued by the Regional Trial Court, Branch 80. When confronted regarding the derogatory record, the accused acknowledged the existence of the criminal case, which he claimed to have believed was already settled. Thereafter, the accused was temporarily placed on hold while this Office secured an official copy of the Warrant of Arrest through the NBI Identification and Records Division (IRD). Upon receipt and verification thereof, this Office immediately effected the lawful arrest of the accused. The accused was informed of the nature and cause of his arrest and was apprised of his constitutional rights pursuant to the Constitution and existing laws. Accused is presently under NBI-ILDO pending appropriate commitment proceedings and further orders from the issuing court. This successful operation underscores the vital role and effectiveness of the NBI Clearance System as a significant law enforcement mechanism in the administration of justice and the maintenance of public safety.

body: PRESS STATEMENT January 30, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } The National Bureau of Investigation-Special Task Force (NBI-STF), under the supervision of NBI Director Judge Jaime B. Santiago (Ret.), arrested five (5) Chinese nationals engaged in illegal intelligence gathering that jeopardizes national security. Following the apprehension of DENG, YUANQING, and his local cohorts last January 17, 2025 for violation of the Espionage Act, the Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) conducted a follow-up casing and surveillance operations on a group suspected of collaborating with DENG, YUANQING. This group is believed to have engaged in aerial reconnaissance via drone operations, collecting data from the Philippines’ naval assets, among others. Intelligence gathering disclosed that a group of Chinese nationals was monitored in Barangay Buenavista, Puerto Princesa City, posing as buyers of marine products, roaming around the city, and surveying for stations selling the products. The group, however was seen frequenting Ulugan Bay, Puerto Princesa, Palawan, conducting aerial surveillance and reconnaissance, collecting imagery intelligence on the Naval Detachment Oyster Bay (NDOB) in Barangay Bahile, which is part of the Philippine Navy’s Naval Forces West (Navforwest) and is strategically positioned near the South China Sea. Acting on the information, the NBI-STF Agents conducted a validation process and identified five (5) members of the group, all of whom were Chinese nationals and members of the Qiaoxing Volunteer Group of the Philippines, as well as the Philippine China Association of Promotion of Peace and Friendship, Inc., namely: CAI SHAOHUANG a.k.a. Richard Tan Chua (Field Commander), CHENG HAI TAO a.k.a. Lestrade (Intelligence Operative), WU CHENG TING a.k.a. Brawn (Intelligence Operative), WANG YONG YI a.k.a. Watson (PRO & Financier), and WU CHIN REN (Member). In a series of hot-pursuit operation conducted by NBI Agents on January 24-25, 2025, above-named Chinese nationals were monitored which resulted in their arrest. Analysis on the running applications on the seized mobile devices from the Chinese nationals revealed photos of Buliluyan ports, Coast Guard station, vessels, small navy crafts/assets, and docks. Other images showed the Philippine Navy’s Del Pilar Class PS 16, terrain maps overlooking the Subic Bay International Airport, Naval Operating Base Subic, and a Chinese character marking being embedded on the screenshot with an arrow from Barreto, Olongapo pointing to the Naval Operating Base Subic. Also discovered were footages of the Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) Vessels BRP THERESA MAGBANUA, and BRP GABRIELA SILANG, docked in PCG-Maritime Safety Service Unit NCR-Cluster. Subjects were informed of their constitutional rights and were brought to the NBI main office for the standard booking procedures. Subjects underwent inquest proceedings before the Office of the State Prosecutor, Department of Justice, for violation of Commonwealth Act No. 616 Section 1(a) and 2(b) in relation to R.A. 10175 the Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012.

body: On April 2, 2020, operatives of NBI-Naga District Office (NBI-NADO) arrested MARILOU REGIDOR y ANTONIO, MARLON REGIDOR y ANTONIO, and JOSE BARRAMEDA y BASCO for selling overpriced alcohol in violation of RA 7581 and RA 7394. Subjects were arrested in entrapment operation which stemmed from the information received pertaining to an individual allegedly involved in the online selling of alcohol with a price higher than the price provided by the DOH and DTI. Acting on the information, NBI-NADO operatives looked it up on Facebook and found out that certain LOU REGIDOR was selling ethyl alcohol for a price of Php 650 per gallon (Php 85.86 per 500ml). With this, operatives transacted with LOU REGIDOR for the order of 20 gallons of ethyl alcohol for Php 13,000. On the above-mentioned date, the entrapment operation was conducted and the meet up was set at Naga City Hall. The operation resulted in the arrest of Subjects MARILOU REGIDOR, MARLON REGIDOR (Driver), and JOSE BARRAMEDA (Helper). Recovered from the Subjects were 55 containers of unbranded ethyl alcohol. Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the City Prosecutor, Naga City. On April 13, 2020, operatives of NBI-Iligan District Office (NBI-ILDO) arrested ANWAR MUSTAPHA y ARIB in entrapment operation for selling overpriced alcohol violating RA 10623, RA 7394, RA 9711, and RA 11469. Bought from the Subject were 70 plastic bottles containing 1 liter of 70% ethyl alcohol. Each bottle was sold in the amount of Php 200 which exceeds the price set by the DOH and DTI. Subject was brought to NBI office for the proper booking procedures. On April 13, 2020, operatives of NBI-Southeastern Mindanao Regional Office (NBI-SEMRO) arrested JOHN PAUL T. ALVARADO and SALVE LLEGO in entrapment operation for violation of RA 11469, RA 7581, and RA 7394, all in relation to RA 10175. Subjects offered for sale online vegetables, fruits, and spices at a very unacceptable price compared to the suggested retail price prescribed by the Department of Agriculture. Subjects, however, were released for regular filing on the account of failure of online inquest implemented by the City Prosecutor’s Office. On April 15, 2020, operatives of NBI-Bohol District Office (NBI-BOHDO) arrested MARIE GRACE LACABA y MANGARON for violation of RA 7581 in relation to 10623. Seized from the Subject were entrapment money, 2 plastic bottle containers of 70% isopropyl alcohol. Subject is detained at NBI-BOHDO Detention Facility. On April 16, 2020, operatives of NBI-Laguna District Office (NBI-LAGDO) arrested MARVIN QUISOL CUNA for Usurpation of Authority, Estafa and Falsification of Public Subject introduced himself as a member of the Presidential Task Force on Moral Recovery allegedly managed under the Office of the President of the Republic of the Philippines. In a photograph secured, Subject was seen displaying his alleged identification card reflecting the seal of the Republic of the Philippines as well as the seal and logos of different government agencies, name and signature of the President of the Philippines. Corollary to that, Subject was allegedly making profit by offering any interested party identification card and become a member thereof in the amount of Php 1,500 to Php 2,000. With this, an entrapment operation was conducted resulting in the arrest of the Subject who gave the poseur-applicant an application form of the alleged Presidential Task Force on Moral Recovery with the letter head of the Office of the President and received the payment of Php 3,000. Subject was brought to the Office of the City Prosecutor, Binan, Laguna for the filing of the above-mentioned misconducts. On April 18, 2020, operatives of NBI-Dipolog District Office (NBI-DIPDO) arrested CHRISTY T. ALAYACYAC for selling overpriced isopropyl alcohol. Subject was arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from a report that one of the online sellers based in Dipolog City was selling overpriced medical supplies amid Covid-19. Acting on the information, poseur-customer contacted the online seller thru social media and ordered several liters of isopropyl alcohol for the price Php 486 per liter including shipment fee. In coordination with DTI Dipolog City, the entrapment operation was conducted at LBC C.P. Garcia Branch, Dipolog City and resulted in the arrest of the Subject. Seized from the Subject were 16 bottles of isopropyl alcohol valued at Php 7,778. On April 20, 2020, operatives of NBI-Naga District Office (NBI-NADO) arrested ALBERT MELOR for selling overpriced isopropyl alcohol. Subject was arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from a report that a certain Albert Melor was allegedly selling alcohol with a price above the price set by the DOH and DTI. With this, operatives, acting as poseur-customer, transacted with the Subject and was able to order from him 10 gallons of isopropyl alcohol for Php 8,500 (Php 850 per gallon). Subject’s initial offer was Php 900 per gallon and the poseur-customer just haggled for a lower price. On the aforementioned date, together with Naval Forces southern Luzon and representative from DFA, the entrapment operation was conducted at Brgy. San Miguel, Bala, Camarines Sur resulting in the arrest of the Subject. Recovered from him were the entrapment money and the 10 gallons of isopropyl alcohol. Subject was presented for inquest proceedings at the Camarines Sur Provincial Prosecution Office for violation of RA 7581. On April 22, 2020, operatives of NBI-Naga District Office (NBI-NADO) arrested Information that a certain Annetztone Enterprise was selling isopropyl alcohol at Php 750 per gallon which is over and above the price set by the DOH and DTI. The owner of the said establishment was already warned to abide by the price ceiling but it was verified from a surveillance that the said establishment was still selling overpriced isopropyl alcohol. With this, in coordination with the FDA Legazpi City, an entrapment operation was conducted resulting in the arrest of REINNAH RAFER y OCOL, the owner of Annetztone Enterprise. Recovered from the Subject were the marked money and the 5 gallons of isopropyl alcohol which were turned over to FDA. Subject was presented for inquest proceedings before the Naga City Prosecutor Office for violation of RA 7581. On that same day, REINNAH RAFER y OCOL posted cash bond of Php 60,000 and thereafter an Order of Release was issued by the RTC Executive Judge. REINNAH RAFER y OCOL was released on that same day from NBI detention cell.
