On the above-mentioned date, the entrapment operation was conducted and the meet up was set at Naga City Hall. The operation resulted in the arrest of Subjects MARILOU REGIDOR, MARLON REGIDOR (Driver), and JOSE BARRAMEDA (Helper). Recovered from the Subjects were 55 containers of unbranded ethyl alcohol. Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the City Prosecutor, Naga City. On April 13, 2020, operatives of NBI-Iligan District Office (NBI-ILDO) arrested ANWAR MUSTAPHA y ARIB in entrapment operation for selling overpriced alcohol violating RA 10623, RA 7394, RA 9711, and RA 11469. Bought from the Subject were 70 plastic bottles containing 1 liter of 70% ethyl alcohol. Each bottle was sold in the amount of Php 200 which exceeds the price set by the DOH and DTI. Subject was brought to NBI office for the proper booking procedures. On April 13, 2020, operatives of NBI-Southeastern Mindanao Regional Office (NBI-SEMRO) arrested JOHN PAUL T. ALVARADO and SALVE LLEGO in entrapment operation for violation of RA 11469, RA 7581, and RA 7394, all in relation to RA 10175. Subjects offered for sale online vegetables, fruits, and spices at a very unacceptable price compared to the suggested retail price prescribed by the Department of Agriculture. Subjects, however, were released for regular filing on the account of failure of online inquest implemented by the City Prosecutor’s Office. On April 15, 2020, operatives of NBI-Bohol District Office (NBI-BOHDO) arrested MARIE GRACE LACABA y MANGARON for violation of RA 7581 in relation to 10623. Seized from the Subject were entrapment money, 2 plastic bottle containers of 70% isopropyl alcohol. Subject is detained at NBI-BOHDO Detention Facility. On April 16, 2020, operatives of NBI-Laguna District Office (NBI-LAGDO) arrested MARVIN QUISOL CUNA for Usurpation of Authority, Estafa and Falsification of Public Subject introduced himself as a member of the Presidential Task Force on Moral Recovery allegedly managed under the Office of the President of the Republic of the Philippines. In a photograph secured, Subject was seen displaying his alleged identification card reflecting the seal of the Republic of the Philippines as well as the seal and logos of different government agencies, name and signature of the President of the Philippines. Corollary to that, Subject was allegedly making profit by offering any interested party identification card and become a member thereof in the amount of Php 1,500 to Php 2,000. With this, an entrapment operation was conducted resulting in the arrest of the Subject who gave the poseur-applicant an application form of the alleged Presidential Task Force on Moral Recovery with the letter head of the Office of the President and received the payment of Php 3,000. Subject was brought to the Office of the City Prosecutor, Binan, Laguna for the filing of the above-mentioned misconducts. On April 18, 2020, operatives of NBI-Dipolog District Office (NBI-DIPDO) arrested CHRISTY T. ALAYACYAC for selling overpriced isopropyl alcohol. Subject was arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from a report that one of the online sellers based in Dipolog City was selling overpriced medical supplies amid Covid-19. Acting on the information, poseur-customer contacted the online seller thru social media and ordered several liters of isopropyl alcohol for the price Php 486 per liter including shipment fee. In coordination with DTI Dipolog City, the entrapment operation was conducted at LBC C.P. Garcia Branch, Dipolog City and resulted in the arrest of the Subject. Seized from the Subject were 16 bottles of isopropyl alcohol valued at Php 7,778. On April 20, 2020, operatives of NBI-Naga District Office (NBI-NADO) arrested ALBERT MELOR for selling overpriced isopropyl alcohol. Subject was arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from a report that a certain Albert Melor was allegedly selling alcohol with a price above the price set by the DOH and DTI. With this, operatives, acting as poseur-customer, transacted with the Subject and was able to order from him 10 gallons of isopropyl alcohol for Php 8,500 (Php 850 per gallon). Subject’s initial offer was Php 900 per gallon and the poseur-customer just haggled for a lower price. On the aforementioned date, together with Naval Forces southern Luzon and representative from DFA, the entrapment operation was conducted at Brgy. San Miguel, Bala, Camarines Sur resulting in the arrest of the Subject. Recovered from him were the entrapment money and the 10 gallons of isopropyl alcohol. Subject was presented for inquest proceedings at the Camarines Sur Provincial Prosecution Office for violation of RA 7581. On April 22, 2020, operatives of NBI-Naga District Office (NBI-NADO) arrested Information that a certain Annetztone Enterprise was selling isopropyl alcohol at Php 750 per gallon which is over and above the price set by the DOH and DTI. The owner of the said establishment was already warned to abide by the price ceiling but it was verified from a surveillance that the said establishment was still selling overpriced isopropyl alcohol. With this, in coordination with the FDA Legazpi City, an entrapment operation was conducted resulting in the arrest of REINNAH RAFER y OCOL, the owner of Annetztone Enterprise. Recovered from the Subject were the marked money and the 5 gallons of isopropyl alcohol which were turned over to FDA. Subject was presented for inquest proceedings before the Naga City Prosecutor Office for violation of RA 7581. On that same day, REINNAH RAFER y OCOL posted cash bond of Php 60,000 and thereafter an Order of Release was issued by the RTC Executive Judge. REINNAH RAFER y OCOL was released on that same day from NBI detention cell.

title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: PRESS STATEMENT March 13, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } NBI SEIZES SUBSTANTIAL VOLUME OF DOG MEAT; FIVE VIETNAMESE NATIONALS ARRESTED IN PASAY AND MAKATI OPERATIONS PASAY CITY, Philippines – The National Bureau of Investigation – Organized and Transnational Crime Division (NBI-OTCD) has arrested five Vietnamese nationals for the unlawful sale and distribution of dog meat. The operations, conducted on March 10, 2026, resulted in the seizure of a significant volume of both raw and cooked dog meat intended for public consumption. The investigation was initiated following an intelligence report regarding a sophisticated online transaction. The Subjects allegedly utilized messaging platforms to market dog meat, featuring digital menus designed to mimic legitimate food delivery applications. To verify the intelligence report, NBI-OTCD agents executed a strategic test-buy. An undercover operative placed an order via the suspects’ mobile platform, which was fulfilled through a third-party courier. The specimen was immediately submitted to the National Meat Inspection Service (NMIS) for forensic examination, which confirmed the species as canine. Upon verification, NBI agents launched a two-pronged entrapment operation. Agents intercepted the delivery and arrested the delivery rider, identified as a Vietnamese national. A second team raided the source of the meat, leading to the arrest of four additional Vietnamese nationals and the confiscation of a large stockpile of meat products The five Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings and face multiple charges for violation of Republic Act No. 9296 (Meat Inspection Code of the Philippines), Republic Act No. 8485 as amended by Republic Act No. 10631 (Animal Welfare Act of 1998), Republic Act No. 9482(Anti-Rabies Act of 2007), and Republic Act No. 10611 (Food Safety Act of 2013). “The NBI will remain relentless in pursuing individuals who engage in unlawful practices that compromise our food safety standards and violate our animal welfare laws,” said NBI Director Atty. Melvin A. Matibag. “We are sending a clear message: no matter the platform or the method, illegal trades will be dismantled, and those responsible will be held accountable.” #NBIServes

body: On March 1, 2019 , operatives of NBI-Laguna District Office (NBI-LAGDO) arrested LLOYD ANJAIL y MONTEGREJO, MARIO ANJAIL y MONTEGREJO, and ROBIN JAY BUTAD y SANTONIA. Subjects falsely represented themselves as employees of NBI while distributing NBI online application forms in front of Lianas Supermarket, Brgy. Parian, Calamba, Laguna. Subjects were wearing NBI bull caps and t-shirts with big NBI letters printed on it. They also have fake NBI badge and ID. Charges for violation of Article 177 and 179 of the Revised Penal Code were filed against the Subjects before the Office of the City Prosecutor of Calamba City. On March 2, 2019 , operatives of NBI-MIMAROPA arrested KRIS SY ONG and FRANCES KAYE LIBRODO MARU in two separate operations for violation of RA 9165 (Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002). Subjects were arrested in event monitoring conducted at the MALASIMBO Music and Arts Festival 2019 in response to the request for assistance of PDEA MIMAROPA IV-B. Subject KRIS SY ONG was arrested around 9:00 in the evening and confiscated during the operation were one (1) piece small self-sealing transparent plastic sachet containing brown powdered substance suspected to be marijuana resins, one (1) piece self-sealing transparent plastic sachet used as container, one (1) improvised pipe used for smoking with suspected marijuana residue, one (1) piece wooden stick used as paraphernalia, and one (1) piece black lighter used as paraphernalia. On the other hand, Subject FRANCES KAYE LIBRODO MARU was arrested around 11:50 in the evening. Confiscated were one (1) piece self-sealing transparent plastic sachet containing one capsule with brownish powder suspected to be ecstacy weighing 0.01 gram with an estimated market value of Php 1,000.00. Arrested Subjects are now under temporary custody of PDEA MIMAROPA while documents were prepared for inquest proceedings before the Provincial Prosecutor’s Office for above-mentioned violation. On March 2, 2019 , operatives of NBI-Special Action Unit (NBI-SAU) arrested SHAO LEI for violation of RA 9165 (Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002). By virtue of Search warrant issued by RTC Branch 37, Manila against CHU WEI KUN, YU HSIEN HSU, and occupants of Unit 1002, Monarch Parksuites, Asean Business Park, Paranaque City, operatives searched the said area and yielded three (3) pieces of transparent plastic sachets, three (3) lighters, one (1) plastic box containing used foils and white crystalline substance. NBI-Forensic Chemistry Division (NBI-FCD) issued a certification that the contents of the plastic sachets tested positive results for the presence of methamphetamine hydrochloride with a net weight of 0.0678 grams. Subject SHAO LEI was brought for inquest proceedings before the Paranaque City Prosecutor’s Office. On March 4, 2019 , operatives of NBI-National Capital Region arrested MARIVIC GRIMALDO MANZANO by virtue of Warrant of Arrest for Estafa. Subject was arrested in her residence located at Unit 215, Tower 2, Urban Deca Homes Campville, Muntinlupa City after being positively identified by the complainant Menchita Valencia Banzuela. Subject was brought to NBI Main Office for the booking procedures and temporary detention. On March 5, 2019 , operatives of NBI-MIMAROPA arrested KRISTINE BARRIENTOS for human trafficking. Subject was arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from a report that she is a notorious pimp who operated in the City of Calapan. She catered to tourists who visit the province of Oriental Mindoro by providing them sexual services from her girls in exchange of fees ranging from Php 1,500-Php 2,500. Subject was arrested after receiving the entrapment money from the poseur customers. Four (4) trafficked victims were rescued and were subsequently turned over to DSWD for custody. Subject was charged for violation of RA 9208 (Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2003) before the inquest prosecutor of Calapan City. On March 6, 2019 , operatives of NBI-Bacolod District Office (NBI-BACDO) arrested FELIPE SANCHO JR. y TIBIRO for selling illegal drugs. Subject was arrested in a buy-bust operation where he was caught en flagrante in violation of Section 5 (Sale of Dangerous Drugs) of RA 9165 (Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002). Eight (8) pieces of lighters, five (5) tooters, one (1) bundle of transparent plastic sachets used for repacking of methamphetamine hydrochloride (shabu), Php 3,090 proceeds of illegal drugs trade, one (1) transparent plastic sachet comtaining white crystalline substance suspected to be shabu, and two (2) small transparent plastic sachets containing residues of suspected shabu were recovered. Subject was immediately brought to NBI-BACDO for the booking procedures. He was presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor for the aforementioned violation. On March 6, 2019 , operatives of the NBI-Rizal District Office (NBI-RIZDO) arrested CHRISTIAN MABBAYAD y SAGUISAG a.k.a. JAIKA and JOHN ROMEL BUENO y BANDULO for human trafficking. Subjects were arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from the information from Destiny Rescue Phils. regarding the human trafficking activities particularly sexual exploitation of minor victims committed by pimps in the areas of Pasig, Makati, Quezon City, and Rizal. Initial verification and surveillance operations conducted confirmed that a certain “Jaika” was maintaining, harboring, offering, and delivering girls for quick sexual intercourse to his clients. With this, in coordination with the representatives from DSWD, local police, and barangay official an entrapment operation was conducted which resulted in the arrest of the Subjects. Eleven (11) victims, three (3) of whom are minors, were likewise rescued and turned over to DSWD. Subjects CHRISTIAN MABBAYAD y SAGUISAG a.k.a. JAIKA and JOHN ROMEL BUENO y BANDULO were presented for inquest proceedings before the City Prosecutors Office of Antipolo for violation of RA 9208 (Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2003) as amended by RA 10364 (Expanded Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2012) and violation of RA 7610 (Special Protection of. Children Against Child Abuse, Exploitation and Discrimination Act). On March 6, 2019 , combined elements of NBI-Counter-Terrorism Division, (CTD), NBI-Death Investigation Division (DID), and NBI-Western Mindanao Regional Office (WEMRO) arrested SALAHIM DAWANI y HAIRAL a.k.a. ABU MOADZ, an Abu Sayyaf Group (ASG) member. Subject was arrested in Barangay Maharlika, Taguig City by virtue of Warrant of Arrest issued by the Regional Trial Court of Basilan for multiple counts of Kidnapping and Serious Illegal Detention. The Warrant of Arrest was issued in connection with the kidnapping of several workers of the Golden Harvest Plantation in Tairan, Lantawan, Basilan by the ASG in 2001. Upon receipt of information on the whereabouts of the Subject, CTD operatives verified his involvement in the Golden Harvest Kidnapping and two (2) victim-witnesses affirmed his active participation therein. According to the victims, Subject ABU MOADZ was with the group who abducted them and was one of those who torched the plantation chapel and residence of the plantation manager. Furthermore, Subject was among those who decapitated Golden Harvest plantation workers Primitivo Falcasantos and Crisanto Suela and served as close-in guard of the rest of the abducted workers including the victim-witnesses until they were rescued. Another government witness, who is a victim in another kidnapping incident perpetrated by the ASG, identified Subject ABU MOADZ as an ASG member. Allegedly, Subject was among those who served as augmentation force to the ASG who kidnapped them at the diving resort in Sipadan, Pulao, Sabah, Malaysia on April 23, 2000. Subject also served as close-in guard of the Sipadan Kidnapping victims after they were brought to Talipao and Patikul, Sulu. On March 6, 2019 , operatives of NBI-Anti-Violence Against Women and Children Division (NBI-AVWCD) arrested FERDINAND AND RAQUEL MATRE for Rape and Child Abuse. Janeth Brigino, a 15-year old rape victim, assisted by her aunt Irene Matildo, filed a complaint against the Subjects. Based on record check, Subjects have previous cases of Frustrated Homicides with Warrants for their arrest. Both Warrants were certified outstanding by issuing courts of Cainta and Antipolo. The Warrant of Arrest were served against the Subjects in their new address in Magalang, Pampanga. Subjects were immediately brought to the NBI Main Office for booking procedures. Rape and Child Abuse cases were filed against the Subjects before the Provoncial Prosecutor’s Office of Pampanga. On March 7, 2019 , operatives of NBI-Anti-Organized and Transnational Crime Division (NBI-AOTCD) arrested TOMASTO PERALTA NAZARIO, NOGARD SANTOS NAZARIO, and LENRICK GAVIOLA AQUINO for illegal bookies/horse racing betting. Subjects were arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from the information received by the NBI that several persons in the area of Calderon St., Sta. Ana, Manila are engaged in the bookies operation without license or permit from the Games and Amusement Board (GAB). Surveillance operations were then conducted confirming the said information. With this, the entrapment operation was conducted resulting in the arrest of the Subjects who served as the bet collectors and bookies personnel. Certification from GAB affirmed that they did not issue any permit or license authorizing the Subjects for horse racing bets. Subjects were brought to the Office of the City Prosecutor, Manila for inquest proceedings. On March 7, 2019 , operatives of NBI-North Eastern Mindanao Regional Office (NBI-NEMRO) seized numerous master cases of cigarettes with fake tax stamps and cigarettes without tax stamps amounting to Php 60 Million. Items were seized in inspection/raid conducted by NBI operatives together with the personnel from BIR Region 10 and representatives of Philip Morris Fortune Tobacco Corp., Japan Tobacco Inc., & IP Manila in warehouses of KDT Logistics located at RN Pelaez Ave., Kausawagan, Cagayan de Oro City. Found in the area were the employees of KDT Logistics and the owner SHI ZHULIAN, Chinese national. According to BIR, the seized items have an estimated loss of revenue of Php 21,070,000.00. Appropriate cases will be pursued against SHI ZHULIAN. On March 7, 2019 , operatives of NBI-Dagupan District Office (NBI-DADO) eleven (11) employees and bet collectors of Globaltech Peryahan ng Bayan namely: ROSARIO, SAMMY y MANSON, ALAMINIANA, JOEVEN y ANCHETA, DALISAY, NAPTALI y FERRER, ROVILLOS, MANUEL y TRINIDAD, MEDRANO, RICO y DE GUZMAN, CHRISTOPHER CRUZ, DE GUZMAN, BERNIE y SORIANO, DE GUZMAN, BANJO y SANTOS, DELA CRUZ, DONALDO y LOMIBAO, and LAMSEN, PETER y CO were arrested for illegal gambling. Subjects were arrested by virtue of Search Warrant issued by RTC Branch 53, Rosales, Pangasinan. Bet money in the total amount of Php 38,900.00 and betting paraphernalia were seized during the operation. Char M. Imbornal, representative of Globaltech, was not present in the premises. Arrested Subjects were temporarily detained at NBI-DADO pending their inquest proceedings at the Office of the Prosecutor. On March 7, 2019 , operatives of NBI-Cordillera Administrative Region (NBI-CAR) arrested LIBERTAD DOMDOM JACILDO, ARNEL TRANGIA JACILDO, and JORDAN DOMDOM JACILDO for selling endangered species. Subjects were arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from an information that Subject Libertad is the registered owner of Jacildo’s Handicraft selling assorted sea shells at Session Road, Baguio City, and some of of the sea shells being sold are prohibited as they are classified as endangered species. Together with the team from the BFAR-CAR, NBI operatives conducted the entrapment operation resulting in the arrest of the Subjects. Seized form the Subjects are six (6) pieces smooth top shells, (2) pieces chambered nautilus, two (2) pieces helmet shells, and three (3) pieces green snails with an aggregate market value of Php 36,200.00 Charges for violations of RA 10654 amending RA 8550 (The Philippine Fisheries Code of 1998) and RA 9147 (Wildlife Resources Conservation and Protection Act) were filed against the Subjects. On March 8, 2019 , operatives of NBI-Anti-Organized and Transnational Crimes Division (NBI-AOTCD) arrested GERLAD RYAN FALCIS y ORGA aka GERALD RYAN FALCIS y ORGA for violation of RA 9165 (Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002). Subject was arrested by virtue of Search Warrant issued by RTC Branch 100, Antipolo. Seized during the search among others were 8 pieces green substance high breed “kush”, 1piece plastic containing several grams of “kush”, cellphone, 8 sachets seeds, plastic bag with brown powder, container with residue, plastic containing orange substance, etc. Certification issued by FCD showed positive results for the presence of Marijuana with total weight of 184.2508 grams while the plastic with orange substance gave positive for methylenedioxy-methamphetamine (MDMA) known as Ecstasy weighing 0.2368 grams. Urine of the Subject was also positive for the presence of Tetrahydrocannabinol commonly known as Marijuana. Subject was charged before the City Prosecutor of Manila for the above-mentioned violation. On March 10, 2019 , joint operatives of NBI-Special Action Unit (NBI-SAU), NBI –Task Force Against Illegal Drugs (NBI-TFAID), and NBI- National Capital Region (NBI-NCR) arrested LUO GEN JIN, CHENG YIGUO, LIU SHENGHUI, DENG SHUIJIN, XIONG JINXIANG, XIONG JONGPENG, and XIONG JILONG, all Chinese nationals for Kidnapping/ Serious Illegal Detention. the operation was based on a complaint filed by Jian Shi Lun, brother of the victim, Jian Shi Xin. According to the complainant, his friend reported to him that the victim was kidnapped at Okada Manila in Parañaque City by unidentified Chinese nationals and illegally detained at an unidentified condominium in Manila. The kidnappers allow the victim to make calls to ask for ransom money in the amount of Php200,000.00. The victim called his brother and asked for help. Jian Shi Xin (victim) discreetly sent to his brother (complainant) the general location of the condominium where he was being detained and beaten. Unknown to the NBI operatives, the complainant through online money transfer, paid the kidnappers the ransom of Php200,000.00 for the release of his brother. On March 10, 2019, the victim was released near City of Dreams, Parañaque City. The victim told the NBI operatives that he was abducted at Okada Manila in Parañaque City and was detained and beaten at Balagtas Royale Mansions in Pasay City. Immediately, the NBI joint operatives rushed to the condominium unit where the victim was detained and found 5 Chinese nationals inside the condominium unit identified as Subjects LIU SHENGSHUI, DENG SHUIJIN, XIONG JINXIANG, XIONG JONPENG, and XIONG JILONG. The victim positively identified the group as his kidnappers but two other subjects were not in the condominium unit. The operatives received information that the two other subjects are in Solaire Resort and Casino in Parañaque City. The operatives then proceeded to the subject area and apprehended LUO GEN JIN and CHEN YIGUO, who were also positively identified by the victim as his kidnappers and brought to the NBI for the usual booking and arrest procedures. The subjects were brought before the Office of the Prosecutor of Pasay City for inquest proceedings and were all charged for kidnapping/ serious illegal detention as defined and penalized under Article 267 of the Revised Penal Code. On March 11, 2019 , operatives of NBI-Special Operations Group (NBI-SOG) arrested GREGGY ROSE C. GUMAPON for Falsification of Public Documents. Subject was arrested by virtue of Warrant of Arrest issued by Metropolitan Trial Court, Pasig City. Said warrant of Arrest was served based on the request of Mr. Elias F. David. NBI-SOG operatives conducted surveillance in areas where Subject Gumapon can be possibly located. In the afternoon of the aforementioned date, operatives were able to track down the Subject in Paranaque City and served the Warrant of Arrest. On March 12, 2019 , operatives of NBI-Intellectual Property Rights Division (NBI-IPRD) seized 436 bottles of E-Juice bearing the label Kit-Kat with an estimated value of 168,000.00. Items were seized in Antipolo City by virtue of Search Warrant. Charges for violation of RA 8293 (Intellectual Property Code of the Philipppines) were filed against VAPE SHOT and JULIET V. SANTOS. On March 12, 2019 , operatives of NBI-Intellectual Property Rights Division (NBI-IPRD) seized 50 boxes of counterfeit mosquito coils with an estimated amount of Php 205,000.00. Items were seized in San Simon, Pampanga by virtue of Search Warrant. Charges for violation of RA 8293 (Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines) were filed against ANDY LIM, HONG WEN QU, JOHN/JANE DOEs, and owners/operators of an establishment located at San Simon Industrial Park, KM 62, Quezon Road, Brgy. San Isidro, San Simon Pampanga. On March 14, 2019 , operatives of NBI-Environmental Crime Division (NBI-EnCD) arrested ELEZABETH RIVERA y BELLEN for trading and possession of 20 rare and endangered Golden Chicken Fern (Cibotium Barometz) in Binondo, Manila. Subject was arrested in an operation which stemmed from the report of DENR-Biodiversity Management Bureau. Subject was presented for inquest proceeding for violation of RA 9147 ((Wildlife Resources Conservation and Protection Act). On March 15, 2019 , operatives of NBI-Tagum District arrested JONAS BUENO y MARTEL for Murder. Subject was arrested by virtue of Warrant of Arrest issued by RTC Branch 25, Danao City, Cebu. Subject, as posted in social media, is also the PNP primary suspect in the brutal killing of 16-year old Christine Lee Silawan in Lapu-Lapu City, Cebu who was stabbed several times and skinned to death. On March 18, 2019 , operatives of NBI-National Capital Region (NBI-NCR) seized six (6) computers using unauthorized or unlicensed Siemen software. Items were seized in Calamba, Laguna by virtue of Search Warrants issued by RTC Branch 158, Pasig City for violation of RA 8293 (Copyright Infringement) against Prima Tech Philippines, Inc., Myeong Jae Cheon, Myung Hee Cheon, Young Pyo Kim, Gum Sun Park, Kyoung Rae Kim, and other owners/operators/stockholders/directors/employees of Prima Tech Philippines, Inc. located at Brgy. Punta, Calamba City, Laguna. Due to the copyright infringement caused by the search warrant respondent, the estimated loss or damage to the copyright holder is Php 12 Million. On March 18, 2019 , operatives of NBI-Cybercrime Division (NBI-CCD) arrested eighteen (18) Subjects, all are Chinese nationals, for Access Device Fraud and Online Illegal Gambling in Angeles City. Subjects were arrested by virtue of Search Warrant issued by RTC Brach 66, Capas, Tarlac. The operation stemmed from an information concerning activities involving Access Device Fraud and illegal online gambling being operated in Royal Genghis International Devt. Inc. located at 3 rd Floor, Savers Mall Bldg., Mc Arthur Highway, Balibago, Angeles City. Sufficient information warranting the application of Search Warrant was based on the verification process and surveillance operations conducted by the NBI operatives. The details of both illegal online activity and counterfeit access device are reflected in the on-site Digital Forensic Report. Mobile phones, desktop computers, laptops, blank java cards, skimming device, various debit cards, unused sim cards, flash drives, routers, and network hubs were seized in the premises. Results of the on-site forensic examination confirmed not only Access Device Fraud activity but also illegal gambling operations conducted by the Subjects who were caught in flagrante delicto. Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the Department of Justice, Office of the State Prosecutor, for violation of RA 8484 (Access Devices Regulation Act) and PD 1602 (Illegal Gambling Law) as amended, both in relation to RA 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012). On March 22, 2019 , operatives of NBI-Environmental Crime Division (NBI-EnCD) arrested WONG KI y YUNG and CHUA JOAN y SY for violation of RA 10654 (The Philippine Fisheries Code of 1998) and RA 9147 (Wildlife Resources Conservation and Protection Act). Subjects were arrested in entrapment operation conducted in Binondo, Manila against a certain establishment trading sea horse, an endangered specie. Recovered from the Subjects are 342 pieces of sea horse and 703 pieces of bird’s nest. Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the DOJ, Manila for the aforementioned violations. On March 19, 2019 , operatives of NBI-Dumaguete District Office (NBI-DUMDO) arrested TAÑARA, FRANCISCO y SAPASAP for alleged illegal extraction of sand and gravel without the necessary permits/licenses to do so. Subject was caught with his driven vehicle loaded with sand at the vicinity of Brgy. Soludpan, Bacong, Negros Oriental where extraction of sand and gravel are being done without the necessary permits/licenses. Laborers were able to scamper away as the operatives were approaching. Appropriate charges were filed against the arrested Subject. A follow-up operation will be conducted in the vicinity and other areas where sand and gravel were allegedly being illegally extracted. On March 20, 2019 , operatives of NBI-North Eastern Mindanao Regional Office (NBI-NEMRO) arrested STEPHEN DAVE OROSCO y DACUT for selling marijuana. Subject was arrested in a buy-bust operation which stemmed from the information that certain individuals including minors are allegedly engaged in the selling of illegal drugs inside and outside the different schools in Cagayan de Oro City. Investigation conducted and it was found out that certain “Dave”, together with still to be identified persons are engaged in selling marijuana. NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION

On March 1, 2019 , operatives of NBI-Laguna District Office (NBI-LAGDO) arrested LLOYD ANJAIL y MONTEGREJO, MARIO ANJAIL y MONTEGREJO, and ROBIN JAY BUTAD y SANTONIA. Subjects falsely represented themselves as employees of NBI while distributing NBI online application forms in front of Lianas Supermarket, Brgy. Parian, Calamba, Laguna. Subjects were wearing NBI bull caps and t-shirts with big NBI letters printed on it. They also have fake NBI badge and ID. Charges for violation of Article 177 and 179 of the Revised Penal Code were filed against the Subjects before the Office of the City Prosecutor of Calamba City. On March 2, 2019 , operatives of NBI-MIMAROPA arrested KRIS SY ONG and FRANCES KAYE LIBRODO MARU in two separate operations for violation of RA 9165 (Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002). Subjects were arrested in event monitoring conducted at the MALASIMBO Music and Arts Festival 2019 in response to the request for assistance of PDEA MIMAROPA IV-B. Subject KRIS SY ONG was arrested around 9:00 in the evening and confiscated during the operation were one (1) piece small self-sealing transparent plastic sachet containing brown powdered substance suspected to be marijuana resins, one (1) piece self-sealing transparent plastic sachet used as container, one (1) improvised pipe used for smoking with suspected marijuana residue, one (1) piece wooden stick used as paraphernalia, and one (1) piece black lighter used as paraphernalia. On the other hand, Subject FRANCES KAYE LIBRODO MARU was arrested around 11:50 in the evening. Confiscated were one (1) piece self-sealing transparent plastic sachet containing one capsule with brownish powder suspected to be ecstacy weighing 0.01 gram with an estimated market value of Php 1,000.00. Arrested Subjects are now under temporary custody of PDEA MIMAROPA while documents were prepared for inquest proceedings before the Provincial Prosecutor’s Office for above-mentioned violation. On March 2, 2019 , operatives of NBI-Special Action Unit (NBI-SAU) arrested SHAO LEI for violation of RA 9165 (Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002). By virtue of Search warrant issued by RTC Branch 37, Manila against CHU WEI KUN, YU HSIEN HSU, and occupants of Unit 1002, Monarch Parksuites, Asean Business Park, Paranaque City, operatives searched the said area and yielded three (3) pieces of transparent plastic sachets, three (3) lighters, one (1) plastic box containing used foils and white crystalline substance. NBI-Forensic Chemistry Division (NBI-FCD) issued a certification that the contents of the plastic sachets tested positive results for the presence of methamphetamine hydrochloride with a net weight of 0.0678 grams. Subject SHAO LEI was brought for inquest proceedings before the Paranaque City Prosecutor’s Office. On March 4, 2019 , operatives of NBI-National Capital Region arrested MARIVIC GRIMALDO MANZANO by virtue of Warrant of Arrest for Estafa. Subject was arrested in her residence located at Unit 215, Tower 2, Urban Deca Homes Campville, Muntinlupa City after being positively identified by the complainant Menchita Valencia Banzuela. Subject was brought to NBI Main Office for the booking procedures and temporary detention. On March 5, 2019 , operatives of NBI-MIMAROPA arrested KRISTINE BARRIENTOS for human trafficking. Subject was arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from a report that she is a notorious pimp who operated in the City of Calapan. She catered to tourists who visit the province of Oriental Mindoro by providing them sexual services from her girls in exchange of fees ranging from Php 1,500-Php 2,500. Subject was arrested after receiving the entrapment money from the poseur customers. Four (4) trafficked victims were rescued and were subsequently turned over to DSWD for custody. Subject was charged for violation of RA 9208 (Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2003) before the inquest prosecutor of Calapan City. On March 6, 2019 , operatives of NBI-Bacolod District Office (NBI-BACDO) arrested FELIPE SANCHO JR. y TIBIRO for selling illegal drugs. Subject was arrested in a buy-bust operation where he was caught en flagrante in violation of Section 5 (Sale of Dangerous Drugs) of RA 9165 (Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002). Eight (8) pieces of lighters, five (5) tooters, one (1) bundle of transparent plastic sachets used for repacking of methamphetamine hydrochloride (shabu), Php 3,090 proceeds of illegal drugs trade, one (1) transparent plastic sachet comtaining white crystalline substance suspected to be shabu, and two (2) small transparent plastic sachets containing residues of suspected shabu were recovered. Subject was immediately brought to NBI-BACDO for the booking procedures. He was presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor for the aforementioned violation. Subjects were arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from the information from Destiny Rescue Phils. regarding the human trafficking activities particularly sexual exploitation of minor victims committed by pimps in the areas of Pasig, Makati, Quezon City, and Rizal. Initial verification and surveillance operations conducted confirmed that a certain “Jaika” was maintaining, harboring, offering, and delivering girls for quick sexual intercourse to his clients. With this, in coordination with the representatives from DSWD, local police, and barangay official an entrapment operation was conducted which resulted in the arrest of the Subjects. JAIKA and JOHN ROMEL BUENO y BANDULO were presented for inquest proceedings before the City Prosecutors Office of Antipolo for violation of RA 9208 (Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2003) as amended by RA 10364 (Expanded Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2012) and violation of RA 7610 (Special Protection of. Children Against Child Abuse, Exploitation and Discrimination Act). Allegedly, Subject was among those who served as augmentation force to the ASG who kidnapped them at the diving resort in Sipadan, Pulao, Sabah, Malaysia on April 23, 2000. Subject Gadiano brought with her three (3) other girls, one of whom was Subject Custodio who left for a bit to fetch more girls and returned with five (5) more. At this juncture, the poseur-clients gave the pre-arranged signal to the strike team, which immediately arrested the two (2) above-named Subjects. The operation also resulted in the rescue of seven (7) victims, six (6) of whom were found to be minors based on the dental examination performed by the NBI – Odontology Division. body: PRESS STATEMENT November 12, 2024 The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) is proud to celebrate its 88th founding anniversary, with the theme “, , ”, marking decades of dedicated service to the people. To commemorate this significant milestone, the Bureau will be having celebratory events that will start on November 14, 2024. body: PRESS STATEMENT June 05, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } In line with the thrust of NBI Director JUDGE JAIME B. SANTIAGO (Ret.) to ensure not only the thorough investigation of cases but also their speedy resolution, the NBI- International Airport Investigation Division (IAID) arrested MANUELITO MELIA CAMACHO aka MONCHING, accused in the murder of Cebu lawyer JOEY LUIS WEE in 2020. The investigation that led to the filing of this case and issuance of a warrant of arrest was conducted by the NBI Cebu District Office (CEBDO). Per report, the Police Intelligence and Investigation Division -Airport Police (PIID) arrested one JAY-R REYES y SANTOS for theft, unjust vexation and resistance and disobedience to a person in authority. These charges are pending with the MTC Branch 166-Pasay City. During Jay-R’s detention, a fight broke out between him and his partner, where it was eventually revealed that JAY-R’s real name is MANUELITO MELIA CAMACHO also known as MONCHING. The Chief of the PIID requested a record check on the said name. Upon record check, it was found that MONCHING has a warrant of Arrest for Murder, issued by the RTC Branch 10, Cebu City. This information was communicated with the Agent-in-Charge of the Cebu District Office (CEBDO), who confirmed to the PIID the positive identification of JAY-R REYES also known as MANUELITO MELIA CAMACHO. Accordingly, the IAID served the Warrant of Arrest on CAMACHO at the office of the Airport Police, Pasay City. During his arrest, CAMACHO admitted that he was the same person charged in the above-named case. It can be recalled that on November 23,2020, two gunmen shot lawyer Joey Luis Wee, 51, in broad daylight as he walked from his car up to the stairs of his office in Barangay Kasambagan, Cebu City, at around 1:30 pm. This case was investigated by the Cebu District Office. Director Santiago commended the agents of the NBI-IAID for the successful implementation of the warrant. He also lauded the agents of NBI-CEBDO and the elements of the PIID for their contribution in the said arrest. The Director emphasized the importance of coordination between NBI offices and other law enforcement agencies.

body: PRESS STATEMENT May 21, 2022 NBI FILES CHARGES AGAINST MUNICIPAL ENGINEER FOR GRAFT AND CORRUPT PRACTICES In line with the relentless campaign of the government against erring government employees and officials, operatives of NBI-Bayombong District Office (NBI-BAYDO) filed charges against a Municipal Engineer of Local Government Unit of Aglipay, Quirino, for extorting money from subcontractors of government projects. NBI Officer-In-Charge (OIC) Director Eric B. Distor identified the Subject as ENGR. DANILO B. CASTILLO, Municipal Engineer of the Local Government Unit of Aglipay, Quirino. The case stemmed from the complaint filed by complainants who own and manage a company that subcontracts government projects awarded to the winning bidders/contractors from different municipalities of Quirino Province. In their construction of projects, they met and transacted with Engr. Castillo. As the Municipal Engineer, the latter has to intervene in those projects in his official capacity since he was the one who approves complainant’s requests for concrete pouring, installation of steel trusses, and others. His work also includes checking of the projects completed by the complainants to ensure that the materials used were not substandard and that they comply with the project’s plan and design and approving the release of the funds of those projects. In those projects handled by complainants in Aglipay, Quirino, it became Engr. Castillo’s practice to demand money and construction materials from complainants as “SOP” or share from the projects. According to the complainants, Engr. Castillo usually demands whenever they needed Engr. Castillo’s signature for the approval of their requests and for the release of the fund for the project. In January 2022, before the start of the construction of a certain project, Engr. Castillo demanded Php 10,000.00 as initial payment for his “SOP” or share and as a grease money for him to facilitate or expedite the approval of their requests and billings. Complainants reluctantly agreed and gave the requested amount to Engr. Castillo. In February 2022, complainants requested for Engr. Castillo’s approval for the installation of steel trusses in the public market buildings. Engr. Castillo told the complainant that before the approval of the request, they have to give Php 50,000.00. Complainant pleaded and told him that they could only produce Php 20,000.00 since they had not yet collected the billing for the project. Engr. Castillo granted the request and immediately approved the same. After giving the money to Engr. Castillo, the latter reiterated that the share or percentage given to him was inadequate and that his share would be 5% of the gross amount of the project which is Php 250,000.00. He added that complainants are obliged to give him the said amount since he was the one who approves their request. On February 23, 2022, complainant called Engr. Castillo because they needed his approval for the pouring request for the slab or flooring of the building. Engr. Castillo pressed for the whole amount of his “SOP” and told the complainant that he will approve the request if they will give the whole amount he was demanding. Feeling that the money extorted by Engr. Castillo was already excessive and they could no longer produce it, complainants sought the assistance of NBI-BAYDO for the conduct of the entrapment operation. NBI-BAYDO immediately planned the entrapment operation to arrest Engr. Castillo while in the act of receiving money from the complainant. However, the same failed because of the possible leakage of the entrapment. Accordingly, NBI-BAYDO filed charges against ENGR. DANILO B. CASTILLO before the Office of the Ombudsman for violations of RA 3019 (Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act) and RA 6713 (The Code of Conduct and Ethical Standards for Public Officials and Employees).

body: PRESS STATEMENT October 24, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } In response to an order from National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Director Judge Jaime B. Santiago (Ret.) to intensify the campaign against sexual abuse and exploitation, the NBI Sarangani District Office (NBI-SARDO) arrested an individual in General Santos City for Rape by Sexual Assault, as defined and penalized under Article 266-A of the Revised Penal Code (RPC), as amended. On October 22, 2025, the victim, accompanied by a representative from the City Social Welfare and Development (CSWD) of General Santos City, formally filed a complaint before the NBI-SARDO. According to the complainant, she was sexually abused and assaulted by her biological father in General Santos City. On the same day, a hot-pursuit operation was launched, prompting NBI-SARDO Agents to initiate a manhunt to apprehend the suspect. Through intelligence gathering, the Agents discovered that the suspect was working as a tricycle driver at the General Santos Public Market. The operatives quickly proceeded to the target area, and after an hour of surveillance, the suspect arrived and was positively identified by the victim. At this juncture, the NBI-SARDO Agents approached the suspect and placed him under arrest. The Subject was taken to the NBI-SARDO office, where he underwent the standard booking procedures and was charged with the aforementioned violations. Director Santiago lauded the Agents of NBI-SARDO for their successful operation that led to the arrest of the Subject. He reaffirmed the NBI’s commitment to protecting women and children from all forms of sexual abuse and exploitation.

body: PRESS STATEMENT August 13, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } Under the leadership of NBI Director Judge Jaime B. Santiago (Ret.), National Bureau of Investigation – Bayombong District Office (NBI-BAYDO) has filed criminal charges of Murder against seven (7) police officers of Nagtipunan, Qurino. The officers, identified as POLICE MAJOR FERNANDO G. MANAYOD, POLICE OFFICERS JOREY CUMAHLING, JIMBOY IRANG, DELMAR SALVADOR, ALLAN FIAD-ONG, and JONATHAN LIMMONG, are accused in connection with the fatal shooting of Jim B. White on May 28, 2025, in San Pugo, Nagtipunan, Quirino. Investigations revealed that Mr. White, a member of the Bugkalot-llongot Indigenous Cultural Community, had previously reached a tribal-mediated amicable settlement in his pending criminal cases. This was supported by an Affidavit of Desistance and scheduled for voluntary surrender on May 29, 2025. The Provincial Director of Quirino was aware of such tribal arrangement. However, a day before the scheduled surrender, police operatives allegedly staged an ambush-style operation along a remote uphill trail, resulting in White’s death. NBI medico legal findings showed that all bullet entry wounds were on White’s back, indicating that he was shot while defenseless. This finding contradicts the officers’ claim that the victim fired first. The NBI also conducted an on-site investigation in the far-flung mountainous area where the crime occurred and concluded that the killing was executed with treachery. This prompted the filing of charges against the named Subjects before the Office of the Provincial Prosecutor of Quirino on August 5, 2025. Director Santiago commended the NBI-BAYDO for its meticulous investigation and emphasized that no one is above the law, not even those sworn to enforce it.

body: In line with the continuing drive of the government against individuals taking advantage of the crisis relative to Covid-19 outbreak, operatives of National Bureau of Investigation-Anti-Human Trafficking Division (NBI-AHTRAD) arrested two (2) Subjects for alleged hoarding, profiteering and price manipulation of particularly disposable face mask. OIC-Director Eric B. Distor identified the Subjects as JERICA CANDELARIA REYES and ARNOLD RAMOS RAZON. Subjects were arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from the information received that Jezhan Enterprises, with business address at 419 Tandang Sora Avenue, Quezon City, is selling medical supplies such as Personal Protective Equipment (PPE), face masks, and thermal scanners at a price grossly in excess of its real price or higher than the price ceiling implemented by the Department of Trade and Industry (DTI). Acting on the said information, NBI-AHTRAD operatives verified the information by pretending as buyer of medical supplies and it was confirmed that Jezhan Enterprises is selling medical supplies higher than the price ceiling. The price of the PPE is more or less Php 400, N95 mask’s highest price is Php 105, and thermal scanner’s highest price is Php 3,400. Subjects were selling the PPE at Php 4,500, N95 mask at Php 250, and thermal scanner at Php 5,000 which are clearly beyond the price ceiling implemented by the DTI. With this, a buy-bust operation was conducted on March 28, 2020 by meeting the Subjects and to receive the 50 kits isolation PPE, 50 kits cover all PPE, 100 pieces N95 mask, and 3 pieces thermal scanner. Items were ordered through Viber and amounting to Php 390,000. The operation resulted in the arrest of Subject JERICA CANDELARIA REYES and her employer Subject ARNOLD RAMOS RAZON who introduced himself as the general manager of Jezhan Enterprises. Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor, Quezon City for violation of Section 5 (Profiteering) of RA 7581 (Price Act) in relation to RA 7394 (Consumer Act of the Philippines) and Section 6 of RA 11469 (Bayanihan to Heal as One Act).

body: PRESS STATEMENT March 17, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } NBI DISMANTLES CEBU CITY DRUG DEN; 15 ARRESTED IN DRUG RAID OPERATION PASAY CITY, Philippines – On March 12, 2026, the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) dismantled a suspected illegal drug den operating within a local lodging house, resulting in the arrest of fifteen (15) individuals. The case stemmed from an intelligence report regarding a drug den operating for a fee within a low-cost lodging house. Following the report, NBI-CEBDO agents conducted surveillance operations to confirm the illicit activities. Operatives from the NBI-CEBDO conducted an entrapment operation on March 12, 2026, in close coordination with the NBI-CEVRO, the Philippine Drug Enforcement Agency (PDEA), the Office of the Regional State Prosecutor (Region 7), and local barangay officials. During the raid, two (2) maintainers were arrested while receiving marked money from an undercover agent. Simultaneously, agents discovered thirteen (13) individuals inside various rooms of the establishment caught in the act of using suspected shabu. The arrested Subjects were presented before the Office of the City Prosecutor in Cebu City to face formal charges for violation of Republic Act No. 9165 (Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002), as amended. The charges specifically include Section 6 (Maintenance of a Den), Section 7 (Visiting a Den), Section 12 (Possession of Drug Paraphernalia), and Section 15 (Use of Illegal Drugs). A separate charge for violating Section 6 was also filed against the owner of the motel/boarding house for allowing the establishment to be utilized for such illicit activities. “The NBI remains committed and steadfast in supporting the government’s effort against drug traffickers and their cohorts in partnership with other concerned law enforcement agencies and parties,” said NBI Director Atty. Melvin A. Matibag. #NBIServes

body: National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) OIC-Director Eric B. Distor will lead top officials of the NBI in this year’s Command Conference. Held annually during the celebration of the anniversary of the NBI, the one-day Command Conference is scheduled on Thursday, November 11, 2021 at the NBI gymnasium in Manila. Joining OIC-Director Distor are the members of the Directorial Staff, namely: Assistant Director Medardo G. de Lemos, also the Over-all Chairperson of this year’s 85th NBI Anniversary; Deputy Director for Financial Service (DDFS) Jose Doloiras; Deputy Director for Regional Operations Service (DDROS) Antonio Pagatpat; Deputy Director for Information and Communication Technology Service (DDICTS) Jose Justo Yap; Deputy Director for Administrative Service (DDAS) Eleanor Rachel Marfil-Angeles; Deputy Director for Investigation Service (DDInvS) Vicente De Guzman III; Deputy Director for Legal Service (DDLS) Leo Edwin Leuterio; Roel Bolivar, OIC for Intelligence Service (IntlS) and Deputy Director for Forensic Investigation Service (DDFIS) and concurrent Spokesperson of the NBI Ferdinand Lavin. The 17 NBI Regional Directors, Agent-In-Charge of the 42 District Offices strategically located nationwide and the Chiefs of Manila-based Divisions will also take part in the whole-day Command Conference. OIC-Director Distor will render a report on the status of implementation of Modernization Program in accordance with the provisions of R.A. 10867 or the NBI Reorganization and Modernization enacted on June 23, 2016, the Anti-COVID 19 Action program and Vaccination to protect the health and safety of NBI personnel and the future direction of the NBI. Other issues to be discussed will include the developments in the newly-established District Offices in strategic areas of the Provinces. Distor will also receive reports on growth and establishment of NBI Satellite Offices with Clearance processing in response to President Rodrigo Roa Duterte’s call to agencies of the government to bring the government services closer to the people. OIC Distor said, “I am glad to report that with the aggressive stance of the NBI in reaching out to more people in order to provide the services of the NBI, we now cover 60% of the 81 provinces of the country. Only in a span of two (2) years since I assume as head of this agency, we have created and established 18 District Offices or an average of about 2 District Offices per month and NBI will continue to do so. They will be under the supervision of the Deputy Director for Regional Operations Service and Regional Directors”, Distor emphasized.

body: PRESS STATEMENT April 21, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } PRESS RELEASE | NBI ARRESTS THREE FOR HUMAN TRAFFICKING; RESCUES 21 TRAFFICKED VICTIMS Pasay City, Philippines – On April 15, 2026, a joint team of NBI-Tarlac District Office (NBI-TARDO) and NBI-Pampanga District Office (NBI-PAMDO), together with the City Social Development Office of Mabalacat City (CSDO Mabalacat), arrested three individuals in Mabalacat City, Pampanga, for violation of Republic Act No. 9208 (Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2003) as amended by R.A. body: PRESS STATEMENT March 05, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } NBI ARRESTS PERPETRATOR OF “SANGLA-TIRA-BENTA” SCAM IN RIZAL PASAY CITY, Philippines – The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) announces the successful arrest of a woman accused of orchestrating a fraudulent “Sangla-Tira-Benta” scheme targeting property renters and buyers in Rizal. On February 24, 2026, operatives from the NBI-Rizal District Office (NBI-RIZDO) conducted an entrapment operation that led to the arrest of the Subject in Cainta, Rizal. Investigation revealed that Subject misrepresented herself as the owner of a condominium unit, advertising it for rent in a Facebook group dedicated to “sangla-tira” arrangements. The victim entered into an agreement with the Subject, loaning her Php300,000.00. In exchange, the victim was allowed to occupy the unit as a concession for the monthly interest. Despite promises, the Subject never provided documentation proving her ownership of the unit. Subsequently, the Subject offered to sell the leased unit to the victim for Php1,500,000.00. Relying on their prior agreement and occupancy, the victim agreed to purchase the property. The scam was exposed when the legitimate owner of the condo unit appeared and demanded payment for two months of rental delinquency, threatening eviction if the debt was not settled. The real owner confirmed that the Subject had no authority to sell the property. Investigation further revealed that the Subject had also illegally mortgaged the legitimate owner’s parking slot without authorization. The Subject failed to remit parking rental fees totaling Php110,000.00 for one year, along with a Php30,000.00 deficiency for the condo unit rental. Following the complaint, NBI-RIZDO agents executed an entrapment operation on February 24, 2026, catching the Subject in the act of selling the fraudulent unit to the victim. The Subject was presented for inquest proceedings on February 25, 2026, at the Provincial Prosecutors’ Office of Rizal for violations of Estafa under Article 315 of the Revised Penal Code, as amended by R.A. 10951. The NBI remains steadfast in its commitment to protecting the public from predatory schemes that exploit the hard-earned savings of Filipinos. This arrest serves as a stern warning to fraudsters who use social media to orchestrate complex property scams like ‘Sangla-Tira-Benta. #NBIServes

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today said operatives of NBI-Cavite District Office (NBI-CAVIDO) arrested a sexual predator who victimized a minor in Cavite City. NBI Officer-In-Charge (OIC) Director Eric B. Distor identified Subject as FROILAN ESTOLANO y ZARAGOSA. OIC Distor said the case stemmed from the complaint of the parent of a 14 – year old victim against alias MIGZ JACOB JAVIER whose true name was is FROILAN ESTOLANO y ZARAGOSA. According to the complaint, Subject FROILAN is a flower/plant trader residing at Purok 5 Pasong Langka, Municipality of Silang Cavite. Complainant stated that Subject FROILAN befriended her daughter thru Facebook. By accident, complainant discovered the exchange of lewd and lustful conversation between Subject and her daughter. Further, Subject threatened the minor that he will expose their chat conversation if she will not send nude photos. Out of fear, the victim sent her nude photos to the Subject. body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) announced today the arrest of a woman in Angeles City, Pampanga for human trafficking. NBI Officer-In-Charge Eric B. Distor identified the subject as 34-year old mother , who was arrested by operatives of the NBI- Anti Human Trafficking Division (NBI-AHTRAD) on May 14, 2020 in an entrapment operation. body: PRESS STATEMENT February 25, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } NBI SMASHES CYBERCRIME HUB IN PAMPANGA; 14 ARRESTED FOR TARGETING RETIREES IN FINANCIAL SCAM PASAY CITY, Philippines – The National Bureau of Investigation-National Capital Region (NBI-NCR) has successfully dismantled a major cyber-financial scamming operation following a high-stakes raid in Clark Freeport, Pampanga. The operation resulted in the arrest of 14 individuals allegedly involved in a sophisticated “social engineering” scheme primarily targeting retirees and vulnerable citizens. On February 21, 2026, NBI-NCR agents executed a Warrant to Search, Seize, and Examine Computer Data (WSSECD) issued by the Regional Trial Court Branch 132 of Makati City. The tactical strike took place at a facility within the Clark Freeport Zone. Upon arrival, NBI agents—coordinated with the Clark Development Corp. (CDC) Security Services Group—served the warrant and conducted an onsite digital forensic examination. The search yielded a significant haul of electronic evidence including high-end computer devices and smartphones, numerous SIM cards used for fraudulent communications and detailed ledgers of potential victims’ personal information. The group’s “social engineering” scheme involved harvesting personal data through deception to target victims with fraudulent investment offers. After being tricked into clicking phishing links, victims were coerced into depositing large sums of money into a fake platform, only to be locked out and denied access to their funds once the transfers were complete. The 14 Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings for violation of Republic Act 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act) and Republic Act 12010 (Anti-Financial Account Scamming Act). The NBI issues a stern warning to the public to remain hyper-vigilant against the rising tide of unsolicited investment schemes and “too good to be true” financial opportunities. Citizens are strongly advised to exercise extreme caution when receiving unexpected calls or messages and are urged never to share sensitive personal information or financial credentials through suspicious links. To protect your hard-earned savings, always verify the legitimacy of any investment platform with the appropriate regulatory bodies before committing any funds. #NBIServes

body: PRESS STATEMENT June 04, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } The National Bureau of Investigation – International Airport Investigation Division (NBI-IAID), under the leadership of Director JUDGE JAIME B. SANTIAGO (Ret.), arrested one (1) individual at the NAIA Terminal 1, Pasay City, for violation of Article 172 (Falsification by Private Individuals) of the Revised Penal Code. On 29 May 2025, the NAIA Task Force Against Trafficking (NAIA-TFAT) endorsed a certain MELISSA DY y BERNADOS to the NBI-IAID for investigation upon discovery that the Subject is holding a counterfeit border stamp impressions on her passport and airline boarding pass by the Immigration Officer. Investigation disclosed that Subject DY was bound for Thailand via a Cebu Pacific flight and departing at NAIA Terminal 3, Pasay City on 28 May 2025. She was recruited for employment to an offshore gaming company in Thailand as a Customer Service Representative with a promised salary of P52,000.00. On the day of her flight, Subject received instructions from a certain @Ahao through Telegram to proceed in front of the OFW lounge located on the 3rd floor of the terminal and to wait for their contact by the name of @Richard. When @Richard came, he took her passport and boarding pass and returned the same several hours later with impressions of BIBS No. 1198 on both documents. While the Subject was in a queue to the Immigration counters, an I-PROBES Immigration Officer noticed that her passport and boarding pass had already been imprinted with departure stamps, prompting the officer to refer her outright for primary inspection. The Primary Officer made the assessment and remarked that the stamps were questionable. Thereafter, the Subject was brought for secondary inspection to validate the earlier assessment. The examination conducted on the BIBS No. 1198 by Immigration Document Examiners found the same to be counterfeit. Upon the conclusion of the investigation that she deliberately and knowingly used her passport containing the forged Immigration border stamp to facilitate her exit from the country, evading the pre-departure formalities of the Immigration, the NBI-IAID arrested Subject DY. Subject DY was brought to Inquest Proceedings held virtually before the Office of the City Prosecutor in Pasay City on 30 May 2025 for violation of Article 172 of the Revised Penal Code.

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today announced the arrest of an employee of the Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR) by the NBI-Vigan District Office (NBI-VIDO) inside BIR office in Bantay, Ilocos Sur for extorting money. NBI Officer-in-Charge (OIC) Director Eric B. Distor identified the subject as CYNGTHIA G. NONES. Director said that the operation stemmed from a complaint filed by the victim of Subject Nones. The complainant alleged that she owned a business and Subject Nones of BIR in Bantay, Ilocos Sur is extorting from her P150,000.00. Subject Nones informed the complainant of her assessed tax liability of Php 300,000.00 for a certain tax period. The complainant then asked for a breakdown of her tax assessment, which showed that her tax liability is only P150,000.00 instead of Php 300,000.00. The complainant asked Subject Nones and for a breakdown of the other half, which Subject responded that the Php 150,000.00 will not appear on paper as they allegedly used some of it for their expenses in processing Complainant’s documents as well as a form of compensation for their reducing of her tax liability in the official records. The complainant proceeded to the payment of her official tax liability of P150,000.00 but the Subject demanded P150,000.00 as their compensation in reducing her tax liability. The complainant then asked Subject enough time to raise the money for fear that the BIR-RDO will make business difficult for her. Due to her fear, the complainant was compelled to report the incident to NBI-VIDO. On November 18, 2021, the complainant informed NBI-VIDO that Subject Nones instructed her to deliver the Php 150,000.00 to her office at the BIR office but it didn’t pushed through because the Subject instructed the complainant that she will just get the money from the latter’s house but the same also did not push through. Subject Nones and the complainant agreed that if the latter cannot come to the subject’s office in Bantay, La Union she will order one of her drivers to deliver the money to the Subject’s office. Thus, on November 19, 2021, NBI-VIDO proceeded to the target meeting area outside the office of Subject Nones. The complainant’s car driven by one of the operatives stopped in front of the BIR office in Bantay, La Union where the Subject approached the vehicle and received the marked money from the complainant. At this juncture, NBI-VIDO operatives immediately arrested the subject. Subject Nones was presented for Inquest proceedings before the Provincial Prosecutors Office for Direct Bribery as defined and penalized under Article 210 of the Revised Penal Code as amended; violation of Section 269 (d) of R.A. 8424, otherwise known as the “Tax Reform Act of 1997”; violation of Section 7 (d) of R.A. 6713, otherwise known as the “Code of Conduct and Ethical Standards for Public Officers”; violation of Section 3 (b) or R.A. 3019, otherwise known as the “Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act”; Robbery with Intimidation as defined and penalized under Article 293 of the Revised Penal Code (RPC); and administrative complaint for Grave Misconduct under pertinent provisions of the Civil Service Law.

body: PRESS STATEMENT June 17, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } Under the supervision of NBI Director JUDGE JAIME B. SANTIAGO (Ret.), the National Bureau of Investigation – Bataan District Office (NBI-BATADO), on June 1, 2025, arrested ALVIN BAGUIO, a registered business owner of Field Sensation’s Bar, along with four others identified as REDEN ROA, JOHN PARRO, SHIRLY CALILONG, and MARILYN FERRER, all of whom were engaged in human trafficking activities in Barangay Balibago, Angeles City. The operation stemmed from a referral received on May 19, 2025, from Destiny Rescue Pilipinas Incorporated, concerning the sex trafficking activities at the said local entertainment bar. Surveillance confirmed that female entertainers were being offered to customers for sexual services under the guise of “barfine” transactions with rates ranging from P5,000 to P10,000. Thus, NBI agents carried out a coordinated entrapment and rescue operation. Arrested Subjects were responsible for managing, recruiting, and facilitating the trafficking scheme. The said operation also led to the rescue of 45 individuals, including 13 minors. Subjects were charged for violations of Republic Act No. 9208, as amended by R.A. 10364 and R.A. 11862, also known as the “Expanded Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2022.” All rescued victims have been turned over to the appropriate social welfare agency for proper care and counseling. The NBI remains committed to the fight against human trafficking and safeguarding the rights and welfare of vulnerable individuals from any threat of violence and exploitation, and ensuring the prosecution of persons involved in trafficking.

body: PRESS STATEMENT November 20, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } The National Bureau of Investigation-Cavite North District Office (NBI-CAVIDO North) arrested eight (8 Chinese nationals in Bacoor City, Cavite, for violation of Republic Act No. 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012) in relation to R.A. No. 12010 (Financial Accounts Scamming Act). The arrested individuals were identified as CHEN XING HE, LIU YONG CHANG, TANG LAO YA, XIAO LONG, XIAO LIU a.k.a. “LI TIN YANG”, LIANG YAOCAI a.k.a. “XIAO WEN, LI XIANG, and XIAO KAI. The operation stemmed from the information received by the NBI-CAVIDO North regarding the illegal online activities being conducted in a residential house in Bacoor City, perpetrated by a group of Chinese nationals. Verification and surveillance operations conducted by the NBI-CAVIDO North agents confirmed the veracity of the information. Subsequently, the Agents applied for a Warrant to Search, Seize, and Examine Computer Data (WSSECD), which was granted by the Regional Trial Court, Branch 110, Bacoor City. On November 15, 2025, Agents of NBI-CAVIDO North implemented the WSSECD against the premises of Chinese nationals located in Bacoor City, Cavite. The operation resulted in the seizure of various computer devices and assorted cellular phones. On-site Triage/examination of the seized items resulted in a positive finding that the items were used in online social engineering schemes. On November 17, 2025, the arrested Chinese nationals were presented for inquest proceedings regarding the aforementioned violations before the Department of Justice (DOJ) in Manila. OIC Director Atty. Angelito DLP Magno emphasized that the success of the recent operation underscores the NBI’s unwavering dedication to tackling cybercrime. He noted that this achievement not only highlights the Bureau’s effective strategies in addressing digital crimes but also reinforces their commitment to protecting the public from the growing threats in cyberspace.

body: The alleged Tiktok user who made a threat in his Tiktok social media post to assassinate presidential candidate Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos voluntarily surrendered to the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI). NBI OIC-Director Eric B. Distor said that Ruel ‘Bong’ Ricafort went to the NBI-Anti Organized and Transnational Crime Division (NBI-AOTCD) yesterday morning thru a friend and expressed his desire to voluntarily submit himself for investigation to clear his name. Ricafort likewise manifested his intention to file complaint against those persons who maliciously used his name, Director Distor added. In January 2022, a Tiktok video went viral in social media platform wherein a certain BONG RICAFORT threatened to assassinate former Senator and Presidential candidate Ferdinand ‘Bongbong’ Marcos, Jr. In his statement to the NBI, Ricafort said that when he was informed of the video, he searched and viewed the video and found out that someone illegally used his Tiktok account making it appear that his group plans to assassinate Bongbong Marcos.

NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION

The alleged Tiktok user who made a threat in his Tiktok social media post to assassinate presidential candidate Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos voluntarily surrendered to the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI). NBI OIC-Director Eric B. Distor said that Ruel ‘Bong’ Ricafort went to the NBI-Anti Organized and Transnational Crime Division (NBI-AOTCD) yesterday morning thru a friend and expressed his desire to voluntarily submit himself for investigation to clear his name. Ricafort likewise manifested his intention to file complaint against those persons who maliciously used his name, Director Distor added. In January 2022, a Tiktok video went viral in social media platform wherein a certain BONG RICAFORT threatened to assassinate former Senator and Presidential candidate Ferdinand ‘Bongbong’ Marcos, Jr. In his statement to the NBI, Ricafort said that when he was informed of the video, he searched and viewed the video and found out that someone illegally used his Tiktok account making it appear that his group plans to assassinate Bongbong Marcos.

Sapad and Joy V. Agassid. · On April 11, 2022, operatives of NBI- Anti-Fraud Division (NBI-AFD) arrested JONAS P. AYUSA and MARLON CZAR L. REYES in an operation in the City of Manila. the operation stemmed from a complaint filed by the representative of Maynilad Water Services Inc. (Maynilad) alleging that two (2) private firetrucks are involved in unauthorized siphoning of water from Maynilad’s fire hydrants. According to the complaint, Maynilad conducted monitoring activities between third (3 rd ) and fourth (4 th ) week of March 2022 in the areas covered under its Manila Business Area. Maynilad personnel discovered that private firetrucks siphoning water from Maynilad’s fire hydrants without authority and supplying the same to business establishments. Maynilad averred that one of these firetrucks is identified as a blue fire truck with plate number RLG 373 was seen delivering water to MEI SUM TEA HOUSE (Mei Sum) located in Binondo, Manila. According to Maynilad, Mei Sum have long been disconnected from the water supply of Maynilad for non-payment of bills and/or penalties and that there were no emergencies that could have triggered the said delivery of water. After confirming the illegal activities of the Subjects, NBI-AFD operatives conducted the entrapment operation and resulted in the arrest of the Subjects. Believing with the representations of Subject Bueno, Sapad deposited Php 63,200.00 in the BDO account of the Subject. Meanwhile, Agassid claimed that Subject Bueno offered her work in Dubai as a cleaner and was told that they will travel first to Singapore as tourists while preparing for her visa for Dubai. Subjects will be recommended to be charged with and be prosecuted for violation of RA 9287 before the Office of the City Prosecutor, Tagum City. · On April 11, 2022, operatives of NBI- Anti-Graft Division (NBI-AGD) filed charges before the Office of the Ombudsman against officers of PhilHealth Regional Office – National Capital Region (PRO-NCR) Accreditation Committee in relation to Health Care Provider (HCP) accreditation renewal. The PRO-NCR officials and personnel were identified as DR. NENITA EPIFANIA F. BALBUENA, DR. IMELDA TRINIDAD DE VERA-PE, JANICE GEM P. PERLAS, MD, ROFIEN H. ISON, MD, DIODE G. LANTORA, ATTY. MAS, Vice President of PRO-NCR informing her that her application for reaccreditation was denied by PRO-NCR Accreditation Sub-Committee from July 1, 2016 to June 4, 2019 due to practice inconsistent with the acceptable quality of care. In May 2017, complainant, through Atty. Paulo S. Selva, requested the NBI to conduct an investigation on the alleged injustice committed by PRO-NCR officials on the HCP reaccreditation. But in July 2017, complainant withdrew her complaint as she received verbal advice from DR. CELSTINA MA. JUDE P. DELA SERNA, former Interim/Officer-In-Charge, President and CEO PHIC that she will be accredited as HCP if she withdrew her complaint in NBI. However, in September 2020, complainant requested for revival of the case as the reaccreditation did not push through. According to PHIC, the denial is due to the administrative case filed against the complainant with the Prosecution Department of PHIC. Complainant, however claimed that she was denied of due process guaranteed under National Health Insurance Act of 1995, the grounds used for the denial was not explained well and there were no specifics given. She was not also informed or notified of any inquiry or validations made by the PHIC. Further, PHIC was not able to resolve the allegations against her after serving the suspension from July 2016 to June 2019. PhilHealth’s authority to deny accreditation of complainant requires that the applicant be first convicted to fraudulent acts. From the records, it appears that complainant was denied of her accreditation even before the case was heard by the Arbitration Office and without a formal complaint and an effort to conduct a fact-finding investigation as mandated by NHI Law. While it is within the PhilHealth’s power to suspend, revoke, or refuse Accreditation, it must be emphasized that the power to suspend or revoke is exercised based on the existence of grounds and must be compliant with law governing the same. The PhilHealth must observe due process in that it must afford the applicant notice and opportunity to be heard. NBI-AGD then recommended that above-mentioned Subjects be prosecuted for violation of Section 3(e) of RA 3019 (Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act). Subjects were also recommended to be administratively charged for violation of RA 6713 (Code of Conduct and Ethical Standards for Public Officials and Employees). · On April 12, operatives of NBI-Central Luzon Regional Office (NBI-CELRO) arrested GRACE M. body: PRESS STATEMENT March 06, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } NBI RESCUES 4 CHILD VICTIMS OF ONLINE SEXUAL EXPLOITATION IN CAVITE OPERATION PASAY CITY, Philippines – On March 4, 2026, the National Bureau of Investigation – Human Trafficking Division (NBI-HTRAD) successfully rescued four (4) male victims of online child sexual abuse and exploitation in Imus, Cavite. The operation was initiated following a request for assistance from the Federal Bureau of Investigation through the Philippine Internet Crimes Against Children Center (PICACC). Intelligence report indicated that an American national had directly engaged with the victims, leading to the mass production and transmission of Child Sexual Abuse and Exploitation Material (CSAEM). Following a thorough open-source investigation, NBI agents identified the victims as students currently enrolled in a public elementary school in Imus. After verifying their identities and locations, a team was mobilized to execute the rescue. This collaborative effort was led by the NBI-HTRAD, with the vital support of the NBI-Violence Against Women and Children Division (NBI-VAWCD), the NBI-Cavite District Office North (NBI-CAVIDO North), the City Social Welfare Development Office (CSWDO), and various Non-Governmental Organizations (NGOs). NBI Director Atty. Melvin A. Matibag commended the NBI-HTRAD agents for their precision and dedication in protecting the country’s most vulnerable citizens. “This successful operation underscores the critical need for fostering and maintaining strong collaborative relationships with our international counterparts,” said Director Matibag. “By sharing resources, intelligence, and strategies, we can effectively dismantle trafficking networks and ensure that victims receive the immediate support and justice they deserve.” The rescued minors are currently under the care of social welfare officers to ensure they receive the necessary psychological and medical interventions. The NBI remains committed to pursuing the perpetrators behind these digital crimes, regardless of their nationality or location. #NBIServes
