body: PRESS STATEMENT June 03, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } PRESS RELEASE | NBI APPREHENDS INDIVIDUAL FOR SELLING UNREGISTERED FIREARMS On May 28, 2026, the NBI-Counter Terrorism Division (NBI-CTD) arrested an individual in Makati City for violating Sections 28(b) and 32 of Republic Act No. 10591 (Comprehensive Firearms and Ammunition Regulation Act). The operation stemmed from information that a gun dealer in Makati Cinema Square, Makati City, was selling unregistered, high-powered, fully automatic long firearms to politicians who maintain private armed groups, particularly from Central Mindanao, Sulu, and Basilan. The information was confirmed when the subject offered to sell unregistered, high-powered, fully automatic long firearms without asking for LTOPF from their customers. On May 28, 2026, joint operatives from NBI-CTD, assisted by the NBI-Counter Intelligence Division (NBI-CID) and NBI-Technical Intelligence Division (NBI-TID) proceeded to the target gun store. They met the subject, who offered to sell four (4) unregistered automatic rifles and two (2) unregistered pistols, all from different imported brands. The subject offered a price of Php1,000,000.00 for all of the unregistered guns. The undercover agents agreed to the offer and handed over the marked money to the subject, who immediately received and counted it in front of the NBI agents. At this juncture, the operatives approached the subject and placed her under arrest. The arrested subject was brought to the NBI office, where she underwent standard booking procedures and will be presented for inquest proceedings for the above-stated violations. NBI Director Atty. Melvin A. Matibag commended the dedicated teamwork and collaborative efforts of the NBI-CTD, NBI-CID, and the NBI-TID. These combined efforts culminated in a crucial operation that successfully uncovered an illegal establishment engaged in the illicit sale and distribution of high-powered firearms. These firearms were notably not registered with any government authorities, posing a significant security threat.

body: PRESS STATEMENT September 08, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } On September 4, 2025, under the leadership of National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Director Judge Jaime B. Santiago (Ret.), the NBI-Olongapo District Office (NBI-OLDO) successfully apprehended ROCHE ARCALA DELOS REYES inside the City Planning and Development Office of the Olongapo City Hall for Robbery Extortion and violation of RA 3019 (Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act) and RA 6713 (Code of Conduct and Ethical Standards for Public Officials and Employees). The operation was initiated following a complaint from a businessman, who alleged that the Subjects, DELOS REYES and his associate EDWARD APOSTOL, told him that his building permit application would be denied unless he used their preferred private architectural and engineering firm for his building design, electrical, and plumbing plans. Furthermore, a failure to comply would reportedly result in a denied permit application and the imposition of additional surcharges and penalties. Allegedly, the Subject initially assessed the complainant a fee of P 98,100.00, which is significantly higher than the correct legal fees, which should be less than Php 30,000.00. Consequently, on September 4, 2025, NBI-OLDO agents conducted an entrapment operation in Olongapo City Hall, leading to the arrest of Subject DELOS REYES. Subject DELOS REYES was presented for inquest proceedings for the aforementioned violations. Additionally, his cohort APOSTOL will be charged with Robbery/Extortion, violation of RA 3019 and RA 6713 through regular filing. The arrest of Subject DELOS REYES highlights the Bureau’s unwavering commitment to preventing graft and corrupt practices within government offices.

body: PRESS STATEMENT February 21, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } The National Bureau of Investigation – Dangerous Drugs Division (NBI-DDD), under the leadership of NBI Director JUDGE JAIME B. SANTIAGO (Ret.) arrested a Chinese national identified as ZHOU, JIEQUN in Paranaque City for violation of R.A. No. 2382 (The Medical Act of 1959). The operation stemmed from the information regarding the illegal practice of medicine by a certain LV. The informant revealed that she was able to get a slot for a face water injection/skin booster procedure that was scheduled at 8:30P.M. on February 06, 2025 in a clinic at Monarch Parksuites, Aseana Business Park, Bradco Avenue, Paranaque City. The informant added that the said procedure is amounting to Php20,000.00 for the first session. Thus, on even date, the Agents of NBI-DDD conducted an entrapment operation against the said clinic. Before the procedure was about to start, the poseur-patient gave the pre-arranged signal to the Agents of NBI-DDD waiting in the vicinity. The NBI-DDD Agents forced opened the door as the clinic occupants refused to open the clinic’s door. The Agents asked Subject Zhou, who was one of the owners of the said clinic to present any license to perform the said procedure or license to practice medicine but Zhou failed to present any, thus, his arrest. One of the Subjects identified as LIZA HE FHENG was able to escape through the backdoor. Subject Zhou was presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the Prosecutor, Paranaque City for the above-stated violation and also charged is Subject Fheng who was still at-large. Director Santiago lauded the Agents of NBI-DDD for the successful apprehension of the foreign Subject and warned the public to refrain from undergoing medical procedures from individuals who are not licensed and/or authorized to perform such procedures.

body: PRESS STATEMENT March 31, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } In accordance with the directive from National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Director JUDGE JAIME B. SANTIAGO (Ret.), to strengthen the campaign against all forms of criminality, the NBI Antique District Office (NBI-ANDO) arrested JEBSON PALMES y GUMAYAO a.k.a. “JAKE” in San Jose, Antique. He was apprehended for violations of Republic Act No. 9995, also known as the Anti- Photo and Video Voyeurism Act of 2009, as well as Article 286 (Grave Coercion) of the Revised Penal Code (RPC), as amended. The operation began in response to a complaint stating that sometime in December 2022, an Alias “Jake” contacted the Complainant on her personal phone number. He claimed to have a video of her naked. The Complainant received a friend request and a message on Facebook Messenger, including an attached video of her sleeping without clothes. Upon receiving this message, the Complainant immediately called “Jake” and demanded that he delete the video. In response, he told her that he would only delete the video if she agreed to have sexual intercourse with him. He also threatened to upload the video on Facebook if she did not comply with his demands. Thus, the Complainant was compelled to have sex with the Subject. On March 24, 2025, the Complainant sent a message to “Jake” requesting the deletion of a video and pleading for an end to the sexual abuse and threats that began in 2022 and continued until she became pregnant. In response, “Jake” instructed the Complainant to come to his house in Dalipe, San Jose, Antique, if she wanted to delete the video. The Complainant then informed the NBI-ANDO agents about the Subject’s instruction. On March 27, 2025, the complainant, accompanied by agents from the NBI-ANDO, went to Jake’s given address, leading to his arrest. Investigation by the agents of NBI-ANDO revealed that Jake’s real name is Jebson Palmes Y Gumayao. On the same day, Subject Palmes was presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the Provincial Prosecutor in San Jose, Antique, regarding the violations mentioned above. Director Santiago commended the NBI-ANDO agents for arresting the subject and assured the public of the NBI’s commitment to upholding the law and protecting the public from criminals.

Tovera, Chief of the Bureau’s Anti-Illegal Drugs Unit (AIDU), the case pertains to a group of persons allegedly introducing themselves as members of Central Committee of the CPP-NPA who were relentlessly extorting large amount of money as revolutionary tax from a certain Noel Francisco of NBF Consulting, Inc. who filed a complaint before the NBI against the group. On Tuesday, April 21, 2015, a certain KA RENE AGUAS a.k.a. Ka Manny again called the Noel Franco and demanded an initial amount of P500,000.00 revolutionary in exchange for the latter’s safety the amount of which was eventually reduced to P200,000.00. In the afternoon of the same day, NBI operatives set up the entrapment at the office of NBF Consulting, Inc. where two operatives posted as employees of the company. As soon as Subject FRANCISCO CALICOY, who came and introduced himself as representative of Subject KA MANNY, received the marked money, he was arrested by the AOTCD-AIDU operatives. Subject MANUEL ADRIANO a.k.a. KA MANNY, who was arrested in a follow up operation, also confessed that prior to their arrest, they were escorted by their leader CRESENTE DIZON PANGILINAN and his cohorts on board a black Toyota Innova. The NBI said the Bureau is still investigating to determine whether or not those are really members of the CPP-NPA.

body: The NBI announces today the arrest of two (2) individuals in an entrapment operation in Intramuros, Manila on May 29, 2020 by the Agents of the NBI-International Operations Division (NBI-IOD). NBI Officer-In-Charge Eric B. Distor identified the subjects as Avi Siwa and her mother, Glorina Juliana Carandang. They were arrested for violation of R.A. No. 9711, otherwise known as the Food and Drug Administration Act of 2009. OIC Distor said that the case against Subject Siwa stemmed from a Complaint filed on May 12, 2020. In the complaint, Siwa allegedly required Complainant for a down payment of P4.6 Million, for a promise to deliver 10,000 sacks of rice amounting to P16.6 Million in Cebu City on May 4, 2020. After Complainant settled in cash the above down payment, Subject failed to comply with her promise. In fact, despite exhaustive efforts to reach her, Subject Siwa evaded to communicate with Complainant. Under the direct supervision of the NBI, and using the name Jane Suarez, Complainant tried to message Subject Siwa thru Facebook on May 17, 2020 upon seeing the latter’s post about the arrival of 10,000 test kits. On May 27, 2020, Subject Siwa responded to Complainant and offered to her various merchandise such as Rapid Test Kits, Face Masks, Sanitation Sprays, Face Shields, Gloves, PPEs, and Rice. Subject Siwa set to meet with Complainant at about 2:00 in the afternoon of May 29, 2020 in Intramuros, Manila, for the purchase of 120 pieces of Rapid Test Kits at P650.00 per piece or a total of P78,000.00, and 6,000 sacks of Sider Denorado Rice and 3,000 sacks of Sifer Golden Rice, amounting to P12,195,000.00 in all. In the entrapment operation organized by the operatives of the NBI-IOD, Subjects were arrested upon their receipt of the payment for the 120 pieces of Rapid Test Kits. Subject AVI SIWA, a.k.a. No. 10175 (The Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012), and violation of Article 315 (Estafa) of the Revised Penal Code, as amended.

body: PRESS STATEMENT December 06, 2024 In accordance with the strict order of National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Director JUDGE JAIME B. SANTIAGO (Ret.) to strengthen the crusade against all forms of criminality, the NBI- National Capital Region (NBI-NCR) arrested a Chinese national identified as YU JIANXIN a.k.a. “ZHANG LIN” in an entrapment operation in Pasay City for violation of R.A. No. 2382 (The Medical Act of 1959) in relation to R.A. No. 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012). Director Santiago said that the operation stemmed from an information regarding a group of foreign nationals led by “ZHANG LIN” is offering medical services exclusively to Chinese nationals for a fee, without necessary license or permit to operate. It was also averred that the Subject is not a licensed physician/nurse/ or medical technologist. Acting on the information, a verification was made with the Department of Health (DOH), which revealed through certification that the “TAI AN” clinic is not a Licensed General Clinical Laboratory and / or has no pending application for a License to Operate (LTO). Also, verification made with the Professional Regulation Commission (PRC) revealed through certification that Subject “ZHANG LIN” is not authorized to perform medical procedures in the country. In addition, online verification with the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) disclosed that no License to Operate (LTO) was issued to the Subject by any drug centers. Thus, violating the country’s Medical Act of 1959. Agents of the NBI-NCR conducted a surveillance operation, which resulted in the discovery of the location of the clinic “TAI AN CLINIC AND LABORATORY INC.” in Pasay City. However, the undercover agents learned that the said clinic is padlocked and a “CLOSED” remarked is posted in the entrance door. Despite the alleged closure of the clinic, the operatives were able to discover that Subject “ZHANG LIN” and his cohorts are still offering medical services to Chinese nationals on calls, and messages through use of the “Telegram” application. The operatives of NBI-NCR with the help of the Confidential Informant, set a meeting with the Subject and availed the medical services being offered by the latter. Subject “ZHANG LIN” set an appointment with the poseur-patient on December 3, 2024 at “TAI AN” clinic. On the said date, the poseur-patient together with the NBI-NCR operatives proceeded to the clinic, however, the Subject instructed the poseur-patient to proceed to a nearby Chinese restaurant where he will be fetched by his emissary. The emissary guided them in the storage of the restaurant, which was revealed to be a clinic where Subject administers his medical services. Upon sending the pre-arranged signal indicating that the Subject has already consummated the crime stated above and that entrapment money was already in his possession, the NBI-NCR operatives immediately proceeded to the storage/clinic, which resulted in the apprehension of the Subject. The operatives were able to seized the passport and driver’s license of Subject “ZHANG LIN”, which revealed that Subject’s real name is YU JIANXIN. Also recovered from the clinic were various Chinese medicines and medical equipment. The arrested Chinese national was presented for inquest proceedings before the Pasay City Prosecutor’s Office for the above-stated violations. Director Santiago commended the operatives of NBI-NCR for the successful apprehension of the Chinese national.

body: PRESS STATEMENT August 13, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } Acting on the instructions of NBI Director Judge Jaime B. Santiago (Ret.) to pursue and dismantle all remaining Philippine Offshore Gaming Operations (POGOs) in the country and the criminal networks exploiting them, the NBI-Southeastern Mindanao Regional Office (NBI-SEMRO) successfully shut down an illegal POGO hub operating from a residential property in Davao City. The operation, conducted on August 12, 2025, was initiated after a homeowner complained about suspicious activities inside a residential property on Gardenia Street, Montclair Highlands Subdivision, Buhangin, Davao City. After surveillance and verification, Agents confirmed the presence of POGO operations on the said property. During the operation, eight (8) Chinese nationals were arrested. Seized from the site were personal computers and multiple mobile phones, all utilized to facilitate the prohibited gaming operations. NBI-SEMRO discovered that an emerging pattern in illegal POGO activities includes operators splitting into smaller groups and moving into residential areas to avoid detection following the nationwide crackdown. This strategic shift underscores the need for constant community vigilance and rapid law enforcement response. The arrested Chinese nationals are now in NBI custody and will be charged under the applicable provisions of Philippine law. Seized devices will undergo forensic examination to trace digital evidence, and uncover the broader network and financial trail of the operation. This operation demonstrates the NBI’s sustained campaign against offshore gaming schemes that undermine the nation’s security, economy and moral fabric, as directed by NBI Director Santiago. The NBI urges the public to report suspicious activities in their communities to help stop illegal offshore gaming operations and the crimes that often accompany them, including money laundering, cybercrime, and human trafficking.

body: PRESS STATEMENT March 10, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } In accordance with the directive from National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Director JUDGE JAIME B. SANTIAGO (Ret.), the NBI-Bataan District Office (NBI-BATADO) has intensified its campaign against human trafficking. As a result, they arrested SHIN KI JUNG and his accomplices in Angeles City, Pampanga, for violations of R.A. No. 11862 (The Expanded Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2022) and R.A. No. 7610 (The Special Protection of Children Against Abuse, Exploitation and Discrimination Act). The operation stemmed from a complaint filed by the husband of one of the trafficked victims. He alleged that a certain individual was recruiting women to work as performers in Korea without the necessary permits and licenses from the Philippine Overseas Employment Administration (POEA). Investigation conducted by the agents of NBI-BATADO revealed that the recruitment process was merely a cover to persuade the victims to work at a club in Angeles City, Pampanga. Further inquiries indicated that the victims would serve as models and provide entertainment for potential customers, particularly foreign nationals, and would be available for hotel check-ins. Furthermore, the victims reported that one of the models employed at the said club is a minor. The victims discreetly transmitted to the agents of NBI-BATADO photographs and videos of the club and the alleged minor, thus validating the illegal activity. On March 6, 2025, the NBI-BATADO in coordination with the Philippine National Police (PNP) and the National Bureau of Investigation’s Human Trafficking Division (NBI-HTRAD), conducted a rescue operation at the said club. Twelve (12) victims including five (5) minors were rescued. Additionally, a foreign national identified as Shin Ki Jung, along with his accomplices, were arrested during the operation. The arrested Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor of Angeles City, Pampanga for the above violations of the special law. Director Santiago commended the agents of NBI-BATADO for their successful rescue operation and the arrest of the subjects.

body: PRESS STATEMENT March 08, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } NBI BUSTS ILLEGAL REAL ESTATE SELLING SCHEME IN KORONADAL CITY The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI), through its Central Mindanao Regional Office (CEMRO), arrested a real estate personnel during an entrapment operation conducted on 5 March 2026 in Koronadal City, South Cotabato, for the unauthorized sale of a subdivision lot. The operation stemmed from a complaint filed by Sahar Carumba Kaddoura, who alleged that portions of a parcel of land located at Purok Everlasting, Barangay New Pangasinan, Koronadal City, covered by TCT No. 145-2022004615, were being marketed and sold without the authority of the legitimate heirs of the registered owner, Teodorico Paraico. Investigation revealed that the property was being offered for sale using a Special Power of Attorney (SPA) purportedly executed by Paraico in 2022. However, records show that the registered owner died in 1979, casting serious doubt on the authenticity of the document used in the transaction. Further verification with the Professional Regulation Commission (PRC) showed that the individual involved was not a licensed real estate practitioner, in violation of Republic Act No. 9646 (Real Estate Service Act). The property was likewise being marketed through P&N Real Estate Services without the required authority from the Department of Human Settlements and Urban Development (DHSUD), in violation of Presidential Decree No. 957. Prior to the operation, NBI agents conducted test-buy operations, confirming that the office was actively offering subdivision lots for sale. At around 10:00 AM on 5 March 2026, NBI operatives proceeded to the office of P&N Real Estate Services in Koronadal City. Upon the pre-arranged signal, agents entered the premises and caught Lilah May Villaruel y Tayo in the act of counting the marked money used as down payment for the purchase of a subdivision lot. The suspect was informed of the reason for her arrest and apprised of her constitutional rights. She now faces charges for violations of: • Republic Act No. 9646 (Real Estate Service Act) • Presidential Decree No. 957 • Article 315 (2) of the Revised Penal Code (Estafa) The suspect was brought to the NBI Central Mindanao Regional Office in Koronadal City for documentation and booking. The subject has already been inquested before the Office of the City Prosecutor of Koronadal City. NBI Director Atty. Melvin Matibag emphasized the Bureau’s commitment to protecting the public from fraudulent real estate transactions. “We urge the public to exercise due diligence when purchasing real estate properties. Always verify the legitimacy of brokers, agents, and supporting documents through the proper government agencies before entering into any transaction. The NBI will continue to pursue individuals who engage in fraudulent schemes that victimize unsuspecting property buyers,” the NBI Director said. #NBIServes

body: One of the accused in the brutal slaying of Ruby Rose Barrameda-Jimenez was arrested by the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) in Cauayan, Isabela yesterday afternoon. In June 2009, the body of Ruby Rose Barrameda-Jimenez, who has been missing since March 2007 was found inside a cemented steel drum recovered in the murky water of Navotas Fish Port. Murder charges were filed against Atty. Manuel Jimenez Jr., Lope Jimenez, Manuel Jimenez III, Manuel Montero, Eric Fernandez, Leonard Descalso, and Robert Ponce before the Malabon Regional Trial Court, and warrants of arrest were issued by Acting Presiding Judge Hector B. Almeyda of the Regional Trial Court of Malabon City, Br 170 against Lope Jimenez, Robert Ponce alias Obet, Eric Fernandez, and Leonard Descalso. On July 30, 2012, the NBI-Special Task Force (STF) received reliable information that Robert Ponce alias “Obet”, an accused in the celebrated killing of Barrameda-Jimenez was spotted in Northern Luzon particularly in the Isabela and Cagayan Valley Region. Acting on said report, the NBI-STF conducted a series of surveillance and undercover operations at the reported place of the accused Robert Ponce in Isabela. It was verified later, that accused is hiding in Bgy.Naganacan, Cauayan, Isabela since June 2009, and is using the name “Alex Peralta” to conceal his true name and identity. To confirm the accused’s identity, the NBI requested the DOJ-WPP’s assistance to contact Manuel Montero, state witness in Ruby Rose Barrameda-Jimenez murder case. The NBI met witness Manuel Montero on September 25, 2012. The photographs of Subject were shown to him and he positively identified the same as Robert Ponce alias “Obet”, one of the accused in the brutal killing of Ruby Rose Barrameda-Jimenez. On October 23, 2012, operatives of the NBI-Special Task Force (STF) and the Death Investigation Division (DID) proceeded to Isabela province in Cagayan Valley Region and serve the warrant of arrest against Ponce. Thereafter, on November 6, 2012, joint operatives of STF and DID, with the assistance of our Intelligence Service, proceeded to Isabela province for the service of the said warrant of arrest. In the afternoon of November 7, 2012, the NBI in coordination with its local office and the PNP, accused Robert “Obet” Ponce a.k.a. Norberto Ponce y Peralta a.k.a. Alex Peralta was arrested in Bgy. Naganacan, Cauayan, Isabela, by virtue of a warrant of arrest issued against him. At early dawn today, the NBI team with accused Ponce arrived at the NBI main office in Manila where Ponce was booked and detained.

body: PRESS STATEMENT May 28, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } The NBI-Cybercrime Division (CCD), under the supervision of NBI Director Judge Jaime B. Santiago (Ret.), and with the assistance of the Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR) and the Department of Trade and Industry (DTI) seized a substantial volume of illegally imported and distributed vape products with an estimated value of Php 63,000,000.00 in three separate operations in Marilao, Bulacan, Parañaque City, and Pasay City. These operations also resulted in the arrest of two Filipinos and three foreign nationals for violation of Republic Act No. 11900 (An Act Regulating the Importation, Manufacture, Sale, Packaging, Distribution, Use and Communication of Vaporized Nicotine and Non-Nicotine Products, and Novel Tobacco Products), and violation of R.A. No. 8424 (Tax Reform Act). Continuous cyber patrolling of the CCD resulted in the discovery of widespread importation, sale, and distribution of illicit nicotine vapor products within the province of Marilao, Bulacan. CCD was able to identify and obtain the contact information and social media accounts of the individuals involved in the illegal importation and distribution of said vapor products. To gather evidence and further infiltrate the operation, poseur-customers placed bulk orders of the illicit products. On 8 May 2025, NBI-CCD conducted an operation at JP Compound III, Luke Street, Block 5, Lot 18, Marilao, Bulacan. The operation resulted in the discovery and confiscation of 85,200 pieces of salt-nicotine-based vapor products. On May 21, 2025, the agents of NBI-CCD seized 25,000 pieces of unregistered vape products in Parañaque City. The operation also resulted in the arrest of two (2) foreign nationals identified as JONATHAN KHER JUN XIAN, a Singaporean, and NATKRITA PHAKHINNIPHAT, a Thai national. On May 26, 2025, the agents of NBI-CCD arrested MATHEW FRANCISCO y RAMOS, IRIS HUI y DEL ROSARIO, and a Chinese national identified as JIANG XING in Pasay City for selling unregistered vape products. One of the arrested Subjects revealed the location of their storage facility in Paranaque City, which resulted in the seizure of 72,000 pieces of unregistered vape products. Director Santiago commended the operatives of NBI-CCD and expressed his gratitude to the BIR and DTI for their invaluable support, which led in the arrest of the Subjects. Director Santiago further stated that the three operations demonstrate the effectiveness of the NBI’s combined cyber patrol, intelligence gathering, and field interdiction strategies, as well as inter-agency coordination. The arrested individuals were presented for inquest proceedings for the above-stated violations.

body: A man who introduced himself as an employee of the Presidential Action Center in Malacañan who can allegedly could facilitate a favor requested from any government agencies was arrested by agents of the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) during an operation last week. The suspect was identified as HENRY ALVAREZ DA SILVA, 63, resident of Magdame St., Bgy. 5, Sariaya, Quezon and Bgy. Balubal, Sariaya, Quezon. Investigation by the NBI – Lucena District Office (LUCDO) revealed that Vicente D. Ferrer, of Tiaong, Quezon filed a complaint before the NBI-LUCDO against Henry Da Silva for estafa. In a meeting, suspect introduced himself as an employee of Malacañan assigned at the Presidential Action Center. He boasted of alleged connections in different government offices and allegedly can work for favorable results of requests addressed to any offices. With Da Silva’s assurance, Ferrer sought for a favorable result of the appeal he filed against his nephew regarding a murder case with the Supreme Court. The former demanded P100,000 for this transaction. However, suspect failed to fulfill his promise and evaded the complainant. This prompted complainant Ferrer to seek NBI investigative assistance on Feb. 26. Upon verification, it was discovered that Da Silva has a string of pending warrants of arrest for Illegal Recruitment and Estafa in different courts in Quezon Province, Manila and Pangasinan. Meanwhile, an information was received by the NBI that Da Silva was about to meet another potential victim in Biñan City on March 1. Acting with dispatch the NBI-LUCDO planned an operation to arrest suspect. At the appointed date and time, as NBI operatives were on their way to the meeting place, they saw the suspect’s vehicle, a Toyota Town Ace cruising around the vicinity of South Luzon Expressway (SLEX), Carmona Exit, Biñan City. They hastily drove towards Da Silva who was about to enter a mini-stop convenience store. They approached him, introduced themselves and informed him of his arrest warrants. Thereafter, he was apprehended and brought to the NBI-LUCDO office for detention. Certification from the Presidential Action Center, Malacañan, Manila disclosed that Henry Da Silva is not an employee of said office. Countless victims continue to troop to the NBI to file their complaints against Da Silva.

body: In line with the relentless drive of the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) against terrorism, operatives of NBI-Counter-Terrorism Division (NBI-CTD) arrested a member of the dreaded Abu Sayyaf Group (ASG) in Maharlika Village, Taguig City. NBI Officer-In-Charge (OIC)-Director Eric B. Distor identified the Subject as WAHAB JAMAL y SABIRANI a.k.a. Ustadz Usman Halipa who was arrested last Friday, May 7, 2021 on the strength of a Warrant of Arrest issued by the Regional Trial Court of Basilan for Kidnapping and Serious Illegal Detention. Distor said that the latest arrest of an ASG member was based upon an information received by the NBI in early April 2021, that an alleged ASG member was sighted in Maharlika Village, Taguig City where he reportedly resides. Distor stressed that after validating the information, the NBI learned that Subject alias Ustadz Usman Halipa later identified as WAHAB JAMAL y SABIRANI as his real name, was involved in the Golden Harvest Plantation Kidnapping in 2001 at Tairan, Lantawan, Basilan Province, and is included in a Warrant of Arrest for his alleged involvement. On April 21, 2021, OIC-Director Distor emphasized, a witness identified a photo from a CTD photo line-up as Ustadz Usman Halipa. On the same date, said witness executed an Affidavit of Identification. A series of casing and surveillance by the NBI then ensued together with counterparts from the AFP and PNP to gather more information on the target area and on subject @Ustadz Usman Halipa and his pattern-of-life, which was completed on May 6, 2021. On May 7, 2021 another witness identified the subject ASG member from a CTD photo line-up and executed an Affidavit of Identification that was subscribed at the Regional Prosecutor’s Office in Zamboanga City, thereby boosting their information against the subject. In the evening of the same day, a joint operation was conducted by operatives of the NBI-CTD and counterparts from the AFP, JTF-NCR and PNP at the target area in Taguig City, resulting in the arrest of Subject @Ustadz Usman Halipa whose name is WAHAB JAMAL y SABIRANI. He was brought to the NBI and turned over to the Detention Center. OIC Distor said “He may have eluded the law for almost 20 years but its long arm has finally caught up with him. Let me assure the public that the NBI will be unwavering in its drive to run after the members of this terrorist group”. To date, the NBI has already arrested 27members of the ASG since 2018.

body: PRESS STATEMENT November 8, 2022 DOJ SECRETARY REMULLA TO SPEAK DURING NBI 86th ANNIVERSARY Department of Justice Secretary JESUS CRISPIN C. REMULLA will be the Guest of Honor and Speaker on the 86th Founding Anniversary Celebration of the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) with the theme “NBI @ 86: Resilient Towards the Challenges and Demands of the Times”. The two-day anniversary celebration will open on November 9, 2022 at Diamond Hotel, Roxas Boulevard, Manila. A thanks-giving mass will be held prior to the formal anniversary program where the Program on Awards and Incentives for Service Excellence (PRAISE) will be had. Secretary Jesus Crispin C. Remulla will grace the anniversary program thru his message as the highlight of the celebration. The event will be attended by the top officials of the Bureau, with the families of the fallen heroes of the NBI. It will be followed by the Command Conference at Diamond Hotel which is to be participated by NBI Regional Directors, Agents-In-Charge, and Division Chiefs of Investigative and Intelligence Services.

body: PRESS STATEMENT May 29, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } PRESS RELEASE | NBI ARRESTS SUSPECT INVOLVED IN ALLEGED IMPERSONATION, ONLINE SCAMMING, AND DRUG-RELATED OFFENSES PASAY CITY — The National Bureau of Investigation – Organized and Transnational Crimes Division (NBI-OTCD) successfully conducted a law enforcement operation resulting in the arrest of one individual on 19 May 2026 in Novaliches, Quezon City. The operation stemmed from a request and intelligence information provided by the Presidential Security Command (PSC) regarding the alleged illegal activities of the subject involving impersonation, online financial scams, extortion, and unlawful use of identities of high-ranking government officials. Acting on verified intelligence and an existing warrant for Service of Sentence for Estafa issued by the Municipal Trial Court in Cities (MTCC), Ilagan, Isabela, operatives of NBI-OTCD proceeded to Unit 531, Tower 5, Trees Residences, Novaliches, Quezon City, where the subject was located and apprehended. During the implementation of the warrant and subsequent lawful search incidental to arrest, NBI operatives recovered suspected illegal drugs and paraphernalia, including several heat-sealed sachets containing white crystalline substance suspected to be methamphetamine hydrochloride or “shabu,” drug paraphernalia, and an electronic cigarette device. Laboratory examination conducted by the NBI Forensic Chemistry Division later confirmed that portions of the seized substances tested positive for Methamphetamine Hydrochloride and Tetrahydrocannabinol (THC). The subject was informed of his constitutional rights and subjected to standard booking and documentation procedures in accordance with existing laws and regulations. Appropriate complaints for violations of Republic Act No. 9165, otherwise known as the “Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002,” were thereafter referred for inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor of Quezon City. Further investigation likewise revealed that the subject allegedly engaged in impersonation schemes involving the names and identities of prominent government officials and personalities through various messaging applications in order to solicit money and defraud prospective victims. The NBI emphasizes that all disclosures and allegations made by the subject during custodial and tactical interviews remain subject to further validation, case build-up, corroboration, and due process. The Bureau continues to conduct a thorough investigation to identify additional complainants and determine possible criminal liabilities of all individuals who may have participated in or benefited from the alleged unlawful activities “The National Bureau of Investigation will continue to pursue all individuals engaged in impersonation, cyber-enabled fraud, extortion, and other criminal activities that undermine public trust and exploit government institutions. No individual is above the law, and we assure the public that all investigations shall be conducted professionally, fairly, and strictly within the bounds of due process,” NBI Director Atty. Melvin D. Matibag said.

body: PRESS STATEMENT October 15, 2024 The National Bureau of Investigation-Cybercrime Division (NBI-CCD), under the leadership of NBI Director Judge Jaime B. Santiago (Ret.), uncovered illicit cyber-related activities perpetrated by foreign nationals in Makati City. Santiago said that through continuous cyber patrolling and intelligence gathering, CCD operatives intercepted an organized cybercrime group engaged in large-scale online scamming activities. On October 11, 2024, CCD operatives, in coordination with the local police, implemented the Warrant to Search, Seize, and Examine Computer Data (WSSECD) issued by RTC Branch 147 against the premises located at #3840 Mascardo Street, Tejeros, Makati City. Through search and examination, several live electronic devices such as desktop computers, laptops, and cellphones utilized in illicit online operations were found. Controlled viewing and onsite forensic examination conducted on the electronic devices led to the discovery of digital evidence, tools, and applications for social engineering schemes, illegal access, misuse of devices, computer-related forgery, and fraud, in violation of RA No. 12010 (Anti-Financial Account Scamming Act and RA No. 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012). The operation likewise resulted in the arrest of fifteen (15) Chinese nationals, one (1) Malaysian, and one (1) Taiwanese, who were all caught red-handed having been engaged in the aforesaid illicit activities. They were apprised of the nature and cause of their arrest as well as their constitutional rights in a language they fully understood. The seized items were subjected to further forensic examination. Director Santiago commended the CCD operatives for the successful operation, stressing that the NBI remains relentless in its battle against cybercriminals.

body: PRESS STATEMENT August 30, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } PRESS RELEASE | NBI ARRESTS TWO SUSPECTED DRUG PUSHERS IN BUY-BUST OPERATION In line with the extensive campaign of the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) against illegal drugs, the NBI-Dangerous Drugs Division (NBI-DDD) arrested two individuals in Taguig City. The case stemmed from a confidential report that a certain individual was engaged in the illegal sale of methamphetamine hydrochloride, or “shabu,” in Taguig City. On August 18, 2026, agents of NBI-DDD conducted a buy-bust operation, which resulted in the arrest of the subject and his cohort, a minor. The operation resulted in the seizure of 96.2098g of shabu with an estimated value of Php 700,000.00. Based on the initial drug screening conducted by the NBI-Forensic Chemistry Division (NBI-FCD), both subjects showed reactions indicative of the presence of shabu. The arrested minor subject was turned over to Bahay Pag-Asa in Taguig City for assessment of his discernment, and, based on the CSWDO’s assessment, he acted with discernment. The subjects were presented for online inquest proceedings for violation of Section 05, in relation to Sec 26 and Sec 15 Article II of Republic Act 9165, or the Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002. NBI Director Atty. Melvin A. Matibag said that the Bureau will remain steadfast in its anti-illegal drug operations, emphasizing that behind every young person victimized by illegal drugs is a Filipino family that suffers. He underscored the pain of parents who witness their children’s lives being destroyed by illegal drugs. “The President shares the same concern and has directed us to maintain the pressure against those who sell and distribute illegal drugs. He does not want our youth to be put in harm’s way. We will continue doing everything within the bounds of the law to protect our youth and our communities,” Director Matibag said. https://www.facebook.com/reel/1374802691525176

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today announced the arrest of an individual by operatives of NBI-Bayombong District Office (NBI-BAYDO) in an entrapment operation in Bambang, Nueva Vizcaya for unlawful selling of chainsaw. NBI-Officer-In-Charge (OIC) Director Eric B. Distor identified the subject as KEVIN HINDAC DULNUAN. Distor said that the operation stemmed from the letter request by the Community Environment and Natural Resources Officer (CENRO) in Nueva Vizcaya, requesting assistance of this office in the investigation of unregistered chainsaw and further informing this office about the temporary suspension of registration of chainsaw in DENR Region 2. NBI-BAYDO immediately conducted a verification and surveillance operations regarding with the information provided by CENRO- Nueva Vizcaya, which revealed that GM’s CORNER VARIETY STORE (GM) in Bambang, Nueva Vizacaya is involved in the sale and distribution of chainsaws and similar cutting implements through electric and internal combustion engine without necessary permit from the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR). Verification made with CENRO also revealed that GM failed to secure a permit from their office before selling or offering in public the subject item, which is in violation of the Chainsaw Act of 2002. Thus, on March 16, 2022 operatives of NBI-BAYDO proceeded to the target establishment and conducted a buy-bust operation, which resulted in the arrest of Subject Dulnuan. The operatives were able to recover one set of chainsaw, the marked money, sales invoice and receipt from the arrested subject. Subject Dulnuan was charged for violation of R.A. 9175 otherwise known as the “Chainsaw Act of 2002”. In addition, the owner of the said establishment identified as MICHAEL GUIMBONGAN KIMAYONG was also charged of the same offense.

body: PRESS STATEMENT February 23, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } NBI AND BI DISMANTLE ILLEGAL POGO HUB IN MAKATI; SIX SOUTH KOREANS ARRESTED PASAY CITY, Philippines – In a coordinated strike against unlicensed offshore gaming, the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) and the Bureau of Immigration (BI) successfully raided an illegal POGO hub operating within a residential condominium on Estrella Street, Makati City that resulted in the arrest of six South Korean nationals. The raid stemmed from a mission order from the Immigration Commissioner following intelligence reports identifying a South Korean fugitive among the group. The individual in question has a pending warrant of arrest in South Korea and is currently the subject of a deportation order. The Subjects were also allegedly involved in game-fixing and online scamming operations specifically targeting South Korean citizens. To facilitate these illicit activities, the group utilized an array of equipment seized by operatives during the search, which included eight personal computers, multiple mobile devices, and several One-Time Password (OTP) generators. NBI-Criminal Intelligence Division emphasized that this crackdown is part of an intensified national campaign against offshore gaming entities that undermine the country’s economic stability and national security. The Subjects are currently facing charges for violations of the Anti-POGO Act of 2025, the Securities Regulation Code, and the Anti-Financial Account Scamming Act (AFASA). NBI will not allow the Philippines to be a sanctuary for fugitives or a hub for cyber-fraud. This operation serves as a clear warning that the NBI, in partnership with the Bureau of Immigration, will continue to dismantle operations that bypass our laws and exploit our digital infrastructure.

body: The relentless drive against counterfeit products scored anew as some P300 million worth of fake imported bags, backpacks and wallets were seized by a joint team of National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) and Bureau of Customs (BOC) operatives during a raid of an outlet in Binondo, Manila yesterday. The joint efforts of both agencies have proven effective in the campaign against counterfeiting and piracy.

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today said charges for Human Trafficking and Syndicated and Large Scale Illegal Recruitment have been filed against a Lebanese national and seven (7) Filipino accomplices before the Department of Justice (DOJ). The NBI said those charged include PASCAL M. SREIH a.k.a. MARIO, a Lebanese national who resides in Harmony Hills Subdivision in San Jose Del Monte, Bulacan, VILMAROSE MATAGAY y BACULI a.k.a. SARAH a.k.a. MADAME, and ROLANDO MATAGAY y BACULI, who both reside in the same address as that of Lebanese national, REYNALDO ROCELLO y TANDOG, a resident of Olongapo City, JOEY PAULINO ESCOBAR and FIDEL S. MENDOZA, Immigration Officers assigned in Zamboanga City, ERIC JOHN C. DE LA CRUZ, a member of the Philippine Coast Guard assigned in Zamboanga and a certain alyas FLOR. Of the 8, only Subjects DE LA CRUZ and alyas FLOR remain at large while the others have been arrested in entrapment operations and hot pursuit by agents of the NBI-Anti Human Trafficking Division (NBI-ATHRAD) with the assistance of operatives from the Presidential Anti Organized Crime Commission (PAOCC) and Naval Intelligence Service Force (NISF). The case stemmed from a complaint filed by MA. GRACELA ANGELES y ARTICULO against Lebanese national PASCAL SREIH, et al. Based on the complaint, an organized group of recruiters in connivance with their foreign counterparts in Lebanon and members of the Philippine Coast Guard and Bureau of Immigration are actively recruiting hapless Filipinas for overseas employment to work as Domestic Helpers in Lebanon without going through the regular process of deployment required by the POEA and despite the existing ban on deployment of OFWs in Lebanon. The NBI said applicants allegedly are being recruited by PASCAL and his Filipina wife SARAH and are billeted in an accommodation house in Camarin, Bagong Silang, Caloocan. From there, they will fly to Zamboanga and depart thru the backdoor exit via Sandakan, Malaysia where they will then travel to Lebanon as their final destination. ANGELES averred in her complaint that a fellow applicant gave her the number of a certain FLOR from whom ANGELES was able to confirm that FLOR was indeed still recruiting workers. On August 28, 2015, ANGELES met with FLOR but instead of bring her to the recruitment agency for interview, she was brought to a parlor in Muzon, San Jose Del Monte in Bulacan where they met Subjects PASCAL and SARAH where she was promised a monthly salary of 300 US Dollars. PASCAL also told her that she would travel as a tourist to Malaysia via Zamboanga because there is an existing deployment ban in Lebanon. She was assured, however, that an agency in Lebanon will process her necessary documents. On September 3, 2015, ANGELES brought Intelligence Agent ROSALVE FRANCA, acting as poseur-applicant, to the accommodation house in Caloocan and was promised by PASCAL to work in Lebanon with a monthly salary of 350 US Dollars. Midnight of September 12, ANGELES and the other applicants were transported to Zamboanga and stayed at Blue Shark Hotel as their temporary accommodation for the eight (8) victims. ANGELES informed the NBI that they will be brought to Zamboanga port on September 14 wearing a peach/pink pony tail on their left wrist as counter sign for identification purposes to enable the elements of Coast Guard and Immigration Officers to easily recognize them. Upon arrival at the Zamboanga port, the victims directly proceeded to the Immigration Office without passing thru the Overseas Passenger Assistance Center (OPAC), which is tasked to check and verify tickets of departing passengers. In this case, the 8 victims were allowed entry by Coast Guards and Immigration officers with no questions asked. When the victims were about to board the shuttle bus that would take them to a merchant ship, operatives of the NBI intercepted the bus with the assistance of the NISF. The NBI agents proceeded to the office of the Bureau of Immigration and after having confirmed from the victims the participation of Subjects ESCOBAR and MENDOZA in the facilitation of would be trafficked victims, they were immediately put under arrest. SARAH a.k.a. MENDOZA, Immigration Officers assigned in Zamboanga City, ERIC JOHN C. DE LA CRUZ, a member of the Philippine Coast Guard assigned in Zamboanga and a certain alyas FLOR. body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today announced the filing of several criminal charges by the NBI-Death Investigation Division (NBI-DID) against eleven (11) individuals who were involved in the untimely death of Christine Angelica F. Dacera. Included in the charge is a Police Official who first conducted the autopsy on the cadaver of Victim Dacera. NBI Officer-in-Charge (OIC) Director Eric B. Distor identified the charged individuals as MARK ANTHONY ROSALES, ROMEL GALIDO Y DALURO, JOHN PASCUAL DELA SERNA III Y REYES, DARWIN JOSEPH MACALLA Y DE LEON, GREGORIO ANGELO RAFAEL DE GUZMAN Y DELA FUENTE, JEZREEL RAPINAN Y PAMISA, ALAIN CHEN Y DAYANAN, REYMAR ENGLIS Y MABINI, ATTY. NEPTALI G. MAROTO, LOUIE DELIMA Y SUNGA, and P/MAJ MICHAEL NICK W. SARMIENTO, M.D. OIC-Director Distor said that upon directive of Department of Justice (DOJ) Secretary Menardo Guevarra and the letter of Sharon Rose Dacera (victim’s mother) requesting a parallel investigation on her daughter’s death, NBI conducted an investigation on the death of Dacera. Testimonies of the witnesses and persons involved revealed that on December 27, 2020, Dacera together with her friends Subjects GALIDO, ENGLIS, DELIMA, DELA SERNA, and RAPINAN booked an overnight stay in City Garden Hotel in Makati City starting from December 31, 2020 to January 1, 2021. According to the Duty Manager of the hotel he was a friend of Dacera’s companion and asked by Dacera’s group to facilitate their booking and accommodated the booking. Dacera’s group was first designated to Room 2309 but later transferred to Room 2209 due to the Air-Conditioning malfunction. In the evening of December 31, 2020, Victim Dacera together with her friends partied in their hotel room while drinking several liquors. Coincidentally, while waiting for the New Year countdown, ED (one of the companions of Victim Dacera in Room 2209) brought them to Room 2207 where his friend identified as DHEEJ is also checked-in. CCTV footages revealed that the victim and her friends were seen go back and forth in Rooms 2207 and 2209. Re-autopsy on the cadaver of Victim Dacera revealed that the cause of her death was microscopic evidence of peri-aortic hemorrhages and aortic wall disruption, suspicious for a bleeding dissecting aneurysm based on the review of slides of PNP Crime Laboratory. Toxicology examinations on the cadaver of the victim showed the presence of DILTIAZEM, a prescription drug for the management of hypertension. Results of the NBI Investigation revealed the glaring inconsistencies in the PNP autopsy report. Results of the autopsy report conducted by the NBI- Medico Legal Division Chief revealed that in contrast to the autopsy report of P/Maj. Sarmiento, M.D., Victim’s urinary bladder was full of urine and in fact the NBI Forensic Team was able to extract 130 ml of urine and no abrasion was found in her labia majora. PNP Crime Laboratory turned-over to the NBI the laboratory result of two pieces of cotton found inside Room 2209. According to the report the two pieces of cotton showed the presence of Flouromethamphetamine and Methamphetamine. According to the testimonies of the witnesses who checked-in at Room 2207, around 03:00 a.m. in the morning, Victim Dacera told them that she did not want to be at Room 2209 because her companions because they were high for taking party drugs in contrast to the sworn statements of the victim’s friends and companions at Room 2209. Thus, based on the forensic evidences and testimonies of the witnesses, NBI-DID filed before the Department of Justice (DOJ): Violation of Sec. 3 (a) and penalized under Sec. 5 of the R.A. 9165 (Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002) against Subject ROSALES for introducing the party drugs to his companions; Violation of Section 3 (k) and penalized under Sec. 26 of R.A. 9165 against Subjects ROSALES and GALIDO for delivering and giving away the party drugs; Perjury against Subjects GALIDO, DELA SERNA, and MACALLA for providing false testimonies; Obstruction of Justice against Subjects ROSALES, GALIDO, DELA SERNA, DE GUZMAN, RAPINAN, CHEN, ENGLIS, MACALLA, and ATTY. MAROTO for giving false or fabricated information to mislead or prevent the law enforcement agencies form apprehending the offenders; Reckless Imprudence Resulting in Homicide against Subjects DELA SERNA, RAPINAN, CHEN, and DELIMA for recklessly neglect the condition of Victim Dacera which led on to her untimely death; Article 171 par. 4 of the RPC (Falsification of Official Document by Public Officer) against POLICE MAJOR SARMIENTO, M.D. for declaring untruthful findings on his autopsy report.

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today announced the arrest of two (2) Nigerian nationals in Imus Cavite last Wednesday for Illegal Drugs. NBI Officer-In-Charge (OIC) Eric B. Distor identified the subjects as SAMUEL CHUKWUEMERA DURUIBE and MMADUAMAKA VITUS OKOLI a.k.a. FRANK IRVIN. OIC Distor said that both subjects were arrested by operatives of the NBI-Task Force Against Illegal Drugs (NBI-TFAID) on the strength of a Search Warrant issued by the Regional Trial Court in Imus Cavite. In October of 2019, the NBI-TFAID received information that a certain SAMUEL CHUKWUEMERA DURUIBE, a Nigerian citizen, with some companions who are also Nigerians, traffic illegal drugs or Shabu, mostly in the area of Cavite. Subject DURUIBE is allegedly a member of the West African Drug Syndicate (WADS) operating in the Philippines. He was previously arrested by NBI-Manila sometime in 2014 thru a buy-bust operation. Seized from his possession was 2 kilos of Methamphetamine Hydrochloride or Shabu. He is on provisional liberty after being granted to post bail bond in the amount of P500,000.00 for violation of Sec 5, R.A. 9165 and P1,000,000.00 for violation of Sec 11, R.A. 9165 sometime in September 2019. Reports revealed that he continued to operate/trafficked illegal drugs even though he was then on jail. He was then on continuous surveillance after his release from jail. Under strict instructions from OIC Distor, on July 29, 2020, Agents and Special Investigators of NBI-TFAID implemented the Search Warrant at the residence of subject DURUIBE in Montefaro Village, Imus City, Cavite resulting in the seizure of 181.21 grams of Methamphetamine Hydrochloride or Shabu and the arrest of the 2 subjects. The seized drugs were submitted for laboratory examination and analysis. A Certification was later issued by the NBI-Forensic Chemistry Division that the specimens submitted for examination were all positive for Methamphetamine Hydrochloride. The arrested subjects were charged for violation of Sec 5, Sec 6 and Sec 11 of R.A. 9165 before the City Prosecutor’s Office of Imus City, Cavite. OIC Distor stressed that under his leadership, the NBI will be relentless in their efforts to stop the proliferation of illegal drugs in coordination with other law enforcement agencies.

body: PRESS STATEMENT July 09, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } In line with the campaign to stop the proliferation of counterfeit products, the National Bureau of Investigation – National Capital Region (NBI-NCR) enforced Search Warrants at an establishment in Pasay City for violation of Republic Act No. 8293 or the “Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines.” On 03 July 2025, NBI-NCR agents, together with the NBI-Intellectual Property Rights Division (IPRD), implemented two (2) search warrants against one (1) establishment for violation of the aforementioned offense. The operation resulted in the discovery and seizure of a total of Nine Thousand and Ninety-Three (9,093) pieces of various counterfeit products, all bearing the trademarks of “Johnson’s,” “Johnson’s Baby,” and “Aveeno,” registered trademarks of KENVUE Inc., and “Cetaphil” and “Cetaphil Gentle Clear,” registered trademarks of GALDERMA HOLDINGS SA, and various business documents including other pieces of evidence which was estimated to be worth more or less Eight Million Pesos (Php 8,000,000.00). The case stemmed from the complaint filed by Orion Support, Inc. (OSI), representing Kenvue Inc. and Galderma Holdings SA. Director Santiago lauded the NBI-NCR for successfully implementing said search warrants and their law enforcement actions to stop the proliferation and distribution of counterfeit/fake products. NBI reminds the public to refrain from patronizing pirated products to give protection to the intellectual property rights owners and enhance our economic growth.

title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: In line with the relentless campaign of the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) against all illegal activities, operatives of NBI-Task Force Against illegal Drugs (NBI-TFAID) seized repacked imported Chinese cigarettes with an estimated value of P1.35 Billion in Subic Bay Gateway Park (SBGP) in Subic Bay Freeport Zone (SBGP) in Olongapo, City, Zambales. The operation also resulted in the arrest two (2) Malaysian nationals. NBI Officer-in-Charge (OIC) Director Eric B. Distor identified the arrested Subjects as TAN AH SENG and TAN YAN TENG, President and Vice President, respectively, of BUMI JAYA INTERNATIONAL CORP. located in Olongapo City. Distor said the case stemmed from information relayed to NBI-TFAID about a warehouse of BUMI JAYA owned by TAN AH SENG and his group who are allegedly involved in the illegal repacking of imported cigarettes from China and diverting it to domestic market. Under strict instructions from Distor, NBI-TFAID operatives instructed the informant to discreetly take a video of the repacking activity inside BUMI JAYA and to get some samples of cigarette tax stamps that workers are putting on each cigarette pack. Investigation revealed that BUMI JAYA was incorporated on January 9, 2002. On November 18, 2015, Mr. Vincent Sauvalere, Head of Tobacco and Counterfeit Goods Unit of European Anti-Fraud Office requested the Bureau of Customs (BOC) to conduct investigation on BUMI JAYA in relation to smuggling of tobacco products into the European Union. BUMI JAYA became a licensed transshipper engaged in transshipping tobacco products to different countries on January 4, 2017. Under BOC Customs Administrative Order (COA) No. 12-2019, the handling and movement of transshipment of goods from the carrier to and within the customs facilities and warehouses inside the port of entry shall be under the continuous supervision and subject to the rules and regulation issued by the BOC to include safeguard measures to ensure that the transshipment goods shall not be diverted to domestic market. On August 17, 2021, informant submitted to NBI-TFAID the video footages and photos showing the repacking and placing of tax stamps on each pack of Chinese cigarettes inside BUMI JAYA warehouse, and further attests that the finished repacked cigarettes were transferred and stored to the second warehouse of BUMI JAYA also in SBFZ. The said acts by BUMI JAYA are in violation of Section 1423 (Removing or Repacking Goods in Warehouse) of RA 10863 (Customs Modernization and Tariff Act). With these, Search Warrants were issued by RTC Branch 97, Olongapo City, directing the TFAID to immediately search the premises of BUMI JAYA. On August 20, 2021, TFAID operatives implemented the Search Warrants which resulted in the seizure of repacked Chinese cigarettes, equipment used in repacking, repacking materials, and several BIR tax stamps. NBI-TFAID also seized 45,000 master boxes of assorted Chinese cigarettes with estimated value of Php 1,350,000,000. Workers of BUMI JAYA were also caught in flagrante repacking Chunghwa cigarettes. TAN AH SENG and TAN YAN TENG were then placed under arrest and were informed of their rights . Subjects TAN AH SENG and TAN YAN TENG were presented for inquest proceedings on August 23, 2021 before the Office of the City Prosecutor, Olongapo City for violation of Section 1423 of RA 10863. Incorporators of BUMI JAYA INTERNATIONAL CORP. namely: GINA TSAI, TAN LIAN HONG, ADELIA C. TAN, and CHI JUNG HSIAO aka CHI YIN HSIAO, all at large, were also charged with violation of Section 1423 of RA 10863 even though they are not present during the implementation of Search Warrants. Pursuing its investigation, NBI-TFAID will request the BIR to certify whether or not the seized tax stamps are counterfeit, in preparation for filing of additional charges against the incorporators/officers of BUMI JAYA for violation of National Internal Revenue Code.

body: PRESS STATEMENT August 10, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } PRESS RELEASE | NBI ARRESTS THREE INDIVIDUALS IN CYBER FRAUD SCHEME TARGETING BPO SECURITY CREDENTIALS On August 4, 2026, operatives from the National Bureau of Investigation Cybercrime Division (NBI-CCD) successfully arrested three individuals involved in a cyber fraud scheme that attempted to breach corporate security credentials and illegally siphon reward points. The Subjects were identified and taken into custody on August 4, 2026, following a series of coordinated entrapment operations across Sampaloc, Manila, and in Novaliches, Quezon City. The investigation stemmed from a February 2026 complaint filed by a BPO after a suspicious Facebook persona, “Fernandez B. Nancy,” began soliciting employees in Manila and Davao. The scheme enticed workers with offers of extra income to make unauthorized transfers of hotel points to designated accounts for complimentary hotel stays. To dismantle the operation, NBI-CCD operatives went undercover, pretending to be a company employee instructed by the fraudster to surrender a “key”— a physical hardware security token granting access to the hotel portal. Undercover operatives dispatched the device using courier services, tracking it through a chain of handoffs until the one subject received the package in Sampaloc. The subject subsequently led agents to the other 2 subjects in Novaliches, Quezon City, where all three were caught receiving the hardware key and were immediately apprehended. Subjects were presented for inquest procedures for Illegal Access, Misuse of Devices, and Computer-Related Fraud under Republic Act No. 10175 (the Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012). https://www.facebook.com/reel/1067114079141585

body: PRESS STATEMENT February 20, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } NBI ARRESTS SUBJECT IN PHP 50 MILLION INTERNATIONAL GOLD INVESTMENT SCAM PASAY CITY, Philippines – The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI), through its Cybercrime Division (CCD), successfully arrested an individual linked to a syndicated scam that defrauded a Hong Kong-based company of approximately USD 874,200.00 (PHP 50,633,226.90.). The scheme began with the unauthorized diversion of an initial gold shipment to Kenya, which was later re-routed to the Philippines without the complainant’s consent. Under pressure, the victim entered a second agreement for an additional 90 kilograms of gold, only to be met with further complications while traveling to Kenya. There, she was introduced to an individual posing as a Congolese embassy official and was eventually told the entire 100-kilogram consignment had been “mistakenly” shipped to the Philippines. The scammers then demanded an additional USD 282,800.00 as a purported “bribe” to facilitate the release of the cargo, effectively trapping the victim in a high-stakes extortion plot. Acting on the complaint, the NBI-CCD organized an entrapment operation on February 13, 2026, at the Lime Resort Manila. The suspect met with the complainant under the guise of escorting her to a bonded warehouse to release the gold upon payment. During the arrest, the Subject—noted for his large physical build—violently resisted, causing minor injuries to NBI operatives. He was eventually subdued and taken into custody. The NBI-CCD has recommended the filing of charges against the Subject for Syndicated Estafa under P.D. 1689 in relation to the Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012 (R.A. 10175), Robbery under Articles 293 and 294 of the Revised Penal Code, and Direct Assault under Article 148 for the physical injuries inflicted upon the arresting officers during the entrapment operation. Lastly, the Subject is being charged with violations of the Access Devices Regulation Act of 1998 (R.A. 8484) to address the fraudulent methods used throughout the gold investment scheme. The National Bureau of Investigation remains steadfast in its mandate to provide equal protection and swift justice to all, regardless of nationality or origin. Our doors are open to every victim of crime, and we assure our foreign partners and investors that their complaints will be met with the same rigor, transparency, and dedication to the law as any local case. In the face of globalized crime, the NBI does not discriminate; we simply pursue the truth and hold those who break our laws accountable #NBIServes Media Contact: HA Palmer U. Mallari NBI Spokesperson [email protected]

body: PRESS STATEMENT July 30, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } Under the leadership of Director Judge Jaime B. Santiago (Ret.), the NBI-Southeastern Mindanao Regional Office (SEMRO) together with the Integrated Bar of the Philippines (IBP)-Davao City Chapter arrested five (5) individuals in different areas of Davao City—specifically in Bolton and Magallanes on July 28, 2025. The case stemmed from the request of IBP-Davao City Chapter to arrest and prosecute individuals who falsely present themselves as lawyers or notaries public and illegally offer notarization services for a fee. In response, NBI-SEMRO agents immediately conducted operations to curb the unlawful activities, resulting in the apprehension of the five Subjects for engaging in unauthorized notarization without being admitted to the bar and authorized to practice law or duly commissioned notaries public pursuant to the Rules on Notarial Practice. Director Santiago reminded the public to exercise vigilance and to verify the identities and authority of individuals claiming to be lawyers or notaries, warning that these unscrupulous acts are illegal and will not be tolerated by the NBI, the IBP, and the Court. He emphasized that violators will be arrested and put to jail in accordance with the law. This joint effort is a firm stand to protect the public, uphold the rule of law, and preserve the dignity of the legal profession.

body: A construction worker who duped a businesswoman into buying a bogus gold bar was arrested by agents of the National Bureau of Investigation during an entrapment in Zambales yesterday. The subject is identified as DOMINGO VILLANUEVA SALAZAR , alias “ Noel “. 42, a foreman, and a resident of Bgy. Salaza, Palauig, Zambales. Investigation bared that in May 2012, complainant Rosalyn T. Belarga alleged that she met Salazar through a friend who convinced her to pool their finances in order to buy a gold bar from an Aeta which then can be sold for a huge profit. Noel allegedly told them that a gold bar is part of a chest of gold bars unearthed by his father-in-law while making charcoal in the mountains of Zambales. After samples of gold grains provided by the suspect turned out to be real gold as appraised by a pawnshop, complainant bought one-half of a purported gold bar for P100,000. However, upon presented for appraisal at a pawnshop, said gold bar turned out to be fake. Complainant told Noel about the findings, but Noel asserted that there is really a gold bar and the fake one was inadvertently given to her. He even instructed her to find a financier who can raise P500,000 and the real gold bar would be sold to them. It was then that the complainant sought investigative assistance from the NBI. Acting on said complaint, an operation was planned. On July 9, 2012, NBI operatives proceeded to a fast food chain in Iba, Zambales. In the afternoon of the same day, Noel called up the complainant and asked her to meet him at the back of the said restaurant where he asked her to go with him to an undisclosed place to pick up the said gold bar. When Noel showed up, and after positive identification by Belarga, NBI agents posted nearby accosted and arrested him. Later, he was brought to the NBI. Charges for Estafa is being readied against the suspect for filing in the Prosecutor’s Office of Iba, Zambales.

body: PRESS STATEMENT July 19, 2022 NBI FILES CHARGES AGAINST AN INDIVIDUAL FOR USURPATION OF AUTHORITY The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today announced the filing of criminal charges before the Department of Justice against an individual for usurpation of authority and Illegal possession of fireams during Election Gun Ban. The NBI has identified the subject as RAMIL DIEZ y BUNAGAN, who introduced himself as an NBI Agent while confronting a motorist in a traffic altercation along the road in Meycauayan City, Bulacan on May 8, 2022. The incident was caught in a video that went viral in the social media. Subject DIEZ was seen pointing a gun at the motorist while threatening him. Verification with the PNP–Firearms and Explosives Office (PNP-FEO) showed that Subject Diez is a registered owner of ten (10) firearms of different kinds of caliber but has not been issued a Permit To Carry Firearms Outside of Residence (PTCFOR) for any type of firearm. Verification with the Bureau’s Personnel Division revealed that Subject Ramil B. Diez is not an employee of the NBI. NBI-AGD also discovered that the altercation transpired during Election Gun Ban. Thus, NBI-AGD verified with the Commission on Election (COMELEC) whether Subject Diez has a Gun Ban Exemption. A Certification issued by the COMELEC stated that Subject Diez has not applied for nor was granted a Certificate of Authority to Bear, Carry or Transport Firearms or Other Deadly Weapons during Election Period. NBI-AGD, based on the testimony of the complainant and evidence gathered, recommended the filing of charges against Subject Diez for violation of Article 177 (Usurpation of Authority) of the Revised Penal Code (RPC), as amended; violation of Article 282 (Grave Threats) of the RPC, as amended; Article 286 (Grave Coercion) of the RPC, as amended; and violation of Batas Pambansa Bilang 881 (Omnibus Election Code) in relation to COMELEC Resolution No. 10728 (Illegal Possession of Firearm during Election Gun Ban).

body: In support to the campaign of government against illegal activities during the Enhanced Community Quarantine (ECQ), the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) announces the arrest of an individual on April 16, 2020 in Binan City for selling fake Presidential Task Force on Moral Recovery (PTFMR) Identification Cards. NBI Officer-In-Charge (OIC) Eric B. Distor identified the subject as MARVIN Q. CUNA, who introduced himself as a member of the Presidential Task Force on Moral Recovery (PTFMR) under the Office of the President and chairman of PTFMR Biñan City Chapter. OIC Distor said the operation stemmed from information that a certain individual is selling PTFMR identification card for Php 1,500.00 to Php 2,000.00 per card to any party interested to possess said identification card and become a member of PTFMR. Distor added that Subject Cuna was photographed displaying the alleged PTFMR ID reflecting the seal of the Republic of the Philippines and other seals and logos of different government agencies, the name and signature of the President of the Philippines and a certain Ema Dela Cruz Danao. Also reflected on the ID is the photo and signature of the subject. Distor stressed that based on this information, operatives of NBI-Laguna District office (NBI-LAGDO) coordinated with the informant and managed to transact with the subject who agreed to meet at the LTO Office in Biñan City. NBI operatives together with the informant/poseur-buyer proceeded to the agreed meeting place. After handing to poseur-buyer an application form and giving the filled-out form back to the subject with the payment of Php 3,000.00 marked money, the subject was placed under arrest. Distor said that Subject Cuna was subjected to inquest proceedings online in Biñan, Laguna for violation of EO# 179 in relation to Art. 179 of the Revised Penal Code, Illegal Use of Presidential Seal and Logo, Bayanihan to Heal as One Act or R.A. 11469.

body: PRESS STATEMENT March 14, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } In accordance with the directive from National Bureau of Investigation Director, JUDGE JAIME B. SANTIAGO (Ret.), to address the illegal sale of unsafe and hazardous meat products in the market, a significant operation was carried out by the NBI-Central Luzon Regional Office (NBI-CELRO). On March 12, 2025, authorities executed a search warrant against Atkins Import and Export Resources Inc. in Meycuayan City, Bulacan, for violating Republic Act No. 7394 (the Consumer Act of the Philippines) in relation to Republic Act No. 10611 (the Food Safety Act of 2013). During the operation, NBI-CELRO agents discovered and seized a massive cache of expired meat products. These products were found in a shocking and unacceptable state-contaminated, foul-smelling, and already decomposing. The discovery underscores a dire public health threat, as consuming such unsafe products can result in severe illness or even death. The seized products will be swiftly and safely disposed of at the Far East Fuel Corporation facility in San Ildefenso, Bulacan, in full compliance with safety protocols. In addition, the NBI-CELRO will file formal charges against the responsible parties within Atkins Import and Export Resources Inc., holding them accountable under the relevant penal laws. Director Santiago has made it clear that the NBI remains unwavering in its commitment to combat illegal trade practices, particularly those involving substandard and dangerous food products. The Bureau will continue to actively investigate and target operators who put the public at risk, including corrupt food safety officers who may be complicit in these illegal activities.

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today announced the arrest of an individual by agents of the NBI-Naga District Office (NBI-NADO) in Naga City for alleged sextortion. NBI Officer-In-Charge (OIC) Director Eric B. Distor identified the subject as NESTOR NOEL PENAS a.k.a. PINES. Director Distor said that the operation stemmed from the complaint filed by the female victim of Subject Penas alleging that the subject is forcing her to meet with him to have sexual act. According to the sworn statement of the victim, she met the subject thru a friend sometime in November 2021 when Victim was in need of money. The victim disclosed that she and Subject Penas had sexual act several times, and during their second meeting, she alleged that Subject recorded their sexual act without her consent. Victim added that sometime on January 2022, Subject Penas threatened the victim that if she will not give in to his demand, Subject will divulge to the friends of the victim about their sexual activities. Thus, the victim gave in to the demands of the subject. On February 9, 2022, Subject Penas sent to the victim their pictures inside a hotel, some pictures showed nude pictures and their sexual act and demanded to meet him at a hotel in Naga City on February 13, 2022 at 08:00PM. The victim informed one of the agents of NBI-NADO about the meeting and an entrapment operation was planned. On February 13, NBI-NADO proceeded to the target hotel and positioned themselves strategically in the vicinity of the hotel. The victim upon entering the room gave the pre-arranged signal to the operatives, which prompted them to rush in the hotel room and caught the subject in flagrante delicto. The operatives were able to seize one (1) video recording device, three (3) smart phones, and one (1) tablet. Subject Penas was presented for inquest proceedings before the Naga City Prosecutor’s Office for violation of Article 288 (Grave Coercion) of the Revised Penal Code and R.A. 9995 (Anti-Photo and Video Voyeurism Act of 2009).

Sa bisa ng search warrants na inisyu ng Makati Regional Trial Court Branch 147, sinalakay ng NBI-IPRD ang ilang tindahan sa Maynila at kinumpiska ang 7,009 piraso ng mga pekeng lotion, body wash, shampoo at bar soap na may tatak na CETAPHIL, 5,779 piraso ng mga produktong may tatak na JOHNSON’S at AVEENO, at 34,608 piraso ng Off Lotion. Kasong paglabag sa Section 155, na may kaugnayan sa Section 170 (Trademark Infringement) ng Republic Act No. 8293 (Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines) ang ipa-file sa may-ari ng mga establisimyento. Nagbabala rin si NBI Director Melvin A. Matibag sa publiko na maging mapanuri at huwag tangkilikin ang mga pekeng produkto dahil maaaring mag dulot itong panganib sa kalusugan at hindi dumaan sa tamang proseso upang mairehistro. https://www.facebook.com/reel/923663243339851

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) arrested 16 undocumented Taiwanese allegedly involved in credit card fraud victimizing other foreigners using the Philippines as their base of operation during a raid of their hideout in Subic Bay, Zambales yesterday. The 16 Taiwanese national were identified as: ZHIYANG CHEN, 23; JIENGDE HUANG, 23; WENJIE HUANG, 25; ZHILONG HUANG, 29; YILEN LIANG, 41; CHANGJIE LIN, 41; GAOFONG LIN, 33; PEIGI LU, 28; WEIHONG QIU, 25; JIANGFONG SU, 34; PENXIU WANG, 24; YIFONG XU, 31; WENQIN ZHUANG, 22; YURAY ZHANG, 30; WEIXIAO ZHANG, 25; and LE TIENG WU, 23. Investigation by the NBI Cyber Crime Division (CCD) disclosed that the NBI received early this week a report about the illegal activities of a group of Taiwanese in the Unit 353-A, B, C and D all located at El Kabayo Road, Forest View Leisure Residences, Binictican Drive, Subic Bay Freeport Zone, Zambales. They used these units as their base of operation. One of the syndicate’s modus operandi is to pretend that they are from the bank. They will call the would-be victim and inform them that their account was compromised and they need to give their account number in order to strengthen the security of the account. In the process, they are able to get the account information where they can subsequently transfer the money to an account of their choice. Another modus is for a syndicate member to pretend as a law enforcer or a prosecutor handling the complaint against the person they are victimizing. To avoid being charged, the victim is convinced to settle the case by depositing a certain amount on a given account. On April 1, 2013, after a series of surveillance that confirmed said report, search warrants were applied for and issued by the Manila RTC Branch 24. Yesterday, teams from NBI- CCD, Olongapo District Office (OLDO), and SBMA Police proceeded to the Forest View Leisure Residences, Subic Bay Freeport, Zambales and served the warrants to the four (4) units occupied by the suspects. Sixteen occupants/suspects were arrested and brought to the NBI main office in Manila for detention. During the search, also found and seized were electronic gadgets, devices and voluminous documents which are being used in the said illegal activities. One of the seized credit card, an American Express card, was found to be fake upon verification. They were referred for inquest at the Balanga, Bataan Prosecutor’s Office for violation of RA 8484 otherwise known as Access, Devices, Regulation Act of 1998.
