body: In line with the thrust of President Rodrigo Roa Duterte of improving the quality of service and bring the government closer to the people, the National Bureau of Investigation today said it has recently opened a new clearance area in NBI-Central Visayas Regional Office, Cebu City. The new NBI-CEVRO Clearance area consists of a two-phase construction involving the roof extension which was built under the support of the Cebu Chamber of Commerce and Industry (CCCI) through its Adopt-A-Station Program. The Clearance booth, on the other hand, was constructed through the goodwill of Engr. Apollo S. Enriquez, a major donor and a friend of the Bureau. NBI Director Dante A. Gierran together with other bureau officials, Assistant Director, Medardo G. de Lemos; Deputy Director for Regional Operations Service, Atty. Antonio M. Pagatpat; Deputy Director for Information Communication Service, Atty. Jose Justo S. Yap; and Chief of Staff, Atty. Ernesto Y. Macabare were present to witness the said event. RD Patricio S. Bernales Jr., in his welcome speech, related that years back, people who wanted to secure NBI clearance had received crude method of welcome, and that time NBI CEVRO had only tents so clearance applicants had to endure the heat and rain. “The CCCI, with benevolent hearts, knew the NBI need this kind of project,” he added. CCCI President, Melanie Ng, for her part, said that they want to improve the facilities of the NBI Region 7 to enhance its services to the people. She also cited that it is only in Cebu that there was close collaboration and partnership between the public and private sector. In his acceptance speech, NBI Director Dante A. Gierran expressed his gratitude to CCCI and Engr. Apollo S. Enriquez for the benevolent donation of the building, and challenged NBI CEVRO personnel to do their best to live up to the bureau’s mandate of serving the people. The turn over ceremony and unveiling of marker was attended by Melanie C. Ng, President of CCCI; Vice President Teodoro B. Locson, Mr. Joe Ng, CCCI Chairman of Adopt-A-Station Program, CCCI Board of Trustees, CCCI project member-donors, and Engr. Apollo S. Enriquez. Bringing the services of the government closer to the people is a way of restoring and enhancing trust, respect and confidence. As of end of May 2017, there are already a total of ninety seven (97) operational NBI clearance sites nationwide.

body: In line with the relentless campaign of the government to stamp out corruption, the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today said operatives of the NBI- Special Task Force (NBI-STF) have arrested two (2) Subjects in an entrapment operation in Lingayen, Pangasinan for extortion activities. NBI Director Dante A. Gierran identified the Subjects as LEONARDO NICOLAS, Sr. Graft Investigator in the Office of the Ombudsman and his cousin, ATTY. ISAGANI NICOLAS, a Labor Arbiter in the National Labor Relations Commission. Both were arrested by NBI-STF operatives in a hotel after receiving the entrapment money they demanded from a Pangasinan Congressman and his son, who is a Municipal Mayor of Bugallon, Pangasinan. Gierran said the case stemmed from a complaint filed by Amado T. Espino, Jr. against Subject LEONARDO NICOLAS for violation of Article 210 of the Revised Penal Code (Direct Bribery), Violation of Article 293 of the Revised Penal Code (Robbery Extortion) and Violation of Section 7(d) in relation to Section 11 of R.A. 6713 otherwise known as “The Code of Conduct and Ethical Standards for Public Officials and Employees. Gierran said that sometime in May, Subject NICOLAS has been calling the Provincial Legal Officer and Provincial Accountant of Pangasinan demanding sums of money for the dismissal of cases filed against Congressman Espino and his son, Jumel (Bugallon, Pangasinan Municipal Mayor), in the Office of the Ombudsman. When Mayor Jumel Espino, Atty.Geraldine Baniqued, met with Subject NICOLAS, NICOLAS demanded that the case may be settled if Mayor Jumel Espino will pay at least P1,350,000.00 for the 9 allegations to which Mayor Jumel Espino, when informed, firmly rejected the illicit proposition. In the second meeting on July 14, 2017 at Star Plaza Hotel, this time with Mr. Arturo V. Soriano, Provincial Accountant of Pangasinan, who received a call from Labor Arbiter Atty. ISAGANI NICOLAS, cousin of Subject LEONARDO NICOLAS, Subject LEONARDO NICOLAS demanded P1,000,000.00 per case or a total of P3,000,000.00 for the 3 pending cases against Congressman Amado Espino, Jr. wherein he can show a resolution of the cases from the Office of the Ombudsman. On July 19, 2017, Mr. Soriano received a call from Subject NICOLAS reiterating his threat that the complaint against Mayor Jumel Espino and Congressman Amado Espino, Jr. will be docketed and Mayor Espino will be suspended. Congressman Espino, on the following day, sought the assistance of the NBI in coordination with the Office of the Ombudsman. Upon strict orders from Director Gierran, the NBI-STF set up an entrapment operation that led to the arrest of the two Subjects.

title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) has endorsed to the Department of Justice (DOJ) the transfer of Rolan “Kerwin” Espinosa to a more secured facility at Bureau of Jail Management and Penology (BJMP) in Bicutan, Taguig City. NBI OIC-Director Eric B. Distor said that the request is aimed at complying with the security and safety protocols of Kerwin Espinosa as a witness under the Witness Protection Program while in the custody of the government and at the same time as an Accused appearing at cases pending in different courts. ¹Director Distor added the move if favorably considered by the Secretary of Justice will result in thep immediate transfer of the young Espinosa to BJMP with ample security facilities equipped to hold a high profile prisoner like Espinosa. On January 13, 2022, the NBI foiled an escape attempt by Kerwin Espinosa and two other detainees thru the hole of the exhaust fan at the ceiling. The swift and timely action of the newly-designated Chief of the Security Management Section (NBI-SMS) and his Executive Officer has prevented the escape of the 3 detainees. “Security measures in the Detention Center and its surrounding premises have already been tightened with regular inspection of jail facilities”, Distor stressed, adding that an on-going review of the status of the detainees case is currently being conducted. As of this date, there are 79 detainees in the NBI Detention Center facing various criminal cases.

body: PRESS STATEMENT July 28, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } PRESS RELEASE | NBI, PAOCC UNCOVER RADIOACTIVE MATERIALS AND SUBSTANDARD STEEL PRODUCTION IN PAMPANGA he National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) uncovered a major industrial and public safety threat involving the alleged unlawful possession and use of radioactive-bearing industrial materials and the manufacture and nationwide distribution of structurally substandard steel products on July 18, 2026, in Magalang, Pampanga. The discovery was a result of a joint intelligence and law enforcement investigation by the NBI- Chemical, Biological, Radiological, Nuclear, and Explosives and Foreign Malign Influence Unit (CFMIU), Office of the Director, and the Presidential Anti-Organized Crime Commission (PAOCC). The implementation of the Search Warrant resulted in the seizure of radioactive-bearing and structurally substandard finished steel products, contaminated production equipment, and other radioactive industrial materials by CHUANGXING STEEL INCORPORATED, valued at more than Php 3 Billion, the arrest of four (4) responsible company officers, and the protection of 347 Filipino and 37 Chinese workers from hazardous industrial conditions. The operation, supported by the Armed Forces of the Philippines, Philippine Nuclear Research Institute (PNRI), Philippine Air Force and Philippine Coast Guard CBRN Units, DENR, DOLE, DOH, and the Local Government Unit of Magalang, effectively halted the production and nationwide distribution of potentially hazardous construction materials. These products could have been incorporated into homes, schools, hospitals, bridges, evacuation centers, airports, seaports, government buildings, military installations, power facilities, and other critical infrastructure. overnment inspections also uncovered extensive labor and occupational safety violations, including wage-related violations, failure to provide mandatory employee benefits, the absence of required Occupational Safety and Health programs and qualified safety personnel, inadequate personal protective equipment, and unsafe industrial equipment and operations. The operation further revealed serious risks to workers, public health, and the environment. Of the 323 workers accounted for, 10 were identified as having suspected occupational radiological exposure after PNRI detected alpha- and gamma-emitting radioactive materials at the facility. The Department of Health (DOH), which conducted health assessments, recommended continued radiological evaluation and long-term medical surveillance. At the same time, the DENR ordered the immediate cessation of operations after determining that the facility posed an imminent, grave, and potentially irreversible danger to worker safety, public health, and environmental integrity. Investigators also documented the melting of coins for industrial use and identified undeclared metallurgical capabilities, including a separate furnace, at least six (6) industrial lathe machines, and other heavy metalworking equipment. The inspection likewise revealed the presence of tungsten pellets, notwithstanding the absence of any apparent relationship between these materials and the company’s declared manufacturing process. Based on the investigation, authorities established probable cause that CHUANGXING STEEL INCORPORATED unlawfully possessed, processed, stored, transported, and utilized radioactive-bearing industrial materials without the licenses, permits, and regulatory authorizations required under Philippine law, while manufacturing and distributing reinforcing steel bars that failed to meet mandatory Philippine National Standards. The NBI has recommended the prosecution of twelve (12) company officers, incorporators, and stockholders, including the four (4) arrested during the implementation of the search warrants, for violations of Republic Act No. 12305 (Philippine National Nuclear Energy Safety Act), Republic Act No. 6969 (Toxic Substances and Hazardous and Nuclear Wastes Control Act), Presidential Decree No. 1586, Republic Act No. 8749 (Philippine Clean Air Act), Republic Act No. 7394 (Consumer Act of the Philippines), and other applicable laws.

body: PRESS STATEMENT February 05, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } NBI TAKES ACCUSED INTO CUSTODY FOLLOWING VOLUNTARY SURRENDER PASAY, Philippines – The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) confirms the voluntary surrender of a Subject before the NBI- National Capital Region (NBI-NCR) on February 4, 2026. A Warrant of Arrest was issued by Regional Trial Court Branch 52 Manila City in connection with a charge for Rape under Article 266-A, Paragraph 1(b) of the Revised Penal Code, as amended by R.A. No. 8353. The Subject surrendered to the NBI-NCR in Ermita, Manila, after his legal counsel formally coordinated his intent to submit to lawful custody. The charge stemmed from a complaint filed by a woman identified in reports as “Anna.” She alleged that she went out one evening in Quezon City with Subject, who allegedly offered to help her reconcile with her husband. They reportedly visited several establishments along Tomas Morato Avenue together with other individuals, including another police officer, a barangay official, and a female companion. “Anna” further alleged that after consuming her last drink, she suddenly lost consciousness and later suspected that her beverage had been tampered with. She later regained awareness inside a motel room where she alleged she was sexually assaulted. She added that the act stopped when she regained consciousness. Prior to the issuance of the warrant, information had been relayed to authorities that the Subject feared for his safety due to circulating reports identifying him as a fugitive. Earlier reports also indicated that the Subject had gone absent without official leave (AWOL) from his work prior to his surrender. The accused is now under the custody of NBI-NCR and will be processed and turned over to the proper court authorities for further legal proceedings. “We welcome the voluntary surrender of the Subject as a step in upholding the rule of law and the authority of our justice system. The NBI will continue to handle this matter with the highest level of professionalism, ensuring that the investigation is thorough, impartial, and guided strictly by due process,” NBI Director Angelito DLP. Magno said. #NBIServes Media Contact: HA Palmer U. Mallari NBI Spokesperson [email protected]

body: PRESS STATEMENT July 21, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } NBI INARESTO ANG ISANG INA DAHIL SA ONLINE SEXUAL EXPLOITATION SA 2 MENOR DE EDAD NA ANAK Inaresto ng National Bureau of Investigation–Violence Against Women and Children Division (NBI-VAWCD) ang isang babae sa Tarlac dahil sa diumano’y pag-exploit sa kanyang dalawang menor de edad na anak na babae sa pamamagitan ng pag-aalok sa kanila para sa mga online sexual activity kasama ang mga dayuhang kliyente. Binigyang-diin ni NBI Director Atty. Melvin Matibag na nananatiling matatag ang ahensya sa komitment nitong protektahan ang mga bata laban sa exploitation, partikular na sa digital na kapaligiran. “Patuloy na lulubusin ng NBI ang pagtugis sa mga indibidwal na nag-eexploit sa mga bata at gumagamit ng teknolohiya upang mapadali ang mga krimeng ito. Sa pamamagitan ng intelligence-driven na imbestigasyon, kakayahang digital forensic, at malapit na kooperasyon sa ating mga kasosyong dayuhan sa pagpapatupad ng batas, patuloy nating tutukuyin ang mga salarin, sasagipin ang mga biktima, at pananagutin ang mga nagkasala sa ilalim ng batas,” dagdag pa niya. Nagsimula ang kaso sa isang referral na natanggap mula sa U.S. Department of Homeland Security Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) Manila noong Disyembre 1, 2025. Sa malawak na imbestigasyong isinagawa ng NBI—kabilang ang pagpapatunay ng identidad, pagsusuri sa digital na ebidensya, paghiling ng impormasyon mula sa GCash, PayPal, at Philippine Statistics Authority, open-source intelligence, pagmamatyag (surveillance), at pakikipagtulungan sa HSI—napatunayan na ginamit diumano ng Subject ang WhatsApp upang makipag-ugnayan sa mga dayuhang kliyente, mag-ayos ng mga mapang-abusong aktibidad gamit ang kanyang mga anak, at tumanggap ng mga bayad. Noong Marso 5, 2026, isang ahente ng NBI-VAWCD, sa pamamagitan ng isang live Zoom session na pinangasiwaan ng HSI, ang mismong nakasaksi sa pagtawag ng respondent sa isang WhatsApp video call kasama ang isang undercover agent ng HSI. Sa tawag na ito, inialok diumano niya ang mapang-abusong online activities gamit ang kanyang mga anak kapalit ng bayad. Batay sa mga nakalap na ebidensya, nag-apply at kumuha ang NBI ng Warrant to Search, Seize, and Examine Computer Data (WSSECD) mula sa Regional Trial Court, Branch 113, Concepcion, Tarlac. Noong Hulyo 14, 2026, isinagawa ng NBI-VAWCD, sa tulong ng NBI-Digital Forensic and Laboratory Division (DFLD) at sa pakikipagtulungan sa HSI, ang isang entrapment at rescue operation kasabay ng pagpapatupad ng WSSECD. Sa gitna ng isang binabantayang online engagement, muling inialok diumano ng Subject ang kanyang dalawang menor de edad na anak para sa mapang-abusong online activities kapalit ng bayad. Matapos makumpirma ang krimen, ipinatupad ng operating team ang warrant at inaresto ang Subject sa mismong akto ng pagkakasala (in flagrante delicto). Dalawang mobile phone ang kinumpiska at isinailalim sa on-site digital forensic preservation bago ang buong forensic examination. Kinumpirma ng sumunod na pagsusuri na ang isa sa mga nakumpiskang aparato ay naglalaman ng WhatsApp account na ginamit diumano ng Subject upang makipag-ugnayan sa mga dayuhang kliyente. Ang mga nakuha ring call logs at chat conversations sa mga numerong nakarehistro sa ibang bansa ay nagpatibay sa mga digital na ebidensyang nakalap noong imbestigasyon. Ligtas na nasagip ang dalawang menor de edad na biktima at itinalaga sa Municipal Social Welfare and Development Office para sa protective custody, medical examination, psychosocial intervention, at aftercare. Ang mga kasong paglabag sa RA No. 11930 (Anti-Online Sexual Abuse or Exploitation of Children and Anti-Child Sexual Abuse or Exploitation Materials Act) at RA No. 9208, na inamyendahan ng Republic Acts Nos. 10364 at 11862 (Expanded Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act), ay isinampa laban sa Subject sa Provincial Prosecutor para sa inquest proceedings. https://www.facebook.com/reel/3972073426429113

body: PRESS STATEMENT May 11, 2022 NBI – SAMDO SEIZES P84M WORTH OF MINERALS, ARRESTS SIX INDIVIDUALS In line with the government’s drive against illegal mining, the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI), have seized illegally- mined minerals in Samar with an estimated value of P84 Million. The operation likewise resulted in the arrest of six (6) individuals. NBI Officer-In-Charge (OIC) Director ERIC B. DISTOR said that the operation stemmed from an intelligence report regarding unlawful extraction of high grade mineral, Ore Pyrite, from an old and closed mining site in Hinabangan, Samar and transported to an unknown destination without the required permit from the DENR. Series of surveillance operation conducted by NBI-SAMDO confirmed the authenticity of the said intelligence report. The operatives also discovered that the trucks transporting the Ore Pyrite are delivered in Brgy Pequit, Paranas, Samar for temporary stockpiling and later transported headed North. Continued surveillance by NBI- SAMDO on April 29 and 30, 2022, revealed that there were movements of laborers in the mining site in Brgy. Bagacay, Hinabangan. Thus, on May 2, 2022, NBI-SAMDO and DENR-PENRO/CENRO flagged down three (3) cargo wing-van trucks as they were moving out of the stockyard. For their failure to present the necessary Ore Transport Permit (OTP) from the DENR when asked by NBI- SAMDO, operatives of the NBI in the presence of Barangay Kagawads with PENRO, CENRO and PNP Paranas Municipal Police Station, seized the Ore Pyrite with an approximate volume of 56,000 kilograms with an estimated value of Php 84,000,000.00 and arrested the Subjects. On May 4, 2022, the 6 arrested individuals were presented for Inquest proceedings before the Office of Prosecutor of Samar for violation of Section 103 (theft of high-grade minerals) of R.A. 7942 (Mining Act of 1995).

body: Two agents of a closed travel agency who defrauded several companies that reserved tour packages for their employees but failed to remit payment were arrested by the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) during an entrapment in Manila this week. The suspects were identified by NBI Director Nonnatus Caesar R. Rojas as: LALLYNE COCAL SAMBILE, 47, and a resident of 1901-a Tayuman St. Tondo, Manila; and AMARYLIS RUIZ SANCHEZ, 42, a resident of 422 Alvarez St., Sta. Cruz, Manila. Investigation conducted by the Anti-Fraud and Action Division (AFGAD) headed by Chief Atty. Cesar A. Bacani disclosed that the NBI received a complaint and sought NBI assistance for the arrest of suspects Sambile and Sanchez for Estafa. Complainant, Edillyne R. Villeno, manager of Flux Design Labs, Inc. alleged that she contacted suspects and bought a tour package for their company’s summer outing in Coron, Palawan scheduled on April 5-7, 2013. She paid a total amount of P130,000. But they decided to hold their outing, instead, at Dos Palmas also in Palawan. Suspects charged and paid an additional amount of P62,400. However, when verified with the Zest Air and Dos Palmas on April 4, 2013, the complainant found out that there were reservations in their employees’ name but were not paid. She immediately contacted the suspects and demanded for the return of their payment but proved futile. On April 23, 2013, an employee of the complainant, Gedrick Roie Roldan, saw an advertisement of suspects in the website. He contacted them, pretending to be interested in their offer and agreed to meet at the Aristocrat Restaurant, Roxas Blvd., Manila in the afternoon of the same date for the down payment. Thereafter, he reported the matter to the NBI. Acting on this information, NBI-AFAD agents immediately planned an entrapment operation. At about 4:30 PM, an undercover agent who accompanied Roldan went to the designated restaurant. Other agents who went with them positioned strategically nearby. However, Sambile insisted that they transact their business in the presence of a policeman so they proceeded to the nearby PNP outpost in Plaza Rjah Sulayman in Malate, Manila. After the complainant handed an envelope containing the marked money as down payment, NBI agents who trailed complainant approached and arrested her. But Sambile requested that she be allowed to contact her companion, Sanchez with whom she was supposed to remit the collected down payment. They agreed to meet in front of Times Plaza at UN Avenue. It was at this juncture that NBI operatives arrested Sanchez. The suspects were brought to the NBI where they were detained. Charges for Estafa as defined and penalized under Art. 315, par 2(a) of the Revised penal Code, as amended were filed against the suspects before the Manila City Prosecutor’s Office.

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today announced the arrest of five (5) individuals by the NBI-Special Action Unit (NBI-SAU) in an entrapment operation in Quezon City for Human Trafficking. NBI Officer-in-Charge (OIC)-Director Eric B. Distor identified the subjects as RYAN PASANA BAUTISTA a.k.a. “RY”, RENE CERENO DAMBAN a.k.a. “REN”/ “RENE”, RONALD RAMIREZ LACAS DE SANTOS a.k.a. “RO”, ROSALIE OSIANA CANILA a.k.a. “SALLY”/”SAL”, and ERIZA ALCANTARA REYES. OIC Director Distor said that the NBI-SAU received a reliable information that a certain residential house in Quezon City is being used for human trafficking activities. NBI-SAU conducted a surveillance and undercover operations for two (2) months and it was verified that a group of individuals are offering women for sexual favors in exchange of monetary consideration in Brgy. Obrero, Quezon City. On May, 21, 2021, NBI-SAU proceeded to the target establishment for an entrapment operation. NBI operatives posed as clients and were offered women for sexual favors. The undercover agents were led into a see-through window to view a room full of women for them to choose from. After the payment, the undercover agents entered their respective room and when the women started to undress, the undercover agents gave the pre-arranged signal to the NBI-SAU raiding team. The raiding team rushed inside the premises and arrested the subjects who are pimps and operators of the sex den. The operation also resulted in the rescue of eleven (11) female victims and seizure of the marked money, Daily Sales Monitoring Sheet, Robust Condom, lubricant, two (2) boxes of Trust Condoms, and several laminated number cards. All of the arrested subjects were presented for Inquest Proceedings at the Prosecutor’s Office for Qualified Trafficking as defined and penalized under Section 4 (a) and (e) in relation to Sec. 6 (c) and (i) of R.A. 9208 (The Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2003), as amended by R.A. 10364 (The Expanded Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act).

title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: Following a relentless campaign by the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) against profiteering, hoarding and overpricing of scarce medical supplies since the COVID – 19 lockdown, the NBI today announced that the estimated value of medical items seized by their operatives has reached about P41.7 Million. NBI Officer-In-Charge Eric B. Distor said these medical supplies include alcohol, hand sanitizer, thermal scanners, PPEs and surgical and face masks which have experienced scarcity in the market when the lockdown was imposed by the national government beginning March 17, 2020 OIC Distor said from the time the lockdown was imposed up to date, the NBI has conducted about 64 operations nationwide by Manila-based and Regional operations units against those who took advantage of the current emergency health crisis brought about by the coronavirus or COVID – 19 pandemic. Aside from the seizure of about P41.7 Million worth of medical supplies, Distor stressed, the NBI also has arrested 122 individuals in buy-bust and entrapment operations conducted against profiteers, hoarders and those who have overpriced the cost of much-needed medical supplies and other items. Distor said that all those arrested have been charged for violations of R.A. 7581 (Price Act of the Philippines), R.A. 7394 ( Consumer Act of the Philippines), R.A. 11469 (Bayanihan to Heal as One Act) and R.A. 10175 (Cyber Crime Prevention Act of 2012) for online sellers of said items. Distor emphasized that the NBI will continue its operations relentlessly against those who take advantage of the present situation and will be dealt with the full force of the law. He also advised anyone who has information on illegal activities to report them to the NBI.

body: PRESS STATEMENT May 22, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI), under the leadership of NBI Director Judge Jaime B. Santiago (Ret.), arrested four (4) Chinese nationals in Liloan, Cebu for violations of Sec. 37(a)(7) and (a)(9) in relation to Sec. 45(c) and (f) of Commonwealth Act No. 613, as amended. The NBI-Special Task Force (STF) and Cybercrime Division (CCD) received a request from the Bureau of Immigration (BI) to serve a Mission Order against a certain ZHAO YANG, Chinese national, and other foreign nationals who may be found at Maxway International Trading Inc., Liloan, Cebu. The Chinese Subject is allegedly working without the appropriate working visa. Acting on the request to serve the Mission Order, the NBI-STF/CCD Agents, on May 13, 2025, conducted covert inquiries and verifications regarding the target area. The next day, after confirming the location identified by intelligence counterparts, NBI-STF/CCD, in coordination with BI representatives, hatched a joint operation to serve the Mission Order. The Subject of the Mission Order, ZHAO YANG, together with three (3) other Chinese nationals identified as WU JUNRONG, QIU GONGCHUN, and WANG CHAOXIN, were present at the location during the operation. They were placed under arrest, apprised of their constitutional rights, and booked at BI-RIOU 7 in Cebu. Arrested Subjects were presented for inquest for the above-stated violations of law. Subsequently, the NBI-STF/CCD operatives assisted the BI-RIOU 7 representatives to transport the Subjects to Manila for their turn-over to the BI Detention Facility in Bicutan.

body: In line with the relentless effort to stamp out graft and corruption in the government, the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) yesterday filed criminal charges before the Office of the Ombudsman against 19 Bureau of Immigration (BI) officers and personnel assigned at NAIA terminals for alleged money-making/so-called Pastillas scheme. NBI Officer-In-Charge (OIC) Director Eric B. Distor identified the BI personnel as GRIFTON SAN PEDRO MEDINA, DEON CARLO ALBAO, FIDEL MENDOZA, ABDULHAFEZ DELA TONGA HADJIBASHER, GABRIEL ERNEST MITRA ESTACIO, RALPH RYAN MACAHILO GARCIA, PHOL BENDAÑA VILLANUEVA, ABDUL FAHAD GURO CALACA, DANILO CARO DEUDOR, MARK DOLLETE MACABABAD, AURELIO SOMERA LUCERO III, GEORGE BITUIN, SALAHUDIN PACALDA HADJINOOR, CHEVY CHASE REYES NANIONG, JEFFREY DALE SALAMEDA IGNACIO, HAMZA USUDAN PACASUM, MANUEL BRILLANTE SARMIENTO III, CHERRY PIE PAYABYAB RICOLCOL, and ER GERMAN TEGIO ROBIN. LIYA WU, private individual and owner of Empire International Travel and Tours was also recommended to be charged for the crime of Corruption of Public Officials as defined and penalized under Article 212 of the Revised Penal Code. OIC Director Distor also said one of the subjects, Immigration Officer (IO) JEFFREY DALE SALAMEDA IGNACIO a.k.a BOSS NYEPI, was likewise recommended to be additionally charged for Qualified Trafficking in Persons under R.A. 9208 for recruiting a lady Taiwanese citizen to work in the Philippines and facilitating and easy entry into the country despite the fact that she was only a holder of a tourist visa. The lady Taiwanese citizen, after a week, was forcibly transferred to a POGO company which she subsequently discovered to be illegal. Her passport was confiscated and she was abused physically, mentally and forced to work like a slave until she was rescued by the NBI-Special Task Force (NBI-STF) on Feb. 3, 2020. OIC Director Distor said a whistle blower, an Immigration Officer, testified under oath on the alleged money-making scheme, referred to among the culprits as “Pastillas” scheme. According to the whistle blower, the Immigration Officers (IO)/ Immigration Personnel (IP) involved in the Pastillas scheme conspired, confederated, mutually helped and aid one another in directly and indirectly requesting and receiving money, gifts, and other benefits, including sexual favors from trafficked foreign women. These IOs/IPs allow foreign nationals entry in the country despite the absence of the necessary documents as required by prevailing Immigration rules and regulations in exchange of so-called “Pastillas money”. Accordingly, OIC Director Distor stressed, foreign travel agencies, clients, and some members of foreign syndicates engaged in illegal activities in the Philippines would forward list of names of foreign nationals together with the arrival schedule thereof to their contacts inside the BI. Said contacts in the BI would forward the list to the Viber groups which they set up to facilitate quick and discreet information sharing among themselves. The Viber Group Chat Administrators (VGCA) would then disseminate the same to the IOs/IPs assigned at the frontline immigration counters, Travel Control and Enforcement Unit (TCEU), and all other IOs/IPs who are members of Pastillas group. Upon arrival of the expected foreign nationals in NAIA, all IOs/IPs are under instruction to allow them entry into the country without so much as a cursory screening nor subjecting them to standard procedures. In return for affording this privilege, these IOs/IPs would regularly receive proportionate shares and commissions from the payments made by travel agencies, clients, and foreign syndicates. Empire International Travel and Tours owned by LIYA WU was named as one of the travel agencies paying Pastillas money for seamless entry of their Chinese passengers. The whistle blower emphasized that Empire is the most popular and powerful travel agency in the BI. To validate the whistle blower’s allegations, Distor emphasized, operatives of NBI-SAU conducted verification with the BI as regards the foreign nationals mentioned in the Viber group. Result of verification showed that those names of foreign nationals in the “Pastillas Viber group” were real and that they actually arrived and were allowed entry in the country. Some were actually processed by the members of the Pastillas group. Records also show that most of them are still in the country despite the lapse of the period given for their stay under immigration rules. OIC Director Distor further emphasized that after an exhaustive investigation by the NBI, the allegations of the whistle blower are meritorious albeit there is a need to conduct further investigation insofar as the other personalities mentioned in his statement is concerned. Based on the evidence gathered, supported by photos and video recordings submitted by the whistle blower, Subjects in this case indeed committed criminal transgressions and should be held liable thereof. Premises considered, Subjects, excluding LIYA WU being a private individual, were recommended to be criminally and administratively charged with violations of Sections 3(a) and 3(j) of RA 3019 otherwise known as the Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act. The NBI also asked the Office of the Ombudsman that Subjects, except LIYA WU, be immediately placed under Preventive Suspension to preclude them from influencing instant investigation.

body: On June 25, 2020, operatives of NBI-International Operations Division (NBI-IOD) arrested PHILIP JACOB L. NOCOM in interdiction operation for alleged violation of RA 9165 and Illegal Possession of Firearms and Ammunitions. Said interdiction operation yielded positive result as it caused the apprehension of the Subject and the seizure of two (2) kilos of shabu and several firearms and hundreds of ammunitions. Subject was presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor of Marikina and is now currently detained at the NBI detention facility. On June 25, 2020, operatives of NBI-Isabela District Office (NBI-ISDO) proceeded to Brgy. Villaluna, Cauayan City, Isabela to serve the Warrant of Arrest for Murder against JESSIE M. ALICUM. The latter voluntarily surrendered and was brought to NBI-ISDO for booking procedures. The Warrant of Arrest was returned to the court of origin in RTC Branch 19, Cauayan City. JESSIE M. ALICUM is under the custody of NBI-ISDO while awaiting for the result of his swab test as needed during the turn over to BJMP. On June 26, 2020, operatives of NBI-Laguna District Office (NBI-LAGDO) arrested CHARITO C. SAUSE et. al for Kidnapping and Failure to Return a Minor. Reference is the Kidnapping case filed by the complainant against the Subjects who allegedly refused to return his minor daughter. On the aforementioned date, NBI-LAGDO operatives, together with Social Worker of CSWD, Binan, proceeded to the residence of the Subjects at Metroville Subdivision, San Francisco, Binan, City, Laguna to conduct rescue operation After an hour, Subject CHARITO arrived and when confronted she claimed that the child was her own and she even showed her passport. But Subject CHARITO eventually revealed the whereabouts of the victim and the latter was recovered at Southview Homes Subdivision, Pacita Complex II, San Vicente, San Pedro City, Laguna. Accordingly, Charges for violation of Article 270, Kidnapping, and Failure to Return a Minor, of the Revised Penal Code were filed against Subject CHARITO. On June 26, 2020, operatives of NBI-Southeastern Mindanao Regional Office (NBI-SEMRO) arrested AIZA A. JACABA and FERDINAND CANLAS for alleged Adultery. Subjects were arrested while in the act of having sexual intercourse inside Subject FERDINAND’s service vehicle. After their arrest, however, the complainant and Subject AIZA came up with a settlement by executing an Agreement of Child’s Custody with Desistance duly notarized by their counsel making inquest moot and academic as complainant manifested thru the executed instrument to desist from pursuing criminal case against the Subjects. On June 29, 2020, operatives of NBI-National Capital Region (NBI-NCR) arrested DAVID KWOK for Robbery/Grave Coercion. Subject was arrested in entrapment operation conducted at Pasay City. Subject KWOK will be presented for inquest proceeding while cohorts of the Subjects JIN JIANG a.k.a. ZHOU a.k.a A HONG will be recommended for preliminary investigation before the Prosecutor’s Office for Robbery. On June 30, 2020, operatives of NBI-Special Action Unit (NBI-SAU) seized various smuggled Chinese medicines and other products in Bacoor, Cavite. NBI-SAU operatives conducted an operation based on an information that unidentified persons are involved in alleged smuggling of suspected Chinese goods mixed with smuggled cigarettes in a warehouse. In coordination with the Customs Intelligence and Investigation Service, Bureau of Customs (CIIS-BoC), a Letter of Authority (LoA) to visit, inspect, and seize the aforementioned illicit articles was issued by the CIIS-BoC. The said LoA was implemented on June 30, 2020 at the subject warehouse. During the inspection, a certain room in an office was found containing assorted Chinese medicines and upon inquiry, it was learned that a certain TIAN QIN, a Chinese national, owns the said medicines. Ten (10) boxes of assorted Chinese medicines were then seized and inventoried. Samples were taken from each box for submission to the Food and Drugs Administration (FDA) for examination and verification. The seized items were then turned over to the Bureau of Customs. Close coordination with the BoC will be undertaken relative to the other personalities that may be involved in the entry and trade of the smuggled medicines in the country. Subsequent to the FDA examination, of the Chinese medicines, inventory and verification of smuggled Chinese goods, appropriate criminal charges shall be filed against QIN and the occupant or operators of the aforementioned office and warehouse. On June 30, 2020, NBI-Special Action Unit (NBI-SAU) file Serious Illegal Detention charges against condominium officials and its security guards for illegally confining and restricting three (3) individuals. Subjects were identified as MEL TUSCO, NAPOLEON BRIÑAS, ATTY. JERICH J. JUCABAN, SADAT MACABANDING, three (3) John Does and two (2) Jane Does, and the assigned security guards of Victoria Towers Condominium, Quezon City. NBI-SAU received a complaint from three (3) individuals through their counsels relative to the illegal confinement and restriction of complainants in their condominium unit for more than three (3) days, from June 22, 2020 by the management and security of Victoria Towers Condominium. Complainants alleged that Subjects had been illegally confining and restricting them in their condominium unit for more than three (3) days despite the fact that they already presented to Subjects medical clearances certifying that they are Covid cleared and thus, fit to return to work. Despite explanation by the operatives, specifically of the existence of the medical certificates issued to complainants who were being continuously detained at their unit, MEL TOSCO, NAPOLEON BRIÑAS, and ATTY. NENETH DE PADUA refused to free the complainants on the ground that they were still awaiting clearance from the Barangay but the Barangay Chairman, Cecilia Tiamson, explained that the only role of the barangay in handling Covid patients and suspected patients are only monitoring and giving them assistance as to their basic needs and that they could not issue health clearance as they respect clearances issued by Infectious Control Consultants. Operatives then proceeded the unit of the complainants to rescue them. MEL TOSCO was apprised of his constitutional rights under the circumstances and was placed under arrest. NAPOLEON BRIÑAS managed to flee from the condominium. Operatives looked for him but to no avail. On the other hand, despite informing the operatives that he was coming, ATTY. JUCABAN did not show up. MEL TOSCO was brought to NBI-SAU office for the proper booking procedures. Serious Illegal Detention under Article 267 of the Revised Penal Code, as amended and Quezon City Executive Order No. 26 s.2020 (Protection of Covid-19 patients/frontliners from any kind of discrimination) were filed against MEL TSOCO, NAPOLEON BRIÑAS, ATTY. JERICH J, JUCUBAN, and security guards SADAT MACABANDING, three (3) John Does and two (2) Jane Does. On July 1, 2020, operatives of NBI-Iligan District Office (NBI-ILDO) arrested BASHER JR BACARAT y TAPANG and EXCHAN GORINSI y PADOMAN for Illegal Practice of Dentistry. Subjects were arrested in entrapment operation in Brgy. Basak Malutlut, Marawi City, Lanao del Sur in coordination with the Philippine Dental Association (PDA)-Marawi City. According to PDA, Subject BASHER JR. was engaged in illegal practice of dentistry at his own dental laboratory together with his assistant Subject EXCHAN. They were allegedly doing invasive and non-invasive dental procedures such as impression taking, denture construction, and tooth preparation. Subjects were apprehended for violation of RA 9484 (Philippine Dental Act). On July 1, 2020, operatives of NBI-Southeastern Mindanao Regional Office (NBI-SEMRO) arrested ARLIN GABAYAN ANASTACIO and JUNE ARDI LOPEZ for violation of RA 9165 (Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act). Subjects were arrested in a buy-bust operation conducted at Main Road, Dona Vicenta Subd. Davao City with operatives of PDEA ROXI. 70 grams of shabu with an estimated value of Php 1,050,000 was confiscated from the Subjects. Cases for violation of RA 9165 are now being prepared for filing in court. On July 3, 2020, operatives of NBI-MIMAROPA arrested PERPETUO BOLINGOT y MONTEJO, JOSEPH EJE y MAULION, and EMAR TOLENTINO y MAULION for Illegal Logging in violation of PD 705. Seized in the operation were Camilina wood with an estimated value of Php 150,000.

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today announced the arrest of an individual in Tuguegarao City by operatives of NBI-Cagayan Valley Regional Office (NBI-CAVRO) for Robbery/Extortion. NBI Officer-In-Charge (OIC) Director Eric B. Distor identified the arrested subject as ROMMEL DELA CRUZ MENDI. OIC-Director Distor said that an owner of a certain hardware filed a complaint against Subject Mendi. According to the complainant, Subject Mendi, who is a news anchor/publisher of Target News based in Tuguegarao, visited their office and demanded money for a subscription contract in the amount of Php 40,000.00. Thereafter, when the complainant turned-down the offer due to financial constraint brought about by the pandemic and travel restrictions, Subject Mendi sent messages through text and Messenger using the account “Rommel Dela Cruz Dimla” threatening the complainant that the latter would crush their business and hurl accusations that the company of the complainant is engaged in illegal activities flourishing under the unlawful protection of the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR). Subject Mendi continuously hurled accusations against the complainant thru Messenger and threatened him that he has the capability to order Regional Director of the DENR- Cagayan Valley to conduct an investigation on his illegal business. The subject told the complainant that he has the power to order the removal of the DENR personnel who are allegedly in cahoots with him. Sometime after, two (2) male persons who identified themselves as personnel of DENR went to the office of the complainant and conducted an ocular inspection. Allegedly, the inspection stemmed from the persistent call from a media practitioner about a stockpiled illegal lumber in the office of the complainant. The two went on their way upon seeing that everything was in order. Due to subject’s continued threat and intimidation, complainant filed a complaint before the NBI-CAVRO against Subject Mendi. Subsequently, while in the NBI-CAVRO office, the complainant continuously received messages from the subject. NBI-CAVRO set up an entrapment operation. Complainant agreed to handover the Php 30,000.00 in their agreed meeting place. Thus, on August 26, 2021, NBI-CAVRO strategically positioned near the meeting place. Upon handing over of the marked money to the subject, NBI-CAVRO operatives apprehended Subject Mendi and was brought to the NBI-CAVRO office where he was processed as per standard booking procedures. Subject Mendi was presented for Inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor of Tuguegarao City for Robbery/Extortion in relation to R.A. 10175, otherwise known as the “Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012”. After the inquest proceeding, an information for Robbery/Extortion was directly filed with the OCC of the Regional Trail Court of Cagayan, Second Judicial Region.

body: PRESS STATEMENT April 20, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } PRESS RELEASE | NBI DISMANTLES A SOPHISTICATED ONLINE SCAMMING HUB IN PARANAQUE; ARRESTS 48 INDIVIDUALS Pasay City, Philippines – On April 17, 2026, the NBI-Special Action Unit (NBI-SAU) conducted an entrapment operation targeting an online scam hub in Paranaque City, resulting in the arrest of 48 individuals. The operation stemmed from information about a group of individuals engaged in illegal online scams, particularly “Love Scamming Activities,” “Pig Butchering,” and “Cryptocurrency Investment Fraud.” NBI-SAU agents validated the information. Accordingly, they applied for a Warrant to Search, Seize, and Examine Computer Data (WSSECD) against the identified units in a condominium in Paranaque City, which the court subsequently granted. Thus, the NBI-SAU agents immediately proceeded to the condominium units and executed the WSSECD. The NBI agents secured the target condominium units to prevent the destruction, alteration, or concealment of digital evidence. During the execution of the warrant, the agents discovered an operational setup consisting of multiple computer workstations, laptops, mobile phones, internet routers, and other digital devices arranged in a manner consistent with a call center-type environment. Examination of the computer units revealed pre-written scripts stored in digital files, containing step-by-step conversational guides designed to engage potential victims, indicating a structured and coordinated modus operandi. Through sustained communication, the subjects employed deceptive representations and emotional manipulation to gain the trust of their victims, using fake profiles that often portrayed them as individuals seeking romantic relationships and inducing them to send money through fabricated scenarios such as financial emergencies, investment opportunities, or urgent personal needs. The victims were then instructed by the subjects to transfer funds through various cryptocurrency wallets. The subjects maintained communication with the victims to continuously solicit money. After establishing that online scamming activities were being conducted on the premises, the NBI-SAU agents arrested 48 individuals, including 41 female Filipino nationals and seven (7) foreign nationals, who were found operating the said online scam hub. The arrested individuals were presented for inquest proceedings for violations of Section 4(b)(2) (Computer-Related Fraud) of Republic Act No. 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012) and of R.A. No. 12010 (AFASA Law). NBI Director Atty. Melvin A. Matibag highly praised the agents of the NBI Special Action Unit (SAU) for their diligent and successful operation in dismantling a sophisticated online scamming network based in Paranaque. Director Matibag issued a strong warning to all individuals involved in this illegal modus operandi, stating that the NBI will spare no effort in relentlessly pursuing and prosecuting them to ensure justice is served. He also reaffirmed the NBI’s unwavering dedication to safeguarding the public from online predators and cyber-criminals, highlighting their ongoing commitment to cybercrime prevention and the protection of citizens in the digital space. #NBIServes

body: PRESS STATEMENT September 10, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } In line with the directive from National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Director JUDGE JAIME B. SANTIAGO (Ret.) to intensify the operations against human trafficking, the NBI-Human Trafficking Division (NBI-HTRAD) arrested HASHIM, SANILYN y LADJA, ASANUDDIN, NURSIDA y JAJI, and HALON MOZAMIL y ABDUL in Tawi-Tawi for violation of Republic Act No. 9208, as amended by R.A. No. 10364, and further amended by R.A. No. 11862 (Expanded-Anti Trafficking in Persons Act of 2022). They were also charged for violation of R.A. No. 8042 (Migrant Workers and Overseas Filipinos Act of 1995). The operation also resulted in the rescue of twenty-seven (27) human trafficking victims (HTVs). The operation stemmed from a complaint filed by one of the human trafficking victims (HTVs), who alleged that a specific group of individuals was involved in human trafficking by recruiting and transporting victims to work abroad illegally. Investigation conducted by the NBI-HTRAD revealed that the recruitment process was done through online messaging platforms, and victims were forced on coerced into crossing international borders using backchannels. During the investigation, Complainant revealed that he was recruited via Telegram by the group to work in a POGO hub in Cambodia. Instead of taking a direct route to Cambodia, the HTVs were instructed to travel irregularly through Manila, Zamboanga, Tawi-Tawi, Malaysia, and finally Cambodia. Their passports would be confiscated, and heavy penalties would be imposed if they failed to complete a one-year contract. Complainant informed NBI-HTRAD agents that he would be travelling with other recruits who were also work in a POGO hub in Cambodia. On September 5, 2025, a combined team consisting of the NBI-HTRAD, NBI-Western Mindanao Regional Office (NBI-WEMRO), Ninoy Aquino International Task Force Against Trafficking (NAIATFAT), Interagency Council Against Trafficking (IACAT), the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD), the Zamboanga Sea-Based Anti-Trafficking Task Force (ZSBATTF), and 1st Special Operations Unit, PNP Maritime Group, closely monitored the Complainant and his group as they traveled to Tawi-Tawi. Upon their arrival at Sanga-Sanga Airport, Tawi-Tawi, the joint operatives followed the Complainant and arrested the two facilitators of their travel, identified as Subjects HASHIM and ASANNUDIN. The operation also resulted in the rescue of the human trafficking victims (HTVs) and the seizure of the subjects’ mobile phones. On September 6, 2025, another facilitator identified as Subject Mozamil was arrested in a follow-up operation while transporting the HTVs. The arrested individuals and the rescued HTVs were then transported from Tawi-Tawi to the NBI-WEMRO office in Zamboanga City. On September 8, 2025, the arrested Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings for the aforementioned violations. Director Santiago commended the agents of NBI-HTRAD and NBI-WEMRO for the arrest of the Subjects. He emphasized their commitment to upholding the law and expressed his gratitude to the other law enforcement and government agencies that provided invaluable support, which contributed to the success of the operation.

title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: Two men misrepresenting themselves as SMARTMATIC representatives who can allegedly influence the outcome of election result, and demanded money from a mayoralty candidate in the South were arrested by agents of the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) in Manila yesterday. The subjects are identified as HADJIE OMAR MASIDING Y RADANGO, a resident of Muludung, Lanao del Sur and 2408 Opalo St., San Andres Bukid, Manila; and SULTAN PUNDATOON BAGUL, residing at Maguing, Lanao del Sur and B11 Lot 20 Vamenta Subd., Barra, Opol. Misamis Oriental. Investigation by the NBI- Counter-Terrorism Division (CTD) bared that complainant Abdulsalam Hadji Harun is a mayoralty candidate for the Municipality of Simunul, province of Tawi-Tawi. On February 18, 2013, suspect Masiding introduced himself as an alleged engineer of Smartmatic employed with the Department of Justice, and his companion, Sultan Pundatoon Bagul, to complainant and his wife Sauda Bagis Harun. They offered their services for a sure victory in the coming local election. Masiding claimed that he has the ability and power to manipulate and disrupt the election results. He further said that he could fixed the programs of the PCOS machines, in exchange for P5 million, with an initial down payment of P2.5 million and the balance to be paid after his proclamation. When complainant informed him that he has no available cash of P2.5 million, Masiding instead demanded P100,000 as payment for “the boys” so that his name will be programmed to the PCOS machine. Yesterday afternoon, before going to his office, Abdulsalam reported to the Chairman of the Commission on Election the nefarious activities of the two suspects. Hence, he was immediately referred to the NBI for investigation and appropriate action. The NBI swiftly planned an entrapment. As arranged, complainant placed the marked money inside a brown envelope. Thereafter, at 7:00 PM last night, complainants, accompanied by NBI agents rushed inside a coffee shop of the Century Park Hotel, Manila, the venue of the pay-off. Later, the complainants arrived and met the suspects during which the former handed the brown envelope with marked money to the latter. Moments thereafter, NBI agents positioned nearby, accosted the suspects, introduced themselves and arrested them. They were brought to the NBI main office for booking. Subsequently, they were referred for inquest before the Manila City Prosecutor’s Office for Estafa and Usurpation of Authority. Suspects are presently detained at the NBI cell.

body: PRESS STATEMENT May 04, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } PRESS RELEASE | NBI ARRESTS ONE FOR HUMAN TRAFFICKING; RESCUES 6 MINORS Pasay City, Philippines – On April 30, 2026, the National Bureau of Investigation – Human Trafficking Division (NBI-HTRAD) arrested an individual in Bislig City, Surigao del Sur, for violation of Section 4(r) of Republic Act No. 11930, otherwise known as the “Anti-Online Sexual Abuse or Exploitation of Children (OSAEC) and Anti-Child Sexual Abuse or Exploitation Materials (CSAEM) Act.” The operation stemmed from a referral by the Australian Federal Police following the arrest of an Australian national in connection with human trafficking activities. Investigation revealed that the foreign subject had been communicating with a Filipina via Facebook. Digital evidence, including chat logs, CSAEM, and financial records, showed that the Filipina received payments in exchange for facilitating the live online sexual exploitation of her children, as well as her minor nephews and nieces. Acting on the information, NBI-HTRAD agents conducted surveillance in a remote barrio, confirming the location of the victims. A Warrant to Search, Seize, and Examine Computer Data (WSSECD) was subsequently secured and implemented. Operatives from NBI-HTRAD and NBI-CARAGA, in coordination with the City Social Welfare and Development Office (CSWDO) of Bislig City and the DOJ’s Cyber-TIP Operations Division (NCC-OSAEC-CSAEM), carried out the operation. On-site forensic examination of seized devices yielded CSAEM, leading to the immediate arrest of the suspect and the rescue of six minor victims. NBI Director Melvin A. Matibag commended the operating teams and reiterated the Bureau’s firm commitment to combat human trafficking. He emphasized that operations will continue, in close coordination with partner agencies, to ensure the protection of vulnerable sectors and the prosecution of offenders.

body: PRESS STATEMENT September 11, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } Under the leadership of NBI Director Judge JAIME B. SANTIAGO (Ret.), NBI-Bataan District Office (BATADO) arrested two (2) individuals for alleged violation of Republic Act No. 9208 as amended by Republic Act No. 10364 as further amended by Republic Act No. 11862, otherwise known as the “Expanded Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2022”. On August 27, 2025, NBI-BATADO received information that a resto-bar in Limay, Bataan, was employing female individuals and offering them for entertainment and sexual services for a fee of Php 2,500. Surveillance operations conducted by agents of NBI-BATADO agents validated the information, and a rescue operation was conducted on September 03, 2025. This resulted in the arrest of REGINA MAE TAGULAO and GRAZEL DE VERA, both of legal age and residents of Limay, Bataan, and who work as Manager and Cashier of the bar, respectively. The operation also led to the rescue of five (5) individuals. Two (2) of them were minor: (one (1) female “trafficked victim” and one (1) male “child-at-risk”. Both were subsequently placed under the custody of the Municipal Social Welfare and Development Office – Limay, Bataan, for eventual turnover to their respective temporary shelters. Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the Provincial Prosecutor for the above-stated violations.

title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: PRESS STATEMENT February 21, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } The National Bureau of Investigation-National Capital Region (NBI-NCR), under the supervision of NBI Director Judge Jaime B. Santiago (Ret.), arrested one (1) Chinese national and his Filipino interpreter for love scam activities. On February 3-4, 2025, the NCR Agents, together with the NBI-Digital Forensic Laboratory (DFL) and NBI-Technical Intelligence Division (TID), implemented Warrants to Search, Seize, and Examine Computer Data (WSSECD) at four (4) clusters or workstations located at the 8th Floor of Circuit Corporate Center One Building, Hippodromo Street, Brgy. Carmona, Makati City. Found thereat were Customer Service Representatives (CSR) in their respective workstations chatting with their prospective “lovers” or victims. They were instructed to follow a procedure given by SUN GUYOUNG with his interpreter TONY PEREZ GO. The CSRs should establish rapport or relationship with their victims, and will then entice them to invest in cryptocurrency exchange. Should the victims agree to their proposals, the CSRs will forward the victims’ profile to either their Chinese managers or to another group that is allegedly located in Cambodia. According to the CSRs, each of them was given scripts that must be strictly followed. If they divert from the script, corresponding sanctions shall be imposed upon them like hefty salary deductions and worst, verbal abuse. Onsite forensic examination on the data gathered yielded positive for love scam activities. Moreover, the Filipino CSRs, models, and employees confirmed the love scam activities they were engaged into. Since SUN, GUOYONG, in connivance with TONY PEREZ GO, were caught in flagrante delicto committing Computer-Related Forgery punishable under Sec. 4(b)(1) and Misuse of Devices punishable under Sec. 5, both of Rep. Act No. 10175 otherwise known as the Cyber Crime Prevention Act of 2012; violation of R.A. No. 12010 otherwise known as the Anti-Financial Account Scamming Law; and violation of R.A. Melvin A. Matibag, ang isang indibidwal sa Quezon City. Inaresto ang individwal dahil sa Robbery With Violence Against or Intimidation of Persons alinsunod sa Article 294 ng Revised Penal Code (RPC) na kaugnay ng Republic Act No. 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012); Illegal Access sa ilalim ng Section 4(a)(1) ng R.A. No. 10175; at Unauthorized Processing of Personal Information and Sensitive Personal Information sa ilalim ng Section 25 ng R.A. No. 10173 (Data Privacy Act of 2012). Ayon sa reklamo ng kinatawan ng isang kumpanya, nakipag-ugnayan ang suspek sa kanilang tanggapan at sinabing hawak nito ang malaking bahagi ng sensitibong impormasyon ng kanilang mga kliyente. body: Immediate response by National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) agents on a report of a baby being sold by her mother led to the rescue of a two-week-old infant in Tuguegarao City, Cagayan Valley last week-end. The suspect, alias GRACE, is in her 30’s, a household help, and a native of Antique province. According to investigation of the NBI-Cagayan Valley Regional Office (CAVRO) it was disclosed that on January 4, 2013, it received a request for assistance by the Department of Social Welfare and Development – Regional Office 2 (DSWD –RO 2) for a possible rescue of a baby being sold by her mother. After confirmation of the report, the mother was sought out by an NBI lady undercover agent who posed as an interested buyer of the baby. It was being offered at P15,000 and payment will be made the following day at a certain place in Soldier’s Hill, Caggay, Tuguegarao City, Cagayan Valley. Coordination was made by the DSWD about the rescue. On the appointed date, time and place, the NBI lady agent met the suspect with the baby, and gave the money. Moments after receiving the payment, NBI agents nearby approached and arrested her. The baby, who was born in mid-December 2012 in Tuguegarao City, was turned over to the DSWD for custody while the suspect was brought to the NBI CAVRO for booking., Further investigation revealed that the suspect left her husband in Antique for a job as household help in Tuguegarao City. During her stay in said place, she had a relationship with a man from Apayao who bore her a daughter. To conceal her shame for the indiscretion, and to have sufficient fare for her trip back home, she put up her new-born baby girl for sale. On January 5, the suspect was referred for inquest proceedings before the City Prosecutor’s Office of Tuguegarao City for violation of RA 7610 in further relation to RA 8369 for Child Trafficking. Subsequently, the City Prosecutor filed the case before the Regional Trail Court, Branch IV (Family Court) the same day.

body: In line with the continuing effort of the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) against illegal activities, operatives of NBI-Special Action Unit (NBI-SAU) seized various smuggled Chinese medicines and other products in Bacoor, Cavite with an estimated value of P1 Million. NBI Officer-In-Charge (OIC) Eric B. Distor said the operatives conducted an operation based on an information that unidentified persons are involved in alleged smuggling of suspected Chinese goods mixed with smuggled cigarettes in a warehouse in Bacoor, Cavite. OIC Distor said that the operation was conducted in coordination with the Customs Intelligence and Investigation Service, Bureau of Customs (CIIS-BoC) that issued a Letter of Authority (LoA) to visit, inspect, and seize the aforementioned illicit items. The said LoA was implemented on June 30, 2020 at the subject warehouse. During the operation, a room was found containing assorted Chinese medicines and upon inquiry, it was learned that a certain TIAN QIN, a Chinese national, owns the said medicines. Ten (10) boxes of assorted Chinese medicines were then seized and inventoried. Samples were taken from each box for submission to the Food and Drugs Administration (FDA) for examination and verification. The seized items were then turned over to the Bureau of Customs. The inventory and verification of other Chinese goods found in the premises are being done by the BoC and currently in progress. Close coordination with the BoC will be undertaken relative to the other personalities who may be involved in the entry and trade of the smuggled medicines in the country. Subsequent to the FDA examination of the Chinese medicines, inventory and verification of smuggled Chinese goods, appropriate criminal charges shall be filed against TIAN QIN and the occupant or operators of the aforementioned office and warehouse.

body: PRESS STATEMENT NBI ARRESTS TWO FOR HUMAN TRAFFICKING, RESCUES EIGHT FEMALE VICTIMS The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today announced the arrest of two (2) individuals in Antipolo City by operatives of NBI- Anti-Violence Against Women and Children Division (NBI-AVAWCD), for Human Trafficking. Eight (8) female victims, five (5) of whom are minors, were also rescued during the operation. Arrested Subjects were identified as RONNETH TOLENTINO y MONTEALEGRE and RENY TUMBALI. Subjects were arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from an information received by NBI-AVAWCD regarding pimps “Trixie” and “RB” who were recruiting and offering minor girls online to clients for sexual exploitation in exchange for a fee. Investigation conducted by AVAWCD operatives confirmed that “Trixie” and “RB”, identified as RONNETH TOLENTINO y MONTEALEGRE and RENY TUMBALI respectively, were offering female victims with ages ranging from 16 to 23 years old, for sexual intercourse in exchange for a fee ranging from Php 5,000 to Php 10,000 depending on age and sexual services to be performed. With these, NBI-AVAWCD hatched an entrapment and rescue operation. Operatives communicated with Subjects thru their Facebook accounts “Trixie Tolentino” and “RB Tumbali” and agreed to meet in a fastfood chain located at Marilaque Highway Cogeo, Antipolo on September 14, 2022. Thereat, Subjects Trixie and RB showed the poseur-customers a group of eight (8) young looking girls confined inside a van. Upon handling the entrapment money to Subjects, AVAWCD operatives immediately announced their authority, apprised the former of their constitutional rights and placed them under arrest. Arrested Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the Department of Justice on September 16, 2022 for violation of RA 9208 as amended by RA 11862 otherwise known as the Expanded Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2002. The operation likewise resulted in the rescue of eight (8) female victims, five (5) of whom are minors. Rescued victims were eventually turned over to the shelter for temporary custody.

While waiting for the approval of her housing loan, Complainant sought for Subject ABARY’s help in obtaining a Title for her house in San Jose Del Monte, Bulacan. body: PRESS STATEMENT September 23, 2022 PASAY COURT ORDERS CONVICTION OF A SUBJECT ARRESTED BY THE NBI The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today said that Regional Trial Court, Branch 112 of Pasay City has issued an order convicting SUMAYA USOP AMAN for violation of Article 172 Paragraph 2 (Falsification by private individual) of the Revised Penal Code. On September 03, 2021, Subject Aman was bound to the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia (KSA) to work as a household service worker. Bureau of Immigration (BI) officers intercepted her after she gave inconsistent answers to the interviewing BI officer. Subject Aman admitted that the date of her birthday appearing on her passport is not her real birth date. Accordingly, BI officers turned over the subject to the NBI-IAID for investigation. NBI-IAID’s investigation revealed that Subject Aman presented herself as a returning household service worker in KSA and claimed that she was Twenty-seven (27) years old and was born on August 29, 1994. However upon further questioning of BI officers, Subject Aman admitted verbally and in writing that she is in fact Twenty-four (24) year of age, contrary to the date of birth appearing on her passport. During investigation, Subject Aman stated that she previously travelled to KSA for employment and at that time she was not yet Twenty-three years old. She claimed that she adjusted her date of birth on her passport because of the requirement that every Filipino who intend to travel to KSA for employment should be at least Twenty-three years of age. Thus, she was arrested by the NBI-IAID and was presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the Prosecutor’s Office, Pasay City. On August 12, 2022, the Court found Subject Aman guilty for violation of Article 172 of the Revised Penal Code.

body: PRESS STATEMENT March 13, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } NBI SEIZES PHP 12 BILLION IN COUNTERFEIT U.S. CURRENCY; SUBJECT ARRESTED IN PASAY CITY OPERATION PASAY CITY, Philippines – On March 11, 2026, the National Bureau of Investigation – Criminal Intelligence Division (NBI-CRID) arrested an individual in Pasay City for allegedly manufacturing, distributing, and possessing counterfeit U.S. dollar notes and Treasury bills. The arrest followed an intensive three-month investigation by the NBI-CRID, involving strategic surveillance and multiple test-buy operations. These undercover purchases confirmed the Subject’s involvement in the distribution of counterfeit currency. After operatives successfully procured three bundles of fake U.S. Dollars, a final transaction was coordinated at a Pasay City mall, leading to the suspect’s apprehension. NBI-CRID operatives, supported by technical experts from the BSP, proceeded to the payout location to finalize the enforcement action. The Subject was arrested in flagrante delicto upon receipt of the marked currency. The operation yielded a massive haul of counterfeit U.S. Treasury instruments and banknotes valued at Php 12 Billion. The Subject was presented for inquest proceedings before the Pasay City Prosecutor’s Office for violation of Article 168 of the Revised Penal Code (Illegal Possession and Use of False Treasury or Bank Notes and Other Instruments of Credit). NBI Director Atty. Melvin A. Matibag stated that “The seizure of a staggering Php 12 Billion in counterfeit U.S. currency is a testament to the precision of intelligence-sharing with the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP). This operation is not merely an arrest; it is a decisive blow against a multi-billion peso threat to our financial integrity. We remain relentless in our mission to dismantle these syndicates and protect the public from such massive-scale deceit.” #NBIServes

body: PRESS STATEMENT September 05, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } PRESS RELEASE | CHINESE NATIONAL INVOLVED IN VISA PROCESSING SCAM AND EXTORTION, ARRESTED BY NBI The National Bureau of Investigation – Criminal Intelligence Division (NBI-CRID) arrested a Chinese national for being involved in a large-scale visa-processing scam and robbery-extortion against a Chinese company and other foreigners. The arrest was carried out through an entrapment operation at a restaurant in Pasay City. The suspect was caught after accepting “marked money” in exchange for returning the victims’ passports. In the operation, the NBI successfully recovered two (22) foreign passports belonging to the victims from China, Vietnam, and Taiwan. The investigation began following a formal complaint from the victims. They requested the NBI-CRID to retrieve the passports allegedly held by the suspect, as they were allegedly used to process their visa renewal applications. However, the suspect continued to hide the documents and the agency claimed to have returned them to the rightful owners. The investigation revealed that the suspect’s modus operandi was to gain the victims’ trust through fake assistance in visa processing, confiscating their passports, and then demanding ₱150,000.00 per passport in return for their return. The loss of passports and documents caused severe harm to the victims due to the lack of legal identification and travel capabilities. NBI Director Melvin Matibag stated that the NBI will formally prosecute the suspect under the following criminal charges in court, including: Robbery-Extortion, Estafa, Grave Coercion and Resistance and Disobedience, Obstruction of Justice. The NBI is once again warning the public, particularly the overseas Filipinos living in the country, to be cautious of individuals offering quick government transactions using so-called “connections,” and to immediately report any such scams to their office. https://www.facebook.com/reel/1527178032499411

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today announced the arrest of an individual by the NBI- Easter Visayas Regional Office (NBI-EVRO) in Abuyog, Leyte for illegal practice of dentistry. NBI Officer-In-Charge (OIC) Director Eric B. Distor identified the subject as ALVIN SY y CAMINONG. Director Distor said that NBI-EVRO received an information regarding an individual is practicing dentistry in Albuyog, Leyte without proper government license. Acting on the said information, NBI-EVRO conducted a surveillance operation on the said area and discovered that Subject Sy is practicing dentistry for a fee in his residence in Brgy. Nalibunan, Albayog, Leyte. NBI-EVRO requested certification from the Professional Regulatory Commission (PRC) in Manila regarding with the subject’s practice of dentistry. According to the certificate issued by the PRC, Subject Sy does not appear in their database as a registered dentist duly authorized to practice Dentistry in the Philippines. Thus, on February 2, 2022, NBI-EVRO proceeded to the residence of the subject for an entrapment operation. Two (2) of the agents of NBI-EVRO posed as patients, and after the dental service was rendered to one of the undercover agents, the NBI-EVRO operatives announced their authority and demanded from the subject his PRC ID and other documents pertaining to his practice of dentistry but the subject failed to show any. Thus, NBI-EVRO operatives apprehended Subject Sy and was brought to the NBI office where he undergone standard booking proceedings. Violation of Article 5, Section 33 of R.A. 9484 “otherwise known as the Philippine Dental Act of 2007” will be filed against the subject.

body: In an effort to intensify the campaign against the proliferation of fake news on COVID-19, NBI Director Eric Distor has activated various units of the NBI to investigate the source of fake news especially those reports that sow chaos and will lead to unrest and anarchy in the country. Director Distor said he has instructed the different units of the NBI such as Cyber Crime Division (CCD), the Digital Forensic Laboratory Division and other Investigative units including the Regional Operations Service to trace the source of fake news. Distor also said the Bureau’s International Operations Division (IOD) is currently coordinating with its foreign counterpart to verify the accuracy of the statenent. The new directive by the NBI Director was prompted by an alleged statement from the US State Department warning of potential looting incidents during its month-long lockdown to curb the spread of COVID-19. Director Distor said all these reports are baseless and totally untrue. He added that the US Embassy in Manila has clarified it releases information and advisories only through its official media platforms and website. The International Operations Division is now gathering relevant data and other information for possible case build up and filing of cases against the perpetrators of fake news. Director Distor said what is clear at the moment is that the NBI our Cyber Crime Division in particular is now investigating all possible sources of fake news being spread in various social media platforms and will submit its results to the Secretary of Justice. Director Distor assures the public that our government the NBI in particular will take all the necessary steps to protect its citizens against the proliferation of fake news and prosecute those responsible for it. He stressed that our citizens are welcome to seek clarification from the NBI on the accuracy of any report that intends to cast doubts on the efforts of our government’s determined effort to stop the spread of COVID-19.

body: PRESS STATEMENT May 19, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } PRESS RELEASE | NBI DISMANTLES ILLEGAL ONLINE GAME FARMING OPERATIONS IN THE CITIES OF IMUS AND ANGELES In line with the government’s drive against scamming activities, the NBI-Special Action Unit (NBI-SAU) arrested five Korean nationals in two (2) separate operations in Imus City, Cavite, and Angeles City, Pampanga. The operations stemmed from credible intelligence information regarding alleged “farming” activities being conducted by foreign nationals using the platform “Lineage Classic,” a Korean online multiplayer role-playing game centered on prolonged character progression, player-versus-player combat, clan warfare, and an in-game economy involving “Adena,” the game’s primary virtual currency. Adena is widely used in the game to purchase equipment, consumables, and in-game assets, and has reportedly developed exchange value in secondary markets where accounts and virtual assets are traded for real-world monetary consideration. Surveillance operations conducted by the NBI-SAU revealed the accuracy of the information and the location of the operations of the illicit activities in the cities of Imus and Angeles. Subsequently, the agents applied for a Warrant to Search, Seize, and Examine Computer Data (WSSECD) against the two identified locations. On May 8, 2026, the agents of NBI-SAU implemented a WSSECD against the occupants, tenants, and employees occupying the second and third floors of a certain building in Buhay na Tubig, Imus City, Cavite. The operation resulted in the seizure of several computers running the online game “Lineage Classic.” They also discovered that the subjects used two messaging applications to relay operational tasks, instructions, and gaming-related updates. The Filipino employees present during the operation disclosed that they were working up to twelve (12) hours daily, with only one rest day per week, and received compensation from their Korean supervisor. The operation resulted in the arrest of the Korean supervisor and his two (2) Korean national cohorts. They were charged with violating Section 5(d) of Republic Act No. 12010 (Anti-Financial Account Scamming Act) and Section 28(e) of R.A. No. 8282 (Social Security Act of 1997). In the second operation, dated May 15, 2026, the agents on NBI-SAU, together with the agents of NBI-Tarlac District Office (NBI-TARDO), successfully implemented WSSECD in Angeles City, Pampanga, which resulted in the arrest of two (2) Korean nationals and the seizure of several computer sets used in the operation of the illegal online game farming operation. They were charged for violations of Section 4(b)(2) of Republic Act No. 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012) and R.A. No. 12010. NBI Director Melvin A. Matibag commended the agents of NBI-SAU and NBI-TARDO for their successful operation that dismantled these illegal online game-farming operations.
