body: PRESS STATEMENT June 10, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } In line with the government’s initiative to combat human trafficking, National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Director JUDGE JAIME B. SANTIAGO (Ret.) ordered the intensification of operations against human trafficking. In response, the NBI-International Airport Investigation Division (NBI-IAID) arrested HAYYA DIANE MOLINA y ACUÑA in Pasay City for violation of Section 5(e) of Republic Act No. 9208 (Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2003) as amended by R.A. No. 11862 (Expanded Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2022). On June 5, 2025, the Bureau of Immigration (BI) Terminal III turned over to the NAIA Task Force Against Trafficking – Inter-Agency Counsil Against Trafficking (NAIATFAT/IACAT) then to NBI-IAID, a female passenger alias “Mary” who was bound for Kuala Lumpur. Mary was intercepted based on the apprehension of another passenger by I-PROBES and Bureau of Immigration (BI) personnel on June 4, 2025. Said passenger was bound for Malaysia with a fraudulent BI Border Stamp and Boarding Pass. She averred in her affidavit that initially, Mary insisted that she passed through the immigration officer and underwent proper pre-departure procedures. Eventually, Mary revealed that she was in contact with Subject Molina and DIANE FIONA. Mary added that she came into contact with the Subjects through her niece, who was residing in Malaysia. Subject Molina promised Mary to facilitate and assist her illegal departure from the Philippines. She even assured Mary that she could provide an escort to avoid the pre-departure formalities of the BI, as she works there and has connections. Mary sent 1,920 USD or approximately Php 110,000.00 through a Cryptocurrency account as payment for the assistance. Thereafter, was instructed by Diane Fiona, who introduced herself as an Immigration Officer stationed at NAIA Terminal 3, as to the procedure of Mary’s departure. Verification made with the number Subject Molina communicated with revealed that it was registered to a GCASH account “HA**A DI** M.”, which can be reasonably inferred that the said number belongs to Subject Molina. Supplemental report provided by Bureau of Immigration disclosed that Subject Molina is employed as a technical support staff of a private company contracted to maintain card readers at the airport’s immigration counters and is presently assigned at NAIA Terminal 3. On June 5, 2025, further verification by the NBI-IAID revealed that Subject Molina is currently on duty and was seen in the vicinity of NAIA Terminal 3. Thus, the agents of NBI-IAID immediately proceeded to NAIA Terminal 3 and successfully apprehended Subject Molina. Subject Molina was presented for inquest proceedings before the Inquest Prosecutor of Pasay City for the aforementioned violations. Director Santiago commended the agents of NBI-IAID for the successful operation, which led in the arrest of the Subject.

body: PRESS STATEMENT February 23, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } NBI Holds Official Turnover of Directorship PASAY CITY — The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) formally conducted its turnover of directorship ceremony today at its headquarters, marking the transition of leadership from Atty. Angelito “Lito” Magno to Atty. Melvin Matibag. Attended by members of the Directorial Staff, division chiefs, agents, and personnel, the ceremony underscored institutional stability and continuity within the Bureau. In his farewell message, Director Magno thanked the men and women of the NBI for their professionalism and steadfast commitment to justice. He emphasized that the Bureau’s strength lies in the integrity and dedication of its personnel. Expressing full confidence in his successor, Director Magno said Director Matibag brings strong management expertise, strategic direction, and organizational discipline that will further strengthen the Bureau’s operational efficiency and institutional systems. Upon assuming office, Director Matibag outlined his vision of a more responsive, disciplined, and globally coordinated NBI. He reiterated the directive to ensure the Bureau remains firm, impartial, and relentless in investigating crimes without fear or favor, while strengthening cooperation against organized crime, human trafficking, cybercrime, and other transnational threats. “The NBI must continue to stand as a pillar of justice and accountability. Our duty is to serve the Filipino people with integrity, competence, and courage,” Director Matibag said. The ceremony marked not only a leadership transition but the continuing mission of the NBI to uphold the rule of law and protect the nation from criminal threats.

body: A storekeeper who is a suspect in the brutal killing of a tricycle driver last year was arrested by the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) in his residence in Lucena City last week. The suspect was identified by NBI Officer-In-Charge Atty. Nonnatus Caesar R. Rojas as: WILLIAM BARRAMEDA ABULAD, 55, a storekeeper, and a former tricycle driver, resident of Bgy. Ilayang Dupay. Lucena City. He was arrested by virtue of a Warrant of Arrest for murder, issued by RTC Presiding Judge Dinah Evangeline Belulia-Bandong, Branch 59, Lucena City docketed in Criminal Case No. 2012-48. The other suspect, Warren Abulad, the son of William is at-large. Victim was Lowell P. Glorioso, a father of four and a tricycle driver. Investigation report of the Lucena District Office under Head Agent Olivo Ramos, disclosed that in the evening of August 22, 2011, while victim Glorioso was on his way home collecting “lino” or left over from restaurants for their hogs’ meal, when suspect William, his son Warren, and a certain PJ Rabe blocked the victim’s path and shot him that caused his death. Suspects fled. The victim’s wife Melida sought NBI assistance in arresting suspects. Acting on a request for assistance, NBI operatives conducted sustained surveillance. One of the suspects was spotted on places frequented by suspect William and on April 17, 2012, he was immediately placed under arrest. William resisted and tried to escape but was subdued. He is now detained at the NBI Lucena City District Office.

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today announced the arrest of an individual by the NBI-Anti Violence Against Women and Children Division (NBI-AVAWCD) in a hot pursuit operation in Caloocan City for alleged Statutory Rape. NBI Officer-In-Charge (OIC) Director Eric B. body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today said the agency will look into reports alleging the involvement of three (3) NBI agents in the kidnapping of a South Korean national in Angeles Pampanga on Friday, November 24, 2017. Upon being informed of the incident, NBI Director Dante A. Gierran said he has already formed a team that will investigate and verify the veracity of statements issued by the PNP Chief in a press briefing that implicated NBI agents in the kidnapping incident. Gierran said he has already received the report from the NBI Regional Director and Acting Assistant Regional Director of the NBI-Central Luzon Regional Office (CELRO), which has jurisdiction over Angeles Pampanga, showing that all NBI Agents assigned in Pampanga are all accounted for. The report, likewise, stated that there was no NBI operation conducted in the area in Angeles Pampanga, that was participated in by any of NBI Agents or personnel of CELRO or in any of the District Offices, which operation involved a Korean citizen being apprehended or being forcibly taken into custody and detention, on the date of the incident where the victim, Lee Jung Dae, was kidnapped. Gierran emphasized that the leadership of the NBI including all its Agents adhere to a high standards of ethics with stringent policies and procedures in the conduct of operations, expressing his deep concern over the statement of the PNP Chief relative to the involvement of NBI Agents, which are all unverified reports by the PNP-Anti Kidnapping Group(ASG). In view of this, the NBI is now studying the filing of charges against the PNP for issuing statements to the media based on unverified reports the statements of which destroy the high credibility of the NBI. It may be recalled that in previous kidnapping incident of another Korean national, the PNP also implicated 3 NBI officials in the kidnapping of Jee Ick Joo who was later killed right inside Camp Crame. The 3 NBI officials were later exonerated by the panel of prosecutors of the Department of Justice.

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today announced the arrest of an individual for alleged rape in Pasay City. NBI Officer-In-Charge (OIC) Director Eric B. Distor identified the Subject as RICHARD RANA CASTINO who was arrested by operatives of the NBI Anti-Organized and Transnational Crime Division (AOTCD) on May 13, 2021 based upon a complaint of the victim’s parents. On May 4, 2021, the victim was going to see a friend in Pasay City. She saw a Facebook (FB) post of Subject Richard offering rent-a-car w/ professional driver and contacted the subject. The next day, subject Richard fetched and drove the victim to Pasay City after which the subject offered to drive the victim again the next time she will go to her friend in Pasay City, to which the latter agreed out of trust. On May 7, 2021, victim again hired Subject Richard to drive her to Pasay City. However, on their way home, the victim noticed that Subject Richard was driving towards a different direction and parked in a garage. Confused why they were there, the victim shouted at Subject telling him to take her home. But the subject just tapped victim’s legs and told her to relax. Subject Richard alighted from the car and forcibly took the victim in one of the rooms of a hotel in Pasay City. Subject then raped the victim on the early hours of May 8, 2021. Because of fear and confusion, victim was only able to tell the incident to her parents on May 10, 2021 after which they reported the incident to Manila Police District (MPD). The MPD, however, said it does not have jurisdiction on the matter as it happened in Pasay City. They then opted to report the matter to NBI. With testimonial pieces of evidence and the report from the NBI-Medico-Legal Division, hot pursuit operation was hatched. Efforts were immediately made to locate the whereabouts of Subject Richard. Operatives learned that Subject Richard uses the name RICHARD RANA CASTINO in his FB account and posted on his cover photo that he is a registered distributor of Zynergia. By feigning interest on Subject’s business, operatives were able to engage with the FB account. When said FB account responded that he is very much willing to share opportunities of his business, a scheduled meeting on May 12, 2021 was set. On the said date, NBI-AOTCD operatives, together with the victim and her parents, proceeded to subject’s office at West Avenue, Project 7, Quezon City. Upon arrival thereat, the victim positively identified the subject. NBI-AOTCD operatives restrained the subject and placed him under arrest. Subject Richard was then informed of his alleged violation and was apprised of his constitutional rights. Subject RICHARD RANA CASTINO was presented for Inquest Proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor of Pasay City for violation of Article 336 (Acts of Lasciviousness) and Article 266 of the Revised Penal Code and violation of RA 7610 (Special Protection of Children Against Child Abuse, Exploitation, and Discrimination), the victim being a 15-year old minor.

body: The continuing drive of the government against overpricing of medical supplies relative to COVID-19 outbreak has led to the arrest of seven (7) subjects in 2 separate operations by Agents of the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) on March 21 and 24, 2020, in Manila. NBI Director Eric B. Distor identified the 7 subjects of whom 3 are Chinese nationals as DAWN CESISTA GABAYRON, DAVID LIANZON ALMO, JR., VICTOR RULLODA RUGAS, MARK JHAIRROUS FERRY CATIGDAY and Chinese nationals LI CHUNYANG, ZHANG ZHIBIN, and LU YOUJUN. Director Distor said in the first operation, the NBI-Cyber Crime Division (NBI-CCD) received an information regarding online sellers of overpriced and/or sub-standard alcohol products and face masks. On the same day, Director Distor added, the online account was viewed selling unbranded and self-manufactured scented alcohol products at P149.00 each 500 ml of 70 % ISOPROPYL ALCOHOL when it should be sold only for P61.00 to P74.25 under the current price ceiling. NBI-CCD operatives ordered 20 bottles of 500ml 70% ZEN ISOPROPYL ALCOHOL which was confirmed by the seller for P130.00 each with the scheduled meet-up in Paco Catholic Church in Manila at 1:00 p.m. on March 21, 2020. Distor stressed on the scheduled meet-up, NBI-CCD operatives proceeded to area with a member of the NBI team alighting from the vehicle to wait for the delivery. As soon as a woman accompanied by a male carrying a box approached the NBI poseur-buyer, after which having confirmed that alcohol products were inside the box, the poseur-buyer handed over the marked money as payment to the sellers. At this point, CCD operatives declared their authority and apprehended the subjects identified as DAWN DESISTA GABAYRON and DAVID LIANZON ALMO, JR. When asked for any document, the arrested subjects failed to present any business registration or any permit to manufacture or to sell alcohol to the public. Director Distor said the operatives, after learning that the subjects has 2 pending orders from 2 direct suppliers with overpriced amount, a follow-up operation was conducted on the same day to apprehend their suppliers.

title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: In line with the continuing anti-drug campaign of the government, the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today said it has seized Five Hundred Five (505) kilos of illegal drugs (shabu) in Valenzuela City last Saturday. The NBI said 505 kilos of shabu seized by the NBI are now under its custody and being examined by the Forensic Chemistry Division (NBI-FCD). NBI Director Dante A. Gierran said that based on the initial examination submitted by the NBI-Forensic Chemistry Division, it showed that the seized drugs are high-grade shabu. Gierran added that FCD personnel will continue to conduct forensic examinations and will submit its report once completed. The NBI said the operation was based on information received by the Bureau of Customs (BOC) from China’s Office of National Narcotics Control Commission for which the BOC, in turn, provided to the NBI that a large shipment of illegal drugs came from China. A local information likewise informed the BOC of the same shipment. Based on the following information, and the corresponding authority from the BOC, the NBI conducted an operation in a brokerage warehouse in Valenzuela City, which identified the crates that allegedly contain the illegal drugs. The NBI said it then conducted panelling on the crates and machinery using drug detection dogs that reacted sharply on said items prompting the NBI operatives to force open the crates resulting in the seizure of the illegal drugs.

body: PRESS STATEMENT August 4, 2022 RE-ARRESTED FUGITIVE, FRANK CHUA, POSITIVELY IDENTIFIED THROUGH FINGERPRINTS The NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION – DACTYLOSCOPY DIVISION has positively identified through fingerprint examination that the arrested Subject bearing the name TSAI RONG CHANG is the wanted fugitive FRANK CHUA, who also used the name TSAI JUNG SHUI. Subject Chua was first arrested in the year 1989 together with the other subjects for smuggling of 58 kilograms of shabu in Ilocos Sur. However, on March 22, 1990, all the accused escaped from Vigan Provincial Jail. Trial in absentia ensued and on October 7, 1994, the court found CHUA and all other accused guilty of the charge against them and sentenced them to suffer the penalty of Reclusion Perpetua or Life imprisonment. CHUA hid in several places in the Philippines and was arrested by the operatives of NBI-Anti-Illegal Drug Task Force and NBI – Olongapo District Office (NBI-OLDO) on July 4, 2003 at Ding Ho Restaurant, Subic Bay Freeport Zone. He refused to admit that he is FRANK CHUA and claimed that his name is TSAI JUNG SHUI. SHUI’s fingerprint was compared to CHUA’s fingerprint record, retrieved from the Provincial Jail of Vigan, Ilocos Sur. NBI operatives discovered that the two (2) fingerprints are identical to each other hence, he was thereafter turned over to the New Bilibid Prison (NBP), where he again escaped in 2004. Finally, on July 28, 2022, NBI – Task Force Against Illegal Drugs (NBI-TFAID) was able to arrest Subject CHUA in Sampaloc, Manila. Again, he denied that he is FRANK CHUA and claimed that he is TSAI RONG CHANG. Comparative examination. conducted by the NBI-Dactyloscopy Division on the fingerprints taken when he was arrested by the NBI in the year 2003, fingerprints taken at the Bureau of Corrections in September 2003; and fingerprints taken from subject after he was arrested by the NBI-TFAID on July 28, 2022, confirmed that FRANK CHUA, TSAI JUNG SHUI, and TSAI RONG CHANG are one and the same person.

body: PRESS STATEMENT May 31, 2024 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } The National Bureau of Investigation – National Capital Region (NBI-NCR) arrested FREDERICK CAGUIMBAL Y PAMESA, SAMUEL RAGILES Y BORBON JR., JOPHEL VALDEZ, JOSEPH ESTOLAS Y GASQUE and MA ERLIN Q. JANAPIN in SM North Edsa, Quezon City, for Qualified Theft by issuing Unofficial and Falsified Receipts. On May 17, 2024, poseur-customer inquired on how much it will cost for the repair of defective laptop in his possession. Upon verifying the legitimacy of the sales invoice issued to the poseur-customer, an entrapment operation was conducted on May 22, 2024, which resulted the arrest of the five (5) individuals. The other individuals were arrested for selling electronic parts that are not being sold by Silicon Valley. Two (2) cohorts remain at large, namely Ace Jonas Reyes y Canonce and John Paul Marquez y Santiago. Arrested Subjects, and the two at-large were charged for Qualified Theft thru Falsification of Documents – Violation of Article 310 in relation to Article 171 and Article 172 of Revised Penal Code of the Philippines as amended by RA 10591 and (b) other deceits under Article 318 of the Revised Penal Code. title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: On January 8, 2019 , operatives of NBI-Bulacan District Office (NBI-BULDO), together with the team of the PNP Bulacan, arrested JAY VINCENT MARMETO y ROCO a.k.a. JAY for Robbery with Multiple Homicide and Frustrated Homicide. Together with the PNP Bulacan, NBI-BULDO operatives conducted investigation regarding the Robbery with Multiple Homicide and Frustrated Homicide incident that transpired at Isabel Village, Brgy. Tabang, Plaridel, Bulacan. In the midst of the investigation, operatives was able to gather information about the location and location of the perpetrator. A joint team effort resulted in the arrest of Subject JAY VINCENT MARMETO who confessed the full account of the incident and asked for forgiveness and consideration to the bereaved family of his victims. On January 9, 2019 , operatives of NBI-Environmental Crime Division (NBI-EnCD), with the assistance of operatives from the Bureau of Fisheries and Aquatic Resources (BFAR), arrested DAVY ANG in buy-bust operation in Parañaque City for violation of RA 8550 (Philippine Fisheries Code as amended). Also recovered and seized from Subject’s possession were Php 1.2 Million worth of hard and soft corals. Seized items were properly inventoried and turned over to the custody of the BFAR. Charges for the aforementioned violation were filed against the Subject before the inquest prosecution of the Department of Justice (DOJ). On January 9, 2019 , operatives of NBI-Dagupan District Office (NBI-DADO) arrested RONEL JALDO for violation of RA 9208 (Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2003). Subject was arrested in an entrapment and rescue operation conducted in JOY KTV Bar located at Brgy. Bantayan, Mangaldan, Pangasinan. The registered owner of the bar, CELIA A. AFRE, was not in the area during the operation. Depsite her absence, she was also charged for violation of RA 9208. Subject JALDO was presented for inquest proceedings and was temporarily detained at NBI-DADO. On January 10, 2019 , operatives of NBI-Special Action Unit (NBI-SAU) arrested HAN KIM, Korean national, for selling fake gold bars. Subject was arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from the complaints of two (2) Korean nationals against the Subject who was selling fake gold bars worth Php 10 Million. Acting on the complaint, an entrapment operation was conducted resulting in the arrest of the Subject. Subject admitted that he has no authority to transact or sell gold bars and that he could not ascertain the genuineness of the items as it were only entrusted to him by his friend. The gold bars were submitted to the Forensic Chemistry Division for laboratory examination. Subject was presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor of Pasay City for Estafa (Article 315 of the Revised Penal Code). On January 14, 2019 , operatives of the NBI-Special Action Unit (NBI –SAU) arrested SHERMAN TOLENTINO y MAYOR, the gunman in the murder of Ron Kristoffer Paulino y Alfonso last December 11, 2018 in Paranaque City. Investigation conducted by NBI-SAU confirmed that the Subject is a hitman of a ranking Las Piñas Police and is engaged in the sale and use of prohibited drugs. An entrapment operation was conducted in Pasay City and resulted in the arrest of the Subject. found in the Subject’s possession the following: two heat sealed sachets containing white crystalline substance, two one thousand peso bills with marking, one Colt .45 pistol chamber loaded with one magazine with nine live ammunitions, two magazines with live ammunition of .45 caliber 15 rounds, 2 transparent plastic sachets, one improvised glass pipe, fifteen live rounds of .45 caliber ammunition and one bulletproof vest. Certification issued by NBI Forensic Chemistry Division (FCD) showed positive result of the prohibited drugs confiscated to the Subject. Likewise, Subject was also tested positive for use of shabu. Subject was presented before the Assistant City Prosecutor of Pasay City for inquest proceedings. Subject is detained at the NBI detention facility awaiting trial. Agent on case will recommend the prosecution of the Subject for Murder, based on the testimony of witnesses who positively identified the Subject as the gunman. On January 15, 2019 , operatives of NBI-Anti-Fraud Division (NBI-AFD) arrested WILFREDO MARCOS, JIMMIE TORRE, and GERALD GO y SENARILLOS for Estafa, Forgery, and Identity Theft. The case stemmed from various complaints from the internet originating from the website “jora.com”, a job search engine found in the internet. Allegedly, the website was being used as an advertising source for vacant positions with different companies like Cebuana Lhuillier, Hybex, Fitsole, Gadgeter, Becalm Baby, Military Flash and other famous companies. Investigation revealed that the modus starts with the posting of vacant positions of various companies by a certain “Weng” at jora.com. After victims had inquired, they would be directed to an alleged office of the company where a member of the group would interview the victims who will also pay a processing fee without corresponding receipt. After submitting all the requirements asked, the applicant would then be advised to render on-the-job training and after completing the OJT, they would be told that they will be called for their actual job assignments. Unfortunately, the victims never received any call and their application turns out to be a farce. Fortunately, the victims were able to contact PJ Lhuiller Inc. (PJLI) or Cebuana Lhuillier and they reported the unscrupulous process of hiring being perpetrated by the group of certain Nicole Garcia, Sir Lou, Francis and other John Doe’s. Cebuana Lhuillier then requested investigative assistance of the NBI. Acting on the request, NBI-AFD conducted an entrapment operation which resulted in the arrest of the above-mentioned Subjects. Charges for Estafa, Business Law Names Law-Act No.3883, the Intellectual Property Code, and Computer-related Forgery and Identity Theft under RA 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012) were filed against the Subjects. On January 16, 2019 , operatives of NBI-Anti-Fraud Division (NBI-AFD) arrested JULIUS DIVINAGRACIA, GENNY DIVINAGRACIA, and LUIS DIVINAGRACIA for Estafa and Falsification of Documents. Subjects were arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from the complaint of a Korean national. Complainant averred that sometime in August 2018, Subjects were introduced to him. Subject JULIUS DIVINAGRACIA claimed that his late forefathers and father owned a large amount of cash and metal accounts kept at the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas and that Subject JULIUS DIVINAGRACIA is the sole heir of these accounts. Enticed by the Subject’s promises, complainant paid a total amount of Php 1,410,000 for the trading program of the funds maintained at the BSP allegedly recorded under Subject JULIUS’ name. Subject even asked for another Php 230,000 for trading registration. However, complainant learned that the documents given by Subject Julius issued by the BSP are all fake and fabricated. Acting on the complaint, NBI-AFD operatives conducted an entrapment operation and resulted in the arrest of the three (3) above-mentioned Subjects who immediately underwent proper post operation procedures. Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor, Caloocan City for violations of Article 315 (Estafa) and Article 172 (Falsification by Private Individual and Use of Falsified Documents) of the Revised Penal Code. On January 16, 2019 , operatives of NBI-Bulacan District Office (NBI-BULDO) arrested JOSE BENJAMIN NATIVIDAD y MATIAS for violation of RA 10591 (Comprehensive Firearms and Ammunition Regulation Act) by virtue of Search Warrant. The search turned positive for forty-four (44) units of different caliber of firearms and a box of live 7.62 ammunitions. Subject was presented for inquest proceedings for the aforementioned violation and was thereafter turned over for custody to NBI Jail, Manila. On January 17, 2019 , JESSIE CUNANAN CADIANG was arrested and deported back to the Philippines from Abu Dhabi via Etihad Airlines Flight no. EY 424. Subject was included in the Interpol Red Notice List based on the Warrant of arrest issued by RTC Branch 66, Capas, Tarlac for Murder. Subject killed a certain Corazon Ofrecio, a local government employee who was allegedly engaged in lending business in Capas, Tarlac City. NBI-IAID coordinated with Etihad Airlines to identify the Subject. Upon identification, subject was arrested inside the aircraft. He was brought to the immigration office for registration of his arrival. Subject was turned over by the NBI-IAID by the Bureau of Immigration for the usual booking procedures and documentation processes. After proper verification of the authenticity of the representation and the completion of the documentation process for the turn-over of the accused, JESSIE CUNANAN CADIANG was subsequently turned over to the PNP Tarlac Office. On January 17, 2019 , operatives of NBI-Special Operations Group (NBI-SOG) arrested INNOCENT UCHENNA NKWOKA a.k.a. STEVE EDWARD a.k.a. AGULU PRINCE, a Nigerian national, and IRENE LEE OKORO a.k.a. JACKIE PASCUAL. The case stemmed from the complaint received by the NBI regarding the alleged blackmailing committed by AGULU PRINCE and ANA FE SANDOVAL. Subject INNOCENT UCHENNA NKWOKA and the complainant knew each other via Tinder, a dating site. They constantly exchanged messages through email until the Subject proposed to the complainant in which the latter agreed. In October 2018, a certain ANA FE SANDOVAL, who introduced herself as an employee of US Embassy, called the complainant and told her that she has to pay Php 5,600.00 for the processing of her fiancé visa application. Complainant informed Subject AGULU PRINCE about it and she was told to just follow SANDOVAL’s instructions. In different occasions, SANDOVAL asked money from the complainant allegedly for the processing of the fiancé visa, medical examination, and Affidavit of Support. In sum, the amount sent by the complainant is Php 50,026.00. On December 5, 2018, complainant, together with her family went to NAIA II to fetch AGULU PRINCE. However, he did not arrive. Complainant received a call from someone who introduced herself as working in the Customs. She told complainant that STEVE EDWARD/AGULU PRINCE was held at the Cebu Airport for carrying $800,000 into the country. Complainant was asked to send Php 25,000 thru Palawan Express Padala for his release. Sensing that she was being duped, complainant did not heed to the woman’s advice. AGULU PRINCE sent a message to the complainant demanding Php 25,000 otherwise, he will post her nude photos she sent to him. Out of fear, complainant sent Php 10,000 to ANA FE SANDOVAL thru Palawan Express Padala. Subject AGULU PRINCE demanded money from the complainant in different occasions threatening her that he will post her nude pictures. Complainant then sought the assistance of the NBI. Acting on the complaint, NBI-SOG operatives conducted investigations and surveillance operations which led to the identification of JACKIE PASCUAL who claimed the money at Palawan Express Padala. Operatives negotiated with PASCUAL who disclosed that she will meet AGULU PRINCE at Las Pinas City. Operatives immediately proceeded to the area and AGULU PRINCE was apprehended. Recovered from the Subject’s possession is the cellular phone where the complainant’s nude photos were saved. AGULU PRINCE/INNOCENT UCHENNA NKWOKA and IRENE LEE OKORO a.k.a. JACKIE PASCUAL underwent booking procedures. They are presented for inquest proceedings for Swindling and Robbery Extortion in relation to RA 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012), and violation of RA 9995 (Anti Photo and Video Voyeurism Act of 2009). ANA FE SANDOVAL remains at large. On January 21, 2019 , operatives of NBI-Special Action Unit (NBI-SAU) arrested FRANCISCO LESACA y YU alias “Kiko” in Guiguinto, Bulacan for violation of RA 4653 (An Act Prohibiting the Commercial Importation of Textile Articles Known as Clothing and Rags). Subject was arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from the information regarding the illegal activity of the Subject together with other unidentified individuals in a warehouse in Guiguinto, Bulacan. Allegedly, Subject is engaged in the sale of smuggled used clothing also known as “ukay-ukay”. After thorough investigation, an entrapment operation was conducted on the above-mentioned date. During the operation, Subject offered to sell one hundred thirty (130) boxes of smuggled used clothing for Php 3,000.00 per box for a total of Php 390,000.00. Subject instructed his workers to show the poseur buyers the ukay-ukay inside the boxes at the warehouse and load them in the truck brought by the poseur customers. Subject was apprehended after he received the entrapment money. Subject was presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the Provincial Prosecutor of Bulcan for the above-mentioned violation. He is presently detained at the NBI Detention Facility awaiting trial. On January 21, 2019 , operatives of NBI-Cordillera Administrative Region (NBI-CAR) arrested JOSE MA. J. RUBRICO by virtue of Warrant of Arrest for Estafa. The NBI received a report that Subject, who has standing Warrant of Arrest for Estafa issued by RTC Branch 6, Baguio City was sighted at Katmandu St., Shangrila Subdivision, San Luis, Baguio City. NBI-CAR operatives immediately coordinated with elements of Baguio City Police Office and after confirming that Subject RUBRICO was indeed inside Katmandu St., Shangrila Subdivision, San Luis, Baguio City, operatives served and implemented the Warrant of Arrest. Subject was brought at the NBI-CAR for the booking procedures. On January 22, 2019 , operatives of NBI-Special Action Unit arrested ILENE JOYCE GERAWA for Large Scale Illegal Recruitment. Subject was arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from the complaints against the Subject. According to the complainants, they were being recruited through direct hiring by the Subejct and Technomaid Domestic Staff Services to work as domestic helpers in Dubai. Verification with the Philippine Overseas Employment Administration (POEA) revealed that Technomaid Domestic Staff Services and Subject Gerawa are not licensed nor authorized to recruit workers for overseas employment. An entrapment operation was then conducted resulting in the arrest of the Subject. Subject was presented for inquest proceeding before the Inquest Prosecutor of Manila for violation of RA 8042 (Migrant Workers and Overseas Filipinos Act). On January 22, 2019 , operatives of NBI-Anti-Human Trafficking Division (NBI-AHTRAD) arrested FELIX JANDOC y JAVELLANA for violation of RA 8042 (Migrant Workers and Overseas Filipinos Act of 1995) and Estafa (Article 315 of the Revised Penal Code). Subject was arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from the complaints against the Subject who offered them job opportunities as seafarers. Through promising words, complainants parted their money for the processing of their applications. Subject promised them that they will be deployed within two to three (2-3) months but it did not materialize. Despite this, Subject still demanded Php 15,000.00 from the complainants and the amount was said to be used for their medical examination and additional payment to the Subject. An entrapment operation was then conducted resulting in the arrest of the Subject. Subject was presented for inquest proceeding before the Office of the City Prosecutor, Manila for the above-mentioned violations. On January 23, 2019 , operatives of NBI-Dagupan District Office (NBI-DADO) arrested ERICSON ESTRADA et al for violation of RA 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012). On the aforementioned date, NBI-DADO, together with the representatives from the NBI-Digital Forensic Laboratory (NBI-DFL) implemented the Search Warrant. Upon thereat, Subjects were able to turn off some of the computers. Nevertheless, the DFL team examined the contents of the computers and found links of obscene videos being distributed online. The operation resulted in the seizure of eight (8) computer sets, one (1) laptop, and receipts of money remittances. A case for violation of RA 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012) was filed against the Subjects. On January 24, 2019 , the NBI-Task Force Against Illegal Drugs (NBI-TFAID) filed charges for violation of RA 9165 (Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002), RA 3019 (Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act), Grave Misconduct for Public Employees, Dereliction of Duty, False Testimony and Subordination of Perjury against the personalities involved in smuggling illegal drugs through the shipment of magnetic lifters from Vietnam and Malaysia. Based on the investigation, the following government officials are involved or liable in the shipment of the magnetic lifter: SEC. ISIDRO S. LAPENA (TESDA), FORMER PSSUPT. EDUARDO P. ACIERTO (PNP), FORMER PDEA DDGA ISMAEL FAJARDO, I01 JIMMY GUBAN (BOC), DEPUTY COMMISIONER RICARDO C. QUINTO (BOC), JOSEPH DIMAYUGA (BOC), P/INSP. LITO PIROTE (PNP), ENGR. GIRLIE UMALI (BOC), JENALINE M. GARCIA (BOC), ATTY. ZSAE CARRIE DE GUZMAN (BOC), JOHN MAR MORALES (BOC), BENJAMIN CAJUCOM (BOC), and ATTY. VENER S. BAQUIRAN (BOC). The private individuals involved are VEDASTO CABRAL BARAQUEL, MARIA LAGRIMAS A. CATIPAN, VIRGINIA BALIENTE, EMELYN LUQUINGAN, MIGUELA SANTOS, KATRINA GRACE CUASAY, MARINA SIGNAPAN, RAMON TUYAY, JHON LERIC OLAVARIO, MARIBETH OLAVARIO, MINERVA VERZO, ROMEO C. NAVAL, JOEL MARITANA, MARY LOU T. ESTRADA, HUMPREY TUMANENG, JOSE MA. SARASOLA, JOHNNY REYES, and FERNANDO MARTIN JUAN DE ACHAVAL. The foreign nationals involved are FHONIE CHAN (China), WILLIN ONG aka WILSON ONG (China), ZHAUQ QUAN aka ZHANG QUAN (China), JIANG QUOQING (Malaysia), Alias MR. TAN (Malaysia), HSU CHUNG-CHUN (Taiwan), JAMES FUNG/FONG, KAN JI HONG (Vietnam), LE THI THUY (Vietnam), LUU THI THU HUONG (Vietnam), DU QUOC DUONG (Vietnam), ROY WANG, and ZHOU QUAN (China). On January 25, 2019 , operatives of NBI-Anti-Fraud Division (NBI-AFD) arrested NANETH M. MENDOZA for Syndicated Estafa and Falsification of Commercial Documents. Subject was arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from the complaint of Nina Rizzi V. Belgica against the Subject who represented herself as a representative of SM Investment Corporation, authorized to look for investors to supply computers to SM for a promising return of 7% to 10% monthly interest. Complainant was lured to part with her Php 50 Million. The transactions were all covered by SM Purchase Orders and Memorandum of Agreements allegedly signed by SM Investment Corporation Head, Jose T. Sio. Subject also issued to complainant several bank checks which were later found out to be spurious and some bounced for insufficiency of funds. It was further revealed that Subject was not an employee nor a representative of SM Investment Corporation and the SM Purchase Orders and Memorandum of Agreements were all counterfeit. Despite this, Subject still continued deceiving the complainant for an additional investment of Php 2 Million. With this, an entrapment operation was conducted resulting in the arrest of the Subject. It was further discovered that Subject was earlier arrested and charged before the Pasig RTC Branch 268 for similar offense and was supposed to be attending her pre-trial conference. Subject was then presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor, Manila for the above-mentioned offenses. On January 28, 2019 , the NBI-Anti-Graft Division (NBI-AGD) filed charges against BERNADETTE BADINAS y BERNABE for Swindling (Estafa) and violation of BP 22 (Bouncing Checks Law). Subject Badinas represented herself as an accountant at Lugang Café and that she has a financing business in the said company. Subject’s disclosure that her financing business pays interest rate as high as 36% monthly depending on the term of investment and with prospective returns enticed complainants to invest various amounts. Subject eventually failed to fulfill the promise to return the investments. Other personalities or Subject’s cohorts who are also charged with the same violations are RONALDO O. BADINAS, CHRISTOPHER L. LUCASAN, LEONILO DE LEON, RONALDO WENCESLAO, and CELIA L. LUCASAN. The operation stemmed from the complaint of Atty. Bengzon of Phoenix Publishing House, Inc. Charges for violation of RA 8293 (Intellectual Property Rights of the Philippines) were filed against ICOPYPRINT SOLUTIONS SERVICES AND TRADING, GERALDINE AQUINO GIRONELLA, owners/managers/employees/occupants of the establishment located at Mendoza St., Brgy. Manggahan, Puerto Princesa City, Palawan. On January 30, 2019 , operatives of NBI-Rizal District Office (NBI-RIZDO) seized counterfeit Casio, Baby G, and G Shock watches with an estimated amount of Php 68.7 Million. Items were seized in Quiapo, Manila by virtue of Search Warrants. Charges for violation of RA 8293 (Intellectual Property Code of the Philippine) were filed against CRISTINA LEE, EDISON CHONG, JOAN CU, FELIX M. CONTES, John/Jane Does, owners/proprietors of various stalls located at Plaza Miranda Shopping Mall, Quiapo, Manila. On January 30, 2019 , operatives of NBI- International Airport Investigation Division (NBI-IAID) arrested JUNE SAJONAS LUMBAD for Estafa and Large Scale Illegal Recruitment. The case stemmed from the complaints against the Subject and other individuals namely Ruben Sevilla, Eleny Reynoso, Gloria Espejo, and Elizabeth Tupaz of JAMT & JADE SKILLS. According to the complainants, sometime in November 2018, they were recruited by Ruben Sevilla to work as farmworkers/fruit pickers. He referred them to Subject June Lumbad, the owner/manager of JAMT & JADE SKILLS. Accordingly, Subject demanded from the complainants the payment of Php160,000.00 as placement fee. Two of the complainants were able to give Php50,000.00 while another one was able to give Php80,000.00 as partial payments. Complainants, however, discovered that other applicants were twice denied departure by the immigration officers at NAIA when they attempted to depart since the documents given to them were fake and that they have no working visa in going to South Korea. When Subject continued to demand payment of the complainants’ balance, the latter sought the assistance of the NBI. Verification from the Philippine Overseas Employment Administration (POEA) revealed that Subject Lumbad is not licensed nor authorized to recruit workers for overseas employment. With this, an entrapment operation was conducted resulting in the arrest of the Subject. Subject was presented for inquest proceedings for Estafa and violation of RA 8042 (Migrant Workers and Overseas Filipinos Act of 1995) as amended by RA 10022. On January 30, 2019 , operatives of NBI-National Capital Region (NBI-NCR) seized Under Armour products with an approximate amount of Php 17.1 Million. Items were seized in Binondo,Manila by virtue of Search Warrants. Charges for violation of RA 8293 (Intellectual Property Rights of the Philippines) were filed against John/Jane Does of the warehouses and stores located at 11/88 Shopping Mall, 168 Shopping Mall, and 999 Shopping Mall, Binondo, Manila. On January 31, 2019 , operatives of NBI-Cybercrime Division (NBI-CCD) arrested KUMAR SUNIL MOTUMAL, CHUTANI RAKHI DARBALA (Indian nationals), and MARY CHRIS P. MABINI for selling illegal drugs. . Subjects were arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from the report that a certain store in Paco, Manila is engaged in the sale of illegal drugs contained in sealed boxes labeled “Kamini Vidrawan Ras” and “For Sale in India Only”. Acting on the information, test-buy operation was conducted at a certain store bearing the name ANMOL INDIAN GENERAL MERCHANDISE located at Paco, Manila. NBI-CCD operatives obtained two (2) sealed gold boxes labeled “Kamini Vidrawan Ras”. Chemical analysis made by the NBI-Forensic Chemistry Division on the subject items yielded positive result for the presence of illegal drugs. An entrapment operation was then conducted resulting in the arrest of the above-mentioned Subjects. During the operation, sealed gold boxes in a paper package were seen in plain view by the operatives. The package contained seven (7) sealed gold boxes labeled “Kamini Vidrawan Ras” and “For Sale in India Only”. Operatives also saw small boxes labeled “Rabipur”, rabies vaccine for human use and “For Sale in India Nepal only”. When asked for the license/certification from FDA for the merchandise, they failed to present any which is a prima facie evidence under FDA Act of 2009. Laboratory examination conducted on the “Kamini Vidrawan Ras” by the Forensic Chemistry Division (FCD) showed positive result for the presence of Opium and Morphine substances. Charges for violations of RA 9165 (Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002), RA 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012), and RA 9711 (Food and Drug Administration Act of 2009) were filed against the Subjects before the Office of the City Prosecutor, Manila. On January 31, 2019 , operatives of NBI-Cybercrime Division (NBI-CCD) arrested JONAS DELA CRUZ SORIANO for violation of RA 9995 (Anti-Photo and Video Voyeurism Act of 2009 and ALFRED TALAMPAS DEL ROSARIO for Direct Assault. The case stemmed from the complaint of Alena Marie Rumbaoa Y Maranan whose phone was fixed by Subject JONAS at Tutuban Center Mall. When complainant’s sister, Mary, brought the cellphone to the Subject, the latter asked for the Icloud username and password for confirmation in fixing the cellphone, which the former had given. The cellphone was eventually fixed. On January 30, 2019, complainant received a private message in Facebook Messenger from an account with the name Jenny Hamilton asking for Php 4,000.00 in exchange of deleting and for not posting and exposing the complainant’s nude photos in social media. Screenshots of complainant’s nude photos were also sent to the latter. Complainant informed her family of the incident and on the same day, Mary went to Jonas to ask him what happened but he wasn’t there. Mary then reported Jonas to the mall management. On January 31, 2019, Mary was informed by the management of the mall that Jonas was already there. Mary and her sister ,then sought the assistance of the NBI. An entrapment operation was then conducted and Subject Jonas was arrested after he showed to Mary the screenshot of her sister’s nude photos. Operatives then approached Subject Jonas but he made a scene and a man identified as Subject ALFRED TALAMPAS DEL ROSARIO approached Jonas and the operatives and violently shouted at them causing commotion from the bystanders and thereby interrupting the arrest of the Subject. Jonas and Alfred were brought to NBI. Upon examination of the Subject’s cellphone, it was confirmed that he was in possession of the screenshot of nude photos sent to complainant. Meanwhile, record check on Subject Afred revealed that he has outstanding Warrant of Arrest for violation of RA 9262 (Anti-Violence Against Women and their Children). Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor, Manila for above-mentioned violations. On January 31, 2019 , operatives of NBI-Anti-Human Trafficking Division (NBI-AHTRAD) arrested CONCHITA PACULBA y DAGAME was arrested in an entrapment operation for Estafa and violation of RA 8042 (Migrant Workers and Overseas Filipinos Act of 1995). Without license from the Philippine Overseas Employment Administration (POEA), Subject Conchita, together with two (2) at large cohorts MARLA MAGSOLING PATARATA and MYLENE AGUINALDO LAGAT SERIL, recruited the complainants for employment as waiters and house helpers in Dubai. Considering that Subject Paculba is demanding payment for placement and processing fees from the complainants, an entrapment operation was conducted resulting in the arrest of Subject Conchita. Subject was presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the Prosecutor, Manila. On January 31, 2019 , operatives of NBI-Intellectual Property Rights Division (NBI-IPRD) seized Php 28.2 Million worth of counterfeit Michael Kors bags, wallets, and jewelry sets. Items were seized in Pasay City by virtue of Search Warrants. Charges for violation of RA 8293 (Intellectual Property Rights of the Philippines) were filed against John/Jane Does/owners/operators of various stalls located at Terminal Plaza 1, Harrison St., Pasay City.

NBI-IAID coordinated with Etihad Airlines to identify the Subject. Upon identification, subject was arrested inside the aircraft. He was brought to the immigration office for registration of his arrival. Subject was turned over by the NBI-IAID by the Bureau of Immigration for the usual booking procedures and documentation processes. After proper verification of the authenticity of the representation and the completion of the documentation process for the turn-over of the accused, JESSIE CUNANAN CADIANG was subsequently turned over to the PNP Tarlac Office. On January 17, 2019 , operatives of NBI-Special Operations Group (NBI-SOG) arrested INNOCENT UCHENNA NKWOKA a.k.a. STEVE EDWARD a.k.a. AGULU PRINCE, a Nigerian national, and IRENE LEE OKORO a.k.a. JACKIE PASCUAL. The case stemmed from the complaint received by the NBI regarding the alleged blackmailing committed by AGULU PRINCE and ANA FE SANDOVAL. Subject INNOCENT UCHENNA NKWOKA and the complainant knew each other via Tinder, a dating site. They constantly exchanged messages through email until the Subject proposed to the complainant in which the latter agreed. In October 2018, a certain ANA FE SANDOVAL, who introduced herself as an employee of US Embassy, called the complainant and told her that she has to pay Php 5,600.00 for the processing of her fiancé visa application. Complainant informed Subject AGULU PRINCE about it and she was told to just follow SANDOVAL’s instructions. In different occasions, SANDOVAL asked money from the complainant allegedly for the processing of the fiancé visa, medical examination, and Affidavit of Support. In sum, the amount sent by the complainant is Php 50,026.00. On December 5, 2018, complainant, together with her family went to NAIA II to fetch AGULU PRINCE. However, he did not arrive. Complainant received a call from someone who introduced herself as working in the Customs. She told complainant that STEVE EDWARD/AGULU PRINCE was held at the Cebu Airport for carrying $800,000 into the country. Complainant was asked to send Php 25,000 thru Palawan Express Padala for his release. Sensing that she was being duped, complainant did not heed to the woman’s advice. AGULU PRINCE sent a message to the complainant demanding Php 25,000 otherwise, he will post her nude photos she sent to him. Out of fear, complainant sent Php 10,000 to ANA FE SANDOVAL thru Palawan Express Padala. Subject AGULU PRINCE demanded money from the complainant in different occasions threatening her that he will post her nude pictures. Complainant then sought the assistance of the NBI. Acting on the complaint, NBI-SOG operatives conducted investigations and surveillance operations which led to the identification of JACKIE PASCUAL who claimed the money at Palawan Express Padala. Operatives negotiated with PASCUAL who disclosed that she will meet AGULU PRINCE at Las Pinas City. Operatives immediately proceeded to the area and AGULU PRINCE was apprehended. Recovered from the Subject’s possession is the cellular phone where the complainant’s nude photos were saved. AGULU PRINCE/INNOCENT UCHENNA NKWOKA and IRENE LEE OKORO a.k.a. JACKIE PASCUAL underwent booking procedures. They are presented for inquest proceedings for Swindling and Robbery Extortion in relation to RA 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012), and violation of RA 9995 (Anti Photo and Video Voyeurism Act of 2009). ANA FE SANDOVAL remains at large. On January 21, 2019 , operatives of NBI-Special Action Unit (NBI-SAU) arrested FRANCISCO LESACA y YU alias “Kiko” in Guiguinto, Bulacan for violation of RA 4653 (An Act Prohibiting the Commercial Importation of Textile Articles Known as Clothing and Rags). Subject was arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from the information regarding the illegal activity of the Subject together with other unidentified individuals in a warehouse in Guiguinto, Bulacan. Allegedly, Subject is engaged in the sale of smuggled used clothing also known as “ukay-ukay”. After thorough investigation, an entrapment operation was conducted on the above-mentioned date. During the operation, Subject offered to sell one hundred thirty (130) boxes of smuggled used clothing for Php 3,000.00 per box for a total of Php 390,000.00. Subject instructed his workers to show the poseur buyers the ukay-ukay inside the boxes at the warehouse and load them in the truck brought by the poseur customers. Subject was apprehended after he received the entrapment money. Subject was presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the Provincial Prosecutor of Bulcan for the above-mentioned violation. He is presently detained at the NBI Detention Facility awaiting trial. On January 21, 2019 , operatives of NBI-Cordillera Administrative Region (NBI-CAR) arrested JOSE MA. J. RUBRICO by virtue of Warrant of Arrest for Estafa. The NBI received a report that Subject, who has standing Warrant of Arrest for Estafa issued by RTC Branch 6, Baguio City was sighted at Katmandu St., Shangrila Subdivision, San Luis, Baguio City. NBI-CAR operatives immediately coordinated with elements of Baguio City Police Office and after confirming that Subject RUBRICO was indeed inside Katmandu St., Shangrila Subdivision, San Luis, Baguio City, operatives served and implemented the Warrant of Arrest. Subject was arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from the complaints against the Subject. According to the complainants, they were being recruited through direct hiring by the Subejct and Technomaid Domestic Staff Services to work as domestic helpers in Dubai. Verification with the Philippine Overseas Employment Administration (POEA) revealed that Technomaid Domestic Staff Services and Subject Gerawa are not licensed nor authorized to recruit workers for overseas employment. An entrapment operation was then conducted resulting in the arrest of the Subject. Subject was presented for inquest proceeding before the Inquest Prosecutor of Manila for violation of RA 8042 (Migrant Workers and Overseas Filipinos Act). On January 22, 2019 , operatives of NBI-Anti-Human Trafficking Division (NBI-AHTRAD) arrested FELIX JANDOC y JAVELLANA for violation of RA 8042 (Migrant Workers and Overseas Filipinos Act of 1995) and Estafa (Article 315 of the Revised Penal Code). Subject was arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from the complaints against the Subject who offered them job opportunities as seafarers. Through promising words, complainants parted their money for the processing of their applications. Subject promised them that they will be deployed within two to three (2-3) months but it did not materialize. Despite this, Subject still demanded Php 15,000.00 from the complainants and the amount was said to be used for their medical examination and additional payment to the Subject. An entrapment operation was then conducted resulting in the arrest of the Subject. Subject was presented for inquest proceeding before the Office of the City Prosecutor, Manila for the above-mentioned violations. On January 23, 2019 , operatives of NBI-Dagupan District Office (NBI-DADO) arrested ERICSON ESTRADA et al for violation of RA 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012). On the aforementioned date, NBI-DADO, together with the representatives from the NBI-Digital Forensic Laboratory (NBI-DFL) implemented the Search Warrant. Upon thereat, Subjects were able to turn off some of the computers. Nevertheless, the DFL team examined the contents of the computers and found links of obscene videos being distributed online. The operation resulted in the seizure of eight (8) computer sets, one (1) laptop, and receipts of money remittances. A case for violation of RA 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012) was filed against the Subjects. On January 24, 2019 , the NBI-Task Force Against Illegal Drugs (NBI-TFAID) filed charges for violation of RA 9165 (Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002), RA 3019 (Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act), Grave Misconduct for Public Employees, Dereliction of Duty, False Testimony and Subordination of Perjury against the personalities involved in smuggling illegal drugs through the shipment of magnetic lifters from Vietnam and Malaysia. ACIERTO (PNP), FORMER PDEA DDGA ISMAEL FAJARDO, I01 JIMMY GUBAN (BOC), DEPUTY COMMISIONER RICARDO C. QUINTO (BOC), JOSEPH DIMAYUGA (BOC), P/INSP. LITO PIROTE (PNP), ENGR. CATIPAN, VIRGINIA BALIENTE, EMELYN LUQUINGAN, MIGUELA SANTOS, KATRINA GRACE CUASAY, MARINA SIGNAPAN, RAMON TUYAY, JHON LERIC OLAVARIO, MARIBETH OLAVARIO, MINERVA VERZO, ROMEO C. NAVAL, JOEL MARITANA, MARY LOU T. ESTRADA, HUMPREY TUMANENG, JOSE MA. SARASOLA, JOHNNY REYES, and FERNANDO MARTIN JUAN DE ACHAVAL. TAN (Malaysia), HSU CHUNG-CHUN (Taiwan), JAMES FUNG/FONG, KAN JI HONG (Vietnam), LE THI THUY (Vietnam), LUU THI THU HUONG (Vietnam), DU QUOC DUONG (Vietnam), ROY WANG, and ZHOU QUAN (China). Belgica against the Subject who represented herself as a representative of SM Investment Corporation, authorized to look for investors to supply computers to SM for a promising return of 7% to 10% monthly interest. Sio. Subject also issued to complainant several bank checks which were later found out to be spurious and some bounced for insufficiency of funds. It was further revealed that Subject was not an employee nor a representative of SM Investment Corporation and the SM Purchase Orders and Memorandum of Agreements were all counterfeit. Despite this, Subject still continued deceiving the complainant for an additional investment of Php 2 Million. With this, an entrapment operation was conducted resulting in the arrest of the Subject. It was further discovered that Subject was earlier arrested and charged before the Pasig RTC Branch 268 for similar offense and was supposed to be attending her pre-trial conference. Subject was then presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor, Manila for the above-mentioned offenses. Subject Badinas represented herself as an accountant at Lugang Café and that she has a financing business in the said company. Subject’s disclosure that her financing business pays interest rate as high as 36% monthly depending on the term of investment and with prospective returns enticed complainants to invest various amounts. Subject eventually failed to fulfill the promise to return the investments. Other personalities or Subject’s cohorts who are also charged with the same violations are RONALDO O. BADINAS, CHRISTOPHER L. LUCASAN, LEONILO DE LEON, RONALDO WENCESLAO, and CELIA L. LUCASAN. The operation stemmed from the complaint of Atty. Bengzon of Phoenix Publishing House, Inc. Manggahan, Puerto Princesa City, Palawan. Items were seized in Quiapo, Manila by virtue of Search Warrants. Charges for violation of RA 8293 (Intellectual Property Code of the Philippine) were filed against CRISTINA LEE, EDISON CHONG, JOAN CU, FELIX M. CONTES, John/Jane Does, owners/proprietors of various stalls located at Plaza Miranda Shopping Mall, Quiapo, Manila. He referred them to Subject June Lumbad, the owner/manager of JAMT & JADE SKILLS. Accordingly, Subject demanded from the complainants the payment of Php160,000.00 as placement fee. Two of the complainants were able to give Php50,000.00 while another one was able to give Php80,000.00 as partial payments. Complainants, however, discovered that other applicants were twice denied departure by the immigration officers at NAIA when they attempted to depart since the documents given to them were fake and that they have no working visa in going to South Korea. When Subject continued to demand payment of the complainants’ balance, the latter sought the assistance of the NBI. Verification from the Philippine Overseas Employment Administration (POEA) revealed that Subject Lumbad is not licensed nor authorized to recruit workers for overseas employment. With this, an entrapment operation was conducted resulting in the arrest of the Subject. Subject was presented for inquest proceedings for Estafa and violation of RA 8042 (Migrant Workers and Overseas Filipinos Act of 1995) as amended by RA 10022. Items were seized in Binondo,Manila by virtue of Search Warrants. Charges for violation of RA 8293 (Intellectual Property Rights of the Philippines) were filed against John/Jane Does of the warehouses and stores located at 11/88 Shopping Mall, 168 Shopping Mall, and 999 Shopping Mall, Binondo, Manila. On January 31, 2019 , operatives of NBI-Cybercrime Division (NBI-CCD) arrested KUMAR SUNIL MOTUMAL, CHUTANI RAKHI DARBALA (Indian nationals), and MARY CHRIS P. MABINI for selling illegal drugs. . Subjects were arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from the report that a certain store in Paco, Manila is engaged in the sale of illegal drugs contained in sealed boxes labeled “Kamini Vidrawan Ras” and “For Sale in India Only”. Acting on the information, test-buy operation was conducted at a certain store bearing the name ANMOL INDIAN GENERAL MERCHANDISE located at Paco, Manila. NBI-CCD operatives obtained two (2) sealed gold boxes labeled “Kamini Vidrawan Ras”. Chemical analysis made by the NBI-Forensic Chemistry Division on the subject items yielded positive result for the presence of illegal drugs. An entrapment operation was then conducted resulting in the arrest of the above-mentioned Subjects. During the operation, sealed gold boxes in a paper package were seen in plain view by the operatives. The package contained seven (7) sealed gold boxes labeled “Kamini Vidrawan Ras” and “For Sale in India Only”. Operatives also saw small boxes labeled “Rabipur”, rabies vaccine for human use and “For Sale in India Nepal only”. When asked for the license/certification from FDA for the merchandise, they failed to present any which is a prima facie evidence under FDA Act of 2009. Laboratory examination conducted on the “Kamini Vidrawan Ras” by the Forensic Chemistry Division (FCD) showed positive result for the presence of Opium and Morphine substances. Charges for violations of RA 9165 (Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002), RA 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012), and RA 9711 (Food and Drug Administration Act of 2009) were filed against the Subjects before the Office of the City Prosecutor, Manila. On January 31, 2019 , operatives of NBI-Cybercrime Division (NBI-CCD) arrested JONAS DELA CRUZ SORIANO for violation of RA 9995 (Anti-Photo and Video Voyeurism Act of 2009 and ALFRED TALAMPAS DEL ROSARIO for Direct Assault. The case stemmed from the complaint of Alena Marie Rumbaoa Y Maranan whose phone was fixed by Subject JONAS at Tutuban Center Mall. When complainant’s sister, Mary, brought the cellphone to the Subject, the latter asked for the Icloud username and password for confirmation in fixing the cellphone, which the former had given. The cellphone was eventually fixed. On January 30, 2019, complainant received a private message in Facebook Messenger from an account with the name Jenny Hamilton asking for Php 4,000.00 in exchange of deleting and for not posting and exposing the complainant’s nude photos in social media. Screenshots of complainant’s nude photos were also sent to the latter. Complainant informed her family of the incident and on the same day, Mary went to Jonas to ask him what happened but he wasn’t there. Mary then reported Jonas to the mall management. On January 31, 2019, Mary was informed by the management of the mall that Jonas was already there. Mary and her sister ,then sought the assistance of the NBI. An entrapment operation was then conducted and Subject Jonas was arrested after he showed to Mary the screenshot of her sister’s nude photos. Operatives then approached Subject Jonas but he made a scene and a man identified as Subject ALFRED TALAMPAS DEL ROSARIO approached Jonas and the operatives and violently shouted at them causing commotion from the bystanders and thereby interrupting the arrest of the Subject. Jonas and Alfred were brought to NBI. Upon examination of the Subject’s cellphone, it was confirmed that he was in possession of the screenshot of nude photos sent to complainant. Meanwhile, record check on Subject Afred revealed that he has outstanding Warrant of Arrest for violation of RA 9262 (Anti-Violence Against Women and their Children). Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor, Manila for above-mentioned violations. On January 31, 2019 , operatives of NBI-Anti-Human Trafficking Division (NBI-AHTRAD) arrested CONCHITA PACULBA y DAGAME was arrested in an entrapment operation for Estafa and violation of RA 8042 (Migrant Workers and Overseas Filipinos Act of 1995). Without license from the Philippine Overseas Employment Administration (POEA), Subject Conchita, together with two (2) at large cohorts MARLA MAGSOLING PATARATA and MYLENE AGUINALDO LAGAT SERIL, recruited the complainants for employment as waiters and house helpers in Dubai. Considering that Subject Paculba is demanding payment for placement and processing fees from the complainants, an entrapment operation was conducted resulting in the arrest of Subject Conchita. Subject was presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the Prosecutor, Manila. Items were seized in Pasay City by virtue of Search Warrants. Charges for violation of RA 8293 (Intellectual Property Rights of the Philippines) were filed against John/Jane Does/owners/operators of various stalls located at Terminal Plaza 1, Harrison St., Pasay City.

body: Four (4) Korean nationals were arrested by agents of the National Capital region (NCR) in Parañaque recently. NBI Director Virgilio L. Mendez identified the suspects as: 1. AN, JUNYOUNG; 2. LIM, HO; 3. PARK, INTAE; and 4. KIM MINIK, all Korean nationals of legal age and residing at Blk. 16, Lot 46, Don Pedro Reyes Street, ICHA Village, BF Parañaque. Investigation report disclosed that the NBI-NCR received intelligence report about the illegal activities being conducted by a group of foreigner in Parañaque City. Surveillance operations were conducted and after verifying said information, a search warrant was applied for and granted by Hon. Lyliha L. Abella-Aquino, Acting Presiding Judge of Branch 24, Manila Regional Trial Court. At around 8:05 in the evening of May 9, 2014, NBI-NCR operatives in coordination with the Southern Police District and the Security Officer of ICHA Village, the said search warrant was implemented. Inside the house, the NBI-NCR operatives caught four (4) Korean nationals while in the act of producing, using, trafficking and in possession of access devices and equipment which they use in the illegal access card operations. Having been caught in the act of engaging in illegal on-line gambling, Subjects were placed under arrest by virtue of Section 5, Rule 113 of the New Rules of Court and apprised of their Constitutional and Statutory Rights. Confiscated from the subjects were several units of computers, telephone, cables and other electronic equipment which are being used as a means for committing the acts prohibited by Section 9 of RA No. 8484 as well as that of PD No. 1602, as amended. After a thorough evaluation of the evidence on hand, it appears that there is sufficient ground to engender a well-founded belief that crime of Violation of Section 9 (f) of RA No. 8484 has been committed by the suspects. Subjects were brought to the NBI-NCR office for booking, photographing and fingerprinting. Subjects were brought before the Prosecutor’s Office of Parañaque City for inquest proceedings for Violation of RA 8484 otherwise known as the “An Act Regulating the Issuance and Use of Access Devices, Prohibiting Fraudulent Acts Committed Relative Thereto, Providing Penalties and for other Purposes” and PD 1602, as amended, otherwise known as “Illegal gambling”.

body: PRESS STATEMENT June 04, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } The National Bureau of Investigation-Organized and Transnational Crimes Division (NBI-OTCD), under the supervision of NBI Director Judge Jaime B. Santiago (Ret.), and in coordination with the Bureau of Immigration-Fugitive Search Unit (BI-FSU), arrested a Korean fugitive in Malate, Manila on June 3, 2025. Based on BI records, the Korean national, identified as KIM YOOSHIK a.k.a. KIM YOOSIK, is an undesirable and overstaying alien and poses risk to public safety and security for being a fugitive from justice as per official communication from Consul Yun Wonchang of the Embassy of the Republic of Korea dated April 17, 2023. Moreover, an Interpol Blue Notice was issued against the Subject indicating that he has a Warrant of Arrest for Fraud in violation of Article 347-(1) of the Criminal Act of Korea, for defrauding his victim with over KRW 10,000,000 in the form of an investment scam on October 14, 2008. Further verification with the BI database shows that Subject has active derogatory records under a Blacklist Order dated June 22, 2023, and Watchlist Order issued on April 5, 2023, both for undesirability, being a fugitive from justice. Upon verification of criminal records in the NBI’s database, it was found that KIM YOOSHIK a.k.a. KIM YOOSIK has an outstanding Warrant of Arrest for Estafa. He was also previously charged with Falsification of Public Documents, Malicious Mischief, Grave Threat, and Damage to Property, as well as Human Trafficking. Subject is temporarily detained at the NBI-OTCD office for investigation and standard booking and arrest procedures, and will be turned over to the custody of BI-FSU.

body: PRESS STATEMENT March 03, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } NBI ARRESTS ADMINISTRATIVE EXECUTIVE IN MUNTINLUPA FOR 176 COUNTS OF QUALIFIED THEFT PASAY CITY, Philippines – On February 25, 2026, operatives from the National Bureau of Investigation – National Capital Region (NBI-NCR) successfully arrested an individual in Muntinlupa City for 176 counts of Qualified Theft in relation to Section 6 of Republic Act No. 10175, also known as the Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012. The operation was initiated following a formal complaint lodged with the NBI-NCR. The Subject served as the Administrative Executive for their company, managing the entirety of account payments to suppliers and creditors. Leveraging this position, the Subject possessed full access to the company’s online banking system, including usernames, passwords, and control over the linked cellphone number utilized for authorizing transactions via SMS One-Time Passwords (OTPs). Investigations revealed that the Subject illicitly transferred large sums of money on 176 separate occasions to their personal online banking account without the authorization of company officers. The total amount embezzled is estimated at Php 5,277,131.88. Following the gathering of sufficient evidence, NBI agents planned and executed an entrapment operation. During the operation, agents witnessed the subject executing an unauthorized transfer of company funds to her personal account. The Subject underwent inquest proceedings for Qualified Theft under the Revised Penal Code, in relation to Section 6 of R.A. 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012). NBI Director Atty. Melvin A. Matibag commended the NBI-NCR agents for their relentless pursuit of justice and swift action in this case. This case serves as a stern warning to those who believe they can exploit their positions of trust for personal gain under the veil of digital transactions. The NBI remains vigilant and technologically equipped to track every illicit peso, regardless of how many times a transaction is layered. We are committed to protecting the integrity of our business sector and ensuring that those who weaponize their administrative access to defraud their employers will face the full force of the law. #NBIServes

Leveraging this position, the Subject possessed full access to the company’s online banking system, including usernames, passwords, and control over the linked cellphone number utilized for authorizing transactions via SMS One-Time Passwords (OTPs). Investigations revealed that the Subject illicitly transferred large sums of money on 176 separate occasions to their personal online banking account without the authorization of company officers. The total amount embezzled is estimated at Php 5,277,131.88. Following the gathering of sufficient evidence, NBI agents planned and executed an entrapment operation. During the operation, agents witnessed the subject executing an unauthorized transfer of company funds to her personal account. The Subject underwent inquest proceedings for Qualified Theft under the Revised Penal Code, in relation to Section 6 of R.A. 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012). NBI Director Atty. Melvin A. Matibag commended the NBI-NCR agents for their relentless pursuit of justice and swift action in this case. This case serves as a stern warning to those who believe they can exploit their positions of trust for personal gain under the veil of digital transactions. The NBI remains vigilant and technologically equipped to track every illicit peso, regardless of how many times a transaction is layered. We are committed to protecting the integrity of our business sector and ensuring that those who weaponize their administrative access to defraud their employers will face the full force of the law. #NBIServes

body: PRESS STATEMENT September 22, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI), through its Human Trafficking Division (HTRAD), arrested an individual in Quezon City on September 18, 2025 for child sexual exploitation. The operation stemmed from a case referral from the Royal Canadian Mountain Police (RCMP) through Philippine Internet Crimes Against Children Center (PICACC). According to the referral, members of the New Westminster Police Department (NWPD) executed a Search Warrant at the residence of a Canadian national. During the service of said warrant, investigators reviewed the Canadian national’s device and found communications with a Skype username. Forensic results forwarded to NBI-HTRAD revealed that the Subject was receiving payments from the arrested Canadian national to facilitate the live online sexual abuse of her 12-year-old daughter. HTRAD Agents conducted multiple surveillance operations to verify the Subject’s activities and the involvement of minor victims. The operations confirmed that the Subject was actively offering her minor children to foreigners in exchange for money. Through coordinated efforts, HTRAD Agents successfully located the Subject and documented her activities. Following information that Subject was offering minor victims for in-person sexual exploitation, NBI-HTRAD launched an entrapment and rescue operation on September 18, 2025. The operation was conducted in coordination with the local police, the City Social Welfare and Development Office (CSWD) of Quezon City, and with the assistance of NBI-Evidential Multimedia Division (EMD), DOJ IACAT, NCC-OSAEC-CSAEM, Cybertip Monitoring Center, and NGO partner. Subject had a direct dialogue with a poseur-customer, explicitly offering access to minor victims. Poseur-customer accepted the offer, and a meet-up was scheduled to facilitate the entrapment and immediate rescue of the children. The operation was successfully executed, resulting in the arrest of the Subject and the rescue of five (5) minor victims. Online Sexual Abuse and Exploitation of Children (OSAEC) and Child Sexual Abuse or Exploitation Material (CSAΕΜ) were seized and documented for evidentiary purposes. Subject was presented for inquest proceedings for Qualified Trafficking in Persons, in violation of R.A No. 9208, as amended by R.A. No. 10364. Documents are being prepared for application of a Warrant to Examine Computer Data for the seized devices. NBI Director Judge Jaime B. Santiago emphasized the Bureau’s unwavering commitment to pursuing perpetrators of child online sexual exploitation and encourages the public to report any suspicious online activities related to the crime, as every report could save children from such illicit activities.

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today announced the suspension of Clearance Processing in all Areas that were declared by the government as under Modified Enhanced Community Quarantine or MECQ beginning today, Tuesday, August 4 until 18, 2020. NBI Officer-In-Charge Eric B. Distor said the areas covered by the suspension are National Capital Region (NBI), Bulacan, Rizal, Cavite and Laguna. All Clearance processing and Satellite Offices in the aforementioned areas will be closed for the duration of the quarantine period or MECQ, OIC Distor added. The NBI supports the action of the national government to put certain areas under MECQ to stem the spread of the COVID-19 pandemic and at the same time heed the overwhelming clamor of frontliners for a “timeout”. The public is, therefore, advised of the cancellation of all clearance transactions during the quarantine period.

SANTIAGO (Ret.), arrested an individual in a hot pursuit operation in Angono, Rizal. Subject was arrested for Rape and violation of Republic Act No. 7610 (Special Protection of Children Against Child Abuse, Exploitation and Discrimination Act). The operation was conducted following a complaint alleging that Subject, who is the minor victim’s uncle, sexually abused her for seven years. The victim recounted that the sexual abuses began in 2018 when she was just 7 years old. Since then, Subject regularly abused her, with some instances occurring nearly every day. During a heartfelt conversation with her mother, the victim finally revealed about her long years of suffering, narrating what her uncle did to her. After recounting to the NBI-CAVIDO North agents about the most recent commission of the sexual abuse that occurred on July 7, 2025, they immediately organized a hot pursuit arrest. On July 8, 2025, agents from NBI-CAVIDO North arrested the suspect, who was then presented for inquest proceedings at the Taytay, Rizal Prosecutor’s Office for the alleged violations. Director Santiago commended the agents of NBI-CAVIDO North for the successful hot-pursuit operation, culminating in the arrest of the Subject. Their determination and quick response played a crucial role in ensuring justice.

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today announced the arrest of six (6) individuals by the NBI-Environmental Crime Division (EnCD) in Lian, Batangas for illegal quarrying. NBI Officer-In-Charge (OIC) Director Eric B. Distor identified the subjects as RODEL MARINDUQUE y VERGARA, FRANCIS DACUYA y EBORDE, CLAUDIO TAMAYO y TUMBAGAHAN, ROGER BETONIA y SALAZAR, SONNY MARINDUQUE y BIATON, and JOVENCIO MALABANAN y TEPORA. OIC Director Distor said that the operation stemmed from the letter sent by the DENR-Environmental Protection and Enforcement Task Force (EPETF) requesting full assistance to conduct investigation in the alleged illegal quarrying operations in Sitio Matuod, Brgy. Binubusan, Lian Batangas. In response, joint teams of NBI-EnCD and DENR-EPETF, Mines and Geoscience Bureau-Region IV-A (MGB Region IV-A) conducted a surveillance operation in the target area which verified the existence of illegal quarrying activities within the area despite issuance of a Cease and Desist Order (CDO). Further verification, the Provincial Government Environment and Natural Resources Office (PGENRO) of Batangas issued an updated list of existing holders of Special Permit to Transport and Dispose within the Province of Batangas. The list revealed that there is no existing permit issued within the area of Lian, Batangas, thus, making the quarrying operation in the target area unlawful and illegal. On June 24, 2021, joint operatives of NBI-ENCD, DENR-MGB Region IV-A, and DENR-Environmental Law Enforcement Protection Service (DENR-ELEPS) conducted a law enforcement operation against the operators of the illegal quarrying activity. The operation resulted in the arrest of the six (6) subjects. The subjects were presented for Inquest proceedings before the Office of Prosecutor General, DOJ Manila for violation of Section 103 of RA 7942, otherwise known as the Philippine Mining Act of 1995.
