body: Induced by job opportunities abroad, 80 prospective overseas Filipino workers were duped of P3.2 million pesos by a labor recruiter and four (4) companions who were arrested by the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) during an entrapment in Manila last Monday. The subject is identified as JULIET RED REMPIS, alias Juliet Rempis Lopez, with postal address at 6/F Room 615, MBI Bldg., Escolta St., Sta. Cruz, Manila; EVELYN AGUIRRE GUNDA ; EDGARDO MATA DARIA HONTIVEROS ; LEONCIA MACALINTAL FULGENCIO ; and; EDGARD RODELAS HONTIVEROS , staff assistants of Rempis. Investigation bared that on July 6, 2012, a complaint from Christian Salamat and several others was received by the NBI about the illegal recruitment activity of the subject Rempis. Complainants said that they paid Rempis the amount of P40,000 each as placement and processing fees for their visas for deployment to New Zealand as fruit pickers, and other jobs. Suspect promised the victims they will be deployed within 1 ½ months after paying the processing fees. But after the lapse of two months, victims failed to receive any visa as well as supposedly processed papers by the Philippine Overseas Employment Administration (POEA). Verification with the POEA shows that Rempis is not licensed and authorized to engage in overseas labor recruitment. On July 9, 2012 one of the complainants was scheduled to pay his placement fee. Moments after Rempis received the money from the complainant, NBI operatives approached and arrested her. Her four (4) companions were likewise apprehended. They were brought to the NBI where they are presently detained. A case for Syndicated (Large Scale) Illegal Recruitment/Estafa (swindling) had been filed before the Manila City Prosecutors Office against the suspects.

title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: The Information Division is pleased to submit herewith the significant cases of the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) for the following aforementioned period as follows: On January 8, 2018 , operatives of NBI-Saranggani District Offie (NBI-SARDO) arrested MARK KEVIN BIALA in an entrapment operation for violation of R.A. 9262 (Anti-Violence Against Women and their Children Act of 2004) in relation to R.A. 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012). The operation stemmed from information relayed that Subject was threatening his ex-girlfriend, the Complainant, thru text messages, that he will kill her if she will not go with him for the last time and have sexual intercourse with him. Complainant agreed to meet with the Subject out of fear and sought the assistance of the NBI. An entrapment operation was then conducted at City Escape Inn, the place where they agreed to meet. The operation resulted in the arrest of the Subject who was found half-naked. Subject was then brought to NBI-SARDO for proper booking procedures and disposition. On January 11, 2018 , operatives of NBI-Criminal Intelligence Division (NBI-CRID) arrested RICO PAGUIO y GARCIA in an entrapment operation in Manila for large scale illegal recruitment. The case stemmed from the complaint of six (6) individuals against the Subject who had been recruiting victims for work abroad, specifically in Saudi Arabia, under the pretext that he was connected to Sunergeous Manpower Services Corporation, when in fact he has resigned from the said corporation since February 2017. Subject had obtained from the Complainants a total of Php 98,200.00 allegedly as down payment for processing their overseas employment. An estimated of more or less fifty (50) victims have been recruited by the Subject. Certification from Philippine Overseas Employment Administration (POEA) revealed that the Subject is not licensed nor authorized to recruit workers for overseas employment. With this information, an entrapment operation was conducted inside a mall in Manila resulting in the arrest of the Subject. Documents are now being readied gathered for filing of charges against Subject RICO PAGUIO for violation of R.A. 8042 (Large Scale Illegal Recruitment) and Estafa. On January 11, 2018 , operatives of NBI-Environmental Crime Division (NBI-EnCD) arrested twenty (20) individuals namely, ALFREDO RELATOR SUNGA, FEDERICO GRINO BRITANICO, CLARO BALANO GASPE, REYMARK RAMIREZ VALERIANO, CIELITO NATIVIDAD RIVERA, JAIME HERMAN JUAT, MICHAEL TOVERA DE JESUS, ROMMEL GALICIA VALERIANO, RICHARD RAMOS GALICICA, WILSON CAPIRAL SAN DIEGO, JAYPEE MANALAYSAY RAMOS, GILFREDO RIVERA GUSI, ALMER JAY PELAREJA, ARGEL DELA CRUZ POLICARPIO, WHELINDEL SILVERIO SALAMAT, MARKK JOHN OMANIA DE ARMAS, NORLITO MARINAS LLANETA, CARLY OCAMPO SILVERIO, JOHN PATRICK MANINGAS PAPA, and RYAN DELOS REYES ROXAS for illegal fishing. The said fishermen were caught in the act of fishing within the municipal waters of Hagonoy, Bulacan without the necessary license or permit. Subjects were arrested and presented for inquest proceedings for violation of R.A. 8550 (Fisheries Code) as amended by R.A. 10654. January 13, 2018 , operatives of NBI-Western Visayas Regional Office (NBI-WEVRO) arrested PO2 KEVEN PIOSCA and EDMAR CAMANGYAN who were involved in the murder of Mae Luzuriaga. The case stemmed from the request of the victim’s sister to investigate the alleged murder of Mae. Autopsy on the body of the victim was conducted as well as ocular inspection of the crime scene. The NBI team inspected the crime scene and subsequently made a re-enactment to understand the actual circumstances in the area. Several witnesses were interviewed and the CCTV footages were reviewed. It was gathered from witnesses that Subject PO2 KEVEN PIOSCA, a policeman assigned at Sara PNP, is the victim’s boyfriend and accordingly, they had quarrels about money considering that Subject PO2 KEVEN PIOSCA owed a big amount of money from the victim. In the course of investigation, a witness was able to identify the gunman based on the CCTV footages. One of the two companions of the victim at the time of the incident voluntarily confessed that the victims’s boyfriend, Subject PIOSCA and Subject CAMANGYAN have direct knowledge and participation in the killing of the victim. A plan to arrest the Subjects was devised and through continuous efforts, both Subjects were arrested. Subjects were presented for inquest and were charged with Murder for the death of Mae Luzuriaga. On January 15, 2018 , operatives of NBI-National Capital Region (NBI-NCR) arrested PILAR DELA CRUZ by virtue of Warrant of Arrest issued by RTC Branch 263, Marikina City for Estafa. Requesting party, Dr. Wilson Gan reported that the Subject will be collecting rentals from her tenants at Sta. Ana Village, Makati City. NBI-NCR operatives then went to the said area and after identifying the Subject, they effected the Warrant of Arrest. Subject was brought at the NBI for proper booking procedures and was later on brought to NBI Detention Center for temporary custody. On January 16, 2018 , operatives of NBI-Cybercrime Division (NBI-CCD) arrested ABDUL RAZAQ BUKHARI y LABII , a Filipino-Pakistani, for violations of R.A. 9262 (Anti-Violence Against Women and their Children Act of 2004), Article 282 (Grave Threat) of the Revised Penal Code in relation to R.A. 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012), and R.A. 9995 (Anti-Photo and Video Voyeurism Act of 2009). The case stemmed from a complaint against the Subject for posting on internet nude photos of Complainant. Complainant alleged that she came to know the Subject through Facebook which later on led to a long distance relationship. They use Facebook Messenger as medium of communication and every time they engaged in video calling, Subject was demanding Complainant to show her private parts which the latter did out of love for the Subject. Complainant then learned that Subject was married to another Filipina so she decided to end their relationship. Subject did not accept the idea and continued to persuade the Complainant, but he got mad after knowing that Complainant had found a new boyfriend. Subject then began blackmailing the Complainant that he would send her nude photos online to her friends if she would not go back to him and break up with her new boyfriend. Complainant ignored the threat until Subject, out of anger, sent the photos to her new boyfriend and workmates. Subject again tried to talk with the Complainant, requesting for a meet up and sex in exchange of the deletion of all the Complainant’s nude photos. At this point, Complainant sought the help of NBI. An entrapment operation was then conducted resulting in the arrest of the Subject. Subject was thereafter presented for inquest proceedings for above-mentioned violations. On January 18, 2018 , operatives of NBI-Ilocos Regional Office (NBI-IRO) arrested CYD CHARISSE GADIA in an entrapment operation for human trafficking. Information from a reliable source was received regarding the illegal activities of Subject GADIA who was allegedly engaged in human trafficking and prostitution of minors and women. After verification and surveillance, NBI-IRO secured and obtained authority to operate for the conduct of entrapment operation against Subject Gadia. Thus, on the above-mentioned date, an entrapment operation was conducted with the representatives from Department of Social and Welfare Development (DSWD) Regional Office 1. The operation resulted in the arrest of Subject GADIA and rescue of three (3) minors aged 15 and 16 years old who were offered to the poseur customers. The rescued minors were then turned over to DSWD for protective custody and investigation processes while Subject GADIA was brought to NBI-IRO office for the proper booking procedures. Subject GADIA was presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor, San Fernando City, La Union for violation of RA 9208 (Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2003 and RA 7610 (Child Abuse Law). On January 18, 2018 , operatives of NBI-Special Task Force (NBI-STF) arrested MERCEDITA R. GONZALES a.k.a. MARILEN GAVIOLA in an entrapment operation in Quezon City for Swindling/Estafa, falsification of documents, and violation of Anti-Alias Law. The case stemmed from complaints against the Subject who allegedly defrauded the victim. Subject GONZALES introduced herself as an employee of PAG-IBIG Fund, and will handle the processing of the approval of the victim’s housing loan. Complainant then gave her more or less Php 200,000 on separate occasions as payment for processing the said loan. Subject GONZALES also offered another house and lot which she claimed to had been processed by the National Home Mortgage Finance Corporation (NHMFC) and now being sold. Complainant did not want to miss the opportunity so she called her sister abroad who showed interest in purchasing the house and lot. They then paid Subject GONZALES Php 238,000 and an official receipt purportedly issued by NHMFC was given to them. Complainant kept on waiting for the approval of their documents but to no avail. She went directly in the office of NHFMC in Makati where she learned that they are not listed in the clients of the agency and the receipt issued to her is not authentic. Another Complainant alleged that she paid Subject GONZALES Php 190,000 as an advanced payment for the purchase price of house and lot but later on was informed that the title of the house and lot she bought is fake. Complainants then filed the complaint before the NBI. After verification with the PAG-IBIG Fund that Subject GONZALES is not an employee of the said office, NBI-STF operatives conducted an entrapment operation which resulted in the arrest of the Subject. Charges for violations of Article 315 (Estafa/Swindling) of the Revised Penal Code, Article 172 in relation to Article 171 of the Revised Penal Code (Falsification of Documents), and R.A. 6085 (Anti-Alias Law) were filed against the Subject. On January 19, 2018 , operatives of NBI-Technical Intelligence Division (NBI-TID) arrested RANDY RUBIO , one of the co-accused of Rosario Baladjay, a celebrated investment and pyramiding scam queen who was arrested and convicted for syndicated estafa on December 3, 2012. Said decision was affirmed by the Supreme Court on July 26, 2017. Subject RUBIO was arrested in Cabanatuan City by virtue of Warrant of Arrest with No Bail Recommended after the NBI received a reliable intelligence information about the whereabouts of the Subject. Relative thereto, the NBI hatched COPLAN PYRAMID to take immediate action on possible apprehension of Subject RANDY RUBIO. On January 20, 2018 , operatives of NBI-Anti-Violence Against Women and Children (NBI-AVAWCD) rescued three (3) minors and arrested DARIUS GACHO OCO in Bicutan City. The case stemmed from a complaint referred by Mr. Mon Tulfo. The case involves Subject DARIUS GACHO OCO , father of three (3) minor children aged ten (10) years old, nine (9) years old, and one (1) year old. Children were taken by their father last December 31, 2017 in the guise that he will bring them for a stroll to a park. However, until the date of the complaint, the father was still not returning the children. The father was allegedly bringing the children to his day job as a taxi driver. Based on the information gathered, there were times that the taxi was being used as temporary shelter for the children and because of this, the two (2) children were failing to attend their school and their teachers were already asking regarding the children’s non-attendance. With this, after proper coordination with the Philippine National Police (PNP), Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD), NBI-AVAWCD operatives, together with the media representative from TULFO, and the mother of the children, a rescue operation was conducted and on the aforementioned date, the children were rescued in Bicutan City, as revealed by Subject DARIUS himself. Appropriate charges will be filed against the father, DARIUS GACHO OCO upon completion of documents and sworn statements of the victims and the complainant. On January 20, 2018 , operatives of NBI-Anti-Organized and Transnational Crime Division (NBI-AOTCD) arrested SU JIANSHUI a.k.a AH SIN and CHENWIN BIN in Pasay City for serious illegal detention. The case stemmed from a report that the Subjects were detaining a handcuffed couple in a house at Moonwalk, Paranaque City. With this, NBI-AOTCD operatives conducted a rescue operation on January 19, 2018 which resulted in the rescue of AI XIAO FENG and XIAO QZAO LING, both Chinese nationals. Also present during the operation were the four (4) bodyguards who later on gave their sworn statements similar to the initial report received by the NBI-AOTCD. Rescued victims, on the other hand, narrated that Subject SU JIANSHUI a.k.a AH SIN accused them of the lost RMB 700,000 (equivalent to Php 5.5 Million) but they denied any knowledge thereto. A follow-up operation was then conducted at Shell Residence located at Pasay City resulting in the arrest of the above-mentioned Subjects who were positively identified by the victims as those who handcuffed and took them away. Subjects were brought to NBI-AOTCD for proper booking procedures and were thereafter presented for inquest proceedings for violation of Article 267 (Serious Illegal Detention) of the Revised Penal Code. Subjects are presently detained at the NBI Detention Jail. On January 22, 2018 , operatives of NBI-National Capital Region (NBI-NCR) arrested LEON CHAMBERS and VICTOR BENJAMIN MIENDJE , citizens of Cameroon, a country in South Africa for Syndicated Estafa and Illegal Possession and Use of False Treasury/Bank notes. the case stemmed from a complaint filed by a Jordanian national, Thamer Alradaideh, on December 27, 2017, regarding the alleged Scam committed or being committed by certain foreign nationals against him. According to the complaint, other foreign nationals who are part of their group, namely: Subjects MARTIN NDANG, NGWA DAKO BROWN, MARY JOSEPH and an Alias CLINTON, have fraudulently obtained money from the complainant by persuading him that piles of banknote-sized paper in a safety box were actually currency notes that have been dyed to avoid detection by authorities. Complainant, on separate occasions has already given the group a total of P1.2 Million allegedly used in buying chemicals for the cleaning up of said U.S. dollars. The complainant added that was persuaded to pay fees and purchase chemicals to remove the dye with a promise of a share in the proceeds. The Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas was even notified the about the group led by Subject Martin Ndang that is engaged in a scheme “Black Dollar Scam” defrauding foreigners in the Philippines. In coordination with the Currency Integrity Staff-Currency issue and Integrity Office of the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (CIO-CIIO, BSP), an entrapment operation was conducted resulting in the arrest of Subjects LEON CHAMBERS and VICTOR BENJAMIN MIENDJE in Makati City and the seizure of counterfeit US dollars and other paraphernalia. Initial examination of CIO-CIIO, BSP Agent Arminda Superales indicated that the US dollar banknotes seized from the Subjects were all found to be counterfeit. Charges for Syndicated Estafa under PD no. 1689 and for violation of Article 168 of the Revised Penal Code (Illegal possession and use of false treasury or banknotes) were filed before the Department of Justice. Other co-conspirators, namely: Martin Ndang, Ngwa Dako Brown, Mary Joseph and Alias Clinto were also included in the complaint-referral to the Prosecutor’s Office. On January 23, 2018 , operatives of NBI-National Capital Region (NBI-NCR), in coordination with International Airport Investigation Unit, Bureau of Immigration and Philippine Airlines, arrested LESLIE CARMONA LIM aka WANG PENG PENG by virtue of Warrant of Arrest. Subject was arrested in NAIA Terminal 2, Pasay City where Subject was on board in Philippine Airlines arriving from Japan. Subject was immediately brought to NBI-NCR for proper booking procedures and is currently detained at the NBI Jail. On January 24, 2018 , operatives of Southeastern Mindanao Regional Office (NBI-SEMRO) arrested KAMAK DJUMOU JEAMLUC aka STEPHAN DJUMUO, SAMUEL ENKAGA, and WILLIAM SMITH in an entrapment operation for violation of Article 315 (Estafa) of the Revised Penal Code in relation to RA 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012), Falsification of Documents and Article 178 of Revised Penal Code (Using Fictitious Name and Concealing True Name). The case stemmed from the complaint of three complainants against the Subject. Charges for aforementioned violations were filed against the Subject. On January 24, 2018 , operatives of Anti-Organized and Transnational Crime Division (NBI-AOTCD) arrested ARNEL MALTO y BERBANO for Estafa and Unauthorized Practice of Customs Broker Profession. Complainant alleged that a friend of her Korean husband shipped a container van from South Korea but the said shipment was put on hold at the Bureau of Customs because the content of which is used clothings (ukay-ukay) She then asked help a certain Jimmy Frenandez who introduced her to Subject ARNEL MALTO who introduced himself as a Custom Broker and asked for Php 400,000 to facilitate the release of said shipment. Complainant gave money to the Subject on different occasions but the latter failed to fulfill the promised release of shipment even after paying the amount he demanded in full. With this, an entrapment operation was conducted at Pasay City where Complainant and Subject Malto agreed to meet. Subject was arrested after receiving the marked money. He was immediately brought to NBI for proper booking procedures and was presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor, Pasay City for Estafa and Unauthorized Practice of Customs Broker Profession. On January 25, 2018 , operatives of Special Action Unit (NBI-SAU) arrested RAMON R. BALATBAT by virtue of Warrant of Arrest issued by RTC Branch 216, Quezon City for Estafa. The service of Warrant of Arrest was based on the request of Mr. Colin Anthony Pearson to be served against CRISELDA MARIE BALATBAT and RAMON BALATBAT. Operatives were able to gather information on the whereabouts of the Subjects. It was discovered that Subjects were residing in Lipa, Batangas so operatives proceeded to the area and upon coordination with the local authorities, Lipa City Police and Barangay Lumbang representatives, a joint operation was arranged for the implementation of Warrants. CRISELDA MARIE BALATBAT was not found and was allegedly out of the country but RAMON BALATBAT was found in the residence so in a peaceful and orderly manner, RAMON BALATBAT was arrested and was thereafter brought to Lipa City Police for proper booking procedures. Subject RAMON BALATBAT is presently detained at the Lipa City Police station awaiting transport to RTC Branch 216, Quezon City. Complainant was then instructed by the subject to send the money to a certain money transfer code via Smart Padala which was located at Taytay, Rizal, as discovered by the operatives. With this, an entrapment operation was conducted in coordination with the owner of the money transfer resulting in the arrest of the Subject. CRUZ-TAN is engaged in dental practice without the necessary license and certificate required under the law. After conducting proper verification and surveillance operation by the NBI-STF wherein Subject RONALYN J. CRUZ-TAN performed a dental procedure on an undercover operative, an entrapment operation was hatched resulting in the arrest of Subject RONALYN J. CRUZ-TAN, who will be charged for violation of R.A. 9484 otherwise known as The Philippine Dental Act of 2007. Upon investigation and surveillance, violations were indeed committed. A rescue operation was then resulting in the rescue of seven (7) female victims. Subject IMAD HAMDAN was arrested in the act of recruiting and harboring. He was then presented for inquested proceedings for violation of Maigrant Workers Act and Anti-Expanded Human Trafficking Act. On January 29, 2018 , operatives of NBI-National Capital Region (NBI-NCR) arrested LEILANIE GATCHALIAN DELA CRUZ in an entrapment operation in Taguig City for Estafa through Falsification of Public Documents. The case stemmed from the complaint of Mr. Ferdinand Espiritu Malanay against the Subject who was caught in flagrante delicto committing the crime of Estafa through Falsification of Public Documents during the operation. Subject was brought for inquest proceedings before the Prosecutor’s Officeof Taguig City and is presently detained in NBI Jail awaiting for the resolution of the case. The counterfeit tablets/capsules were seized on the strength of Search Warrant at the premises of Subjects BOY ALVANIA and JANINE TELOZA both located in Plaridel, Bulacan. Charges for violation of RA 8293 (Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines) were filed against the Subjects. TAGUBA II, the Customs Broker who facilitated the importation of more than 600 kilos of methamphetamine Hydrochloride or shabu that were seized by the NBI and Philippine Drug Enforcement Agency in May 2017, in coordination with the Bureau of Customs. Subject was arrested by virtue of Warrant of Arrest issued against him and seven other individuals for Violation of R.A. 9165 or the Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002. On January 25, 2018, the Department of Justice (DOJ) filed criminal charges against Subject MARK RUBEN G. TAGUBA II and eight (8) other individuals before the Regional Trial Court of Manila for Violation of R.A. 9165 otherwise known as the Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002. The other individuals included in the charges are Subjects CHEN JULONG a.k.a. RICHARD TAN, LI GUANG FENG a.k.a MANNY LI, DONG YI SHEN XI a.k.a. KENNETH DONG, EIRENE MAE A. TATAD, TEEJAY A. MARCELLANA, CHEN I-MIN, JHU MING JYUN, and CHEN RONG HUAN . Subject was placed under the custody of the NBI. ROSALES, ROSELYN DOHINOG y PINLAC, TEDDY ENDRIGA y MONIZ, ENT OBESO y JELARDES, WARLIE YBAROLA y LAQUIO, PETER JOHN GUZMAN y NILLAS, SHAIRA JACOB y OPPENLENTISIMA, MARINA TALISIC y PILARION, CELINE ALVAREZ y COSTINO, JOMARIE NEMIS, JEROLD BLAZA y GUZMAN, CRESLYN GALOPE y MALBAS, SHARLENE JOY ORTIZ, SANNY GARNICA y VALENCIA, JESSIE GERADIAZ y PACULANG, ROSNINTIVE DAYASCAL y SAMEON, JAMARAH RASUMAN y MOHAMMAD, DULCE CAPANGPANGAN y ANASCO, EVANGELINE ALLEGO y NAVARRO, SELINE PABURAN y GARDAN, GENNY ROSE GUERGO y CABONITA, MARJORIE OLIVVAR y EPON, BABIE CLAIRE BACLAAN y FALCON, JOESARIE VILLAMOR y PAMILAR, and LOUGEL HALASAN y CEPRIANO for illegal gambling. On January 9, 2018, ANTONIO OCMER y NIEVA, LOLITA HYASTRO de JAVIER y DIPAS, GIRLIE JAVIER y HYASTRO, and EUSEBIO GRAPEZA JR. y MOLDEZ were arrested in Sitio Visaya, Alabang, Muntinlupa City. On January 15, 2018 , AERICK MOISES y LUNA, BENJAMIN PABILONIA y AMPARADO, and ANGELITO LAURORA y APIN were arrested in Brgy. Cupang, Muntinlupa City. On January 18, 2018 , ROGER BRAVO y GUANZON and EUGENIA LOMEDA de GARCIA y JOSE were arrested in Brgy. Alabang, Muntinlupa City. Seized from their possessions were jueteng paraphernalia and bet money. Charges for violation of PD 1602 (Simplifying and Providing Stiffer Penalties for Violations of Gambling Laws) as amended by R.A. 9287 (An Act Increasing the Penalties for Illegal Numbers Games, Amending Certain provisions of P.D. 1602 and for Other Purposes) were filed against all the arrested Subjects.

Charges for violations of Article 315 (Estafa/Swindling) of the Revised Penal Code, Article 172 in relation to Article 171 of the Revised Penal Code (Falsification of Documents), and R.A. 6085 (Anti-Alias Law) were filed against the Subject. On January 19, 2018 , operatives of NBI-Technical Intelligence Division (NBI-TID) arrested RANDY RUBIO , one of the co-accused of Rosario Baladjay, a celebrated investment and pyramiding scam queen who was arrested and convicted for syndicated estafa on December 3, 2012. Said decision was affirmed by the Supreme Court on July 26, 2017. Subject RUBIO was arrested in Cabanatuan City by virtue of Warrant of Arrest with No Bail Recommended after the NBI received a reliable intelligence information about the whereabouts of the Subject. Relative thereto, the NBI hatched COPLAN PYRAMID to take immediate action on possible apprehension of Subject RANDY RUBIO. On January 20, 2018 , operatives of NBI-Anti-Violence Against Women and Children (NBI-AVAWCD) rescued three (3) minors and arrested DARIUS GACHO OCO in Bicutan City. The case stemmed from a complaint referred by Mr. Mon Tulfo. The case involves Subject DARIUS GACHO OCO , father of three (3) minor children aged ten (10) years old, nine (9) years old, and one (1) year old. Children were taken by their father last December 31, 2017 in the guise that he will bring them for a stroll to a park. However, until the date of the complaint, the father was still not returning the children. The father was allegedly bringing the children to his day job as a taxi driver. Based on the information gathered, there were times that the taxi was being used as temporary shelter for the children and because of this, the two (2) children were failing to attend their school and their teachers were already asking regarding the children’s non-attendance. With this, after proper coordination with the Philippine National Police (PNP), Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD), NBI-AVAWCD operatives, together with the media representative from TULFO, and the mother of the children, a rescue operation was conducted and on the aforementioned date, the children were rescued in Bicutan City, as revealed by Subject DARIUS himself. Appropriate charges will be filed against the father, DARIUS GACHO OCO upon completion of documents and sworn statements of the victims and the complainant. On January 20, 2018 , operatives of NBI-Anti-Organized and Transnational Crime Division (NBI-AOTCD) arrested SU JIANSHUI a.k.a AH SIN and CHENWIN BIN in Pasay City for serious illegal detention. The case stemmed from a report that the Subjects were detaining a handcuffed couple in a house at Moonwalk, Paranaque City. With this, NBI-AOTCD operatives conducted a rescue operation on January 19, 2018 which resulted in the rescue of AI XIAO FENG and XIAO QZAO LING, both Chinese nationals. Also present during the operation were the four (4) bodyguards who later on gave their sworn statements similar to the initial report received by the NBI-AOTCD. Rescued victims, on the other hand, narrated that Subject SU JIANSHUI a.k.a AH SIN accused them of the lost RMB 700,000 (equivalent to Php 5.5 Million) but they denied any knowledge thereto. A follow-up operation was then conducted at Shell Residence located at Pasay City resulting in the arrest of the above-mentioned Subjects who were positively identified by the victims as those who handcuffed and took them away. Subjects were brought to NBI-AOTCD for proper booking procedures and were thereafter presented for inquest proceedings for violation of Article 267 (Serious Illegal Detention) of the Revised Penal Code. Subjects are presently detained at the NBI Detention Jail. On January 22, 2018 , operatives of NBI-National Capital Region (NBI-NCR) arrested LEON CHAMBERS and VICTOR BENJAMIN MIENDJE , citizens of Cameroon, a country in South Africa for Syndicated Estafa and Illegal Possession and Use of False Treasury/Bank notes. the case stemmed from a complaint filed by a Jordanian national, Thamer Alradaideh, on December 27, 2017, regarding the alleged Scam committed or being committed by certain foreign nationals against him. According to the complaint, other foreign nationals who are part of their group, namely: Subjects MARTIN NDANG, NGWA DAKO BROWN, MARY JOSEPH and an Alias CLINTON, have fraudulently obtained money from the complainant by persuading him that piles of banknote-sized paper in a safety box were actually currency notes that have been dyed to avoid detection by authorities. Complainant, on separate occasions has already given the group a total of P1.2 Million allegedly used in buying chemicals for the cleaning up of said U.S. dollars. The complainant added that was persuaded to pay fees and purchase chemicals to remove the dye with a promise of a share in the proceeds. Charges for Syndicated Estafa under PD no. 1689 and for violation of Article 168 of the Revised Penal Code (Illegal possession and use of false treasury or banknotes) were filed before the Department of Justice. Other co-conspirators, namely: Martin Ndang, Ngwa Dako Brown, Mary Joseph and Alias Clinto were also included in the complaint-referral to the Prosecutor’s Office. Complainant alleged that a friend of her Korean husband shipped a container van from South Korea but the said shipment was put on hold at the Bureau of Customs because the content of which is used clothings (ukay-ukay) She then asked help a certain Jimmy Frenandez who introduced her to Subject ARNEL MALTO who introduced himself as a Custom Broker and asked for Php 400,000 to facilitate the release of said shipment. body: PRESS STATEMENT February 12, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } NBI ARRESTS 10 CHINESE NATIONALS AND 16 FILIPINOS IN MAJOR ANTI-ILLEGAL MINING CRACKDOWN IN BUKIDNON PASAY, Philippines — The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) has successfully dismantled a large-scale illegal mining operation in Libona, Bukidnon, resulting in the arrest of ten (10) Chinese nationals and sixteen (16) Filipinos, as well as the seizure of significant mineral resources and heavy machinery. On 09 February 2026, operatives from the NBI-Northeastern Mindanao Regional Office (NEMRO) and the NBI-Bukidnon District Office (NBI-BUKDO) executed a raid in Barangay Gango and uncovered a sophisticated mining site featuring an extensive tunnel system designed for high-volume mineral extraction. During the sweep, NBI-BUKDO seized a massive volume of copper ore and a specialized processing plant, alongside heavy equipment used in the illicit activity such as a dump truck, a backhoe, and industrial-grade generator sets. In a critical discovery, operatives also found a stockpile of commercial explosives on site for which the Subjects were unable to provide any valid permits or licenses. To ensure public safety, personnel from the PNP Explosive Ordnance Disposal (EOD) unit were called in to secure the site and neutralize these hazardous materials. The success of this mission was the result of seamless inter-agency collaboration. The operation was conducted through the joint efforts of the NBI-BUKDO, the Mines and Geosciences Bureau (MGB), the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR), and the Libona Municipal Police Station. Arrested Subjects have been presented for inquest proceedings and are charged with violations of Republic Act No. 7942, also known as the Philippine Mining Act of 1995. This operation underscores the government’s firm stance against the unauthorized exploitation of the country’s natural resources by foreign entities. “This operation serves as a stern warning that we will not tolerate the plunder of our natural resources. The NBI remains committed to protecting our environment and strictly enforcing our laws against any foreign entities who attempt to exploit our land through illegal means,” stated by NBI Acting Director Atty. Angelito DLP. Magno. ATTY. ANGELITO DLP. MAGNO Acting Director, NBI #NBIServes Media Contact: HA Palmer U. Mallari NBI Spokesperson [email protected]

body: In an effort to protect the members of the legal profession and judiciary, the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) has signed a Memorandum of Agreement (MOA) with the Integrated Bar of the Philippines (IBP). NBI OIC-Director Eric B. Distor said the MOA is a welcome development between the two institutions as it will strengthen coordination and communication of NBI with the various chapter organizations of the IBP. Distor added that the MOA hopes to prevent further attacks against lawyers and members of the judiciary. In a 5-page document signed by NBI OIC-Director Eric B. Distor and IBP President Atty. Domingo Q. Cayosa at the new Corporate Office of NBI in V-Tech Tower along Araneta avenue in Quezon City on Friday, June 25, 2021, the NBI will provide timely assistance to lawyers, prosecutors and magistrates in distress and extend appropriate security and protection in cases of threats or hazards in the performance of their duties and functions as may be allowed by law and regulations. The NBI will also expedite the investigation and give preferential attention to incidents or cases of violence against members of the legal profession and to ensure that the perpetrators are held accountable and that justice is swiftly done. For its part of the agreement, the IBP will provide legal assistance, through its legal aid program, to qualified NBI personnel who are unjustly harassed for doing their job and who do not have access to competent lawyers. The MOA also states that the IBP will establish and manage an appropriate incentive and reward fund to assist and encourage informants and witnesses for the successful investigation, arrest, and prosecution of suspects in the killing of or attack against lawyers, prosecutors, and magistrates. The MOA further states that the IBP will advocate measures that intend to upgrade law enforcement capabilities, ensure the prompt resolution and disposition of criminal cases, and motivate the NBI officers and lawyers to work together in upholding the rule of law in the service of our country and its people. In their strong desire to make the MOA more effective, the NBI and IBP agreed to establish and maintain direct lines of communication between their national and local leaders for faster coordination to pre-empt, avoid, or reduce violence against their members and to expedite and monitor the investigation, arrest and prosecution, punishment and reformation of the malefactors. Both parties also agreed, to the extent allowed by their respective rules and policies and within the bounds of the law, the participants shall share data and information to promptly and effectively contain or adequately address threats to the life and security of their members.

body: PRESS STATEMENT July 14, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } In line with the directive from National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Director JAIME B. SANTIAGO (Ret.), agents of NBI-National Capital Region (NBI-NCR) and NBI-Organized and Transnational Crime Division (NBI-OTCD), together with the NBI Forensic Team, located the cadaver of Victim REYMOND ENRIQUEZ CABRERA along Zaragoza-San Antonio Road in Barangay Batitang, Zaragoza, Nueva Ecija on July 11, 2025. On May 19, 2025, MA. MEYA BIÑAS CABRERA went to the office of NBI-National Capital Region (NBI-NCR) requesting assistance to locate her husband, REYMOND ENRIQUEZ CABRERA, a Transport Network Vehicle Service (TNVS) driver, who had been missing since May 18, 2025. Per investigation, on May 18, 2025, REYMOND received a booking from one EMMANUEL DE JESUS for pick-up at a hotel in Paranaque City. Three (3) male individuals, later identified as JOHN KEVIN DE OCAMPO, JUSTINE DALAFU, and JIN ARMIN DE OCAMPO were seen boarding the same. The vehicle proceeded to a casino hotel in the same city then left towards Cavite. Dashcam recording captured the conversation between the three male individuals and that REYMOND was already stabbed and bleeding. They also discussed the possible places to dump the body of the driver. In the afternoon of the same day, the vehicle was seen passing in Valenzuela City until it was recovered by the Agents of the NBI-NCR on May 20, 2025. Forensic examination of the vehicle showed traces of blood at the second row and back portion of the vehicle. NBI agents, at this point, were unable to recover victim’s remains, as the perpetrators deliberately traversed multiple locations. Furthermore, the personal belongings of the victim, REYMOND ENRIQUEZ CABRERA, were missing and were not found inside the vehicle. Nevertheless, NBI-NCR recommended the conduct of preliminary investigation for the crimes of carnapping and robbery with homicide before the Department of Justice against the following individuals ─ JOHN KEVIN BANTING DE OCAMPO, JUSTINE DE GUZMAN DALAFU, JIN ARMIN BANTING DE OCAMPO, EMMANUEL DE JESUS (the identity used to book the TNVS driver victim), and JOHN DOE or “BLACK” (the unidentified individual seen in the CCTV footage). On July 10, 2025, a crucial turn of events occurred when the three (3) Subjects voluntarily surrendered to Manila MAYOR ISKO MORENO DOMAGOSO. Mayor Moreno personally called NBI Director Santiago about the voluntary surrender of the Subjects. In response to this development, on July 10, 2025, the NBI-OTCD, upon the directive of Director Santiago, proceeded to the Office of Mayor Moreno and formally received custody of the aforementioned Subjects. Subjects JOHN KEVIN and JUSTINE volunteered to show where Victim’s body is located. Hence, in the early morning of July 11,2025, the NBI agents proceeded to the identified location in Nueva Ecija. Thereat, Subject himself pointed to the exact location along the grass-covered roadside area in Zaragoza-San Antonio Road in Barangay Batitang, Zaragoza, Nueva Ecija. Indeed, upon instant checking over the bushes, the agents saw the decomposing body. Recovered from the scene of the crime by the NBI Forensic Team are the following items, to wit: one (1) cadaver in an advanced state of decomposition, suspected to be the remains of REYMOND E. CABRERA, one (1) piece of blue shirt, one (1) piece of car rubber mat, and one (1) piece of shoe. After completion of the necessary forensic procedures, the remains of the victim were turned over to a morgue in Nueva Ecija, for conduct of autopsy/medico-legal examination and proper disposition. body: PRESS STATEMENT December 19, 2024 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } In line with the strict order of National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Director JUDGE JAIME B. SANTIAGO (Ret.) to eradicate human trafficking activities in the country, the NBI – Alaminos District Office (NBI-ALDO) arrested ROCHELLE CORTEZ, EDMUND LANAYOG CORPUZ, RAMONES JERVY MENDOZA. BONIFACIO ESTA, and JEXTER CRUZ SISON in an entrapment operation in Alaminos City, Pangasinan for violation of R.A. No. 9208 (Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2003), as amended. Director Santiago said that the office of the NBI-ALDO received information from a non-government organization (NGO) that exists to rescue women and children from human trafficking that Shayawayne Videoke Bar (Shayawayne) is engaged in prostitution of women, including minors. A series of surveillance operations conducted by NBI-ALDO confirmed the veracity of the information revealing that Shayawayne is indeed offering women, including minors for sexual services in exchange for a fee. On December 12, 2024, joint operatives of NBI-ALDO, NBI-DADO, and NBI-IRO together with the representatives from the NGO and PSWDO proceeded to Shayawayne and conducted an entrapment operation, which resulted in the arrest of the above-stated Subjects, in the act of violating the Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2003. The operation also resulted in the rescue of ten (10) trafficked victims, seven of whom were revealed to be minors based on the Dental Aging Examination conducted on them. The rescued victims were turned over to the Provincial Social Welfare and Development Office (PSWDO) in Lingayen for counselling and social protection. The arrested Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the City Prosecutor’s Office, Alaminos City, Pangasinan for violation of R.A No. 9208, as amended by R.A. No. 10364. In a Resolution, the City Prosecutor’s Office, Alaminos City, Pangasinan stated that based on the pieces of evidence and affidavits of the rescued victims, the Subjects are liable for violation of R.A. No. 9208, as amended by R.A. No. 10364 and recommended that the corresponding information be filed against them. Director Santiago commended the operatives of NBI-ALDO, NBI-DADO, and NBI-IRO for following his order, which resulted in the arrest of the Subjects and rescue of the victims. body: PRESS STATEMENT May 9, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } The National Bureau of Investigation-Olongapo District Office (NBI-OLDO) and Special Task Force (NBI-STF), under the supervision of NBI Director Judge Jaime B. Santiago (Ret.), arrested six (6) individuals who plotted to manipulate voting machines for mayoral candidate’s victory. Subjects were identified as ROLAND UCAB y BAYSON, TEODY ABALOS Y ALMAZAN, JOSEPH ONG Y GAMAO, CHERRYLYN ADRIANO y UMLAS, RALP EDWARD SALAS Y DE LUNA, and FRANCIS JAMES MAPUA y LASCANO. The case stemmed from the COMELEC’s referral regarding Iba, Zambales mayoral candidate, Atty. Genaro N. Montefalcon, who was offered by Subjects his secured win in the upcoming election. In April 2025, Atty. Montefalcon was approached by Subjects Teody Abalos y Almazan and Cherrylyn Adriano y Umlas. They claimed connections within the Commission on Elections (COMELEC) and offered to secure his victory in the upcoming May 12 elections by manipulating the Automated Counting Machines, for a fee of P30 million. Abalos further claimed to have a direct connection with the previous COMELEC chairman, stating that he is the nephew of senator-candidate Benhur Abalos and a grandson of former COMELEC Chairman Benjamin Abalos. Skeptical of their claims and offer, Atty. Montefalcon reported the incident to the COMELEC, providing screenshots of their communications. The COMELEC promptly referred the matter to the National Bureau of Investigation’s Olongapo District Office (NBI-OLDO). In coordination with the NBI Special Task Force (NBI-STF), an entrapment operation was hatched on May 8, 2025. Under the pretense of agreeing to their proposal, Atty. Montefalcon met with the suspects in a hotel in Quezon City. During the meeting, Subjects told Atty. Montefalcon, that he needed to pay Php 30 Million for his guaranteed victory, but they only requested for a down payment of P15 million and that the remaining amount would be paid after the election. Subjects ADRIANO, ABALOS, and ONG were the ones who met Atty. Montefalcon and undercover operatives in the hotel lobby, while Subjects UCAB, SALAS, and MAPUA were the ones who transacted with Atty. Montefalcon in a hotel room. After handing over the marked money, Subjects in both the hotel room and in the hotel lobby were placed under arrest. Arrested Subjects were apprised of their constitutional rights and underwent standard booking procedures at the STF Office. Charges for Estafa/Violation of Article 315 of the Revised Penal Code, Usurpation of Authority/Violation of Article 177 of the Revised Penal Code, and Section 28 of Republic Act No. 9369, also known as the Automated Election System Law, were filed against the Subjects.

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) announced today the arrest of a businesswoman for large-scale selling of adulterated alcohol in Manila on May 12, 2020. NBI Officer-In-Charge (OIC) Eric B. Distor identified the Subject as CHERRYGIL DEL ROSARIO ARRIOLA, who was arrested in an entrapment operation by the operatives of NBI-Special Action Unit (NBI-SAU). OIC Distor said that the case stemmed from an intelligence report on the alleged large-scale sale of adulterated alcohol from subject’s shop, CreativeLab Cosmetic Products, located in Sampaloc, Manila. According to the report, subject Arriola personally mixes ethyl alcohol and methanol to increase its volume. Methanol, by its nature, is highly corrosive and is a toxic substance not suitable for human consumption. OIC Distor further said that the NBI-SAU operatives conducted a test buy operation on April 27, 2020, wherein three (3) gallons of ethyl alcohol and three (3) gallons of disinfectant were purchased from the subject at P330.00 per gallon. The gallons were labelled as “Ethyl Alcohol 99.9%” and “Bacfree Disinfectant”. The NBI, thereafter, submitted to Food and Drug Administration (FDA) the above items for laboratory examination. On May 8, 2020, FDA confirmed that the alleged ethyl alcohol contains 96.1% Methanol and 4.9% Ethanol, a solution that is toxic and harmful to human. Pursuant thereto, OIC Distor said that an entrapment operation was conducted on May 11, 2020, wherein subject Arriola was arrested after receiving from the poseur-customer the marked money. Also, subject failed to show any authority to sell the said products or to present chemical analysis of the claimed 99.9% ethyl alcohol that she sells to the public. Subject CHERRYGIL DEL ROSARIO ARRIOLA was recommended to be prosecuted for violation of RA 11469 (Bayanihan to Heal as One Act), RA 7394 (Consumer Act of the Philippines), and RA 9711 (Food and Drug Administration Act of 2009). Finally, OIC Distor said that the NBI works diligently to ensure that consumers are protected from the spikes of fake products. He strongly urges the public to exercise caution and care and purchase only FDA approved and verified disinfectant products.

body: The National Bureau of Investigation expresses its deepest sympathies for the passing away of former NBI Director and former Manila Mayor Alfredo S. Lim. The NBI said the reforms that Director Lim instituted when he served as head of the NBI on December 23, 1989 up to March 20, 1992 will always continue to be a part of the Bureau. body: PRESS STATEMENT August 19, 2025 .jusatified-text { text-align: justify; } The National Bureau of Investigation-Cybercrime Division (NBI-CCD), on August 15, 2025, arrested two (2) foreign nationals in Parañaque City for illegal practice of medicine. The operation stemmed from a report about certain foreign nationals who were engaged in an unauthorized practice of medicine, in violation of R.A. No. 2382, also known as the “Medical Act of 1959,” in relation to R.A. No. 10175, also known as the “Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012.” Acting on the information received, NBI-CCD agents interacted with the social media accounts associated with the foreigners. During the engagement, one of the individuals, who identified himself as DR. DO THI BINH, disclosed his name to the poseur client. The NBI-CCD then verified his identity with the Professional Regulation Commission (PRC) to determine whether a Special Temporary Permit (STP) or Special Permit (SP) had been granted for him to practice medicine in the Philippines. Through a certification, the PRC confirmed that no such permit had been granted to Dr. Do Thi Binh. In a surveillance operation, NBI-CCD agents confirmed that the foreign nationals were operating a Beauty Clinic and offering various medical procedures and medicines to the poseur client. These services, which included but were not limited to chin fillers, sexy alar trim, liposuction, rhinoplasty, blepharoplasty, and facelift, were the same ones they had been advertising online. As a result, an entrapment operation was conducted by NBI-CCD operatives on August15, 2025, resulting in the arrest of two (2) Vietnamese Nationals identified as NGUYEN THE THANG and MAI QUY LOC alias DO THI BINH. They were caught in flagrante delicto while committing the crime. Various items used in the illegal practice of medicine were likewise seized. Arrested Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings for the following charges: •Illegal Practice of Medicine, penalized under Section 8 and Section 28 of R.A. No. 2382, also known as the “Medical Act of 1959,” in relation to R.A. No. 10175, also known as the “Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012” •Sale of Unregistered Health Products and Adulterating/Misbranding of Health Products, penalized under Section 11(a) of R.A. No. 9711, also known as the “Food and Drug Administration Act” •Dispensing/Sale of Pharmaceutical Products, penalized under Section 30 of R.A. No. 10918, also known as the “Philippine Pharmacy Act” The arrest of the Vietnamese nationals is in line with the Bureau’s commitment to protecting the public from unauthorized and potentially dangerous medical practices. This operation also serves to promote safety for patients availing of aesthetic clinic services, which must be regulated and monitored by proper authorities.

title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today said operatives of the NBI-Anti-Human Trafficking Division (NBI-AHTRAD) have rescued seventeen (17) minors who were offered for sexual services, and arrested two (2) human traffickers in Caloocan City, yesterday. NBI Director Dante A. Gierran said the operation was based on information received by the Bureau that a group composed of several pimps (bugaw) had been offering young girls for sexual services to male clients, local and foreigners. Under his strict order, NBI-AHTRAD operatives arranged a meet up with the pimps to verify the information which was later confirmed. The pimps were asking for Six Thousand Pesos (Php 6,000) for every girl that would be chosen while those who are not chosen would be given a consolation of One Thousand Pesos (Php1,000). On July 27, 2017, as agreed upon, two pimps, identified as GLADY DULOT y EUGENIO and CHERRY ANN LASCANO y BATITIS, brought seventeen (17) young girls to a private resort in Caloocan City where the NBI-DSWD team was waiting. After the payment for the sexual service of one girl was received, Subjects were immediately apprehended while the victims were taken into custody by the DSWD. Initial assessment showed that all seventeen (17) victims are minors, the eldest of which is seventeen (17) years old and the youngest is thirteen (13). Subjects will be presented for inquest proceedings before the Department of Justice (DOJ) for violations of R.A. 9208 (Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act, as amended) and R.A. 7610 (Anti-Child Abuse Law). Follow-up investigation will be conducted to identify and possibly apprehend/charge other members of the group.

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today announced the arrest of five (5) individuals for operating an abortion clinic in Cebu City. NBI OIC – Director Eric B. Distor identified the arrested subjects as JOEY PAULINO GUIRIGAY a.k.a. “JOEY”; FRANCISCA ABATAYO REBAMONTE a.k.a. “FRANK”; GLORIA DALOGDOG GABUTIN a.k.a. “AMAY”, MERYTEISSIE PODE RURAL a.k.a. “DADAY”; AMPARO LUMAGBAS GEMARANGAN a.k.a. “PARING”. OIC Director Distor said that the case stemmed from the information received from a reliable informant regarding with the illegal activities of one of the subjects identified as Subject Guirigay. The information originated from a complaint for alleged violation of R.A. 9262 and Rape. The complainant stated that Subject Guirigay is offering his services for abortion to prospective clients online using Facebook account @Michelle Mayer in exchange for Php 9,500.00 to Php 30,000.00. Operatives of NBI-Central Eastern Visayas Regional Office (NBI-CEVRO) immediately established communication with Subject Guirigay thru his mobile number and was able to transact with the Subject Guirigay regarding with his abortion services. Subject Guirigay texted to the poseur-client the two (2) options of terminating unwanted pregnancy. 1st is Suction Abortion which will be done by licensed OB Gyne doctors in a private clinic which would cost Php 30,000.00. 2nd is a set of abortive pills which would cost Php 9,500.00 per kit, safe and effective. Subject Guirigay and the poseur-client agreed to meet on April 29, 2021 in the area of Chong Hospital Fuente Osmeña. The undercover agent and the poseur-client were fetched by Subject Rebamonte and was brought to Subject Gemarangan in Talisay City. NBI operatives discreetly followed them. While waiting for Subject Gemarangan to complete the preliminary interview with the poseur-client, Subject Rebamonte demanded the payment of P30,000.00 for the abortion service. As soon as handing over the marked money and when overt acts of intentional abortion were made, operatives of NBI immediately arrested subjects Gemarangan and Rebamonte. During the arrest, subject Guirigay was continuously calling Subject Rebamonte for an update on the collection of payment. NBI operatives instructed Subject Rebamonte to take the call and put it on a loud speaker. Subject Guirigay told Rebamonte that he has called Gabutin and Rural to perform the abortion in A. Lopez, Brgy. Labangon, Cebu City if Gemarangan refused. With this dev elopment, the NBI operatives immediately proceeded to A. Lopez, Labangon Cebu, which led to the arrest of subjects Gabutin and Rural and eventually Subject Guirigay in front of a hotel. By the confluence of events, NBI-CEVRO concluded that all the 5 subjects had a prior agreement and considered to have conspired to commit the crime of intentional abortion. On May 3, 2021, all the 5 Subjects were presented for Inquest proceedings before the Talisay City Prosecutor’s Office for Intentional Abortion penalized under Article 256 in relation to Article 8 (Conspiracy) of the RPC and in relation to Section 6 of R.A. 10175, otherwise known as the Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012.

title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: PRESS STATEMENT March 21, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } NBI ARRESTS FAKE NOTARY PUBLIC IN LAS PIÑAS ENTRAPMENT OPERATION PASAY CITY, Philippines – The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) – Organized and Transnational Crime Division (NBI-OTCD) has successfully arrested an individual in Las Piñas City for the unauthorized use of a notarial commission, and violations of the Revised Penal Code in relation to the Cybercrime Prevention Act. The operation was initiated following a referral from the Vice Executive Judge of Manila. A complainant lawyer reported that the Subject was fraudulently offering notarial services by illegally using the lawyer’s name and professional credentials. Investigation revealed that the Subject was operating under the business name “Rush Online Notary Service,” actively soliciting clients through various social media messaging applications. On March 18, 2026, the NBI-OTCD executed an entrapment operation at the Subject’s office in Las Piñas City. The Subject was caught in the act of performing notarial functions while misrepresenting themselves as the complainant lawyer. The Subject is facing criminal charges under the Revised Penal Code, including Falsification of Public Documents (Articles 171 and 172), Possession of Instruments for Falsification (Article 176), Usurpation of Authority or Official Functions (Article 177), and Estafa by Means of Deceit (Article 315). Furthermore, these offenses are being charged in relation to Section 6 of Republic Act No. 10175, also known as the Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012. The Subject was presented for inquest proceedings at the Office of the City Prosecutor in Las Piñas City on March 19, 2026. NBI Director Atty. Melvin A. Matibag stated that “The NBI remains steadfast in its mission to protect the integrity of our legal system. We will not tolerate individuals who undermine the notarial process and deceive the public for personal gain. We urge the public to remain vigilant and ensure they only avail of notarial services from legitimate notary publics.” #NBIServes

title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: On November 6, 2018 , operatives of NBI-National Capital Region (NBI-NCR) arrested spouses ARMANDO and LYDIA QUIMIRISTA who were recruiting workers for deployment in Canada as mushroom picker. Subjects were asking additional money for the alleged processing/facilitation of fees. Per verification, Subjects are not licensed/authorized by POEA to recruit workers for overseas employment. Subjects were arrested in entrapment operation conducted at Aristocrat Restaurant, Malate, Manila. They were presented for inquest proceedings before the City Prosecutors Office of Manila for Estafa and Large Scale Illegal Recruitment. Subjects are presently detained at the NBI Jail. On November 12, 2018 , operatives of NBI-Central Mindanao Regional Office (NBI-CEMRO), together with the operatives of NBI-Saranggani District Office (NBI-SARDO), NBI-Cybercrime Division (NBI-CCD), and NBI-Digital Forensic Laboratory (NBI-DFL) arrested JOLLEMAE VALENCIA for child trafficking and child pornography. Based on the report acquired validated by casing and surveillance operations conducted, a probable cause to believe that the Subject was indeed involved in child sexual molestation. Pictures of the Subject doing lascivious acts to the children were being sent to a certain person through Facebook. On the basis of Search Warrant, NBI operatives, in coordination with the PNP General Santos City, implemented the Search Warrant which resulted in the rescue of three (3) minor victims and the arrest of the Subject. Rescued victims were turned over to CSWD while Subject was presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor, General Santos city for violation of RA 10364 (Expanded Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2012) and violation of RA 7610 (Special Protection of. Children Against Child Abuse, Exploitation and Discrimination Act), RA 9775 (Anti-Child Pornography Act of 2009), and RA 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012). On November 12, 2018 , operatives of NBI-Special Action Unit (NBI-SAU) arrested MELANIE NICOLE MERCADO NAMUAG for alleged Swindling/Estafa and Usurpation of Authority. The case stemmed against two (2) complaints against the Subject. According to the complaint of Mr. Hilarion Pimentel y Collado, the Subject represented herself as connected with Malacanang and offered him services to manipulate the counting machines in the upcoming 2019 elections to ensure the win of his relative, La Paz, Tarlac, a mayoralty candidate, for a fee of Php 5 Million as downpayment. With this, an entrapment operation was conducted. During the operation, Subject was wearing a jacket bearing a big seal of the Office of the President of the Philippines. Subject stated that her group is connected with Smartmatic as she is of Mercado family who owns the warehouse in Laguna where PCOS machines are kept. She likewise alleged that her group has IT experts that can manipulate the PCOS machines. In a peaceful and orderly manner, the Subject was apprehended. Immediately after the arrest, several personalities appeared before the NBI-SAU reporting other alleged fraud committed by the Subject. With respect to the complaints, complainant has yet to submit a demand letter which is needed in filling of charges against the Subject. On November 12, 2018 , operatives of NBI-Iligan District Office (NBI-ILDO) arrested MICHAEL HEPIGA y CALUNOD for selling illegal drugs. Subject was arrested in a buy-bust operation which stemmed from the information that a certain CHRISTOPHER ZALSOS was engaged in the proliferation of illegal drugs in the areas of Iligan City. A buy-bust operation was then conducted resulting in the arrest of Subjects MICHAEL HEPIGA y CALUNOD and CHRISTOPHER ZALSOS. Recovered from the Subjects’ possession were transparent plastic sachets containing white crystalline substance believed to be shabu. Subject MICHAEL HEPIGA y CALUNOD was brought to Iligan City Police Station 4 for documentation while Subject CHRISTOPHER ZALSOS was brought to Don Gregorio Lluch Memorial Hospital. Case for violation of RA 9165 (Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002) were prepared for filing and disposition. On November 13, 2018 , operatives of NBI-Anti-Organized and Transnational Crime Division (NBI-AOTCD) arrested DANILO M. CANDABA, a notorious swindler. The case stemmed from the complaint against the Subject who sold house and lot property to the complainants in the agreed amount of Php 2.3 Million. Complainants asked the Subject if he is the owner of the property but Subject showed them instead a Special Power of Attorney (SPA) giving him authority to sell the said property. The complainants paid the initial payment of Php 1.5 Million and started to make repairs on the property. However, they were surprised when somebody informed them that a certain Rowell Capal is the real owner of the property. Complainants talked to Mr. Capal who denied giving the Subject a SPA to sell his house and lot. He further told the complainants that the original title of the property is in his possession. With this, complainants sought the NBI’s assistance since Subject is demanding Php 45,000.00 as additional payment. An entrapment operation was conducted and resulted in the arrest of Subject Candaba. Record check on the Subject revealed that he has several cases of Estafa, Falsification of Public Documents, violation of RA 6425 (The Dangerous Drugs Act of 1972), and Perjury. Subject was brought to the Office of the City Prosecutor, Las Piñas City for inquest proceedings for Estafa. On November 13, 2018 , operatives of NBI-Iligan District Office (NBI-ILDO) arrested two (2) alleged Philippine Army assigned at 304 th Battalion namely PFC GILBERT PASICOLAN y GALAPON and CPL ANDY PASTORAL y LORZANO and a civilian Subject ELEAZAR TORMON y LUCEINARA. Subjects were arrested in a joint operation of NBI-ILDO, Iligan City Police Station 4 (ICPS 4), SWAT team, and CIDG Iligan, which stemmed from the information that Subject ELEAZAR TORMON y LUCEINARA and certain JOSE FRANCISCO L. RAMOS III, both Balik-Islam or Muslim Convert and allegedly a member of the local terrorist Maute-ISIS Group were sighted in Iligan City. After knowing that Subjects’ vehicle were heading South 1 Central School, a checkpoint was established thereat. After checking the identities and necessary permits to substantiate thelegality to possess and carry the firearms, Subjects carried questionable Acknowledgment Receipt of Equipment (ARE). Confiscated from the Subjects were various firearms, ammunitions, and fictitious identification cards. Subjects were now under the custody of ICPS 4 for filing of appropriate charges. Case for violation of RA 10591 (Comprehensive Firearms and Ammunition Regulation Act) and RA 9561 (Law on Explosives). On November 14, 2018 , operatives of NBI-National Capital Region (NBI-NCR), NBI-Bulacan District Office (NBI-BULDO), NBI-Laguna District Office (NBI-LAGDO), arrested sixty two (62) Subjects for illegal gambling. The operation stemmed from the letter of Philippine Charity Sweepstakes Office (PCSO) signed by Manuel N. Fraginal Sr., Chief of Nationwide Inter-Branch Security Monitoring, and Marcelo G Flores. Vice President of Great Platinum Gaming Online, Inc., requesting for law enforcement assistance against Globaltech’s illegal number game of Peryahan ng Bayan operating in different areas in Quezon City. Acting on the information, Search Warrants were secured and implemented on the above-mentioned date. Simultaneous operations were conducted in West Point Cubao, Brgy. Sangandaan, Brgy. Baesa, Brgy. San Bartolome, all located in Quezon City. The operation resulted in the arrest of sixty two (62) Subjects. Arrested Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the Prosecutor General, Department of Justice, Manila for Illegal Gambling in violation of RA 9287 (Illegal Gambling Law). On November 14, 2018 , operatives of NBI-National Capital Region (NBI-NCR) arrested RAJA MAHARI ISMAEL and FRANCIS BUENAFE JR. for selling illegal drugs. Subjects were arrested in a buy-bust operation which stemmed from a report that a certain “William Sy”, a Chinese national, and his driver alias “Muslim”, Filipino national who were allegedly engaged in the sale, trading, administration, dispensation, delivery, distribution and transportation of dangerous drugs in the cities of Paranaque and Pasay. With this, an entrapment operation was conducted resulting in the arrest of Subjects RAJA MAHARI ISMAEL and FRANCIS BUENAFE JR. Found in their possession were six (6) packs of plastic sachet containing white crystalline substance positive for the presence of Norephedrine HCI, a dangerous drug. Subjects were brought for inquest proceedings before the Office of the Prosecutor of Paranaque City for violation of RA 9165 (Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002 ). On November 14, 2018 , ASHELY ALVERO, ANTHONY ERWINSON E. DESLATE, and SEUN CHARLES OGUN, a Nigerian-born US citizen, were arrested in entrapment operation for Estafa, Computer-related Forgery and Identity Theft. The case stemmed from the complaint of spouses Victor and Rosita Lao for the alleged computer-related fraud. Their counterpart’s (AIYU) email [email protected] was hacked which resulted to the diversion of funds to a certain Metrobank account owned by Subject Engr. Ashely Alvero who has an outstanding Warrant of Arrest. The latter was eventually taken into custody. According to the Affidavit executed by Subject ALVERO, the other two (2) Subjects were identified. Subject DESLATE voluntarily confessed his involvement to the transaction and other related incidents. He also pointed out certain Tony and Charles. While Subject Deslate was under the custody of the NBI, Tony called Deslate as the former was expecting to receive money. With this, an entrapment operation was conducted. The operation resulted in the arrest of Subject SEUN CHARLES OGUN. Tony did not appear during the operation. Charges for Estafa and violation of RA 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act) were filed against the arrested Subjects. On November 14, 2018 , operatives of NBI-National Capital Region (NBI-NCR) seized counterfeit Underarmour products with an estimated amount of Php 35,650,000.00. Items were seized in Binondo and Tondo, Manila by virtue of Search Warrants. Charges for violation of RA 8293 (Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines) were filed against JOHN/JANE DOEs, operators, owners, managers of various establishments located at Sunjoy Building Tower 2, Muelle De Binondo, Tondo, Manila and at 168 and 999 Shopping Malls, Binondo, Manila. On November 16, 2018 , operatives of NBI- International Airport Investigation Unit (NBI-IAIU) arrested ARLYN MONDEJAN GRIPO for human trafficking and illegal recruitment. Illegally recruited three (3) individuals to work in Dubai as domestic helpers. Subject facilitated and secured the travel documents of the three (3) who are bound to Dubai on a tourist visa on November 16, 2018. They were instructed by the Subject that they will be fetched by the Subjects’ sister Crizelda Gripo Abdulwahab upon reaching their destination and once thereat they would be deployed by a recruitment agency in Sharja, UAE to their respective employers. One of the victims, who learned from her friend of the inhuman treatment done to her by her employer, changed her mind, backed out from her flight, and filed a complaint before the Airport Police at Ninoy Aquino International Airport (NAIA), Terminal 2. Verification with POEA revealed that Subject Gripo is not licensed/authorized to recruit workers for overseas employment, thereof, placing her under arrest for Human Trafficking and Illegal Recruitment. Subject was presented before the City Prosecutor of Pasay on inquest proceeding City for violation of R.A. No. 9208 as amended by R.A. No. 10364 (Human Trafficking) and R.A. 10022 (Large Scale Illegal Recruitment). On November 16, 2018 , operatives of NBI-Anti-Organized and Transnational Crime Division (NBI-AOTCD) arrested EDUARDO DAVID y ORDONEZ for Robbery/Extortion. According to the complainant, Subject went to her clinic for consultation due to difficulty in walking. Subject underwent laboratory tests and chest x-ray and was diagnosed having a pneumonia. Complainant then prescribed an injectable and amino-acids. He was advised to continue his amino-acids for complete recovery. However, Subject went to the complainant’s clinic and alleged that his life was put into danger due to complainant’s advice. He then threatened complainant that he will damage her reputation to her patients and her radio program unless complainant will pay him Php 1 Million. He further demanded that payment should be made through check for his convenience. Accordingly, an entrapment operation was conducted resulting in the arrest of the Subject. He was presented for inquest proceeding before the Department of Justice and was recommended to be charged for Robbery. On November 16, 2018 , operatives of the NBI- Anti-Graft Division (NBI-AGD) arrested JASON NAPOLES RABE a.k.a “ARNEL JAY OCAMPO”/ “JERON JAY AREBES” for Estafa. The operation stemmed from a complaint of Dominador Bruno, a Filipino based in Italy together with complainants Mercedes Cancinco , Ginmarie Asuncion, and Divine De Guzman Gatbunton. According to Bruno, Subject Rabe introduced himself as Jeron Jay Arebes thru social media “Facebook Messenger” and after continuous conversation, Dominador was induced by Subject Rabe to invest in a grocery business, market stall, and a house and lot in Isabel, Leyte. Subject said that the market stall, grocery and a house and lot were owned by certain Mercedes Cancino. Victim Dominador was able to send money under the name of Mercedes Cancino with an estimated amount of Php 4,000,000.00 thru various remittances as payment for the market stall, grocery business and house and lot in Isabel, Leyte. Months after, Subject Rabe told Dominador that Mercedes died and additional money is needed for the transfer of title of the market stall and house and lot. Out of trust, Dominador continued to send money to Jason Rabe thru the name Ginmarie Asuncion. Suspicious with the identity of Subject Rabe, Divine De Guzman Gatbunton friend of the victim contacted Cancino and Asuncion thru FB Messenger and discovered about the false claims of made by Subject Rabe and that Cancino and Asuncion were used to claim the remittances of Victim Dominador. Furthermore, Subject Rabe demanded Php100,000.00 from Dominador for his investments. With this, an entrapment operation was conducted resulting in the arrest of the Subject. Charges for violation of Article 315 (Estafa) of the Revised Penal Code and R.A. 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act) were filed against the Subject before the Office of the City Prosecutor of Manila. On November 19, 2018 , operatives of NBI-Anti-Fraud Division (NBI-AFD) arrested CRISTINA SERA FLORES and EDGAR ENERIO LAGURA for Estafa and Falsification of Public Documents. The case stemmed from the complaint of Mary Jane Joson who posted on Facebook group chat account “Sanla Tira Taguig Makati Pasig” that was looking for sanla-tira, condo or house. A certain Rubylene Torres referred her to Subject CRISTINA SERA FLORES. Subject introduced herself as the owner of Unit 3114 in Tower 2 Light Residences, Madison St., Mandaluyong City and agreed to enter into a Sanla-Kolekta agreement with the complainant. Pursuant to their agreement, complainant issued a check for Php 150,000.00 to Subject Flores as downpayment for the mortgaged unit and the remaining balance to be paid on a later date. Subject in return surrendered to the complainant the Condominium Title Certificate bearing her name as the unit owner. However, verification made with the Registry of Deeds of Mandaluyong confirmed that the Condominium Title Certificates are spurious. Despite this, Subject Flores kept insisting for the payment of the remaining balance. With this, an entrapment operation was conducted resulting in the arrest of Subject Flores and Subject Lagura who acted as a lookout. Subjects were brought before the Manila Prosecutor’s Office for inquest proceedings for Estafa and Falsification and Use of Public Documents. On November 22, 2018 , operatives of the NBI-Cybercrime Division (NBI-CCD) arrested PAN JIANBEI, PAN TAIYUAN, JIE LU, SHENGBO ZHANG and JIAN LOU ZHOU, Chinese nationals, who were engaged in illegal online gambling operations. After verification made by the agent on case through extensive surveillance, his findings were later approved and was able to secure Search Warrants against the occupants/tenants of Units P2A, P4B and 2602 of Alpha Grandview Condominium. NBI-CCD operatives, assisted by the NBI-Digital Forensic Lab (DFL) operatives proceeded to target area where the five Subjects were arrested. Seized from the units were mobile wifi, router, passport copies, one-time passport devices, assorted smartphones, laptops, and desktops computers. Data extracted from computers showed the mechanics of gambling activities, browsing and log-in to the financial and web-payment facilities as well as browsing of betting websites. Onsite forensic procedures conducted by NBI-Digital Forensic Laboratory (DFL) revealed the browsing history which captured screenshots of online gambling activities that include online payment facilities, online banking transactions and betting lottery game. Subjects likewise failed to produce necessary license and permits required in operating an online gambling business. Subjects were presented before the City Prosecutor of Manila on inquest proceeding for violation of P.D. 1602, otherwise known as “Anti-Illegal Gambling Act” in relation to R.A 10175 otherwise known as the Cybercrime Prevention Act. On November 22, 2018 , operatives of NBI-Special Task Force (NBI-STF) arrested PO2 GLENN MAGALSO y OCCUPIADO, FELIZ ALERIA y PINKIAN, and MARK ALERIA y AMORA in Tagum City for illegally selling high explosives. Subjects were arrested in an entrapment operation conducted based on the information that explosives are being sold to private citizens and are being used by unlicensed miners at Mt. Diwalwal, Compostela, Valley. It was also reported that these explosives are reaching the hands of some cessionist and insurgent groups such as the National People’s Army (NPA) and the Abu Sayyaff Group (ASG). Verification and surveillance operations were conducted confirming the aforesaid information. Fifteen (15) sets of explosives at Php 18,000.00 per set or a total of Php 270,000.00 were ordered from the illegal distributor who was identified as Subject FELIZ ALERIA y PINKIAN. The entrapment operation was conducted resulting in the arrest of Subjects FELIZ ALERIA y PINKIAN, and MARK ALERIA y AMORA. Recovered and seized were fifteen (15) sealed bags, each containing twenty five (25) kilograms or a total of 375 kilograms of ammonium nitrate mixed with fuel oil, and one (1) sealed box containing 1,000 meters safety fuse, one (1) roll safety fuse measuring approximately 86 meters, and fifteen (15) boxes each containing 100 pieces of non-electric blasting caps or a total of 1,500 pieces of blasting caps. As calculated by the EOD expert of the NBI-STF, the seized items can produce a destructive effect of decimating one whole barangay if activated and armed. After the arrest, Subject FELIZ ALERIA was constantly receiving calls from “Ser Glen” who was later identified as Subject PO2 GLENN MAGALSO y OCCUPIADO. Subject PO2 MAGALSO was furiously asking for the money or the proceeds of the sale of the explosives. Subject FELIZ ALERIA, together with NBI-STF operatives went to the meeting place to meet Subject PO2 MAGALSO and deliver the money. Subject PO2 MAGALSO tried to escape when he noticed some persons inside the operatives’ van but the other vehicle of the NBI was able to block his path resulting to his immediate arrest. Subjects PO2 GLENN MAGALSO y OCCUPIADO, FELIZ ALERIA y PINKIAN, and MARK ALERIA y AMORA were presented for inquest before the City Prosecutor of Tagum City for violation of RA 9516 (Law on Explosives). On November 27, 2018 operatives of NBI-Dumaguete District Office (NBI-DUMDO) arrested SPO1 ROBERTO ABADIANO JR. y DELA CRUZ for Extortion and Graft. The case stemmed from the complaint of Mr. Rene Ledesma against the Subject who demanded Php50,000 from the complainant, the purpose of which is for the Subject not to show up as a witness in the court hearing so he could not testify against Mr. Ledesma who is facing a criminal charge for Comelec gun ban. According to Mr. Ledesma, SPO1 ABADIANO told him that he if could not come up with the money, SPO1 ABADIANO threatened to castrate Mr. Ledesma’s life. Worried on the plight of his life with the impending threats, Mr. Ledesma sought the assistance of the NBI. After evaluation of the instant case, an entrapment operation was conducted which resulted in the arrest of SPO1 ABADIANO who was caught in flagrante while in the act of counting the money that Mr. Ledesma gave. Subject was presented for inquest proceeding before the City Prosecutor Office, Dumaguete City for Extortion and violation of RA 3019 (Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices). On November 27, 2018 , operatives of NBI-Anti-Fraud Division (NBI-AFD) arrested EVELYN ZAMORA by virtue of Warrant of Arrest. Prior to the arrest, a case for Estafa was filed against the Subject. Verifications made revealed that Subject has numerous criminal cases pending with different courts in Quezon City. After securing the Certified True Copy of the Arrest Warrant, operatives proceeded to Almar Subdivision, Camarin Rd, Caloocan City. When the Subject was spotted in her office, operatives affected the Warrant of Arrest. Subjects were asking additional money for the alleged processing/facilitation of fees. Per verification, Subjects are not licensed/authorized by POEA to recruit workers for overseas employment. Subjects were arrested in entrapment operation conducted at Aristocrat Restaurant, Malate, Manila. They were presented for inquest proceedings before the City Prosecutors Office of Manila for Estafa and Large Scale Illegal Recruitment. Subjects are presently detained at the NBI Jail.
