Based on the report acquired validated by casing and surveillance operations conducted, a probable cause to believe that the Subject was indeed involved in child sexual molestation. Pictures of the Subject doing lascivious acts to the children were being sent to a certain person through Facebook. On the basis of Search Warrant, NBI operatives, in coordination with the PNP General Santos City, implemented the Search Warrant which resulted in the rescue of three (3) minor victims and the arrest of the Subject. Rescued victims were turned over to CSWD while Subject was presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor, General Santos city for violation of RA 10364 (Expanded Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2012) and violation of RA 7610 (Special Protection of. Children Against Child Abuse, Exploitation and Discrimination Act), RA 9775 (Anti-Child Pornography Act of 2009), and RA 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012). The case stemmed against two (2) complaints against the Subject. According to the complaint of Mr. Hilarion Pimentel y Collado, the Subject represented herself as connected with Malacanang and offered him services to manipulate the counting machines in the upcoming 2019 elections to ensure the win of his relative, La Paz, Tarlac, a mayoralty candidate, for a fee of Php 5 Million as downpayment. Subject stated that her group is connected with Smartmatic as she is of Mercado family who owns the warehouse in Laguna where PCOS machines are kept. She likewise alleged that her group has IT experts that can manipulate the PCOS machines. In a peaceful and orderly manner, the Subject was apprehended. body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today announced the arrest of a subject by operatives of NBI-Sarangani District Office (NBI-SARDO) for blackmailing victim to have sex with him. NBI Officer-In-Charge (OIC) Director Eric B. Distor identified the subject as ROSMAN HADJI IBRAHIM. Subject was arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from the complaint filed by the victim against subject Ibrahim for alleged blackmailing, which was later on determined to constitute violation of RA 9262 otherwise known as Anti-Violence Against Women and Children Act of 2004 in relation to RA 10175 or the Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012. According to the victim- complainant, she and Subject Ibrahin had an illicit affair since 2017 up to 2020. She broke up with the Subject last December 2020 but the latter kept on texting her. Subject Ibrahim even threatened victim-complainant that he will keep sending her nude photos if she will not go out with him for the last time to have sex. On April 23, 2021, she informed the NBI-SARDO that she will meet with subject Ibrahim, to end her agony of fear from subject’s threats by talking it out but she feared of being compelled to engage in sexual activity. Thus, she sought assistance from the NBI. Promptly acting on the complaint, operatives of NBI-SARDO hatched an operation. In the afternoon of the same day, operatives proceeded to the meeting place of Subject and victim- complainant in a lodge located at Brgy. Lagao, General Santos City. At a pre-arranged signal, operatives swooped down on the room of the lodge and found thereat was Subject Ibrahim who was half-naked, wearing only his undergarment, beside the still dressed victim- complainant in bed. Subject was arrested and apprised of his rights. Subject was brought to NBI-SARDO office where he was booked, fingerprinted, and photographed. Subject Ibrahim was presented for inquest proceeding before the Prosecutor’s Office of General Santos City.

body: PRESS STATEMENT May 27, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } The National Bureau of Investigation Organized and Transnational Crimes Division (OTCD), under the leadership of Director JUDGE JAIME B. SANTIAGO (Ret.), arrested a certain MA DULCE CEREZO y ESTACIO for violation of Article 172 (Falsification by Private Individuals) in relation to Article 171(1) and Article 171(2), Article 176 (Possession of Instruments or Implements for Falsification), Article 177 (Usurpation of Authority or Official Functions), and Article 315 par. 2(a) (Estafa by means of Deceit) of the Revised Penal Code. The case stemmed from a complaint lodged before the OTCD. In his Affidavit, the Complainant averred that he discovered that Subject CEREZO was notarizing documents using a fake notarial stamp that bore his notarial details, and a rubber stamp that imitated his signature, without his knowledge, authority, or consent. Surveillance was conducted to verify this information, and thus, confirmed the Subject’s illegal notarial practice. On 20 May 2025, OTCD agents devised an entrapment operation resulting in the arrest of MA DULCE CEREZO y ESTACIO and the seizure of various instruments or implements for falsification from her possession at the scene, including rubber stamps bearing the notarial details of the Complainant and rubber stamps bearing his signature, among others. Subject CEREZO was brought to the OTCD office for standard booking and arrest procedures and placed under temporary custody and detention. On 21 May 2025, Subject CEREZO was presented for Inquest Proceeding before the Office of the City Prosecutor of Pasig. Thereafter, she was turned over to the NBI Detention Facility for custody and detention.

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today announced the arrest of three (3) individuals in Brgy. Tigbe, Norzagaray, Bulacan for operating a recycling plant of aluminum wastes without permit from the government. NBI Officer-In-Charge (OIC) Director Eric B. Distor identified the subject as ANALIZA OMBLERO y PACTOL de VENDER, LABERTO DELA CRUZ y PACTOL and ARIEL HELVERO y DELA CRUZ. OIC Director Distor said that the operation stemmed from an intelligence report regarding the alleged existence of Aluminum Chips Recycling Plant. The report stated that said recycling plant is engaged in the recycling of aluminum wastes without the necessary environmental compliance certificate from the Environment Management Bureau (EMB) and has no valid permit to operate from the Provincial Environment and Natural Resources Office (PENRO) and from Bulacan Environment and Natural Resources Office (BENRO). It further stated that the plant used hazardous chemical Sodium Silicoflouride, a toxic chemical compound used for fluoridation, insecticide and rodenticide, which is hazardous to the health of the people living near the area. The recycling plant also has no proper sewerage system for the proper disposal of their toxic waste product. Acting swiftly on the information received, operatives of NBI-BULDO conducted surveillance and sting operation in the target recycling plant. The operatives were able to confirm the existence of the recycling plant which violated certain environmental laws. Thus on June 16, NBI-BULDO together with representatives of BENRO proceeded to the target recycling plant to conduct the operation. The operatives swooped down the area and arrested Subjects Dela Cruz and Helvero together with two minors working in the makeshift recycling plant. While, conducting the operation, the owner of the recycling plant identified as Subject Omblero arrived and was also apprehended. The operation resulted in the seizure of 100 pieces of ingot (aluminum clocks); several drums used for oils; sacks of toxic chemicals known as Sodium Silicoflouride; undetermined number of Berota (Aluminum waste) sacks; makeshift cauldron used as burner incinerator; tons of DROSS (non-liquefied aluminum waste) and a long wing-van truck. The subjects were presented before the Provincial Prosecutor’s Office of Bulacan for violation of R.A. 9231, R.A. 6969, R.A. 1586, R.A. 8749 and R.A. 9003. Meanwhile, the two minors who were also working at the plant were turned over to the custody of the Provincial Social Welfare and Development of Bulacan in Malolos City.

body: In an attempt to smuggle illegal drugs into the country by swallowing improvised capsules, a member of the West African drug Syndicate was caught Friday evening in close coordination with the Bureau of Immigration, the Airport Task Force on Drug Couriers and the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI). NBI Director Nonnatus Caesar R. Rojas identified the suspect as AKILOU BASSI, 30, a citizen of the Republic of Benin. Investigation conducted by the NBI-Reaction and Interdiction Division (RAID) headed by Head Agent Ross Jonathan Galicia revealed that Akilou swallowed 60 improvised capsule containing shabu, which are about the size of a thumb. He agreed to travel from Togo, Benin in consideration for USD4,000 for a successful delivery of the contraband to a local contact. However, vigilant immigration officers at the airport who conducted a thorough interview felt suspicious about Akilou’s purpose of entering the country. Upon agreement with the Task Force on Drug Couriers, the subject was later turned over to the NBI for investigation. Akilou, who complained of stomach problems on Friday afternoon, was brought to a hospital for medical examination. X-ray reports revealed the presence of several capsule-like objects in Akilou’s stomach. In the presence of NBI agents and investigators, Akilou has so far defecated 34 capsules which were later certified by NBI Forensic chemist to be positive for Methamphetamine Hydrochloride (shabu) with a net weight of 448 grams. Akilou was placed under arrest on June 7, 2013 and was provided legal assistance by a representative of the Public Attorney’s Office. He was brought to the City Prosecutor of Manila on June 9, 2013 where he was charged for violation of Sec. 5 (Transportation of Dangerous Drugs) and Sec. 11 (Possession of Dangerous Drugs) Art. II of RA 9165 (The Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002). Seized by the NBI-CCD team from the suspects were the P500,000.00 cash used in trying to bribe the operatives, counterfeit automated teller machine (ATM) cards and counterfeit credit cards, electronic gadgets used in illegal duplication of credit cards and ATM cards, and documents. This is the first case encountered by the authorities wherein the courier swallowed improvised capsules of shabu and the offender is caught at a stage wherein the capsules are still concealed in his body. In previous incidents, the drugs were placed inside luggages. Apparently to avoid drug sniffing dogs, a courier thought of this smuggling method by swallowing drugs. Meanwhile, Akilou is currently being monitored as more capsules are expected to be expelled in the following hours or days. Investigation is likewise being undertaken in order to establish the identities of Akilou’s local contacts and to file appropriate charges.

title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today announced the arrest of an employee of the Philippine Sports Commission (PSC) for falsifying the payroll register of the athletes and coaches and credited their allowances into his own bank account. NBI Officer-In-Charge Eric B. Distor identified the subject PSC employee as PAUL MICHAEL PADUA IGNACIO. OIC Distor said that the case stemmed from a letter sent by PSC seeking assistance for the investigation of suspected fraud committed by a PSC employee. The letter likewise stated that Land Bank of the Philippines (LBP) sent a letter to OIC Merlita R. Ibay of the PSC regarding with the unusual payroll transactions credited to the account of Subject Ignacio. OIC Distor added that initial investigation conducted by OIC Ibay revealed that Subject Ignacio is an employee under the PSC-Personnel Office, who is tasked to prepare the payroll for the monthly allowance of qualified coaches and athletes and forward the same to the LBP. Subject Ignacio then includes the names of unqualified coaches and athletes in the payroll and puts his own payroll account number as the account number of the unqualified coaches and athletes. Based on initial verification Subject Ignacio has already embezzled Php 14,448,254.35 from August of 2015 up to May of 2020. On July 14, 2020, operatives of NBI-Special Action Unit (NBI-SAU) proceeded to PSC Office to conduct an initial investigation. It was discovered that for the month of June 2020, Subject Ignacio included in the payroll three (3) unqualified coaches and three (3) unqualified athletes with a total amount of Php 450,150.00 to be credited into the subject’s payroll account. On the same day, with sufficient evidence on hand, NBI-SAU arrested Subject Ignacio in his office at the PSC in Manila. The NBI also seized the laptop and desktop unit of the Subject issued by the PSC for for forensic examination. Subject Ignacio will be presented for inquest proceedings for violation of Article 310 in relation to Article 309 (Qualified Theft) through violation of Article 172 in relation to Article 171 (Falsification of Public Documents), all under the RPC, and for violation of R.A. 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012).

body: PRESS STATEMENT May 19, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } In line with the directive from the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Director JUDGE JAIME B. SANTIAGO (Ret.) to curb the rampant online sexual exploitation of children in the country, the NBI-Human Trafficking Division (NBI-HTRAD) arrested an individual in Mabalacat, Pampanga. body: PRESS STATEMENT October 30, 2024 The National Bureau of Investigation-Cybercrime Division (NB-CCD), together with the NBI-Special Task Force (NBI-STF), under the leadership of NBI Director Judge Jaime B. Santiago (Ret.), arrested a total of eighteen (18) Chinese nationals who conspired in scamming operations. Director Santiago said that CCD received an information that at least four condominium units in Casiana Residences in Parañaque City were being utilized as a scam hub by a syndicate of foreign nationals. Surveillance operations conducted revealed that these units contained multiple workstations engaged in various fraudulent activities, including the theft of bank account information, fraudulent investment schemes, cryptocurrency scams, and illegal gambling operations. On October 29, 2024, in coordination with the local police, CCD operatives, together with the NBI-STF, proceeded to the target area to serve the Warrant to Search, Seize, and Examine Computer Data (WSSECD) issued by RTC Branch 258, Parañaque City. Santiago said that operatives found a total of seventeen (17) Chinese nationals in the three units where the WSSECD was served. The said nationals were discovered to be actively engaged with their desktop computers, wherein various scripts and communication flows indicative of a sophisticated scam and other fraudulent operations, were found. Further, onsite examinations on their devices uncovered a scheme that employed social engineering tactics to exploit victims. Subjects initiated contact via platforms such as WhatsApp or Telegram, posing as representatives of legitimate businesses or acquaintances. By establishing rapport and appealing to the victims’ emotions, they lured them into making investments in cryptocurrency through deceptive “mining’ or “farming” schemes. Additionally, the Subjects also utilized manipulated gambling sites designed to ensure users consistently lost, further enriching the syndicate. The Chinese nationals namely: ZHAO JIANJUN, HUANG CHENG CHI, HUANG BI YING, LI HUI JUAN, LENGXIN YU, LIU XING RONG, CHEN ZIHAO, ZHOU YOU LIANG, CHEN XING, CHEN QING GANG, HUANG ZHIXON, RIU CHEN, MAO JING HANG, LIU XUAN WU, WANG WEN BIN, YAN XIAO HONG, and YANG YUN were then placed under arrest for violations of Illegal Access, Misuse of Devices, Computer-Related Forgery, and Computer-Related Fraud under RA 10175, otherwise known as the Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012, as well as Social Engineering Schemes and Economic Sabotage under RA 12010, otherwise known as the Anti-Financial Account Scamming Act. While transporting the arrested Subjects to NBI Office in Quezon City, one of the arrested Subjects tried to bribe the operatives by offering Php 300,000 for each detainee’s release, or a total of Php 5,100,000.00 for all the seventeen Chinese nationals. Operatives played along to maintain control of the situation, and to hatch an entrapment operation. On even date, another Chinese national arrived and handed a backpack with an amount of Php 1,500,000.00 which is intended as a payment for the release of the first batch of the arrested Subjects. After confirming that the bag contained the bribe money, CCD operatives arrested the Chinese individual identified as HOU JUSEN, whose fake Postal ID contains the name JASON PONTE HAO. He was then charged with Corruption of Public Officials, Falsification of Public Document, and violation of the Anti-Alias Law. Director Santiago commended the CCD and STF operatives for the successful operation. He stressed that the NBI always upholds its integrity, keeping the organization’s core values and ethical standards.

body: PRESS STATEMENT May 26, 2022 PRESIDENT DUTERTE CONFERS ORDER OF LAPU-LAPU AWARD TO NBI DIRECTOR DISTOR, 8 OTHER NBI OFFICIALS President RODRIGO ROA DUTERTE has conferred the Order of Lapu-Lapu Award to NBI Director ERIC B. DISTOR and eight (8) other officials. The Order of Lapu-Lapu (Kamagi) was conferred by the President in ceremonies in Malacañan Palace on May 23, 2022 to the NBI officials led by Director DISTOR in recognition for the seizure of about 1.6 tons (shabu) worth Php 11 Billion, which turned out to be the largest drug haul in the history of law enforcement in the Philippines. Among the NBI officials who were also conferred the Order of Lapu-Lapu are ARD Roel S. Bolivar, Assistant Director for Intelligence Service: HA Ross Jonathan V. Galicia, Task Force Commander of NBI-Task Force Against Illegal Drugs (TFAID): SA Levi-Omar M. Orille, Agent-on-case, TFAID: SI IV Gary Ibabao Meñez, Agent-on-case, TFAID: SRA Oliver Baisa, Chief of Research and Analysis Division (RAD): and Ms. Angelica F. Wycoco, Mr. Miguel Fernando Suarez and Mr. Maynard Ramones, Chemists-on-case. Under Executive Order No. 35, the award of Order of Lapu-Lapu with the rank of Kamagi, shall be given to officials and personnel of the government, in recognition for their invaluable service in relation to campaign advocacy of the President. Last March 15, 2022, NBI-TFAID with the assistance of NBI-RAD hatched an illegal drug operation in Infanta, Quezon resulting in the seizure of the illegal drugs. Also, the joint operatives were able to arrest 10 individuals in the course of the operation. Thus, on May 23, 2022, at the Malacañan Palace, the Order of Lapu-Lapu medals were personally pinned by President Duterte assisted by Senator Bong Go to Director DISTOR and 8 other NBI Officials. One of the prestigious awards conferred to a public servant, this is the first time in the 85 year-history of the NBI that the Order of Lapu-Lapu has been conferred to the NBI Director, Officials and Operatives of the Bureau and could pave the way for others who are deserving of such honors for meritorious and exceptional accomplishments. DISTOR emphasized that the award sets a new dimension and the bar higher for others to emulate and greatly inspire the next generation of NBI Officials and personnel in pursuit of excellence.

body: PRESS STATEMENT February 14, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } In line with the continuing battle against child sexual exploitation, the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) under the leadership of NBI Director Judge Jaime B. Santiago (Ret.), arrested a foreign national and a Filipino for child pornography. On August 27, 2024, the NBI-Violence Against Women and Children Division (VAWCD) received a case referral from the U.S. Department of Homeland Security, Homeland Security Investigations, Manila Attaché Office (HSI Manila), concerning US citizen JOSEPH JOHN GRAHAM, who was believed to be in Pampanga and is suspected to be abusing minor victims for sexual exploitation. HSI and NBI’s investigation led to the discovery of multiple photos and videos depicting child sexual abuse or exploitation materials (CSAEM) from the phone of GRAHAM. Further, HSI FLORIDA likewise received Cyber Tip Report from the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children (NCMEC) that images and videos of naked children were found on a phone belonging to US citizen JOSEPH GRAHAM who travels to the Philippines for the purpose of child sex tourism. On September 30, 2024, an Arrest Warrant was issued by the 19th Judicial Circuit Indian River, Indian River County, State of Florida, against JOSEPH JOHN GRAHAM for 55 Counts of Possession of CSAEM. In view of the Arrest Warrant issued against GRAHAM, coordination was made with the Bureau of Immigration Fugitive Search Unit (BI-FSU) to hold GRAHAM in case he passes through our immigration before departure from the Philippines and to process his arrest pursuant to the Arrest Warrant issued by the United States. On October 16, 2024, the NBI-VAWCD received an information that GRAHAM was bound to depart the Philippines from Clark International Airport. Thus, in coordination US-HSI, PNP-AVSEU, BCIU-CIA and NBI-Pampanga District Office (PAMDO), enforcement operations was conducted at Clark International Airport which resulted to the arrest of JOSEPH JOHN GRAHAM. Consequently, GRAHAM was inquested by the Bureau of Immigration for violation of immigration laws and is currently awaiting deportation for being declared as an undesirable alien. Following the arrest of GRAHAM, further investigation was conducted to identify the female adult and the three minor children appearing in the pornographic materials together with GRAHAM. Investigation revealed that a Filipina Subject was sending the CSAEMs to GRAHAM. Using an undercover account, NBI Agents communicated with her, wherein she confirmed that she knows GRAHAM and the children in the photos she was sending to him are her own kids. In the course of their continuous communication, Subject offered her minor children for sexually explicit live shows. On February 11, 2025, NBI Agents, together with the representatives from the Homeland Security Investigations, Manila, proceeded to Bamban, Tarlac to implement the Warrant to Search, Seize and Examine Computer Data (WSSECD) issued by Branch 66, Regional Trial Court of Capas, Tarlac. The Agents introduced themselves and announced their purpose. The cellular phone used by the Subject was immediately seized, and Subject was placed under arrest for offering and selling sexually explicit live online shows of minor children. The operation likewise resulted in the rescue of three (3) minors. On February 12, 2025, Subject was presented for inquest proceedings before the Department of Justice for violations of R.A. 11930 or the Anti-Online Sexual Abuse or Exploitation of Children (OSAEC); Anti-Child Sexual Abuse and Exploitation Materials (CSAEM) Act; R.A. 9208 otherwise known as Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2003 as amended by R.A. 10364 or Expanded Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2012; R.A. 11862 or the Expanded Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2022; and R.A. 7610 or the Special Protection of Children Against Abuse, Exploitation and Discrimination Act.

body: PRESS STATEMENT July 02, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI), proudly announces its successful ISO 9001:2015 recertification, an internationally recognized standard for Quality Management Systems (QMS). This achievement underscores the Bureau’s continuing commitment to excellence, professionalism, and accountability in the delivery of its services to the Filipino people. The recertification process, conducted by SOCOTECH CERTIFICATION PHILIPPINES INC., an independent third-party certifying body, involved a rigorous and comprehensive audit of the NBI’s systems, procedures, and operations. Auditors assessed the Bureau’s ability to consistently provide services that meet client and regulatory requirements, its dedication to continuous improvement, and the effective implementation of its QMS across all operational units. Through the leadership of Judge JAIME B. SANTIAGO (Ret.) and the full cooperation of its officers and personnel, the Bureau demonstrated strong adherence to the principles of quality management, particularly in enhancing customer satisfaction, process efficiency, risk management, and organizational performance. This recertification also affirms that the NBI’s services ranging from investigative operations to administrative support adhere to globally accepted standards. The ISO 9001:2015 recertification is not merely a ceremonial milestone, but a strategic imperative aligned with the Bureau’s vision of being a highly competent, effective, and trustworthy law enforcement agency. It reflects a culture of integrity and performance-driven governance that is essential in addressing the ever-evolving challenges of criminality, corruption, cybercrime, and other threats to national security and public order. The NBI’s sustained compliance with ISO standards also reinforces the government’s thrust toward professionalizing public service institutions and fostering a culture of accountability, transparency, and citizen-centered service. The NBI extends its appreciation to all internal auditors, process owners, personnel, and officials who contributed to this achievement and looks forward to strengthening its quality initiatives in the years to come. As it marks this renewed certification, the Bureau remains resolute in pursuing its mandate under the law, upholding human rights, and delivering investigative excellence with the highest standards of ethics and integrity.

body: PRESS STATEMENT February 28, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } In line with the government’s efforts to eradicate all forms of criminality, the National Bureau of Investigation – Special Task Force (NBI-STF), under the direct supervision of NBI Director Judge Jaime B. Santiago (Ret.), has arrested twenty (20) foreign nationals for violating Section 4(b)(1) (Social Engineering Schemes) of R.A. No. 12010 (Anti-Financial Account Scamming Act) in relation to R.A. No. 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012). Among those arrested was LIU ZHI TAO, also known as “Ren Jia,” who faces additional charges for violation of Article 267 (Serious Illegal Detention) of the Revised Penal Code (RPC). The operation stemmed from a complaint made by the wife of a Chinese kidnapped victim. She alleged that her husband, who worked as a Customer Service Representative (CSR) for a POGO company operating under the trade name “LWE,” was being held against his will by his employers. The Complainant revealed that the said POGO company is located at Aseana 3, West Tower, 8912 Avenue, Paranaque City. On February 25, 2025, the agents of NBI-STF raided the office of the said POGO company, leading to the rescue of the kidnapped victim and the arrest of his captor, Subject Liu Zhi Tao. During the operation, the agents of NBI-STF also uncovered a fully operational scam hub, revealing that the foreign nationals working inside were engaged in online scamming activities. Consequently, the NBI agents apprehended these individuals for violating the AFASA Law. The arrested Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor – Paranaque City. Director Santiago commended the agents of NBI-STF for the arrest of the foreign nationals and rescue of the Chinese victim.

body: PRESS STATEMENT January 11, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } NBI Always Ready to Respond to Calls for Assistance From Government Agencies and the Citizenry Following Ombudsman Request to Investigate Fake News of Death The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) stands ready to serve and respond to requests for assistance from all government agencies. In particular, the circulation of false information on social media regarding the alleged death of Ombudsman Remulla constitutes the dissemination of fake news through information and communications technology. Such an act is a violation of Republic Act No. 10175, otherwise known as the Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012, which is within the jurisdiction of the Bureau to investigate. In fact, the Bureau has long been assisting ordinary citizens with their complaints regarding misinformation, disinformation, and such other online libelous publications against them. While the Bureau is flooded with cases of such nature, we always do our best to resolve them in the soonest possible time. We have not stopped there. We are already aggressively moving not only against misinformation and disinformation, but also against products (food, medicine) and services that are illegal and unregulated (not FDA-approved) being advertised and offered for sale on online platforms. We are doing this in coordination with the Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT), Department of Trade and Industry (DTI), and Department of Health (DOH). This is in line with the initiative of Sen. Raffy Tulfo in his privilege speech concerning unregulated drugs in the market. The NBI acknowledges the significance of what the good Senator has started with public health and safety. Likewise, it is consistent with the NBI’s broad mandate to investigate any offense when public interest requires it, and more importantly, under the Cybercrime Law for online sale of counterfeit or unregulated drugs and health-related scams. —- Atty. Angelito DLP Magno Director, National Bureau of Investigation #NBIServes

body: PRESS STATEMENT November 26, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } The National Bureau of Investigation – Pampanga District Office (NBI-PAMDO), with the 301st Counterintelligence Squadron, 301st Special Mission Group, and the 300th Air Intelligence Security Wing – Philippine Air Force (PAF), in coordination with the Clark Development Corporation – Public Safety Division (CDC-PSD), arrested VITALYS AWA NJINWA a.k.a. JOHNSON BROWN and PENSIGA DERICK SAMA a.k.a. STEPHANE ANDRE OBAME, both Cameroonian nationals, in an entrapment operation on November 20, 2025, for Robbery (Extortion) and Swindling (Estafa). NBI-PAMDO received a complaint from a Korean national, who reported that the Subjects had defrauded him of 731,750 USDT (cryptocurrency), equivalent to approximately Php42,441,500.00, in connection with a purported Gold Transport Operation from Nairobi, Kenya, to Incheon, South Korea. The amount represented alleged fees for customs processing, cargo insurance, warehouse charges, and other fabricated expenses. The subjects provided fraudulent documents, including falsified landing permits and air waybills, videos and photographs of the supposed gold bars, in order to convince the complainant that the gold had been shipped and was being held by the Bureau of Customs – Port of Clark in Pampanga. Over time, additional payments were demanded and complainant was threatened that the gold would not be shipped unless he paid an additional 1,000,000 USDT (more or less Php58,000,000.00), purportedly as a bribe for the Chief of the Bureau of Customs in Clark. Realizing that he had been defrauded, the complainant sought assistance from NBI-PAMDO, prompting them to launch an entrapment operation. During the arranged meetup at a café inside a hotel in Clark, the Subjects attempted to collect the demanded 1,000,000 USDT, consisting of 25,000 USD in cash and the remaining balance stored in a cryptocurrency cold-storage ledger. The subjects were immediately arrested. Accordingly, the Bureau of Customs – Port of Clark certified that the Airway Bill presented by the subjects as purported proof of the gold shipment was not registered in the Bureau of Customs’ Electronic-to-Mobile (E2M) System and had no record of arrival at the Port of Clark International Airport. Subjects were presented for Inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor of Mabalacat, Pampanga, for the above-cited violations. The NBI encourages those who believe they may be a victim of extortion or swindling to gather evidence and information and report it to authorities immediately. Be vigilant of too-good-to-be-true offers and pressure to act quickly from the offering party. Don’t fall victim to scams and be aware of scams and their evolving nature.

body: To serve the people faster and more conveniently, the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) has introduced the E-clearance (electronic clearance) system, in which one can now apply for an NBI clearance through the internet. The new system is a 24/7 (twenty-four hours-seven days a week) service that significantly reduces the long lines of NBI clearance applicants in the main office clearance center and satellite offices in certain Metro Manila city halls, and Robinson’s Mall branches. Effective next week, the E-clearance lane will open in certain malls and local government units in Metro Manila. Said lane is for the purpose of the live scan fingerprinting and photograph of applicants which is an essential part of the clearance application. Eventually, the installation of the E-clearance lane for fingerprinting will be completed in all malls and satellite offices nationwide. The NBI has issued specific procedures/steps on how to avail of the E-clearance. How to get NBI Clearance Online Step 1: PAYMENT – Go to Globe Payment Center or your own Globe Gcash account in your cellphone (globe money transfer) and pay for the clearance fee – You will get a payment Reference No. or you will receive it via text message Step 2: ONLINE REGISTRATION – Fill up the application form online provide the reference number, email address, date of payment and the purpose of NBI clearance. – After a successful online application the QR code (an image code) provided should be printed as a proof of the application. – Schedule an appointment by sending a booking request via text message. STEP 3: IMAGE CAPTURE AND FINGERPRINT SCANNING – Go to the e-clearance lane of the NBI Clearance Center on the confirmed booking date. – Present your QR code and a valid ID. – Your image will be captured and fingerprint will be scanned. – Your Clearance Certificate will be printed if you have no namesake. For more informations: Call HELPDESK 5261294, 5238231 local 5499 Or Text”Help” 0917638052

body: Two employees of a beauty products firm who stole and sold said merchandise were arrested by agents of the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) in an entrapment in Makati City this week. The suspects were identified as: ROMAR GEROLEO, driver, and CIPRIANO LAYCO, warehouseman of Beauty Lane Philippines. Investigation report by the Technical Intelligence Division (TID) disclosed that Beauty Lane Philippines, the exclusive distributor of Brazilian Blowout in the Philippines, through its representative said that the company is incurring losses in the amount of P2 million as of January 2013. She alleged that they suspect that the loss of these products were caused by some Beauty Lane employees. Accordingly, during the delivery of the products, some of them pilfered the delivered goods and later sold them at a much lower price. On February 11, 2013, an employee of Beauty Lane said that while hitching a ride in one of their delivery panel, she noticed some undelivered products. She inquired from driver Geroleo on the excess of undelivered products. He alleged that he would temporarily keep it for safekeeping in their house as it might cause some problems when returned to the warehouse. Sometime in February 2013, a client of Beauty Lane revealed that an unidentified person, later identified as Geroleo, was selling Brazillian Blowout products to them at discounted price. This prompted the client to inform Beauty Lane management about this development. To stop this illegal activity, the management arranged with said client to act in their behalf and continued negotiating for the purchase of their products at much lower price. On February 18, 2013, the client and Geroleo met at a mall in Makati for the purchase of the products at a much lower cost. Top management sought NBI assistance and an entrapment was planned. In the afternoon of the same day, NBI agents accompanied the clients and certain top management personnel for the entrapment of Geroleo. At 3:00 P.M. suspect came with Layco on board a motorcycle. When Geroleo and the client met, the latter gave the marked money representing the cost of the agreed cost of the merchandise purchased. However, Geroleo sensed the unusual presence of the Bureau agents and attempted to escape in their motorcycle. Immediately alert NBI agents prevented their escape. Found and seized were the beauty products and the marked money in the possession of Geroleo. The duo were brought to the NBI for detention. Charges of Qualified Theft and violation of PD 1612 also known as Anti-Fencing Law were filed against the suspects before the Makati City Prosecutor’s Office.

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today announced the arrest of four (4) individuals in 2 separate entrapment operations by Agents of the NBI-Special Task Force (NBI-STF) in Quezon City. NBI Officer-In-Charge (OIC) Director Eric B. Distor identified the subjects as MARIA CHRISTINA MANAIG, CHRISTOPHER BOYDON, PHILIP BALES, and BERNARD TOMMY BUNYI. OIC Director Distor said that the simultaneous operations stemmed from information received by the NBI-STF about thr rampant online selling of Remdesiver, an investigational drug used for treatment of COVID-19 patients in the country. The Food and Drug Administration (FDA) in its announcement informed the public that the used of the anti-viral drug requires a Compassionate Special Permit (CSP). Accordingly a CSP is not tantamount to a Certificate of Product Registration issued by the FDA. The FDA added that CSP is only granted to licensed doctors and hospitals who shall take full responsibility for the use and dispensing of Remdesivir. A CSP holder must fully inform the patient of the benefits and risk of the product, and provide a report to the FDA of the outcomes for every patient who they administered the drug. The FDA also stressed out that a drug product which was issued a CSP, is not an assurance of the product quality, safety and efficacy. Thus, no product with CSP can be marketed commercially. NBI-STF was able to established communication with the individuals selling Rendisivir online and ordered from two sellers a vial each of the drug for the price of Php 4,500.00 and Php 5,000.00 respectively. Thus, on 15 June 2021, NBI-STF hatched two (2) simultaneous entrapment operations against the two sellers which resulted in the arrest of subjects Manaig, Boydon, and Bale in West avenue Quezon City by the first team of Agents of STF while the 2nd team wa able to arrest Subject Bunyi in Timog Quezon City. The arrested subjects were persented for Inquest proceedings before the City Prosecutor of Quezon City for violations of R.A. 9711, otherwise known as the “Food Administration Act of 2009” and R.A. 5921, otherwise known as the “Philippine Pharmacy Act”.

body: Two Muslim members of a syndicate selling illegal firearms were arrested during a buy-bust operation by agents of the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) in Quezon City the other day. The suspects were identified by NBI Officer-In-Charge Atty. Nonnatus Caesar R. Rojas as: MINSUARI LANGCAP OROGAN, 34, security guard, and a resident of Lot 5, Block 25, Don Mariano St., North Fairview, Quezon City; and SALIC MACADATO LANGCO, 39, security guard, and a resident of Block 38, Lot 12, Bayer St., North Fairview, Quezon City. Investigation report of the Counter Intelligence Division (CID ) headed by Atty. Dave Segunial disclosed that the Bureau received reliable information that a certain group who called themselves as the “Guardian” are selling loose firearms used by criminals. They allegedly come from a certain “SUPREMO” in Cebu and are shipped to Manila through the ports. The handguns, .45 caliber pistols, and sub machine guns (SMGs) are sold by the syndicate at P15,000 and P29,000 a piece with the suspects earning commissions at P1,500 and P3,500, respectively. NBI undercover operatives were able to trace the source in Bgy. Samasapi, North Fairview, Quezon City and bought from suspects a .45 caliber pistol on March 2, 2012 and a 9 mm sub-machine gun on March 15, 2012, with magazines and ammunitions. After the initial purchases, NBI operatives conducted a buy-bust operation near their residence on March 27, 2012 resulting to the arrest of the suspects, Orogan and Langco. It is also believed that they were among those responsible for the proliferation of loose firearms in the streets which are being used by the “riding in tandem” robbery/hold-up gang. Recovered from them were three (3) .45 caliber pistols and a 9mm sub-machine gun (SMG) with magazines and ammunitions. Suspects were referred for inquest before Asst. City Prosecutor Diovie M. Macaraig-Calderon, of the Quezon City Prosecutor’s Office who recommended the filing of a case for violation of PD 1866, as amended by RA 8294.

body: PRESS STATEMENT May 03, 2024 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } The Department of Justice (DOJ) scored another victory following the conviction of Deniece Millinette Cornejo, Cedric Cua Lee, Ferdinand Guerrero, and Simeon Palma Raz, Jr. for the crime of serious illegal detention for ransom filed by movie actor and TV host Ferdinand “Vhong” Navarro. Justice Secretary Jesus Crispin “Boying” C. Remulla lauded Antipolo City Prosecutor Mari Elvira B. Herrera, Senior Deputy State Prosecutor Hazel C. Decena-Valdez and Deputy State Prosecutor Olivia L. Torrevillas for successfully prosecuting the case. In a 94-page Judgment dated 02 May 2024, Presiding Judge Mariam G. Bien of the Taguig City Regional Trial Court-Branch 153, found Cornejo et al guilty beyond reasonable doubt for the crime of serious illegal detention for ransom and sentenced them the penalty of Reclusion Perpetua. The Court did not believe the accused’s defense that they performed a citizen’s arrest on Vhong Navarro after the latter supposedly attempted to rape Cornejo in the condominium unit. “No less than the Supreme Court found no credence on Cornejo’s story of rape,” the Court noted. During the promulgation of the Decision, only accused Deniece Cornejo and Ferdinand Guerrero were present. The Court immediately canceled the bail posted for their provisional liberty and ordered them committed to jail. On the other hand, the Court issued warrants for the arrest of accused Cedric Lee and Simeon Palma Raz who were both not in court. It can be recalled that in 2014, the DOJ through this prosecution panel charged the accused for conspiring to detain Vhong Navarro in a condominium unit in Bonifavio Global City, Taguig City, and while being deprived of his liberty, the accused inflicted serious physical injuries and threatened to kill the victim and demanded money as a condition for his release. “This conviction is a testament of the hardwork and dedication of our prosecutors that the DOJ will always serve as a beacon of hope for victims of injustice, reaffirming our commitment to the people that justice will be enforced to or against anyone regardless of social status, fame, power or wealth,” Sec. Remulla

body: PRESS STATEMENT September 11, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } Under the leadership of NBI Director Judge JAIME B. SANTIAGO (Ret.), the NBI-Bataan District Office (NBI-BATADO) arrested an individual for alleged violation of R.A. 7610, also known as the “Special Protection of Children Against Abuse, Exploitation, and Discrimination Act”, and violation of R.A. 11930, also known as the “Anti-Online Sexual Abuse or Exploitation of Children Act (OSAEC) and Anti-Child Sexual Abuse or Exploitation Materials (CSAEM)”. The operation stemmed from the complaint of the victim’s mother. The victim is a 17 years old female with a mental age of 11 years and 3 months, indicative of Mild Intellectual Disability, according to the assessment and evaluation of the Bureau’s Behavioral Science Division. Subject AR-JAY LAGATA, a 19 years old construction worker from Lipa City, Batangas, was arrested at the workers’ barracks at a construction site in Balanga City, Bataan on August 27, 2025. Subject LAGATA had a sexual relationship with the victim for at least three (3) months since May 2025. The victim’s mother discovered the subject’s exploitation of her daughter through messages the suspect sent to the victim’s phone. Reading thru the messages, she also learned that the subject had been asking for videos of the victim performing sexual acts and had also threatened the victim that he would expose their sexual relationship to the victim’s mother and friends if she refused. This prompted the mother to report the matter to NBI-BATADO, whose agents were immediately dispatched, resulting to the arrest of Subject LAGATA. Subject was presented before the City Prosecutor’s Office of Balanga City with the recommendation that he be prosecuted for violation of R. A. No. 7610 and R. A. No. 11930.

SANTIAGO (Ret.), the NBI-Bataan District Office (NBI-BATADO) arrested an individual for alleged violation of R.A. 7610, also known as the “Special Protection of Children Against Abuse, Exploitation, and Discrimination Act”, and violation of R.A. 11930, also known as the “Anti-Online Sexual Abuse or Exploitation of Children Act (OSAEC) and Anti-Child Sexual Abuse or Exploitation Materials (CSAEM)”. The operation stemmed from the complaint of the victim’s mother. The victim is a 17 years old female with a mental age of 11 years and 3 months, indicative of Mild Intellectual Disability, according to the assessment and evaluation of the Bureau’s Behavioral Science Division. Subject AR-JAY LAGATA, a 19 years old construction worker from Lipa City, Batangas, was arrested at the workers’ barracks at a construction site in Balanga City, Bataan on August 27, 2025. Subject LAGATA had a sexual relationship with the victim for at least three (3) months since May 2025. The victim’s mother discovered the subject’s exploitation of her daughter through messages the suspect sent to the victim’s phone. Reading thru the messages, she also learned that the subject had been asking for videos of the victim performing sexual acts and had also threatened the victim that he would expose their sexual relationship to the victim’s mother and friends if she refused. This prompted the mother to report the matter to NBI-BATADO, whose agents were immediately dispatched, resulting to the arrest of Subject LAGATA. Subject was presented before the City Prosecutor’s Office of Balanga City with the recommendation that he be prosecuted for violation of R. A. No. 7610 and R. A. No. 11930.

body: PRESS STATEMENT December 10, 2024 In line with the order of National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Director JUDGE JAIME B. SANTIAGO (Ret.) to intensify law enforcement operations against financial scammers, the National Bureau of Investigation – Bataan District Office (NBI-BATADO) arrested one for defrauding a renowned forwarding company that has been a victim of these scamming activities since 2023. Director Santiago said that the forwarding company was contracted as a delivery service provider by a high-end electronics company to deliver its products ordered online through the Cash on Delivery (COD) scheme. By using fictitious names and false identities, the imposters would switch the high-value contents with low-value articles, return the parcels with fabricated complaints, and evade payment. The Modus Operandi of the syndicate is that during the delivery of the products, they would claim that they had insufficient cash on hand for the payment of the product. They would receive the parcel, bring the same inside the house and ask the delivery staff to wait outside while they ask somebody to go to the ATM to withdraw cash. Unbeknownst to the delivery staff, the parcel would then be opened by the subjects, its contents replaced and repacked. After a short while, the subject would return the package to the delivery staff seemingly unopened, claiming that the electronic company had called him and asked him to return the product because of defects. This scheme has resulted in significant losses for the forwarding company, amounting to millions of pesos. Investigation and intelligence operations conducted by NBI-BATADO Agents identified one of these fraudsters to be one ALDWIN CHRISTOPHER BACANI ACEBU. An entrapment operation was planned against said Subject who was eventually arrested on 03 December 2024 after ordering electronic products worth Php64,421.80 which was payable through Cash on Delivery from the complainant courier company. After receiving the parcels, Subject requested the delivery staff to withdraw money in the amount of fifty thousand pesos (Php50,000.00) from subject’s ATM claiming that he did not have enough cash on hand and that he couldn’t leave his child who is alone in the house. Though hesitant, the delivery staff was eventually persuaded by the subject to leave the parcels behind, with the understanding that Subject would not open the parcels until he returns with the money. NBI operatives stationed nearby observed the Subject hastily leaving the house a few minutes later carrying a duffle bag on one hand and a parcel on the other. Recognizing the Subject’s intent to evade payment and flee with the items, the operatives quickly intercepted and arrested the Subject before he could escape with the parcels. It was later on discovered that the ATM had insufficient balance (0.90 cents) to cover the Fifty Thousand pesos (Php50,000.00) withdrawal as instructed by the Subject, confirming that the Subject’s request for money was a mere ploy to take possession of the parcels without paying. This further validated the fraudulent nature of the Subject’s actions. The operatives also found that the Subject had already attempted to open one of the parcels, further corroborating his intent to alter the contents or flee with the items. The items recovered from the subject’s possession, which included high-end electronic products and accessories, were properly documented and secured for evidence. These items, along with the packaging tapes and other tools found in the Subject’s possession, further supported the claim of deceit or fraud. Subject was brought to the Office of the Provincial Prosecutor of Bataan for Inquest Proceedings for the crime of Estafa (Swindling), under Article 315 of the Revised Penal Code, and other related offenses. Subject’s fraudulent actions, including deceit, false pretenses, and the unlawful taking of goods delivered under the COD scheme, caused significant financial loss to the forwarding company. Director Santiago commended the Operatives of NBI-BATADO for the successful operation and encouraged the public to report to the NBI any similar fraudulent activities.

body: The Information Division is pleased to submit herewith the significant cases of the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) for the following aforementioned period as follows: On September 1, 2017 , operatives of NBI-Cordillera Administrative Region (NBI-CAR) arrested ENRICO LEGASPI y DELA CRUZ for Robbery-Extortion, violation of R.A. 10175 (Cyber Crime Prevention Act of 2012, and violation of R.A. 9262 (Anti-Violence Against Women and their Children 2004). Subject threatened the Complainant that he will post their photographs on social media when the Complainant was trying to split up with him. Complainant begged the Subject but when the former did not follow some of the latter’s instructions, he uploaded photographs showing them kissing. Subject then demanded money from the Complainant and she sent money to the Subject via mobile banking cash deposits. When Subject demanded Php100,000.00, an entrapment operation was planned resulting in the arrest of the Subject. On September 4, 2017 , operatives of Special Operations Group (NBI-SOG) arrested EUGENIO ILAGAN y YTE for selling fake NBI Clearance in Sta. Cruz, Manila. Information from a reliable source said that Subject was offering NBI Clearance to clients along C.M. Recto Avenue, Sta. Cruz, Manila. An entrapment was then set after validation and case build. The operation resulted in the arrest of Subject ILAGAN who asked for Six Hundred Pesos (Php600) in exchange for the fake NBI Clearance. Certification from the NBI-ICTD confirmed that NBI Clearance certificates from the Subject were not duly issued by the NBI. Charges for violation of Article 172 (Falsification by Private Individual and Use of Falsified Documents) of the Revised Penal Code were filed against the Subject. On September 5, 2017 , operatives of NBI-Intellectual Property Rights Division (NBI-IPRD) seized counterfeit Louis Vuitton products with an estimated value of Php 62,442,414.90 or US$ 1,222,055.00 . The fake products were seized at Greenhills Shopping Center, San Juan, Manila on the strength of Search Warrants issued by RTC Manila. The case stemmed from the complaint of Atty. Anthony Francis L. Manankil representing Louis Vuitton. Charges for violation of R.A. 8293 (Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines were filed against the owners/managers/operators/occupants of various stalls in the said shopping center. On September 12, 2017 , operatives of NBI-National Capital Region (NBI-NCR) arrested JEFFREY PAYAWAL for Estafa. The case stemmed from the complaint of Charles Allison S. Chua against the Subject who was demanding from him Php150,000.00 allegedly to be given to Congressman Lazatin of Angeles City. Relative thereto, Complainant has an ongoing government contract worth Php1,799,000.00 for the construction of classroom in Angeles City, Pampanga. Failure to give the said money to the Congressman would allegedly result in the cancellation of the contract. However, upon his verification, the said Congressman was not asking any amount of money. Thus, an entrapment operation was conducted resulting in the arrest of the Subject. He was brought for inquest proceedings before the Provincial Prosecutor’s Office, Malolos City, Bulacan for violation of Article 312 of the Revised Penal Code (Estafa). On September 13, 2017 , operatives of NBI-Central Visayas Regional Office (NBI-CEVRO) arrested ROSELYN RESPETO y ELMECINO, ANDREA ELMECINO y YUSON, JESSUEL LONGAKIT y AWIT, REGELITA ARISGADO y NARVASA, MARLO ALBARICO y ESTRERA, and ALICIA BINONDO y ORIAS in an entrapment operation for maintaining alleged illegal Lucky 3/Swertres games operated by Globaltech Inc., an entity whose authority to operate Lucky 3/Swertres games was terminated by PCSO. The operation stemmed from the complaint of PCSO 7 and Miguel C. Ortiz, representative of Saturn Gaming N’ Entertainment Corp. and First Golden Fortune Leisure Inc., the authorized Agent Corporations (AAC) of Mandaue City and Cebu province, respectively. Charges for violation of Illegal Gambling (P.D. 1602 in relation to R.A. 9287) were filed against the Subjects. On September 13, 2017 , operatives of NBI-Central Visayas Regional Office (NBI-CEVRO) arrested REYNALDO SAPIO JR. y LAZAR and JOEY VALIENTE y SAGAYNO for faking NBI Clearance and LTO license. An information was relayed concerning the falsification for a fee by certain Joseph who could fabricate NBI Clearance, LTO License and other government issued licenses using a stall where he plies his illegal activities. After validation of information, an entrapment operation was conducted resulting in the arrest of the Subjects. During the operation, the undercover poseur was able to arrange for an NBI Clearance and LTO License for a fee of Php2,600. Charges for Falsification of Public Documents were filed against the Subjects. On September 13, 2017 , operatives of NBI-Dumaguete District Office (NBI-DUMDO) arrested twelve (12) Subjects namely, ALPHA CHRISTIAN B. VILLANUEVA, JOSEPH T. NOMBRE, BERNARDO S. SARAGINA, ALBERT C. MARASIGAN, RAYLESTER C. LIZARDO, EDWARD M. MIJARES, NINO A. PINIDO, ERICKSON M. RAYMUNDO, JONATHAN D. ADAJAR, RAMON D. RODRIGUEZ, JOHN CLYDE M. ANGELES and CHRISTOPHER S. FERNANDEZ for violation of R.A. 8484 (Access Device Regulation Act) in relation to R.A. 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act). Subjects came to the City to employ their scheme by using fake credit cards to purchase several high valued articles. However, BDO was able to track their irregularity since it was their terminals that were mostly used by the establishments in the City. Subsequently, many stores were immediately alerted although several purchases have already passed in several stores. Other purchase transactions, on the other hand, failed at about time of the notice alert. Charges for above-mentioned violation were filed against the Subjects. On September 15, 2017 , operatives of NBI-International Operations Division (NBI-IOD) arrested MARKIS SCOTT TURNER a.k.a. FILIP NOVAK , an Australian national who is facing criminal cases for drug trafficking in Australia. Subject TURNER had been hiding in the Philippines for a couple of years to evade prosecution. The Australian Government sought the Provisional Arrest of Subject TURNER thru the Secretary of the Department of Justice (DOJ), pursuant to Article 9 of the Treaty of Extradition between Australia and the Republic of the Philippines (PH-AU Extradition Treaty). Between the period January 2009 and May 2011, Subject TURNER with cooperation of Colombian nationals imported about 71.6 kilograms of cocaine for the purpose of selling in Australia. Thru his company, CQE Materials and Handling, the drugs were hidden inside the drums of hydraulic oil and concealing the same by suspending the drugs at the midpoint of the oil inside the machinery. To avoid prosecution, Subject TURNER left Australia in August 2015 and stayed in the Philippines and lived in Island Garden City of Samal, Davao City using the name, FILIP NOVAK, where he was arrested by operatives of the NBI-International Operations Division. On September 18, 2017 , operatives of NBI-Central Visayas Regional Office (NBI-CEVRO) arrested LORNA OPORTO y NGOJO , MICHELL SOLON y TAGALOG , RICHELLE BALAGAN y FLOR , GERALDINE CARBONILLA y GULAY , JINKY ESTOCONING y ESTORCO , APRIL JOY HERRERA y EBARLE and RICHELL BALAGAN y FLOR for violation of Illegal Gambling Law. Subjects were arrested in an entrapment operation where they served as maintainers/collectors who accepted bets from the operatives. The operation stemmed from the complaint of PCSO 7 and Miguel C. Ortiz representing Saturn Gaming N’ Entertainment Corp. and First Golden Fortune Leisure Inc., the Authorized Agent Corporations (AAC) of Mandaue City and Cebu province respectively. Charges for violations of P.D. 1602 (Simplifying and Providing Stiffer Penalties for Violations of Gambling Laws) in relation to R.A. 9287 (An Act Increasing the Penalties for Illegal Numbers Games, Amending Certain provisions of P.D. 1602 and for Other Purposes) were filed against the arrested Subjects. On September 19, 2017 , operatives of NBI-Cagayan Valley Regional Office rescued eleven (11) child workers from Eggcellent Farm Corporation located at Brgy. Paredes, Diffun, Quirino, where they were exposed in hazardous working condition and paid below minimum wage. The case stemmed from an intelligence report that Eggcellent poultry farm is employing minors as workers wherein they are working in unhealthy environment. Acting on the said information, joint operatives of NBI-CAVRO, NBI-ISDO, and NBI-BAYDO, together with labor inspectors of DOLE-Region 2 and representatives from DSWD-Region 2, entered the premises of Eggcellent farm using visitorial power of DOLE to conduct inspection and investigate any fact or condition which may be necessary to determine violations. During the operation, eleven (11) child workers were rescued and now under the protective custody of DSWD. Child labor and human trafficking charges will be filed against the incorporators of the farm. On September 20, 2017 , operatives of NBI-Cagayan Valley Regional Office (NBI-CAVRO), together with the PDEA II, NBI-Bayombong District Office and NBI-Isabela District Office, discovered and destructed two (2) marijuana plantation sites with a street value of Ten Million (Php 10 Million) in Brgy. Luccong, Tinglayan, Kalinga. During the operation, no apprehensions were made since there were no occupants nor tillers found in the area. Nevertheless, charges for violation of RA 9165 (Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002) will be filed against those who are responsible for the cultivation of the marijuana plantation. On September 22, 2017 , operatives of NBI-National Capital Region (NBI-NCR) arrested JEFFREY ANDREOUS CADORNA CLAROS in Makati City by virtue of Warrant of Arrest for Estafa and Qualified Theft. The case stemmed from the letter request of Roxas Delos Reyes Laurel Rosario Leagogo Law Office c/o Atty. Benjamin B. Fernando Jr to serve the Warrant of Arrest issued against the Subject who is a former accountant of their law firm, for the aforementioned crimes. Subject is temporarily detained at the NBI Jail awaiting Court Order committing him to the Bureau of Jail Management and Penology, Makati City. On September 22, 2017 , Subject CARLITO AMOROSO y BAGALACSA , who has an Order of Arrest for Murder issued by RTC Branch 55 of Manila, surrendered to the NBI-Anti-Fraud Division (NBI-AFD). Subject Amoroso is one of the ten (10) accused in the death of Navy Ensign Philip Pestaño on September 27, 1995. Pestaño, a 1993 graduate of Philippine Military Academy was found dead aboard BRP Bacolod City. All of the accused were charged for Murder and Warrant of Arrest was issued against them. Upon his surrender, Subject was booked, fingerprinted, photographed, and was turned over to the NBI Jail. On September 22, 2017 , operatives of NBI-Bacolod District Office (NBI-BACDO) arrested SPO1 JOSHUA BARILE y TUPAS for violation of PD 1866 as amended by R.A. 8294 and 9516 (Codifying the Laws on Illegal/Unlawful Possession, Manufacture, Dealing in, Acquisition or Disposition of Firearms, Ammunition or Explosives or Instruments Used in the Manufacture of Firearm, Ammunition or Explosives, and Imposing Stiffer Penalties for Certain Violations Thereof, and for Relevant Purposes), violation of R.A. 9165 (Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002) and R.A. 10591 (Comprehensive Firearms and Ammunition Regulation Act). On September 22, 2017 , operatives of NBI-Task Force Against Illegal Drugs (NBI-TFAID) arrested EDILBERTO SALAS ASIS, IVAN CHESTER MESA LOZADA, and JOSE DARAING PALEVINO for violation of R.A. 9165 (Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002). NBI-TFAID received information that a certain “Eding” later identified as Edilberto Salas Asis, together with Ivan Lozada y Mesa, Aaron Lozada and their cohorts are using Unit 536 of Tenement Building, Brgy. 902, Zone 100, Punta, Sta. Ana, Manila as a drug den. Series and surveillance and test-buy operations were conducted and on the aforementioned date, Search Warrant issued by RTC Branch 89, Quezon City was implemented. The operation resulted in the arrest of the above-mentioned Subjects who were caught in flagrante having a pot session. Found and seized in the premises were methamphetamine hydrochloride or shabu, other drug paraphernalia, two (2) pieces live ammunition and one (1) folding knife. Based on tactical interrogation, Subject Edilberto Salas Asis was previously imprisoned for Murder while Subject Jose Daraing Palevino was freed from jail after serving his sentence for Homicide. On the other hand, Subject Ivan Chester Mesa Lozada was freed from jail after serving his sentence for Theft. The arrested Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the Prosecutor, Manila. On September 24, 2017 , operatives of NBI-Pagadian District Office arrested AYNA KAMILAH ALI de MINDAMOAO y BOTERIE and MERLINDA JUMANDOS GOLANDRINA for Falsification of Official Documents. While conducting inspection to different testing centers of Professional Regulation Commission (PRC), Licensure Examination for Teachers, operatives received information of an impersonation in Pagadian City Pilot School. While thereat, they were able to apprehend the impersonator, Subject Furthermore, Subject GOLANDRINA , the person who applied for the PRC Licensure Exam for Teachers, was also apprehended based on the information provided by the PRC Over-all Coordinator. Both were brought to the NBI-PAGDO office for proper booking procedures. On September 26, 2017 , operatives of NBI-Anti-Organized and Transnational Crime Division (NBI-AOTCD) arrested ALLAN LUCBAN y BALANDAY in Imus, Cavite by virtue of an alias Warrant of Arrest issued by RTC Branch 42, Manila Violation of P.D. 1866 as amended by R.A. 8294 (Illegal Possession of Firearms and Ammunitions) with bail recommended at Php 80,000.00. Subject LUCBAN was the subject of a letter complaint of Canyon Ranch Homeowners Association Inc. (CRHAI), Carmona, Cavite, headed by its President Benjamin E. Branson, American national, for being unruly and creating a very hostile environment in the community. Subject is presently detained at the NBI detention center. On September 26, 2017 , operatives of NBI-South Eastern Mindanao Regional Office (NBI-SEMRO) arrested spouses REZIL ESTOY and JOELAN ESTOY for violation of R.A. 9484 (The Philippine Dental Act of 2007). The case stemmed from the complaint of Dr. Carlos T. Capitan II, DMD, MPD of Davao City Dental Chapter. Surveillance operations were conducted leading to the entrapment operation which resulted in the arrest of the Subjects. Charges for the aforementioned violation were filed against the Subjects. On September 27, 2017 , operatives of NBI-International Operations Division (NBI-IOD) arrested YU, YONGSEOK , a Korean national who is wanted for prosecution for Special Robbery as he and his cohorts committed robbery with abduction against three (3) Korean victims in Cebu City, Philippines last 2013. Warrant of Arrest against the Subject has been issued by the Seoul Central District Court of the Republic of Korea. The NBI received a letter request from PSupt. Oh Ikjoon, Police Liaison Officer of the Korean National Police Agency, requesting for investigation, arrest and deportation of Subject YU, YONGSEOK. An Interpol Red Notice was then issued against the Subject. After securing an authorization to apply for Provisional Arrest Warrant pursuant to the provisions of the Treaty on Extradition between the Republic of Korea and the Republic of the Philippines, in relation to P.D. 1069, an Ex-Parte Application for Provisional Arrest of Subject YU, YONGSEOK was filed. Thus, RTC Branch 45. Manila issued a Provisional Arrest prelude to a Formal Request for Extradition. On the above-mentioned date, joint operatives of NBI-IOD and NBI-IPRD proceeded to Lucksea Global Corp. located at the Penthouse of Shaw Center Mall, Shaw Blvd., Mandaluyong City and served the Provisional Warrant of Arrest against YU, YONGSEOK. Subject was then brought to NBI where he underwent the proper booking procedures in the presence of his counsel, Atty. Jose Valentino G. Dave and interpreter, Kim Junghyun. On September 27, 2017 , operatives of NBI-Cagayan Valley Regional Office (NBI-CAVRO) arrested AURELIA PERALTA y VALLEJO, ELISEO DENIEGA, MARTIN PORFINIO JR, AND WILSON VALEROZO for human trafficking. Subjects were arrested in an entrapment operation wherein Subject PERALTA was caught en flagrante delicto sexually exploiting women while Subject DENIEGA was facilitating the trafficking of victims. Meanwhile, Subjects PORFINIO JR and VALEROZO were arrested after being caught en flagrante delicto having carnal knowledge with two (2) trafficked victims. The operation stemmed from an intelligence report regarding the alleged illegal activities at Angie’s Kambingan and Restaurant located in Ramon, Isabela. Said establishment is allegedly being used as a prostitution den. Validation of the intelligence report was conducted confirming the said report. Entrapment operation was then conducted resulting in the arrest of the Subjects and rescue of the victims. Charges for violation of R.A. 9208 (The Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2003) were prepared against the arrested Subjects. On September 28, 2017 , operatives of NBI-Anti-Human Trafficking Division (NBI-AHTRAD) rescued two (2) minors and a twenty-two year old woman who were victims of pornography in Batangas City. An information was provided by the Australian Federal Police (AFP) that a certain facebook user with an account username “Gyeong Aerum” believed to be Subject Angelica Camille Vilaruz y Custodio who is working in Malaysia was engaged in the distribution of child pornography materials. A surveillance operation was conducted confirming the information. Coordination with the Barangay Officials and the parents of the victims were made. Surrounding circumstances were explained to the parents and guardians of the victims. The victims were then peacefully turned over to the DSWD for custody. On September 28, 2017 , operatives of NBI-North Eastern Mindanao Regional Office (NBI-NEMRO) arrested CHARLIE QUINTANA y LANTICSE alias DARLING for violation of Article 168 of the Revised Penal Code (Illegal possession and use of false treasury or bank notes and other instruments of credit). The case stemmed from the letter of Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas thru Nestor H. Arenas, Bank Officer II of Currency Issue and Integrity Office and Currency Investigation Division of the BSP, requesting assistance for the planning of anti-counterfeit operation against certain individuals who are said to be violating Articles 166, 168 and 176 of the Revised Penal Code. Said individuals, accordingly, proliferate counterfeit Philippine, United States and other foreign currency bank notes in Cagayan de Oro City and nearby provinces, cities and municipalities. Entrapment operation was then conducted against the Subjects resulting in the arrest of Subject CHARLIE QUINTANA. Seized from his possession were several counterfeit bills. In three (3) separate operations, operatives of NBI-Laguna District Office (NBI-LAGDO) arrested a total of thirty (30) individuals engaged in illegal gambling operations. The operations stemmed from the request of Philippine Charity Sweepstakes Office (PCSO) Chairman to curb illegal gambling and based on the complaint of Happy Cool Games and Amusement Corporation, the Authorized Agent Corporation (AAC) that operates small town lottery in Southern District of National Capital Region that illegal number game still proliferates and remained unabated in Muntinlupa City. On September 20, 2017, ANNIE REYES y PANTIG and thirteen (13) others were arrested while engaged in jueteng operations in Taguig City. Seized from them were jueteng paraphernalia and bet money. On September 21, 2017 , EDUARDO ELVINA y SOLMIO and eight (8) others were arrested in Muntinlupa City while conducting jueteng operations and acting as bet collectors. Seized from them were several pieces of betting list and bet money. On September 27, 2017 , RONILO AYAPANA y PAREJA and five (5) others (all jueteng Kubrador) were arrested while conducting jueteng operations and acting as bet collectors in the areas of Cupang, Alabang and Putatan, Muntinlupa City. Seized from the Subjects’ possession are several pieces of betting list and bet money. Subjects in all the operations shall be charged for violations of P.D. 1602 (Simplifying and Providing Stiffer Penalties for Violations of Gambling Laws) as amended by R.A. 9287 (An Act Increasing the Penalties for Illegal Numbers Games, Amending Certain provisions of P.D. 1602 and for Other Purposes) before the City Prosecutor Office of Muntinlupa City. In five (5) successive operations, operatives of NBI-National Capital Region (NBI-NCR) seized counterfeit items with an aggregate amount of Php 93,628,000.00 . On September 4, 2017 , forty one (41) counterfeit window films bearing the 3M trademark with an estimated amount of Php600,000 were seized in Davao city by virtue of Search Warrant. On September 5, 2017 , counterfeit Lacoste shoes/footwears with an estimated amount of Php 19 Million were seized in Pasay and Paranaque City on the strength of Search Warrants issued by RTC Branch 46, Manila. On September 15, 2017 , counterfeit Marlboro and Fortune cigarettes with an estimated amount of Php 294,000 were seized in Tondo, Manila on the strength of Search Warrants issued by RTC Branch 24, Manila. On September 19, 2017 , counterfeit Apple Beats and Skullcandy products with an estimated amount of Php 51,934,000 were seized in Binondo, Manila by virtue of Search Warrants issued by RTC Branch 46, Manila. On September 22, 2017 , counterfeit Apple Beats and Skullcandy products with an estimated amount of Php 21,800,000 were seized in Quiapo, Manila by virtue of Search Warrants issued by RTC Branch 24, Manila. Charges for violation of R.A. 8293 (Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines) were filed against John/Jane Does, owners/managers/operators/occupants of various warehouses where the counterfeit products were seized.

On September 4, 2017 , operatives of Special Operations Group (NBI-SOG) arrested EUGENIO ILAGAN y YTE for selling fake NBI Clearance in Sta. Cruz, Manila. Information from a reliable source said that Subject was offering NBI Clearance to clients along C.M. Recto Avenue, Sta. Cruz, Manila. An entrapment was then set after validation and case build. The operation resulted in the arrest of Subject ILAGAN who asked for Six Hundred Pesos (Php600) in exchange for the fake NBI Clearance. Certification from the NBI-ICTD confirmed that NBI Clearance certificates from the Subject were not duly issued by the NBI. Charges for violation of Article 172 (Falsification by Private Individual and Use of Falsified Documents) of the Revised Penal Code were filed against the Subject. On September 5, 2017 , operatives of NBI-Intellectual Property Rights Division (NBI-IPRD) seized counterfeit Louis Vuitton products with an estimated value of Php 62,442,414.90 or US$ 1,222,055.00 . The fake products were seized at Greenhills Shopping Center, San Juan, Manila on the strength of Search Warrants issued by RTC Manila. The case stemmed from the complaint of Atty. Anthony Francis L. Manankil representing Louis Vuitton. Charges for violation of R.A. 8293 (Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines were filed against the owners/managers/operators/occupants of various stalls in the said shopping center. On September 12, 2017 , operatives of NBI-National Capital Region (NBI-NCR) arrested JEFFREY PAYAWAL for Estafa. The case stemmed from the complaint of Charles Allison S. Chua against the Subject who was demanding from him Php150,000.00 allegedly to be given to Congressman Lazatin of Angeles City. Relative thereto, Complainant has an ongoing government contract worth Php1,799,000.00 for the construction of classroom in Angeles City, Pampanga. Failure to give the said money to the Congressman would allegedly result in the cancellation of the contract. However, upon his verification, the said Congressman was not asking any amount of money. Thus, an entrapment operation was conducted resulting in the arrest of the Subject. He was brought for inquest proceedings before the Provincial Prosecutor’s Office, Malolos City, Bulacan for violation of Article 312 of the Revised Penal Code (Estafa). On September 13, 2017 , operatives of NBI-Central Visayas Regional Office (NBI-CEVRO) arrested ROSELYN RESPETO y ELMECINO, ANDREA ELMECINO y YUSON, JESSUEL LONGAKIT y AWIT, REGELITA ARISGADO y NARVASA, MARLO ALBARICO y ESTRERA, and ALICIA BINONDO y ORIAS in an entrapment operation for maintaining alleged illegal Lucky 3/Swertres games operated by Globaltech Inc., an entity whose authority to operate Lucky 3/Swertres games was terminated by PCSO. The operation stemmed from the complaint of PCSO 7 and Miguel C. Ortiz, representative of Saturn Gaming N’ Entertainment Corp. and First Golden Fortune Leisure Inc., the authorized Agent Corporations (AAC) of Mandaue City and Cebu province, respectively. Charges for violation of Illegal Gambling (P.D. 1602 in relation to R.A. 9287) were filed against the Subjects. On September 13, 2017 , operatives of NBI-Central Visayas Regional Office (NBI-CEVRO) arrested REYNALDO SAPIO JR. y LAZAR and JOEY VALIENTE y SAGAYNO for faking NBI Clearance and LTO license. An information was relayed concerning the falsification for a fee by certain Joseph who could fabricate NBI Clearance, LTO License and other government issued licenses using a stall where he plies his illegal activities. After validation of information, an entrapment operation was conducted resulting in the arrest of the Subjects. During the operation, the undercover poseur was able to arrange for an NBI Clearance and LTO License for a fee of Php2,600. Charges for Falsification of Public Documents were filed against the Subjects. On September 13, 2017 , operatives of NBI-Dumaguete District Office (NBI-DUMDO) arrested twelve (12) Subjects namely, ALPHA CHRISTIAN B. VILLANUEVA, JOSEPH T. NOMBRE, BERNARDO S. SARAGINA, ALBERT C. MARASIGAN, RAYLESTER C. LIZARDO, EDWARD M. MIJARES, NINO A. PINIDO, ERICKSON M. RAYMUNDO, JONATHAN D. ADAJAR, RAMON D. RODRIGUEZ, JOHN CLYDE M. ANGELES and CHRISTOPHER S. FERNANDEZ for violation of R.A. 8484 (Access Device Regulation Act) in relation to R.A. 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act). Subjects came to the City to employ their scheme by using fake credit cards to purchase several high valued articles. However, BDO was able to track their irregularity since it was their terminals that were mostly used by the establishments in the City. Subsequently, many stores were immediately alerted although several purchases have already passed in several stores. Other purchase transactions, on the other hand, failed at about time of the notice alert. Charges for above-mentioned violation were filed against the Subjects. Ortiz representing Saturn Gaming N’ Entertainment Corp. and First Golden Fortune Leisure Inc., the Authorized Agent Corporations (AAC) of Mandaue City and Cebu province respectively. Paredes, Diffun, Quirino, where they were exposed in hazardous working condition and paid below minimum wage. During the operation, eleven (11) child workers were rescued and now under the protective custody of DSWD. Child labor and human trafficking charges will be filed against the incorporators of the farm. On September 20, 2017 , operatives of NBI-Cagayan Valley Regional Office (NBI-CAVRO), together with the PDEA II, NBI-Bayombong District Office and NBI-Isabela District Office, discovered and destructed two (2) marijuana plantation sites with a street value of Ten Million (Php 10 Million) in Brgy. Luccong, Tinglayan, Kalinga. During the operation, no apprehensions were made since there were no occupants nor tillers found in the area. Nevertheless, charges for violation of RA 9165 (Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002) will be filed against those who are responsible for the cultivation of the marijuana plantation. Ana, Manila as a drug den. Series and surveillance and test-buy operations were conducted and on the aforementioned date, Search Warrant issued by RTC Branch 89, Quezon City was implemented.
