Found and seized in the premises were methamphetamine hydrochloride or shabu, other drug paraphernalia, two (2) pieces live ammunition and one (1) folding knife. Based on tactical interrogation, Subject Edilberto Salas Asis was previously imprisoned for Murder while Subject Jose Daraing Palevino was freed from jail after serving his sentence for Homicide. On the other hand, Subject Ivan Chester Mesa Lozada was freed from jail after serving his sentence for Theft. The arrested Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the Prosecutor, Manila. Branson, American national, for being unruly and creating a very hostile environment in the community. Subject is presently detained at the NBI detention center. On September 26, 2017 , operatives of NBI-South Eastern Mindanao Regional Office (NBI-SEMRO) arrested spouses REZIL ESTOY and JOELAN ESTOY for violation of R.A. 9484 (The Philippine Dental Act of 2007). The case stemmed from the complaint of Dr. Carlos T. Capitan II, DMD, MPD of Davao City Dental Chapter. Surveillance operations were conducted leading to the entrapment operation which resulted in the arrest of the Subjects. Charges for the aforementioned violation were filed against the Subjects. Oh Ikjoon, Police Liaison Officer of the Korean National Police Agency, requesting for investigation, arrest and deportation of Subject YU, YONGSEOK. Charges for violation of R.A. 9208 (The Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2003) were prepared against the arrested Subjects. Surrounding circumstances were explained to the parents and guardians of the victims. The victims were then peacefully turned over to the DSWD for custody. Arenas, Bank Officer II of Currency Issue and Integrity Office and Currency Investigation Division of the BSP, requesting assistance for the planning of anti-counterfeit operation against certain individuals who are said to be violating Articles 166, 168 and 176 of the Revised Penal Code. Said individuals, accordingly, proliferate counterfeit Philippine, United States and other foreign currency bank notes in Cagayan de Oro City and nearby provinces, cities and municipalities. Entrapment operation was then conducted against the Subjects resulting in the arrest of Subject CHARLIE QUINTANA. Seized from his possession were several counterfeit bills. The operations stemmed from the request of Philippine Charity Sweepstakes Office (PCSO) Chairman to curb illegal gambling and based on the complaint of Happy Cool Games and Amusement Corporation, the Authorized Agent Corporation (AAC) that operates small town lottery in Southern District of National Capital Region that illegal number game still proliferates and remained unabated in Muntinlupa City. On September 20, 2017, ANNIE REYES y PANTIG and thirteen (13) others were arrested while engaged in jueteng operations in Taguig City. Seized from them were jueteng paraphernalia and bet money. On September 21, 2017 , EDUARDO ELVINA y SOLMIO and eight (8) others were arrested in Muntinlupa City while conducting jueteng operations and acting as bet collectors. Seized from them were several pieces of betting list and bet money. On September 27, 2017 , RONILO AYAPANA y PAREJA and five (5) others (all jueteng Kubrador) were arrested while conducting jueteng operations and acting as bet collectors in the areas of Cupang, Alabang and Putatan, Muntinlupa City. Seized from the Subjects’ possession are several pieces of betting list and bet money. Subjects in all the operations shall be charged for violations of P.D. 1602 (Simplifying and Providing Stiffer Penalties for Violations of Gambling Laws) as amended by R.A. 9287 (An Act Increasing the Penalties for Illegal Numbers Games, Amending Certain provisions of P.D. 1602 and for Other Purposes) before the City Prosecutor Office of Muntinlupa City. On September 19, 2017 , counterfeit Apple Beats and Skullcandy products with an estimated amount of Php 51,934,000 were seized in Binondo, Manila by virtue of Search Warrants issued by RTC Branch 46, Manila. On September 22, 2017 , counterfeit Apple Beats and Skullcandy products with an estimated amount of Php 21,800,000 were seized in Quiapo, Manila by virtue of Search Warrants issued by RTC Branch 24, Manila. Charges for violation of R.A. 8293 (Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines) were filed against John/Jane Does, owners/managers/operators/occupants of various warehouses where the counterfeit products were seized.

body: One of the most wanted Chinese national in their homeland for economic crimes was apprehended by agents of the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) in a hotel in Manila yesterday. The suspect was identified by NBI Director Nonnatus Caesar R. Rojas as: WANG BOTAO , 47, Chinese, businessman, temporarily residing at 20 Robinson Tower, Adriatico, Manila. The case stemmed from a request on July 12, 2013 of the Police attaché, Embassy of the Peoples Republic of China to the NBI Director requesting assistance to locate and arrest subject Wang Botao. He has been involved in economic crimes amounting to RMB10,000,000,00 (PhP70,000,000.00) and being wanted by China’s police authorities. Accordingly, Wang’s passport has been cancelled/revoked by the Chinese government. The photograph and pre-paid cellular phone number of Wang were provided by the Fugitive Affair’s Division, Economic Crime Investigation Department of the Ministry of Public Security. Acting on said request, the NBI Foreign Liaison Division under Head Agent Daniel D. Daganzo verified with the Bureau of Immigration (BI) that revealed Wang was issued on Sept. 20, 2012 a working visa (9G) with the aforesaid address. Discreet investigation confirmed that Wang is a tenant of Adriatico Residence Tower I located at M. Adriatico St., Malate, Manila. It was gathered that he reportedly owns a stall at the 5th level of Robinsons Place Manila selling Chinese wares. Thus NBI agents made a stake-out yesterday night at the vicinity of Adriatico residence Tower I. At 8:30 pm Wang was seen coming out from the Robinson’s Department Store. As he was about to enter the Adriatico Residence Tower I, NBI agents hastily approached and stopped him. They introduced themselves and informed him that he is wanted by the authorities in his home country. Subsequently, he was placed under arrest. He was brought to the NBI main office for booking and detention. He will be eventually turned over to the Bureau of Immigration (BI) for their consideration and appropriate action.

San Rafael, Rodriguez, Rizal. NBI Officer-In-Charge (OIC) Director Eric B. body: PRESS STATEMENT September 10, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } Under the leadership of National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Director Judge Jaime B. Santiago (Ret.), the NBI-Cordillera Administrative Region (CAR) arrested Subject MARIO LUMAGUE y CAUBANG for Murder. He had been a fugitive for 41 years. The case stemmed from an Intelligence Report concerning Subject LUMAGUE, who had a Warrant of Arrest for Murder dated February 27, 1986, issued by then Presiding Judge, Regional Trial Court, Branch 5, Baguio City. Based on the report, Subject LUMAGUE was charged with MURDER before the Courts of Baguio City in 1983, but escaped from police custody before his scheduled court hearing on November 19, 1984. Consequently, a Warrant for his Arrest was issued by the Court. The report further alleged that Subject LUMAGUE had been sighted in Baguio City, driving a taxi cab. Verification revealed that during drinking sessions with his co-drivers, Subject LUMAGUE had been boasting that he killed somebody in Baguio City in 1980’s, and that, after being arrested, he was able to escape from the custody of his arresting officers and go into hiding. Upon verifying that Subject LUMAGUE had a Warrant of Arrest for MURDER, NBI-CAR conducted a series of verifications to determine his current. Likewise, all garages/locations where he frequently parked his car were subjected to constant surveillance. On September 04, 2025, after receiving confirmation that Subject LUMAGUE was inside his rented apartment in Upper Pinget, Baguio City, NBI-CAR agents entered the premises and served the Warrant against Subject LUMAGUE in an orderly and peaceful manner. Subject LUMAGUE was then informed of the reason of his arrest, as well as his rights as an arrested person. Subject LUMAGUE was immediately brought to the NBI-CAR Office and undergone standard booking procedure. On September 05, 2025, Subject LUMAGUE was presented before the RTC Branch 5, Baguio City, which issued the commitment order for his detention at the Baguio City Jail. Immediately thereafter, Subject LUMAGUE was turned-over at the Baguio City Jail Male Dormitory, Abanao Street, Baguio City.

On September 04, 2025, after receiving confirmation that Subject LUMAGUE was inside his rented apartment in Upper Pinget, Baguio City, NBI-CAR agents entered the premises and served the Warrant against Subject LUMAGUE in an orderly and peaceful manner. Subject LUMAGUE was then informed of the reason of his arrest, as well as his rights as an arrested person. Immediately thereafter, Subject LUMAGUE was turned-over at the Baguio City Jail Male Dormitory, Abanao Street, Baguio City.

body: On June 25, 2020, NADJULLAH RASHID y SYBIL, a resident of Binan City, Laguna, filed a case of Kidnapping against spouses ELESER and CHARITO SAUSE. RASHID narrated that on June 19, 2018, he entrusted his daughter ALLIAH, one year old then, to his mother SEDA SYBIL for he and his wife had to work. Thereafter, they only visited the child every 15 days to provide for her needs. However, after a month, RASHID learned that CHARITO, with whom SEDA owed Seven Thousand Pesos (P7,000.00), barrowed his daughter. Upon learning it, RASHID and his wife immediately proceeded to SAUSE’s house at Block 9, Lot 2, Phase 3, Metroville Complex, San Francisco, Binan City, Laguna to get back the child. CHARITO, however, refused to return the child and demanded the payment of Seven Thousand Pesos that his mother owed to her. RASHID claimed that he had no money during that time so he promised to return but CHARITO forced them to sign a document as a leverage. When RASHID already had the money, he returned to SAUSE’s house but CHARITO again refused to return the child and claimed that he owed her more because she rushed his daughter to a private hospital and had undergone an operation, but she failed to show any proof of the alleged expenses. CHARITO also threatened to have RASHID arrested if he continues to visit the child. RASHID and his wife likewise tried to talk to ELESER but to no avail. Thus, they decided to return to their hometown in Visaya to earn more money. On June 16, 2020, RASHID’s family decided to return to Binan, Laguna to get back their child. The following day they tried to visit their daughter, but when CHARITO saw them, she immediately hid the child inside her house. The couple confronted CHARITO and asked her to return their child otherwise they would file a case against her. However, CHARITO was not intimidated and still adamant to return the child. She even demanded through Facebook Messenger One Million Pesos from the couple in exchange for their daughter. Desperate to recover his daughter, RASHID sought the help of his friends, who in turn referred his case to NBI-LAGDO. Acting on the complaint, on June 26, 2020 around 12 noon, a rescue operation was hatched in coordination with the City Social Welfare and Development Office (CSWD) of Binan, Laguna and the local police. Together with Social Worker JULIETA PARATE, the NBI-LAGDO operatives proceeded to the residence of ELESER and CHARITO SAUSE at Block 9, Lot 2, Phase 3, Metroville Complex, San Francisco, Binan City, Laguna, but no one was home. After an hour CHARITO arrived and the operatives immediately confronted her. At first, CHARITO claimed that ALLIAH was her own child and she even showed its passport with the name VHRNIE JHANE CAMENTO SAUSE. Thereafter, CHARITO was compelled to reveal the whereabouts of the child and she claimed that she left the child to her Aunt’s house at Block 2, Lot 5, Wisteria St., Southview Homes Subdivision, Pacita Complex II, Barangay San Vicente, San Pedro City, Laguna. Immediately, the operatives proceeded to the said address, where they found the child. At that juncture, CHARITO was accosted and placed under arrest. Accordingly, a case of Violation of Article 270, “Kidnapping and Failure to Return a Minor” of the Revised Penal Code was filed against Spouses CHARITO and ELESER SAUSE.

body: PRESS STATEMENT May 10, 2022 NBI ARRESTS 2 INDIVIDUALS FOR ESTAFA In line with the government’s drive against criminality, the National Bureau of Investigation announces the arrest of two (2) individuals by operatives of NBI-Special Action Unit (NBI-SAU) in an entrapment operation in Taguig City. Director Distor identified the subjects as FILENCE CARLA LAM alias CARLA LAM and FELIX LIM. Director Distor said that the operation stemmed from a complaint filed by the victim of Subject Lam and her cohort. According to the complaint, Subject Lam offered her a food supply project to more than 3,000 PNP personnel inside Camp Crame. In order to entice the Complainant, Subject Lam used the names of various PNP officials as parties to the transaction. Subject even created a text and call app account of a particular PNP official to make it appear that the latter is indeed part of the transaction. Consequently, Complainant shelled out Php 6 Million to Subject Lam, allegedly to facilitate favorable bidding result for the Complainant. Subject even provided the Complainant with documents concerning the transaction, which upon verification with the PNP, were confirmed to be falsified. On April 27, 2022, Subject Lam asked for Php 1.5 Million from the Complainant to be used as “under the table”/bribe for the speedy approval of the said food supply project. The Complainant then proceeded before the NBI-SAU and filed a complaint against Subject Lam. Thus, on the same date, an entrapment operation was hatched against Subject Lam. NBI-SAU operatives were able to arrest Subject Lam and Lim in a restaurant in Taguig City where the entrapment money was received by Subject Lam. Seized during the operation include entrapment money, cellular phones and IDs of the Subjects. The arrested Subjects were presented for Inquest proceedings before the Prosecutor’s Office of Taguig City for Estafa thru Falsification of documents.

body: PRESS STATEMENT January 14, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } The NBI-Cybercrime Division (CCD) and NBI-Special Task Force (STF), under the leadership of NBI Director Judge Jaime B. Santiago (Ret.), arrested twelve (12) Chinese nationals for scamming activities, and four (4) Filipinos for bribing the arresting officers. On January 8, 2025, the operatives of NBI-Cybercrime Division (CCD) and NBI-Special Task Force (STF) augmented the Bureau of Immigration (BI) in the implementation of Mission Order, wherein the BI Officers were directed to conduct verification and investigation operation against foreign nationals found at RI RANCE CORPORATE CENTER II ASEANA CITY, Tambo, Paranaque City who are in violation of Philippine Immigration Act. Subsequently, during the implementation of the Mission Order, while the BI Officers were verifying the identities of the foreign nationals, CCD and STF operatives coincidentally witnessed a fully operational office setup of a scam hub, which clearly shows that the individuals inside were engaged in scamming activities. The active desktops present at the scene were examined in plain view by the NBI-CCD digital forensic agents which yielded positive to the presence of romance or love scam scripts, messaging applications with fictitious accounts, bank accounts, and fraudulent cryptocurrency scams, and fake investment schemes. The discovery resulted to the arrest of 12 Chinese nationals namely: XU CHAO, MENG WEI SHI, XING CHAO, QIN HAI FENG, LI XIANG HUA, ZHANG WEI, WANG QIN XIANG, WANG JIA FA, JIANG QI LONG, LUO SHANG FEN, QIXIN WANG, and CHEN JIANG SONG. While the NBI operatives were preparing to return to the NBI Office with the arrested Subjects, EZECHIEL BERNALES, a Filipino-Chinese, volunteered to come, claiming that he is the Subjects’ only official interpreter. EZECHIEL was repeatedly telling the NBI operatives that Subjects Wang Qin Xiang and Qixin Wang were offering to pay Php 300,000.00 for each arrested individual or a total of Php 3,600,000.00 in exchange for the release for the12 arrested Chinese nationals. Operatives agreed to such arrangement in order to make it appear that operatives concur with the offer. An entrapment operation was then hatched to arrest the persons who will bring the money. In the afternoon of January 10, 2025, three cars arrived at the NBI 2nd floor parking lot. After the driver handed over to one of the operatives a black eco bag containing Php 900,000.00, CCD operatives who were strategically positioned at the 2nd floor parking lot, immediately arrested the driver identified as ROBUSTIANO HIZON, along with the other individuals identified as JOHN ABUNDA VILLANUEVA, KRISTOFFER RYAN HABELITO BAGUNA and HANIF MALA BAUTIL. The 12 Chinese nationals were presented for inquest proceedings before the City Prosecutor’s Office, Paranaque City for Computer-Related Forgery under Section 4(b)(1) of RA 10175 otherwise known as the Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012; Social Engineering Schemes under Section 4(b)(1), and Economic Sabotage under Section 4(c)(1) of R.A 12010 otherwise known as the Anti-Financial Account Scamming Act (AFASA) in relation to R.A. 10175. The 5 Filipinos were presented for inquest proceedings before the City Prosecutor Office, Pasay City for Corruption of Public Officials under Article 212 of the Revised Penal Code.

body: PRESS STATEMENT June 06, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } On June 05, 2025, expelled Congressman Arnolfo Teves Jr. who is facing multiple criminal charges attended his arraignment before the Regional Trial Court (RTC), Branch 12, Manila. Acting on the directive of NBI Director Judge Jaime B. Santiago (Ret.), a joint team composed of NBI-Cyber Crime Division (CCD), NBI-Special Task Force (STF) and NBI-Security Management Division (SMD) escorted Teves from the NBI Detention Facility in Building 14, New Bilibid Prison, Muntinlupa City to RTC Branch 12 of Manila. This is in compliance with the court order requiring to produce the living body of Teves for his arraignment yesterday at 8:30 a.m. During the arraignment, Teves assisted by a counsel, invoked his right to remain silent. The Presiding Judge entered a not guilty plea on behalf of accused Teves with regard to the charges of illegal possession of firearms and explosives. Teves remains in the custody at the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) detention facility within the New Bilibid Prison in Muntinlupa City.

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today announced the arrest of an individual in Bacoor City for investment scam. NBI Officer-in-Charge (OIC) Director Eric B. Distor identified the subject as JOHN CARL MICHAEL LUALHATI. OIC Director Distor said that the operation stemmed from a complaint filed by the victim of Subject Lualhati. According to the complainant, Subject Lualhati posted an advertisement on Facebook offering a business investment opportunity in the company known as FIL-INVEST (FILIPINO INVESTORS CORPORATION), which was later on change to HC Holdings (Hedge Chance Holdings). The complainant inquired to the Facebook page of the subject and was convinced to accept the offer because of the huge percentage of the return of investment. The complainant then gave to the subject the investment money in several tranches consisting of the consolidated money of his family, co-workers, and friends totaling Php 1,567,000.00. Thereafter, the complainant inquired to the subject regarding the payment of the interest on their investment but Subject Lualhati failed to comply with his obligation of paying the interest to the complainant. The complainant was then compelled to pay Php 793,500.00 to his family, friends, and co-workers as the payment of the interest of their investment. The complainant inquired with the Bacoor City Business Permit and Licensure Office the legitimacy of the subject’s company. A reply-certification was issued which stated that FIL-INVEST or HC HOLDINGS have no registered business in their city, clearly indicating that the investment was a scam. After sometime, Subject Lualhati contacted the complainant asking for additional investment of Php 100,000.00 to be given in Solaire Hotel and Casino Resort in Pasay City. Before the meeting takes place the complainant reported the matter to the NBI-National Capital Region (NBI-NCR). Thus, on September 23,2020, NBI-NCR together with the complainant proceeded to the agreed meeting place. Upon receipt by Subject Lualhati of the marked money, operatives of NBI-NCR immediately placed him under arrest. Forensic examination showed the presence of fluorescent specks and smudges on his hands. Subject Lualhati will be charged for violation of Article 315 (Estafa) of the Revised Penal Code.

body: PRESS STATEMENT June 10, 2022 NBI BEEFS UP CYBERCRIME DIVISION WITH 200 MORE AGENTS ACROSS THE COUNTRY; ACQUIRES CUTTING EDGE FORENSIC EQUIPMENT AND ANTI-CYBERCRIME TOOLS WORTH HUNDREDS OF MILLIONS OF PESOS In line with the direct order of National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Director ERIC B. DISTOR to boost the cybercrime investigative capabilities of the NBI in response to increasing complaints and cases of cybercrimes recorded by the Bureau, the NBI acquired various high-tech equipment that will improve cyber response, cybercrime investigation and cyber security of the NBI-Cybercrime Division (NBI-CCD). On June 09, 2022, as part of the continuous upgrade of the NBI-CCD, Director Distor led the turnover of various Digital Forensic equipment to the Agents of NBI-CCD. The NBI has purchased high end Digital Forensic Equipment that will help the NBI Cybercrime agents and forensic experts in providing modern investigation and technical assistance in the investigation of cyber-related crimes and as well as preservation and examination of digital evidence. DISTOR emphasized, “Today, I have assigned ten (10) more agents in Cybercrime Division in Manila and designated two hundred (200) agents for Regional and District offices of the NBI as cybercrime agents who will handle cybercrime related cases. DISTOR added that the NBI, under Republic Act 10867 [An Act Reorganizing and Modernizing the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI)], is mandated to undertake investigation and detection of crimes and offenses specified therein. The primary jurisdiction of the NBI as provided for by the said law includes “Violation of RA 10175 otherwise known as the Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012.” In the first quarter of 2022, DISTOR ordered to strengthen the anti-cybercrime capabilities of the bureau to enable it to immediately respond to cybercrime cases and complaints filed by private citizens such as identity theft, online scam or fraud, hacking of bank accounts and personal accounts, phishing, cyber libel, forensic accounting, and other violations that fall within the ambit of the Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012. He also assigned an entire batch of 16 newly trained agents to the Cybercrime Division, thus improving its manpower capabilities. DISTOR assures the public that the NBI will continue to provide adequate and necessary tool and equipment to effectively perform its service to the people.

body: PRESS STATEMENT May 23, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } On May 19, 2025, the National Bureau of Investigation-Organized and Transnational Crime Division (NBI-OTCD), under the leadership of NBI Director JUDGE JAIME B. SANTIAGO (Ret.), arrested an individual in an entrapment operation in Quezon City for sextortion. According to the Complainant, the Subject was her former boyfriend, who coerced her into resuming their romantic relationship. He threatened to send intimate videos of her to her family if she did not comply with his demands. An entrapment operation was then initiated. Subject instructed the complainant to meet him at an establishment in Tomas Morato, Quezon City. Complainant went to the designated establishment, while the agents positioned themselves strategically. During their conversation, Subject continued to pressure the complainant to resume their relationship, stating that he would only delete the video and stop the threats if they would proceed to her condominium for sexual intercourse. After the complainant gave the pre-arranged signal, the NBI-OTCD agents immediately apprehended the subject while he was coercing the complainant to go with him to have sexual intercourse. On May 20, 2025, the Subject was presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor of Quezon City for Grave Threats under Article 282 and Grave Coercion under Article 286 of the Revised Penal Code (RPC); violation of Section 5(e), (g), and (i) of Republic Act No. 9262 (Anti-Violence Against Women and Their Children Act of 2004); and violation of Section 4(a) of R.A. No. 9995 (Anti-Photo and Video Voyeurism Act of 2009), all in relation to R.A. No. 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012). Director Santiago commended the agents of the NBI-OTCD for their successful operation, which resulted in the arrest of Subject. He urged the public to report any incidents of sextortion to the NBI, assuring them that the agency is ready to take action.

PRESS STATEMENT May 23, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } On May 19, 2025, the National Bureau of Investigation-Organized and Transnational Crime Division (NBI-OTCD), under the leadership of NBI Director JUDGE JAIME B. SANTIAGO (Ret.), arrested an individual in an entrapment operation in Quezon City for sextortion. According to the Complainant, the Subject was her former boyfriend, who coerced her into resuming their romantic relationship. He threatened to send intimate videos of her to her family if she did not comply with his demands. An entrapment operation was then initiated. Subject instructed the complainant to meet him at an establishment in Tomas Morato, Quezon City. Complainant went to the designated establishment, while the agents positioned themselves strategically. During their conversation, Subject continued to pressure the complainant to resume their relationship, stating that he would only delete the video and stop the threats if they would proceed to her condominium for sexual intercourse. After the complainant gave the pre-arranged signal, the NBI-OTCD agents immediately apprehended the subject while he was coercing the complainant to go with him to have sexual intercourse. On May 20, 2025, the Subject was presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor of Quezon City for Grave Threats under Article 282 and Grave Coercion under Article 286 of the Revised Penal Code (RPC); violation of Section 5(e), (g), and (i) of Republic Act No. 9262 (Anti-Violence Against Women and Their Children Act of 2004); and violation of Section 4(a) of R.A. No. 9995 (Anti-Photo and Video Voyeurism Act of 2009), all in relation to R.A. No. 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012). Director Santiago commended the agents of the NBI-OTCD for their successful operation, which resulted in the arrest of Subject. He urged the public to report any incidents of sextortion to the NBI, assuring them that the agency is ready to take action.

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today announced the rescue of fourteen (14) women by operatives of NBI- Special Task Force (NBI-STF) and the arrest of four (4) individuals for Human Trafficking in Lipa City Batangas. NBI Officer-In-Charge (OIC) Director Eric B. Distor identified the arrested subjects as WILSON EBREO y REYES, ALORA ALMOGUERA y GUETA, JUNE DERILO y RAZ, ROBIN SEÑAR y GIBAO. OIC-Director Distor said that the operation stemmed from the information provided by Destiny Rescue Pilipinas Inc. (Destiny), a Non-Government Organization (NGO) engaged in combatting human trafficking. According to the information, subject spouses are allegedly involved in human trafficking of several women, minors, and even their own minor child. Acting on the said information, the NBI-STF operatives who acted as poseur- customers were able to establish communication with the subject spouses. The subject spouses offered the operatives several women for sexual pleasures in the amount of Php 3,500.00-Php 6,000.00. NBI-STF conducted a surveillance operation in the vicinity of the rented residence of the subjects located at Barangay Balintawak, Lipa City. The surveillance operation yielded positive results and it was confirmed that the subject spouses are indeed into prostitution, offering minor girls who are in their custody for sexual pleasure in exchange for a fee. On June 20 ,2021, NBI-STF operatives who posed as seafarers and acted as poseur-customers contacted the subject spouses about the availability of women preferably minors who were earlier offered by the subjects. The subjects affirmed that one of the minors will be available. Thus, on the same date, NBI-STF operatives proceeded to the target premises to conduct the entrapment operation. While on their way to the target area the subjects sent pictures of the available women including a minor girl and were asked to buy liquor so that they can fetch other women if the customers dislike the first batch of women being offered. Upon arrival of the poseur-customers, they were entertained by the subject spouses together with another two (2) subjects. The undercover agents expressed their distaste to the first batch of women that were offered and one of the subject spouses fetched several women. The undercover agents then handed over the marked money to one of the subject spouses as payment to the supposed sexual services and subsequently gave the pre-arranged signal that the transaction has been completed. The NBI-STF operatives swooped into the premises and apprehended the four (4) subjects. One of the female subjects who was later identified as MARY GRACE FLORES was able to flee and evade arrest. The operation also led to the rescue of fourteen (14) women of whom three (3) are minor during the operation. Also rescued was a nine (9) month old child who was with his mother who is also a victim. The four (4) arrested subjects were presented for Inquest proceedings before the Office of the Prosecutor of Lipa City for violation of R.A. 9208, as amended by R.A. 10364 (Expanded Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2012) in relation to R.A. 7610 (Special Protection of Children Against Abuse, Exploitation and Discrimination Act), in relation also to R.A.10175 (Cybercrime Law).

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today said operatives of NBI-International Airport Investigation Division (NBI-IAID) arrested an individual for Usurpation of Authority NBI Officer-In-Charge (OIC) Director Eric Distor identified the Subject as LAMBERTO Q. PAYONGAYONG. Subject sent various letters to Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP) addressed to BSP Governor Benjamin E. Diokno and Atty. Henry De Vera, Manager, Currency Integrity Staff (CIS), Currency Issue and Integrity Office (CIIO), BSP wherein he represented himself as a lawyer. In his letters, OIC-Director Distor said, Subject Payngayong declared that he is a Trustee of a private individual involving Trust Account covering $300 Dodecallion which allegedly matured in 2007 and which he sought to be withdrawn with the help of the BSP. Subject also mentioned that he is an Assignee of a parcel of land covered by Original Certificate of Title allegedly being used by the Central Bank of the Philippines to back up the printing of legal tender notes. BSP conducted verification and certification issued by the Office of the Bar Confidant (OBC), Supreme Court and the Integrated Bar of the Philippines (IBP) states that Subject PAYONGAYONG is not a member of the Philippine Bar. When IAID operatives were informed that Subject was advised that a reply was ready for release and pick up, an entrapment operation was conducted on September 16, 2020 resulting in the arrest of the Subject. Subject PAYONGAYONG will be subjected for inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor, Quezon City for violation of Article 177 (Usurpation of Authority of Official Functions) of the Revised Penal Code.

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today announced the arrest of an individual in Tarlac City for Falsification of documents and Estafa. NBI Officer-in-Charge (OIC)-Director Eric B. Distor identified the subject as JENNY CASTRO. Director Distor said that the operation stemmed from the complaint filed by the victim against Subject Castro. According to the complainant, sometime in year 2018, Subject Castro mortgaged the portion of her property to the complainant for Php 5,300,000.00. The said property is located at Brgy. Banaguanan, Tarlac City, Tarlac containing an area of 312 square meters. On September 28, 2021, Subject Castro sold the property to the complainant for Php 7,000,000.00 evidenced by a Deed of Absolute Sale signed by Subject Castro. Both parties agreed that the amount covered by the mortgage of Php 5.3 Million will serve as advance payment and the balance of Php 1,700,000.00 will be payable on September 30, 2021. On September 29, the complainant verified the Transfer Certificate of Title (TCT) of the property and found out that the TCT of the subject property sold to her by Subject Castro was fake as declared by one of the employees of the Register of Deeds (RD). Upon securing the Certification and/or Acknowledgement from the Register of Deeds, NBI-TARDO set up an entrapment operation. The following day, September 30, 2021, NBI operatives together with the complainant proceeded to the target meeting area and positioned themselves strategically in the vicinity. After the payment consisting of boodle money and a check worth Php 1.7 Million as full payment for the said property was received by the subject and had signed the acknowledgement receipt, NBI operatives immediately apprehended Subject Castro. Subject Castro was presented for inquest proceedings before the City Prosecutor’s Office for violation of Article 172 (Falsification by Private Individual and Use of Falsified Documents) and Article 315 (Estafa) of the Revised Penal Code, as amended.

body: PRESS STATEMENT August 26, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } PRESS RELEASE | NBI RESCUES FIVE VIETNAMESE FROM PROSTITUTION RING Pasay City – In a strong move to combat human trafficking, NBI Director Atty. Melvin A. Matibag issued a directive to intensify ongoing efforts and campaigns against this grave crime. In response, the NBI-Human Trafficking Division (NBI-HTRAD) expanded its operations, including undercover investigations, surveillance, and collaboration with local and international law enforcement agencies. These concerted efforts culminated in the successful rescue of five (5) Vietnamese nationals, all identified as victims coerced and exploited by human trafficking networks. Director Matibag commended the NBI-HTRAD agents for their successful operation against a notorious prostitution ring. He emphasized that the NBI remains steadfast in its commitment to its mandate to combat all forms of human trafficking, highlighting the importance of ongoing efforts, interagency cooperation, and continued vigilance to protect vulnerable individuals, including foreign nationals, across the country. The rescue operation was initiated following an intelligence report indicating that a Vietnamese national was involved in sex trafficking. The individual was reportedly recruiting and transporting foreign women, including alleged minors, to Manila for commercial sexual exploitation. Acting on this information, an undercover agent from the NBI-HTRAD contacted the suspect via Telegram. Throughout their interactions, the Subject offered women for sexual services in exchange for payment. After negotiations, the Subject agreed to deliver a woman of his choosing to a specific location, a hotel in Pasay City, where the undercover agent was waiting. On August 11, 2026, agents from NBI-HTRAD, together with the Pasay Social Welfare and Development Department (PSWDD), arrived at the hotel to conduct an entrapment and rescue operation. They discreetly positioned themselves at nearby strategic locations to maintain surveillance. During the operation, the operatives intercepted two Vietnamese women. One was identified as the woman believed to have been selected to provide sexual services within the illicit trafficking network. The other was recognized as having access to a Telegram account, later confirmed to be a trafficked victim. The rescued victims reported that their belongings were in a unit in a condominium building in Pasay and that operatives from the NBI-HTRAD and personnel from PSWDD accompanied the retrieval. While inside the unit, the NBI agents observed, in plain sight, a transparent plastic sachet containing suspected shabu (methamphetamine) and three drug paraphernalia items. The trafficked victims admitted that they used these illegal drugs before every meeting with their clients. During the investigation, one of the trafficked victims revealed that she had previously been housed in another condominium unit in Pasay with other trafficked victims. Acting on this information, the NBI-HTRAD operatives proceeded to the condominium and rescued three (3) Vietnamese nationals, who were also victims of human trafficking. https://www.facebook.com/reel/2102422053984448

body: PRESS STATEMENT November 20, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } Today, the Pasig Regional Trial Court found former Bamban, Tarlac Mayor Alice Guo, along with Rachelle Malonzo Carreon, Jaimielyn Cruz, and Walter Wong Rong, guilty of qualified human trafficking for their roles in a large-scale Philippine Offshore Gaming Operation (POGO) hub in Bamban. All four were sentenced to reclusión perpetua and ordered to pay Php 2 Million in fines. This conviction is an important milestone in the government’s ongoing effort to dismantle criminal syndicates and protect victims of exploitation. It is also a clear affirmation of the administration’s policy direction under President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr., who has consistently mandated that agencies intensify the fight against human trafficking and POGO-related abuses. As the President has emphasized, the rule of law must prevail, and public office must never be used as a shield for criminality. Under this mandate, the NBI pursued the case with rigor, professionalism, and unrelenting resolve. The evidence found by the NBI Task Force Guo bolstered the conviction on the said trafficking case. The verdict demonstrates that no network is too sophisticated, no operation too well-funded, and no position too powerful to escape accountability. Justice has been served today, not only for the victims, but for the nation. Human trafficking reduces people to commodities. The court’s ruling makes clear that anyone who engages in, supports, or protects such exploitation will face the full force of the law. On behalf of the NBI, we commend our investigators and partner agencies who worked tirelessly to uncover the truth and ensure that this case was brought before the courts. We reaffirm our commitment to the President’s directive to safeguard our communities, uphold the rule of law, and protect the vulnerable from organized criminal activity. We will continue to follow the evidence wherever it leads, strengthen its operations against trafficking and POGO-linked crimes, and ensure that no individual, regardless of position, privilege, or influence, stands beyond the reach of justice. Justice may take time. But it arrives – and when it does, it carries the full authority of the Republic. Though it may sometimes move with measured steps, justice never loses its direction. Atty. Angelito DLP Magno Officer-in-Charge, NBI

body: PRESS STATEMENT April 17, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } PRESS RELEASE | ALICE GUO AND HER COHORTS INDICTED ANEW FOR ANTI-DUMMY LAW Pasay City, Philippines – On March 3, 2026, the Department of Justice – National Prosecution Service (DOJ-NPS) issued a Resolution granting the Motion for Reconsideration and recommending that GUO HUA PING a.k.a. ‘ALICE GUO’ and her cohorts be charged with simulation of minimum capital stock, penalized under Section 2 of Commonwealth Act No. 108 (Anti-Dummy Law) The Resolution was based on the Motion for Reconsideration filed by NBI-Dagupan District Office (NBI-DADO) before the DOJ-NPS, seeking the inclusion of charges under the Anti-Dummy Law. The motion stemmed from previous charges filed against Guo and her cohorts for Falsification of Public documents and violations of the Anti-Dummy Law in connection with the incorporation and operations of 3LIN Q-Farm Inc., in Pangasinan. The case highlights findings that certain incorporators misrepresented their identities and nationalities, allegedly to circumvent a statutory restriction on foreign land ownership. In response to the NBI-DADO’s charges against the subjects, the DOJ-NPS issued a resolution indicting the respondents for seven (7) counts of falsification of public documents. However, it dismissed the complaints alleging violations of the Anti-Dummy Law. In its motion, the NBI-DADO argues that the respondents’ circumvention of the law, through falsification of documents and simulation of stocks, was undertaken for the ultimate goal of making 3LIN legitimate and enjoying the rights and privileges accorded to domestic corporations in the country. NBI-DADO added that the dismissal of the case on the ground that the purchase of the parcels of land was made before the issuance of the Articles of Incorporation (AOI) would set a dangerous precedent, as violators could simply purchase parcels of land before incorporation and thereby be immune from any suit for violation of the Anti-Dummy Law. NBI Director Atty. Melvin A. Matibag commended the unwavering dedication and meticulous efforts of the NBI-DADO agents in their extensive investigation and case-building procedures. These concerted efforts culminated in the appropriate and solid charges being filed against Guo and her associates, ensuring accountability. He emphasized that the NBI is diligently and thoroughly managing each case with the utmost professionalism to guarantee that all individuals arrested by the bureau are successfully prosecuted, thereby reinforcing public trust in the justice system. #NBIServes

body: PRESS STATEMENT July 25, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } NBI AT ROBINSONS LAND CORPORATION., 15 TAONG PAGSASAMA PARA SA LINGKOD PAMPUBLIKO Noong Hulyo 24, 2026, opisyal na pinanibago ng National Bureau of Investigation (NBI), sa ilalim ng pamumuno ni Direktor Atty. Melvin A. Matibag, ang pakikipagtulungan nito sa Robinsons Land Corporation. Sa ilalim ng Lingkod Pinoy Center, pinagtibay ng NBI at Robinsons ang kanilang pagsasama sa pamamagitan ng paglagda sa isang Memorandum of Agreement (MOA). Dahil dito, magiging accessible o madaling mapupuntahan ang mga serbisyo ng NBI Clearance sa mga piling Robinsons Malls sa buong bansa. Bahagi ito ng mas malawak na diskarte ng pamahalaan na naglalayong pagandahin at ilapit ang mga pangunahing serbisyo sa publiko. Sa pamamagitan ng paglalagay ng mga clearance center na ito sa mga sikat at madaling mapuntahang mall, sinisikap ng NBI na itama at gawing mas simple ang proseso ng aplikasyon para sa mga taong kukuha ng NBI clearance.Malaki ang kahalagahan ng pag-unlad na ito dahil ipinapangako nitong babawasan ang abala na karaniwang nararanasan sa pagkuha ng mga mahalagang dokumento tulad nito. Madalas kasing kailangan ang NBI clearance para sa iba’t ibang legal na usapin, trabaho, at paglalakbay. body: PRESS STATEMENT September 22, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } PRESS RELEASE | NBI APPREHENDS ILLEGAL STREET NOTARIES IN MAKATI CITY The National Bureau of Investigation – Organized and Transnational Crimes Division (NBI-OTCD) arrested two individuals allegedly engaged in illegal notarization activities during an entrapment operation conducted on September 15, 2026, in Makati City. NBI Director Melvin A. Matibag said the latest operation demonstrated the Bureau’s commitment to safeguarding the integrity of legal and judicial processes and to taking appropriate action against individuals who unlawfully represent themselves as authorized legal professionals or misuse the credentials of legitimate members of the Philippine Bar. The investigation began with a formal complaint from a lawyer who reported that unauthorized street operators were allegedly using her expired notarial commission without authority on various legal documents. In parallel, the team observed illegal notarial operations along Kamagong Extension, Barangay San Antonio, Makati City. Pursuant to an Office Order issued by the RTC Makati, the team undertook formal inter-court coordination with RTC Manila. Certifications issued by the Office of the Bar Confidant (Supreme Court) and the RTC Office of the Clerk of Court of Makati confirmed that the complainant was never commissioned as a Notary Public in Makati City. On July 31, 2026, NBI-OTCD operatives conducted an undercover operation to verify the reported activities. During the operation, one of the Subjects processed and notarized an Affidavit of Loss using the name and credentials of a lawyer. The lawyer, a member of the Philippine Bar admitted in 1984, later confirmed that he never authorized or consented to anyone performing notarizations or using his professional credentials. He then executed an Affidavit-Complaint on September 3, 2026. The investigation further disclosed that unauthorized street operators were allegedly producing notarial documents using falsified dry seals, mechanical daters, and stamps bearing the names or credentials of legitimate lawyers, without those lawyers’ knowledge or consent. Based on evidence gathered and intelligence developed during the investigation, an entrapment operation was conducted on September 15, 2026, in coordination with the PNP Southern Police District. In accordance with Supreme Court Administrative Matter No. 21-06-08-SC, two body-worn cameras were used during the operation. Prior to the operation, the NBI Forensic Chemistry Division marked two genuine P100 bills and treated them with fluorescent powder for identification purposes. At approximately 2:00 p.m., an undercover operative and a poseur-customer approached the makeshift notarial setup on Kamagong Extension. The Subjects received an Affidavit of Loss and quoted a fee of P100 to notarize it. One of the Subjects applied notarial markings and a mechanical date stamp to the document, filled in the corresponding Document, Page, Book, and Series numbers, and affixed a metal seal bearing the credentials of a lawyer whose authority had not been established. After receiving the marked money, the pre-arranged signal was transmitted to the arresting team. NBI operatives immediately moved in, identified themselves, and informed the Subjects that the transaction had been recorded using body-worn cameras. When asked to present proof of their authority to perform notarization or valid identification showing their professional credentials, Subjects failed to present any. They were subsequently arrested and apprised of their constitutional rights. Subjects were brought to the NBI-OTCD office for standard booking procedures, documentation, and a medical examination. Based on the evidence gathered, the investigation established that the Subjects engaged in unauthorized notarial activities and used falsified instruments in connection with the preparation and notarization of legal documents. Inquests and the filing of appropriate criminal charges for Falsification, Usurpation of Authority, and Estafa are being conducted before the proper Prosecutor’s Office of Makati City. https://www.facebook.com/reel/1477783597737445

body: In line with the relentless campaign of the government against illegal drugs, operatives of National Bureau of Investigation-National Capital Region (NBI-NCR) arrested an individual in Paranaque City for selling illegal drugs. NBI Officer-in-Charge (OIC) Director Eric B. Distor identified the Subject as JOREN MARI TAMAYO BECHAYDA. Distor said that the case stemmed from a report regarding a certain alias Corine and his cohorts who were allegedly engaged in the sale, trading, administration, dispensation, delivery, distribution, and transportation of dangerous drugs in the cities of Paranaque and Pasay, in violation of RA 9165 otherwise known as the Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002. Acting on the information received, NBI-NCR operatives hatched an entrapment operation on July 28, 2021 in coordination with PDEA and PNP to arrest alias Corine and his cohorts who were allegedly notoriously selling substantial quantities of Kush, a pure or hybrid Cannabis indica and considered an illegal drug. The informant sent a text message to the Subject for an order of Kush. Alias JOREN instantly responded that he has Kush in his possession for sale. A poseur-buyer then agreed to meet with JOREN at 5A Cesar Virata St., Classic Homes, BF Homes, Paranaque City. At around 5:34pm, Subject identified as JOREN MARI TAMAYO BECHAYDA arrived and alighted from SUV white Chevrolet Trailblazer with plate number WC 9561. He then approached the informant and the poseur-buyer and took out twelve (12) packs of transparent plastic sachets containing substances with remarkable resemblance to Kush, which costs Php 25,000. Subject then handed the Kush to the poseur-buyer and received the marked money afterwards. With this, NBI operatives approached the Subject, introduced themselves, their authority, and frisked the Subject. The latter was informed of his constitutional rights and was placed under arrest. Seized items during the operation, which include a total of fifteen (15) packs of plastic sachets containing substances with resemblance to Kush and the marked money, were inventoried in the presence of Subject JOREN, local barangay, and media representative. The fifteen (15) packs of plastic sachets containing substances with resemblance to Kush, upon examination of NBI-Forensic Chemist, tested positive for the presence of Marijuana, a dangerous drug. Subject JOREN MARI TAMAYO BECHAYDA was presented for Inquest proceedings before the Office of the Prosecutor of Paranaque City.

body: The Information Division is pleased to submit herewith the significant cases of the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) for the following aforementioned period as follows: • On October 2, 2017, operatives of NBI-National Capital Region (NBI-NCR) arrested WILLIAM DIAN for allegedly raping a minor victim, Jessabelle Dian, fourteen years old. The case stemmed from the letter of Commission on Human Rights requesting for assistance in rescuing Jessabelle and her newborn child. Victim was brought to Caloocan from Camiguin Island, Calayan, Cagayan to serve as a housemaid. While in Caloocan, Jessabelle told her mother, Elvira Dian, that she was sexually abused repeatedly by her Uncle William. Jessabelle got pregnant and gave birth to a baby boy. This prompted the mother to ask for help from the Social Welfare in their place in rescuing her daughter. The Social Welfare then wrote a letter to the Commission on Human Rights to address the concerns of the victim’s mother. After the preparation of documents and standard briefing prior to the the operation, taking full consideration of the imminent threat to the minor and her newborn child, NBI-NCR operatives immediately proceeded to Bagombong, Caloocan City. The victim’s mother entered the house and found thereat were Jessabelle together with her newborn child, and Subject WILLIAM DIAN. Subject WILLIAM was immediately brought to the NBI-NCR for post-operation processing and was presented for inquest proceedings at the National Prosecution Service, Department of Justice (DOJ). Subject opted a Preliminary Investigation waiving his rights under Article 125 of the Revised Penal Code. He was turned over to SMD for custody. • On October 3, 2017, operatives of NBI-Cagayan Valley District Office (NBI-CAVRO) rescued KATRINA SAMAYO SISON, 16 years old from the custody of JOHN CHRISTIAN DE LEON. The operation stemmed from the email request of Mrs. Delia Sison to rescue her granddaughter who was allegedly kidnapped by her boyfriend last September at their residence in Molino 3, Bacoor, Cavite. On the above-mentioned date, NBI-CAVRO operatives, together with the representatives from Municipal Social Welfare and Development and barangay officials of Abulug, Cagayan, successfully rescued Katrina from the custody of JOHN CHRISTIAN DE LEON in Simayong, Abulug, Cagayan. The rescued minor is now under the protective custody of DSWD-Region 2 while charges for alleged kidnapping are now being prepared for filing. • On October 5, 2017, operatives of NBI-Naga District Office arrested NUNILON PANTE-OLBES for illegal practice of dentistry in Calabanga, Camarines Sur. The case stemmed from the complaint of Dr. Rowena Q. Abrera and Dr. Carol Dell Villanueva against NUNILON JULIA PANTE-OLBES, CAROL GALICIA VERDEJO, RALPH ARCILLA, JOVENCIO ARCILLA and LOLITA REGNIM LOMBOY for violation of R.A. 9484 otherwise known as the Philippine Dental Act of 2007. Surveillance operations were conducted to verify the veracity of the information and the operations yielded positive result that Subject is engaged in the illegal practice of dentistry. An entrapment operation was then conducted resulting in the arrest of Subject NUNILON PANTE-OLBES who was caught in flagrante delicto practicing dentistry without the required license. Subject was brought before the office of the Provincial Prosecutor, Naga City for inquest proceedings for violation of R.A. 9484 (Philippine Dental Act of 2007). • On October 5, 2017, operatives of NBI-Intellectual Property Rights Division (NBI-IPRD) seized Php 40,000.00 worth of items in the premises of Subjects BRYAN NAVARRO, CHRISTIAN NAVARRO, and ESTELLA BERNISE NAVARRO. According to the complainant, Mr. Peter Paul Mendoza of Bean Leaf Coffee, Subjects’ premise is an unauthorized store to sell Bean Leaf. Items were seized on the strength of Search Warrants in the Subjects’ premises located at Unit 5 Ground Floor Casa Solanda Bldg. Anda St., corner San Juan De Letran St., Brgy. 654. Intramuros Manila. Charges for violation of R.A. 8293 (Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines) will be filed against the Subjects. • On October 10, 2017, operatives of NBI-Central Visayas Regional Office (CEVRO) arrested PARK JUNG HO, a Korean national, by virtue of Warrant of Arrest issued by RTC Branch 23, Cebu City, for Syndicated Estafa. The operation is based on the complaint of Cho Young Kyun and is connected with the operation conducted last August 2017 which resulted in the arrest of Park Jung Park, older brother of the Subject who is also charged for Large Scale Qualified Theft and Syndicated Estafa, both with No Bail fixed by RTC Branch 23 and 58 respectively. • On October 11, 2017, operatives of NBI-Counter Terrorism Division (NBI-CTD) arrested KAREN AIZHA HAMIDON by virtue of Search Warrant for spreading radical Islamic extremist propaganda and recruitment of foreign fighters to come to the Philippines for terrorist acts and inciting rebellion through the use of the internet and social media. Subject HAMIDON has been a person of interest to authorities since she gained international notoriety in the middle of 2016 when she successfully recruited several Indian nationals to come to the Philippines and join the radical Islamic extremist groups in Mindanao. Subject is further of interest to the Philippine Government since she is the wife of MOHAMMAD JAAFAR MAGUID, a.k.a. TOKBOY a.k.a. ABU SHARIFA, the former leader of the ANSAR KHALIFA PHILIPPINES (AKP), a group responsible in the September 2016 Davao City night market bombing in cooperation with the MAUTE Group, as well as the failed attempt to bomb the US Embassy in Manila last December 2016. MOHAMMAD JAAFAR MAGUID was killed by the Police in January 2017 in Saranggani. Aside from being the ex-wife of MUHAMMAD SHAMIN MOHAMMED SIDEK, a Singaporean national who was detained for his links with ISIS, Subject HAMIDON is also a known associate of MUSA CERANTONIO, an Australian Islamist preacher who has inspired numerous foreign to join ISIS. When Subject HAMIDON posted on various public groups in social media application “Telegram” statements calling on Muslims to come to the Philippines and join the fight against the government forces in Marawi City in order to establish a province of the Islamic State of Iraq and Syria (ISIS), NBI-CTD operatives effected the Search Warrant resulting in the arrest of the Subject and the seizure of cellphones, laptops, tablets and other electronic devices being used for her illegal online activities. After forensic examinations on her cellphone, an additional 296 posts of the same message promoting rebellion in Marawi City were discovered. Subject HAMIDON was charged before the Department of Justice (DOJ) for fourteen (14) counts of violation of Article 318 (Inciting a Rebellion or Insurrection) of the Revised Penal Code, as amended, in relation to Section 6 of R.A. 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012). Another rebellion related charges will be filed against her using the 296 posts that were retrieved from her cellphone. • On October 12, 2017, operatives of NBI-Intellectual Property Rights Division (NBI-IPRD) arrested PRESHYL SALACSACAN a.k.a TECIA ROMERO for violation of R.A. 9711 (FDA Act of 2009). The case stemmed from the letter of Atty. Anthony D. Bengzon and Atty. Erika M. Alfonso of Bengzon Negre Untalan (BNU) Intellectual Property Attorney representing Astellas US Technologies Inc., a corporation organized and existing under the laws of Delaware. They alleged that certain individuals in Quezon City are engaged in the unauthorized sale and distribution of unregistered or counterfeit Astellas products; hence their request for investigation. Acting on the letter request, surveillance and test-buy operations were conducted and upon finding that the “Prograf 1mg” bought from the Subject is unregistered, operatives planned a buy bust operation resulting in the arrest of the Subject. Subject PRESHYL SALACSACAN was charged for violation of R.A. 9711 and was brought before the City Prosecutor of Quezon City for inquest proceedings. • On October 14, 2017, operatives of NBI-Environmental Crime Division arrested ALVEN BAROSSA PLANTADO for two (2) counts of Usurpation of Authority. A certain Ernesto Monteza Jr. y Campo arrived at the EnCD office together with Mohammad Umair Qureshi. The former personally sought the latter and brought him before the NBI to file a complaint for alleged carnapping. Thereafter, Irfan Qadri, father of Qureshi arrived with a person who introduced himself as ATTY. ALVEN BAROSSA PLANTADO, lawyer of Qadri and Qureshi. The “lawyer” interfered with the operatives’ investigation and spoke in a loud manner. He rattled off legal maxims and articles of the law in defense of his clients. The operatives, however, observed some fallacies in his rhetoric which motivated them to ask for the lawyer’s name and appropriate identification to which he responded that he is Atty. Alven Barossa Plantado, connected with the Pasay City Courts and Manila Police District Station 5. Unknown to the Subject, operatives had already obtain his name with the Gate Security and had checked him at the updated Law List of the Supreme Court Website where his name was not registered in the roll of Attorneys. When asked for his Police Identification, Subject confessed that he is no longer connected with the MPD. When pressed for his IBP Identification Card, Subject reasoned out that he forgot it at home. The operatives then confronted the Subject of the fact that he had already transgressed Section 177 of the Revised Penal Code (Usurpation of Authority) for claiming and introducing himself both as a legitimate policeman and lawyer when in fact he’s not. Subject was placed under arrest and underwent booking procedures. Record check on the Subject revealed that he was subject of a Robbery/Extortion case by a complainant whom he had arrested before for violation of P.D. 1602. Subject was brought for inquest on the same day before Manila Assistant City Prosecutor. • On October 17, 2017, operatives of NBI-Cabanatuan District Office (NBI-CABDO) arrested JUANCHO DELA CRUZ y ABES, FERNAN YASANIA y GONZALES, GABBY GERMAN y RIVERA and OSCAR DELA CRUZ y BUSOG for violation P.D. 705 (Revised Forestry Code). The Subjects were arrested in an interdiction operation along Maharlika Highway, Quezon District, Cabanatuan City, Nueva Ecija. The operation also resulted in the seizure of two hundred eleven (211) pieces of assorted common hardwood with a total volume/board feet of 4,643 and with an estimated estimated value of Php 139,290.00. According to the DENR, the confiscation of more than 4,000 board feet of lumber is one of the biggest if not, the biggest seizure of illegally cut lumber by all law enforcement entity in Nueva Ecija in the past 10 years. Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the duty Prosecutor of Cabanatuan City, Nueva Ecija for violation of P.D. 705 (Revised Forestry Code) with no bail recommended. • On October 17, 2017, operatives of NBI-Anti-Organized and Transnational Crime Division (NBI-AOTCD) arrested JOCELYN CABRERA y TORREDES in Clarin, Bohol by virtue of Warrant of Arrest issued by RTC Branch 276, Muntinlupa City for Qualified Theft with No Bail recommended. Subject was a former employee of MB Aguirre Pawnshop for 13 years and served as the Branch Manager of Bayanan, Muntinlupa City Branch Office. Subject was presently detained at the NBI Detention Cell. • On October 18, 2017, operatives of NBI-National Capital Region arrested FEDERICO “RICKY” ANGULO for demanding to meet with the victim, Jellen Eisha Marasigan in exchange for the destruction of the nude photographs of the victim. Subject FEDERICO ANGULO was arrested in an entrapment operation when he and the victim went to SOGO motel in Ermita, Manila wherein victim demanded the copies of nude pictures but Subject refused to give the said photographs. Charges for violation of R.A. 9995 (Anti-Photo and Video Voyeurism Act of 2009 were filed against Subject FEDERICO ANGULO. • On October 19, 2017, operatives of NBI-National Capital Region (NBI-NCR), together with the Bureau of Internal Revenue, implemented the BIR Mission Orders against unauthorized/illegal cigarettes without tax stamps being distributed and sold in public markets in the provinces of Nueva Ecija, Bulacan, Pampanga, Tarlac, and Aurora. The Information Division is pleased to submit herewith the significant cases of the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) for the following aforementioned period as follows: • On October 2, 2017, operatives of NBI-National Capital Region (NBI-NCR) arrested WILLIAM DIAN for allegedly raping a minor victim, Jessabelle Dian, fourteen years old. The case stemmed from the letter of Commission on Human Rights requesting for assistance in rescuing Jessabelle and her newborn child. Victim was brought to Caloocan from Camiguin Island, Calayan, Cagayan to serve as a housemaid. While in Caloocan, Jessabelle told her mother, Elvira Dian, that she was sexually abused repeatedly by her Uncle William. Jessabelle got pregnant and gave birth to a baby boy. This prompted the mother to ask for help from the Social Welfare in their place in rescuing her daughter. The Social Welfare then wrote a letter to the Commission on Human Rights to address the concerns of the victim’s mother. After the preparation of documents and standard briefing prior to the the operation, taking full consideration of the imminent threat to the minor and her newborn child, NBI-NCR operatives immediately proceeded to Bagombong, Caloocan City. The victim’s mother entered the house and found thereat were Jessabelle together with her newborn child, and Subject WILLIAM DIAN. Subject WILLIAM was immediately brought to the NBI-NCR for post-operation processing and was presented for inquest proceedings at the National Prosecution Service, Department of Justice (DOJ). Subject opted a Preliminary Investigation waiving his rights under Article 125 of the Revised Penal Code. He was turned over to SMD for custody. • On October 3, 2017, operatives of NBI-Cagayan Valley District Office (NBI-CAVRO) rescued KATRINA SAMAYO SISON, 16 years old from the custody of JOHN CHRISTIAN DE LEON. Abrera and Dr. Carol Dell Villanueva against NUNILON JULIA PANTE-OLBES, CAROL GALICIA VERDEJO, RALPH ARCILLA, JOVENCIO ARCILLA and LOLITA REGNIM LOMBOY for violation of R.A. 9484 otherwise known as the Philippine Dental Act of 2007. Subject HAMIDON has been a person of interest to authorities since she gained international notoriety in the middle of 2016 when she successfully recruited several Indian nationals to come to the Philippines and join the radical Islamic extremist groups in Mindanao. ABU SHARIFA, the former leader of the ANSAR KHALIFA PHILIPPINES (AKP), a group responsible in the September 2016 Davao City night market bombing in cooperation with the MAUTE Group, as well as the failed attempt to bomb the US Embassy in Manila last December 2016. body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today announced the seizure of fake Coppermask by the NBI-National Capital Region (NBI-NCR) in several stores located in the City of Manila and Pasay, and a warehouse in Biñan, Laguna. NBI Officer-in-Charge (OIC)- Director Eric B. Distor said that the operation stemmed from a complaint by JC Premiere Business International, requesting investigative assistance and enforcement actions to stop the proliferation and distribution of counterfeit/fake Coppermask products. NBI-NCR requested for Search Warrants against the subject stores and warehouse for violation of trademark Infringement under R.A. 8293, which were granted and issued by RTC Branch 46 of Manila. Thus, on February 4, 2020, NBI-NCR implemented seven (7) Search Warrants against several stores in Binondo, Manila and Pasay City, and a warehouse located in Biñan, Laguna. The search was conducted in a peaceful and orderly manner in the presence of Respondents’ witnesses, Mall Security, and Barangay personnel. The operation resulted in the seizure of counterfeit/fake Coppermasks with an estimated value of Php 37,956,680.00.

body: PRESS STATEMENT August 5, 2022 NBI ARRESTS ONE FOR HUMAN TRAFFICKING AND CHILD PORNOGRAPHY Operatives of National Bureau of Investigation-Anti- Human Trafficking Division (NBI-AHTRAD) have arrested an individual in Cebu City for selling pornographic materials online. Arrested Subject was identified as ROMILO ROMERO. Subject ROMERO was arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from the report received by NBI-AHTRAD from the Department of Justice Inter-Agency Council Against Trafficking – Cyber-TIP Monitoring Center (DOJ IACAT-NBI CYBERTIP) regarding a certain individual behind a Twitter account @MarkjasonCj who is also using other social media platforms such as Telegram and Facebook to promote and sell self-produced videos of him performing sexual acts to male victims, some of whom are minors. NBI-AHTRAD and DOJ-IACAT NBI-CYBERTIP conducted cyber surveillance, which confirmed that ROMILO ROMERO, a resident of Bulacao, Cebu City, is the user of the Twitter account @MarkjasonCj who sells child pornographic materials through allowing access to channels containing said materials to paying clients. Operatives also found out that ROMERO was offering young males to paying customers for meetups in Cebu and cybersex. Armed with a Warrant to Search, Seize, and Examine Computer Data (WSSECD) issued by RTC of Cebu Branch 11, a team composed of NBI-AHTRAD and NBI-Central Visayas Regional Office (NBI-CEVRO), in coordination with the DOJ-IACAT, IACAT Region VII, DSWD Region VII, and with the support of the NGO partners from the International Justice Mission Region VII, proceeded to Sitio Cabancalan II, Bulacao, Cebu City on July 29, 2022 and successfully arrested ROMILO ROMERO. Subject was arrested in flagrante delicto offering an individual for sexual intercourse in exchange for a sum of money, and selling child pornographic materials in violation of Section 5(b) of RA 9208 as amended by RA 11862 and RA 9775 otherwise known as “Anti-Child Pornography Act of 2009 in relation to RA 10175 or the Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012. Implementation of the WSSECD likewise resulted in the seizure of digital devices used by Subject ROMERO in committing the illegal acts. During the operation, one male victim was rescued and taken into custody.

body: The Information Division is pleased to submit herewith the significant cases of the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) for the following aforementioned period as follows: • On April 1, 2020, operatives of NBI-Tagum District Office (NBI-TAGDO) arrested VASQUEZ, BERNIE y MENDOZA for violation of RA 7394 (Consumer Protection Act) and RA 7581 (Price Act). The operation resulted in the seizure of 2,150 pieces of dust mask sold at Php 110 per piece and 100 gallons of hand sanitizer sold at Php 1,250 per gallon, all amounting to Php 361,500. Cases for the above-mentioned violations were filed against the Subjects. • On April 1, 2020, operatives of NBI-Cordillera Administrative Region (NBI-CAR) arrested RUNNELLE MERCADO y MADAYAG for violation of RA 7581 as amended by RA 10623, RA 7394 and DOH Dept. Order No.2020-0133. Subject was selling ethyl alcohol at Php 190 per liter way beyond the ceiling price of Php 74.25 per 500ml. Seized from the Subject were 63 pieces of the aforementioned products. Subject was presented for inquest before the Prosecutor’s Office concern for his final disposition. • On April 1, 2020, operatives of NBI-Northeastern Mindanao Regional Office (NBI-NEMRO) an entrapment operation against Subject Mark Luna who was allegedly involved in manufacturing unregistered and overpriced alcohol and was at that time, loading truck of aforesaid product right inside Narra Park Subdivision, Tigatto, Davao City. But while operatives was about to enter the said subdivision, subject security guards denied them entry despite the operatives’ compliance to their request to have quarantine footbath and hand sanitizing. They further interrogate the operatives about the latter’s purpose of going inside the said subdivision. Further, upon knowing that they will be conducting operation, the guards refused entry of the operatives telling them that they still need have to obtain approval from their superior. Because of the delay, Subject Mark Luna eluded arrest. This prompted the operatives to check the status of the guards and it was found out that subject guards have no license of issued firearms, the Duty Detail presented was expired and there was no Monthly Disposition Report to justify their authority to render duty. These lapses resulted in their arrest. Subject guards were presented for inquest at City Prosecution Office, Davao City for Obstruction of Justice and violations of RA 5487 and RA 10591. • On April 2, 2020, operatives of NBI-Central Visayas Regional Office (NBI-CEVRO) arrested JEREMY PANTALEON CANO in entrapment operation for violation of RA 7581 (Price Act of 1992). Five (5) units of non-contact IR Thermometer with a total value of Php 29,500.00 were seized in the operation. • On April 2, 2020, operatives of NBI-Central Mindanao Regional Office (NBI-CEMRO) arrested JONAH BIODES CABIGAS and ALEX JOEY PORCELIN ABUGADIL were arrested in entrapment operation for violation of RA 7581 as amended by RA 10623 in relation to RA 10175, and RA 7394 in relation to RA 10175. Subjects were caught in the act of selling overpriced alcohol-based sanitizing solution and sanitizing gel and in possession of Sodium Ascorbate C Plus and Honey C Orange Flavored Drink Mix. Seized in the operation were sanitizing gel, sanitizing solution, sodium ascorbate C plus, and Honey C Orange Drink Mix with a total amount of Php 186,250.00 were likewise seized in the operation. • On April 2, 2020, operatives of NBI-Central Visayas Regional Office (NBI-CEVRO), arrested JOHER LAWAS ARDON in entrapment operation for violation of RA 7581 (Price Act of 1992). Four (4) pieces of non-contact IR Thermometer worth Php 23,600 were seized in the operation. • On April 2, 2020, operatives of NBI-CALABARZON arrested MANALO, JANET and ORETGA RUEL y MIRASOL in entrapment operation for violation of RA 7581 and RA 7394. Seized from the Subjects were alcohol products which they sold at Php 100,610 when the DOH price is only at Php 50,300. Charges were filed against the Subjects. • On April 2, 2020, operatives of NBI-Naga District Office (NBI-NADO) arrested MARILOU REGIDOR y ANTONIO, MARLON REGIDOR y ANTONIO and JOSE BARRAMEDA y BASCO in entrapment operation for violation of RA 7581 and RA 7394. Seized in the operation were 55 gallons of ethyl alcohol with an estimated amount of Php 35,750. • On April 2, 2020, operatives of NBI-CALABARZON arrested BALITA, MELODY y LAYGO and BALITA, ALDRIAN y MAGADIA for violation of RA 7581. Subjects were arrested in entrapment operation which stemmed from the information about the alleged selling in Padre Garcia, Batangas of rubbing alcohol without brand name and by more than twice the government-mandated price. Seized from the Subjects were alcohol products with an estimated value of Php 13,640. Case will be directly filed relative to the Department Order No.008-C. • On April 2, 2020, operatives of NBI-Western Visayas Regional Office (NBI-WEVRO), together with the Food and Drugs Administration (FD) conducted joint-inspection operation on several drugstores/pharmacy in Iloilo City. Found in Super Value Pharmacy located at Huervana St., Lapaz, Iloilo City were thirteen (13) gallons/234 liters of suspected alcohol. When the owner, NANCY L. CHUA, was asked, she explained that the said items were intended to someone who will distribute them to a certain Local Government Unit. However, she refused to reveal who the said person was. She also failed to show delivery receipts to show that she brought the said alcohol from a manufacturer or other supplier. Further, she refused to give any information as to its source. The FDA then took custody of the said items pending their investigation as to its content and as to whether the manufacturer thereof is registered with their office or not. Meanwhile, NANCY L. CHUA was invited to the NBI office to shed light on the circumstances surrounding the presence of the said suspected alcohol with that volume in their drug store. • On April 3, 2020, operatives of NBI-Northeastern Mindanao Regional Office (NBI-NEMRO) arrested MARICHU ARIAS y SAMOCENO and JASMIN AQUINO y JUMAMOY in entrapment operation for violation of RA 7581 (Price Act) in relation to DTI Memorandum Circular No.20-7 and DOH Memorandum No.2020-0131, in relation to RA 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act). Seized from the Subjects were 16 pieces KN95 face masks sold at Php 235 per piece, 18 pieces blue disposable face masks sold at disposable face masks and 40 pieces washable cloth masks. Subjects were presented for inquest before the City Prosecutor’s Office, Cagayan de Oro City. • On April 3, 2020, operatives of NBI-Cabanatuan District Office (NBI-CABDO) arrested RODOLFO SANTIAGO y DELA CRUZ in entrapment operation for selling overpriced alcohol. Around 11 containers of 1 gallon, 16 containers of 1 liter and 4 containers of ½ gallon of isopropyl alcohol were seized from the Subject’s possession. The said items have no appropriate price tag, label or marking publicly displayed to indicate price. Subjects also failed to present pertinent documents authorizing him to engage in such business. Documents are now being prepared for inquest proceedings before Cabanatuan City Prosecutor’s Office, Nueva Ecija for violation of RA 7581 and RA 7394. • April 3, 2020, operatives of NBI-Southeastern Mindanao Regional Office (NBI-SEMRO) arrested JUAN AMORIO PADILLA JR., TEODORO E. SAMORANO JR., PANFILO REY TINGCON DE GUZMAN, LEO RUSTAN MORDENO PLAZA, ERNESTO CABARABAN SAPSAL, BENJIE PELAGO AMBAT, and NORBERTO SEVILLA PIELAGO for illegal gambling in violation of RA 9287 in relation to Davao Region Covid-19 Task Force Order No. 2020-007 which enjoined mass gathering and encouraging social distancing. Subjects were caught in flagrante delicto playing madjong and card game tong its. Gambling bets and the gambling paraphernalia were confiscated. Subjects were presented for inquest before the City Prosecutor, Davao City. • April 3, 2020, operatives of NBI-Southeastern Mindanao Regional Office (NBI-SEMRO) arrested MONIQUE AYVILE LAYNO and CIRILO SOCRATES CADAYONA JR., Chief Executive Officers of MNQ Skincare Laboratory. The Bureau of Food and Drug Administration, invoking its visitorial power to conduct inspection on factories producing health products, sought the assistance of the NBI for the purpose of conducting laboratory/factory inspection at MNQ Skincare Laboratory in Juna Subd., Matina, Davao City. After the inspection, the FDA certified that MNQ has no license to operate though it has LTO at Soroptimist, Jacinto St., Davao City. The FDA further noted that the liquid foot soap and hand sanitizer manufactured and marketed by MNQ have no Certificate of Product Notification from their office. Subjects were presented for inquest before the City Prosecutor’s Office, Davao City for violation of RA 3720 and RA 11469. • On April 4, 2020, operatives of NBI-Central Luzon Regional Office (NBI-CELRO) arrested GILBERT TIQUI y TORRICOR and MIKE TAASAN for selling overpriced alcohol. Subjects were arrested in entrapment operation which stemmed from a report of FDA and concerned citizen that Daitso Convenience Store is selling, distributing, and/or displaying 70% ethanol rubbing alcohol products at a very excessive amount beyond suggested retail price. The said alcohol was sold at Php 479 per 500ml when it is supposed to be sold at Php Php 61-74 on the SRP per DTI and DOH Memorandum No. 2020-0058. Subjects will be subjected for inquest before the City Prosecutor’s Office, Angeles City, Pampanga for violation of RA 7581 and RA 7394. • On April 14, 2020, operatives of NBI-Cybercrime Division (NBI-CCD) arrested JAYSON DELA CRUZ y NARCISO and KEVIN MARMOLEJO y LIZARDO for violations RA 8484 (Access Devices Regulation Act of 1998) in relation to RA 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012). Subjects were arrested in entrapment operations which stemmed from the report that a certain JAYSON CRUZ y NARCISO posted an advertisement on Facebook offering to purchase access devices for online banking accounts for a fee. The two Subjects were engaged in the wholesale purchase of access devices that does not have legitimate or lawful purpose, were guilty of violating RA 8484 (Access Device Regulation Act). The only reason for procuring these access devices is to perpetrate their fraudulent schemes by having the means to store or withdraw their stolen funds. Subjects DELA CRUZ and MARMOLEJO were presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the Chief City Prosecutor, Quezon City.
