body: PRESS STATEMENT November 8, 2022 NBI ARRESTS A PRIEST FOR QUALIFIED SEDUCTION The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) announced the arrest of a priest in Solana, Cagayan by operatives of NBI-Cagayan Valley District Office (NBI-CAVRO). Arrested Subject was identified as FATHER KAROLE REWARD ISRAEL y UBINA. Subject was arrested in an operation which stemmed from the complaint of the victim. Accompanied by her parents, the victim reported before the NBI-CAVRO that Subject called her demanding for sexual favor otherwise he will post publicly the videos he obtained during their sexual encounter. On October 18, 2022, operatives proceeded to Solana, Cagayan where Subject and victim agreed to meet. At around 7:35pm, a Toyota pick-up arrived and fetched the victim. Operatives tailed the said vehicle until they arrived at an uninhabited rice field located at Brgy. Iraga near Iraga Elementary School and Iraga Presbyterian Church, Solana, Cagayan Valley. When the pick-up vehicle then parked in a dark area, operatives immediately rushed and peacefully approached the vehicle. A male individual, identified as FATHER KAROLE, opened the window at the driver’s side. Subject, who was about to abuse the victim, was neutralized and arrested. Subject was brought to NBI-CAVRO office for the standard booking procedures and was presented for inquest proceedings before the Provincial Prosecutor’s Office of Tuguegarao for violation of Article 337 (Qualified seduction) of the Revised Penal Code, RAv 9995 (Anti-Photo and Video Voyeurism Act of 2009), and RA 7610 (Special Protection of Children Against Abuse, Exploitation and Discrimination Law).

body: Sustained sleuthing and cyber technology led to the arrest by the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) agents of two men engaged in fraudulent game fowl deals through the internet in Cebu City recently. The suspects are identified as: JADE BARIA CATALAN resident of Sitio Seaside, Brgy. Poblacion, Compostela, Cebu and ROGER LAVADOR MORRE resident of Sitio Aegis, Brgy. Poblacion, Compostela, Cebu. Investigation conducted by NBI-Computer Crimes Division (CCD) disclosed that on February 14, 2013, the NBI received a complaint from Rafael P. Campos, Edwin N. Aranez and Harold D. Natalia that certain persons introducing themselves as Edwin N. Aranez (later on identified as Jade Catalan) and Roger Morre who pretended to be owners of Red Gamefarm, one of the top five breeders. However, the real owners of Red Gamefarm are Aranez and Campos. Suspects Morre and Catalan created a fake facebook account in the name of Red Gamefarm with URL/Link redgamefarm99 and sold Game fowls and Pullets. They sold game fowls and pullets but upon receipt of payment from buyer-victims through LBC, they did not delivered the purchased items. Catalan used photographs of Aranez and his family taken from the magazine “Pitgames” where the Red Gamefarm was featured. Most of the victims are Overseas Filipino Workers (OFWs) in USA, Canada and Middle East. In October 2012, Complainant Natalia who happens to be a friend of Aranez and Campos paid through LBC P10,000.00 for the pullet, but did not received the same. In late February this year, Natalia using another name made a deal with Morre and Catalan. Thus, the NBI-CCD arranged for an entrapment of the duo in which payment will be received by suspects at the LBC Liloan Branch in Cebu. In the morning of February 28, 2013, NBI-CCD agents proceeded to the LBC Liloan Branch, and positioned themselves inside. They waited for the name of Morre to be called to receive payment. Some moments later, his name was called and received the marked P1,000.00. The NBI operatives approached Morre and subsequently apprehended him. Afterwards, Morre revealed his principal Jade Catalan who instructed him to claim the money. A follow-up operation led to the arrest of Catalan. Both are detained at the NBI Cebu Office. Charges for Violation of Art. 315 RPC, otherwise known as Fraud/Estafa, and Violation of Republic Act 8792, otherwise known as “Electronic Commerce Act of 2000” were recommended against the two suspect before the Provincial Prosecutor of Cebu.

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today announced the arrest of two (2) individuals by the NBI- Rizal District Office (NBI-RIZDO) in Parañaque City for human trafficking. NBI Officer-in-Charge (OIC)- Director Eric B. Distor identified the arrested subjects as Spouses KONG, MA. ANGELICA y BELGA and KONG, XIANGCE (Chinese national). OIC Director Distor said the operation also resulted in the rescue of twenty (20) women-victims of whom 2 have been identified by the NBI as minors. Distor said that the operation stemmed from an intelligence report that a group of unidentified individuals are engaged in prostitution and human trafficking activities, particularly sexual exploitation of minor victims. According to the report, booking of women for sexual services is done through messaging in private group chats intended solely for Chinese Customers. In addition, the said group operates in NCR plus bubble area for easier transporting of women, as they are reportedly housed in an exclusive village in Parañaque City. One of the NBI-RIZDO operatives established communication with the subjects by sending a message through a contact given by the informant through mobile messaging app TELEGRAM as to the sexual services being offered. Subjects sent a ready list of prices of the sexual services being offered written in Chinese language. NBI-RIZDO requested the assistance of Destiny Rescue Philippines, an NGO which rescue children from sexual exploitation and human trafficking. After confirming that human trafficking activities are being committed by the operator/s of private group chat in TELEGRAM, an entrapment operation ensued. With the help of a Chinese translator, NBI-RIZDO was able to secure a booking. Both the poseur-customer and subject agreed to meet in a motel in Pasay City. Thus, two teams of NBI-RIZDO operatives were dispatched. One in the agreed motel in Pasay City wherein the poseur-customer went inside the room and after giving the pre-arranged signal, the rest of the first team immediately stormed in the room and rescued the victim who was being offered to perform sexual services. The other team proceeded to an exclusive village in Parañaque City where the other girls are reported to be housed, maintained, and offered for sexual services. After confirming with the victim earlier rescued, that the girls are being advertised for prostitution through a private group chat Telegram app, the second team immediately stormed the accommodation house and arrested Subjects Spouses KONG which also led to the rescue of the other 19 female victims, 2 of whom were later identified as minors. In the conduct of post-operation processing, 2 of the rescued victims were found to be positive for COVID-19 rapid antigen test that was conducted on them. All occupants of the accommodation house including the arrested subjects were recommended to be placed under quarantine pending the result of their RT-PCR tests.

body: With a long and colorful history as the country’s premier investigative agency, the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) will celebrate its 78th founding anniversary in simple but fitting ceremonies at the main office in Manila on November 13, 2014. The theme for this year’s celebration is “Makabagong NBI Tungo sa Katotohanan at Katarungan”. The celebration, which, started with a Painting and Photo Exhibit on November 3 and will run until December 5, was hosted by the NBI-Investigators Mutual Benefit Association, Inc. (NBI-IMBAI) in a joint collaboration with the Unified Women Artists Association of the Philippines (UWAAP). Organized and spearheaded by Ms. Ligaya Banawan of the Photography and Printing Section – Laboratory Division, the exhibit was participated in by NBI artists including Ms. Ligaya Banawan, photographers and guest artists such as Menchu Arandilla, Minerva Dacanay, Liz Tarnate, Nick Masangkay, Vince Jaudian, Erin Locsin, Buboy Dinapo, and other invited artists. The Guest Speaker for the event was Mr. Mario P. Marcos of GO JT Trading Realty Marketing Development Corporation while the invocation and welcome remarks were given by Ms. Banawan and Deputy Director for Forensic Investigation Service Rafael Marcos Ragos, respectively. On the same occasion, a photo competition was held and joined in by NBI employees including artists and photographer-participants in the exhibit. The competition was divided into two (2) categories, namely: conventional and mobile photography. Adjudged winners in the photo contest were: “Human Shield” by Antonio Estabillo; Conventional category; “Modernizing Equipments” by TJC Munar, Mobile category; “NBI Leaders for Truth or Justice” by Esperidion G. Curugan; and “The Crime Scene Skecher” by Tony Estabillo, Special Prize, Most Popular Conventional. P500 consolation prizes were given to “Wacky” by Joy Garcia; “Bosing Deep Thought” by Ligaya Banawan; “Forensic Chemist In Action” by Antonio Estabillo; “Balolong Case” by Carl Lisboa and “Multi-Tasking Photographer in Action” by GS G. Orbeta. A badminton tournament was held on November 5 at the NBI gym while the volleyball tournament will begin on November 6 also at the gym. On November 7 – 8, 2014, there will be a Fun Shoot co-sponsored by Mac-Mac Firing Range in Pulilan, Bulacan. Said event is open to all NBI personnel, guests and celebrities and the same will be held at Mac-Mac Firing Range in Pulilan, Bulacan. The following day, November 8, 2014, there will be a Fun Run to be followed by a Zumba exercise at the NBI Gymnasium. The Bureau will also hold a week-long bazaar – “tiangge” on November 10-14, 2014 in the holding area of the Clearance Section sponsored by the NBI Employees Association (NBIEA). A Golf Tournament will also be held on November 15, 2014 at the Fontana (Korea Country Club), Clark Free Port Zone, Clarkfield, Mabalacat City, Pampanga. In the morning of November 13, the anniversary of the creation of the NBI, a simple program at the NBI gym will be held with Honorable Feliciano Belmote, Jr, Speaker of the House of Representatives, as Guest of Honor to give the Keynote Address. He will be introduced by NBI Director Virgilio L. Mendez. Department of Justice Secretary Leila M. De Lima, on the other hand, will deliver the DOJ Secretary’s message. In the afternoon of the same day, the annual NBI command conference will be held until the following day. Regional Directors, Agents-in-Charge and Division Chiefs of Manila-based units of all services are expected to attend the two-day conference.

body: PRESS STATEMENT June 27, 2024 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } The National Bureau of Investigation-Human Trafficking Division (NBI-HTRAD) arrested two individuals in Quezon City for sexual exploitation of a minor. The case stemmed from a referral received by NBI-HTRAD from “The Exodus Road”, a Non-Governmental Organization, about telegram users “AYVAH” and “YNA” who were allegedly offering sexual-video recorded content and live sexual shows to foreign customers for Php 25,000.00 per transaction. Investigation and verification of HTRAD operatives, revealed that there was a continuing offer of the minor victim by Subjects for sexual exploitation in exchange for a certain amount of money. Upon instruction of newly-appointed NBI Director Jaime B. Santiago, an entrapment and rescue operation was conducted on June 25, 2024 by HTRAD operatives, together with NBI-Evidential Multimedia Division (NBI-EMD) and assistance of Exodus Road, DOJ-NBI-CyberTIP Monitoring Center, DOJ-IACAT, and Social Workers of Social Service Development Department Quezon City. The operation resulted in the arrest of Subjects “YNA” and “SAM” who were caught in flagrante delicto offering the minor victim for sexual exploitation. Victim was transported from Navotas to Quezon City to do live sexual shows. Arrested Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings for violations of RA 11862 (Expanded Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2022), RA 11930 (Anti-Online Sexual Abuse or Exploitation of Children and Anti-Child Sexual Abuse or Exploitation Materials Act), and RA 7610 (Special Protection of Children Against Abuse, Exploitation, and Discrimination Act). Rescued child victim was turned over to the social workers of SSDD Quezon City for custody. Director Santiago expressed his gratitude to the NGO, Exodus Road and other partner organizations for bringing the matter to the attention of the NBI, adding “the NBI will continue to be relentless in its drive against human trafficking and the exploitation of children as well as all other crimes”.

body: PRESS STATEMENT October 03, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } The National Bureau of Investigation-National Capital Region (NBI-NCR), under the leadership of Director Judge Jaime B. Santiago (Ret.), arrested an individual in Cubao, Quezon City on September 30, 2025, for an illegal investment scheme targeting pensioners. The operation stemmed from a complaint filed before the NBI-NCR regarding an alleged illegal investment scheme targeting pensioners and other individuals. The group, led by Subject DOMINGA SUPNET MEJIA, solicited funds from the public, promising high returns but operating without the necessary license from the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC). According to the complainant, their group’s lump sum pension of Php 900,000.00 was entrusted to Subject Mejia, leaving only Php 120,000.00 with them. Complainant’s attempts to recover her money were unsuccessful, as the funds were allegedly controlled by Mejia. Further investigation revealed that several other individuals were similarly defrauded by Mejia’s group, which operated without SEC authorization to solicit investments. The group’s modus operandi involved recruiting investors to finance loans for supposed retired soldiers, collecting processing fees, and misappropriating the proceeds, while providing only minimal returns to investors and borrowers. Acting on the complaint, an entrapment operation was organized in a mall in Cubao, Quezon City, which resulted in the arrest of Subject Mejia after she received Php 1,000,000.00, consisting of cash and a check, from the complainant. Based on the certification from the SEC, Company Registration and Monitoring Department, DS MEJIA DOCUMENTS FACILITATION SERVICE is neither registered as a corporation nor a partnership. Furthermore, it has not been issued any secondary license as a Lending Company, Broker and/or Dealer of Securities, Dealer in Government Securities, Investment Adviser of an Investment Company, Investment House, or Transfer Agent, and it has not neither filed nor has any pending application for such alicense. The SEC Certification also states that DOMINGA SUPNET MEJIA has not been issued a Certificate of Registration as a registered Associated Person, Compliance Officer, Salesman and/or Certified Investment Solicitor of a Broker Dealer in Securities, Investment House, Underwriter of Securities, Investment Company Adviser, and/or Mutual Fund Distributor. Subject was presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor, Quezon City for violation of R.A. No. 11765 (Financial Products and Services Consumer Protection Act), Article 315 of the Revised Penal Code (Swindling/Estafa), as amended, and violation of Section 8 and Section 28 of Security Regulation Act of R.A. No. 8799. With the successful arrest of the Subject, Director Santiago reminds the public to exercise vigilance and verify the legitimacy of investment offers before entrusting their hard-earned money.

body: A suspect with a standing Warrant of Arrest for Murder was arrested by agents of the National Bureau of Investigation – Iligan District Office (NBI-ILDO) together with elements of the 65th Infantry Batallion, Philippine Army recently. NBI Director Virgilio L. Mendez identified the suspect as: SANSARONA ABUBACAR GUMAMA a.k.a. ACMAD PANGAGA OTI NBI-Iligan District Office (NBI-ILDO) headed by Atty. Alex Carbornay assisted by elements of 65th Infantry Batallion, Philippine Army conducted an operation on 01 July 2014 in the vicinity of Pantao-Raya, Saguiran, Lanao del Norte to implement several Warrants of Arrest against a reported hired killer/hitman who has several criminal records. The said operation resulted in the successful arrest of SANSARONA ABUBACAR GUMAMA a.k.a. ADMAD PANGAGA OTI. The principal suspect in the failed ambush on the former Mayor of Pantao Ragat, Lanao del Sur and now incumbent Vice-Mayor of same Municipality. Recovered from his possession is one M16 Armalite Rifle with twenty-three (23) live ammunitions and one (1) magazine. Furthermore, Subject has a standing Warrant of Arrest for Murder pending at Branch 41,RTC of Cagayan De Oro City for killing a certain Deomedez Chavez and a pending warrant for FRUSTRATED MURDER for fatally wounding a certain Roy Chavez and Ruel Espinosa. He also has a pending case for Illegal Possession of Firearm at a court in Marawi City. Subject was immediately brought to Cagayan de Oro City where a commitment order was issued by the Court for his detention in the Provincial Jail of Misamis Oriental, Provincial Capitol Compound, Cagayan de Oro City. Charges for possession of M16 Armalite Rifle, and Illegal Use of Alias and Surname as well as Falsification of Public Documents is set to be filed against the suspect.

body: PRESS STATEMENT May 04, 2022 DISTOR TO LEAD NBI MID-TERM COMMAND CONFERENCE The NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION (NBI) will hold its Mid-Term Command Conference tomorrow, Thursday, May 05, 2022 at the NBI Head office at V-Tech Tower in Quezon City. NBI OIC-Director ERIC B. DISTOR will lead top officials of the premier investigative agency of the government in a one-day Command Conference to report on the status and developments on the NBI Modernization Program and Post-pandemic initiatives undertaken by the Agency. DISTOR will be joined by the members of the Directorial Staff composed of Assistant Directors and Deputy Directors of the different Services, namely: Investigative, Intelligence, Regional Operations, Forensic Investigation, Legal, Financial, Administrative and Information and Communication Technology. Also attending the Mid-Term Command Conference are the Regional Directors (RD) and Chief of Staff (COS) of all Services. Highlighting the Mid-Term Conference is an update on the Expansion and Establishment of District Offices (DOs) primarily aimed at bringing the services of the government, NBI in particular, to the people as mandated by President Rodrigo Roa Duterte. As of January 2022, the number of District Offices under the leadership of DISTOR has ballooned to 46 as against 22 DOs in 2016 prior to the passage of the NBI Modernization Law. Another highlight is the creation of the National Forensic Research Center and Procurement and Acquisition of modern technology and equipment in aid of forensic investigation being conducted by the NBI. In addition, an update on the Pandemic Experience and Post-Pandemic Initiatives will be rendered by the Forensic Investigation Service (FIS).

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) recommended the prosecution of two alleged caretakers of the Marcos assets, enticed 81 victims/investors and demanded money from them purportedly to have a share of the Marcos’ wealth. The suspects were identified as FELICISIMA FALTADO CANTOS, of 26 A. Jison St., EBS BF Homes, Parañaque City and EMMANUEL D. DESTURA, of 9F Pontiac St., Fairview, Quezon City. Investigation by the NBI disclosed that in January 2012, Destura and Cantos introduced themselves to complainants as caretakers of the assets of the late President Ferdinand E. Marcos amounting to billions of dollars. As such, they enduced them into investing in their company called Bullion Buyers Limited with office address in China, if they wanted to avail, claim or share the said wealth of Marcos. Further, suspects persuaded them to recruit more members nationwide so that accordingly, by numbers, they have their strength as claimants of the Marcos’ wealth and could have more share in the company. The prospects of gaining wealth through the persuasion of the duo, complainants/victims, mostly from Binmaley, Urdaneta, Lingayen City, Rosales in Pangasinan, and in Paniqui, Tarlac, found their offer irresistible in joining their company. Suspects demanded P2,000 from each investor in exchange for a Deed of Assignment stating that after 30 banking days, they would receive their share of the Marcos’ wealth or properties amounting from P5 million to US$5 million. However, after the lapse of the given time and despite several demands, Destura and Cantos failed to fulfill their promise and nowhere to be found. Hence, complainant Remedios Salango, and eighty (80) others trooped to the NBI and sought investigative assistance. Although, initially, nobody knew their whereabouts, verification with NBI files disclosed their addresses in Parañaque City and Fairview, Quezon City. Thus, subpoenas were sent to them but failed to honor the same. Subsequently, on March 19, 2013, cases were submitted for preliminary investigation for Syndicated Estafa against the suspects before the Office of the Provincial Prosecutors of Tarlac, Urdaneta, and Lingayen, Pangasinan.

body: PRESS STATEMENT September 03, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } In an effort to uphold the law and protect society by immediately addressing criminal activity, the National Bureau of Investigation – Antique District Office (NBI-ANDO), under the leadership of Director Judge Jaime B. Santiago (Ret.), brought three (3) individuals for inquest before the Antique Provincial Prosecutor’s Office: JOSE ROMEL CLAUDIO GALLANO CHAVEZ, JOSE DIORIC GEROGENE APAITAN CHAVEZ, and ANNALIZA GORERO AGUSTIN JAVIER, officers of GSD, an investment company operating in San Jose, Antique, were arrested by virtue of Warrantless Arrest. They face charges for violation of Article 315 of the Revised Penal Code in relation to Presidential Decree 1869 (Syndicated Estafa) and Republic Act No. 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012), and violation of Republic Act No. 8799 (The Securities Regulation Code). Investigation revealed that Subject enticed the public, mostly students and barangay residents, to join their financial investment scheme, promising high profits in a short period. Subjects told Complainants that a larger investment would lead to a more profitable return. GSD provided a computer platform for investors to monitor their accounts and earn profits by completing simple tasks. The company also offered promotion such as “double-your-money”, “commissions”, and “salary” for every member recruited. To create a semblance of legality, the Subjects operated from a legitimate-looking office, where they displayed their business permits their business, DTI registration, and BIR documents. The manager, JOSE ROMEL CHAVEZ, a teacher at St. Anthony’s College, allegedly took advantage of his position to persuade his students to invest. Furthermore, GSD allowed complainants to experience a few initial payouts, which earned the business a false sense of trustworthiness. However, after the victims poured more of their money into the scheme, the business suddenly collapsed, and they could no longer access their accounts. Subject Chavez operated from his office in San Jose, Antique, assisted by his co-principals, Subjects Jose Dioric Chavez and Annaliza Javier. Subjects defrauded the victims when they failed to deliver their promise to pay profits and interest on their investment. It was also discovered that GSD does not hold a secondary license from the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), which is required to solicit investments from the public; thus, violating the provisions of R.A. No. 8799. On August 30, 2025, approximately fifty (50) angry investors went to the NBI-ANDO to file their respective complaints and personally endorse the Subjects for formal charging and inquest. As of the latest update, this office has recorded ninety-five (95) complaints and counting. On September 01, 2025, Subjects were presented for Inquest Proceedings before the Office of the Provincial Prosecutor, San Jose, Antique, and are presently detained at the NBI-ANDO Detention Facility.

body: In line with the relentless campaign of the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) against trafficking, operatives of the NBI-International Airport Investigation Unit (IAIU) on July 24, 2018 arrested one Japanese national in Malate, Manila for alleged violations of Republic Act No. 6955 (Mail Order Bride or Matching Filipino Woman for Marriage) and RA No. 9208 as amended by RA No. 10364 (Expanded Trafficking in Persons Act of 2012). NBI Director Dante A. Gierran identified the arrested Subject as JIRO SAITO aka “Saito San” and “Ken Suzuki”, who facilitated the departure of the complainant Ma. body: A labor recruiter was arrested and four girls including a minor who were to work as Guest Relations Officers (GROs) in Pampanga were rescued by agents of the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) in Pampanga last Monday. NBI Director Nonnatus Caesar R. Rojas identified the suspect as: HERMINIGILDA HERMOSA MAÑALAC, 49, OF Habilan, Floridablanca, Pampanga. Investigation by the NBI Central Luzon Regional Office (CELRO) National Capital Region (NCR) headed by Acting Regional Director Atty. Jose Justo S. Yap disclosed that on May 21, 2013, the NBI received an intervention request in Cebu from the International Justice Mission (IJM), a non-government organization handling cases involving human trafficking and sexual exploitation of women and children about the case of two women who were enticed to work in Pampanga but ended up in a bar as GRO. Accordingly, two sisters, aged 17 and 22 were recruited by a certain “Jacklyn” in Cebu City to work in a bar in Pampanga City. When the girls arrived, they were turned over to a “mama-san,” (maintainer), Jacklyn’s sister, Hilda. They were told that they were going to be GROs at Princess Refreshment supposedly located at Basa Airbase, Florida Blanca, Pampanga and would provide their services to customers. The girls resented and refused to work, and thus, the two girls were padlocked in a room with a guard posted nearby. One of the sisters, “Nene” (not her real name) was able to contact her mother through her cell phone begging to be rescued. This prompted the mother to contact IJM who in turn referred the matter to the NBI on May 21, 2013. After validating the report to be true, a rescue operation was planned in the evening of same date. NBI operatives, together with some DSWD personnel went to the Princess Refreshment bar. They found Nene and her sister, and after securing them, a pre-arranged signal was made for the NBI operatives to rush inside. Consequently, suspect Hilda was arrested, and the two sisters, together with two others, one of them a minor, were rescued. They were turned over to DSWD for custody and disposition. Suspect Hilda was brought to the NBI-CELRO where she was booked and fingerprinted. Charges for Human Trafficking in relation to RA 7610 was filed against the suspect before Provincial Prosecutor’s Office, City of San Fernando, Pampanga.

body: On October 1, 2018 , operatives of NBI-Cybercrime Division (NBI-CCD) arrested LEO ANGELO TORIO RIVERA at General Trias, Cavite by virtue of Warrant of Arrest for the crime of Rape (no bail). The arrest was based on the letter request of Edgardo Balabis of Caloocan City to serve the Warrant of Arrest issued by RTC Branch 89, Quezon City against the Subject. Information was received that Subject was sighted in his residence at General Trias, Cavite so on the above-mentioned-date, NBI-CCD operatives proceeded to the area and served the said warrant. Subject was brought to NBI Manila for the booking procedures and was subsequently detained at the NBI Jail. On October 2, 2018 , operatives of NBI-International Operations Division (NBI-IOD) arrested MARYLOU OLIVAY y FABITO, MERRYCAR BAUTISTA y FERNANDEZ de NEGAD, VIVIAN PULIA y GUIRUELA de BERONIO, and JUSTIN CO y MELLAN in Carmona, Cavite for human trafficking and child abuse. The case stemmed from the complaint filed against the managers and supervisors of EVER FORTUNE RECYCLE CORP. (EVER FORTUNE), a domestic corporation located at Brgy. Bancal, Carmona, Cavite which endeavors in recycling plastic. According to one complainant, who worked at Ever Fortune for six (6) years as classifier, her daughter also worked as a classifier after her morning class from the afternoon to about 7:00 in the evening. Her daughter had to work to defray the rent charged amounting to Php 300.00 per child every week for each family housed in their living quarters. Another complainant, a former driver of Ever Fortune, added that his three minor children also had to work in order to defray the cost of rent. The two (2) complainants together with their families, were all dismissed from work and prevented from entering Ever Fortune premises immediately after the management learned that they went to the Department of Labor and Employment (DOLE) to file a complaint for underpayment, absence of work benefits and inhumane working conditions. On October 2, 2018, NBI-IOD operatives together with representatives from DSWD and DOLE entered the premises of Ever Fortune and found thereat were minors. Subjects JUSTIN CO, the manager, MARYLOU OLIVAY, supervisor, MERRYCAR BAUTISTA, crusher-in-charge, and VIVIAN PULIA, secretary of Ever Fortune were arrested and brought to the NBI for the booking procedures. Fourteen (14) individuals were rescued of whom thirteen (13) are minors, as confirmed by dental examination. Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings for violations of RA 9208 as amended by RA 10364 (Expanded Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2012) and RA 7610 (Special Protection of Children Against Abuse, Exploitation and Discrimination Act). On October 3, 2018 , operatives of NBI-Dumaguete District Office (NBI-DUMDO) arrested JOSEPH ALBERT LIM y RAGOT for violation of RA 8048 (Coconut Preservation Act of 1995) as amended by RA 10593 and violation of RA 9175 (Chainsaw Act of 2002). The case stemmed from an information received that there was cutting of coconut trees at Purok Pag-asa, Banilad, Dumaguete City. Upon verification of the information, NBI operatives encountered a chariot carriage carrying several pieces of coco lumbers parked in the way and saw traces of coconut trees that were cut down. Subject, who was engrossed in processing the coco trunk into pieces using a chainsaw, was left in the area. Upon inquiry, it was found out that he has not secured a permit to cut trees, no permit to use a chainsaw, and no delivery receipt to transport the coco lumber products with the Philippine Coconut Authority. After informing the Subject of his violations, operatives placed him under arrest. Certification issued by the Philippine Coconut Authority (PCA) states that there was no permit to cut coconut trees issued to the Subject. Another certification states that Subject is not a registered coconut lumber processor/dealer. Subject was presented for inquest proceedings for the above-mentioned violations. On October 4, 2018 , operatives of NBI-Dumaguete District Office (NBI-DUMDO) arrested JOVER ACADEMIA y YUCOR GEORGE ISO y ZERNA for illegal extraction of sands and minerals in Bacong, Negros Oriental without necessary permits and licenses. The operation was conducted based on the verified information that alleged illegal extraction of sand and gravel were being done in the vicinity of Brgy. Sulodpan, Brgy. Isugan and Brgy. Combado, Bacong, Negros Oriental and other areas of Valencia, Negros Oriental. Subjects were caught with their vehicles loaded with sand. Laborers were able to scamper away as operatives were approaching. Meanwhile, appropriate charges were filed against the arrested Subjects. Follow up operation will be conducted in the vicinity and other areas where sand and gravel were allegedly being extracted. On October 5, 2018 , operatives of NBI- Anti-Organized and Transnational Crime Division (NBI-AOTCD) arrested MANUEL BALA y VALDELLON for falsification of documents. The case stemmed from a letter of Isaiah Roland II, Attache, US Department of State, Diplomatic Security Service, Overseas Criminal Investigations (OCI), requesting assistance in the investigation of Kevin Keith Fajardo and Jarra Rowella, both applicants for a tourist visa as a married couple and were scheduled for interview. However, based on the investigation conducted by OCI and as per Certificates of No Marriage (CENOMAR) from the Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA), they are not married. Thus, the passport of Jarra Fajardo is considered fraudulently obtained. Moreover, upon online DTI verification by the US Embassy, the business allegedly owned by Kevin is not found. They were then confronted by US Embassy officials about the falsified documents they submitted and were thereafter referred to the NBI for investigation. According to Jarra and Kevin, the falsified documents were provided by Subject Manuel Bala who told them that it is easier for a married couple to get an approval for visa application, thus he paired the two. They also disclosed that they have a prior understanding with the Subject that they will meet in a hotel in Paco, Manila to get the purported original documents. With this, an entrapment operation was conducted resulting in the arrest of the Subject. Record check on the Subject revealed that he had served sentence for Falsification of public or official document in National Bilibid Prison. Subject was presented for inquest proceeding for violation of Article 172 (Falsification by Private Individual) in relation to Article 171 of the Revised Penal Code. On October 5, 2018 , operatives of NBI-Rizal District Office (NBI-RIZDO) seized Php 3.5 Million worth of counterfeit Penshoppe apparel products by virtue of Search Warrants. Charges for violation of RA 8293 (Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines) were filed against the owners, proprietors, employees, and occupants of various establishments located at New Galleria Baclaran Shopping Mall, Pasay City. On October 6, 2018 , composite elements of NBI-Ilocos Regional Office (NBI-IRO), NBI-Cagayan Valley District Office (NBI-CAVRO), NBI-Laoag District Office (NBI-LADO), NBI-Vigan District Office (NBI-VIDO), NBI-Cordillera Administrative Region (NBI-CAR), NBI-Dagupan District Office (NBI-DADO), and PDEA destroyed marijuana plants with a market value of Php 4.3 Million. The continuous wide scale marijuana eradication in the municipality of Tinglayan, Kalinga province resulted in the uprooting and destruction of 21,750 pieces of fully grown marijuana plants in five (5) plantation sites with an aggregate land area of 2,350 square meters. On October 8, 2018 , operatives of NBI-National Capital Region (NBI-NCR) arrested ROCHELLE LLARINA y BRESEMIO for Falsification of Private Documents and Estafa. The case stemmed from the complaint of Marilou Cruz and Fenelyn Liwanag, authorized representatives of UNITOP General Merchandise, Inc. against the Subject. Prior to their complaint, a certain Crizelle Shaddel M. Cedalla reported that Subject was issuing fake documents of UNITOP such as Identification Cards and Certificate of Employment (COE) for a fee. In order to verify the allegations, the NBI requested Crizelle Cedalla if she could secure a copy of her COE from the Subject. On October 4, 2018, Cedalla was able to get a copy of COE from the Subject for Php 1,000. According to the representatives of UNITOP, the COE of Cedalla which came from the Subject is falsified. With this, an entrapment operation was conducted in Sta. Rosa, Laguna resulting in the arrest of the Subject. Subject was presented for inquest before the Office of the City Prosecutor, Sta. Rosa, Laguna. On October 9, 2018 , operatives of NBI-Special Action Unit recovered two (2) carnapped vehicles owned by Mr. Robert R. Saluta, on October 9, 2018 at the parking lot of an establishment in Newport Boulevard, Pasay City. the operation was conducted based on the complaint filed by Mr. Saluta before the Bureau. Mr. Saluta, a businessman, asserted that sometime in August 25, 2018, at around 7:00pm, one of his customers, a certain ALELI FROILAN YAP called him and signify her intention to buy two vehicles, a 2013 model Mercedes Benz, G-550 (Bullet Proof Level B-6), and a 2015 model Toyota Land Cruiser (Bullet Proof Level B-6). Being a long time customer, he acceded to the request of Subject Aleli, to bring the vehicles to the latter’s house located at Pina St., Ayala, Alabang, for a test drive. Upon arrival, Mr. Saluta turned over the keys of the Mercedes Benz to Subject Aleli while the key to Land Cruiser was turned over to an unidentified person, a representative of Subject Aleli. Mr. Saluta was assured by Subject Aleli that she will return the vehicle after an hour, but to no avail. Efforts to contact Aleli thru her mobile phone and diligent effort to locate her whereabouts in her given address only proved futile. Interview conducted by NBI-SAU operatives to certain individuals revealed that the said vehicles was mortgaged in Resorts World Hotel and Casino, Pasay City. On October 9, 2018 , operatives of NBI-Cybercrime Division (NBI-CCD) arrested MARK LOUIE GALLIGUEZ y MORALES for computer-related identity-theft. The case stemmed from the complaint against the Subject who was misusing without right existing Facebook accounts owned by another users for his cybercriminal design. He manipulated these identities using their profile pictures and other information, to engage in online dating relationship with other users, posing himself as a female. Through this modus operandi, Subject was able to lure the complainant to engage in online relationship with his fake Facebook account. All the while, complainant thought that the relationship was a legitimate one that he was even made to support the Subject’s financial needs. During the entrapment operation, Subject was caught in flagrante in the act of collecting the money deposited by the complainant. Subject was then placed under arrest. When asked whether he owned the Facebook accounts in question, he explained that he only used and assumed those identities for online transactions. He further disclosed that he even used the ATM card of his grandmother in furtherance of his illicit enterprise. Subject was brought before the office of Inquest Prosecutor, Department of Justice for inquest proceeding. On October 9, 2018 , operatives of NBI-Cybercrime Division (NBI-CCD) arrested GERARD JOSEPH LIWAG for violation of RA 8484 (Access Device Regulation Act of 1998) in relation to RA 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012). The case stemmed from a complaint filed against the Subject for illegal use and production of ATM and credit cards. Based on the information received, the modus operandi of the group is to secure information and credit card details through call centers and other business establishment skimmers. Subject would contact the latter to ask for the expiry date and available credit limits and will activate the “Installment Option” for high value purchases to be approved upon usage of the credit card details. Using sophisticated gadgets, Subject is able to use cards for shopping. After series of surveillance, validation, verification, and documentation, Search Warrant was secured and on the aforementioned date, Subject was arrested as he was walking towards the main gate of a condominium tower in BGC, Taguig City. A search in Subject’s condominium unit resulted in the seizure of sophisticated gadgets used in his illegal activities such as HITI card printer, embossing machine, Fargo High Definition Printer, Removable Storage Device, Skimming Device, Laptops, Point-of-Sale Card Terminal, HUB (A4RTech), Java Blank Cards and Eighty (80) pieces of various cards. Also recovered were several identification cards including passports that are allegedly spurious and counterfeit. Subject was presented for inquest proceedings for the above-mentioned violations. On October 10, 2018 , operatives of NBI-Dumaguete District Office arrested SYMON CORDOVA in flagrante sniffing shabu. The arrest stemmed from the complaint against the Subject who was a notoriously known drug dependent. According to the complainant, Subject often goes violently crazy in front of their residence and would physically abuse his mother whenever the latter would refuse to give him money. On the aforementioned date, when the Subject got violent again, complainant contacted NBI DUMDO. Instantly, operatives proceeded at the complainant’s residence and caught the Subject in flagrante sniffing shabu in plain view with drug paraphernalia. Subject was then placed under arrest for violation of RA 9165 (Comprehensive Dangerous Drug Act of 2002). Subject was transferred to Dumaguete City Detention Facility. On October 15, 2018 , operatives of NBI-Anti-Organized and Transnational Crime Division arrested P/SUPT SALAVADOR C. DURAN JR. who has outstanding warrant of arrest for their conviction of violation of RA 3019 (Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act). Investigation conducted by the Ombudsman revealed that Subject DURAN, together with P/SUPT ARTURO MONTANO made possible the release of 100 checks worth Php 10,000,000.00 in favor of four (4) companies owned by MARGARITA B. TUGAOEN, the supposed supplier of combat, clothing, and individual equipment for the PNP CAPCOM. Graft investigators uncovered pieces of evidence that the abovenamed accused conspired with each other to make it appear that the Php 10,000,000.00 was released as payment for the CCIE, but in fact, no actual delivery delivery of CCIE was ever made to the PNP. Accordingly, they were convicted by the Sandiganbayan and were sentenced to 6 to 10 years imprisonment and were ordered to indemnify the PNP the amount of Php 10,000,000.00. When the NBI-AOTCD received reliable information as to the whereabouts of accused DURAN, operatives immediately dispatched that resulted to the arrest of DURAN at Maligaya Park, Novaliches, Quezon City. Report on the arrest of DURAN was forwarded to the Sandiganbayan. He is presently detained at the NBI detention cell awaiting for the commitment order from the Sandiganbayan. On October 18, 2018 , operatives of NBI-Laguna District Office (NBI-LAGDO) arrested VIVIAN ZAMORA DOLLESIN y PAUNILLAN, and EUGENIO MORANTE y SUNGALIA in Bicutan Public Market, Paranaque City for illegal jueteng operations. Subjects were arrested while collecting bets for jueteng. Seized from the Subjects’ possession are jueteng paraphernalia, fake Golden Era STL IDs and bet money. Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the Paranaque City Prosecutor Office for violation of RA 9287 (Illegal Gambling Law). On October 23, 2018 , operatives of NBI-Bulacan District Office (NBI-BULDO) arrested JHON V. ROCES and PEDRO BARRION MILAN for Syndicated Estafa. The case stemmed from the complaint of Teody C. San Andres, President of St. Andrew Publishing House. Subjects offered the complainant business proposal that the contract for the reprinting of Kindergarten and Grade 1 English Activity Sheets be produced abroad for less costing in which the Subjects specifically identified Shen Zhen Jinhao Color Printing Co., Ltd, Jing Hao Yi (HK) Trading Co. Finding the said company to be legitimate, complainant acceded to the project proposal of the Subjects. Subjects then instructed the complainant to deposit 50% down payment amounting to $50,000.00. However, the latter was able to deposit only $9,808.00. For more or less eight (8) months, complainant did not act a clear status of the project in China from the Subjects. They gave false information and kept on insisting for the Subject to pay the full amount. The complainant later found out the wrong doings of the Subjects. An entrapment operation was then conducted and resulted in the arrest of the Subjects. Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the Malolos City Prosecutor’s Office for violation of Article 315 (Syndicated Estafa) of the Revised Penal Code. On October 24, 2018 , operatives of NBI-Special Action Unit (NBI-SAU) arrested CRIS CABRIDO and MILABEL LAMATA for Large Scale Illegal Recruitment. Subjects were arrested after information about the illegal recruitment activities of the Subjects were gathered. With due coordination with the Philippine National Police and the management of Jollibee, SM Mall of Asia, NBI-SAU operatives proceeded to the location for the entrapment operation. The operation resulted in the arrest of the Subjects who were verified as not licensed or authorized by the Philippine Overseas Employment Administration (POEA) to recruit workers for overseas employment. Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the Pasay City Prosecutor Office for Large Scale Illegal Recruitment as defined under RA 8042 as amended by RA 10022 (Migrant Workers and Overseas Filipinos Act of 1995). On October 24, 2018, operatives of NBI-Environmental Crime Division (NBI-EnCD) arrested JODY MENDIORO y VILLAR, RODOLFO MANIQUIS y DOMINGO, NESTOR GALVES y HERNANDEZ, FERNANDO LOGRONIO y SALVE, JUAN FRANCISCO y CRUZ, and CEZAR RAMIREZ y VALDERAMA for illegal open dumpsite operation. The case stemmed from the complaint regarding an alleged illegal operation of an open dumpsite in Barangay Tanawan, Bustos, Bulacan. Surveillance of the area confirmed the said illegal activity. Verification of the records from the Department of Environment and National Resources-Environmental Management Bureau Region III (DENR-EMB III) disclosed that the operation of the open dumpsite is illegal and that no permits, licenses or grants were given to any person or entity to operate an open dumpsite in the Municipality of Bustos, Bulacan. Thus, NBI-EnCD operatives, together with the personnel of DENR-EMB III proceeded to the area and caught in flagrante delicto were the Subjects conducting the illegal activity. Subjects were presented before the Office of the Prosecutor General, National Prosecution Service, Department of Justice for violation of Section 37 (use of open dumpsite) and Section 48 (transportation and dumping in bulk of collected wastes) of RA 9003 otherwise known as the Ecological Solid Waste Management Act of 2000 and violation of Section 107 (Aquatic Pollution) of RA 8550 otherwise known as the Fisheries Code of the Philippines. On October 24, 2018 , operatives of NBI-National Capital Region (NBI-NCR) seized an estimated amount of Php 56 Million worth of counterfeit Lacoste and Herschel products by virtue of Search Warrants. Charges for violation of RA 8293 (Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines) were filed against Zeke General Merchandise located in 999 Shopping Mall, Binondo, Manila, Henny General Merchandise located in 168 Shopping Mall, Binondo, Manila, a warehouse in 999 shopping mall located in C.M. Recto Avenue, Manila, as well as various establishments/stores located in New Divisoria Mall, Tondo, Manila. On October 26, 2018 , operatives of NBI-National Capital Region (NBI-NCR) arrested MA. CONCEPCION YAPTINCHAY y CAIDO by virtue of Warrant of Arrest for Carnapping. Subject YAPTINCHAY was charged with violation of RA 6539 (Anti-Carnapping Law) at the RTC Branch 12, Manila. On the aforementioned date, NBI-NCR operatives went to Loyola Memorial Chapel, Makati City, during the wake of her father and served the Warrant of Arrest. Subject was thereafter brought to the NBI for the booking procedures. On October 29, 2018 , operatives of the NBI- Anti-Graft Division (NBI-AGD) arrested BERNADETTE BERNABE BADINAS for Large scale Swindling/Estafa. The case stemmed from the complaints regarding the unlawful scheme of the Subject. Complainant Madrid narrated that on March 2018 Subject Badinas invited them to put some investment in her financing business and promised to earn at least 10% monthly interest. Complainant Madrid then deposited a total amount of Php800,000.00 through her BDO account. Complainant Madrid further narrated that she was able to received interest through cash deposit in her BDO account but the Php45,000.00 and Php85,000.00 interest covered by UCPB checks bounced as manifested in the retuned checks. Complainant Madrid told the operatives of the NBI-AGD that she will meet Subject Badinas in a mall located at Sta. Cruz, Manila at around 4:00 in the afternoon to give the additional investment of Php30,000.00 on top of the initial investment of Php800,000.00. Thus, an entrapment operation was conducted resulting in the arrest of the Subject. Subject was brought for inquest before the City of Manila Prosecutors Office for violation of Article 315 of the Revised Penal Code. In six (6) successful operations, operatives of operatives of NBI-Intellectual Property Rights Division (NBI-IPRD) seized Php an estimated aggregate amount of Php 85.8 Million worth of counterfeit products. On October 1, 2018 , Php 12,000 worth of counterfeit medical books were seized in Valenzuela City. Charges for violation of RA 8293 (Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines) were filed against ANNIE RODRIGUEZ and ANNE RICARR RODRIGUEZ. On October 5, 2018 , Php 22 Million worth of counterfeit Under Armour products were seized in Binondo, Manila by virtue of Search Warrants. Charges for violation of RA 8293 (Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines) were filed against John/Jane Does, owners, occupants, proprietors of various stalls located at 168, 999, and 11/88 shopping malls in Binondo, Manila. On October 8, 2018 , Php 44.2 Million worth of counterfeit Louis Vuitton products were seized in Binondo and Malate, Manila by virtue of Search Warrants. Charges for violation of RA 8293 (Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines) were filed against John/Jane Does, owners/operators of various stalls located at 168 shopping mall in Binondo, Manila and Altra Center, Malate, Manila. On October 9, 2018 , Php 18.9 Million worth of counterfeit Kate Spade products were seized in Binondo, Manila by virtue of Search Warrants. Charges for violation of RA 8293 (Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines) were filed against the owners/operators of various stalls located at 999 shopping mall in Binondo, Manila. On October 10, 2018 , Php 200,000 worth of Power Tiger sinages, dispensing pumps and dispensing pumps overhead were seized in the cities of Valenzuela and Tarlac by virtue of Search Warrants. Charges for violation of RA 8293 (Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines) were filed against the owners/operators of Power Tiger Petroleum Corporation located in the said cities. On October 24, 2018 , Php 550,000.00 worth of unregistered cosmetic products were seized by virtue of Search Warrants. Charges for violation of RA 8293 (Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines) were filed against John/Jane Does, owners, occupants, proprietors of various stalls located at 168 and 999 shopping malls in Binondo, Manila.

On October 1, 2018 , operatives of NBI-Cybercrime Division (NBI-CCD) arrested LEO ANGELO TORIO RIVERA at General Trias, Cavite by virtue of Warrant of Arrest for the crime of Rape (no bail). The arrest was based on the letter request of Edgardo Balabis of Caloocan City to serve the Warrant of Arrest issued by RTC Branch 89, Quezon City against the Subject. Information was received that Subject was sighted in his residence at General Trias, Cavite so on the above-mentioned-date, NBI-CCD operatives proceeded to the area and served the said warrant. Subject was brought to NBI Manila for the booking procedures and was subsequently detained at the NBI Jail. On October 2, 2018 , operatives of NBI-International Operations Division (NBI-IOD) arrested MARYLOU OLIVAY y FABITO, MERRYCAR BAUTISTA y FERNANDEZ de NEGAD, VIVIAN PULIA y GUIRUELA de BERONIO, and JUSTIN CO y MELLAN in Carmona, Cavite for human trafficking and child abuse. The case stemmed from the complaint filed against the managers and supervisors of EVER FORTUNE RECYCLE CORP. (EVER FORTUNE), a domestic corporation located at Brgy. Bancal, Carmona, Cavite which endeavors in recycling plastic. According to one complainant, who worked at Ever Fortune for six (6) years as classifier, her daughter also worked as a classifier after her morning class from the afternoon to about 7:00 in the evening. Her daughter had to work to defray the rent charged amounting to Php 300.00 per child every week for each family housed in their living quarters. Another complainant, a former driver of Ever Fortune, added that his three minor children also had to work in order to defray the cost of rent. The two (2) complainants together with their families, were all dismissed from work and prevented from entering Ever Fortune premises immediately after the management learned that they went to the Department of Labor and Employment (DOLE) to file a complaint for underpayment, absence of work benefits and inhumane working conditions. On October 2, 2018, NBI-IOD operatives together with representatives from DSWD and DOLE entered the premises of Ever Fortune and found thereat were minors. Subjects JUSTIN CO, the manager, MARYLOU OLIVAY, supervisor, MERRYCAR BAUTISTA, crusher-in-charge, and VIVIAN PULIA, secretary of Ever Fortune were arrested and brought to the NBI for the booking procedures. Fourteen (14) individuals were rescued of whom thirteen (13) are minors, as confirmed by dental examination. Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings for violations of RA 9208 as amended by RA 10364 (Expanded Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2012) and RA 7610 (Special Protection of Children Against Abuse, Exploitation and Discrimination Act). On October 3, 2018 , operatives of NBI-Dumaguete District Office (NBI-DUMDO) arrested JOSEPH ALBERT LIM y RAGOT for violation of RA 8048 (Coconut Preservation Act of 1995) as amended by RA 10593 and violation of RA 9175 (Chainsaw Act of 2002). The case stemmed from an information received that there was cutting of coconut trees at Purok Pag-asa, Banilad, Dumaguete City. Upon verification of the information, NBI operatives encountered a chariot carriage carrying several pieces of coco lumbers parked in the way and saw traces of coconut trees that were cut down. Subject, who was engrossed in processing the coco trunk into pieces using a chainsaw, was left in the area. Upon inquiry, it was found out that he has not secured a permit to cut trees, no permit to use a chainsaw, and no delivery receipt to transport the coco lumber products with the Philippine Coconut Authority. After informing the Subject of his violations, operatives placed him under arrest. Certification issued by the Philippine Coconut Authority (PCA) states that there was no permit to cut coconut trees issued to the Subject. Another certification states that Subject is not a registered coconut lumber processor/dealer. Subject was presented for inquest proceedings for the above-mentioned violations. On October 4, 2018 , operatives of NBI-Dumaguete District Office (NBI-DUMDO) arrested JOVER ACADEMIA y YUCOR GEORGE ISO y ZERNA for illegal extraction of sands and minerals in Bacong, Negros Oriental without necessary permits and licenses. The operation was conducted based on the verified information that alleged illegal extraction of sand and gravel were being done in the vicinity of Brgy. Sulodpan, Brgy. Isugan and Brgy. Combado, Bacong, Negros Oriental and other areas of Valencia, Negros Oriental. Subjects were caught with their vehicles loaded with sand. Laborers were able to scamper away as operatives were approaching. Meanwhile, appropriate charges were filed against the arrested Subjects. Follow up operation will be conducted in the vicinity and other areas where sand and gravel were allegedly being extracted. On October 5, 2018 , operatives of NBI- Anti-Organized and Transnational Crime Division (NBI-AOTCD) arrested MANUEL BALA y VALDELLON for falsification of documents. The case stemmed from a letter of Isaiah Roland II, Attache, US Department of State, Diplomatic Security Service, Overseas Criminal Investigations (OCI), requesting assistance in the investigation of Kevin Keith Fajardo and Jarra Rowella, both applicants for a tourist visa as a married couple and were scheduled for interview. However, based on the investigation conducted by OCI and as per Certificates of No Marriage (CENOMAR) from the Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA), they are not married. Thus, the passport of Jarra Fajardo is considered fraudulently obtained. Moreover, upon online DTI verification by the US Embassy, the business allegedly owned by Kevin is not found. They were then confronted by US Embassy officials about the falsified documents they submitted and were thereafter referred to the NBI for investigation. According to Jarra and Kevin, the falsified documents were provided by Subject Manuel Bala who told them that it is easier for a married couple to get an approval for visa application, thus he paired the two. They also disclosed that they have a prior understanding with the Subject that they will meet in a hotel in Paco, Manila to get the purported original documents. With this, an entrapment operation was conducted resulting in the arrest of the Subject. Record check on the Subject revealed that he had served sentence for Falsification of public or official document in National Bilibid Prison. Subject was presented for inquest proceeding for violation of Article 172 (Falsification by Private Individual) in relation to Article 171 of the Revised Penal Code. On October 5, 2018 , operatives of NBI-Rizal District Office (NBI-RIZDO) seized Php 3.5 Million worth of counterfeit Penshoppe apparel products by virtue of Search Warrants. Charges for violation of RA 8293 (Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines) were filed against the owners, proprietors, employees, and occupants of various establishments located at New Galleria Baclaran Shopping Mall, Pasay City. On October 6, 2018 , composite elements of NBI-Ilocos Regional Office (NBI-IRO), NBI-Cagayan Valley District Office (NBI-CAVRO), NBI-Laoag District Office (NBI-LADO), NBI-Vigan District Office (NBI-VIDO), NBI-Cordillera Administrative Region (NBI-CAR), NBI-Dagupan District Office (NBI-DADO), and PDEA destroyed marijuana plants with a market value of Php 4.3 Million. The continuous wide scale marijuana eradication in the municipality of Tinglayan, Kalinga province resulted in the uprooting and destruction of 21,750 pieces of fully grown marijuana plants in five (5) plantation sites with an aggregate land area of 2,350 square meters. On October 8, 2018 , operatives of NBI-National Capital Region (NBI-NCR) arrested ROCHELLE LLARINA y BRESEMIO for Falsification of Private Documents and Estafa. The case stemmed from the complaint of Marilou Cruz and Fenelyn Liwanag, authorized representatives of UNITOP General Merchandise, Inc. against the Subject. Prior to their complaint, a certain Crizelle Shaddel M. Cedalla reported that Subject was issuing fake documents of UNITOP such as Identification Cards and Certificate of Employment (COE) for a fee. In order to verify the allegations, the NBI requested Crizelle Cedalla if she could secure a copy of her COE from the Subject. On October 4, 2018, Cedalla was able to get a copy of COE from the Subject for Php 1,000. According to the representatives of UNITOP, the COE of Cedalla which came from the Subject is falsified. With this, an entrapment operation was conducted in Sta. Rosa, Laguna resulting in the arrest of the Subject. Subject was presented for inquest before the Office of the City Prosecutor, Sta. Rosa, Laguna. On October 9, 2018 , operatives of NBI-Special Action Unit recovered two (2) carnapped vehicles owned by Mr. Robert R. Saluta, on October 9, 2018 at the parking lot of an establishment in Newport Boulevard, Pasay City. the operation was conducted based on the complaint filed by Mr. Saluta before the Bureau. Mr. Saluta, a businessman, asserted that sometime in August 25, 2018, at around 7:00pm, one of his customers, a certain ALELI FROILAN YAP called him and signify her intention to buy two vehicles, a 2013 model Mercedes Benz, G-550 (Bullet Proof Level B-6), and a 2015 model Toyota Land Cruiser (Bullet Proof Level B-6). Being a long time customer, he acceded to the request of Subject Aleli, to bring the vehicles to the latter’s house located at Pina St., Ayala, Alabang, for a test drive. Upon arrival, Mr. Saluta turned over the keys of the Mercedes Benz to Subject Aleli while the key to Land Cruiser was turned over to an unidentified person, a representative of Subject Aleli. Mr. Saluta was assured by Subject Aleli that she will return the vehicle after an hour, but to no avail. Efforts to contact Aleli thru her mobile phone and diligent effort to locate her whereabouts in her given address only proved futile. Interview conducted by NBI-SAU operatives to certain individuals revealed that the said vehicles was mortgaged in Resorts World Hotel and Casino, Pasay City. On October 9, 2018 , operatives of NBI-Cybercrime Division (NBI-CCD) arrested MARK LOUIE GALLIGUEZ y MORALES for computer-related identity-theft. The case stemmed from the complaint against the Subject who was misusing without right existing Facebook accounts owned by another users for his cybercriminal design. He manipulated these identities using their profile pictures and other information, to engage in online dating relationship with other users, posing himself as a female. Through this modus operandi, Subject was able to lure the complainant to engage in online relationship with his fake Facebook account. All the while, complainant thought that the relationship was a legitimate one that he was even made to support the Subject’s financial needs. During the entrapment operation, Subject was caught in flagrante in the act of collecting the money deposited by the complainant. Subject was then placed under arrest. When asked whether he owned the Facebook accounts in question, he explained that he only used and assumed those identities for online transactions. He further disclosed that he even used the ATM card of his grandmother in furtherance of his illicit enterprise. Subject was brought before the office of Inquest Prosecutor, Department of Justice for inquest proceeding. On October 9, 2018 , operatives of NBI-Cybercrime Division (NBI-CCD) arrested GERARD JOSEPH LIWAG for violation of RA 8484 (Access Device Regulation Act of 1998) in relation to RA 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012). The case stemmed from a complaint filed against the Subject for illegal use and production of ATM and credit cards. Based on the information received, the modus operandi of the group is to secure information and credit card details through call centers and other business establishment skimmers. Subject would contact the latter to ask for the expiry date and available credit limits and will activate the “Installment Option” for high value purchases to be approved upon usage of the credit card details. Using sophisticated gadgets, Subject is able to use cards for shopping. After series of surveillance, validation, verification, and documentation, Search Warrant was secured and on the aforementioned date, Subject was arrested as he was walking towards the main gate of a condominium tower in BGC, Taguig City. A search in Subject’s condominium unit resulted in the seizure of sophisticated gadgets used in his illegal activities such as HITI card printer, embossing machine, Fargo High Definition Printer, Removable Storage Device, Skimming Device, Laptops, Point-of-Sale Card Terminal, HUB (A4RTech), Java Blank Cards and Eighty (80) pieces of various cards. Also recovered were several identification cards including passports that are allegedly spurious and counterfeit. Subject was presented for inquest proceedings for the above-mentioned violations. On October 10, 2018 , operatives of NBI-Dumaguete District Office arrested SYMON CORDOVA in flagrante sniffing shabu. The arrest stemmed from the complaint against the Subject who was a notoriously known drug dependent. According to the complainant, Subject often goes violently crazy in front of their residence and would physically abuse his mother whenever the latter would refuse to give him money. On the aforementioned date, when the Subject got violent again, complainant contacted NBI DUMDO. Instantly, operatives proceeded at the complainant’s residence and caught the Subject in flagrante sniffing shabu in plain view with drug paraphernalia. Subject was then placed under arrest for violation of RA 9165 (Comprehensive Dangerous Drug Act of 2002). Subject was transferred to Dumaguete City Detention Facility. On October 15, 2018 , operatives of NBI-Anti-Organized and Transnational Crime Division arrested P/SUPT SALAVADOR C. DURAN JR. who has outstanding warrant of arrest for their conviction of violation of RA 3019 (Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act). Investigation conducted by the Ombudsman revealed that Subject DURAN, together with P/SUPT ARTURO MONTANO made possible the release of 100 checks worth Php 10,000,000.00 in favor of four (4) companies owned by MARGARITA B. TUGAOEN, the supposed supplier of combat, clothing, and individual equipment for the PNP CAPCOM. Graft investigators uncovered pieces of evidence that the abovenamed accused conspired with each other to make it appear that the Php 10,000,000.00 was released as payment for the CCIE, but in fact, no actual delivery delivery of CCIE was ever made to the PNP. Accordingly, they were convicted by the Sandiganbayan and were sentenced to 6 to 10 years imprisonment and were ordered to indemnify the PNP the amount of Php 10,000,000.00. When the NBI-AOTCD received reliable information as to the whereabouts of accused DURAN, operatives immediately dispatched that resulted to the arrest of DURAN at Maligaya Park, Novaliches, Quezon City. Report on the arrest of DURAN was forwarded to the Sandiganbayan. He is presently detained at the NBI detention cell awaiting for the commitment order from the Sandiganbayan. On October 18, 2018 , operatives of NBI-Laguna District Office (NBI-LAGDO) arrested VIVIAN ZAMORA DOLLESIN y PAUNILLAN, and EUGENIO MORANTE y SUNGALIA in Bicutan Public Market, Paranaque City for illegal jueteng operations. Subjects were arrested while collecting bets for jueteng. Seized from the Subjects’ possession are jueteng paraphernalia, fake Golden Era STL IDs and bet money. Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the Paranaque City Prosecutor Office for violation of RA 9287 (Illegal Gambling Law). On October 23, 2018 , operatives of NBI-Bulacan District Office (NBI-BULDO) arrested JHON V. ROCES and PEDRO BARRION MILAN for Syndicated Estafa. The case stemmed from the complaint of Teody C. San Andres, President of St. Andrew Publishing House. Subjects offered the complainant business proposal that the contract for the reprinting of Kindergarten and Grade 1 English Activity Sheets be produced abroad for less costing in which the Subjects specifically identified Shen Zhen Jinhao Color Printing Co., Ltd, Jing Hao Yi (HK) Trading Co. Finding the said company to be legitimate, complainant acceded to the project proposal of the Subjects. Subjects then instructed the complainant to deposit 50% down payment amounting to $50,000.00. However, the latter was able to deposit only $9,808.00. For more or less eight (8) months, complainant did not act a clear status of the project in China from the Subjects. They gave false information and kept on insisting for the Subject to pay the full amount. The complainant later found out the wrong doings of the Subjects. An entrapment operation was then conducted and resulted in the arrest of the Subjects. Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the Malolos City Prosecutor’s Office for violation of Article 315 (Syndicated Estafa) of the Revised Penal Code. On October 24, 2018 , operatives of NBI-Special Action Unit (NBI-SAU) arrested CRIS CABRIDO and MILABEL LAMATA for Large Scale Illegal Recruitment. Subjects were arrested after information about the illegal recruitment activities of the Subjects were gathered. With due coordination with the Philippine National Police and the management of Jollibee, SM Mall of Asia, NBI-SAU operatives proceeded to the location for the entrapment operation. The operation resulted in the arrest of the Subjects who were verified as not licensed or authorized by the Philippine Overseas Employment Administration (POEA) to recruit workers for overseas employment. Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the Pasay City Prosecutor Office for Large Scale Illegal Recruitment as defined under RA 8042 as amended by RA 10022 (Migrant Workers and Overseas Filipinos Act of 1995). On October 24, 2018, operatives of NBI-Environmental Crime Division (NBI-EnCD) arrested JODY MENDIORO y VILLAR, RODOLFO MANIQUIS y DOMINGO, NESTOR GALVES y HERNANDEZ, FERNANDO LOGRONIO y SALVE, JUAN FRANCISCO y CRUZ, and CEZAR RAMIREZ y VALDERAMA for illegal open dumpsite operation. The case stemmed from the complaint regarding an alleged illegal operation of an open dumpsite in Barangay Tanawan, Bustos, Bulacan. Surveillance of the area confirmed the said illegal activity. Verification of the records from the Department of Environment and National Resources-Environmental Management Bureau Region III (DENR-EMB III) disclosed that the operation of the open dumpsite is illegal and that no permits, licenses or grants were given to any person or entity to operate an open dumpsite in the Municipality of Bustos, Bulacan. Thus, NBI-EnCD operatives, together with the personnel of DENR-EMB III proceeded to the area and caught in flagrante delicto were the Subjects conducting the illegal activity. Subjects were presented before the Office of the Prosecutor General, National Prosecution Service, Department of Justice for violation of Section 37 (use of open dumpsite) and Section 48 (transportation and dumping in bulk of collected wastes) of RA 9003 otherwise known as the Ecological Solid Waste Management Act of 2000 and violation of Section 107 (Aquatic Pollution) of RA 8550 otherwise known as the Fisheries Code of the Philippines. On October 24, 2018 , operatives of NBI-National Capital Region (NBI-NCR) seized an estimated amount of Php 56 Million worth of counterfeit Lacoste and Herschel products by virtue of Search Warrants. Charges for violation of RA 8293 (Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines) were filed against Zeke General Merchandise located in 999 Shopping Mall, Binondo, Manila, Henny General Merchandise located in 168 Shopping Mall, Binondo, Manila, a warehouse in 999 shopping mall located in C.M. Recto Avenue, Manila, as well as various establishments/stores located in New Divisoria Mall, Tondo, Manila. On October 26, 2018 , operatives of NBI-National Capital Region (NBI-NCR) arrested MA. CONCEPCION YAPTINCHAY y CAIDO by virtue of Warrant of Arrest for Carnapping. Subject YAPTINCHAY was charged with violation of RA 6539 (Anti-Carnapping Law) at the RTC Branch 12, Manila. On the aforementioned date, NBI-NCR operatives went to Loyola Memorial Chapel, Makati City, during the wake of her father and served the Warrant of Arrest. Subject was thereafter brought to the NBI for the booking procedures. On October 29, 2018 , operatives of the NBI- Anti-Graft Division (NBI-AGD) arrested BERNADETTE BERNABE BADINAS for Large scale Swindling/Estafa. The case stemmed from the complaints regarding the unlawful scheme of the Subject. Complainant Madrid narrated that on March 2018 Subject Badinas invited them to put some investment in her financing business and promised to earn at least 10% monthly interest. Complainant Madrid then deposited a total amount of Php800,000.00 through her BDO account. Complainant Madrid further narrated that she was able to received interest through cash deposit in her BDO account but the Php45,000.00 and Php85,000.00 interest covered by UCPB checks bounced as manifested in the retuned checks. Complainant Madrid told the operatives of the NBI-AGD that she will meet Subject Badinas in a mall located at Sta. Cruz, Manila at around 4:00 in the afternoon to give the additional investment of Php30,000.00 on top of the initial investment of Php800,000.00. Thus, an entrapment operation was conducted resulting in the arrest of the Subject. Subject was brought for inquest before the City of Manila Prosecutors Office for violation of Article 315 of the Revised Penal Code. In six (6) successful operations, operatives of operatives of NBI-Intellectual Property Rights Division (NBI-IPRD) seized Php an estimated aggregate amount of Php 85.8 Million worth of counterfeit products. On October 1, 2018 , Php 12,000 worth of counterfeit medical books were seized in Valenzuela City. Charges for violation of RA 8293 (Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines) were filed against ANNIE RODRIGUEZ and ANNE RICARR RODRIGUEZ. On October 5, 2018 , Php 22 Million worth of counterfeit Under Armour products were seized in Binondo, Manila by virtue of Search Warrants. Charges for violation of RA 8293 (Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines) were filed against John/Jane Does, owners, occupants, proprietors of various stalls located at 168, 999, and 11/88 shopping malls in Binondo, Manila. On October 8, 2018 , Php 44.2 Million worth of counterfeit Louis Vuitton products were seized in Binondo and Malate, Manila by virtue of Search Warrants. Charges for violation of RA 8293 (Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines) were filed against John/Jane Does, owners/operators of various stalls located at 168 shopping mall in Binondo, Manila and Altra Center, Malate, Manila. On October 9, 2018 , Php 18.9 Million worth of counterfeit Kate Spade products were seized in Binondo, Manila by virtue of Search Warrants. Charges for violation of RA 8293 (Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines) were filed against the owners/operators of various stalls located at 999 shopping mall in Binondo, Manila. On October 10, 2018 , Php 200,000 worth of Power Tiger sinages, dispensing pumps and dispensing pumps overhead were seized in the cities of Valenzuela and Tarlac by virtue of Search Warrants. Charges for violation of RA 8293 (Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines) were filed against the owners/operators of Power Tiger Petroleum Corporation located in the said cities. On October 24, 2018 , Php 550,000.00 worth of unregistered cosmetic products were seized by virtue of Search Warrants. Charges for violation of RA 8293 (Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines) were filed against John/Jane Does, owners, occupants, proprietors of various stalls located at 168 and 999 shopping malls in Binondo, Manila.

body: PRESS STATEMENT April 01, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } In support of the government’s initiative to strengthen the campaign against all forms of criminality, the National Bureau of Investigation – Cagayan Valley Regional Office (NBI-CAVRO), under the leadership of NBI Director JUDGE JAIME B. SANTIAGO (Ret.), has collaborated with the Philippine National Police – PRO 2 and PNP-PRO 3. The collaboration culminated in the arrest of ROMMEL PALTAO y LACANILAO and DENNIS DE GUZMAN y GONZALES in Nueva Ecija for six counts of Murder. On March 25, 2025, a joint manhunt operation was conducted by the NBI-CAVRO, PNP-PRO 2, and PNP-PRO 3, which resulted in the arrest of Subject Paltao in Brgy. Mallorca, San Leonardo, Nueva Ecija and Subject De Guzman in Brgy. Luna, Sta. Rosa, Nueva Ecija. The arrests were made pursuant to a warrant issued against the Subjects by the Regional Trial Court – Branch 28, Bayombong, Nueva Vizcaya, for the Murder/Ambush of Aparri Vice Mayor, Rommel Alameda, and five (5) other victims on February 19, 2023 in Bagabag, Nueva Vizcaya. The arrested Subjects will be turned over to the issuing court for proper disposition. Ongoing intelligence gathering is being conducted to locate other individuals involved in the killing of the victims. Director Santiago commended the agents of NBI-CAVRO for their successful operation and expressed his gratitude to the PNP for their invaluable support. Santiago said that the Bureau will continue its collaboration with other law enforcement agencies to combat crime effectively.

title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: PRESS STATEMENT August 20, 2025 .jusatified-text { text-align: justify; } The Regional Trial Court (RTC) Branch 13 of Lipa City has rendered a decision finding two individuals, FRANCISCO QUIAMCO y BATIQUIN and RAMMEL RELOS y ESLAO, GUILTY beyond a reasonable doubt of Kidnapping for Ransom. The court sentenced both men to reclusion perpetua without eligibility for parole, stemming from an entrapment operation conducted by agents of the National Bureau of Investigation – National Capital Region (NBI-NCR) in Mangatarem, Pangasinan on July 30, 2015, that successfully rescued a kidnapping victim. The investigation began after a complaint was filed by the victim’s relatives. The victim was abducted on July 24, 2015, after leaving a supermarket in Lipa City, Batangas. The abductors demanded a ransom of Php 30 million for the victim’s release. NBI-NCR closely monitored communications between the kidnappers and the family. Through meticulous surveillance, agents were able to pinpoint the location of both the victim and the abductors in Mangatarem, Pangasinan. On July 30, 2015, NBI-NCR agents proceeded to a pharmacy where the victim was expected to buy medicine. The agents observed the suspects’ vehicle, a Toyota Previa. When one of the abductors exited the vehicle, agents moved in, successfully rescuing the victim and arresting the two suspects on the spot. Director Santiago commended the NBI-NCR agents for their “tireless and unwavering dedication” to the case. Their investigative skills were crucial in locating and rescuing the victim and ultimately bringing the perpetrators to justice.
