body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) is set to celebrate its 79th Founding Anniversary on Friday, November 13, 2015. With the theme “NBI…Valuing the Past, Embracing the Future”, the Bureau will undertake a week-long series of activities culminating with a simple program on the date of its establishment. In a statement, Nick V. Suarez, Chief of Information Division, said the celebration has already started on Saturday, November 07, 2015 with the NBI Fun Run 2015 led by Assistant Director Medardo G. de Lemos and Deputy Directors Edmundo Arugay, Rafael Marcos Ragos and Jose Doloiras. They were joined by about 1,000 personnel of the Bureau. Winners in the Fun Run were given cash prizes. On Monday, November 9, during its Flag raising ceremony, which opens the Anniversary week, NBI Director Virgilio L. Mendez will lead the Directorial Staff in giving Special Awards to journalists who have covered the NBI beat in recognition of their commitment to provide the various stakeholders relevant, timely and accurate information. The special award is also in appreciation to various media institutions for being a strong partner of the NBI in strengthening the rule of law and in pursuit of truth and justice. Suarez also said that during the week, from Monday until Friday, there will be Tiangge at the open grounds of the NBI clearance at reasonable prices to cater to applicants of NBI clearance, free eye check-up and free facial services for employees at the 2nd floor of the Dorm building. He also said photo exhibits will also be opened to the public beginning Monday at the covered walkway and at the lobby of the Main building in recognition of the contribution of the various operating Units, Divisions, Regional and District Offices and Services to the accomplishments of the NBI. Suarez emphasized that aside from the Thanksgiving Mass and simple ceremonies commemorating the Anniversary, highlighting the celebration on November 13, 2015 are twin events that will make the Anniversary more memorable and meaningful. First is the Unveiling of the NBI Wall of Honor in memory of the heroism of NBI Agents and Special Investigators who have died in the line of duty, and second is the launching of the first Coffee Table Book of the NBI that chronicles its eight (8) decades of existence.

The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) is set to celebrate its 79th Founding Anniversary on Friday, November 13, 2015. Suarez, Chief of Information Division, said the celebration has already started on Saturday, November 07, 2015 with the NBI Fun Run 2015 led by Assistant Director Medardo G. de Lemos and Deputy Directors Edmundo Arugay, Rafael Marcos Ragos and Jose Doloiras. Mendez will lead the Directorial Staff in giving Special Awards to journalists who have covered the NBI beat in recognition of their commitment to provide the various stakeholders relevant, timely and accurate information. body: PRESS STATEMENT May 16, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } The NBI-Cybercrime Division (CCD), under the supervision of NBI Director Judge Jaime B. Santiago (Ret.), and with the assistance of the Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR), seized Php 55 Million worth of illegally imported and distributed vape products in Marilao, Bulacan. Continuous cyber patrolling of the CCD resulted in the discovery of widespread importation, sale, and distribution of illicit nicotine vapor products within the province of Marilao, Bulacan. CCD was able to identify and obtain the contact information and social media account of an individual involved in the illegal importation and distribution of said vapor products. To gather evidence and further infiltrate the operation, poseur-customers placed bulk order of the illicit products. After identifying the whereabouts of the illicit vape products, CCD requested the assistance of the Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR) to facilitate a joint interdiction operation. In response, the BIR promptly issued a Mission Order authorizing the enforcement action in accordance with the provisions of the National Internal Revenue Code of 1997. Thus, on 8 May 2025, a joint operation was conducted at JP Compound III, Luke Street, Block 5, Lot 18, Marilao, Bulacan. The operation resulted in the discovery and confiscation of 85,200 pieces of salt-nicotine-based vapor products with an estimated street value of Php 55,380,000.00. Based on BIR Investigation Team’s assessment, Subject’s total unpaid excise tax obligation amounts to Php 52,653,600.00. Further, applying the prescribed penalty of ten (10) times excise tax due, the total liability increases to Php 579,189,600.00. The seized items were placed under the custody of the BIR, while cases for violation of National Internal Revenue Code are being prepared jointly by the NBI-CCD and BIR.

body: PRESS STATEMENT July 21, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } NBI ARRESTS THREE FILIPINOS FOR THE ILLEGAL SALE OF PRE-REGISTERED SIM CARDS; NIGERIAN NATIONAL FOR COMPUTER-RELATED IDENTITY THEFT AND COMPUTER-RELATED FRAUD Pasay City – Following the directive of NBI Director Atty. Melvin A. Matibag, the NBI Cybercrime Division (NBI-CCD), intensified its campaign against online fraud. This effort led to a series of operations, which culminated in the arrest of three Filipinos for selling pre-registered SIM cards, as well as one Nigerian national for identity theft and computer-related fraud associated with an online “love scam” operation. The operation was initiated due to ongoing cyber surveillance and a thorough investigation by NBI-CCD agents, which revealed that pre-registered SIM cards were being sold to operators of POGO, scam hubs, illegal online lending application (OLA) collection agents, and other cybercriminals. On July 9, 2026, agents from the NBI-CCD conducted an entrapment operation at a mall in Pasay City, resulting in the arrest of an individual selling pre-registered SIM cards. During the operation, the arrested subject revealed through her social media account that another delivery of pre-registered SIM cards was scheduled for Makati City to an African national who had previously purchased pre-registered SIM cards from her on several occasions. On an even date, a follow-up operation was conducted to apprehend the foreign national. A controlled delivery was initiated in the residence of the African national in a condominium in Makati City, which resulted in his arrest. During this operation, agents seized the suspect’s gadgets, which were subjected to forensic examination. This examination revealed that the individual was involved in love scam activities using various social media platforms. After the arrest of the foreign national, the arrested Filipino subject revealed that the suppliers of the pre-registered SIM cards were already demanding payment from the Subject. Thus, another follow-up operation was conducted to apprehend the suppliers. The agents of the NBI-CCD proceeded to Paranaque City to hand over the payment for the 300 SIM cards to one of the suppliers. Upon handing over the marked money, the agents immediately apprehended the supplier and recovered 550 pre-registered SIM cards. Subsequently, the agents proceeded to the City of Manila to hand over the payment for another set of 300 SIM cards, which resulted in the arrest of the other supplier and the seizure of 180 pre-registered SIM cards. The three Filipino subjects were presented for inquest proceedings for violation of Section 7 of Republic Act No. 11934 (SIM Registration Act) in relation to Section 6 of R.A. No. 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012). Meanwhile, the Nigerian national was also presented for inquest proceedings for Computer-Related Fraud under Section 49b)(2) and Computer-Related Identity Theft under Section 4(b)(3) of R.A. No. 10175. NBI Director Matibag commended the agents of the NBI-CCD for their thorough and meticulous investigation efforts, which culminated in the successful dismantling of a highly sophisticated and well-organized scamming network responsible for a wide range of online fraudulent activities. Director Matibag emphasized the importance of this operation, which not only targeted the scammers but also focused on disrupting the entire supply chain involved in the scam ecosystem. This included apprehending the suppliers of pre-registered SIM cards, as well as the intermediaries tasked with distributing these SIM cards to various scam operators, thereby addressing multiple levels of the illegal operation. https://www.facebook.com/reel/3472003179635054

body: PRESS STATEMENT February 24, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } NBI FILES CYBER LIBEL AND UNLAWFUL PUBLICATION COMPLAINT VS. VLOGGER JACK ARGOTA PASAY CITY, Philippines — The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) on Tuesday formally filed before the Department of Justice (DOJ) a complaint for Cyber Libel under Section 4(c)(4) of Republic Act No. 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012), in relation to Article 353 of the Revised Penal Code, and Unlawful Publication under Article 154 of the Revised Penal Code, against vlogger Jack Argota. The complaint stems from the alleged dissemination and republication through social media of fabricated medical records purportedly belonging to President Ferdinand Marcos, Jr. The NBI Cyber Crime Division (NBI-CCD) submitted the complaint at the DOJ Main Building in Manila at approximately 3:00 p.m. on Tuesday. Records show that Argota appeared before the NBI pursuant to a subpoena issued in connection with the investigation. During the proceedings, he admitted posting the alleged medical records on his social media platform for engagement purposes and “to keep up with the trend.” He further stated that he sourced the materials from various social media pages, including accounts of individuals claiming association with pro-Marcos content. The NBI underscores that the act of publishing or republishing false, fabricated, or unverified documents through electronic means may constitute Cyber Libel, when such publication tends to cause dishonor, discredit, or contempt against a person. Likewise, the dissemination of false news or information capable of injuring a person’s reputation may fall under Unlawful Publication of False News pursuant to Article 154 of the Revised Penal Code. The Bureau reiterates that freedom of expression is constitutionally protected; however, such right does not extend to the malicious or reckless spread of false information that may cause reputational damage or public harm. Earlier, the NBI also filed separate cyber libel complaints against former broadcaster Jay Sonza and vlogger Jeffrey Luces Celiz, also known as “Ka Eric Celiz,” in connection with the same issue involving the alleged spread of fabricated medical records. The case is now subject to preliminary investigation before the Department of Justice. The NBI remains committed to the impartial enforcement of the law and to upholding accountability in the digital space. #NBIServes

body: PRESS STATEMENT May 8, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } In line with the order of National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Director JUDGE JAIME B. SANTIAGO (Ret.) to intensify the operations against scamming activities in the country, the NBI-Cybercrime Division (NBI-CCD) and NBI-Special Task Force (NBI-STF) arrested MARVIN EUGENIO and MERCEDES CLEMENTE in Tala and Bagong Silang, Caloocan City. The arrested subjects were facing charges for Money Mauling Activities under Section 4(a)(2,4, and 5) of Republic Act No. 12010, otherwise known as the “Anti-Financial Account Scamming Act (AFASA)”; Illegal Inteception under Section 4(a)(2) and Misuse of Devices under Section 4(a)(5), both under the R.A. No. 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act 2012); and R.A. No. 8484 (Access Devices Regulation Act of 1998) in relation to R.A. No. 10175. The operation stemmed from cyber patrolling operations conducted by the NBI-CCD and NBI-STF in response to the increasing threat posed by individuals using fake digital financial accounts. These accounts, which include falsified or counterfeit wallets, are used to conceal the origin of illicit funds or to facilitate fraudulent transactions. The primary goal of this initiative was to identify and dismantle networks responsible for creating and using these dummy wallets. As a result of this effort, investigators identified the individuals involved in these illegal activities. The Regional Trial Court (RTC) Branch 123 of Caloocan City issued Warrants to Search, Seize, and Examine Computer Data (WSSECD) against the two identified locations where these unlawful acts are being conducted. On May 3, 2025, the joint team of NBI-CCD and NBI-STF served the Warrants at two addresses located in Tala and Bagong Silang, Caloocan City, which led to the arrest of the above-named subjects. The operation also resulted in the seizure of 6,000 suspected pre-registered SIM Cards, four sets of 32-port SIM Banks, and a set of computers and several cell phones. A digital forensic examination of the seized items revealed that the subjects had used software installed on their computers to intercept and save facial recognition data utilized as passwords or authentication for online financial accounts and digital wallets, such as GCash and other platforms. This data, along with physical SIM cards, was sold to fraudsters and scammers to assist in their money laundering activities. The modus operandi of Subjects Eugenio and Clemente was confirmed by the conversation threads found in their online messaging applications. The arrested subjects were charged with the above-stated violations. Director Santiago praised the NBI-CCD and NBI-STF agents for their tireless cyber patrolling efforts, which led to the identification of personalities responsible for the fraudulent sale of SIM cards.

body: PRESS STATEMENT March 05, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } NBI SEIZES OVER ₱237 MILLION IN COUNTERFEIT GOODS DURING BINONDO RAIDS PASAY CITY, Philippines – The National Bureau of Investigation – Intellectual Property Rights Division (NBI-IPRD) conducted massive enforcement operations on March 02, 2026 and March 03, 2026 targeting multiple retail outlets within a shopping mall in Binondo, Manila. Acting on intelligence regarding the large-scale distribution of infringing merchandise, NBI agents executed several search warrants that led to the discovery and seizure of 2,820 pieces of counterfeit “LOUIS VUITTON” items. The total estimated market value of the confiscated goods is placed at approximately ₱217,470,489.60, marking a significant blow to the local trade of fraudulent luxury goods. n the following day’s enforcement action on March 03, NBI operatives successfully seized an additional haul of counterfeit merchandise bearing the “LONGCHAMP” trademark. The seizure included 2,316 assorted bags, eight coin purses, and two wallets, with a combined estimated value of approximately ₱20,900,000. The Bureau confirmed that the production, sale, and distribution of these fake items constitute a direct violation of Republic Act No. 8293, otherwise known as the “Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines.” This operation is part of the NBI’s broader and ongoing commitment to upholding the law and protecting the rights of legitimate brand owners within the Philippine market. #NBIServes

body: PRESS STATEMENT October 07, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } In support of the government’s drive to eradicate the illegal drug trade and protect the welfare of children, the National Bureau of Investigation-Organized and Transnational Crime Division (NBI-OTCD) arrested six (6) individuals. The arrestees include the father of the rescued minors, and were charged for violations of Republic Act No. 7610 (Child Abuse), and Sections 7 and 15 of R.A. No. 9165 (Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002). The operation stemmed from a complaint against the Subject for child abuse and for maintaining a drug den at his residence in Rodriguez, Rizal. Surveillance confirmed that drug sessions were held almost daily at the Subject’s residence, where his children also lived. body: Thirty one (31) members of a large Chinese syndicates engaged in fraudulent acts through the use of access devices whose illegal operation is in Metro Manila were arrested during a raid by the agents of the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) in Paranaque City last Tuesday. The suspects were identified as: CHAN CHI-JOU; HSIEH MING-HSUN; HUANG CHENG-NUNG; LAI GUAN-LING; LIN XIUYAN; HUANG FENG-MENG; WANG LING-JUAN; CHANG FENGYI; ZHENG XIAOMEI; YU XIUJUAN; XYE HONGFANG; CHEN CHUN-KAI; HSIEH YI-TING; WANG CHIH-CHIEN; HUANG YEN-TSAI; LING BANGBIN; MING JUANFAN; FANG TEN-YU; NU QUAIO-CHAN; YU BIN; YU ZHENGQIANG; LIN BANGSHOU; YU LINGLING; HUANG YU-CHIN; WANG XIANBIN; HE CAILING; ZHENG MENGSHA; CHEN YU-SHU; TSAI YUNG-CHIEH; LAI KWAN-HONG; YANG IN-SHA; all residents of No. 70 D. Tuazon St., Gate 7, Sector 10, Paranaque City. At large is a certain Mr. Ong also of the same address. Intelligence sources disclosed that the syndicate composed mostly of Chinese nationals in collaboration with Taiwanese citizens engaged themselves in the illegal operation of access device fraud through the internet and are in the illegal activity of producing, using, trafficking in one or more counterfeit access devices and having in control or custody of/or possessing device-making or altering equipment. Moreover, it was learned that they are not in the business or employment which lawfully deals with the manufacture of such devices. It was also gathered that this syndicate conducted fraudulent on-line transaction and stole credit card information of unsuspecting victims through hacking and other malicious misrepresentation in the internet and through telecommunication. After validating this information, surveillance operations were conducted by the NBI Technical Intelligence Division (TID). A search warrant was applied for and issued by Judge Rainelda H. Estacio Montesa of Br 46 of the Manila RTC on October 23, 2012. On the same date, and on the strength of said search warrant, NBI TID operatives raided the residence located at No. 70 D. Tuazon St., Gate 7, Sector 10, Paranaque City. The suspects/occupants were found in said place. Found and seized from their possession were: skimming device, assorted credit cards, routers, laptops, telephones, internet broadband, signal decoder and assorted documents including copies of scripts with Chinese characters. Mere possession of access device equipment or skimming device without being in the business or employment which lawfully deals with the manufacture of such devices is punishable by law. Four(4) laptops, one of which has a skimming device, and eighteen (18) telephones all connected to thirty (30) voip gateway/routers which were all switched on were found during the conduct of the Search at the 2/F of the house at No. 70 D. Tuazon St., Gate 7, Sector 10, Paranaque. There were also sixteen (16) blank credit cards and three(3) City Mastercards along with one (1) BDO Credit Card found scattered among the discovered laptops. Other pieces of evidence found on the second floor were two (2) PLDT My DSL Broadbands, (1) printer, one usb, three(3) internet switches, three (3) GLOBE tattoo broadbands, one (1) signal decoder and other various documents. On the first floor, four (4) laptops were found along with four (4) telephones, five (5) cellphones, three (3) blank cards, one (1) City Mastercard, various documents and monies consisting of different denominations. Some of the documents with Chinese characters when translated into English turned out to be a script being used and read by the arrested Subjects in their online transactions with their victims. The script disclosed a mock conversation with someone presenting himself either of the following- – China policeman, Law Enforcement Member of China, an Officer of China Financial Investigating Body specializing in Money Laundering, an authorized officer in China who could help the prospect/victim in solving his/her legal problems by providing/furnishing the former with the latter’s personal information including but not limited to the latter’s bank account number and credit card number. Subsequently, the suspects were brought to the NBI for booking and detention. Charges for Viol of Sec.9 (a) and (f) of RA 8484 or Access Devices Regulation Act of 1998 and Viol of Sec. 4 (a) (5) Misuse of Devices, Sec. 4 (b) (3) Computer-related Identity Theft and Sec 6 of RA 10175 or the Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012.

body: PRESS STATEMENT October 11, 2024 The National Bureau of Investigation-Cabanatuan District Office (NBI-CABDO), with the guidance of NBI Director Judge Jaime B. Santiago (Ret.), arrested an individual in Nueva Ecija for sexually abusing his minor relatives. Director Santiago said that a thirteen-year-old complainant, assisted by her mother, filed a complaint against her uncle, alleging that she had been sexually molested by the Subject since she was five (5) years old until she turned eleven (11). With the help of a Psychological Evaluation Report, it was revealed that victim had endured multiple instances of sexual abuse perpetrated by her uncle. When questioned about the delayed disclosure, victim explained that she was made to believe that her uncle’s sexual advances were normal. Several other nieces of the Subject came forward and disclosed that they, too, had been victims of their uncle’s sexual molestations, but kept the incidents hidden for the same reason as the complainant. It was further revealed that the Subject was continuously sexually abusing most of his female relatives, particularly the minor ones without the knowledge of the family. Subject’s victims had suffered significant psychological harm as a result of his abusive deeds. Based on the information and to save the other minor relatives as would be possible victims, NBI-CABDO operatives, on October 2, 2024, proceeded to San Gregorio, Cabiao, Nueva Ecija to arrest the Subject. Upon proper identification of the complainants, Subject was placed under arrest and was informed of his rights as well as the nature of complaint against him. Subject was brought to the NBI-CABDO office for the standard operating and booking procedures. On October 3, 2024, Subject was presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the Provincial Prosecutor, Cabanatuan City for Acts of Lasciviousness under Article 336 of the Revised Penal Code, in relation to RA 7610 (Special Protection of Children against Child Abuse). Director Santiago commended the NBI-CABDO for successfully arresting the Subject.

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) recently filed a criminal case against a nanny, who pretended to help out a British national pursue another case of fraud in the country, but collected almost P1 million for fraudulent attorney’s and litigation fees. In a report to NBI Director Nonnatus Caesar R. Rojas, the NBI Cybercrime Division (CCD), headed by Head Agent Ronald Aguto Jr., identified the suspect as Marikit Navarro Arsenio, female, 33, born in Malinao, Aklan, and resident of Cubao, Quezon City. Arsenio was presented for inquest and charged for violation of Article 318 of the Revised Penal Code, otherwise known as estafa, before the Manila Prosecutor’s Office. She may be facing 125 counts of estafa, as she committed the crime at least 125 times during the past one and a half years. The complainant was identified as Lexington Decordova Burke, British national, businessman, of legal age, and resident of 11-12North View, Staple Hill, Bristol, BS16-5RU, United Kingdom. The case is being investigated by NBI-CCD Agent Efren B. Abantao. According to a report made by Abantao, last July 17, Burke filed a complaint for alleged online fraud/estafa against Arsenio whom he first met sometime December 2011 through an online dating site known as www.filipinocupid.com. Burke said he was deceived by Arsenio by pretending that she was helping him in pursuing a similar case of online fraud two other suspects, who also both scammed him in exchange for a promised relationship. The other case against the two other suspects in the relationship scam was earlier filed before the NBI Computer Crimes Unit (now known as the Cybercrime Division or CCD). The suspect had asked the complainant, who was traveling from the United Kingdom to the Philippines occasionally, to send money to her allegedly to be used for payment of attorney’s and litigation fees and other related court expenses in the total amount of P992,258.76. The money was sent in different amounts in several occasions from January 22, 2012 until sometime July 2013, through Western Union, MoneyGram and LBC, after the complainant had trusted the suspect that she would help him out. However, the complainant began to sense that he was only being fooled by the suspect as the manner of asking by the subject for more money became habitual. On the second week of July 2013, complainant went to the Philippines to confirm the various incidents relayed to him by the suspect. One of the stories relayed by the suspect to the complainant was allegedly for hospitalization in Asian Hospital in Alabang, of a certain lawyer only identified as Atty. Didolo, whom the suspect said was helping out in the case being pursued. Upon visiting Asian Hospital, there was no Atty. Didolo hospitalized, and that the allegation of the suspect was false. All other information given by the suspect to the complainant were also false. Before Arsenio’s arrest, Burke confronted the suspect during a cellular phone call. However, the suspect still made several alibis and also continued to ask for more money. The complainant then went to the NBI on July 17 and asked to conduct an entrapment operation. The first attempt to entrap the suspect was conducted on July 18, at around 11 p.m., at the Ninoy Aquino International Airport (NAIA). Unfortunately, the suspect failed to show up. On the following day, the suspect agreed to meet with the complainant at Lotus Garden Hotel in Ermita, Manila, where the complainant was billeted. The suspect also failed to show up. The complainant then coordinated with the hotel’s security office. Only July 20, at around 10:30 p.m., the suspect surfaced at the Lotus Hotel. The complainant invited the suspect to the dining room and signaled Hotel security officer Ebrahim Dalinding, while the suspect was again demanding around P6,000, for plane tickets and trial fees for a certain Judge Candelaria, who is allegedly handling another fraud case. The story made by Arsenio about the judge was also false. Around 10:45 p.m., the security officer asked for assistance of two police officers from Police Community Precinct (PCP) 5 of the Manila Police District (MPD) identified as SPO3 Alexander Gacayan and PO1 Isagani Jimenez. The police officers then brought the suspect, and eventually turned her over to the NBI-CCD, at around 2:30 a.m. of July 21. At the NBI-CCD, the complainant positively identified the suspect as the one who scammed him through online fraud and continuously demanded money using fabricated incidents and stories to obtain money. The suspect was then placed under arrest by the NBI. She was then eventually booked and underwent medical as per standard operating procedure (SOP) of the NBI. Recovered from the possession of the suspect were her Samsung cellular phone and postal identification card. The cellphone was subjected to forensics examination. Request was also made with the Philippine Postal Corporation to determine the authenticity of the postal ID of the suspect.

On April 27, 2014, Accused CEDRIC CUA LEE and SIMEON PALMA RAZ were escorted to NBI Manila for their temporary detention at this Bureau’s Jail under the Security Management Division (SMD). The manhunt against the rest of the Accused in this case is still in effect.

title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: Two men, who used the identity of another in social media website Facebook to collect money from a Filipino-American for a non-existent business, were arrested recently during an entrapment operation conducted by the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Cybercrime Division (CCD) in Dinalupihan, Bataan. In a report to NBI Director Nonnatus Caesar R. Rojas, CCD chief Head Agent Ronald P. Aguto identified the arrested suspects as Antonio N. Llemos, of legal age, and resident of No. 538 Saguing, Dinalupihan, Bataan; and Frederick L. Serrano, of legal age, tricycle driver, nephew of Llemos, and resident of Saguing, Dinalupihan, Bataan The NBI-CCD recommended to the Prosecutor General of the Department of Justice (DOJ) the filing of estafa and anti-alias charges against both suspects. The two suspects are now detained in the NBI detention in Manila. NBI-CCD Agent Efren Abantao, agent on case, identified the Fil-American complainant as Timogene A. Mencio, American citizen, of legal age, with address at 701 Seabrook Court Unit 203, Altamonte Springs, Florida, United States, and presently staying at No. 1 Upper Camp 7 East Kennon Road, Baguio City. The other complainant, whose identity was illegally used, was identified as Terence P. Dilla, 22, and resident of FB098 Balili, La Trinidad, Benguet. Llemos set up an account with Facebook using the alias Terrence Renz and photo of complainant Dilla to dupe the complainant. Mencio said, sometime April 2013, Llemos befriended him in Facebook, and continuous on-line communication between the two followed. Llemos sweet-talked Mencio into establishing a fastfood business partnership in the Philippines. Because of their agreement, Mencio wire-transferred, thru XOOM (a U.S.-based remittance company), various amounts for 13 times totaling US$5,633.87. The wire transfers were all claimed and received by Serrano in the Philippines at Cebuana Lhullier Branch 3, located at Dinalupihan, Bataan. Mencio later on discovered that the photo appearing on Facebook under the name Terrence Renz, is belonging to another person later identified as complainant Terrence P. Dilla. Dilla executed an affidavit affirming that his photo was stolen and was used by somebody else. He also said that he has no business transaction or communicated with Mencio Mencio also said that the fastfood business is non-existent. On the other hand, Llemos continued to demand from Mencio additional amount of P20,000.00 through text messages and Facebook. On July 17, 2013, Mencio filed a complaint before the CCD. A few weeks later, an entrapment was hatched against the subjects on August 8, 2013 at Dinalupihan, Bataan. The amount of P4,263.10 was wire transferred to the account of Serrano, who was receiving the money sent by the victim. At around 11 a.m. of August 8, the CCD operatives, together with Mencio, proceeded to Cebuana Lhullier Branch 3, Dinalupihan, Bataan. At around 1 p.m., Serrano arrived, collected the money and was immediately arrested. Recovered from Serrano was the money and the Cebuana Lhuillier receipt with Serrano’s name on it. After his arrest, Serrano told the CCD operatives that he was only instructed by Llemos, whom he also identified as “Buba”. Serrano then brought the CCD operatives to the residence of Llemos. Upon reaching Llemos’ residence, the former asked Serrano about the money. After Serrano gave the money to Llemos, the CCD operatives, who strategically positioned themselves in the area, arrested the suspect. Recovered from Llemos was a Samsung Galaxy Tab, where cellular phone numbers the suspect used to defraud Mencio was revealed. When asked about the complaint against him, Llemos admitted that the fastfood business partnership with Mencio is non-existent and he only duped complainant to obtain money by assuming/stealing the identity of Dilla in his Facebook account. The two were presented for inquest proceedings at the DOJ upon arrival in Manila.

title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: The Information Division is pleased to submit herewith the significant cases of the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) for the following aforementioned period as follows: • On February 2, 2018, operatives of NBI-Bayombong District Office (NBI-BAYDO) arrested DEBORAH RUTH TOMAS in entrapment operation for violation of RA 9514 (Revised Fire Code of the Philippines of 2008), RA 4109 (An Act to Convert the Division of Standards Under the Bureau of Commerce into a Bureau of Standards) and RA 7394 (The Consumer Act of the Philippines). Subject was recommended for inquest proceeding before the Provincial Prosecutor, Bayombong, Nueva Viscaya for the aforementioned violations. • On February 2, 2018, operatives of NBI-Saranggani District Office (NBI-SARDO) arrested JARRY T. GUCILA for Qualified Theft. The case stemmed from the complaint of Adonis Agreda, Chief Executive Officer of AGREDA HOLDINGS INC. located in Koronadal City. According to the complainant, they have on-going construction on the second floor of their building and Subject JARRY T. GUCILA is a room boy/utility man whom they hired. As such, Subject enjoys their trust and confidence and has full access to the building. However, when they had their periodic review of the CCTV footages, they discovered that Subject stole cartons of tiles from their building. CCTV footages showed that Subject hid the tiles at the 3rd floor of the building and when the roving security guard was no longer around, he carried the items down to the ground floor. NBI-SARDO operatives then conducted a search at the said premises by virtue of Search Warrants. Found and seized thereof were the stolen items. Subject was arrested and was brought to NBI-SARDO office for proper booking procedures and for proper disposition. • On February 5, 2018, operatives of NBI-Anti-Organized and Transnational Crime Division (NBI-AOTCD) arrested four (4) Korean nationals namely, YOUNG TAE YOUN, BYUNG WOOK AHN, KIM MIN DUNG, and PARK HYUN. The case stemmed from a complainant who sought the assistance of NBI for alleged carnapping. Complainant alleged that she normally allows PARK HYUN, a tour guide, to use her Ford EcoSports whenever they have Korean guests. Sometime last week, complainant asked PARK HYUN to get her other car, Kia Picanto and bring it to her place in Makati. However, PARK HYUN failed to do so and said that he will borrow the car until February 5 since he will use it in transferring to another condo unit. Moreover, complainant’s partner received a call from PARK HYUN asking for help as he was caught by persons whom he owed money and that her cars were taken and were demanding for Php 1 Million plus Php 360,000 interest before the complainant could get her cars back. Complainant was instructed to bring the money at Casino Filipino – Manila Bay. Acting on the complaint, an entrapment operation was conducted which resulted in the arrest of the Subjects. Investigation revealed that PARK HYUN is in cahoots with the other Subjects. Subjects were charged on inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor, Manila for violation of RA 10883 (Carnapping). • On February 6, 2018, operatives of NBI-Naga District Office (NBI-NADO) arrested WILLIAM BRINAS y VARGAS by virtue of Warrant of Arrest for the crime of Rape. It was on November 2017 when the Provincial Prosecutor’s Office of Camarines Sur released its resolution upholding the recommendation to charge the Subject for the crime of Rape and violation of R.A. 7610 and corresponding information were filed to the RTC Branch 63, Calabanaga, Camarines Sur. Three (3) Arrest Warrants, two (2) of which were recommended no bail, were issued by RTC Branch 63. On the above-mentioned date, NBI-NADO operatives served the said Warrants of Arrest to Subject WILLIAM BRINAS in Calabanga, Camarines Sur. The arrest warrants were returned to issuing court and corresponding commitment orders were issued. Subsequently, the Subject was turned over to the Provincial Jail in Tinangis, Pili, Camarines Sur. • On February 7, 2018, operatives of NBI-North Eastern Mindanao Regional Office (NBI-NEMRO) arrested JANETH MONTEJO y BISTO, JESSA MONTEJO y BISTO and JOANNA YACAPIN y YAMIS in entrapment operation for illegal gambling. The operation stemmed from the letter of Alexander Ferrer Balutan, Genral Manager of PCSO, Mandaluyong City, requesting investigative assistance in connection with the proliferation of illegal numbers gane perpetrated by Peryahan ng Bayan in Cagayan de Oro and Misamis Oriental. After confirming the active operations in the said areas, entrapment operation was conducted resulting in the arrest of the Subjects. Confiscated from their possession were assorted gambling paraphernalia and cash bet money. Charges for violation of PD 1602 as amended by RA 9287 (Illegal Gambling Law) were filed against the Subjects. • On February 7, 2018, operatives of NBI-Laguna District Office (NBI-LAGDO) arrested ERWIN DACUYCUY y BUERA for alleged kidnapping of minor. The case stemmed from the complaint of US Embassy. The operation resulted in the arrest of the Subject and rescue of a 16 year old US citizen. The operation was assisted by representatives from MSWD of Taytay, Majayjay, Laguna and elements of 301st AISG, Philippine Air Force. Subject and victim were brought to NBI-LAGDO for further investigation while violations of related laws were readied against the Subject. • On February 7, 2018, operatives of NBI-Bacolod District Office (NBI-BACDO) arrested ROVI SIASON y BOBILA for human trafficking. The NBI-BACDO received a memorandum from NBI-Dumaguete District Office (NBI-DUMDO) that four (4) females, who were illegally recruited/victims of trafficking, were on their way to Bacolod City on board CERES bus from Dumaguete City. One of the victims, whose contact number was listed in the memorandum, was contacted and said that they were instructed by Subject ROVI SIASON a.k.a. Amor to meet her in a mall in Bacolod City. Verification with the Philippine Overseas Employment Administration (POEA) revealed that Subject ROVI SIASON is not an authorized or licensed to recruit workers for overseas employment. After proper coordination with Police Station 3, Bacolod City, an operation to rescue the victims and arrest the Subject was hatched and resulted in the arrest of the Subject who was caught while having her briefing with the victims. Subject was brought to NBI-BACDO office for the booking procedures and was thereafter brought before the Office of the City Prosecutor, Dumaguete City for inquest proceedings for violations of RA 10364 (Expanded Anti-Human Trafficking Act of 2012) and RA 10022 (Migrant Workers and Overseas Filipinos Act of 1995). • On February 8, 2018, operatives of NBI-Central Luzon Regional Office (NBI-CELRO) arrested MILENE BORGONIA y DIZON in Balanga City, Bataan for Estafa. The case stemmed from a complaint against the Subject who represented herself as a Certified Public Accountant who works in the United Kingdom. Subject promised complainants that for a fee she can help them work in different countries in Europe. Subject was arrested in an entrapment operation inside a mall in Balanga City, Bataan after she received an envelope containing Php 60,000 marked money. Certification issue by the Philippine Overseas Employment Administration (POEA) stated that Subject is not licensed or authorized to recruit workers for overseas employment. The cases of Estafa and Large Scale Illegal Recruitment were filed against the Subject before the Office of the City Prosecutor, Balanga, Bataan. • On February 8, 2018, operatives of NBI-Death Investigation Division (NBI-DID) arrested ROLLY CARDINES y MANA-AY in Iloilo City for Rape and Child Abuse. Subject was arrested by virtue of Warrants of Arrest issued by RTC Branch 72, Antipolo City for the crime of Rape and Warrant of Arrest issued by RTC Branch 98, Antipolo City for Child Abuse. The aforesaid cases of Rape arose from the complaint of a mother, then the live-in partner of Subject and her 10-year old daughter. Records show that Subject CARDINES sexually assaulted the said minor once in their home and twice in a tricycle in February 2016 in Antipolo City. Subject was arrested by virtue of Warrants of Arrest issued by RTC Branch 72, Antipolo City for the crime of Rape and Warrant of Arrest issued by RTC Branch 98, Antipolo City for Child Abuse. The aforesaid cases of Rape arose from the complaint of a mother, then the live-in partner of Subject and her 10-year old daughter. Records show that Subject CARDINES sexually assaulted the said minor once in their home and twice in a tricycle in February 2016 in Antipolo City. Subject is presently detained at the NBI Jail awaiting order from the courts concerned for his transfer to the Antipolo City Jail. A bright prospect that witnesses may come out to testify while Subject is behind bars. • On February 8, 2018, operatives of NBI-Laguna District Office (NBI-LAGDO) arrested EDITHA CALINAO y MALATE, ANGELITO PALINO y MANZANO, GLADYS JOY LATAGAN y GORDON, and LUIS BALASCO JR. y QUILISTI in entrapment operation for illegal gambling. The operation stemmed from the complaint of Hon. Jose Jorge C. Corpuz of PCSO. Subjects were arrested after caught in the act of delivering their respective collection money for jueteng operations. Seized from their possessions are jueteng paraphernalia and bet money. Charges for violation of PD 1602 in realtion to RA 9287 (Illegal Gambling Law) shall be filed against the Subjects on inquest proceedings at the City Prosecutor Office, Las Pinas City. • On February 8, 2018, operatives of NBI-Eastern Visayas Regional Office (NBI-EVRO) arrested REX BYRON PINDOT y UGNIT for Robbery and Illegal Possession of Bladed Weapon. The case stemmed from the complaint of Vanessa Wareza, owner of Food Eatery/Fast Food “M and V Food Avenue”. According to the complainant, she hired Subject Rex and one Rodel to work as helpers. However, the two were not performing well with their work so complainant terminated them. After which, complainant was informed by her cook that the window of her house was broken. She immediately went home and found out that her valuables including wristwatches, laptop, and jewelry. Later on, complainant learned from her other staff that Subject Rex and Rodel called and told them that they took the complainant’s valuables. Thus, a complaint was filed with the NBI. Hot pursuit operation was conducted to locate the Subjects. When an information was received that Subjects were offering laptop, cellphone and G-Shock wristwatch, an entrapment operation was conducted and resulted in the arrest of Subject REX BYRON. Recovered from the Subject was a knife/bladed weapon. Charges for Robbery and Illegal Possession of Bladed Weapon were filed against the arrested Subject. • On February 10, 2018, operatives of NBI-Central Visayas Regional Office arrested EMELIANO ESPARRAGO y MAGPANTAY for Carnapping. The case stemmed from the complaint against the Subject who signified interest in buying the vehicle of the Complainant. They had agreed that after the completion of the repair works, Complainant will execute a Deed of Assignemnt with Assumption of Mortgage in Subject’s favor in consideration of the sum of Php 200,000 less than the payment of four (4) months monthly amortization at Php 32,213 per month. However, Subject reneged his promise to pay the amount agreed. Subject kept ignoring the Complainant despite the latter’s repeated request for the Subject’s payment. Complainant even demanded for the return of her car with the commitment to pay the advances made by the Subject, but Subject EMELIANO flatly ignored the complainant. Subject was arrested after he refused to surrender the vehicle to the Complainant despite the tender of the payment being offered. Charges for violation of RA 10883 (Carnapping) were filed against the Subject. • On February 13, 2018, operatives of NBI-Rizal District Office (NBI-RIZDO) arrested FERNANDO PASANO PADUA, JOSE ADEMAR PASANO PADUA, and ROWENA JESUITAS VALDEZ for human trafficking and rescued four women in Tanay, Rizal. They are the alleged owner, operation manager, and cashier of Keno Lodge where the trafficking takes place. The case stemmed from an information received by NBI-RIZDO that Keno Lodge located at Tanay, Rizal is engaged in illicit sex trade of women mostly are minors. Series of surveillance operations were conducted confirming the information received. Subsequently, in coordination with the Provincial DSWD Social Workers, an entrapment operation was conducted on February 13, 2018 resulting in the arrest of the above-mentioned Subjects and the rescue of four (4) women, two (2) of whom are minors. The aforesaid minors, in their sworn statements, said that their nature of work is to give sexual favors to customers being introduced and brought to them by Subject ROWENA JESUITAS VALDEZ. A witness, a room boy of Keno Lodge, said in his sworn statement that the owner of the lodge, Subject FERNANDO PASANO PADUA knows about the illegal sex trade going on in his establishment but chose not to do anything about it. The three (3) arrested Subjects were presented for inquest before the Associate Rizal Provincial Prosecutor for violations of R.A. 9208 (Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2003) as amended by R.A. 10364 and violation of R.A. 7610 (Special Protection Against Child Abuse, Exploitation, and Discrimination Act • On February 13, 2018, operatives of NBI-Pagadian District Office (NBI-PAGDO) arrested MILAGROS “ROSE” LANDONG for human trafficking and rescued two (2) minor girls in Buug, Zamboanga, Sibugay Province. A confidential asset informed the NBI-PAGDO about the possible violation of R.A. 9208 (Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act) committed by the Subject for recruiting the two minors as dancers in a club with a promise of Php 5,000 per night. Victims were enticed to leave their homes and went to a designated place in Diplahan and Sibugay Province in order to be fetched by the Subject for the purpose of bringing them to Dumaguete City. The informant was advised to contact the parents or guardian. A rescue operation was then hatched resulting in the rescue of the two minors and the arrest of the Subject. Subject MILAGORS LANDONG was brought for inquest before the Provincial Prosecutors Office, Zamboanga, Sibugay for violation of R.A. 9208 as amended by R.A. 10364 (Expanded Anti-Trafficking of Persons Act of 2012. Subject was temporarily detained in Buug Municipal Police Station. • On February 14, 2018, operatives of NBI-Central Luzon Regional Office (NBI-CELRO) arrested CLIMON ARNEJO y MAQUILAN in an entrapment operation for human trafficking in Angeles City, Pampanga. The case stemmed from the endorsement letter of the Presidential Action Center, Malacanang about an alleged prostitution and sexual exploitation of young Filipina women in Angeles City and Intelligence Report regarding Police Colonel of Pampanga – protector of the deployment of sex workers for alleged human trafficking. After extensive and thorough surveillance and validation, a composite team of Inter Agency Council Against Trafficking (IACAT) in Pampanga (composing of NBI-CELRO and DSWD-R3) conducted an entrapment operation • On February 15, 2018, operatives of NBI-Rizal District Office (NBI-RIZDO) seized Php 55 Million worth of counterfeit Nike and Converse rubber shoes. Items were seized in Pasay City and Valenzuela City by virtue of Search Warrants issued by RTC Manila Branch 46. Charges for violation of R.A. 8293 (Intellectual Property Code of Philippines) were filed against Nikki Li and other proprietors/officers/employees of the storage facilities located at Baclaran Bagong Milenyo Plaza, FB Harrison St., Pasay City and Kapitan Ambo St., Pasay City. • On February 19, 2018, operatives of NBI-Special Action Unit (NBI-SAU) arrested ARLAN EUGENIO y ESPIRITU and ALVIN QUIJANO y DE GUZMAN for possession, use, and sale of prohibited drugs. RTC Manila issued Search Warrants for immediate search and seizure of undetermined quantity of high grade marijuana (cannabis) otherwise known as “kush” and an undetermined amount of methamphetamine hydrochloride known as shabu against Adrian Cristobal and occupants of a house located at Tramo St., Manuyo Uno, Las Pinas City. After proper coordination with the Philippine Drug Enforcement Agency and the local authorities who has jurisdiction of the place to be searched, NBI-SAU operatives conducted the entrapment operation which resulted in the arrest of the aforementioned Subjects to whom 350 grams of shabu and two (2) ounces of kush were purchased. Subjects ARLAN EUGENIO and ALVIN QUIJANO were presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the Prosecutor, Las Pinas City for violation of R.A. 9165 (Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002). • On February 20, 2018, operatives of NBI-Environmental Crime Division (EnCD) arrested RONALD MARCELO DEL ROSARIO, JEFFREY UBAS OCQUIA, EDILBERTO VILLAMOR DELOS SANTOS, and EDISON VILLAMOR DELOS SANTOS for illegal quarrying in San Ildefonso, Bulacan. Subjects were arrested while in the act of illegally extracting and transporting mineral products commonly called “limestone”. Seized during the operation were several heavy equipment and conveyance with an estimated value of Four Million Pesos (Php 4M) which were being used in the said illegal quarrying. Certification issued by Mines and Geosciences Bureau Region III of the Department of Environment and Natural Resources revealed that based on the records, above-mentioned Subjects had no valid or existing quarrying permit. Therefore, they are not authorized to conduct mining activity in the said area. Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the Department of Justice for violation of Section 103 (Theft of Minerals) of R.A. 7942 (Philippine Mining Act of 1995). Subjects were detained at the NBI Detention Center. • On February 21, 2018, operatives of NBI-Rizal District Office (NBI-RIZDO) arrested LOIDA ADAN AGUILAR CARPIO, ERLINDA CUADRO OPENA DELA CRUZ, HELEN ARCAGWA TANGONAN, CRISTINA AGUINALDO CALANO VERGINO, ERWIN ESTRELLA INFANTE, and ANTONIO LENPEN REYES in Caloocan City for Illegal Gambling. NBI received a complaint from Mr. Cesar V. Areza, President of Rollover Gaming Corporation, the company authorized by PCSO for small town lottery operation in Caloocan City, against individuals engaged in illegal numbers game. Surveillance operations were then conducted confirming the illegal gambling activities along Heroes Street, Caloocan City. An entrapment operation was then conducted on the above-mentioned date resulting in the arrest of the Subjects. Verification with the list of authorized sales supervisors and sales representatives of Rollover Gaming Corporation furnished by PCSO, Subjects’ name did not appear therein which is tantamount to unauthorized/illegal collection of bets. Information was received that Subject was seen working as Purchaser at Star Builder located at Brgy. City Heights, General Santos City. Immediately thereafter, operatives proceeded to the area and effected the arrest. Accused was temporarily detained at NBI-SARDO. • On February 23, 2018, operatives of NBI-Environmental Crime Division (NBI-EnCD) arrested JOEL SOCOBOS y BETINOL, WENIFREDO BRENBUELA y ARCALA, and REYNALDO MONFORTE y PIENCIVANES for illegal logging in Las Nieves, Agusan del Norte. Subjects were arrested by NBI-EnCD operatives and DENR CARAGA – Region VIII on the strength of Search Warrants. Seized during the operation were various naturally-grown and planted timbers or lumbers with an estimated value of Php 1.2 Million as well as heavy equipment and conveyances with an estimated value of Php 9 Million. Said equipment were used in processing illegal logs into final products. Certification issued by Region VIII of the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR) revealed that based on the records, Subjects’ sawmill has an expired license since 2012 and Subjects were not authorized to conduct saw-mill operation in the said area. An intelligence information from Naval Intelligence and Security Force (NISF) of the Philippine Navy was received regarding Subject PRENSICA CLODUALDO. Verification from Identification and Records Division (IRD) and validation of gathered intelligence information confirmed that Subject PRENSICA CLODUALDO, together with other accused Paran Pacanza Y Malate and Lamberto Pancanza y Malate Jr., was found guilty beyond reasonable doubt of the crime of Robbery and sentenced to suffer the penalty of imprisonment of six (6) years and one (1) day of Prision Correccional as minimum to ten (10) years of Prision Mayor as maximum and all its accessory penalties under the law. Surveillance operations were conducted at the exact residence of the Subject where the alleged human trafficking activities take place. JIKING and JIMMY BLA y SAPIH a.k.a. BIN LADEN a.k.a. ASSAN, members of the terrorist organization Abu Sayyaf Group (ASG). Subjects were arrested by virtue of Warrants of Arrest for Kidnapping and Serious Illegal Detention with Ransom which stemmed from the incident last June 11, 2001 wherein a team of Abu Sayyaf bandits went to Brgy. Tairan, Lantawan Basilan and forcibly took employees of the Golden Harvest Plantation as well as the “Jehovah’s Witness Kidnapping” incident of August 2002 where the ASG took hostages from the Jehovah’s Witness religious group in Patikul, Sulu. Meanwhile, Subject BLA was identified as an outer perimeter guard and one who was knowledgeable in the improvisation of explosive devices from mortar shells. Subject BLAH was also noted to be well-versed in the jungle terrains of Sulu. Maria, Zamboanga City while Subject JIMMY BLA was arrested just after midnight into the next day at Brgy. Rio Hondo Settlement Area, Boggok, Sta. Catalina, Zamboanga City. Aside from the above-mentioned reinforcements, foreign counterparts led by the Australian Federal Police also provided information and technical support to the NBI. Subjects HOOD ABDULLAH and JIMMY BLA were brought to NBI Manila for the booking procedures and were thereafter turned over to the NBI-SMS Detention facility for custody. • On February 28, 2018, operatives of NBI-North Eastern Mindanao Regional Office (NBI-NEMRO) arrested JASON SALOGAN ERMAC for violation of RA 9165 (Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002). Subject was caught in the act of planting and cultivating marijuana plants. Confiscated from his possession and control were six (6) hills of medium grown marijuana plants which were planted in the mountainous part of Purok 5, Brgy. Luinab, Iligan City and planted in plain view within a hectare land located in Purok 5, Upper Luinab, Iligan City. Upon ocular inspection in the area, several traces of uprooted marijuana plants were noticed in the area numbering to more or less one hundred (100) hills of suspected uprooted marijuana plants. Subject is currently under the temporary custody of NBI-NEMRO pending the filing of case for the above-mentioned violation on inquest proceedings.

NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION

The Information Division is pleased to submit herewith the significant cases of the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) for the following aforementioned period as follows: • On February 2, 2018, operatives of NBI-Bayombong District Office (NBI-BAYDO) arrested DEBORAH RUTH TOMAS in entrapment operation for violation of RA 9514 (Revised Fire Code of the Philippines of 2008), RA 4109 (An Act to Convert the Division of Standards Under the Bureau of Commerce into a Bureau of Standards) and RA 7394 (The Consumer Act of the Philippines). GUCILA for Qualified Theft. The case stemmed from the complaint of Adonis Agreda, Chief Executive Officer of AGREDA HOLDINGS INC. located in Koronadal City. According to the complainant, they have on-going construction on the second floor of their building and Subject JARRY T. GUCILA is a room boy/utility man whom they hired. As such, Subject enjoys their trust and confidence and has full access to the building. However, when they had their periodic review of the CCTV footages, they discovered that Subject stole cartons of tiles from their building. CCTV footages showed that Subject hid the tiles at the 3rd floor of the building and when the roving security guard was no longer around, he carried the items down to the ground floor. NBI-SARDO operatives then conducted a search at the said premises by virtue of Search Warrants. Found and seized thereof were the stolen items. Complainant was instructed to bring the money at Casino Filipino – Manila Bay. Acting on the complaint, an entrapment operation was conducted which resulted in the arrest of the Subjects. Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings for violation of R.A. 9208 (Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2003) as amended by R.A. 10364 (Expanded Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2012), violation of R.A. 7610 (Special Protection Against Child Abuse, Exploitation and Discrimination, and for other Purposes) as amended, violation of R.A. 9775 (Anti-Child Pornography Act of 2009, and violation of R.A. 10175 (The Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012) were filed against the Subject before the Office of the City Prosecutor, Tacloban City. • On February 27 and 28, 2018, operatives of NBI-Counter Terrorism Division (NBI-CTD), NBI-Special Operations Group (NBI-SOG), NBI-Western Mindanao Regional Office (NBI-WEMRO) together with elements from the Naval Special Operations Group (NAVSOG) of the Armed Forces of the Philippines – Western Mindanao Command (AFP-WESMINCOM), PNP Regional Office 9 (PRO 9), and the Zamboanga City Police arrested HOOD ABDULLAH y SALVADOR a.k.a. JIKING and JIMMY BLA y SAPIH a.k.a. BIN LADEN a.k.a. ASSAN, members of the terrorist organization Abu Sayyaf Group (ASG). Subjects were arrested by virtue of Warrants of Arrest for Kidnapping and Serious Illegal Detention with Ransom which stemmed from the incident last June 11, 2001 wherein a team of Abu Sayyaf bandits went to Brgy. Tairan, Lantawan Basilan and forcibly took employees of the Golden Harvest Plantation as well as the “Jehovah’s Witness Kidnapping” incident of August 2002 where the ASG took hostages from the Jehovah’s Witness religious group in Patikul, Sulu. Subject ABDULLAH was an inner guard securing the kidnap victims, and was a Shabu user but capable fighter who taught younger ASG members on how to fight and bear arms against the government forces. Meanwhile, Subject BLA was identified as an outer perimeter guard and one who was knowledgeable in the improvisation of explosive devices from mortar shells. Subject BLAH was also noted to be well-versed in the jungle terrains of Sulu. On February 27, 2018, joint elements of NBI-CTD, NBI-SO G, NBI-WEMRO, NAVSOG-WESMINCOM, PNP-PRO 9, and the Zamboanga City Police arrested Subject HOOD ABDULLAH at Brgy. Sta. Maria, Zamboanga City while Subject JIMMY BLA was arrested just after midnight into the next day at Brgy. Rio Hondo Settlement Area, Boggok, Sta. Catalina, Zamboanga City. Aside from the above-mentioned reinforcements, foreign counterparts led by the Australian Federal Police also provided information and technical support to the NBI. Subjects HOOD ABDULLAH and JIMMY BLA were brought to NBI Manila for the booking procedures and were thereafter turned over to the NBI-SMS Detention facility for custody. • On February 28, 2018, operatives of NBI-North Eastern Mindanao Regional Office (NBI-NEMRO) arrested JASON SALOGAN ERMAC for violation of RA 9165 (Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002). Subject was caught in the act of planting and cultivating marijuana plants. Confiscated from his possession and control were six (6) hills of medium grown marijuana plants which were planted in the mountainous part of Purok 5, Brgy. Luinab, Iligan City and planted in plain view within a hectare land located in Purok 5, Upper Luinab, Iligan City. Upon ocular inspection in the area, several traces of uprooted marijuana plants were noticed in the area numbering to more or less one hundred (100) hills of suspected uprooted marijuana plants. Subject is currently under the temporary custody of NBI-NEMRO pending the filing of case for the above-mentioned violation on inquest proceedings.

body: A woman who introduced herself as someone who could facilitate the annulment of a marriage was arrested by agents of the Anti-Violence Against Women and Children Division in an entrapment operation in Pasay City recently. The suspect was identified by NBI Director Virgilio L. Mendez as: MAY PANAGA TAZARO, of legal age and a resident of 120 Kaingin St., Malolos, and Bulacan. Investigation disclosed that sometime in July 2013, an acquaintance of Rodolfo Collantes Barcelona (complainant) named Lene Alinsonod and her companion named May Tazaro, visited him at his office in Pasay City. They came to discuss with him the topic of annulment. According to complainant, Tazaro told him that she is capable of processing court annulment cases. Thus, complainant told Tazaro about his friend a.k.a. Joseph who desires to have his marriage annulled. After complainant’s conversation with Lene Alinsonod and May Tazaro, he was convinced and believed that they indeed have the capacity to expedite the annulment of the marriage of his friend. He immediately called up Joseph and told him that he has someone who could help him in his annulment problem. Joseph gave complainant his approval to secure the services of the duo (Alinsonod and Tazaro). Complainant then told Alinsonod and Tazaro that they would be needing their services, who then demanded the amount of TWO HUNDRED FIFTY THOUSAND PESOS (Php 250,000.00) for the whole process. Of the aforesaid amount, Alinsonod and Tazaro immediately demanded the payment of the amount of ONE HUNDRED FIFTY THOUSAND PESOS (Php 150,000.00) as down payment, which the complainant had in his office and gave to them. The suspects in turn promised to finish the annulment case of a.k.a. Joseph and his wife by December 2013. Sometime in December 2013, May Tazaro and Lene Alinsonod gave Complainant copies of court documents from RTC Branch 85, Malolos City, Bulacan, purportedly the case for the annulment of marriage of a.k.a JOSEPH and his wife to wit: 1. Certification that the Court rendered a decision for Declaration of Nullity of Marriage; 2. Decision stating among others that “… judgement is hereby rendered, declaring the marriage between Petitioner and the Respondent VOID AB INITIO….”, 3. Entry of Judgement/Certificate of Finality of Judgment; and 4. Decree of Declaration of Absolute Nullity of Marriage. May Tazaro and Lene Alinsonod likewise furnished Complainant an NSO copy of the Certificate of Marriage between a.k.a. JOSEPH and his wife with marginal remarks (note) that “Pursuant to the Decision issued on May 10, 2012 by Judge xxx, Regional Trial Court, Third Judicial Region Branch xxx, Malolos, Bulacan under Civil Case No. xxx – M2011 the Marriage between JOSEPH xxx celebrated on January 7, 2001 in Calumpit, Bulacan is hereby declared null and void”; Because of the discrepancies in the documents that May Tazaro and Lene Alinsonod gave Complainant, he decided to file a complaint against them with the NBI. On April 30, 2014, a verification was made with the Philippine Statistics Authority (formerly National Statistics Office), regarding the copy of the Certificate of Marriage of a.k.a. JOSEPH and his wife, with the marginal remarks (note), given to the Complainant. It was learned that the said document is a fake. Sometime in the last week of April 2014, Suspect Tazaro followed-up with Complainant the payment of the remaining ONE HUNDRED THOUSAND PESOS (Php 100,000.00). Barcelona agreed to meet with her on 05 May 2014 at or about 12:00 o’ clock noon at the rotunda seat inside Harrison Plaza. He informed the NBI – AVAWCD investigators regarding the agreed meeting. At around 12:00 o’ clock noon of May 5, 2014, Complainant met with May Tazaro at Harrison Plaza in Manila. At around 01:00 o’clock on even date, Complainant’s son together with NBI investigators proceeded to Harrison Plaza while the operatives positioned themselves near the rotunda seats. When May Tazaro arrived at the appointed place and reminded complainant about his unpaid balance, he handed over the marked money to Tazaro. Investigators then approached Tazaro, introduced themselves and informed her of her case. May Tazaro gave her full name as MAY PANAGA TAZARO was apprised of her rights, and was brought to the NBI main office in Taft Avenue Manila where she was booked, photographed and fingerprinted and physically examined. Subject Tazaro was recommended for prosecution before the City Prosecutor of Manila for Swindling (Estafa) under Art. 315 of the Revised Penal Code, as amended.
