title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: On August 1, 2019, operatives of NBI-Special Operations Group (NBI-SOG) JENNY ANN PAJARES COLUMNA was arrested for Qualified Theft by virtue of Warrant of Arrest. Reference is the letter request of Ortega, Bacorro, Odulio, Calma & Carbonnel Law Office addressed to the Director to serve the Warrant of Arrest issued by RTC, Pasay City, Branch 114 against the Subject. COLUMNA was accused of taking Php 35,898,581.11 from SITC, the company she worked with as cashier. In the afternoon of the aforementioned date, NBI-SOG operatives was able to track down the Subject in Paranaque City, served the Warrant of Arrest and arrested the Subject. On August 2, 2019, operatives of NBI-Anti Violence Against Women and Children (NBI-AVAWCD) MAYOR CHESTER VERGARA y VILLAPANDO, Mayor of a municipality in Batangas, and his hitman RIZALITO MIRONDO y RAMIREZ a.k.a BONG for Grave Coercion. Subjects were arrested in an operation which stemmed from the complaint against alias Bong later identified as Subject Mirondo. According to the victim, she had been receiving death threats from Subject Mirondo and she filed cases with the RTC Imus, Cavite way back in 2005 for Acts of Lasciviousness and RA 7610 against the kin of the mayor. Subject Bong threatened the victim that she will be liquidated or killed if she will not withdraw the charges. On August 2, 2019, at around 4:45 p.m. Subject Bong together with a man who was later identified as Mayor Chester Vergara y Villapando of Batangas met the victim inside a restaurant in Malate, Manila. At this juncture, the NBI-AVAWCD operatives swoop in and arrested Subject Mayor Vergara and Subject Bong while convincing the victim to withdraw the charges. Subjects were informed of their rights under the Miranda Doctrine. Subjects were presented for Inquest before the Office of the City Prosecutor, Manila for Grave Coercion. On August 2, 2019, operatives of NBI-Central Visayas Regional Office (NBI-CEVRO) arrested ZENG DAN, QUAN YIQING, XIUZHU WEI, and XIUSHEN WEI (Chinese nationals) for Human Trafficking. Subjects were arrested for directly confederated and helped one another in consummating a transaction for monetary consideration in return for sexual favors. On the aforementioned date, an entrapment operation was conducted at the premises of Royal One KTV located within the compound of Tourist Golden Hotel and resulted in the arrest of the Subjects and the rescue of thirty-four (34) female Chinese nationals who disclosed that they were recruited for work in legal online gambling operation but were made to work as GRO at the KTV bar. Subjects allegedly asked for Php 35,000 as bar fine in return for sexual favors for three (3) trafficked persons. Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings for violation of RA 9208 as amended by RA 10364 (Expanded Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act). On August 5, 2019, operatives of NBI-Rizal District Office (NBI-RIZDO) seized counterfeit Lacoste perfumes with an estimated market value of Php 14.5 Million. Items were seized in Pasay City by virtue of Search Warrants. Charges for violation of RA 8293 (Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines) were filed against REVEZ TRADING, ALADA ONLINE SHOP, JINGZHU WU, JENIFER WU, LADONI MERCHANDISING, MINGZHU OUYANG, any of the proprietors, officers, employees, occupants of various stalls located at Baclaran Terminal Plaza and HSP2 Park Avenue Shoe Plaza, Pasay City. On August 5, 2019, operatives of NBI- Anti-Organized and Transnational Crime Division (NBI-AOTCD) arrested TAN XIAGUANG, ZHENG JIA LEI, SU ZHIWEI, LIN JIAN ZHOU (Chinese nationals), TRIAN BUI THU THUY (Vietnamese), and VIRGILIO CUYUGAN SAN JUAN (Filipino) for Kidnapping and Serious Illegal Detention. The case stemmed from a report of the Head Security of Alabang Village, Muntinlupa City regarding an alleged victim found in the village. According to the victim who works as an electrician for a Chinese employer who runs an online gambling company, he and his wife were kidnapped by Chinese nationals after they were suspected to have reported to the Chinese police the illegal activities of their employer. The victim said when he and his wife came home from Clark, Pampanga, they were suddenly handcuffed by Chinese nationals unknown to him at their residence and was locked. The victim stressed that they were detained for ten (10) days during which they were tortured. The victim was able to find an opportunity to escape and reported the situation to the village security guards. Unfortunately, he was not able to take his pregnant wife with him. Operatives proceeded to Southkey Hun, Alabang, Muntinlupa and found thereat the above-named Subjects whom the victim positively identified. It was then learned that the victim’s wife was sent back to China by the Subjects after they learned that they were being pursued by the authorities. Subjects were then placed under arrest for Kidnapping and Serious Illegal detention. They were presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor of Muntinlupa City. They are currently held at the NBI detention facility. In two separate operations dated August 6 & 7, 2019, operatives of NBI-Anti-Organized and Transnational Crime Division (NBI-AOTCD) arrested ROBERT WAYNE BOLING JR. and ALLAN ALBERT KERR aka SKIP, both American citizens. The US Embassy as well as US Department of Defense (DoD) agents requested the NBI to conduct a parallel investigation regarding US citizens and other foreigners who were able to hack DoD network systems and huge caches of documents containing personal information belonging to thousands of US military members. The information were then fraudulently used to obtain large amounts of money and sent to recipients most of whom are living in the Philippines. The hackers were later found out to be living in the Philippines. Thus, on August 6, 2019, a joint operation led by the Bureau of Immigration (BI), together with operatives of US Embassy Overseas Criminal Investigation, agents from US DoD and the NBI-AOTCD, was conducted resulting in the arrest of ROBERT WAYNE BOLING JR. in the province of Pampanga by virtue of Mission Order issued by the BI in lieu of Deportation Order on the ground that Subjects are undocumented aliens. BOLING is wanted in the US based on charges of wire fraud, conspiracy to commit money laundering and aggravated identity theft. The next day, August 7, 2019, ALLAN ALBERT KERR was arrested in the same province. Since subject foreigners are to be deported, Filipino citizens who will be proven to be in connivance with Subjects and received the benefits of the illegal acts shall be charged. Investigation of the said local cohorts is still being conducted. On August 6, 2019, operatives of NBI-National Capital Region (NBI-NCR) confiscated two (2) computers with a server using unauthorized or unlicensed Siemen software by virtue of Search Warrants. Due to the copyright infringement, the estimated loss or damage to the copyright holder is Php 10,400,000.00. The case stemmed from the letter complaint filed by Quisumbing Torres Law Office, on behalf of their client, Siemens Product Lifestyle Management Software Inc., respectfully requesting investigation and enforcement actions against an entity located in Calamba, Laguna that is engaged in unauthorized reproduction and unauthorized use of computer software programs containing copyrights created, developed, and owned by Siemens Product Lifestyle Management Software Inc. Charges for violation of RA 8293 (Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines) were filed against CALAMBA SHINEI INDUSTRY PHILIPPINES CORP. and/or CALAMBA SHINEI, AKIHIRO SUZUKI, HIDENORI TADA, KOZO SUGIURA, SHINICHI FUKUSHIMA, KENGO SUDA, TOMOHIRO KUBARU, JONA C. BRIZUELA, JONG HI KIM, CHOON SOO OH, KWAN SUN JIN, YOON SUNG LEE, ADAMSON PISIGAN, CHERRIE MANASE, CHONA GARCIA-ENDAYA, and/or any of its other proprietors, stockholders, directors, incorporators, officers, managers, employees, lessees, occupants of the premises located at Blk.6, Lot 2, Calamba Premiere International Park, Brgy. Batino, Calamba, Laguna. On August 6, 2019, operatives of NBI-Environmental Crime Division (NBI-EnCD) arrested ROMEO PADLAN y PEREZ for Robbery Extortion. Subject was arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from the complaint of DPWH Undersecretary Emil K. Sadain against the Subject. Subject was arrested after receiving Php 200,000.00. Subject threatened and intimidated Undersecretary Sadain to destroy his public image, career and his private life by taking advantage of his position as a media practitioner of DWSS 1494 unless given a monthly “payola” and a sum of Php 200,000.00. Subject was presented for inquest proceeding before the Office of the City Prosecutor, Manila City for violation of Article 219 (Robbery Extortion) of the Revised Penal Code, as amended. On August 8, 2019, operatives of NBI-International Airport Investigation Division (NBI-IAID) arrested LUCIO DICAL DALAWAMPU for Falsification of Documents. Subject was arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from the complaint of one of Subject’s victim who was denied departure by the Bureau of Immigration (BI) and who was charged with Falsification of Document as a result. According to the complainant/victim, she was applying for a Philippine passport when she came across the Subject who represented himself as an employee of the Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA) and he could expedite the processing of her passport for a fee amounting to Php 5,500.00. Believing that the passport was authentic, she travelled to Japan with her fiancé but was help by the BI for possession of fake passport. Consequently, she cooperated with the NBI and an entrapment operation was conducted resulting in the arrest of the Subject. Subject was charged with violation of Article 172 in relation to Article 171 of the Revised Penal Code before the Inquest Prosecutor of Pasay City. On August 10, 2019, operatives of NBI- Special Action Unit (NBI-SAU) arrested JUNG JU WAN, KIM TEA YANG, OH YOUNG SEONG, SONG JONG MIN, JIN JUN YOUNG, KIM DAE HYUN, SUNG WON KANG, YEONG HAK TAK, and YOUNG JO CHOI, all Korean nationals for Phishing. The operation stemmed from the information received by NBI-SAU concerning the illegal activity allegedly operated in two (2) residences by a group of Korean nationals in Angeles City. According to the information, the group’s modus is to steal personal and financial information from their telephone fraud/voice phishing victims and transfer their information into different blank cards. The group also possesses fraudulently-acquired bank cards and password machines which they use in transferring funds coming from said victims into different bank accounts under their control. They also used blank cards to duplicate the accounts and transfer the funds to other accounts which they have fraudulently applied. NBI-SAU operatives recovered one (1) heat-sealed, transparent plastic sachet containing white crystalline substance, two (2) pieces of aluminum foil, seven (7) sets of transparent sachet containing four (4) tablets, several dried stems contained inside a cigarette box, used foil contained inside a white sheet of paper, and loose crystalline substance placed on top of a transparent self-sealing plastic contained inside a white sheet of paper. The forensic examination of the seized items yielded positive with presence of METHAMPHETAMINE HYDROCHLORIDE, and MARIJUANA. Moreover, one of the subjects, KIM TEA YOUNG is allegedly a fugitive in Korea for fraud. Verification is being done through the NBI-International Operations Division (NBI-IOD). Violations of R.A 8484 (Access Devices Regulation Act of 1998) and R.A. 9165 (Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002) were filed against the Subjects. On August 12, 2019, operatives of NBI-Anti-Organized and Transnational Crime Division arrested ANICETO DAVID y CAPARINO for Statutory Rape. Subject was arrested by virtue of Warrant of Arrest for Lascivious Conduct and Statutory Rape. The case stemmed from the complaint of a minor who was molested and raped by the Subject in separate occasions sometime in April 2014 and April 2015. The victim stated that she did not tell anybody about what the Subject did to her because he threatened to stab her. But when the victim learned that Subject was in prison, she finally told her mother what Subject Aniceto did her in the past. On February 7, 2018, criminal complaint for Rape in relation to RA 7610 was then filed by the PNP, Bacolod City Police Office, Women and Children Protection Desk before the City Prosecutors Office, Bacolod City against Subject Aniceto. When an information was received that Subject was hiding at his cousin’s house in Malinao, Aklan, a joint operation by NBI-AOTCD and NBI Antique was conducted resulting in the arrest of Subject Aniceto. Subject is presently detained at NBI Antique. On August 16, 2019, operatives of NBI-International Operation Division (NBI-IOD) arrested AHMED RAGAB RAMADAN AHMED (Egyptian national) MUWAFAG YUSUF OMER MUSA alias MWAFAG YUSUF OMER (Sudanese national), LOREZEL MAINIT REYES-SARTE alias LORIZEL SARTE, LAILA VERANO AQUINO, JHONA PESTIJO PASTORA, RHAZMALYN IBRAHIM MUSA, JOSEPHUS ASKIN PACER, VEA CASANDRA TINDUGAN BERJA, HOWARD JUSTIN VILLATE APUNTAR, GEANMARIE GARAY NER alias JEAN MARIE NER, and JULIETA FERRER MENDOZA (Filipino) for illegal recruitment. A complaint was filed against RM ADVENT SERVICES INC., a recruitment agency situated in Pasay City. According to the victims, they were interviewed on the first week of August 2019 by Subject Omer who assured them that they could be deployed in Saudi Arabia as domestic helpers provided that they complete the necessary documents. They also stated that they were pre-interviewed by Subject Ner and they were assisted by Subjects Sarte, Aquino, and ZESSAR ANTIGRO (at-large). The complainants/victims alleged that they were directed by the employees of RM ADVENT to recruit workers for overseas employment pending their deployment to Saudi Arabia. The three complainants/victims were scheduled to return to the office of RD ADVENT on August 16, 2019 to submit the required documents. At this juncture NBI operatives scheduled an interdiction at RD ADVENT. The operation resulted in the arrest of the Subjects who could not present any authority or license to recruit workers for overseas employment. Violation of R.A. 8042 as amended by R.A. 10022 or the Migrant Workers and Overseas Filipinos Act of 1995 were filed against the eleven (11) arrested subjects, two (2) subjects at-large and all of RM ADVENT GLOBAL SERVICES INC. On August 16, 2019, JOSE ADRIAN TIAMSON DERA, co-accused of Senator Leila De Lima in an illegal drug case and the only co-accused who remained at large for the last two (2) years, was arrested. Subject Dera was never arrested and did not surrender to authorities and remained at large for 2 years since the Warrant of Arrest for violation of RA 9165. After the joint efforts of NBI-Special Task Force (NBI-STF), NBI-Death Investigation Division (NBI-DID), and NBI-Anti-Human Trafficking Division (NBI-AHTRAD), Subject Dera was finally located at Diamond Subdivision, Balibago, Angeles City, Pampanga and was therefore arrested at his residence in the said location. On August 19, 2019, operatives of NBI-National Capital Region (NBI-NCR) arrested ANGEL P. BAUTISTA, Acting-Deputy Director General for Administration and concurrent Chief Administrative Officer of the Cultural Properties Division (CPRD); and ERNESTO B. TORIBIO JR., Administrative Assistant II of the CPRD, National Museum of the Philippines. Subjects were arrested in an operation which stemmed from the complaint referred by Commissioner Greco B. Belgica, of the Presidential Anti-Corruption Commission (PACC). According to the complaint, a certain Ernesto B. Toribio, an employee of the National Museum of the Philippines, demanded Php 120,000.00 from the complainant, an American treasure-hunter, to expedite/fast tract the issuance of treasure-hunting permit. The complainant disclosed that he is scheduled to meet Subject Toribio in a restaurant in Pasay City on August 19, 2019. With this, the entrapment operation was conducted resulting in the arrest of the Subjects. Charges for Violation of Article 210 (Direct Bribery) of the Revised Penal Code and Violation of R.A. 3019 (Anti-Graft Practices Act) were filed against the subjects before the Office of the Prosecutor, Pasay City. On August 19, 2019, operatives of NBI-CALABARZON JIMMUEL D. CRUZAT and JAN HENRY JAVIER for Human Trafficking. Subjects were arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from the information received about the alleged human trafficking activities of the owner/proprietor of Sir Manny BRS Spa located at Brgy. Bolbok, Batangas City. Acting on the information, the entrapment operation was conducted resulting in the arrest of the Subjects. Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings for violation of RA 9208 (Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act). A recommendation for the direct filing of charges against the registered owner of the said spa, MANUEL D. DIMACUHA, was also made and sustained by the prosecutor. In six (6) separate operations, operatives of NBI-Intellectual Property Rights Division (NBI-IPRD) seized various counterfeit products with an estimated aggregate amount of Php 21,043,080.00. On August 5, 2019, counterfeit Powerflex and Hypertech cable wires with an estimated value of Php 102,500.00 were seized in Binondo and Tondo, Manila by virtue of Search Warrants. Charges for violation of RA 8293 (Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines) were filed against John/Jane Does/owners/operators/occupants of various stores located in the said area. On August 6, 2019, counterfeit Puma shirts, jackets, slippers, and shorts with an estimated amount of Php 416,000.00 were seized in Pasay City by virtue of Search Warrants. Charges for violation of RA 8293 (Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines) were filed against John/Jane Does/owner/occupants/proprietors of various stores in Baclaran, Pasay City. On August 7, 2019, 30,860 pieces of Irwin diamond discs/blades with an estimated value of Php 11,726,800.00 were seized in Meycauayan, Bulacan and Quezon City by virtue of Search Warrants. Charges for violation of RA 8293 (Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines) were filed against Vicente C. Pao, Nenita U. Sinfuego, Jowett Sinfuego, Maridel T. Subjects were given ample opportunity to explain. But instead of complaining, they started pointing to each other and mentioning a certain Via Gozo and a lawyer whose name they could not recall. It was at this point that the operatives were contrained to place them under arrest. The BSP Banknote and Securities Production Management Department issued a certification that the two (2) pieces 100 US Dollars notes, representative samples of the 196 pieces submitted for examination were found to be counterfeit. Subjects were brought for inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor for violation of Article 168 of the Revised Penal Code. Information was received that several young girls were allegedly being trafficked and exploited for commercial sex in a spa massage parlor inside BF Homes, Paranaque City. Surveillance operations were conducted thereafter. Then on the above-mentioned date, rescue and entrapment operation was conducted with the assistance of CSWD, Paranaque City and Southern Police District. The operation resulted in the arrest of the Subjects and the rescue of seven (7) victims, three (3) of whom are minors. Based on the evidence gathered, it was revealed that sometime in March 2017, Complainant and Subject began their romantic relationship but in April 2017, Subject threatened the Complainant that if the latter will not heed to the monetary demands of the former, he will expose their relationship to Complainant’s brother and children. Complainant became very afraid of the threats so she heeded to the said demands. Subject also forced the Complainant to use methamphetamine hydrochloride which the Complainant did out of extreme fear of the threats and this happened several times. Complainant did not also know that Subject hid a camera and recorded the activity for the purpose of blackmail in the future. Complainant only knew of the videos recently when new threats were sent by the Subject, demanding Php 3,000.00, a car, and a laptop. Subject threatened the Complainant that should the latter fail to meet his demands, he will upload the video on Facebook, and send it as well to the Complainant’s family, workplace, and around her community. With this, the entrapment operation was conducted resulting in the arrest of the Subject. They were instructed to tell that they were 23 years old and that Subject would take care of securing their birth certificate from the Philippine Statistics Authority. Subject was presented for Inquest Proceedings before the Department of Justice and is currently detained at the NBI Detention Facility. A certain Linda Amigos Solaiman applied for an NBI clearance and presented PhilHealth ID and photocopy of Certificate of Live Birth. When asked as to her date of birth, she failed to answer correctly as stated in the Certificate of Live Birth. Due to constant questioning, she admitted that it was not her true birth certificate. Subject RANIA surrendered machine copies of Philippine passport and LTO student permit both in the name of Linda Amigos Solaiman. Subject was then placed under arrest. Charges for Falsification of Public Documents under Article 172 in relation Article 171 of the Revised Penal Code were filed against the Subject before the Office of the Prosecutor, Pagadian City.

NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION

On August 1, 2019, operatives of NBI-Special Operations Group (NBI-SOG) JENNY ANN PAJARES COLUMNA was arrested for Qualified Theft by virtue of Warrant of Arrest. Reference is the letter request of Ortega, Bacorro, Odulio, Calma & Carbonnel Law Office addressed to the Director to serve the Warrant of Arrest issued by RTC, Pasay City, Branch 114 against the Subject. COLUMNA was accused of taking Php 35,898,581.11 from SITC, the company she worked with as cashier. In the afternoon of the aforementioned date, NBI-SOG operatives was able to track down the Subject in Paranaque City, served the Warrant of Arrest and arrested the Subject. Subjects were arrested in an operation which stemmed from the complaint against alias Bong later identified as Subject Mirondo. According to the victim, she had been receiving death threats from Subject Mirondo and she filed cases with the RTC Imus, Cavite way back in 2005 for Acts of Lasciviousness and RA 7610 against the kin of the mayor. Subject Bong threatened the victim that she will be liquidated or killed if she will not withdraw the charges. On August 2, 2019, at around 4:45 p.m. Subject Bong together with a man who was later identified as Mayor Chester Vergara y Villapando of Batangas met the victim inside a restaurant in Malate, Manila. At this juncture, the NBI-AVAWCD operatives swoop in and arrested Subject Mayor Vergara and Subject Bong while convincing the victim to withdraw the charges. Subjects were informed of their rights under the Miranda Doctrine. Subjects were presented for Inquest before the Office of the City Prosecutor, Manila for Grave Coercion. Subjects were arrested for directly confederated and helped one another in consummating a transaction for monetary consideration in return for sexual favors. On the aforementioned date, an entrapment operation was conducted at the premises of Royal One KTV located within the compound of Tourist Golden Hotel and resulted in the arrest of the Subjects and the rescue of thirty-four (34) female Chinese nationals who disclosed that they were recruited for work in legal online gambling operation but were made to work as GRO at the KTV bar. Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings for violation of RA 9208 as amended by RA 10364 (Expanded Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act). The case stemmed from a report of the Head Security of Alabang Village, Muntinlupa City regarding an alleged victim found in the village. According to the victim who works as an electrician for a Chinese employer who runs an online gambling company, he and his wife were kidnapped by Chinese nationals after they were suspected to have reported to the Chinese police the illegal activities of their employer. The victim said when he and his wife came home from Clark, Pampanga, they were suddenly handcuffed by Chinese nationals unknown to him at their residence and was locked. The victim stressed that they were detained for ten (10) days during which they were tortured. The victim was able to find an opportunity to escape and reported the situation to the village security guards. Unfortunately, he was not able to take his pregnant wife with him. Operatives proceeded to Southkey Hun, Alabang, Muntinlupa and found thereat the above-named Subjects whom the victim positively identified. It was then learned that the victim’s wife was sent back to China by the Subjects after they learned that they were being pursued by the authorities. Subjects were then placed under arrest for Kidnapping and Serious Illegal detention. They were presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor of Muntinlupa City. They are currently held at the NBI detention facility. The US Embassy as well as US Department of Defense (DoD) agents requested the NBI to conduct a parallel investigation regarding US citizens and other foreigners who were able to hack DoD network systems and huge caches of documents containing personal information belonging to thousands of US military members. The information were then fraudulently used to obtain large amounts of money and sent to recipients most of whom are living in the Philippines. The hackers were later found out to be living in the Philippines. Thus, on August 6, 2019, a joint operation led by the Bureau of Immigration (BI), together with operatives of US Embassy Overseas Criminal Investigation, agents from US DoD and the NBI-AOTCD, was conducted resulting in the arrest of ROBERT WAYNE BOLING JR. in the province of Pampanga by virtue of Mission Order issued by the BI in lieu of Deportation Order on the ground that Subjects are undocumented aliens. BOLING is wanted in the US based on charges of wire fraud, conspiracy to commit money laundering and aggravated identity theft. The next day, August 7, 2019, ALLAN ALBERT KERR was arrested in the same province. Since subject foreigners are to be deported, Filipino citizens who will be proven to be in connivance with Subjects and received the benefits of the illegal acts shall be charged. Investigation of the said local cohorts is still being conducted. Subjects were given ample opportunity to explain. But instead of complaining, they started pointing to each other and mentioning a certain Via Gozo and a lawyer whose name they could not recall. It was at this point that the operatives were contrained to place them under arrest. The BSP Banknote and Securities Production Management Department issued a certification that the two (2) pieces 100 US Dollars notes, representative samples of the 196 pieces submitted for examination were found to be counterfeit. Subjects were brought for inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor for violation of Article 168 of the Revised Penal Code. Information was received that several young girls were allegedly being trafficked and exploited for commercial sex in a spa massage parlor inside BF Homes, Paranaque City. Surveillance operations were conducted thereafter. A certain Linda Amigos Solaiman applied for an NBI clearance and presented PhilHealth ID and photocopy of Certificate of Live Birth. When asked as to her date of birth, she failed to answer correctly as stated in the Certificate of Live Birth. Due to constant questioning, she admitted that it was not her true birth certificate. Linda Amigos Solaiman presented her true birth certificate and it was found out that her true name is RANIA ALON PAHME. Subject RANIA surrendered machine copies of Philippine passport and LTO student permit both in the name of Linda Amigos Solaiman. Subject was then placed under arrest. Charges for Falsification of Public Documents under Article 172 in relation Article 171 of the Revised Penal Code were filed against the Subject before the Office of the Prosecutor, Pagadian City.

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today announced the arrest of an individual by operatives of NBI-Special Action Unit (NBI-SAU) in Pasay City for alleged online scam. NBI Officer-in-Charge (OIC) Director Eric B. Distor identified the Subject as HANNA CHRIS GONZALES DADEA. Distor said that the case stemmed from a complaint filed against an alias MARILOU EFSOR for Alleged Identity Theft and Estafa in connection with an online scam. According to the complainant, she is in business with MARILOU ZARTIGA EFSOR and that they’ve been transacting with MARICEL MENDOZA in selling gold jewelries. Surprisingly, complainant found out that they’ve been subjects of online rants and complaints as scammers after buyer-victims purportedly paid them for jewelries they failed to deliver. It turns out that a fake Facebook account under the name MARILOU EFSOR had been transacting with buyers and soliciting sales of gold jewelries thru online banking. Meanwhile, MARICEL MENDOZA, under false pretenses, would communicate with business partners. MARILOU EFSOR would then claim that she was the one who deposited the payments by sending edited screenshots of the online deposits. Through delivery riders, it is MARILOU EFSOR who would in fact receive the gold jewelries that were meant for the buyer-victim. Consequently, complainant and MARILOU EFSOR would lose all the gold jewelries to MARICEL MENDOZA and fake MARILOU EFSOR. They were then made accountable for the fraudulent transactions to their damage and prejudice. Under strict orders from OIC-Director Distor, NBI-SAU operatives conducted an entrapment operation to apprehend the culprits. Coincidentally, complainant was set to give a set of jewelry and Php 4,000 cash to MARICEL MENDOZA through a delivery rider service. MARICEL MENDOZA falsely represented herself again as the buyer when in truth, another person made the payments for the jewelries. The delivery service rider agreed to cooperate with the operatives and provided information on the details of the drop off and who booked the transport. It was found out that a certain MARILOU booked the transport and a person named CHRIS is the recipient. An undercover delivery rider then proceeded to deliver the said jewelries and cash. Upon reaching the drop-off point at No.125 P. Manahan St., Pasay City, a female individual, named CHRIS later identified as HANNA CHRIS GONZALES DADEA, received the package. Operatives then identified themselves, authority, and purpose of the operation. HANNA CHRIS GONZALES DADEA was apprised of her constitutional rights and was apprehended. Subject HANNA CHRIS GONZALES DADEA was brought to SAU office for the proper booking procedures. Several complainants manifested that they will file complaints against Subject DADEA for alleged online scam. Thorough investigation continues on other personalities such as DADEA’s father, sister, boyfriend, and other individuals in their possible involvement in the said online scam. Subject was presented for Inquest proceeding before the Office of Prosecutor of Pasay City.

title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today announced the arrest of three individuals in Recto Avenue, Manila, on February 1, 2021, for falsifying various government documents. NBI Officer-in-Charge (OIC) Director Eric B. Distor identified the Subjects as JAY TINIO y HUGANAS, JOJO DELIM y ROCABERTE, and ABBYGAIL PASCUA y RUGAY. Distor said that the case stemmed from an information received regarding individuals who are allegedly selling fake NBI clearances and other various government documents such as LTO ID/Student Permits, PSA Birth Certificate, and TIN ID along Recto Avenue, Manila near Interface Computer College Recto Campus. He added that surveillance operation was conducted to verify the said information. Result of surveillance established that anyone who passes by that area in Recto Avenue is being asked the question “Magpapagawa ka bang ID/NBI Clearance/Birth Certificate?” Some sellers even have signage of the documents that they cater. Sellers charge Php2,500 for rush transactions and Php500 for non-rush transactions. Yielding positive result in the surveillance operation, an entrapment operation was hatched on February 1, 2021. Poseur customers went to the target area. Thereat, Subject JAY TINIO approached them and asked if they will avail of ID, Birth Certificate, NBI Clearance, or LTO. One poseur customer asked for the cost of NBI Clearance to which Subject JAY answered that it costs Php2,500. Poseur customer haggled until Subject JAY agreed to give it for Php2,000. Subject then asked for fifty percent down payment and afterwards asked for the poseur customer’s personal details. Subject JAY told the poseur customer that he could get the NBI Clearance after two hours. When the Subject sent a message to the poseur customer that the NBI Clearance is ready for release, NBI-AOTCD operatives positioned themselves for the entrapment operation. The said clearance was set to be delivered at a fast food chain. Thereat, a man identified as Subject JOJO DELIM arrived and delivered a small brown envelope to a girl identified as Subject ABBYGAIL PASCUA. Subject ABBYGAIL approached Subject JAY and handed over to him the brown envelope. Subject JAY then gave the brown envelope containing the fake NBI Clearance to the poseur customer. Upon hand over the marked money, operatives announced their authorities and placed the Subjects under arrest. Found and seized from the possession of Subject JAY were the marked money, his cellphone, and fake NBI Clearance while taken from Subjects ABBYGAIL and JOJO was an ecobag containing various documents with a dry seal stamp, signages of documents they were offering, and their cellphones. Verification with the NBI Information and Communication Technology Services revealed that the NBI Clearance from the Subjects was not duly issued by the NBI. Charges for violation of Article 172 in relation to Article 171 of the Revised Penal Code (Falsification of Public Documents) were charged against the Subjects before the Office of the City Prosecutor, Manila.

title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today said operatives of NBI-Task Force Against Illegal Drugs (NBI-TFAID) arrested seven (7) Chinese nationals on August 3, 2020 for Kidnapping and Serious Illegal Detention. NBI Officer-In-Charge (OIC) Eric B. Distor identified the Subjects as NI LINGKANG, HU RUIGUANG, XIAO HUI aka XIE CHUN HUI, XIAO ZI aka WANG HAO WEI, XIAO JI aka XIE ZHI HONG, ALE WONG aka WANG XIAO LONG, and ALANG CHEN HAI LONG aka SHU WEI SONG. OIC Distor said an information was received regarding the alleged abduction of three (3) Chinese nationals and subsequently detained against their will at Multinational Village, Paranaque City. After confirming the whereabouts of the three (3) Chinese nationals abducted, NBI-TFAID immediately coordinated with the local police and security officers of the said village and devised a plan for the rescue operation. Operatives were able to tactically enter and thereat they saw two (2) Chinese nationals namely: NI LIKANG and HU RUIGUANG, guarding three (3) Chinese nationals lying inside a room on the second floor with apparent contusions, hematoma, and abrasions all over their bodies and suffering from excruciating pain.With the help of an NBI interpreter, TFAID operatives were able to interview the three (3) Chinese nationals. According to them, in the afternoon of August 2, 2020, while inside their house located in Betlehem St., Multinational Village Village, Paranaque City, several Chinese barged in, and without any explanation, forced them to board a vehicle and brought them to a house located at No.2 Judea St., Multinational Village. While inside the house, they were immediately blindfolded by seven (7) Chinese men and were asked to return the money they allegedly stole from their boss. Hard-hitting blows were thrown upon them causing several injuries to different parts of their bodies. The three (3) Chinese victims were detained against their will for two (2) days until they were rescued TFAID Agents. Above-named Subjects were then arrested and were informed of their rights under the circumstances through the NBI interpreter. They were,thereafter, presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor, Paranaque City for violation of Article 267 (Kidnapping and Serious Illegal Detention) of the Revised Penal Code of the Philippines. They are presently detained at NBI Detention Center.

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) thru its Gender and Development – Focal Person System (GAD-FPS) joins the celebration of the National Women’s Month in March 2022. NBI OIC-Director Eric B. A similar activity offering freebies for women employees will also be conducted at the NBI Office in Vtech Tower in Araneta avenue, QC, in support of the celebration. body: PRESS STATEMENT April 21, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } PRESS RELEASE | NBI ARRESTS AN INDIVIDUAL FOR VOYEURISM, VIOLENCE, AND GRAVE THREATS The National Bureau of Investigation-Cybercrime Division (NBI-CCD) apprehended a male individual for alleged violations of R.A. No. 9995, R.A. No. 9262, Grave Threats, Grave Coercion, and Robbery. On April 10, 2026, Complainant filed a complaint before the NBI-CCD against the Subject who was her former partner. Complainant alleged that she was previously in a romantic relationship with the Subject, which began in 2018 under false pretenses, as the latter misrepresented himself to be single despite being legally married. Subject later turned abusive, involving repeated acts of physical violence, intimidation, harassment, and unlawful entry even after their separation in December 2023. On March 6, 2026, the Subject forcibly entered Complainant’s residence, physically assaulted and raped her, and recorded the act without her consent. He subsequently used the video to threaten, humiliate, and coerce her, and later disseminated it to third parties when she refused to comply. The Subject also committed acts of robbery, theft, and grave threats, including an incident on April 16, 2026 in Baclaran, Pasay City, and continued sending death threats through social media while displaying images of a firearm. Despite being under fear for her life and placed under protective custody, the Complainant continued to receive threats, including a direct statement from the Subject that he would kill her. On April 18, 2026, the Subject persisted in harassing the Complainant via video call, coercing her to meet him while threatening further harm and distribution of the recorded video. Acting on real-time information, NBI-CCD operatives conducted a hot pursuit operation. Subject was successfully located and arrested. A screwdriver was recovered from his possession, further raising concern for the Complainant’s safety had authorities not intervened. Subject was presented for inquest before the Office of the City Prosecutor in Pasay City. “This arrest sends a strong message that those who exploit, abuse, and instill fear will be found and held accountable. The use of intimate images to threaten, coerce, or humiliate will be pursued with the full force of the law,” NBI Director Atty. Melvin A. Matibag said. He further urged the victims of this kind of offense to come forward so authorities can act decisively. #NBIServes

body: PRESS STATEMENT May 11, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } PRESS RELEASE | NBI RECEIVES COMPLAINT SEEKING INVESTIGATION OF PGMN, FRANCO MABANTA, AND CJ HIRRO OVER ALLEGED DISINFORMATION OPERATIONS AND PAID POLITICAL CONTENT PASAY CITY, Philippines — The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) received a formal request from former Quezon City 4th District Congressman Marvin D. Rillo seeking the investigation of Peanut Gallery Media Network (PGMN), Franco Mabanta, and CJ Hirro over allegations of disinformation operations, fake news, and malicious paid political content creation during the 2025 Midterm Elections. In his letter addressed to NBI Director Melvin Matibag, Rillo alleged that PGMN and its personalities published several online videos and social media posts that imputed corruption and dishonesty against him in connection with an infrastructure project involving the Carlos L. Albert High School Gymnasium. Rillo claimed that the online materials were malicious, misleading, and failed to include available clarifications from the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH), which had earlier stated that the project was undergoing phased construction. The former lawmaker further alleged that the publication of said materials may have been part of a paid or commissioned political operation intended to damage his reputation during the election period. He cited recent reports and public discussions involving PGMN’s alleged dealings with political clients, as well as the recent NBI entrapment operation involving PGMN founder Franco Mabanta. body: The National Bureau of Investigation today said operatives of NBI-Anti-Organized and Transnational Crime Division (NBI-AOTCD) have arrested an individual representing herself as sister of the late Senator Miriam Defensor Santiago, for alleged Estafa and Usurpation of Authority on May 29, 2017. NBI-AOTCD received a complaint concerning a certain ATTY. PAULA DIMPNA BEATRIZ PALMA DEFENSOR for alleged Estafa and Usurpation of Authority. Complainant met the subject at the Department of Justice (DOJ) sometime in July 2016 when she was following-up a case against her. Verification conducted with RTC Branch 20, Malolos, Bulacan revelead that Subject has an outstanding Warrant of Arrest for Estafa issued on May 24, 2007. body: PRESS STATEMENT January 28, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI), under the leadership of NBI Director Judge Jaime B. Santiago (Ret.), arrested five (5) individuals for selling imported meat products without necessary documents or clearances from regulatory government agencies. On January 20, 2025, the NBI-Special Task Force (STF) received a request for assistance from the Office of the Executive Director of National Meat Inspection Service (NMIS) against certain individuals for alleged selling of “hot meats.” NMIS disclosed that there was an on-going transaction involving the unknown individuals who were offering imported wholesale meat products for a price less than its market value. It was relayed that a certain KIEL ROZZAN BARBADO MENDOZA arranged a meet up in Caloocan City to collect the ordered 75 sacks of “hot meat” with a total weight of 1,500 kilograms, sold for Php163.00 per kilogram. Accordingly, the amount would be paid through online transfer but agreed to accept in part cash amounting to P50,000.00 as initial payment. With these, an entrapment operation was hatched in the afternoon of January 20, 2025. The operation resulted in the arrest of MELBA CABENIAN y YURAG, MARK CHRISTIAN MISSION y ZAMORA, BREGIDO ELBINA y LACERNA, and RINIE SANCHEZ Y CUPAL. A total of 3,680 kilograms of poultry products originating from China were found inside the two refrigerated trucks. Further investigation disclosed that the “hot meats” came from a cold storage plant in Sta. Maria, Bulacan. Thus, a follow-up operation was conducted which resulted in the arrest of ANA CRISTINA GALVEZ y DEXIMO after she failed to present necessary documents and permits related to the discovered “hot meats”. A total of 22,000 kilograms of assorted frozen meats and poultry products originating from China were found in the said storage plant. NMIS certified the discovery as Unfit for Human Consumption and Subject to Confiscation due to violation of RA 10536, an Act amending RA 9296, also known as “The Meat Inspection Code of the Philippines”, in relation to Department of Agriculture Administrative Order No. 26, Series of 2005. The confiscated poultry products were brought to the NBI Office in Pasay for temporary custody and further instruction from the NMIS. Charges for violations of Sections 48, 49, 50, 51, 52, 53, and 54 under Chapter XII of RA 9296, as amended by RA 10536, and violations of Sec 7 (g) and (j) of RA 12022 or the “Anti-Agricultural Sabotage Act of 2024” were filed against MARK CHRISTIAN MISSION, MELBA CABENIAN, BREGIDO LACERNNA ELBIÑA, Jr., RINIE SANCHEZ, ANA CRISTINA GALVEZ, and KIEL ROZAN BARBADO MENDOZA (at-large).

body: PRESS STATEMENT August 19, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } NBI, BOC Pinuri ang Joint Task Force sa Pagkakadakip ng Bilyon-Bilyong Iligal na Kargamento Sa pagpapakita ng pagkakaisa at tagumpay na operasyon, kinilala nina National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Director Atty. Melvin Matibag at Bureau of Customs (BOC) Commissioner Ariel F. Nepomuceno ang mga huwarang tauhan mula sa dalawang ahensya sa pamamagitan ng Certificates of Commendation noong Agosto 13, 2026, sa ginanap na BOC Collectors Conference. Pormal na kinikilala ng pagpaparangal ang kritikal na kontribusyon ng mga operatiba ng NBI at ng Customs Intelligence and Investigation Service (CIIS) sa magkasanib na mga operasyon. Ang pinagsamang pagsisikap na ito ay nagresulta sa malakihang pagharang at pagkakadakip sa mga kargamento ng iligal na sigarilyo sa North Harbor sa Maynila at sa Mandaue City, Cebu. Sa kanyang talumpati, binigyang-diin ni Atty. Matibag na kumplikado ang pagpapatupad ng batas laban sa mga smuggler, kaya ang mga modernong kampanya laban sa smuggling ay nangangailangan ng pagtutulungan ng mga ahensya ng gobyerno. “Ang tagumpay na ito ay karapat-dapat na kilalanin dahil ang pagpapatigil sa pagpasok at paggalaw ng mga iligal na kalakal ay hindi madaling gawin,” pahayag ni Director Matibag. Idinagdag pa niya: “Nangangailangan ito ng impormasyon, maingat na koordinasyon, tamang pagpaplano, at higit sa lahat, mga taong handang gawin ang kanilang bahagi at tapusin ang operasyon.” Ang malalaking pagkumpiskang ito ay nagpapatunay ng pinalakas na kasunduan sa pagitan ng NBI at BOC. Muling nagkasundo ang pamunuan ng dalawang ahensya na aktibong suportahan ang isa’t isa, sa pamamagitan ng pagsasama ng kanilang mga intelligence framework at mapagkukunan para sa iisang layunin: ang pagtataguyod ng mas ligtas na mga komunidad, pagbuo ng mas matatag na pamahalaan, at paghahatid ng tapat na serbisyo publiko. Alinsunod sa direktiba ni Pangulong Ferdinand Marcos, Jr., kinumpirma ng NBI at BOC na patuloy pang paiigtingin ang mga agresibo, magkasama, at intelligence-driven na operasyon sa lahat ng pangunahing daungan sa Pilipinas upang kalasin ang mga network ng iligal na kalakalan at pangalagaan ang pambansang seguridad sa ekonomiya. https://www.facebook.com/reel/1082103574764606

body: In line with the relentless campaign of the government against illegal drugs, the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today said operatives of the NBI-Task Force Against Illegal Drugs (NBI-TFAID) have seized more than10 kilos of dangerous drugs in Ermita, Manila last Friday. NBI Director Dante A. Gierran said the seized drugs have an estimated street value of about Php 60 Million, stressing that the NBI will continue in its war against all forms of illegal drugs and other substances. The operation stemmed from a letter from the Bureau of Corrections requesting assistance in the arrest of a group that is allegedly involved in large scale selling of drugs in south of Metro Manila. Under strict orders from Director Gierran, NBI-TFAID operatives coordinated with the BuCor officials for the implementation of counter action against the aforesaid group resulting in the seizure of the drugs. During the conduct of the operation, the NBI operatives only found the abandoned vehicle park along the sidewalk that contained the illegal drugs. During the examination of the seized drugs by the NBI-Forensic Chemistry Division, it showed positive indication for the presence of DIMETHOXY METHYLPHENETHYLANIME, a dangerous drug.

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today announced the conviction of a woman for human trafficking by a Quezon City Court. In a 28-page decision rendered by Branch 86, Regional Trial Court of Quezon City on April 7, 2021, the Court sentenced JENNIFFER PESTAÑO y CHUA a.k.a. Jennylyn to life imprisonment and to pay the fine of P5Million. The Court also ordered Jennelyn to pay each of the 3 private complainants P50,000.00 as Moral damages and P50,000.00 as Exemplary damages. NBI Officer-in-Charge (OIC) Director Eric B. Distor said Subject JENNIFER PESTAÑO and a Minor were arrested by Agents of NBI-Anti-Violence Against Women and Children Division (NBI-AVAWCD) on September 10, 2019 in Novaliches, Quezon City. The subject minor was turned to the DSWD while subject PESTAÑO was charged for 12 counts of Qualified Trafficking in Persons under R.A. 9208 or the Anti-trafficking in Persons Act of 2003 as amended by R.A. 10364 or the “Expanded Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2012”. Distor said that last September 2019, NBI-AVAWCD received a report regarding the human trafficking activities of the subjects in Quezon City. Distor added that after verifying the veracity of the information, NBI-AVAWCD operatives hatched the entrapment operation which resulted in the arrest of the two (2) subjects and rescue of twelve (12) minor girls. In a series of court appearances, 3 NBI-AVAWCD operatives, one (1) NBI Photographer, and three (3) minors from the alleged victims were offered by the prosecution as witnesses. Thus, on April 07, 2021, a judgment was promulgated by the court finding the subject PESTAÑO guilty beyond reasonable doubt for Qualified Trafficking in Persons as defined and penalized under R.A. 9208 as further amended by R.A, 10364.

body: In line with the government’s relentless campaign to eradicate intellectual property piracy in the country, the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) conducted a series of operations that led to the seizure of P362 million worth of fake goods for the first month of the year. For the entire month of January 2013, the NBI – Intellectual Property Rights Division based on the complaints of the registered trademark/tradename holder and/or their representative, was able to secure the issuance of forty four (44) search warrants. By virtue of these search warrants, 2,552,073.00 articles/items with an estimated value of Php 363,475,000.00 were seized. Among the major operations for January were: 1) On January 11, 2013, the NBI-IPRD served a search warrant on manufacturing firm in Taliba St. San Rafael Village, Tondo, Manila resulting in the seizure of 2,406,000,000 pieces of fake Snow Bear Candy with an estimated value of Php 2,400,000.00; 2) A week after, a warehouse located at Del Monte Avenue Quezon City was raided yielding 141,020.00 pieces of counterfeit Nokia products amounting to Php 352,550,000.00; and 3) Later, on January 29, 2013, by virtue of search warrants, 17 stalls located at F.B. Harrison, Baclaran, Pasay City was raided and some 5,000 pairs of faked sandals/footwear bearing the trademark Hotflops/Hotflopz and Gellato with an estimated value of Php 7,500,000.00 Subsequently, charges for Violation of Republic Act 8293 were recommended against the owners/managers and/or occupants of the aforementioned firms in different prosecutor’s offices in Metro Manila. For the past years, the NBI has kept its commitment to the global concern against producers and distributors of counterfeit goods. Operatives of the NBI-AOCD arranged an operation for the suspect’s arrest. In the afternoon of February 25, 2013, complainant and suspect meet at SM Manila. NBI operatives who accompanied Edano strategically positioned themselves nearby. Edano handed the marked money to Villaflor. Moments after, NBI agents moved in and apprehended suspect Villaflor. He was subsequently brought to the NBI. At the Bureau, suspect gave his name as Major Ricardo V. Villaflor of the Armed Forces of the Philippines. body: PRESS STATEMENT May 30, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } NBI Director Judge Jaime B. Santiago (Ret.) gave recognition to the men and women of the Comptroller Service, headed by Assistant Director Rommel J. Vallejo, for their relentless effort in maintaining the unmodified opinion from the Commission on Audit (COA) for 2024. The COA rendered “unqualified opinion” stating in its opinion that the NBI financial statements present fairly, in all material respects, the financial position of the Bureau as of December 31, 2024 and its financial performance, cash flows, changes in net assets/equity, comparison of budget and actual accounts for the year ended, in accordance with International Public Sector Accounting Standards (IPSAS). An unqualified opinion, also known as a clean opinion, is the most favorable type of audit opinion an auditor can give. It signifies that the auditor believes the financial statements are fairly presented, in all material respects, and prepared in accordance with applicable financial reporting standards. Essentially, it means the Auditor found no material misstatements in the financial statements. “Ang NBI ay hindi lang magaling sa imbestigasyon at pag lutas ng Krimen, Kundi magaling din sa admininstrative work”, Santiago said. “It is just proper to give them recognition for their achievements and accomplishments. They are the “unsung” heroes of the Bureau”, he added.

body: PRESS STATEMENT November 08, 2024 In line with the directive of National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Director JUDGE JAIME B. SANTIAGO (Ret.) to intensify the campaign against the proliferation of smuggled cigarettes in the country, the NBI-Olongapo District Office (NBI-OLDO) arrested MELODY EDQUIBAL TAWATAO in Masinloc, Zambales for violation of R.A. No. 12022 ( Anti-Agricultural Economic Sabotage Act of 2024) and violation of R.A. No. 10863 (Customs Modernization and Tarrif Act). The operation also resulted in the seizure of fifty-five (55) boxes of “Modern” cigarettes containing 27,500 packs. The operation stemmed from an information received regarding the alleged proliferation of smuggled cigarettes in the province of Zambales. Additional information disclosed that Subject Tawatao is in possession of substantial number of “Modern” and “HP” cigarettes and is selling the same to her buyers. Investigation and test-buy conducted by the NBI-OLDO confirmed that Subject Tawatao is indeed selling smuggled cigarettes. Verification with the National Tobacco Administration and Bureau of Customs revealed, through certification, that Subject Tawatao is not licensed to import tobacco products. Thus, NBI-OLDO applied for a Search Warrant against the premises of Subject Tawatao, which was granted by the Olongapo RTC, Branch 74. On November 6, 2024, the operatives of NBI-OLDO proceeded to a warehouse in Masinloc, Zambales where the smuggled cigarettes were being stored. Subsequently, the operatives implemented the Search Warrant, which resulted in the arrest of Subject Tawatao and seizure of the smuggled cigarettes. The arrested Subject will be presented for inquest proceedings for the above-stated violations and the seized cigarettes will be turned over to the custody of the Bureau of Customs for the determination of the appraised value in accordance with R.A. No. 10863. Director Santiago lauded the operatives of NBI-OLDO for the arrest of the Subject and confiscation of the smuggled cigarettes.

body: PRESS STATEMENT April 29, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } In support to government’s fight against the spread of fake news and rage bait in social media, NBI Director Judge Jaime B. Santiago (Ret.) urges the public to be vigilant against the problem. Director Santiago explains that rage baits are posts in social media that are usually viral and are made for the sake of stirring anger. This leads to more engagement and reactions that further promote the social media content. People should be aware of what a rage bait is. He added that when we encounter these posts, one should try to relax and calm down before engaging with it. This allows us to think before we act and avoid promoting this on social media algorithm. Santiago emphasized that not all information found on social media is accurate. He advised the public to rely only on trustworthy media outlets and content creators. He stressed the importance of distinguishing between false information and factual information by identifying primary and secondary sources. Primary sources are based on first-hand accounts or direct evidence, while secondary sources interpret and analyze information from primary sources, typically created by individuals who have expertise in a particular topic. Finally, Director Santiago encourages everyone to fact-check information on social media and verify the credibility of the author of any post before believing it or even sharing it.

body: Two Bangladeshi nationals who extorted money from and threatened a compatriot were arrested by agents of the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) during an entrapment in Manila recently. The suspects were identified by NBI Director Nonnatus Caesar R. Rojas as: MOHIUDDIN AHMED SWAPAN, and MOHAMED WASIM, both Bangladeshi and residents of 946 San Andres St., Malate, Manila. Investigation by the NBI-Violence against Women and Children Division (VAWCD) headed by Head Agent Auralyn L. Pascual disclosed that a Bangladeshi businessman, Anwar Hossain, sought NBI assistance regarding two compatriots, suspects Swapan and Wasim, who kept on harassing and threatening him with death. Accordingly, the complainant and suspects are engaged in the garments business in the country, and the former supplied suspects with assorted garments amounting to P749,486.00. They paid a check in the amount of P200,000 that bounced when encashed. When the suspects were informed of the bounced checks and the demand for payment was made, suspects instead threatened to kill Hossain. Instead of paying, Wasim demanded P200,000 from the complainant in exchange for his life and safety. Hossain claimed that Wasim was continuously harassing him even making calls in the middle of the night compromising his business activities. In his latest communication, Wasim urged the complainant to give the money on May 31, 2013 at MEHFIL Restaurant along San Andres St., Malate, Manila. This prompted Hossain to report the matter to the NBI. Hossain immediately contacted the NBI and an entrapment was planned and coordination was made with the local police. At the appointed date and time, NBI operatives accompanied Hossain for the pay-off. At around 10:00 PM, suspects Wasim and Swapan arrived. Hossain handed over the marked money to Wasim. After accepting it, NBI agents nearby approached, introduced themselves and arrested suspects. They were brought to the NBI for booking and detention. Charges for Robbery with Intimidation of Persons were recommended filed against the suspects before the Manila City Prosecutor’s Office.

body: On July 1, 2019, operatives of NBI-Intellectual Property Rights Division (NBI-IPRD) seized Php 3.1Million worth of steel products that do not conform with the standards set by RA 7394 (Consumer Act of the Philippines). Items were seized in Dalandanan, Valenzuela City by virtue of Search Warrants. Charges for violation of RA 8293 (Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines) were filed against ELISON’S STEEL BARS MARKETING. On July 2, 2019, operatives of NBI-Laoag District Office (NBI-LADO) arrested JOHN CARLOS TUGAS for violation of RA 9995 (Anti-Photo and Video Voyeurism Act) in relation to RA 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act), and RA 9262 (Anti-Violence Against Women and Their Children Act of 2004). Subject was arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from the complaint of Mary Jane Garcia who alleged that she and Subject had a short-lived relationship which ended when complainant jilted the Subject in favor of another guy. The disgruntled Subject then posted on social media complainant’s nude pictures that were viewed by her friends, relatives, and townmates. Complainant also said that Subject is in possession of her sex video which he threatened to post on social media if she won’t come and have sex with him. This prompted the complainant to reveal the matter to her family who then accompanied her to seek assistance from the NBI. Thus, an entrapment operation was conducted resulting in the arrest of the Subject. Subject was presented for inquest for the abovementioned violations. On July 2, 2019, operatives of NBI-Anti-Fraud Division (NBI-AFD arrested MARILYN CORPUZ in Makati City for Extortion. Subject was arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from the complaint against the Subject. The complainant met the Subject, a sex worker engaged in escort service, through the worldwide dating, website locanto.com and on several occasions, complainant hired the service of the Subject. After which, Subject was continuously sending email messages to the complainant demanding for money and threatening him that if he will not send money, Subject will contact the complainant’s wife and will disclose everything that happened between them. Out of fear, complainant sent money to the Subject a total of Php 286,450.00. Despite the money received, Subject still harassed and threatened the complainant by sending malicious emails, demanding for money. Hence, the complaint. Charges for violation of Article 293 (Extortion) of the Revised Penal Code in relation to RA 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012) were filed against the Subject. On July 2, 2019, operatives of NBI-Anti-Fraud Division (NBI-AFD) arrested CRYSTALAINE KAHANAP TRIA and JEFF REYNALD YNCIERTO GETUBIG for Estafa and violation of RA 8484 (Access Device Regulation Act). Subjects were arrested in entrapment operation which stemmed from the complaint of ABENSON VENTURES,INC. represented by Randy Dela Cruz against CRYSTALAINE K. TRIA, JEFF REYNALD GETUBIG, IRELYN JOY. VICTORINO, ELENE K, TRIA, and PAUL ADRIAN AYA. According to the complaint, the said individuals purchased items in Abenson-Filinvest and paid them through GCash. However, it was found out that the transactions were not credited and further verification with GCash revealed that the transaction IDs involving the purchases of the Subjects were not found in their system and are invalid. When Subject TRIA demanded for the delivery of the alleged pending items, the entrapment operation was conducted resulting in the arrest of Subjects CRYSTALAINE KAHANAP TRIA and JEFF REYNALD YNCIERTO GETUBIG. They were brought to inquest proceedings before the Office of the Provincial Prosecutor of Cavite for violation of RA 8484 (Access Device Regulation Act) and Estafa. On July 2, 2019, operatives of NBI-Dumaguete District Office (NBI-DUMDO) conducted series of bet-bust operations against agents/representatives of Globaltech Mobile Online Gaming Corporation in the municipalities of Lazi, and San Juan in the province of Siquijor. The operation resulted in in flagrante delicto arrest of five (5) agents/staff of Globaltech who were subjected to inquest proceedings for violation of PD 1602 as amended by RA 9287 in relation to RA 10175, and the filing of cases against eight (8) agents/staff of Globaltech who were believed to have been tipped off of the ongoing raid and were able to escape. Fifteen (15) booths used by Globaltech as betting were also dismantled. On July 3, 2019, operatives of NBI-Ilocos Regional Office (NBI-IRO) arrested KITH JIMENEZ JAVONILLO for violation of RA 9208 in relation to RA 7610. Subject was arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from the complaint of a minor boy who reported that he was sexually exploited by the Subject on November 26, 2018 at an abandoned restobar in San Fernando City, La Union. Subject communicated with the complainant on July 2, 2019 and instructed the latter to meet with him to have sexual intercourse. Complainant received a message from the Subject that they will meet at 7/11 convenience store and will proceed to Tavern Motel. Complainant then informed the NBI operatives about this and the entrapment operation was conducted the following day resulting in the arrest of the Subject. Subject was brought for inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor, San Fernando City, La Union for violation of RA 9208 (Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2003) in relation to RA 7610 (Special Protection of Children Against Abuse, Exploitation and Discrimination Act). On July 3, 2019, operatives of NBI-Intellectual Property Rights Division (NBI-IPRD) seized cigarette labels and printing machines with an estimated amount of Php 450,000,000.00. Items were seized in a joint operation of NBI-IPRD and BIR in Malabon City which stemmed from the complaint of John Sacriz, Managing Director, IP Manila Associates on behalf of Philip Morris Fortune Tobacco Corp (PMFTC) and Japan Tobacco International (JTI). Charges for violation of RA 8293 (Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines) were filed against John/Jane Doe/owner/operator of warehouse located at No.29 MH Del Pilar St. Tugatog, Malabon City. On July 4, 2019, operatives of NBI-Special Action Unit (NBI-SAU) arrested PELAGIA DUMASIG for Estafa. Subject was arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from the complaint of Mr. Cesar A. Costales referred by Atty. Charito A. Zamora, Officer-in-Charge, Office of Cybercrime, DOJ Manila. Mr. Costales alleged that thru Messenger, a female American introduced herself as Eliane, a soldier assigned in Afghanistan. After constant exchange of messages, the two became a couple. One day, Eliane told Mr. Costales that she would send him a luggage containing money and jewelry. After a couple of days, an alleged Customs employee sent a text message to Mr. Costales informing him that his luggage had arrived and that he needed to pay Php 37,000.00 for local fees and taxes. Mr. Costales promptly paid the said amount via money remittance center. When he asked for the luggage, Mr. Costales was asked to pay a violation fee since accordingly, there was a large sum of money inside the luggage. He then paid it but when he was again asked to pay Php 168,000.00 for insurance fees. It was at this point that he realized it was all a scam. He reported the matter to the NBI. An entrapment operation was then conducted in Navotas City resulting in the arrest of Subject PELAGIA DUMASIG who was caught in the act of paying out the amount of Php 168,000.00 from certain money remittance center using various government-issued IDs. Charges for Estafa were filed against the Subject. On July 4, 2019, operatives of NBI-North Eastern Mindanao Regional Office (NBI-NEMRO) arrested MARICHE N. VIRTUDAZO for Large Scale Illegal Recruitment and Estafa/Swindling. Subject was arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from the complaint of five (5) complainants against the Subject who recruited them and several others to work as ordinary seaman abroad with monthly salary of 400 US Dollars excluding overtime. Subject demanded and collected from the complainants placement and processing fees ranging from Php 50,000 to Php 80,000. However, the promised overseas employment did not materialize, prompting complainants to demand for the return of their money. Verification from POEA revealed that Subject is not authorized to recruit workers for overseas employment. Thus, on the above-mentioned date, the entrapment operation was conducted resulting in the arrest of the Subject. Subject was brought to NBI-NEMRO for proper booking procedures. On July 4, 2019, operatives of NBI-Anti-Organized and Transnational Crime Division (NBI-AOTCD) arrested ROSE MELODY S. AQUINO by virtue of Warrant of Arrest for Large Scale Illegal Recruitment and Estafa. A request from Isaiah Roland II, Attache, US Department of State, Diplomatic Security Service, Overseas Criminal Investigations (OCI), to arrest Irmalyn Melodias-Torres on the basis of Warrants of Arrest issued by RTC Branch 52, Puerto Princesa City. Upon perusal of the warrants, there were other accused together with Irmalyn namely GERALD C. MELODIAS and ROSE MELODY S. AQUINO. A reliable information was received that Subject ROSE MELODY was seen in her parents’ residence in Villamor Air Base, Pasay City. On the aforementioned date, after several stakeout, Warrant of Arrest was served to ROSE MELODY. She is now detained at the NBI Detention facility awaiting commitment order. On July 4, 2019, operatives of NBI-Special Action Unit (NBI-SAU) arrested IVAN PAUL DE GUZMAN k.a. ‘PATRICK DEPP’ for Sextortion. Subject was arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from the complaint of a victim against the Subject. According to the victim, she and Subject Singson engaged in a sexual intercourse some time ago. The victim was surprised when she was told by her mother and neighbors that there were sensitive photos of her circulating online. This prompted the victim to contact the subject but instead of deleting the sex video and nude photos of the victim, Subject Singson demanded for another sexual intercourse where he would take another sex video. Subject Singson also demanded from the victim Php20,000.00 so he would not upload the sex video online. With this, an entrapment operation was conducted resulting in the arrest of the Subject. Charges for Robbery Extortion, Grave Coercion, and violations of R.A. 9262 (Anti-Violence Against Women and Their Children Act of 2004), R.A. 9995 (Anti-Photo and Video Voyeurism Act of 2009), and R.A. 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012 were filed against the Subject. On July 5, 2019 operatives of NBI-Environmental Crime Division (NBI-EnCD) arrested eight (8) individuals for violation of Section 103 (Theft of Minerals) of RA 7942 (Philippine Mining Act of 1995). Subjects were arrested in an operation conducted in Brgy. Potrero, Bacolor, Pampanga. Seized in the operation were two (2) backhoes and one (1) dump truck loaded with sand with an estimated value of Php 5 Million. Subjects were brought to Office of the Prosecutor, DOJ Manila for inquest proceedings. On July 5, 2019, operatives of NBI-Western Visayas Regional Office (NBI-WEVRO) arrested SHAWN B. AGREGADO after he was caught in flagrante delicto receiving marked money representing the alleged additional fee for the work application of victim/complainant Kyle Dane Niel with the Philippine Coast Guard (PCG). Subject was recruiting applicants to the PCG and AFP without authorization nor vested with power to approve application papers and collect/receive money from the said government agencies. Also seized from the Subject was a .45 Cal.Pistol that he was carrying on an outside holster when apprehended. Subject failed to present any LTOPF, PTC, and license for the said firearm. Subject was brought for inquest proceeding before the City Prosecutors Office, Iloilo City and was charged for Estafa, Usurpation of Authority, and Illegal Possession of Firearm. On July 8, 2019, operatives of NBI-National Capital Region (NBI-NCR) arrested MARY GRACE LODIOMON CABALLERO for Large Scale Illegal Recruitment, Human Trafficking, and Estafa. Subject was arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from the complaint against the Subject who misinterpreted herself as a chiefmate of Magsaysay and made it appear that she knew much about the agency and that she could deploy the complainants provided that they pay money for their US Visa, Medical, etc. Subject added that complainants shall be deployed to a tanker vessel owned by Arcadia bound overseas route. She promised complainants deployment but failed to do so. When operatives knew that Subject was still demanding money from the complainants, an entrapment operation was conducted resulting in the apprehension of the Subject. The NBI also received the complaint of Luz Cacho who disclosed that Subject was able to get Php 185,000.00 from her after Subject promised overseas employment to her son. Subject even brought her baby as guarantee to them that she will eventually pay her debt. Out of pity, Cacho accepted the child until the latter was totally abandoned by the Subject. Believing that the crime of Qualified Trafficking has become a continuing offense, Subject was likewise arrested for the said crime. A letter from a concerned citizen that Subject was in possession of wild life without permit from government authorities. body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) said today that it has filed graft and corruption cases against three (3) barangay officials in relation to anomalies in the distribution of Social Amelioration Program (SAP) funds in Hagonoy, Bulacan. NBI Officer-In-Charge (OIC) Eric B. Distor identified those charged as Barangay Kagawad DANILO FLORES, Brgy. Executive Assistant RICHARD “BOY” BAUTISTA and Barangay Chairman JASON G. MENDOZA, who are all officials of Barangay San Agustin, Hagonoy, Bulacan. OIC Distor added that two (2) private individuals, namely: former Barangay Kagawad LEVI COSAY; and REGINE BAUTISTA, wife of subject Bautista were likewise included in the charges filed on May 11, 2020 before the Department of Justice (DOJ) in Manila. Pursuant to Republic Act No. 11469, otherwise known as the Bayanihan to Heal as One Act, signed by President Rodrigo Roa Duterte on March 23, 2020, that declared a state of national emergency, the government will provide emergency financial subsidies to low income households ranging from P5,000.00 to P8,000.00. The NBI said that in Barangay San Agustin, Hagonoy Bulacan, three (3) complainants alleged that SAP beneficiaries received Six Thousand Five Hundred Pesos (Php 6,500.00) each from the DSWD on April 27, 2020, at San Agustin Elementary School in Hagonoy, Bulacan. In the afternoon of even date, Subject Flores, accompanied by a certain Michael Perez, demanded from them the amount of P4,000.00, a portion of the SAP subsidy they received. Subject Flores allegedly claimed that the P3,500.00 shall be given to Hagonoy Municipal Mayor Raulito T. Manlapaz, Sr., and the remaining P500.00 will be given to the frontliners of the Municipality of Hagonoy. Against their will, complainants gave back to subject Flores the amount of P4,000.00. The NBI said that further investigation revealed that subject Flores threatened the complainants that if they refuse to give back the P4,000.00, they will be blacklisted and eventually delisted as beneficiaries of all subsequent relief or amelioration grants of the government. Witnesses stated that a total of P117,000.00 collected by Subject Flores was turned over to Subject Bautista and his wife Regine Bautista. Witnesses further averred that it is common knowledge in their barangay that being the Executive Assistant, which position requires the Barangay Chairman’s trust and confidence, Subject Bautista has indeed gained the confidence of Chairman Mendoza, thus, they believe that Subject Bautista could not have acted on his own without the imprimatur of his boss, incumbent Chairman Mendoza. Finally, OIC Distor strongly urges the public to be vigilant and to not hesitate to report to NBI, any LGU officer who fails to comply with the Bayanihan to Heal as One Act, especially with the distribution of SAP funds.

body: PRESS STATEMENT February 28, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } In accordance with the government’s initiative to strengthen the Philippines’ foreign relations policy, the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI)—International Operations Division (NBI-IOD) and NBI – National Capital Region (NBI-NCR), under the guidance of NBI Director JUDGE JAIME B. SANTIAGO (Ret.)—has apprehended a Korean national identified as CHANGHOON HAN a.k.a. “CHANG-HOONHAN.” This individual faces charges for violating the Korean National Sports Promotion Act, the Criminal Act, and the Act on the Regulation of Punishment for Concealment of Criminal Proceeds. The apprehension was carried out based on a provisional warrant of arrest for extradition. On February 20, 2025, agents from the NBI-IOD and NBI-NCR went to the Bureau of Immigration Warden Facility (BIWF) in Lower Bicutan, Taguig City, to execute the Provisional Warrant issued by the Regional Trial Court of Manila, Branch 173. This operation resulted in the apprehension of Subject Changhoon. After the arrest, Changhoon was taken to the NBI-IOD office for the standard booking procedure and was subsequently transferred to the NBI Detention Center in Muntinlupa City, in compliance with the order from RTC Manila, Branch 173. Director Santiago commended the agents of NBI-IOD and NBI-NCR for their successful operation. Santiago emphasized the importance of building strong relationships with foreign counterparts to ensure effective law enforcement operations involving foreign nationals.

body: Based on intelligence information, joint elements of the Provincial Public Safety Company, Misamis Occidental, PNP PRO-10, Regional Intelligence Division NCRPO and NBI Criminal Intelligence Division, arrested one of the country’s Top 20 Most Wanted Bank Robbers in his hide-out at Purok 3, Barangay Lower Rizal, Oroquieta City on April 7, 2012 after six (6) years in hiding. The suspect was identified by NBI Officer-In-Charge Atty. Nonnatus Caesar R. Rojas as: Four (4) warrants of arrest for Bank Robbery, a warrant of arrest for Illegal Possession of Firearms and another warrant of Arrest for Direct Assault were served to CRISPIN BONGOLO JR. by authorities. Records show that CRISPIN BONGOLO was one of the dreaded members of AMPANG COLANGCO Bank Robbery Group that shot and wounded five (5) security guards escort of a roving teller of Banco De Oro and carted away more than P36 Million pesos cash at SM South Mall, Las Pinas City on August 7, 2004. On June 27, 2007, while out on bail, CRISPIN BONGOLO and the heavily armed AMPANG COLANGCO Bank Robbery Group stormed the PS Bank Cainta Branch in broad daylight and carted away more than P171,000 cash. They even fired upon the two (2) traffic policemen that passed by. On January 22, 2008, CRISPIN BONGOLO and the heavily armed AMPANG COLANGCO Bank Robbery Group barged into the Land Bank of the Philippines West Avenue Branch, Quezon City and stole more than P1 Million Pesos in cash. On August 11, 2008, CRISPIN BONGOLO was one of the armed men that robbed the money carrier of Metrobank in the amount of more than P2 Million pesos cash at Blue Wave Mall located along Sumulong Highway, Marikina City. CRISPIN BONGOLO is presently held at the NBI Detention Cell. HE will soon be committed to the National Bilibid Prison (NBP) to serve his sentence of 12 years to 16 years in connection with his conviction re: Banco De Oro robbery case in 2004. He will be joining at NBP the leaders of AMPANG COLANGCO BANK Robbery Group, ROY GILBERT COLANGCO @ AMPANG @ HERBERT and another member EDWIN AYOP who are already serving sentence in connection with their conviction for the same offense.
