Distor announced that the operatives of NBI-Special Action Unit (NBI-SAU) arrested an individual in a buy-bust operation in Makati City for selling shabu. Director Distor identified the subject as QIZHI LI a.k.a. “LAO LEE”. On March 10, 2022, NBI-SAU planned a buy-bust operation and proceeded to Brgy. Poblacion, Makati City. The operation resulted in the arrest of Subject Li and confiscation of fifty-six pieces shabu pills and one (1) piece metal canister containing white crystalline substance with an estimated street value of Php 300,000.00. During the course of the operation the operatives were able to recover from the possession of the subject one (1) Tanfolgio 9 mm caliber pistol with two (2) magazines and twenty-one (21) live 9mm ammunition. The arrested subject was brought to the NBI-SAU office for the usual booking, photograph, and arrest procedures. The confiscated illegal drugs were forwarded to the NBI-Forensic Chemistry Division (NBI-FCD) for examination. Subject Li was presented for inquest proceedings before the Makati City for violation of Sections 5 and 11 of R.A. 9165 otherwise known as “The Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002” and Illegal Possession of Firearms in relation to COMELEC Gun Ban.

title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: PRESS STATEMENT July 08, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } The Clark International Airport Inter-Agency Drug Interdiction Task Group (CRK-IADITG) composed of National Bureau of Investigation – Pampanga District Office (NBI-PAMDO), Philippine Drug Enforcement Agency (PDEA), Bureau of Customs (BOC), and Philippine National Police (PNP), conducted a Drug Interdiction at FedEx Warehouse, Clark Freeport Zone, Mabalacat City, Pampanga. On July 03, 2025, the team commenced and examined a package sent through FedEx which was declared as Reading Pillows. Concealed inside was a transparent plastic package containing KUSH (Marijuana fruiting tops), weighing 472 grams and with an estimated market value of more or less Php708,000.00. Information showed that the package was sent by a certain ALAIN J DELA ROSA from Michigan, United States of America to the Consignee named RICKY VILLAMOR JR. of Cebu City. Samples of Kush were marked, weighed, and turned over to PDEA in the presence of the Members of the Task Force and the rest of the seized contraband are in the custody of the BOC. An ample portion of samples for PDEA’s further testing were likewise weighed, marked by the BOC Examiner and were turned over to PDEA.

title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: • On October 1, 2021, operatives of NBI- Death Investigation Division (NBI-DID) dismantled a multi-million investment company scam in Quezon City by virtue of an entrapment operation. based on investigation, AUREA ORGANICA milked millions of pesos from unsuspecting victims who were lured to invest their money in exchange for thirty percent (30%) return after thirty (30) days. The company uses beauty essentials such as whitening soap, oils, skin toner, and perfume as the face of their business. Upon verification, AUREA ORGANICA is not registered with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) nor does it possess a secondary license to operate as an investment company. Arrested during the entrapment operation is the company secretary LOTTA LOVE REYES who received the entrapment money. Subject was properly charged before the Quezon City Prosecutor’s Office for violation of RA 8799 otherwise known as the Securities Regulation Code. Meanwhile, charges for violation of RA 8799 and Syndicated Estafa are being prepared against BEATRIZ PIA ESPINA WHITE a.k.a. PIA ESPINA, JOSE NARCISO D. TERRADO a.k.a. JOHN TERRADO II, and other officers/operators of AUREA ORGANICA. • On October 1, 2021, the composite team of NBI-Anti-Organized and Transnational Crime Division together with Bureau of Custom (BOC) CIIS-POM, Philippine Coast Guard (PCG), and a representative from the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas – Payments and Currency Investigation Group (BSP-PCIG) seized luxury cars and Philippine Peso coins worth Php 50 Million stored in a warehouse in Brgy. Laging Handa, Quezon City. The operation stemmed from an intelligence report regarding with several Filipino-Chinese who were engaged in hoarding of more or less Php 50 Million and commercial importation of luxury vehicles through misdeclaration, misclassification, and undervaluation of the said vehicles. NBI-AOTCD operatives validate the said information through a series of surveillance and coordination made with the BOC. The BOC in turn, issued a Letter of Authority (LOA) and Mission Order (MO) against the Owners/Lessees/ Lessors/ Occupants/ Representatives or whoever is in possession of the alleged counterfeit/imported merchandise stored at a warehouse in Brgy. Laging Handa, Quezon City. The operation resulted in the seizure of one (1) Lamborghini; one (1) Nissan GTR; Ferrari Italia; Ford Shelby GT500; Mercedes Benz, Karosserie; Ford Raptor, and Nissan Cefiro. The joint team also found and seize Php 50 Million worth of Philippine Peso coins. • On October 4, 2021, the NBI-Anti-Graft Division (NBI-AGD) filed charges against MARC CEDRIC PEREZ y CALASICAS, Chief Executive Officer of AGM Advertising and JED WILLEM CARADO y SAGUINSIN, President of AGM Advertising before the City Prosecutor of Pasig City for Estafa under Article 315 (2)(a) of the Revised Penal Code; Violation of Section 26 and 28 in relation to Section 73 of R.A. 8799, otherwise known as the “Securities Regulation Code of the Philippines”; violation of Section 165 and 170 in relation to Section 20 of R.A. 11232, otherwise known as the “Revised Corporation Code of the Philippines”; and violation of Section 374 in relation to Section 114 and 115 of City Ordinance No. 51 S. 2017 of Pasig City, otherwise known as the “2017 Revised Pasig Revenue Code”. The case stemmed from a complaint filed by the victims of the subjects regarding with the alleged illegal foreign exchange trading and investment scam. According to the complaint the subjects introduced themselves as Chief Executive Officer and President of AGM Advertising. Investigation conducted by the NBI-AGD revealed that the subjects were in fact engaged in an investment pyramiding scam which is facilitated under the guise of a foreign exchange trading. The subjects introduced AGM ADVERTISING to the complainants as a “Forex Trader” and “Marketing Arm” of FX DIRECT DEALER PHILIPPINES also known as FXDD PHILIPPINES (FXDD). The subjects also claimed that FXDD is allegedly a “Broker” which serves as a platform in “Forex Trading”. The complainants revealed that the subjects were able to collect from them a total amount of Php 5,450,000.00 as investments to AGM ADVERTISING. The NBI-AGD conducted verification with the concerned government authorities revealed that the subjects including their company does not possess the necessary license either as lending company, broker and/or dealer of securities, dealer in government securities, investment adviser of and investment company, investment house and transfer agent. Further, the company AGM Advertising and Subject Perez, the DTI-registered owner, have neither registered nor renewed any business license from the concerned local government unit. Based on the foregoing, the NBI-AGD filed the above-mentioned charges against the Subjects. • On October 6, 2021, operatives of NBI-Environmental Crime Division (NBI-EnCD) arrested VIRIGILIO L. CANDELARIA for illegal construction of concrete establishments within a protected landscape in Baras, Rizal. The operation stemmed from the complaint of the President of Masungi Georeserve Foundation about the numerous concrete establishments within the Upper Marikina River Basin Protected Landscape (UMRBPL). NBI-EnCD operatives conducted a series of surveillance operations which confirmed the presence of multiple concrete establishments such as houses and pools operating as resorts. Further confirmation with the DENR-PENRO, Rizal stated that the subject establishments are indeed located within UMRBPL. Thus, after gathering enough evidences that there was indeed violations of the environmental laws the NBI-EnCD, on October 6, 2021, proceeded to the target area which resulted in the apprehension of Subject Candelaria. The owner of the resort identified as EFRAIM GONZALES was not in the area during the operation. Subject Candelaria was presented for inquest proceedings before the Provincial Prosecutor of Rizal for violation of Section 81 (formerly Section 71) of P.D. 705, as amended, otherwise known as the “Revised Forestry Code of the Philippines”. The owner of the establishment EFRAIM GONZALES was also included in the charged for violation of Section 81 (formerly Section 71) of P.D. 705, as amended, otherwise known as the “Revised Forestry Code of the Philippines” and Section 20 (n) and (o) of R.A. 7856, as amended by R.A. 11038, otherwise known as the “Expanded National Integrated Protected Areas System Act of 2018”. • On October 7, 2021, operatives of NBI-International Operations Division (NBI-IOD) rescued twenty-six (26) OFW victims and arrested two (2) individuals in Sta. Ana, Manila for Illegal Recruitment and Serious Illegal Detention. The arrested Subjects were identified as PAULO QUIZA and ROWENA LOFAMIA. On October 6, 2021, complainants sought the assistance of NBI-IOD to seek redress against Joint Venture Resources Inc. (JVR) which allegedly delays their deployment to Kuwait despite the fact that all necessary fees were already paid by their respective employers in Kuwait. Complainants also filed complaint against spouses PAULO QUIZA and ANNALYN QUIZA and ROWENA LOFAMIA, owner and administrative officer of JVR Placement Co., Inc. located at Pedro Gil corner Agoncillo St., Malate, Manila. Complainants submitted their documents and were thereafter instructed to proceed to an accommodation house maintained by the agency. Said accommodation house served as temporary shelter for applicants who mostly came from the provinces while waiting for deployment. Complainants lamented that the living condition in the accommodation house was poor and that they were prevented from leaving the premises. Complainants decided to leave and requested for their documents from the JVR but Subjects refused to return the submitted documents and continued to padlock the applicants left in the accommodation house. With these, NBI-IOD operatives conducted simultaneous operations in the accommodation house and at the office of JVR. The operations resulted in the rescue of twenty-six (26) OFW applicants from the accommodation house and the arrest of Subjects PAULO QUIZA and ROWENA LOFAMIA. Arrested Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings on October 9, 2021 before the Manila Prosecutor’s Office for Serious Illegal Detention and Illegal Recruitment under Section 6 (k) of RA 8042 otherwise known as Migrant Workers and Overseas Filipinos Act of 1995 as amended by RA 10022. • On October 12, 2021, operatives of NBI-Environmental Crime Division (NBI-EnCD) arrested five (5) individuals for illegal quarrying activities. Subjects were identified as RONALD PANGILINAN MALIG, quarry operator; KIER GANIA ARCIGA, backhoe operator; MARK JOSHUA AVENGOZA SAMPANG, loader operator; DANILO UMALI MALABANAN, truck driver; and ARNOLD SALAK CADIANG, elf-truck driver. The operation stemmed from an information received by NBI-EnCD regarding the alleged illegal mining/quarrying activities being conducted in the Municipalities of Capas, Concepcion, Bamban, and Tarlac City. Thus, on October 12, 2021, after verification with the concerned government agencies, NBI-EnCd together with the DENR-MGB Region III, proceeded to the target areas to conduct an anti-illegal mining operation. Upon arrival at the target areas, the joint operatives were able to witness the actual operation of illegal quarrying being conducted by the five (5) subjects. Joint operatives asked Subject Malig (Quarry Operator) the necessary documents and permits to operate a quarry within the target area. Subject Malig was given ample time to produce the documents or permits but failed to present any. Operatives then apprehended the above-named subjects and seized 3 pcs. excavator, 2 pcs. wheel loader, 1 pc. 22-wheeler truck loaded with sand, 1 pc. 6-wheeler ruck loaded with sand, and 40 cubic meter river sand material with an estimated value of Php 8,396,000. Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the Provincial Prosecutor’s Office of the Province of Tarlac for violation of Section 103 (Theft of Minerals) under R.A. 7942, otherwise known as the “Philippine Mining Act of 1995”. Subsequently, an information was filed at the Municipal Trial Court of Capas- Bamban-Concepcion, Capas, Tarlac for the above-mentioned violation committed by the subjects. • On October 13, 2021, operatives of NBI-Dagupan District Office (NBI-DADO) arrested REAH ELLASUS y SALINAS for selling dog meat products. On September 16, 2021, NBI- DADO received a report that REAH’S CANTEEN located in Mapandan, Pangasinan is engaged in selling and distribution of dog meat products to different personalities in the province. Operatives coordinated the information to Department of Agriculture Region 1, National Meat Inspection Service for validation and surveillance. On October 13, 2021, after the information was validated and securing authority to operate, NBI-DADO operatives proceeded to the target area and conducted the entrapment operation which resulted in the arrest of Subject REAH Subject was arrested in possession and selling two (2) dog heads, eight (8) meat legs, and cooked dog meat. Subject REAH ELLASUS y SALINAS was presented for inquest proceedings before the Provincial Prosecution Office, Dagupan City, Pangasinan for violation of The Animal Welfare Act of 1998 as amended by RA 10631. • On October 13, 2021, operatives of NBI-Puerto Princesa City District Office (NBI- PUERDO) arrested JULIE MAE LUMANTA-CAABAY and IVAN IMPERIAL GECERA for Adultery. The case stemmed from a complaint filed by the husband of Subject Julie, alleging that Subject Julie left their conjugal dwelling and live with Subject Ivan as husband and wife, despite his knowledge that Subject Julie is already married to the complainant. After sometime, the complainant informed NBI-PUERDO that he needed immediate assistance, claiming that he caught in flagrante delicto the two (2) subjects in the act of sexual intercourse. NBI-PUERDO immediately proceeded to the love nest of the subjects and witnessed both subjects inside a room. Without wasting time, the NBI- PUERDO operatives apprehended both subjects and informed them of their constitutional rights. NBI-PUERDO also recovered from the subjects a cellphone and 10 pieces of photographs of Subjects Julie and Ivan together. The two (2) subjects were brought to the NBI-PUERDO office where they undergone standard booking procedures. Thereafter, the subjects were brought for inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor, Puerto Princesa City for Adultery as defined and penalized under Article 333 of the Revised Penal Code. • On October 18, 2021, operatives of NBI-Environmental Crime Division (NBI-EnCD) arrested ERICSON CINCO y MAYO, RAUL GARCIA y LOBETANA, WINDEL BUENO y TALAGA PABLO RIMORIN y GAPASIN, NICO YUNAPA, ROLDAN BONIFE y HONOR, DEXTER COLAS y COCOY, JOJIE MANZANILLO y DE GUZMAN, ALBERT ESTO y COCOY, FERNANDO LOPEZ y CRISTY, RANDY CAGANAN y LORING, and DANIEBOY ALEJANDRO y SALEM for illegal quarrying activities in Rodriguez, Rizal. The operation stemmed from the information received by the NBI-EnCD on August 26, 2021, regarding with the alleged rampant illegal mining/quarrying activities being conducted by certain individuals in Barangay San Isidro, Rodriguez, Rizal. The information also revealed that this group of individuals were extracting and disposing minerals without the necessary permit from the Provincial Mining Regulatory Board of the Province of Rizal and the Department of Environment and Natural Resources – Mines and Geosciences Bureau Region IV (DENR-MGB Region IV). Surveillance operation conducted confirmed that the ongoing quarrying operation. A certification issued by DENR-MGB on October 12, 2021 states that there was no valid and existing Mineral Production Sharing Agreement or Industrial Sand and Gravel Permit that was issued for the extraction of materials in relation to the sanitary landfill project in the Municipality Rodriguez, Rizal. The certification also provides that based on the data provided by the Provincial Mining Regulator Board of Rizal, as of 2nd Quarter of 2021, no valid and existing Quarry Permit, Industrial Sand and Gravel, Small Scale Mining Contract or Special Permit to Transport and Dispose was issued in relation to the sanitary landfill project in the said municipality. Thus, on October 18, 2021, joint operatives led by the NBI-EnCD together with the personnel from the DENR-MGB Region IV-A proceeded to Barangay San Isidro, Rodriguez, Rizal which resulted in the arrest of the subjects. Arrested subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of Provincial Prosecutor of Rizal for violation of Section 103 (Theft of Minerals) under R.A. 7942, otherwise known as the “Philippine Mining Act of 1995”. In Addition, JOSE ALLAN CRUZ y ABARRA (at-large), was also included in the charged for the same violation of the law. • In a series of operations, operatives of NBI-Intellectual Property Rights Division (NBI- IPRD) seized counterfeit items with an estimated total amount of Php 136,883,380.00. On October 21, 2021, 5,938 pcs of Unilab products with an estimated amount of Php 59,380.00 were seized in San Mateo, Rizal by virtue of Search Warrants for violation of RA 8293 issued against VHENUELI PHRAMACY and/or MA. VICTORIA SA CUNTAPAY and ADRIAN O. NIEVA. On October 22, 2021, 793 boxes of Hypertech products and 1,233 of boxes of Powerflex products with an estimated amount of Php 6,117,000.00 were seized in Caloocan City by virtue of Search Warrants for violation of RA 8293 issued against JIANJUN QUI and/or operators/occupants of WANG LI FORWARDER; KENNETH KING and/or owners/operators/occupants of KING COMMERCIAL; and ERIC PAREDES HUANG and/or owners/operators/occupants of KING POWER HARDWARE. On October 23, 2021, 4 boxes of Powerflex with an estimated amount of Php 12,000.00 were seized in Malabon and Caloocan City by virtue of Search Warrants for violation of RA 8293 issued against KEVIN YASAY CO and/or owners/operators of KYC CONSTRUCTION SUPPLY and JAMES CO and/or owners and/or operators of LUCKY OLYM TRADING INC. On October 25, 2021, numerous sacks of onions, garlic, ginger, black pepper, and monggo beans with a total estimated amount of Php 2,000,000,000.00 were seized in Tondo, Manila in an operation with the Bureau of Customs. Charges for violation of RA 10845 (Anti-Agricultural Smuggling Act) were filed against STELLA GAN HUANG, MR. DONGFA HONG, and JOHNSON COHOKCHONG TAN. On October 27, 2021, 20,400 pairs of Nike shorts and 2,670 Nike pants with an estimated amount of Php 38,610,000.00 were seized in Las Pinas City by virtue of Search Warrants issued against SHARON TAN for violation of RA 8293. On October 28, 2021, various counterfeit Nike products with an estimated total amount of Php 90,085,000.00 were seized in Pasay City by virtue of Search Warrants issued against GARY ONG, SU YONG, ALEX TAN, MAU YU, SHAW LIN, and GARRY ONG for violation of RA 8293. • On October 27, 2021, operatives of NBI-Central Visayas Regional Office (NBI-CEVRO) arrested FAUSTO GERRY DELIGERO a.k.a. “TATAY”, IMELDA TOLING DELIGERO a.k.a. “NANAY, WILLIN PEVIDA SOPSOP a.k.a. “WINNIE”, ZALDE PEVIDA SOPSOP a.k.a. “UNCLE TITING”, ARLENE SOPSOP FLORES, and JOSE BANDOJO a.k.a. “UNCLE OTIK” in Bogo City and Tabogo, Cebu for the killing of Romneck Ando Potot. the operation stemmed from the Murder/Parricide cases filed by NBI-CEVRO against the ten (10) of the accused, responsible for the killing of Romneck Ando Potot on July 12, 2020 in Tabogon, Cebu. RTC Branch 80 of Bogo City issued Warrant of Arrests for the crime of Murder with No Bail recommended against the six (6) arrested subjects. At the same time, RTC Branch 80 of Bogo City also issued a Warrant of Arrest against the accused-wife GERALDINE DELIGERO POTOT. Thus, on October 27, 2021, NBI-CEVRO divided themselves in to four (4) teams to serve the Warrants of Arrest against the above-named subjects. Team 1 arrested FAUSTO DELIGERO and IMELDA DELIGERO in Bogo City, while Team 2, 3, and 4 respectively, arrested ZALDE SOPSOP, ARLENE FLORES, and JOSE BANDOJO in Tabogon, Cebu. Unfortunately, Subject Geraldine Potot was not in the target area when the NBI-CEVRO implemented the Warrant of Arrest. The arrested subjects were turned-over to Medellin District Jail, Cebu, and the Warrant of Arrest was immediately returned to the issuing court. • On November 2, 2021, operatives of NBI-Special Projects Team (NBI-SPT) ZOSIMO BELLO y ESCOVER, Section Chief, Assessment, Port of Manila (BOC) and SALVADOR SELETARIA JR. y VERGA for Robbery/Extortion and violation of the Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act. • On November 3, 2021, operatives of NBI-Anti-Organized and Transnational Crime Division (NBI-AOTCD) arrested MARIA ANNALYN H. RIVERA for illegal practice of medicine. Subject was arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from the complaint of against Subject ANNA RIVERA a.k.a. DOC ANA and PAUL TAMARES for alleged Estafa and Illegal Practice of Medicine in violation of RA 2382 as amended by RA 4224 (The Medical Act of 1959) RIVERA and TAMARES represented themselves as doctor and nurse, respectively and provided medical assistance to complainant’s mother who got sick in exchange of cash in the total amount of Php 56,290.00. However, complainant discovered through online searching and verification with the Professional Regulation Commission (PRC) that Subjects RIVERA and TAMARES are not registered as doctor and nurse. It was also found out that RIVERA and TAMARES are using various names as follows: ANNALYN RIVERA SANTOS, ANNA LYN HERNANDEZ RIVERA, ANNALIZA RIVERA, ANNA LYN RIVERA, ANNALYN RIVERA, MARIA ANNA HERNANDEZ RIVERA, ANA RIVERA, PAUL TAMARES, and PAUL FRANCISCO. Separate verification by the NBI- AOTCD with the PRC revealed that the said names do not appear in the database for Physicians duly authorized to practice medicine in the Philippines. The name PAUL TAMARES and PAUL FRANCISCO do not appear in the database for nurses duly authorized to practice nursing in the Philippines. After ascertaining that Subjects were still actively medicine, an entrapment operation was conducted on November 3, 2021 resulting in the arrest of Subject RIVERA and one EDRALIN D. RUBIO. Arrested Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the City Prosecutor’s Office of Imus City for Estafa, Falsification of Public Documents (6 counts) under Article 172 in relation to Article 171 of the Revised Penal Code; Using Fictitious Name and Concealing True Name under Article 178 of the Revised Penal Code; violation of RA 6085 (Act Amending Commonwealth Act 142 regulating the Use of Aliases; Illegal Practice of Medicine in violation of RA 2382 as amended by RA 4224 (Medical Act of 1959) and violation of RA 10918 (The Philippine Pharmacy Act). PAUL TAMARES (at large) was also recommended to be charged with Estafa and Illegal Practice of Medicine. On November 5, 2021, NBI- AOTCD received an email from Investigation Sta. Cruz requesting for the service of the Warrants of Arrest issued against Subject ANNA LYN RIVERA for violation of Article 315 of the RPC and BP 22 both issued by the Municipal Trial Court of Sta. Cruz, Occidental Mindoro on September 13, 2018 and November 29, 2018. On November 12, 2021, NBI- AOTCD from the NBI-SMS with a copy of an Order issued by Assisting Judge Rex Q. Nerves of Imus Cavite Municipal Trial Court for the Release of the accused Annalyn Rivera after she has posted bail in the amount of Php 69,000.00. The arraignment and pre-trial conference for the case was set on November 19, 2021 and on the same date, after securing the printed copies of the Warrants of Arrest, the same were served and received by MARIA ANNALYN H. RIVERA inside the NBI Detention Center, Taft Ave. Manila. • On November 4, 2021, operatives of NBI-CALABARZON arrested eight (8) individuals who were caught in the act committing illegal gambling known as bookies. Subjects were arrested in an entrapment operation conducted by NBI-CALABARZON assisted by NBI- Cavite District Office (NBI-CAVIDO). Charges for violation of PD 1602 as amended by RA 9287 were filed against the arrested individuals before the Batangas Provincial Prosecutor’s Office. The copy of the inquest documents and photographs were submitted after the inquest proceedings. • On November 5-6, 2021, operatives of NBI-National Capital Region (NBI-NCR) seized counterfeit PUMA and CHAMPION with an estimated amount of Php 8,991,000.00. Items were seized in Manila and Pasay City by virtue of Search Warrant for violation of Trademark Infringement under RA 8293 issued against various stores and stalls located in Divisoria Mall,168 Shopping Mall, and Baclaran Shopping Mall. The search was conducted in a peaceful and orderly manner in the presence of respondent’s witnesses, building admin personnel/security, and barangay representative who signed/received a copy of Search Warrant and Inventory of Seized Articles/Property. • On November 6, 2021, operatives of NBI-Southeastern Mindanao Regional Office (NBI- SEMRO) arrested REVSAN ETHELBERT PAPAY ELIZALDE, EANA FAYE MARIE PALABRAS OLEA, BRYK JORDAN TEMPLADO ARCHIVAL, KURK BRYAN CARMONA TIUBOT, CARLO GUERERO, ARIEL BAER BUENO, JAN LORD BARCENAS MASONG, RONALD ENTE CHUAN, CHRISTOPHER DAGUMAN PRUDENTE, EDEL RUBIO CABALLERO, TOM JHUN BERNARDINO DOBLAS, JESUS BENTONON RAGAS, JASON OBEDENCIO VIDUYA, GIOVANI LUMABI TABANAO, MARK CHRISTOPHER ANISCO ISIP, FRITZ CHENTE DINOPOL and JOMARK FLORES APING for violation of RA 9165 (Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002). The case stemmed from the request of the Regional Director of PDEA XI to augment the PDEA Agents in the conduct of drug operation at Sea Eagle Resort, Purok Manaklay, Brgy. Pindasan, Mabini, Davao de Oro. The operation also resulted in the seizure of ten (10) grams of shabu, 722 capsules of suspected ecstacy, 200 grams of marijuana, 77 pieces of suspected LSD, 9 plastic bottles of suspected liquid ecstacy, and 2 vials of suspected liquid ecstacy. • On November 7, 2021, operatives of NBI-Eastern Visayas Regional Office (NBI-EVRO) arrested ALMA ALCAYDE y COROCOTO for Human Trafficking and rescued ten (10) trafficked victims. Subject was arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from the information that a nightclub or bar named “NINONG’S KTV BAR” located in Brgy. Guidapunan, Palo, Leyte is a prostitution and sex den managed by a certain “CINDY” later identified as CANDIDO SALVADOR and owned by JOCELYN CHUA BANEZ. According to the information, the nightclub is offering women entertainers/ dancers for sexual pleasure in exchange for a fee ranging from Php 2,000.00 – Php 3,000.00. In addition to the sexual services fee, the customers must pay each VIP room priced at Php 1,500.00. Thus, on November 7, 2021, NBI-EVRO proceeded to the target area, which resulted in the arrest of Subject Alcayde, cashier of the said night club, who received the marked money. Ten (10) female trafficked victims were likewise rescued in the operation. Subject Alcayde was presented for inquest proceedings for violation of R.A. 9208, as amended by R.A. 10364 (Expanded Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2012) while BANEZ and SALVADOR who are still at-large, will be charged of the same offense. • On November 10, 2021, operatives of NBI-Naga District Office (NBI-NADO) arrested JOLIVIA LAGASCA TAN a.k.a “VIA” and JOAQUIN TAN JR. for Robbery/Extortion in relation to R.A. 10175. • On November 10, 2021, operatives of NBI-Rizal District Office (NBI-RIZDO) seized 27.5 giant mountain bike frame, Fox fork, shimano XT brakes, Hope brakes rotors, ZTR Crest wheel rims, Hope wheel hubs and Continental tires with an approximate value of Php120,000.00. NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION

• On October 1, 2021, operatives of NBI- Death Investigation Division (NBI-DID) dismantled a multi-million investment company scam in Quezon City by virtue of an entrapment operation. based on investigation, AUREA ORGANICA milked millions of pesos from unsuspecting victims who were lured to invest their money in exchange for thirty percent (30%) return after thirty (30) days. The company uses beauty essentials such as whitening soap, oils, skin toner, and perfume as the face of their business. Upon verification, AUREA ORGANICA is not registered with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) nor does it possess a secondary license to operate as an investment company. Arrested during the entrapment operation is the company secretary LOTTA LOVE REYES who received the entrapment money. Subject was properly charged before the Quezon City Prosecutor’s Office for violation of RA 8799 otherwise known as the Securities Regulation Code. Meanwhile, charges for violation of RA 8799 and Syndicated Estafa are being prepared against BEATRIZ PIA ESPINA WHITE a.k.a. PIA ESPINA, JOSE NARCISO D. TERRADO a.k.a. JOHN TERRADO II, and other officers/operators of AUREA ORGANICA. • On October 1, 2021, the composite team of NBI-Anti-Organized and Transnational Crime Division together with Bureau of Custom (BOC) CIIS-POM, Philippine Coast Guard (PCG), and a representative from the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas – Payments and Currency Investigation Group (BSP-PCIG) seized luxury cars and Philippine Peso coins worth Php 50 Million stored in a warehouse in Brgy. Laging Handa, Quezon City. The operation stemmed from an intelligence report regarding with several Filipino-Chinese who were engaged in hoarding of more or less Php 50 Million and commercial importation of luxury vehicles through misdeclaration, misclassification, and undervaluation of the said vehicles. NBI-AOTCD operatives validate the said information through a series of surveillance and coordination made with the BOC. The BOC in turn, issued a Letter of Authority (LOA) and Mission Order (MO) against the Owners/Lessees/ Lessors/ Occupants/ Representatives or whoever is in possession of the alleged counterfeit/imported merchandise stored at a warehouse in Brgy. Laging Handa, Quezon City. The operation resulted in the seizure of one (1) Lamborghini; one (1) Nissan GTR; Ferrari Italia; Ford Shelby GT500; Mercedes Benz, Karosserie; Ford Raptor, and Nissan Cefiro. The joint team also found and seize Php 50 Million worth of Philippine Peso coins. • On October 4, 2021, the NBI-Anti-Graft Division (NBI-AGD) filed charges against MARC CEDRIC PEREZ y CALASICAS, Chief Executive Officer of AGM Advertising and JED WILLEM CARADO y SAGUINSIN, President of AGM Advertising before the City Prosecutor of Pasig City for Estafa under Article 315 (2)(a) of the Revised Penal Code; Violation of Section 26 and 28 in relation to Section 73 of R.A. 8799, otherwise known as the “Securities Regulation Code of the Philippines”; violation of Section 165 and 170 in relation to Section 20 of R.A. 11232, otherwise known as the “Revised Corporation Code of the Philippines”; and violation of Section 374 in relation to Section 114 and 115 of City Ordinance No. 51 S. 2017 of Pasig City, otherwise known as the “2017 Revised Pasig Revenue Code”. The case stemmed from a complaint filed by the victims of the subjects regarding with the alleged illegal foreign exchange trading and investment scam. According to the complaint the subjects introduced themselves as Chief Executive Officer and President of AGM Advertising. Investigation conducted by the NBI-AGD revealed that the subjects were in fact engaged in an investment pyramiding scam which is facilitated under the guise of a foreign exchange trading. The subjects introduced AGM ADVERTISING to the complainants as a “Forex Trader” and “Marketing Arm” of FX DIRECT DEALER PHILIPPINES also known as FXDD PHILIPPINES (FXDD). The subjects also claimed that FXDD is allegedly a “Broker” which serves as a platform in “Forex Trading”. The complainants revealed that the subjects were able to collect from them a total amount of Php 5,450,000.00 as investments to AGM ADVERTISING. The NBI-AGD conducted verification with the concerned government authorities revealed that the subjects including their company does not possess the necessary license either as lending company, broker and/or dealer of securities, dealer in government securities, investment adviser of and investment company, investment house and transfer agent. Further, the company AGM Advertising and Subject Perez, the DTI-registered owner, have neither registered nor renewed any business license from the concerned local government unit. Based on the foregoing, the NBI-AGD filed the above-mentioned charges against the Subjects. • On October 6, 2021, operatives of NBI-Environmental Crime Division (NBI-EnCD) arrested VIRIGILIO L. CANDELARIA for illegal construction of concrete establishments within a protected landscape in Baras, Rizal. The operation stemmed from the complaint of the President of Masungi Georeserve Foundation about the numerous concrete establishments within the Upper Marikina River Basin Protected Landscape (UMRBPL). NBI-EnCD operatives conducted a series of surveillance operations which confirmed the presence of multiple concrete establishments such as houses and pools operating as resorts. Further confirmation with the DENR-PENRO, Rizal stated that the subject establishments are indeed located within UMRBPL. Thus, after gathering enough evidences that there was indeed violations of the environmental laws the NBI-EnCD, on October 6, 2021, proceeded to the target area which resulted in the apprehension of Subject Candelaria. The owner of the resort identified as EFRAIM GONZALES was not in the area during the operation. Subject Candelaria was presented for inquest proceedings before the Provincial Prosecutor of Rizal for violation of Section 81 (formerly Section 71) of P.D. 705, as amended, otherwise known as the “Revised Forestry Code of the Philippines”. The owner of the establishment EFRAIM GONZALES was also included in the charged for violation of Section 81 (formerly Section 71) of P.D. 705, as amended, otherwise known as the “Revised Forestry Code of the Philippines” and Section 20 (n) and (o) of R.A. 7856, as amended by R.A. 11038, otherwise known as the “Expanded National Integrated Protected Areas System Act of 2018”. • On October 7, 2021, operatives of NBI-International Operations Division (NBI-IOD) rescued twenty-six (26) OFW victims and arrested two (2) individuals in Sta. Ana, Manila for Illegal Recruitment and Serious Illegal Detention. The arrested Subjects were identified as PAULO QUIZA and ROWENA LOFAMIA. On October 6, 2021, complainants sought the assistance of NBI-IOD to seek redress against Joint Venture Resources Inc. (JVR) which allegedly delays their deployment to Kuwait despite the fact that all necessary fees were already paid by their respective employers in Kuwait. Complainants also filed complaint against spouses PAULO QUIZA and ANNALYN QUIZA and ROWENA LOFAMIA, owner and administrative officer of JVR Placement Co., Inc. located at Pedro Gil corner Agoncillo St., Malate, Manila. Complainants submitted their documents and were thereafter instructed to proceed to an accommodation house maintained by the agency. Said accommodation house served as temporary shelter for applicants who mostly came from the provinces while waiting for deployment. Complainants lamented that the living condition in the accommodation house was poor and that they were prevented from leaving the premises. Complainants decided to leave and requested for their documents from the JVR but Subjects refused to return the submitted documents and continued to padlock the applicants left in the accommodation house. With these, NBI-IOD operatives conducted simultaneous operations in the accommodation house and at the office of JVR. The operations resulted in the rescue of twenty-six (26) OFW applicants from the accommodation house and the arrest of Subjects PAULO QUIZA and ROWENA LOFAMIA. Arrested Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings on October 9, 2021 before the Manila Prosecutor’s Office for Serious Illegal Detention and Illegal Recruitment under Section 6 (k) of RA 8042 otherwise known as Migrant Workers and Overseas Filipinos Act of 1995 as amended by RA 10022. • On October 12, 2021, operatives of NBI-Environmental Crime Division (NBI-EnCD) arrested five (5) individuals for illegal quarrying activities. Subjects were identified as RONALD PANGILINAN MALIG, quarry operator; KIER GANIA ARCIGA, backhoe operator; MARK JOSHUA AVENGOZA SAMPANG, loader operator; DANILO UMALI MALABANAN, truck driver; and ARNOLD SALAK CADIANG, elf-truck driver. The operation stemmed from an information received by NBI-EnCD regarding the alleged illegal mining/quarrying activities being conducted in the Municipalities of Capas, Concepcion, Bamban, and Tarlac City. Thus, on October 12, 2021, after verification with the concerned government agencies, NBI-EnCd together with the DENR-MGB Region III, proceeded to the target areas to conduct an anti-illegal mining operation. Upon arrival at the target areas, the joint operatives were able to witness the actual operation of illegal quarrying being conducted by the five (5) subjects. Joint operatives asked Subject Malig (Quarry Operator) the necessary documents and permits to operate a quarry within the target area. Subject Malig was given ample time to produce the documents or permits but failed to present any. Operatives then apprehended the above-named subjects and seized 3 pcs. excavator, 2 pcs. wheel loader, 1 pc. 22-wheeler truck loaded with sand, 1 pc. 6-wheeler ruck loaded with sand, and 40 cubic meter river sand material with an estimated value of Php 8,396,000. Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the Provincial Prosecutor’s Office of the Province of Tarlac for violation of Section 103 (Theft of Minerals) under R.A. 7942, otherwise known as the “Philippine Mining Act of 1995”. Subsequently, an information was filed at the Municipal Trial Court of Capas- Bamban-Concepcion, Capas, Tarlac for the above-mentioned violation committed by the subjects. • On October 13, 2021, operatives of NBI-Dagupan District Office (NBI-DADO) arrested REAH ELLASUS y SALINAS for selling dog meat products. Subject REAH ELLASUS y SALINAS was presented for inquest proceedings before the Provincial Prosecution Office, Dagupan City, Pangasinan for violation of The Animal Welfare Act of 1998 as amended by RA 10631. • On October 13, 2021, operatives of NBI-Puerto Princesa City District Office (NBI- PUERDO) arrested JULIE MAE LUMANTA-CAABAY and IVAN IMPERIAL GECERA for Adultery. Without wasting time, the NBI- PUERDO operatives apprehended both subjects and informed them of their constitutional rights. NBI-PUERDO also recovered from the subjects a cellphone and 10 pieces of photographs of Subjects Julie and Ivan together. The two (2) subjects were brought to the NBI-PUERDO office where they undergone standard booking procedures. Thereafter, the subjects were brought for inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor, Puerto Princesa City for Adultery as defined and penalized under Article 333 of the Revised Penal Code. • On October 18, 2021, operatives of NBI-Environmental Crime Division (NBI-EnCD) arrested ERICSON CINCO y MAYO, RAUL GARCIA y LOBETANA, WINDEL BUENO y TALAGA PABLO RIMORIN y GAPASIN, NICO YUNAPA, ROLDAN BONIFE y HONOR, DEXTER COLAS y COCOY, JOJIE MANZANILLO y DE GUZMAN, ALBERT ESTO y COCOY, FERNANDO LOPEZ y CRISTY, RANDY CAGANAN y LORING, and DANIEBOY ALEJANDRO y SALEM for illegal quarrying activities in Rodriguez, Rizal. The operation stemmed from the information received by the NBI-EnCD on August 26, 2021, regarding with the alleged rampant illegal mining/quarrying activities being conducted by certain individuals in Barangay San Isidro, Rodriguez, Rizal. The information also revealed that this group of individuals were extracting and disposing minerals without the necessary permit from the Provincial Mining Regulatory Board of the Province of Rizal and the Department of Environment and Natural Resources – Mines and Geosciences Bureau Region IV (DENR-MGB Region IV). Surveillance operation conducted confirmed that the ongoing quarrying operation. A certification issued by DENR-MGB on October 12, 2021 states that there was no valid and existing Mineral Production Sharing Agreement or Industrial Sand and Gravel Permit that was issued for the extraction of materials in relation to the sanitary landfill project in the Municipality Rodriguez, Rizal. The certification also provides that based on the data provided by the Provincial Mining Regulator Board of Rizal, as of 2nd Quarter of 2021, no valid and existing Quarry Permit, Industrial Sand and Gravel, Small Scale Mining Contract or Special Permit to Transport and Dispose was issued in relation to the sanitary landfill project in the said municipality. Thus, on October 18, 2021, joint operatives led by the NBI-EnCD together with the personnel from the DENR-MGB Region IV-A proceeded to Barangay San Isidro, Rodriguez, Rizal which resulted in the arrest of the subjects. Arrested subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of Provincial Prosecutor of Rizal for violation of Section 103 (Theft of Minerals) under R.A. 7942, otherwise known as the “Philippine Mining Act of 1995”. In Addition, JOSE ALLAN CRUZ y ABARRA (at-large), was also included in the charged for the same violation of the law. • In a series of operations, operatives of NBI-Intellectual Property Rights Division (NBI- IPRD) seized counterfeit items with an estimated total amount of Php 136,883,380.00. VICTORIA SA CUNTAPAY and ADRIAN O. NIEVA. Unfortunately, Subject Geraldine Potot was not in the target area when the NBI-CEVRO implemented the Warrant of Arrest. The arrested subjects were turned-over to Medellin District Jail, Cebu, and the Warrant of Arrest was immediately returned to the issuing court. • On November 2, 2021, operatives of NBI-Special Projects Team (NBI-SPT) ZOSIMO BELLO y ESCOVER, Section Chief, Assessment, Port of Manila (BOC) and SALVADOR SELETARIA JR. y VERGA for Robbery/Extortion and violation of the Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act. • On November 3, 2021, operatives of NBI-Anti-Organized and Transnational Crime Division (NBI-AOTCD) arrested MARIA ANNALYN H. DOC ANA and PAUL TAMARES for alleged Estafa and Illegal Practice of Medicine in violation of RA 2382 as amended by RA 4224 (The Medical Act of 1959) RIVERA and TAMARES represented themselves as doctor and nurse, respectively and provided medical assistance to complainant’s mother who got sick in exchange of cash in the total amount of Php 56,290.00. Cruz requesting for the service of the Warrants of Arrest issued against Subject ANNA LYN RIVERA for violation of Article 315 of the RPC and BP 22 both issued by the Municipal Trial Court of Sta. RIVERA inside the NBI Detention Center, Taft Ave. Manila. • On November 4, 2021, operatives of NBI-CALABARZON arrested eight (8) individuals who were caught in the act committing illegal gambling known as bookies. Rosa, Laguna. The operations resulted in the arrest of two male individuals and the seizure of over 2.5 tons of meat products. The enforcement stemmed from a complaint filed on June 25, 2026, by a private individual. Subsequent investigations confirmed that the targeted facilities were operating without the required local government permits and lacked mandatory accreditation from the NMIS. A total of 2,515.72 kilograms of illegally dressed chicken was confiscated during the raids. The seized items have been turned over to the NMIS for proper disposal in compliance with regulatory standards. Both subjects have been processed and have undergone inquest proceedings for violations of Republic Act No. 10536, otherwise known as the Meat Inspection Code of the Philippines. https://www.facebook.com/reel/1301650711993234

body: PRESS STATEMENT November 04, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } In support of the government’s initiative against the spread of counterfeit products, the National Bureau of Investigation – Intellectual Property Rights Division (NBI-IPRD) carried out operations on two separate occasions. These operations resulted in the seizure of a significant quantity of Louis Vuitton products and four laptops containing counterfeit software. On October 27, 2025, the NBI-IPRD agents implemented nine Search Warrants against four stalls at Baclaran, LRT Shopping Mall, three stalls at Baclaran Terminal 1 Building, both in Pasay City, and an establishment in the City of Manila for violation of Republic Act No. 8293 (Trademark Infringement). The operation resulted in the seizure of 3,063 pieces of fake Louis Vuitton products worth Php 342,668,188.00. On October 28, 2025, NBI-IPRD agents, armed with a search warrant for violation of R.A. No. 8293 (Trademark Infringement), seized four laptops containing counterfeit STAAD Bentley Software, valued at Php 1,431,574.40, from a company in Pasig City. The operation was initiated following a complaint from the software owners regarding this company. Surveillance conducted by NBI-IPRD agents confirmed the validity of the complaint, leading to the planned operation and implementation of the search warrant. Charges will be filed against the owners of the establishments named above for the above-stated violations. The NBI is committed to protecting and supporting the interests of legitimate business owners and investors. These operations aim to enhance foreign investor confidence and ensure that legitimate businesses can thrive. The NBI strongly discourages the public from supporting counterfeit products, as this negatively impacts our economy.

body: A female labor recruiter who defrauded several prospective seafarers is facing criminal charges following her arrest by agents of the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) during an entrapment in Parañaque City last week. The suspect was identified as: JULIE ANN ATANACIO de LAYOLA, a resident of Gladiola St., TS Cruz Subdivision, Almanza II, Las Piñas City. Also facing charges is Carla Atanacio de Jurilla, sister of Julie Ann and a resident of Balagtas St., Tuazon Village, Pamplona I, Las Piñas City. Investigation by the National Capital Region (NCR) under RD Elfren L. Meneses Jr., disclosed that on July 26, 2013, the NCR received complaints from Felomino Mendoza and four others against suspects sisters Julie Ann Layola and Carla Atanacio Jurilla. Accordingly, from February to March, 2013, Julie Ann referred her sister Carla to the complainants who offered jobs on board a certain tanker ship as deck crew or utility crew with a salary of $300-$500 US$ monthly. In consideration thereof, suspects demanded P25,000 each for the “line-up” of every applicant payable immediately, and another P25,000 payable before boarding the ship. They were made to deposit their payments to the Bank Account of Carla Jurilla as previously agreed upon. Moreover, Julie Ann asked for additional P2,500 from each complainant as her commission. Applicants were promised to board ship within two months after payment of fees. Transactions made by suspects were all done outside their respective offices. However, after five months have passed since payment, and complainants noted no developments. Despite repeated demands for the return of their money, suspects refused and continued to give same promises to them. Despite this, Julie Ann still demanded P2,500 from each of them as her referral fee. Verification with the Philippine Overseas Employment Administration (POEA) disclosed that suspect Carla is not connected with Asia World nor licensed/authorized to recruit workers overseas. On the other hand, Julie Ann Layola is connected with Venture Management Systems Inc. as Assistant Documentation Officer. Further investigation made led to the discovery that Venture Management Systems Inc. is a land-based recruitment agency, and not involved in the deployment of seafarers. On July 26, 2013, an entrapment operation was scheduled at 7-11 Convenience Store located at Sky Freight Building, Ninoy Aquino Avenue corner Pascor Drive, Parañaque City. At 3:00 PM of the same date, suspect Julie Ann Layola arrived at the store and approached the complainants who also came earlier. She handed to them a piece of paper on which was written an account number where to deposit the additional amount demanded. Thereafter, one of the complainants handed over the marked money to suspect Julie Ann. Moments after the pay-off, NBI agents positioned nearby approached the suspect and arrested her. She was brought to the NBI office for booking and detention.

body: PRESS STATEMENT October 22, 2024 In accordance with the directive of National Bureau of Investigation Director JUDGE JAIME B. SANTIAGO (Ret.) to beef up the NBI’s drive against illegal recruitment, the NBI-Caraga Regional Office (NBI-CARAGA) arrested MELIGHT C. ESGUERRA in Butuan City for Illegal Recruitment under Section 6 of R.A. No. 8042 (Migrant Workers and Overseas Filipinos Act of 1995), as amended. The operation stemmed from a complaint filed against the Subject for Illegal Recruitment. Investigation conducted by the NBI-CARAGA revealed that the Complainant was being recruited by the Subject to work in Canada in exchange for a sum of money. The Complainant shelled out Php749,500.00 for the processing fee and preparation of necessary documents. Subject Esguerra asked additional money from the Complainant for the processing and went to Butuan City to personally get the demanded money. Verification with the Department of Migrant Workers -Regional Office XIII revealed that Subject is not a license or holder of authority to engage in the recruitment of workers for employment abroad. Thus, on October 14, 2024, NBI-CARAGA conducted an entrapment operation in Butuan City, which resulted in the arrest of Subject Esguerra in the act of accepting the entrapment money. Subject was presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor of Butuan City. Director Santiago congratulated the operatives of NBI-CARAGA for the successful apprehension of the Subject.

body: PRESS STATEMENT February 25, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } In line with the directive of National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Director Judge Jaime B. Santiago (Ret.) to intensify the campaign against Trafficking in Persons of minors, the NBI – Batangas District Office (NBI- BatDO) arrested a certain “AZIS” in Batangas City, Batangas for violation of Republic Act 9208, as amended by Republic Act 10364 and Republic Act 11862 otherwise known as the “Expanded Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2022”. The entrapment operation also resulted in the rescue of six (6) victims, including three (3) minors. The operation stemmed from an information that the Subject was engaged in human trafficking of minors within the province of Batangas, particularly in Lipa City. The Subject offers male and female victims including minors for sexual exploitation in exchange for a fee ranging from Php 2,000.00 – Php 8,000.00 pesos. Acting on the said information, a rescue and entrapment operation was hatched by NBI-BATDO Agents, in coordination with the Department of Justice – Inter-Agency Council Against Trafficking (DOJ-IACAT) and Office of the City Social Welfare – Batangas City and NBI-Human Trafficking Division (HTRAD) to augment the operation. Subject agreed with the undercover agents to transport and deliver the victims from Lipa City to Batangas City with the purpose of sexual exploitation. On February 18, 2025, the Subject arrived at the agreed place together with victims where the sexual exploitation will happen. Thereafter, Subject offered the six (6) victims to the undercover agents and received the pre-marked entrapment money. After the transaction has been completed, NBI-BatDO and HTRAD Agents declared their authority under the law and arrested the Subject and rescued all the victims. The victims were assessed by the Social Welfare Officers and were eventually turned over to the custody of DOJ-IACAT Tahanan ng Inyong Pag-Asa (TIP) Center for processing. The arrested Subject was presented for Inquest Proceedings for violation of the aforementioned law before the Office of the City Prosecutor – Batangas.

body: PRESS STATEMENT July 05, 2022 DOJ DESIGNATES DE LEMOS AS NBI OFFICER-IN-CHARGE NBI Deputy Director (DD) MEDARDO G. de LEMOS has been designated Officer-in-Charge of the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI). Department of Justice (DOJ) Secretary Jesus Crispin Remulla issued the Department Order dated 1 July 2022 designating DD de LEMOS as NBI OIC until 31 July 2022. Prior to the designation, Atty. Medardo G. de Lemos was the second in command in the Bureau. He is the most senior officer of the National Bureau of Investigation. He has been with the Bureau for the last 37 years. Atty. de Lemos graduated from the University of the Philippines, College of Law in 1983. He is a graduate of NBI Academy in 1985. He completed the Officers Senior Executive Course conducted by the Philippine Public Safety College in 1994. He finished the training course jointly conducted by the Federal Bureau of Investigation (192nd Session) and the University of Virginia in 1998. He obtained a Career Executive Service Officer Rank (CESO) in 2003. Atty. de Lemos has been with law enforcement for the longest time. He wrote the paper on “Shootings of and by NBI Agents and Special Investigators”. He was instrumental in crafting the Bureau’s Rules of Engagement which defined the policy on the use of deadly force in its enforcement operations. He is a regular lecturer at the Philippine Judicial Academy on the use of deadly force in the security training for Judges. Atty. de Lemos was born and raised in Iligan City where he finished his primary and secondary education. He obtained his Bachelor of Arts major in Philosophy from the University of the Philippines, Diliman, Quezon City, and his Masters in Management from the Philippine Christian University.

body: PRESS STATEMENT June 29, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } PRESS RELEASE | NBI EXTENDS HUMANITARIAN ASSISTANCE TO EARTHQUAKE-AFFECTED COMMUNITIES AND PERSONNEL IN GLAN, SARANGANI The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI), through the collective generosity and voluntary contributions of its officials and personnel from offices nationwide, has extended humanitarian assistance to the Municipality of Glan, Sarangani Province, following the devastating 7.8 magnitude earthquake that affected the area. Demonstrating its steadfast commitment to public service and compassion, the NBI Family formally turned over Five Hundred Thousand Pesos (₱500,000.00) in financial assistance to the Local Government Unit (LGU) of Glan. The donation is intended to augment the LGU’s ongoing relief operations, emergency response, and rehabilitation efforts for families and communities severely affected by the disaster. In addition to the financial assistance, the NBI donated essential relief goods, including bottled drinking water and sacks of rice, to help address the immediate needs of displaced residents and families impacted by the earthquake. The relief items were turned over together with the cash assistance as part of the Bureau’s continuing humanitarian response. SANTIAGO (Ret.) as seventy-six (76) Special Investigators, who have been serving the Bureau with pride and honor for the longest time, were reclassified from SI III (Salary Grade 18) to Investigation Agent III (Salary Grade 22), a milestone in the history of the Agency. ”Under the NBI Modernization law, once an SI retires, the item shall be considered dissolved. Rolando Toledo, and Secretary Amenah Pangandaman. “The reclassification of the Agents will provide more quality service to the Filipino people, improve their performance in the solution of crime, and raise the bar of competency in the field of law enforcement,” said the Director.

body: PRESS STATEMENT April 10, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } PRESS RELEASE | NBI ARRESTS INDIAN NATIONAL FOR CORRUPTION OF PUBLIC OFFICIALS Pasay City, Philippines – On April 6, 2026, the NBI-Ilocos Regional Office (NBI-IRO) arrested an Indian national for violation of Article 212 (Corruption of Public Officials) of the Revised Penal Code (RPC). On March 17, 2026, the Subject visited the NBI-IRO Clearance Section to apply for an NBI Clearance. During the processing of his application, a “WITH HIT” status was flagged under his name. This indicated the presence of a possible criminal record or namesake that required further verification. The Subject was informed that his name was associated with a derogatory record related to a pending warrant for rape in the Regional Trial Court of Capiz, which he denied. He was advised to obtain a court clearance and a certificate confirming that he is not the individual charged with the crime. Weeks later, the subject spoke with the Officer-in-Charge of the clearance section and boldly inquired how much he would have to pay for the immediate release of his NBI clearance. As a result, an entrapment operation was organized, leading to the subject’s arrest while he was in the act of handing over the offered bribe money. The NBI-IRO has charged the subject with the aforementioned violation and is seeking assistance from the NBI-Capiz District Office to verify whether the individual arrested is the same person accused of the pending rape case before the Regional Trial Court of Capiz. NBI Director Atty. Melvin A. Matibag commended the agents of the NBI-IRO for their rapid and effective action, which ultimately resulted in the successful arrest of the Subject. Director Matibag reinforced the agency’s integrity, asserting that the NBI continues to operate with a steadfast commitment to incorruptibility and justice, assuring the public of their resolve to maintain high ethical standards in all their operations. #NBIServes

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today said operatives of NBI-Anti-Organized and Transnational Crime Division (NBI-AOTCD) arrested OFELIA OLLAVE y MACAS a.ka. OFELIA OLLAVE y CORTEZ alias “LEAH”, JOCELYN AMANCIO y ALQUIZAR, and RUBEN FLORES y CASTOR for Falsification by Private Individuals under Article 172 of the Revised Penal Code. In connection with outstanding request of the Bureau of Customs to assist their office in combating the proliferation of smuggling activities. The NBI said an intelligence report was received involving the production of falsified import documents such as, but not limited to, import permits, import clearances from various agencies and AFTA (ASEAN Free Trade Area) Certificates. Investigation conducted showed that there are indeed personalities in Recto area engaged in the production of the aforementioned documents. Focus was made on the falsification of the AFTA, particularly the ASEAN-CHINA FREE TRADE AREA PREFERENTIAL TARIFF CERTIFICATE OF ORIGIN which grants holder of preferential tariff concessions or discounts in the payment of taxes. Two (2) personalities engaged in falsifying AFTA certificates, alias “LEAH” and alias “JOY”, were contacted by poseur buyers to order AFTA documents. Two (2) simultaneous entrapment operations were set. One in Isettan, Recto and one in National Bookstore, Rizal Avenue, Manila. The entrapment operation conducted in Rizal Avenue, Manila on January 7, 2017, resulted in the arrest of Subjects JOCELYN AMANCIO y ALQUIZAR and RUBEN FLORES y CASTOR. Subjects delivered five (5) AFTA documents which costs Php 4,000.00 each. They were arrested upon receipt of the balance payment of Php 14,000.00. On the other hand, Subject “LEAH” later identified as OFELIA OLLAVE y MACAS a.k.a. OFELIA OLLAVE y CORTEZ was arrested in the entrapment operation conducted in Isettan, Recto. Three (3) AFTA documents with entries and ten (10) blank AFTA documents were ordered for a total price of Php 58,500.00 and Php 4,500.00 each. Php 6,000.00 deposit was made. On February 7, 2017, the documents were delivered, and upon receipt of the balance of Php 52,500.00, inclusive of the marked money, Subject was arrested. The simultaneous operations were conducted with operatives of the Bureau of Customs. Subjects will be charged with Falsification by Private Individuals under Article 172 of the Revised Penal Code before the Inquest Prosecutor of Manila.

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today announced the arrest of two (2) individuals by the NBI-Naga District Office in Calabanga, Camarines Sur for selling illegal drugs. NBI Officer-in-Charge (OIC)-Director Eric B. Distor identified the subjects as ROMMEL MEDROSO y ROMERO a.k.a. BEBE and LEONER AGUILAR y PANTE. The operation stemmed from the information received by NBI-NADO that a.k.a BEBE was involved in the sale, trade, administration, and distribution of Methampetamine Hydro Chloride or commonly known as SHABU in Brgy. San Vicente, Calabanga, Camarines Sur. Director Distor said that on September 13, 2021, after proper coordination to PDEA 5, operatives of NBI-NADO proceeded to the target area in strategic positions for a buy-bust operation. Upon arrival of the Subject, there was a change of mind of the Subject and instead instructed the confidential informant to proceed to Barangay San Vicente, Calabanga and that he would be picked up by a blue tricycle. After a while, a blue tricycle approached the confidential informant and instructed him to board the tricycle. Upon handing over the entrapment money, the tricycle sped away but was immediately flagged down by the operatives resulting in the arrest of the two subjects. Recovered from the possession of the subjects were eleven (11) pieces heat sealed transparent plastic sachet containing white crystalline substance suspected to be shabu, one (1) digital weighing scale, one (1) improvised plastic tooter, (1) lighter, (1) Gcash Card, and one (1) LTO Driver’s License. The recovered plastic sachets containing the alleged shabu was sent to the PNP Regional Crime Laboratory Office 5 for laboratory examination. The result of the examination revealed that the recovered items where indeed shabu with a total weight of 25.797 grams. Also, the arrested subjects were subjected to drug test which their urine specimen yielded positive result for the presence of Methampetamine. Director Distor added, that on September 14, 2021, the subjects were brought for inquest proceeding before the Office of the Provincial Prosecutor Camarines Sur for violation of Section 5 of R.A. 9165, otherwise known as the “Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002”.

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today announced the arrest of five (5) individuals by operatives of NBI-Environmental Crime Division (NBI-EnCD) in the Province of Tarlac for illegal quarrying activities. NBI Officer-in-Charge (OIC)-Director Eric B. Distor identified the subjects as RONALD PANGILINAN MALIG, quarry operator; KIER GANIA ARCIGA, backhoe operator; MARK JOSHUA AVENGOZA SAMPANG, loader operator; DANILO UMALI MALABANAN, truck driver; and ARNOLD SALAK CADIANG, elf-truck driver. OIC Director Distor said that the operation stemmed from an information received by NBI-EnCD regarding the alleged illegal mining/quarrying activities being conducted in the Municipalities of Capas, Concepcion, Bamban, and Tarlac City. NBI-EnCD operatives immediately conducted a series of surveillance operations in the said municipalities which confirmed that there were indeed numerous active quarry sites on the stated areas. NBI-EnCD operatives then verified and requested with Provincial Governor Environmental and Natural Resources Office (PGEnRO) of the Province of Tarlac the entities/persons that have been granted quarry permit, sand gravel permit, special minerals extraction permit, special permit, gratuitous permit or any other similar permit authorizing the development and utilization of mineral resources. Operatives also verified and requested with the Department of Environment and Natural Resources- Mines and Geo-Sciences Bureau Regional Office No. 3 (DENR-MGB Region III) a certified copy of list of persons/entities that have an existing and valid Area Status and Clearance or Consent for Mining Applications in the Province of Tarlac. Thus, on October 12, 2021, after verification with the concerned government agencies, NBI-EnCd together with the DENR-MGB Region III, proceeded to Capas, Tarlac to conduct an anti-illegal mining operation. Upon arrival at the target area, the joint operatives were able to witness the actual operation of illegal quarrying being conducted by the five (5) subjects. The joint operatives asked Subject Malig (Quarry Operator) the necessary documents and permits to operate a quarry within the target area. Subject Malig was given ample time to produce the documents or permits but failed to present any. The joint operatives then, apprehended the above-named subjects and seized 3 pcs. excavator, 2 pcs. wheel loader, 1 pc. 22-wheeler truck loaded with sand, 1 pc. 6-wheeler ruck loaded with sand, and 40 cubic meter river sand material with an estimated value of Php 8,396,000. On October 13, 2021, the five apprehended subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the Provincial Prosecutor’s Office of the Province of Tarlac for violation of Section 103 (Theft of Minerals) under R.A. 7942, otherwise known as the “Philippine Mining Act of 1995”. Subsequently, an information was filed at the Municipal Trial Court of Capas-Bamban-Concepcion, Capas, Tarlac for the above-mentioned violation committed by the subjects.

body: Operatives of the NBI- Anti-Fraud Division (NBI-AFD) have arrested on Tuesday, June 5, an individual in an entrapment operation in NAIA Terminal 1, Pasay City for Estafa thru Falsification of Commercial and Public Documents. NBI Director Dante A. Gierran identified the Subject as JUNJIE BANAAG ALIMPAROS who also uses the names JEFFREY TUAZON YAP, ANGELO TUAZON YAP , and JEFFREY REYES CRUZ , who has victimized dealers of motor vehicles. On June 1, 2018, Rizal Autozone, Inc., dealer of Honda cars, reported an incident which transpired on May 25, 2018 at their Honda Rizal branch. The Subject, using the name JEFFREY TUAZON YAP, ordered a Honda HRV unit via phone call and submitted thru e-mail an approved Purchased Order from Malayan Bank, which appears to be authentic. He also submitted Driver’s License and PRC License in support of his alleged loan application with Malayan Bank. After the release of the said vehicle, it was found that the documents submitted by the Subject are all fake and falsified. On the same day Rizal Autozone, Inc. learned from their other branch in Carmona, Cavite that the Subject had ordered a Honda CRV and instructed the Honda Sales Agent to register the unit under his brother’s name, ANGELO TUAZON YAP , as it was supposed to be a gift for him. The Subject carried out the same modus wherein he submitted thru e-mail a purportedly approved Purchase Order from Malayan Bank, together with Driver’s License and PRC License bearing the names of his alleged Brother ANGELO TUAZON YAP . Based on the pictures contained on the IDs submitted by the Subject, JEFFREY TUAZON YAP and his alleged brother ANGELO TUAZON YAP are one and the same person. On this basis, operatives of the NBI-AFD hatched an entrapment operation and posed as Honda Carmona Sales Agents tasked to deliver the Honda CRV Unit to Subject at the agreed time and place, resulting in the arrest of Subject JUNJIE BANAAG ALIMPAROS . Subject was presented for inquest for the crime of Estafa thru Falsification of Commercial Document / Falsification of Public Document before the office of the Prosecutor in Pasay City.

body: In line with the relentless campaign of the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) against illegal activities, operatives of NBI-Anti-Organized and Transnational Crime Division (NBI-AOTCD) arrested three (3) individuals for Swindling / Estafa in Quezon City. NBI Director Dante A. Gierran identified the subjects as ENRIQUITO T. DIZON, LOURDES V. BONIFACIO, and JOHN ALVIN B. DIGUANGCO. The operation stemmed from the complaint filed before the office of the NBI-AOTCD that certain individuals who claimed to have authority to represent National Housing Authority (NHA) in obtaining/securing contracts for their housing projects nationwide. The group enticed the complainant to grab the contract offered by the NHA. The group assured the victim that they could easily obtain the contract if they could provide Ten Million Pesos (Php 10,000,000.00) as buy-out fee and to lock-in the said project. The victim and his associate contractors agreed to pay Three Million Pesos (Php 3,000,000.00) as part of the Php 10 Million buy-out fee and agreed to meet in one of the restaurants at White Plains, Quezon City. The complainant verified the authority of the subjects from the NHA and found that the group has no authority to obtain/secure contracts of work from any NHA office. On January 10, 2019, NBI-AOTCD operatives together with the complainant and his associates proceeded to the meeting area where the partial payment of P3 Million will be handed to the subjects. The complainant showed the P3 Million (marked money) to the subjects. Subject Dizon instructed Subject Bonifacio to count the money in the comfort room. At this juncture, the operatives of NBI-AOTCD announced their authority and arrested the subjects. The entrapment operation resulted in the seizure of several documents pertaining to alleged NHA projects. Charges for violation of Article 315 of the Revised Penal Code in relation to P.D. No. 1689 were filed against the arrested subjects, ADEL GERONA (at large), and one Alias “HENRY”.

In line with the relentless campaign of the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) against illegal activities, operatives of NBI-Anti-Organized and Transnational Crime Division (NBI-AOTCD) arrested three (3) individuals for Swindling / Estafa in Quezon City. NBI Director Dante A. Gierran identified the subjects as ENRIQUITO T. DIZON, LOURDES V. BONIFACIO, and JOHN ALVIN B. DIGUANGCO. The operation stemmed from the complaint filed before the office of the NBI-AOTCD that certain individuals who claimed to have authority to represent National Housing Authority (NHA) in obtaining/securing contracts for their housing projects nationwide. The group enticed the complainant to grab the contract offered by the NHA. The group assured the victim that they could easily obtain the contract if they could provide Ten Million Pesos (Php 10,000,000.00) as buy-out fee and to lock-in the said project. The victim and his associate contractors agreed to pay Three Million Pesos (Php 3,000,000.00) as part of the Php 10 Million buy-out fee and agreed to meet in one of the restaurants at White Plains, Quezon City. The complainant verified the authority of the subjects from the NHA and found that the group has no authority to obtain/secure contracts of work from any NHA office. On January 10, 2019, NBI-AOTCD operatives together with the complainant and his associates proceeded to the meeting area where the partial payment of P3 Million will be handed to the subjects. The complainant showed the P3 Million (marked money) to the subjects. Subject Dizon instructed Subject Bonifacio to count the money in the comfort room. At this juncture, the operatives of NBI-AOTCD announced their authority and arrested the subjects. The entrapment operation resulted in the seizure of several documents pertaining to alleged NHA projects. Charges for violation of Article 315 of the Revised Penal Code in relation to P.D. No. 1689 were filed against the arrested subjects, ADEL GERONA (at large), and one Alias “HENRY”.

body: PRESS STATEMENT October 11, 2024 The Inter-Agency Task Force Against Illegal Drugs composed of the National Bureau of Investigation – Pampanga District Office (NBI-PAMDO), Philippine Drug Enforcement Agency (PDEA), Bureau of Customs (BOC), and Philippine National Police (PNP), conducted a Drug Interdiction at FEDEX Warehouse, Clark Freeport Zone, Mabalacat City, Pampanga. On October 08, 2024, operatives commenced and opened one (1) FEDEX box containing four (4) plastic pouches wrapped in garments containing 1,048 grams of dried leaves and fruiting tops suspected as High-Grade Marijuana (Kush) inside the FEDEX Warehouse in Clark Freeport Zone, Mabalacat City, Pampanga. Initial tests showed that the items appeared to be Cannabinoid with an estimated value of more or less Php 1,572,000.00. Samples of each said pack of Cannabinoid were marked, weighed, and turned over to PDEA in the presence of the Members of the Task Force and the rest of the seized contraband are in the custody of the BOC. An ample portion of samples for PDEA’s further testing were likewise weighed, marked by the BOC Examiner and later turned over to PDEA.

title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) is cautioning the public about ATM skimming, the latest bank fraud that hits the country. ATM skimming is the theft of card information from the magnetic strips on the back of the ATM card that occurs during legitimate transactions from the ATM. An electronic device called skimmer, smaller than a deck of cards is fastened or installed over the normal card reading slot of the ATM machine. The skimmer would then record the data from the magnetic strip on the back of the ATM card. While a tiny camera hidden near the skimmer will record the PIN as it is entered by the depositor. The thieves then use all the information they gathered to manufacture a counterfeit card which they will use to withdraw money from the depositors bank account. Skimming devices come in many forms and are hard to detect. The places to check for possible tampering are the light diffuser area, speaker area, ATM side fascia, card reader entry slot and the ATM keyboard area. In a normal fascia, the flashing card entry indicator can easily be seen, while in most skimming devices, no flashing card entry indicator can be seen and the shape of the snout is different.

body: PRESS STATEMENT February 20, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } PHP 7.7 MILLION SHABU SEIZURE: NBI HALTS 5.4KG SHABU SHIPMENT AT NAIA COMPLEX PASAY CITY, Philippines – The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI), as part of a multi-agency task force, successfully seized a substantial volume of illegal drugs at the Ninoy Aquino International Airport (NAIA) complex on February 11, 2026. The seizure took place at the PAIR PAGS Center through the coordinated efforts of the NAIA-Inter-Agency Drug Interdiction Task Group (NAIA-IADITG). This group includes the NBI’s International Airport Investigation Division (NBI-IAID) and various law enforcement partners. During a meticulous inspection of incoming cargo, agents discovered 5.425 kilograms of a white crystalline substance suspected to be Shabu (Methamphetamine Hydrochloride). The illegal substances were discovered within three abandoned shipments, where the contraband had been professionally concealed inside common declared items to evade detection. This sophisticated smuggling attempt involved hiding the drugs within the components of CCTV cameras and the false linings of various handbags. With an estimated street value of Php 7,799,712.00, the seized narcotics were immediately turned over to the Philippine Drug Enforcement Agency (PDEA) for forensic examination and official custody. A follow-up investigation is underway to track the origin of the shipments, identify the individuals involved, and initiate the filing of appropriate criminal charges under the Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act. This successful interdiction is a testament to our unyielding stance against the illegal drug trade. Through the power of inter-agency synergy, we have fortified our nation’s gateways against sophisticated smuggling attempts. The NBI, in seamless coordination with our partners in the NAIA-IADITG and PDEA, remains a formidable barrier, ensuring that our borders are closed to those who seek to poison our communities. #NBIServes Media Contact: HA Palmer U. Mallari NBI Spokesperson [email protected]

body: PRESS STATEMENT February 24, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } NBI RESCUES THREE MINORS, ONE ADULT IN MULTI-CITY CRACKDOWN ON CHILD EXPLOITATION PASAY CITY, Philippines – The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) announced today the successful rescue of four victims of human trafficking and the recovery of illegal materials during a series of coordinated operations across Metro Manila and Rizal province. On February 19, 2026, the NBI-Human Trafficking and Related Crimes Division (NBI-HTRAD) deployed three specialized teams to Valenzuela City, Angono, and Binangonan to execute search warrants and rescue operations targeting a trafficking and child exploitation network. The mission successfully rescued four victims—three of whom are minors—who are now under the protective custody of the MSWD in Angono and Binangonan. Beyond these rescues, NBI agents in Valenzuela City seized electronic gadgets containing Child Sexual Abuse and Exploitation Materials (CSAEM). Preliminary investigations have already uncovered a disturbing foreign link, revealing that a Filipino facilitator had been supplying large volumes of this illegal material to a long-term partner in Germany. The success of this operation serves as a powerful testament to the efficacy of modern inter-agency and public-private partnerships. The NBI’s HTRAD unit worked in seamless coordination with the Department of Justice (DOJ) through the Inter-Agency Council Against Trafficking (IACAT) and Cyber-TIP, which provided the necessary legal and administrative framework. Furthermore, the field expertise of non-government organizations Destiny Rescue Philippines and Exodus Philippines proved vital to the mission’s execution, while the participation of Local Government Units ensured immediate, compassionate aftercare for the rescued victims. #NBIServes
