body: On May 19, 2020, operatives of NBI-Cybercrime Division (NBI-CCD) served a Warrant of Arrest against NORMAN MANGUSIN a.k.a. FRANCIS LEO MARCOS. On April 2020, the NBI-CCD received a complaint against NORMAN MANGUSIN a.k.a. FRANCIS LEO MARCOS for violation of RA 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act). Investigation disclosed that FRANCIS LEO MARCOS is a social media personality portraying himself as a philanthropist/businessman who helps people. However, upon record check, it shows that there pending cases against one FRANCIS LEO MARCOS and NORMAN MANGUSIN y ANTONIO. Further verification shows that FRANCIS LEO MARCOS and NORMAN MANGUSIN y ANTONIO are one and the same person based on the issued clearance and a copy of passport. His photographs on the said documents bearing the name NORMAN MANGUSIN revealed to be the same person as the one who carried the name FRANCIS LEO MARCOS. NBI-CCD was able to obtain a copy of Warrant of Arrest issued by RTC, Baguio City against NORMAN MANGUSIN a.k.a. FRANCIS LEO MARCOS for violation of RA 8050 (Revised Optometry Law). The said Warrant of Arrest was verified as outstanding. Therefore, operatives proceeded to Le Grand, Tower 2, Eastwood, Quezon City to serve the Warrant of Arrest. Implementation of the Warrant of Arrest was done in a peaceful manner and Subject was informed of his constitutional rights. On May 22, 2020, operatives of NBI-Central Luzon Regional Office (NBI-CELRO) arrested RYAN BENEDICT T. DAVID for violations of RA 9262 (VAWC) and RA 9995 (Anti-Photo and Video Voyeurism Act). Subject was arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from a complaint against him for the above-mentioned violations. Complainant agreed to meet the Subject on the condition that the latter will stop spreading the nude photos of the complainant. Subject was presented for inquest proceedings before the City Prosecutors Office, Angeles City, Pampanga. On May 25, 2020, operatives of NBI-Central Luzon Regional Office (NBI-CELRO) arrested PHILIP G. VELASCO, RIA B. TALICTIC, GLADYS D. PATHAK, SHEIR AM M. MACOMB, LAWRENCE N. FERRER, JAMES JOSEPH M. MOSE, and MAXER TAJAN for violations of RA 7394 (Consumer Act of the Philippines), RA 9711 (Food and Drugs Administration Act), and RA 10611 (Food Safety Act). Subjects were arrested in an operation which stemmed from a report of a concerned employee against his employer Mr. Philip Velasco, et.al. a part owner of Phil–Em Enterprises, Incorporated, a company believed to be engaged in procuring fake, near expiry, and expired huge numbers of consumer products specifically from their contacts in Manila and Pampanga and they corrupt the products by tampering the expiration dates with the use of improvised machines and thereafter resale the same in bulk locally and abroad. Investigation and validation by the operatives confirmed the said report. Enforcement operation of the Search Warrant was then conducted inside the company’s premises at Bldg. 187, Gridley Road, Global Industrial Park, Subic Bay Freeport Zone-SMBA, Zambales. Found and seized thereat were the adulterated consumer products, machines, and papers. Subjects were presently detained at NBI-Olongapo District Office and will be presented for inquest before the Chief City Prosecutor, Olongapo City for the above-mentioned violations. On May 27, 2020, operatives of NBI-Central Luzon Regional Office (NBI-CELRO) assisted the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) in the inspection of 2 nd Floor of J.F. Dee Academy in Clark Hills which was allegedly used as medical and dental clinic with pharmacy without authorization/permits from the Department of Health (DOH) and FDA, in violations of RA 2382 (Medical Act of 1959), RA 3720 (Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act), as amended by RA 9711 (FDA Act of 2009). Upon arrival, operatives were approached by Ms. Almira M. Mangsal, the owner of 365 Mix Mini Mart that occupies the said premises which was being used as their warehouse. According to Ms. Mangsal, said area was indeed previously a medical clinic being managed and operated by Chinese people. However, the latter vacated the premises several weeks ago. Nevertheless, the FDA team still conducted investigation as it was seen in plain view boxes of items/products bearing Chinese and Korean names/labels. After the inspection, samples of the products were taken by the FDA for laboratory examinations to determine whether or not there have been violations of the FDA law. On May 28, 2020, operatives of NBI-Central Luzon Regional Office (NBI-CELRO) arrested CHEN ZHENG ZHONG and CHEN HAI FANG, Chinese nationals, for illegal practice of medicine and operating a medical clinic/hospital and pharmacy. Subjects were arrested in entrapment operation which stemmed from the report and test buy conducted on May 27, 2020. Recovered during the operation were the entrapment money and a medicine named “Quake” which is submitted for laboratory examination to the FDA office. Officers/personnel of the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) confiscated the medicines, equipment, and other paraphernalia used in the operations of the alleged medical clinic by the said Chinese nationals. Subjects were presented for inquest before the City Prosecutors Office of Angeles City, Pampanga for violations of RA 2382 (Medical Act of 1959), RA 3720 (Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act), as amended by RA 9711 (FDA Act of 2009).

body: PRESS STATEMENT October 21, 2024 The National Bureau of Investigation-Human Trafficking Division (NBI-HTRAD), under the leadership of NBI Director Judge Jaime B. Santiago (Ret.), arrested an individual on October 13, 2024, for human trafficking. Director Santiago said that the NAIA Task Force Against Trafficking referred three intercepted passengers who were bound for Thailand. During primary inspection by the Bureau of Immigration, the three claimed that they were a group of friends going on a tour at Bangkok, Thailand for six (6) days, and that they were supposedly employed by TTEC as Customer Service Representatives. However, due to several inconsistencies in their declarations of two of them, as well as their failure to establish their relationship with one another and their doubtful purpose of travel, the three were referred for secondary inspection. The two passengers then admitted that they are not employees of TTEC and that they were bound for Thailand to be surrogate mothers via in-vitro fertilization (IVF) procedure in exchange for 8,000 to 10,000 USD. Their co-passenger, FREEZLE ROSE BALONDO y RICANOR, supplied their employment documents for their departure. The Bureau of Immigration turned over the three to the IACAT, and were afterwards brought to NBI-HTRAD for further investigation. FREEZLE ROSE BALONDO admitted that she was working for MLE&MLANG International Surrogacy, LLC as a coordinator wherein she assists prospective surrogate mothers before and during their departure from the Philippines to undergo IVF. Prospective surrogate mothers’ referrals for OB-Gyne checkups were made by a certain DR. JIRATH WICHIANPITAYA of IBABY FERTILITY AND GENETIC CENTER located in Bangkok, Thailand. Accordingly, the money needed for these checkups as well as incidental expenses were sent to them either from WENSEN’s GCash Account number 09155184101, BALONDO’s GCash Account, and BALONDO’s GoTyme Account. FREEZLE ROSE BALONDO was then placed under arrest for Trafficking in Persons under RA 9208 as amended by RA 10364 and RA 11862. She was presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor, Pasay City for the aforesaid violation of law.

body: PRESS STATEMENT August 13, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } On August 7, 2025, the National Bureau of Investigation – Cybercrime Division (NBI-CCD), under the supervision of Director Judge Jaime B. Santiago (Ret.), arrested five (5) Vietnamese nationals in Barangay La Paz, Makati City for violations of Republic Act No. 2382 (The Medical Act of 1959) in relation to Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012 (Republic Act No. 10175), the Food and Drug Administration Act (Republic Act No. 9711), and the Philippine Pharmacy Act (Republic Act No. 10918). The operation was initiated after the NBI-CCD received verified information that certain foreign nationals were engaging in the unauthorized practice of medicine. They individuals were found to be advertising their services on social media platforms, offering cosmetic procedures such as brow lifts, lip surgery, fox eye surgery, under-eye fillers, thread lifts, and upper eyelid surgery. Subsequent surveillance confirmed that these individuals were performing medical procedures without the necessary government licenses from the Professional Regulation Commission (PRC). On August 07, 2025, an entrapment operation was conducted by the NBI-CCD agents that led to arrest of PHAN NGOC DUC, TUAN ANH PHAM, THI DIEU LINH DINH, VUONG THI NGAN, and LO THI MAI, who were caught in flagrante delicto of performing the overt act. Medical tools and related paraphernalia used in the procedures were also seized. Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings for the aforementioned violations.

Santiago (Ret.), arrested five (5) Vietnamese nationals in Barangay La Paz, Makati City for violations of Republic Act No. 2382 (The Medical Act of 1959) in relation to Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012 (Republic Act No. 10175), the Food and Drug Administration Act (Republic Act No. 9711), and the Philippine Pharmacy Act (Republic Act No. 10918). The operation was initiated after the NBI-CCD received verified information that certain foreign nationals were engaging in the unauthorized practice of medicine. They individuals were found to be advertising their services on social media platforms, offering cosmetic procedures such as brow lifts, lip surgery, fox eye surgery, under-eye fillers, thread lifts, and upper eyelid surgery. Subsequent surveillance confirmed that these individuals were performing medical procedures without the necessary government licenses from the Professional Regulation Commission (PRC). On August 07, 2025, an entrapment operation was conducted by the NBI-CCD agents that led to arrest of PHAN NGOC DUC, TUAN ANH PHAM, THI DIEU LINH DINH, VUONG THI NGAN, and LO THI MAI, who were caught in flagrante delicto of performing the overt act. Medical tools and related paraphernalia used in the procedures were also seized. Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings for the aforementioned violations.

title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today said operatives of the NBI Cybercrime Division (NBI-CCD), NBI Isabela District Office, and DOJ Office of Cybercrime have arrested CHRISTIAN IAN P. SALVADOR, a 22 year old Computer Science student of Isabela State University, Cauayan Campus, on March 3, 2017 for Phishing, an act of illegally obtaining sensitive information such as usernames, passwords, and credit card details in an electronic communication. On the strength of a Search Warrant issued by the Cybercrime Court of RTC Manila, operatives raided the apartment of the Subject in Cauayan City, Isabela. Subject was arrested after being found in flagrante delicto violating the Cybercrime Prevention Act, Access Device Regulation Act, and Data Privacy Act. Subject had illegally obtained online banking username and password, personal information, and credit card information including card number, security code and expiration date of customers of a local bank. Subject sent thousands of emails to various customers of the bank making it appear that the emails came from the bank itself. In the said emails, victims were informed that due to security reasons, the bank was performing an update of its online banking database and therefore customers need to update their bank information by clicking on a link. The link then would take the customers to a fake website where they would input their online banking details as well as their credit card information. Subject had copied the legitimate website and made alterations to it so it would look almost exactly like the legitimate website of the bank. Once the customers put in their personal information, online banking information and credit card details, it would automatically be collated and sent to the Subject’s designated email address. Subject used the phished credit card credentials to purchase gadgets like cellphones, laptops, and other devices which he would then sell for cash. He also sold the phished information to third parties over the internet. Through this illegal activity, Subject was able to purchase a brand new Toyota Vios, Honda Beat, Toyota Mio motorcycles, and several high end gadgets. Subject was brought to the Department of Justice in Manila for inquest proceedings. Charges for violation of Section 4(a)(5)(ii) of R.A. 10175 or the Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012 [Misuse of Devices], Section 25(a) of R.A. 10173 or the data Privacy Act of 2012 [Unauthorized Processing of Personal Information], and Section 9(k) of R.A. 8484 or the Access Device Regulation Act of 1998 [Unauthorized Possession of Access Device] were recommended , with the latter two (2) offenses in relation to Section 6 of R.A. 10175. Pending the results of the full forensic examination of the seized devices, additional charges, particularly Computer Related Forgery, computer Related Identity Theft, and Cybersquatting all under R.A. 10175 may also be filed against the Subject.

title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: On June 1, 2019, operatives of NBI-Cybercrime Division (NBI-CCD) arrested PETER LIM SANTOS, WANG LIPING, and AU PANG LIANG, all Chinese nationals, for bribery inside the NBI headquarters. The Chinese nationals were arrested after they offered the agents of the NBI-CCD a sum of money in exchange of the freedom of another three (3) Chinese nationals who were arrested on May 31, 2019 for Kidnapping and Serious Illegal Detention. CCD operatives reported the incident to the CCD Chief and conducted an entrapment operation when the Subjects went to the CCD office to discuss the payment for the release of the Chinese nationals. Subjects were arrested thereafter. Seized from the Subjects were five (5) bundles of Php 1,000 bills amounting to Php 500,000.00. Charges for violation of Article 212 under the Revised Penal Code were filed against the Subject. On June 5, 2019, operatives of NBI-International Airport Investigation Division (NBI-IAID) arrested JUDITH TIRU MAQUILING a.k.a. Boss Ping and Teng for Human Trafficking. Subject has been involved in human trafficking activities for years by facilitating the exit of female Filipino workers at NAIA going to Malaysia and offering them to work in night clubs as Guest Relations Officers (GRO) or entertainers. Subject was arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from the information coming from said victims who were recruited by the Subject to work in Malaysia as GRO/entertainers which include going out with customers for extra service where they could earn 500 Malaysian Ringgit for an hour. Subject instructed the victims to send copies of their passport bio-page, whole body and close up pictures through WhatsApp account for the processing of their travel documents. Subject then sent the victims’ plane tickets and told them to meet her at NAIA Terminal 3 for their flight to Malaysia via Hongkong. Subject also told them that she would accompany the victims in going to Malaysia to facilitate their exit out of the country. With this, the entrapment operation was hatched resulting in the arrest of the Subject. Subject will be presented for inquest proceedings before the Inquest Prosecutor, Pasay City for violations of RA 8042 (Migrant Workers and Overseas Filipinos Act) and RA 9208 (Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act). On June 6, 2019, operatives of Rizal District Office (NBI-RIZDO) seized five (5) rolls and one (1) box containing scarp/cutlets of counterfeit window film (tint) all bearing the trademarks and logos owned by 3M Company (3M). Items were seized in Imus, Cavite by virtue of Search Warrants. Charges for violation of RA 8293 (Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines) were filed against M.C.W. Auto Supply/M.C. W. Car Accessories, Maria Cristina s. Tinio, Emil Wang,a nd any the proprietors/officers of its premises. On June 8, 2019, operatives of NBI-Cordillera Administrative Region (NBI-CAR) arrested SAMI OSMAN y SAIFELDIN and MOHAMED ALI OSMAN ALI for violation of RA 9165 (Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002). Subjects were arrested in an operation which stemmed from a report that Subjects were allegedly involved in the sale and use of illegal drugs particularly shabu. In coordination with the PDEA, NBI-CAR operatives proceeded to the Subjects’ boarding house at Brgy. Upper San Vicente, Baguio City and implemented the Search Warrants issued against the Subjects. The operation yielded positive result. Subjects were arrested and were turned over to PDEA-CAR for inquest proceedings. On June 10, 2019, operatives of NBI-Rizal District Office (NBI-RIZDO) and Laguna District Office (NBI-LAGDO) implemented the Search Warrant against KAPA Community Ministry International, Inc. for violation of Sections 8 and 26 in relation to Section 73 of RA 8799 (Regulation Securities Code). KAPA Community Ministry International Inc. is an entity duly registered with the SEC as a non-stock and non-profit religious organization that engages in massive recruitment of members and accepting investment money from its members under the guise of donation. Despite the advisory as well as the Cease and Desist Order issued by the SEC, KAPA was defiant thereby prompting the SEC to cancel or revoke KAPA’s certificate of Corporate Registration. However, KAPA still continued its operation and even expanded its operation and recruitment activities to the other regions in the Philippines. Hence, President Duterte ordered the NBI and CIDG to close down the operation of KAPA. The implementation of Search Warrant resulted in the seizure of the proceeds of the crime amounting to Php 2,230,713.55, three (3) desktop computers, four (4) counting machines, one (1) photocopy machine that are used in the selling/offering of securities/investment contracts. Filing of cases against KAPA, particularly its founder, Pastor Joel Apolinario and KAPA’s Area Manager in Cebu, Engr. Christopher D. Abad, will follow. On June 10, 2019, operatives of NBI-Anti-Violence Against Women and Children (NBI-AVAWCD) arrested JACQUELYN JULIAN y OSIT, JONARD OSIT, and MERY DESERIE VILLENA y PALANG for Human Trafficking. Subjects were arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from an information that a network of young girls called walkers were being offered for sex for a price depending on the age that ranges between 14-17 years old. The girls were being traded for sexual pleasure by a pimp known as “Jack-Jack” and her cohorts “Barbie” and “Daisy”. A team was immediately dispatched at Isetan, Recto where there were several food stalls and cocktail tables were built at the center where public and walkers can bring their food and drinks while waiting or looking for someone. Upon positive confirmation, the entrapment operation was conducted resulting in the arrest of the above-mentioned Subjects and the rescue of eight (8) victims, seven (7) of whom are minors. Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings for violation of RA 9208 (Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2003) as amended by RA 10364 (Expanded Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2012). On June 10, 2019, the NBI-Anti-Graft Division (NBI-AGD) has filed charges against ten (10) individuals regarding the alleged irregular claims “(ghost dialysis scandal”) for payment of dialysis and other medical treatment of Philippine Health Insurance Corporation (PhilHealth) members and beneficiaries. The following persons recommended for prosecution for violation of Article 315 and Article 172 in relation to Article 171 of the Revised Penal Code of the Philippines: Dr. BRYAN CHRISTOPHER SY y WANG, LIEZEL AILEEN y SANTOS DE LEON, and EDWIN ROBERTO y CORITA. Also included for prosecution are the following persons (at large) Dr. JOHN RAY M. GONZALES, CLARO SY y NGO, ALVIN SY y WANG, THERESE FRANCESCA TAN y RODRIGO, DICK ONG y SY, Dr. PORSHIA NATIVIDAD y COMES and Dr. JOEMIE SORIANO y DICHOSO. On June 10, 2019, NBI-AGD issued Subpoena Ad Testificandum commanding Dr. Sy, Dr. Gonzales, Ms. Rodriguez and Atty. Ernesto P. Barbado Jr. to appear before the said office. Sy and his companions arrived at the AGD office with the assistance of their counsel. Mr. Cueto and Atty. Barbado, both from the Fact-Finding, Investigation and Enforcement Department of the Philippine Health Insurance Corp. (PHIC) also appeared and submitted various documents in relation to their investigation. They were interviewed and they narrated the fraudulent schemes made by Wellmed Dialysis & Laboratory Center Corporation. Cueto submitted a Supplemental Sworn Statement on May 30, 2019 in relation to the PHIC’s complaint. It was revealed by Cueto that Wellmed Dialysis & Laboratory Center Corporation continuously files PhilHealth Reimbursement Forms for their patients at the PhilHealth Regional Office NCR. Two whistleblower namely De Leon and Roberto voluntarily appeared with their Counsel before the Office of the Deputy Director for Investigative Service (DDInvs) and showed their willingness to testify against Wellmed Dialysis & Laboratory Center Corporation. On March 30, 2016, according to Roberto who was the Assistant Manager at the company and in charge of the operation including the processing of claims of patient-members that time was ordered by Dr. Sy to charge a dialysis billing amounting to Php 2,600.00 Philhealth claims of dead individuals. He then instructed De Leon to generate PhilHealth Benefit Eligibility Form from PhilHealth Portal together with the Claim Form 2 and Member’s Data Record (MDR). De Leon filled up the said form per instruction of Dr. Sy. Further, it was disclosed that a number of claims were made again by De Leon following the instructions of Dr. Sy. A total amount of Php600,600.00 composing of 200 dialysis sessions were settled by PhilHealth to Wellmed Dialysis & Laboratory Center Corporation, said patients were already dead but were able to avail of the PhilHealth dialysis benefits. Furthermore, a total of 27 claims composed of 280 dialysis sessions with a total amount of Php808,600.00 was also credited to the account of Wellmed Dialysis & Laboratory Center Corporation. On June 13, 2019, operatives of NBI-Environmental Crime Division (NBI-EnCD), together with the DENR-Mines and Geoscience Bureau (MGB), arrested four (4) individuals for illegal quarrying in Brgy. Talacsan, San Rafael, Bulacan. Several heavy equipment with an estimated value of more than Php 7 Million were likewise seized. The arrested Subjects were brought for inquest proceedings before the DOJ Inquest Prosecutor for violation of the Philippine Mining Act. On June 13, 2019, operatives of NBI-Special Action Unit (NBI-SAU) arrested TIASIR NARDO y BERNALES, JOSEPH EDDARD EDDUN y IDEMNE, RESSIELEEN REFUGIDO y BARRO, and KATRINA IGLE y PERALTA for violation of RA 9165 (Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002). Subjects were arrested in a buy-bust operation conducted wherein Subject TIASIR NARDO was selling liquid and capsule ecstasy worth Php 13,000.00. Subjects JOSEPH EDDARD EDDUN, RESSIELEEN REFUGIDO, and KATRINA IGLE were arrested for being the companions of Subject TIASIR and for possession of illegal drugs particularly ecstasy and shabu. Laboratory examination on the seized items done by the PDEA yielded positive for Gamma-butyrolactone (GBL), Methyledioxymethamphetamine (MDMA), Methamphetamine Hydrochloride, and Marijuana. Arrested Subjects were presented for inquest proceeding before the Office of the City Prosecutor, Makati City for violation of RA 9165 (Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002). On June 13, 2019, operatives of of NBI-Special Action Unit (NBI-SAU) arrested MARK KONSTANTIN MARQUEZ, JOHN KENNETH TORENO, CRISTINE VARGAS, ALLEN MARK MANGANIZA, and CRYST KYLE CHUA for violation of RA 9165 (Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002). Subjects were arrested by virtue of Search Warrants conducted at Unit 3417, Tower 2, Grass Residences, Nueva Viscaya St., Bago Bantay, Quezon City. Seized during the operation were glass bottles containing transparent liquid, transparent self-sealing plastic sachets containing dried leaves and cigarette sticks, pitchers containing yellow and brown liquid, plastic bottles containing transparent liquid, and plastic bottle containing several pieces of tablets. Laboratory examination on the seized items done by the PDEA yielded positive for Gamma-butyrolactone (GBL), Methyledioxymethamphetamine (MDMA), Methamphetamine Hydrochloride, and Marijuana. Subjects were presented for inquest proceeding before the Office of the City Prosecutor, Quezon City for violation of RA 9165 (Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002). On June 13, 2019, operatives of NBI-Special Operations Group (NBI-SOG) arrested IDA JOSEPHINE SIOCO HERMOSA and DELTHA PASCO BERNARDO for introducing themselves as the representative of Mayor Sara Z. Duterte to influence a certain case handled by NLRC. operation stemmed from a letter dated June 11, 2019, received from Mr. Raul Nadela, Chief of Staff of the Office of the City Mayor of Davao City. According to Mr. Nadela he sent the letter in behalf of Mayor Sarah Duterte requesting for a thorough investigation about unscrupulous individuals who make appearances before the National Labor Relation Commission (NLRC) in Quezon City using the name of Mayor Sara Z. Duterte and/ or the Office of the City Mayor of Davao City. On the same date, Mayor Sara Z. Duterte of Davao City, executed an affidavit stating that she have not asked, instructed, or caused anyone to represent her or her office to various government agencies including the NLRC. on June 3, 2019 a certain individual who introduced herself as Mayor Sara Duterte (daughter of President Rodrigo Roa Duterte) called the Office of Commissioner Alex A. Lopez to talk about a case involving PHILTRANCO and VICTORY LINER handled by the NLRC and told Ms. Javier that Malacañang had already ordered the investigation of the case and that they noted irregularity. On June 13, 2019, a certain JOSEPHINE VILLAHERMOSA together with DELTHA BERNARDO appeared before the office of Commissioner Lopez. Ms. Javier introduced the two women to Atty. Melquiades Sol D. Del Rosario as the representatives of Mayor Sara Duterte. An hour later, Commissioner Lopez came to his office and noticed two women talking to his Chief-of –Staff, Atty. Del Rosario and the two were introduced to Commissioner Lopez. At this juncture, the NBI-SOG operatives were already in the vicinity of the office of Commissioner Lopez. Before the two women left the office of Commissioner Lopez, one of the agents approached them and asked one of them if she is the JOSEPHINE VILLAHERMOSA whose name appeared on the security log book of the building. Initially, she denied that she was Villahermosa but afterwards she admitted that she is indeed JOSEPHINE VILLAHERMOSA. Thereafter, the two women were placed under arrest and were informed of their Constitutional rights. Subjects were brought before the Quezon City Office of the City Prosecutor for violation of Article 177 (Usurpation of Authority or Official Function) of the Revised Penal Code. In addition, it was found that the subjects have cases for Estafa, Illegal Recruitment, and B.P. 22. On June 17, 2019, the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) has recommended the filing of charges against NHA officials for violation of RA 9184 (Government Procurement Act) and RA 3019 (Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act) as well as Grave Misconduct. The recommendation is in relation to the irregularities that they had committed pertaining to Yolanda Permanent Housing Project. The NBI has recommended the filing of charges for violation of RA 9184, RA 3019, and Irregularities in the Procedure against twenty-three (23) individuals who are public officers and acting as members of the Bids and Awards Committee of the Technical Working Group of the Yolanda Permanent Housing Program (YPHP). To recall, the Commission on Audit (COA) flagged the irregularities behind the Yolanda Permanent Housing Program (YPHP), a rehabilitation program that was implemented by the National Housing Authority (NHA). Accordingly, the lack of manpower, splitting of contracts, and extension of contacts led to the delayed completion of projects under the YPHP. Based on the investigation, JC Tayag Builders, the contractor, is not technically capable to undertake to implement the projects because of its limited Allowable Range of Contract Cost (ARCC), List of Personnel and Equipment. To remedy the incapability, NHA officials and JC Tayag Builders resorted to splitting the projects into sites to accommodate for the execution of the contracts. This act of NHA officials is intended to give favor to JC Tayag Builders. Moreover, the members of the BAC1, BAC2, and their respective TWGs are administrative liable for Grave Misconduct. The NHA officials disregarded the law and were manifestly remiss in their duties in strictly observing the directives of RA 9184 which resulted in undue benefits to JC Tayag Builders. On June 17, 2019, operatives of NBI- Task Force Against Illegal Drugs (NBI-TFAID) arrested FREDDIE NACION JR. a.k.a. GLENN, ESPERANZA PIDO, JOAN GARCIA, RONNIE G. LAO, SULPICIO R. CASSILER JR., and LEONARDO D.C. ASA for selling of illegal drugs within the vicinity of Malacañang Complex, Manila. the operation stemmed from a reliable information given by the Presidential Intelligence Command, that a certain Fredie Nacion, Esperanza Pido, and Ronnie Lao are engaged in selling and distribution of shabu within the vicinity of Malacañang Complex. Surveillance operation confirmed the said information. Thus, by virtue of Search Warrants, operaatives proceeded to the house of Subjects Nacion, Pido, and Garcia in Brgy. 662, Paco, Manila. Search conducted at the residence of the three subjects resulted to the seizure of six (6) heat sealed plastic sachet containing shabu and several used drug paraphernalia. Arrested individuals were subjected to drug test that gave positive results for the presence of Methamphetamine Hydrochloride and its metabolite. Another team went to the residence of Subject Lao in Brgy. 831 Paco, Manila. Subject Lao together with Subjects Cassiler and Asa were caught in flagrante delicto in a pot session at the ground floor stock room of the house. Seized were several drug paraphernalia, eight (8) transparent plastic sachets containing shabu, one (1) transparent plastic sachet containing dried marijuana, one (1) pistol with magazine and ammunitions. Seized white crystalline substance tested positive of Methamphetamine Hydrochloride. Likewise, the sachet containing marijuana weighing .202 gram gave positive results. Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the Manila Prosecutors Office for violation of RA 9165 (Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002) On June 19, 2019, operatives of NBI-Environmental Crime Division (NBI-EnCD) arrested JIEMVO D. CADORNA, DRANREB L. GEGANTE, JOEY M. ESPANOLA, RUBEN G. GARCIA, DANILO D. CARIDA, ERIK B. QUIAMBAO, WILFREDO G. GONZALES, MARY JANE L. NUGUID, ANTONIO S. BUYSON (Filipino), and the Chinese nationals GENG PING y ZHU and GE WEI CHEN in Floridablanca, Pampanga for illegal quarrying. On February 11, 2019, the NBI received a complaint from Palakol Quarry & Development Corporation through its general manager, regarding the illegal quarry operations in Floridablanca, Pampanga. NBI-EnCD operatives then conducted surveillance operations. Operatives ascertained that several operators of quarry, vibro processing, and washing plant are operating along Gumain River, Floridablanca, Pampanga and it include Riah Yuan Vibro and Antonio Buyson Quarry. Careful examination of the documents and several surveillances, disclosed that Riah Yuan Vibro is not registered with the DENR-MGB III and that the quarry of Mr. Antonio Buyson is done outside its permitted area. With this, NBI-EnCD operatives, together with the DENR-MGB III proceeded to Brgy. Consuelo, Floridablanca, Pampanga on June 19, 2019. While traversing the Consuelo Bridge, it was observed that the backhoes situated in Gumain River were extracting minerals and loading the same to a truck. Simultaneously, a truck was unloading minerals in the vibro plant to be processed. Dump trucks were also observed in the area. Subjects were also found in the act of dumping minerals in the vibro, arranging/preparing the minerals at the vibro plant, operating backhoes. The above-mentioned Subjects were placed under arrest for mutually helping one another and acting in unison to carry out theft of minerals by quarrying and extracting outside the permitted area, processing the raw minerals in Riah Yuan Vibro and disposing the same with intent to gain in violation of Section 103 (Theft of Minerals) of RA 7942 (Philippine Mining Act of 1995). Subjects were brought for inquest proceedings before the Office of the Prosecutor General, Department of Justice for the aforementioned violation On June 19, 2019, operatives of NBI-Intellectual Property Rights Division (NBI-IPRD) seized counterfeit Louis Vuitton products with an estimated value of Php 70 Million. Items were seized in Harrison Plaza, Manila by virtue of Search Warrants. Charges for violation of RA 8293 (Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines) were filed against John/Jane Does/owners/operators of various stalls located at Harrison Plaza A. Mabini St. and Adriatico St., Manila. On June 19, 2019, operatives of NBI-Western Mindanao Regional Office (NBI-WEMRO) arrested JUL-ASBI SAMPANG y SADJILI for engaging in anomalous issuance of Tax Identification Number and TIN Cards. Subject was arrested in an entrapment operation conducted in BIR office in Zamboanga City. Subject resisted arrest but was eventually apprehended. Subject was brought to the NBI-WEMRO office for the proper booking procedures. On June 20, 2019, operatives of NBI-Rizal District Office (NBI-RIZDO) arrested LILIBETH ROBLES y VELASCO and KIM VOLANTE y PIQUE for Human Trafficking. Subjects were arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from an information that alleged human trafficking activities were taking place in the areas of Quezon City and Rizal. Information revealed that a pimp known as “Kim” was maintaining prostitutes who appear to be minors and were offering them to possible clients for a quick sexual intercourse in exchange for monetary considerations. Surveillance operations were conducted and confirmed the said information. Thereafter, the entrapment operation was conducted resulting in the arrest of the Subjects and the rescue of fourteen (14), two (2) of whom are minors. Subjects LILIBETH ROBLES y VELASCO and KIM VOLANTE y PIQUE were presented for inquest proceedings before the City Prosecutors Office of Quezon City for violation of RA 9208 (Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2003) as amended by RA 10364 (Expanded Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2012) in relation to RA 7610 (Special Protection of Children Against child Abuse, Exploitation and Discrimination Act). On June 21, 2019, operatives of NBI-Central Visayas Regional Office (NBI-CEVRO) arrested thirty six (36) collectors manning Peryahan ng Bayan betting outlets. Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings for violation of PD 1602 as amended by RA 9287 (Anti-Illegal Gambling Law). On June 21, 2019, operatives of NBI-Cordillera Administrative Region (NBI-CAR) arrested VALERY TAKOUKAM y GISCARD, Canadian national for Estafa and violation of Article 168 in relation to Article 166 of the Revised Penal Code. On the said date, Jackson B. Aliping sought the assistance of the NBI regarding an alleged dollar scam. Accordingly, two (2) foreign nationals swindled his cousin with more or less 19,200 US Dollars. When the transaction with one of the foreigners in Baguio City failed, the latter was arrested and confiscated the chemicals in his possession and decided to refer the matter with the NBI as they did not know what to do. Complainant Roger A. Padingil informed the operatives regarding the “black dollar scam” or the “wash wash scam” and that they have in their custody one of the Subjects named VALERY TAKOUKAM y GISCARD. Complainant Padingil, together with Aliping and Johnny Palangdosan turned over Subject TAKOUKAM, whom they arrested after he failed to turn the bundle of blank papers into genuine US Dollar bills. Subject TAKOUKAM was then placed under arrest for Estafa and violation of Article 168 in relation to Article 166 of the Revised Penal Code. Subject was presented before the Baguio City Prosecutor’s Office for Inquest Proceedings and was later turned over at the Baguio City Jail upon written order of Inquest Prosecutor. In two (2) separate operations dated June 20 and 21, 2019, operatives of NBI-Anti-Organized and Transnational Crime Division (NBI-AOTCD) IRMALYN MELODIAS-TORRES and GERALD C. MELODIAS for Estafa and Large Scale Illegal Recruitment. On July 26, 2018, the NBI received a letter from the U.S. Embassy requesting the arrest of the Subject. She was then arrested and was brought to the NBI Main Office for the booking procedures. After several stakeout, it was discovered that Subject GERALD is living with Subject IRMALYN at Candido St., Brgy. Ugong, Valenzuela City. Hence, on June 21, 2019, Warrants of Arrest were served to Subject GERALD C. MELODIAS. He is now detained at the NBI detention facility awaiting commitment order. Items, with an estimated value of Php 50,000.00, were seized in Sta. Cruz, Manila by virtue of Search Warrants. Charges for violation of RA 8293 (Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines) were filed against Puljed Trading and/or Edna Pulido and/or any of its proprietors, officers, employees, and occupants. Sapang, Sta. Barbara, Pangasinan. Subjects were presented for inquest for violation of PD 1602 a amended by RA 9287 (Anti-Illegal Gambling Law). On June 25, 2019, operatives of NBI-Anti-Organized and Transnational Crime Division (NBI-AOTCD) arrested LJUBOMIR CALIXTERIO TAMAYO for Extortion and Estafa. Subject served as the business partner of the complainant who is an owner and managing partner of JPM88 Manpower Agency located in Ermita, Manila. Complainant applied for POEA license and was required to have at least one employee who is knowledgeable in construction business. He then offered the Subject to be his business partner. In May 2019, POEA released the full license of Complainant’s agency. Subject then submitted a proposal letter to the Subject for his business marketing strategy and he will recruit domestic helpers in Luzon and asked Php 1 Million for expenses. Complainant disagreed and reasoned out that they did not have job orders for domestic helpers and that he could not afford the said amount. Subject insisted and did not intend to leave the complainant’s office empty-handed so the latter lowered the amount to Php 250,000.00 and issued two (2) post-dated “pay to cash” checks amounting to Php 50,000.00 each. Subject was not able to encash the checks because Complainant told the Subject that he had no sufficient fund in the bank. Complainant said that because he discovered that Subject was lying about the marketing strategy which the latter admitted saying that he badly needed money for his children’s tuition fee. On June 11, 2019, Subject went to Complainant’s office. He was punching the table, pointed his finger at the Complainant and tried to punch the latter. Subject was shouting at the Complainant to give him Php 2 Million, otherwise, he will ask the POEA to cancel the agency’s license. He was just pacified by one of the employees but threatened the Complainant of more harm if he would not give in to his demand. Out of fear for physical harm, Complainant told the Subject that he will give him Php 1 Million. With this, Complainant sought the help of the NBI as he could no longer bear the threats of the Subject. Acting on the complaint, an entrapment operation was conducted resulting in the arrest of the Subject. Subject was presented for inquest proceedings before the City Prosecutor of Manila for Extortion and Estafa. On June 26, 2019, operatives of NBI-Bicol Regional Office (NBI-BRO) arrested AGNES INGLIS RODRIGUEZ and RUBEN MIRABEL for dealing, selling, and disposing illegal drugs in Brgy. 26, Dinagaan, Legazpi City. Subjects were arrested after the Search Warrants were implemented in their premises. Eleven (11) pieces of heat-sealed transparent sachets suspected to be shabu with an estimated street value of Php 68,000.00. Subjects are now under the custody of PDEA ROV detention facility for proper disposition. Appropriate case was prepared to file in the court. In two (2) separate operations dated June 26 and 28, 2019, operatives of NBI-Counter Terrorism Division (NBI-CTD) arrested two (2) Abu Sayyaf Group (ASG) members identified as IBNO ISMAEL alias ABU KODANO and TOTONI HAIRON. The NBI received information that alleged Basilan-based Abu Sayyaf Group (ASG) members were recently sighted here in Metro Manila. Subject IBNO ISMAEL was seen in Maharlika, Taguig City while Subject TOTONI HAIRON was seen in Port Area, Manila. Subjects Ismael and Hairon have both standing Warrants of Arrest issued by the Basilan RTC for eight (8) counts of Kidnapping and Serious Illegal Detention in connection with the Golden Harvest Kidnapping Case in Basilan on 2001. Both subjects have been hiding from the law for almost twenty (20) years. Subject Ismael hiding under the name PAWWAD L. JAMDA was working as a construction worker, while Subject Hairon also known as Ismael Faisal Saral, has been working as a security guard for a very long time on Port Area, Manila. On June 26, 2019, joint operatives of NBI Counter Terrorism Division (CTD), Special Task Force (STF), Anti-Graft Division (AGD), Technical Intelligence Division (TID), Special Operations Group (SOG), and Office of the Assistant Director for Intelligence Service (OADInts) with counterparts from the Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) planned, arranged and executed the capture/arrest of the subject Abu Kodano in Maharlika, Taguig City. In a follow up operation on June 28, 2019, Subject Hairon was arrested by the joint operatives of NBI-CTD, NBI-TID, and AFP on his way to work at the South Harbor, Port Area in Manila. The 2 arrested ASG members are currently detained in the NBI Detention Facility awaiting for their transfer to Zamboanga City Jail, BJMP

NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION

On June 1, 2019, operatives of NBI-Cybercrime Division (NBI-CCD) arrested PETER LIM SANTOS, WANG LIPING, and AU PANG LIANG, all Chinese nationals, for bribery inside the NBI headquarters. The Chinese nationals were arrested after they offered the agents of the NBI-CCD a sum of money in exchange of the freedom of another three (3) Chinese nationals who were arrested on May 31, 2019 for Kidnapping and Serious Illegal Detention. CCD operatives reported the incident to the CCD Chief and conducted an entrapment operation when the Subjects went to the CCD office to discuss the payment for the release of the Chinese nationals. Subjects were arrested thereafter. Seized from the Subjects were five (5) bundles of Php 1,000 bills amounting to Php 500,000.00. Charges for violation of Article 212 under the Revised Penal Code were filed against the Subject. On June 5, 2019, operatives of NBI-International Airport Investigation Division (NBI-IAID) arrested JUDITH TIRU MAQUILING a.k.a. Boss Ping and Teng for Human Trafficking. Subject has been involved in human trafficking activities for years by facilitating the exit of female Filipino workers at NAIA going to Malaysia and offering them to work in night clubs as Guest Relations Officers (GRO) or entertainers. Subject was arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from the information coming from said victims who were recruited by the Subject to work in Malaysia as GRO/entertainers which include going out with customers for extra service where they could earn 500 Malaysian Ringgit for an hour. Subject instructed the victims to send copies of their passport bio-page, whole body and close up pictures through WhatsApp account for the processing of their travel documents. Subject then sent the victims’ plane tickets and told them to meet her at NAIA Terminal 3 for their flight to Malaysia via Hongkong. Subject also told them that she would accompany the victims in going to Malaysia to facilitate their exit out of the country. With this, the entrapment operation was hatched resulting in the arrest of the Subject. Subject will be presented for inquest proceedings before the Inquest Prosecutor, Pasay City for violations of RA 8042 (Migrant Workers and Overseas Filipinos Act) and RA 9208 (Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act). On June 6, 2019, operatives of Rizal District Office (NBI-RIZDO) seized five (5) rolls and one (1) box containing scarp/cutlets of counterfeit window film (tint) all bearing the trademarks and logos owned by 3M Company (3M). Items were seized in Imus, Cavite by virtue of Search Warrants. Charges for violation of RA 8293 (Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines) were filed against M.C.W. Auto Supply/M.C. W. Car Accessories, Maria Cristina s. Tinio, Emil Wang,a nd any the proprietors/officers of its premises. On June 8, 2019, operatives of NBI-Cordillera Administrative Region (NBI-CAR) arrested SAMI OSMAN y SAIFELDIN and MOHAMED ALI OSMAN ALI for violation of RA 9165 (Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002). Subjects were arrested in an operation which stemmed from a report that Subjects were allegedly involved in the sale and use of illegal drugs particularly shabu. In coordination with the PDEA, NBI-CAR operatives proceeded to the Subjects’ boarding house at Brgy. Upper San Vicente, Baguio City and implemented the Search Warrants issued against the Subjects. The operation yielded positive result. Subjects were arrested and were turned over to PDEA-CAR for inquest proceedings. On June 10, 2019, operatives of NBI-Rizal District Office (NBI-RIZDO) and Laguna District Office (NBI-LAGDO) implemented the Search Warrant against KAPA Community Ministry International, Inc. for violation of Sections 8 and 26 in relation to Section 73 of RA 8799 (Regulation Securities Code). KAPA Community Ministry International Inc. is an entity duly registered with the SEC as a non-stock and non-profit religious organization that engages in massive recruitment of members and accepting investment money from its members under the guise of donation. Despite the advisory as well as the Cease and Desist Order issued by the SEC, KAPA was defiant thereby prompting the SEC to cancel or revoke KAPA’s certificate of Corporate Registration. However, KAPA still continued its operation and even expanded its operation and recruitment activities to the other regions in the Philippines. Hence, President Duterte ordered the NBI and CIDG to close down the operation of KAPA. The implementation of Search Warrant resulted in the seizure of the proceeds of the crime amounting to Php 2,230,713.55, three (3) desktop computers, four (4) counting machines, one (1) photocopy machine that are used in the selling/offering of securities/investment contracts. Filing of cases against KAPA, particularly its founder, Pastor Joel Apolinario and KAPA’s Area Manager in Cebu, Engr. Christopher D. Abad, will follow. On June 10, 2019, operatives of NBI-Anti-Violence Against Women and Children (NBI-AVAWCD) arrested JACQUELYN JULIAN y OSIT, JONARD OSIT, and MERY DESERIE VILLENA y PALANG for Human Trafficking. Subjects were arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from an information that a network of young girls called walkers were being offered for sex for a price depending on the age that ranges between 14-17 years old. The girls were being traded for sexual pleasure by a pimp known as “Jack-Jack” and her cohorts “Barbie” and “Daisy”. A team was immediately dispatched at Isetan, Recto where there were several food stalls and cocktail tables were built at the center where public and walkers can bring their food and drinks while waiting or looking for someone. Upon positive confirmation, the entrapment operation was conducted resulting in the arrest of the above-mentioned Subjects and the rescue of eight (8) victims, seven (7) of whom are minors. Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings for violation of RA 9208 (Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2003) as amended by RA 10364 (Expanded Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2012). The following persons recommended for prosecution for violation of Article 315 and Article 172 in relation to Article 171 of the Revised Penal Code of the Philippines: Dr. BRYAN CHRISTOPHER SY y WANG, LIEZEL AILEEN y SANTOS DE LEON, and EDWIN ROBERTO y CORITA. Also included for prosecution are the following persons (at large) Dr. JOHN RAY M. GONZALES, CLARO SY y NGO, ALVIN SY y WANG, THERESE FRANCESCA TAN y RODRIGO, DICK ONG y SY, Dr. PORSHIA NATIVIDAD y COMES and Dr. JOEMIE SORIANO y DICHOSO. On June 10, 2019, NBI-AGD issued Subpoena Ad Testificandum commanding Dr. Sy, Dr. Gonzales, Ms. Rodriguez and Atty. Ernesto P. Barbado Jr. to appear before the said office. Sy and his companions arrived at the AGD office with the assistance of their counsel. Mr. Cueto and Atty. Barbado, both from the Fact-Finding, Investigation and Enforcement Department of the Philippine Health Insurance Corp. (PHIC) also appeared and submitted various documents in relation to their investigation. They were interviewed and they narrated the fraudulent schemes made by Wellmed Dialysis & Laboratory Center Corporation. Cueto submitted a Supplemental Sworn Statement on May 30, 2019 in relation to the PHIC’s complaint. It was revealed by Cueto that Wellmed Dialysis & Laboratory Center Corporation continuously files PhilHealth Reimbursement Forms for their patients at the PhilHealth Regional Office NCR. Two whistleblower namely De Leon and Roberto voluntarily appeared with their Counsel before the Office of the Deputy Director for Investigative Service (DDInvs) and showed their willingness to testify against Wellmed Dialysis & Laboratory Center Corporation. He then instructed De Leon to generate PhilHealth Benefit Eligibility Form from PhilHealth Portal together with the Claim Form 2 and Member’s Data Record (MDR). De Leon filled up the said form per instruction of Dr. Sy. Further, it was disclosed that a number of claims were made again by De Leon following the instructions of Dr. Sy. A total amount of Php600,600.00 composing of 200 dialysis sessions were settled by PhilHealth to Wellmed Dialysis & Laboratory Center Corporation, said patients were already dead but were able to avail of the PhilHealth dialysis benefits. Furthermore, a total of 27 claims composed of 280 dialysis sessions with a total amount of Php808,600.00 was also credited to the account of Wellmed Dialysis & Laboratory Center Corporation. Talacsan, San Rafael, Bulacan. Several heavy equipment with an estimated value of more than Php 7 Million were likewise seized. The arrested Subjects were brought for inquest proceedings before the DOJ Inquest Prosecutor for violation of the Philippine Mining Act. Duterte of Davao City, executed an affidavit stating that she have not asked, instructed, or caused anyone to represent her or her office to various government agencies including the NLRC. on June 3, 2019 a certain individual who introduced herself as Mayor Sara Duterte (daughter of President Rodrigo Roa Duterte) called the Office of Commissioner Alex A. Lopez to talk about a case involving PHILTRANCO and VICTORY LINER handled by the NLRC and told Ms. Javier that Malacañang had already ordered the investigation of the case and that they noted irregularity. Before the two women left the office of Commissioner Lopez, one of the agents approached them and asked one of them if she is the JOSEPHINE VILLAHERMOSA whose name appeared on the security log book of the building. Initially, she denied that she was Villahermosa but afterwards she admitted that she is indeed JOSEPHINE VILLAHERMOSA. Thereafter, the two women were placed under arrest and were informed of their Constitutional rights. Subjects were brought before the Quezon City Office of the City Prosecutor for violation of Article 177 (Usurpation of Authority or Official Function) of the Revised Penal Code. In addition, it was found that the subjects have cases for Estafa, Illegal Recruitment, and B.P. 22. On June 17, 2019, the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) has recommended the filing of charges against NHA officials for violation of RA 9184 (Government Procurement Act) and RA 3019 (Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act) as well as Grave Misconduct. The recommendation is in relation to the irregularities that they had committed pertaining to Yolanda Permanent Housing Project. The NBI has recommended the filing of charges for violation of RA 9184, RA 3019, and Irregularities in the Procedure against twenty-three (23) individuals who are public officers and acting as members of the Bids and Awards Committee of the Technical Working Group of the Yolanda Permanent Housing Program (YPHP). To recall, the Commission on Audit (COA) flagged the irregularities behind the Yolanda Permanent Housing Program (YPHP), a rehabilitation program that was implemented by the National Housing Authority (NHA). Accordingly, the lack of manpower, splitting of contracts, and extension of contacts led to the delayed completion of projects under the YPHP. Based on the investigation, JC Tayag Builders, the contractor, is not technically capable to undertake to implement the projects because of its limited Allowable Range of Contract Cost (ARCC), List of Personnel and Equipment. To remedy the incapability, NHA officials and JC Tayag Builders resorted to splitting the projects into sites to accommodate for the execution of the contracts. This act of NHA officials is intended to give favor to JC Tayag Builders. Moreover, the members of the BAC1, BAC2, and their respective TWGs are administrative liable for Grave Misconduct. The NHA officials disregarded the law and were manifestly remiss in their duties in strictly observing the directives of RA 9184 which resulted in undue benefits to JC Tayag Builders. ASA for selling of illegal drugs within the vicinity of Malacañang Complex, Manila. the operation stemmed from a reliable information given by the Presidential Intelligence Command, that a certain Fredie Nacion, Esperanza Pido, and Ronnie Lao are engaged in selling and distribution of shabu within the vicinity of Malacañang Complex. Mabini St. and Adriatico St., Manila. body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) is set to celebrate its Anniversary on Friday, November 13, 2015. With the theme “NBI…Valuing the Past, Embracing the Future”, the Bureau will undertake a week-long series of activities culminating with a simple program on the date of its establishment. In a statement, Nick V. Suarez, Chief of Information Division, said newly-appointed Department of Justice (DOJ) Secretary Alfredo Benjamin S. Caguioa will be this year’s Anniversary Guest of Honor and Speaker. Officials of DOJ and heads of attached agencies, counterpart agencies of the NBI and guests from the private sector are also expected to attend the celebration. Suarez said a Thanksgiving Mass will be held at 8:00 a.m. to be followed by a simple program at the NBI gym where Special Awards will be given to employees. Suarez also said that during the week, from Monday until Friday, the NBI Employees Association (NBIEA) will sponsor a Tiangge at the open grounds of the NBI clearance, free eye check-up, free facial services for employees at the 2nd floor of the Dorm building.

body: PRESS STATEMENT April 08, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } PRESS RELEASE | NBI ARRESTS 22 INDIVIDUALS IN MAKATI FOR MASSIVE INVESTMENT FRAUD SCHEME PASAY CITY, Philippines – The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) has successfully dismantled a sophisticated online investment fraud operation, resulting in the arrest of twenty-two (22) individuals during a high-stakes raid in Makati City on March 30, 2026. The joint operation, conducted by the NBI-Cybercrime Division (NBI-CCD) and the NBI-Special Action Unit (NBI-SAU), targeted an entity operating out of a business plaza on Gil Puyat Avenue. The arrests follow a detailed investigation into fraudulent trading platforms used to siphon funds from unsuspecting investors. The investigation stemmed from a formal complaint alleging violations of Article 315 of the Revised Penal Code (Estafa) through the use of Information and Communications Technology (ICT). According to the complainant and a former employee, the group managed several online investment trading platforms in the Philippines. Investigation revealed that the operation utilized these platforms to display inauthentic data, including fabricated trading figures, false profit indicators and manipulated account balances. These deceptive visuals were designed to trick victims into believing their investments were yielding high returns, inducing them to invest more capital into the fraudulent system. On March 26, 2026, the Regional Trial Court Branch 64 of Makati City issued a Search Warrant (SW) and a Warrant to Search, Seize, and Examine Computer Data (WSSECD). The warrants cited violations of Estafa in relation to the Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012 (R.A. 10175). During the implementation of the warrants on March 30, NBI operatives arrested 22 employees and are currently facing charges for violating the Securities Regulation Code (R.A. 8799) in relation to R.A. 10175. NBI Director Atty. Melvin A. Matibag reaffirmed the Bureau’s commitment to purging the country of cyber-enabled financial crimes. “The NBI continues to strengthen its efforts against those who exploit technology to defraud our citizens. We advise the public to exercise extreme caution when engaging in online investment opportunities. Always verify the legitimacy of any entity offering financial services through official regulatory channels before committing your hard-earned money.” #NBIServes

body: A self-proclaimed General of a group known as USAFFE and two (2) others were arrested by agents of the Anti-Organized and Transnational Crime Division (AOTCD) in Pasay City. NBI Director Virgilio L. Mendez identified the arrested suspects as: 1. GRANDEUR PEPITO GUERRERO y GACUTAN a.k.a. JOJO, the self-proclaimed General of USAFFE, 43 years old, and a resident of 14 Regina Village, Pasong Tamo, Tandang Sora, Quezon City; 2. EMMANUEL SAN PEDRO y VALENCIA a.k.a. MANI, 22 years old of Tambubong, San Rafael, Bulacan; and 3. SONNY YOHANON y ALBES, 25, resident of Bgy. Sabang, Oras, Eastern Samar. Investigation disclosed that sometime in July 2014, AOTCD received intelligence report that an alleged group called USAFFE, a name taken from the former United States Armed Forces in the Far East during the World War II, is planning to cause chaos in the city through explosion using an IID (Improvised Incendiary Device) which they planned to set up at the NAIA Terminal 3, SM Mall of Asia in Pasay City, and strafing at the Chinese Embassy and the D. M. Consunji Inc. (DMCI) Building, both in Makati City. The USAFFE is considered an ultra-rightist group who claims to be the “Defenders of the Filipino People” and considers China and the “oligarch taipans”, who are engaged in the monopolistic business practices and illegal mining as their arch enemy. A series of surveillance operations were conducted by the AOTCD. Information revealed that the initial plan to launch their operation which was scheduled on August 25, 2014, National Heroes’ Day, was halted. Instead, the plan to create havoc was moved to the first day of September. They intend to set-off bomb/explosive devices at the NAIA Terminal 3, strafing at the Chinese Embassy and the DMCI building in the early morning of September 1, to be followed by an explosion at the SM Mall of Asia upon its opening. However, AOTCD agents learned of the group’s final meeting before they were able to execute their plan at the NAIA Terminal 3 parking area where they will also give the IID’s to the assigned bombers at the Mall of Asia. It is there where the AOTCD agents arrested GUERRERO and his two (2) companions. Seized from the suspects were “Improvised Incendiary Device” (IID) and various documents including Guerrero’s prepared public message which he intends to release to the media upon the completion of their plan. Charges are being prepared against the subjects.

body: PRESS STATEMENT April 29, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } PRESS RELEASE | DRUGS HIDDEN IN ‘CHURCH PACKAGE’ FROM ZIMBABWE INTERCEPTED IN CLARK—₱5.6M SHABU AND KUSH SEIZE The Clark Inter-Agency Task Force Against Illegal Drugs (CRK-IATFAID), composed of the National Bureau of Investigation – Pampanga District Office (PAMDO), Philippine Drug Enforcement Agency (PDEA), Bureau of Customs (BOC), and Philippine National Police (PNP), conducted a drug interdiction operation at the courier warehouse inside Clark Freeport Zone, Mabalacat City, Pampanga, on 24 April 2026. The task force examined a brown package declared as “1 X File with Documents” and, upon opening, discovered two (2) self-sealing transparent plastic sachets containing white crystalline substance suspected to be methamphetamine hydrochloride or shabu. The items weighed a total of 710 grams and had an estimated market value of Php 4,828,000.00. Records show that the package was sent from an address in Bulawayo, Zimbabwe, to a church in Silang, Cavite, Philippines. On the same date, a second package declared to contain “CEACO Puzzles 500 pieces 4 included Food Trucks” was opened. Inside was one (1) self-sealing transparent plastic package, suspected to contain illegal drugs, specifically Kush. The items had a total weight of 540 grams and an estimated market value of Php 810,000.00. As per records, the parcel was sent from a residential house in Costa Mesa, Orange County, California, United States of America, to a condominium in Pasig, Philippines. Importation, dispensing, and delivering dangerous drugs is an illegal act under Republic Act No. 9165, otherwise known as the “Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002.” The seized items were marked, weighed, and brought to the BOC for further testing by the PDEA.

body: PRESS STATEMENT June 2, 2022 DISTOR RECOMMENDS THE RELIEF OF ARD VIC LORENZO AND ORDERS REVIEW OF CYBERCRIME AND OTHER OPERATIONAL GUIDELINES NBI OIC Director ERIC B. DISTOR has recommended the relief of ARD Vic Lorenzo as head of the NBI-Cybercrime Investigation and Assessment Center (CIAC) and other officers of Cybercrime Division (CCD) over an alleged anomalous operation pending results of investigation by NBI Internal Affairs Division (IAD). DISTOR also ordered the review of the existing cybercrime and other operational guidelines and procedures to have a more organized standards and measures as regards the operations being conducted by various operational units of the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) nationwide. In giving out his directive, OIC Director DISTOR said that the NBI will thoroughly re-examine the agency’s guidelines on operations including service of Search Warrant operations, Intelligence operations, and investigation operations. DISTOR stressed that henceforth, all operational authority must come from the Office of the Director and must be under the control and supervision of the said office, with assistance from the respective Deputy Directors. He added that all Regional Directors, Agents-In-Charge and Central Office Chiefs are likewise ordered to submit to the Office of the Director their performance/accomplishment reports for review. DISTOR emphasized that a re-assessment and revisiting of the Bureau’s operational guidelines also aim to scale down abuse of authority to leave no room for trust and integrity issues and increase professionalism among operatives as well as to further reinforce the Bureau’s ongoing success in combating crimes and illicit activities with maximum efficiency and effectiveness. DISTOR added a review of operational standards and procedures periodically undertaken is always necessary as part of management’s response to increasing role of the NBI to the challenges in a modern and highly technologically advanced society. DISTOR further pointed out that a continuous cleansing of the Bureau’s personnel will be undertaken so that only the highly skilled, competent and deserving will be retained, adding that he will not tolerate unprofessionalism in the NBI.

Santiago (Ret.) arrested 8 Chinese nationals in Parañaque City for online phishing operations. body: In line with the relentless campaign of the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) against all forms of criminality, operatives of NBI-Special Action Unit (NBI-SAU) arrested a Subject on February 26, 2020 in Cainta, Rizal for Estafa and Usurpation of Authority. NBI OIC-Director Eric B. Distor identified the Subject was identified as GENEROSO BITALAC LIM alias BOYET CRUZ. Distor said Subject was arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from the complaint against the Subject who, according to the complainant, went to their residence on February 18 and 24, 2020 bringing with him a copy of the Rape case filed by her daughter before the Office of the Provincial Prosecutor-Rizal. Subject told the complainant that he is from NBI-VAWCD and has influence in courts. Subject also claimed that he has the capacity to delay or prevent the issuance of subpoenas to respondents in on-going cases in courts resulting to the respondent’s non-appearance in hearings and the subsequent instant issuance of Warrant of Arrest by the courts. Subject also threatened the complainant by telling the latter that the respondents in the present Rape case have links with the Mayor of Cainta and capacity to influence the result of the case in respondent’s favor. Subject also informed the complainant that her cases will be dismissed upon death of complaining parties, making the latter more threatened. Distor added that out of fear, complainant and her husband transferred their daughter in a safe place and reported the matter to the NBI. Subject was, by that time, asking money from the complainant. Thus, the entrapment operation was conducted in Brgy. San Juan, Cainta, Rizal and resulted in the arrest of the Subject. Certification issued by the NBI stated that Subject GENEROSO BITALAC LIM alias BOYET CRUZ is not a bonafide Agent of the NBI nor an employee of the Bureau. Subject was presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the Provincial Prosecutor-Rizal for Estafa and Usurpation of Authority.

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) has filed graft charges against a supervisor of Duty Free Philippines, a government owned and controlled corporation (GOCC). NBI Director Dante A. Gierran identified the Subject as MARK LESTER TEREM TOLEDO, supervisor of Duty Free Philippines – Iloilo. The case stemmed from the letter of Vicente Pelagio A. Angala, Chief Operating Officer of Duty Free Philippines Corporation (DFPC) requesting the NBI to conduct investigation regarding undeposited sales of DFPC-Iloilo which was allegedly committed by the Subject. Acting on the said request, certified true copy of certificate of employment, duties and responsibilities, service record, latest Personal Data Sheet (PDS), and all available Statement of Liabilities and Net Worth (SALN) of the Subject as well as the certified true copy of Incident Report, Audit Findings with Management Reply, Landbank cash deposit slip, Summary of Deposits certified by Landbank, Statement of Reconciliation, Cash Take-out Report and Summary of Consolidated Sales were requested and likewise received. Atty. Max B. Salvador, Regional Director of NBI-Western Visayas Regional Office (NBI-WEVRO) issued subpoena to Subject requesting to appear before the NBI-WEVRO office. However, it was the Subject’s mother, Mrs. Merlinda Toledo, who appeared on behalf of his son who was out of town that time. Mrs. Toledo revealed that they have already returned to DFPC a partial amount of the undeposited sales. Thereafter, they were given fifteen (15) days to submit counter affidavit. Upon expiration of the 15-day period, Mrs. Toledo said she had no knowledge of the whereabouts of her son and that they will not file a counter-affidavit. A copy of the Final Report on the Cash Deposit of DFPC-Iloilo for the period 2017 to February 2018 conducted by DFPC was received by the NBI. The report disclosed that the purported initials of Landbank pick-up tellers on deposit slips dated June 6, August 24, and December 14, 2017 and January 23, 2018 with a total amount of Php 979,362.00 were actually that of Landbank pick-up tellers. The report confirmed that the peso sales amounting to Php 979,362.00 was not deposited to Landbank. Subject indirectly admitted his wrongdoing by depositing Php 200,000.00 to the Landbank account of DFPC as partial payment to the undeposited sales he took. The elemental requirements of Malversation of Public Funds is sufficiently established. Subject is a public officer, having been appointed as COD Supervisor of the DFPC-Iloilo. He has custody or control of the peso sales of DFPC, which are public funds. His deliberate failure to report for work since February 21, 2018 to satisfactorily account for the undeposited sales created the legal presumption that he indeed misappropriated the said public funds. This legal presumption was further bolstered by Subject’s act of depositing to DFPC account a part of the undeposited sales without accounting for the remaining balance. Thus, the NBI recommends for prosecution of Subject MARK LESTER TEREM TOLEDO for Malversation of Public Funds as defined and penalized under Article 217 of the Revised Penal Code.

title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today said agents of Anti-Fraud Division (AFD) have arrested two individuals in an entrapment operation for swindling. In a Post-Operation Report, the AFD identified the arrested individuals, Elaine Crisostomo and her companion, Katrina Marie Tulabut, who have swindled Charles Miccolo Abrenica an undetermined amount of cash he has invested in several concerts and the sums of money paid to two companies to produce said concerts. On July 27, 2015, Abrenica filed a complaint with the NBI against Crisostomo. Investigation showed that Complainant first met Subject Crisostomo in the United States who related to him how lucrative it is to produce shows. Because of this, Complainant became interested in concert production. The AFD said Complainant decided to invest in several concerts and as an investor, thru Subject Crisostomo, was made to pay sums of money purportedly to pay Magic Media Productions, purportedly a company which promotes and represents concert artists, and to DJK Events, purportedly a marketing company. Complainant, however, subsequently learned that Magic Media Productions and DJK Events do not actually exists. On July 31, 2015, Complainant informed AFD that he agreed to meet with Subject Crisostomo on August 4, 2015 after the latter followed up on another payment for DJK in the amount of P46,000.00. The entrapment operation led to the arrest of Subject Crisostomo and her companion. The 2 were brought to the Office of the City Prosecutor of Pasay City for inquest proceedings.

title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: Agents of the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) rescued three (3) minors and arrested a couple for child internet porno in Cebu during the weekend. NBI Director Nonnatus Caesar R. Rojas identified the suspects as spouses; “AILEEN” and “WILLIE”, both in their mid-thirties, of Sitio Sun-Ok, Cordova, Cebu. Early this month, the NBI Anti-Human Trafficking Division (AHTRAD) headed by Atty. Dante B. Bonoan received information from the Immigration and Customs Enforcement in the US, that a couple was using their daughter, Annie (not her real name), 13; niece, Josie (not her real name), 15; and nephew, Dustin (not his real name), 17 in pimping other girls including minors residing in the sitio, to clients in the internet. Investigation disclosed that the children were instructed to post pictures of girl victims for viewing by clients. They were even told to commit lasciviousness, and worse to engage in actual sexual act. Upon receipt of the information, the NBI-AHTRAD coordinated with the NBI-Central Visayas Regional Office (CEVRO) in Cebu City. A series of surveillance was conducted which confirmed the report. On May 24, 2013, a search warrant was applied for and issued by the Cebu Regional Trial Court 7th Judicial Region, Branch 10, Cebu City. Two (2) days thereafter, on May 26, 2013, NBI agents proceeded to the residence of spouses ONTONG and served the warrant. With the validated information, the couple was arrested and the three (3) minors were rescued. On May 27, 2013, the suspects were brought before the Inquest Prosecutor of the Cebu Provincial Prosecutor’s Office for inquest proceedings. Charges for violation of RA 9208, violation of RA 7955, violation of RA 7610 and violation of Art. 201 of the Revised Penal Code were recommended. In compliance with the commitment order, suspects were duly turned over the Cebu Provincial Jail. No bail was recommended for their provisional release.

title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: In line with the provisions of R.A. 10173 or Data Privacy Act, the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) has designated officials as Compliance Officers for Privacy (COP) of their respective offices. In Memorandum Order No. 29, NBI Officer-In-Charge (OIC) Director Eric Distor designated incumbent NBI Regional Directors (RD), Agent-in-Charge (AIC) and Officers-in-Charge (OIC) as Compliance Officers for Privacy of their respective offices who shall perform the following duties and responsibilities. 1. Ensure proper data breach and security incident management in their respective offices including the preparation and submission to the NPC of reports and other documentation concerning security incidents or data breaches within the prescribed period. b. Inform and cultivate awareness on privacy and data protection within their respective office, including all relevant laws, rules and regulations and issuances of the NPC. c. Advocate for the development, review and/or revision of policies, guidelines, projects and/or programs of the NBI relating to privacy and data protection, by adopting a privacy by design approach. d. Serve as the contact person of the NBI Director vis-à-vis data subjects, the NPC and other authorities, in all matters concerning data privacy or security issues or concerns of their respective offices. e. Cooperate, coordinate, and seek advice of the NPC regarding matters concerning data privacy and security. f. Perform other duties and tasks that may be assigned by the NBI Director that will further the interest of data privacy and security and uphold the rights of the data subjects. In addition, COPs shall also assist the Data Protection Officer (DPO) in the performance of his functions. The Memorandum Order (MO) was issued by OIC Director Distor in compliance to National Privacy Commission’s (NPC) advisory for each government agency to designate a DPO. The MO likewise states that where a government agency has regional, provincial, district, city, municipal offices, or any other similar sub-units, it may designate or appoint a COP for each sub-unit. The designation of COPs is to ensure that the Data Privacy Act, which was signed to law on August 15, 2012, its Implementing Rules and Regulations, issuances by the National Privacy Commission, and other applicable laws and regulations relating to privacy and data protection, are complied with at all NBI Regional, District, and Satellite Offices. Currently, the NBI has 17 Regional Offices and 25 District Offices.
