title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today announced the arrest of a Japanese national in a 5-star hotel in Paranaque City by operatives of the NBI-Special Task Force (NBI-STF). NBI OIC-Director Eric B. Distor identified the arrested subject as WATANABE YUKI also known as KENJI SHIMADA/SHI SHIMADA. OIC-Director Distor said that based on the information received by the NBI-STF, subject WATANABE YUKI is an international wanted fugitive with BLUE NOTICE in Interpol. A Blue Notice is a category in the Interpol to collect additional information about a person’s identity, location or activities in relation to a crime. Distor added that subject YUKI was hiding in the country due to his involvement in various crimes in Japan and other countries. He is also allegedly operating syndicate activities in the Philippines, such as but not limited to, online fraud and extortions. Verification conducted by the NBI-STF to ascertain the veracity of the information revealed that subject YUKI is said to be the “Big Boss” of the largest telecommunication fraud syndicate, whose international operations cover several countries including Japan and Philippines. Information further disclosed that subject YUKI also known as KENJI SHIMADA/SHI SHIMADA can be found in a Hotel in Paranaque City. Acting on the said information, operatives of the NBI-Special Task Force coordinated with the Bureau of Immigration (BI). A letter request was sent with a prayer of a possible law enforcement operation against subject WATANABE YUKI. By virtue of a Mission Order duly signed and issued by the BI Commissioner, agents of the NBI-Special Task Force and BI operatives proceeded to the hotel where Subject YUKI was believed to be hiding. He was apprehended at said hotel at around 9:30 in the evening of April 19, 2021 together with 2 other Japanese nationals, TOMONOBU SAITO and KOUSUKE II. The latter Japanese, when asked about their passports and ACR, failed to present any document, thus, they were brought to the NBI for further verification and booking procedures. On April 20 2021, the NBI-STF was supposed to formally turn over the custody of subjects WATANABE YUKI, TOMONOBU SAITO and KOUSUKE II to the BI for their appropriate action. However, in compliance with BI’s procedure, all subjects must first be tested for COVID-19 virus. Subject Yuki was tested positive with while the two others tested negative, but since they were exposed to a COVID-positive, they will remain in isolation and quarantine for re swabbing. All Subjects were then turned-over to the NBI-Security Mangement Section (NBI-SMS) for temporary custody so that they can be properly isolated and quarantined. Subsequently, the NBI received a commitment order from BI, directing the Chief, STF to commit into custody subjects Watanabe Yuki, and Tomonobu Saito. Said Commitment Order cited that subject Yuki was charged for Undersirability (Fugitive) and Illegal Entrant, while Tomonobu Saito has an outstanding Summary Deportation Order. On the other hand, A Release Order was issued by the BI in favor of Kousuke II citing the lack of evidence to establish probable cause. Considering likewise that verification from BI’s record reveal that he is not an overstaying alien as his tourist visa is valid until May 2021. Prior to the issuance of a release order for Kousuke II, NBI was asked if there is an opposition for his release. After a record check made against Kousuke II, a non-derogatory was found. Hence, no opposition was made. Due to lack of evidence to establish probable cause and no criminal record was found in the NBI data base to legally hold Kousuke II, the BI-Legal Division recommended his immediate release. After being cleared ftom COVID-19 by San Lazaro Hospital, subjects Watanabe Yuki and Tomonobu Saito were turn-over to the Bureau of Immigation pursuant to a commitment order by the agency.

title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: A Korean national performing dentistry without license was arrested by the National Bureau of Investigation- National Capital Region (NBI- NCR) operatives during an entrapment operation conducted recently. NBI Director VIRGILIO L. MENDEZ identified the subject as Dr. PHILIP KIM a.k.a. KYE HOON KIM, of legal age and with office address at U- B 2/F Don Rafael Bldg., 504 Guerrero Street corner Makati Ave., Makati City. The case arose when NBI office received a complaint from Sarah Dela Cruz and Ella Mae Rodriguez on June 17, 2014 against the subject who performed dental surgery malpractice. Investigation disclosed that based on the existing records taken from the Professional Regulatory Commission, there were only two (2) Korean nationals licensed in the Philippines by which Philip King is not one of them. Having verified information, NBI- NCR operatives implemented an entrapment operation on July 25, 2014 at Pean- ahn e Dental Clinic located at 504 Guerrero Street corner Makati Ave., Makati City where subject performs his dental procedures and surgery. The complainant went to the clinic of the subject to perform dental surgery while NBI operatives strategically positioned themselves at the clinic and took pictures and videos during the course of dental procedure. After the dental surgery, dental assistant received the marked money, purposely prepared for the entrapment operation, as payment for the surgery. Apprised of his statutory and constitutional rights, the subject was arrested by NBI operatives and thereafter brought to the NBI- NCR Office in Taft Avenue, Manila where he was properly booked, photographed and fingerprinted. The subject was brought before the Makati Prosecutor’s Office for inquest proceedings and was charged for violation of RA No. 9484 Section 33 (a) for Dental Practice without License; (2) Estafa under Article 315 2(a), (3) Violation of Immigration Laws for Failure to present the necessary alien documents, (4) National Internal Revenue Code for issuance of unregistered receipts and (5) Labor Code of the Philippines for using expired Alien Employment Card.

title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: In its continuing support to the government’s relentless campaign against the proliferation of illegal drugs, the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today said operatives of NBI-Special Action Unit (NBI-SAU) have arrested a Japanese national in an anti-illegal drug operation on May 13, 2017 in a hotel in Manila. NBI Director Dante A. Gierran identified the Japanese national as TAKAHIRO YANO who was arrested on the basis of a search warrant issued against him. The intelligence report received by the NBI cited that the Subject is engaged in illegal drugs activities. Seized during the operation are ten (10) transparent heat-sealed plastic sachets containing white crystalline substance, one (1) transparent heat-sealed plastic sachet with white crystalline substance placed inside a steel case with maxman label, and other drug paraphernalia. Director Gierran stressed that the NBI continues to conduct its anti-illegal drugs operation against any group or individual with the restoration of its power to investigate cases involving illegal drugs. Charges for violation of R.A. 9165 otherwise known as The Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002 have been filed before the Office of the Prosecutor of Manila against the Subject who is currently detained at the NBI detention facility.

title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today announced the rescue of a female minor kidnap victim by the NBI-Iligan District Office (NBI-ILDO) in Marawi City. NBI Officer-In-Charge (OIC) Director Eric B. Distor said that on February 5, 2022, a complaint was filed by the cousin of the minor victim, regarding with the abduction of the latter. According to the complainant, the minor victim was forcibly abducted by her stepmother identified as ROHAIMA PAMUDAWAN y RAMBANGO together with about nine (9) unidentified men at their residence in Purok Mangga, Barangay Tubod, Iligan City. NBI-ILDO operatives conducted investigation and formed a tracking team to locate the possible whereabouts of the victim and the subjects. On February 6, 2022, NBI-ILDO operatives were able to track down the whereabouts of the victim and the subject. The operatives discovered that the complainant and the subjects are close relatives. The operatives employed the Maranao traditional ways of settling issues by asking the assistance of the local traditional leaders and community elders for the immediate safe release of the kidnap victim. body: PRESS STATEMENT November 06, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } The NBI-Organized and Transnational Crimes Division (NBI-OTCD) successfully arrested RAMIL BAUTISTA y BARAL, alias “EDDIE CRUZ, and AUDWIN FLORES Y ALMEDA, alias “BARRY,” who falsely represented themselves as personnel of NBI-Intelligence and allegedly extorted money from a private business entity. The operation was conducted in response to the directive of NBI Officer-in-Charge Atty. Angelito Magno – calling for an intensified internal cleansing program aimed at eradicating corruption and restoring public trust in the Bureau The operation stemmed from a formal complaint filed against “MAX ARANETA SANTOS” and “EDDIE CRUZ for alleged Robbery Extortion. Complainant received a call from a person identifying himself as “MAX ARANETA SANTOS from NBI Intelligence, who warned her that her company was included in a list of importers with misdeclarations and that their warehouse would be subjected to a law enforcement raid unless they “cooperated. She was later instructed to contact another supposed NBI Intelligence Operative, “EDDIE CRUZ.” On October 29, 2025, “EDDIE CRUZ demanded Php33,000 weekly or 66 shipment containers each worth Php500 from the Complainant, to be handed over at a coffee shop in Malate, Manila, to ensure the safety of her company’s warehouses from law enforcement raids and for non-interference in the company’s import activities. Thus, NBI-OTCD hatched an entrapment operation. On date of the operation, Complainant met with “EDDIE CRUZ” at the agreed location. The latter introduced another man, “BARRY,” who was to receive the money. As the transaction was made, NBI-OTCD agents swiftly moved in and arrested both subjects. The two were later identified as RAMIL BAUTISTA Y BARAL, and AUDWIN FLORES Y ALMEDA. Recovered from Subject Bautista were four (4) cellular phones and several identification cards under his name. Seized from Subject Flores were the transaction money amounting to Php33,0000, an NBI wallet badge, several NBI identification cards, and a mobile phone. Verification confirmed that the numbers contained in the recovered mobile phones matched those previously used to contact Complainant, as well as those that had been used to call other import brokers who have since coordinated with the NHI. Subsequent verification revealed that Subject Flores is a Job Order personnel, while Subject Bautista is a former Job Order employee whose contract had already expired. RAMIL BAUTISTA y BARAL and AUDWIN FLORES y ALMEDA were then presented for inquest Proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor, Manila, for Robbery with Violence against or Intimidation of Persons by way of Extortion, as defined and penalized under Article 294 of the Revised Penal Code (RPC) in relation to Section 6 of Republic Act No. 10175, otherwise known as the “Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012 and Usurpation of Authority under the RPC. Subject Bautista was also charged with Using a Fictitious Name and Concealing True Name under Article 178 of the RPC. Lastly, a charge against “MAX ARANETA SANTOS,” who remains at large, for Robbery with Violence against or Intimidation of Persons by Extortion under RPC Art. 294. The NBI remains steadfast in its mandate to protect the public and uphold the highest standards of professionalism, integrity, and accountability. The Bureau reiterates its call to the public to remain vigilant and immediately report through the Bureau’s official Facebook page or hotline numbers any individual claiming to be an NBI agent or personnel who engages in extortion or illegal/suspicious activities.

body: On October 1, 2019, operatives of NBI-Anti-Human Trafficking Division (NBI-AHTRAD) arrested MARK EUGINE ANDO a.k.a. MONIC ANDO and his two minor companions CARL JUSTINE MONGCAL and KRISTINE JOY PRILA CHAGAS for offering women for sexual intercourse. Subjects were arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from the report that a certain individual has been recruiting and offering minor girls with ages 13-17 years old to perform sexual acts in exchange for a fee of Php 5,000.00. On the aforementioned date, operatives proceeded to the target area and caught the Subjects in flagrante delicto offering women for sexual intercourse for a fee. Subjects were then placed under arrest. The operation also resulted in the rescue of 8 female victims, 5 of whom are minors. The minor victims were turned over to the custody of The two arrested minor Subjects, children in conflict with the law (CICL), were likewise turned over to the custody of Social Welfare Officer of the Manila Department of Social Welfare (MDSW). Subject MARK EUGINE ANDO was presented for inquest proceedings before the Department of Justice for violation of RA 10364 (Expanded Trafficking in Persons Act of 2012). On October 2, 2019, operatives of NBI-National Capital Region (NBI-NCR) seized counterfeit Oakley eye wears with an estimated value of Php 1.6 Billion. Items were seized in the city of Manila by virtue of Search Warrants. Charges for violation of RA 8293 (Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines) were filed against EAF GENERAL MERCHANDISE and/or ELIZABETH AMITASO FLORESCA and/or “ASIONG” and/or “MADAME LOU”, G.M. BELGA GENERAL MERCHANDISE and/or GRACE MUBALDO BELGA, RCL GENERAL MERCHANDISE and/or ROBERT CAMASO LOMOCSO, R.M. GATAN GENERAL MERCHANDISE, and/or RUBILYN MARANAN GATAN, J.A. PAJARITO GENERAL MERCHANDISE and/or JOEL ALTOVA PAJARITO, NBQ TRADING, and/or NANCY BALMES QUIMSON, EAF GENERAL MERCHANDISE and/or ELIZABETH AMITASO FLORESCA, and other JOHN/JANE DOEs. On October 7, 2019, operatives of NBI-Cybercrime Division (NBI-CCD) arrested AZHAR and TAMOOR for selling illegal drugs. Subjects were arrested in a buy-bust operation which stemmed from the report received regarding the sale of illegal drugs under the Php 430,000.00. Complainant convinced the captors that he will try to borrow money just to produce the ransom money. On the aforementioned date, NBI-STF operatives proceeded to the hotel at Gil Puyat, Pasay City and saw thereat Wang damp and tied on his both hands, together with another captive, Fan Lei. While the operatives were accosting the captors, they violently resisted arrest until NBI-STF operatives managed to tackle and subdued the Chinese nationals. The arrested Chinese nationals were brought to NBI for the booking procedures. On October 8, 2019, operatives of NBI-International Airport Investigation Division (NBI-IAID) arrested WAHIBA BAUTISTA for illegal recruitment. Subject was arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from the complaints against him. According to the complainants, Subject Bautista offered and convinced them to work as domestic helpers in Saudi Arabia with a salary of $400 each. She told complainants that she is connected with a recruitment agency and demanded an amount Php 25,000 to be delivered at Macapagal Blvd., Paranaque City. Subject Bautista was caught in flagrante delicto receiving the marked money from the complainants. Subject was then arrested and brought the NBI-IAID for the booking procedures. Verification with the POEA disclosed that Subject Bautista is not licensed or authorized to recruit workers for deployment overseas. Subject Bautista was presented for inquest at the Paranaque City Prosecutor’s Office. On October 8, 2019 operatives of NBI-Anti-Organized and Transnational Crime Division (NBI-AOTCD) arrested MARY GRACE VILLAROSA de TAN y CABRERA, Warehouse Plant Manager of ETK Plastic Trading, for violation of R.A. 1612 or the Anti-Fencing Law. aside from the arrested subject, two (2) other subjects who are at large were charged for the same offense, namely: DENNIS KING y SY, the registered owner of ETK Plastic Trading, and a certain Alias NEIL (FNU) while four (4) other subjects who are also at large were charged for Violation of Article 310 (Qualified Theft) of the Revised Penal Code, namely: EDWIN CABRERA, JOSEPH AMANSEC, EDWIN CAMARIN, and EDMAR ASIS. The operation stemmed from a complaint filed by a private corporation engaged in the manufacture of pulp, paper and paperboard. The complainant stated that their truck driver provided information regarding the stolen plastic resin with a total value of P5,915,460.00 belonging to the corporation. Based on the truck driver’s narration, on September 29, 2019, driver EDWIN CAMARIN and helper EDMAR ASIS were designated to pick up a metal container full of plastic resin owned by the complainant and to deliver them to the complainant corporation’s warehouse in Silang, Cavite. In connivance with the truck drivers, Subject ERWIN CABERA tasked Subject JOSEPH AMANSEC to pick up one of the metal containers and sold its content, 990 sacks of plastic resin, to the owner/occupant of a warehouse located along service road, Barangay Paseo De Blas, Valenzuela City. Subject ERWIN CABRERA, thereafter, divided the proceeds of the sale among those drivers/helpers who confederated in the commission of the crime. Based on these data, AOTCD operatives conducted surveillance operation to validate the information. After securing a Search Warrant, AOTCD operatives conducted the operation against the said premises, found and seized 419 sacks of Lotte Chemical Titan, PP, as particularly described in the Warrant. It was later learned that the warehouse is owned by ETK Plastic Trading with Subject DENNIS SY KING as the registered owner. Subject MARY GRACE VILLAROSA de TAN who was in the premises at the time of operation and who refused to sign and acknowledge the Search Warrant was placed under arrest and was presented before the Office of the City Prosecutor of Valenzuela. The 5 other subjects who are at large were also charged. On October 9, 2019, operatives of NBI-Technical Intelligence Division (NBI-TID) arrested EDWIN SAN JUAN y LUCERO for alleged violation of Anti-Fencing Law. Subject was arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from the complaint of Ernesto I. Yao Jr. for Robbery against certain Ram Leuterio San Juan who was selling road bike on Facebook in which, the said road bike had been missing since September 11, 2018. According to the complainant, his road bike which costs Php 680,000 was stolen at his residence by an unknown perpetrator. After validation that the stolen property was indeed for sale in the public online through a Facebook page. An entrapment operation was then conducted resulting in the arrest of Subject EDWIN SAN JUAN, father of Ram Leuterio San Juan, for violation of Anti-Fencing Law of 1979. Subject was presented for inquest proceedings before the Prosecutor Office, Taguig City. On October 10, 2019, operatives of NBI-International Airport Investigation Division (NBI-IAID) arrested DANILO CLEOFAS CASTILLO II for Human Trafficking. On the same day, passengers Mary Grace Meneses Alcantara, Krystelle May Limos Viaje and Subject Danilo were turned over to NBI-IAID by the NAIA Task Force Against Trafficking in Persons. They were about to depart for Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia but they were deferred from their flight for failing substantiate the purpose of their travel. Passengers Alcantara and Viaje pointed to Subject Castillo as the one who would accompany them in going to Kuala Lumpur. They said that a certain “Honey” endorsed them to Subject Castillo to escort them going to the said country. Alcantara paid “Honey” Php 10,000.00 while Viaje paid a total of Php 73,000.00. On October 9, 2019, Alcantara and Viaje met Subject Danilo and the latter briefed them on what to do and to say when interviewed by an immigration officer at the airport so they could easily pass. The next day, the three of them were held at the airport and Subject Danilo was then placed under arrest for violations of RA 9208 as amended by RA 10364 (Expanded Trafficking in Persons Act) and RA 8042 (Migrant Workers and Overseas Filipinos Act) as amended by RA 10022. He was presented for inquest before the Pasay City Prosecutor’s Office. On October 11, 2019, operatives of NBI-Counter-Terrorism Division (NBI-CTD) arrested ABDEL-AMIN BANDAHALA y ANDAL for eight (8) counts of Kidnapping and Serious Illegal Detention. Subject was arrested by virtue of Warrant of Arrest issued bt RTC of Basilan in relation to the Golden Harvest Kidnapping case which was carried out by the Abu Sayyaf Group on June 11, 2001 in Lantawan, Basilan. An information that Subject ABDEL-AMIN BANDAHALA a.k.a. Abu Black was working as a security guard in a commercial building in Kawit, Cavite. The said information was verified and Subject was spotted at Robertson Plaza working as a security guard. A composite team from NBI-CTD, NBI-TID, Philippine Navy-Naval Intelligence and Security Group, and PNP-Southern Police District planned and successfully executed the arrest of Subject Abu Black. He was brought to NBI headquarters and was turned over to the SMS. He is currently detained at the NBI Detention Facility. On October 11, 2019, operatives of NBI-Dagupan District Office (NBI-DADO) arrested HEROLD SUING y MUSNI, CLARISSA LOPEZ y ENRIQUEZ and MARY JOY GUINTO for Human Trafficking. Subjects were arrested in an entrapment operation conducted at Sweet and Kisses Videoke Bar located at Brgy. Aserda, Mapandan, Pangasinan. The operation also resulted in the rescue of eleven (11) trafficked victims. Subjects were charged before the Provincial Prosecutor’s Office, Dagupan City for violation of RA 9208 (Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act). On October 11, 2019, operatives of NBI-Environmental Crime Division (NBI-EnCD) arrested QING LIN y NAN, JONATHAN GUZMAN y DJOHAN, and ROBERTO INTES y HERMARANGAN for illegal selling of agarwood, endangered species. Subjects were arrested in an operation which stemmed from an information regarding certain individual selling agarwood. Subjects traded and were in possession of 15 kilos of agarwood worth Php 2,500,000.00. Subjects were presented before the City Prosecutor’s Office, Quezon City for violation of RA 9147 (Wildlife Resources Conservation Act) and PD 705 (Revised Forestry Code of the Philippines). On October 11, 2019, joint operatives of NBI-MIMAROPA and NBI-National Capital Region (NBI-NCR) arrested PO2 JHUNE RESTIE ELIAS y OLARTE, an active member of the PNP assigned at Malabon City Police Station, for illegally selling high-powered firearms and ammunitions. Subject was arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from a report that a certain police officer is allegedly engaged in illegal gunrunning activities within the CAMANAVA area. On the aforementioned date, the entrapment operation was conducted in Quezon City resulting in the arrest of the Subject who was caught in flagrante selling high-powered firearms. Subject was presented before the City Prosecutor of Quezon City for inquest proceedings for violation of RA 10591 (Comprehensive Firearms Law). On October 14, 2019, operatives of NBI-Rizal District Office (NBI-RIZDO) seized counterfeit Sanrio products with an estimated value of Php 50,000.00. Items were seized in Binondo, Manila by virtue of Search Warrants. Charges for violation of RA 8293 (Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines) were filed against GENTRO INTERNATIONAL PRODUCTS, INC. On October 14, 2019, operatives of NBI-Rizal District Office (NBI-RIZDO) seized counterfeit Sanrio products with an estimated market value of Php 50,000.00. Items were seized in the city of Manila by virtue of Search Warrants. Charges for violation of RA 8293 (Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines) were filed against GENTRO INTERNATIONAL PRODUCTS, INC. On October 15, 2019, operatives of NBI-Environmental Crime Division (NBI-EnCD) arrested CESAR ESPIRITU, RENATO ATAPEDARA y FAJARDO, PAOLO GALANG y PALLANAN, GLEN SANTIAGO y PILLARANA, LEOPOLDO DE GUZMAN y SERRANO, and NONILON GARCIA y YAMBOT for illegal mining. The case stemmed from a complaint and request for assistance by Mine Management Division of the Department of Environment and Natural Resources-Mines and Geosciences Bureau (DENR-MGB) – Region III. According to the complaint, a certain Mr. Cesar Espiritu is engaged in the illegal extraction of earth materials along the portion of a river embankment of Pampanga River and portion of his alleged private lot in Brgy. Sto. Tomas South, Jaen, Nueva Ecija, without necessary permit from Provincial Mining and Regulatory Board of Nueva Ecija and DENR-MGB Region III and despite a Cease and Desist Order (CDO) from DENR-MGB Region III. Investigation and surveillance validated the illegal activities. Thus, on the above-mentioned date, operatives proceeded to the area and arrested the above-mentioned Subjects who were caught operating the back hoe and loading the dump trucks with earth materials. Subjects were charged before the inquest prosecutor of Department of Justice, Manila for violation of RA 7942 (Philippine Mining Act of 1995). On October 15, 2019, operatives of NBI-National Capital Region (NBI-NCR) seized counterfeit Vans products with an estimated value of Php 48 Million. Items were seized in Pasay City and Paranaque City by virtue of Search Warrants. Charges for violation of RA 8293 (Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines) were filed against John/Jane Does. On October 16, 2019, operatives of NBI-Central Luzon Regional Office (NBI-CELRO) arrested HONG XINSEN, Chinese national, for Falsification by Private Individuals, Use of Falsified Documents, and Use of Fictitious Name and Concealing True Name. Subject assumed and used a name ANG, JIMMY ANG, making false statement or information under oath in his passport application, passport, certificate of live birth, driver’s license, and NBI clearance. HONG XINSEN was formally turned over by the Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA), Consular Office-Angeles City to the NBI for further investigation and appropriate action. On October 16, 2019, operatives of NBI-International Operations Division (NBI-IOD) arrested AGATHA REYES y CUARTO a.k.a. AGATHA, JOHANNA SY JAO for Identity Theft. Subject was arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from the complaint filed by actress Angelica Panganiban regarding her hacked credit card. Subject Reyes was able to successfully use a simulated credit card using the name of Ms. Panganiban and her details in paying the bills she incurred in a coffee shop and gasoline station in Angeles City. Subject Reyes also tried to withdraw money amounting to Php 175,200.00 by using the simulated card in three different transactions but it was declined due to suspected fraud. NBI-IOD was able to create a cartographic thru the help of an employee of the hotel in Pampanga. The cartographic showed similarity with the face and appearance of Subject Reyes. Verification conducted by the operatives disclosed that Subject Reyes has a pending Warrant of Arrest issued by RTC Manila Branch 40 for violation of RA 8484 (Access Devices Regulation Act). A Certified True Copy of Warrant of Arrest was secured and on the above-mentioned date, NBI-IOD operatives served the Warrant of Arrest and arrested the Subject in her address at Sampaloc, Manila. Subject Reyes was temporarily detained at the NBI Detention Center awaiting for the Court’s order. On October 17, 2019, operatives of NBI-Anti-Fraud Division (NBI-AFD) arrested MHEANNE VALDEZ DIZON and ELLAMAE BAUTISTA QUIRONA for investment scam. Subject was arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from the report regarding an alleged investment scam being perpetrated by Right Circle Trading Inc. (RCTI). Operatives had established facts that RCTI was duping the public into believing that it is a legitimate Forex Trading entity to encourage investors to their company. One of their misinterpretation and fraudulent information being used to entice the investors is that RCTI had created an Artificial Intelligence which was programmed to capacitate their Forex Trading. Verification from Securities and Exchange Commission showed that RCTI does not have nor has it applied for a secondary license to operate as a lending company, broker, or dealer of securities. With this, the entrapment operation was conducted resulting in the arrest of the Subjects. Subjects were brought to Quezon City Prosecutor’s Office for inquest proceedings for violation of RA 7899 (Securities Regulation Code). NBI will also file additional charges against the Directors/Officers/Employees/Agents/Brokers of RCTI upon receipt of results of the subpoena duces tecum issued to SEC. body: A notorious illegal recruiter, Tita Cacayan, who had victimized several overseas Filipino workers (OFW) one of who was a drug courier executed in China, was re-arrested by the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) in Isabela last Saturday. The case of Cacayan caught much attention in the wake of the NBI’s relentless drive against drug mules particularly the West African Drug Syndicate (WADS). The execution of Sally Ordinario Villanueva by Chinese authorities underscores the illegal drug trade which has escalated globally. Cacayan was principally responsible for the travel of Ordinario to China. The NBI investigated accused TITA CACAYAN last year for the recruitment and deployment of Sally Ordinario Villanueva. Cacayan allegedly provided the travelling bag containing illegal drugs to Ordinario-Villanueva who was intercepted and arrested upon arrival in China. She was executed in March 2011 for drug trafficking. Earlier, last year the Justice Department (DOJ) resolved the complaints filed by the Bureau against Cacayan and filed cases of violations of Section 5 of RA 9165 and Section 6 of RA 8042 (Illegal Recruitment in Large Scale) before the RTC of Manila and Isabela respectively. The RTC Manila dismissed provisionally the charges against Cacayan because of the non-appearance of the complaining witnesses. Cacayan was released as the warrant for her arrest in regards to violation of RA 8042 has not been issued at the time. On September 8, 2012, NBI operatives served the warrant of arrest against TITA CACAYAN y NERA issued by the RTC, Branch 20 of Cauayan City, Isabela. Cacayan was brought to the NBI main office in Manila where she is presently detained.

body: PRESS STATEMENT July 18, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } In line with the directive from the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Director JUDGE JAIME B. SANTIAGO (Ret.), to intensify the operations against child online exploitation, the NBI-Human Trafficking Division (NBI-HTRAD) arrested alias “LELE” in Marikina City for violation of Republic Act No. 11930 (CSAEM and OSAEC Law). The operation stemmed from a referral by the Police Antwerpen Defensor Liberatis (Belgian Police). According to their report, the Belgian Police executed a search warrant at the residence of a Belgian national, which led to the seizure of his device. Upon reviewing the device, the Belgian Police discovered communications, between the Belgian national with a Skype user named “LELE.” A forensic examination of the device was subsequently conducted by the Belgian Police, which revealed that the Subject “Lele” was receiving money from the arrested Belgian National to facilitate live online child sexual abuse of her 10-year-old niece. This information was forwarded to the NBI-HTRAD for their further investigation. Through multiple surveillance operations, agents from the NBI-HTRAD successfully located the whereabouts of the Subject and the minor victims. Fortwith, the investigating team secured a Warrant to Search, Seize, and Examine Computer Data (WSSECD) against the Subject from the Regional Trial Court, Branch 7, Marikina City. On July 7, 2025, NBI-HTRAD agents proceeded to the Subject’s location and implemented the WSSECD. During an on-site forensic examination of Subject’s seized mobile phone, agents found Child Sexual Abuse Materials, prompting her immediate arrest. Subject was presented for inquest proceedings for the above-stated violation. Director Santiago commended the NBI-HTRAD agents for arresting Subject Lele and reaffirmed the NBI’s commitment to protecting children from such crimes.

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) announced today the arrest of four (4) Chinese nationals in Parañaque City for operating a makeshift hospital, exclusively for Chinese workers. NBI Officer-In-Charge Eric B. Distor identified the Chinese nationals as LIANG JUNSHUAI, PINGQIANG LONG, YANYUN JIANG, and TANG HONG SHAN . OIC Distor said that information received by the NBI- Task Force Against Illegal Drugs (NBI-TFAID) is that certain Chinese nationals led by Subject Liang are engaged in illegal activities. Investigation revealed that Subject Liang’s group has created makeshift hospital for Chinese workers inside an exclusive village in Parañaque City, without License to Operate or Certificate of Accreditation duly issued by the Bureau of Medical Services of the Department of Health (DOH). Further investigation showed that the group is also engaged in the illegal practice of medicine by physically examining, treating, operating, or prescribing any remedy for any human disease, injury, deformity, or any ailment for a fee, without authorization from the Board of Medical Examiners. The group also prescribes and sells Chinese drugs not approved and registered with the Food and Drug Administration (FDA). With enough evidence, NBI-TFAID conducted an entrapment operation. On May 29, 2020, NBI-TFAID proceeded to the area after which an undercover poseur-customer went inside the premises and noticed, in plain view, a makeshift hospital with a large volume of assorted medicines in Chinese characters and several types of hospital equipment and paraphernalia. The garage of the premises is used for diagnosis, treatment, and care of individuals suffering from illness, disease, injury or in need of other medical and nursing care. Upon handing of the marked-money to subject Liang, the undercover poseur-customer declared their authority resulting in the arrest of Subjects Liang, Pingqiang, Jiang, and Tang. Subjects failed to present a License to Operate as a private hospital duly issued by the Bureau of Medical Services (DOH) nor any Authorization from the Board of Medical Examiners to practice medicine in the Philippines. Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings on June 01, 2020, before the Office of the City Prosecutor of Parañaque City for violations of R.A. 2382 (The Medical Act of 1959), R.A. 9711 (Food and Drug Administration Act of 2009), R.A. 7394 (The Consumer Act of the Philippines), and R.A. 4226 (Hospital Licensure Act).

body: PRESS STATEMENT April 02, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } In line with the directive from National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Director Judge Jaime B. Santiago (Ret.), to intensify the campaign against all forms of criminality, the NBI- National Capital Region (NBI-NCR) has arrested twelve (12) Chinese nationals in Muntinlupa City for violation of Republic Act No. 10591 (Comprehensive Firearms and Ammunition Regulation Act). The operation stemmed from three (3) Search Warrants issued by the Regional Trial Court of Muntinlupa City against residential houses and vehicles in Ayala Alabang Village, Muntinlupa City, for violation of R.A. No. 10591. On March 31, 2025, agents from the NBI-NCR, assisted by barangay officials, representatives from the Homeowners Association, security officers of Ayala Alabang Village, and after coordination from the local PNP, implemented the search warrants at the specified premises. On the first location, the agents seized five pistols, along with magazines and ammunition. On the second subject area, the agents recovered four pistols with magazines and ammunition, two Taser guns, three bulletproof vests, tactical knives, a kitchen knife, handcuffs, and identification cards belonging to individuals named Yi Wan, Wang Zenghui, Yichun Liu, Zhou Chenchen, Zhang Yu, Xiu Zhang, and Zhang Qi Ja. On the third target place to be searched, the agents seized one pistol with a magazine and ammunition, tactical gear for pistols, and identification cards under the name Wang Zenghui and Wang Weibin. The operation also led to the arrest of twelve Chinese nationals. Two vehicles, subject of the search warrants, were also seized. The arrested Subjects and other occupants were presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor of Muntinlupa. Director Santiago commended the NBI-NCR agents for the arrest of the foreign nationals and seizure of numerous firearms. He warned those involved in illegal activities that the NBI will be steadfast in enforcing the law.

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today said operatives of NBI-Environmental Crime Division (NBI-ENCD) arrested REY “RHEY’ ASIODCHE y MONTEROSO for selling and possession of wildlife species without the necessary permit. The NBI said that on January 18, 2017, an information from a confidential informant revealed that a certain RHEY is in possession of various wildlife species. Subject was using pseudo account ‘RHEY ASIODCHE’ and was utilizing his account in trading said wildlife species. Furthermore, RHEY does not have any necessary permit to possess and trade the species, which is a clear violation of R.A. 9147 otherwise known as the Wildlife Resources Conservation and Protection Act of 2001. In one of his posts on his account, he is in possession of various wildlife species such as scorpions, tarantulas and reptiles which he delivers to buyers via meet ups or shipping it nationwide. Confidential informant also said that RHEY gets his stocks from a certain MICHAEL EVANGELO a.k.a Mike24 or “Southside Exotics”. NBI-ENCD operatives conducted a test buy on January 19, 2017. Poseur buyer was able to buy two (2) pieces live Heterometrus longimanus (Asian Forest Scorpion), an endemic specie that could be found in Palawan. Another purchase was set on February 9, 2017 where poseur buyer and RHEY agreed to meet in Recto, Manila. RHEY brought various wildlife species in exchange for Php 15,000.00. The buy-bust operation resulted in the arrest of the Subject. ENCD operatives asked Subject RHEY to present the necessary permits for possessing and trading of the said wildlife species but Subject failed to present any permit for that purpose. Recovered from the Subject were different types of tarantula, scorpion, and baboons. Seized wildlife species were brought to the DENR-BMB for custody and safekeeping. Certification issued by the DENR-Biodiversity Management Bureau showed that Subject RHEY had not been issued a permit to collect, possess, transport or trade wildlife. Another certification showed that recovered wildlife species are categorized as threatened. Criminal case for Illegal Trading in Violation of Sec.27 paragraph (e) of R.A. 9147, in relation to Sec.6 of R.A. 10175, and Illegal Possession of Wildlife in violation of Sec.27 paragraph (f) of R.A. 9147 was filed against Subject RHEY.

title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: The Information Division is pleased to submit herewith the significant cases of the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) for the following afore-mentioned period as follows: • On May 5, 2017, ROMEO BELDA y DE MESA, was killed after he opened fire at the operatives of NBI-Laguna District Office (NBI-LAGDO) when the latter tried to implement a search warrant against ROMEO BELDA , in San Pablo City, Laguna. ROMEO BELDA was reportedly in possession of several unlicensed firearms and often engaged in indiscriminate firing in their barangay. Record check also revealed that he was previously charged for Assault Upon a Person in Authority in san Pablo City, Laguna and Robbery in Band with Less Serious Physical Injuries in his hometown in Pili, Camarines Sur. After validation of the information, a Search Warrant was secured against him for violations of the Comprehensive Firearms and Ammunitions Act. Accordingly, a team composed of NBI-LAGDO and elements of 300th AISG of the Philippine Airforce, proceeded to his house to enforce the warrant. Subject BELDA, however, sneaked out of his house thru the back door and started to shoot at the approaching operatives prompting the latter to return fire. Subject BELDA was hit on the head while Technical Sergeant Reyes of AISG sustained a gunshot wound. Both were immediately rushed to the hospital but Subject BELDA was pronounced dead on arrival. Recovered from the premises of the Subject were .45 Caliber Llama pistol, 1 Carbine M2 with 2 magazines loaded with live ammunitions, assorted live ammunitions of different caliber, and five (5) empty shells/cartridges of .45 Caliber bullets. • On May 10, 2017, operatives of NBI-Task Force Against Illegal Drugs (NBI-TFAID) arrested DORIAN ALAN PEÑA, Filipino-American professional basketball player; JOSE PAOLO AMPESO, a.k.a. “JP”, son of Jose Arthur Ampeso, former Chief Consul General for Vancouver, Canada; and LEDY MEA MESIA VILCHEZ a.k.a. “Mae”, escort girl and live in partner of Ampeso. In pursuit of fugitive JUN NO, a Korean-American national, who is wanted for drug trafficking, involving the trafficking of a party drug ecstacy, the NBI-TFAID stumbled upon an information that Subject “Mae” was the last known companion of Jun No after the latter escaped from the hospital. Intelligence network brought in the information that “Mae” is an escort girl who delivers drugs for Korean clients. With the help of the informant, a drug deal between “Mae” and an undercover operative was set up at Merryland Village in Mandaluyong City. The operation resulted in the arrest of the aforementioned Subjects who were having pot session. Subjects tested positive for drug use. Several pieces of drug paraphernalia and weighing scale were seized during the operation. The three (3) Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings for violations of Sections 5, 6, 11, 12, 15 and 26 of R.A. 9165 (Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002) with respect to Subjects JOSE PAOLO AMPESO and LEDY MEA MESIA VILCHEZ, and violations of Sections 7 and 15 of R.A. 9165 for Subject DORIAN PEÑA. • On May 11, 2017, operatives of NBI-Laguna District Office (NBI-LAGDO) arrested EFREN PRANADA y ASTOVESA for Rape. After proper coordination with the authorities, joint operatives of the NBI-LAGDO, elements from MIG4, Philippine Army, Naval Intelligence and Security Group (NISG) and the 1st Infantry Battalion Philippine Army, proceeded to Brgy. Binibitinan, Polilio Island via Infanta, Quezon on board several boats to serve the Warrant of Arrest issued by RTC Branch 80, Morong, Rizal against the Subject for Rape. Operatives proceeded to the location where he was tending a small farm and the said Warrant of Arrest was served. Subject, who did not resist arrest, was brought to NBI-LAGDO for the standard booking procedures. • On May 12, 2017, operatives of NBI-Anti Organized and Transnational Crime Division (NBI-AOTCD) arrested REYNALDO NAZARETH y ZULUETA, CLORDELIZA CAGUIOA CORTEZ-ROTOR, ARLENE TIN TEE, ROSE MARZAN FERNANDEZ, and ANTHONY RAZAL MORAN for illegal gambling in two (2) simultaneous entrapment operations in Sta. Cruz and Quiapo, Manila. The case stemmed from a request from the Chairman of the Games and Amusement Board (GAB), Abraham Kahlil B. Mitra, seeking assistance and action of NBI on suspected illegal bookie operations on the aforementioned areas. Subjects were arrested for violation PD 1602 (Prescribing Stiffer Penalties for Illegal Gambling) as amended by R.A. 9287 (an Act Increasing Penalties for Illegal Numbers Games), with penalties ranging from a minimum of six (6) years up to twelve (12) years imprisonment. All Subjects have been charged before the Office of the Prosecutor of Manila. • On May 13, 2017, operatives of NBI-Special Action Unit (NBI-SAU) arrested TAKAHIRO YANO, a Japanese national, in an anti-illegal drugs operation in a hotel in Manila on the basis of a Search Warrant issued against him. Intelligence report received by the NBI cited that Subject is engaged in illegal drugs activities. Seized during the operation are ten (10) transparent heat-sealed plastic sachets containing white crystalline substance, one (1) transparent heat-sealed plastic sachet with white crystalline substance placed inside a steel case with maxman label, and other drug paraphernalia. Charges for violation of R.A. 9165 (Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002) have been filed against the Subject before the Office of the Prosecutor of Manila. • On May 16, 2017, operatives of NBI-Intellectual Property Rights Division (NBI-IPRD) seized 153 boxes of Snowbear candies with an approximate amount of Php 500,000.00 in Davao City. Items were seized on the strength of a Search Warrant issued by Judge Rainelda H. Estacio-Montesa, Branch 46, Manila against John/Jane Doe, owners and operators of Lucky Box Commercial Center located at F. Bangoy St., Brgy. 27-C, Poblacion, Davao City and a facility located at No. 70 Cervantes St., corner Villamor St., Davao City. The case stemmed from a complaint of Mr. Mitchell Vy Chua of Snowbear. Seized items are under the temporary custody of NBI-IPRD, to be produced upon order of the Court. Charges for violation of R.A. 8393 (Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines) were filed against the Subjects. • On May 16, 2017, operatives of NBI-Cybercrime Division (NBI-CCD) arrested five (5) Korean nationals, namely CHEONJI KIM, ILHWAN YANG, WONSUP YANG, JEONG HYEOK KIM, and MOON KYU KANG for illegal online gambling in Pasig City. Subjects were arrested as a consequence of the implementation of Search Warrant issued by Judge Maria Victoria A. Soriano-Villadolid of Branch 24, RTC Manila. The aforementioned Subjects operate or manage the administrator web page for the online sports betting, sports toto, and online casino. They also used this kind of modus to facilitate money laundering activities. They likewise chose exclusive subdivisions as their operation venue to hide from the law enforcement arm. Charges for violation of P.D. 1602 (Prescribing Stiffer Penalties on Illegal Gambling) in relation to R.A. 10165 (Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012) were filed against the Subjects. • On May 18, 2017, operatives of NBI-Anti-Organized and Transnational Crime Division (NBI-AOTCD) arrested twelve (12) individuals namely: GEORGE REYES VELASCO, ROLAN ALLAN DE LEON RAMOS, JIM PHILLIP CESAR CONCHA, EDITHA SILVESTRE CHAN, ANTONIO ADRIANO BALORAN, BENITO HAO DY, BONIFACIO OROLFO ARBOLEDA JR, ROLANDO TUANO ORTEGA, SANNY BELLO BOBARES, ERIC CUNANAN DELA CRUZ, CHRISTIAN DE GUZMAN LANDICHO, and CHUA CHI BEN for illegal gambling in Sta. Cruz, Manila. The NBI received a letter from Abraham Kahlil B. Mitra, Chairman of Games and Amusement Board (GAB), requesting action on suspected illegal bookie operations. Acting on the said request, AOTCD operatives conducted surveillance operations to validate the information, after which, an entrapment operation was conducted resulting in the arrest of the Subjects. YJARES, married and a resident of B-18 L-12 Asamba Compound, Baesa, Quezon City. The case stemmed from a letter request of Gov. Paul R.. Daza, governor of Northern Samar requesting investigative assistance. He met Narit in 2012 who introduced himself as Donmar Jones, an alleged producer of GMA 7. PRESS STATEMENT February 26, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } On February 19, 2025, under the leadership of National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Director JUDGE JAIME B. SANTIAGO, the NBI- Lucena District Office (NBI-LUCDO) arrested an individual in Lucena City for violation of R.A. No. 8353 (Anti-Rape Law) and R.A. No. 7610 (Special Protection of Children Against Abuse, Exploitation, and Discrimination Act) The operation stemmed from the complaint filed by the mother of the 13-year-old victim against the Subject. According to the complaint, the Subject raped the victim on three (3) different occasions in December 2024, January 2025 and February 17, 2025. Apart from the rape, the minor victim was also forced by the Subject to take illegal drugs. On February 19, 2025, agents from the NBI-LUCDO launched a search and hot pursuit operation to apprehend Subject. This operation continued until February 20, 2025, when the Philippine National Police (PNP) informed NBI-LUCDO that the Subject had voluntarily surrendered at their office. The Subject was aware that he was being pursued by NBI agents, thus, his voluntary surrender. Following his surrender, PNP personnel promptly transferred him to the agents of NBI-LUCDO. The Subject was presented for inquest proceedings at the City Prosecutor’s Office for the aforementioned violations. Director Santiago commended the agents of NBI-LUCDO for the subject’s arrest and expressed his appreciation to the PNP for their assistance.

title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today announced the arrest of eight (8) individuals in Capas, Tarlac for excavating lahar sand and loading in a dump truck for disposition without necessary permits from the authorities. NBI Officer-In-Charge Eric B. Distor identified the subjects as ERWIN FELICIANO y GUECO, RENOEL PAULINO y LABORDO, EUGENE MADOLID y CALLOS, ROLLY VERDEFLOR y LAPIG, ALEX GATO y FIL, RODEL DE JESUS y RAMIRO, RICO DURON y OBINA, and GILBERT CUBELO y YAGAO. Intelligence information received by NBI- Environmental Crime Division (NBI-EnCD) that illegal quarrying activities are being conducted in Brgy. Sta. Lucia, Capas, Tarlac. Verification and surveillance operations conducted by NBI-EnCD revealed the presence of a group of heavy equipment extracting minerals (lahar materials) from the river and directly loading the same in the queuing trucks. The surveillance team observed that there are no indicated location map, flagship, boundaries, area clearance, Environmental Compliance Certificate, and mining permit showing the metes and bounds of the quarry site displayed therein. The surveillance team also discovered that the quarry operation is being held and conducted by “A SAND QUARRY” that sells the mineral from Bangut River for Php 5,000.00 to Php 6,000.00 per dump truck. Verification revealed that no quarry permits were issued for the whole province of Tarlac by the Provincial Mining Regulatory Board – Tarlac. Also, a list of mining and quarry permittees from the Regional Director of Mines and Geosciences Bureau, Region 3 (DENR MGB III) showed that “A SAND QUARRY” had no existing mining and quarry permit. Based on the evidences gathered, it appears that the conduct of quarry operation of “A SAND QUARRY” in Brgy. Sta. Lucia, Capas, Tarlac is not authorized nor listed as one of the permittee by the DENR. Thus, on June 24, 2020, joint operatives of NBI-EnCD and DENR MGB III proceeded to the quarry location in Brgy. Sta. Lucia, Capas, Tarlac where illegal quarrying operation is being conducted by “A SAND QUARRY”. Upon arriving in the target area the joint operatives saw three (3) dump trucks which were halted by the raiding team loaded with lahar sand coming from Bangut River, operated by Subjects Madolid, Verdeflor, and Gato. Other members of the raiding team proceeded to the quarry site where Subject Paulino was caught loading lahar sand to the dump trucks of Subjects De Jesus and Cubelo. Subject Duron was later caught with his dump truck full of lahar sand on his way to the cashier’s office for payment. The operatives also went to the cashier/checker’s place wherein Subject Feliciano was seen preparing receipts of payment for dump truck loaded with lahar sand. Subjects failed to present documents and permits necessary to conduct quarry operations, prompting the operatives to place them under arrest. Seized from the subjects were six (6) dump trucks and two (2) pay loader and one (1) backhoe with an estimated value of Php 10,860,000.00. On June 25, 2020, the eight (8) subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the Provincial Prosecutor-Tarlac City for violation of Section 103 (Theft of Minerals) of R.A. 7942, otherwise known as the “Philippine Mining Act of 1995”

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today said operatives of NBI-Anti-Fraud Division (NBI-AFD) have arrested an individual yesterday afternoon in Manila for investment scam. Director Dante A. Gierran identified the Subject as TOMAS NECASIO NAZARENO who was arrested in an entrapment operation where he was to receive an amount of Php 500,000.00 from a complainant. The case stemmed from a complaint against the Subject who allegedly has an account wherein 30 Billion US Dollars were being deposited. According to the complainant, he was informed by a certain Pastor Gavino M. Ronquillo about the assets pertaining to the bank accounts which has deposits amounting to 30 Billion US Dollars which were maintained at HSBC Thailand, and that the original signatory to the aforesaid accounts passed away and the deposits were transferred to Subject TOMAS NECASIO NAZARENO. Subject, however, has no financial capability as of that time to proceed to Thailand and process the necessary documentation for the deposit to be withdrawn. Pastor Gavino then asked the complainant if he would be interested to be financier or investor wherein he needed to provide Php 2 Million to be utilized allegedly for travel expenses and logistical needs and in turn, he would be given profit or proceeds equivalent to 1% of the deposit or about 300 Million US Dollars monthly based on the guaranteed profits on the investment trading activities. After being presented with several documents, complainant was convinced and enticed that Subject’s offer of investment is valid and legitimate. He then communicate with the Subject thru his cellphone number, Viber, email,a nd Facebook Messenger. Complainant, together with his group, then decided to contribute funds, hence, he transmitted an initial amount of USD 7,0000 to the Subject via Western Union. Thereafter, Subject continued to ask money from the complainant allegedly for processing of other documents. The complainant, convinced by the Subject’s scheme, then remitted money in several tranches. However, even after the remittances, the complainant did not receive the Memorandum from Subject’s depository bank and the Standby Letter of Credit that the Subject promised. Complainant then told the Subject that another financier is willing to give the amount he was requesting and reported the matter before the NBI. Subject agreed to meet with the complainant to deliver the money amounting to Php 500,000.00 An entrapment operation was then set and resulted in the arrest of the Subject. Subject will be brought before the Office of the City Prosecutor of Manila for Inquest Proceedings for charges of Estafa as defined and penalized under the Revised Penal Code.

title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: In line with the relentless drive of National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) against Human Trafficking, operatives of NBI-Rizal District Office (NBI-RIZDO) arrested an individual in Taytay, Rizal on July 7, 2021, for Human Trafficking. NBI Officer-in-Charge (OIC) Director Eric B. Distor identified the Subject as ANGELICA OLLAGUE y FUTOL. OIC Director Distor said NBI-RIZDO received an information that alleged human trafficking activities are taking place in the nearby towns of Rizal. According to the information, several pimps at the said area are maintaining prostitutes who appear to be minors and are offering them to possible clients for a quick sexual intercourse in nearby hotels and resorts in exchange for monetary considerations. Acting swiftly on the information, NBI-RIZDO conducted surveillance operation wherein the information was positively confirmed. The pimp, identified as “Geca”, is maintaining, harboring, offering, and delivering girls who appear to be minors for sexual intercourse and other sexual favors. After confirming the human trafficking activities committed by the said pimp, an entrapment and rescue operation was hatched on July 7, 2021. The operation resulted in the arrest of pimp “Geca” identified as ANGELICA OLLAGUE y FUTOL. Nine (9) trafficked victims of whom five (5) are minors, were likewise rescued in the operation. Subject ANGELICA “GECA” OLLAGUE y FUTOL was presented for inquest proceedings before Rizal Provincial Prosecutor’s Office for violation of RA 9208 (Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2003) as amended by RA 10364 (Expanded Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2012) and violation of RA 7610 (Special Protection Against Child Abuse, Exploitation and Discrimination Act).

body: PRESS STATEMENT February 10, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } Makiisa sa pagdiriwang ng Safer Internet Day (SID) for Children Philippines ngayong ika-10 ng Pebrero 2026! Ang SID ay isang internasyonal na pagdiriwang na isinasagawa taun-taon upang isulong ang ligtas at responsableng paggamit ng internet lalo na sa mgakabataan. Mula nang ilunsad ito noong 2004, higit sa 100 na bansa na ang nakiisa sa pagdiriwang ito upang palaganapin ang kamalayan tungkol sa kahalagahan ng digital literacy at online safety. title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: PRESS STATEMENT August 05, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Director JUDGE JAIME B. SANTIAGO (Ret.), inquired from the NBI-Puerto Princesa City District Office (NBI-PUERDO) regarding the explosion incident that happened in Palawan. In response, NBI-PUERDO promptly reported an explosion that took place on August 4, 2025. Agents of NBI-PUERDO’s initial investigation revealed that the residents across Puerto Princesa City reported hearing a loud explosion emanating from the sky. The sound was described as a deep and reverberating boom, prompting concern among local communities and initial speculation of an aerial or seismic event. Subsequent verification conducted by NBI-PUERDO revealed that the explosion coincided with the scheduled launch of China’s Long March 12 rocket, which occurred between 6:14 PM and 6:42 PM from the Hainan International Commercial Launch Center in Wenchang, Hainan Province, China. According to the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council (NDRRMC), the rocket’s trajectory passed near Palawan, with potential debris zones identified approximately 21 NM off Puerto Princesa and 18 NM from Tubbataha Reef. Likewise, liaising with the Philippine Space Agency (PSA) confirmed that the acoustic shockwave was consistent with atmospheric effects from high-altitude rocket propulsion and stage separation. Fortunately, no immediate damage or injuries were reported, but the incident caused temporary alarm, particularly in coastal barangays. Director Santiago urged the public to avoid contact with any suspected rocket fragments due to potential toxic fuel residues and to remain calm, as the authorities are working diligently to manage the situation.

body: PRESS STATEMENT August 09, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } The National Bureau of Investigation – Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (NBI-BARMM), under the leadership of NBI Director Judge Jaime B. Santiago (Ret.), arrested JOHN RHEVEN R. MALLARI in a buy-bust operation in Cotabato City, for violation of Republic Act No. 11900, otherwise known as the “Vaporized Nicotine and Non-Nicotine Products Regulation Act” and Republic Act No. 7394 or the “Consumer Act of the Philippines.” The operation was prompted by a letter from the Department of Trade and Industry, Office for Special Mandate on Vaporized Nicotine and Non-Nicotine Products, their Devices and Novel Tobacco Products (DTI-OSMV). The letter provided references to support the enforcement operations, including: a.) briefer on vape-related offences with criminal penalties; b.) Social Card guide to assist in identifying non-compliant vapor products; and, c.) Link to the official DTI-OSMV website, which contains an updated list of PS License holders and trading suspensions. In response to this communication, the NBI conducted surveillance to verify the existence of a vape shop/store in Cotabato City. Once the store was confirmed, a test-buy was made. On August 05, 2025, an entrapment operation was set. NBI agents observed that the vape store was openly displaying vape sets for sale without the proper point-ofsale signage required under R.A. No. 11900. Some of the products had Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR) stickers, while others did not. During the operation, Subject MALLARI cooperated and freely handed over the vapes that lacked BIR stickers. MALLARI was then placed under arrest for the above-stated violations and informed of his constitutional rights before being taken to the NBI-BARMM Office. Subject MALLARI was subsequently submitted for inquest proceedings before the Prosecutor’s Office of Cotabato City. Director Santiago commended the NBI-BARMM for the successful operation, saying it demonstrate Bureau’s continued efforts to pursue and apprehend individuals who are engaged in illegal activities.

body: PRESS STATEMENT September 22, 2022 NBI ARRESTS ONE FOR ILLEGAL PRACTICE OF DENTISTRY The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today said operatives of NBI-Lucena District Office (NBI-LUCDO) arrested an individual in Lucena City for illegal practice of dentistry. Subject was identified as BLANCA PERJES CAPISONDA- LOBUSTA. Said Subject was arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from an information received by NBI-LUCDO regarding a certain TITA COSA who was engaged in illegal practice of dentistry in Lucena City. Having no dental clinic, TITA COSA was doing home service by treating patients in their respective houses. Aside from tooth extraction, she was also making complete dentures and removable partial dentures for some of her patients. Confirmatory acts were done which established the veracity of the aforesaid information. With this, the entrapment operation was conducted on September 8, 2022 wherein TITA COSA, whose real name is BLANCA PERJES CAPISONDA-LOBUSTA, was caught en flagrante delicto receiving marked money from the poseur-patient and about to administer the anesthesia preparatory to the extraction of tooth. Seized from the Subject were dental equipment such as mouth mirror, dental aspirating syringe, topical anesthetic agent, licodine carpule, dental forcep, cowhorn dental forcep, surgical hand instrument, short needles, and local anesthetic agent. The Professional Regulation Commission (PRC) certified that BLANCA PERJES CAPISONDA-LOBUSTA “TITA COSA”, resident of Purok Atin-Atin II, Barangay Marketview, Lucena City, is not a holder of valid certificate of registration and professional identification card in Dentistry. Thus, her name is not included in the roster of registered dentists in the Philippines. It was further revealed that Subject was previously arrested by elements of Criminal Investigation and Detection Group (CIDG) on March 16, 2021 for the same offense in which she was under probation. Subject was presented for inquest proceedings before the Inquest Prosecutor of Lucena City Prosecutor’s Office for violation of RA 9484 otherwise known as The Philippine Dental Act of 2007.

The operation stemmed from the cybercrime monitoring and surveillance efforts conducted by the NBI-STF agents across various social media platforms. The agents uncovered a significant importation, sale, and distribution of illegal vapor products in Cavite and Laguna. By utilizing Open-Source Intelligence (OSINT) and Human Intelligence (HUMINT), they were able to identify the individual responsible for these illicit activities. Additionally, they obtained the subject’s contact information, business details, and social media accounts. Agents of NBI-STF conducted a surveillance and test-buy operation at Hype VapeShop located at Bacoor Boulevard, corner NIA Road, City of Bacoor, Cavite via online transaction and were able to transact with the Subject. Thus, confirming that the establishment is involved in the illicit trade of unregistered vape products without the necessary BIR tax stamps and DTI registration. The undercover agent and the Subject agreed to meet at a coffee shop in Muntinlupa City for the delivery of the unregistered vape products. body: PRESS STATEMENT May 10, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } PRESS RELEASE | NBI ARRESTS SEVEN IN PARAÑAQUE FOR HUMAN TRAFFICKING; RESCUES MINORS AND INFANT FROM SEXUAL EXPLOITATION Pasay City, Philippines — The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI), through its Homicide Division, successfully arrested seven (7) individuals and rescued twelve (12) trafficked victims, including several minors and an infant, during a series of entrapment and rescue operations conducted on May 7, 2026, in Parañaque City for violation of Republic Act No. 10364, otherwise known as the Expanded Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2012. The operation stemmed from intelligence information provided by a non-governmental organization (NGO) regarding the activities of a suspected human trafficking group engaged in the sexual exploitation of minors under the guise of spa and wellness services. The group allegedly offered victims to clients as “therapists” for so-called “nuru massage” and “lingam massage,” which, upon investigation, were found to involve sexual services in exchange for money. Acting on the report, agents of the NBI-Homicide Division conducted extensive surveillance, monitoring, and online coordination with the subjects through social media platforms. This led operatives to an establishment identified as “Rainbow Spa,” where undercover agents confirmed the illegal activities being conducted therein. During the operation, undercover agents were offered the services of two female therapists and were subsequently brought to a nearby apartelle. After the marked money was handed over as payment, the operatives identified themselves and immediately rescued the victims. Two male individuals responsible for transporting and delivering the minor victims to clients were arrested on site. Further investigation revealed that several victims and suspects were staying together in a residence located in Fortunata Village, Parañaque City. NBI agents immediately proceeded to the area, resulting in the arrest of two additional individuals and the rescue of eight more victims. The operation further uncovered that two minor victims were still being transported to service clients in separate locations. Follow-up investigation identified the alleged operators of the trafficking syndicate, a couple residing in Fourth Estate, Brgy. San Antonio, Parañaque City. A subsequent operation led to their successful arrest. Simultaneously, another team of NBI-Homicide Division agents conducted a rescue operation at a motel in Pasay City, where a minor victim was rescued and her male client was arrested. Additionally, another female victim was recovered during an inventory and verification operation conducted at the Fortunata Village residence. The arrested subjects have already been inquested before the appropriate prosecutorial office for violations of Republic Act No. 10364 and other applicable laws. NBI Director Atty. Melvin A. Matibag commended the operatives of the NBI-Homicide Division for the successful conduct of the operations and reaffirmed the Bureau’s unwavering commitment against human trafficking and the sexual exploitation of children. “Human trafficking is a cruel assault on human dignity, especially when the victims are minors who are robbed of their innocence and future. The NBI will continue to intensify its operations against trafficking syndicates and ensure that those responsible are brought before the law,” Director Matibag stated. The NBI likewise urged the public to remain vigilant and immediately report any information relating to human trafficking, online exploitation, and other crimes involving minors to proper authorities. https://www.facebook.com/reel/972161115222922

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today announced the seizure of furnitures made of endangered Mangkono tree by the NBI-Environmental Crime Division (NBI-EnCD) in San Agustin, Surigao Del Sur. NBI Officer-In-Charge (OIC) Eric B. Distor said that the operation stemmed from the letter from the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR) CARAGA Region XIII requesting assistance in the conduct of investigation regarding with the alleged illegal trading of Mangkono (Xanthostemon werdugonianus) finished items. NBI-EnCD operatives conducted a surveillance operation in twelve (12) open souvenir/furniture shops in San Agustin, Surgao Del Sur and was able to verify that the owners of the said shops are in possession and control of Mangkono lumber and flitches. The furniture and souvenir items are all made of Mangkono wood and the operatives were able to buy sample items. The DENR-CARAGA issued a Cerification identifying that the sample items acquired and turned over to them were indeed Mangkono items. The DENR-CARAGA also added that Mangkono species is categorized as Endangered Species. The NBI-EnCD applied for twelve (12) Search Warrants and was granted by the Tag-San Miguel 3rd Municipal Circuit Trial Court. Thus, on August 4, 2021, NBI-EnCD together with NBI-Agusan Del Sur District Office (NBI-ADSDO), DENR-CARAGA, Local PNP, and AFP troops implemented the Search Warrants against the subject shops which resulted in the seizure of Mangkono and Dipterocarps lumber and flitches, furniture souvenir, and novelty items worth Php 2,440,156.40. The NBI-EnCD is now preparing charges for violation of R.A. 9147 otherwise known as the Wildlife Resources Conservation and Protection Act.

body: The National Bureau of Investigation today said operatives of NBI-Task Force Against Illegal Drugs (NBI-TFAID) have seized 16.967 kilos of methamphetamine hydrochloride or commonly known as shabu. Due to the mutual effort of Bureau of Corrections Director, Atty. Benjamin Delos Santos, and the NBI-TFAID operatives, several high profile drug traffickers were recruited and promised to cooperate and help the government in its drive against illegal drugs. Hence, the Case Operation Plan ‘PAGBABAGO’. Based on the project initiated by Director Delos Santos, a case build up was made by joint NBI-National Capital Region (NBI-NCR) and Anti-Illegal Drugs Division (NBI-AIDD) operatives. A series of surveillance operations were then conducted. On January 29, 2017, reliable information was relayed to the undersigned that a group of Chinese nationals headed by a certain alias “Feng” was about to deliver an undetermined amount of shabu, from a posh condominium in Binondo, Manila to an unknown place using a red Nissan Exalta with plate number WNL 700. Acting on the said information, NBI operatives led by Assistant Regional Director Rommel Vallejo proceeded to the aforementioned condo and waited for the vehicle to come out from the parking area. When the vehicle was spotted coming out from the building, the operatives discreetly followed it but lost the same when it made a sudden turn before reaching Jones Bridge, Manila. Operatives searched for the said vehicle and found it parked along Muelle del Banco Nacional St. corner Yuchenco St., Manila. Operatives monitored the vehicle and had it discreetly sniffed by a K-9 sniffing dog, to which the dog sat indicating that it the vehicle contains dangerous drugs. Informant later on notified the operatives that the group sensed that they were being tailed so they decided to leave the vehicle. They opted to summon representative from the barangay covering the area and a representative from the media to witness the search to be conducted. The search yielded to the discovery and seizure of a travelling bag containing seventeen (17) zip-locked bags containing white crystalline substance which tested positive for methamphetamine hydrochloride or shabu, and has a total weight of 16, 967.45 grams or 16.967 kilos. A follow up investigation is being conducted.

body: PRESS STATEMENT August 19, 2025 .jusatified-text { text-align: justify; } The National Bureau of Investigation – Tarlac District Office (NBI-TARDO), under the leadership of Director Judge Jaime B. Santiago (Ret.), arrested JOHN SUK aka JOHN SEUK aka SUK SANG HONG on August 14, 2025 in Clark Freeport Zone, Pampanga for violations of Section 8 and 10 of the Medical Act of 1959 under RA 2382 as amended by RA 4224 and Section 11 (a) of the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) ACT of 2009 under RA 9711. The operation was initiated following an intelligence report that Subject Suk, Korean national, was practicing medicine in the Philippines without the necessary registration from the Professional Regulation Commission (PRC). NBI-TARDO used a poseur patient, who went to Eirene Clinic for a medical consultation about dark marks on his face and a cyst on his back. After an interview, the poseur patient and NBI-TARDO agent entered a consultation room where Subject Suk was waiting. Subject Suk examined the poseur patient and advised him to return in two (2) weeks for surgical removal of the cyst. Since Subject Suk could not present a license or accreditation, he was immediately arrested. Evidence was recovered from the clinic, including vaccines, antibiotics and other medicines (some were unregistered with the FDA), a laptop and a certificate of attendance belonging to Subject Suk. Subject Suk was brought to NBI-TARDO for standard booking procedure and was presented for inquest proceedings. Director Santiago commended NBI-TARDO agents for arresting the Subject.

body: The leader of a group selling fictitious lands and defrauded prospective buyers of millions of pesos, was nabbed red-handed during an entrapment by agents of the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) in Cavite last week. The suspect was identified by NBI Director Nonnatus Caesar R. Rojas as: SAILETO MAYOR LONTABO, a resident of Block 5 Lot 2 Springville Garden 2, Molino, Bacoor, Cavite. He is the head of the Bagong Lahing Pilipino Cooperative, a self-styled association selling fictitious lots in Molino, Bacoor, Cavite. Investigation conducted by the Cavite District Office (CAVIDO) headed by Atty. Onos Mangotara disclosed that the NBI received a complaint from Rima L. Montano against Lontabo who gypped her in a land deal. On March 23, 2013, complainant met suspect Lontabo who offered to sell two (2) parcels of land, one in Springville Subdivision, Molino 3, Bacoor, Cavite and another in Camella Homes, Bgy. Tunasan, Muntinlupa City which he claimed ownership. The persistence of the glib-tongued Lontabo eventually convinced Montano to accept the offer for which she paid the full amount of P660,000.00. A few days later, when Montano verified with the Register of Deed, she found out that the said title is spurious. Certification issued by the Land Registration Authority dated July 10, 2013 revealed that the title covering the lots and the mother plan situated in Bgy. Tunasan, Muntinlupa City does not appear on the registry of the said office. On July 11, 2013, Montano informed the NBI about Lontabo’s continues demand for money in addition to the fees already paid. Thus, an entrapment was planned. A meeting was set on July 16, 2013 in Bacoor, Cavite. In the afternoon of the aforesaid date, Montano and Lontabo met. During the meeting, complainant handed suspect Lontabo P1,500.00. Moments after receiving the marked money, NBI agents approached and after introducing themselves apprehended Lontabo. He was brought to the NBI office for booking and detention. Lontabo voluntarily informed the NBI that the certificate of title given to Montano came from two cohorts who are members of the Bagong Lahing Pilipino Cooperative. Their whereabouts are now being trace by NBI operatives. Further investigation bared that the group had victimized several lot buyers of varying amounts. Charges for violation of Art. 315 RPC as amended by PD 1689 (Syndicated Estafa), Art. 293 RPC (Robbery/ Extortion); and Falsification of Public Document were filed against the suspect before the Bacoor, Cavite City Prosecutor’s Office.

body: PRESS STATEMENT July 23, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } INARESTO NG NBI-CAR ANG DALAWA (2) KATAO SA OPERASYON NG BUY-BUST SA BAGUIO CITY; 9 NA GRAMO NG SHABU NASAMSAM Sa patuloy na pagpapatupad ng mga batas laban sa iligal na droga sa bansa, inaresto ng National Bureau of Investigation – Cordillera Administrative Region (NBI-CAR) ang dalawang (2) indibidwal sa isang operasyong buy-bust sa isang inn sa kahabaan ng Marcos Highway, Baguio City, noong Hulyo 16, 2026. Ang mga nakumpiskang ebidensya mula sa mga suspek, na may bigat na 9.0 gramo, ay nagpositibo sa methamphetamine hydrochloride, na karaniwang kilala bilang “shabu,” isang mapanganib na droga sa ilalim ng Republic Act No. 9165 (Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002). body: PRESS STATEMENT July 27, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } PRESS RELEASE | NBI ISSUES COMMENDATION HONORING BUREAU PERSONNEL Pasay City – On July 27, 2026, during the Monday Flag Ceremony, NBI Director Atty. Melvin A. Matibag commended agents of the NBI-Violence Against Women and Children Division (VAWCD), NBI-Central Visayas Regional Office (CEVRO), and NBI-Cebu District Office (CEBDO) for their successful operations. Director Matibag praised NBI-VAWCD agents for meticulous case preparation and tireless law enforcement, which led to favorable court judgments in two significant operations. He highlighted how their dedication and thoroughness contributed to successful legal outcomes. He also acknowledged the valuable assistance from the NBI-Digital Forensic Laboratory Division (DFLD) and NBI-Tarlac District Office (TARDO) teams during these operations, emphasizing the importance of inter-unit collaboration in achieving shared objectives. The Director also praised the efforts of NBI-CEVRO and NBI-CEBDO agents for their recent coordinated operation in Mandaue and Cebu City. This operation led to the successful seizure of eleven (11) 40-foot container vans stored with smuggled cigarettes, with an estimated value of Php 813,000.00. Additionally, NBI-CEBDO agents received commendation for their role in confiscating twenty-five (25) 20-foot container vans also containing smuggled cigarettes, valued at approximately Php 980,000.00. Also, on July 20, 2026, Director Matibag commended the agents of NBI-SAU for their successful operation that led to the seizure of a substantial volume of smuggled onions and cigarettes. The Director also presided over the historic awarding of the inaugural NBI Shield of Bravery to Agent Francisco of the NBI-OTCD in recognition of his exemplary courage during an incident that occurred on May 13, 2026, in the GSIS building. Director Matibag said that these awards recognize and honor dedicated NBI agents who consistently demonstrate exemplary service in their duties. Each week, selected agents will be acknowledged for their outstanding contributions, underscoring their commitment to the agency and the public. He added that this initiative aims to motivate all personnel to strive for excellence and uphold the NBI’s values.
