body: PRESS STATEMENT July 11, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } The National Bureau of Investigation-Cavite North District Office (CAVIDO North), under the supervision of NBI Director Judge Jaime B. Santiago (Ret.), arrested an individual on July 8, 2025 for distribution of fake Civil Aviation Authority of the Philippines (CAAP) Licenses. The NBI received a letter from CAAP Security and Intelligence Service (CSIS) requesting for assistance on the investigation on the online sale of fake CAAP licenses, which according to CAAP, has been rampant and circulating on social media. Through this modus, an individual or group of individuals could acquire CAAP License without possessing the necessary skills and government regulatory requirements in exchange of certain amount of money. This exploitation of fake CAAP License poses potential aviation accident which is detrimental to the national interest due to high-risk stake involving aviation. On July 8, 2025, NBI-CAVIDO North Agents, together with the personnel of CAAP, conducted an entrapment operation in a mall in the City of Manila. The operation resulted in the arrest of Subject EDDIE BAYOTAS PLEJE after handing over to the poseur-customer the documents, CAAP license, and certification as Pilot and Aircraft Mechanic, and receiving the marked money afterwards. Subject EDDIE BAYOTAS PLEJE was brought to NBI-CAVIDO North office for the standard booking procedures. He was thereafter presented for inquest proceedings before the Manila City Prosecutor’s Office for violation of Article 172 par.(1) and (2) (Falsification by Private Individuals and Use of Falsified Documents) of the Revised Penal Code (RPC) in relation to R.A. No. 10175, otherwise known as Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012, and Article 315 par.2 (a) of the RPC.

body: PRESS STATEMENT October 17, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } As a crusader of peace and order, the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) has intensified its campaign against all threats to public safety. As a result, the NBI-Central Luzon Regional Office (NBI-CELRO) arrested SHEILA GONZALES y APRICANO in a hot pursuit operation in Angeles City, Pampanga, for violation of Presidential Decree No. 1727 (Bomb Prank Law). The local government of Pandan, Angeles City, Pampanga, sought the assistance of NBI-CELRO in regards to multiple bomb threats that were made against several schools and universities in the Province of Pampanga. These threats were communicated through social media and the internet, but it was later determined that these bomb threats were hoaxes, and no actual bombings occurred. In response, NBI-CELRO Agents quickly initiated a cyber-investigation, leading to the tracing and identification of the actual user and creator of the fraudulent social media account that created the bomb threats. The user was identified as Subject Gonzales, residing in Angeles City, Pampanga. Further investigation revealed that Subject was, in fact, a 21-year-old delinquent high school student enrolled at a local high school in Angeles City. On October 13, 2025, the NBI-CELRO Agents, with the assistance of the officials of Barangay Pandan, apprehended Subject Gonzales in her residence. During the operation, the Subject’s mobile phone was seized and underwent an on-site digital forensic examination. The results revealed that the subject fake social media account, linked to the bomb threats, was logged in and active on the phone. Subject Gonzales was subsequently presented for inquest proceedings for the aforementioned violation. NBI Director JUDGE JAIME B. SANTIAGO commended the agents of NBI-CELRO for the apprehension of Subject Gonzales. The Director emphasizes that the NBI, as a vanguard in upholding peace and order, will remain committed to addressing public safety issues.

body: PRESS STATEMENT March 12, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } NBI DISMANTLES ORGANIZED SOCIAL ENGINEERING SYNDICATE IN MAJOR ANTI-FRAUD RAID; 37 APPREHENDED PASAY CITY, Philippines – On March 12, 2026, the National Bureau of Investigation – Human Trafficking Division (NBI-HTRAD) successfully dismantled a large-scale social engineering and online fraud operation during a high-stakes raid. The operation, which involved the execution of a Warrant to Search, Seize, and Examine Computer Data (WSSECD) in San Pedro, Laguna, targeted a syndicate specializing in systematic deception and the manipulation of human trust. In coordination with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) Region IV-A and the NBI-Laguna District Office (NBI-LAGDO), NBI-HTRAD operatives uncovered a highly organized office divided into specialized fraudulent stations. Investigators confirmed that thirty-seven (37) Filipino employees were engaged in coordinated activities such as posing as fictitious Apple technical support, offering fraudulent debt financing and misleading marketing services, and persuading victims to grant remote access to their computers to gain unauthorized system entry. These activities constitute a flagrant violation of Republic Act No. 12010, also known as the Anti-Financial Account Scamming Act (AFASA), which penalizes financial account scamming and social engineering, and Republic Act No. 10175, or the Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012, which addresses illegal access, data interference, and system interference. Due to the complexity of the digital infrastructure found at the site, all recovered electronic devices and gadgets have been transported to the NBI Headquarters in Pasay City. Specialized forensic teams are currently conducting a comprehensive off-site analysis to preserve digital evidence and identify further links to broader criminal networks. Our successful intervention in this sophisticated scheme demonstrates our firm resolve to confront high-tech criminality head-on,” stated NBI Director Atty. Melvin A. Matibag. “However, enforcement is only half the battle; we call on the public to remain our partners in security by staying vigilant against unsolicited offers and protecting their digital boundaries. #NBIServes

body: On May 22, 2020, operatives of NBI-Western Mindanao Regional Office (NBI-WEMRO), together with the personnel from the Bureau of Customs (BOC), and Philippine National Police (PNP) conducted a joint operation against illegally imported/smuggled items and illegal manufacture of cigarettes being perpetrated in Pagadian City and its nearby municipalities. Said operation rooted from the report of counterparts that resulted to the immediate issuance of Authority from BOC to conduct joint operation. The operation resulted in the seizure of spurious BIR Documentary Stamp Tax, raw materials used in manufacturing cigarettes, master cases of cigarettes and imported and locally manufactured items/products believed to be counterfeit in seven (7) target warehouses covered by BOC Letter of authority (LOA) and MO, with total estimated value of more or less Php 150.7 Million. On June 4, 2020, operatives of NBI-Task Force Against Illegal Drugs arrested ZHANG CHEN XIN for violations of RA 10918 (Philippine Pharmacy Act), RA 9711 (FDA Act), and RA 7394 (Consumer Act of the Philippines). Subject was arrested in entrapment operation which stemmed from the information regarding ZHANG CHEN XIN, Chinese national, operating an online pharmacy/drug outlet without a Certificate of Registration (COR) and Professional Identification Card duly issued by the Professional Regulation Commission (PRC) and License to Operate issued by the Food and Drugs Administration (FDA). Investigation revealed that ZHANG created an underground online pharmacy/drug outlet at B107 Marina Bay Homes, Paranaque City, peddling only to Chinese nationals. ZHANG is also one of the suppliers of Chinese drug medicines and cosmetic products to Chinese nationals in NCR. She also engages in the illegal practice of dispensing medicinal drugs to Chinese nationals without prescription from a licensed physician. On June 4, 2020, the entrapment operation was hatched resulting in the arrest of the Subject ZHANG CHEN XIN. Subject failed to present Certificate of Registration (COR) and Professional Identification Card duly issued by the Professional Regulation Commission (PRC) and License to Operate issued by the Food and Drugs Administration (FDA). Charges for the above-mentioned violations were filed against the Subject before the Office of the City Prosecutor, Paranaque City. On June 8, 2020, operatives of NBI-Environmental Crime Division (NBI-EnCD) arrested BERNIE BAGAY y CARONIA and ROMIL ONG y BABAYLAN for possession of Agarwood without permit to possess and transport. Subjects were arrested in entrapment operation which stemmed from a report regarding a group of individuals engaged in possession and selling Agarwood, an endangered specie. Recovered from the possession of Subjects were 10.9 kilograms of forest products identified as Agarwood with a market value of Php 1,700,000.00, a white Nissan Terra vehicle, and a weighing scale. Recovered items were turned over to the custody of DENR-BMB and EPETF. Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the Pasig Prosecutor’s Office for violations of PD 705 (Revised Forestry code of the Philippines as amended by RA 7161), EO 277 s.2011, and RA 9147 (Wildlife Resources Conservation and Protection Act). On June 11, 2020, operatives of NBI-Special Operations Group (NBI-SOG) arrested KIRK GARBRIEL BAUZA DAVID a.k.a SARAH CRUZ for Swindling. Subject was arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from the complaint against the Subject. According to the complainant, a certain “Sarah Cruz” on Facebook ordered from him two (2) airsoft guns and one (1) Hard Case Scope in three (3) separate transactions through Facebook. Complainant sent Subject’s orders upon seeing the screenshot of the online money transfer as payment sent through FB Messenger. When complainant checked his bank statement, he discovered that the three (3) money transfers of the Subject were not credited to his bank account. Believing that complainant is unaware of his modus operandi, Subject ordered again a John Wick Xcortech and sent his proof of payment. The next day, Subject ordered the same item and sent to the complainant another proof of payment. The complainant then sought the help of the NBI-SOG. Acting on the complaint, the entrapment operation was conducted resulting in the arrest of the Subject KIRK GARBRIEL BAUZA DAVID who used the name SARAH CRUZ. The driver of the delivery service company dialed the number of Sarah Cruz and the cellphone of Subject Kirk rang therefore positively identifying that Kirk and Sarah are one and the same person. Subject was presented before the Office of the City Prosecutor of Manila for violation of Article 315 (Swindling) of the Revised Penal Code in relation to RA 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act). On June 13, 2020, operatives of NBI-Task Force Against Illegal Drugs (NBI-TFAID) arrested ERIC EULOGIO, ODESSA DE GUZMAN PATENA, RENATO ABAYA JR., and APRIL KYLE GONZALES for selling and using illegal drugs. Subjects were arrested in a buy-bust operation which stemmed from a report that a certain organized crime group known as “Akyat Condo Gang” headed by ERIC EULOGIO, has offered to sell them high-grade shabu. Investigation revealed that Eric’s group is notoriously engaged in robbery, theft, drug peddling, and maintenance of drug dens, usually picking on condominium owners within Metro Manila and Quezon City area. Moreover, the group was already arrested by the operatives of PNP-NCRPO sometime in 2016 for stealing from a condominium owner in Quezon City. On June 12, 2020, the informants received information that ERIC has with him certain amount of shabu and offers his rented unit specifically located at Unit 20 Oyo V-Cat Hotel, Blumentritt, Manila as a den for any drug sniffing activity. Acting on the development, NBI-TFAID operatives devised a plan to conduct buy-bust operation. On June 13, 2020, after proper coordination with the Philippine Drug Enforcement Agency and the PNP-Manila Police District, NBI-TFAID operatives proceeded to Oyo V-Cat Hotel for the buy-bust operation. Poseur-buyer was able to buy shabu worth Php2,000. NBI operatives caught the above-named Subjects in the act of sniffing shabu, hence, their arrest. Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor, Manila for violation of RA 9165 (comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002). On June 8, 2020, operatives of NBI-Environmental Crime Division (NBI-EnCD) arrested RIZAL MOFAR y CLARITO and ARJHUN GAVIOLA y DOGUITOM. Subjects were arrested in entrapment operation in Cainta, Rizal which stemmed from an information received regarding a group of individuals who are selling and in possession of forest product identified as Agarwood. Subjects sold high-grade Agarwood to poseur-buyers at the agreed price of Php 5 Million. Recovered from the possession of the Subjects were 8.8 kilograms of Agarwood chips with an estimated market value of Php 1.4 Million. The total value representing the market value, forest charges and environmental damages is Php14,379,136.64. Charges for violation of PD 705 as amended by EO 277, RA 7161 (Revised Forestry Code of the Philippines), and RA 9147 (Wildlife Resources Conservation and Protection Act) were filed against the Subjects. On June 8, 2020, joint operatives of NBI-Task Force Against Illegal Drugs, (NBI-TFAID), NBI-Laoag District Office (NBI-LADO), NBI-Isabela District Office (NBI-ISDO), and BIR personnel implemented the Mission Orders to search three (3) units inside Camella Homes, Brgy. Silawit, Cauayan City. Seized from the rented units were fake Internal Revenue Stamps approximately 7,000 pieces, several booklets of checks from different banks with Chinese accounts names, and several packs of Chinese brand cigarettes. Unfortunately, the Chinese occupants of the two (2) units left few days after the raid in their warehouses while the occupants of the other unit left few hours before the Mission Orders were to be implemented. Nonetheless, the Chinese occupants, whose identities were established and photos were surreptitiously taken during the casing operations, will be charged for violation of National Internal Revenue Code as co-conspirators of those previously arrested and charged in connection with the two (2) warehouses located in Brgy. Palattao, Naguilian, Isabela and Brgy. Victoria, Alicia, Isabela. On June 11, 2020, operatives of NBI-Bulacan Dictrict Office (NBI-BULDO) arrested RICHARD DELA CRUZ y FELIPE by virtue of Warrant of Arrest for the crime of Rape. Subject came to NBI Malolos to process his clearance application for local employment purposes. Verification conducted by the clearance personnel disclosed that Subject has a Warrant of Arrest issued by RTC Branch 077 for the crime of Rape, a non-bailable offense. Operatives served the Warrant of Arrest to the Subject and furnished him a copy thereof. Subject underwent booking procedures and was thereafter brought to NBI-Security Management Division for custody. On June 11, 2020, operatives of NBI-National Capital Region (NBI-NCR) stemmed from a report that a certain condominium in Manila, operated by Chinese individuals, is engaged in possible unauthorized makeshift medical facility and health workers using unapproved medications and medical devices allegedly used in performaing Covid-19 test. Bureau of Permits issued a certification that based on their database, no business permit was issued to the address 27 th Floor Room 21 of Century Peak Tower Brgy.669 Ermita, Manila. Further, DOH issued a certification that based on records of the regulatory bureau, there is no existing registered medical clinic or any health facility located at the said address. On the aforementioned date, NBI-NCR operatives conducted enforcement action along with the personnel from DOH-HFSRB. During the operation, undetermined amount of alleged illegal medicines were seized for FDA validations. On June 15, 2020, operatives of NBI-Environmental Crime Division (NBI-EnCD) arrested as LOVELIAN REYES BOOL, RENATO MONSALUD y BOOL, MARCELINO GUSTERO MAÑOSA JR., and APOLLO TABIOS CONSTANTINO for illegal occupation of foreshore land in Botolan, Zambales. Subjects were arrested in an operation which stemmed from a report concerning alleged illegal occupation of foreshore land by Sunrise Paradise Resort in Botolan, Zambales. According to the Provincial Environment and Natural Resources Office, Iba, Zambales, the occupation of foreshore land of Sunrise Paradise Resort is illegal and despite the order to cease and desist from the on-going construction activities, Sunrise did not refrain from constructing and installing structures. NBI-EnCD operatives conducted surveillance and it was established that there were structures constructed in the seashore like floating cottages and a bridge made of steel. It was also noticed that there were on-going construction and installation of structures along the foreshore. LOVELIAN and RENATO BOOL JR. presented some documents of the resort. When asked for certain permits like Environment Compliance Certificate and Miscellaneous Lease Agreement/Foreshore Lease Agreement issued by DENR, they cannot produce any. MARCELINO GUSTERO MAÑOSA JR., the Engineer/Contractor, also showed up as he was in his regular routine of visiting and checking the overall progress of the project. Representatives from PENRO-Zambales and CENRO-Masinloc arrived in the area to conduct ocular inspection and inspect possible violation of the resort. They were able to ascertain that some of the structures built were already on the foreshore area, some were in the salvage area, and one structure was already offshore. body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today said it has recommended the prosecution of two (2) Bureau of Immigration Officers before the Department of Jusrice (DOJ) for falsifying travel records of an Austrian national with criminal records. NBI Officer-In-Charge (OIC) Director Eric B. Distor identified the Immigration Officers (IO) as PERRY MICHAEL Q. PANCHO, IO assigned at Mactan Cebu International Airport (MCIA) and MARCUS S. NICODEMUS, IO at NAIA Terminal 1, Pasay City. OIC Director Distor said that on June 25, 2020, when reports came out that Austrian national JAN MARSALEK, the subject in the US 2.2 Billion Dollar Wirecard fraud in Germany, had entered the Philippines on June 23, 2020 in order to evade authorities in Europe, operatives of NBI-International Airport Investigation Division (NBI-IAID) headed by HA Palmer Mallari, conducted an investigation. OIC Director Distor said the investigation showed that MARSALEK’s most recent travel records to the country include spurious ones, to wit: Arrival on June 23, 2020 at NAIA 1 processed by a certain IO Darren R. Ilagan but with a mysterious “cancelled by user” remark, and a Departure on June 24, 2020 at Mactan Cebu International Airport processed by IO Perry Michael Pancho. The investigation also showed that records were found to be spurious due to the following: Existing immigrations protocol as of that date disallowing passengers in entering Philippine territory due to the sCOVID situation; Absence of actual scanned data page of the passport of Marsalek; Existing protocol that incoming flights of airlines disallowing the boarding of a passenger who will be prevented entry based on the destination country’s protocol as of flight date; and IO Ilagan was not in the official list of IOs on duty for midflight schedule on that date and thus believed to have merely went beyond his duty to encode the same. Likewise, Marsalek’s Departure is spurious based on the following: CCTV footages at the MCIA on June 24, 2020 showing that the BI counters are unmanned because there are no available flights immediately before and after the supposed spurious flights; absence of actual scanned data page of the passport but a page of an unknown passport with the stamp of the Bureau of Quarantine; Certification issued by Philippine Airport Ground Staff (PAGS)/Cebu Station Flight Dispatcher indicating that such flight was cancelled since February 1, 2020 due to COVID situation; Impossibility of Marsalek to be in Cebu the morning of June 24 after his arrival in Manila in the evening of June 23; and IO Perry Michael Pancho was not in the official list of IOs on duty for the morning schedule on June 24, 2020 and thus believed to have merely went beyond his duty to encode the same. According to MISD protocol, when a passenger presents himself at the Immigrations Counter for arrival or departure formalities, the assigned IO performs a derogatory check. By doing so, the IO would be able to know if a passenger has derogatory record (outstanding Warrant of Arrest inclusion in hold departure list or watchlist, blacklisted). This derogatory record check may also be cancelled by the IO by encoding a “cancelled by user” remark. As a consequence, the next user should be able to see such and thus be notified of the status when the same passenger resurfaces at the BI counter for the departure formalities. In this case, the next IO should be able to act accordingly which was contrary to what IO PANCHO did when he still encoded a departure record on MARSALEK. It was discovered that the IO Supervisor for the March 5, 2020 departure of MARSALEK, a certain IO MARCOS NICODEMUS was also the duty supervisor on June 23, 2020. When IOs ILAGAN and PANCHO were summoned by the NBI, only the former appeared. In his affidavit, he alleged, among others, that the idea of conducting a derogatory record check on MARSALEK was the order of his supervisor IO NICODEMUS. He further alleged that when he realized it’s wrong, he immediately encoded a remark “canceled by user” in order to notify the next immigration officer to act accordingly. He added that it was after a few days when he realized that he was made a victim of a “pabokol scheme” where some of his co-workers and superiors made a seemingly harmless and significant request for their personal interests and benefits. The NBI also said that there are no indications that MARSALEK is still in the country due to the confirmation that he indeed arrived on March 3, 2020 at NAIA 3 via Qatar Airways and departure flight on March 5, 2020 also via Qatar Airways and the absence of a genuine arrival thereafter. The entries on the BI records for June 23 and 24, 2020, both spurious, appear to be mere diversionary in order to divert the attention of the authorities in Europe to focus its attention in the Philippines and not in their jurisdiction. On August 7, the NBI recommended to the Department of Justice the prosecution of Immigration Officers PERRY MICHAEL Q. PANCHO and MARCUS S. NICODEMUS for Falsification of Public Documents by a Public Official under Article 171 of the Revised Penal Code and violation of RA 6713 (Code of Conduct and Ethical Standards for Public Officials and Employees) in relation to RA 3019 (Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act).

body: Agents of NBI-Counter Terrorism Division (CTD) supported by the Presidential Anti-Organized Crime Commission (PAOCC) successfully conducted a buy bust operation in SM Marikina City recently. The subjects were identified by NBI Director Virgilio L. Mendez as: RAMON PEYNADO STA. ROSA, a resident of B3 L34 MSGR. A. Sta. Ana St., PLTV 2, Cainta, Rizal, JOAQUIN VILORIA MIRANDA, resident of Mayamot, Sumulong Highway, Antipolo, Rizal and MARCO CARAGAY PAMATMAT of 15 Katipunan Ave., Concepcion, Marikina City. Investigation report of Counter Terrorism Division (CTD) disclosed that on April 2, 2014 they received an intelligence information, that there is an alleged syndicate that sells high powered firearms in Marikina City and that the group sells high powered weapons to politicians. The information gathered disclosed that 10 different high powered firearms were to be sold costing to around P1.5million. On the same day a buy bust operation was planned to arrest the suspected syndicate. At around 1:00 pm, CTD operatives went to SM Marikina open parking lot to conduct the entrapment operation. An undercover agent acted as a poseur buyer and pretended to be a son of a politician from Masbate who needs firearms for the 2016 national and local election. The poseur buyer went to Starbucks Coffee shop and waited for the firearm dealer to come. At around 3:30 p.m. the suspected firearm dealer who arrived at Starbucks Coffee wearing a yellow t-shirt revealed his identity through texting as MARCO CARAGAY PAMATPAT. The poseur buyer approached him, seated with him and introduced himself. They (the undercover agent and firearm dealer) walked to the parking lot where the car of the firearm dealer is parked and the high powered firearms are being kept. The two went inside a while Isuzu Crosswind where three (3) other occupants are inside. There are two (2) male adults and a child. After a few minutes the undercover agent gave the pre-arranged signal that the sale was consummated. Upon seeing the pre-arranged signal, the CTD operatives approached the vehicle and effected the arrest of subjects MARCO CARAGAY PAMATPAT and his two (2) other cohorts JOAQUIN VELORIA MIRANDA and RAMON STA.ROSA PEYNADO. They were brought to the NBI main office where they were booked, photographed and fingerprinted. In the NBI headquarters, subjects personal belongings were inspected, it revealed drug paraphernalia and an aluminum foil which was immediately subjected for forensic examination. The arrested subjects were also subjected to drug test. The preliminary drug test kit revealed positive results for all three, but the final result has yet to be released. Charges for Violation of P.D. 1866 as amended by RA 8294 as amended by 9516 and of section 28npar. © and section 32, of RA 10591 otherwise known as the “Comprehensive Firearms and Ammunition Regulation Act”; Violation of Section 15 Use of Dangerous Drug of RA 9165 “The Dangerous Drug Act” and Violation of Sec.12 Criminal Liability for Fixers of RA 9485 “Anti Red Tape Act” all in relation to Article 8 of the Revised Penal Code were recommended filed against the subjects before the Marikina City Prosecutor’s Office.

body: In the relentless drive against illegal drugs, the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) raided a known drug lair and arrested a notorious illegal drugs dealer during a raid in Bacolod City last week. ACAOILI, former casual employee of LTFRB, for robbery/extortion. NBI-AOTCD cited that the conduct of the operation on January 30, 2016 was based on the complaint of MR. DIONESIO C. ALONZO. Subject was sacked from the service at LTRFB last June 2015, but despite his separation from service, he continue to illegally engage in fixing documents for transport franchising in exchange for huge amounts of money. One of the victims was the Complainant who paid more than One Million Pesos (Php 1,000,000.00) to the Subject for a promised bus franchise, which the Subject failed to deliver. ACAOILI contacted again MR. ALONZO on January 26, 2016 and demanded an additional amount of Php 375, 000.00 as reservation fee for prioritize bidder and later asked the latter to raise the amount to Php 400,000.00. body: PRESS STATEMENT August 27, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } PRESS RELEASE | NBI RESCUES TWO SEXUAL ABUSE VICTIMS IN MISAMIS ORIENTAL, QUIRINO The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI), through its Human Trafficking Division (NBI-HTRAD), successfully rescued two victims in two separate operations in Misamis Oriental and Quirino. In the first operation stemming from a referral by the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), the NBI-HTRAD, in coordination with the NBI-Northeastern Mindanao Regional Office (NBI-NEMRO), located and rescued a woman on August 17, 2026, who had been identified as a victim in a series of child sexual abuse and exploitation materials first referred to the Philippines in 2013. The case remained unresolved for more than a decade until a review in October 2025 yielded new information that helped investigators identify and locate the victim, who is now an adult. The investigation used open-source intelligence, digital tracing, and cross-checks of social media accounts and government records to establish the victim’s identity and current location. Field verification and surveillance were also conducted before the victim was approached. Following her rescue, she provided a sworn statement to NBI-HTRAD investigators in Misamis Oriental. She disclosed that intimate images of her had been taken without her consent and later circulated online by a foreign national with whom she had been involved at the time. Her statement will be provided to FBI to support its continuing investigation into the subject within its jurisdiction. In the second operation, the NBI-HTRAD, in coordination with the NBI-Cagayan Valley Regional Office (NBI-CAVRO), NBI-Bayombong District Office (NBI-BAYDO), NBI-Isabela District Office (NBI-ISDO), and the Municipal Social Welfare and Development Office (MSWDO) of Diffun, Quirino, conducted a physical surveillance operation on August 19, 2026, following a request for assistance from the UK National Crime Agency (UK NCA). The operation resulted in the successful location and rescue of a minor victim who was allegedly subjected to illicit communications and activities involving a British national. The minor was subsequently placed under the custody of the Diffun MSWDO for proper care, protection, and appropriate intervention. These successful operations highlight the NBI’s continuing commitment to protecting victims of exploitation, particularly children, and pursuing cases in cooperation with international law enforcement partners. They also demonstrate the importance of sustained investigation and case review, as advances in digital investigative methods, access to records, and stronger international cooperation can help resolve cases that may have remained unsolved for years. The NBI likewise recognizes the assistance of the FBI, UK NCA, National Center for Missing & Exploited Children, MSWDO of Manticao, Misamis Oriental, MSWDO of Diffun, Quirino, and NGO partner Justice Reigns and Just Philippines Project in these efforts.

body: On September 8, 2020, said operatives of NBI-Central Visayas Regional Office (NBI-CEVRO) arrested JOVELYN B. CERIACO for falsifying BIR TIN cards. Subject was arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from a letter from BIR 13 Regional Director requesting assistance against the rampant selling of TIN cards online in Cebu, in violation of Section 257(B)(8) of the Tax Code, TIN cards being an accountable form of the BIR. After series of investigation, NBI-CEVRO operatives conducted an entrapment operation on September 8, 2020 which resulted in the arrest of Subject JOVELYN B. CERIACO. Subject was caught in the act of handing over to the poseur-customer a falsified BIR TIN card. More falsified TIN cards were also recovered from the Subject. Subject is awaiting for the schedule of the inquest proceedings at the City Prosecutors Office of Cebu City for violating the provisions of Section 257(B)(8) of the Tax Code and Estafa through Falsification of Document penalized under Article 315 in relation to Article 172 of the Revised Penal Code, all in relation to RA 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012). On September 11, 2020, operatives of NBI-Intellectual Property Rights Division (NBI-IPRD) seized 455 bottles of health products (Vitamin C) with an estimated value of more or less Php 300,000.00. Items were seized by virtue of Search Warrants for violation of RA 8293 (Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines) and RA 9711 (Food and Drug Administration Act of 2009) issued against JPMC8 Health Care Products Trading, Inc. located at Vitas, Tondo, Manila. On September 14, 2020, the NBI-Anti-Graft Division (NBI-AGD) filed charges for Slander by Deed, Oral Defamation, Light Coercion (Unjust Vexation) and violation of City Ordinance No.2020-012 S.2020 (Paranaque City) against MERIAM CASTILLO y APOLITO before the City Prosecutor of Paranaque City. Charges were filed in relation to the alleged discrimination of the Subject towards the complainant who is a registered nurse employed at Makati Medical Center. According to the complainant, Subject threw liquid bleach agent upon her and uttered humiliating remarks despite the fact that complainant told the Subject that she is not a Covid positive. Complainant, through her sister, reported the incident to the Office of Barangay BF Homes, Paranaque City but no immediate action was received from the Barangay. At this point, complainant decided to report the incident to the NBI. After proper evaluation of the case, there is sufficient evidence for Subject to be charged with Slander by Deed, Oral Defamation, Light Coercion (Unjust Vexation), and City Ordinance No.2020-012 S.2020 (Paranaque City). Charges were filed against Subject MERIAM CASTILLO y APOLITO before the City Prosecutor of Paranaque City. On September 14, 2020, operatives of NBI-Intellectual Property Rights Division (NBI-IPRD) seized 39 pieces of assorted counterfeit Stihl products with an estimated value of more or less Php 2,535,000.00. Items were seized by virtue of Search Warrants for violation of RA 8293 (Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines) issued against John and Jane Does, owners, operators of WJBA General Merchandise located at 530 Moriones St. Brgy. 6, Zone 1, Tondo, Manila. On September 15, 2020, operatives of NBI-Central Luzon Regional Office (NBI-CELRO) arrested ENGR. RENELEE CHIINGCUANGCO for Estafa. Subject was arrested in an entrapment operation conducted at Marquee Mall, Angeles City, Pampanga. Subject is now under temporary custody of NBI-CELRO while necessary documents were being prepared for submission of Subject for inquest proceedings before the Angeles city Prosecutor’s Office for the crime of Estafa defined and penalized under Article 315 of Revised Penal Code. On September 16, 2020, operatives of NBI-Ilagan District Office (NBI-ISDO) arrested DIOSDADO C. MEDRANO and ANTONIO A. AGGABAO, employees of Community Environment and Natural Resources (CENRO) for extortion activities on acquiring permit to travel woods. Subjects were arrested in an entrapment operation conducted at Cabagan, Isabela. During the operation, marked money was recovered from Subject’s possession. Subjects were brought to NBI-ISDO for booking and proper disposition. On September 16, 2020, operatives of NBI-International Airport arrested LAMBERTO Q. PAYONGAYONG for Usurpation of Authority. Subject sent various letters to Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP) and represented himself as a lawyer. In the letters, Subject declared that he is a trustee of someone with Trust Account covering $300 Dodecallion which allegedly matured in 2007 and which he sought to be withdrawn with the help of BSP. He also mentioned that he is an assignee of a parcel of land covered by Original Certificate of Title allegedly being used by the Central Bank of the Philippines to back up the printing of legal tender notes. Certification issued by the Integrated Bar of the Philippines (IBP) states that Subject PAYONGAYONG is not a member of the Philippine Bar. On the above-mentioned date, an entrapment operation was conducted and resulted in the arrest of the Subject. He will be subjected for inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor, Quezon City for violation of Article 177 (Usurpation of Authority or Official Functions) of the Revised Penal Code. On September 17, 2020, operatives of NBI-Iligan District Office (NBI-ILDO) arrested JOSEPH YU y PAJO for violation of RA 10591 (Comprehensive Firearms and Ammunition Regulation Act). Subject was arrested by virtue of Search Warrant issued against the Subject who is a retired engineer of NPC. Seize from the Subject were one (1) unit Caliber .38 revolver, fifteen (15) pcs live ammunition for Caliber .38 revolver, fifteen (15) pcs special ammunition for Caliber .38, two (2) pcs live was cutter ammunition for Caliber.38 revolver, one (1) empty shell for Caliber.38 revolver, and one (1) holster color brown for Caliber.38 revolver. Subject was thereafter brought to CIDG Iligan CFU for booking procedures and temporary detention. On September 17, 2020, operatives of NBI-Bohol District Office (NBI-BOHDO) arrested EDGAR SARPAMONES y LABAJO for Online Libel. EDGAR SARPAMONES y LABAJO was arrested in Pondol, Loon, Bohol by virtue of Warrant of Arrest. On September 17, 2020, operatives of NBI-Cordillera Administrative Region (NBI-CAR) arrested VICTOR ALEC SALES LEAL in a buy-bust operation for violation of Sections 5, 6, and 12 of RA 9165 (Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002). Seized during the operation were one (1) clear plastic sachet containing 0.2 grams of Shabu, several plastic sachets contained in Calypso Polypropylene, one (1) black eyewear case containing various illegal drug paraphernalia, several drug paraphernalia, two (2) mobile phones, and marked money. Items seized have an estimated value of Php 15,000.00. Subject will undergo inquest proceedings for violation of RA 9165.

body: PRESS STATEMENT August 18, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } PRESS RELEASE | NBI FILES CASES VS DAVAO MIGHTY FOR RADIOACTIVE, SUBSTANDARD STEEL PRODUCTS The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) has referred to the Department of Justice (DOJ) the case involving Davao Mighty Steel Corporation (DAVAO MIGHTY) after its investigation found radioactive-bearing materials in the company’s steel manufacturing operations and radioactive-bearing and substandard Davao Mighty Steel “DMS” reinforcing steel bars already circulating in the commercial market. The investigation expanded after the Philippine Nuclear Research Institute (PNRI) detected Uranium-238 and Thorium-232 in commercially distributed DMS rebars. Subsequent laboratory examinations by Nanotech Analytical Services And Training Corp. (NASAT), as technically evaluated by PNRI, confirmed the presence of uranium and thorium in finished DMS rebars, with examined samples preliminarily determined to have exceeded applicable exemption levels under Code of PNRI Regulations (CPR Part 3), Standards for Protection Against Radiation. Separate product-standard testing found that four of eight (50 percent) of DMS rebar samples purchased from commercial hardware establishments in Mindanao failed the mandatory mass-variation requirement under PNS 49:2020. DMS-marked rebars were also found in the rubble of structures that collapsed following the magnitude 7.8 Mindanao earthquake on June 8, 2026, in parts of Sarangani, Davao del Sur, and Davao Occidental. The presence of the rebars in the rubble does not, by itself, establish that they caused the structural collapses. On August 13, 2026, the NBI and Presidential Anti-Organized Crime Commission (PAOCC), with the assistance of PNRI, Philippine Air Force and Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) – Chemical, Biological, Radiological, and Nuclear (CBRN) units, PCG Special Operations Group, and the 10th Infantry Division of the Philippine Army, implemented Search Warrants at DAVAO MIGHTY’s facility in Barangay Ilang, Bunawan, Davao City. The technical search documented Uranium-238, Thorium-228, Thorium-232, and Radium-226 in finished rebars and other production and stored materials, including furnace-related materials, industrial powders, dust, wastes, and wastewater. PNRI found uranium and thorium above applicable exemption limits in examined solid wastes and thorium above the applicable exemption level in examined liquid waste. PNRI also certified that DAVAO MIGHTY and its identified officers and personnel did not possess the required radioactive material license or authority. Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR) likewise found that the company’s Environmental Compliance Certificate did not declare or authorize the presence, handling, processing, storage, or use of radioactive materials at the facility. The operation also resulted in the rescue of 174 Filipino workers. The NBI referred the case to the DOJ for appropriate proceedings for alleged violations of Republic Act No. 12305, Republic Act No. 6969, Presidential Decree No. 1586, and Republic Act No. 7394. The NBI and PAOCC will continue coordinating with PNRI, DENR, Department of Trade and Industry (DTI), Department of Labor and Employment (DOLE), Department of Health (DOH), and other concerned agencies to secure radioactive-bearing materials, protect workers and communities, trace affected DMS products in commerce, and prevent potentially unsafe reinforcing steel from further entering the construction supply chain. Further product tracing, testing, and appropriate engineering assessment will also be undertaken to determine the extent of distribution and use of the affected products.

On August 13, 2026, the NBI and Presidential Anti-Organized Crime Commission (PAOCC), with the assistance of PNRI, Philippine Air Force and Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) – Chemical, Biological, Radiological, and Nuclear (CBRN) units, PCG Special Operations Group, and the 10th Infantry Division of the Philippine Army, implemented Search Warrants at DAVAO MIGHTY’s facility in Barangay Ilang, Bunawan, Davao City. The technical search documented Uranium-238, Thorium-228, Thorium-232, and Radium-226 in finished rebars and other production and stored materials, including furnace-related materials, industrial powders, dust, wastes, and wastewater. PNRI found uranium and thorium above applicable exemption limits in examined solid wastes and thorium above the applicable exemption level in examined liquid waste. PNRI also certified that DAVAO MIGHTY and its identified officers and personnel did not possess the required radioactive material license or authority. Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR) likewise found that the company’s Environmental Compliance Certificate did not declare or authorize the presence, handling, processing, storage, or use of radioactive materials at the facility. The operation also resulted in the rescue of 174 Filipino workers. The NBI referred the case to the DOJ for appropriate proceedings for alleged violations of Republic Act No. 12305, Republic Act No. 6969, Presidential Decree No. 1586, and Republic Act No. 7394. The NBI and PAOCC will continue coordinating with PNRI, DENR, Department of Trade and Industry (DTI), Department of Labor and Employment (DOLE), Department of Health (DOH), and other concerned agencies to secure radioactive-bearing materials, protect workers and communities, trace affected DMS products in commerce, and prevent potentially unsafe reinforcing steel from further entering the construction supply chain. Further product tracing, testing, and appropriate engineering assessment will also be undertaken to determine the extent of distribution and use of the affected products.

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today said it will file Murder charges against the perpetrators of the ambush-killing of ROLANDO FAJARDO and his driver, THOMAS ANDAYA on June 24, 2014 in Calamba Laguna. The NBI-Death Investigation Unit (NBI-DIU) said that based on its investigation, it has found probable cause to charge the suspects, PINSP. MARCO POLO ESTRERA, PO2 JEROME DATINGUINOO and PO2 MARK DE LA PAZ with multiple murder charges. It was established that Fajardo was killed reportedly in an ambush along the national highway in Barangay Bagong Kalsada, Calamba City at around 7:30 in the evening. He was sitting on the passenger side of his Audi sedan, together with his driver, Thomas Andaya, and personal bodyguard, Marcelinano Batan Jr., who was sitting behind him, when unidentified gunmen opened fire at them. Fajardo and Andaya died instantly while Batan was able to return fire at their assailants, who hurriedly fled the scene. In a Sworn statement, Batan claimed that he was able to see the faces of the two (2) gunmen and consequently identified them after being shown a lineup of photos. Dumlao and Dante Alvarez, and they were traversing the national highway when a gray car suddenly blocked their way. Moments after, he saw the 2 gunmen open fire at them. Batan failed to recount the exact firearm used by the gunmen but claimed that they used a high-powered firearm, adding that he returned fire which caused the assailants to fell on their white getaway motorcycle.

body: PRESS STATEMENT December 13, 2024 The NBI-Intellectual Property Rights Division (IPRD), on December 9, 2024, implemented thirty-four (34) Search Warrants for violation of RA 8293 (Trademark Infringement) against five (5) shops/stalls in Tondo, Manila. The operation stemmed on the complaint filed by Lee Bumgarner Inc. (LBI) as regards the proliferation of fake products bearing ADIDAS, VANS, PUMA and NEW BALANCE trademark. The said operation resulted in the seizure of more or less 1,502 pairs of counterfeit footwear of ADIDAS, VANS, PUMA and NEW BALANCE with an estimated value of Php 8,518,000.00. The search was conducted peacefully in the presence of representatives and witnesses, who signed the inventory. NBI Director Judge Jaime Santiago (Ret.) commended the NBI-IPRD for the enforcement action taken to stop the proliferation and distribution of counterfeit products.

body: PRESS STATEMENT April 30, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } The 7.7 magnitude earthquake that hit Myanmar last March 28, 2025 killed at least 5,352 people, injured 4,800, and left 341 still missing, according to the latest update given by the Myanmar government. It was the most powerful earthquake that hit the said country. Upon the instruction of President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. through the Department of Foreign Affairs – Office of the Undersecretary for Migration Affairs (DFA-OUMA), NBI Director Judge Jaime B. Santiago directed the immediate dispatch of NBI Forensic Team composed of doctors, dentist, forensic chemist, DNA Analysts, photographer, and other support staff, to help and assist in the identification of fatalities. Thus, on April 4, 2025, the NBI forensic team led by the Chief of the Disaster Victim Identification Division Dr. Wilfredo E. Tierra arrived in Yangon, the largest city in Myanmar where they were met by the Chargé d’ Affaires and other officials of the Philippine Embassy. Thereat, the embassy officials turned over biological samples (hair and two (2) teeth from each body) of two (2) Filipinos previously retrieved from the collapsed Sky Villa Condominium in Mandalay, the second largest and the most badly hit city in Myanmar. On April 5, 2025, the group travelled from Yangon to Mandalay. Two (2) other Filipino casualties were recovered by local authorities and later identified by the NBI Forensic Experts with the assistance of the relatives of the deceased, through secondary parameters (tattoos, personal belongings, identification documents, and similarity on the comparison of dental profile with the photographs of the teeth on the recovered remains). The dental profile picture was provided by relatives and friends of the victims. On April 9, 2025, another dead body of a Filipino was retrieved from the condominium and was properly identified and documented with the guide of dental photographs and profile. The assistance provided by the NBI forensic team was greatly acknowledge not only by the Myanmar government but also by the whole international community. The NBI Director congratulates the brave men and women of the forensic team for their hardship, sacrifices, and commitment to public service in performing their respective task despite the hazard and risks under the circumstances.

body: Three (3) females and two (2) males were arrested by agents of the NBI–Anti Organized and Transnational Crime Division (NBI AOTCD) during an entrapment operation in Better Living Subdivision, Paranaque City recently. The suspects were identified by NBI Director Virgilio L. Mendez as follows: SOLEDAD ANGUE SISRACON @ SOL, of legal age, a resident of 3-317 Thurs St., St. Joseph Village, Panapaan 3 Bacoor, Cavite MYRNA PEDROSO TANALEON, of legal age, a resident of Block 2, Lot 31, Phase 2, Celina Royale, Bayanan, Bacoor, Cavite ELIZABETH NIEVA CALIG, of legal age, a resident of Block 27, Lot 3, Phase 2, Villa Apolonia, Naic, Cavite ALBERTO NONES HOFFMAN, of legal age, a resident of No. 127 Barrio Timalan, Naic, Cavite ROMMEL MONTALBAN HOFFMAN, of legal age, a resident of Block 14, Lot 11, Phase 1, Villa Apolonia, Naic, Cavite Investigation disclosed sometime in May 2013, Subjects MERIAM VIDAL and MARIA LUZ TRIAS loaned an amount of Sixty Thousand Pesos (P60,000.00) from Complainant TAKAHASHI. As guarantee for the payment of the said loan, Subjects VIDAL and TRIAS pawned a 78 sq.m. lot title located in Imus, Cavite under the name of Paul Que. However, they failed to redeem it within a month as they promised. Instead, they introduced Subject SOLEDAD SISRACON to complainant as the owner of the said property. SISRACON offered to sell to complainant another property covering 72 square meters, likewise under the name of Paul Que as she was having a hard time paying the interest. Because of her representation, Complainant paid an additional Forty Thousand Pesos (Php 40,000.00) as full payment of the two properties. Sometime at the later part of January 2014, Subject SISRACON borrowed from Complainant because her car had figured in an accident and that she is in dire need of money. As guarantee for the said loan, Subject gave Complainant two (2) land titles covering 65 square meters and 61 square meters respectively, located in Dasmarinas, Cavite under the name of one AMPARO OCAMPO. Sometime in February 2014, Subject SISRACON gave Complainant a deed of sale for the said property allegedly executed by Amparo Ocampo. However, Complainant is not interested in the said properties. Subject SISRACON took back the said two (2) land titles purportedly to show other prospective buyers. On February 10, 2014, Subject SISRACON went to Complainant’s house and introduced SUSAN GREGORIO who is selling her lot consisting of 904 square meters located in Tagaytay City for Four Hundred Thousand Pesos (Php 400,000.00). Having been induced by their presentation, Complainant gave the initial amount of One Hundred Sixty Five Thousand Pesos (Php 165,000.00). On February 17, 2014, Complainant paid the amount of Two Hundred Thirty Five Thousand Pesos (Php 235,000.00) to Subject SISRACON as full payment for the said property. After sometime, SUSAN GREGORIO went back to Complainant’s house and confessed that she is not the real SUSAN GREGORIO. Instead she introduced herself as CONCHITA MANTE TAROG, who was paid by Subject SISRACON to act as such. On February 12, 2014, Subject SISRACON mortgaged to Complainant another lot title entrusted to her by EDILBERTO G. ASPREC in the amount of Fifty Thousand Pesos (Php 50,000.00). However, when Complainant brought the said document at the Register of Deeds, Caloocan City on April 24, 2014, she was informed that the title under TCT No. 38141 had already been cancelled. On February 13, 2014, Subject SISRACON together with LOLITA CHANG CANTUBA enticed Complainant to finance the processing of the loan application of Henry Munar Chan, owner of the 33.901 property in Trece Martires, Cavite, and one Mariana Cabalfin, owner of the property located in Bayanbayanan, Marikina City. Accordingly, Henry Chan and Marciana Cabalfin need a financier. In return, they promised Complainant a “double your money back” guarantee once the loan is approved by the bank. Because of the good offer, Complainant gave Subjects SISRACON and CANTUBA the total amount of Five Hundred Eighty Nine Thousand Pesos (Php 589,000.00). In return Subjects SISRACON and CANTUBA gave Complainant Owners Duplicate Certificates of HENRY CHAN (TCT No. T-301400) and MARCIANA C. CABALFIN (TCT- NO. 233868). However, on April 3, 2014, Complainant verified said certificates with the Tagaytay City Register of Deeds. Complainant was informed that Owners Duplicate Certificate of HENRY MUNAR CHAN under TCT No. T-301400 is “Patently Fake”. On March 14, 2014, Subject SISRACON mortgaged to Complainant TCT No. T-1212341 covering 700 square meters located in Brgy. Tejero, Gen. Trias, Cavite under the name of SERENIDAD ABUEG and SALVADOR ABUEG. Similarly, the owners just want to mortgage the said property in the amount of One Hundred Thousand Pesos (Php 100,000.00). To entice the Complainant, Subject SISRACON presented Senior Citizen ID of the owners, LRA receipt, assessment and payment forms and issued a PNB postdated check no. 0729270 under the account name of FLORENCIO BATO. When the check was presented by the Complainant to the bank for payment, it was denied for reason of “ACCOUNT CLOSED”. Verification with the Register of Deeds, Trece Martirez, Cavite on April 24, 2013, showed that the documents presented to her were all fake. Sometime in March 2014, Complainant gave Subject SISRACON the amount of One Hundred Twelve Thousand Pesos (Php 112,000.00) for another lot in the name of MYRNA GREGORIO. On April 28, 2014, Subject SISRACON called Complainant and demanded the amount of Ten Thousand Pesos (Php10,000.00) for the loan application of HENRY MUNAR CHAN and Fifteen Thousand Pesos (Php15,000.00) as additional payment for the mortgaged property of MYRNA GREGORIO. Having previous knowledge of the unscrupulous acts committed against her by the Subjects, Complainant agreed to meet with her on a later date. She then decided to file a complaint with the NBI- AOTCD. On May 2, 2014, operatives of the Anti-Organized and Transnational Crime Division proceeded to Complainants residence at No. 49 Columbia St., Better Living Subdivision in Paranaque City. At around 2:30 p.m. on even date, Subject SISRACON and company arrived. She introduced her companion as MYRNA GREGORIO, the alleged owner of a lot mortgaged to her, and the other woman as ELVIRA HOFFMAN. One of the two (2) men was also introduced as ALBERTO HOFFMAN, husband of Elvira, they owned a property in Timalan, Concepcion, Naic, Cavite which they would want to mortgage. The other man was introduced as ROMMEL HOFFMAN, brother of ALBERTO. Thereafter, Subject demanded for the Twenty Five Thousand Pesos which they had previously agreed upon. Complainant then handed over the marked money to Subject SISRACON, who after counting the money, handed it over to MYRNA GREGORIO who took her turn in counting the same. At this juncture, Complainant gave the pre-arranged signal to the NBI operatives, who then approached them. Subjects SISRACON, MYRNA GREGORIO, ELVIRA HOFFMAN, ALBERTO HOFFMAN and ROMMEL HOFFMAN were apprehended and were apprised of their Constitutional Rights. They were then brought to the NBI office where they were photographed, booked and fingerprinted. It was learned that Subject SISRACON’s real name is SOLEDAD ANGUE SISRACON. Record check revealed that she had been previously charged for Estafa in various courts with Arrest Warrants having been issued. Record check on suspect MYRNA GREGORIO whose real name is MYRNA PEDROSO TANALEON. Record check revealed that she was also convicted of the crime of Estafa and was sentenced to suffer an indeterminate prison term of six (6) months one (1) day of prison correctional to twenty (20) years of reclusion temporal on August 15, 2013 by RTC Branch 32. She managed to escape right after the promulgation of the case. Thus a Warrant of Arrest was issued by the court on August 22, 2013. The said warrant was served to MYRNA PEDROSO TANALEON. Similarly, she had been charged for various cases ranging from Violation of BP 22, Qualified Theft and Carnapping. She was also convicted by the Manila RTC Bra xxx for Estafa with an Arrest Warrants having been issued. ELVIRA HOFFMAN revealed that her true name is ELIZABETH NIEVA CALIG, found in her possession is a Comelec ID bearing her true name, and a VITA ID bearing her assumed name. ALBERTO HOFFMAN was identified as ALBERTO NONES HOFFMAN while ROMMEL HOFFMAN is ROMMEL MONTALBAN HOFFMAN. Charges for Estafa thru Falsification of Public Documents in relation to PD 1866 (Syndicated Estafa) were filed against the suspects before the Office of the City Prosecutor, Paranaque City.

title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: PRESS STATEMENT January 30, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } NBI Arrests Two for Real Estate Scams and Falsification of Public Documents PASAY, Philippines – On January 20, 2026, the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI), through its Bulacan District Office (NBI-BULDO), successfully apprehended two (2) individuals in a targeted entrapment operation for their involvement in a large-scale real estate scam. The Subjects are facing charges for multiple counts of Estafa through Falsification of Public Documents, as defined and penalized under Articles 315 and 171, in relation to Article 48, of the Revised Penal Code. Investigation revealed that Subjects misrepresented themselves as legitimate owners, sellers, or authorized agents of various real estate properties. They used this facade to entice unsuspecting buyers into high-value transactions. The complainant discovered the scheme only after realizing that the land titles and supporting legal documents provided by the Subjects were forgeries, siphoning the former of their money amounting to P1.6 Million. Thereafter, Complainant reported the said fraudulent scheme to the NBI. Acting on the report, an entrapment operation was subsequently executed resulting to the arrest of the Subjects. After being appraised with their constitutional rights, they were transported to the NBI-BULDO Office for standard booking procedures and documentation. Thereafter, they were brought to the Office of the City Prosecutor of Malolos City for inquest proceedings. NBI Acting Director Angelito Magno warned the public regarding the rise of property-related fraud. “We urge all prospective buyers to exercise extreme caution in real estate dealings,” said Director Magno. “Do not rely on appearances alone. Perform thorough due diligence and always verify the authenticity of land titles and documents directly with the Land Registration Authority (LRA) or the Registry of Deeds before any exchange of funds.” ATTY. ANGELITO DLP. MAGNO Acting Director, NBI Media Contact: HA Palmer U. Mallari NBI Spokesperson [email protected] #NBIServes

title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today announced the arrest of an individual in Cebu City for selling overpriced Tocilizumab, a medicine found to be effective in reducing mortality rate of severe COVID-19. NBI Officer-in-Charge (OIC)-Director Eric B. Distor identified the subject as CHERRY JALARON y ROBLES. OIC Director Distor said the operation stemmed from a meeting called by OPAV Secretary Michael Lloyd Dino for the Price Regulation of COVID-19 Life Saving Medicines, participated in by OPAV, DOH-7, DTI-7 and IATF-,Visayas. NBI-CEVRO was tasked to pursue the lead on a certain KAREN GO, who is allegedly engaged in the illegal selling of Tocilizumab. After surveillance and verification, NBI-CEVRO confirmed the illegal activity. NBI-CEVRO was able to establish communication with KAREN GO . On Sept. 13, 2021, an Agent acted as poseur-buyer and ordered online one vial of Tocilizumab for 97,000.00, more than the MRP set by the gov’t at 20,581.45. The undercover Agent and KAREN GO agreed to meet at Barangay Guadalupe, Cebu City to deliver the medicine. Thus, NBI-CEVRO operatives proceeded to the target meeting place. In the evening of the same day, After the transaction has been completed, operatives apprehended the courier of Tocilizumab identified as CHERRY JALARON y ROBLES. According to the arrested Subject, she is the secretary of KAREN GO and was instructed by the latter to deliver the medicine. Subject Jalaron was presented for Inquest proceeding before the Office of City Prosecutor of Cebu City for violation of Section 24 in relation to Section 25 of R.A. 9502, otherwise known as “Universally Accessible Cheaper and Quality Medicines Act of 2008” in relation to R.A. 7581 (Price Act) and Department Circular-DOH No. 2021-0291, Suggested Retail Price (SRPs) for Emergency Essential Medical Devices due to Coronavirus Disease 2019 (COVID-19) Health Event and in relation to Article 8 (Conspiracy) of the Revised Penal Code, and in relation to Section 6 of R.A. 10175, otherwise known as the “Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012”. In addition, KAREN GO (at large) was also charged for the same violations of the law.

title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: In line with the relentless campaign of the government against illegal gambling, operatives of NBI-Cagayan Valley Regional Office (NBI-CAVRO) arrested seventy-five (75) Chinese nationals and three (3) Filipinos on August 4, 2020 for online illegal gambling. NBI Officer-in-Charge (OIC) Director Eric B. Distor said the operation stemmed from an information provided by CEZA that several Chinese nationals are facilitating and operating online gambling, in violation of existing laws and regulations, within CEZA’s area of jurisdiction in the municipality of Sta. Ana, Cagayan. After verifying the said information, a Warrant to Search and Seize was sought and granted. On August 4, 2020, NBI-CAVRO operatives proceeded to Sta. Ana, Cagayan for the implementation of the Search Warrant. In coordination with the Philippine National Police of Cagayan and Cagayan Economic Zone Authority (CEZA), NBI-CAVRO operatives implemented the Search Warrant against the premises of Frank Yu, a Chinese national, for alleged violation of PD 1602 as amended by RA 9287 (An Act Increasing the Penalties for Illegal Numbers Games in relation to RA 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012). In the course of the operation, several Chinese nationals were seen using computer systems and in plain view, with the assistance of CEZA, it was confirmed that they were indeed operating online gambling. Hence, having been caught in flagrante delicto directly operating and facilitating illegal and unauthorized activities and games, they were immediately placed under arrest and informed them of their right under the Philippine Constitution. Accordingly, seventy-five (75) Chinese nationals and three (3) Filipinos identified as ERWIN DIGOL, ALEXIS ISAAC FERRO, and MYLENE TUAZON were arrested in the course of the operation. Arrested Subjects were properly booked, fingerprinted, and photographed as part of the standard operating procedure. They were thereafter presented for inquest proceedings for violation of PD 1602 as amended by RA 9287 (An Act Increasing the Penalties for Illegal Numbers Games in relation to RA 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012). An ongoing investigation against the owner of the resort and establishment and the management of OFA Cagayan Realty Developer Corporation are being conducted and pursued. If evidently found that they are facilitating and operating illicit activities under the guise of a legitimate business and if other circumstances warrant, additional criminal charges will be filed.

title: All Covered Persons to Deal Only with Designated Non-Financial Businesses and Professions Registered with the AMLC
body: AMLC Resolution No. 81 dated 09 May 2019 directed the issuance of an advisory to covered persons (CPs) dealing with clients who are classified under the sector of Designated Non-Financial Businesses and Professions (DNFBPs) to demand presentation of their Certificate of Registration (COR) or Provisional COR (PCOR) with the AMLC as part of Customer Due Diligence (CDD) measures under Section 3.5(b)(1) of the 2018 Implementing Rules and Regulations of the AMLA, as amended. Failure of a DNFBP to supply its P/COR is a ground to conduct enhanced due diligence measure (EDD) and/or to re-evaluate the business relationship. On the part of the CP failing to comply with this directive, it may be cited for the applicable administrative sanctions under the Rules of Procedure in Administrative Cases (RPAC). All CPs must deal only with registered DNFBPs with valid or subsisting P/COR or may risk being cited for a Serious Violation under Section 2(C)(25), Rule IV, of the RPAC. The updated list of Registered DNFBPs as of 31 May 2026 is posted at this link .. For the names of newly registered DNFBPs not yet included in the list, CPs may contact for confirmation/validation the Registration Staff of the Compliance and Supervision Group, Detection and Prevention Department, at telephone numbers (632) 5302-3848 , 5310-3244 , 8708-7067 .

title: President Marcos Directs Whole-of-Government Support for the 2026–2030 National AML-CTF-CPF Strategy
body: The Anti-Money Laundering Council (AMLC) welcomes the issuance of Memorandum Circular No. 113 (MC 113), directing all relevant government agencies, government-owned and -controlled corporations (COCCs), and encouraging local government units (LGUs) to support the drafting and implementation of the National Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism/Counter-Proliferation Financing Strategy (NACS) 2026-2030. Signed on 12 February 2026 by Executive Secretary Ralph G. Recto, by authority of President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr., MC 113 tasked the AMLC, as the National Anti-Money Laundering/Counter-Terrorism Financing/Counter-Proliferation Financing Coordinating Committee (NACC) Secretariat, to provide technical and administrative support, set timelines, and monitor agency compliance in preparing the updated NACS. The directive also instructs heads of government agencies and instrumentalities to align their institutional action plans for the NACS 2026-2030 with available resources, consistent with existing laws, rules, and regulations, while encouraging LGUs and GOCCs to actively participate in its formulation and implementation. The updating of the NACS follows the completion of the Philippines' Third National Money Laundering, Terrorism Financing, and Proliferation Financing Risk Assessment (NRA) covering 2021-2024. The NRA identified priority threats and vulnerabilities and recommended risk-based measures to strengthen the country's Anti-Money Laundering (AML), Counter-Terrorism Financing (CTF), and Counter-Proliferation Financing (CPF) framework. The NACS translates the findings of the Third NRA into concrete, measurable, and risk-based actions across all sectors. The NACS 2026-2030 will serve as the country's principal policy roadmap as the Philippines prepares for its Fourth Mutual Evaluation by the Asia/Pacific Group on Money Laundering (APG) in 2027. This evaluation will assess the country's technical compliance with the Financial Action Task Force's (FATF) forty (40) Recommendations and effectiveness across eleven (11) Immediate Outcomes. The issuance of Memorandum Circular No. 113 affirms the President's strong commitment to a whole-of-government approach in safeguarding the integrity of the Philippine financial system. The AMLC looks forward in actively engaging with concerned agencies, LGUS, and COCCs in the drafting process and aligning their institutional plans with national priorities under the NACS 2026-2030.

title: AMLC Secures Another Major Conviction Against PDAF Scam Mastermind
body: In a Decision dated 01 October 2025, the Regional Trial Court (RTC) Branch 158, Pasig City has convicted Janet Lim Napoles on 13 counts of money laundering in connection with her orchestration of 2013's Priority Development Assistance Fund (PDAF) scam, widely known as the "pork barrel" scam. The case was jointly initiated and prosecuted by the Anti-Money Laundering Council (AMLC) and the Department of Justice (DOJ), marking another milestone in the fight against corruption and financial crimes. This is the second conviction secured by the AMLC against Napoles involving the "pork barrel" scam, following a 2024 decision issued by RTC Branch 24, Manila-affirming AMLC's effectiveness in prosecuting money laundering cases linked to corruption. In this 2025 conviction, the Trial Court found that Napoles planned a scheme involving the creation of bogus non-government organizations (NGOs) to receive pork barrel funds for ghost projects. By making it appear that the funds originated from legitimate sources, Napoles concealed its criminal origin-an act that fully satisfied the elements of money laundering under the Anti-Money Laundering Act of 2001, as amended. Napoles was sentenced to 7 to 14 years of imprisonment for each count and was ordered to pay a P94.15 million fine. Said judgment of conviction may be subject to appeal. The conviction comes at a time when the AMLC is intensifying its efforts to investigate financial crimes tied to the flood control project controversy.iThis sends a strong message: those who abuse public funds will be held accountable," said AMLC Executive Director Atty. Matthew M. David. &The AMLC welcomes this court decision as a demonstration of AMLC's relentless pursuit of individuals who exploit the financial system to conceal corruption the Executive Director added. The successful prosecution of this case emphasizes the power of inter-agency cooperation in dismantling complex financial schemes and reinforces the government's unified stance against corruption. Together with its partners, the AMLC continues to build momentum in holding accountable those who abuse public trust and divert resources meant for national development.

title: AMLC SECURES FREEZE ORDER AGAINST ASSETS OF LAWMAKER LINKED TO HIGH-VALUE GOVERNMENT PROJECTS
body: The Anti-Money Laundering Council (AMLC) has obtained a Freeze Order from the Court of Appeals (CA) on the assets of a lawmaker associated with government contracts for projects worth billions of pesos. In a Resolution dated 25 August 2026, the CA ordered the freezing of the assets of the lawmaker, a construction company linked to the legislator, and other associated individuals. The CA found probable cause that the assets were linked to violations of Republic Act No. 3019, as amended, otherwise known as the Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act. The case arose from investigations by the Office of the Ombudsman and the Bureau of Internal Revenue, as well as a separate administrative inquiry by the House of Representatives. Although the lawmaker claimed he had divested himself of his interest in the construction business before assuming public office, records showed he continued to receive proceeds from the business while in public office, indicating he continued tol exercise control over the construction companies. The Freeze Order covers 5S bank accounts and four insurance policies. The AMLC remains steadfast in carrying out its mandate to protect the integrity of the Philippine financial system and uphold the rule of law. Through close coordination with partner agencies, the AMLC will continue to pursue measures authorized under the Anti-Money Laundering Act, as amended, to identify, trace, preserve, and recover assets linked to corruption and other unlawful activities.

title: ADVISORY on Individuals and Entities Misrepresenting Themselves as AMLC Employees
body: The Anti-Money Laundering Council (AMLC) warns the public to remain vigilant against individuals and entities unlawfully representing themselves as officers, staff, offices, or units of the AMLC. These individuals and entities unscrupulously use the names or signatures of former and present AMLC officers and staff or the AMLC's name, logo, or e-mail address in their letters, notices, e-mails, messages, websites, or social media accounts to obtain personal information as part of their modus operandi to perpetrate scams and other fraudulent activities. The act of misrepresenting the AMLC or one of its officers is punishable by law. To guard against these illegal activities, the AMLC strongly urges the public to refrain from providing personal or financial account information to these individuals and entities or sending money to unverified or suspicious sources. title: Advisory (English and Filipino version) on Trusted Legal Help for Scammers Victim PH - Facebook Page
body: Advisory on Trusted Legal Help for Scammers Victims PH – Facebook Page The Anti-Money Laundering Council (AMLC) advises the public to be vigilant against a fraudulent scheme involving the unauthorized use of the names of public officials. The AMLC clarifies that it has no affiliation with the Facebook page, “Trusted Legal Help for Scam Victims PH,” or any similar online platform offering recovery of funds, legal assistance, or investment-related services. The AMLC and its officials do not solicit money, provide private legal assistance, or communicate with individuals through unofficial social media accounts for such purposes. The Arbitration Agreement being circulated on the Facebook page is FAKE and was not issued by Atty. Matthew David. The AMLC, Secretariat its officers and employees does not issue Arbitration Agreements. The public is strongly advised to exercise caution, verify information through official government channels, and refrain from engaging with or sending money to individuals or entities claiming association with the AMLC without proper verification. Any suspicious activities or incidents involving the misuse of the AMLC’s name or its officials should be reported to the appropriate authorities. This Advisory is issued to inform and protect the public from fraudulent schemes and misrepresentation. Paalala sa Publiko ukol sa Facebook Page na “Trusted Legal Help for Scam Victims PH” Pinapayuhan ng Anti-Money Laundering Council (AMLC) ang publiko na maging mapagmatyag laban sa isang mapanlinlang na gawain na kinasasangkutan ng hindi awtorisadong paggamit ng mga pangalan ng mga opisyal ng pamahalaan. Nililinaw ng AMLC na wala itong anumang kaugnayan sa Facebook page na may pangalang “Trusted Legal Help for Scam Victims PH,” na umano’y nagpapanggap at ginagamit ang pangalan ng AMLC at ng Executive Director nito, Atty. Matthew M. David, upang manlinlang ng mga miyembro ng publiko. Ang AMLC at ang mga opisyal nito ay hindi humihingi ng pera, hindi nagbibigay ng pribadong serbisyong legal, at hindi nakikipag-ugnayan sa mga indibidwal sa pamamagitan ng mga hindi opisyal na social media account para sa mga nasabing layunin. Ang pinapakalat na Arbitration Agreement sa Facebook page ay HINDI TOTOO at hindi nanggaling kay Atty. Matthew M. David. Ang AMLC, Secretariat at ang mga opisyal at empleyado nito ay kailanman hindi naglalabas ng Arbitration Agreement. Mahigpit na pinapayuhan ang publiko na mag-ingat, iberipika ang impormasyon sa pamamagitan ng mga opisyal na channel ng pamahalaan, at iwasang makipag-ugnayan o magpadala ng pera sa mga indibidwal o entidad na nagsasabing may kaugnayan sa AMLC nang walang wastong beripikasyon. Ang anumang kahina-hinalang gawain o insidente na may kinalaman sa maling paggamit ng pangalan ng AMLC o ng mga opisyal nito ay nararapat na iulat sa mga kinauukulang awtoridad. Ang Advisory na ito ay inilabas upang magbigay ng babala at maprotektahan ang publiko laban sa mga mapanlinlang na gawain at maling pagpapakilala.

title: AMLC Names Atty. Ronel U. Buenaventura as New Executive Director
body: AMLC NAMES ATTY. RONEL U. BUENAVENTURA AS NEW EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR The Anti-Money Laundering Council (AMLC) appointed Atty. Ronel U. Buenaventura as the new Executive Director, effective 14 April 2026. Under Section 8 of Republic Act No. 9160 or the Anti-Money Laundering Act of 2001, as amendea, the AMLC is authorized to establish a secretariat to be headed by an Executive Director, who shall be appointed by the Council for a term of five (5) years. The Executive Director must be a member of the Philippine Bar, at least 35 years of age, and of good moral character, unquestionable integrity, and known probity. Executive Director Buenaventura, who succeeded former Executive Director Matthew M. David, brings with him a distinguished record of public service and academic excellence. Previously, Executive Director Buenaventura served as the Acting Deputy Director of the Commitments and Policy Group of the AMLC Secretariat, where he played a key role in securing the country's exit from the Financial Action Task Force Greylist, and as Acting Legal Officer IV of the Office of the General Counsel and Legal Services at the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas. Prior to rejoining the AMLC, Atty. Buenaventura served as Vice President for a fintech company where he led the anti-money laundering compliance and regulatory and policy analysis of evolving global financial trends in payments and digital economy. His professional experience also includes serving as Associate Solicitor III at the Office of the Solicitor General. The new Executive Director placed tenth in the 2015 Bar Examinations. Atty. Buenaventura graduated magna cum laude from the Bulacan State University College of Law and earned his Bachelor of Arts in Psychology from the University of the Philippines in Diliman. He also holds a Master of Corporate Law degree from the University of Cambridge in 2024, graduating with First Class Honors, and Master of Arts in Philosophy from the University of the Philippines in Diliman. He teaches Commercial Law across respected academic institutions such as the University of Sto. Tomas Faculty of Civil Law, Bulacan State University College of Law, and Tarlac State University School of Law, among others. ###
