title: Philippines reinforces leadership in refugee protection at National Refugee Day 2026 launch
body: Manila, Philippines — The Government of the Philippines, through the Department of Justice – Refugees and Stateless Persons Protection Unit (DOJ-RSPPU), with support from UNHCR, the UN Refugee Agency and partners, officially launched National Refugee Day 2026 on 04 June 2026 with the theme Solutions in Motion: Rebuilding Futures Together, reaffirming its strong commitment to protecting refugees and promoting their inclusion in society. The launch signifies the start of this year’s national commemoration, which coincides with the 75th anniversary of the 1951 Refugee Convention, the landmark international agreement that affirms the right of individuals forced to flee conflict, violence, or persecution to seek safety and rebuild their lives in dignity. The event convened representatives from key government agencies, including the Presidential Communications Office (PCO) and the Judiciary, alongside UNHCR, academic institutions, and forcibly displaced persons. It highlighted the Philippines’ whole-of-government and whole-of-society approach to refugee protection. Chief State Counsel Dennis Arvin L. Chan, Head of the DOJ-RSPPU, reiterated that the country has long welcomed individuals escaping conflict and persecution for decades. “As a nation, we have chosen to respond not with indifference, but with compassion and protection for those seeking refuge. This commitment remains steadfast today,” the Chief State Counsel Chan emphasized. Building on this longstanding humanitarian tradition, PCO Undersecretary Ramon A. Ilagan, who joined the event, encouraged Filipinos to show compassion in both word and deed. He underscored the importance of unity and generosity, saying, “To our fellow Filipinos, let us prove to the world that bayanihan extends beyond our own countrymen and reaches anyone in need.” In support of these efforts, the courts also play a vital institutional role within the broader government protection framework. In 2022, the Supreme Court underscored this commitment by promulgating the Rule on Facilitated Naturalization of Refugees and Stateless Persons, which streamlines the judicial naturalization process and removes burdensome procedural requirements for bona fide refugees and stateless individuals. Presiding Judge Maria Josefina G. San Juan-Torres expressed pride, stating, “We are proud to note that the first judicial naturalization decision under this Rule was recently issued by the Manila Regional Trial Court, through Presiding Judge Eduardo Ramon R. Reyes.” In the Philippines, the Government has demonstrated leadership in advancing inclusive and rights-based policies for refugees and stateless persons. These include access to education, healthcare, and livelihood opportunities, as well as the enjoyment of freedom of movement and freedom of abode, underscoring the country’s longstanding commitment to humanitarian principles and the Filipino value of bayanihan. In support of the Government’s efforts, UNHCR reaffirmed its partnership in strengthening protection systems and promoting durable solutions for forcibly displaced populations. “Together with the Government of the Philippines, we continue to work toward ensuring that refugees are protected and included,” said Maria Ermina Valdeavilla-Gallardo, Head of National Office of UNHCR Philippines. “This campaign reminds us that the right to seek safety must be upheld, especially at a time when global displacement remains at unprecedented levels,” she added. Honoured at the media launch, Janice Tarlue, a recognized refugee, expressed her sincere appreciation to the Philippines for opening its doors to her, as this gave her the opportunity to rebuild her life with her family. Tarlue shared, “While my arrival was filled with challenges, from adjusting to a new environment to providing for my child, I also found something just as powerful: compassion that helped me begin again.” The Philippines has long been a steadfast champion of protection in the region. As a State Party to the 1951 Refugee Convention and its 1967 Protocol, alongside the 1954 and 1961 Statelessness Conventions, the country continues to lead with a principled, rights-based and inclusive approach to displacement. Marked each year on 20 June under Presidential Proclamation No. 265, s. 2023, National Refugee Day, aligned with the global observance of World Refugee Day, reiterates the country’s enduring commitment to safeguarding those forced to flee and advancing lasting solutions for refugees, stateless persons, and those at risk of statelessness. Consistent with this commitment, the media launch highlighted a series of key activities in celebration of National Refugee Day. These include the National Refugee Day Forum on 23 June 2026, which will provide a platform to discuss initiatives, opportunities, and expressions of solidarity with refugees. Supporting this effort, the initiative will also feature the 4th Refugee Film Festival and Short Film Competition on 20 June 2026 in partnership with UNHCR and De La Salle University-Manila (DLSU-Manila), offering young filmmakers an opportunity to showcase their storytelling skills and creative talents. Director Anna Lyn M. Bandagosa of DLSU’s Center for Social Concern and Action affirmed that the Film Festival offers a valuable platform for audiences to appreciate not only the challenges faced by refugees, but also their talents, resilience, and aspirations. “We also hope that this film festival will inspire more higher education institutions to open their doors, creating pathways for inclusion, support, and opportunity for refugees, and contributing to a more compassionate and welcoming society for all,” Bandagosa added. In addition, the Blue Monday initiative will see government agencies wearing blue in commemoration of Refugee Day, demonstrating collective support for displaced communities. A One-Stop Shop and Food Bazaar will likewise be organized, where refugee entrepreneurs can present and promote their products and businesses. These activities form part of the broader national observance aimed at fostering awareness, inclusion, and support for refugees. Government buildings and institutions are also invited to illuminate their facade in blue on 20 June 2026. This initiative shall serve as a symbolic expression of solidarity with individuals worldwide who are forcibly displaced, stateless, or at risk of statelessness. At this pivotal moment, the Philippines calls on the international community to stand in solidarity, strengthening collective responsibility, amplifying protection efforts, and ensuring that no one forced to flee is left behind.

title: Remulla vows compliance on PBBM’s year-end POGO total ban deadline
body: Justice Secretary Jesus Crispin “Boying” C. Remulla committed to exerting all efforts to meet President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos, Jr.’s directive to totally stop all POGO operations in the country by the end of the year. The Secretary made this assurance along with the deferment of the 60-day deadline set by the Bureau of Immigration (BI) on foreigners working in POGO hubs to voluntarily leave the country. title: Last 5 March 2025, the Bayombong Nueva Vizcaya Regional Trial Court (RTC) Branch 37 sentenced Teddy Jay Mejia, a notorious child trafficker
body: Last 5 March 2025, the Bayombong Nueva Vizcaya Regional Trial Court (RTC) Branch 37 sentenced Teddy Jay Mejia, a notorious child trafficker, to imprisonment for seven counts of Republic Act (R.A.) No. 9208, as amended, or the Anti-Trafficking in Persons (TIP) Act and violation of R.A. No. 11930 or the Anti-Online Sexual Abuse and Exploitation of Children (OSAEC) and Anti-Child Sexual Abuse or Exploitation Materials (CSAEM) Act. Mejia’s accomplice was also convicted and sentenced for OSAEC and sexual assault-related crimes. The criminals had records of violating the Anti-Child Abuse Law and the Anti-Photo and Video Voyeurism Act, preying on the innocent before being relentlessly pursued and brought to justice by authorities. The successful conviction was the result of coordinated efforts by the Regional Anti-Child Sexual Exploitation and Trafficking Task Force II (RACETTF II), Women and Children Protection Center Luzon Field Unit (WCPC-LFU), and the Regional Anti-Cybercrime Unit 02 (RACU 02) of the Philippine National Police (PNP). In 2023, these agencies responded to reports of exploitative materials involving minors being sold online. After further verification, it led to an investigation and eventually, the rescue of trafficking victims. Authorities uncovered that Mejia had exploited over 100 minors, selling explicit photos and videos on Telegram and collecting payments through online wallets like GCash. Their extensive probe also exposed how the trafficker had hidden his empire of online exploitation schemes through blackmailing the victims by leaking their sexual materials if they refused to obey him. Following an International Criminal Police Organization (INTERPOL) Red Notice, the suspect was finally arrested in Dubai, United Arab Emirates, and deported to the Philippines in September 2024. In the decision issued by RTC Branch 37, Mejia was sentenced to 20 years of imprisonment and fined ₱1,000,000 for each of three counts of violation of R.A. No. 11862 or the Anti-TIP Act. Additionally, the court imposed reclusion temporal and a fine of ₱300,000 for each of four counts of violating R.A. No. 11930. His accomplice was likewise sentenced to reclusion temporal and fined ₱10,000 for violating the Anti-OSAEC-CSAEM Act. The court also found the accomplice guilty of sexual assault-related offenses. This conviction marks a significant victory for government agencies in their fight against human trafficking. The RTC Branch 37 ruling highlights the growing effectiveness of inter-agency cooperation in law enforcement and victim protection. Undersecretary Nicholas Felix Ty commended the relentless efforts of all those who worked together to bring Teddy Jay Mejia to justice. "This victory is the result of the blood and sweat of our law enforcement officers and prosecutors. There is no place in our society for those who exploit and abuse our children. As public servants, it is our duty to fight for the rights of every young victim and ensure they are given a new chance at life," said Usec. Ty. He also urged various sectors to unite and strengthen efforts against human trafficking, emphasizing that Filipinos must unite against this heinous crime, "Protecting our children is not just the government's responsibility—it is the duty of the entire nation. Let us take to heart that we are one nation, with one action, and that is to end human trafficking." This case also underscores the expanding cross-border partnership in law enforcement and victim protection, demonstrating the unified commitment of government agencies in the fight against human trafficking. The Government of the Philippines, through the Department of Justice - Philippines, as the lead agency of the Inter-Agency Council Against Trafficking extends its gratitude to Interpol and the authorities of Dubai, United Arab Emirates, for their unwavering cooperation and swift action in the successful apprehension and deportation of the Filipino trafficker.

title: DOJ convenes key stakeholders to advance compassionate justice for Persons Deprived of Liberty (PDLs)
body: In an effort to render real and compassionate justice for all, especially for the well-being of persons deprived of liberty (PDLs), the Department of Justice (DOJ) hosted today a high-level prison conference with the theme “Beyond Bars: Healing Lives Through Compassionate Release and Medical Parole” at the Admiral Hotel in Malate, Manila. In collaboration with the Medical Action Group (MAG), the DOJ seeks to utilize a whole-of-government approach in responding to pressing issues hounding the current state of the country’s PDLs, particularly affecting the elderly, seriously ill disabled PDLs over issues of jail congestion and serious medical conditions. Likewise, it aims to establish a framework where compassionate release is thoughtfully considered and recognized as an essential component of justice. Advancing the mission of Justice Secretary Jesus Crispin “Boying” Remulla of delivering compassionate justice to every Filipino, this conference aims to serve as an avenue for discussion, ideas, reforms and best practices in developing compassionate/humane release mechanisms for qualified PDLs. Specifically, the goals of this undertaking are formulation of policy recommendations, crafting of technical guidelines and establishment of a post-release framework for the rehabilitation and reformation of PDLs. “The work we do here today will not only benefit those incarcerated, but will also create a ripple effect throughout our society – one that reaffirms our commitment to justice, human dignity and rehabilitation,” said Secretary Remulla, in his keynote message, delivered by Undersecretary Raul T. Vasquez. “To achieve true and lasting change we need your help our international and civil society organizations, your expertise, insights and continuous dedication to our shared causes will aid the crafting of meaningful policies that will pave the way for new avenues that will give second chances to our PDLs,” added Undersecretary-in-Charge for the DOJ Corrections Cluster Deo L. Marco. Key participants of the event included experts and representatives from the Board of Pardons and Parole (BPP), Parole and Probation Administration (PPA), Bureau of Corrections (BuCor), Bureau of Jail Management and Penology (BJMP), Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG), Commission on Human Rights (CHR), Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD), Department of Health (DOH), United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC), International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC), PhilHealth and many more.

title: Remulla: Diplomatic Immunity is not ‘absolute’
body: Justice Secretary Jesus Crispin “Boying” C. Remulla said that diplomatic immunity is never ‘absolute’ and is always regulated within the bounds of law enforced by the receiving State. This, after the Chinese Embassy reportedly released the alleged transcript and recordings of the conversation between a Philippine military official and a Chinese diplomat involving Ayungin Shoal. Secretary Remulla ordered the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) to conduct an in-depth investigation into the reported illegal and unlawful activities committed by foreign diplomats. The Secretary said, “while enjoying the privileges and immunities accorded to foreign diplomats, it is also their duty to respect the laws and regulations of the receiving state.” Remulla vowed to taking appropriate actions, if warranted, against these diplomats. “Diplomatic immunity should never be used as a license to exploit our country’s peace and harmony for selfish motives, this privilege does not shield anyone from the consequences of the Rule of Law,” the Secretary stressed. According to the Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations, diplomats, employees of international organizations and their immediate family members are covered by a certain degree of diplomatic immunity during their stay in a receiving State. However, diplomatic immunity is only with respect to official acts performed in the exercise of official duties and functions necessary for advocating international comity, policies and interests.

title: Delivering Real Justice for All in a Global Stage: Remulla spearheads signing of various PH treaties with UAE
body: Guided by the principles of the Bagong Pilipinas brand of governance, Justice Secretary Jesus Crispin "Boying" C. Remulla, along with the Philippine delegation led by First Lady (FL) Liza Araneta-Marcos, took utmost pride and honor in representing our country in the World Governments Summit (WGS) this year held in Dubai, United Arab Emirates (UAE). For the Department of Justice (DOJ), the main highlight of the event was the signing of various treaties with UAE involving matters such as Mutual Legal Assistance Treaty (MLAT), extradition and transfer of sentenced persons. SOJ Remulla signed on behalf of the Philippines while the UAE justice minister was his counterpart as witnessed by FL Marcos. Themed "Shaping Future Governments", the 3-day WGS from 11-13 February 2025 convened different heads of governments across the world, international organizations, thought leaders from both public and private sectors around the globe. This endeavor aims to champion international cooperation by guiding governments in laying out a feasible working plan to form innovative solutions for future challenges in leadership and governance, ultimately inspiring and empowering the next generation of State leaders. More importantly, the Summit serves as a platform in gathering prominent leaders, policy makers and experts around the globe to address critical global challenges, such as access to justice, poverty and hunger. Last but definitely not the least, the event also paved the way for the signing by other government agencies like DBM, DSWD and DMW of Memorandum of Agreements (MOAs) which target their respective mandates to advance the mutual prosperity of both the Philippines and the UAE. "The Philippines and the UAE have long shared a deep and enduring relationship, with over 600,000 Filipinos contributing the UAE's economy and society. These agreements reinforce our mutual trust, ensuring that our legal frameworks not only protect our citizens but also uphold the principles of justice and fairness," Secretary Remulla highlighted. "Today's signing is not just a legal milestone, it is a testament to what nations can achieve when they choose cooperation over division, justice over impunity, and partnership over isolation," the Secretary added. Since its inception in 2013 under the leadership of Dubai leader Mohammed bin Rashid al Maktoum, the WGS has engaged a total of 140 countries.

title: Remulla, PCA Secretary-General vow to elevate partnership
body: Justice Secretary Jesus Crispin "Boying" Remulla personally received Dr. Marcin Czepelak, Permanent Court of Arbitration (PCA) Secretary-General, during a courtesy call today, 30 August 2024 at the Department of Justice (DOJ) Main Office in Ermita, Manila. Other officials of the DOJ were present during the welcoming of the international body official along with the PCA entourage. It was a light and cordial meet and greet encounter between the representatives of both organizations, with a common goal of strengthening the connection and partnership between the Philippines and the PCA. The discussions centered mostly on possible business and investment partnerships viable for the Philippines and members of the PCA. “We are delighted to welcome this alliance with the PCA board, which perfectly aligns with our dedication to simplifying the business landscape, particularly for foreign investment. This partnership will enhance the credibility of doing business in the Philippines and foster an environment of trust and innovation. Together, we are forging a future where these values drive our shared success.” the Secretary stressed. The parties ended the meeting with a mutual expression of willingness to work together.

title: DOJ culminates Women’s Month with strong digital safety pledge
body: The Department of Justice (DOJ) wrapped up National Women’s Month with a powerful Flag Raising Ceremony on 30 March 2026 at the DOJ Main Building in Manila. The event reaffirmed the agency’s commitment to protecting women and children in both physical and digital spaces. Rep. Ann Garcia-Matibag of Laguna’s First District, Chairperson of the House Committee on Women and Gender Equality, delivered the keynote address as special guest. She urged stronger accountability and proactive safeguards, especially online where new threats endanger women’s safety saying, “Let us also commit to make our digital spaces, just as safe as our physical ones, where women and children are protected, where violations are swiftly addressed and accountability is clear and uncompromising.” Secretary Fredderick A. Vida echoed her call, noting that justice must adapt to modern threats. “The DOJ stands resolute: every violation against women and children will face swift justice, and every voice raised will be heard, protected, and acted upon,” he declared. As part of the culminating program, the DOJ also recognized the winners of its Women’s Month photo contest, highlighting compelling visual narratives that capture the strength, resilience, and vital contributions of women in society and within the justice sector. The DOJ’s Women’s Month celebration reaffirms its commitment to advancing gender-responsive justice, strengthening protection frameworks, and ensuring that the voices of women translate into concrete action and meaningful change in both traditional and digital spaces.

title: Remulla: DOJ, PNP collab to ensure quality, airtight cases
body: The Department of Justice (DOJ) expressed its full support and willingness to forge an alliance with the Philippine National Police (PNP) to ensure quality cases are filed. This after PNP authorities are set to form committees to thoroughly review cases they have filed before the courts but were eventually dismissed. “I welcome this move of the PNP of creating committees to revisit the cases they have previously filed but were dismissed. The DOJ will collaborate with the PNP to bridge the gaps,” Secretary Jesus Crispin “Boying” Remulla stressed. “Our prosecutors will take proactive involvement in case build-up, making sure that no stones are left unturned,” he added. By virtue of Department Circular No. 20 series of 2023, prosecutors are directed to be proactive in case build up, fully-equipping them with the 'know-hows' in establishing a strong prima facie case supported by actual evidence, witnesses, documents, and the like. Further, the PNP said officers who handled the cases dismissed would undergo refresher courses to beef up their competency, while those to be designated as investigators should be a graduate of a relevant course and have handled cases that led to successful convictions. “The collaborative efforts of the DOJ and the PNP will safeguard the innocent while bringing the perpetrators to justice. Evidence planting and case fabrication have no place, they are and never will be allowed in this administration, legal processes will be in place so that justice will be served to whom it is due,” Remulla stressed.

title: DOJ-CIW collab with Irish Embassy to host dance workshop for female PDLs
body: In an effort to revitalize and improve the Corrections system in the country, the Department of Justice - Correctional Institution for Women (DOJ-CIW) partnered with the Irish Embassy in the Philippines to facilitate a dance workshop for female persons deprived of liberty (PDLs). Sanidad, Irish Ambassador to the Philippines Emma Hickey and Embassy of Ireland in the Philippines Head of Consular Naomi McElroy were able to personally grace the occasion. They were welcomed by Undersecretaries Deo L. Marco and Margarita N. Gutierrez, as well as BuCor Director Gregorio P. title: Training on International Legal Cooperation: Mutual Legal Assistance in Criminal Matters
body: The Office of the Chief State Counsel successfully concluded the second “Training on International Legal Cooperation: Mutual Legal Assistance in Criminal Matters” on 28-30 April 2025 at Hotel Benilde Maison De La Salle, Manila. It was organized to bring together experts with working experience as central authority lawyers or competent authorities dealing with international cooperation requests, with a particular focus on mutual legal assistance in criminal matters. Participants included representatives from the Philippine National Police, National Bureau of Investigation, Anti-Money Laundering Council, Office of the Ombudsman, and Securities and Exchange Commission, as well as prosecutors from the city prosecution offices of Quezon City, Makati City, Lapu-Lapu City, Iloilo City, Talisay City, Dumaguete City, Bacolod City, Tagbilaran City, Tacloban City, Cebu City, and Mandaue City, and from the provincial prosecution offices of Aklan, Leyte, Iloilo, Samar, Negros Oriental, Cebu, and Negros Island. The training was aimed to strengthen the capacity of central authority lawyers, law enforcement and prosecution authorities in the investigation and prosecution of cases involving transnational elements by providing the participants with the knowledge and skills necessary to utilize mutual legal assistance in criminal matters (MLA) in the case buildup, investigation and prosecution of offenses, and recovering proceeds of crime. It also discussed the effective and timely execution of requests for assistance from foreign jurisdictions. The sessions were led by hand-picked speakers with extensive expertise on international legal cooperation, who offered the most up-to-date and relevant information. They provided participants with an invaluable opportunity to broaden their perspectives and challenge themselves in the field of international legal cooperation, specifically inmaking and executing MLA requests. The training covered essential topics, such as an overview of the MLA framework, the respective roles and functions of central and competent authorities, and specific areas of concern, including requests for assistance in cases involving online sexual exploitation and abuse of children, which was presented by Ms. Joline Ten Haken from the Embassy of the Netherlands. Other sessions addressed MLA in the context of transnational crimes, with Ms. Flavia Romiti of the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC) serving as speaker, and comparative insights from foreign jurisdictions, delivered by Mr. Dominic Norman of the Embassy of the United Kingdom. The second day of the training focused on the practical application of MLA procedures, including the role of the Department of Justice as the central authority, the guiding principles and procedural requirements under Philippine law, and the handling of MLA requests related to money laundering offenses, which was presented by Atty. Ma. Rhea M. Santos-Mendoza_ of the Anti-Money Laundering CouncilSecretariat. Finally, the training also included a workshop on the drafting of MLA requests. Open discussions were also held, which allowed for an open exchange of ideas and opinions between the speakers and the participants on good practices, and challenges encountered in making or executing a request for assistance. This provided for an excellent opportunity for everyone to learn from one another and gain new insights. These series of trainings underscore the Department of Justice’s sustained commitment to strengthening institutional and inter-agency collaboration, and to promoting continuous capacity-building in the field of international legal cooperation, with the end view of effectively addressing and combatting cross-border criminal activities.

title: Steering the nation towards a “Bagong Pilipinas”: DOJ, affiliate agency leaders convene
body: In a bid to harmonize and synchronize efforts to ensure the delivery of Justice Secretary Jesus Crispin “Boying” C. Remulla’s Real Justice for All under the “Bagong Pilipinas” era, the Department of Justice (DOJ) spearheaded its annual Executive/Management Committee (Execom/Mancom) Meeting at the Dusit Thani Hotel in Makati City last 31 July 2025. The activity also included a Strategic Planning for Fiscal Year 2026, bringing together key officials of the DOJ and its attached agencies to discuss accomplishments, address operational challenges and align with the goals of the present administration. Secretary Remulla hailed the progress of the DOJ for the past three years, emphasizing the importance of having “fortitude and willpower” to achieve institutional goals. Highlighted during the event was the National Prosecution Service’s (NPS) 91.46% prosecution success rate and its creation of a special team to handle agricultural smuggling, the Land Registration Authority’s (LRA) rollout of advanced digitization/e-services and the release of 25,000 PDLs by the Bureau of Corrections (BuCor) attributed to the effective implementation of the revised IRR of the GCTA Law. The Bureau of Immigration’s (BI) modernization efforts, the Presidential Commission on Good Government’s (PCGG) relentless recovery efforts of ill-gotten wealth and the excellent performance rating of the Public Attorney’s Office (PAO) were also commended during the event. As ways forward to sustain organization success, the panel has agreed to continuously pursue the following goals: a. DOJ Optimization Bill of 2025 which is a draft bill aimed at modernizing and aligning the DOJ’s functions with the “Bagong Pilipinas” agenda; b. Unified Position Paper that is equivalent to a comprehensive paper which will be drafted with attached agencies to address common needs for personnel office space and funding to be submitted to the Office of the President (OP); c. Financial Authority where attendees agreed to explore a special provision in the General Appropriations Act (GAA) to allow agencies to retain a portion of their collections for self-funding; and d. ARTA Compliance to assure the public that processes are streamlined and more convenient.

title: DOJ, LGUs unite to strengthen child protection with Revised CANE+D Protocol
body: The Department of Justice (DOJ) announced the Provincial Launch of the Revised Protocol for the Case Management of Child Victims of Abuse, Neglect, Exploitation, and Discrimination (CANE+D) held on 26 March 2026 at the New Provincial Government of Cavite Capitol in Trece Martires City, marking a significant step forward in strengthening child protection in the Philippines. Building on the original 2013 Protocol and its National Launch on 14 August 2025, the Revised Protocol, which was developed by the Committee for the Special Protection of Children (CSPC), establishes a more comprehensive, standardized, and harmonized system that responds to evolving threats and emerging forms of abuse against children. The initiative was formalized through a ceremonial signing of a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) between the DOJ, as Chairperson of the CSPC, and the LGUs of Cavite, reinforcing a unified, accountable, and child-centered approach to safeguarding children’s rights and welfare. “This Revised Protocol is a product of collaboration among duty-bearers and stakeholders across sectors, reflecting a shared commitment to a coordinated, multi-disciplinary, and child-centered system grounded in law, compassion, and accountability,” Justice Secretary Fredderick A. Vida said. Amid rapid technological change, evolving forms of abuse, and increasing coordination demands, the Revised Protocol addresses critical gaps by strengthening inter-agency collaboration and improving frontline responsiveness. The CSPC expressed confidence that the strengthened framework will enhance protection mechanisms and help secure a safer, more just future for every Filipino child. About the CSPC Established under Executive Order No. 275, s. 1995, as amended by Executive Order No. 53, s. 2011, the CSPC serves as the government’s primary inter-agency body tasked with coordinating and monitoring cases involving violations of Republic Act No. 7610 and other child protection laws.

title: DOJ hoists clearer procedures in handling online harassment cases
body: The Department of Justice (DOJ), in collaboration with the Philippine National Police (PNP) and the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today launched the Guidelines in Gathering Evidence and Case Build-up of Gender-Based Online Sexual Harassment (GBOSH). Mandated to spearhead the development of protocols and standards for GBOSH cases, the DOJ has partnered with law enforcement agencies to establish clear procedures for receiving complaints, addressing incidents, and collecting evidence. These guidelines will equip authorities with the necessary tools to effectively investigate and prosecute offenders, involving electronic evidence regardless of the location of evidence. “These innovative GBOSH guidelines mark a significant stride in our fight against online violence. We are committed to creating a safer digital space for all Filipinos,” declared Justice Secretary Jesus Crispin Boying Remulla. The launch coincides with the 2024 Women’s Month celebration, further emphasizing the DOJ’s commitment to protecting women and all Filipinos from online sexual harassment. Emphasizing the importance of collaboration, Undersecretary Raul Vasquez said, “With the guidelines prepared by the task force, we already have a game plan, we already have these processes that would ensure that from here and thereafter, we have a truly coordinated and comprehensive effort of law enforcement and prosecution against sexual predators.” Resource persons from various law enforcement agencies also contributed their expertise to developing these comprehensive protocols.

title: ‘A big blow on ASG network’: Remulla hails conviction of Abu Sayyaf financial facilitator
body: Justice Secretary Jesus Crispin Boying Remulla applauds the successful conviction of an Abu Sayyaf Group (ASG) member who acted as an accessory in terror financing for the designated terrorist organization Abu Sayyaf. In its Judgement promulgated on 04 April 2024, the Zamboanga City Regional Trial Court (RTC) Branch 33 found Norkisa Omar Asnalul, also known as Norkisa Omar Ibno, guilty beyond reasonable doubt of three counts of violation of Section 7 of Republic Act (R.A.) No. 10168 or the Terrorism Financing Prevention and Suppression Act of 2012. The sentences shall be served successively with full credit of her period of detention. In the Information filed by the DOJ panel of prosecutors, Asnalul was charged with three counts of violation of Section 8 of RA 10168, which carries significant penalty. The charges stemmed from allegations that she facilitated the transfer of funds in 2015 on behalf of the Abu Sayyaf. During the arraignment, the accused entered separate pleas of not guilty to the three charges. However, the accused, through counsel, proffered to a plea bargain by pleading guilty to the lesser offenses – acting as an accessory in terror financing. Taking into account the plea bargain entered and the attending mitigating circumstances, Asnalul was meted the lower penalty of imprisonment of four (4) months and one (1) day as minimum to one (1) year, seven (7) months and ten (10) days as maximum, and to pay a fine of one hundred thousand pesos (P100,000.00) In its Decision, the Court said the provisions of RA No. 10168 do not prohibit plea bargaining. “The Court finds no legal impediment to the plea-bargaining agreement entered into by the prosecution and the defense, particularly considering that the lower offense to which the accused wishes to now plead guilty to is penalized under the same law as that for which she is originally charged,” Judge Shaldilyn Bangsaja stressed. Justice Secretary Remulla said, “The conviction of a member of the terrorist group more so, a financial facilitator, strengthens the government’s resolve not to give in to their unlawful demands.” Remulla, likewise, recognized the panel of prosecutors who worked hard for this conviction. “I congratulate you for a job well done. This serves as a big win against the ASG network,”the Secretary added. The Secretary further emphasized the DOJ's relentless pursuit of disrupting terror networks, protecting Filipinos, and guaranteeing national security through all legal means. Asnalul was arrested in December 2023 for receiving money from foreign sources for terrorist activities.

title: DOJ and UNODC to partner on intensified cybercrime enforcement in the country
body: The Department of Justice’s Office of Cybercrime and the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC) are currently in talks to partner on various projects on strengthening criminal justice, especially on intensified enforcement of cybercrime laws in the Philippines. Among the activities that the DOJ and the UNODC intend to undertake is increasing the government’s pool of digital forensic experts and boosting their capacities of cybercrime investigators and prosecutors. This, as DOJ Secretary Jesus Crispin C. Remulla himself highlighted this need due to the steady increase in cybercrimes and cyber-enabled offenses or incidents in the country. To negotiate on the details of this partnership, Secretary Remulla himself is leading a small delegation of DOJ officials to the UNODC headquarters in Vienna, Austria, to sit down with its Executive Director, Ghada Fathi Waly. The delegation will also visit UNODC’s Crime Laboratory. These meeting and visit will happen on the sidelines of the 68th Session of the UN Commission on Narcotic Drugs, which the Secretary is also attending along with the Philippine Delegation. Undersecretary Jesse Hermogenes T. Andres, head of DOJ’s Law Enforcement Cluster and who is leading the conversations with UNODC’s team in the Philippines, also envisions to institutionalize the government’s ability to procure and utilize the necessary digital forensic tools and software applications used in cybercrime investigations. He stressed that funding for the renewal of licenses of these important investigative tools must always be given priority. DOJ and UNODC are looking at signing a comprehensive Memorandum of Agreement to cover the various justice sector programs, including prison reform and forensics, in May of this year.

title: DOJ Marks 129th Anniversary, Honors Historic Home
body: Secretary Fredderick A. Vida led the opening of the Department of Justice’s (DOJ) 129th Founding Anniversary celebration, honoring more than a century of public service while taking new steps toward a more accessible and modern justice system. Grounded in this year’s theme “Tanglaw ng Bayan: Pantay na Hustisya, Tunay na Pag-asa”, this year’s celebration features a series of activities celebrating the Department’s history, people, and continuing transformation. In his message, Sec. Vida expressed his deepest appreciation to the DOJ officials and employees for their enduring efforts and for organizing engaging activities that honor the Department’s decades-long legacy, reiterating that every milestone must serve as a beacon of hope to the Filipino people. “Angkop na angkop ang tema ng ating selebrasyon ngayon–tanglaw, beacon. Tayo ang tinitingnan. What do you need in a place of darkness? Only one light ‘diba? To make everything. That small light defines the darkness. Kaya walang problema ang kadiliman, basta’t may pinanggagalingan ng liwanag,” said Sec. Vida. DOJ 129TH Anniversary Committee Chairperson Chief State Counsel Dennis Arvin L. Chan echoed this pledge in his welcoming remarks, vowing to invigorate and expand the scope of DOJ services to assure the public of timely and convenient access to justice. “Pantay na Hustisya speaks’ of our unwavering commitment to fairness and impartiality where the law applies equally to all, regardless of status, influence, or circumstance,” Chief Chan stated. The opening ceremony featured the DOJ Photo Contest Display themed "Walking Down Memory Lane," to pay tribute to the rich history and cherished memories that have shaped the Department through the years. More than a look back at the DOJ’s past, the exhibit honors the people, milestones, and moments that have built its enduring legacy of public service. Another highlight of the day was the BuCor painting exhibit that showcased the talent and artistry of its PDLs, giving the DOJ personnel and guests a glimpse into the Department’s efforts to provide comprehensive rehabilitation and restorative justice within the correctional system. Beyond creative expression, the artworks reflected the capacity for growth, transformation, and renewed purpose, underscoring that the pursuit of justice also recognizes the dignity of every person and the possibility of rebuilding lives. Adding to the day’s activities was the Financial Literacy Talk conducted in partnership with the Land Bank of the Philippines, providing practical knowledge to the DOJ employees on how to make smarter and more informed financial decisions. Culminating the day was the opening of the Government Service Caravan, where the Social Security System (SSS), Government Service Insurance System (GSIS), National Bureau of Investigation (NBI), and Pagtutulungan sa Kinabukasan: Ikaw, Bangko, Industriya at Gobyerno (Pag-IBIG), and Land Bank of the Philippines brought their frontline services directly to DOJ employees as part of the Department’s recognition of its employees’ hard work and needs for a more hassle-free access to government services. As it enters its 130th year of public service, the DOJ carries forward the legacy of its historic home while continuing its transformation toward a justice system that is more accessible, responsive, and closer to the everyday lives of Filipinos.

title: On Safer Internet Day, Remulla declares all-out war vs online child predators
body: Justice Secretary Jesus Crispin Boying declared an “all-out war” against individuals who abuse children and young people online as the country celebrates the Safer Internet Day Philippines today, 13 February 2024. This, as Secretary Remulla commended the National Coordination Center Against Online Sexual Abuse or Exploitation of Children and Child Sexual Abuse or Exploitation Materials (NCC-OSAEC-CSAEM) and other public and private partners for spearheading the successful commemoration of the Safer Internet Day this year. “Your dedication and unwavering commitment to this noble cause truly deserve deepest appreciation,” Sec. title: DOJ, PAGCOR forge pact to bar personnel from casinos nationwide
body: The Department of Justice (DOJ) and its attached agencies signed a landmark Memorandum of Agreement (MOA) with the Philippine Amusement and Gaming Corporation (PAGCOR), establishing a secure data-sharing system to bar DOJ officials and employees from entering casinos nationwide. Led by Justice Secretary Fredderick A. Vida and PAGCOR Chairman and Chief Executive Officer (CEO) Alejandro H. Tengco, the agreement enables sharing of personnel profiles between the DOJ and PAGCOR, which empowers the PAGCOR to enforce entry restrictions. “Let me be clear: this is not about restriction for its own sake. This is about safeguarding the integrity of public office. It is about ensuring that every public servant remains worthy of the trust bestowed upon him/her by the Filipino people,” declared Secretary Vida. For his part, PAGCOR Chair and CEO Tengco said that the DOJ and its attached agencies are the first government entities to voluntarily partner with them through a MOA. He emphasized the broader responsibility of public servants, “Civil servants are judged not just by their office duties, but by their choices outside them. Our actions, where we go, how we spend time, shape public perception and trust.” The MOA strengthens DOJ’s internal discipline through technology and inter-agency collaboration, enhancing transparency, curbing vulnerabilities, and elevating public service dignity. This proactive measure not only shields DOJ personnel from temptation but also signals zero tolerance for ethical lapses, inspiring similar pacts across agencies and reinforcing President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos, Jr.’s anti-corruption agenda. It models coordinated governance, tackling integrity risks with practical solutions to foster professionalism government-wide.

title: IACAT nagtungo sa ZamBaSulTa upang paigtingin ang pagbabantay sa mga “backdoor exit” ng Pilipinas laban sa Trafficking in Persons (TIP) at pagpupuslit ng mga migrante
body: Naging matagumpay ang paglalakbay ng Inter-Agency Council Against Trafficking (IACAT) mula 21 hanggang 26 ng Enero 2024 sa Zamboanga, Basilan, Sulu, at Tawi-Tawi o “ZamBaSulTa” para sa unang yugto ng pananaliksik ukol sa "backdoor exits" na ginagamit bilang ruta ng human traffickers palabas ng Pilipinas. Sa pamumuno ng Undersecretary-in-Charge ng IACAT, Nicholas Felix L. Ty, at walang humpay na suporta ng Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) sa pamamahala ni Commandant CG Admiral Ronnie Gil Gavan at sa katauhan ni Coast Guard District Southwestern Mindanao (CGDSWM) CG Commo Marco Antonio Gines, at tulong mula sa Presidential Anti-Organized Crime Commission (PAOCC), ang IACAT contingent ay binubuo ng tatlumpu’t walong (38) delegado mula sa Department of Justice (DOJ), Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD), PCG, PAOCC, Bureau of Immigration (BI), Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA), Department of Migrant Workers (DMW), Philippine National Police (PNP), Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM) Member of Parliament (MP), BARMM Regional Anti-Trafficking Task Force (RATTF), Palawan and Puerto Prinsesa Anti-Trafficking Task Force (PPATF), Zamboanga Sea-Based Anti-Trafficking Task Force (ZSBATTF), at NAIA Task Force Against Trafficking (NAIATFAT). Nakipagpulong sila sa mga opisyal ng ZamBaSulTa tungkol sa sitwasyon ng backdoor exits na ginagamit sa human trafficking sa karagatan. Naging positibo ang pananaw ni Usec. Ty na mahalagang hakbang ang naging paglalakbay ng IACAT sa ZamBaSulTa upang mas lumawak ang kamalayan ng Pilipino sa human trafficking. Sa pamamagitan nito, nakita ang determinasyon ng bansa sa paglaban sa anumang uri ng pang-aabuso at pananamantala na nagdudulot ng modern day slavery o human trafficking. Marami pang hakbang upang paigtingin ang pagbabantay sa mga backdoor exits sa karagatan. Nagpasalamat ang IACAT sa lahat ng nagbigay suporta upang makapaglayag at makadalaw sa mga LGUs ng ZamBaSulTa.

title: DOJ anti-terrorism task force scores conviction vs 2 CPP-NPA members
body: The Department of Justice Task Force on Counter-Terrorism I (DOJ-TFCT 1) scored another victory against two members of the Communist Party of Philippines-New People’s Army (CPP-NPA). This as the Roxas, Mindoro Oriental Regional Trial Court (RTC) Branch 43, in a decision promulgated on July 9, 2024, found Arnulfo Aumentado y Torres aka Aryo/Inod and Mary Joyce Lizada y Tapawan aka Louise guilty beyond reasonable doubt of Unauthorized Issuance of Authority to Carry Firearm and Ammunition Outside of Residence and Illegal Transfer/Registration of Firearms. The Court sentenced both Aumentado and Lizada one year imprisonment for each crime. “The period within which they are detained shall be credited in full should they abide by and follow the rules and regulations of the institution where they are continuously detained,” said the Court. Court records show that on 26 April 2023, members of the Philippine Army apprehended at Barangay Santa Teresita, Mansalay, Oriental Mindoro Aumentado and Lizada. Authorities recovered from both accused one carbine rifle, a chamber-loaded Intratec submachine gun, one improvised hand grenade and two pieces of blasting caps. Initially, both accused pleaded not guilty to the charges of Illegal Possession of Improvised Explosive Devices and class-A light weapons, penalized under Section 3 of PD 1866, as amended by RA 9516 and Section 28(c), in relation to Section 3(t) and 28(e)(1), of RA 10591. However, with the guidance of their legal counsel, both accused eventually entered into a plea-bargain agreement with the prosecution. Justice Secretary Jesus Crispin Boying Remulla hailed the DOJ TFCT led by Senior Deputy State Prosecutor (SDSP) Peter L. Ong and team: Asst. State Prosecutor (ASP) Jenny A. De Castro, Prosecution Attorneys (PAs) Ruth Anne P. Zamora, Lyra Carissa M. Profugo, Roy C. De Vesa and Michael Elvin T. Tan for their unwavering efforts in prosecuting the case which led to the successful conviction of the accused. "Terrorism must have no place in society, especially under the present administration's rule where peace and unity reigns supreme over violence or hatred. As highlighted by President Marcos in his State of the Nation Address (SONA) 2024 that extermination was never part of the administration's drug war, it is but also fair to extend the same policy in the government's battle against terrorism where justice rules above meaningless fighting," the Secretary stressed.

title: DOJAC Expands People-Centered Justice Through Successful Katarungan Caravan in Navotas
body: Reinforcing its mandate to bring justice closer to the Filipino people, the Department of Justice (DOJ), through the DOJ Action Center (DOJAC), successfully conducted a Katarungan Caravan in partnership with the local government of Navotas City on 21 March 2026. The initiative reflects the Department’s strengthened commitment to accessible, efficient, and citizen-focused public service. Held at the Navotas Convention Center, the one-day caravan delivered free legal assistance and essential government services directly to the community, helping eliminate common barriers to access. The caravan brought together key justice sector agencies, including the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI), Bureau of Immigration (BI), Land Registration Authority (LRA), Public Attorney’s Office (PAO), Integrated Bar of the Philippines (IBP), National Prosecution Service (NPS), Board of Claims (BOC), Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA), and the Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT). Local officials, led by Navotas City Mayor John Rey Tiangco and City Prosecutor Armando H. Cavalida, expressed strong support for the DOJ’s initiative, highlighting its meaningful impact on the community. The event was further supported by key stakeholders and legal aid partners, including representatives from the IBP and the local government. Undersecretary Margarita N. Gutierrez led the program and emphasized the Department’s continuing efforts to make justice more responsive and inclusive. “This initiative embodies our commitment to ensure that no Filipino is left behind when it comes to accessing justice and government services,” she stated. With more than 400 Navoteños served, the activity demonstrated the tangible impact of DOJAC’s efforts in making justice accessible at the grassroots level. In addition to frontline services, the DOJ underscored its commitment to legal empowerment through a parallel lecture series. Representatives from the IBP conducted discussions on the Katarungang Pambarangay Law and the Safe Spaces Act (Bawal Bastos Law), while Assistant State Prosecutor Joan Carla V. Guevarra delivered a timely lecture on sextortion and cybercrime. “Through the Katarungan Caravan, we bring justice closer to the people, making it faster, more accessible, and truly responsive to their needs,” Justice Secretary Fredderick A. Vida stated. The success of the Navotas Katarungan Caravan highlights the DOJ’s proactive approach in bridging the gap between government services and the people. By bringing together multiple agencies in a single platform, the Department continues to set a standard for integrated, responsive, and people-centered justice delivery. The DOJ, through DOJAC, remains steadfast in its mission to uphold the rule of law and ensure that justice is not only served - but made accessible to all.

title: PNP-WCPC Rescues 1 Minor Victim from Online Sexual Abuse in Ozamiz City Operation
body: Ozamiz City, Misamis Occidental, December 6, 2024 – The Philippine National Police’s Women and Children Protection Center (PNP WCPC) successfully rescued one (1) male minor victim from online sexual abuse and exploitation following a series of coordinated rescue operations conducted on December 6, 2024, in Purok 3, Barangay Malaubang, Ozamiz City, Misamis Occidental. The victim, who had been subjected to various forms of online abuse, is now safe and under the protective custody of social welfare agencies. "This rescue of the victim is a significant victory in our fight against the online sexual exploitation of children," said PLTCOL Mario M. Baquiran, Jr., from the PNP WCPC Mindanao Field Unit. "Our top priority is to ensure their safety and provide them with the necessary care and support for recovery." The rescue operation was launched by the PNP Women and Children Protection Center-Mindanao Field Unit, led by PLTCOL Baquiran, Jr., with the collaboration of other operating units of the PNP, along with key partners such as the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) Region 10, the City Social Welfare and Development Office (CSWDO-Ozamiz City), the International Justice Mission (IJM), and RIACAT/RATTF10. The rescued child has been transferred to the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) for immediate medical and psychological care. The PNP WCPC is working closely with the DSWD to ensure that the victim receives comprehensive emotional and legal support to aid in their recovery and rebuilding process. Although no arrests were made during this specific operation, the PNP WCPC continues to investigate and remains determined to apprehend the individuals responsible for these heinous crimes. Authorities are confident that the perpetrators will soon face justice. "This operation conveys a decisive message – that we are committed to taking all necessary measures to protect our children from exploitation," stated the PNP WCPC spokesperson. "However, we require the ongoing support and vigilance of the public." The PNP WCPC encourages the public to stay vigilant and report any incidents of online sexual abuse and exploitation of children. The center operates a 24/7 Facebook page where citizens can confidentially report any information: PNP Women and Children Protection Center Facebook Page.

title: DOJ hits 20% energy savings target amid global oil crisis
body: The Department of Justice (DOJ) has successfully met its 20% energy savings target through work-from-home (WFH) arrangements and solar panel installations at its main office in Padre Faura Street, Ermita, Manila, without interrupting any public services. From 26 February to 26 March 2026, the DOJ's power usage decreased to 72,000 kWh from 108,000 kWh recorded in the prior period of 26 January to 26 February 2026, delivering 33% actual savings. The DOJ actively aligns its operations with sustainability objectives by adopting practical and innovative measures. These measures respond directly to the global oil crisis caused by ongoing Middle East hostilities, which continue to drive up electricity prices nationwide. This achievement highlights its commitment and meaningful contribution to the “Go Green” campaign of the government, advancing sustainability, operational efficiency, and responsible governance. “We are committed to continuously exploring long-term solutions that enhance efficiency while upholding our mandate to serve the Filipino people without hindrance or delay. Real justice for all will always prevail in the face of any crisis and this is our vow as your DOJ,” said Justice Secretary Fredderick A. Vida. The WFH arrangement and other energy conservation efforts was implemented throughout DOJ offices nationwide by virtue of Department Circular No. 10 dated 09 March 2026 while the Solar Panels became operational last 03 March 2026.

title: SOJ Remulla Conducts State Visit to Timor Leste
body: Secretary of Justice Jesus Crispin "Boying" Remulla, together with key officials from the Department of Justice (DOJ), recently concluded a state visit to Timor Leste. The visit, which highlighted critical diplomatic and security issues, was marked by a high-level meeting between the Philippine delegation and top officials of Timor Leste. Secretary Remulla conveyed an official message from President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. to Timor Leste President José Ramos-Horta, addressing two key agenda points of significant regional importance. First, the delegation formally informed the Timor Leste government that President Marcos has officially banned the operations of Philippine Offshore Gaming Operators (POGOs) in the Philippines. It was relayed that there are reports indicating Timor Leste as one of the possible destinations where POGO operations could transfer. Given the shared Catholic heritage and values of both the Philippines and Timor Leste, the Philippine government deemed it essential to inform Timor Leste of the potential socio-economic and security challenges posed by allowing POGOs to operate within its borders. Secretary Remulla took the opportunity to detail the difficulties encountered by the Philippines during the tenure of POGO operations, including issues related to crime, regulatory evasion, and potential threats to public safety. These factors ultimately led to the decision to cease their operations in the country. title: DOJ Addresses PRRD’s Seditious Pronouncements
body: The Department of Justice (DOJ) categorically emphasizes that there is no such thing as “fractured governance,” as claimed by the former President, whatever that may mean. In an interview, Undersecretary Jesse Hermogenes T. Andres addressed the alleged "seditious and legally actionable" pronouncements made by former President Rodrigo R. Duterte, who described the present administration as a "fractured government" in which military intervention is purportedly needed. “It is a great disservice to the country and an insult to the working bureaucracy for the former President to portray the government as if it is no longer delivering socio-economic assistance, health services, police protection, judicial recourse, and other services of a fully functioning democracy. We have an effective and strong Republic. Therefore, instigating the military to take action as a supposed ‘remedy’ is totally uncalled for and out of order. The military has no direct role in civil governance, and the former President should not attempt to provoke the military into acting as a solution to a so-called ‘fractured governance.’ Such actions may be considered seditious and legally actionable. Only the Supreme Court can make pronouncements on the legal infirmities of the actions of the executive and legislative branches, not the former President,” Andres stressed. Meanwhile, Justice Secretary Jesus Crispin "Boying" C. Remulla assured the public that "the DOJ will never back down against insurgency or any form of lawlessness and will forever remain committed to protecting not only the Chief Executive but the entire Filipino nation as well.

title: PH-UK Treaty on the Transfer of Sentenced Persons Signed in Manila
body: Today at the DOJ Justice Hall in Manila, Secretary of Justice Jesus Crispin C. Remulla and the United Kingdom (UK) Ambassador to the Philippines, Her Excellency Laure Beaufils, put pen to paper, officiating the signing of the PH-UK Treaty on the Transfer of Sentenced Persons. This act further solidifies strengthening of bilateral relations between the Philippines and the UK. The Treaty, aligning with international standards, offers a framework where individuals sentenced in one Contracting State can opt to serve their sentences in their native country. The underlying rationale is that being closer to family, friends, and familiar culture can better facilitate the rehabilitation of the sentenced individuals. Consequently, Filipinos convicted in the UK can now choose to serve their remaining sentences in the Philippines, easing their reintegration into society upon completion. This new Treaty is seen as complementary to the PH-UK Extradition Treaty and the PH-UK Mutual Legal Assistance in Criminal Matters Treaty, both of which were established in London back in 2009. The discussions that led to this Treaty were held over two days, from 25-26 July 2023, in Manila. These negotiations were hosted by the Department of Justice (DOJ), primarily through the Legal Staff (Office of the Chief State Counsel), which acts as the country's central authority for International Legal Cooperation. By the Special Authority issued on 21 July 2023, His Excellency Ferdinand R. Marcos, Jr. assigned Chief State Counsel Dennis Arvin L. Chan to helm the Negotiating Panel. He was joined by Assistant Chief State Counsel Mildred Bernadette B. Alvor, State Counsels Florina C. Agtarap and Jennelyn D. Bilocura. Key officials from the Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA) and the Bureau of Corrections (BuCor) also played a pivotal role in the discussions. The UK's side was led by Ms. Sarah Wilson, Foreign National Office Policy Manager from the Ministry of Justice. This Treaty stands as testament to the shared dedication of both countries in enhancing their mutual relations and commitments.

title: DOJ trains frontline partners and legal aid practitioners on Trafficking and OSAEC
body: In pursuit of the Gender and Development mandate, the Department of Justice (DOJ) through the DOJ Action Center (DOJAC) held a Gender and Development Seminar on Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act (R.A. No. 9208) and Anti-Online Sexual Abuse or Exploitation of Child (OSAEC) and Anti-Child Sexual Abuse or Exploitation Materials (CSAEM) Act (R.A No. 11930), training almost 100 lawyers, prosecutors, and law student volunteers, from the DOJ), Public Attorney’s Office (PAO), Integrated Bar of the Philippines (IBP) RSM, Quezon City, CALMANA, PPLM, and Nueva Ecija Chapters, San Beda Legal Aid Bureau, Emilio Aguinaldo College (EAC) School of Law, Philippine Law School (PLS), and Legal Aid Society of the Philippines (LASP), last 08 September 2025. DOJAC Undersecretary-in-Charge Margarita N. Gutierrez opened the seminar by highlighting the harsh realities experienced by the vulnerable sectors, especially women and children, being victims of trafficking, abuse, and exploitation in all aspects. She, further, invited all the participants to take on the challenge to be vanguards of justice in protecting these vulnerable sectors from such cruel plight. The discussion on the Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act, delivered by Atty. Hannah Lizette S. Manalili, Executive Director of the Inter-Agency Council Against Trafficking (IACAT), encapsulated the present legal structure on Trafficking; an eye-opener to the Philippine Institutional Framework with the mission of protecting the victim-survivors and holding the perpetrators accountable. On the other hand, the discourse on Anti-OSAEC and Anti-CSAEM Act was expounded by Deputy Regional Prosecutor Barbara Mae P. Flores, OIC-Executive Director of the National Coordination Center Against OSAEC and CSAEM, which focused on the salient features of the law, as well as, relevant case studies. Towards the end, Undersecretary Raul T. Vasquez graced the event and expressed his unconditional support to DOJAC’s initiative of equipping frontline partners in its mission of bringing DOJ closer to people. The success of the training reinvigorates the participants’ sense of dedication; a call to be duty-bearers in championing a proactive gender-sensitive response for victimized vulnerable sectors. "Together, let us break the chains of human trafficking and online exploitation, these evils have to stop and there is no better time than now," Justice Secretary Jesus Crispin "Boying" C. Remulla underscored.

title: National Refugee Day Forum 2026
body: The Department of Justice, through the Refugees and Stateless Persons Protection Unit (DOJ-RSPPU), as Chair of the Inter-Agency Committee (IAC) for the Protection of Refugees and Stateless Persons, created pursuant to E.O. No. 163, s. 2022, in commemoration of the National Refugee Day and World Refugee Day and in solidarity with the refugees and other persons of concern (POCs), spearheaded the conduct of the National Refugee Day (NRD) Forum held on 23 June 2026 at the Seda Vertis North, Quezon City. This year’s NRD theme was “ Solutions in Motion, Rebuilding Futures Together ” in the context of forced displacement and/or statelessness, emphasizing the whole-of-government and whole-of-society approach in addressing the issues relative to forced displacement and statelessness and providing protection for POCs. Chief State Counsel Dennis Arvin L. Chan opened the NRD Forum with his welcome remarks and he likewise read the Message of Solidarity of His Excellency, President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. Panel Discussion 1 of the NRD Forum, entitled: “ Shared Responsibility, Shared Solution s ” , was moderated by Miss April Joy S. Aquin̈o , Project Development Officer of the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD). The panel of experts for livelihood, education, local integration, and naturalization was composed of Mr. Ryan Roberto E. Delos Reyes , Supervising Labor and Employment Officer of the Department of Labor and Employment (DOLE), Fr. Eric Dela Cruz , College President of Columban College, Inc., Mr. Rufino Seva , Project Coordinator of the Urban Refugee Project of the Community and Family Services International (CFSI), and Atty. Melissa Dimson Bautista , PHILJA Attorney IV and a Member of the Special Committee on the Facilitated Naturalization for Refugees and Stateless Persons. The panel discussion underscored the importance of a comprehensive, rights-based, multi-sectoral, and whole-of-society approach to the inclusion of refugees and stateless persons in the Philippines. Discussions highlighted that durable solutions for refugees and stateless persons require not only legal protection through facilitated naturalization and access to justice, but also meaningful opportunities for employment, education, and community participation. The panel discussion likewise stressed the importance of community-based support systems, including local government engagement, refugee-led organizations, protection monitoring, and initiatives that foster inclusion, belongingness and self-reliance. Effective refugee integration requires coordinated efforts among government agencies, the judiciary, educational institutions, civil society organizations, international partners, and host communities. Panel Discussion 2 of the NRD Forum, entitled: “ Leading the Way to Inclusive Futures ” was moderated by Mr. Atom Araullo , United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) National Goodwill Ambassador. He was joined by persons of concern as panelists - Janice, Zaid, Raffy, and Jalal. One of the panelist is a former refugee and now a naturalized Filipino national. Coming from different countries, they shared their lived experiences, emphasizing the challenges of forced displacement and the resilience that enables individuals and communities to rebuild their lives. They underscored the importance of dignity, inclusion, and self-reliance and stressed the essential role of refugee-led organizations and community networks relative to the needs of fellow refugees. The discussions ultimately reinforced the importance of building inclusive societies where refugees are empowered to thrive and contribute meaningfully to their host communities. During the event, the Top 3 Winners of the Refugee Short Film Festival were shown to raise awareness and build empathy on the plight of POCs. A Message of Support of Secretary Ma. Theresa P. Lazaro of the Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA) was read by Dir. Jet C. Olfato of the Office of the United Nations and International Organizations (UNIO) of the DFA. Gracing the productive NRD forum was DOJ Assistant Secretary Robert Nomar V. Leyretana who awarded the Certificates of Appreciation and tokens to the distinguished moderators and panelists. Finally, Dir. Norielyn C. Tabag , RSW, Community Engagement Center, San Beda College presented the synthesis for the event highlighting the important points during the two (2) Panel Discussions. United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) Head of National Office, Atty. Maria Ermina Valdeavilla-Gallardo concluded the NRD Forum with a closing remarks. She also read the Message of Solidarity of Mr. Arnaud Peral , United Nations Resident Coordinator.

title: DOJ successfully concludes diplomacy and protocol training
body: The Department of Justice (DOJ) successfully concluded an introductory training on diplomacy and protocol on 14 February 2025. This initiative, led by the Office of the Chief State Counsel (OCSC) (Legal Staff), provided the OCSC personnel with a robust grounding in ceremonial protocol and etiquette. It is aimed to enhance the capacity of the participants on organizing and overseeing official and social events that involve interactions with diplomatic figures, foreign dignitaries, and high-level government officials, thereby enabling them to adeptly coordinate and manage significant events involving the diplomatic community. In his Welcome Remarks, Chief State Counsel Dennis Arvin L. Chan highlighted the OCSC’s role as this Department’s focal office in treaty negotiations, requiring coordination with foreign counterparts. He emphasized the importance of upholding the Philippine hospitality and setting the appropriate tone in diplomatic discussions. He underscored the significance of protocol in preserving the dignity and decorum of official engagements, stating adherence to diplomatic protocols in official functions, high-level negotiations, and formal receptions ensure the professional and credible representation of the institution. The training was facilitated by the Department of Foreign Affairs – Office of Protocol, led by Acting Director O’myr Faisal Mustafa C. Abdalla, and was structured to provide participants with both theoretical foundations and practical competencies in protocol management. Training sessions covered key topics such as basic diplomatic protocol, event and conference management, order of precedence, ceremonial functions, and the duties of a protocol officer. The training was attended by State Counsels, lawyers and administrative staff of the OCSC and the Inter-Agency Council Against Trafficking in Persons (IACAT) Secretariat. Chief State Counsel Chan, in his Closing Remarks, committed that “this [training] is definitely not the last. We must update our skills to meet the evolving demands of our work.”

title: DOJ successfully concludes comprehensive dialogue with the United Nations Special Rapporteur
body: Manila, Philippines -- The Department of Justice (DOJ) is pleased to announce the successful conclusion of a comprehensive dialogue with the United Nations Special Rapporteur, Ms. Irene Khan. The dialogue, which took place at the DOJ main office, provided an opportunity for a robust exchange of views and ideas on the current state of freedom of expression and opinion in the Philippines. The discussion also focused on the challenges and opportunities in upholding and safeguarding these fundamental rights, in line with international standards and best practices. During the dialogue, Undersecretary Raul Vasquez highlighted the policy reforms, programs, and developments that the DOJ has implemented to promote and protect freedom of expression and opinion in the Philippines. Usec. Vasquez emphasized the government's commitment to upholding these rights while maintaining law and order in the country. He added that the meeting “strengthened our commitment to transparency, accountability, and the pursuit of justice and human rights. title: DOJ confirms arrest of Teves in Timor Leste
body: The Department of Justice (DOJ) confirmed the arrest of former Negros Oriental congressman and designated terrorist Arnolfo “Arnie” Teves Jr., in Dili, East Timor today at around 4:00 pm while playing golf at the Top Golf Driving Range and Bar. Teves, Jr. is facing multiple murder charges in connection with the killing of Negros Oriental Gov. Roel Degamo and five others in March 2023. The arrest of Teves was made possible through the collaborative efforts of law enforcement agencies, including the International Police (INTERPOL) National Central Bureau (NCB) in Dili, in coordination with the East Timorese Police. “Today’s apprehension of Teves is a testament to the power of international cooperation. It sends a clear message that no terrorist can evade justice and that nations stand united in safeguarding the safety and security of their citizens,” said Justice Secretary Jesus Crispin “Boying” Remulla. Teves, who has been the subject of a Red Notice, is now under the custody of Timorese Police while his extradition to the Philippines is being worked out by NCB-Dili in coordination with the team from NCB-Manila and Dili Philippine Embassy. “The capture of Teves only proves that through concerted efforts and determination, terrorism can be thwarted and peace preserved,” Secretary Remulla added. Remulla urged Teves, “Face your long-delayed trial without setting any conditions, face the courts squarely.” “Rest assured that the DOJ remains committed to providing regular updates on Teves’ return to the Philippines,” the Secretary said. The Secretary likewise thanked the Philippine law enforcement team as well as our international law enforcement partners in their relentless efforts in fighting lawlessness to achieving peace.

title: Statement of the DOJ condemning the violent acts of a DOJAC client
body: Justice Secretary Jesus Crispin "Boying" Remulla vehemently condemns the appalling violence perpetrated by a walk-in client at the DOJ Action Center (DOJAC) on July 18, 2024. The client forcefully entered the Office, causing a disturbance and physically assaulting DOJAC personnel, including the Program Director. As we pursue justice for the perpetrator, we stand resolutely with DOJAC personnel and the entire DOJ family. We are unwavering in our commitment to ensure that such reprehensible acts do not go unpunished. It is imperative that we address this issue promptly and implement necessary policies and regulations to safeguard the safety and well-being of our staff. This incident marks the second violent attack on our personnel within one day, following the severe injury of a DOJ security guard who was assaulted by protesters attempting to vandalize our main office. Despite these challenges, we reaffirm our steadfast dedication to fulfilling our duty to the Filipino people by upholding the Rule of Law with unwavering integrity.

title: Arrest warrants out for Guo and 15 others for qualified trafficking; Remulla urges other co-accused to surrender
body: Justice Secretary Jesus Crispin “Boying” C. Remulla confirmed today that arrest warrants or commitment orders were issued against Alice Leal Guo and 15 other co-accused for qualified trafficking charges. “The arrest warrants issued by the Pasig Regional Trial Court (RTC) Branch 167 merely confirmed the findings of our prosecutors of the alleged involvement of Guo and others in the qualified trafficking case,” averred Remulla. “The law must take its course, it’s time for Guo and co-accused to face the charges against them in Court,” added the Secretary. In a four-page Order dated 19 September 2024, the Court has found probable cause to detain former Bamban, Tarlac Mayor Alice Guo and 15 others for qualified trafficking. In view of Guo’s current detention at the NCR CIDG Custodial Facility in Camp Crame, the Pasig local court directed her transfer to the Pasig City Jail Female Dormitory. Aside from Guo, Malaysian national Walter Wong Long who was nabbed in an illegal POGO hub in Bamban, Tarlac earlier this year is also detained at the Tarlac Provincial Jail in Dolores, Tarlac City and is ordered to be brought before the Pasig City Jail. Other than Guo and Long, Huang Zhiyang whom the Presidential Anti-Organized Crime Commission (PAOCC) tagged as POGO’s “Boss of all Bosses”, former Technology and Livelihood Resource Center (TLRC) Deputy Director General Dennis Cunanan, as well as other co-accused remain at large. “All the accused in these cases are NOT ENTITLED to post bail as the charges against them are all non-bailable,” the Court Order read. “The detention of Alice Guo and Walter Wong Long, as well as the pending arrest orders against their cohorts is testament that the wheels of justice are efficiently rolling towards the right direction,” Secretary Remulla underscored. “To the remaining co-accused still playing hide-and-seek with authorities, immediately surrender without hesitation or asking any condition, the law will definitely catch-up with you,” the Secretary added.

title: Brother of Teves nabbed on terrorism charges
body: The Department of Justice (DOJ) confirms the arrest of Pryde Henry Alipit Teves, a designated terrorist and the brother of former Negros Oriental congressman Arnolfo Teves Jr., by the Criminal Investigation and Detection Group (CIDG) in Dumaguete City. Teves, 51, was apprehended following his designation as a most-wanted person (MWP) at both the provincial and regional levels. The charges against Teves stemmed from violations of The Terrorism Financing Prevention and Suppression Act of 2012, as issued by the Cebu City Regional Trial Court (RTC) Branch 74 on 13 May 2024. "The arrest of Pryde Henry Alipit Teves demonstrates our resolute commitment to fighting terrorism and upholding the rule of law," stated Justice Secretary Jesus Crispin "Boying" C. Remulla. This arrest is further underscored by Teves’ prior designation as a terrorist by the Anti-Terrorism Council (ATC) on 26 July 2023, through Resolution Number 43, citing his alleged involvement in killings and harassment in Negros Oriental as reasons for this designation. "The CIDG's diligent efforts have ensured that those who threaten peace and security are brought to justice," Secretary Remulla added. The DOJ commends the CIDG for their successful apprehension of Teves. This arrest underscores the government's commitment to upholding the law and bringing terrorism suspects to justice. Teves' bail has been set at Php200,000.00 for his temporary liberty.
